english: Dhritarashtra said: What did my (people) and the Pandavas do, O Sangaya! when they assembled together on the holy field of Kurukshetra, desirous to do battle?
The ascetic Vālmīki asked Nārada, the best of sages and foremost of those conversant with words, ever engaged in austerities and Vedic studies.
Sangaya said: Seeing the army of the Pandavas drawn up in battlearray, the prince Duryodhana approached his preceptor, and spoke (these) words:

sanskrit: कोन्वस्मिन् साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान् कश्च वीर्यवान्
transliteration: konvasmin sāmprataṃ loke guṇavān kaśca vīryavān
english: Who at present in this world is like crowned with qualities, and with prowess, knowing duty, and grateful, and truthful, and firm in vow.
'O preceptor! observe this grand army of the sons of Pandu, drawn up in battle-array by your talented pupil, the son of Drupada.

sanskrit: चारित्रेण च को युक्तः सर्वभूतेषु को हितः
विद्वान् कः कः समर्थश्च कश्च एक प्रियदर्शनः
transliteration: cāritreṇa ca ko yuktaḥ sarvabhūteṣu ko hitaḥ
vidvān kaḥ kaḥ samarthaśca kaśca eka priyadarśanaḥ
english: Who is qualified by virtue of his character, and who is engaged in the welfare of all creatures? Who is learned and capable. Who alone is ever lovely to behold?
In it are heroes (bearing) large bows, the equals of Bhima and Arguna in battle (namely), Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, the master of a great car, and

sanskrit: आत्मवान् को जित क्रोधो द्युतिमान् कः अनसूयकः
कस्य बिभ्यति देवाः च जात रोषस्य संयुगे
transliteration: ātmavān ko jita krodho dyutimān kaḥ anasūyakaḥ
kasya bibhyati devāḥ ca jāta roṣasya saṃyuge
english: Who has subdued his heart, and controlled his anger, is endowed with splendour, and devoid of malice; and whom enraged in battle, do even the gods, fear?
Dhrishtaketu, Kekitana, and the valiant king of Kasi, Purugit and Kuntibhoga, and that eminent man Saibya;

sanskrit: एतत् इच्छामि अहम् श्रोतुम् परम् कौतूहलम् हि मे
महर्षे त्वम् समर्थोऽसि ज्ञातुम् एवम् विधम् नरम्
transliteration: etat icchāmi aham śrotum param kautūhalam hi me
maharṣe tvam samartho'si jñātum evam vidham naram
english: I have great curiosity to hear of such a person. You can, O Maharşi,* know about a man of this description. *A great saint. The word, however, signifies one belonging to a particular order of saints.
the heroic Yudhamanyu, the valiant Uttamaugas, the son of Subhadra, and the sons of Draupadi all masters of great cars.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा च एतत् त्रिलोकज्ञो वाल्मीकेः नारदो वचः
श्रूयताम् इति च आमंत्र्य प्रहृष्टो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: śrutvā ca etat trilokajño vālmīkeḥ nārado vacaḥ
śrūyatām iti ca āmaṃtrya prahṛṣṭo vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing Vālmīki's words, Nărada, cognizant of the three worlds, said with alacrity, “listen to me”!

sanskrit: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते
transliteration: asmākaṁ tu viśhiṣhṭā ye tānnibodha dwijottama
nāyakā mama sainyasya sanjñārthaṁ tānbravīmi te
english: And now, O best of Brahmanas! learn who are most distinguished among us, and are leaders of my army. I will name them to you, in order that you may know them well.

sanskrit: बहवो दुर्लभाः च एव ये त्वया कीर्तिता गुणाः
मुने वक्ष्ष्यामि अहम् बुद्ध्वा तैः उक्तः श्रूयताम् नरः
transliteration: bahavo durlabhāḥ ca eva ye tvayā kīrtitā guṇāḥ
mune vakṣṣyāmi aham buddhvā taiḥ uktaḥ śrūyatām naraḥ
english: Rare as are the qualities mentioned by you, I will, O sage, having duly considered, describe to you a person endued with them.
Yourself, and Bhishma, and Karna, and Kripa the victor of (many) battles; Asvatthaman, and Vikarna, and also the son of Somadatta,

sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकु वंश प्रभवो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः
नियत आत्मा महावीर्यो द्युतिमान् धृतिमान् वशी
transliteration: ikṣvāku vaṃśa prabhavo rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ
niyata ātmā mahāvīryo dyutimān dhṛtimān vaśī
english: There is one sprung from the line of Ikşvāku, known by the name of Rāma. He is of subdued soul; and is exceedingly powerful; effulgent; endowed with patience; having senses under control.

sanskrit: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः
transliteration: anye cha bahavaḥ śhūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ
english: and many other brave men, who have given up their lives for me, who fight with various weapons, (and are) all dexterous in battle.

sanskrit: बुद्धिमान् नीतिमान् वाङ्ग्मी श्रीमान् शत्रु निबर्हणः
transliteration: buddhimān nītimān vāṅgmī śrīmān śatru nibarhaṇaḥ
english: He is intelligent; learned in morality; eloquent; crowned with grace; the slayer of foes: broad-shouldered; possessed of mighty arms, a conch-shaped neck, fleshy jaws.
Thus our army which is protected by Bhishma is unlimited; while this army of theirs which is protected by Bhima is very limited.

And a broad chest; a powerful bowman; the repressor of foes; having plump shoulder-blades; of arms reaching down to his knees; with a beautiful head, and a graceful forehead; and endowed with excellent might.
And therefore do ye all, occupying respectively the positions I assigned to you, protect Bhishma only.'

sanskrit: समः सम विभक्त अंगः स्निग्ध वर्णः प्रतापवान्
पीन वक्षा विशालाक्षो लक्ष्मीवान् शुभ लक्षणः
transliteration: samaḥ sama vibhakta aṃgaḥ snigdha varṇaḥ pratāpavān
pīna vakṣā viśālākṣo lakṣmīvān śubha lakṣaṇaḥ
english: And having symmetrical limbs, and of a cool hue; and possessed of prowess; and having a well-developed chest; with expansive eyes; crowned with auspiciousness and favourable marks.
Then his powerful grandsire, Bhishma, the oldest of the Kauravas, roaring aloud like a lion, blew his conch, (thereby) affording delight to Duryodhana.

sanskrit: धर्मज्ञः सत्यसन्धः च प्रजानाम् च हिते रतः
transliteration: dharmajñaḥ satyasandhaḥ ca prajānām ca hite rataḥ
english: Knowing duty; firm in promise; always engaged in the good of his subjects; of accomplished renown; furnished with knowledge; pure in body and spirit; obedient towards superiors; versed in self-knowledge.
And then all at once, conchs, and kettledrums, and tabors, and trumpets were played upon; and there was a tumultuous din.

sanskrit: प्रजापति समः श्रीमान् धता रिपु निषूदनः
transliteration: prajāpati samaḥ śrīmān dhatā ripu niṣūdanaḥ
english: Narada says-Like Prajapati himself; blessed with prosperity; protecting all; the destroyer of enemies, and protector of all living beings.
Then, too, Madhava and the son of Pandu (Arguna), seated in a grand chariot to which white steeds were yoked, blew their heavenly conchs.

sanskrit: रक्षिता स्वस्य धर्मस्य स्व जनस्य च रक्षिता
वेद वेदाङ्ग तत्त्वज्ञो धनुर् वेदे च निष्ठितः
transliteration: rakṣitā svasya dharmasya sva janasya ca rakṣitā
veda vedāṅga tattvajño dhanur vede ca niṣṭhitaḥ
english: Practising all the duties of his class; and preserving those cleaving to him; versed in the profundities of the Vedas and the Vedāngas; accomplished in archery.
Hrishikesa blew the Pankaganya, and Dhanangaya the Devadatta, and Bhima, (the doer) of fearful deeds, blew the great conch Paundra.

sanskrit: सर्व शास्त्र अर्थ तत्त्वज्ञो स्मृतिमान् प्रतिभानवान्
transliteration: sarva śāstra artha tattvajño smṛtimān pratibhānavān
english: Well versed in the dicta of all the sciences; brilliant; gifted with a good memory; the darling of all; unreproved; of unvanquished spirit; proficient in every branch of learning.
King Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavigaya and Nakula and Sahadeva (respectively) the Sughosha and Manipushpaka.

sanskrit: सर्वदा अभिगतः सद्भिः समुद्र इव सिन्धुभिः
अर्यः सर्वसमः च एव सदैव प्रिय दर्शनः
transliteration: sarvadā abhigataḥ sadbhiḥ samudra iva sindhubhiḥ
aryaḥ sarvasamaḥ ca eva sadaiva priya darśanaḥ
english: Ever resorted to by the good persons even as the ocean is by the rivers; worthy of being honoured; having an equal regard for all; and capable of filling the heart with ever new sensations.
And the king of Kasi, too, who has an excellent bow, and Sikhandin, the master of a great car, and Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unconquered Satyaki, and

sanskrit: स च सर्व गुणोपेतः कौसल्य आनंद वर्धनः
समुद्र इव गाम्भीर्ये धैर्येण हिमवान् इव
transliteration: sa ca sarva guṇopetaḥ kausalya ānaṃda vardhanaḥ
samudra iva gāmbhīrye dhairyeṇa himavān iva
english: Crowned with all sort of qualities, he enhances the joys of Kausalyā; being like that of the sea in gravity, and that of the Himavat in patience.
Drupada, and the sons of Draupadi, and the son of Subhadra, of mighty arms, blew conchs severally from all sides, O king of the earth!

sanskrit: विष्णुना सदृशो वीर्ये सोमवत् प्रिय दर्शनः
काल अग्नि सदृशः क्रोधे क्षमया पृथ्वी समः
transliteration: viṣṇunā sadṛśo vīrye somavat priya darśanaḥ
kāla agni sadṛśaḥ krodhe kṣamayā pṛthvī samaḥ
english: In prowess, he is like as Vişnu, and boasts of the personal attractions of the Moon. In anger he resembles the fire raging at the time of dissolution; and in forgiveness, he is like that of the Earth.
That tumultuous din rent the hearts of all (the people) of Dhritarashtra's (party), causing reverberations throughout heaven and earth.

sanskrit: धनदेन समः त्यागे सत्ये धर्म इव अपरः
तम् एवम् गुण संपन्नम् रामम् सत्य पराक्रमम्
transliteration: dhanadena samaḥ tyāge satye dharma iva aparaḥ
tam evam guṇa saṃpannam rāmam satya parākramam
hṛiṣhīkeśhaṁ tadā vākyam idam āha mahī-pate
english: Then seeing (the people of) Dhritarashtra's party regularly marshalled, the son of Pandu, whose standard is the ape, raised his bow, after the discharge of missiles had commenced, and O king of the earth! spake these words to Hrishikesa:

sanskrit: ज्येष्टम् श्रेष्ट गुणैः युक्तम् प्रियम् दशरथः सुतम्
प्रकृतीनाम् हितैः युक्तम् प्रकृति प्रिय काम्यया
transliteration: jyeṣṭam śreṣṭa guṇaiḥ yuktam priyam daśarathaḥ sutam
prakṛtīnām hitaiḥ yuktam prakṛti priya kāmyayā
senayor ubhayor madhye rathaṁ sthāpaya me ’chyuta
english: 'O undegraded one! station my chariot between the two armies,

sanskrit: यौव राज्येन संयोक्तुम् ऐच्छत् प्रीत्या महीपतिः
तस्य अभिषेक संभारान् दृष्ट्वा भार्या अथ कैकयी
transliteration: yauva rājyena saṃyoktum aicchat prītyā mahīpatiḥ
tasya abhiṣeka saṃbhārān dṛṣṭvā bhāryā atha kaikayī

english: while I observe those, who stand here desirous to engage in battle, and with whom, in the labours of this struggle, I must do battle.

sanskrit: पूर्वम् दत्त वरा देवी वरम् एनम् अयाचत
transliteration: pūrvam datta varā devī varam enam ayācata
english: Beholding the provisions of the installation, that lady the king's consort, Kaikeyī, who had previously been promised two boons, even asked him for those viz., the exile of Ráma, and the installation of Bharata.
I will observe those who are assembled here and who are about to engage in battle, wishing to do service in battle to the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.'

sanskrit: स सत्य वचनात् राजा धर्म पाशेन संयतः
transliteration: sa satya vacanāt rājā dharma pāśena saṃyataḥ
english: Bound by the ties of duty in consequence of his promise, king Dasaratha banished his favourite son Rāma.
Sangaya said: Thus addressed by Gudakesa, O descendant of Bharata! Hrishikesa stationed that excellent chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhishma and Drona and of all the kings of the earth,

sanskrit: स जगाम वनम् वीरः प्रतिज्ञाम् अनुपालयन्
पितुर् वचन निर्देशात् कैकेय्याः प्रिय कारणात्
transliteration: sa jagāma vanam vīraḥ pratijñām anupālayan
pitur vacana nirdeśāt kaikeyyāḥ priya kāraṇāt
english: In pursuance of his father's promise, and with the view of compassing the pleasure of Kaikeyī, that heroic one, commanded by his sire, repaired to the forest.

transliteration: uvācha pārtha paśhyaitān samavetān kurūn iti
english: and said: 'O son of Pritha! look at these assembled Kauravas.'

sanskrit: तम् व्रजंतम् प्रियो भ्राता लक्ष्मणः अनुजगाम ह
स्नेहात् विनय संपन्नः सुमित्र आनंद वर्धनः
transliteration: tam vrajaṃtam priyo bhrātā lakṣmaṇaḥ anujagāma ha
snehāt vinaya saṃpannaḥ sumitra ānaṃda vardhanaḥ
english: On the eve of his departure for the forest, that enhancer of Sumitrā's joy and favourite of his brother (Rāma), his dear brother Lakşmaņa, endowed with humility, displaying brotherliness, followed him out of affection.

transliteration: tatrāpaśhyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitṝīn atha pitāmahān
āchāryān mātulān bhrātṝīn putrān pautrān sakhīṁs tathā
śhvaśhurān suhṛidaśh chaiva senayor ubhayor api
english: There the son of Pritha saw in both armies, fathers and grandfathers, preceptors, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, companions, fathers-in-law, as well as friends.

sanskrit: भ्रातरम् दयितो भ्रातुः सौभ्रात्रम् अनु दर्शयन्
रामस्य दयिता भार्या नित्यम् प्राण समा हिता
transliteration: bhrātaram dayito bhrātuḥ saubhrātram anu darśayan
rāmasya dayitā bhāryā nityam prāṇa samā hitā
tān samīkṣhya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn avasthitān
english: And seeing all those kinsmen standing (there), the son of Kunti was overcome by excessive pity, and spake thus despondingly.

sanskrit: जनकस्य कुले जाता देव मायेव निर्मिता
सर्व लक्षण संपन्ना नारीणाम् उत्तमा वधूः
transliteration: janakasya kule jātā deva māyeva nirmitā
sarva lakṣaṇa saṃpannā nārīṇām uttamā vadhūḥ
english: As Rohini followed with the moon, Rāma's beloved spouse, sprung in Janaka's line-like as an embodiment of Divine power-sear (Rāma) as life itself, and engaged in acts of good, and furnished with every auspicious mark, and the best of wives, followed Rāma. Having been followed far by his father Dasaratha along with the citizens.
Arguna said: Seeing these kinsmen, O Krishna! standing (here) anxious to engage in battle, my limbs droop down:

sanskrit: सीताप्य अनुगता रामम् शशिनम् रोहिणी यथा
पौरैः अनुगतो दूरम् पित्रा दशरथेन च
transliteration: sītāpya anugatā rāmam śaśinam rohiṇī yathā
pauraiḥ anugato dūram pitrā daśarathena ca

sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति
transliteration: sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṁ cha pariśhuṣhyati
vepathuśh cha śharīre me roma-harṣhaśh cha jāyate
english: my mouth is quite dried up; a tremor comes over my body; and my hairs stand on end; the Gandiva (bow) slips from my hand; my skin burns intensely.

sanskrit: शृन्गिबेर पुरे सूतम् गंगा कूले व्यसर्जयत्
गुहम् आसाद्य धर्मात्मा निषाद अधिपतिम् प्रियम्
transliteration: śṛngibera pure sūtam gaṃgā kūle vyasarjayat
guham āsādya dharmātmā niṣāda adhipatim priyam
english: Rāma met with the virtuous and beloved king of the Nişādas; and then in company with Guha, Laksmana, and Sita, Rama dismissed his charioteer on the banks of the Ganges at Srigaverapura.

sanskrit: न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः
transliteration: gāṇḍīvaṁ sraṁsate hastāt tvak chaiva paridahyate
na cha śhaknomy avasthātuṁ bhramatīva cha me manaḥ
english: I am unable, too, to stand up; my mind whirls round, as it were; O Kesava! I see adverse omens;

sanskrit: गुहेअन सहितो रामो लक्ष्मणेन च सीतया
ते वनेन वनम् गत्वा नदीः तीर्त्वा बहु उदकाः
transliteration: guheana sahito rāmo lakṣmaṇena ca sītayā
te vanena vanam gatvā nadīḥ tīrtvā bahu udakāḥ
na cha śhreyo ’nupaśhyāmi hatvā sva-janam āhave
english: and I do not perceive any good (likely to accrue) after killing (my) kinsmen in the battle. I do not wish for victory, O Krishna! nor sovereignty, nor pleasures:

sanskrit: रम्यम् आवसथम् कृत्वा रममाणा वने त्रयः
transliteration: ramyam āvasatham kṛtvā ramamāṇā vane trayaḥ
english: Then wending from one forest to another, and having crossed many broad rivers, they, in accordance with Bharadvăja's directions, arrived at the Citrakūta; and constructing a romantic abode, the three began to live there.

sanskrit: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा
transliteration: na kāṅkṣhe vijayaṁ kṛiṣhṇa na cha rājyaṁ sukhāni cha
kiṁ no rājyena govinda kiṁ bhogair jīvitena vā
english: what is sovereignty to us, O Govinda! what enjoyments, and even life?

sanskrit: देव गन्धर्व संकाशाः तत्र ते न्यवसन् सुखम्
चित्रकूटम् गते रामे पुत्र शोक आतुरः तथा
transliteration: deva gandharva saṃkāśāḥ tatra te nyavasan sukham
citrakūṭam gate rāme putra śoka āturaḥ tathā
english: They spent their days in delight, in the company of gods and Gandharvas. And when Rāma had reached the Citrakuța, king Dasaratha, distressed on account of his son, went to heaven, bewailing the latter.

sanskrit: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च
transliteration: yeṣhām arthe kāṅkṣhitaṁ no rājyaṁ bhogāḥ sukhāni cha
ta ime ’vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṁs tyaktvā dhanāni cha
english: Even those, for whose sake we desire sovereignty, enjoyments, and pleasures, are standing here for battle, abandoning life and wealth-preceptors, fathers, sons as well as grandfathers,

sanskrit: राजा दशरथः स्वर्गम् जगाम विलपन् सुतम्
गते तु तस्मिन् भरतो वसिष्ठ प्रमुखैः द्विजैः
transliteration: rājā daśarathaḥ svargam jagāma vilapan sutam
gate tu tasmin bharato vasiṣṭha pramukhaiḥ dvijaiḥ
āchāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrās tathaiva cha pitāmahāḥ
mātulāḥ śhvaśhurāḥ pautrāḥ śhyālāḥ sambandhinas tathā
english: maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, as also (other) relatives. These I do not wish to kill, though they kill (me), O destroyer of Madhu! even for the sake of sovereignty over the three worlds, how much less then for this earth (alone)?

sanskrit: नियुज्यमानो राज्याय न इच्छत् राज्यम् महाबलः
स जगाम वनम् वीरो राम पाद प्रसादकः
transliteration: niyujyamāno rājyāya na icchat rājyam mahābalaḥ
sa jagāma vanam vīro rāma pāda prasādakaḥ
english: When king Dasaratha had passed away heaven, the mighty Bharata, although pressed by the Brāhmaṇas headed by Vasiştha, to rule the kingdom, did not wish for dominion. And that hero went the forest, with the view of propitiating Rāma.

sanskrit: अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते
transliteration: etān na hantum ichchhāmi ghnato ’pi madhusūdana
api trailokya-rājyasya hetoḥ kiṁ nu mahī-kṛite
english: What joy shall be ours, O Ganardana! after killing Dhritarishtra's sons?

sanskrit: गत्वा तु स महात्मानम् रामम् सत्य पराक्रमम्
अयाचत् भ्रातरम् रामम् आर्य भाव पुरस्कृतः
transliteration: gatvā tu sa mahātmānam rāmam satya parākramam
ayācat bhrātaram rāmam ārya bhāva puraskṛtaḥ
english: Having come to the high-souled Rāma, with truth for his prowess, he besought his brother, with every mark of respect.

transliteration: nihatya dhārtarāṣhṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana
english: Killing these felons we shall only incur sin. Therefore it is not proper for us to kill our own kinsmen, the sons of Dhritarashtra. For how, O Madhava! shall we be happy after killing our own relatives?

sanskrit: त्वम् एव राजा धर्मज्ञ इति रामम् वचः अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tvam eva rājā dharmajña iti rāmam vacaḥ abravīt

sanskrit: स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव
transliteration: tasmān nārhā vayaṁ hantuṁ dhārtarāṣhṭrān sa-bāndhavān
sva-janaṁ hi kathaṁ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
english: Although they have their consciences corrupted by avarice, they do not see the evils flowing from the extinction of a family, and the sin in treachery to friends;

sanskrit: न च इच्छत् पितुर् आदेशात् राज्यम् रामो महाबलः
पादुके च अस्य राज्याय न्यासम् दत्त्वा पुनः पुनः
transliteration: na ca icchat pitur ādeśāt rājyam rāmo mahābalaḥ
pāduke ca asya rājyāya nyāsam dattvā punaḥ punaḥ
english: Bharata said, You are only the king conversant with Dharma. And the exceedingly generous, illustrious and mighty Rāma of a cheerful countenance did not wish for the kingdom, in consonance with his father's injunction. And having made over to Bharata, as his substitute on the throne, his own sandals, Bharata's elder brother repeatedly forbade him.

transliteration: yady apy ete na paśhyanti lobhopahata-chetasaḥ
english: still, O Ganardana! should not we, who do see the evils flowing from the extinction of a family, learn to refrain from that sin?

sanskrit: स कामम् अनवाप्य एव राम पादा उपस्पृशन्
transliteration: sa kāmam anavāpya eva rāma pādā upaspṛśan
kathaṁ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum
english: On the extinction of a family, the eternal rites of families are destroyed. Those rites being destroyed, impiety predominates over the whole family.

sanskrit: नन्दि ग्रामे अकरोत् राज्यम् राम आगमन कांक्षया
गते तु भरते श्रीमान् सत्य सन्धो जितेन्द्रियः
transliteration: nandi grāme akarot rājyam rāma āgamana kāṃkṣayā
gate tu bharate śrīmān satya sandho jitendriyaḥ
dharme naṣhṭe kulaṁ kṛitsnam adharmo ’bhibhavaty uta
english: In consequence of the predominance of impiety, O Krishna! the women of the family become corrupt; and the women becoming corrupt, O descendant of Vrishni! intermingling of castes results;

sanskrit: रामः तु पुनः आलक्ष्य नागरस्य जनस्य च
तत्र आगमनम् एकाग्रो दण्डकान् प्रविवेश ह
transliteration: rāmaḥ tu punaḥ ālakṣya nāgarasya janasya ca
tatra āgamanam ekāgro daṇḍakān praviveśa ha
english: And when the auspicious Bharata, firm in his promise and of subdued sense, had gone away, Rāma again perceiving there the influx of citizens and others, eagerly entered Dandaka.

that intermingling necessarily leads the family and the destroyers of the family to hell; for when the ceremonies of (offering) the balls of food and water (to them) fail, their ancestors fall down (to hell).

sanskrit: प्रविश्य तु महाअरण्यम् रामो राजीव लोचनः
विराधम् राक्षसम् हत्वा शरभंगम् ददर्श ह
transliteration: praviśya tu mahāaraṇyam rāmo rājīva locanaḥ
virādham rākṣasam hatvā śarabhaṃgam dadarśa ha
english: Having entered that mighty vast, the lotuseyed Rāma slew the Räkşasa Virädha, and saw Sarabhanga, Sutiksna, Agastya and Agastya's brother.
By these transgressions of the destroyers of families, which occasion interminglings of castes, the eternal rites of castes and rites of families are subverted.

sanskrit: सुतीक्ष्णम् च अपि अगस्त्यम् च अगस्त्य भ्रातरम् तथा
अगस्त्य वचनात् च एव जग्राह ऐन्द्रम् शरासनम्
transliteration: sutīkṣṇam ca api agastyam ca agastya bhrātaram tathā
agastya vacanāt ca eva jagrāha aindram śarāsanam

english: And O Ganardana! we have heard that men whose family-rites are subverted, must necessarily live in hell.

sanskrit: खड्गम् च परम प्रीतः तूणी च अक्षय सायकौ
वसतः तस्य रामस्य वने वन चरैः सह
transliteration: khaḍgam ca parama prītaḥ tūṇī ca akṣaya sāyakau
vasataḥ tasya rāmasya vane vana caraiḥ saha

english: Alas! we are engaged in committing a heinous sin, seeing that we are making efforts for killing our own kinsmen out of greed of the pleasures of sovereignty.

sanskrit: ऋषयः अभ्यागमन् सर्वे वधाय असुर रक्षसाम्
स तेषाम् प्रति शुश्राव राक्षसानाम् तथा वने
transliteration: ṛṣayaḥ abhyāgaman sarve vadhāya asura rakṣasām
sa teṣām prati śuśrāva rākṣasānām tathā vane

sanskrit: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्
transliteration: aho bata mahat pāpaṁ kartuṁ vyavasitā vayam
english: If the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapon in hand, were to kill me in battle, me being weaponless and not defending (myself), that would be better for me.

sanskrit: प्रतिज्ञातः च रामेण वधः संयति रक्षसाम्
transliteration: pratijñātaḥ ca rāmeṇa vadhaḥ saṃyati rakṣasām
english: Thereupon in the presence of those ascetics like the flaming fire, inhabiting the Daņdaka forest, he promised to slay those Räkşasas in battle.

transliteration: dhārtarāṣhṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣhemataraṁ bhavet
english: Sangaya said: Having spoken thus, Arguna cast asde his bow together with the arrows, on the battle-field, and sat down in (his) chariot, with a mind agitated by grief.

sanskrit: तेन तत्र एव वसता जनस्थान निवासिनी
transliteration: tena tatra eva vasatā janasthāna nivāsinī
english: It was while he was living there that, that dweller of Janasthāna, the Rākṣasī Śūrpanakhā, capable of assuming any form at will, was disfigured.

sanskrit: ततः शूर्पणखा वाक्यात् उद्युक्तान् सर्व राक्षसान्
खरम् त्रिशिरसम् च एव दूषणम् च एव राक्षसम्
transliteration: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā vākyāt udyuktān sarva rākṣasān
kharam triśirasam ca eva dūṣaṇam ca eva rākṣasam

english: To him, who was thus overcome with pity, and dejected, and whose eyes were full of tears and turbid, the destroyer of Madhu spoke these words.

sanskrit: निजघान रणे रामः तेषाम् च एव पद अनुगान्
transliteration: nijaghāna raṇe rāmaḥ teṣām ca eva pada anugān

english: The Deity said: How (comes it that) this delusion, O Arguna! which is discarded by the good, which excludes from heaven, and occasions infamy, has overtaken you in this (place of) peril?

sanskrit: रक्षसाम् निहतानि असन् सहस्राणि चतुर् दश
ततो ज्ञाति वधम् श्रुत्वा रावणः क्रोध मूर्छितः
transliteration: rakṣasām nihatāni asan sahasrāṇi catur daśa
tato jñāti vadham śrutvā rāvaṇaḥ krodha mūrchitaḥ

sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते
transliteration: klaibyaṁ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayyupapadyate
english: Be not effeminate, O son of Pritha! it is not worthy of you. Cast off this base weakness of heart, and arise, O terror of (your) foes!

sanskrit: कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन
transliteration: kathaṁ bhīṣhmam ahaṁ sankhye droṇaṁ cha madhusūdana
english: Arguna said: How, O destroyer of Madhu! shall I encounter with arrows in battle Bhisma and Drona both, O destroyer of enemies! entitled to reverence?

sanskrit: न विरोधो बलवता क्षमो रावण तेन ते
अनादृत्य तु तत् वाक्यम् रावणः काल चोदितः
transliteration: na virodho balavatā kṣamo rāvaṇa tena te
anādṛtya tu tat vākyam rāvaṇaḥ kāla coditaḥ
english: And although strongly dissuaded by Mārīca, saying. You ought not to enter into hostilities with that powerful one. Do you, therefore, O Ravana, excuse me! yet, disregarding those words of his, Ravana, urged on by Fate, went into that asylum in company with Mārīca.

Without killing (my) preceptors (men) of great glory it is better to live even on alms in this world. But if killing them, though that are avaricious of worldly goods, I should only enjoy blood-tainted enjoyments.

sanskrit: जगाम सह मारीचः तस्य आश्रम पदम् तदा
तेन मायाविना दूरम् अपवाह्य नृप आत्मजौ
transliteration: jagāma saha mārīcaḥ tasya āśrama padam tadā
tena māyāvinā dūram apavāhya nṛpa ātmajau

sanskrit: यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः
transliteration: yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ
english: Nor do we know which of the two is better for us whether that we should vanquish them, or that they should vanquish us. Even those, whom having killed, we do not wish to live even thse sons of Dhritarashtra stand (arrayed) against us.

sanskrit: जहार भार्याम् रामस्य गृध्रम् हत्वा जटायुषम्
गृध्रम् च निहतम् दृष्ट्वा हृताम् श्रुत्वा च मैथिलीम्
transliteration: jahāra bhāryām rāmasya gṛdhram hatvā jaṭāyuṣam
gṛdhram ca nihatam dṛṣṭvā hṛtām śrutvā ca maithilīm

english: With a heart contaminated by the taint of helplessness, with a mind confounded about my duty, I ask you. Tell me what is assuredly good for me. I am your disciple: instruct me, who have thrown myself on your (indulgence).

sanskrit: राघवः शोक संतप्तो विललाप आकुल इन्द्रियः
ततः तेन एव शोकेन गृध्रम् दग्ध्वा जटायुषम्
transliteration: rāghavaḥ śoka saṃtapto vilalāpa ākula indriyaḥ
tataḥ tena eva śokena gṛdhram dagdhvā jaṭāyuṣam

english: For I do not perceive what is to dispel that grief which will dry up my organs after I shall have obtained a properous kingdom on earth without a foe, or even the sovereignty of the gods.

sanskrit: मार्गमाणो वने सीताम् राक्षसम् संददर्श ह
कबंधम् नाम रूपेण विकृतम् घोर दर्शनम्
transliteration: mārgamāṇo vane sītām rākṣasam saṃdadarśa ha
kabaṃdham nāma rūpeṇa vikṛtam ghora darśanam
english: Having with unassuaged sorrow burnt the vulture Jațāyu, as he was searching for Sità in that forest, he fell in with a Rākṣasa, Kabandha by name, of a dreadful and deformed shape. Having slain him, the mighty-armed one burnt his body,-and thereupon he went to heaven.

sanskrit: न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह
transliteration: na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣhṇīṁ babhūva ha
english: Sangaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesa, O terror of (your) foes! Gudakesa said to Govinda, 'I shall not engage in battle;' and verily remain silent.

sanskrit: तम् निहत्य महाबाहुः ददाह स्वर्गतः च सः
स च अस्य कथयामास शबरीम् धर्म चारिणीम्
transliteration: tam nihatya mahābāhuḥ dadāha svargataḥ ca saḥ
sa ca asya kathayāmāsa śabarīm dharma cāriṇīm

english: To him thus desponding between two armies, O descedant of Bharata! Hrishikesa spoke these words with a slight smile.

sanskrit: श्रमणाम् धर्म निपुणाम् अभिगच्छ इति राघव
सः अभ्य गच्छन् महातेजाः शबरीम् शत्रु सूदनः
transliteration: śramaṇām dharma nipuṇām abhigaccha iti rāghava
saḥ abhya gacchan mahātejāḥ śabarīm śatru sūdanaḥ

english: The Deity said: You have grieved for those who deserve no grief, and you speak words of wisdom. Learned men grieve not for the living nor the dead.

sanskrit: शबर्या पूजितः सम्यक् रामो दशरथ आत्मजः
पंपा तीरे हनुमता संगतो वानरेण ह
transliteration: śabaryā pūjitaḥ samyak rāmo daśaratha ātmajaḥ
paṃpā tīre hanumatā saṃgato vānareṇa ha

sanskrit: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्
transliteration: na tvevāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ
na chaiva na bhaviṣhyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
english: Never did I not exist, nor you, nor these rulers of men; nor will any one of us ever hereafter cease to be.

sanskrit: हनुमत् वचनात् च एव सुग्रीवेण समागतः
सुग्रीवाय च तत् सर्वम् शंसत् रामो महाबलः
transliteration: hanumat vacanāt ca eva sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ
sugrīvāya ca tat sarvam śaṃsat rāmo mahābalaḥ
english: Than he met with Hanuman on the banks of the Pampā. Then, agreeably to Hanumān's advice, the exceedingly powerful Rāma saw Sugrīva. And detailed to him all specially touching Sitā.

transliteration: dehino ’smin yathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā
tathā dehāntara-prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati
english: As in this body, infancy and youth and old age (come) to the embodied (self), so does the acquisition of another body; a sensible man is not deceived about that.

sanskrit: आदितः तत् यथा वृत्तम् सीतायाः च विशेषतः
सुग्रीवः च अपि तत् सर्वम् श्रुत्वा रामस्य वानरः
transliteration: āditaḥ tat yathā vṛttam sītāyāḥ ca viśeṣataḥ
sugrīvaḥ ca api tat sarvam śrutvā rāmasya vānaraḥ

english: The contacts of the senses, O son of Kunti! which produce cold and heat, pleasure and pain, are not permanent, they are for ever coming and going. Bear them, O descendant of Bharata!

sanskrit: चकार सख्यम् रामेण प्रीतः च एव अग्नि साक्षिकम्
ततो वानर राजेन वैर अनुकथनम् प्रति
transliteration: cakāra sakhyam rāmeṇa prītaḥ ca eva agni sākṣikam
tato vānara rājena vaira anukathanam prati

sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ
transliteration: yaṁ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣhaṁ puruṣharṣhabha
english: For, O chief of men! that sensible man whom they afflict not, (pain and pleasure being alike to him), he merits immortality.

sanskrit: रामाय आवेदितम् सर्वम् प्रणयात् दुःखितेन च
प्रतिज्ञातम् च रामेण तदा वालि वधम् प्रति
transliteration: rāmāya āveditam sarvam praṇayāt duḥkhitena ca
pratijñātam ca rāmeṇa tadā vāli vadham prati

sanskrit: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः
transliteration: nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ
english: There is no existence for that which is unreal; there is no non-existence for that which is real. And the (correct) conclusion about both is perceived by those who perceive the truth.

sanskrit: वालिनः च बलम् तत्र कथयामास वानरः
सुग्रीवः शंकितः च आसीत् नित्यम् वीर्येण राघवे
transliteration: vālinaḥ ca balam tatra kathayāmāsa vānaraḥ
sugrīvaḥ śaṃkitaḥ ca āsīt nityam vīryeṇa rāghave
english: Then Ráma vowed that he would slay Vālī. Thereupon the monkey described to Raghava the prowess of Vālī, and he feared lest Räma should not prove a match for Válī.

sanskrit: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्
transliteration: avināśhi tu tadviddhi yena sarvam idaṁ tatam
vināśham avyayasyāsya na kaśhchit kartum arhati
english: Know that to be indestructible which pervades all this; the destruction of that inexhaustible (principle) none can bring about.

sanskrit: राघवः प्रत्ययार्थम् तु दुंदुभेः कायम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: rāghavaḥ pratyayārtham tu duṃdubheḥ kāyam uttamam
english: And with the view of convincing Raghava (as to Vali's might), Sugriva showed to him the huge corpse of Dundubhi, resembling a hill.
These bodies appertaining to the embodied (self) which is eternal, indestructible, and indefinable, are declared to be perishable; therefore do engage in battle, O descendant of Bharata!

sanskrit: उत्स्मयित्वा महाबाहुः प्रेक्ष्य च अस्ति महाबलः
पाद अंगुष्टेन चिक्षेप संपूर्णम् दश योजनम्
transliteration: utsmayitvā mahābāhuḥ prekṣya ca asti mahābalaḥ
pāda aṃguṣṭena cikṣepa saṃpūrṇam daśa yojanam
english: And looking at the skeleton, Rāma endued with exceeding prowess, smiling the while, with his toe cast it off at the distance of full ninety miles.

sanskrit: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते
transliteration: ya enaṁ vetti hantāraṁ yaśh chainaṁ manyate hatam
ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṁ hanti na hanyate
english: He who thinks one to be the killer and he who thinks one to be killed, both know nothing. He kills not, is not killed.

sanskrit: बिभेद च पुनः सालान् सप्त एकेन महा इषुणा
गिरिम् रसातलम् चैव जनयन् प्रत्ययम् तथा
transliteration: bibheda ca punaḥ sālān sapta ekena mahā iṣuṇā
girim rasātalam caiva janayan pratyayam tathā
english: With a single mighty shaft he pierced seven palmyra palms, a hill, and the sixth nether worlds, carrying conviction to Sugriva.

sanskrit: न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः
transliteration: nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
english: He is not born, nor does he ever die, nor, having existed, does he exist no more.

sanskrit: ततः प्रीत मनाः तेन विश्वस्तः स महाकपिः
किष्किंधाम् राम सहितो जगाम च गुहाम् तदा
transliteration: tataḥ prīta manāḥ tena viśvastaḥ sa mahākapiḥ
kiṣkiṃdhām rāma sahito jagāma ca guhām tadā
english: Thus convinced, the mighty monkey well pleased went with Rāma towards the cave called Kiskindha.

sanskrit: कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्
transliteration: vedāvināśhinaṁ nityaṁ ya enam ajam avyayam
kathaṁ sa puruṣhaḥ pārtha kaṁ ghātayati hanti kam
english: Unborn, everlasting, unchangeable, and very ancient, he is not killed when the body is killed. O son of Pritha! how can that man who knows the self thus to be indestructible, everlasting, unborn, and imperishable, kill any one, or cause any one to be killed?

sanskrit: ततः अगर्जत् हरिवरः सुग्रीवो हेम पिंगलः
transliteration: tataḥ agarjat harivaraḥ sugrīvo hema piṃgalaḥ
english: And having arrived there, that best of monkeys, Sugrīva of a tawny and golden hue, set up loud roars. And at those mighty sounds, out came the lord of monkeys; and having obtained Tārā's consent came before Sugrīva for battle. Then Rāghava killed Vālī on the spot with a single shaft.
As a man, casting off old clothes, puts on others and new ones, so the embodied (self), casting off old bodies, goes to others and new ones.

sanskrit: निजघान च तत्र एनम् शरेण एकेन राघवः
transliteration: nijaghāna ca tatra enam śareṇa ekena rāghavaḥ
english: And having arrived there, that best of monkeys, Sugrīva of a tawny and golden hue, set up loud roars. And at those mighty sounds, out came the lord of monkeys; and having obtained Tārā's consent came before Sugrīva for battle. Then Rāghava killed Vālī on the spot with a single shaft.

sanskrit: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः
transliteration: nainaṁ chhindanti śhastrāṇi nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ
na chainaṁ kledayantyāpo na śhoṣhayati mārutaḥ
english: Weapons do not divide the self (into pieces); fire does not burn it; waters do not moisten it; the wind does not dry it up.

sanskrit: ततः सुग्रीव वचनात् हत्वा वालिनम् आहवे
सुग्रीवम् एव तत् राज्ये राघवः प्रत्यपादयत्
transliteration: tataḥ sugrīva vacanāt hatvā vālinam āhave
sugrīvam eva tat rājye rāghavaḥ pratyapādayat
english: And, in compliance with Sugrīva's request, having slain Vālī in battle, Raghava conferred the kingdom on Sugriva.

It is not divisible; it is not combustible; it is not to be moistened; it is not to be dried up. It is everlasting, all-pervading, stable, firm, and eternal. It is said to be unperceived, to be unthinkable, to be unchangeable.

sanskrit: स च सर्वान् समानीय वानरान् वानरर्षभः
transliteration: sa ca sarvān samānīya vānarān vānararṣabhaḥ
english: Then that best of monkeys having summoned all the various monkeys, sent them in various directions in search of Janaka's daughter.
Therefore knowing it to be such, you ought not to grieve.

sanskrit: ततो गृध्रस्य वचनात् संपातेः हनुमान् बली
शत योजन विस्तीर्णम् पुप्लुवे लवण अर्णवम्
transliteration: tato gṛdhrasya vacanāt saṃpāteḥ hanumān balī
śata yojana vistīrṇam pupluve lavaṇa arṇavam
english: Then at the suggestion of the vulture Sampāti, the mighty Hanuman crossed the salt sea extending for a hundred Yojanas (900 miles).

sanskrit: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्
transliteration: atha chainaṁ nitya-jātaṁ nityaṁ vā manyase mṛitam
tathāpi tvaṁ mahā-bāho naivaṁ śhochitum arhasi
english: But even if you think that the self is constantly born, and constantly dies, still, O you of mighty arms! you ought not to grieve thus.

sanskrit: तत्र लंकाम् समासाद्य पुरीम् रावण पालिताम्
ददर्श सीताम् ध्यायन्तीम् अशोक वनिकाम् गताम्
transliteration: tatra laṃkām samāsādya purīm rāvaṇa pālitām
dadarśa sītām dhyāyantīm aśoka vanikām gatām
english: Thereby arriving at the city of Lankā, ruled by Rāvana, he found Sītā in the midst of an Asoka garden, absorbed in thought.

sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च
transliteration: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛityur dhruvaṁ janma mṛitasya cha
tasmād aparihārye ’rthe na tvaṁ śhochitum arhasi
english: For to one that is born, death is certain; and to one that dies, birth is certain. Therefore about (this) unavoidable thing, you ought not to grieve.

sanskrit: निवेदयित्वा अभिज्ञानम् प्रवृत्तिम् च निवेद्य च
transliteration: nivedayitvā abhijñānam pravṛttim ca nivedya ca
english: Then having shown her the sign, he rtlated to her all about the friendship between Rāma and Sugrīva, and having convinced Videha's daughter, he smashed the gate of the place.
The source of things, O descendant of Bharata! is unperceived; their middle state is perceived; and their end again is unperceived. What (occasion is there for any) lamentation regarding them?

sanskrit: पंच सेन अग्रगान् हत्वा सप्त मंत्रि सुतान् अपि
शूरम् अक्षम् च निष्पिष्य ग्रहणम् समुपागमत्
transliteration: paṃca sena agragān hatvā sapta maṃtri sutān api
śūram akṣam ca niṣpiṣya grahaṇam samupāgamat
english: Then having slain five generals, and seven counsellors' sons, and crushed the heroic Aksa, he was bound fast (by the arms of Indrajit.)
One looks upon it as a wonder; another similarly speaks of it as a wonder; another too hears of it as a wonder; and even after having heard of it, no one does really know it.

sanskrit: अस्त्रेण उन्मुक्तम् आत्मानम् ज्ञात्वा पैतामहात् वरात्
मर्षयन् राक्षसान् वीरो यन्त्रिणः तान् यदृच्छया
transliteration: astreṇa unmuktam ātmānam jñātvā paitāmahāt varāt
marṣayan rākṣasān vīro yantriṇaḥ tān yadṛcchayā
english: Then knowing that in virtue of the grandsire's boon, he was free, he forgave those Raksasas that were leading him (to Ravana.)

transliteration: dehī nityam avadhyo ’yaṁ dehe sarvasya bhārata
tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṁ śhochitum arhasi
english: This embodied (self), O descendant of Bharata! within every one's body is ever indestructible. Therefore you ought not to grieve for any being.

sanskrit: ततो दग्ध्वा पुरीम् लंकाम् ऋते सीताम् च मैथिलीम्
रामाय प्रियम् आख्यातुम् पुनः आयात् महाकपिः
transliteration: tato dagdhvā purīm laṃkām ṛte sītām ca maithilīm
rāmāya priyam ākhyātum punaḥ āyāt mahākapiḥ
english: Then having burnt down the city of Lankā, with the exception of the place occupied by Mithila's daughter, the mighty one returned, with the intention of delivering the glad tidings to Rama.

transliteration: swa-dharmam api chāvekṣhya na vikampitum arhasi
dharmyāddhi yuddhāch chhreyo ’nyat kṣhatriyasya na vidyate
english: Having regard to your own duty also, you ought not to falter, for there is nothing better for a Kshatriya than a righteous battle.

sanskrit: सः अभिगम्य महात्मानम् कृत्वा रामम् प्रदक्षिणम्
न्यवेदयत् अमेयात्मा दृष्टा सीता इति तत्त्वतः
transliteration: saḥ abhigamya mahātmānam kṛtvā rāmam pradakṣiṇam
nyavedayat ameyātmā dṛṣṭā sītā iti tattvataḥ
english: That one of immeasurable soul having come before the high-souled Rāma, and circled him addressed him, saying,— I have truly seen Sītā.

transliteration: sukhinaḥ kṣhatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛiśham
english: Happy those Kshatriyas, O son of Pritha! who can find such a battle (to fight) come of itself an open door to heaven!

sanskrit: ततः सुग्रीव सहितो गत्वा तीरम् महा उदधेः
transliteration: tataḥ sugrīva sahito gatvā tīram mahā udadheḥ
english: Thereafter accompanied by Sugrīva, Rāma repaired to the shore of the mighty ocean, and with shafts resembling the sun, vexed the deep.

sanskrit: अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि
transliteration: atha chet tvam imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṅgrāmaṁ na kariṣhyasi
tataḥ sva-dharmaṁ kīrtiṁ cha hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi
english: But if you will not fight this righteous battle, then you will have abandoned your own duty and your fame, and you will incur sin.

sanskrit: दर्शयामास च आत्मानम् समुद्रः सरिताम् पतिः
समुद्र वचनात् च एव नलम् सेतुम् अकारयत्
transliteration: darśayāmāsa ca ātmānam samudraḥ saritām patiḥ
samudra vacanāt ca eva nalam setum akārayat
english: Then that lord of rivers, the Ocean, showed himself. And agreeably to the advice of the Ocean, Nala constructed a bridge (over the water.)
All beings, too, will tell of your everlasting infamy; and to one who has been honoured, infamy is (a) greater (evil) than death.

sanskrit: तेन गत्वा पुरीम् लंकाम् हत्वा रावणम् आहवे
रामः सीताम् अनुप्राप्य पराम् व्रीडाम् उपागमत्
transliteration: tena gatvā purīm laṃkām hatvā rāvaṇam āhave
rāmaḥ sītām anuprāpya parām vrīḍām upāgamat
english: By that bridge Rama went to the city of Lankā, and slew Rāvana in battle. And, having recovered Sītā, Rāma experienced high shame (in consequence of Sītā's having lived so long in Ravana's place.)

sanskrit: येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्
transliteration: bhayād raṇād uparataṁ mansyante tvāṁ mahā-rathāḥ
yeṣhāṁ cha tvaṁ bahu-mato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
english: (Warriors who are) masters of great cars will think that you abstained from the battle through fear, and having been highly thought of by them, you will fall down to littleness.

sanskrit: ताम् उवाच ततः रामः परुषम् जन संसदि
अमृष्यमाणा सा सीता विवेश ज्वलनम् सती
transliteration: tām uvāca tataḥ rāmaḥ paruṣam jana saṃsadi
amṛṣyamāṇā sā sītā viveśa jvalanam satī
english: Language towards Sītā in the presence of all. Incapable of bearing it, the chaste Sītā entered flaming fire.

sanskrit: निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्
transliteration: nindantastava sāmarthyaṁ tato duḥkhataraṁ nu kim
english: Your enemies, too, decrying your power, will speak much about you that should not be spoken. And what, indeed, more lamentable than that?

sanskrit: ततः अग्नि वचनात् सीताम् ज्ञात्वा विगत कल्मषाम्
कर्मणा तेन महता त्रैलोक्यम् स चराचरम्
transliteration: tataḥ agni vacanāt sītām jñātvā vigata kalmaṣām
karmaṇā tena mahatā trailokyam sa carācaram
english: Thereupon assured by Agni as to the sinlessness of Sītā, Rāma became exceedingly pleased, and was honoured by all the deities. And at that great act of Rāma's the three worlds with all that was mobile and immobile in them, along with the sages and gods, were well pleased with the mighty-souled Rāghava.

sanskrit: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्
transliteration: hato vā prāpsyasi swargaṁ jitvā vā bhokṣhyase mahīm
english: Killed, you will obtain heaven; victorious, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore arise, O son of Kunti! resolved to (engage in) battle.

sanskrit: स देवर्षि गणम् तुष्टम् राघवस्य महात्मनः ॥बभौ रामः संप्रहृष्टः पूजितः सर्व देवतैः
transliteration: sa devarṣi gaṇam tuṣṭam rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ babhau rāmaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭaḥ pūjitaḥ sarva devataiḥ
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṁ pāpam avāpsyasi
english: Looking on pleasure and pain, on gain and loss, on victory and defeat as the same, prepare for battle, and thus you will not incur sin.

sanskrit: अभ्यषिच्य च लंकायाम् राक्षस इन्द्रम् विभीषणम्
कृतकृत्यः तदा रामो विज्वरः प्रमुमोद ह
transliteration: abhyaṣicya ca laṃkāyām rākṣasa indram vibhīṣaṇam
kṛtakṛtyaḥ tadā rāmo vijvaraḥ pramumoda ha
english: Then installing that foremost of Rākşasas, Vibhișana, on the throne of Lankā, Rāma was perfectly easy, and rejoiced exceedingly.

sanskrit: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु
english: The knowledge here declared to you is that relating to the Sankhya. Now hear that relating to the Yoga. Possessed of this knowledge, O son of Pritha! you will cast off the bonds of action.

sanskrit: देवताभ्यो वराम् प्राप्य समुत्थाप्य च वानरान्
अयोध्याम् प्रस्थितः रामः पुष्पकेण सुहृत् वृतः
transliteration: devatābhyo varām prāpya samutthāpya ca vānarān
ayodhyām prasthitaḥ rāmaḥ puṣpakeṇa suhṛt vṛtaḥ
english: Then Rāma, obtaining a boon from the celestials, revived the monkeys fallen in battle, and surrounded by friends, set out for Ayodhyā on the Puspaka.

transliteration: svalpam apyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
english: In this (path to final emancipation) nothing that is commenced becomes abortive; no obstacles exist; and even a little of this (form of) piety protects one from great danger.
And repairing to Bharadvāja's hermitage, Rāma, having truth for his prowess, despatched Hanuman to Bharata.
There is here O descendant of Kuru! but one state of mind consisting in firm understanding. But the states of mind of those who have no firm understanding are manifold and endless.

sanskrit: पुनः आख्यायिकाम् जल्पन् सुग्रीव सहितः तदा
पुष्पकम् तत् समारूह्य नंदिग्रामम् ययौ तदा
transliteration: punaḥ ākhyāyikām jalpan sugrīva sahitaḥ tadā
puṣpakam tat samārūhya naṃdigrāmam yayau tadā
english: Then talking over past affairs, accompanied with Sugriva, Rama, mounted on the Puspaka, and departed for Nandigrāma.

The state of mind which consists in firm understanding regarding steady contemplation does not belong to those; O son of Pritha! who are strongly attached to (worldly) pleasures and power, and whose minds are drawn away by that flowery talk which is full of (the ordinances of)

sanskrit: नंदिग्रामे जटाम् हित्वा भ्रातृभिः सहितो अनघः
रामः सीताम् अनुप्राप्य राज्यम् पुनः अवाप्तवान्
transliteration: naṃdigrāme jaṭām hitvā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito anaghaḥ
rāmaḥ sītām anuprāpya rājyam punaḥ avāptavān
english: Having arrived at Nandigrāma, the sinless Rāma sheared himself of his matted locks along with his brothers, and having regained Sītā, got back his kingdom
specific acts for the attainment of (those) pleasures and (that) power, and which promises birth as the fruit of acts (that flowery talk) which those unwise ones utter,

sanskrit: प्रहृष्टो मुदितो लोकः तुष्टः पुष्टः सुधार्मिकः
निरामयो हि अरोगः च दुर्भिक्ष भय वर्जितः
transliteration: prahṛṣṭo mudito lokaḥ tuṣṭaḥ puṣṭaḥ sudhārmikaḥ
nirāmayo hi arogaḥ ca durbhikṣa bhaya varjitaḥ
english: (During his reign) his subjects will enjoy happiness, and contentment, and become hale, and grow in righteousness, and be devoid of mental disquietude and disease, and free from the fear of famine.
who are enamoured of Vedic words, who say there is nothing, else, who are full of desires, and whose goal is heaven.

sanskrit: न पुत्र मरणम् केचित् द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुरुषाः क्वचित्
नार्यः च अविधवा नित्यम् भविष्यन्ति पति व्रताः
transliteration: na putra maraṇam kecit drakṣyanti puruṣāḥ kvacit
nāryaḥ ca avidhavā nityam bhaviṣyanti pati vratāḥ
english: Where a no person is to witness his son's death, and women will be ever chaste, and never bear widow-hood.

The Vedas (merely) relate to the effects of the three qualities; do you, O Arguna! rise above those effects of the three qualities, and be free from the pairs of opposites, always preserve courage, be free from anxiety for new acquisitions or protection of old acquisitions, and be self-controlled.

sanskrit: न च अग्निजम् भयम् किन्चित् न अप्सु मज्जन्ति जन्तवः
न वातजम् भयम् किन्चित् न अपि ज्वर कृतम् तथा
transliteration: na ca agnijam bhayam kincit na apsu majjanti jantavaḥ
na vātajam bhayam kincit na api jvara kṛtam tathā

english: To the instructed Brahmana, there is in all the Vedas as much utility as in a reservoir of water into which waters flow from all sides.

sanskrit: न च अपि क्षुत् भयम् तत्र न तस्कर भयम् तथा
नगराणि च राष्ट्राणि धन धान्य युतानि च
transliteration: na ca api kṣut bhayam tatra na taskara bhayam tathā
nagarāṇi ca rāṣṭrāṇi dhana dhānya yutāni ca
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi
english: Your business is with action alone; not by any means with fruit. Let not the fruit of action be your motive (to action). Let not your attachment be (fixed) on inaction.

sanskrit: नित्यम् प्रमुदिताः सर्वे यथा कृत युगे तथा
अश्वमेध शतैः इष्ट्वा तथा बहु सुवर्णकैः
transliteration: nityam pramuditāḥ sarve yathā kṛta yuge tathā
aśvamedha śataiḥ iṣṭvā tathā bahu suvarṇakaiḥ

sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते
transliteration: yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga uchyate
english: Having recourse to devotion, O Dhanangaya! perform actions, casting off (all) attachment, and being equable in success or ill-success; (such) equability is called devotion.

sanskrit: गवाम् कोट्ययुतम् दत्त्वा विद्वभ्यो विधि पूर्वकम्
transliteration: gavām koṭyayutam dattvā vidvabhyo vidhi pūrvakam

english: Action, O Dhanangaya! is far inferior to the devotion of the mind.

sanskrit: राज वंशान् शत गुणान् स्थाप इष्यति राघवः
चातुर् वर्ण्यम् च लोके अस्मिन् स्वे स्वे धर्मे नियोक्ष्यति
transliteration: rāja vaṃśān śata guṇān sthāpa iṣyati rāghavaḥ
cātur varṇyam ca loke asmin sve sve dharme niyokṣyati
tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśhalam
english: In that devotion seek shelterWretched are those whose motive (to action) is the fruit (of action). He who has obtained devotion in this world casts off both merit and sin. Therefore apply yourself to devotion; devotion in (all) actions is wisdom.

sanskrit: दश वर्ष सहस्राणि दश वर्ष शतानि च
रामो राज्यम् उपासित्वा ब्रह्म लोकम् प्रयास्यति
transliteration: daśa varṣa sahasrāṇi daśa varṣa śatāni ca
rāmo rājyam upāsitvā brahma lokam prayāsyati
english: And having reigned for ten thousand and as many hundred years. Rāma will depart for the regions of Brahmā.

sanskrit: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः
transliteration: karma-jaṁ buddhi-yuktā hi phalaṁ tyaktvā manīṣhiṇaḥ
english: The wise who have obtained devotion cast off the fruit of action; and released from the shackles of (repeated) births, repair to that seat where there is no unhappiness.

sanskrit: इदम् पवित्रम् पापघ्नम् पुण्यम् वेदैः च संमितम्
यः पठेत् राम चरितम् सर्व पापैः प्रमुच्यते
transliteration: idam pavitram pāpaghnam puṇyam vedaiḥ ca saṃmitam
yaḥ paṭhet rāma caritam sarva pāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: He that reads this sacred, sin-destroying, merit-bestowing history of Rāma like that of the Veda itself, becomes cleansed from all sin.

sanskrit: तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च
transliteration: tadā gantāsi nirvedaṁ śhrotavyasya śhrutasya cha
english: When your mind shall have crossed beyond the taint of delusion, then will you become indifferent to all that you have heard or will hear.

sanskrit: एतत् आख्यानम् आयुष्यम् पठन् रामायणम् नरः
स पुत्र पौत्रः स गणः प्रेत्य स्वर्गे महीयते
transliteration: etat ākhyānam āyuṣyam paṭhan rāmāyaṇam naraḥ
sa putra pautraḥ sa gaṇaḥ pretya svarge mahīyate
english: And the man that reads this Rāmāyaṇa conferring length of days, after death, is on honoured in heaven, along with his sons, and grandsons, and relations.
When your mind, that was confounded by what you have heard, will stand firm and steady in contemplation, then will you acquire devotion.

sanskrit: स्यात् क्षत्रियो भूमि पतित्वम् ईयात् ॥वणिक् जनः पण्य फलत्वम् ईयात्
जनः च शूद्रो अपि महत्त्वम् ईयात्
transliteration: syāt kṣatriyo bhūmi patitvam īyāt vaṇik janaḥ paṇya phalatvam īyāt
janaḥ ca śūdro api mahattvam īyāt
english: If a Brāhmaṇa reads it, he attains excellence in speech; if a Kșatriya, he will acquire lordship over landed possessions, if a Vaisya, abundance of wealth in trade; and if a Sudra, greatness.

sanskrit: स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्
transliteration: sthita-dhīḥ kiṁ prabhāṣheta kim āsīta vrajeta kim
english: Arguna said: What are the characteristics, O Kesava! of one whose mind is steady, and who is intent on contemplation? How should one of a steady mind speak, how sit, how move?

sanskrit: नारदस्य तु तद्वाक्यम् श्रुत्वा वाक्य विशारदः
transliteration: nāradasya tu tadvākyam śrutvā vākya viśāradaḥ
english: Hearing those words of Nārada, that one of virtuous soul, skilled in speech, together with his disciples, worshipped that great sage.

sanskrit: प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्
transliteration: prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān
english: The Deity said: When a man, O son of Pritha! abandons all the desires of his heart, and is pleased in his self only and by his self, he is then called of a steady mind.

sanskrit: यथावत् पूजितः तेन देवर्षिः नारदः तथा
transliteration: yathāvat pūjitaḥ tena devarṣiḥ nāradaḥ tathā
english: Having received due honours, that Devarși Nārada taking leave of him went to his ethereal regions.

He whose heart is not agitated in the midst of calamities, who has no longing for pleasures, and from whom (the feelings of) affection, fear, and wrath have departed, is called a sage of a steady mind.

sanskrit: स मुहूर्तं गते तस्मिन् देवलोकम् मुनिः तदा
transliteration: sa muhūrtaṃ gate tasmin devalokam muniḥ tadā
english: And when Nārada had left for the celestial regions, that holy person went to the banks of the Tamasā not very far from Jāhnavī.

sanskrit: नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
transliteration: yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śhubhāśhubham
nābhinandati na dveṣhṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
english: His mind is steady, who, being without attachments anywhere, feels no exultation and no aversion on encountering, the various agreeable and disagreeable (things of this world).

sanskrit: स तु तीरम् समासाद्य तमसाया मुनिः तदा
शिष्यम् आह स्थितम् पार्श्वे दृष्ट्वा तीर्थम् अकर्दमम्
transliteration: sa tu tīram samāsādya tamasāyā muniḥ tadā
śiṣyam āha sthitam pārśve dṛṣṭvā tīrtham akardamam
english: And having arrived at the banks of that river, the pious one, observing a holy spot devoid of mud, spoke to his disciple standing by.
A man's mind is steady, when he withdraws his senses from (all) objects of sense, as the tortoise (withdraws) its limbs from all sides.

sanskrit: रमणीयम् प्रसन्न अम्बु सन् मनुष्य मनो यथा
transliteration: ramaṇīyam prasanna ambu san manuṣya mano yathā
english: Saying-O Bharadvāja, behold this holy spot devoid of mud. And it is beautiful, and contains pleasant waters, even like the minds of good men.
Objects of sense withdraw themselves from a person who is abstinent; not so the taste (for those objects). But even the taste departs from him, when he has seen the Supreme.

sanskrit: न्यस्यताम् कलशः तात दीयताम् वल्कलम् मम
इदम् एव अवगाहिष्ये तमसा तीर्थम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: nyasyatām kalaśaḥ tāta dīyatām valkalam mama
idam eva avagāhiṣye tamasā tīrtham uttamam
english: O child, do you, put down your pitcher, and give me my bark. I will bathe even in this Tamasā, the best of holy spots.
The boisterous senses, O son of Kunti! carry away by force the mind even of a wise man, who exerts himself (for final emancipation).

sanskrit: प्रयच्छत मुनेः तस्य वल्कलम् नियतः गुरोः
transliteration: prayacchata muneḥ tasya valkalam niyataḥ guroḥ
english: Thus accosted by the high-souled Vālmīki, Bharadvāja ever intent upon serving his spiritual guide, presented the sage his bark.

sanskrit: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता
transliteration: tāni sarvāṇi sanyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ
vaśhe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
english: Restraining them, all, a man should remain engaged in devotion, making me his only resort. For his mind is steady whose senses are under his control.

sanskrit: स शिष्य हस्तात् आदाय वल्कलम् नियतेन्द्रियः
विचचार ह पश्यन् तत् सर्वतो विपुलम् वनम्
transliteration: sa śiṣya hastāt ādāya valkalam niyatendriyaḥ
vicacāra ha paśyan tat sarvato vipulam vanam
english: That one of subdued senses, having received his bark from his disciple, began to range around, surveying that extensive forest.
The man who ponders over objects of sense forms an attachment to them; from (that) attachment is produced desire; and from desire anger is produced;

sanskrit: तस्य अभ्याशे तु मिथुनम् चरन्तम् अनपायिनम्
ददर्श भगवान् तत्र क्रौङ्चयोः चारु निस्वनम्
transliteration: tasya abhyāśe tu mithunam carantam anapāyinam
dadarśa bhagavān tatra krauṅcayoḥ cāru nisvanam
english: In the vicinity of the forest, that worshipful one espied a pair of Krauñcas, emitting melodious notes, and ranging around never parting from one another.

from anger results want of discrimination; from want of discrimination, confusion of the memory; from confusion of the memory, loss of reason; and in consequence of loss of reason he is utterly ruined.integrity

sanskrit: तस्मात् तु मिथुनात् एकम् पुमांसम् पाप निश्चयः
transliteration: tasmāt tu mithunāt ekam pumāṃsam pāpa niścayaḥ
english: At this juncture, a wicked-minded fowler, singling out the male, without any cause of hostility, slew him in the very presence of the holy man.
But the self-restrained man who moves among objects with senses under the control of his own self, and free from affection and aversion, obtains tranquillity.discipline

sanskrit: भार्या तु निहतम् दृष्ट्वा रुराव करुणाम् गिरम्
transliteration: bhāryā tu nihatam dṛṣṭvā rurāva karuṇām giram
english: Observing him struggling on the earth, bathed in blood, his female companion began to bewail in piteous accents.
When there is tranquillity, all his miseries are destroyed, for the mind of him whose heart is tranquil soon becomes steady.

sanskrit: ताम्र शीर्षेण मत्तेन पत्रिणा सहितेन वै
transliteration: tāmra śīrṣeṇa mattena patriṇā sahitena vai
english: At the prospect of her separation from her copper-crested oviparous husband, engaged in sport with extended plumage.

transliteration: na chābhāvayataḥ śhāntir aśhāntasya kutaḥ sukham
english: there is no tranquillity for him who does not persevere in the pursuit of self-knowledge; and whence can there be happiness for one who is not tranquil?

sanskrit: तथा विधिम् द्विजम् दृष्ट्वा निषादेन निपातितम्
transliteration: tathā vidhim dvijam dṛṣṭvā niṣādena nipātitam
english: Finding the bird in that condition thus brought down by the fowler, the pity of that pious and righteous-souled Rși was excited exceedingly.

transliteration: tadasya harati prajñāṁ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi
english: For the heart which follows the rambling senses leads away his judgment, as the wind leads a boat astray upon the waters.

sanskrit: ततः करुण वेदित्वात् अधर्मो अयम् इति द्विजः
निशाम्य रुदतीम् क्रौन्चीम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रैइत्
transliteration: tataḥ karuṇa veditvāt adharmo ayam iti dvijaḥ
niśāmya rudatīm krauncīm idam vacanam abraiit
english: Then considering it to be an unrighteous deed, with a heart moved with pity, that twice-born one, beholding the weeping Krauñci, spoke these words.
Therefore, O you of mighty arms! his mind is steady whose senses are restrained on all sides from objects of sense.
O fowler, since you have slain one of a pair of Krauñcas, you shall never attain prosperity (respect)!

sanskrit: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः
transliteration: yā niśhā sarva-bhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti sanyamī
yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśhā paśhyato muneḥ
english: The self-restrained man is awake, when it is night for all beings; and when all beings are awake, that is the night of the right-seeing, sage.

sanskrit: तस्य एवम् ब्रुवतः चिन्ता बभूव हृदि वीक्षतः
शोकार्तेन अस्य शकुनेः किम् इदम् व्याहृतम् मया
transliteration: tasya evam bruvataḥ cintā babhūva hṛdi vīkṣataḥ
śokārtena asya śakuneḥ kim idam vyāhṛtam mayā
english: Having uttered this, he got worried within himself, What is this that I have said, afflicted with grief for the bird?

He into whom all objects of desire enter, as waters enter the ocean, which, (though) replenished, (still) keeps its position unmoved, he only obtains tranquillity; not he who desires (those) objects of desire.

sanskrit: चिन्तयन् स महाप्राज्ञः चकार मतिमान् मतिम्
शिश्यम् च एव अब्रवीत् वाक्यम् इदम् स मुनिपुङ्गवः
transliteration: cintayan sa mahāprājñaḥ cakāra matimān matim
śiśyam ca eva abravīt vākyam idam sa munipuṅgavaḥ
english: Resolving thus in his mind, that highly-wise one and best of sages addressed his disciple, saying.

transliteration: vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumānśh charati niḥspṛihaḥ
english: The man who, casting off all desires, lives free from attachments, who is free from egoism, and from (the feeling that this or that is) mine, obtains tranquillity.

sanskrit: पाद बद्धः अक्षर समः तन्त्री लय समन्वितः
शोकार्तस्य प्रवृत्तो मे श्लोको भवतु न अन्यथा
transliteration: pāda baddhaḥ akṣara samaḥ tantrī laya samanvitaḥ
śokārtasya pravṛtto me śloko bhavatu na anyathā
english: This speech that I have uttered is of equal bound with metre and accents; it has rhythm and is capable of being chanted according to measure to stringed accompaniment. Let it therefore go forth as a sloka!

sanskrit: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति
transliteration: eṣhā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati
english: This, O son of Pritha! is the Brahmic state; attaining to this, one is never deluded; and remaining in it in (one's) last moments, one attains (brahma-nirvana) the Brahmic bliss.

sanskrit: शिष्यः तु तस्य ब्रुवतो मुनेर् वाक्यम् अनुत्तमम्
प्रति जग्राह संतुष्टः तस्य तुष्टोअः अभवत् मुनिः
transliteration: śiṣyaḥ tu tasya bruvato muner vākyam anuttamam
prati jagrāha saṃtuṣṭaḥ tasya tuṣṭoaḥ abhavat muniḥ
english: When the sage had spoken thus, his disciple, well pleased, assented to his excellent speech; and thereat that pious person was gratified.

sanskrit: तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव
transliteration: jyāyasī chet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana
tat kiṁ karmaṇi ghore māṁ niyojayasi keśhava
english: Arguna said: If, O Ganardana! devotion is deemed by you to be superior to action, then why, O Kesava! do you prompt me to (this) fearful action?

sanskrit: सोऽभिषेकम् ततः कृत्वा तीर्थे तस्मिन् यथाविधि
तम् एव चिन्तयन् अर्थम् उपावर्तत वै मुनिः
transliteration: so'bhiṣekam tataḥ kṛtvā tīrthe tasmin yathāvidhi
tam eva cintayan artham upāvartata vai muniḥ
english: Then having duly performed his ablutions at that holy spot, the reverend sage retraced his steps, pondering over the incidents touching the sloka.

transliteration: tad ekaṁ vada niśhchitya yena śhreyo ’ham āpnuyām
english: You seem, indeed, to confuse my mind by equivocal words. Therefore, declare one thing determinately, by which I may attain the highest good.

sanskrit: भरद्वाजः ततः शिष्यो विनीतः श्रुतवान् गुरोः
transliteration: bharadvājaḥ tataḥ śiṣyo vinītaḥ śrutavān guroḥ
english: His disciple also, accomplished in learning, and of meek demeanour, followed Vālmīki, carrying on his back a pitcher filled with water.

transliteration: loke’smin dvi-vidhā niṣhṭhā purā proktā mayānagha
english: The Deity said: O sinless one! I have already declared, that in this world there is a twofold path that of the Sankhyas by devotion in the shape of (true) knowledge; and that of the Yogins by devotion in the shape of action.

sanskrit: स प्रविश्य आश्रम पदम् शिष्येण सह धर्मवित्
उपविष्टः कथाः च अन्याः चकार ध्यानमास्थितः
transliteration: sa praviśya āśrama padam śiṣyeṇa saha dharmavit
upaviṣṭaḥ kathāḥ ca anyāḥ cakāra dhyānamāsthitaḥ
english: Having entered the hermitage along with his disciple, conversant with righteousness engaged in diverse kinds of talk, revolved in his mind the circumstances connected with the verses.

transliteration: na cha sannyasanād eva siddhiṁ samadhigachchhati
english: A man does not attain freedom from action, merely by not engaging in action; nor does he attain perfection by mere renunciation.

sanskrit: आजगाम ततः ब्रह्मो लोककर्ता स्वयम् प्रभुः
चतुर् मुखो महातेजा द्रष्टुम् तम् मुनिपुङ्गवम्
transliteration: ājagāma tataḥ brahmo lokakartā svayam prabhuḥ
catur mukho mahātejā draṣṭum tam munipuṅgavam
english: It came to pass that desirous of seeing the best of sages, there arrived, that lord and creator of all, the effulgent Brahmā, furnished with four countenances.

transliteration: na hi kaśhchit kṣhaṇam api jātu tiṣhṭhatyakarma-kṛit
kāryate hyavaśhaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛiti-jair guṇaiḥ
english: For nobody ever remains even for an instant without performing some action; since the qualities of nature constrain everybody, not having free-will (in the matter), to some action.

sanskrit: वाल्मीकिः अथ तम् दृष्ट्वा सहसा उत्थाय वाग्यतः
प्रान्जलिः प्रयतो भूत्वा तस्थौ परम विस्मितः
transliteration: vālmīkiḥ atha tam dṛṣṭvā sahasā utthāya vāgyataḥ
prānjaliḥ prayato bhūtvā tasthau parama vismitaḥ
english: Beholding him Vālmīki rose up suddenly and, wondering greatly, humbly and silently stood before him with clasped hands.

sanskrit: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्
transliteration: karmendriyāṇi sanyamya ya āste manasā smaran
english: The deluded man who restraining the organs of action, continues to think in his mind about objects of sense, is called a hypocrite.

sanskrit: पूजयामास तम् देवम् पाद्य अर्घ्य आसन वन्दनैः
प्रणम्य विधिवत् च एनम् पृष्ट्वा च एव निरामयम्
transliteration: pūjayāmāsa tam devam pādya arghya āsana vandanaiḥ
praṇamya vidhivat ca enam pṛṣṭvā ca eva nirāmayam
english: And duly bending low in reverence, Vālmīki offered that deity water to wash his feet, and other things for reception.
But he, O Arguna! who restraining his senses by his mind, and being free from attachments, engages in devotion (in the shape) of action, with the organs of action, is far superior.

sanskrit: अथ उपविश्य भगवान् आसने परम अर्चिते
वाल्मीकये च ऋषये सन्दिदेश आसनम् ततः
transliteration: atha upaviśya bhagavān āsane parama arcite
vālmīkaye ca ṛṣaye sandideśa āsanam tataḥ
english: Having sat-down on a highly-honoured seat, that worshipful one enquired after the welfare of that sage Vālmīki knowing no deterioration, and then asked him to be seated.

sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः
transliteration: niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ
śharīra-yātrāpi cha te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ
english: Do you perform prescribed action, for action is better than inaction, and the support of your body, too, cannot be accomplished with inaction.

sanskrit: उपविष्टे तदा तस्मिन् साक्षात् लोक पितामहे
transliteration: upaviṣṭe tadā tasmin sākṣāt loka pitāmahe

english: This world is fettered by all action other than action for the purpose of the sacrifice. Therefore, O son of Kunti! do you, casting off attachment, perform action for that purpose.

sanskrit: तत् गतेन एव मनसा वाल्मीकिः ध्यानम् आस्थितः
पापात्मना कृतम् कष्टम् वैर ग्रहण बुद्धिना
transliteration: tat gatena eva manasā vālmīkiḥ dhyānam āsthitaḥ
pāpātmanā kṛtam kaṣṭam vaira grahaṇa buddhinā

english: The Creator, having in olden times created men together with the sacrifice, said 'Propagate with this. May it be the giver to you of the things you desire.

sanskrit: यत् तादृशम् चारुरवम् क्रौन्चम् हन्यात् अकारणात्
शोचन् एव पुनः क्रौन्चीम् उप श्लोकम् इमम् जगौ
transliteration: yat tādṛśam cāruravam krauncam hanyāt akāraṇāt
śocan eva punaḥ krauncīm upa ślokam imam jagau
devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ
english: Please the gods with this, and may those gods please you. Pleasing each other, you will attain the highest good.

sanskrit: पुनर् अन्तर्गत मना भूत्वा शोक परायणः
तम् उवाच ततो ब्रह्मा प्रहसन् मुनिपुंगवम्
transliteration: punar antargata manā bhūtvā śoka parāyaṇaḥ
tam uvāca tato brahmā prahasan munipuṃgavam
english: Then smiling, Brahmā spoke to the excellent sage,-Those verses of your which you have composed a sloka shall attain celebrity: no doubt need be entertained on this head, It is because I had intended so, that those verses had come out of your lips.

sanskrit: तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः
transliteration: iṣhṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ
tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
english: For pleased with the sacrifices, the gods will give you the enjoyments you desire. And he who enjoys himself without giving them what they have given, is, indeed, a thief.'

sanskrit: श्लोक एवास्त्वयाम् बद्धो न अत्र कार्या विचारणा
मत् च्छन्दात् एव ते ब्रह्मन् प्रवृत्ते अयम् सरस्वती
transliteration: śloka evāstvayām baddho na atra kāryā vicāraṇā
mat cchandāt eva te brahman pravṛtte ayam sarasvatī
english: Then smiling, Brahmā spoke to the excellent sage,-Those verses of your which you have composed a sloka shall attain celebrity: no doubt need be entertained on this head, It is because I had intended so, that those verses had come out of your lips.

sanskrit: भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्
transliteration: bhuñjate te tvaghaṁ pāpā ye pachantyātma-kāraṇāt
english: The good, who eat the leavings of a sacrifice, are released from all sins. But the unrighteous ones, who prepare food for themselves only, incur sin.

sanskrit: रामस्य चरितम् कृत्स्नम् कुरु त्वम् ऋषिसत्तम
transliteration: rāmasya caritam kṛtsnam kuru tvam ṛṣisattama
english: Do you now, O best of saints, compose the entire history of Rāma. Do you relate to the world the history of the righteous-souled and intelligent Rāma crowned with qualities. And do you, as you have heard it from Närada.
From food are born (all) creatures; from rain is the production of food; rain is produced by sacrifices; sacrifices are the result of action;

sanskrit: वृत्तम् कथय धीरस्य यथा ते नारदात् श्रुतम्
रहस्यम् च प्रकाशम् च यद् वृत्तम् तस्य धीमतः
transliteration: vṛttam kathaya dhīrasya yathā te nāradāt śrutam
rahasyam ca prakāśam ca yad vṛttam tasya dhīmataḥ
tasmāt sarva-gataṁ brahma nityaṁ yajñe pratiṣhṭhitam
english: know that action has its source in the Vedas; the Vedas come from the Indestructible. Therefore the all-comprehending Vedas are always concerned with sacrifices.

sanskrit: रामस्य सह सौमित्रे राक्षसानाम् च सर्वशः
वैदेह्याः च एव यद् वृत्तम् प्रकाशम् यदि वा रहः
transliteration: rāmasya saha saumitre rākṣasānām ca sarvaśaḥ
vaidehyāḥ ca eva yad vṛttam prakāśam yadi vā rahaḥ
english: Relate all what is known, and all what is unknown to the world, O wise one, concerning Rāma, and Laksmana, and Videha's daughter, and all the Rākşasas. And even what is not known to Nārada, shall be unfolded to you.

transliteration: aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati
english: He who in this world does not turn round the wheel revolving thus, is of sinful life, indulging his senses, and, O son of Pritha! lie lives in vain.

sanskrit: तत् च अपि अविदितम् सर्वम् विदितम् ते भविष्यति
न ते वाक् अनृता काव्ये काचित् अत्र भविष्यति
transliteration: tat ca api aviditam sarvam viditam te bhaviṣyati
na te vāk anṛtā kāvye kācit atra bhaviṣyati

sanskrit: आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते
transliteration: yas tvātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛiptaśh cha mānavaḥ
ātmanyeva cha santuṣhṭas tasya kāryaṁ na vidyate
english: But the man who is attached to his self only, who is contented in his self, and is pleased with his self, has nothing to do.

sanskrit: कुरु राम कथाम् पुण्याम् श्लोक बद्धाम् मनोरमाम्
यावत् स्थास्यन्ति गिरयः सरितः च महीतले
transliteration: kuru rāma kathām puṇyām śloka baddhām manoramām
yāvat sthāsyanti girayaḥ saritaḥ ca mahītale

english: He has no interest at all in what is done, and none whatever in what is not done, in this world; nor is any interest of his dependent on any being.

sanskrit: यावत् रामस्य च कथा त्वत् कृता प्रचरिष्यति
transliteration: yāvat rāmasya ca kathā tvat kṛtā pracariṣyati
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samāchara
asakto hyācharan karma param āpnoti pūruṣhaḥ
english: Therefore always perform action, which must be performed, without attachment. For a man, performing action without attachment, attains the Supreme.

sanskrit: तावत् ऊर्ध्वम् अधः च त्वम् मत् लोकेषु निवत्स्यसि
इति उक्त्वा भगवान् ब्रह्मा तत्र एव अन्तरधीयत
ततः स शिष्यो भगवान् मुनिः विस्मयम् आययौ
transliteration: tāvat ūrdhvam adhaḥ ca tvam mat lokeṣu nivatsyasi
iti uktvā bhagavān brahmā tatra eva antaradhīyata
tataḥ sa śiṣyo bhagavān muniḥ vismayam āyayau
english: Having said this, the Lord Brahmä disappeared there. And thereat the sage and his disciples marvelled greatly.
By action alone, did Ganaka and the rest work for perfection. And having regard also to the keeping of people (to their duties) you should perform action.

sanskrit: तस्य शिष्याः ततः सर्वे जगुः श्लोकम् इमम् पुनः
मुहुर् मुहुः प्रीयमाणाः प्राहुः च भृश विस्मिताः
transliteration: tasya śiṣyāḥ tataḥ sarve jaguḥ ślokam imam punaḥ
muhur muhuḥ prīyamāṇāḥ prāhuḥ ca bhṛśa vismitāḥ
english: His disciples sang those verses again and again; and, momentarily experiencing pleasure, recited it with exceeding wonder.

transliteration: yad yad ācharati śhreṣhṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate
english: Whatever a great man does, that other men also do. And people follow whatever he receives as authority.

sanskrit: समाक्षरैः चतुर्भिः यः पादैः गीतो महर्षिणा
सः अनुव्याहरणात् भूयः शोकः श्लोकत्वम् आगतः
transliteration: samākṣaraiḥ caturbhiḥ yaḥ pādaiḥ gīto maharṣiṇā
saḥ anuvyāharaṇāt bhūyaḥ śokaḥ ślokatvam āgataḥ
english: Those verses, composed of equal accents, and furnished with four parts, have been sung by the great saint, have, in virtue of frequent repetition, been associated with a world of pathos and have attained the eminence of a sloka.

sanskrit: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन
transliteration: na me pārthāsti kartavyaṁ triṣhu lokeṣhu kiñchana
nānavāptam avāptavyaṁ varta eva cha karmaṇi
english: There is nothing, O son of Pritha! for me to do in (all) the three worlds, nothing to acquire which has not been acquired. Still I do engage in action.

sanskrit: तस्य बुद्धिः इयम् जाता महर्षेः भावितात्मनः
transliteration: tasya buddhiḥ iyam jātā maharṣeḥ bhāvitātmanaḥ
english: Now it is the intention of that illustrious and self-centred sage to compose the entire Rāmāyaṇa in this metre.

sanskrit: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः
transliteration: yadi hyahaṁ na varteyaṁ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ
english: For should I at any time not engage without sloth in action, men would follow in my path from all sides, O son of Pritha!

sanskrit: उदार वृत्त अर्थ पदैः मनोरमैःतदा अस्य रामस्य चकार कीर्तिमान्
सम अक्षरैः श्लोक शतैः यशस्विनोयशस्करम् काव्यम् उदार दर्शनः
transliteration: udāra vṛtta artha padaiḥ manoramaiḥtadā asya rāmasya cakāra kīrtimān
sama akṣaraiḥ śloka śataiḥ yaśasvinoyaśaskaram kāvyam udāra darśanaḥ
english: The great ascetic Vālmīki of gracious appearance and unparalleled renown composed a poetry consisting of hundreds of verses in melodious measure, couching the significance of the history of Rāma.

sanskrit: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्
transliteration: utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṁ karma ched aham
sankarasya cha kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ
english: If I did not perform actions, these worlds would be destroyed, I should be the cause of casteinterminglings; and I should be ruining these people.

sanskrit: तद् उपगत समास सन्धि योगम्सम मधुरोपनत अर्थ वाक्य बद्धम्
रघुवर चरितम् मुनिप्रणीतम्दश शिरसः च वधम् निशामय अध्वम्
transliteration: tad upagata samāsa sandhi yogamsama madhuropanata artha vākya baddham
raghuvara caritam munipraṇītamdaśa śirasaḥ ca vadham niśāmaya adhvam
english: Listen to the annals of the foremost of Raghu's race, and the destruction of the Tenheaded one composed by the ascetic, with Samāsas, Sandhis, Prakrtis, and Pratayas; and lucid with sweet and equally-accented words.
As the ignorant act, O descendant of Bharata! with attachment to action, so should a wise man act without attachment, wishing to keep the people (to their duties).

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा वस्तु समग्रम् तत् धर्म अर्ध सहितम् हितम्
व्यक्तम् अन्वेषते भूयो यद्वृत्तम् तस्य धीमतः ॥१-३-१
transliteration: śrutvā vastu samagram tat dharma ardha sahitam hitam
vyaktam anveṣate bhūyo yadvṛttam tasya dhīmataḥ 1-3-1
english: Having heard the entire prevalent history of the intelligent Rāma, capable of conferring religious merit and the two other cognate objects, as well as emancipation, Vālmīki again sought to get insight into it.
A wise man should not shake the convictions of the ignorant who are attached to action, but acting with devotion (himself) should make them apply themselves to all action.

sanskrit: उपस्पृस्य उदकम् सम्यक् मुनिः स्थित्वा कृताञ्जलिः
प्राचीन अग्रेषु दर्भेषु धर्मेण अन्वेषते गतिम् ॥१-३-२
transliteration: upaspṛsya udakam samyak muniḥ sthitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ
prācīna agreṣu darbheṣu dharmeṇa anveṣate gatim 1-3-2
english: And, sitting himself facing the east on a cushion of kuća grass, and sipping water according to the ordinance, he addressed himself to the contemplation of the subject through Yoga.
He whose mind is deluded by egoism thinks himself the doer of the actions, which, in every way, are done by the qualities of nature.

sanskrit: राम लक्ष्मण सीताभिः राज्ञा दशरथेन च
स भार्येण स राष्ट्रेण यत् प्राप्तम् तत्र तत्त्वतः ॥१-३-३
transliteration: rāma lakṣmaṇa sītābhiḥ rājñā daśarathena ca
sa bhāryeṇa sa rāṣṭreṇa yat prāptam tatra tattvataḥ 1-3-3
english: And by virtue of his Yoga powers, he clearly observed before him Rāma, and Lakşmana, and Sītá, and Dasaratha together with his wives in his kingdom, laughing, and talking, and acting, and bearing themselves as in real life.

sanskrit: गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते
transliteration: guṇā guṇeṣhu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
english: But he, O you of mighty arms! who knows the truth about the difference from qualities and the difference from actions, forms no attachments, believing that qualities deal with qualities.

sanskrit: हसितम् भाषितम् च एव गतिर्यायत् च चेष्टितम्
तत् सर्वम् धर्म वीर्येण यथावत् संप्रपश्यति ॥१-३-४
transliteration: hasitam bhāṣitam ca eva gatiryāyat ca ceṣṭitam
tat sarvam dharma vīryeṇa yathāvat saṃprapaśyati 1-3-4
english: And by virtue of his Yoga powers, he clearly observed before him Rāma, and Lakşmana, and Sītá, and Dasaratha together with his wives in his kingdom, laughing, and talking, and acting, and bearing themselves as in real life.

transliteration: tān akṛitsna-vido mandān kṛitsna-vin na vichālayet
english: But those who are deluded by the qualities of nature form attachments to the actions of the qualities. A man of perfect knowledge should not shake these men of imperfect knowledge (in their convictions).

sanskrit: स्त्री तृतीयेन च तथा यत् प्राप्तम् चरता वने
transliteration: strī tṛtīyena ca tathā yat prāptam caratā vane
english: He also saw all that was endured by Rāma firm in promise, with his wife as the third accompanist roaming in the forest

Dedicating all actions to me with a mind knowing the relation of the supreme and individual self, engage in battle without desire, without (any feeling that this or that is) mine, and without any mental trouble.

sanskrit: ततः पश्यति धर्मात्मा तत् सर्वम् योगमास्थितः
पुरा यत् तत्र निर्वृत्तम् पाणाव आमलकम् यथा ॥१-३-६
transliteration: tataḥ paśyati dharmātmā tat sarvam yogamāsthitaḥ
purā yat tatra nirvṛttam pāṇāva āmalakam yathā 1-3-6
english: And like an embolic myrobalan on his palm, that righteous-souled sage by virtue of his yoga, perceived all that had happened as well as all that would happen in the past.

transliteration: ye me matam idaṁ nityam anutiṣhṭhanti mānavāḥ
english: Even those men who always act on this opinion of mine, full of faith, and without carping, are released from all actions.

sanskrit: तत् सर्वम् तात्त्वतो दृश्ट्वा धर्मेण स महामतिःअभिरामस्य रामस्य तत् सर्वम् कर्तुम् उद्यतः ॥१-३-७
transliteration: tat sarvam tāttvato dṛśṭvā dharmeṇa sa mahāmatiḥabhirāmasya rāmasya tat sarvam kartum udyataḥ 1-3-7
