english: Having truly seen everything by virtue of his contemplation, that magnanimous one set about recording the charming Rāma's history.

transliteration: ye tvetad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣhṭhanti me matam
english: But those who carp at my opinion and do not act upon it, know them to be devoid of discrimination, deluded as regards all knowledge, and ruined.

sanskrit: कामार्थ गुण संयुक्तम् धर्मार्थ गुण विस्तरम्
समुद्रम् इव रत्नाढ्यम् सर्व श्रुति मनोहरम् ॥१-३-८
transliteration: kāmārtha guṇa saṃyuktam dharmārtha guṇa vistaram
samudram iva ratnāḍhyam sarva śruti manoharam 1-3-8
english: And agreeably to what had been related by the . mighty-souled Nārada, that worshipful saint composed the history of Raghu's line, conferring profit and pleasure, and impregnated with qualities fraught with them, and like to the ocean, abounding in riches, and captivating ear and mind.

sanskrit: प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति
transliteration: sadṛiśhaṁ cheṣhṭate svasyāḥ prakṛiter jñānavān api
prakṛitiṁ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṁ kariṣhyati
english: Even a man of knowledge acts consonantly to his own nature. All beings follow nature. What will restraint effect?

sanskrit: स यथा कथितम् पूर्वम् नारदेन महात्मना
रघु वंशस्य चरितम् चकार भगवान् मुनिः ॥१-३-९
transliteration: sa yathā kathitam pūrvam nāradena mahātmanā
raghu vaṃśasya caritam cakāra bhagavān muniḥ 1-3-9
english: And agreeably to what had been related by the . mighty-souled Nārada, that worshipful saint composed the history of Raghu's line, conferring profit and pleasure, and impregnated with qualities fraught with them, and like to the ocean, abounding in riches, and captivating ear and mind.

transliteration: tayor na vaśham āgachchhet tau hyasya paripanthinau
english: Every sense has its affections and aversions towards its-objects fixed. One should not become subject to them, for they are one's opponents.

sanskrit: लोकस्य प्रियताम् क्षान्तिम् सौम्यताम् सत्य शीलताम् ॥१-३-१०
transliteration: lokasya priyatām kṣāntim saumyatām satya śīlatām 1-3-10
english: Rama's birth, his mighty prowess, and kindness to all, and popularity, and forbearance, and goodness, and truthfulness.
One's own duty, though defective, is better than another's duty well performed. Death in (performing) one's own duty is preferable ; the (performance of the) duty of others is dangerous.

sanskrit: नाना चित्र कथाः च अन्याः विश्वामित्र सहायेन
जानक्याः च विवाहम् च धनुषः च विभेदनम् ॥१-३-११
transliteration: nānā citra kathāḥ ca anyāḥ viśvāmitra sahāyena
jānakyāḥ ca vivāham ca dhanuṣaḥ ca vibhedanam 1-3-11

sanskrit: अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः
transliteration: atha kena prayukto ’yaṁ pāpaṁ charati pūruṣhaḥ
anichchhann api vārṣhṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ
english: Arguna said: But by whom, O descendant of Vrishni! is man impelled, even though unwilling and, as it were, constrained by force, to commit sin?

sanskrit: राम राम विवादम् च गुणान् दाशरथेः तथा
transliteration: rāma rāma vivādam ca guṇān dāśaratheḥ tathā

english: The Deity said: It is desire, it is wrath, born from the quality of passion; it is very ravenous, very sinful. Know that that is the foe in this world.

sanskrit: राज्ञः शोकम् विलापम् च पर लोकस्य च आश्रयम् ॥१-३-१३
transliteration: rājñaḥ śokam vilāpam ca para lokasya ca āśrayam 1-3-13

english: As fire is enveloped by smoke, a mirror by dust, the foetus by the womb, so is this enveloped by desire.
Knowledge, O son of Kunti! is enveloped by this constant foe of the man of knowledge, in the shape of desire, which is like a fire and insatiable.

sanskrit: गङ्गायाः च अपि संतारम् भरद्वाजस्य दर्शनम्
transliteration: gaṅgāyāḥ ca api saṃtāram bharadvājasya darśanam
english: And the swimming of the Gangā and Rāma sinter view with Bharadvāja; and his arrival at Citrakūta in consonance with Bharadvāja's injunction.
The senses, the mind, and the understanding are said to be its seat; with these it deludes the embodied (self) after enveloping knowledge.

sanskrit: वास्तु कर्म निवेशम् च भरत अगमनम् तथा
प्रसादनम् च रामस्य पितुः च सलिल क्रियाम् ॥१-३-१६
transliteration: vāstu karma niveśam ca bharata agamanam tathā
prasādanam ca rāmasya pituḥ ca salila kriyām 1-3-16
english: And Rāma's building a mansion there and sojourn; and Bharata's arrival, and his propitiation of Rāma; and Rāma's offering oblations to the manes of his father.
Therefore 'O chief of the descendants of Bharata! first restrain your senses, then cast off this sinful thing which destroys knowledge and experience.

sanskrit: पादुका अग्र्य अभिषेकम् च नन्दि ग्राम निवासनम्
transliteration: pādukā agrya abhiṣekam ca nandi grāma nivāsanam
english: And the installation of the sandals; and Bharata's dwelling at Nandigrāma: and Rāma's removal to Dandaka and killing of Virādha.

sanskrit: मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः
transliteration: manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ
english: It has been said, Great are the senses, greater than the senses is the mind, greater than the mind is the understanding. What is greater than the understanding is that.

sanskrit: अनसूया समाख्या च अङ्गराग्स्य च अर्पणम् ॥१-३-१८
transliteration: anasūyā samākhyā ca aṅgarāgsya ca arpaṇam 1-3-18
english: And Rāma's interview with Sarabhanga and meeting with Sutiksna; and Sita's companionship with Anasūyā, and the latter's painting the former.

transliteration: evaṁ buddheḥ paraṁ buddhvā sanstabhyātmānam ātmanā
english: Thus knowing that which is higher than the understanding, and restraining (your)self by (your)self, O you of mighty arms! destroy this unmanageable enemy in the shape of desire.

sanskrit: दर्शनम् च अपि अगस्त्यस्य धनुषो ग्रहणम् तथा
transliteration: darśanam ca api agastyasya dhanuṣo grahaṇam tathā
english: And Rāma's interview with Agastya, and his obtaining the bow from him; and the dialogue of Śūrpanakha and her disfigurement.

transliteration: imaṁ vivasvate yogaṁ proktavān aham avyayam
english: The Deity said: This everlasting (system of) devotion I declared to the sun, the sun declared it to Manu, and Manu communicated it to Ikshvaku.

sanskrit: वधम् खरः त्रिशिरसः उत्थानम् रावणस्य च
मारीचस्य वधम् च एव वैदेह्या हरणम् तथा ॥१-३-२०
transliteration: vadham kharaḥ triśirasaḥ utthānam rāvaṇasya ca
mārīcasya vadham ca eva vaidehyā haraṇam tathā 1-3-20
english: And the slaughter of Khara and Trisiras; and the exertions of Rāvana; the killing of Mārīca, and the carrying away of Vaidehī.

sanskrit: स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप
transliteration: sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣhṭaḥ parantapa
english: Coming thus by steps, it became known to royal sages. But, O terror of (your) foes! that devotion was lost to the world by long (lapse of) time.

sanskrit: राघवस्य विलापम् च गृध्र राज निबर्हणम्
कबन्ध दर्शनम् च एव पम्पायाः च अपि दर्शनम् ॥१-३-२१
transliteration: rāghavasya vilāpam ca gṛdhra rāja nibarhaṇam
kabandha darśanam ca eva pampāyāḥ ca api darśanam 1-3-21
english: Rāghava's lamentations, and the death of the king of vultures; Rāma's encounter with Kabandha, and his view of Pampā.

sanskrit: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम्
transliteration: sa evāyaṁ mayā te ’dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ
bhakto ’si me sakhā cheti rahasyaṁ hyetad uttamam
english: That same primeval devotion I have declared to you to-day, seeing that you are my devotee and friend, for it is the highest mystery.

sanskrit: शबरी दर्शनम् च एव फल मूल अशनम् तथा
प्रलापम् च एव पम्पायम् हनुमद् दर्शनम् ॥१-३-२२
transliteration: śabarī darśanam ca eva phala mūla aśanam tathā
pralāpam ca eva pampāyam hanumad darśanam 1-3-22
english: Rāma's interview with Śabarī, and his subsistence there on fruits and roots; Rāma's lamentations at Pampā, and meeting with Hanumān.

sanskrit: अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः
transliteration: aparaṁ bhavato janma paraṁ janma vivasvataḥ
katham etad vijānīyāṁ tvam ādau proktavān iti
english: Arguna said: Later is your birth; the birth of the sun is priorHow then shall I understand that you declared (this) first?
The former's sojourn to the Rşyamūka, and meeting with Sugrīva; Rāma's raising the confidence of Sugrīva and his friendship with the latter; and the encounter between Vāli and Sugriva.

sanskrit: बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप
transliteration: bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava chārjuna
tānyahaṁ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṁ vettha parantapa
english: The Deity said: I have passed through many births, O Arguna! and you also. I know them all, but you, O terror of (your) foes! do not know them.

sanskrit: वालि प्रमथनम् च एव सुगीव प्रतिपादनम्
तारा विलापम् समयम् वर्ष रात्र निवासनम् ॥१-३-२४
transliteration: vāli pramathanam ca eva sugīva pratipādanam
tārā vilāpam samayam varṣa rātra nivāsanam 1-3-24
english: The destruction of Vâli, and the installation of Sugrīva and Tara's lamentations%3B the understanding between Rāma and Sugrīva as to the time for commencing the march. Rāma's stay at the wet night, and the ire of Rama the lion of Raghu's race; the levying of forces; and the despatch of envoys in deferent directions; and the assignment by Sugrīva of different quarters to the monkeys.
Even though I am unborn and inexhaustible in (my) essence, even though I am lord of all beings, still I take up the control of my own nature, and am born by means of my delusive power.

sanskrit: दिशः प्रस्थापनम् च एव पृथिव्याः च निवेदनम् ॥१-३-२५
transliteration: diśaḥ prasthāpanam ca eva pṛthivyāḥ ca nivedanam 1-3-25
english: The destruction of Vâli, and the installation of Sugrīva and Tara's lamentations%3B the understanding between Rāma and Sugrīva as to the time for commencing the march. Rāma's stay at the wet night, and the ire of Rama the lion of Raghu's race; the levying of forces; and the despatch of envoys in deferent directions; and the assignment by Sugrīva of different quarters to the monkeys.

sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत
transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata
english: Whensoever, O descendant of Bharata! piety languishes, and impiety is in the ascendant, I create myself.

sanskrit: अङ्गुलीयक दानम् च ऋक्ष्स्य बिल दर्शनम्
प्रायोपवेशनम् च अपि संपातेः च अपि दर्शनम् ॥१-३-२६
transliteration: aṅgulīyaka dānam ca ṛkṣsya bila darśanam
prāyopaveśanam ca api saṃpāteḥ ca api darśanam 1-3-26
english: The making over of his ring by Rāma to Hanuman; Rksa's discovery of the cave. The abstemious abode of the monkeys on the shore of the ocean; Hanuman's interview with Sampāti.
I am born age after age, for the protection of the good, for the destruction of evil-doers, and the establishment of piety.

sanskrit: पर्वत आरोहणम् च अपि सागर्स्य अपि लङ्घनम्
समुद्र वचनात् च एव मैनाकस्य च दर्शनम् ॥१-३-२७
transliteration: parvata ārohaṇam ca api sāgarsya api laṅghanam
samudra vacanāt ca eva mainākasya ca darśanam 1-3-27
english: Hanuman's ascension of the mountain, and his bounding over the main; and his sight of the Maināka at the injunction of Ocean; the roaring of Raksasis; Hanuman's meeting with the Rākşasa Chāyāgrāha. Hanumān's destruction of Simhikāyā; and Hanuman's sight of Lankā.

sanskrit: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन
transliteration: janma karma cha me divyam evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ
tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so ’rjuna
english: Whoever truly knows thus my divine birth and work, casts off (this) body and is not born again. He comes to me, O Arguna!

sanskrit: राक्षसी तर्जनम् च एव छाया ग्राहस्य दर्शनम्
सिंहिकायाः च निधनम् लङ्का मलय दर्शनम् ॥१-३-२८
transliteration: rākṣasī tarjanam ca eva chāyā grāhasya darśanam
siṃhikāyāḥ ca nidhanam laṅkā malaya darśanam 1-3-28
english: Hanuman's ascension of the mountain, and his bounding over the main; and his sight of the Maināka at the injunction of Ocean; the roaring of Raksasis; Hanuman's meeting with the Rākşasa Chāyāgrāha. Hanumān's destruction of Simhikāyā; and Hanuman's sight of Lankā.
Many from, whom affection, fear, and wrath have departed, who are full of me, who depend on me, and who are purified by the penance of knowledge, have come into my essence.

sanskrit: रात्रौ लंका प्रवेशम् च एकस्य अपि विचिंतनम्
transliteration: rātrau laṃkā praveśam ca ekasya api viciṃtanam
english: His entrance by night into Lankā; his ascertaining of conduct in times of helplessness; his journey to the Āpāna ground; and his sight of his car Puşpaka; his walk to the Asoka forest, and sight there of Şītā.

sanskrit: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्
transliteration: ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāns tathaiva bhajāmyaham
english: I serve men in the way in which they approach me. In every way, O son of Pritha! men follow in my path.

sanskrit: दर्शनम् रावणस्य अपि पुष्पकस्य च दर्शनम्
अशोक वनिकायानम् सीतायाः च अपि दर्शनम् ॥१-३-३०
transliteration: darśanam rāvaṇasya api puṣpakasya ca darśanam
aśoka vanikāyānam sītāyāḥ ca api darśanam 1-3-30
english: His entrance by night into Lankā; his ascertaining of conduct in times of helplessness; his journey to the Āpāna ground; and his sight of his car Puşpaka; his walk to the Asoka forest, and sight there of Şītā.

sanskrit: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा
transliteration: kāṅkṣhantaḥ karmaṇāṁ siddhiṁ yajanta iha devatāḥ
kṣhipraṁ hi mānuṣhe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā
english: Desiring the success of actions, men in this world worship the divinities, for in this world of mortals, the success produced by action is soon obtained.

sanskrit: अभिज्ञन प्रदानम् च सीतायाः च अपि भाषणम्
राक्षसी तर्जनम् च एव त्रिजटा स्वप्न दर्शनम् ॥१-३-३१
transliteration: abhijñana pradānam ca sītāyāḥ ca api bhāṣaṇam
rākṣasī tarjanam ca eva trijaṭā svapna darśanam 1-3-31
english: His presentation of the ring to Sītā and converse with her; and the roaring of the Rākṣasis; and the dreaming of the dream by Trijatā.

transliteration: tasya kartāram api māṁ viddhyakartāram avyayam
english: The fourfold division of castes was created by me according to the apportionment of qualities and duties. But though I am its author, know me to be inexhaustible, and not the author.

sanskrit: मणि प्रदानम् सीतायाः वृक्ष भंगम् तथ एव च
transliteration: maṇi pradānam sītāyāḥ vṛkṣa bhaṃgam tatha eva ca
english: Sīta's handing a gem to Hanumān; and the breaking down of trees; and the fight of the Rakasasis, and the slaughter of the salves.

sanskrit: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते
transliteration: na māṁ karmāṇi limpanti na me karma-phale spṛihā
iti māṁ yo ’bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate
english: Actions defile me notI have no attachment to the fruit of actions. He who knows me thus is not tied down by actions.

sanskrit: ग्रहणम् वायु सूनोश्च लंका दाह अभिगर्जनम्
प्रति प्लवनम् एव अथ मधूनाम् हरणम् तथा ॥१-३-३३
transliteration: grahaṇam vāyu sūnośca laṃkā dāha abhigarjanam
prati plavanam eva atha madhūnām haraṇam tathā 1-3-33
english: The wind-god's son being taken captive; and his terrible roars while burning down Lankā; and his bounding back over the ocean; and the forcible possession of honey.

sanskrit: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम्
transliteration: evaṁ jñātvā kṛitaṁ karma pūrvair api mumukṣhubhiḥ
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṁ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṁ kṛitam
english: Knowing this, the men of old who wished for final emancipation, performed action. Therefore do you, too, perform action as was done by men of old in olden times.

sanskrit: राघव आस्वासनम् चैव मणि निर्यातनम् तथा
संगमम् च समुद्रेण नल सेतोः च बन्धनम् ॥१-३-३४
transliteration: rāghava āsvāsanam caiva maṇi niryātanam tathā
saṃgamam ca samudreṇa nala setoḥ ca bandhanam 1-3-34
english: Hanumān's consoling Rāghava, and handing him the gem; Rāma's interview with ocean; and Nala's constructing the bridge.

transliteration: kiṁ karma kim akarmeti kavayo ’pyatra mohitāḥ
tat te karma pravakṣhyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣhyase ’śhubhāt
english: Even sages are confused as to what is action, what inaction. Therefore I will speak to you about action, and learning that, you will be freed from (this world of) evil.

sanskrit: प्रतारम् च समुद्रस्य रात्रौ लंका अवरोधनम्
transliteration: pratāram ca samudrasya rātrau laṃkā avarodhanam
english: The army's crossing of the ocean; and the nightly siege of Lankā; and Rāma, interview with Bibhishana; the communication as to the means of destruction.

sanskrit: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः
transliteration: karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṁ boddhavyaṁ cha vikarmaṇaḥ
akarmaṇaśh cha boddhavyaṁ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ
english: One must possess knowledge about action; one must also possess knowledge about prohibited action; and again one must possess knowledge about inaction. The truth regarding action is abstruse.

sanskrit: रावणस्य विनाशम् च सीतावाप्तिम् अरेः पुरे ॥१-३-३६
transliteration: rāvaṇasya vināśam ca sītāvāptim areḥ pure 1-3-36
english: And the killing of Kumbhakarna and Meghanāda; and the destruction of Răvaņa, and the recovery of Sītā in the enemy's city.

sanskrit: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः
स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्
transliteration: karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśhyed akarmaṇi cha karma yaḥ
sa buddhimān manuṣhyeṣhu sa yuktaḥ kṛitsna-karma-kṛit
english: He is wise among men, he is possessed of devotion, and performs all actions, who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction.

sanskrit: विभीषण अभिषेकम् च पुष्पकस्य च दर्शनम्
transliteration: vibhīṣaṇa abhiṣekam ca puṣpakasya ca darśanam
english: And the coronation of Vibhīşaņa, and the sight of Puspaka; Rama's return towards Ayodhyā, and meeting with Bharadvāja.
The wise call him learned, whose acts are all free from desires and fancies, and whose actions are burnt down by the fire of knowledge.

sanskrit: राम अभिषेक अभ्युदयम् सर्व सैन्य विसर्जनम्
स्व राष्ट्र रंजनम् च एव वैदेह्याः च विसर्जनम् ॥१-३-३८
transliteration: rāma abhiṣeka abhyudayam sarva sainya visarjanam
sva rāṣṭra raṃjanam ca eva vaidehyāḥ ca visarjanam 1-3-38
english: Despatch of Hanumān; and Rāma's meeting with Bharata; and the installation of Rāma; and the dismissal of all the forces.
Forsaking all attachment to the fruit of action, always contented, dependent on none, he does nothing at all, though he engages in action.

sanskrit: अनागतम् च यत् किंचिद् रामस्य वसुधा तले
तत् चकार उत्तरे काव्ये वाल्मीकिः भगवान् ऋषिः
transliteration: anāgatam ca yat kiṃcid rāmasya vasudhā tale
tat cakāra uttare kāvye vālmīkiḥ bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: Rāma's pleasing his subjects and renunciation of Sītā,-alleles besides concerning Rāma on earth, that has not yet taken place-have been dealt with by the worshipful sage in the following poem. earth, that has not yet taken place-have been dealt with by the worshipful sage in the following poem.

transliteration: śhārīraṁ kevalaṁ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣham
english: Devoid of expectations, restraining the mind and the self, and casting off all belongings, he incurs no sin, performing actions merely for the sake of the body.

sanskrit: प्राप्त राज्यस्य रामस्य वाल्मीकिर् भगवान् ऋषिः
चकार चरितम् कृत्स्नम् विचित्र पदम् अर्थवत्
transliteration: prāpta rājyasya rāmasya vālmīkir bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
cakāra caritam kṛtsnam vicitra padam arthavat
english: When Rāma had obtained his kingdom that worshipful sage , Vālmīki, composed the entire history (of that hero in) excellent metre and fraught with high meaning.

sanskrit: समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते
transliteration: samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau cha kṛitvāpi na nibadhyate
english: Satisfied with earnings coming spontaneously, rising above the pairs of opposites, free from all animosity, and equable on success or ill-success, he is not fettered down, even though he performs (actions).

sanskrit: तथा सर्ग शतान् पंच षट् काण्डानि तथा उत्तरम्
transliteration: tathā sarga śatān paṃca ṣaṭ kāṇḍāni tathā uttaram
english: The saint recited twenty-four thousand slokas; and it consists of five hundred sections, and is divided into six Kāndas with the Uttara.
The acts of one who is devoid of attachment, who is free, whose mind is fixed on knowledge, and who performs action for (the purpose of) the sacrifice are all destroyed.

sanskrit: कृत्वा तु तन् महाप्राज्ञः स भविष्यम् सह उत्तरम्
transliteration: kṛtvā tu tan mahāprājñaḥ sa bhaviṣyam saha uttaram
english: And having composed it, including as well future incidents to happen afterwards, that lord relected as to who should publish the same before assemblies.

transliteration: brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam
english: Brahman is the oblation; with Brahman (as a sacrificial instrument) it is offered up; Brahman is in the fire; and by Brahman it is thrown; and Brahman, too, is the goal to which he proceeds who meditates on Brahman in the action.

sanskrit: अगृह्णीताम् ततः पादौ मुनि वेषौ कुशी लवौ
transliteration: agṛhṇītām tataḥ pādau muni veṣau kuśī lavau
english: And as that great sage of purified soul was thus pounding, in came Kuśi and Lava, in the guise of the sons of ascetics, and touched his feet.
Some devotees perform the sacrifice to the gods, some offer up the sacrifice by the sacrifice itself in the fire of Brahman.

sanskrit: कुशी लवौ तु धर्मज्ञौ राज पुत्रौ यशश्विनौ
भ्रातरौ स्वर संपन्नौ ददर्श आश्रम वासिनौ
transliteration: kuśī lavau tu dharmajñau rāja putrau yaśaśvinau
bhrātarau svara saṃpannau dadarśa āśrama vāsinau

english: Others offer up the senses, such as the sense of hearing and others, in the fires of restraint; others offer up the objects of sense, such as sound and so forth, into the fires of the senses.

sanskrit: स तु मेधाविनौ दृष्ट्वा वेदेषु परिनिष्टितौ
transliteration: sa tu medhāvinau dṛṣṭvā vedeṣu pariniṣṭitau

english: Some again offer up all the operations of the senses and the operations of the life-breaths into the fire of devotion by self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.

sanskrit: काव्यम् रामायणम् कृत्स्नम् सीतायाः चरितम् महत्
पौलस्त्य वधम् इति एवम् चकार चरित व्रतः
transliteration: kāvyam rāmāyaṇam kṛtsnam sītāyāḥ caritam mahat
paulastya vadham iti evam cakāra carita vrataḥ

english: Others perform the sacrifice of wealth, the sacrifice of penance, the sacrifice of concentration of mind, the sacrifice of Vedic study, and of knowledge, and others are ascetics of rigid vows.

sanskrit: पाठ्ये गेये च मथुरम् प्रमाणैः त्रिभिर् अन्वितम्
जातिभिः सप्तभिः युक्तम् तन्त्री लय समन्वितम्
transliteration: pāṭhye geye ca mathuram pramāṇaiḥ tribhir anvitam
jātibhiḥ saptabhiḥ yuktam tantrī laya samanvitam

english: Some offer up the upward life-breath into the downward life-breath, and the downward life-breath into the upper life-breath, and stopping up the motions of the upward and downward life-breaths, devote themselves to the restraint of the life-breaths. Others, who (take) limited food, offer up the life-breaths into the life-breaths.

sanskrit: रसैः शृंगार करुण हास्य रौद्र भयानकैः
विरादिभी रसैर् युक्तम् काव्यम् एतत् अगायताम्
transliteration: rasaiḥ śṛṃgāra karuṇa hāsya raudra bhayānakaiḥ
virādibhī rasair yuktam kāvyam etat agāyatām

english: All of these, conversant with the sacrifice, have their sins destroyed by the sacrifice. Those who eat the nectar-like leavings of the sacrifice repair to the eternal Brahman.

sanskrit: तौ तु गान्धर्व तत्त्वज्ञौ स्थान मूर्च्छन कोविदौ
भ्रातरौ स्वर संपन्नौ गन्धर्वाः इव रूपिणौ
transliteration: tau tu gāndharva tattvajñau sthāna mūrcchana kovidau
bhrātarau svara saṃpannau gandharvāḥ iva rūpiṇau

english: This world is not for those who perform no sacrifice, whence (then) the other, O best of the Kauravas!

sanskrit: रूप लक्षण संपन्नौ मधुर स्वर भाषिणौ
बिंबात् इव उथीतौ बिंबौ राम देहात् तथा अपरौ
transliteration: rūpa lakṣaṇa saṃpannau madhura svara bhāṣiṇau
biṃbāt iva uthītau biṃbau rāma dehāt tathā aparau

sanskrit: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे
transliteration: evaṁ bahu-vidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe
karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān evaṁ jñātvā vimokṣhyase
english: Thus sacrifices of various sorts are laid down in the Vedas. Know them all to be produced from action, and knowing this you will be released (from the fetters of this world).

sanskrit: तौ राज पुत्रौ कार्त्स्न्येन धर्म्यम् आख्यानम् उत्तमम्
वाचो विधेयम् तत् सर्वम् कृत्वा काव्यम् अनिन्दितौ
transliteration: tau rāja putrau kārtsnyena dharmyam ākhyānam uttamam
vāco vidheyam tat sarvam kṛtvā kāvyam aninditau
english: Even as the reflection of the solar or the lunar disc resembles that disc; got by heart that excellent and moral story in its entirety; and those princes versed in the Fine arts, with a concentrated mind chanted it as they had learnt it, in the assemblies of ascetics and Brāhmaṇas and good men.
The sacrifice of knowledge, O terror of (your) foes! is superior to the sacrifice of wealth, for action, O son of Pritha! is wholly and entirely comprehended in knowledge.

sanskrit: ऋषीणाम् च द्विजातीनाम् साधूनाम् च समागमे
यथा उपदेशम् तत्त्वज्ञौ जगतुः तौ समाहितौ
transliteration: ṛṣīṇām ca dvijātīnām sādhūnām ca samāgame
yathā upadeśam tattvajñau jagatuḥ tau samāhitau

english: That you should learn by salutation, question, and service. The men of knowledge who perceive the truth will teach knowledge to you.

sanskrit: तौ कदाचित् समेतानाम् ऋषीणाम् भवित आत्मनाम्
transliteration: tau kadācit sametānām ṛṣīṇām bhavita ātmanām
yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṁ yāsyasi pāṇḍava
english: Having learnt that, O son of Pandu! you will not again fall thus into delusion; and by means of it, you will see all beings, without exception, first in yourself, and then in me.

sanskrit: मध्ये सभम् समीपस्थौ इदम् काव्यम् अगायताम्
तत् श्रुत्वा मुनयः सर्वे बाष्प पर्याकुलेक्षणाः
transliteration: madhye sabham samīpasthau idam kāvyam agāyatām
tat śrutvā munayaḥ sarve bāṣpa paryākulekṣaṇāḥ
api ched asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛit-tamaḥ
english: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinful men, you will cross over all trespasses by means of the boat of knowledge alone.

sanskrit: साधु साध्विति ता ऊचुः परम् विस्मयम् आगताः
ते प्रीत मनसः सर्वे मुनयो धर्म वत्सलाः
transliteration: sādhu sādhviti tā ūcuḥ param vismayam āgatāḥ
te prīta manasaḥ sarve munayo dharma vatsalāḥ

english: As a fire well kindled, O Arguna! reduces fuel to ashes, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.

sanskrit: अहो गीतस्य माधुर्यम् श्लोकानाम् च विशेषतः
transliteration: aho gītasya mādhuryam ślokānām ca viśeṣataḥ
english: Praised the praiseworthy Kuśi and Lava as they sang, saying,-Ah! what charming music! What sweetness of the verses!

sanskrit: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते
transliteration: na hi jñānena sadṛiśhaṁ pavitramiha vidyate
english: For there is in this world no means of sanctification like knowledge, and that one perfected by devotion finds within one's self in time.

sanskrit: चिरनिर्वृत्तम् अपि एतत् प्रत्यक्षम् इव दर्शितम्
प्रविश्य ता उभौ सुष्ठु तथा भावम् अगायताम्
transliteration: ciranirvṛttam api etat pratyakṣam iva darśitam
praviśya tā ubhau suṣṭhu tathā bhāvam agāyatām
english: All this happened long ago, yet it seems as if we saw it before us. And unified with the theme, both of them singing together sweetly, and at a high pitch, by means of şadja and the other notes, they entranced the audience.
He who has faith, whose senses are restrained, and who is assiduous, obtains knowledge. Obtaining knowledge, he acquires, without delay, the highest tranquillity.

sanskrit: सहितौ मधुरम् रक्तम् संपन्नम् स्वर संपदा
एवम् प्रशस्यमानौ तौ तपः श्लाघ्यैः महर्षिभिः
transliteration: sahitau madhuram raktam saṃpannam svara saṃpadā
evam praśasyamānau tau tapaḥ ślāghyaiḥ maharṣibhiḥ

sanskrit: नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः
transliteration: nāyaṁ loko ’sti na paro na sukhaṁ sanśhayātmanaḥ
english: He who is ignorant and devoid of faith, and whose self is full of misgivings, is ruined. Not this world, not the next, nor happiness, is for him whose self is full of misgivings.

sanskrit: प्रीतः कश्चिन् मुनिः ताभ्याम् संस्थितः कलशम् ददौ
transliteration: prītaḥ kaścin muniḥ tābhyām saṃsthitaḥ kalaśam dadau

english: Actions, O Dhanangaya! do not fetter one who is self-possessed, who has renounced action by devotion, and who has destroyed misgivings by knowledge.

sanskrit: प्रसन्नो वल्कलम् कश्चिद् ददौ ताभ्याम् महायशाः
अन्यः कृष्णाजिनम् अदद् यज्ञ सूत्रम् तथा अपरः
transliteration: prasanno valkalam kaścid dadau tābhyām mahāyaśāḥ
anyaḥ kṛṣṇājinam adad yajña sūtram tathā aparaḥ
english: Some one in the assembly pleased with them presented them with a water-pitcher; and some one of high fame, being delighted, made them a present of a bark garment; and some one gave them a dark deer skin and some holy thread.
Therefore, O descendant of Bharata! destroy, with the sword of knowledge, these misgivings of yours which fill your mind, and which are produced from ignorance. Engage in devotion. Arise!

sanskrit: कश्चित् कमण्डलुम् प्रदान् मौञ्जीम् अन्यो महामुनिः
ब्रुसीमन्यः तदा प्रादत् कौपीनम् अपरो मुनिः
transliteration: kaścit kamaṇḍalum pradān mauñjīm anyo mahāmuniḥ
brusīmanyaḥ tadā prādat kaupīnam aparo muniḥ
english: Some gave a kamandalu (An earthen or wooden water pot used by an ascetic) and some great saint conferred on them a muñja (grass) made girdle; and some person granted them a brsi (The seat of an ascetic), and some a kaupina (a small piece of cloth worn by ascetics.)

sanskrit: संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि
transliteration: sannyāsaṁ karmaṇāṁ kṛiṣhṇa punar yogaṁ cha śhansasi
yach chhreya etayor ekaṁ tan me brūhi su-niśhchitam
english: Arguna said: O Krishna! you praise renunciation of actions and also the pursuit (of them). Tell me determinately which one of these two is superior.

sanskrit: ताभ्याम् ददौ तदा हृष्टः कुठारम् अपरो मुनिः
काषायम् अपरो वस्त्रम् चीरम् अन्यो ददौ मुनिः
transliteration: tābhyām dadau tadā hṛṣṭaḥ kuṭhāram aparo muniḥ
kāṣāyam aparo vastram cīram anyo dadau muniḥ
english: Then some ascetic, well-pleased, gave them an axe; and some a saffron, another a casual clothings.
The Deity said: Renunciation and pursuit of action are both instruments of happiness. But of the two, pursuit of action is superior to renunciation of action.

sanskrit: जटाबन्धनम् अन्यः तु काष्ठ रज्जुम् मुदान्वितः
यज्ञ भाण्डम् ऋषिः कश्चित् काष्ठभारम् तथा परः
transliteration: jaṭābandhanam anyaḥ tu kāṣṭha rajjum mudānvitaḥ
yajña bhāṇḍam ṛṣiḥ kaścit kāṣṭhabhāram tathā paraḥ

sanskrit: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति
transliteration: jñeyaḥ sa nitya-sannyāsī yo na dveṣhṭi na kāṅkṣhati
nirdvandvo hi mahā-bāho sukhaṁ bandhāt pramuchyate
english: He should be understood to be always an ascetic, who has no aversion and no desire. For, O you of mighty arms! he who is free from the pairs of opposites is easily released from (all) bonds.

sanskrit: औदुम्बरीम् ब्रुसीम् अन्यः स्वस्ति केचित् तदा अवदन्
आयुष्यम् अपरे प्राहुर् मुदा तत्र महर्षयः
transliteration: audumbarīm brusīm anyaḥ svasti kecit tadā avadan
āyuṣyam apare prāhur mudā tatra maharṣayaḥ
sānkhya-yogau pṛithag bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ
english: Children not wise men talk of sankhya and yoga as distinct. One who pursues either well obtains the fruit of both.

sanskrit: ददुः च एवम् वरान् सर्वे मुनयः सत्यवादिनः
transliteration: daduḥ ca evam varān sarve munayaḥ satyavādinaḥ

sanskrit: एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति
transliteration: yat sānkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṁ tad yogair api gamyate
ekaṁ sānkhyaṁ cha yogaṁ cha yaḥ paśhyati sa paśhyati
english: The seat which the sankhyas obtain is reached by the yogas also. He sees (truly), who sees the sankhya and yoga as one.

sanskrit: परम् कवीनाम् आधारम् समाप्तम् च यथा क्रमम्
अभिगीतम् इदम् गीतम् सर्व गीतेषु कोविदौ
transliteration: param kavīnām ādhāram samāptam ca yathā kramam
abhigītam idam gītam sarva gīteṣu kovidau
sannyāsas tu mahā-bāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ
english: Renunciation, O you of mighty arms! is difficult to reach without devotion; the sage possessed of devotion attains Brahman without delay.

sanskrit: आयुष्यम् पुष्टि जननम् सर्व श्रुति मनोहरम्
transliteration: āyuṣyam puṣṭi jananam sarva śruti manoharam

english: He who is possessed of devotion, whose self is pure, who has restrained his self, and who has controlled his senses, and who identifies his self with every being, is not tainted though he performs (actions).

sanskrit: स्व वेश्म च आनीय ततो भ्रातरौ स कुशी लवौ
transliteration: sva veśma ca ānīya tato bhrātarau sa kuśī lavau
naiva kiñchit karomīti yukto manyeta tattva-vit
pralapan visṛijan gṛihṇann unmiṣhan nimiṣhann api
english: The man of devotion, who knows the truth, thinks he does nothing at all, when he sees, hears, touches, smells, eats, moves, sleeps, breathes,

sanskrit: आसीनः कांचने दिव्ये स च सिंहासने प्रभुः
transliteration: āsīnaḥ kāṃcane divye sa ca siṃhāsane prabhuḥ
pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇann unmiṣan nimiṣann api indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan
english: talks, throws out, takes, opens or closes the eyelids; he holds that the senses deal with the objects of the senses.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा तु रूप संपन्नौ विनीतौ भ्रातरौ उभौ
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā tu rūpa saṃpannau vinītau bhrātarau ubhau

sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः
transliteration: brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ
lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram ivāmbhasā
english: He who, casting off (all) attachment, performs actions dedicating them to Brahman, is not tainted by sin, as the lotus-leaf (is not tainted) by water.

sanskrit: उवाच लक्ष्मणम् रामः शत्रुघ्नम् भरतम् तथा
श्रूयताम् एतद् आख्यानम् अनयोः देव वर्चसोः
transliteration: uvāca lakṣmaṇam rāmaḥ śatrughnam bharatam tathā
śrūyatām etad ākhyānam anayoḥ deva varcasoḥ
kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalair indriyair api
english: Devotees, casting off attachment, perform actions for attaining purity of self, with the body, the mind, the understandincy, or even the senses (all) free (from egoistic notions).

sanskrit: तौ च अपि मधुरम् रक्तम् स्वचित्तायत निःस्वनम्
transliteration: tau ca api madhuram raktam svacittāyata niḥsvanam
yuktaḥ karma-phalaṁ tyaktvā śhāntim āpnoti naiṣhṭhikīm
english: He who is possessed of devotion, abandoning the fruit of actions, attains the highest tranquillity. He who is without devotion, and attached to the fruit (of action), is tied down by (reason of his) acting in consequence of (some) desire.

sanskrit: ह्लादयत् सर्व गात्राणि मनांसि हृदयानि च
श्रोत्राश्रय सुखम् गेयम् तद् बभौ जनसंसदि
transliteration: hlādayat sarva gātrāṇi manāṃsi hṛdayāni ca
śrotrāśraya sukham geyam tad babhau janasaṃsadi
english: Thereupon causing the down of the audience to stand on end, and ravishing their minds and hearts, they began to sing melodiously and distinctly and in as high a pitch as they could command, and in strains rivalling the notes of a Vīņā. And that song of their enchanted the ear of that assembly.

sanskrit: नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन्
transliteration: nava-dvāre pure dehī naiva kurvan na kārayan
english: The self-restrained, embodied (self) lies at ease within the city of nine portals, renouncing all actions by the mind, not doing, nor causing (anything) to be done.

sanskrit: इमौ मुनी पार्थिव लक्षणान्वितौकुशी लवौ च एव महातपस्विनौ
ममा अपि तद् भूति करम् प्रचक्षतेमहानुभावम् चरितम् निबोधत
transliteration: imau munī pārthiva lakṣaṇānvitaukuśī lavau ca eva mahātapasvinau
mamā api tad bhūti karam pracakṣatemahānubhāvam caritam nibodhata
english: Rāma said, Although these Kuśa and Lava, of rigid penances, look like ascetics, yet they bear on their persons the signs of royalty. And, besides, the story conduces to my fame. Do you, therefore, listen to that history fraught with great worth!

sanskrit: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः
transliteration: na kartṛitvaṁ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛijati prabhuḥ
english: The Lord is not, the cause of actions, or of the capacity of performing actions amongst men, or of the connexion of action and fruit. But nature only works.

sanskrit: ततः तु तौ राम वचः प्रचोदितौअगायताम् मार्ग विधान संपदा
स च अपि रामः परिषद् गतः शनैर्बुभूषय आसक्तमना बभूव
transliteration: tataḥ tu tau rāma vacaḥ pracoditauagāyatām mārga vidhāna saṃpadā
sa ca api rāmaḥ pariṣad gataḥ śanairbubhūṣaya āsaktamanā babhūva
english: And then commanded by Rāma, they began to chant according to the Märga mode, and Rāma seated in the midst of his court, was drawn to the music, anxious for the perpetuation of his history.

sanskrit: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः
transliteration: nādatte kasyachit pāpaṁ na chaiva sukṛitaṁ vibhuḥ
english: The Lord receives no one's sin, nor merit either. Knowledge is enveloped by ignorance, hence all creatures are deluded.

sanskrit: सर्वा पूर्वम् इयम् येषाम् आसीत् कृत्स्ना वसुंधरा
transliteration: sarvā pūrvam iyam yeṣām āsīt kṛtsnā vasuṃdharā
jñānena tu tad ajñānaṁ yeṣhāṁ nāśhitam ātmanaḥ
teṣhām āditya-vaj jñānaṁ prakāśhayati tat param
english: But to those who have destroyed that ignorance by knowledge of the self, (such) knowledge, like the sun, shows forth that supreme (principle).

sanskrit: येषाम् स सगरो नाम सागरो येन खानितः
षष्टिः पुत्र सहस्राणि यम् यान्तम् पर्यवारयन्
transliteration: yeṣām sa sagaro nāma sāgaro yena khānitaḥ
ṣaṣṭiḥ putra sahasrāṇi yam yāntam paryavārayan

english: And those whose mind is (centred) on it, whose (very) self it is, who are thoroughly devoted to it, and whose final goal it is, go never to return, having their sins destroyed by knowledge.

sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकूणाम् इदम् तेषाम् राज्ञाम् वंशे महात्मनाम्
महद् उत्पन्नम् आख्यनम् रामायणम् इति श्रुतम्
transliteration: ikṣvākūṇām idam teṣām rājñām vaṃśe mahātmanām
mahad utpannam ākhyanam rāmāyaṇam iti śrutam

sanskrit: शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः
transliteration: śhuni chaiva śhva-pāke cha paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśhinaḥ
english: The wise look upon a Brahmana possessed of learning and humility, on a cow, an elephant, a dog, and a Svapaka, as alike.

sanskrit: धर्म काम अर्थ सहितम् श्रोतव्यम् अनसूयता
transliteration: dharma kāma artha sahitam śrotavyam anasūyatā
english: We shall now chant the entire history of that dynasty from the beginning. Do you, with minds free from ill will, listen to that story conferring merit, profit and pleasure.

sanskrit: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः
निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः
transliteration: ihaiva tair jitaḥ sargo yeṣhāṁ sāmye sthitaṁ manaḥ
nirdoṣhaṁ hi samaṁ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ
english: Even here, those have conquered the material world, whose mind rests in equability; since Brahman is free from defects and equable, therefore they rest in Brahman.

sanskrit: कोसलो नाम मुदितः स्फीतो जनपदो महान्
निविष्ट सरयू तीरे प्रभूत धन धान्यवान्
transliteration: kosalo nāma muditaḥ sphīto janapado mahān
niviṣṭa sarayū tīre prabhūta dhana dhānyavān
english: There is on the banks of the Sarayū a great and flourishing country called Kośala abounding in corn and wealth, in which the inhabitants passed their days pleasantly.

transliteration: na prahṛiṣhyet priyaṁ prāpya nodvijet prāpya chāpriyam
english: He who knows Brahman, whose mind is steady, who is not deluded, and who rests in Brahman, does not exult on finding anything agreeable, nor does he grieve on finding anything disagreeable.

sanskrit: अयोध्या नाम नगरी तत्र आसीत् लोक विश्रुता
मनुना मानव इन्द्रेण या पुरी निर्मिता स्वयम्
transliteration: ayodhyā nāma nagarī tatra āsīt loka viśrutā
manunā mānava indreṇa yā purī nirmitā svayam
english: The capital of that country was Ayodhyā famed among men, which was founded by Manu himself that foremost of men.

One whose self is not attached to external objects, obtains the happiness that is in (one's) self; and by means of concentration of mind, joining one's self (with the Brahman), one obtains indestructible happiness.

sanskrit: आयता दश च द्वे च योजनानि महापुरी
श्रीमती त्रीणि विस्तीर्णा सु विभक्ता महापथा
transliteration: āyatā daśa ca dve ca yojanāni mahāpurī
śrīmatī trīṇi vistīrṇā su vibhaktā mahāpathā
english: That beautiful and mighty city was twelve Yojanas in length and Three in breadth; and was intersected outside with spacious roads laid out orderly.

sanskrit: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते
आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः
transliteration: ye hi sansparśha-jā bhogā duḥkha-yonaya eva te
ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣhu ramate budhaḥ
english: For the enjoyments born of contact (between senses and their objects) are, indeed, sources of misery; they have a beginning as well as an end. O son of Kunti! a wise man feels no pleasure in them.

sanskrit: मुक्ता पुष्प अवकीर्णेन जल सिक्तेन नित्यशः
transliteration: muktā puṣpa avakīrṇena jala siktena nityaśaḥ
english: And scattered with blown blossoms, and regularly sprinkled with water; the well-arranged broad high-ways looked beautiful.

sanskrit: कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः
transliteration: kāma-krodhodbhavaṁ vegaṁ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ
english: He who even in this world, before his release from the body, is able to bear the agitations produced from desire and wrath, is a devoted man, he is a happy man.

sanskrit: ताम् तु राजा दशरथो महाराष्ट्र विवर्धनः
transliteration: tām tu rājā daśaratho mahārāṣṭra vivardhanaḥ
english: That one bringing prosperity into great kingdoms, King Dasaratha, lived in that city, like that of the lord of the deities inhabiting the celestial regions.

The devotee whose happiness is within (himself), whose recreation is within (himself), and whose light (of knowledge) also is within (himself), becoming (one with) the Brahman, obtains the Brahmic bliss.

sanskrit: सर्व यंत्र अयुधवतीम् उषिताम् सर्व शिल्पिभिः
transliteration: sarva yaṃtra ayudhavatīm uṣitām sarva śilpibhiḥ
english: And the city was furnished with doors and gates, and well-arranged rows of shops. And it contained all kinds of instruments and arms, and was inhabited by all classes of artizans.
The sages whose sins have perished, whose misgivings are destroyed, who are self-restrained, and who are intent on the welfare of all beings, obtain the Brahmic bliss.

sanskrit: सूत मागध संबाधाम् श्रीमतीम् अतुल प्रभाम्
transliteration: sūta māgadha saṃbādhām śrīmatīm atula prabhām
english: And that graceful and matchlessly brilliant city abounded in eulogists and genealogists. And it was crowned with stately edifices with flags, and guarded by hundreds of Satāghnis. (A weapon commonly described as a stone set round with iron spiles).
To the ascetics, who are free from desire and wrath, and whose minds are restrained, and who have knowledge of the self, the Brahmic bliss is on both sides (of death).

sanskrit: वधू नाटक सन्घैः च संयुक्ताम् सर्वतः पुरीम्
उद्यान आम्र वणोपेताम् महतीम् साल मेखलाम्
transliteration: vadhū nāṭaka sanghaiḥ ca saṃyuktām sarvataḥ purīm
udyāna āmra vaṇopetām mahatīm sāla mekhalām
english: And the mighty city contained theatres for females, and gardens, and mango-groves; and was enclosed by a wall of såla trees.

transliteration: sparśhān kṛitvā bahir bāhyānśh chakṣhuśh chaivāntare bhruvoḥ
vigatechchhā-bhaya-krodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ
english: The sage who excludes (from his mind) external objects, (concentrates) the visual power between the brows, and making the upward and downward lifebreaths even, confines their movements within the nose,

sanskrit: दुर्ग गंभीर परिखाम् दुर्गाम् अन्यैः दुरासदम्
वाजीवारण संपूर्णाम् गोभिः उष्ट्रैः खरैः तथा
transliteration: durga gaṃbhīra parikhām durgām anyaiḥ durāsadam
vājīvāraṇa saṃpūrṇām gobhiḥ uṣṭraiḥ kharaiḥ tathā
english: And encircled by a deep moat, the city was not accessible for enemies. And it abounded with elephants and horses, and kine and camels and asses.

sanskrit: विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः
transliteration: yatendriya-mano-buddhir munir mokṣa-parāyaṇaḥ vigatecchā-bhaya-krodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ
english: who restrains senses, mind, and understanding, whose highest goal is final emancipation, from whom desire, fear, and wrath have departed, is, indeed, for ever released (from birth and death).

sanskrit: सामंत राज सन्घैः च बलि कर्मभिः आवृतम्
नाना देश निवासैः च वणिग्भिः उपशोभिताम्
transliteration: sāmaṃta rāja sanghaiḥ ca bali karmabhiḥ āvṛtam
nānā deśa nivāsaiḥ ca vaṇigbhiḥ upaśobhitām
english: It was thronged with neighbouring kings come to pay tribute, and inhabited by merchants from various countries.

transliteration: suhṛidaṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ jñātvā māṁ śhāntim ṛichchhati
english: He knowing me to be the enjoyer of all sacrifices and penances, the great Lord of all worlds, and the friend of all beings, attains tranquillity.

sanskrit: प्रासादै रत्न विकृतैः पर्वतैः इव शोभिताम्
कूटागारैः च संपूर्णाम् इन्द्रस्य इव अमरावतीम्
transliteration: prāsādai ratna vikṛtaiḥ parvataiḥ iva śobhitām
kūṭāgāraiḥ ca saṃpūrṇām indrasya iva amarāvatīm
english: And adorned with mountain like palaces glittering with gems, and filled with sportingplaces for females, and like to Indra's Amarāvati.

sanskrit: अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः
स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः
transliteration: anāśhritaḥ karma-phalaṁ kāryaṁ karma karoti yaḥ
sa sannyāsī cha yogī cha na niragnir na chākriyaḥ
english: The Deity said: He who, regardless of the fruit of actions, performs the actions which ought to be performed, is the devotee and renouncer; not he who discards the (sacred) fires, nor he who performs no acts.

sanskrit: चित्रम् अष्टापद आकाराम् वर नारी गणैर् युताम्
सर्व रत्न समाकीर्णाम् विमान गृह शोभिताम्
transliteration: citram aṣṭāpada ākārām vara nārī gaṇair yutām
sarva ratna samākīrṇām vimāna gṛha śobhitām
english: The city was wonderful to behold, gleaming with gold-burnished ornaments, and inhabited by troops of courtezans, and abounding in all kinds of gems, and graced with royal palaces.

sanskrit: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव
transliteration: yaṁ sannyāsam iti prāhur yogaṁ taṁ viddhi pāṇḍava
english: Know, O son of Pandu! that what is called renunciation is devotion; for nobody becomes a devotee who has not renounced (all) fancies.

sanskrit: गृह गाढाम् अविच्छिद्राम् सम भूमौ निवेशिताम्
शालि तण्डुल संपूर्णाम् इक्षु काण्ड रसः उदकाम्
transliteration: gṛha gāḍhām avicchidrām sama bhūmau niveśitām
śāli taṇḍula saṃpūrṇām ikṣu kāṇḍa rasaḥ udakām
english: And it abounded in paddy and rice, and its water was sweet as the juice of the sugar-cane.

transliteration: ārurukṣhor muner yogaṁ karma kāraṇam uchyate
english: To the sage who wishes to rise to devotion, action is said to be a means, and to him, when be has risen to devotion, tranquillity is said to be a means.

sanskrit: दुन्दुभीभिः मृदन्गैः च वीणाभिः पणवैः तथा
नादिताम् भृशम् अत्यर्थम् पृथिव्याम् ताम् अनुत्तमाम्
transliteration: dundubhībhiḥ mṛdangaiḥ ca vīṇābhiḥ paṇavaiḥ tathā
nāditām bhṛśam atyartham pṛthivyām tām anuttamām
english: And it resounded with the sounds of Dundubhis and Mrdargas and Viņās and Panavas.
When one does not attach oneself to objects of sense, nor to action, renouncing all fancies, then one is said to have risen to devotion.

sanskrit: विमानम् इव सिद्धानाम् तपस अधिगतम् दिवि
transliteration: vimānam iva siddhānām tapasa adhigatam divi
english: And that foremost spot of all the earth was like an aerial car obtained in heaven by the Siddhas, through force of ascetic austerities, and thronged with the best specimens of humanity.

transliteration: ātmaiva hyātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ
english: (A man) should elevate his self by his self; he should not debase his self, for even (a man's) own self is his friend, (a man's) own self is also his enemy.

sanskrit: ये च बाणैः न विध्यन्ति विविक्तम् अपरा परम्
शब्द वेध्यम् च विततम् लघु हस्ता विशारदाः
transliteration: ye ca bāṇaiḥ na vidhyanti viviktam aparā param
śabda vedhyam ca vitatam laghu hastā viśāradāḥ

english: To him who has subjugated his self by his self, his self is a friend; but to him who has not restrained his self, his own self behaves inimically, like an enemy.

sanskrit: सिंह व्याघ्र वराहाणाम् मत्तानाम् नदताम् वने
हन्तारो निशितैः शस्त्रैः बलात् बाहु बलैर् अपि
transliteration: siṃha vyāghra varāhāṇām mattānām nadatām vane
hantāro niśitaiḥ śastraiḥ balāt bāhu balair api

english: The self of one who has subjugated his self and is tranquil, is absolutely concentrated (on itself), in the midst of cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as honour and dishonour.

sanskrit: तादृशानाम् सहस्रैः ताम् अभि पूर्णाम् महारथैः
transliteration: tādṛśānām sahasraiḥ tām abhi pūrṇām mahārathaiḥ

english: The devotee whose self is contented with knowledge and experience, who is unmoved, who has restrained his senses, and to whom a sod, a stone, and gold are alike, is said to be devoted.

sanskrit: ताम् अग्निमद्भिः गुणवद्भिः आवृताम्द्विजोत्तमैः वेद षडङ्ग पारगैः
सहस्रदैः सत्य रतैः महात्मभिःमहर्षि कल्पैः ऋषिभिः च केवलैः
transliteration: tām agnimadbhiḥ guṇavadbhiḥ āvṛtāmdvijottamaiḥ veda ṣaḍaṅga pāragaiḥ
sahasradaiḥ satya rataiḥ mahātmabhiḥmaharṣi kalpaiḥ ṛṣibhiḥ ca kevalaiḥ
english: It abounded mostly in excellent Brāhmaṇas, lighting the sacrificial fire, and crowned with qualities, and versed in the Vedas and the Vedāngas, and giving away thousands, and ever abiding by truth, and high-souled, and resembling might ascetics.

And he is esteemed highest, who thinks alike about well-wishers, friends, and enemies, and those who are indifferent, and those who take part with both sides, and those who are objects of hatred, and relatives, as well as about the good and the sinful.

sanskrit: तस्याम् पुर्याम् अयोध्यायाम् वेदवित् सर्व संग्रहः
transliteration: tasyām puryām ayodhyāyām vedavit sarva saṃgrahaḥ
english: In that city of Ayodhyā resided king Dasaratha, versed in the Vedas, commanding all resources, far-sighted, of mighty prowess, dear to the inhabitants both rural and urban.

transliteration: yogī yuñjīta satatam ātmānaṁ rahasi sthitaḥ
english: A devotee should constantly devote his self to abstraction, remaining in a secret place, alone, with his mind and self restrained, without expectations, and without belongings.
He was an Athiratha in the Ikşvāku line, performing sacrifices, engaged in the performance of duties, self-controlled like a Maharși, a royal saint famed in the three worlds.

transliteration: śhuchau deśhe pratiṣhṭhāpya sthiram āsanam ātmanaḥ
english: Fixing his seat firmly in a clean place, not too high nor too low, and covered over with a sheet of cloth, a deerskin, and (blades of) Kusa (grass),

sanskrit: बलवान् निहत अमित्रो मित्रवान् विजित इन्द्रियः
धनैः च संचयैः च अन्यैः शक्र वैश्रवण उपमः
transliteration: balavān nihata amitro mitravān vijita indriyaḥ
dhanaiḥ ca saṃcayaiḥ ca anyaiḥ śakra vaiśravaṇa upamaḥ
english: He possessed of strength, the destroyer of foes, having friends, of subdued senses, comparable to ſakra and Vaiśravaņa by virtue of accumulated riches and other possessions.
and there seated on (that) seat, fixing his mind exclusively on one point, with the workings of the mind and senses restrained, he should practice devotion for purity of self.
As the highly-powerful Manu protected the people, Dasaratha did the same.
Holding his body, head, and neck even and unmoved, (remaining) steady, looking at the tip of his own nose, and not looking about in (all) directions,

sanskrit: पालिता सा पुरी श्रेष्टा इन्द्रेण इव अमरावती
transliteration: pālitā sā purī śreṣṭā indreṇa iva amarāvatī
english: As Indra rules Amarāvatī, that one firm in promise, and following duty, profit, and pleasure, ruled that best of cities.

sanskrit: मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः
transliteration: manaḥ sanyamya mach-chitto yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ
english: with a tranquil self, devoid of fear, and adhering to the rules of Brahmakarins, he should restrain his mind, and (concentrate it) on me, and sit down engaged in devotion, regarding me as his final goal.

sanskrit: नराः तुष्ठाः धनैः स्वैः स्वैः अलुब्धाः सत्यवादिनः
transliteration: narāḥ tuṣṭhāḥ dhanaiḥ svaiḥ svaiḥ alubdhāḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: In that excellent city, the men were happy and righteous-souled, and widely-read, and each contented with his possessions, and devoid of covetousness, and speaking the truth.
Thus constantly devoting his self to abstraction, a devotee whose mind is restrained, attains that tranquillity which culminates in final emancipation, and assimilation with me.

sanskrit: न अल्प संनिचयः कश्चिद् आसीत् तस्मिन् पुरोत्तमे
कुटुंबी यो हि असिद्धर्थः अगवा अश्व धन धान्यवान्
transliteration: na alpa saṃnicayaḥ kaścid āsīt tasmin purottame
kuṭuṃbī yo hi asiddharthaḥ agavā aśva dhana dhānyavān
english: In that prime of cities, there was none who had not at his command a plenteous supply of the good things, and there was no householder who was not well off in horses and kine, and corn and wealth.
Devotion is not his, O Arguna! who eats too much, nor his who eats not at all; not his who is addicted to too much sleep, nor his who is (ever) awake.

sanskrit: कामी वा न कदर्यो वा नृशंसः पुरुषः क्वचित्
द्रष्टुम् शक्यम् अयोध्यायाम् न अविद्वान् न च नास्तिकः
transliteration: kāmī vā na kadaryo vā nṛśaṃsaḥ puruṣaḥ kvacit
draṣṭum śakyam ayodhyāyām na avidvān na ca nāstikaḥ
english: And one could see nowhere in Ayodhyā persons given up to lust, or unsightly, or crooked-minded, or unlettered, or atheistical.
That devotion which destroys (all) misery is his, who takes due food and exercise, who toils duly in all works, and who sleeps and awakes (in) due (time).

sanskrit: सर्वे नराः च नार्यः च धर्मशीलाः सु संयताः
मुदिताः शील वृत्ताभ्याम् महर्षय इव अमलाः
transliteration: sarve narāḥ ca nāryaḥ ca dharmaśīlāḥ su saṃyatāḥ
muditāḥ śīla vṛttābhyām maharṣaya iva amalāḥ
english: And all the men and all the women were of excellent character, and subdued senses, and a happy frame of mind, and both on respect of occupation and conduct spotless like to the Maharsis.
When (a man's) mind well restrained becomes steady upon the self alone, then he being indifferent to all objects of desire, is said to be devoted.

sanskrit: न अकुण्डली न अमुकुटी न अस्रग्वी न अल्पभोगवान्
न अमृष्टो न अलिप्ताङ्गो न असुगन्धः च विद्यते
transliteration: na akuṇḍalī na amukuṭī na asragvī na alpabhogavān
na amṛṣṭo na aliptāṅgo na asugandhaḥ ca vidyate
english: And all wore ear-rings and tiaras and garlands, and abundantly enjoyed the good things of life. And all were clean, daubing their limbs, and perfuming their persons.

sanskrit: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता
transliteration: yathā dīpo nivāta-stho neṅgate sopamā smṛitā
english: As a light standing in a windless (place) flickers not, that is declared to be the parallel for a devotee, whose mind is restrained, and who devotes his self to abstraction.

sanskrit: न अमृष्ट भोजी न अदाता न अपि अनङ्दनिष्कधृक्
न अहस्ताभरणो वा अपि दृश्यते न अपि अनात्मवान्
transliteration: na amṛṣṭa bhojī na adātā na api anaṅdaniṣkadhṛk
na ahastābharaṇo vā api dṛśyate na api anātmavān
english: And feeding on pure food, and giving away, and wearing Angadas (A bracelet worn upon the upper arm) and Niskas (An ornament for the breast or neck.) and hand-ornaments, and repressing passions.
That (mental condition), in which the mind restrained by practice, of abstraction, ceases to work; in which too, one seeing the self by the self, is pleased in the self;

sanskrit: न अनाहित अग्नीः न अयज्वा न क्षुद्रो वा न तस्करः
कश्चित् असीत् अयोध्यायाम् न च आवृत्तो न संकरः
transliteration: na anāhita agnīḥ na ayajvā na kṣudro vā na taskaraḥ
kaścit asīt ayodhyāyām na ca āvṛtto na saṃkaraḥ
english: There were not on Ayodhyā persons not lighting the sacrificial fire, or not performing sacrifices, or mean-minded, or thieving, or engaged in improper occupations, or of impure descent.

sanskrit: वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः
transliteration: sukham ātyantikaṁ yat tad buddhi-grāhyam atīndriyam
vetti yatra na chaivāyaṁ sthitaśh chalati tattvataḥ
english: in which one experiences that infinite happiness which transcends the senses, and which can be grasped by the understanding only; and adhering to which, one never swerves from the truth; acquiring which, one thinks no other acquisition higher than it;

sanskrit: स्व कर्म निरता नित्यम् ब्राह्मणा विजितेन्द्रियाः
दान अध्यन शीलाः च संयताः च प्रतिग्रहे
transliteration: sva karma niratā nityam brāhmaṇā vijitendriyāḥ
dāna adhyana śīlāḥ ca saṃyatāḥ ca pratigrahe
english: The Brāhmaṇas of subdued senses were always engaged in the performance of their own duties, giving away in charity, and studying, and receiving gifts with discrimination.

sanskrit: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः
transliteration: yaṁ labdhvā chāparaṁ lābhaṁ manyate nādhikaṁ tataḥ
yasmin sthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vichālyate
english: and adhering to which, one is not shaken off even by great misery; that should be understood to be called devotion in which there is a severance of all connexion with pain.

sanskrit: नास्तिको न अनृती वा अपि न कश्चित् अबहुश्रुतः
न असूयको न च अशक्तो न अविद्वान् विद्यते क्वचित्
transliteration: nāstiko na anṛtī vā api na kaścit abahuśrutaḥ
na asūyako na ca aśakto na avidvān vidyate kvacit
english: None of them was atheistical or untruthful or be reft of hearing scriptures or detracting or incompetent or illiterate.
That devotion should be practised with steadiness and with an undesponding heart.

sanskrit: न अषडंग वित् न अस्ति न अव्रतो न असहस्रदः
न दीनः क्षिप्त चित्तओ वा व्यथितो वा अपि कश्चन
transliteration: na aṣaḍaṃga vit na asti na avrato na asahasradaḥ
na dīnaḥ kṣipta cittao vā vyathito vā api kaścana
english: There was no Brāhmaṇa who was not versed in the Vedas and Vedangas, or poor-spirit, or of insane mind, or afflicted.
Abandoning, without exception, all desires, which are produced from fancies, and restraining the whole group of the senses on all sides by the mind only,

sanskrit: कश्चिन् नरो वा नारी वा न अश्रीमान् न अपि अरूपवान्
द्रष्टुम् शक्यम् अयोध्यायाम् न अपि राजन्य अभक्तिमान्
transliteration: kaścin naro vā nārī vā na aśrīmān na api arūpavān
draṣṭum śakyam ayodhyāyām na api rājanya abhaktimān
english: And no man and no woman was seen devoid of grace or beauty, or lacking in reverence for their monarch.

sanskrit: आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत्
transliteration: ātma-sansthaṁ manaḥ kṛitvā na kiñchid api chintayet
english: one should by slow steps become quiescent, with a firm resolve coupled with courage; and fixing the mind upon the self, should think of nothing.

sanskrit: वर्णेषु अग्र्य चतुर्थेषु देवता अतिथि पूजकाः
कृतज्ञाः च वदान्यः च शूरा विक्रम संयुताः
transliteration: varṇeṣu agrya caturtheṣu devatā atithi pūjakāḥ
kṛtajñāḥ ca vadānyaḥ ca śūrā vikrama saṃyutāḥ
english: The four orders with Brāhmanas at their head contained persons serving gods and guests, and endowed with gratitude, and munificent, and heroic, and possessing prowess.

transliteration: yato yato niśhcharati manaśh chañchalam asthiram
tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmanyeva vaśhaṁ nayet
english: Wherever the active and unsteady mind breaks forth, there one should ever restrain it, and fix it steadily on the self alone.

sanskrit: दीर्घ आयुषो नराः सर्वे धर्मम् सत्यम् च संश्रिताः
सहिताः पुत्र पौत्रैः च नित्यम् स्त्रीभिः पुरोत्तमे
transliteration: dīrgha āyuṣo narāḥ sarve dharmam satyam ca saṃśritāḥ
sahitāḥ putra pautraiḥ ca nityam strībhiḥ purottame
english: And the men were long-lived; and ever abode by duty and truth; and lived in that best of cities, always surrounded by sons and grandsons and wives.
The highest happiness comes to such a devotee, whose mind is fully tranquil, in whom the quality of passion has been suppressed, who is free from sin, and who is become (one with) the Brahman.

sanskrit: क्षत्रम् ब्रह्ममुखम् च आसीत् वैश्याः क्षत्रम् अनुव्रताः
शूद्राः स्व धर्म निरताः त्रीन् वर्णान् उपचारिणः
transliteration: kṣatram brahmamukham ca āsīt vaiśyāḥ kṣatram anuvratāḥ
śūdrāḥ sva dharma niratāḥ trīn varṇān upacāriṇaḥ
english: The Kşatriyas were obedient the Brahmanas, and the Vaisyas followed the Kșatriyas, and the sadras, occupied with their proper vocations, ministered to the three other orders.
Thus constantly devoting his self to abstraction, a devotee, freed from sin, easily obtains that supreme happiness-contact with the Brahman.

sanskrit: सा तेन इक्ष्वाकु नाथेन पुरी सु परिरक्षिता
transliteration: sā tena ikṣvāku nāthena purī su parirakṣitā
english: That city was ably govered by Dasaratha that lord of Ikşvāku's line, even as that foremost of men, the intelligent Manu, had governed it before him.
He who has devoted his self to abstraction, by devotion, looking alike on everything, sees the self abiding in all beings, and all beings in the self.

sanskrit: संपूर्णा कृत विद्यानाम् गुहा केसरिणाम् इव
transliteration: saṃpūrṇā kṛta vidyānām guhā kesariṇām iva
english: And as a mountain-cavern abounds with lions, it was filled with warriors resembling flaming fire, of straight ways, unforbearing, and of accomplished learning. to

sanskrit: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति
transliteration: yo māṁ paśhyati sarvatra sarvaṁ cha mayi paśhyati
tasyāhaṁ na praṇaśhyāmi sa cha me na praṇaśhyati
english: To him who sees me in everything, and everything in me, I am never lost, and he is not lost to me.

sanskrit: कांभोज विषये जातैः बाह्लिकैः च हय उत्तमैः
वनायुजैः नदीजैः च पूर्णा हरिहय उत्तमैः
transliteration: kāṃbhoja viṣaye jātaiḥ bāhlikaiḥ ca haya uttamaiḥ
vanāyujaiḥ nadījaiḥ ca pūrṇā harihaya uttamaiḥ
english: And the city abounded with excellent horses sprung in Kamboja, and Vahlika, and Vanayu, and the banks of the Sindhu, and like to that best of horses, Hari's charger.

sanskrit: सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते
transliteration: sarvathā vartamāno ’pi sa yogī mayi vartate
english: The devotee who worships me abiding in all beings, holding that all is one, lives in me, however he may be living.

sanskrit: विंध्य पर्वतजैः मत्तैः पूर्णा हैमवतैः अपि
transliteration: viṃdhya parvatajaiḥ mattaiḥ pūrṇā haimavataiḥ api
english: With fierce elephants sprung on the Vindhya mountain, and the Himavat, filled with juice, and of exceeding strength, and resembling hills.

sanskrit: सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः
transliteration: sukhaṁ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṁ sa yogī paramo mataḥ
english: That devotee, O Arguna! is deemed to be the best, who looks alike on pleasure or pain, whatever it may be, in all (creatures), comparing all with his own (pleasure or pain).

sanskrit: इरावत कुलीनैः च महापद्म कुलैः तथा
transliteration: irāvata kulīnaiḥ ca mahāpadma kulaiḥ tathā

sanskrit: एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम्
transliteration: yo ’yaṁ yogas tvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana
etasyāhaṁ na paśhyāmi chañchalatvāt sthitiṁ sthirām
english: Arguna said: I cannot see, O destroyer of Madhu! (how) the sustained existence (is to be secured) of this devotion by means of equanimity which you have declared in consequence of fickleness.

sanskrit: भद्रैः मन्द्रैः मृगैः च एव भद्र मन्द्र मृगैः थथा
भद्र मन्द्रैः भद्र मृगैः मृग मन्द्रैः च सा पुरी
transliteration: bhadraiḥ mandraiḥ mṛgaiḥ ca eva bhadra mandra mṛgaiḥ thathā
bhadra mandraiḥ bhadra mṛgaiḥ mṛga mandraiḥ ca sā purī

sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्
transliteration: chañchalaṁ hi manaḥ kṛiṣhṇa pramāthi balavad dṛiḍham
tasyāhaṁ nigrahaṁ manye vāyor iva su-duṣhkaram
english: For, O Krishna! the mind is fickle, boisterous, strong, and obstinate; and I think that to restrain it is as difficult as (to restrain) the wind.

sanskrit: नित्य मत्तैः सदा पूर्णा नागैः अचल सन्निभैः
सा योजने च द्वे भूयः सत्यनामा प्रकाशते
यस्याम् दशरथो राजा वसन् जगत् अपालयत्
transliteration: nitya mattaiḥ sadā pūrṇā nāgaiḥ acala sannibhaiḥ
sā yojane ca dve bhūyaḥ satyanāmā prakāśate
yasyām daśaratho rājā vasan jagat apālayat

sanskrit: अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते
transliteration: abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa cha gṛihyate
english: The Deity said: Doubtless, O you of mighty arms! the mind is difficult to restrain, and fickle. Still, O son of Kunti! it may be restrained by constant practice and by indifference (to worldly objects).

sanskrit: ताम् पुरीम् स महातेजा राजा दशरथो महान्
transliteration: tām purīm sa mahātejā rājā daśaratho mahān

sanskrit: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः
transliteration: asaṅyatātmanā yogo duṣhprāpa iti me matiḥ
english: It is my belief, that devotion is hard to obtain for one who does not restrain his self. But by one who is self-restrained and assiduous, it can be obtained through (proper) expedients.

sanskrit: ताम् सत्य नामाम् दृढ तोरण अर्गलाम्गृहैः विचित्रैः उपशोभिताम् शिवाम्
पुरीम् अयोध्याम् नृ सहस्र संकुलाम्शशास वै शक्र समो महीपतिः
transliteration: tām satya nāmām dṛḍha toraṇa argalāmgṛhaiḥ vicitraiḥ upaśobhitām śivām
purīm ayodhyām nṛ sahasra saṃkulāmśaśāsa vai śakra samo mahīpatiḥ
english: Repressing enemies, that city was governed by the great and the exceedingly. And that lord of earth resembling Sakra govemed that city of Ayodhya bearing a true name furnished with strong gates and bolts, and auspicious, and graced with excellent edifices, and teeming with thousands.

sanskrit: अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति
transliteration: aprāpya yoga-sansiddhiṁ kāṅ gatiṁ kṛiṣhṇa gachchhati
english: Arguna, said: What is the end of him, O Krishna! who does not attain the consummation of his devotion, being not assiduous, and having a mind shaken off from devotion, (though) full of faith?

sanskrit: तस्य अमात्या गुणैर् आसन् इक्ष्ह्वकोस्तु महात्मनः
मंत्रज्ञाः च इङ्गितज्ञाः च नित्यम् प्रिय हिते रताः
transliteration: tasya amātyā guṇair āsan ikṣhvakostu mahātmanaḥ
maṃtrajñāḥ ca iṅgitajñāḥ ca nityam priya hite ratāḥ
english: That high-souled one of Ikşvāku's line had competent counsellors, capable of administering business, of diving into the motives of others, and ever intent upon the good of the monarch. And that heroic king had eight famous Counsellors, pure and devoted to the royal service.
Does he, fallen from both (paths), go to ruin like a broken cloud, being, O you of mighty arms! without support, and deluded on the path (leading) to the Brahman?

sanskrit: अष्टौ बभूवुः वीरस्य तस्य अमात्या यशस्विनः
शुचयः च अनुरक्ताः च राजकृत्येषु नित्यशः
transliteration: aṣṭau babhūvuḥ vīrasya tasya amātyā yaśasvinaḥ
śucayaḥ ca anuraktāḥ ca rājakṛtyeṣu nityaśaḥ
english: That high-souled one of Ikşvāku's line had competent counsellors, capable of administering business, of diving into the motives of others, and ever intent upon the good of the monarch. And that heroic king had eight famous Counsellors, pure and devoted to the royal service.

transliteration: etan me sanśhayaṁ kṛiṣhṇa chhettum arhasyaśheṣhataḥ
english: Be pleased, O Krishna! to entirely destroy this doubt of mine, for none else than you can destroy this doubt.

sanskrit: धृष्टिर् जयन्तो विजयो सुराष्ट्रो राष्ट्र वर्धनः
अकोपो धर्मपालः च सुमंत्रः च अष्टमो अर्थवित्
transliteration: dhṛṣṭir jayanto vijayo surāṣṭro rāṣṭra vardhanaḥ
akopo dharmapālaḥ ca sumaṃtraḥ ca aṣṭamo arthavit
english: They were, Dhrsti, Jayanta, and Vijaya, and Surăştra, and Răstravardhana, and Akopa and Dharmapala, and Sumantra the cight, conversant with profit.

transliteration: pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśhas tasya vidyate
na hi kalyāṇa-kṛit kaśhchid durgatiṁ tāta gachchhati
english: The Deity said: O son of Pritha neither in this world nor the next, is ruin for him; for, O dear friend! none who performs good (deeds) comes to an evil end.

sanskrit: ऋत्विजौ द्वौ अभिमतौ तस्याः ताम् ऋषि सत्तमौ
वशिष्ठो वामदेवः च मंत्रिणः च तथा अपरे
transliteration: ṛtvijau dvau abhimatau tasyāḥ tām ṛṣi sattamau
vaśiṣṭho vāmadevaḥ ca maṃtriṇaḥ ca tathā apare
english: And he had two family priests beloved to him; viz., those foremost of saints. Vasistha and Vamadeva.

transliteration: prāpya puṇya-kṛitāṁ lokān uṣhitvā śhāśhvatīḥ samāḥ
english: He who is fallen from devotion attains the worlds of those who perform meritorious acts, dwells (there) for many a year, and is afterwards born into a family of holy and illustrious men.

sanskrit: सुयज्ञो अपि अथ जाबालिः काशय्पो अपि अथ गौतमः
मार्कण्डेयः तु दीर्घायुः तथा कात्यायनो द्विजः
transliteration: suyajño api atha jābāliḥ kāśaypo api atha gautamaḥ
mārkaṇḍeyaḥ tu dīrghāyuḥ tathā kātyāyano dvijaḥ
english: And he had other counsellors besides, viz; Suyajna, and Javali, and Kasyapa, and Gautama, and the long-lived Markandeya, and the regenerate Katyayana.

transliteration: atha vā yoginām eva kule bhavati dhīmatām
etad dhi durlabhataraṁ loke janma yad īdṛiśham
english: Or he is even born into a family of talented devotees; for such a birth as that in this world is more difficult to obtain.

sanskrit: एतैः ब्रह्मर्षिभिर् नित्यम् ऋत्विजः तस्य पौर्वकाः
transliteration: etaiḥ brahmarṣibhir nityam ṛtvijaḥ tasya paurvakāḥ

sanskrit: यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन
transliteration: yatate cha tato bhūyaḥ sansiddhau kuru-nandana
english: There he comes into contact with the knowledge which belonged to him in his former body, and then again, O descendant of Kuru! he works for perfection.

sanskrit: श्रीमन्तः च महात्मनः शास्त्रज्ञा धृढ विक्रमाः
transliteration: śrīmantaḥ ca mahātmanaḥ śāstrajñā dhṛḍha vikramāḥ

english: For even though reluctant, he is led away by the self-same former practice, and although he only wishes to learn devotion, he rises above the (fruits of action laid down in the) divine word.

sanskrit: तेजः क्षमा यशः प्राप्ताः स्मित पूर्व अभिभाषिणः
क्रोधात् काम अर्थ हेतोर् वा न ब्रूयुर् अनृतम् वचः
transliteration: tejaḥ kṣamā yaśaḥ prāptāḥ smita pūrva abhibhāṣiṇaḥ
krodhāt kāma artha hetor vā na brūyur anṛtam vacaḥ

english: But the devotee working with great efforts, and cleared of his sins, attains perfection after many births, and then reaches the supreme goal.

sanskrit: तेषाम् अविदितम् किंचत् श्वेषु नास्ति परेषु वा
क्रियमाणम् कृतम् वा अपि चारेण अपि चिकीर्षितम्
transliteration: teṣām aviditam kiṃcat śveṣu nāsti pareṣu vā
kriyamāṇam kṛtam vā api cāreṇa api cikīrṣitam
english: And they were not unknown to what was done or sought to be done in the midst of their own or a hostile party. And they were adept in intercourse with people, and well-tried in friendship by the monarch.
The devotee is esteemed higher than the performers of penances, higher even than the men of knowledge, and the devotee is higher than the men of action; therefore, O Arguna! become a devotee.

sanskrit: प्राप्त कालम् यथा दण्डम् धारयेयुः सुतेषु अपि
transliteration: prāpta kālam yathā daṇḍam dhārayeyuḥ suteṣu api
english: And they were not unknown to what was done or sought to be done in the midst of their own or a hostile party. And they were adept in intercourse with people, and well-tried in friendship by the monarch.

sanskrit: श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मां स मे युक्ततमो मतः
transliteration: śhraddhāvān bhajate yo māṁ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ
english: And even among all devotees, he who, being full of faith, worships me, with his inmost self intent on me, is esteemed by me to be the most devoted.

sanskrit: कोश संग्रहणे युक्ता बलस्य च परिग्रहे
अहितम् च अपि पुरुषम् न हिंस्युर् अविदूषकम्
transliteration: kośa saṃgrahaṇe yuktā balasya ca parigrahe
ahitam ca api puruṣam na hiṃsyur avidūṣakam
english: And they were ever busy in replenishing the exchequer and in levying troops. And they did not cherish ill will even towards enemies, when innocent.

sanskrit: असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु
transliteration: asanśhayaṁ samagraṁ māṁ yathā jñāsyasi tach chhṛiṇu
english: Deity said: O son of Pritha! now hear how you can without doubt know me fully, fixing your mind on me, and resting in me, and practising devotion.

sanskrit: वीराः च नियतोत्साहा राज शास्त्रम् अनुष्ठिताः
शुचीनाम् रक्षितारः च नित्यम् विषय वासिनाम्
transliteration: vīrāḥ ca niyatotsāhā rāja śāstram anuṣṭhitāḥ
śucīnām rakṣitāraḥ ca nityam viṣaya vāsinām
english: And they were heroic, and ever high-spirited, following policy, and protecting those citizens that were pure.
I will now tell you exhaustively about knowledge together with experience; that being known, there is nothing further left in this world to know.

sanskrit: ब्रह्म क्षत्रम् अहिंसन्तः ते कोशम् समपूरयन्
transliteration: brahma kṣatram ahiṃsantaḥ te kośam samapūrayan
english: And not bearing ill will towards Brahmaņas and Khatriyas, and filling the treasury, by inflicting punishments according lo the offences of the persons guilty.

transliteration: yatatām api siddhānāṁ kaśhchin māṁ vetti tattvataḥ
english: Among thousands of men, only some work for perfection; and even of those who have reached perfection, and who are assiduous, only some know me truly.

sanskrit: न आसीत् पुरे वा राष्ट्रे वा मृषा वादी नरः क्वचित्
transliteration: na āsīt pure vā rāṣṭre vā mṛṣā vādī naraḥ kvacit
english: And during the time when those pure ones of one mind presided over the justice of the kingdom, there was neither in the city nor the provinces any that was a liar, or 'wicked, or going after others' wives. And peace reigned all around the city and the provinces.

sanskrit: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च
transliteration: bhūmir-āpo ’nalo vāyuḥ khaṁ mano buddhir eva cha
ahankāra itīyaṁ me bhinnā prakṛitir aṣhṭadhā
english: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, understanding, and egoism, thus is my nature divided eightfold.

sanskrit: कश्चिन् न दुष्टः तत्र आसीत् पर दार रतिर् नरः
प्रशांतम् सर्वम् एव असीत् राष्ट्रम् पुरवरम् च तत्
transliteration: kaścin na duṣṭaḥ tatra āsīt para dāra ratir naraḥ
praśāṃtam sarvam eva asīt rāṣṭram puravaram ca tat
apareyam itas tvanyāṁ prakṛitiṁ viddhi me parām
english: But this is a lower (form of my) natureKnow (that there is) another (form of my) nature, and higher than this, which is animate, O you of mighty arms! and by which this universe is upheld.

sanskrit: सु वासस सु वेषाः च ते च सर्वे शुचिव्रताः
हितार्थः च नरेन्द्रस्य जाग्रतो नय चक्षुषा
transliteration: su vāsasa su veṣāḥ ca te ca sarve śucivratāḥ
hitārthaḥ ca narendrasya jāgrato naya cakṣuṣā
english: And the ministers wore excellent raiment, and ornaments, and were engaged in observing pure Vows, and ever kept their eye of policy open in the interest of the monarch.

transliteration: ahaṁ kṛitsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā
english: Know that all things have these (for their) sourceI am the producer and the destroyer of the whole universe.

sanskrit: गुरोर् गुण गृहीताः च प्रख्याताः च पराक्रमे
विदेशेषु अपि विज्ञाता सर्वतो बुद्धि निश्चयाः
transliteration: guror guṇa gṛhītāḥ ca prakhyātāḥ ca parākrame
videśeṣu api vijñātā sarvato buddhi niścayāḥ
english: And the king considered them as crowned with virtues, and they were famed on account of their prowess, concluding unerringly in consequence of their intelligence of other countries. And in all climes and times they could manifest their noble qualities.

sanskrit: मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव
transliteration: mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat kiñchid asti dhanañjaya
mayi sarvam idaṁ protaṁ sūtre maṇi-gaṇā iva
english: There is nothing else, O Dhanangaya! higher than myself; all this is woven upon me, like numbers of pearls upon a thread.

sanskrit: अभितो गुणवन्तः च न च आसन् गुण वर्जिताः
transliteration: abhito guṇavantaḥ ca na ca āsan guṇa varjitāḥ
english: They inculcated noble qualities in all aspects and were not devoid of virtues. And they were cognizant of war and peace, and possessed of goodness, passion and ignorance.

sanskrit: प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु
transliteration: praṇavaḥ sarva-vedeṣhu śhabdaḥ khe pauruṣhaṁ nṛiṣhu
english: I am the taste in water, O son of Kunti! I am the light of the sun and moon. I am 'Om' in all the Vedas, sound in space, and manliness in human beings;

sanskrit: मंत्र संवरणे शक्ताः शक्ताः सूक्ष्मासु बुद्धिषु
नीति शास्त्र विशेषज्ञाः सततम् प्रिय वादिनः
transliteration: maṃtra saṃvaraṇe śaktāḥ śaktāḥ sūkṣmāsu buddhiṣu
nīti śāstra viśeṣajñāḥ satatam priya vādinaḥ
english: And they could keep their counsel and judge of things finely, and were well-versed in the art of policy, and ever fair-spoken.

sanskrit: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ
transliteration: puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛithivyāṁ cha tejaśh chāsmi vibhāvasau
english: I am the fragrant smell in the earth, refulgence in the fire; I am life in all beings, and penance in those who perform penance.

sanskrit: ईदृशैः तैः अमात्यैः च राजा दशरथोऽनघः
transliteration: īdṛśaiḥ taiḥ amātyaiḥ ca rājā daśaratho'naghaḥ
english: Surrounded by such counseliors endowed with various qualities, the faultless king Dasaratha ruled the earth.

sanskrit: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम्
transliteration: bījaṁ māṁ sarva-bhūtānāṁ viddhi pārtha sanātanam
buddhir buddhimatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham
english: Know me, O son of Pritha! to be the eternal seed of all beings; I am the discernment of the discerning ones, and I the glory of the glorious.
And gathering intelligence by means of spies, and righteously protecting the subjects, and preserving the people, and not sacrificing his duties.
I am also the strength, unaccompanied by fondness or desire, of the strong. And, O chief of the descendants of Bharata! I am love unopposed to piety among all beings.

sanskrit: विश्रुतः त्रिषु लोकेषु वदान्यः सत्य संगरः
स तत्र पुरुषव्याघ्रः शशास पृथ्वीम् इमाम्
transliteration: viśrutaḥ triṣu lokeṣu vadānyaḥ satya saṃgaraḥ
sa tatra puruṣavyāghraḥ śaśāsa pṛthvīm imām
english: Famed over the three worlds, and munificent, and linn in promise in battle, the tiger among men ruled over this earth.

sanskrit: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि
transliteration: ye chaiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāśh cha ye
matta eveti tān viddhi na tvahaṁ teṣhu te mayi
english: And all entities which are of the quality of goodness, and those which are of the quality of passion and of darkness, know that they are, indeed, all from me; I am not in them, but they are in me.

sanskrit: न अध्यगच्छत् विशिष्टम् वा तुल्यम् वा शत्रुम् आत्मनः
मित्रवान् नत सामन्तः प्रताप हत कण्टकः
स शशास जगत् राजा दिवि देव पतिर् यथा
transliteration: na adhyagacchat viśiṣṭam vā tulyam vā śatrum ātmanaḥ
mitravān nata sāmantaḥ pratāpa hata kaṇṭakaḥ
sa śaśāsa jagat rājā divi deva patir yathā
english: Nor did he ever meet with a foe that was either his equal or superior. And possessed of friends, and having obedient commanders, and extricating his thorns by his might, that king ruled the earth, even as the lord of celestials rules heaven.

transliteration: tribhir guṇa-mayair bhāvair ebhiḥ sarvam idaṁ jagat
english: The whole universe deluded by these three states of mind, developed from the qualities, does not know me, who am beyond them and inexhaustible;

sanskrit: तैः मंत्रिभिः मंत्र हितेः निविष्टैःवृतोऽनुरक्तैः कुशलैः समर्थैः
स पार्थिवो दीप्तिम् अवाप युक्तःतेजोमयैः गोभिः इव उदितः अर्कः
transliteration: taiḥ maṃtribhiḥ maṃtra hiteḥ niviṣṭaiḥvṛto'nuraktaiḥ kuśalaiḥ samarthaiḥ
sa pārthivo dīptim avāpa yuktaḥtejomayaiḥ gobhiḥ iva uditaḥ arkaḥ
english: And surrounded by those counsellors studious of his welfare, and bearing affection towards him, and clever, and competent, that king, by virtue of his prowess in subduing others, resembled the sun surrounded by his rays.

sanskrit: दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते
transliteration: daivī hyeṣhā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā
mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te
english: for this delusion of mine, developed from the qualities, is divine and difficult to transcend. Those who resort to me alone cross beyond this delusion.

sanskrit: तस्य च एवम् प्रभावस्य धर्मज्ञस्य महात्मनः
सुतार्थम् तप्य मानस्य न असीत् वंशकरः सुतः
transliteration: tasya ca evam prabhāvasya dharmajñasya mahātmanaḥ
sutārtham tapya mānasya na asīt vaṃśakaraḥ sutaḥ
english: And although engaged in austerities with the view of having sons born to him, the powerful and high-souled king, had no son capable of perpetuating his race.

sanskrit: न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः
transliteration: na māṁ duṣhkṛitino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ
english: Wicked men, doers of evil (acts), who are deluded, who are deprived of their knowledge by (this) delusion, and who incline to the demoniac state of mind, do not resort to me.

sanskrit: चिन्तयानस्य तस्य एवम् बुद्धिः आसीन् महात्मनः
सुतार्थम् वाजिमेधेन किम् अर्थम् न यजामि अहम्
transliteration: cintayānasya tasya evam buddhiḥ āsīn mahātmanaḥ
sutārtham vājimedhena kim artham na yajāmi aham
