sanskrit: न च अवज्ञा प्रयोक्तव्या काम क्रोध वशात् अपि
यज्ञ कर्मसु ये व्यग्राः पुरुषाः शिल्पिनः तथा
transliteration: na ca avajñā prayoktavyā kāma krodha vaśāt api
yajña karmasu ye vyagrāḥ puruṣāḥ śilpinaḥ tathā

sanskrit: दिशो न जाने न लभे च शर्म
transliteration: diśho na jāne na labhe cha śharma
english: And seeing your mouths terrible by the jaws, and resembling the fire of destruction, I cannot recognise the (various) directions, I feel no comfort. Be gracious, O lord of gods! who pervadest the universe.

sanskrit: तेषाम् अपि विशेषेण पूजा कार्या यथा क्रमम्
ये स्युः संपूजिता सर्वे वसुभिः भोजनेन च
transliteration: teṣām api viśeṣeṇa pūjā kāryā yathā kramam
ye syuḥ saṃpūjitā sarve vasubhiḥ bhojanena ca

english: And all these sons of Dhritarashtra, together with all the bands of kings, and Bhishma and Drona, and this charioteer's son likewise, together with our principal warriors also,

sanskrit: यथा सर्वम् सुविहितम् न किंचित् परिहीयते
तथा भवन्तः कुर्वन्तु प्रीति युक्तेन चेतसा
transliteration: yathā sarvam suvihitam na kiṃcit parihīyate
tathā bhavantaḥ kurvantu prīti yuktena cetasā
english: And servants, who being entertained with gifts, do everything completely, and omit nothing. And do you, with hearts mollified by love, act so, that all our friends be well pleased with us.

transliteration: vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti daṁṣṭrā-karālāni bhayānakāni kecid vilagnā daśanāntareṣu sandṛśyante cūrṇitair uttamāṅgaiḥ
english: are rapidly entering your mouths, fearful and horrific by (reason of your) jaws. And some with their heads smashed are seen (to be) stuck in the spaces between the teeth.

sanskrit: ततः सर्वे समागम्य वसिष्ठम् इदम् अब्रुवन्
यथेष्टम् तत् सुविहितम् न किंचित् परिहीयते
transliteration: tataḥ sarve samāgamya vasiṣṭham idam abruvan
yatheṣṭam tat suvihitam na kiṃcit parihīyate

english: As the many rapid currents of a river's waters run towards the sea alone, so do these heroes of the human world enter your mouths blazing all round.

sanskrit: यथोक्तम् तत् करिष्यामो न किंचित् परिहीयते
ततः सुमंत्रम् आहूय वसिष्ठो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: yathoktam tat kariṣyāmo na kiṃcit parihīyate
tataḥ sumaṃtram āhūya vasiṣṭho vākyam abravīt

english: As butterflies, with increased velocity, enter a blazing fire to their destruction, so too do these people enter your mouths with increased velocity (only) to their destruction.

sanskrit: निमंत्रयस्व नृपतीन् पृथिव्याम् ये च धार्मिकाः
ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियान् वैश्यान् शूद्राम् च एव सहस्रशः
transliteration: nimaṃtrayasva nṛpatīn pṛthivyām ye ca dhārmikāḥ
brāhmaṇān kṣatriyān vaiśyān śūdrām ca eva sahasraśaḥ

english: Swallowing all these people, you are licking them over and over again from all sides, with your blazing mouths. Your fierce splendours, O Vishnu! filling the whole universe with (their) effulgence, are heating it.
With proper honour yourself bring the righteous, truthful, and heroic Janaka, lord of Mithilā. And it is because he is our old friend that I first mention him.
Tell me who you are in this fierce form. Salutations be to thee, O chief of the gods! Be gracious. I wish to know you, the primeval one, for I do not understand your actions.

sanskrit: तम् आनय महाभागम् स्वयम् एव सुसत्कृतम्
पूर्व संबन्धिनम् ज्ञात्वा ततः पूर्वम् ब्रवीमि ते
transliteration: tam ānaya mahābhāgam svayam eva susatkṛtam
pūrva saṃbandhinam jñātvā tataḥ pūrvam bravīmi te
english: With proper honour yourself bring the righteous, truthful, and heroic Janaka, lord of Mithilā. And it is because he is our old friend that I first mention him.

The Deity said: I am death, the destroyer of the worlds, fully developed, and I am now active about the overthrow of the worlds. Even without you, the warriors standing in the adverse hosts, shall all cease to be.

sanskrit: तथा काशी पतिम् स्निग्धम् सततम् प्रिय वादिनम्
सद् वृत्तम् देवसंकाशम् स्वयम् एव अनयस्व ह
transliteration: tathā kāśī patim snigdham satatam priya vādinam
sad vṛttam devasaṃkāśam svayam eva anayasva ha
english: Then do yourself bring the amiable and ever fair-spoken lord of Kāśī, of excellent character, resembling a celestial.
Therefore, be up, obtain glory, and vanquishing (your) foes, enjoy a prosperous kingdom. All these have been already killed by me. Be only the instrument, O Savyasakin!

sanskrit: तथा केकय राजानम् वृद्धम् परम धार्मिकम्
श्वशुरम् राज सिंहस्य सपुत्रम् त्वम् इह आनय
transliteration: tathā kekaya rājānam vṛddham parama dhārmikam
śvaśuram rāja siṃhasya saputram tvam iha ānaya
english: Then do you bring here along with his son, the highly-pious, old king of Kekaya, who is the father-in-law of this tiger of a monarch.

sanskrit: द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च
transliteration: droṇaṁ cha bhīṣhmaṁ cha jayadrathaṁ cha
mayā hatāṁs tvaṁ jahi mā vyathiṣhṭhā
english: Drona, and Bhishma, and Gayadratha, and Karna, and likewise other valiant warriors also, whom I have killed, do you kill. Be not alarmed. Do fight. And in the battle you will conquer (your) foes.

sanskrit: वयस्यम् राज सिंहस्य सपुत्रम् तम् इह आनय
transliteration: vayasyam rāja siṃhasya saputram tam iha ānaya
english: Then also bring with due honours the king of Anga, and that mighty archer, the illustrious Romapada, the friend of that lion among the kings, along with his son.

Sangaya said: Hearing these words of Kesava, the wearer of the coronet, trembling, and with joined hands, bowed down and sorely afraid, and with throat choked up, he again spoke to Krishna after saluting him.

sanskrit: मगध अधिपतिम् शूरम् सर्व शास्त्र विशारदम्
transliteration: magadha adhipatim śūram sarva śāstra viśāradam

english: Arguna said: It is quite proper, O Hrishikesa! that the universe is delighted and charmed by your renown, that the demons run away affrighted in all directions, and that all the assemblages of Siddhas bow down (to you).

sanskrit: प्राचीनान् सिन्धु सौवीरान् सौराष्ठ्रेयाम् च पार्थिवान्
transliteration: prācīnān sindhu sauvīrān saurāṣṭhreyām ca pārthivān
kasmāch cha te na nameran mahātman
tvam akṣharaṁ sad-asat tat paraṁ yat
english: And why, O high-souled one! should they not bow down to you (who are) greater than Brahman, and first cause? O infinite lord of gods! O you pervading the universe! you are the indestructible, that which is, that which is not, and what is beyond them.

sanskrit: दाक्षिणात्यान् नरेन्द्राम् च समस्तान् आनयस्व ह
सन्ति स्निग्धाः च ये च अन्ये राजानः पृथिवी तले
transliteration: dākṣiṇātyān narendrām ca samastān ānayasva ha
santi snigdhāḥ ca ye ca anye rājānaḥ pṛthivī tale

sanskrit: वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम
transliteration: vettāsi vedyaṁ cha paraṁ cha dhāma
english: You are the primal god, the ancient being, you are the highest support of this universe. You are that which has knowledge, that which is the object of knowledge, you are the highest goal. By you is this universe pervaded, O you of infinite forms!

sanskrit: तान् आनय यथा क्षिप्रम् स अनुगान् सह बान्धवान्
एतान् दूतैः महाभागैः आनयस्व नृप आज्ञ्या
transliteration: tān ānaya yathā kṣipram sa anugān saha bāndhavān
etān dūtaiḥ mahābhāgaiḥ ānayasva nṛpa ājñyā
punaśh cha bhūyo ’pi namo namas te
english: You are the wind, Yama, fire, Varuna, the moon, you Pragapati, and the great grandsire. Obeisance be to thee a thousand times, and again and again obeisance to thee!

sanskrit: वसिष्ठ वाक्यम् तत् श्रुत्वा सुमंत्रः त्वरितः तदा
व्यादिशत् पुरुषान् तत्र राज्ञाम् आनयने शुभान्
transliteration: vasiṣṭha vākyam tat śrutvā sumaṃtraḥ tvaritaḥ tadā
vyādiśat puruṣān tatra rājñām ānayane śubhān
english: Having heard those words of Vasistha, Sumantra speedily ordered the emissaries to bring the kings.
In front and from behind obeisance to thee! Obeisance be to thee from all sides, O you who are all! You are of infinite power, of unmeasured glory; you pervade all, and therefore you are all!

sanskrit: स्वयम् एव हि धर्मात्मा प्रयातो मुनि शासनात्
transliteration: svayam eva hi dharmātmā prayāto muni śāsanāt
english: The virtuous Sumantra, in accordance with the injunction of the ascetic, himself speedily set out for the purpose of bringing the monarchs.

sanskrit: हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति
transliteration: he kṛiṣhṇa he yādava he sakheti
english: Whatever I have said contemptuously, for instance, 'O Krishna!' 'O Yadava!' 'O friend!' thinking you to be (my) friend, and not knowing your greatness (as shown in) this (universal form),

sanskrit: ते च कर्मान्तिकाः सर्वे वसिष्ठाय च महर्षये
सर्वम् निवेदयन्ति स्म यज्ञे यत् उपकल्पितम्
transliteration: te ca karmāntikāḥ sarve vasiṣṭhāya ca maharṣaye
sarvam nivedayanti sma yajñe yat upakalpitam
english: Then the servants came and informed the intelligent Vasiştha as to the articles that had been got ready for the sacrifice.

or through friendliness, or incautiously; and whatever disrespect I have shown you for purposes of merriment, on (occasions of) play, sleep, dinner, or sitting (together), whether alone or in the presence (of friends), for all that, O undegraded one! I ask pardon of you who are indefinable.

sanskrit: ततः प्रीतो द्विज श्रेष्ठः तान् सर्वान् मुनिर् अब्रवीत्
अवज्ञया न दातव्यम् कस्य चित् लीलया अपि वा
transliteration: tataḥ prīto dvija śreṣṭhaḥ tān sarvān munir abravīt
avajñayā na dātavyam kasya cit līlayā api vā
english: Then well pleased that best of twice-born ones, the ascetic Vasistha, said to them, Do not give away disrespectfully or lightly. A gift bestowed with disrespect, indubitably destroy the giver.

transliteration: tvam asya pūjyaśh cha gurur garīyān
english: You are the father of the world movable and immovable you its great and venerable master; there is none equal to you, whence can there be one greater, O you whose power is unparalleled in all the three worlds?

sanskrit: अवज्ञया कृतम् हन्यात् दातारम् न अत्र संशयः
ततः कैश्चित् अहो रात्रैः उपयाता महीक्षितः
transliteration: avajñayā kṛtam hanyāt dātāram na atra saṃśayaḥ
tataḥ kaiścit aho rātraiḥ upayātā mahīkṣitaḥ

english: Therefore I bow and prostrate myself, and would propitiate you, the praiseworthy lord. Be pleased, O god! to pardon (my guilt) as a father (that of his) son, a friend (that of his) friend, or a husband (that of his) beloved.

sanskrit: बहूनि रत्नानि आदाय राज्ञो दशरथस्य ह
ततो वसिष्ठः सुप्रीतो राजानम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: bahūni ratnāni ādāya rājño daśarathasya ha
tato vasiṣṭhaḥ suprīto rājānam idam abravīt
tad eva me darśhaya deva rūpaṁ
english: I am delighted at seeing what I had never seen before, and my heart is also alarmed by fear. Show me that same form, O god! Be gracious, O lord of gods! O you pervading the universe!

sanskrit: उपयाता नर व्याघ्र राजानः तव शासनात्
मया अपि सत्कृताः सर्वे यथा अर्हम् राज सत्तम
transliteration: upayātā nara vyāghra rājānaḥ tava śāsanāt
mayā api satkṛtāḥ sarve yathā arham rāja sattama
english: Thereupon Vasiştha well-pleased said to the king, O tiger among men, obeying your mandate the kings have come here; and I too according to merit, have received those excellent kings with respect.
I wish to see you bearing the coronet and the mace, with the discus in hand, just the same (as before). O you of thousand arms! O you of all forms! assume that same four-handed form.

sanskrit: यज्ञीयम् च कृतम् सर्वम् पुरुषैः सुसमाहितैः
निर्यातु च भवान् यष्टुम् यज्ञ आयतनम् अन्तिकात्
transliteration: yajñīyam ca kṛtam sarvam puruṣaiḥ susamāhitaiḥ
niryātu ca bhavān yaṣṭum yajña āyatanam antikāt
english: Everything has been carefully made ready for the sacrifice by the persons concerned. Do you, therefore, repair to the sacrificial ground, for performing the sacrifice.

transliteration: yan me tvad anyena na dṛiṣhṭa-pūrvam
english: The Deity said: O Arguna! being pleased (with you), I have by my own mystic power shown you this supreme form, full of glory, universal, infinite, primeval, and which has not been seen before by any one else but you, O you hero among the Kauravas!
O foremost of monarchs, it behove you to view the place, filled with all desirable objects, and looking as if prepared by imagination herself.

transliteration: na cha kriyābhir na tapobhir ugraiḥ
english: I cannot be seen in this form by any one but you, (even) by (the help of) the study of the Vedas, or of sacrifices, nor by gifts, nor by actions, nor by fierce penances.

sanskrit: तथा वसिष्ठ वचनात् ऋष्यशृन्गस्य च उभयोः
transliteration: tathā vasiṣṭha vacanāt ṛṣyaśṛngasya ca ubhayoḥ
english: Then in accordance with the injunctions of both Vasiştha and Rşyasſga, the king came to the sacrificial spot on a day presided over by an auspicious star.

sanskrit: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो
transliteration: mā te vyathā mā cha vimūḍha-bhāvo
tad eva me rūpam idaṁ prapaśhya
english: Be not alarmed, be not perplexed, at seeing this form of mine, fearful like this. Free from fear and with delighted heart, see now again that same form of mine.

sanskrit: ततो वसिष्ठ प्रमुखाः सर्व एव द्विजोत्तमाः
ऋष्यशृन्गम् पुरस्कृत्य यज्ञ कर्म आरभन् तदा
transliteration: tato vasiṣṭha pramukhāḥ sarva eva dvijottamāḥ
ṛṣyaśṛngam puraskṛtya yajña karma ārabhan tadā
english: Then, with, Rsyasrriga at their head, Vasistha and the other principal Brāhmaṇas wending to the sacrificial ground, began the ceremony, according to the ordinance; and in due form. And the auspicious king, in company with his wives, was initiated into the ceremony.
Sangaya said: Having thus spoken to Arguna, Vasudeva again showed his own form, and the high-souled one becoming again of a mild form, comforted him who had been affrighted.

sanskrit: यज्ञ वाटम् गताः सर्वे यथा शास्त्रम् यथा विधि
श्रीमान् च सह पत्नीभी राजा दीक्षाम् उपाविशत्
transliteration: yajña vāṭam gatāḥ sarve yathā śāstram yathā vidhi
śrīmān ca saha patnībhī rājā dīkṣām upāviśat
english: Then, with, Rsyasrriga at their head, Vasistha and the other principal Brāhmaṇas wending to the sacrificial ground, began the ceremony, according to the ordinance; and in due form. And the auspicious king, in company with his wives, was initiated into the ceremony.

transliteration: dṛiṣhṭvedaṁ mānuṣhaṁ rūpaṁ tava saumyaṁ janārdana
idānīm asmi saṁvṛittaḥ sa-chetāḥ prakṛitiṁ gataḥ
english: Arguna said: O Ganardana! seeing this mild, human form of yours, I am now in my right mind, and have come to my normal state.

sanskrit: अथ संवत्सरे पूर्णे तस्मिन् प्राप्ते तुरंगमे
सरय्वाः च उत्तरे तीरे राज्ञो यज्ञो अभ्यवर्तत
transliteration: atha saṃvatsare pūrṇe tasmin prāpte turaṃgame
sarayvāḥ ca uttare tīre rājño yajño abhyavartata
english: After the expiry of full one year, when the sacrificial horse had returned, the sacrifice, of the king commenced on the north bank of the Sarayu.

transliteration: su-durdarśham idaṁ rūpaṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi yan mama
devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṁ darśhana-kāṅkṣhiṇaḥ
english: The Deity said: Even the gods are always desiring to see this form of mine, which it is difficult to get a sight of, and which you have seen.
And with Rşyasſága at their head, the principal twice-born ones began the proceedings in that mighty horse-sacrifice of that high-souled monarch.

sanskrit: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया
शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा
transliteration: nāhaṁ vedair na tapasā na dānena na chejyayā
śhakya evaṁ-vidho draṣhṭuṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi māṁ yathā
english: I cannot be seen, as you have seen me, by (means of) the Vedas, not by penance, not by gift, nor yet by sacrifice.

sanskrit: यथा विधि यथा न्यायं परिक्रामन्ति शास्त्रतः
transliteration: yathā vidhi yathā nyāyaṃ parikrāmanti śāstrataḥ
english: And the priests, each duly and according to the ordinance performing his proper part, engaged in the ceremony in consonance with the scriptures.

sanskrit: ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप
transliteration: bhaktyā tv ananyayā śhakya aham evaṁ-vidho ’rjuna
jñātuṁ draṣhṭuṁ cha tattvena praveṣhṭuṁ cha parantapa
english: But, O Arguna! by devotion to me exclusively, I can in this form be truly known, seen, and assimilated with, O terror of your foes!

sanskrit: प्रवर्ग्यम् शास्त्रतः कृत्वा तथा एव उपसदम् द्विजाः
चक्रुः च विधिवत् सर्वम् अधिकम् कर्म शास्त्रतः
transliteration: pravargyam śāstrataḥ kṛtvā tathā eva upasadam dvijāḥ
cakruḥ ca vidhivat sarvam adhikam karma śāstrataḥ
english: And the regenerate ones, having performed the pravargya as well as the upasada according to the ordinance, duly completed the additional ceremonies. Then, worshipping the deities with glad hearts, those foremost of ascetics duly performed the morning ablutions and the other prescribed rites.

sanskrit: निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव
transliteration: nirvairaḥ sarva-bhūteṣhu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava
english: He who performs acts for (propitiating) me, to whom I am the highest (object), who is my devotee, who is free from attachment, and who has no enmity towards any being, he, O son of Pandu I comes to me.

sanskrit: अभिपूज्य तदा हृष्टाः सर्वे चक्रुः यथा विधि
transliteration: abhipūjya tadā hṛṣṭāḥ sarve cakruḥ yathā vidhi
english: And the regenerate ones, having performed the pravargya as well as the upasada according to the ordinance, duly completed the additional ceremonies. Then, worshipping the deities with glad hearts, those foremost of ascetics duly performed the morning ablutions and the other prescribed rites.

sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचएवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते
transliteration: evaṁ satata-yuktā ye bhaktās tvāṁ paryupāsate
ye chāpy akṣharam avyaktaṁ teṣhāṁ ke yoga-vittamāḥ
english: Arguna said: Of the worshippers, who thus, constantly devoted, meditate on you, and those who (meditate) on the unperceived and indestructible, which do best know devotion?

sanskrit: ऐन्द्रश्च विधिवत् दत्तो राजा च अभिषुतोऽनघः
मध्यंदिनम् च सवनम् प्रावर्तत यथा क्रमम्
transliteration: aindraśca vidhivat datto rājā ca abhiṣuto'naghaḥ
madhyaṃdinam ca savanam prāvartata yathā kramam
english: The oblations of clarified butter first having been offered to Indra, according to the ritual, the king with a purified heart performed his ablutions. And then the mid-day ablutions took place in proper sequence.

sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते
transliteration: mayy āveśhya mano ye māṁ nitya-yuktā upāsate
śhraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamā matāḥ
english: The Deity said: Those who being constantly devoted, and possessed of the highest faith, worship me with a mind fixed on me, are deemed by me to be the most devoted.

sanskrit: चक्रुः ते शाश्त्रतो दृष्ट्वा तथा ब्राह्मण पुंगवाः
transliteration: cakruḥ te śāśtrato dṛṣṭvā tathā brāhmaṇa puṃgavāḥ
english: Those foremost of Brahmanas, in due form, and according to the ordinance, officiated at the third bath of that high-souled monarch.

transliteration: ye tv akṣharam anirdeśhyam avyaktaṁ paryupāsate
te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ
english: But those, who, restraining the (whole) group of the senses, and with a mind at all times equable, meditate on the indescribable, indestructible, unperceived (principle) which is all-pervading, unthinkable, indifferent,
The priests presided over by Rşyasſiga, invoked Śakra and the other deities, reciting measured mantras.

transliteration: sanniyamyendriya-grāmaṁ sarvatra sama-buddhayaḥ te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ
english: immovable, and constant, they, intent on the good of all beings, necessarily attain to me.

sanskrit: गीतिभिः मधुरैः स्निग्धैः मन्त्र आह्वानैः यथार्हतः
transliteration: gītibhiḥ madhuraiḥ snigdhaiḥ mantra āhvānaiḥ yathārhataḥ
english: The sacrificial priests, chanting sweet Samans and soft mantras, duly invoking the dwellers of the celestial regions, offered each his share of the oblations.

transliteration: avyaktā hi gatir duḥkhaṁ dehavadbhir avāpyate
english: For those whose minds are attached to the unperceived, the trouble is much greater.

sanskrit: न च अहुतं आभूत् तत्र स्खलितम् वा न किंचन
दृश्यते ब्रह्मवत् सर्वम् क्षेमयुक्तम् हि चक्रिरे
transliteration: na ca ahutaṃ ābhūt tatra skhalitam vā na kiṃcana
dṛśyate brahmavat sarvam kṣemayuktam hi cakrire
english: And no part of the ceremony was performed improperly, or left out, and every thing was satisfactorily celebrated with mantras.

sanskrit: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः
transliteration: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat-paraḥ
english: Because the unperceived goal is obtained by embodied (beings) with difficulty.

sanskrit: न तेषु अहस्सु श्रान्तो वा क्षुधितो वा न दृश्यते
न अविद्वान् ब्राह्मणः कश्चिन् न अशत अनुचरः तथा
transliteration: na teṣu ahassu śrānto vā kṣudhito vā na dṛśyate
na avidvān brāhmaṇaḥ kaścin na aśata anucaraḥ tathā
english: And on that day no Brāhmaṇa ever felt tired, or hungry and there was none that was not learned, or that was not followed by an hundred persons.

transliteration: bhavāmi na chirāt pārtha mayy āveśhita-chetasām
english: As to those, however, O son of Pritha! who, dedicating all their actions to me, and (holding) me as their highest (goal), worship me, meditating on me with a devotion towards none besides me, and whose minds are fixed on me, I, without delay, come forward as their deliverer from the ocean of this world of death.

sanskrit: ब्राह्मणा भुंजते नित्यम् नाथवन्तः च भुंजते
तापसा भुंजते च अपि श्रमणाः चैव भुंजते
transliteration: brāhmaṇā bhuṃjate nityam nāthavantaḥ ca bhuṃjate
tāpasā bhuṃjate ca api śramaṇāḥ caiva bhuṃjate
english: Brāhmaṇas, and Śūdras having among them ascetics, and Sramanas, and the aged, and the infirm, and women, and children, were continually fed. And although they ate their fill, yet they know no repletion.

sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय
निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः
transliteration: mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṁ niveśhaya
nivasiṣhyasi mayy eva ata ūrdhvaṁ na sanśhayaḥ
english: Place your mind on me only; fix your understanding on me. In me you will dwell, hereafter, (there is) no doubt.

sanskrit: वृद्धाः च व्याधिताः च एव स्त्री बालाः तथा एव च
transliteration: vṛddhāḥ ca vyādhitāḥ ca eva strī bālāḥ tathā eva ca
english: Brāhmaṇas, and Śūdras having among them ascetics, and Sramanas, and the aged, and the infirm, and women, and children, were continually fed. And although they ate their fill, yet they know no repletion.

sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम्
transliteration: atha chittaṁ samādhātuṁ na śhaknoṣhi mayi sthiram
english: But if you are unable to fix your mind steadily on me, then, O Dhanangaya! endeavour to obtain me by the abstraction of mind (resulting) from continuous meditation.

sanskrit: दीयताम् दीयताम् अन्नम् वासांसि विविधानि च
इति संचोदिताः तत्र तथा चक्रुः अनेकशः
transliteration: dīyatām dīyatām annam vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca
iti saṃcoditāḥ tatra tathā cakruḥ anekaśaḥ
english: And Give food, and clothes of various kinds (was heard all around) And those employed in the task gave away profusely.

transliteration: mad-artham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi
english: If you are unequal even to continuous meditation, then let acts for (propitiating) me be your highest (aim). Even performing actions for (propitiating) me, you will attain perfection.

sanskrit: अन्न कूटाः च दृश्यन्ते बहवः पर्वत उपमाः
दिवसे दिवसे तत्र सिद्धस्य विधिवत् तदा
transliteration: anna kūṭāḥ ca dṛśyante bahavaḥ parvata upamāḥ
divase divase tatra siddhasya vidhivat tadā
english: And every day food dressed properly in due form was to be seen in countless heaps resembling hills.

transliteration: athaitad apy aśhakto ’si kartuṁ mad-yogam āśhritaḥ
english: If you are unable to do even this, then resort to devotion to me, and, with self-restraint, abandon all fruit of action.

sanskrit: नाना देशात् अनुप्राप्ताः पुरुषाः स्त्री गणाः तथा
अन्न पानैः सुविहिताः तस्मिन् यज्ञे महात्मनः
transliteration: nānā deśāt anuprāptāḥ puruṣāḥ strī gaṇāḥ tathā
anna pānaiḥ suvihitāḥ tasmin yajñe mahātmanaḥ
english: And men and women coming from various countries to the sacrifice of that high-souled one were excellently entertained with meats and drinks.

transliteration: śhreyo hi jñānam abhyāsāj jñānād dhyānaṁ viśhiṣhyate
english: For knowledge is better than continuous meditation; concentration is esteemed higher than knowledge; and the abandonment of fruit of action than concentration; from (that) abandonment, tranquillity soon (results).

sanskrit: अन्नम् हि विधिवत् स्वादु प्रशन्सन्ति द्विजर्षभाः
अहो तृप्ताः स्म भद्रम् ते इति शुश्राव राघवः
transliteration: annam hi vidhivat svādu praśansanti dvijarṣabhāḥ
aho tṛptāḥ sma bhadram te iti śuśrāva rāghavaḥ
english: The foremost regenerate ones said, The viands have been prepared in the prescribed form, and they taste excellent. We have been gratified. God bless you! All this was heard by the descendant of Raghu.

sanskrit: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च
transliteration: adveṣhṭā sarva-bhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva cha
english: That devotee of mine, who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, who is free from egoism, and from (the idea that this or that is) mine, to whom happiness and misery are alike, who is forgiving,

sanskrit: उपासन्ते च तान् अन्ये सुमृष्ट मणि कुण्डलाः
transliteration: upāsante ca tān anye sumṛṣṭa maṇi kuṇḍalāḥ
english: Persons adorned with ornaments distributed the victuals among the Brāhmaṇas, and they were assisted by others wearing jewelled pendants.

transliteration: mayy arpita-mano-buddhir yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
english: contented, constantly devoted, self-restrained, and firm in his determinations, and whose mind and understanding are devoted to me, he is dear to me.
In the interval between the completion of one bath and the beginning of the next, mild and eloquent Vipras, desirous of victory, engaged in various disputations.

sanskrit: हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः
transliteration: yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate cha yaḥ
harṣhāmarṣha-bhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa cha me priyaḥ
english: He through whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world, who is free from joy and anger and fear and agitation, he too is dear to me.

sanskrit: दिवसे दिवसे तत्र संस्तरे कुशला द्विजाः
सर्व कर्माणि चक्रुः ते यथा शास्त्रं प्रचोदिताः
transliteration: divase divase tatra saṃstare kuśalā dvijāḥ
sarva karmāṇi cakruḥ te yathā śāstraṃ pracoditāḥ
english: Every day in that sacrifice, skilful Brāhmaṇas, engaged in the ceremony, did everything, according to the ritual.

sanskrit: सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः
transliteration: sarvārambha-parityāgī yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
english: That devotee of mine, who is unconcerned, pure, assiduous, impartial, free from distress, who abandons all actions (for fruit), he is dear to me.

sanskrit: न अषडङ्ग वित् अत्र आसीत् न अव्रतो न अबहुश्रुतः
सदस्यः तस्य वै राज्ञो न अवाद कुशला द्विजाः
transliteration: na aṣaḍaṅga vit atra āsīt na avrato na abahuśrutaḥ
sadasyaḥ tasya vai rājño na avāda kuśalā dvijāḥ
english: There was no twice-born one that was not versed in the Vedas and the Vedāngas, or that did not observe vows, or that was not profoundly learned, nor did any assist at the sacrifice that could not argue ably.

sanskrit: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति
transliteration: yo na hṛiṣhyati na dveṣhṭi na śhochati na kāṅkṣhati
śhubhāśhubha-parityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ sa me priyaḥ
english: He who is full of devotion to me, who feels no joy and no aversion, who does not grieve and does not desire, who abandons (both what is) agreeable and (what is) disagreeable, he is dear to me.

sanskrit: प्राप्ते यूपः उच्छ्रये तस्मिन् षड् बैल्वाः खादिराः तथा
तावन्तो बिल्व सहिताः पर्णिनः च तथा अपरे
transliteration: prāpte yūpaḥ ucchraye tasmin ṣaḍ bailvāḥ khādirāḥ tathā
tāvanto bilva sahitāḥ parṇinaḥ ca tathā apare
english: And when the time came for planting the Yüpas of bilva, as many of catechu, and as many of Palasa, and one of Sleşmätaka, and two of Devadāru well-made and measuring two outstretched arms.

sanskrit: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः
transliteration: samaḥ śhatrau cha mitre cha tathā mānāpamānayoḥ
english: He who is alike to friend and foe, as also in honour and dishonour, who is alike in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, who is free from attachments,

sanskrit: द्वावेव तत्र विहितौ बाहु व्यस्त परिग्रहौ
transliteration: dvāveva tatra vihitau bāhu vyasta parigrahau
english: And when the time came for planting the Yüpas of bilva, as many of catechu, and as many of Palasa, and one of Sleşmätaka, and two of Devadāru well-made and measuring two outstretched arms.

transliteration: aniketaḥ sthira-matir bhaktimān me priyo naraḥ
english: to whom praise and blame are alike, who is taciturn, and contented with anything whatever (that comes), who is homeless, and of a steady mind, and full of devotion, that man is dear to me.

sanskrit: शोभाअर्थम् तस्य यज्ञस्य कांचन अलंकृत अभवन्
transliteration: śobhāartham tasya yajñasya kāṃcana alaṃkṛta abhavan
ye tu dharmyāmṛitam idaṁ yathoktaṁ paryupāsate
śhraddadhānā mat-paramā bhaktās te ’tīva me priyāḥ
english: But those devotees who, imbued with faith, and (regarding) me as their highest (goal), resort to this holy (means for attaining) immortality, as stated, they are extremely dear to me.

sanskrit: एक विंशति यूपाः ते एक विंशत् अरत्नयः
transliteration: eka viṃśati yūpāḥ te eka viṃśat aratnayaḥ

sanskrit: प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञमेव च
transliteration: prakṛitiṁ puruṣhaṁ chaiva kṣhetraṁ kṣhetra-jñam eva cha
etad veditum ichchhāmi jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ cha keśhava
english: The Deity said: This body, O son of Kunti! is called Kshetra and the learned call him who knows it the Kshetragna.

sanskrit: विन्यस्ता विधिवत् सर्वे शिल्पिभिः सुकृता दृढाः
अष्ट आस्रयः सर्व एव श्लक्ष्ण रूप समन्विताः
transliteration: vinyastā vidhivat sarve śilpibhiḥ sukṛtā dṛḍhāḥ
aṣṭa āsrayaḥ sarva eva ślakṣṇa rūpa samanvitāḥ

sanskrit: एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः
transliteration: idaṁ śharīraṁ kaunteya kṣhetram ity abhidhīyate
etad yo vetti taṁ prāhuḥ kṣhetra-jña iti tad-vidaḥ
english: And know me also, O descendant of Bharata! to be the Kshetragna in all Kshetras.

sanskrit: आच्छादिताः ते वासोभिः पुष्पैः गन्धैः च पूजिताः
सप्त ऋषयो दीप्तिमन्तो विराजन्ते यथा दिवि
transliteration: ācchāditāḥ te vāsobhiḥ puṣpaiḥ gandhaiḥ ca pūjitāḥ
sapta ṛṣayo dīptimanto virājante yathā divi
english: And being wrapped up in cloths, and worshipped with flowers, they looked like the seven Rșis appearing in the welkin.

sanskrit: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत
transliteration: kṣhetra-jñaṁ chāpi māṁ viddhi sarva-kṣhetreṣhu bhārata
kṣhetra-kṣhetrajñayor jñānaṁ yat taj jñānaṁ mataṁ mama
english: The knowledge of Kshetra and Kshetragna is deemed by me (to be real) knowledge. Now hear from me in brief what that Kshetra (is), what (it is) like, what changes (it undergoes), and whence (it comes), and what is he, and what his powers,

sanskrit: इष्टकाः च यथा न्यायम् कारिताः च प्रमाणतः
transliteration: iṣṭakāḥ ca yathā nyāyam kāritāḥ ca pramāṇataḥ
english: And an adequate number of bricks was also duly made (for the ceremony.) And Brāhmaṇas accomplished in the arts constructed the sacrificial fire-place with those bricks.

sanskrit: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक् च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत्
स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च तत्समासेन मे श्रृणु
transliteration: tat kṣhetraṁ yach cha yādṛik cha yad-vikāri yataśh cha yat
sa cha yo yat-prabhāvaśh cha tat samāsena me śhṛiṇu
english: (all which) is sung in various ways by sages in numerous hymns, distinctly, and in well-settled texts full of argument, giving indications or full instruction about the Brahman.

sanskrit: सचित्यो राज सिंहस्य संचितः कुशलैः द्विजैः
गरुडो रुक्मपक्षो वै त्रिगुणो अष्टा दशात्मकः
transliteration: sacityo rāja siṃhasya saṃcitaḥ kuśalaiḥ dvijaiḥ
garuḍo rukmapakṣo vai triguṇo aṣṭā daśātmakaḥ
ṛiṣhibhir bahudhā gītaṁ chhandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛithak
english: The great elements, egoism, the understanding, the unperceived also, the ten senses, and the one, and the five objects of sense,

sanskrit: नियुक्ताः तत्र पशवः तत् तत् उद्दिश्य दैवतम्
उरगाः पक्षिणः च एव यथा शास्त्रम् प्रचोदिताः
transliteration: niyuktāḥ tatra paśavaḥ tat tat uddiśya daivatam
uragāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ ca eva yathā śāstram pracoditāḥ
mahā-bhūtāny ahankāro buddhir avyaktam eva cha
english: desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, body, consciousness, courage, thus in brief has been declared the Kshetra with changes.

sanskrit: शामित्रे तु हयः तत्र तथा जलचराः च ये
ऋषिभिः सर्वम् एवै तन् नियुक्तम् शास्त्रतः तदा
transliteration: śāmitre tu hayaḥ tatra tathā jalacarāḥ ca ye
ṛṣibhiḥ sarvam evai tan niyuktam śāstrataḥ tadā
ichchhā dveṣhaḥ sukhaṁ duḥkhaṁ saṅghātaśh chetanā dhṛitiḥ
english: Absence of vanity, absence of ostentatiousness, absence of hurtfulness, forgiveness, straightforwardness, devotion to a preceptor, purity, steadiness, self-restraint,

sanskrit: पशूनाम् त्रिशतम् तत्र यूपेषु नियतम् तदा
अश्व रत्नः उत्तमम् तस्य राज्ञो दशरथस्य ह
transliteration: paśūnām triśatam tatra yūpeṣu niyatam tadā
aśva ratnaḥ uttamam tasya rājño daśarathasya ha
english: And to these Yūpas were bound, three hundred beasts, as well as the foremost of the best horses belonging to king Dasaratha.
indifference towards objects of sense, and also absence of egoism; perception of the misery and evil of birth, death, old age, and disease;

sanskrit: कौसल्या तम् हयम् तत्र परिचर्य समंततः
कृपाणैः विशशासः एनम् त्रिभिः परमया मुदा
transliteration: kausalyā tam hayam tatra paricarya samaṃtataḥ
kṛpāṇaiḥ viśaśāsaḥ enam tribhiḥ paramayā mudā
english: Then Kausalyā, having performed the preliminary rites, with three strokes slew that horse, experiencing great glee.
absence of attachment, absence of self-identifying regard for son, wife, home, and so forth; and constant equability on the approach of (both what is) agreeable and (what is) disagreeable;

sanskrit: पतत्रिणा तदा सार्धम् सुस्थितेन च चेतसा
अवसत् रजनीम् एकाम् कौसल्या धर्म काम्यया
transliteration: patatriṇā tadā sārdham susthitena ca cetasā
avasat rajanīm ekām kausalyā dharma kāmyayā
english: And with the view of reaping merit, Kausalyā, with an undisturbed heart passed one night with that horse furnished with wings.
unswerving devotion to me, without meditation on any one else; resorting to clean places, distaste for assemblages of men,

sanskrit: होता अध्वर्युः तथ उद्गाता हस्तेन समयोजयन्
महिष्या परिवृत्त्या अथ वावाताम् अपराम् तथा
transliteration: hotā adhvaryuḥ tatha udgātā hastena samayojayan
mahiṣyā parivṛttyā atha vāvātām aparām tathā
english: Hotás and Adhvaryus, and the Udgatás joined the king's Vāvātā along with his Mahișī and Parivrtti.* And priests of subdued senses, wellup in sacrificial rites, began to offer oblations with the fat of the winged-horse, according to the ordinance. *The Kșatriya kings could marry wives from among Kșatriyas, Vaişyas and Śūdras. The Kșatriya wife is called Mahiși, the Vaişya wife Vávātā and the Śūdra wife Parivrtti.
constancy in knowledge of the relation of the individual self to the supreme, perception of the object of knowledge of the truth, this is called knowledge; that is ignorance which is opposed to this.

Hotás and Adhvaryus, and the Udgatás joined the king's Vāvātā along with his Mahișī and Parivrtti.* And priests of subdued senses, wellup in sacrificial rites, began to offer oblations with the fat of the winged-horse, according to the ordinance. *The Kșatriya kings could marry wives from among Kșatriyas, Vaişyas and Śūdras. The Kșatriya wife is called Mahiși, the Vaişya wife Vávātā and the Śūdra wife Parivrtti.

transliteration: etaj jñānam iti proktam ajñānaṁ yad ato ’nyathā
english: I will declare that which is the object of knowledge, knowing which, one reaches immortality; the highest Brahman, having no beginning nor end, which cannot be said to be existent or non-existent.

sanskrit: धूम गन्धम् वपायाः तु जिघ्रति स्म नराधिपः
यथा कालम् यथा न्यायम् निर्णुदन् पापम् आत्मनः
transliteration: dhūma gandham vapāyāḥ tu jighrati sma narādhipaḥ
yathā kālam yathā nyāyam nirṇudan pāpam ātmanaḥ
english: The lord of men, desirous of removing his sins, at the proper time smelt the odour of the smoke arising from the fat, agreeably to the scriptures.

transliteration: jñeyaṁ yat tat pravakṣhyāmi yaj jñātvāmṛitam aśhnute
anādi mat-paraṁ brahma na sat tan nāsad uchyate
english: It has hands and feet on all sides, it has eyes, heads, and faces on all sides, it has ears on all sides, it stands pervading everything in the world.

sanskrit: हयस्य यानि च अंगानि तानि सर्वाणि ब्राह्मणाः
अग्नौ प्रास्यन्ति विधिवत् समस्ताः षोडश ऋत्विजः
transliteration: hayasya yāni ca aṃgāni tāni sarvāṇi brāhmaṇāḥ
agnau prāsyanti vidhivat samastāḥ ṣoḍaśa ṛtvijaḥ
english: Then sixteen sacrificial priests in the prescribed form offered the various parts of the horse to the fire.

transliteration: sarvataḥ śhrutimal loke sarvam āvṛitya tiṣhṭhati
english: Possessed of the qualities of all the senses, (but) devoid of all senses, unattached, it supports all, is devoid of qualities, and the enjoyer of qualities.

sanskrit: प्लक्ष शाखासु यज्ञानाम् अन्येषाम् क्रियते हविः
अश्व मेधस्य यज्ञस्य वैतसो भागः इष्यते
transliteration: plakṣa śākhāsu yajñānām anyeṣām kriyate haviḥ
aśva medhasya yajñasya vaitaso bhāgaḥ iṣyate
asaktaṁ sarva-bhṛich chaiva nirguṇaṁ guṇa-bhoktṛi cha
english: It is within all things and without them; it is movable and also immovable; it is unknowable through (its) subtlety; it stands afar and near.

sanskrit: त्र्यहोऽश्व मेधः संख्यातः कल्प सूत्रेण ब्राह्मणैः
transliteration: tryaho'śva medhaḥ saṃkhyātaḥ kalpa sūtreṇa brāhmaṇaiḥ
bahir antaśh cha bhūtānām acharaṁ charam eva cha
sūkṣhmatvāt tad avijñeyaṁ dūra-sthaṁ chāntike cha tat
english: Not different in (different) things, but standing as though different, it should be known to be the supporter of (all) things, and that which absorbs and creates (them).

sanskrit: कारिताः तत्र बहवो विहिताः शास्त्र दर्शनात्
transliteration: kāritāḥ tatra bahavo vihitāḥ śāstra darśanāt

sanskrit: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम्
भूतभर्तृ च तज्ज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च
transliteration: avibhaktaṁ cha bhūteṣhu vibhaktam iva cha sthitam
bhūta-bhartṛi cha taj jñeyaṁ grasiṣhṇu prabhaviṣhṇu cha
english: It is the radiance even of the radiant (bodies); it is said (to be) beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the object of knowledge, that which is to be attained to by knowledge, and placed in the heart of all.

sanskrit: ज्योतिष्टोम आयुषी च एवम् अतिरात्रौ विनिर्मितौ
अभिजित् विश्वजित् च एवम् अप्तोर्यामो महाक्रतुः
transliteration: jyotiṣṭoma āyuṣī ca evam atirātrau vinirmitau
abhijit viśvajit ca evam aptoryāmo mahākratuḥ
english: And then the jyotisloma, and then Āyuştoma, and the Atirātra, and the Abhijit, and the Visvajit, and the Āptoryāma, all these various great sacrifices were celebrated with due rites.

sanskrit: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य विष्ठितम्
transliteration: jyotiṣhām api taj jyotis tamasaḥ param uchyate
jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ jñāna-gamyaṁ hṛidi sarvasya viṣhṭhitam
english: Thus in brief have Kshetra, knowledge, and the object of knowledge been declared. My devotee, knowing this, becomes fit for assimilation with me.

sanskrit: प्राचीम् होत्रे ददौ राजा दिशम् स्वकुल वर्धनःअध्वर्यवे प्रतीचीम् तु ब्रह्मणे दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
transliteration: prācīm hotre dadau rājā diśam svakula vardhanaḥadhvaryave pratīcīm tu brahmaṇe dakṣiṇām diśam
english: And in this mighty horse-sacrifice founded of yore by Svayambhū, that perpetuator of his line, the king, bestowed the Eastern quarter on his chief sacrificial priest, the Western on his Adhvaryu, the Southern on Brahmă, and the Northern on the Udgātā, as Daksinās.

sanskrit: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः
transliteration: iti kṣhetraṁ tathā jñānaṁ jñeyaṁ choktaṁ samāsataḥ
english: Know nature and spirit both (to be) without beginning, and know all developments and qualities (to be) produced from nature.

sanskrit: उद्गात्रे च तथा उदीचीम् दक्षिणैएषा विनिर्मिता
transliteration: udgātre ca tathā udīcīm dakṣiṇaieṣā vinirmitā
english: And in this mighty horse-sacrifice founded of yore by Svayambhū, that perpetuator of his line, the king, bestowed the Eastern quarter on his chief sacrificial priest, the Western on his Adhvaryu, the Southern on Brahmă, and the Northern on the Udgātā, as Daksinās.

transliteration: prakṛitiṁ puruṣhaṁ chaiva viddhy anādī ubhāv api
vikārānśh cha guṇānśh chaiva viddhi prakṛiti-sambhavān
english: Nature is said to be the origin of the capacity of working (residing) in the body and the senses; and spirit is said (to be) the origin of the capacity of enjoying pleasures and pains.

sanskrit: क्रतुं समाप्य तु तदा न्यायतः पुरुषर्षभः
ऋत्विग्भ्यो हि ददौ राजा धराम् ताम् कुलवर्धनः
transliteration: kratuṃ samāpya tu tadā nyāyataḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
ṛtvigbhyo hi dadau rājā dharām tām kulavardhanaḥ
english: Having completed that sacrifice, that perpetuator of his race, and foremost of men, the king, conferied on the priests the earth; and having conferred it, that auspicious descendant of Ikşvāku experienced high delight. And then the priests spoke to that monarch, who had all his sins purged off saying.
For spirit with nature joined, enjoys the qualities born of nature. And the cause of its birth in good or evil wombs is the connexion with the qualities.

sanskrit: एवम् दत्त्वा प्रहृष्टो अभूत् श्रीमान् इक्ष्वाकु नन्दन
ऋत्विजः तु अब्रुवन् सर्वे राजानम् गत किल्बिषम्
transliteration: evam dattvā prahṛṣṭo abhūt śrīmān ikṣvāku nandana
ṛtvijaḥ tu abruvan sarve rājānam gata kilbiṣam
english: Having completed that sacrifice, that perpetuator of his race, and foremost of men, the king, conferied on the priests the earth; and having conferred it, that auspicious descendant of Ikşvāku experienced high delight. And then the priests spoke to that monarch, who had all his sins purged off saying.

transliteration: puruṣhaḥ prakṛiti-stho hi bhuṅkte prakṛiti-jān guṇān
english: The supreme spirit in this body is called supervisor, adviser, supporter, enjoyer, the great lord, and the supreme self also.

sanskrit: भवान् एव महीम् कृत्स्नाम् एको रक्षितुम् अर्हति
न भूम्या कार्यम् अस्माकम् न हि शक्ताः स्म पालने
transliteration: bhavān eva mahīm kṛtsnām eko rakṣitum arhati
na bhūmyā kāryam asmākam na hi śaktāḥ sma pālane
english: You alone are worthy to protect the entire world. We do not want the earth; nor can we rule it, being, O lord of Earth, constantly engaged in Vedic studies. Do you, therefore, confer upon us something instead, as the price thereof.

transliteration: paramātmeti chāpy ukto dehe ’smin puruṣhaḥ paraḥ
english: He who thus knows nature and spirit, together with the qualities, is not born again, however living.

sanskrit: रताः स्वाध्याय करणे वयम् नित्यम् हि भूमिप
निष्क्रयम् किंचित् एव इह प्रयच्छतु भवान् इति
transliteration: ratāḥ svādhyāya karaṇe vayam nityam hi bhūmipa
niṣkrayam kiṃcit eva iha prayacchatu bhavān iti
english: You alone are worthy to protect the entire world. We do not want the earth; nor can we rule it, being, O lord of Earth, constantly engaged in Vedic studies. Do you, therefore, confer upon us something instead, as the price thereof.

sanskrit: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैःसह
transliteration: ya evaṁ vetti puruṣhaṁ prakṛitiṁ cha guṇaiḥ saha
english: Some by concentration see the self in the self by the self; others by the Sankhya-yoga; and others still by the Karma-yoga;

sanskrit: मणि रत्नम् सुवर्णम् वा गावो यद् वा समुद्यतम्
तत् प्रयच्छ नरश्रेष्ट धरण्या न प्रयोजनम्
transliteration: maṇi ratnam suvarṇam vā gāvo yad vā samudyatam
tat prayaccha naraśreṣṭa dharaṇyā na prayojanam
english: Do you confer upon us gems, or gold, or kine, or anything else, for, O foremost of monarchs, we do not want earth.
others yet, not knowing this, practise concentration, after hearing from others. They, too, being (thus) devoted to hearing (instruction) cross beyond death.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तो नरपतिः ब्राह्मणैः वेद पारगैः
गवाम् शत सहस्राणि दश तेभ्यो ददौ नृपः
transliteration: evam ukto narapatiḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ veda pāragaiḥ
gavām śata sahasrāṇi daśa tebhyo dadau nṛpaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the Brāhmaṇas versed in the Veda, that best of kings bestowed upon them ten lace of kine, and ten Koțis of gold, and forty of silver.

transliteration: anye tv evam ajānantaḥ śhrutvānyebhya upāsate
english: Whatever thing movable or immovable comes into existence, know that to be from the connexion of Kshetra and Kshetragna, O chief of the descendants of Bharata!

sanskrit: दश कोटि सुवर्णस्य रजतस्य चतुर् गुणम्
ऋत्विजः च ततः सर्वे प्रददुः सहिता वसु
transliteration: daśa koṭi suvarṇasya rajatasya catur guṇam
ṛtvijaḥ ca tataḥ sarve pradaduḥ sahitā vasu

english: He sees (truly), who sees the supreme lord abiding alike in all entities, and not destroyed though they are destroyed.

sanskrit: ततः ते न्यायतः कृत्वा प्रविभागम् द्विजोत्तमाः
transliteration: tataḥ te nyāyataḥ kṛtvā pravibhāgam dvijottamāḥ
english: Then those priests in a body, accepting the wealth, brought it to the ascetic Rșyaśộnga and the intelligent Vasiştha. Then having received each his share, those foremost of regenerate ones were exceedingly pleased, and said, We have been highly gratified.

transliteration: vinaśhyatsv avinaśhyantaṁ yaḥ paśhyati sa paśhyati
english: For he who sees the lord abiding everywhere alike, does not destroy himself by himself, and then reaches the highest goal.

sanskrit: सुप्रीत मनसः सर्वे प्रत्यूचुः मुदिता भृशम्
transliteration: suprīta manasaḥ sarve pratyūcuḥ muditā bhṛśam

sanskrit: न हिनस्त्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं ततो याति परां गतिम्
transliteration: samaṁ paśhyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśhvaram
na hinasty ātmanātmānaṁ tato yāti parāṁ gatim
english: He sees (truly), who sees (all) actions (to be) in every way done by nature alone, and likewise the self (to be) not the doer.

sanskrit: जांबूनदम् कोओटि संख्यम् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ तदा
दरिद्राय द्विजाय अथ हस्त आभरणम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: jāṃbūnadam kooṭi saṃkhyam brāhmaṇebhyo dadau tadā
daridrāya dvijāya atha hasta ābharaṇam uttamam
yaḥ paśhyati tathātmānam akartāraṁ sa paśhyati
english: When a man sees all the variety of entities as existing in one, and (all as) emanating from that, then he becomes (one with) the Brahman.

sanskrit: कस्मै चित् याचमानाय ददौ राघव नंदनः
ततः प्रीतेषु विधिवत् द्विजेषु द्विज वत्सलः
transliteration: kasmai cit yācamānāya dadau rāghava naṃdanaḥ
tataḥ prīteṣu vidhivat dvijeṣu dvija vatsalaḥ

sanskrit: तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा
transliteration: tata eva cha vistāraṁ brahma sampadyate tadā
english: This inexhaustible supreme self, being without beginning and without qualities, does not act, and is not tainted, O son of Kunti! though stationed in the body.

sanskrit: प्रणामम् अकरोत् तेषाम् हर्ष व्याकुलित इन्द्रियः
transliteration: praṇāmam akarot teṣām harṣa vyākulita indriyaḥ

sanskrit: शरीरस्थोऽपि कौन्तेय न करोति न लिप्यते
transliteration: śharīra-stho ’pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate
english: As by (reason of its) subtlety the all-pervading space is not tainted, so the self stationed in every body is not tainted.

sanskrit: ततः प्रीत मना रजाअ प्राप्य यज्ञम् अनुत्तमम्
transliteration: tataḥ prīta manā rajāa prāpya yajñam anuttamam

english: As the sun singly lights up all this world, so the Kshetragna, O descendant of Bharata! lights up the whole Kshetra. Those who, with the eye of knowledge, thus understand the difference between Kshetra and Kshetragna, and the destruction of the nature of all entities, go to the supreme.

sanskrit: पाप अपहम् स्वर् नयनम् दुस्तरम् पार्थिवर्षभैः
transliteration: pāpa apaham svar nayanam dustaram pārthivarṣabhaiḥ

sanskrit: क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्नं प्रकाशयति भारत
transliteration: yathā prakāśhayaty ekaḥ kṛitsnaṁ lokam imaṁ raviḥ
kṣhetraṁ kṣhetrī tathā kṛitsnaṁ prakāśhayati bhārata

sanskrit: कुलस्य वर्धनम् त्वम् तु कर्तुम् अर्हसि सुव्रत
तथेति च स राजानम् उवाच द्विजसत्तमः
भविष्यन्ति सुता राजन् चत्वारः ते कुलोद्वहाः
transliteration: kulasya vardhanam tvam tu kartum arhasi suvrata
tatheti ca sa rājānam uvāca dvijasattamaḥ
bhaviṣyanti sutā rājan catvāraḥ te kulodvahāḥ
english: Thereupon the best of Brāhmaṇas told the king that he would have four sons, born to him, as perpetuators of his race.

sanskrit: भूतप्रकृतिमोक्षं च ये विदुर्यान्ति ते परम्
transliteration: bhūta-prakṛiti-mokṣhaṁ cha ye vidur yānti te param

sanskrit: स तस्य वाक्यम् मधुरम् निशम्यप्रणम्य तस्मै प्रयतो नृपेन्द्र
जगाम हर्षम् परमम् महात्मातम् ऋष्यश्R^ङ्गम् पुनरपि उवाच
transliteration: sa tasya vākyam madhuram niśamyapraṇamya tasmai prayato nṛpendra
jagāma harṣam paramam mahātmātam ṛṣyaśṅgam punarapi uvāca
english: Hearing these sweet words of his, that foremost of monarchs bended low to him with controlled faculties, and experienced the excess of joy. And then that high-souled one again spoke to Rşyaśțnga.

sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचपरं भूयः प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम्
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनयः सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गताः
transliteration: paraṁ bhūyaḥ pravakṣhyāmi jñānānāṁ jñānam uttamam
yaj jñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṁ siddhim ito gatāḥ
english: The Deity said: Again I will declare (to you) the highest knowledge, the best of (all sorts of) knowledge, having learnt which, all sages have reached perfection beyond (the bonds of) this (body).

sanskrit: मेधावी तु ततो ध्यात्वा स किङ्चित् इदम् उत्तरम्
लब्ध सङ्ज्ञः ततः तम् तु वेदज्ञो नृपम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: medhāvī tu tato dhyātvā sa kiṅcit idam uttaram
labdha saṅjñaḥ tataḥ tam tu vedajño nṛpam abravīt
english: Then that one of capacious intelligence, versed in the Vedas, having pondered for a time, and regained his senses, returned to the king this excellent answer.

sanskrit: सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च
transliteration: idaṁ jñānam upāśhritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ
sarge ’pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti cha
english: Those who, resorting to this knowledge, reach assimilation with my essence, are not born at the creation, and are not afflicted at the destruction (of the universe).

sanskrit: इष्टिम् तेऽहम् करिष्यामि पुत्रीयाम् पुत्र कारणात्
अथर्व सिरसि प्रोक्तैः मन्त्रैः सिद्धाम् विधानतः
transliteration: iṣṭim te'ham kariṣyāmi putrīyām putra kāraṇāt
atharva sirasi proktaiḥ mantraiḥ siddhām vidhānataḥ
english: On your behalf, and with the view of obtaining sons for you, I will by help of mantras laid down in the Atharva Veda, duly celebrate the famous ceremony, capable of crowning you with offspring.

transliteration: mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaṁ dadhāmy aham
english: The great Brahman is a womb for me, in which I cast the seed. From that, O descendant of Bharata! is the birth of all things.

sanskrit: ततः प्राक्रमत् इदम् इष्टिम् ताम् पुत्रीयाम् पुत्र कारणात्
जुहाव अग्नौ च तेजस्वी मन्त्र दृष्टेन कर्मणा
transliteration: tataḥ prākramat idam iṣṭim tām putrīyām putra kāraṇāt
juhāva agnau ca tejasvī mantra dṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Then with the view of obtaining sons (for the king,) that effulgent one set about the sonconferring ceremony; and in accordance with the ordinance, and with mantras, offered oblations to the sacrificial fire.

transliteration: tāsāṁ brahma mahad yonir ahaṁ bīja-pradaḥ pitā
english: Of the bodies, O son of Kunti! which are born from all wombs, the (main) womb is the great Brahman, and I (am) the father, the giver of the seed.

sanskrit: ततो देवाः स गन्धर्वाः सिद्धाः च परम ऋषयः
transliteration: tato devāḥ sa gandharvāḥ siddhāḥ ca parama ṛṣayaḥ
english: And the deities, with the Gandharvas, and the Siddhas, and the principal saints, assembled there duly with the object of each obtaining his share of the offerings.

transliteration: sattvaṁ rajas tama iti guṇāḥ prakṛiti-sambhavāḥ
english: Goodness, passion, darkness, these qualities born from nature, O you of mighty arms! bind down the inexhaustible soul in the body.

sanskrit: ताः समेत्य यथा न्यायम् तस्मिन् सदसि देवताः
अब्रुवन् लोक कर्तारम् ब्रह्माणम् वचनम् ततः
transliteration: tāḥ sametya yathā nyāyam tasmin sadasi devatāḥ
abruvan loka kartāram brahmāṇam vacanam tataḥ
english: And having duly assembled there, the deities addressed these words to Brahmă the lord of creatures.
Of these, goodness, which, in consequence of being untainted, is enlightening and free from (all) misery, binds the soul, O sinless one! with the bond of pleasure and the bond of knowledge.

sanskrit: भगवन् त्वत् प्रसादेन रावणो नाम राक्षसः
सर्वान् नो बाधते वीर्यात् शासितुम् तम् न शक्नुमः
transliteration: bhagavan tvat prasādena rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ
sarvān no bādhate vīryāt śāsitum tam na śaknumaḥ
english: O you possessed of the six attributes, through your grace, a Rākşasa named Rāvaņa oppresses us all by his prowess, nor can we baffle him.
Know that passion consists in being enamoured, and is produced from craving and attachment. That, O son of Kunti! binds down the embodied (self) with the bond of action.

sanskrit: त्वया तस्मै वरो दत्तः प्रीतेन भगवन् तदा
मानयन्तः च तम् नित्यम् सर्वम् तस्य क्षमामहे
transliteration: tvayā tasmai varo dattaḥ prītena bhagavan tadā
mānayantaḥ ca tam nityam sarvam tasya kṣamāmahe
english: O lord, as you have well-pleased conferred on him a boon, we always suffer him in deference to it.

transliteration: tamas tv ajñāna-jaṁ viddhi mohanaṁ sarva-dehinām
english: Darkness (you must) know to be born of ignorance, it deludes all embodied (selfs). And that, O descendant of Bharata! binds down (the self) with heedlessness, indolence, and sleep.

sanskrit: उद्वेजयति लोकान् त्रीन् उच्छ्रितान् द्वेष्टि दुर्मतिः
transliteration: udvejayati lokān trīn ucchritān dveṣṭi durmatiḥ
english: The wicked-minded one harasses the three worlds furnished with prosperity, and bears illwill against them and seek o defeat Indra, the king of Tridaśa.

sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत
transliteration: sattvaṁ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata
jñānam āvṛitya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayaty uta
english: Goodness unites (the self) with pleasure; passion, O descendant of Bharata! with action; and darkness with heedlessness, after shrouding up knowledge.

sanskrit: ऋषीन् यक्षान् स गन्धर्वान् असुरान् ब्राह्मणान् तथा
transliteration: ṛṣīn yakṣān sa gandharvān asurān brāhmaṇān tathā
english: And blinded by the boon he has received, that irrepressible one intends to bring down the lord himself of the celestials, and the Yakşas, and the Gandharvas, and the Brahmanas, and the Asuras.

sanskrit: रजः सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा
transliteration: rajas tamaśh chābhibhūya sattvaṁ bhavati bhārata
rajaḥ sattvaṁ tamaśh chaiva tamaḥ sattvaṁ rajas tathā
english: Passion and darkness being repressed, goodness stands, O descendant of Bharata! Passion and goodness (being repressed), darkness; and likewise darkness and goodness (being repressed), passion.

sanskrit: नैनम् सूर्यः प्रतपति पार्श्वे वाति न मारुतः
चलोर्मिमाली तम् दृष्ट्वा समुद्रोऽपि न कम्पते
transliteration: nainam sūryaḥ pratapati pārśve vāti na mārutaḥ
calormimālī tam dṛṣṭvā samudro'pi na kampate
english: And the Sun does not burn him, or the Wind blow about him; and at sight of him, that one engarlanded with billows, the Ocean, dares not stir.

transliteration: jñānaṁ yadā tadā vidyād vivṛiddhaṁ sattvam ity uta
english: When in this body at all portals light (that is to say) knowledge prevails, then should one know goodness to be developed.

sanskrit: तन् महन्नो भयम् तस्मात् राक्षसात् घोर दर्शनात्
वधार्थम् तस्य भगवन् उपायम् कर्तुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: tan mahanno bhayam tasmāt rākṣasāt ghora darśanāt
vadhārtham tasya bhagavan upāyam kartum arhasi
english: Therefore, great is the fear that afflict us, coming from that Rākşasa of dreadful appearance. And, O lord, it behoves you to devise some means for destroying him.

transliteration: lobhaḥ pravṛittir ārambhaḥ karmaṇām aśhamaḥ spṛihā
english: Avarice, activity, performance of actions, want of tranquillity, desire, these are produced, O chief of the descendants of Bharata! when passion is developed.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः सुरैः सर्वैः चिन्तयित्वा ततोऽब्रवीत्
हन्ता अयम् विदितः तस्य वधोपायो दुरात्मनः
transliteration: evam uktaḥ suraiḥ sarvaiḥ cintayitvā tato'bravīt
hantā ayam viditaḥ tasya vadhopāyo durātmanaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the deities in a body, he said, Alas! I have, however, decided on the means of destroying that wicked-souled one. He had asked, 'May I be incapable of being slain by Gandharvas, and Yaksas, and gods, and Raksasas!,-whereat I said, 'Be it so!'

transliteration: aprakāśho ’pravṛittiśh cha pramādo moha eva cha
english: Want of light, want of activity heedlessness, and delusion, these are produced, O descendant of Kuru! when darkness is developed.

sanskrit: तेन गन्धर्व यक्षाणाम् देवतानाम् च रक्षसाम्
अवध्योऽस्मि इति वागुक्ता तथेति उक्तम् च तन् मया
transliteration: tena gandharva yakṣāṇām devatānām ca rakṣasām
avadhyo'smi iti vāguktā tatheti uktam ca tan mayā
english: Thus addressed by the deities in a body, he said, Alas! I have, however, decided on the means of destroying that wicked-souled one. He had asked, 'May I be incapable of being slain by Gandharvas, and Yaksas, and gods, and Raksasas!,-whereat I said, 'Be it so!'

sanskrit: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत्
transliteration: yadā sattve pravṛiddhe tu pralayaṁ yāti deha-bhṛit
english: When an embodied (self) encounters death, while goodness is developed, then he reaches the untainted worlds of those who know the highest.

sanskrit: न अकीर्तयत् अवज्ञानात् तत् रक्षो मानुषाम् तदा
तस्मात् स मानुषात् वध्यो मृत्युः न अन्योऽस्य विद्यते
transliteration: na akīrtayat avajñānāt tat rakṣo mānuṣām tadā
tasmāt sa mānuṣāt vadhyo mṛtyuḥ na anyo'sya vidyate
english: Through disdain, the Rākşasa did not at that time mention men. Therefore, by men alone he is capable of being slain; nor can his end be compassed by any other means.
Encountering death during (the prevalence of) passion, he is born among those attached to action. Likewise, dying during (the prevalence of) darkness, he is born in the wombs of the ignorant.

sanskrit: एतत् श्रुत्वा प्रियम् वाक्यम् ब्रह्मणा समुदाहृतम्
देवा महर्षयः सर्वे प्रहृष्टाः ते अभवन् तदा
transliteration: etat śrutvā priyam vākyam brahmaṇā samudāhṛtam
devā maharṣayaḥ sarve prahṛṣṭāḥ te abhavan tadā
english: Hearing this welcome speech uttered by Brahmā, the deities and the Maharșis became exceedingly delighted.

transliteration: rajasas tu phalaṁ duḥkham ajñānaṁ tamasaḥ phalam
english: The fruit of meritorious action is said to be good, untainted; while the fruit of passion is misery; and the fruit of darkness ignorance.

sanskrit: श्ङ्ख चक्र गदा पाणिः पीत वासा जगत्पतिः
transliteration: śṅkha cakra gadā pāṇiḥ pīta vāsā jagatpatiḥ
english: At this juncture, that lord of the universe, the highly-eifulgent Visnu, clad in yellow apparel, and bearing in his hands the conch, the discus, and the mace, and adorned with burnished Keyūras, (A bracelet worn on the upper arm.) arrived there, riding Vinatā's son; like to the Sun riding the clouds. And worshipped by the foremost of the celestials, he drew near Brahmā, and sat down with a collected mind.

sanskrit: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च
transliteration: sattvāt sañjāyate jñānaṁ rajaso lobha eva cha
english: From goodness is produced knowledge, from passion avarice, and from darkness heedlessness and delusion and ignorance also.

sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः
transliteration: ūrdhvaṁ gachchhanti sattva-sthā madhye tiṣhṭhanti rājasāḥ
english: Those who adhere to (the ways of) goodness go up; the passionate remain in the middle; while those of the qualities of darkness, adhering to the ways of the lowest quality, go down.

sanskrit: ब्रह्मणा च समागम्य तत्र तस्थौ समाहितः
तम् अब्रुवन् सुराः सर्वे समभिष्टूय संनताः
transliteration: brahmaṇā ca samāgamya tatra tasthau samāhitaḥ
tam abruvan surāḥ sarve samabhiṣṭūya saṃnatāḥ
guṇebhyaśh cha paraṁ vetti mad-bhāvaṁ so ’dhigachchhati
english: When a right-seeing person sees none but the qualities (to be) the doers (of all action), and knows what is above the qualities, he enters into my essence.

sanskrit: त्वाम् नियोक्ष्यामहे विष्णो लोकानाम् हित काम्यया
राज्ञो दशरथस्य त्वम् अयोध्य अधिपतेः विभोः
transliteration: tvām niyokṣyāmahe viṣṇo lokānām hita kāmyayā
rājño daśarathasya tvam ayodhya adhipateḥ vibhoḥ
guṇān etān atītya trīn dehī deha-samudbhavān
english: The embodied (self), who transcends these three qualities, from which bodies are produced, attains immortality, being freed from birth and death and old age and misery.

sanskrit: अस्य भार्यासु तिसृषु ह्री श्री कीर्ति उपमासु च
transliteration: asya bhāryāsu tisṛṣu hrī śrī kīrti upamāsu ca
kair liṅgais trīn guṇān etān atīto bhavati prabho
kim āchāraḥ kathaṁ chaitāns trīn guṇān ativartate
english: Arguna said: What are the characteristics, O lord! of one who has transcended these three qualities? What is his conduct, and how does he transcend these three qualities?

sanskrit: विष्णो पुत्रत्वम् आगच्छ कृत्वा आत्मानम् चतुर्विधम्
तत्र त्वम् मानुषो भूत्वा प्रवृद्धम् लोक कण्टकम्
transliteration: viṣṇo putratvam āgaccha kṛtvā ātmānam caturvidham
tatra tvam mānuṣo bhūtvā pravṛddham loka kaṇṭakam

sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव
न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति
transliteration: prakāśhaṁ cha pravṛittiṁ cha moham eva cha pāṇḍava
na dveṣhṭi sampravṛittāni na nivṛittāni kāṅkṣhati
english: The Deity said: He is said to have transcended the qualities, O son of Pandu! who is not averse to light and activity and delusion (when they) prevail, and who does not desire (them when they) cease;

sanskrit: अवध्यम् दैवतैः विष्णो समरे जहि रावणम्
स हि देवान् स गन्धर्वान् सिद्धान् च ऋषि सत्तमान्
transliteration: avadhyam daivataiḥ viṣṇo samare jahi rāvaṇam
sa hi devān sa gandharvān siddhān ca ṛṣi sattamān
udāsīna-vad āsīno guṇair yo na vichālyate
guṇā vartanta ity evaṁ yo ’vatiṣhṭhati neṅgate
english: who sitting like one unconcerned is never perturbed by the qualities; who remains steady and moves not, (thinking) merely that the qualities exist; who is self-contained;

sanskrit: राक्षसो रावणो मूर्खो वीर्य उद्रेकेण बाधते
ऋषयः च ततः तेन गन्धर्वा अप्सरसः तथा
transliteration: rākṣaso rāvaṇo mūrkho vīrya udrekeṇa bādhate
ṛṣayaḥ ca tataḥ tena gandharvā apsarasaḥ tathā
english: And by him bereft of the sense of right and wrong, have saints and Gandharvas and Apsaras sporting in the groves of Nandana, been wantonly slain.
to whom pain and pleasure are alike; to whom a sod and a stone and gold are alike; to whom what is agreeable and what is disagreeable are alike; who has discernment;

sanskrit: वधार्थम् वयम् आयाताः तस्य वै मुनिभिः सह
transliteration: vadhārtham vayam āyātāḥ tasya vai munibhiḥ saha

english: to whom censure and praise of himself are alike; who is alike in honour and dishonour; who is alike towards the sides of friends and foes; and who abandons all action.

sanskrit: सिद्ध गन्धर्व यक्षाः च ततः त्वाम् श्ररणम् गताः
त्वम् गतिः परमा देव सर्वेषाम् नः परंतपः
transliteration: siddha gandharva yakṣāḥ ca tataḥ tvām śraraṇam gatāḥ
tvam gatiḥ paramā deva sarveṣām naḥ paraṃtapaḥ
english: It is to compass his death that accompanied by the ascetics, we have come here: it is for this that the Siddhas and the Gandharvas and the Yaksas have taken refuge in you! O God, you are the prime way of us all, O repressor of foes! Do you, for bringing destruction to the enemies of the gods, turn your thoughts to being born as man.
And he who worships me with an unswerving devotion, transcends these qualities, and becomes fit for (entrance into) the essence of the Brahman.

sanskrit: वधाय देव शतॄणाम् नृणाम् लोके मनः कुरु
एवम् स्तुतस्तु देवेशो विष्णुः त्रिदशः पुंगवः
transliteration: vadhāya deva śatṝṇām nṛṇām loke manaḥ kuru
evam stutastu deveśo viṣṇuḥ tridaśaḥ puṃgavaḥ
english: Thus besought, that foremost of gods and chief of celestials, Visnu, worshipped of all creatures, addressed the assembled deities, following Duty, with the grand-sire at their head, saying.
For I am the embodiment of the Brahman, of indefeasible immortality, of eternal piety, and of unbroken happiness.

sanskrit: पितामह पुरोगान् तान् सर्व लोक नमस्कृतःअब्रवीत् त्रिदशान् सर्वान् समेतान् धर्म संहितान्
transliteration: pitāmaha purogān tān sarva loka namaskṛtaḥabravīt tridaśān sarvān sametān dharma saṃhitān
english: Thus besought, that foremost of gods and chief of celestials, Visnu, worshipped of all creatures, addressed the assembled deities, following Duty, with the grand-sire at their head, saying.

sanskrit: छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्
transliteration: chhandānsi yasya parṇāni yas taṁ veda sa veda-vit
english: The Deity said: They say the inexhaustible Asvattha has (its) roots above, (its) branches below; the Khandas are its leaves. He who knows it knows the Vedas.

sanskrit: भयम् त्यजत भद्रम् वो हितार्थम् युधि रावणम्
स पुत्र पौत्रम् स अमात्यम् स मित्र ज्ञाति बान्धवम्
transliteration: bhayam tyajata bhadram vo hitārtham yudhi rāvaṇam
sa putra pautram sa amātyam sa mitra jñāti bāndhavam
english: Do you renounce fear! For your behoof, slaying in battle the wily and irrepressible Răvaņa, dreadful to the saints and the celestials, together with his sons, and grandsons, and friends, and counsellors, and relatives, and acquaintances, I will abide among mortals, ruling this earth for ten thousand and as many hundred years.

Upwards and downwards extend its branches, which are enlarged by the qualities, and the sprouts of which are sensuous objects. And downwards to this human world are continued its roots which lead on to action.

sanskrit: हत्वा क्रूरम् दुराधर्षम् देव ऋषीणाम् भयावहम्
दश वर्ष सहस्राणि दश वर्ष शतानि च
transliteration: hatvā krūram durādharṣam deva ṛṣīṇām bhayāvaham
daśa varṣa sahasrāṇi daśa varṣa śatāni ca
english: Do you renounce fear! For your behoof, slaying in battle the wily and irrepressible Răvaņa, dreadful to the saints and the celestials, together with his sons, and grandsons, and friends, and counsellors, and relatives, and acquaintances, I will abide among mortals, ruling this earth for ten thousand and as many hundred years.

sanskrit: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा
transliteration: nānto na chādir na cha sampratiṣhṭhā
english: Its form is not thus known here, nor (its) end, nor beginning, nor support. But having with the firm weapon of unconcern, cut this Asvattha, whose roots are firmly fixed,

sanskrit: वत्स्यामि मानुषे लोके पालयन् पृध्वीम् इमाम्
एवम् दत्वा वरम् देवो देवानाम् विष्णुः आत्मवान्
transliteration: vatsyāmi mānuṣe loke pālayan pṛdhvīm imām
evam datvā varam devo devānām viṣṇuḥ ātmavān
english: Having thus conferred a boon upon the gods, the lord Vişnu of subdued soul fell to thinking as to the place where he would be born among men.

sanskrit: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः
तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी
english: then should one seek for that seat from which those that go there never return, (thinking) that one rests on that same primal being, from whom the ancient course (of worldly life) emanated.

sanskrit: ततः पद्म पलाशाक्षः कृत्वा आत्मानम् चतुर्विधम्
transliteration: tataḥ padma palāśākṣaḥ kṛtvā ātmānam caturvidham
english: Then that one of eyes resembling lotus-petals, dividing self into four parts, chose even king Dasaratha for his father.

Those who are free from pride and delusion, who have overcome the evils of attachment, who are constant in (contemplating) the relation of the supreme and individual self, from whom desire has departed, who are free from the pairs (of opposites) called pleasure and pain, go undeluded to that imperishable seal.

sanskrit: तदा देव ऋषि गन्धर्वाः स रुद्राः स अप्सरो गणाः
transliteration: tadā deva ṛṣi gandharvāḥ sa rudrāḥ sa apsaro gaṇāḥ
english: Thereat the celestials and the saints and the Gandharvas and the Rudras and the Apsaras hymned the Slayer of Madhu in excellent hymns.

sanskrit: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम
transliteration: na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śhaśhāṅko na pāvakaḥ
yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama
english: The sun does not light it, nor the moon, nor fire. That is my highest abode, going to which none returns.

sanskrit: तम् उद्धतम् रावणम् उग्र तेजसम्प्रवृद्ध दर्पम् त्रिदशेश्वर वर द्विषम्
विरावणम् साधु तपस्वि कण्टकम्तपस्विनाम् उद्धर तम् भयाअवहम्
transliteration: tam uddhatam rāvaṇam ugra tejasampravṛddha darpam tridaśeśvara vara dviṣam
virāvaṇam sādhu tapasvi kaṇṭakamtapasvinām uddhara tam bhayāavaham
english: Do you utterly uproot the haughty Råvaņa of fierce prowess and enhanced insolence-that foe of the lord of celestials, who is the occasion of the tears of the three * Lit. the thorns of pious ascetics.
An eternal portion of me it is, which, becoming an individual soul in the mortal world, draws (to itself) the senses with the mind as the sixth.

sanskrit: तमेव हत्वा स बलम् स बान्धवम्विरावणम् रावणम् उग्र पौरुषम्
स्वर् लोकम् आगच्छ गत ज्वरः चिरम्सुरेन्द्र गुप्तम् गत दोष कल्मषम्
transliteration: tameva hatvā sa balam sa bāndhavamvirāvaṇam rāvaṇam ugra pauruṣam
svar lokam āgaccha gata jvaraḥ ciramsurendra guptam gata doṣa kalmaṣam
english: Slaying that one of terrible prowess, who distresses the three worlds, with his forces and friends, do you, O foremost of gods, your fever of heart removed, repair to the celestial regions protected by you and purged of all its faults and sins.

transliteration: śharīraṁ yad avāpnoti yach chāpy utkrāmatīśhvaraḥ
english: Whenever the ruler (of the bodily frame) obtains or quits a body, he goes taking these (with him) as the wind (takes) perfumes from (their) seats.

sanskrit: ततो नारायणो देवो विषुणुः नियुक्तः सुर सत्तमैः
जानन् अपि सुरान् एवम् श्लक्ष्णम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tato nārāyaṇo devo viṣuṇuḥ niyuktaḥ sura sattamaiḥ
jānan api surān evam ślakṣṇam vacanam abravīt
english: Thus besought by the foremost of the celestials, that searcher of hearts, Visnu, although cognizant of the means whereby Rāvana was to be destroyed, asked the gods these amiable words,-What, you gods, is the means of compassing which I could slay that thorn of the ascetics? Nara means a multitude, and Ayana, dwellingplace. He whose dwelling-place is a multitude, is Nārāyana. Metaphorically, the word means evidently the Scorcher of hearts, worlds, and dreadful to ascetics!

sanskrit: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च
transliteration: śhrotraṁ chakṣhuḥ sparśhanaṁ cha rasanaṁ ghrāṇam eva cha
english: And presiding over the senses of hearing and seeing and touch, and taste, and smell, and the mind, he enjoys sensuous objects.

sanskrit: उपायः को वधे तस्य राक्ष्साधिपतेः सुराः
यम् अहम् तम् समास्थाय निहन्याम् ऋषि कण्टकम्
transliteration: upāyaḥ ko vadhe tasya rākṣsādhipateḥ surāḥ
yam aham tam samāsthāya nihanyām ṛṣi kaṇṭakam
english: Thus besought by the foremost of the celestials, that searcher of hearts, Visnu, although cognizant of the means whereby Rāvana was to be destroyed, asked the gods these amiable words,-What, you gods, is the means of compassing which I could slay that thorn of the ascetics? Nara means a multitude, and Ayana, dwellingplace. He whose dwelling-place is a multitude, is Nārāyana. Metaphorically, the word means evidently the Scorcher of hearts, worlds, and dreadful to ascetics!

sanskrit: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम्
transliteration: utkrāmantaṁ sthitaṁ vāpi bhuñjānaṁ vā guṇānvitam
english: Those who are deluded do not see (him) remaining in or quitting (a body), enjoying or joined to the qualities; they see, who have eyes of knowledge.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्ताः सुराः सर्वे प्रत्यूचुः विष्णुम् अव्ययम्
मानुषम् रूपम् आस्थाय रावणम् जहि संयुगे
transliteration: evam uktāḥ surāḥ sarve pratyūcuḥ viṣṇum avyayam
mānuṣam rūpam āsthāya rāvaṇam jahi saṃyuge
english: Thus addressed, the deities answered Visnu, incapable of deterioration, saying,-Assuming the form of a human being, do you in battle slay Rāvana!

transliteration: yatanto yoginaśh chainaṁ paśhyanty ātmany avasthitam
english: Devotees making efforts perceive him abiding within their selfs. But those whose selfs have not been refined, and who have no discernment, do not perceive him even (after) making efforts.

sanskrit: स हि तेपे तपः तीव्रम् दीर्घ कालम् अरिंदम
येन तुष्टोऽभवत् ब्रह्मा लोक कृत् लोक पूर्वजः
transliteration: sa hi tepe tapaḥ tīvram dīrgha kālam ariṃdama
yena tuṣṭo'bhavat brahmā loka kṛt loka pūrvajaḥ
english: He, O repressor of foes, had for a long course of time performed rigid austerities; and thereat, that creator of all, the first-create Brahmā, was well pleased.

transliteration: yach chandramasi yach chāgnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam
english: Know that glory (to be) mine which, dwelling in the sun, lights up the whole world, or in the moon or fire.

sanskrit: सन्तुष्टः प्रददौ तस्मै राक्षसाय वरम् प्रभुः
नानाविधेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो भयम् न अन्यत्र मानुषात्
transliteration: santuṣṭaḥ pradadau tasmai rākṣasāya varam prabhuḥ
nānāvidhebhyo bhūtebhyo bhayam na anyatra mānuṣāt
english: And propitiated by his penances, the Master conferred a boon on the Raksasa to the effect, that, save man, no fear should come to him from the various beings.

sanskrit: पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः
transliteration: gām āviśhya cha bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā
puṣhṇāmi chauṣhadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ
english: Entering the earth, I by my power support all things, and becoming the juicy moon, I nourish all herbs.

sanskrit: अवज्ञाताः पुरा तेन वरदाने हि मानवाः
transliteration: avajñātāḥ purā tena varadāne hi mānavāḥ
english: And in the matter of that boon-bestowing, man had formerly been disregarded (by Ravana). And puffed up with pride in consequence of the boon he received from the Grand-sire.

transliteration: ahaṁ vaiśhvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṁ deham āśhritaḥ
english: I becoming the fire, and dwelling in the bodies of (all) creatures, and united with the upward and downward life-breaths, cause digestion of the fourfold food.

sanskrit: उत्सादयति लोकान् त्रीईन् स्त्रियः च अपि अपकर्षति
तस्मात् तस्य वधो दृष्टो मानुषेभ्यः परन्तप
transliteration: utsādayati lokān trīīn striyaḥ ca api apakarṣati
tasmāt tasya vadho dṛṣṭo mānuṣebhyaḥ parantapa
english: He commits ravages upon the three worlds and carries away the fair sex by violence. Therefore, O subduer of enemies, we have even fixed upon man for bringing about his death.

sanskrit: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च
transliteration: vedaiśh cha sarvair aham eva vedyo
english: And I am placed in the heart of all; from me (come) memory, knowledge, and their removal; I alone am to be learnt from all the Vedas; I am the author of the Vedantas; and I alone know the Vedas.

sanskrit: इति एतत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा सुराणाम् विष्णुः आत्मवान्
transliteration: iti etat vacanam śrutvā surāṇām viṣṇuḥ ātmavān
english: Hearing this speech of the celestials, Vişnu of subdued soul chose even king Dasaratha for his father.

sanskrit: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च
transliteration: dvāv imau puruṣhau loke kṣharaśh chākṣhara eva cha
english: There are these two beings in the world, the destructible and the indestructible. The destructible (includes) all things. The unconcerned one is (what is) called the indestructible.

sanskrit: स च अपि अपुत्रो नृपतिः तस्मिन् काले महाद्युतिः
transliteration: sa ca api aputro nṛpatiḥ tasmin kāle mahādyutiḥ
english: At that time, eagerly wishing to have sons, that destroyer of enemies, the effulgent king Dasaratha, who was sonless, was celebrating the sacrifice that confer male offspring.

transliteration: uttamaḥ puruṣhas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛitaḥ
yo loka-trayam āviśhya bibharty avyaya īśhvaraḥ
english: But the being supreme is yet another, called the highest self, who as the inexhaustible lord, pervading the three worlds, supports (them).

sanskrit: स कृत्वा निश्चयम् विष्णुः आमन्त्र्य च पितामहम्
अन्तर्धानम् गतो देवैः पूज्य मानो महर्षिभिः
transliteration: sa kṛtvā niścayam viṣṇuḥ āmantrya ca pitāmaham
antardhānam gato devaiḥ pūjya māno maharṣibhiḥ
english: Then, having ascertained the course to follow, Visnu, having greeted the Grand-sire, vanished there, worshipped by deities and the Maharsis.

sanskrit: अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः
transliteration: yasmāt kṣharam atīto ’ham akṣharād api chottamaḥ
ato ’smi loke vede cha prathitaḥ puruṣhottamaḥ
english: And since I transcend the destructible, and since I am higher also than the indestructible, therefore am I celebrated in the world and in the Vedas as the best of beings.

sanskrit: ततो वै यजमानस्य पावकात् अतुल प्रभम्
transliteration: tato vai yajamānasya pāvakāt atula prabham
yo mām evam asammūḍho jānāti puruṣhottamam
sa sarva-vid bhajati māṁ sarva-bhāvena bhārata
english: He who, undeluded, thus knows me the best of beings, worships me every way, O descendant of Bharata! knowing everything.

sanskrit: कृष्णम् रक्ताम्बर धरम् रक्ताअस्यम् दुन्दुभि स्वनम्
स्निग्ध हर्यक्ष तनुज श्मश्रु प्रवरम् ऊर्धजम्
transliteration: kṛṣṇam raktāmbara dharam raktāasyam dundubhi svanam
snigdha haryakṣa tanuja śmaśru pravaram ūrdhajam
iti guhyatamaṁ śhāstram idam uktaṁ mayānagha
etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛita-kṛityaśh cha bhārata
english: Thus, O sinless one! have I proclaimed this most mysterious science. He who knows this, has done all he need do, and he becomes possessed of discernment.

sanskrit: शुभ लक्षण संपन्नम् दिव्य आभरण भूषितम्
शैल शृङ्ग समुत्सेधम् दृप्त शार्दूल विक्रमम्
transliteration: śubha lakṣaṇa saṃpannam divya ābharaṇa bhūṣitam
śaila śṛṅga samutsedham dṛpta śārdūla vikramam
dānaṁ damaśh cha yajñaśh cha svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam
english: Freedom from fear, purity of heart, perseverance in (pursuit of) knowledge and abstraction of mind, gifts, self-restraint, and sacrifice, study of the Vedas, penance, straightforwardness,

transliteration: ahinsā satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ śhāntir apaiśhunam
dayā bhūteṣhv aloluptvaṁ mārdavaṁ hrīr achāpalam
english: harmlessness, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranquillity, freedom from the habit of backbiting, compassion for (all) beings, freedom from avarice, gentleness, modesty, absence of vain activity,

sanskrit: दिव्य पायस संपूर्णाम् पात्रीम् पत्नीम् इव प्रियाम्
प्रगृह्य विपुलाम् दोर्भ्याम् स्वयम् मायामयीम् इव
transliteration: divya pāyasa saṃpūrṇām pātrīm patnīm iva priyām
pragṛhya vipulām dorbhyām svayam māyāmayīm iva
tejaḥ kṣhamā dhṛitiḥ śhaucham adroho nāti-mānitā
english: noblemindedness, forgiveness, courage, purity, freedom from a desire to injure others, absence of vanity, (these), O descendant of Bharata! are his who is born to godlike endowments.

sanskrit: समवेक्ष्य अब्रवीत् वाक्यम् इदम् दशरथम् नृपम्
प्राजापत्यम् नरम् विद्धि माम् इह अभ्यागतम् नृप
transliteration: samavekṣya abravīt vākyam idam daśaratham nṛpam
prājāpatyam naram viddhi mām iha abhyāgatam nṛpa
english: He addressed the king, saying, O monarch, take me as a person commissioned by Prajāpati.

transliteration: dambho darpo ’bhimānaśh cha krodhaḥ pāruṣhyam eva cha
english: Ostentatiousness, pride, vanity, anger, and also harshness and ignorance (are) his, O son of Pritha! who is born to demoniac endowments.

sanskrit: ततः परम् तदा राजा प्रति उवाच कृत अंजलिः
भगवन् स्वागतम् तेऽस्तु किमहम् करवाणि ते
transliteration: tataḥ param tadā rājā prati uvāca kṛta aṃjaliḥ
bhagavan svāgatam te'stu kimaham karavāṇi te
english: Hearing him speak thus, Dasaratha, with folded hands, said, Lord, you are welcomed? What can I do for you?

transliteration: mā śhuchaḥ sampadaṁ daivīm abhijāto ’si pāṇḍava
english: Godlike endowments are deemed to be (means) for final emancipation, demoniac for bondage. Grieve not, O descendant of Bharata! you are born to god-like endowments.

sanskrit: अथो पुनः इदम् वाक्यम् प्राजापत्यो नरोऽब्रवीत्
राजन् अर्चयता देवान् अद्य प्राप्तम् इदम् त्वया
transliteration: atho punaḥ idam vākyam prājāpatyo naro'bravīt
rājan arcayatā devān adya prāptam idam tvayā
english: Thereupon, that person despatched by Prajapati again spoke thus, O king, having adored the deities, you have to-day obtained this.

sanskrit: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च
दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे श्रृणु
transliteration: dvau bhūta-sargau loke ’smin daiva āsura eva cha
daivo vistaraśhaḥ prokta āsuraṁ pārtha me śhṛiṇu
english: (There are) two classes of created beings in this world, the godlike and the demoniac; the godlike (class) has been described at length; now hear from me, O son of Pritha! about the demoniac.

sanskrit: इदम् तु नृप शार्दूल पायसम् देव निर्मितम्
प्रजा करम् गृहाण त्वम् धन्यम् आरोग्य वर्धनम्
transliteration: idam tu nṛpa śārdūla pāyasam deva nirmitam
