prajā karam gṛhāṇa tvam dhanyam ārogya vardhanam
english: O tiger of a king, accept this excellent and divinely-prepared Pāyasa, conferring sons, health, and affluence, which you are to give to your worthy consorts, saying, Partake it. Through them you will, O monarch, obtain sons, for obtaining whom you have performed this sacrifice.

sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः
न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते
transliteration: pravṛittiṁ cha nivṛittiṁ cha janā na vidur āsurāḥ
na śhauchaṁ nāpi chāchāro na satyaṁ teṣhu vidyate
english: Demoniac persons know not action or inaction, neither purity nor yet (correct) conduct nor veracity are in them.

sanskrit: भार्याणाम् अनुरूपाणाम् अश्नीत इति प्रयच्छ वै
तासु त्वम् लप्स्यसे पुत्रान् यदर्थम् यजसे नृप
transliteration: bhāryāṇām anurūpāṇām aśnīta iti prayaccha vai
tāsu tvam lapsyase putrān yadartham yajase nṛpa
english: O tiger of a king, accept this excellent and divinely-prepared Pāyasa, conferring sons, health, and affluence, which you are to give to your worthy consorts, saying, Partake it. Through them you will, O monarch, obtain sons, for obtaining whom you have performed this sacrifice.

transliteration: asatyam apratiṣhṭhaṁ te jagad āhur anīśhvaram
english: They say the universe is devoid of truth, devoid of fixed principle, and devoid of a ruler, produced by union (of male and female) caused by lust, and nothing else.

sanskrit: तथा इति नृपतिः प्रीतः शिरसा प्रति गृह्य ताम्
पात्रीम् देव अन्न संपूर्णाम् देव दत्ताम् हिरण्मयीम्
transliteration: tathā iti nṛpatiḥ prītaḥ śirasā prati gṛhya tām
pātrīm deva anna saṃpūrṇām deva dattām hiraṇmayīm
english: Thereupon, saying, So be it, the lord of men delightedly placed that divinely-bestowed golden vessel filled with the divine Payasa upon his head. And having saluted that wonderful being of gracious presence, he in excess of joy began to go round him again and again.
Holding this view, (these) enemies of the world, of ruined; selfs, of little knowledge, and of ferocious actions, are born for the destruction (of the world).

sanskrit: अभिवाद्य च तत् भूतम् अद्भुतम् प्रिय दर्शनम्
transliteration: abhivādya ca tat bhūtam adbhutam priya darśanam
english: Thereupon, saying, So be it, the lord of men delightedly placed that divinely-bestowed golden vessel filled with the divine Payasa upon his head. And having saluted that wonderful being of gracious presence, he in excess of joy began to go round him again and again.
Entertaining insatiable desire, full of vanity, ostentatiousness, and frenzy, they adopt false notions through delusion, and engage in unholy observances.

sanskrit: ततो दशरथः प्राप्य पायसम् देव निर्मितम्
बभूव परम प्रीतः प्राप्य वित्तम् इव अधनः
transliteration: tato daśarathaḥ prāpya pāyasam deva nirmitam
babhūva parama prītaḥ prāpya vittam iva adhanaḥ
english: Then Daśaratha, having received that divinely prepared Pāyasa, waxed exceeding glad; like that of a pauper attaining plenty. Then that highly effulgent being of a wonderful form, having performed that mission of his, vanished even there.
Indulging in boundless thoughts ending with death, given up to the enjoyment of objects of desire, being resolved that that is all,

sanskrit: ततः तत् अद्भुत प्रख्यम् भूतम् परम भास्वरम्
संवर्तयित्वा तत् कर्म तत्र एव अन्तरधीयत
transliteration: tataḥ tat adbhuta prakhyam bhūtam parama bhāsvaram
saṃvartayitvā tat karma tatra eva antaradhīyata
english: Then Daśaratha, having received that divinely prepared Pāyasa, waxed exceeding glad; like that of a pauper attaining plenty. Then that highly effulgent being of a wonderful form, having performed that mission of his, vanished even there.
bound down by nets of hopes in hundreds, given up to anger and desire, they wish to obtain heaps of wealth unfairly for enjoying objects of desire.

sanskrit: हर्ष रश्मिभिः उद्द्योतम् तस्य अन्तःपुरम् आबभौ
शारदस्य अभिरामस्य चंद्रस्य इव नभः अंशुभिः
transliteration: harṣa raśmibhiḥ uddyotam tasya antaḥpuram ābabhau
śāradasya abhirāmasya caṃdrasya iva nabhaḥ aṃśubhiḥ
english: And Dasaratha's inner apartment, being graced with the rays of joy, looked like the welkin flooded with the lovely beams of the autumnal moon.

transliteration: idam adya mayā labdham imaṁ prāpsye manoratham
idam astīdam api me bhaviṣhyati punar dhanam
english: 'This have I obtained to-day; this wish I will obtain; this wealth is mine; and this also shall be mine;

sanskrit: सः अन्तःपुरम् प्रविश्य एव कौसल्याम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
पायसम् प्रतिगृह्णीष्व पुत्रीयम् तु इदम् आत्मनः
transliteration: saḥ antaḥpuram praviśya eva kausalyām idam abravīt
pāyasam pratigṛhṇīṣva putrīyam tu idam ātmanaḥ
english: Then entering the inner apartment, he spoke to Kausalyā, saying, Take you this, Pāyasa; for this will make you bear a son.

transliteration: asau mayā hataḥ śhatrur haniṣhye chāparān api
īśhvaro ’ham ahaṁ bhogī siddho ’haṁ balavān sukhī
english: this foe I have killed; others too I will destroy; I am lord, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, strong, happy;

sanskrit: कौसल्यायै नरपतिः पायस अर्धम् ददौ तदा
अर्धात् अर्धम् ददौ च अपि सुमित्रायै नराधिपः
transliteration: kausalyāyai narapatiḥ pāyasa ardham dadau tadā
ardhāt ardham dadau ca api sumitrāyai narādhipaḥ
english: Having said this, the king offered to her a half portion of this Pāyasa.'Then he conferred upon Sumitrā a fourth of it.
I have wealth; I am of noble birth; who else is like me? I will sacrifice; I will make gifts; I will rejoice.' Thus deluded by ignorance,

sanskrit: कैकेय्यै च अवशिष्ट अर्धम् ददौ पुत्रार्थ कारणात्
प्रददौ च अवशिष्ट अर्धम् पायसस्य अमृत उपमम्
transliteration: kaikeyyai ca avaśiṣṭa ardham dadau putrārtha kāraṇāt
pradadau ca avaśiṣṭa ardham pāyasasya amṛta upamam
english: Then in order that she might have a son, king Dasaratha made over to Kaikeyi an equal portion of what remained. And then having reflected, the mighty-minded one gave to Sumitrā the remaining portion of the Pāyasa resembling ambrosia.

transliteration: aneka-citta-vibhrāntā moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ prasaktāḥ kāma-bhogeṣu patanti narake 'śucau
english: tossed about by numerous thoughts, surrounded by the net of delusion, and attached to the enjoyment of objects of desire, they fall down into impure hell.

sanskrit: एवम् तासाम् ददौ राजा भार्याणाम् पायसम् पृथक्
transliteration: evam tāsām dadau rājā bhāryāṇām pāyasam pṛthak
english: Then in order that she might have a son, king Dasaratha made over to Kaikeyi an equal portion of what remained. And then having reflected, the mighty-minded one gave to Sumitrā the remaining portion of the Pāyasa resembling ambrosia.

Honoured (only) by themselves, void of humility, and full of the pride and frenzy of wealth, these calumniators; (of the virtuous) perform sacrifices, which are sacrifices only in name, with ostentatiousness and against prescribed rules;

sanskrit: ताः च एवम् पायसम् प्राप्य नरेन्द्रस्य उत्तमाः स्त्रियः
सम्मानम् मेनिरे सर्वाः प्रहर्ष उदित चेतसः
transliteration: tāḥ ca evam pāyasam prāpya narendrasya uttamāḥ striyaḥ
sammānam menire sarvāḥ praharṣa udita cetasaḥ
english: Thus the king dispensed the Pāyasa to each and all of his wives. And those foremost wives of the king, having received that Pāyasa, became exceedingly delighted, and considered themselves as highly honoured.

sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः
transliteration: ahankāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ cha sanśhritāḥ
english: indulging (their) vanity, brute force, arrogance, lust, and anger; and hating me in their own bodies and in those of others.

sanskrit: ततस्तु ताः प्राश्य तद् उत्तम स्त्रियोमहीपतेः उत्तम पायसम् पृथक्
हुताशन आदित्य समान तेजसःअचिरेण गर्भान् प्रतिपेदिरे तदा
transliteration: tatastu tāḥ prāśya tad uttama striyomahīpateḥ uttama pāyasam pṛthak
hutāśana āditya samāna tejasaḥacireṇa garbhān pratipedire tadā
english: Then those excellent consorts of the lord of earth, having separately partaken of that choice Pāyasa, shortly bore offspring, resembling fire or the Sun.

transliteration: tān ahaṁ dviṣhataḥ krūrān sansāreṣhu narādhamān
kṣhipāmy ajasram aśhubhān āsurīṣhv eva yoniṣhu
english: These enemies, ferocious, meanest of men, and unholy, I continually hurl down to these worlds, only into demoniac wombs.

sanskrit: ततस्तु राजा प्रतिवीक्ष्य ताः स्त्रियःप्ररूढ गर्भाः प्रति लब्ध मानसः
बभूव हृष्टः त्रिदिवे यथा हरिःसुरेन्द्र सिद्ध ऋषि गणाभिपूजितः
transliteration: tatastu rājā prativīkṣya tāḥ striyaḥprarūḍha garbhāḥ prati labdha mānasaḥ
babhūva hṛṣṭaḥ tridive yathā hariḥsurendra siddha ṛṣi gaṇābhipūjitaḥ
english: The king, beholding those wives of his bearing children, obtained his desire and became delighted; Vişnu, while being worshipped by the Siddhas and the ascetics. even as

transliteration: āsurīṁ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani
mām aprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṁ gatim
english: Coming into demoniac wombs, deluded in every birth, they go down to the vilest state, O son of Kunti! without ever coming to me.

sanskrit: पुत्रत्वम् तु गते विष्णौ राज्ञः तस्य महात्मनः
उवाच देवताः सर्वाः स्वयंभूः भगवान् इदम्
transliteration: putratvam tu gate viṣṇau rājñaḥ tasya mahātmanaḥ
uvāca devatāḥ sarvāḥ svayaṃbhūḥ bhagavān idam
english: When Vişņu had accepted the sonship of that high-souled king, the self-create Lord addressed the celestials, saying,

transliteration: kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṁ tyajet
english: Threefold is this way to hell, ruinous to the self, lust, anger, and likewise avarice; therefore one should abandon this triad.

sanskrit: सत्य संधस्य वीरस्य सर्वेषाम् नो हितैषिणः
विष्णोः सहायान् बलिनः सृजध्वम् काम रूपिणः
transliteration: satya saṃdhasya vīrasya sarveṣām no hitaiṣiṇaḥ
viṣṇoḥ sahāyān balinaḥ sṛjadhvam kāma rūpiṇaḥ
etair vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamo-dvārais tribhir naraḥ
ācharaty ātmanaḥ śhreyas tato yāti parāṁ gatim
english: Released from these three ways to darkness, O son of Kunti! a man works out his own salvation, and then proceeds to the highest goal.

sanskrit: माया विदः च शूराम् च वायु वेग समान् जवे
नयज्ञान् बुद्धि संपन्नान् विष्णु तुल्य पराक्रमान्
transliteration: māyā vidaḥ ca śūrām ca vāyu vega samān jave
nayajñān buddhi saṃpannān viṣṇu tulya parākramān

sanskrit: न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम्
transliteration: na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukhaṁ na parāṁ gatim
english: He who abandoning scripture ordinances, acts under the impulse of desire, does not attain perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal.

sanskrit: सर्व अस्त्र गुण संपन्नानन् अमृत प्राशनान् इव
transliteration: sarva astra guṇa saṃpannānan amṛta prāśanān iva

english: Therefore in discriminating between what should be done and what should not be done, your authority (must be) scripture. And knowing what is declared by the ordinances of scripture, you should perform action in this world.

sanskrit: अप्सरस्सु च मुख्यासु गन्धर्वाणाम् तनूषु च
यक्ष पन्नग कन्यासु ऋक्ष विद्याधरीषु च
transliteration: apsarassu ca mukhyāsu gandharvāṇām tanūṣu ca
yakṣa pannaga kanyāsu ṛkṣa vidyādharīṣu ca
english: And from forth the bodies of the foremost Apsaras, Gandharvis, Yaksis, and Pannagis, Rks is (She-bears) and Vidhyādharis, Kinnaris and Vānaris (She-monkeys) do you produce sons wearing the shapes of monkeys.

sanskrit: तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः
transliteration: teṣhāṁ niṣhṭhā tu kā kṛiṣhṇa sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ
english: Arguna said: What is the state of those, O Krishna! who worship with faith, (but) abandoning scripture ordinances goodness, passion, or darkness?

sanskrit: किंनरीणाम् च गात्रेषु वानरीनाम् तनूसु च
सृजध्वम् हरि रूपेण पुत्रान् तुल्य पराक्रमान्
transliteration: kiṃnarīṇām ca gātreṣu vānarīnām tanūsu ca
sṛjadhvam hari rūpeṇa putrān tulya parākramān
english: And from forth the bodies of the foremost Apsaras, Gandharvis, Yaksis, and Pannagis, Rks is (She-bears) and Vidhyādharis, Kinnaris and Vānaris (She-monkeys) do you produce sons wearing the shapes of monkeys.

sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचत्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु
transliteration: tri-vidhā bhavati śhraddhā dehināṁ sā svabhāva-jā
sāttvikī rājasī chaiva tāmasī cheti tāṁ śhṛiṇu
english: The Deity said: Faith is of three kinds in embodied (beings), it is produced from dispositions. It is of the quality of goodness, of the quality of passion, and of the quality of darkness. Hear about it.

sanskrit: पूर्वम् एव मया सृष्टो जांबवान् ऋक्ष पुङ्गवः
transliteration: pūrvam eva mayā sṛṣṭo jāṃbavān ṛkṣa puṅgavaḥ
english: Formerly I had created that foremost of bears, Jāmbavān, who suddenly came out of my mouth as I was yawning.

sanskrit: श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः
transliteration: śhraddhā-mayo ‘yaṁ puruṣho yo yach-chhraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ
english: The faith of all, O descendant of Bharata! is conformable to the heart. A being here is full of faith, and whatever is a man's faith, that is a man himself.

sanskrit: ते तथा उक्ताः भगवता तत् प्रति श्रुत्य शासनम्
जनयामासुः एवम् ते पुत्रान् वानर रूपिणः
transliteration: te tathā uktāḥ bhagavatā tat prati śrutya śāsanam
janayāmāsuḥ evam te putrān vānara rūpiṇaḥ
english: Hearing this mandate of Him possessed of the six attributes, they began to produce sons endowed with monkey's forms.

transliteration: pretān bhūta-gaṇānśh chānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ
english: Those of the quality of goodness worship the gods; those of the quality of passion the Yakshas and Rakshases; and the others, the people of the quality of darkness, worship departed (spirits) and the multitudes of Bhutas.

sanskrit: ऋषयः च महात्मानः सिद्ध विद्याधर उरगाः
चारणाः च सुतान् वीरान् ससृजुः वन चारिणः
transliteration: ṛṣayaḥ ca mahātmānaḥ siddha vidyādhara uragāḥ
cāraṇāḥ ca sutān vīrān sasṛjuḥ vana cāriṇaḥ
english: And high-souled ascetics, and Siddhas, and Vidyādharas, and Uragas, and Caranas, generated heroic sons, rangers of woods.

sanskrit: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः
transliteration: aśhāstra-vihitaṁ ghoraṁ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ
english: Know those to-be of demoniac convictions, who practise fierce penance not ordained by scripture; who are full of ostentatiousness and egoism, and of desire, attachment, and stubbornness; who are without discernment;

sanskrit: वानरेन्द्रम् महेन्द्र आभम् इन्द्रः वालिनम् आत्मजम्
transliteration: vānarendram mahendra ābham indraḥ vālinam ātmajam
english: And Indra beget as his son that foremost of monkeys, Vāli, resembling the Mahendra hill, and that best of those imparting heat, the Sun, Sugriva.

transliteration: māṁ chaivāntaḥ śharīra-sthaṁ tān viddhy āsura-niśhchayān
english: and who torment the groups of organs in (their) bodies, and me also seated within (those) bodies.

sanskrit: बृहस्पतिः तु अजनयत् तारम् नाम महा कपिम्
transliteration: bṛhaspatiḥ tu ajanayat tāram nāma mahā kapim
english: Brhaspati beget the mighty ape named Tāra, who was the most excellent and intelligent of the prime monkeys.

transliteration: āhāras tv api sarvasya tri-vidho bhavati priyaḥ
yajñas tapas tathā dānaṁ teṣhāṁ bhedam imaṁ śhṛiṇu
english: The food also, which is liked by all, and likewise the sacrifice, the penance, and gifts, are of three kinds. Listen to the distinctions regarding them as follows.

sanskrit: विश्वकर्मा तु अजनयन् नलम् नाम महा कपिम्
transliteration: viśvakarmā tu ajanayan nalam nāma mahā kapim
english: The Bestower of riches beget as his son the graceful ape Gandhamādana. And Viśvakarman beget that mighty monkey named Nala.

sanskrit: रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः
transliteration: rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛidyā āhārāḥ sāttvika-priyāḥ
english: The kinds of food which increase life, energy, strength, health, comfort, and relish, which are savoury, oleaginous, full of nutrition, and agreeable, are liked by the good.

sanskrit: पावकस्य सुतः श्रीमान् नीलः अग्नि सदृश प्रभः
transliteration: pāvakasya sutaḥ śrīmān nīlaḥ agni sadṛśa prabhaḥ
english: Agni beget as his son the powerful and graceful Nīla in effulgence like to the fire, who surpassed even his sire in energy, prowess, and renown.
The kinds of food which are bitter, acid, saltish, too hot, sharp, rough, and burning, and which cause pain, grief, and disease, are desired by the passionate.

sanskrit: मैन्दम् च द्विविदम् च एव जनयामासतुः स्वयम्
transliteration: maindam ca dvividam ca eva janayāmāsatuḥ svayam
english: And the beautiful Asvins, endowed with the wealth of loveliness, beget Mainda and Dvivida.

sanskrit: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत्
transliteration: yāta-yāmaṁ gata-rasaṁ pūti paryuṣhitaṁ cha yat
english: And the food which is cold, tasteless, stinking, stale, impure, and even leavings, are liked by the dark.
Varuņa beget the monkey named Sușeņa; and Parjanya beget Sarabha, possessed of great strength.

transliteration: yaṣhṭavyam eveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ
english: That sacrifice is good which, being prescribed in (scripture) ordinances, is performed by persons not wishing for the fruit (of it), and after determining (in their) mind that the sacrifice must needs be performed.

sanskrit: मारुतस्य औरसः श्रीमान् हनुमान् नाम वानरः
transliteration: mārutasya aurasaḥ śrīmān hanumān nāma vānaraḥ
english: And the Wind-god beget the graceful monkey named Hanumān, endued with a frame hard as adamant; in fleetness like to Vinatā's offspring.

sanskrit: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम्
transliteration: abhisandhāya tu phalaṁ dambhārtham api chaiva yat
ijyate bharata-śhreṣhṭha taṁ yajñaṁ viddhi rājasam
english: But when a sacrifice is performed, O highest of the descendants of Bharata! with an expectation of fruit (from it), and for the purpose of ostentation, know that sacrifice (to be) passionate.

sanskrit: सर्व वानर मुख्येषु बुद्धिमान् बलवान् अपि
ते सृष्टा बहु साहस्रा दशग्रीव वधे उद्यताः
transliteration: sarva vānara mukhyeṣu buddhimān balavān api
te sṛṣṭā bahu sāhasrā daśagrīva vadhe udyatāḥ
english: And the most intelligent as well as the most powerful amongst all the principal monkeys. Thus produced, there suddenly came into being by thousands, mighty bears, and monkeys, and Gopucchas, (Cow-tailed monkeys.) and of immeasurable strength, and heroic, and powerful, assuming shapes at will, endowed with bodies resembling elephants or hills, even those who would engage in compassing the destruction of the Ten-headed Rāvana.

They call that sacrifice dark, which is against the ordinances (of scripture), in which no food is dealt out (to Brahmanas, &c.), which is devoid of Mantras, devoid of Dakshina presents, and which is without faith.

sanskrit: अप्रमेय बला वीरा विक्रान्ताः काम रूपिणः
ते गज अचल संकाशा वपुष्मंतो महाबलाः
transliteration: aprameya balā vīrā vikrāntāḥ kāma rūpiṇaḥ
te gaja acala saṃkāśā vapuṣmaṃto mahābalāḥ
brahmacharyam ahinsā cha śhārīraṁ tapa uchyate
english: Paying reverence to gods, Brahmanas, preceptors, and men of knowledge; purity, straightforwardness, life as Brahmakarin, and harmlessness, (this) is called the penance bodily.

sanskrit: ऋक्ष वानर गोपुच्छाः क्षिप्रम् एव अभिजज्ञिरे
यस्य देवस्य यद् रूपम् वेषो यः च पराक्रमः
transliteration: ṛkṣa vānara gopucchāḥ kṣipram eva abhijajñire
yasya devasya yad rūpam veṣo yaḥ ca parākramaḥ

sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्
transliteration: anudvega-karaṁ vākyaṁ satyaṁ priya-hitaṁ cha yat
english: The speech which causes no sorrow, which is true, agreeable, and beneficial, and the study of the Vedas, (this) is called the penance vocal.

sanskrit: अजायत समम् तेन तस्य तस्य पृथक् पृथक्
गोलान्गूलेषु च उत्पन्नाः किंचिद् उन्नत विक्रमाः
transliteration: ajāyata samam tena tasya tasya pṛthak pṛthak
golāngūleṣu ca utpannāḥ kiṃcid unnata vikramāḥ
english: The sons of the deities retained distinctly the respective hues, forins, and prowess, that characterized their several sires. And those that sprang from the Golāngulas, possessed even more than the might of the gods.

transliteration: bhāva-sanśhuddhir ity etat tapo mānasam uchyate
english: Calmness of mind, mildness, taciturnity, selfrestraint, and purity of heart, this is called the penance mental.

sanskrit: ऋक्षीषु च तथा जाता वानराः किंनरीषु च
देवा महर्षि गन्धर्वाः तार्क्ष्य यक्षा यशस्विनः
transliteration: ṛkṣīṣu ca tathā jātā vānarāḥ kiṃnarīṣu ca
devā maharṣi gandharvāḥ tārkṣya yakṣā yaśasvinaḥ
english: Likewise, on Rksis and Kinnaris were gladly begot thousands upon thousands of monkeys, by the gods, Maharsis, Gandharvas, Tarksyas, and famous Yaksas, Nagas, and Kimpurusas (beings half-man and half-beast) Siddhas, Vidyadharas, and Uragas.

transliteration: śhraddhayā parayā taptaṁ tapas tat tri-vidhaṁ naraiḥ
english: This threefold penance, practised with perfect faith, by men who do not wish for the fruit, and who are possessed of devotion, is called good.

sanskrit: नागाः किम्पुरुषाः च एव सिद्ध विद्याधर उरगाः
transliteration: nāgāḥ kimpuruṣāḥ ca eva siddha vidyādhara uragāḥ
english: Likewise, on Rksis and Kinnaris were gladly begot thousands upon thousands of monkeys, by the gods, Maharsis, Gandharvas, Tarksyas, and famous Yaksas, Nagas, and Kimpurusas (beings half-man and half-beast) Siddhas, Vidyadharas, and Uragas.

transliteration: kriyate tad iha proktaṁ rājasaṁ chalam adhruvam
english: The penance which is done for respect, honour, and reverence, and with ostentatiousness, and which is uncertain and transient, is here called passionate.

sanskrit: चारणाः च सुतान् वीरान् ससृजुः वन चारिणः
वानरान् सु महाकायान् सर्वान् वै वन चारिणः
transliteration: cāraṇāḥ ca sutān vīrān sasṛjuḥ vana cāriṇaḥ
vānarān su mahākāyān sarvān vai vana cāriṇaḥ
english: Upon the principal Apsaris, and the Vidyadharis, and the daughters of the Nāgas, and the Gandharvis were begot by the Cāraņas as sons, heroic monkeys of gigantic bodies, ranging the forests and living on fruits and roots.
And that penance is described as dark, which is performed under a misguided conviction, with pain to oneself, or for the destruction of another.

sanskrit: अप्सरस्सु च मुख्यासु तदा विद्यधरीषु च
नाग कन्यासु च तदा गन्धर्वीणाम् तनूषु च
काम रूप बलोपेता यथा काम विचारिणः
transliteration: apsarassu ca mukhyāsu tadā vidyadharīṣu ca
nāga kanyāsu ca tadā gandharvīṇām tanūṣu ca
kāma rūpa balopetā yathā kāma vicāriṇaḥ
english: Upon the principal Apsaris, and the Vidyadharis, and the daughters of the Nāgas, and the Gandharvis were begot by the Cāraņas as sons, heroic monkeys of gigantic bodies, ranging the forests and living on fruits and roots.

sanskrit: देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्
transliteration: deśhe kāle cha pātre cha tad dānaṁ sāttvikaṁ smṛitam
english: That gift is said (to be) good, which is given, because it ought to be given, to one who (can) do no service (in return), at a (proper) place and time, and to a (proper) person.

sanskrit: सिंह शार्दूल सदृशा दर्पेण च बलेन च
शिला प्रहरणाः सर्वे सर्वे पर्वत योधिनः
transliteration: siṃha śārdūla sadṛśā darpeṇa ca balena ca
śilā praharaṇāḥ sarve sarve parvata yodhinaḥ
english: All these monkeys were endowed with strength; and could assume shapes and repair everywhere, at will. And they were like to lions and tigers, both in pride and in prowess. And they fought with crags and hurled hills.

sanskrit: दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम्
transliteration: yat tu pratyupakārārthaṁ phalam uddiśhya vā punaḥ
dīyate cha parikliṣhṭaṁ tad dānaṁ rājasaṁ smṛitam
english: But that gift which is given with much difficulty, for a return of services, or even with an expectation of fruit, is said to be passionate.

sanskrit: नख दन्ष्ट्र आयुधाः सर्वे सर्वे सर्व अस्त्र कोविदाः
विचाल येयुः शैलेन्द्रान् भेद येयुः स्थिरान् द्रुमान्
transliteration: nakha danṣṭra āyudhāḥ sarve sarve sarva astra kovidāḥ
vicāla yeyuḥ śailendrān bheda yeyuḥ sthirān drumān
english: And they fought with nails and teeth, and were accomplished in all weapons. And they could move the largest hills, and crush the fixed trees,

transliteration: adeśha-kāle yad dānam apātrebhyaśh cha dīyate
english: And that gift is described as dark, which is given to unfit persons, at an unfit place and time, without respect, and with contempt.

sanskrit: क्षोभ येयुः च वेगेन समुद्रम् सरिताम् पतिम्
दार येयुः क्षितिम् पद्भ्याम् आप्लवेयुः महा अर्णवन्
transliteration: kṣobha yeyuḥ ca vegena samudram saritām patim
dāra yeyuḥ kṣitim padbhyām āplaveyuḥ mahā arṇavan
english: With their impetus, vex that lord of rivers, the Ocean. And they could with their kicks rend the Earth, and swim over the mighty main.

transliteration: oṁ tat sad iti nirdeśho brahmaṇas tri-vidhaḥ smṛitaḥ
brāhmaṇās tena vedāśh cha yajñāśh cha vihitāḥ purā
english: Om, Tad, and Sat, this is said (to be) the threefold designation of the Brahman. By that, the Brahmanas and the Vedas and sacrifices were created in olden times.

sanskrit: नभस्थलम् विशेयुर् च गृह्णीयुर् अपि तोयदान्
गृह्णीयुर् अपि मातंगान् मत्तान् प्रव्रजतो वने
transliteration: nabhasthalam viśeyur ca gṛhṇīyur api toyadān
gṛhṇīyur api mātaṃgān mattān pravrajato vane
english: They could penetrate into the welkin, and capture the clouds. And they could subdue mad elephants ranging the forest.
Hence, the performance by those who study the Brahman, of sacrifices, gifts, and penances, prescribed by the ordinances (of scripture, always commence after saying 'Om.'

sanskrit: नर्दमानाः च नादेन पात येयुः विहंगमान्
transliteration: nardamānāḥ ca nādena pāta yeyuḥ vihaṃgamān
english: And with their roars, they could bring down birds singing. Thus came into being Koțis of high-souled leaders of monkey-herds, assuming forms at will.
Those who desire final emancipation perform the various acts of sacrifice and penance, and the various acts of gift, without expectation of fruit, after (saying) 'Tad.'

sanskrit: प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते
transliteration: sad-bhāve sādhu-bhāve cha sad ity etat prayujyate
praśhaste karmaṇi tathā sach-chhabdaḥ pārtha yujyate
english: 'Sat' is employed to express existence and goodness; and likewise, O son of Pritha! the word 'Sat' is used to express an auspicious act.

sanskrit: बभूवुर् यूथप श्रेष्ठान् वीराम् च अजनयन् हरीन्
transliteration: babhūvur yūthapa śreṣṭhān vīrām ca ajanayan harīn

sanskrit: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते
transliteration: yajñe tapasi dāne cha sthitiḥ sad iti chochyate
karma chaiva tad-arthīyaṁ sad ity evābhidhīyate
english: Constancy in (making) sacrifices, penances, and gifts, is called 'Sat'; and (all) action, too, of which that is the object, is also called 'Sat.'

sanskrit: अन्ये नाना विधान् शैलान् काननानि च भेजिरे
सूर्य पुत्रम् च सुग्रीवम् शक्र पुत्रम् च वालिनम्
transliteration: anye nānā vidhān śailān kānanāni ca bhejire
sūrya putram ca sugrīvam śakra putram ca vālinam

sanskrit: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत्
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह
transliteration: aśhraddhayā hutaṁ dattaṁ tapas taptaṁ kṛitaṁ cha yat
asad ity uchyate pārtha na cha tat pretya no iha
english: Whatever oblation is offered, whatever is given, whatever penance is performed, and whatever is done, without faith, that, O son of Pritha! is called 'Asat,' and that is nought, both after death and here.

sanskrit: भ्रातरौ उपतस्थुः ते सर्वे च हरि यूथपाअः
नलम् नीलम् हनूमन्तम् अन्यांश्च हरि यूथपान्
transliteration: bhrātarau upatasthuḥ te sarve ca hari yūthapāaḥ
nalam nīlam hanūmantam anyāṃśca hari yūthapān

english: Arguna said: O you of mighty arms! O Hrishikesa! O destroyer of Kesin! I wish to know the truth about renunciation and abandonment distinctly.

sanskrit: ते तार्क्ष्य बल संपन्नाः सर्वे युद्ध विशारदाः
transliteration: te tārkṣya bala saṃpannāḥ sarve yuddha viśāradāḥ
english: All the leaders of monkey-herds stayed with those brothers, Sugriva, the son of the Sun-god and Vali, that of Sakra, and also with Nala, and Nila, and Hanuman, and other leaders of monkey-herds. And endowed with the might of Garuda, and accomplished in fight, they ranged around, pounding lions, and tigers, and mighty Uragas.

sanskrit: काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः
transliteration: kāmyānāṁ karmaṇāṁ nyāsaṁ sannyāsaṁ kavayo viduḥ
english: The Deity said: By renunciation the sages understand the rejection of actions done with desires. The wise call the abandonment of the fruit of all actions (by the name) abandonment.

sanskrit: जुगोप भुज वीर्येण ऋक्ष गोपुच्छ वानरान्
transliteration: jugopa bhuja vīryeṇa ṛkṣa gopuccha vānarān
english: And the mighty-armed Vālī of great prowess and redoubtable strength protected by virtue of the energy of his arms Ķkşas, and Gopucchas, and monkeys.

transliteration: tyājyaṁ doṣha-vad ity eke karma prāhur manīṣhiṇaḥ
english: Some wise men say, that action should be abandoned as being full of evil; and others, that the actions of sacrifice, gift, and penance should not be abandoned.

sanskrit: तैः इयम् पृध्वी शूरैः सपर्वत वन अर्णवा
कीर्णा विविध संस्थानैः नाना व्यंजन लक्षणैः
transliteration: taiḥ iyam pṛdhvī śūraiḥ saparvata vana arṇavā
kīrṇā vividha saṃsthānaiḥ nānā vyaṃjana lakṣaṇaiḥ

sanskrit: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम
transliteration: niśhchayaṁ śhṛiṇu me tatra tyāge bharata-sattama
english: As to that abandonment, O best of the descendants of Bharata! listen to my decision; for abandonment, O bravest of men! is described (to be) threefold.

sanskrit: तैः मेघ बृन्दाचल कूट संनिभैःमहाबलैः वानर यूथप अधिपैः
बभूव भूः भीम शरीर रूपैःसमावृता राम सहाय हेतोः
transliteration: taiḥ megha bṛndācala kūṭa saṃnibhaiḥmahābalaiḥ vānara yūthapa adhipaiḥ
babhūva bhūḥ bhīma śarīra rūpaiḥsamāvṛtā rāma sahāya hetoḥ
english: This earth, furnished with mountains, and forests, and oceans, began to teem with those heroic lords of leaders of monkey-herds, inhabiting different places, bearing characteristic marks, resembling masses of clouds, mountain-peaks, possessed of mighty strength, and of terrible bodies and visages, in order that they might assist Rāma. or

transliteration: yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyaṁ kāryam eva tat
yajño dānaṁ tapaśh chaiva pāvanāni manīṣhiṇām
english: The actions of sacrifice, gift, and penance should not be abandoned; they must needs be performed; for sacrifices, gifts, and penances are means of sanctification to the wise.

sanskrit: निर्वृत्ते तु क्रतौ तस्मिन् हयमेधे महात्मनः
प्रति गृह्य अमरा भागान् प्रतिजग्मुः यथा आगतम्
transliteration: nirvṛtte tu kratau tasmin hayamedhe mahātmanaḥ
prati gṛhya amarā bhāgān pratijagmuḥ yathā āgatam
english: When the horse-sacrifice of the high-souled Dasaratha had been completed, the immortals, accepting each his share, returned whence they had come.

sanskrit: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च
transliteration: etāny api tu karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā phalāni cha
kartavyānīti me pārtha niśhchitaṁ matam uttamam
english: But even these actions, O son of Pritha! should be performed, abandoning attachment and fruit; such is my excellent and decided opinion.

sanskrit: समाप्त दीक्षा नियमः पत्नी गण समन्वितः
प्रविवेश पुरीम् राजा स भृत्य बल वाहनः
transliteration: samāpta dīkṣā niyamaḥ patnī gaṇa samanvitaḥ
praviveśa purīm rājā sa bhṛtya bala vāhanaḥ
english: And the monarch, having observed all the rules of initiation, entered the palace with his equipage and retinue.
The renunciation of prescribed action is not proper. Its abandonment through delusion I is described as of the quality of darkness.

sanskrit: यथा अर्हम् पूजिताः तेन राज्ञा च पृथिवीश्वराः
मुदिताः प्रययुः देशान् प्रणम्य मुनि पुंगवम्
transliteration: yathā arham pūjitāḥ tena rājñā ca pṛthivīśvarāḥ
muditāḥ prayayuḥ deśān praṇamya muni puṃgavam
english: And the lords of the earth, having been received suitably by the king, with glad hearts set out for their own countries, saluting that foremost of ascetics (Rsyaśặnga).

sanskrit: स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत्
transliteration: duḥkham ity eva yat karma kāya-kleśha-bhayāt tyajet
sa kṛitvā rājasaṁ tyāgaṁ naiva tyāga-phalaṁ labhet
english: When a man abandons action, merely as being troublesome, through fear of bodily affliction, he does not obtain the fruit of abandonment by making (such) passionate abandonment.

sanskrit: श्रीमताम् गच्छताम् तेषाम् स्वगृहाणि पुरात् ततः
transliteration: śrīmatām gacchatām teṣām svagṛhāṇi purāt tataḥ
english: And clad in bright apparel, the delighted Own forces belonging to those graceful kings repairing to their homes, looked exceedingly beautiful.

sanskrit: सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः
transliteration: kāryam ity eva yat karma niyataṁ kriyate ‘rjuna
saṅgaṁ tyaktvā phalaṁ chaiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ
english: When prescribed action is performed, O Arguna! abandoning attachment and fruit also, merely because it ought to be performed, that is deemed (to be) a good abandonment.
When the lords of the earth had gone away, the graceful king Dasaratha re-entered his palace, with the foremost of regenerate ones at his head.

transliteration: na dveṣhṭy akuśhalaṁ karma kuśhale nānuṣhajjate
english: He who is possessed of abandonment, being full of goodness, and talented, and having his doubts destroyed, is not averse from unpleasant actions, is not attached to pleasant (ones).

Followed by the intelligent monarch with his retinue, Rsyasrnga, having been duly honoured, set out with śāntā. Having thus dismissed them all, the king, his object attained, began to dwell there happily, expecting sons.

sanskrit: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः
transliteration: na hi deha-bhṛitā śhakyaṁ tyaktuṁ karmāṇy aśheṣhataḥ
yas tu karma-phala-tyāgī sa tyāgīty abhidhīyate
english: Since no embodied (being) can abandon actions without exception, he is said to be possessed of abandonment, who abandons the fruit of action.

sanskrit: एवम् विसृज्य तान् सर्वान् राजा संपूर्ण मानसः
उवास सुखितः तत्र पुत्र उत्पत्तिम् विचिंतयन्
transliteration: evam visṛjya tān sarvān rājā saṃpūrṇa mānasaḥ
uvāsa sukhitaḥ tatra putra utpattim viciṃtayan
english: Followed by the intelligent monarch with his retinue, Rsyasrnga, having been duly honoured, set out with śāntā. Having thus dismissed them all, the king, his object attained, began to dwell there happily, expecting sons.

sanskrit: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम्
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित्
transliteration: aniṣhṭam iṣhṭaṁ miśhraṁ cha tri-vidhaṁ karmaṇaḥ phalam
bhavaty atyāgināṁ pretya na tu sannyāsināṁ kvachit
english: The threefold fruit of action, agreeable, disagreeable, and mixed, accrues after death to those who are not possessed of abandonment, but never to renouncers.

sanskrit: ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु ऋतूनाम् षट् समत्ययुः
ततः च द्वादशे मासे चैत्रे नावमिके तिथौ
transliteration: tato yajñe samāpte tu ṛtūnām ṣaṭ samatyayuḥ
tataḥ ca dvādaśe māse caitre nāvamike tithau

english: Learn from me, O you of mighty arms! these five causes of the completion of all actions, declared in the Sankhya system.

sanskrit: नक्क्षत्रे अदिति दैवत्ये स्व उच्छ संस्थेषु पंचसु
ग्रहेषु कर्कटे लग्ने वाक्पता इंदुना सह
transliteration: nakkṣatre aditi daivatye sva uccha saṃstheṣu paṃcasu
graheṣu karkaṭe lagne vākpatā iṃdunā saha

sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्
transliteration: adhiṣhṭhānaṁ tathā kartā karaṇaṁ cha pṛithag-vidham
vividhāśh cha pṛithak cheṣhṭā daivaṁ chaivātra pañchamam
english: The substratum, the agent likewise, the various sorts of organs, and the various and distinct movements, and with these the deities, too, as the fifth.

sanskrit: कौसल्या अजनयत् रामम् सर्व लक्षण संयुतम्
transliteration: kausalyā ajanayat rāmam sarva lakṣaṇa saṃyutam

sanskrit: न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः
transliteration: nyāyyaṁ vā viparītaṁ vā pañchaite tasya hetavaḥ
english: Whatever action, just or otherwise, a man performs with his body, speech, and mind, these five are its causes.

sanskrit: विष्णोः अर्धम् महाभागम् पुत्रम् ऐक्ष्वाकु नंदनम्
लोहिताक्षम् महाबाहुम् रक्त ओष्टम् दुंदुभि स्वनम्
transliteration: viṣṇoḥ ardham mahābhāgam putram aikṣvāku naṃdanam
lohitākṣam mahābāhum rakta oṣṭam duṃdubhi svanam

sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः
transliteration: tatraivaṁ sati kartāram ātmānaṁ kevalaṁ tu yaḥ
paśhyaty akṛita-buddhitvān na sa paśhyati durmatiḥ
english: That being so, the undiscerning man, who being of an unrefined understanding, sees the agent in the immaculate self, sees not (rightly).

sanskrit: कौसल्या शुशुभे तेन पुत्रेण अमित तेजसा
यथा वरेण देवानाम् अदितिः वज्र पाणिना
transliteration: kausalyā śuśubhe tena putreṇa amita tejasā
yathā vareṇa devānām aditiḥ vajra pāṇinā

sanskrit: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते
transliteration: yasya nāhankṛito bhāvo buddhir yasya na lipyate
hatvā ‘pi sa imāl lokān na hanti na nibadhyate
english: He who has no feeling of egoism, and whose mind is not tainted, even though he kills (all) these people, kills not, is not fettered (by the action).

sanskrit: भरतो नाम कैकेय्याम् जज्ञे सत्य पराक्रमः
साक्षात् विष्णोः चतुर्थ भागः सर्वैः समुदितो गुणैः
transliteration: bharato nāma kaikeyyām jajñe satya parākramaḥ
sākṣāt viṣṇoḥ caturtha bhāgaḥ sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ
english: Then was born of Kaikeyī, named Bharata, having truth for prowess, endowed with all the virtues, and representing the very fourth part of Visnu.
Knowledge, the object of knowledge, the knower threefold is the prompting to action. The instrument, the action, the agent, thus in brief is action threefold.

sanskrit: अथ लक्ष्मण शत्रुघ्नौ सुमित्रा अजनयत् सुतौ
वीरौ सर्व अस्त्र कुशलौ विष्णोः अर्ध समन्वितौ
transliteration: atha lakṣmaṇa śatrughnau sumitrā ajanayat sutau
vīrau sarva astra kuśalau viṣṇoḥ ardha samanvitau
english: Then Sumitrā gave birth to Lakşmaņa and Satrughna, heroic, and skilled in all weapons, and endowed with the half of Vişnu.

sanskrit: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः
transliteration: jñānaṁ karma cha kartā cha tridhaiva guṇa-bhedataḥ
prochyate guṇa-saṅkhyāne yathāvach chhṛiṇu tāny api
english: Knowledge and action and agent are declared in the enumeration of qualities (to be) of three classes only, according to the difference of qualities. Hear about these also as they really are.

sanskrit: पुष्ये जातः तु भरतो मीन लग्ने प्रसन्न धीः
सार्पे जातौ तु सौमित्री कुLईरे अभ्युदिते रवौ
transliteration: puṣye jātaḥ tu bharato mīna lagne prasanna dhīḥ
sārpe jātau tu saumitrī kuīre abhyudite ravau
english: And Bharata of purged intelligence was born under the asterism Pușya, when the Sun had entered Pisces; while the two sons of Sumitrā were born when the Sun arose in Cancer, under the asterism of Aslesa. (The ninth lunar mansion)

transliteration: avibhaktaṁ vibhakteṣhu taj jñānaṁ viddhi sāttvikam
english: Know that knowledge to be good, by which (a man) sees one entity, inexhaustible, and not different in all things (apparently) different (from one another).

sanskrit: राज्ञः पुत्रा महात्मानः चत्वारो जज्ञिरे पृथक्
गुणवंतः अनुरूपाः च रुच्या प्रोष्ठ पदोपमाः
transliteration: rājñaḥ putrā mahātmānaḥ catvāro jajñire pṛthak
guṇavaṃtaḥ anurūpāḥ ca rucyā proṣṭha padopamāḥ
english: Thus were separately born four high-souled sons to the king, crowned with qualities, and graceful, and in loveliness resembling the constellations Prosthapada.* Thereat the Gandharvas began to chaunt sweetly, and the Apsaras to dance. And the celestial kettledrums sounded; and there showered down blossoms from the sky. *Otherwise called Uttarabhadrapada and Purvabhādrapada.

sanskrit: वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम्
transliteration: pṛithaktvena tu yaj jñānaṁ nānā-bhāvān pṛithag-vidhān
vetti sarveṣhu bhūteṣhu taj jñānaṁ viddhi rājasam
english: Know that knowledge to be passionate, which is (based) on distinctions (between different entities), which sees in all things various entities of different kinds.

sanskrit: जगुः कलम् च गंधर्वा ननृतुः च अप्सरो गणाः
देव दुंदुभयो नेदुः पुष्प वृष्टिः च खात् पतत्
transliteration: jaguḥ kalam ca gaṃdharvā nanṛtuḥ ca apsaro gaṇāḥ
deva duṃdubhayo neduḥ puṣpa vṛṣṭiḥ ca khāt patat
english: Thus were separately born four high-souled sons to the king, crowned with qualities, and graceful, and in loveliness resembling the constellations Prosthapada.* Thereat the Gandharvas began to chaunt sweetly, and the Apsaras to dance. And the celestial kettledrums sounded; and there showered down blossoms from the sky. *Otherwise called Uttarabhadrapada and Purvabhādrapada.

transliteration: yat tu kṛitsna-vad ekasmin kārye saktam ahaitukam
atattvārtha-vad alpaṁ cha tat tāmasam udāhṛitam
english: And that is described as dark, which clings to one created (thing) only as everything, which is devoid of reason, devoid of real principle, and insignificant.

sanskrit: उत्सवः च महान् आसीत् अयोध्यायाम् जनाकुलः
रथ्याः च जन संबाधा नट नर्तक संकुलाः
transliteration: utsavaḥ ca mahān āsīt ayodhyāyām janākulaḥ
rathyāḥ ca jana saṃbādhā naṭa nartaka saṃkulāḥ
aphala-prepsunā karma yat tat sāttvikam uchyate
english: That action is called good, which is prescribed, which is devoid of attachment, which is not done from (motives of) affection or aversion, (and which is done) by one not wishing for the fruit.

sanskrit: गायनैः च विराविण्यो वादनैः च तथ अपरैः
विरेजुर् विपुलाः तत्र सर्व रत्न समन्विताः
transliteration: gāyanaiḥ ca virāviṇyo vādanaiḥ ca tatha aparaiḥ
virejur vipulāḥ tatra sarva ratna samanvitāḥ

sanskrit: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः
transliteration: yat tu kāmepsunā karma sāhankāreṇa vā punaḥ
english: That is described as passionate, which (occasions) much trouble, is performed by one who wishes for objects of desire, or one who is full of egotism.

sanskrit: प्रदेयांश्च ददौ राजा सूत मागध वंदिनाम्
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ वित्तम् गो धनानि सहस्रशः
transliteration: pradeyāṃśca dadau rājā sūta māgadha vaṃdinām
brāhmaṇebhyo dadau vittam go dhanāni sahasraśaḥ
anubandhaṁ kṣhayaṁ hinsām anapekṣhya cha pauruṣham
mohād ārabhyate karma yat tat tāmasam uchyate
english: The action is called dark, which is commenced through delusion, without regard to consequences, loss, injury, or strength.

sanskrit: अतीत्य एकादश आहम् तु नाम कर्म तथा अकरोत्
ज्येष्ठम् रामम् महात्मानम् भरतम् कैकयी सुतम्
transliteration: atītya ekādaśa āham tu nāma karma tathā akarot
jyeṣṭham rāmam mahātmānam bharatam kaikayī sutam
english: When the eleventh day had gone by, the king performed the Naming ceremony of his sons. And experiencing great delight, Vasistha conferred the names. And the high-souled eldest one was called Rāma; and Kaikeyi's son was called Bharata; and Sumitrā's son was called Laksmana, and the last was named Satrughna.
That agent is called good, who has cast off attachment, who is free from egotistic talk, who is possessed of courage and energy, and unaffected by success or ill-success.

sanskrit: सौमित्रिम् लक्ष्मणम् इति शत्रुघ्नम् अपरम् तथा
वसिष्ठः परम प्रीतो नामानि कुरुते तदा
transliteration: saumitrim lakṣmaṇam iti śatrughnam aparam tathā
vasiṣṭhaḥ parama prīto nāmāni kurute tadā
english: When the eleventh day had gone by, the king performed the Naming ceremony of his sons. And experiencing great delight, Vasistha conferred the names. And the high-souled eldest one was called Rāma; and Kaikeyi's son was called Bharata; and Sumitrā's son was called Laksmana, and the last was named Satrughna.
That agent is called passionate, who is full of affections, who wishes for the fruit of actions, who is covetous, cruel, and impure, and feels joy and sorrow.

sanskrit: उददद् ब्राह्मणानाम् च रत्नौघम् अमलम् बहु
transliteration: udadad brāhmaṇānām ca ratnaugham amalam bahu
english: And the king fed the Brāhmaṇas as well as the inhabitants rural and urban; and he bestowed heaps of jewels upon Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते
transliteration: viṣhādī dīrgha-sūtrī cha kartā tāmasa uchyate
english: That agent is called dark, who is without application, void of discernment, headstrong, crafty, malicious, lazy, melancholy, and slow.

sanskrit: तेषाम् जन्म क्रिय आदीनि सर्व कर्माणि अकारयत्
तेषाम् केतुः इव ज्येष्ठो रामो रतिकरः पितुः
transliteration: teṣām janma kriya ādīni sarva karmāṇi akārayat
teṣām ketuḥ iva jyeṣṭho rāmo ratikaraḥ pituḥ
english: Thus did he celebrate the natal rites of the princes. And among all those princes, the eldest, Rāma, like that of Ketu, (The ninth of the planets.) and the special delight of his father, became the object of general regard, even as the self-create Himself. And all of them were versed in the Vedas, and heroic, and intent upon the welfare of others.

transliteration: buddher bhedaṁ dhṛiteśh chaiva guṇatas tri-vidhaṁ śhṛiṇu
english: Now hear, O Dhanangaya! the threefold division of intelligence and courage, according to qualities, which I am about to declare exhaustively and distinctly.

sanskrit: बभूव भूयो भूतानाम् स्वयम् भूः इव सम्मतः
सर्वे वेद विदः शूराः सर्वे लोकहिते रताः
transliteration: babhūva bhūyo bhūtānām svayam bhūḥ iva sammataḥ
sarve veda vidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve lokahite ratāḥ
english: Thus did he celebrate the natal rites of the princes. And among all those princes, the eldest, Rāma, like that of Ketu, (The ninth of the planets.) and the special delight of his father, became the object of general regard, even as the self-create Himself. And all of them were versed in the Vedas, and heroic, and intent upon the welfare of others.

sanskrit: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी
transliteration: pravṛittiṁ cha nivṛittiṁ cha kāryākārye bhayābhaye
bandhaṁ mokṣhaṁ cha yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī
english: That intelligence, O son of Pritha! is good which understands action and inaction, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, danger and the absence of danger, emancipation and bondage.

sanskrit: तेषाम् अपि महातेजा रामः सत्य पराक्रमः
transliteration: teṣām api mahātejā rāmaḥ satya parākramaḥ
english: And all were accomplished in knowledge; and endowed with virtues. And among them all, the exceedingly puissant Rāma, having true for prowess, was the desire of every one, and spotless like to the Moon himself. He could ride on elephants and horses, and was an adept in managing cars. And he was ever engaged in the study of arms, and aye occupied in ministering to his sire.

sanskrit: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च
transliteration: yayā dharmam adharmaṁ cha kāryaṁ chākāryam eva cha
ayathāvat prajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
english: That intelligence, O son of Pritha! is passionate, by which one imperfectly understands piety and impiety, what ought to be done and also what ought not to be done.

sanskrit: इष्टः सर्वस्य लोकस्य शशांक इव निर्मलः
गज स्कन्धे अश्व पृष्टे च रथ चर्यासु सम्मतः
transliteration: iṣṭaḥ sarvasya lokasya śaśāṃka iva nirmalaḥ
gaja skandhe aśva pṛṣṭe ca ratha caryāsu sammataḥ
adharmaṁ dharmam iti yā manyate tamasāvṛitā
sarvārthān viparītānśh cha buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
english: That intelligence, O son of Pritha! is dark, which shrouded by darkness, understands impiety (to be) piety, and all things incorrectly.

sanskrit: धनुर्वेदे च निरतः पितुः शुशॄषणे रतः
बाल्यात् प्रभृति सुस्निग्धो लक्ष्मणो लक्ष्मि वर्धनः
transliteration: dhanurvede ca nirataḥ pituḥ śuśṝṣaṇe rataḥ
bālyāt prabhṛti susnigdho lakṣmaṇo lakṣmi vardhanaḥ

english: That courage, O son of Pritha! is good courage, which is unswerving, and by which one controls the operations of the mind, breath, and senses, through abstraction.

sanskrit: सर्व प्रिय करः तस्य रामस्य अपि शरीरतः
transliteration: sarva priya karaḥ tasya rāmasya api śarīrataḥ

sanskrit: प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी
transliteration: prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣhī dhṛitiḥ sā pārtha rājasī
english: But, O Arguna! that courage is passionate, by which one adheres to piety, lust, and wealth, and through attachment wishes, O son of Pritha! for the fruit.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणो लक्ष्मि संपन्नो बहिः प्राण इव अपरः
न च तेन विना निद्राम् लभते पुरुषोत्तमः
transliteration: lakṣmaṇo lakṣmi saṃpanno bahiḥ prāṇa iva aparaḥ
na ca tena vinā nidrām labhate puruṣottamaḥ

sanskrit: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी
transliteration: yayā svapnaṁ bhayaṁ śhokaṁ viṣhādaṁ madam eva cha
na vimuñchati durmedhā dhṛitiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī
english: That courage is dark, O son of Pritha! by which an undiscerning man does not give up sleep, fear, sorrow, despondency, and folly.

sanskrit: मृष्टम् अन्नम् उपानीतम् अश्नाति न हि तम् विना
यदा हि हयम् आरूढो मृगयाम् याति राघवः
transliteration: mṛṣṭam annam upānītam aśnāti na hi tam vinā
yadā hi hayam ārūḍho mṛgayām yāti rāghavaḥ

sanskrit: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ
transliteration: sukhaṁ tv idānīṁ tri-vidhaṁ śhṛiṇu me bharatarṣhabha
abhyāsād ramate yatra duḥkhāntaṁ cha nigachchhati
yat tad agre viṣham iva pariṇāme ‘mṛitopamam
english: Now, O chief of the descendants of Bharata! hear from me about the three sorts of happiness.

sanskrit: अथ एनम् पृष्ठतः अभ्येति स धनुः परिपालयन्
भरतस्य अपि शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मण अवरजो हि सः
transliteration: atha enam pṛṣṭhataḥ abhyeti sa dhanuḥ paripālayan
bharatasya api śatrughno lakṣmaṇa avarajo hi saḥ
english: When mounted on horse-back, Rāghava went a-hunting, Lakṣmaṇa went at his back bow in hand, protecting him. And that younger brother of Laksmana, Satrughna, likewise became ever dearer to Bharata than life itself.

transliteration: yat tad agre viṣam iva pariṇāme 'mṛtopamam tat sukhaṁ sāttvikaṁ proktam ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam
english: That happiness is called good, in which one is pleased after repetition (of enjoyment), and reaches the close of all misery, which is like poison first and comparable to nectar in the long run, and which is produced from a clear knowledge of the self.

sanskrit: प्राणैः प्रियतरो नित्यम् तस्य च आसीत् तथा प्रियः
स चतुर्भिः महाभागैः पुत्रैः दशरथः प्रियैः
transliteration: prāṇaiḥ priyataro nityam tasya ca āsīt tathā priyaḥ
sa caturbhiḥ mahābhāgaiḥ putraiḥ daśarathaḥ priyaiḥ
pariṇāme viṣham iva tat sukhaṁ rājasaṁ smṛitam
english: That happiness is called passionate, which (flows) from contact between the senses and their objects, and which is at first comparable to nectar and in the long run like poison.

sanskrit: बभूव परम प्रीतो देवैः इव पितामहः
ते यदा ज्ञान संपन्नाः सर्वैः समुदिता गुणैः
transliteration: babhūva parama prīto devaiḥ iva pitāmahaḥ
te yadā jñāna saṃpannāḥ sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ
yad agre chānubandhe cha sukhaṁ mohanam ātmanaḥ
english: That happiness is described as dark, which arises from sleep, laziness, heedlessness, which deludes the self, both at first and in its consequences.

sanskrit: ह्रीमन्तः कीर्तिमन्तः च सर्वज्ञा दीर्घ दर्शिनः
तेषाम् एवम् प्रभावाणाम् सर्वेषाम् दीप्त तेजसाम्
transliteration: hrīmantaḥ kīrtimantaḥ ca sarvajñā dīrgha darśinaḥ
teṣām evam prabhāvāṇām sarveṣām dīpta tejasām
english: And when they came to be furnished with knowledge, and crowned with virtues, and endowed with bashfulness and fame, and to attain wisdom in everything, and to be farsighted, Dasaratha, the father of such powerful and flamingly effulgent sons, became delighted even like that lord of worlds-Brahmā.

sanskrit: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः
transliteration: na tad asti pṛithivyāṁ vā divi deveṣhu vā punaḥ
sattvaṁ prakṛiti-jair muktaṁ yad ebhiḥ syāt tribhir guṇaiḥ
english: There is no entity either on earth or in heaven among the gods, which is free from these three qualities born of nature.

sanskrit: पिता दशरथो हृष्टो ब्रह्मा लोकाधिपो यथा
ते च अपि मनुज व्याघ्रा वैदिक अध्ययने रताः
transliteration: pitā daśaratho hṛṣṭo brahmā lokādhipo yathā
te ca api manuja vyāghrā vaidika adhyayane ratāḥ

english: The duties of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaisyas, and of Sudras, too, O terror of your foes! are distinguished according to the qualities born of nature.

sanskrit: पितृ शुश्रूषण रता धनुर् वेदे च निष्टिताः
अथ राजा दशरथः तेषाम् दार क्रियाम् प्रति
transliteration: pitṛ śuśrūṣaṇa ratā dhanur vede ca niṣṭitāḥ
atha rājā daśarathaḥ teṣām dāra kriyām prati
śhamo damas tapaḥ śhauchaṁ kṣhāntir ārjavam eva cha
english: Tranquillity, restraint of the senses, penance, purity, forgiveness, straightforwardness, also knowledge, experience, and belief (in a future world), this is the natural duty of Brahmanas.

sanskrit: चिंतयामास धर्मात्मा सह उपाध्यायः स बान्धवः
transliteration: ciṃtayāmāsa dharmātmā saha upādhyāyaḥ sa bāndhavaḥ
english: Once upon a time, when the virtuous king Dasaratha, surrounded by his priests and friends, was reflecting about the nuptials of his sons, to that high-souled one engaged in thought in the midst of his counsellors came the mighty ascetic Visvamitra.

transliteration: śhauryaṁ tejo dhṛitir dākṣhyaṁ yuddhe chāpy apalāyanam
dānam īśhvara-bhāvaśh cha kṣhātraṁ karma svabhāva-jam
english: Valour, glory, courage, dexterity, not slinking away from battle, gifts, exercise of lordly power, this is the natural duty of Kshatriyas.

sanskrit: स राज्ञो दर्शन आकांक्षी द्वार अध्यक्षान् उवाच ह
transliteration: sa rājño darśana ākāṃkṣī dvāra adhyakṣān uvāca ha

english: Agriculture, tending cattle, trade, (this) is the natural duty of Vaisyas. And the natural duty of Sudras, too, consists in service.

sanskrit: शीघ्रम् आख्यात माम् प्राप्तम् कौशिकम् गाधिनः सुतम्
तत् श्रुत्वा वचनम् तस्य राज्ञो वेश्म प्रदुद्रुवुः
transliteration: śīghram ākhyāta mām prāptam kauśikam gādhinaḥ sutam
tat śrutvā vacanam tasya rājño veśma pradudruvuḥ

sanskrit: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः
transliteration: sve sve karmaṇy abhirataḥ sansiddhiṁ labhate naraḥ
sva-karma-nirataḥ siddhiṁ yathā vindati tach chhṛiṇu
english: (Every) man intent on his own respective duties obtains perfection. Listen, now, how one intent on one's own duty obtains perfection.

sanskrit: संभ्रान्त मनसः सर्वे तेन वाक्येन चोदिताः
ते गत्वा राज भवनम् विश्वामित्रम् ऋषिम् तदा
transliteration: saṃbhrānta manasaḥ sarve tena vākyena coditāḥ
te gatvā rāja bhavanam viśvāmitram ṛṣim tadā
english: Hearing those words of his, they, urged on by them, all hurriedly began to run towards the royal chambers. And coming to the royal apartments, they communicated to Ikşváku's descendant the arrival of the ascetic Viśvāmitra.

transliteration: yataḥ pravṛittir bhūtānāṁ yena sarvam idaṁ tatam
sva-karmaṇā tam abhyarchya siddhiṁ vindati mānavaḥ
english: Worshipping, by (the performance of) his own duty, him from whom all things proceed, and by whom all this is permeated, a man obtains perfection.

sanskrit: तेषाम् तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा सपुरोधाः समाहितः
transliteration: teṣām tat vacanam śrutvā sapurodhāḥ samāhitaḥ

english: One's duty, though defective, is better than another's duty well performed.

sanskrit: प्रति उज्जगाम संहृष्टो ब्रह्माणम् इव वासवः
तम् दृष्ट्वा ज्वलितम् दीप्त्या तपसम् संशित व्रतम्
transliteration: prati ujjagāma saṃhṛṣṭo brahmāṇam iva vāsavaḥ
tam dṛṣṭvā jvalitam dīptyā tapasam saṃśita vratam

sanskrit: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्
transliteration: saha-jaṁ karma kaunteya sa-doṣham api na tyajet
english: Performing the duty prescribed by nature, one does not incur sin. O son of Kunti! one should not abandon a natural duty though tainted with evil; for all actions are enveloped by evil, as fire by smoke.

sanskrit: प्रहृष्ट वदनो राजा ततः अर्घ्यम् उपहारयत्
स राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्य अर्घ्यम् शास्त्र दृष्टेन कर्मणा
transliteration: prahṛṣṭa vadano rājā tataḥ arghyam upahārayat
sa rājñaḥ pratigṛhya arghyam śāstra dṛṣṭena karmaṇā

english: One who is self-restrained, whose understanding is unattached everywhere, from whom affections have departed, obtains the supreme perfection of freedom from action by renunciation.

sanskrit: कुशलम् च अव्ययम् च एव पर्य पृच्छत् नराधिपम्
पुरे कोशे जनपदे बान्धवेषु सुहृत्सु च
transliteration: kuśalam ca avyayam ca eva parya pṛcchat narādhipam
pure kośe janapade bāndhaveṣu suhṛtsu ca

sanskrit: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा
transliteration: siddhiṁ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me
samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣhṭhā jñānasya yā parā
english: Learn from me, only in brief, O son of Kunti! how one who has obtained perfection attains the Brahman, which is the highest culmination of knowledge.

sanskrit: अपि ते संनताः सर्वे सामंत रिपवो जिताः
transliteration: api te saṃnatāḥ sarve sāmaṃta ripavo jitāḥ

sanskrit: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्याऽऽत्मानं नियम्य च
transliteration: buddhyā viśhuddhayā yukto dhṛityātmānaṁ niyamya cha
śhabdādīn viṣhayāns tyaktvā rāga-dveṣhau vyudasya cha
english: A man possessed of a pure understanding, controlling his self by courage, discarding sound and other objects of sense, casting off affection and aversion;

sanskrit: दैवम् च मानुषम् च एव कर्म ते साधु अनुष्टितम्
transliteration: daivam ca mānuṣam ca eva karma te sādhu anuṣṭitam

english: who frequents clean places, who eats little, whose speech, body, and mind are restrained, who is always intent on meditation and mental abstraction, and has recourse to unconcern,

sanskrit: ऋषीम् च तान् यथा न्यायम् महाभाग उवाच ह
ते सर्वे हृष्ट मनसः तस्य राज्ञो निवेशनम्
transliteration: ṛṣīm ca tān yathā nyāyam mahābhāga uvāca ha
te sarve hṛṣṭa manasaḥ tasya rājño niveśanam

sanskrit: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम्
transliteration: ahankāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ parigraham
english: who abandoning egoism, stubbornness, arrogance, desire, anger, and (all) belongings, has no (thought that this or that is) mine, and who is tranquil, becomes fit for assimilation with the Brahman.

sanskrit: विविशुः पूजिताः तेन निषेदुः च यथा अर्हतः
अथ हृष्ट मना राजा विश्वामित्रम् महामुनिम्
transliteration: viviśuḥ pūjitāḥ tena niṣeduḥ ca yathā arhataḥ
atha hṛṣṭa manā rājā viśvāmitram mahāmunim

sanskrit: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम्
transliteration: brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śhochati na kāṅkṣhati
samaḥ sarveṣhu bhūteṣhu mad-bhaktiṁ labhate parām
english: Thus reaching the Brahman, and with a tranquil self, he grieves not, wishes not; but being alike to all beings, obtains the highest devotion to me.

sanskrit: उवाच परम उदारो हृष्टः तम् अभिपूजयन्
यथा अमृतस्य संप्राप्तिः यथा वर्षम् अनूदके
transliteration: uvāca parama udāro hṛṣṭaḥ tam abhipūjayan
yathā amṛtasya saṃprāptiḥ yathā varṣam anūdake

sanskrit: ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम्
transliteration: bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaśh chāsmi tattvataḥ
tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā viśhate tad-anantaram
english: By (that) devotion he truly understands who I am and how great. And then understanding me truly, he forthwith enters into my (essence).

sanskrit: यथा सदृश दारेषु पुत्र जन्म अप्रजस्य वै
प्रणष्टस्य यथा लाभो यथा हर्षो महोदये
transliteration: yathā sadṛśa dāreṣu putra janma aprajasya vai
praṇaṣṭasya yathā lābho yathā harṣo mahodaye

english: Even performing all actions, always depending on me, he, through my favour, obtains the imperishable and eternal seat.

sanskrit: तथा एव आगमनम् मन्ये स्वागतम् ते महामुने
कम् च ते परमम् कामम् करोमि किमु हर्षितः
transliteration: tathā eva āgamanam manye svāgatam te mahāmune
kam ca te paramam kāmam karomi kimu harṣitaḥ

english: Dedicating in thought all actions to me, be constantly given up to me, (placing) your thoughts on me, through recourse to mental abstraction.

sanskrit: पात्र भूतोऽसि मे ब्रह्मन् दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोऽसि मानद
अद्य मे सफलम् जन्म जीवितम् च सु जीवितम्
transliteration: pātra bhūto'si me brahman diṣṭyā prāpto'si mānada
adya me saphalam janma jīvitam ca su jīvitam
english: You, O Brahmana, are worthy of my best services. By luck it is that, O bestower of honour, I have gained you. To-day my birth has been crowned with fruit to-day has my life attained its object.

transliteration: atha chet tvam ahankārān na śhroṣhyasi vinaṅkṣhyasi
english: (Placing) your thoughts on me, you will cross over all difficulties by my favour. But if you will not listen through egotism, you will be ruined.

sanskrit: यस्माद् विप्रेन्द्रम् अद्राक्षम् सुप्रभाता निशा मम
पूर्वम् राजर्षि शब्देन तपसा द्योतित प्रभः
transliteration: yasmād viprendram adrākṣam suprabhātā niśā mama
pūrvam rājarṣi śabdena tapasā dyotita prabhaḥ
english: And truly yesterday night has been succeeded by an auspicious morning, since I have beheld you. Having first attained exceeding effulgence by virtue of austerities performed for obtaining the title of Rājarşi, you have afterwards obtained the status of a Brahmarși. You are worthy of manifold homage from me. This your exceedingly holy arrival appear wonderful.

transliteration: yad ahankāram āśhritya na yotsya iti manyase
mithyaiṣha vyavasāyas te prakṛitis tvāṁ niyokṣhyati
english: If entertaining egotism, you think that you may not fight, vain, indeed, is that resolution of yours.

sanskrit: तत् अद्भुतम् अभूत् विप्र पवित्रम् परमम् मम
transliteration: tat adbhutam abhūt vipra pavitram paramam mama
english: And truly yesterday night has been succeeded by an auspicious morning, since I have beheld you. Having first attained exceeding effulgence by virtue of austerities performed for obtaining the title of Rājarşi, you have afterwards obtained the status of a Brahmarși. You are worthy of manifold homage from me. This your exceedingly holy arrival appear wonderful.

transliteration: kartuṁ nechchhasi yan mohāt kariṣhyasy avaśho ’pi tat
english: Nature will constrain youThat, O son of Kunti! which through delusion you do not wish to do, you will do involuntarily, tied down by your own duty, flowing from your nature.

sanskrit: शुभ क्षेत्र गतः च अहम् तव संदर्शनात् प्रभो
ब्रूहि यत् प्रार्थितम् तुभ्यम् कार्यम् आगमनम् प्रति
transliteration: śubha kṣetra gataḥ ca aham tava saṃdarśanāt prabho
brūhi yat prārthitam tubhyam kāryam āgamanam prati
english: O lord, by beholding you, surely my body has been rendered pure. Tell me, what is it that you would have, and what is the purpose of your coming?
The lord, O Arguna! is seated in the region of the heart of all beings, turning round all beings (as though) mounted on a machine, by his delusion.

sanskrit: कार्यस्य न विमर्शम् च गंतुम् अर्हसि सुव्रत
transliteration: kāryasya na vimarśam ca gaṃtum arhasi suvrata
tam eva śharaṇaṁ gachchha sarva-bhāvena bhārata
tat-prasādāt parāṁ śhāntiṁ sthānaṁ prāpsyasi śhāśhvatam
english: With him, O descendant of Bharata! seek shelter in every way; by his favour you will obtain the highest tranquillity, the eternal seat.

sanskrit: कर्ता च अहम् अशेषेण दैवतम् हि भवान् मम
मम च अयम् अनुप्राप्तो महान् अभ्युदयो द्विज
तव आगमन जः कृत्स्नो धर्मः च अनुत्तमो द्विज
transliteration: kartā ca aham aśeṣeṇa daivatam hi bhavān mama
mama ca ayam anuprāpto mahān abhyudayo dvija
tava āgamana jaḥ kṛtsno dharmaḥ ca anuttamo dvija
english: I wish that I may be obliged by doing your will. And, ( you of excellent vows, you ought not to hesitate. I will every way accomplish your will; for you are my god. O regenerate one, surely great prosperity come to me in consequence of your coming, inasmuch as it shall be the means of bringing me entire and excellent merit, O Brāhmaṇa!

transliteration: iti te jñānam ākhyātaṁ guhyād guhyataraṁ mayā
english: Thus have I declared to you the knowledge more mysterious than any mystery. Ponder over it thoroughly, and then act as you like.

sanskrit: इति हृदय सुखम् निशम्य वाक्यम्श्रुति सुखम् आत्मवता विनीतम् उक्तम्
प्रथित गुण यशा गुणैः विशिष्टःपरम ऋषिः परमम् जगाम हर्षम्
transliteration: iti hṛdaya sukham niśamya vākyamśruti sukham ātmavatā vinītam uktam
prathita guṇa yaśā guṇaiḥ viśiṣṭaḥparama ṛṣiḥ paramam jagāma harṣam
english: Hearing this soul-soothing, ear-charming, and free-humble speech that was uttered, the illustrious prime of ascetics crowned with virtues, and furnished with all perfections, experienced exceeding delight.

sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्
transliteration: sarva-guhyatamaṁ bhūyaḥ śhṛiṇu me paramaṁ vachaḥ
iṣhṭo ‘si me dṛiḍham iti tato vakṣhyāmi te hitam
english: Once more, listen to my excellent words most mysterious of all. Strongly I like you, therefore I will declare what ts for your welfare.

sanskrit: तत् शुर्त्वा राज सिंहस्य वाक्यम् अद्भुत विस्तरम्
transliteration: tat śurtvā rāja siṃhasya vākyam adbhuta vistaram
english: Hearing those astonishing words of that lionlike king, the highly-energetic Viśvāmitra with his down standing on end, said.

sanskrit: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे
transliteration: man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru
mām evaiṣhyasi satyaṁ te pratijāne priyo ‘si me
english: On me (place) your mind, become my devotee, sacrifice to me, reverence me, and you will certainly come to me. I declare to you truly, you are dear to me.

sanskrit: सदृशम् राज शार्दूल तव एव भुवि न अन्यतः
transliteration: sadṛśam rāja śārdūla tava eva bhuvi na anyataḥ
english: O tiger of a king, sprung from an illustrious line, and having Vasistha, for your guide, these words become you alone on earth and no one else.

sanskrit: अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः
transliteration: sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śharaṇaṁ vraja
ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣhayiṣhyāmi mā śhuchaḥ
english: Forsaking all duties, come to me as (your) sole refuge. I will release you from all sins. Be not grieved.

sanskrit: यत् तु मे हृद् गतम् वाक्यम् तस्य कार्यस्य निश्चयम्
कुरुष्व राज शार्दूल भव सत्य प्रतिश्रवः
transliteration: yat tu me hṛd gatam vākyam tasya kāryasya niścayam
kuruṣva rāja śārdūla bhava satya pratiśravaḥ
english: Do you, O tiger of a king, ascertain your course in respect of the matter I bear in my heart; and do you prove firm in promise!

sanskrit: न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति
transliteration: na chāśhuśhruṣhave vāchyaṁ na cha māṁ yo ‘bhyasūtayi
english: This you should never declare to one who performs no penance, who is not a devotee, nor to one who does not wait on (some preceptor), nor yet to one who calumniates me.

sanskrit: तस्य विघ्नकरौ द्वौ तु राक्षसौ काम रूपिणौ
transliteration: tasya vighnakarau dvau tu rākṣasau kāma rūpiṇau
english: For celebrating a sacrifice, I, O foremost of men, abide by some prescribed course. And it comes to pass that two Rākşasas assuming shapes at will, have become bent upon disturbing the ceremony.

transliteration: ya idaṁ paramaṁ guhyaṁ mad-bhakteṣhv abhidhāsyati
bhaktiṁ mayi parāṁ kṛitvā mām evaiṣhyaty asanśhayaḥ
english: He who, with the highest devotion to me, will proclaim this supreme mystery among my devotees, will come to me, freed from (all) doubts.

sanskrit: व्रते मे बहुशः चीर्णे समाप्त्याम् राक्षसाविमौ
मारीचः च सुबाहुः च वीर्यवन्तौ सुशिक्षितौ
transliteration: vrate me bahuśaḥ cīrṇe samāptyām rākṣasāvimau
mārīcaḥ ca subāhuḥ ca vīryavantau suśikṣitau

sanskrit: भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि
transliteration: na cha tasmān manuṣhyeṣhu kaśhchin me priya-kṛittamaḥ
bhavitā na cha me tasmād anyaḥ priyataro bhuvi
english: No one amongst men is superior to him in doing what is dear to me. And there will never be another on earth dearer to me than he.

sanskrit: तौ मांस रुधिर ओघेण वेदिम् ताम् अभ्यवर्षताम्
अवधूते तथा भूते तस्मिन् नियम निश्चये
transliteration: tau māṃsa rudhira ogheṇa vedim tām abhyavarṣatām
avadhūte tathā bhūte tasmin niyama niścaye

sanskrit: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः
transliteration: adhyeṣhyate cha ya imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṁvādam āvayoḥ
jñāna-yajñena tenāham iṣhṭaḥ syām iti me matiḥ
english: And he who will study this holy dialogue of ours, will, such is my opinion, have offered to me the sacrifice of knowledge.

sanskrit: कृत श्रमो निरुत्साहः तस्मात् देशात् अपाक्रमे
न च मे क्रोधम् उत्स्रष्टुम् बुद्धिः भवति पार्थिव
transliteration: kṛta śramo nirutsāhaḥ tasmāt deśāt apākrame
na ca me krodham utsraṣṭum buddhiḥ bhavati pārthiva
śhraddhāvān anasūyaśh cha śhṛiṇuyād api yo naraḥ
so ‘pi muktaḥ śhubhāl lokān prāpnuyāt puṇya-karmaṇām
english: And the man, also, who with faith and without carping will listen (to this), will be freed (from sin), and attain to the holy regions of those who perform pious acts.

sanskrit: तथा भूता हि सा चर्या न शापः तत्र मुच्यते
स्व पुत्रम् राज शार्दूल रामम् सत्य पराक्रमम्
transliteration: tathā bhūtā hi sā caryā na śāpaḥ tatra mucyate
sva putram rāja śārdūla rāmam satya parākramam
english: For such is the nature of that business, that it is not proper for one engaged in it to utter a curse. Therefore, O tiger of a monarch, it behoves you to grant me your eldest son, the heroic Rāma of genuine prowess, with the sidelocks.

transliteration: kachchid etach chhrutaṁ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa chetasā
english: Have you listened to this, O son of Pritha! with a mind (fixed) on (this) one point only? Has your delusion (caused) by ignorance been destroyed, O Dhanangaya?

sanskrit: काक पक्ष धरम् शूरम् ज्येष्ठम् मे दातुम् अर्हसि
शक्तो हि येष मया गुप्तो दिव्येन स्वेन तेजसा
transliteration: kāka pakṣa dharam śūram jyeṣṭham me dātum arhasi
śakto hi yeṣa mayā gupto divyena svena tejasā
naṣhṭo mohaḥ smṛitir labdhā tvat-prasādān mayāchyuta
english: Arguna said: Destroyed is my delusion; by your favour, O undegraded one! I (now) recollect myself I stand freed from doubts. I will do your bidding.

sanskrit: राक्षसा ये विकर्तारः तेषाम् अपि विनाशने
श्रेयः च अस्मै प्रदास्यामि बहुरूपम् न संशयः
transliteration: rākṣasā ye vikartāraḥ teṣām api vināśane
śreyaḥ ca asmai pradāsyāmi bahurūpam na saṃśayaḥ

sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः
transliteration: ity ahaṁ vāsudevasya pārthasya cha mahātmanaḥ
english: Sangaya said: Thus did I hear this dialogue between Vasudeva and the high-minded son of Pritha, (a dialogue) wonderful and causing the hair to stand on end.

sanskrit: त्रयाणाम् अपि लोकानाम् येन ख्यातिम् गमिष्यति
न च तौ रामम् आसाद्य शक्तौ स्थातुम् कथम् च न
transliteration: trayāṇām api lokānām yena khyātim gamiṣyati
na ca tau rāmam āsādya śaktau sthātum katham ca na
vyāsa-prasādāch chhrutavān etad guhyam ahaṁ param
yogaṁ yogeśhvarāt kṛiṣhṇāt sākṣhāt kathayataḥ svayam
english: By the favour of Vyasa, I heard this highest mystery, (this) devotion, from Krishna himself, the lord of the possessors of mystic power, who proclaimed it in person.

sanskrit: न च तौ राघवात् अन्यो हन्तुम् उत्सहते पुमान्
वीर्य उत्सिक्तौ हि तौ पापौ काल पाश वशम् गतौ
transliteration: na ca tau rāghavāt anyo hantum utsahate pumān
vīrya utsiktau hi tau pāpau kāla pāśa vaśam gatau
rājan sansmṛitya sansmṛitya saṁvādam imam adbhutam
keśhavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṁ hṛiṣhyāmi cha muhur muhuḥ
english: O king! remembering and (again) remembering this wonderful and holy dialogue of Kesava and Arguna, I rejoice over and over again.

sanskrit: रामस्य राज शार्दूल न पर्याप्तौ महात्मनः
न च पुत्र गतम् स्नेहम् कर्तुम् अर्हसि पार्थिव
transliteration: rāmasya rāja śārdūla na paryāptau mahātmanaḥ
na ca putra gatam sneham kartum arhasi pārthiva

sanskrit: विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः
transliteration: tach cha sansmṛitya saṁsmṛitya rūpam aty-adbhutaṁ hareḥ
vismayo ye mahān rājan hṛiṣhyāmi cha punaḥ punaḥ
english: And remembering and (again) remembering that excessively wonderful form of Hari also, great is my amazement, O king! and I rejoice over and over again.

sanskrit: अहम् ते प्रति जानामि हतौ तौ विद्धि राक्षसौ
अहम् वेद्मि महात्मानम् रामम् सत्य पराक्रमम्
transliteration: aham te prati jānāmi hatau tau viddhi rākṣasau
aham vedmi mahātmānam rāmam satya parākramam

sanskrit: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः
transliteration: yatra yogeśhvaraḥ kṛiṣhṇo yatra pārtho dhanur-dharaḥ
tatra śhrīr vijayo bhūtir dhruvā nītir matir mama

sanskrit: वसिष्ठोऽपि महातेजा ये च इमे तपसि स्थिताः
यदि ते धर्म लाभम् तु यशः च परमम् भुवि
transliteration: vasiṣṭho'pi mahātejā ye ca ime tapasi sthitāḥ
yadi te dharma lābham tu yaśaḥ ca paramam bhuvi

sanskrit: स्थिरम् इच्छसि राजेन्द्र रामम् मे दातुम् अर्हसि
यदि अभ्यनुज्ञाम् काकुत्स्थ ददते तव मंत्रिणः
transliteration: sthiram icchasi rājendra rāmam me dātum arhasi
yadi abhyanujñām kākutstha dadate tava maṃtriṇaḥ

sanskrit: वसिष्ठ प्रमुखाः सर्वे ततो रामम् विसर्जय
transliteration: vasiṣṭha pramukhāḥ sarve tato rāmam visarjaya

sanskrit: दश रात्रम् हि यज्ञस्य रामम् राजीव लोचनम्
न अत्येति कालो यज्ञस्य यथा अयम् मम राघव
transliteration: daśa rātram hi yajñasya rāmam rājīva locanam
na atyeti kālo yajñasya yathā ayam mama rāghava
english: Even this is my wish, and he also has come of age. Do you, therefore, part with your son, the lotus-eyed Rāma, for the ten days of the sacrifice! Do you act so, O descendant of Raghu, that the time appointed for the ceremony may not be overpassed. Good betide you! Let not your mind indulge in grief!

sanskrit: तथा कुरुष्व भद्रम् ते मा च शोके मनः कृथाः
इति एवम् उक्त्वा धर्मात्मा धर्मार्थ सहितम् वचः
transliteration: tathā kuruṣva bhadram te mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
iti evam uktvā dharmātmā dharmārtha sahitam vacaḥ

sanskrit: स तन् निशम्य राजेन्द्रो विश्वामित्र वचः शुभम्
transliteration: sa tan niśamya rājendro viśvāmitra vacaḥ śubham
english: And hearing the auspicious words of Viśvāmitra, that foremost of kings shook with a mighty sorrow, and became bewildered.

sanskrit: शोकेन महता आविष्टः चचाल च मुमोह च
लब्ध संज्ञः ततो उतथाय व्यषीदत भयान्वितः
transliteration: śokena mahatā āviṣṭaḥ cacāla ca mumoha ca
labdha saṃjñaḥ tato utathāya vyaṣīdata bhayānvitaḥ

sanskrit: इति हृदय मनो विदारणम्मुनि वचनम् तद् अतीव शुश्रुवान्
नरपतिः अभवत् महान् महात्माव्यथित मनाः प्रचचाल च असनात्
transliteration: iti hṛdaya mano vidāraṇammuni vacanam tad atīva śuśruvān
narapatiḥ abhavat mahān mahātmāvyathita manāḥ pracacāla ca asanāt
english: Then, having regained his senses, he rose up, and became cast down through apprehension. Having heard the words of the ascetic, capable of rending the mind and heart, the high-souled king of men became stricken with grief and shook on his seat.

sanskrit: तत् श्रुत्वा राज शार्दूलो विश्वामित्रस्य भाषितम्
मुहूर्तम् इव निस्सज्ञः सज्ञावान् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tat śrutvā rāja śārdūlo viśvāmitrasya bhāṣitam
muhūrtam iva nissajñaḥ sajñāvān idam abravīt
english: Hearing the words of Viśvāmitra, that tiger of a monarch remained insensible for a time, and then regaining his senses, spoke thus.

sanskrit: ऊन षोडश वर्षो मे रामो राजीव लोचनः
न युद्ध योग्यताम् अस्य पश्यामि सह राक्षसैः
transliteration: ūna ṣoḍaśa varṣo me rāmo rājīva locanaḥ
na yuddha yogyatām asya paśyāmi saha rākṣasaiḥ
english: My lotus-eyed Ráma is not yet turned of sixteen; and I do not perceive his fitness to cope with Raksasas in battle.

sanskrit: इयम् अक्षौहिणी सेना यस्य अहम् पतिः ईश्वरः
अनया सहितो गत्वा योद्ध अहम् तैर् निशाचरैः
transliteration: iyam akṣauhiṇī senā yasya aham patiḥ īśvaraḥ
anayā sahito gatvā yoddha aham tair niśācaraiḥ
english: I am the lord of this Akşauhiņi (A complete army consisting of 1,09,350 foot, 65,610 horse, 21,870 chariots, and 21,870 elephants.) of forces. Marching with this, will I engage with the night-rangers.

sanskrit: इमे शूराः च विक्रान्ता भृत्याः मे अस्त्र विशारदाः
योग्या रक्षोगणैः योद्धुम् न रामम् नेतुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: ime śūrāḥ ca vikrāntā bhṛtyāḥ me astra viśāradāḥ
yogyā rakṣogaṇaiḥ yoddhum na rāmam netum arhasi
english: And these servants of mine are Valiant, and warlike, and accomplished in weapons, and capable of fighting the Rākşasas,-therefore, it behove you not to take Rāma.

sanskrit: अहम् एव धनुष्पाणिः गोप्ता समर मूर्धनि
यावत् प्राणान् धरिष्यामि तावत् योत्स्ये निशाचरैः
transliteration: aham eva dhanuṣpāṇiḥ goptā samara mūrdhani
yāvat prāṇān dhariṣyāmi tāvat yotsye niśācaraiḥ
english: And myself bow in hand, stationed at the van of the array, will battle with the rangers of the night as long as life is spared to me.

sanskrit: निर्विघ्ना व्रत चर्या सा भविष्यति सुरक्षिता
अहम् तत्र आगमिष्यामि न रामम् नेतुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: nirvighnā vrata caryā sā bhaviṣyati surakṣitā
aham tatra āgamiṣyāmi na rāmam netum arhasi
english: Then well protected, your sacrifice will hold an unimpeded course. Therefore, I will repair thither, and it behoves you not to take Rāma.

sanskrit: बालो हि अकृत विद्यः च न च वेत्ति बलाबलम्
न च अस्त्र बल संयुक्तो न च युद्ध विशारदः
transliteration: bālo hi akṛta vidyaḥ ca na ca vetti balābalam
na ca astra bala saṃyukto na ca yuddha viśāradaḥ
english: Youthful, and unaccomplished, and not knowing what constitutes strength and what not, and not equipped with the science of missiles, and unskilful in fight.

sanskrit: न च असौ रक्षसा योग्यः कूट युद्धा हि राक्षसा
विप्रयुक्तो हि रामेण मुहूर्तम् अपि न उत्सहे
transliteration: na ca asau rakṣasā yogyaḥ kūṭa yuddhā hi rākṣasā
viprayukto hi rāmeṇa muhūrtam api na utsahe
english: He is not a match for Räkşasas,-they being deceitful warriors. Bereft of Rāma, O tiger among ascetics, I cannot live for a moment. Therefore, it behove you not to take him. If, O Brahman, it is your intention to take Rāma, then O you of excellent vows, do you also take me along with the Caturanga forces! (An army consisting of foot, horse, elephants, and cars.)

sanskrit: जीवितुम् मुनि शार्दूल न रामम् नेतुम् अर्हसि
यदि वा राघवम् ब्रह्मन् नेतुम् इच्छसि सुव्रत
transliteration: jīvitum muni śārdūla na rāmam netum arhasi
yadi vā rāghavam brahman netum icchasi suvrata

sanskrit: चतुरंग समायुक्तम् मया सह च तम् नय
षष्टिः वर्ष सहस्राणि जातस्य मम कौशिक
transliteration: caturaṃga samāyuktam mayā saha ca tam naya
ṣaṣṭiḥ varṣa sahasrāṇi jātasya mama kauśika

sanskrit: कृच्छ्रेण उत्पादितः च अयम् न रामम् नेतुम् अर्हसि
चतुर्णाम् आत्मजानाम् हि प्रीतिः परमिका मम
transliteration: kṛcchreṇa utpāditaḥ ca ayam na rāmam netum arhasi
caturṇām ātmajānām hi prītiḥ paramikā mama

sanskrit: ज्येष्ठे धर्म प्रधाने च न रामम् नेतुम् अर्हसि
किम् वीर्याः राक्षसाः ते च कस्य पुत्राः च के च ते
transliteration: jyeṣṭhe dharma pradhāne ca na rāmam netum arhasi
kim vīryāḥ rākṣasāḥ te ca kasya putrāḥ ca ke ca te

sanskrit: कथम् प्रमाणाः के च एतान् रक्षन्ति मुनिपुंगव
कथम् च प्रति कर्तव्यम् तेषाम् रामेण रक्षसाम्
transliteration: katham pramāṇāḥ ke ca etān rakṣanti munipuṃgava
katham ca prati kartavyam teṣām rāmeṇa rakṣasām

sanskrit: मामकैः वा बलैः ब्रह्मन् मया वा कूट योधिनाम्
सर्वम् मे शंस भगवन् कथम् तेषाम् मया रणे
transliteration: māmakaiḥ vā balaiḥ brahman mayā vā kūṭa yodhinām
sarvam me śaṃsa bhagavan katham teṣām mayā raṇe

sanskrit: स्थातव्यम् दुष्ट भावानाम् वीर्योत्सिक्ता हि राक्षसाः
तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो अभ्यभाषत
transliteration: sthātavyam duṣṭa bhāvānām vīryotsiktā hi rākṣasāḥ
tasya tad vacanam śrutvā viśvāmitro abhyabhāṣata

sanskrit: पौलस्त्य वंश प्रभवो रावणो नाम राक्षसः
स ब्रह्मणा दत्त वरः त्रैलोक्यम् बाधते भृशम्
transliteration: paulastya vaṃśa prabhavo rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ
sa brahmaṇā datta varaḥ trailokyam bādhate bhṛśam

sanskrit: श्रूयते च महाराजा रावणो राक्षस अधिपः
transliteration: śrūyate ca mahārājā rāvaṇo rākṣasa adhipaḥ

sanskrit: साक्षात् वैश्रवण भ्राता पुत्रो विश्रवसो मुनेः
यदा न खलु यज्ञस्य विघ्न कर्ता महाबलः
transliteration: sākṣāt vaiśravaṇa bhrātā putro viśravaso muneḥ
yadā na khalu yajñasya vighna kartā mahābalaḥ

sanskrit: तेन संचोदितौ तौ तु राक्षसौ च महाबलौ
मारीचः च सुबाहुः च यज्ञ विघ्नम् करिष्यतः
transliteration: tena saṃcoditau tau tu rākṣasau ca mahābalau
mārīcaḥ ca subāhuḥ ca yajña vighnam kariṣyataḥ
english: When that one possessed of mighty strength does not stoop to disturb the sacrifice himself, those powerful Raksasas, Marica and Subāhu, being incited by him, disturb the rites.

sanskrit: इति उक्तो मुनिना तेन राजा उवाच मुनिम् तदा
न हि शक्तो अस्मि संग्रामे स्थातुम् तस्य दुरात्मनः
transliteration: iti ukto muninā tena rājā uvāca munim tadā
na hi śakto asmi saṃgrāme sthātum tasya durātmanaḥ
english: The ascetic having spoken thus, the king then answered him, I am incapable of standing that wicked-souled one in fight.

sanskrit: स त्वम् प्रसादम् धर्मज्ञ कुरुष्व मम पुत्रके
मम च एव अल्प भाग्यस्य दैवतम् हि भवान् गुरुः
transliteration: sa tvam prasādam dharmajña kuruṣva mama putrake
mama ca eva alpa bhāgyasya daivatam hi bhavān guruḥ
english: Therefore, do you, O you versed in morality, extend your favour to my son! Of slender fortune as I am, you are my guide and my god.

sanskrit: देव दानव गंधर्वा यक्षाः पतग पन्नगाः
न शक्ता रावणम् सोढुम् किम् पुनर् मानवा युधि
transliteration: deva dānava gaṃdharvā yakṣāḥ pataga pannagāḥ
na śaktā rāvaṇam soḍhum kim punar mānavā yudhi
english: Even the celestials and the Dānavas and the Gandharvas and the Birds and the Snakes are incapable of bearing Rāvana in battle, what then is man?

sanskrit: स तु वीर्यवताम् वीर्यम् आदत्ते युधि रावणः
तेन च अहम् न शक्तोऽस्मि संयोद्धुम् तस्य वा बलैः
transliteration: sa tu vīryavatām vīryam ādatte yudhi rāvaṇaḥ
tena ca aham na śakto'smi saṃyoddhum tasya vā balaiḥ

sanskrit: सबलो वा मुनिश्रेष्ठ सहितो वा मम आत्मजैः
कथम् अपि अमर प्रख्यम् संग्रामाणाम् अकोविदम्
