sanskrit: करिष्यामि तव प्रीतिं सुकृतेनापि ते शपे
transliteration: kariṣyāmi tava prītiṃ sukṛtenāpi te śape
english: You see the power you wield in me, therefore it behove you not to fear. I will do your pleasure, by my good deeds do I swear this.
Thereat intent upon her own interests, that exalted dame seeing her own wish (almost) attained, assuming an attitude of intercession, being rejoiced, spoke harsh words (to the monarch).
And delighted at the king's speech, she unfolded that dreadful intention of hers like to the approaching death.

sanskrit: यथा क्रमेण शपसि वरं मम ददासि च
transliteration: yathā krameṇa śapasi varaṃ mama dadāsi ca
english: You swear repeatedly, and confer on me a boon. Let the three and thirty deities headed by Indra, hear this.

Let the Sun, and the Moon, and the Sky, and the Planets, and Night, and Day, and the Cardinal Points, and the Universe, and the Earth, with the Gandharvas and Rākşasas, and the Rangers of the night, and all Beings, and the house-hold gods residing in dwellings, together with all other creatures, know your utterances.

Let the Sun, and the Moon, and the Sky, and the Planets, and Night, and Day, and the Cardinal Points, and the Universe, and the Earth, with the Gandharvas and Rākşasas, and the Rangers of the night, and all Beings, and the house-hold gods residing in dwellings, together with all other creatures, know your utterances.

sanskrit: वरं मम ददात्येष तन्मे शृण्वन्तु देवताअः
transliteration: varaṃ mama dadātyeṣa tanme śṛṇvantu devatāaḥ
english: Let all the deities hear that a highly energetic one speaking the truth, and pure, and cognizant of morality, and abiding by his promise, has conferred on me a boon.

Having entreated the monarch thus with a view to prevent him from swerving, and keeping him firm in his promise, she again addressed that mighty bowman, overcome by desire, who was ready to confer on her a boon.

sanskrit: स्मर राज्न् पुरा वृत्तं तस्मिन् दैवासुरे रणे
transliteration: smara rājn purā vṛttaṃ tasmin daivāsure raṇe
english: Remember, o king, the incidents that took place formerly in the war between gods and Asuras. Incapable of taking your life, your enemy had rendered you exceedingly feeble.

sanskrit: तत्र चापि मया देव यत्त्वं समभिरक्षितः
transliteration: tatra cāpi mayā deva yattvaṃ samabhirakṣitaḥ
english: Because, O respected Sir, I tending you sleeplessly, preserved you, you did grant me two boons.

sanskrit: तौ तु दत्तौ वरौ देव निक्षेपौ मृगयाम्यहम्
transliteration: tau tu dattau varau deva nikṣepau mṛgayāmyaham
english: Entrusting the boons then with you, dc I now, O descendant of the Raghus, ask for them (at your hands), O lord of the earth. If having religiously promised to that effect, you did not confer the boon, this very day, will I, coming by this disgrace from you, renounce my life.

sanskrit: तत्प्रतिश्रुत्य धर्मेण न चेद्दास्यसि मे वरम्
transliteration: tatpratiśrutya dharmeṇa na ceddāsyasi me varam
english: Entrusting the boons then with you, dc I now, O descendant of the Raghus, ask for them (at your hands), O lord of the earth. If having religiously promised to that effect, you did not confer the boon, this very day, will I, coming by this disgrace from you, renounce my life.

sanskrit: वाङ्मात्रेण तदा राजा कैकेय्या स्ववशे कृतः
transliteration: vāṅmātreṇa tadā rājā kaikeyyā svavaśe kṛtaḥ
english: When the king was completely brought under the influence of Kaikeyi, he was ensnared by her speech for his destruction, like a deer entering into the noose.

sanskrit: वरौ यौ मे त्वया देव तदा दत्तौ महीपते
transliteration: varau yau me tvayā deva tadā dattau mahīpate
english: Thereafter she thus spoke to the king about to confer a boon, who was under the influence of passion, saying, Of the boons that you had then promised me, I shall speak to-day: do you listen to my words. Preparations are being made for installing Rāghava. Do you with the provisions made ready install Bharata in the kingdom.

sanskrit: तौ तावदहम्द्यैव वक्ष्यामि शृणु मे वचः
transliteration: tau tāvadahamdyaiva vakṣyāmi śṛṇu me vacaḥ
english: Thereafter she thus spoke to the king about to confer a boon, who was under the influence of passion, saying, Of the boons that you had then promised me, I shall speak to-day: do you listen to my words. Preparations are being made for installing Rāghava. Do you with the provisions made ready install Bharata in the kingdom.

sanskrit: यो द्वितीयो वरो देव दत्तः प्रीतेन मे त्वया
transliteration: yo dvitīyo varo deva dattaḥ prītena me tvayā
english: O exalted one, the time has also come for you to confer on me the second boon which you being pleased had promised in the war of the gods and Asuras.

sanskrit: तदा दैवासुरे युद्धे तस्य कालोऽय मागतः
transliteration: tadā daivāsure yuddhe tasya kālo'ya māgataḥ

english: Let the gentle Rāma, clad in deer-skin, lead the life of a mendicant in the Dandaka forest for the space of nine and five years. And let Bharata gain the heir-apparentship rid of thorns.

sanskrit: एष मे परमः कामो दत्तमेव वरं वृणे
अद्यचैव हि पश्येयं प्रयान्तं राघवं वन्म्
transliteration: eṣa me paramaḥ kāmo dattameva varaṃ vṛṇe
adyacaiva hi paśyeyaṃ prayāntaṃ rāghavaṃ vanm
english: Even this in my prime wish; and I beseech you but to grant the boon you have already promised. Even this very day will I see Rāma despatched to the woods.

sanskrit: कुलं च शीलं च हि रक्ष जन्म च
transliteration: kulaṃ ca śīlaṃ ca hi rakṣa janma ca
english: Do you by proving true to your word, become the king of kings; and preserve your race, character, and birth. Truthful speech, say the ascetics, is of supreme welfare to men in the next world.

sanskrit: ततः श्रुत्वा महाराजः कैकेय्या दारुणम् वचः
transliteration: tataḥ śrutvā mahārājaḥ kaikeyyā dāruṇam vacaḥ
english: Hearing Kaikeyi's fell speech, the monarch bewailed for a time, and then thought.

sanskrit: किम् नु मे यदि वा स्वप्नश्चित्तमोहोओऽपि वामम
transliteration: kim nu me yadi vā svapnaścittamohoo'pi vāmama
english: Is this a day-dream to me or has bewilderment befallen my senses? Is this owing to influence of some evil spirit or has my mind been affected?

sanskrit: इति सम्चिन्त्य तद्राजा नाध्यगच्छ त्तदा सुखम्
transliteration: iti samcintya tadrājā nādhyagaccha ttadā sukham
english: Thinking thus, the king could not arrive at the origin of (this phenomenon); and then he swooned away. Then regaining his senses, he was filled with grief on recollecting Kaikeyi's words.

sanskrit: व्यथितो विक्लबशचैव व्याघ्रीम् दृष्ट्वा यथा मृगः
transliteration: vyathito viklabaśacaiva vyāghrīm dṛṣṭvā yathā mṛgaḥ
english: And pained and woebegone, like to a deer at the sight of a tigress, he fetched a deep sigh, and sat down on the uncovered ground. Like a venomous snake confined by power of incantation within a circle, the lord of men, in indignation exclaimed. “O fie!" And deprived of his senses by grief, he again swooned away.

And pained and woebegone, like to a deer at the sight of a tigress, he fetched a deep sigh, and sat down on the uncovered ground. Like a venomous snake confined by power of incantation within a circle, the lord of men, in indignation exclaimed. “O fie!" And deprived of his senses by grief, he again swooned away.

sanskrit: चिरेण तु नृपः सम्ज्ञाम् प्रतिलभ्य सुदुःखितः
transliteration: cireṇa tu nṛpaḥ samjñām pratilabhya suduḥkhitaḥ

sanskrit: किम् कृतम् तव रामेण पापं पापे मयापि वा
transliteration: kim kṛtam tava rāmeṇa pāpaṃ pāpe mayāpi vā

sanskrit: कौसल्याम् वा सुमित्राम् वा त्यजेयमपि वा श्रियम्
transliteration: kausalyām vā sumitrām vā tyajeyamapi vā śriyam

sanskrit: जीवितम् वात्मनो रामम् न त्वेव पितृवत्सलम्
transliteration: jīvitam vātmano rāmam na tveva pitṛvatsalam

sanskrit: अपश्यतस्तु मे रामम् नष्टा भवति चेतना
तिष्ठेल्लोको विना सूर्यम् सस्यम् वा सलिलम् विना
transliteration: apaśyatastu me rāmam naṣṭā bhavati cetanā
tiṣṭhelloko vinā sūryam sasyam vā salilam vinā

sanskrit: न तु रामम् विना देहे तिष्ठेत्तु मम जीवितम्
transliteration: na tu rāmam vinā dehe tiṣṭhettu mama jīvitam

sanskrit: अपिते चरणौ मूर्ध्ना स्पृशाम्येष प्रसीद मे
transliteration: apite caraṇau mūrdhnā spṛśāmyeṣa prasīda me
english: Do you then that entertains unrighteous aims, abandon this intention of yours. I lay my head at your feet. Be propitious to me. Why does you, O sinful one, cherish in your mind such a frightful idea?

sanskrit: अथ जीज्ञाससे माम् त्वम् भरतस्य प्रियाप्रिये
transliteration: atha jījñāsase mām tvam bharatasya priyāpriye
english: You (often) asked me whether I love Bharata or not. Be that which you had formerly told me in favour of that descendant of Raghu.

sanskrit: स मे ज्येष्ठः सुतः श्रीमान् धर्मज्येष्ठ इतीव मे
transliteration: sa me jyeṣṭhaḥ sutaḥ śrīmān dharmajyeṣṭha itīva me
english: That blessed one is my eldest son, and the most righteous of them all even this, with the view of pleasing me, you sweet speeched one had said.

sanskrit: आविष्टासि गृहम् शून्यम् सा त्वम् परवशम् गता
transliteration: āviṣṭāsi gṛham śūnyam sā tvam paravaśam gatā
english: Now hearing of the installation of Rāma, you yourself filled with grief, are making me exceedingly aggrieved. Or in this empty chamber having been possessed, you have come under influence not your own.

sanskrit: अनयो नयसम्पन्ने यत्र ते विकृता मतिः
transliteration: anayo nayasampanne yatra te vikṛtā matiḥ
english: And this signal lawlessness, O exalted lady, has befallen the race of the Ikşvākus, the cause of which, O You versed in moral laws, is your mental derangement.

sanskrit: न हि किम्चिदयुक्तम् वा विप्रियम् वा पुरा मम
transliteration: na hi kimcidayuktam vā vipriyam vā purā mama
english: You did not formerly do to me aught that was improper or disagreeable; therefore, O you of expansive eyes, I cannot rely upon you (as sane).

sanskrit: बहुशो हि स्म बाले त्वम् कथयसे मम
transliteration: bahuśo hi sma bāle tvam kathayase mama
english: You did O girl, many a time tell me that Rāma was equal to you with the high-souled Bharata.

sanskrit: कथम् रोचयसे भीरु नव वर्षाणि पञ्च च
transliteration: katham rocayase bhīru nava varṣāṇi pañca ca
english: Wherefore then, O bashful one, do you like that the illustrious and righteous Rāma, O exalted dame, should reside in the forest for five and nine years?
Why do you like that the exceedingly tender Rāma with his soul established in virtue, should dwell in the woods, undergoing terrible hardship?
Why do you, O you of graceful eyes, wish Rāma, captivating all creatures, and engaged in ministering to you, to be banished?

sanskrit: विशेषम् त्वयि तस्मात्तु भरतस्य न लक्षये
transliteration: viśeṣam tvayi tasmāttu bharatasya na lakṣaye
english: Rāma verily serve you far more than does Bharata; and I do not find that Bharata regard you more than Rāma.
Who will, save that foremost of men, so devotedly minister to you, regard you, enhance your influence, and do your will.
Not one of the many thousands of females and the innumerable retainers (in the palace), has been able to fasten reproach upon Rāma for real or false misconduct.
Soothing all creatures with a pure heart, that great soul by means of good offices secure the affections of the inhabitants of the kingdom,

sanskrit: सत्येन लोकान् जयति दीनान् दानेन राघवः
गुरून् शुश्रूषया वीरो धनुशा युधि शात्रवान्
transliteration: satyena lokān jayati dīnān dānena rāghavaḥ
gurūn śuśrūṣayā vīro dhanuśā yudhi śātravān
english: He conquers all the twice-born ones by gifts; and that hero conquers his superiors by ministrations; and his enemies by encountering them with the bow.
For certain, in Rāghava are truth and charity, and asceticism, and self renunciation, and friendship, and purity, and sincerity, and learning, and the disposition to tend his superiors.
How, O respected one, can you ask for this that will bring you sin, touching Rāma endowed with candour, and energetic like to a Maharsi, and resembling a celestial?

sanskrit: स कथम् त्वत्कृते रामम् वक्ष्यामि प्रियमप्रियम्
transliteration: sa katham tvatkṛte rāmam vakṣyāmi priyamapriyam
english: I do not recollect to have heard Rāma, who ever speaks sweet words, to have used any unpleasant speech to any one; how can I then foi your sake unfold this disagreeable matter to the beloved Rāma.

sanskrit: क्षमा यस्मिन् दमस्त्यागः सत्यम् धर्मः कृतज्ञता
अप्यहिम्सा च भूतानाम् तमृते का गतिर्मम
transliteration: kṣamā yasmin damastyāgaḥ satyam dharmaḥ kṛtajñatā
apyahimsā ca bhūtānām tamṛte kā gatirmama
english: And what stay have I save him in whom abide forgiveness, and asceticism and renunciation, and verity, and righteousness, and gratitude, and harmlessness towards all creatures.
It behove you, O Kaikeyi, to have pity on me, aged and on the verge of death, and afflicted with grief, and distressed, and engaged in lamentations.

sanskrit: तत्सर्वम् तव दास्यामि मा च त्वाम् मन्युराविशेत्
transliteration: tatsarvam tava dāsyāmi mā ca tvām manyurāviśet
english: Whatever can be obtained in this earth bounded by the ocean I will confer on you, do you not bring about my death,

sanskrit: अञ्जलिम् कुर्मि कैकेयि पादौ चापि स्पृशामि ते
शरणम् भव रामस्य माऽधर्मो मामिह स्पृशेत्
transliteration: añjalim kurmi kaikeyi pādau cāpi spṛśāmi te
śaraṇam bhava rāmasya mā'dharmo māmiha spṛśet
english: O Kaikeyi, I clasp my palms, I fall at your feet, do you be the protector of Rāma, so that sin may not taint me.

When the terrible Kaikeyī in still more terrible language addressed the mighty king, who was burning in grief, and bewailing, and deprived of his senses, and feeling a sensation of whirling, and overwhelmed with woe, and again and again beseeching for crossing this ocean of sorrow, saying.

When the terrible Kaikeyī in still more terrible language addressed the mighty king, who was burning in grief, and bewailing, and deprived of his senses, and feeling a sensation of whirling, and overwhelmed with woe, and again and again beseeching for crossing this ocean of sorrow, saying.

sanskrit: यदि दत्वा वरौ राजन् पुनः प्रत्यनुतप्यसे
transliteration: yadi datvā varau rājan punaḥ pratyanutapyase
english: If, O monarch, having conferred the boon, you repent afterwards, how, O hero, will you speak of your righteousness in the world?
When, O you versed in duty, the Rajarsis assembled around you shall ask you regarding this matter, what will you answer?

sanskrit: यस्याः प्रसादे जीवामि या च मामभ्यपालयत्
तस्याः कृतम् मया मिथ्या कैकेय्या इति वक्ष्यसि
transliteration: yasyāḥ prasāde jīvāmi yā ca māmabhyapālayat
tasyāḥ kṛtam mayā mithyā kaikeyyā iti vakṣyasi
english: Wilt you say, “by whose favour do I live and who had tended me, to that Kaikeyi have I broken my promise?'
Surely, O lord of men, you will bring disgrace to all the monarchs (of your line), since having conferred the boons this very day, you speak otherwise.

Śaibya granted his own flesh to the bird in the matter of the hawk and the pigeon.* And Alarka, having granted his eyes (to a blind Brahmin) attained excellent state. *The story goes that desirous of testing the charity of Saibya, Indra and Agni assuming the forms of a hawk and a pigeon respectively, went to the king, the former pursuing the latter. The pigeon in a fright asked the protection of the monarch, whereon he granted it. But the hawk urged, 'why do you retain the food that has been appointed by Providence?' But the king declined, and cut off his own flesh and gave it to the hawk.
And the ocean, having bound himself by promise, never passes beyond his shores. Remembering these old stories render not your promise nugatory.

sanskrit: स त्वम् धर्मम् परित्यज्य रामम् राज्येऽभिषिच्यच
transliteration: sa tvam dharmam parityajya rāmam rājye'bhiṣicyaca
english: O you of perverted understanding, renouncing righteousness, and installing Rāma in the kingdom, you wish ever to give yourself up to pleasure with Kausalyă.

sanskrit: भवत्वधर्मो धर्मो वा सत्यम् वा यदि वानृतम्
यत्त्वया सम्श्रुतम् मह्यम् तस्य नास्ति व्यतिक्रमः
transliteration: bhavatvadharmo dharmo vā satyam vā yadi vānṛtam
yattvayā samśrutam mahyam tasya nāsti vyatikramaḥ
english: Whether what I have proposed be righteous or otherwise, whether you have promised truly or falsely, swerve not from your word.

sanskrit: अहम् हि विषमद्यैव पीत्वा बहु तवाग्रतः
transliteration: aham hi viṣamadyaiva pītvā bahu tavāgrataḥ
english: If you install Rāma, this very day drinking poison, I will surely die before you.
If I for a single day behold Rāma's mother receiving homage rendered with clasped hands, I will consider death even as welcome.
O lord of men, by Bharata's self dear to me as my own life, I swear that save the exile of Rama, nothing shall satisfy me.

sanskrit: विलपन्तम् च राजानम् न प्रतिव्याजहार सा
transliteration: vilapantam ca rājānam na prativyājahāra sā
english: Having said this, Kaikeyi paused; and maintained silence disregarding the bewailing monarch.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु राजा कैकेय्या वृतम् परमशोभनम्
रामस्य च वने वासमैश्वर्यम् भरतस्य च
transliteration: śrutvā tu rājā kaikeyyā vṛtam paramaśobhanam
rāmasya ca vane vāsamaiśvaryam bharatasya ca
english: The king with his senses overwhelmed with grief, hearing Kaikeyi's exceedingly bitter words, reflected on Rama's abode in the woods, and the advancement of Bharata, and being bewildered for a while spoke not to Kaikeyi but gazed steadfastly at that exalted dame. a

The king with his senses overwhelmed with grief, hearing Kaikeyi's exceedingly bitter words, reflected on Rama's abode in the woods, and the advancement of Bharata, and being bewildered for a while spoke not to Kaikeyi but gazed steadfastly at that exalted dame. a

sanskrit: ताम् हि वज्रसमाम् वाचमाकर्ण्य हृदया प्रियाम्
transliteration: tām hi vajrasamām vācamākarṇya hṛdayā priyām
english: His beloved wife, who had uttered disagreeable things. And having heard that speech resembling thunder-bolt, and unpleasant to the heart, and surcharged with grief, the king was extremely pained.

sanskrit: स देव्या व्यवसायम् च घोरम् च शपथम् कृतम्
transliteration: sa devyā vyavasāyam ca ghoram ca śapatham kṛtam
english: Then recollecting that revered lady's resolve, and his own terrible oath, he, sighing forth, “O Rāma," dropped down like a felled tree.
And then that master of the earth being deprived of his sense, was like a mad man, or a patient with his faculties wildered, or a serpent whose energy has been exhausted.

sanskrit: दीनया तु गिरा राजा इति होवाच कैकयिम्
transliteration: dīnayā tu girā rājā iti hovāca kaikayim
english: In sad and distressful words, he addressed Kaikeyi, saying, Who is it that has convinced you that this exceedingly heinous course is a proper one?

sanskrit: कुतो वा ते भयम् जातम् या त्वमेवम्विदम् वरम्
transliteration: kuto vā te bhayam jātam yā tvamevamvidam varam

sanskrit: यदि भर्तुः प्रियम् कार्यम् लोकस्य भरतस्य च
transliteration: yadi bhartuḥ priyam kāryam lokasya bharatasya ca

sanskrit: किम् नु कुःखमLईकम् वा मयि रामे च पश्यसि
transliteration: kim nu kuḥkhamaīkam vā mayi rāme ca paśyasi

sanskrit: रामादपि हि तम् मन्ये धर्मतो बलवत्तरम्
कथम् द्रक्ष्यामि रामस्य वनम् गच्छेति भाषिते
transliteration: rāmādapi hi tam manye dharmato balavattaram
katham drakṣyāmi rāmasya vanam gaccheti bhāṣite

sanskrit: ताम् हि मे सुकृताम् बुद्धिम् सुहृद्भिः सह निश्चिताम्
transliteration: tām hi me sukṛtām buddhim suhṛdbhiḥ saha niścitām

sanskrit: किम् माम् वक्ष्यन्ति राजानो नानादिग्भ्यः समागताह्
transliteration: kim mām vakṣyanti rājāno nānādigbhyaḥ samāgatāh

sanskrit: यदा तु बहवो वृद्धा गुणवन्तो बहुश्रुताह्
transliteration: yadā tu bahavo vṛddhā guṇavanto bahuśrutāh

english: And when many aged folks, endowed with virtues, and accomplished in various lore will ask me concerning Kākutstha, what then shall i say to them, 'Sore pressed by Kaikeyſ, have I banished Rama?

sanskrit: किम् माम् वक्ष्यति कौसल्या राघवे वनमास्थिते
transliteration: kim mām vakṣyati kausalyā rāghave vanamāsthite
english: Even if I speak this truly, yet none will lend credence to it. And what will Kausalya say to me, when Rāma shall have gone to the forest? Having done her this mighty wrong, what shall I say to her?

sanskrit: यदा यदा ही कौसल्या दासीवच्च सखीव च
transliteration: yadā yadā hī kausalyā dāsīvacca sakhīva ca

english: Kausalyă serves me at the same time like a slave, and a friend, and wife, and sister, and mother. Ever studious of my welfare, dearly loving her son, and speaking every one fair, that exalted lady, although deserving of homage at my hands, has up to this time not been regarded by me, because of you.

sanskrit: न मया सत्कृता देवि सत्कारार्हा कृते तव
इदानीम् तत्तपति माम् यन्मया सुकृतम् त्वयि
transliteration: na mayā satkṛtā devi satkārārhā kṛte tava
idānīm tattapati mām yanmayā sukṛtam tvayi

sanskrit: विप्रकारम् च रामस्य सम्प्रयाणम् वनस्य च
transliteration: viprakāram ca rāmasya samprayāṇam vanasya ca

sanskrit: सुमित्रा प्रेक्ष्यवै भीता कथम् मे विश्वसिष्यति
transliteration: sumitrā prekṣyavai bhītā katham me viśvasiṣyati

sanskrit: माम् च पञ्चत्वमापन्नम् रामम् च वनमाश्रितम्
वैदेही बत मे प्राणान् शोचन्ती क्षपयिष्यति
transliteration: mām ca pañcatvamāpannam rāmam ca vanamāśritam
vaidehī bata me prāṇān śocantī kṣapayiṣyati

sanskrit: न हि राममहम् दृष्ट्व प्रवसन्तम् महावने
transliteration: na hi rāmamaham dṛṣṭva pravasantam mahāvane

sanskrit: सा नूनम् विधवा राज्यम् सपुत्रा कारयिष्यसि
transliteration: sā nūnam vidhavā rājyam saputrā kārayiṣyasi
english: When I shall witness Rāma repairing to the mighty forest, and Sītā weeping (in grief), I shall not hope for a long life; and you, becoming a widow, will reign along with your son.

sanskrit: न हि प्रवाजिते रामे देवि जीवितुमुत्सहे
transliteration: na hi pravājite rāme devi jīvitumutsahe

sanskrit: अनृतैर्बहु माम् सान्वैःसा न्त्वयन्ती स्म स्मभाषसे
transliteration: anṛtairbahu mām sānvaiḥsā ntvayantī sma smabhāṣase

sanskrit: अहो दुःखमहो कृच्छ्रम् यत्र वाचः क्षमे तव
transliteration: aho duḥkhamaho kṛcchram yatra vācaḥ kṣame tava

sanskrit: चिरम् खलु मया पापे त्वम् पापेनाभिरक्षिता
transliteration: ciram khalu mayā pāpe tvam pāpenābhirakṣitā

english: Surely, people will be justified in condemning me wicked-minded that I am, for my son having been deprived of his ancestral kingdom by me; saying.

sanskrit: यः स्त्रीकृते प्रियम् पुत्रम् वनम् प्रस्थापयिष्यति
transliteration: yaḥ strīkṛte priyam putram vanam prasthāpayiṣyati

sanskrit: नालम् द्वितीयम् वचनम् पुत्रो माम् प्रति भाषितुम्
transliteration: nālam dvitīyam vacanam putro mām prati bhāṣitum

sanskrit: यदि मे राघवः कुर्याद्वनम् गच्चेति चोदितः
transliteration: yadi me rāghavaḥ kuryādvanam gacceti coditaḥ

sanskrit: प्रतिकूलम् प्रियम् मे स्यान्न तु वत्सः करिष्यति
शुद्धिभावो हि भावम् मे न तु ज्ञास्यति राघवः
transliteration: pratikūlam priyam me syānna tu vatsaḥ kariṣyati
śuddhibhāvo hi bhāvam me na tu jñāsyati rāghavaḥ

sanskrit: स वनम् प्रव्रजे त्युक्तोबाढ वित्येव वक्ष्यति
राघवे हि वनम् प्राप्ते सर्वलोकस्य धिक्कृतम्
transliteration: sa vanam pravraje tyuktobāḍha vityeva vakṣyati
rāghave hi vanam prāpte sarvalokasya dhikkṛtam

sanskrit: राघवे हि वनम् प्राप्ते सर्वलोकस्य धिक्कृतम्
transliteration: rāghave hi vanam prāpte sarvalokasya dhikkṛtam

sanskrit: मृते मयि गते रामे वनम् मनुजपुङ्गवे
transliteration: mṛte mayi gate rāme vanam manujapuṅgave

sanskrit: इष्टे मम जने शेषे किम् पापम् प्रतिवत्स्यसे
कौसल्या माम् च रामम् च पुत्रौ च यदि हास्यति
transliteration: iṣṭe mama jane śeṣe kim pāpam prativatsyase
kausalyā mām ca rāmam ca putrau ca yadi hāsyati

sanskrit: कौसल्याम् च सुमित्राम् च माम् च पुत्रैस्त्रिभिः सह
transliteration: kausalyām ca sumitrām ca mām ca putraistribhiḥ saha

sanskrit: प्रक्षिव्य नरके सा त्वम् कैकेयि सुखिता भव
मया रामेण च त्यक्तम् शाश्वतम् सत्कृतम् गुणैः
transliteration: prakṣivya narake sā tvam kaikeyi sukhitā bhava
mayā rāmeṇa ca tyaktam śāśvatam satkṛtam guṇaiḥ

sanskrit: मा स्म मे भरतः कार्षीत् प्रेतकृत्यम् गतायुषः
transliteration: mā sma me bharataḥ kārṣīt pretakṛtyam gatāyuṣaḥ

sanskrit: मृते मयि गते रामे वनम् पुरुषपुङ्गवे
transliteration: mṛte mayi gate rāme vanam puruṣapuṅgave
english: When I am dead, and when that foremost of men has gone to the forest, do you, a widow, rule the kingdom along with your son.
O daughter of a king, when by chance you reside in my mansion, I must come by signal infamy and discomfiture in the world, and meet with general disregard, like a sinful person.

sanskrit: पद्भ्याम् रामो महारण्ये वत्सो मे विचरिष्यति
transliteration: padbhyām rāmo mahāraṇye vatso me vicariṣyati

sanskrit: स कथन्नु कषायाणि तिक्तानि कटुकानि च
transliteration: sa kathannu kaṣāyāṇi tiktāni kaṭukāni ca
english: How will my son, at the approach of whose meal-time, cooks wearing ear-rings and emulating each other prepare excellent meats and drinks, pass his days, living on fare furnished by the woods, of astringent, or bitter, or pungent taste?

sanskrit: न ब्रवीमि स्त्रियः सर्वा भरतस्यैव मातरम्
transliteration: na bravīmi striyaḥ sarvā bharatasyaiva mātaram
english: O you that is intent upon doing mischief to all, O you addicted to selfishness, O cruel one, has God made your mind so very vile, only to torment me? What wrong have you come by either through me, or Rāma ever engaged in your welfare?
On beholding Rāma plunged in sorrow, fathers will forsake sons, and wives attached to their husbands will forsake them, and the entire earth will be affected with ill-humour.
When I hear him coming, adorned like to a son of the celestials, I rejoice on casting my eyes on him, and I feel as if I had regained my youth.
Men may do without the Sun, and the wielder of the thunder-bolt not raining, but none, I apprehend, can live, on witnessing Rāma repairing hence.

I have kept in my mansion, like to my own death, you that desire my destruction, and are intent upon doing me wrong, and are my foe. I have for a long time held you on my lap, like to a she-snake of virulent poison; therefore in consequence of my folly, I now meet with destruction.

sanskrit: पुरम् च राष्ट्रम् च निहत्य बान्धवान्
transliteration: puram ca rāṣṭram ca nihatya bāndhavān
english: Now dissevered from me, and Rāma together with Lakşmaņa, let Bharata govern the city and the kingdom along with you. Destroying your relatives, do you enhance the joy of my enemies.

O you cruelly-disposed, O you bringer on of calamities, since banishing all sense of the relation in which we stand to each other as husband and wife, you have spoken thus, why reduced to thousand fragments your teeth drop not from off your mouth down to the ground?
Rāma has not used any harsh speech towards you. Indeed Rāma knows no harsh speech; why then do you seek to inflict upon Rāma (ever) pleasant spoken, and endowed with agreeable qualities, such wrongs.

sanskrit: प्रताम्य वा प्रज्वल वा प्रणश्य वा
transliteration: pratāmya vā prajvala vā praṇaśya vā
english: O you that render infamous the king of the Kekayas, whether you become miserable, or enter into fire, or kill yourself by taking poison, or dive into the bowels of the earth opened at thousand places, I will not execute your fell intention that is fraught with evil to me.

I do not wish, that you, like to a razor, and ever speaking pleasant falsehoods, and possessed of a vile heart, the destroyer of your own race, you that wish to burn my heart and life, you un-beautiful one, may remain alive.

sanskrit: न जीवितम् मेऽस्ति पुनः कुतः सुखम्
transliteration: na jīvitam me'sti punaḥ kutaḥ sukham
english: My life itself is in jeopardy, where then is my happiness? Where is the happiness of parents without their sons? It behove you not, O noble dame, to do evil to me. I take hold of your feet; do you be propitious to me.

As bewailing thus like one forlorn the ruler of earth whose heart was captivated by Kaikeyi on account of her supreme beauty proceeded to take hold of her feet, who having banished all self respect, sat with her legs stretched, he, without being able to come at them, fell down in a swoon, like one enfeebled with disease.

sanskrit: अतत् अर्हम् महा राजम् शयानम् अतथा उचितम्
ययातिम् इव पुण्य अन्ते देव लोकात् परिच्युतम्
transliteration: atat arham mahā rājam śayānam atathā ucitam
yayātim iva puṇya ante deva lokāt paricyutam
english: Then as the mighty king was lying down in this unbeseeming and improper guise, like Yayāti dropped from the celestial, that lady, personating the ruin of the race, not fearing public odium, who had discerned danger from Rāma to Bharata, not having attained her wish, again addressed the monarch, concerning the boon he had promised to her.

sanskrit: अनर्थ रूपा सिद्ध अर्थाअभीता भय दर्शिनी
पुनर् आकारयाम् आस तम् एव वरम् अन्गना
transliteration: anartha rūpā siddha arthāabhītā bhaya darśinī
punar ākārayām āsa tam eva varam anganā
english: Then as the mighty king was lying down in this unbeseeming and improper guise, like Yayāti dropped from the celestial, that lady, personating the ruin of the race, not fearing public odium, who had discerned danger from Rāma to Bharata, not having attained her wish, again addressed the monarch, concerning the boon he had promised to her.

sanskrit: त्वम् कत्थसे महा राज सत्य वादी द्Rढ व्रतः
मम च इमम् वरम् कस्मात् विधारयितुम् इच्चसि
transliteration: tvam katthase mahā rāja satya vādī dḍha vrataḥ
mama ca imam varam kasmāt vidhārayitum iccasi
english: You describe yourself, O mighty monarch, as speaking the truth and firm in vow. Why then do you hesitate to confer this boon on me?

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः तु कैकेय्या राजा दश रथः तदा
प्रत्युवाच ततः क्रुद्धो मुहूर्तम् विह्वलन्न् इव
transliteration: evam uktaḥ tu kaikeyyā rājā daśa rathaḥ tadā
pratyuvāca tataḥ kruddho muhūrtam vihvalann iva
english: Thus addressed by Kaikeyi king Dasaratha, remaining stupefied for a while thus answered her in wrath.

sanskrit: म्Rते मयि गते रामे वनम् मनुज पुम्गवे
हन्त अनार्ये मम अमित्रे रामः प्रव्राजितः वनम्
transliteration: mte mayi gate rāme vanam manuja pumgave
hanta anārye mama amitre rāmaḥ pravrājitaḥ vanam
english: O ignoble one! O enemy of mine! On my being dead and that chief of men, Rāma, repairing to the woods, do you, yours wish attained, become happy.
When in heaven, questioning me as to Rāma's welfare, the celestials, learning of his banishment to the woods, will tax me on this score, how shall I also bear that reproach of theirs?

sanskrit: यदि सत्यम् ब्रवीम्य् एतत् तत् असत्यम् भविष्यति
transliteration: yadi satyam bravīmy etat tat asatyam bhaviṣyati
english: If I shall truthfully say I have sent Rāma to the woods for compassing Kaikeyi's pleasure, that will count for a falsehood.

sanskrit: अपुत्रेण मया पुत्रः श्रमेण महता महान्
रामो लब्धो महाबाहुः स कथं त्यज्यते मया
transliteration: aputreṇa mayā putraḥ śrameṇa mahatā mahān
rāmo labdho mahābāhuḥ sa kathaṃ tyajyate mayā
english: Sonless first, I have obtained the exceedingly energetic and mighty Rāma by great pain, how can I then renounce him?
How shall I banish Rāma having eyes resembling lotus' petals, who is heroic, and accomplished and of subdued anger, and forgiving.
How shall I dismiss to Dandaka the charming Rāma of dark blue hue like that of a blue lotus, possessed of mighty arms, and having great strength?
How shall I behold the intelligent Rāma in evil plight, who has never known suffering, and has always enjoyed felicity?
If without inflicting injury upon Rāma, I meet with death, I shall then attain happiness.

sanskrit: किम् विप्रियेण कैकेयि प्रियं योजयसे मम
transliteration: kim vipriyeṇa kaikeyi priyaṃ yojayase mama
english: O cruel Kaikeyi, O you of evil purpose, why do you do this wrong to my beloved Rāma having truth for prowess? If I banish Rāma, an unparalleled obloquy will surely darken (my fair fame).
As king Dasaratha was bewailing thus with a heart wrought up with grief, the sun set and night came on.

sanskrit: अस्तम् अभ्यगमत् सूर्यो रजनी च अभ्यवर्तत
सा त्रि यामा तथा आर्तस्य चन्द्र मण्डल मण्डिता
transliteration: astam abhyagamat sūryo rajanī ca abhyavartata
sā tri yāmā tathā ārtasya candra maṇḍala maṇḍitā

sanskrit: तथैव उष्णम् विनिह्श्वस्य व्Rद्धो दशरथो न्Rपः
transliteration: tathaiva uṣṇam vinihśvasya vddho daśaratho npaḥ

sanskrit: विललाप आर्तवद् दुह्खम् गगन आसक्त लोचनः
न प्रभातम् त्वया इच्चामि मया अयम् रचितः अन्जलिः
transliteration: vilalāpa ārtavad duhkham gagana āsakta locanaḥ
na prabhātam tvayā iccāmi mayā ayam racitaḥ anjaliḥ

sanskrit: अथवा गम्यताम् शीघ्रम् न अहम् इच्चामि निर्घ्Rणाम्
अथ वा गम्यतां शीघ्रं नाहमिच्छामि निर्घृणाम्
transliteration: athavā gamyatām śīghram na aham iccāmi nirghṇām
atha vā gamyatāṃ śīghraṃ nāhamicchāmi nirghṛṇām

sanskrit: न्Rशम्साम् कैकेयीम् द्रष्टुम् यत् क्Rते व्यसनम् महत्
एवम् उक्त्वा ततः राजा कैकेयीम् सम्यत अन्जलिः
transliteration: nśamsām kaikeyīm draṣṭum yat kte vyasanam mahat
evam uktvā tataḥ rājā kaikeyīm samyata anjaliḥ

sanskrit: प्रसादयाम् आस पुनः कैकेयीम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
साधु व्Rत्तस्य दीनस्य त्वद् गतस्य गत आयुषः
transliteration: prasādayām āsa punaḥ kaikeyīm ca idam abravīt
sādhu vttasya dīnasya tvad gatasya gata āyuṣaḥ

sanskrit: प्रसादः क्रियताम् देवि भद्रे राज्ञो विशेषतः
शून्येन खलु सुश्रोणि मया इदम् समुदाह्Rतम्
transliteration: prasādaḥ kriyatām devi bhadre rājño viśeṣataḥ
śūnyena khalu suśroṇi mayā idam samudāhtam

sanskrit: कुरु साधु प्रसादम् मे बाले सह्Rदया हि असि
प्रसीद देवि रामो मे त्वद्धत्तं राज्यमव्ययम्
transliteration: kuru sādhu prasādam me bāle sahdayā hi asi
prasīda devi rāmo me tvaddhattaṃ rājyamavyayam

sanskrit: मम रामस्य लोकस्य गुरूणां भरतस्य च
transliteration: mama rāmasya lokasya gurūṇāṃ bharatasya ca

english: Having heard the exceedingly piteous words of her husband, the king of pure sentiment, who was distressed, with his eye rendered coppery and flowing with tears, that wicked minded and merciless woman spoke not.

sanskrit: ततः स राजा पुनर् एव मूर्चितः
transliteration: tataḥ sa rājā punar eva mūrcitaḥ
english: Thereat seeing that his favourite dissatisfied wife persisted in urging the banishment of his son, the king struck with grief, again fell down to the earth, senseless.
As the wise king afflicted with sorrow was sighing hot and hard, the night passed away Then as the eulogists attempted to sung his praises for awakening him, he prohibited them to do so.

sanskrit: पुत्र शोक अर्दितम् पापा विसम्ज्ञम् पतितम् भुवि
विवेष्टमानम् उदीक्ष्य सा ऐक्ष्वाकम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: putra śoka arditam pāpā visamjñam patitam bhuvi
viveṣṭamānam udīkṣya sā aikṣvākam idam abravīt
english: Then that sinful woman, seeing the descendant of Ikşvāku distressed on account of his son, and deprived of consciousness, and lying inert on the ground, spoke to him, saying.

sanskrit: पापम् क्Rत्वा इव किम् इदम् मम सम्श्रुत्य सम्श्रवम्
शेषे क्षिति तले सन्नः स्थित्याम् स्थातुम् त्वम् अर्हसि
transliteration: pāpam ktvā iva kim idam mama samśrutya samśravam
śeṣe kṣiti tale sannaḥ sthityām sthātum tvam arhasi
english: Having promised to grant me the boon, how distressed do you lie on the ground, as if you did commit some sin? It behove you to keep untainted your dignity by performing what you have promised.

sanskrit: आहुः सत्यम् हि परमम् धर्मम् धर्मविदो जनाः
सत्यम् आश्रित्य हि मया त्वम् च धर्मम् प्रचोदितः
transliteration: āhuḥ satyam hi paramam dharmam dharmavido janāḥ
satyam āśritya hi mayā tvam ca dharmam pracoditaḥ
english: Truth, say persons cognizant of it, is the prime virtue. And it is in the interests of virtue, that I have been exhorting you.

sanskrit: सम्श्रुत्य शैब्यः श्येनाय स्वाम् तनुम् जगती पतिः
प्रदाय पक्षिणो राजन् जगाम गतिम् उत्तमाम्
transliteration: samśrutya śaibyaḥ śyenāya svām tanum jagatī patiḥ
pradāya pakṣiṇo rājan jagāma gatim uttamām
english: Having promised his own person to the hawk, that lord of earth, Saivya, having granted the same to the bird, went the excellent way.

sanskrit: तथ हि अलर्कः तेजस्वी ब्राह्मणे वेद पारगे
transliteration: tatha hi alarkaḥ tejasvī brāhmaṇe veda pārage
english: In the same manner, Alarka, being asked, plucked out his eyes readily and bestowed them on a certain Brāhmana versed in the Vedas.

sanskrit: सरिताम् तु पतिः स्वल्पाम् मर्यादाम् सत्यम् अन्वितः
सत्य अनुरोधात् समये वेलाम् खाम् न अतिवर्तते
transliteration: saritām tu patiḥ svalpām maryādām satyam anvitaḥ
satya anurodhāt samaye velām khām na ativartate
english: And the lord of rivers, having promised, even on occasions of Parvas, does not pass over his bounds for the sake of truth.
The one syllable (Om signifying) Brahma is the truth itself. In truth is established righteousness. Truth is the undecaying Vedas, and through truth people attain the foremost state.

sanskrit: सत्यं समनुवर्त्स्व यदि धर्मे धृता मतिः
सफलः स वरो मेऽस्तु वरदो ह्यसि सत्तम
transliteration: satyaṃ samanuvartsva yadi dharme dhṛtā matiḥ
saphalaḥ sa varo me'stu varado hyasi sattama
english: If your mind is established in virtue, do you then follow truth. Since, O excellent one, you have promised the boon, let that boon bear fruit.

sanskrit: प्रव्राजय सुतं रामम् त्रिः खलु त्वां ब्रवीम्यहम्
transliteration: pravrājaya sutaṃ rāmam triḥ khalu tvāṃ bravīmyaham
english: Do you, incited by me with the view of maintaining virtue, banish Rāma. Thrice, do I tell you.

sanskrit: समयम् च मम आर्य इमम् यदि त्वम् न करिष्यसि
transliteration: samayam ca mama ārya imam yadi tvam na kariṣyasi
english: If you did not fulfil this noble vow, O worshipful Lord, you have made to me, forsaken by you will I even in your very presence renounce my life.

sanskrit: न अशकत् पाशम् उन्मोक्तुम् बलिर् इन्द्र क्Rतम् यथा
transliteration: na aśakat pāśam unmoktum balir indra ktam yathā
english: Thus fearlessly urged by Kaikeyſ the king could not take off from himself the noose (of promise), even as Bali could not take off the noose that had been fixed upon him (by Upendra) at the instance of Indra.

sanskrit: उद्भ्रान्त ह्Rदयः च अपि विवर्ण वनदो अभवत्
स धुर्यो वै परिस्पन्दन् युग चक्र अन्तरम् यथा
transliteration: udbhrānta hdayaḥ ca api vivarṇa vanado abhavat
sa dhuryo vai parispandan yuga cakra antaram yathā
english: Thereupon, the king looked blank, and his heart became agitated, like to a beast of burden moving tortuously when placed within the yoke and wheels.

sanskrit: विह्वलाभ्याम् च नेत्राभ्याम् अपश्यन्न् इव भूमिपः
क्Rच्च्रात् धैर्येण सम्स्तभ्य कैकेयीम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: vihvalābhyām ca netrābhyām apaśyann iva bhūmipaḥ
kccrāt dhairyeṇa samstabhya kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: Then calming himself with a great effort, the king, as if not seeing Kaikeyi, with his haggard eyes, addressed her, saying.

sanskrit: यः ते मन्त्र क्Rतः पाणिर् अग्नौ पापे मया ध्Rतः
तम् त्यजामि स्वजम् चैव तव पुत्रम् सह त्वया
transliteration: yaḥ te mantra ktaḥ pāṇir agnau pāpe mayā dhtaḥ
tam tyajāmi svajam caiva tava putram saha tvayā
english: "I do here, O wicked wretch, renounce that hand of yours which I had held with mantras before the sacrificial fire, and I do also renounce along with you own-begotten* your son Bharata. * This is a new coinage rendered necessary for the exigencies of translation. If 'first-born' is justifiable, 'own-begotten,' is also such.
O exalted one, the night has departed; and as soon as the Sun rises, the superiors will surely urge me for installing Rāma with the provisions that have been procured for the purpose.
But if, O you of auspicious ways, hinder the installation of Răma, Rāma will perform my funeral obsequies, when I am dead, and not you accompanied by your son shall perform the same.

sanskrit: न च शक्नोम्यहं द्रषुं पूर्वं तथा सुखम्
transliteration: na ca śaknomyahaṃ draṣuṃ pūrvaṃ tathā sukham
english: That countenance of Rāma which I have once seen expanded in delight, I shall never be able to behold bereft of joy and cheerfulness, and down, with melancholy clouding it
As the high-souled ruler of earth was speaking thus to her, the night engarlanded with the moon and stars.was succeeded by the morning.

sanskrit: ततः पाप समाचारा कैकेयी पार्थिवम् पुनः
उवाच परुषम् वाक्यम् वाक्यज्ञा रोष मूर्चिता
transliteration: tataḥ pāpa samācārā kaikeyī pārthivam punaḥ
uvāca paruṣam vākyam vākyajñā roṣa mūrcitā
english: Then Kaikeyi of vile ways versed in speech, rendered senseless by wrath, again addressed the monarch in harsh language, saying.

sanskrit: किम् इदम् भाषसे राजन् वाक्यम् गर रुज उपमम्
आनाययितुम् अक्लिष्टम् पुत्रम् रामम् इह अर्हसि
transliteration: kim idam bhāṣase rājan vākyam gara ruja upamam
ānāyayitum akliṣṭam putram rāmam iha arhasi

sanskrit: स्थाप्य राज्ये मम सुतम् क्Rत्वा रामम् वने चरम्
निह्सपत्नाम् च माम् क्Rत्वा क्Rत क्Rत्यो भविष्यसि
transliteration: sthāpya rājye mama sutam ktvā rāmam vane caram
nihsapatnām ca mām ktvā kta ktyo bhaviṣyasi
english: What words, O king, do you say, comparable to poison or painful indisposition's. It behove you to summon hither your son, the energetic Rāma. Having established my son in the kingdom, and rendered Rāma a ranger of the woods and made myself rid of rivals, I shall attain my end.

sanskrit: स नुन्नैव तीक्षेन प्रतोदेन हय उत्तमः
राजा प्रदोचितः अभीक्ष्णम् कैकेयीम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sa nunnaiva tīkṣena pratodena haya uttamaḥ
rājā pradocitaḥ abhīkṣṇam kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: Thus urged by Kaikeyī, the king like to an excellent steed stung by a sharp goad, again spoke to her.

sanskrit: धर्म बन्धेन बद्धो अस्मि नष्टा च मम चेतना
ज्येष्ठम् पुत्रम् प्रियम् रामम् द्रष्टुम् इच्चामि धार्मिकम्
transliteration: dharma bandhena baddho asmi naṣṭā ca mama cetanā
jyeṣṭham putram priyam rāmam draṣṭum iccāmi dhārmikam
english: I have been bound fast by the ties of virtue, therefore have I lost my senses. I now only wish to behold my beloved eldest son, the righteous Rama.

sanskrit: पुण्ये नक्षत्रयोगे चे मुहूर्ते च समाहिते
transliteration: puṇye nakṣatrayoge ce muhūrte ca samāhite
english: Then when the night had gone by and day broke and the Sun arose, and when the sacred astral hour had arrived, Vasistha endowed with many virtues, surrounded by his disciples and furnished with the provisions, entered that foremost of cities.

Then when the night had gone by and day broke and the Sun arose, and when the sacred astral hour had arrived, Vasistha endowed with many virtues, surrounded by his disciples and furnished with the provisions, entered that foremost of cities.

Whose streets had been swept and watered and which had been decorated with streamers, and which was filled with people rejoicing, and whose stalls overflowed with articles, and which resounded with the noise of festivity, and which was populous with folks eager for the installation of Rāghava, and which was every where scented with sandal and dhüpa and aguru.
Therefore the highly energetic Vasiştha said to the kilful scr. of the charioteer, Do you speedily acquaint the mighty monarch that I have come.

sanskrit: क्षौद्रम् दधि घृतं लाजा दर्भाः सुमनसः पयः
अष्टौ च कन्या रुचिरा मत्तश्छ वरवारणः
transliteration: kṣaudram dadhi ghṛtaṃ lājā darbhāḥ sumanasaḥ payaḥ
aṣṭau ca kanyā rucirā mattaścha varavāraṇaḥ

sanskrit: केसरी च चतुर्दंष्ट्रो हि श्रेष्ठो महाबलः
transliteration: kesarī ca caturdaṃṣṭro hi śreṣṭho mahābalaḥ

sanskrit: एते चान्ये च बहवो नीयमानाः प्रियम्वदाः
transliteration: ete cānye ca bahavo nīyamānāḥ priyamvadāḥ

sanskrit: इति तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सूतपुत्रो महात्मनः
transliteration: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā sūtaputro mahātmanaḥ

sanskrit: तं तु पूर्वोदितं वृद्धं द्वारस्था राजसम्मतम्
transliteration: taṃ tu pūrvoditaṃ vṛddhaṃ dvārasthā rājasammatam

english: Do you please us delightedly and with a glad heart, even as the strong ocean pleases people at the rising of the sun.
The charioteer Mätali used to hymn Indra at this season, and (encouraged by that eulogy) he conquered the Dänavas. Even so do I hymn you.

sanskrit: आदित्यः सह चन्द्रेण यथा भूतधरां शुभाम्
transliteration: ādityaḥ saha candreṇa yathā bhūtadharāṃ śubhām

sanskrit: गता भगवती रात्रिः कृतकृत्य मिदं तव
transliteration: gatā bhagavatī rātriḥ kṛtakṛtya midaṃ tava

sanskrit: स्वयं वसिष्ठो भगवान् ब्राह्मणैः सह तिष्ठति
transliteration: svayaṃ vasiṣṭho bhagavān brāhmaṇaiḥ saha tiṣṭhati

sanskrit: यथा ह्यपालाः पशवो यथा सेना ह्यानायका
transliteration: yathā hyapālāḥ paśavo yathā senā hyānāyakā

sanskrit: यथा च्न्द्रं विना रात्रिर्यथा गावो विना वृषम्
एवं हि भविता राष्ट्रं यत्र राजा न दृश्यते
transliteration: yathā cndraṃ vinā rātriryathā gāvo vinā vṛṣam
evaṃ hi bhavitā rāṣṭraṃ yatra rājā na dṛśyate
english: Like to cattle's without their keeper, like to and army without its commander, like to a night without the moon, like to kines without their bull, is a kingdom without a king. Hearing these words of Sumantra, bland and appropriate, the lord of earth was afresh overwhelmed with grief.

Like to cattle's without their keeper, like to and army without its commander, like to a night without the moon, like to kines without their bull, is a kingdom without a king. Hearing these words of Sumantra, bland and appropriate, the lord of earth was afresh overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: ततः स राजा तम् सूतम् सन्न हर्षः सुतम् प्रति
शोक आरक्त ईक्षणः श्रीमान् उद्वीक्ष्य उवाच धार्मिकः
transliteration: tataḥ sa rājā tam sūtam sanna harṣaḥ sutam prati
śoka ārakta īkṣaṇaḥ śrīmān udvīkṣya uvāca dhārmikaḥ
english: Then the graceful and virtuous king, waxing disconsolate, on account of his son, and with his eyes reddened with the effect of grief, seeing the charioteer, said, “This eulogy of your pains me the more."

sanskrit: वाक्यैस्तु खलु मर्माणि मम भूयो निकृन्तसि
सुमन्त्रः करुणम् श्रुत्वा द्Rष्ट्वा दीनम् च पार्थिवम्
transliteration: vākyaistu khalu marmāṇi mama bhūyo nikṛntasi
sumantraḥ karuṇam śrutvā dṣṭvā dīnam ca pārthivam

sanskrit: प्रग्Rहीत अन्जलिः किम्चित् तस्मात् देशात् अपाक्रमन्
यदा वक्तुम् स्वयम् दैन्यान् न शशाक मही पतिः
transliteration: praghīta anjaliḥ kimcit tasmāt deśāt apākraman
yadā vaktum svayam dainyān na śaśāka mahī patiḥ

sanskrit: तदा सुमन्त्रम् मन्त्रज्ञा कैकेयी प्रत्युवाच ह
transliteration: tadā sumantram mantrajñā kaikeyī pratyuvāca ha

sanskrit: राममानय भद्रं ते नात्र कार्या विचारणा
स मन्यमानः कल्याणम् हृदयेन नन्नन्ध च
transliteration: rāmamānaya bhadraṃ te nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
sa manyamānaḥ kalyāṇam hṛdayena nannandha ca

english: Sumantra, Bring the beautiful Răma here, I want to see him. Thinking that some good would accrue to Rāma, he was pleased at heart and away he went speedily delighted at the royal mandate. Being asked again by Kaikeyi to hurry on at the time of departure Sumantra thought within himself.

sanskrit: इति सूतो मतिं कृत्वा हर्षेण महता वृतः
transliteration: iti sūto matiṃ kṛtvā harṣeṇa mahatā vṛtaḥ
english: "Evident it is that the Queen has become impatient to see Rāma's installation and hence is the hurry, and the king will now take rest.' Thinking this the energetic charioteer with great delight, intent on seeing Rāma, issued out of the city like a lake near the ocean.

"Evident it is that the Queen has become impatient to see Rāma's installation and hence is the hurry, and the king will now take rest.' Thinking this the energetic charioteer with great delight, intent on seeing Rāma, issued out of the city like a lake near the ocean.
Having come out of the presence of the king suddenly, he saw the warders, various citizens and great personages sitting at the gate.

sanskrit: ते तु ताम् रजनीम् उष्य ब्राह्मणा वेद पारगाः
transliteration: te tu tām rajanīm uṣya brāhmaṇā veda pāragāḥ
english: The Brahmana, versed in in Veda, the counsellors, the commanders of military forces and the leading merchants, together with the royal priest, all brimming with joy on account of Rāma's installation, were waiting at the royal gate all night long

sanskrit: अमात्या बल मुख्याः च मुख्या ये निगमस्य च
राघवस्य अभिषेक अर्थे प्रीयमाणाः तु सम्गताः
transliteration: amātyā bala mukhyāḥ ca mukhyā ye nigamasya ca
rāghavasya abhiṣeka arthe prīyamāṇāḥ tu samgatāḥ
english: The Brahmana, versed in in Veda, the counsellors, the commanders of military forces and the leading merchants, together with the royal priest, all brimming with joy on account of Rāma's installation, were waiting at the royal gate all night long

sanskrit: उदिते विमले सूर्ये पुष्ये च अभ्यागते अहनि
transliteration: udite vimale sūrye puṣye ca abhyāgate ahani

sanskrit: कान्चना जल कुम्भाः च भद्र पीठम् स्वलम्क्Rतम्
transliteration: kāncanā jala kumbhāḥ ca bhadra pīṭham svalamktam

sanskrit: याश्चान्याः सरितः पुण्या ह्रदाः कूपाः सरांसि च
transliteration: yāścānyāḥ saritaḥ puṇyā hradāḥ kūpāḥ sarāṃsi ca

sanskrit: क्षौद्रं दधि घृतं लाजा दर्भाः सुमनसः पयः
transliteration: kṣaudraṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ lājā darbhāḥ sumanasaḥ payaḥ

english: And all musical instruments, bringing these and all other things necessary for the installation of the descendants of Ikşvāku, in accordance with the king's permission, the panegyrists and other persons were assembled there.

And all musical instruments, bringing these and all other things necessary for the installation of the descendants of Ikşvāku, in accordance with the king's permission, the panegyrists and other persons were assembled there.

Not finding the king present there, they began to speak amongst themselves;, “Who will intimate the king of our arrival? The Sun is up and we do not see the king amongst us as yet. All articles necessary for the installation of the intelligent Rāma are ready."

sanskrit: रामः च सम्यग् आस्तीर्णो भास्वरा व्याघ्र चर्मणा
transliteration: rāmaḥ ca samyag āstīrṇo bhāsvarā vyāghra carmaṇā

sanskrit: गन्गा यमुनयोह् पुण्यात् सम्गमात् आह्Rतम् जलम्
transliteration: gangā yamunayoh puṇyāt samgamāt āhtam jalam

sanskrit: सदासक्तं च तद्वेश्म सुमन्त्रः प्रविवेश ह
तुष्टावास्य तदा वंशं प्रविश्य स विशां पतेः
transliteration: sadāsaktaṃ ca tadveśma sumantraḥ praviveśa ha
tuṣṭāvāsya tadā vaṃśaṃ praviśya sa viśāṃ pateḥ

sanskrit: स्तुवन्तं तम् तदा सूतं सुमन्त्रं मन्त्रकोविदम्
transliteration: stuvantaṃ tam tadā sūtaṃ sumantraṃ mantrakovidam

english: Oh Charioteer, 'Bring Rāma here' was the order I gave you; what is it that makes you neglect my command? I am not asleep; go and bring up Rāma here instantly. Saying this, king Dasaratha despatched Sumantra again.

sanskrit: स राजवचनं श्रुत्वा शिरसा प्रतिपूज्य तम्
transliteration: sa rājavacanaṃ śrutvā śirasā pratipūjya tam

english: Hearing the words of the king and bowing him with his head down, he issued out of the king's residence, thinking that some great good was awaiting. And having reached the public roads adorned with flags and pennons, he, filled with an excess of joy, began to wend his way, casting his look around. There on his way he heard the passers by, all talking about Rāma and his installation, as if brimming with joy on that account.

Then proceeding a little, Sumantra saw the beautiful palace of Rāma towering like the Kailāsa hill and resembling the abode of Sakra. It was closed with two big panels at the gate way (of which the trap-door was flung open), and adorned with hundreds of terraces, on its top were many idols made of gold, and arches crested with pearls and diamonds; its colour was white as the autumnal cloud and bright as the golden cave of Sumeru.

Then proceeding a little, Sumantra saw the beautiful palace of Rāma towering like the Kailāsa hill and resembling the abode of Sakra. It was closed with two big panels at the gate way (of which the trap-door was flung open), and adorned with hundreds of terraces, on its top were many idols made of gold, and arches crested with pearls and diamonds; its colour was white as the autumnal cloud and bright as the golden cave of Sumeru.

It was ornamented with highly brilliant jewels set in the garlands of gold flowers and strewn with pearls and diamonds and sprinkled with sandal and Agaru, the fragrance of which captivates the mind like the summit of the hill Dardura; it was graced with the presence of Sarasas and peacocks emitting pleasant sounds.

It was ornamented with highly brilliant jewels set in the garlands of gold flowers and strewn with pearls and diamonds and sprinkled with sandal and Agaru, the fragrance of which captivates the mind like the summit of the hill Dardura; it was graced with the presence of Sarasas and peacocks emitting pleasant sounds.

And covered with well-made figures of wolves and pictures of artistic excellence, the splendour of which captivates the mind and the eye as well; bright as the sun and moon, resembling the abode of Kuvera and the capital of the king of the celestials; filled with birds of various kinds and high as the summit of Sumeru.

And covered with well-made figures of wolves and pictures of artistic excellence, the splendour of which captivates the mind and the eye as well; bright as the sun and moon, resembling the abode of Kuvera and the capital of the king of the celestials; filled with birds of various kinds and high as the summit of Sumeru.

Thereupon arriving at this abode filled with wealth, and having its beauty greatly intensified with deer's and peacocks, moving to and fro, resembling the exquisitely splendid palace of the lord of the celestials, that charioteer was extremely enraptured, having the hairs of the body erect.

Then that charioteer entering several apartments, well adorned and resembling the Kailāsa hill and the abode of the celestials and passing by many persons, dear to Rāma and abiding in his purpose, entered the apartment of the ladies.
And he became exceedingly pleased on hearing pleasant words, meaning well to the son of the king, from all persons, engaged in some sort of service for the installation.

He saw the pleasant abode of Rāma, resembling that of Mahendra, and filled with deers and birds, having its top high as the summit of Meru and situated well in splendour, and the gateway filled with millions of citizens with clasped hands keeping their conveyances outside and coming from various quarters with presents for Rāma.

He saw there a wild elephant by the name of Śatruñjaya or the conqueror of foes having a huge body resembling a mountain enveloped in dark clouds, beautiful, capable of bearing the goading hook and intended Rāma's conveyance.

He saw well adorned ministers dear to the king with horses, chariots and elephants; and leaving them all on either side, entered unprevented, like to the marine monster Makara entering the ocean containing many pearls and diamonds, the splendid apartment of the ladies, resembling the clouds that hover over the summit of the Hill Himadri, and having a number of beautiful houses comparing with great celestial cars. as

sanskrit: स तत् अन्तः पुर द्वारम् समतीत्य जन आकुलम्
transliteration: sa tat antaḥ pura dvāram samatītya jana ākulam
english: Sumantra, well versed in legends, after passing by the gateways crowded with people, reached the solitary apartment (of Rāma).

sanskrit: प्रास कार्मुक बिभ्रद्भिर् युवभिर् मृष्ट कुण्डलैः
transliteration: prāsa kārmuka bibhradbhir yuvabhir mṛṣṭa kuṇḍalaiḥ
english: Having youthful warders, carrying dares and bows, wearing ear-rings, cautious, attentive and devoted and saw (seated at the gate) several old men commanding female warders, mindful of duty, wearing red cloths and excellent ornaments, and having rattans in their hands.

sanskrit: तत्र काषायिणो वृद्धान् वेत्र पाणीन् स्वलम्कृतान्
ददर्श विष्ठितान् द्वारि स्त्र्य् अध्यक्षान् सुसमाहितान्
transliteration: tatra kāṣāyiṇo vṛddhān vetra pāṇīn svalamkṛtān
dadarśa viṣṭhitān dvāri stry adhyakṣān susamāhitān
english: Having youthful warders, carrying dares and bows, wearing ear-rings, cautious, attentive and devoted and saw (seated at the gate) several old men commanding female warders, mindful of duty, wearing red cloths and excellent ornaments, and having rattans in their hands.

sanskrit: ते समीक्ष्य समायान्तम् राम प्रिय चिकीर्षवः
सह भार्याय रामाय क्षिप्रम् एव आचचक्षिरे
transliteration: te samīkṣya samāyāntam rāma priya cikīrṣavaḥ
saha bhāryāya rāmāya kṣipram eva ācacakṣire
english: They all seeing Sumantra, ever wishing good to Rāma, approach, rose suddenly up from their seats with due respect.

sanskrit: तत्र एव आनाययाम् आस राघवः प्रिय काम्यया
transliteration: tatra eva ānāyayām āsa rāghavaḥ priya kāmyayā
english: Rāma hearing of the arrival of his father's charioteer, ordered him to enter into the apartment, having his father's pleasure in view.

The humble minded charioteer then said to them, Go and speedily communicate to Rāma that Sumantra is waiting at the gate. At this the warders, desirous of doing good to their master, nearing Rāma, speedily communicated these words to him who was in the company of his wife.
Rāma hearing of the arrival of his father's charioteer, ordered him to enter into the apartment, having his father's pleasure in view.

sanskrit: दादर्श सूतः पर्यन्के सौवणो स उत्तरच् चदे
transliteration: dādarśa sūtaḥ paryanke sauvaṇo sa uttarac cade
english: He (on entering) saw Rāma resembling Vaiśravaņa, will adorned and seated on a rolled sofa, with a beautiful coverlet on.

sanskrit: वराह रुधिर आभेण शुचिना च सुगन्धिना
अनुलिप्तम् पर अर्ध्येन चन्दनेन परम् तपम्
transliteration: varāha rudhira ābheṇa śucinā ca sugandhinā
anuliptam para ardhyena candanena param tapam
english: Having his body sprinkled with holy and fragrant sandal of the best kind, red as the blood of a hog; and having by him Sītā with a chowry in her hand, like moon himself in the company of citra.

sanskrit: स्थितया पार्श्वतः च अपि वाल व्यजन हस्तया
उपेतम् सीतया भूयः चित्रया शशिनम् यथा
transliteration: sthitayā pārśvataḥ ca api vāla vyajana hastayā
upetam sītayā bhūyaḥ citrayā śaśinam yathā
english: Having his body sprinkled with holy and fragrant sandal of the best kind, red as the blood of a hog; and having by him Sītā with a chowry in her hand, like moon himself in the company of citra.

sanskrit: तम् तपन्तम् इव आदित्यम् उपपन्नम् स्व तेजसा
transliteration: tam tapantam iva ādityam upapannam sva tejasā
english: Whereupon Sumantra, acquainted with decorum, humbly saluted him (Rāma), the conferrer of great boons, and resplendent like the mid-day sun.

sanskrit: प्रान्जलिस् तु सुखम् पृष्ट्वा विहार शयन आसने
राज पुत्रम् उवाच इदम् सुमन्त्रः राज सत्कृतः
transliteration: prānjalis tu sukham pṛṣṭvā vihāra śayana āsane
rāja putram uvāca idam sumantraḥ rāja satkṛtaḥ
english: And he well honoured by the king, seeing the king's son seated on the sleeping sofa with a delighted countenance, spoke these words to him with clasped hands.

sanskrit: कौसल्या सुप्रभा देव पिता त्वम् द्रष्टुम् इच्चति
महिष्या सह कैकेय्या गम्यताम् तत्र माचिरम्
transliteration: kausalyā suprabhā deva pitā tvam draṣṭum iccati
mahiṣyā saha kaikeyyā gamyatām tatra māciram
english: Oh, Rāma, great son of Kausalyā, your father and the queen Kaikeyi want to see you; so it behove you to go there without delay.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः तु सम्हृष्टः नर सिम्हो महा द्युतिः
ततः सम्मानयाम् आस सीताम् इदम् उवाच ह
transliteration: evam uktaḥ tu samhṛṣṭaḥ nara simho mahā dyutiḥ
tataḥ sammānayām āsa sītām idam uvāca ha
english: Being pleased with these words the mighty hero of great effulgence, honoured his father's behest and spoke to Sītā thus.

sanskrit: देवि देवः च देवी च समागम्य मद् अन्तरे
transliteration: devi devaḥ ca devī ca samāgamya mad antare
english: Oh, darling, doubt there is none that my father, going to Kaikeyi. is parleying with her regarding my installation.

sanskrit: लक्षयित्वा हि अभिप्रायम् प्रिय कामा सुदक्षिणा
सम्चोदयति राजानम् मद् अर्थम् मदिर ईक्षणा
transliteration: lakṣayitvā hi abhiprāyam priya kāmā sudakṣiṇā
samcodayati rājānam mad artham madira īkṣaṇā
english: Conceiving the king's intention that clever lady, of dark eyes and desirous of doing good to the king, that mother, the daughter of the king of Kekaya, pleased and intent upon king's welfare as will as upon that of mine, is hastening the monarch for my installation.

Conceiving the king's intention that clever lady, of dark eyes and desirous of doing good to the king, that mother, the daughter of the king of Kekaya, pleased and intent upon king's welfare as will as upon that of mine, is hastening the monarch for my installation.

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या खलु महाराजो महिष्या प्रियया सह
transliteration: diṣṭyā khalu mahārājo mahiṣyā priyayā saha
english: Fortunately for me, the monarch in the company of his queen has despatched Sumantra, intent upon my welfare.

sanskrit: ध्रुवम् अद्य एव माम् राजा यौवराज्ये अभिषेक्ष्यति
transliteration: dhruvam adya eva mām rājā yauvarājye abhiṣekṣyati
english: Worthy of the meeting at the inner apartment, the messenger has come, and I doubt not that the monarch shall install me to-day as the heirapparent of his throne.

sanskrit: हन्त शीघ्रम् इतः गत्वा द्रक्ष्यामि च मही पतिः
सह त्वम् परिवारेण सुखम् आस्स्व रमस्य च
transliteration: hanta śīghram itaḥ gatvā drakṣyāmi ca mahī patiḥ
saha tvam parivāreṇa sukham āssva ramasya ca
english: Therefore I shall speedily go hence and see my father. Do you remain and enjoy here the company of your friends.

sanskrit: पति सम्मानिता सीता भर्तारम् असित ईक्षणा
transliteration: pati sammānitā sītā bhartāram asita īkṣaṇā
english: Regarded by her husband, Sītā of dark eyes and intent upon her husband's welfare, followed him to the entrance and said.
May the great monarch bestow upon you first the heir-apparentship, and afterwards the dignity of the Paramount power like Brahma granting kingdom to Vāsava.
I shall be ministering to you, seeing you initiated, engaged in ceremonies, wearing excellent deer skin for cloth and carrying horns in the hands.

sanskrit: पूर्वाम् दिशम् वज्रधरो दक्षिणाम् पातु ते यमः
transliteration: pūrvām diśam vajradharo dakṣiṇām pātu te yamaḥ
english: May Indra protect you on the East, may Yama (Death) protect you on the South and Varuņa (god of water) on the West and Kuvera (God of wealth) on the North.

Being greeted with benedictory ceremonies, Rāma, bidding farewell to Sītā, issued out of his house like to a lion, living in the den of a mountain. He saw Lakşmaņa standing at the gate with clasped hands.

Being greeted with benedictory ceremonies, Rāma, bidding farewell to Sītā, issued out of his house like to a lion, living in the den of a mountain. He saw Lakşmaņa standing at the gate with clasped hands.

sanskrit: स सर्वान् अर्थिनो दृष्ट्वा समेत्य प्रतिनन्द्य च
transliteration: sa sarvān arthino dṛṣṭvā sametya pratinandya ca
english: And met all his friends assembled at the middle apartment. Then that great son of the king, casting a glance upon them all who were present there to see him and pleasing them with sweet words ascended, like to the thousand-eyed Indra.

sanskrit: ततः पावक सम्काशम् आरुरोह रथ उत्तमम्
transliteration: tataḥ pāvaka samkāśam āruroha ratha uttamam

sanskrit: मुष्णन्तम् इव चक्षूम्षि प्रभया हेम वर्चसम्
transliteration: muṣṇantam iva cakṣūmṣi prabhayā hema varcasam
english: The splendid chariot, made of silver and coated with tiger-skin, and bright like the fire itself, making a noise (when going) like the roaring of clouds. defying all obstacles, adorned with jewels, and gold, dazzling the eye-sight and bright like the golden peaks of Sumeru.

sanskrit: करेणु शिशु कल्पैः च युक्तम् परम वाजिभिः
हरि युक्तम् सहस्र अक्षो रथम् इन्द्रैव आशुगम्
transliteration: kareṇu śiśu kalpaiḥ ca yuktam parama vājibhiḥ
hari yuktam sahasra akṣo ratham indraiva āśugam
english: It had two excellent horses tied to it like to two young elephants, and was of quick motion, resembling that of Indra's chariot carried by his horses.

sanskrit: प्रययौ तूर्णम् आस्थाय राघवो ज्वलितः श्रिया
transliteration: prayayau tūrṇam āsthāya rāghavo jvalitaḥ śriyā
english: Ascending the car, Raghava, of great effulgence, went speedily on, making (the space) resounded like to the muttering cloud on the sky. He issued out of his abode like the beautiful moon passing through a huge cloud.

sanskrit: निकेतान् निर्ययौ श्रीमान् महा अभ्रात् इव चन्द्रमाः
चत्र चामर पाणिस् तु लक्ष्मणो राघव अनुजः
transliteration: niketān niryayau śrīmān mahā abhrāt iva candramāḥ
catra cāmara pāṇis tu lakṣmaṇo rāghava anujaḥ
english: Lakşmaņa, the younger brother of Rāghava, standing behind him on the car with a splendid Chowry in his hand, began to guard his body.

sanskrit: जुगोप भ्रातरम् भ्राता रथम् आस्थाय पृष्ठतः
ततः हल हला शब्दः तुमुलः समजायत
transliteration: jugopa bhrātaram bhrātā ratham āsthāya pṛṣṭhataḥ
tataḥ hala halā śabdaḥ tumulaḥ samajāyata

english: Then followed in his train many hundreds and thousands of beautiful horses and elephants resembling hills in their appearance; and went before him hundreds of heroes, well accoutred, and having their bodies sprinkled with sandal and Agaru and holding swords and arms in their hands, and other persons uttering benedictions.

sanskrit: नूनम् नन्धिति ते माता कौसल्या मातृनन्दन
transliteration: nūnam nandhiti te mātā kausalyā mātṛnandana

sanskrit: अमन्यन्त हि ता नार्यो रामस्य हृदयप्रियाम्
तया सुचरितम् देव्या पुरा नूनम् महत्तपः
transliteration: amanyanta hi tā nāryo rāmasya hṛdayapriyām
tayā sucaritam devyā purā nūnam mahattapaḥ
english: Those ladies thought that Sītā, the captivater of Rāma's heart was surely the best of all women and for certain had she performed some great austerities in her past life or else she would not have been the companion of Răma, like to Rohini, the companion of Moon.
Rāghava then heard the people coming from different quarters and the well-pleased citizens, talking amongst themselves regarding him in the following strain.
This Rāghava going shall obtain through the grace of the king great wealth, and all our desires will be gratified when he will become our governor.

sanskrit: लाभो जनस्य अस्य यद् एष सर्वम्
transliteration: lābho janasya asya yad eṣa sarvam

english: Like to Vaisravana he began to proceed, being dignified by the horses and elephants going before sending forth great sound, and eulogised in various metres by persons singing his glory, by the panegyrists and by men tracing his noble ancestry.
He saw the courtyard thronged with young and old elephants, horses, chariots, and the high ways crowded all over with people, many pearls and various merchandises.

sanskrit: स रामः रथम् आस्थाय सम्प्रह्Rष्ट सुह्Rज् जनः
transliteration: sa rāmaḥ ratham āsthāya samprahṣṭa suhj janaḥ
english: Rāma, having his friends delighted, ascending the car, and viewing the city adorned with pennons and flags and incensed with Dhūpa and Agaru, entered the high way, crowded with people and containing houses coloured as the pale white clouds, and the place between the two rows whereof scented with Dhūpa and Agaru.

sanskrit: अपश्यन् नगरम् श्रीमान् नाना जन समाकुलम्
स ग्Rहैः अभ्र सम्काशैः पाण्डुरैः उपशोभितम्
transliteration: apaśyan nagaram śrīmān nānā jana samākulam
sa ghaiḥ abhra samkāśaiḥ pāṇḍuraiḥ upaśobhitam

sanskrit: राज मार्गम् ययौ रामः मध्येन अगरु धूपितम्
transliteration: rāja mārgam yayau rāmaḥ madhyena agaru dhūpitam

sanskrit: शोभमानम् असम्बाधम् तम् राज पथम् उत्तमम्
सम्व्Rतम् विविधैः पण्यैः भक्ष्यैः उच्च अवचैः अपि
transliteration: śobhamānam asambādham tam rāja patham uttamam
samvtam vividhaiḥ paṇyaiḥ bhakṣyaiḥ ucca avacaiḥ api

sanskrit: ददर्श तं राजपथं दिवि देवपथम् यथा
transliteration: dadarśa taṃ rājapathaṃ divi devapatham yathā

sanskrit: आशीर् वादान् बहून् श्Rण्वन् सुह्Rद्भिः समुदीरितान्
transliteration: āśīr vādān bahūn śṇvan suhdbhiḥ samudīritān
english: Having heard benedictions uttered by many in the following strain and paying proper respects to all, he wended his way.

sanskrit: यथा अर्हम् च अपि सम्पूज्य सर्वान् एव नरान् ययौ
transliteration: yathā arham ca api sampūjya sarvān eva narān yayau

sanskrit: अद्य उपादाय तम् मार्गम् अभिषिक्तः अनुपालय
यथा स्म लालिताः पित्रा यथा पूर्वैः पितामहैः
transliteration: adya upādāya tam mārgam abhiṣiktaḥ anupālaya
yathā sma lālitāḥ pitrā yathā pūrvaiḥ pitāmahaiḥ

sanskrit: ततः सुखतरम् सर्वे रामे वत्स्याम राजनि
अलमद्य हि भुक्तेन परम अर्थैः अलम् च नः
transliteration: tataḥ sukhataram sarve rāme vatsyāma rājani
alamadya hi bhuktena parama arthaiḥ alam ca naḥ

sanskrit: यथा पश्याम निर्यान्तम् रामम् राज्ये प्रतिष्ठितम्
ततः हि न प्रियतरम् न अन्यत् किम्चित् भविष्यति
transliteration: yathā paśyāma niryāntam rāmam rājye pratiṣṭhitam
tataḥ hi na priyataram na anyat kimcit bhaviṣyati
english: Seek not we earthly comforts or the highest things (in the life to come), if we can only see. Rāma installed in the kingdom issuing out from his father's abode. There is nothing more pleasant to us than the installation of the highly energetic Rāma on the throne.

sanskrit: यथा अभिषेको रामस्य राज्येन अमित तेजसः
एताः च अन्याः च सुह्Rदाम् उदासीनः कथाः शुभाः
transliteration: yathā abhiṣeko rāmasya rājyena amita tejasaḥ
etāḥ ca anyāḥ ca suhdām udāsīnaḥ kathāḥ śubhāḥ

sanskrit: आत्म सम्पूजनीः श्Rण्वन् ययौ रामः महा पथम्
न हि तस्मान् मनः कश्चिच् चक्षुषी वा नर उत्तमात्
transliteration: ātma sampūjanīḥ śṇvan yayau rāmaḥ mahā patham
na hi tasmān manaḥ kaścic cakṣuṣī vā nara uttamāt

sanskrit: नरः शक्नोति अपाक्रष्टुम् अतिक्रान्ते अपि राघवे
यश्च रामं न पश्येत्तु यं च रामो न पश्यति
transliteration: naraḥ śaknoti apākraṣṭum atikrānte api rāghave
yaśca rāmaṃ na paśyettu yaṃ ca rāmo na paśyati

sanskrit: सर्वेषाम् स हि धर्म आत्मा वर्णानाम् कुरुते दयाम्
transliteration: sarveṣām sa hi dharma ātmā varṇānām kurute dayām

sanskrit: चतुर्णाम् हि वयह्स्थानाम् तेन ते तम् अनुव्रताः
transliteration: caturṇām hi vayahsthānām tena te tam anuvratāḥ

sanskrit: स राज कुलम् आसाद्य महा इन्द्र भवन उपमम्
transliteration: sa rāja kulam āsādya mahā indra bhavana upamam

english: He proceeded leaving on his left side the junctions of four roads, the path leading to temples, the religious fig trees and altars, and reached after all the family dwelling of the king, with its palatial tops piercing the sky, looking beautiful, resembling mass of clouds, white as the celestial cars and high as the hill Kailāsa, and with sporting houses sporting with pearls. And the son of the monarch, shining in beauty, entered into the palace of his father, the best on earth resembling the abode of Mahendra.

sanskrit: राज पुत्रः पितुर् वेश्म प्रविवेश श्रिया ज्वलन्
transliteration: rāja putraḥ pitur veśma praviveśa śriyā jvalan
english: Dasaratha's son, the best of men, crossed in his chariot three apartments guarded by warriors with bows in their hands, and other two of foot.

sanskrit: स सर्वाः समतिक्रम्य कक्ष्या दशरथ आत्मजः
transliteration: sa sarvāḥ samatikramya kakṣyā daśaratha ātmajaḥ

sanskrit: सम्निवर्त्य जनम् सर्वम् शुद्ध अन्तः पुरम् अभ्यगात्
जनः स सर्वो मुदितः न्Rप आत्मजे
transliteration: samnivartya janam sarvam śuddha antaḥ puram abhyagāt
janaḥ sa sarvo muditaḥ npa ātmaje
english: That son of the king entering into the presence of his father, all were extremely gladdened and were eagerly expecting his return like to the lord of water expecting the appearance of the moon.

sanskrit: स ददर्श आसने रामः निषण्णम् पितरम् शुभे
transliteration: sa dadarśa āsane rāmaḥ niṣaṇṇam pitaram śubhe
english: Rāma saw his father, seated on a beautiful sofa with Kaikeyi, looking sorry and poorly and with his countenance dried up.

sanskrit: स पितुः चरणौ पूर्वम् अभिवाद्य विनीतवत्
transliteration: sa pituḥ caraṇau pūrvam abhivādya vinītavat
english: And humbly bowing down at the feet of his father first, he saluted Kaikeyi with due solemnity.

sanskrit: राम इति उक्त्वा च वचनम् वाष्प पर्याकुल ईक्षणः
शशाक न्Rपतिर् दीनो न ईक्षितुम् न अभिभाषितुम्
transliteration: rāma iti uktvā ca vacanam vāṣpa paryākula īkṣaṇaḥ
śaśāka npatir dīno na īkṣitum na abhibhāṣitum
english: Uttering the word "Rāma" only, the poor king with his eyes full of tears could not see him nor could he speak to him.

sanskrit: तत् अपूर्वम् नर पतेर् द्Rष्ट्वा रूपम् भय आवहम्
रामः अपि भयम् आपन्नः पदा स्प्Rष्ट्वा इव पन्नगम्
transliteration: tat apūrvam nara pater dṣṭvā rūpam bhaya āvaham
rāmaḥ api bhayam āpannaḥ padā spṣṭvā iva pannagam
english: Seeing this unforeseen and terrible appearance of the king, like to a serpent trampled under foot, Rāma was exceedingly terrified.

sanskrit: इन्द्रियैः अप्रह्Rष्टैअः तम् शोक सम्ताप कर्शितम्
निह्श्वसन्तम् महा राजम् व्यथित आकुल चेतसम्
transliteration: indriyaiḥ aprahṣṭaiaḥ tam śoka samtāpa karśitam
nihśvasantam mahā rājam vyathita ākula cetasam
english: He was dejected and pulled down much with sorrow and penitence. He was sighing hot and hard and his heart was greatly pained. His heart was troubled like the wavy ocean agitating though incapable of agitation, and clouded like the Sun possessed by Rahu, and (that of) an ascetic speaking falsehood.

sanskrit: ऊर्मि मालिनम् अक्षोभ्यम् क्षुभ्यन्तम् इव सागरम्
उपप्लुतम् इव आदित्यम् उक्त अन्Rतम् Rषिम् यथा
transliteration: ūrmi mālinam akṣobhyam kṣubhyantam iva sāgaram
upaplutam iva ādityam ukta antam ṣim yathā
english: He was dejected and pulled down much with sorrow and penitence. He was sighing hot and hard and his heart was greatly pained. His heart was troubled like the wavy ocean agitating though incapable of agitation, and clouded like the Sun possessed by Rahu, and (that of) an ascetic speaking falsehood.

sanskrit: अचिन्त्य कल्पम् हि पितुस् तम् शोकम् उपधारयन्
transliteration: acintya kalpam hi pitus tam śokam upadhārayan
english: Thinking of this unthought of sorrow of the king he became agitated like to the ocean during the course of the full-moon.

sanskrit: चिन्तयाम् आस च तदा रामः पित्R हिते रतः
किम्स्विद् अद्य एव न्Rपतिर् न माम् प्रत्यभिनन्दति
transliteration: cintayām āsa ca tadā rāmaḥ pit hite rataḥ
kimsvid adya eva npatir na mām pratyabhinandati
english: And clever Rāma, intent on his father's welfare, thought within himself:, Why does not the king display joy on my arrival to-day.

sanskrit: अन्यदा माम् पिता द्Rष्ट्वा कुपितः अपि प्रसीदति
तस्य माम् अद्य सम्प्रेक्ष्य किम् आयासः प्रवर्तते
transliteration: anyadā mām pitā dṣṭvā kupitaḥ api prasīdati
tasya mām adya samprekṣya kim āyāsaḥ pravartate
english: Angry though, he used to express joy whenever he saw me; then why does his sorrow prevail even seeing me to-day?

sanskrit: स दीनैव शोक आर्तः विषण्ण वदन द्युतिः
कैकेयीम् अभिवाद्य एव रामः वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sa dīnaiva śoka ārtaḥ viṣaṇṇa vadana dyutiḥ
kaikeyīm abhivādya eva rāmaḥ vacanam abravīt
english: Being pressed with sorrow, Rāma of pale countenance, like one miserable, saluting KaikeyI, spoke to her the following words.

sanskrit: कच्चिन् मया न अपराधम् अज्ञानात् येन मे पिता
कुपितः तन् मम आचक्ष्व त्वम् चैव एनम् प्रसादय
transliteration: kaccin mayā na aparādham ajñānāt yena me pitā
kupitaḥ tan mama ācakṣva tvam caiva enam prasādaya
english: Is it not that I committed some offence through ignorance that I see my father angry? Do you propitiate him therefore.

sanskrit: अप्रसन्नमनाः किम् नु सदा मां प्रति वत्सलः
विवर्ण वदनो दीनो न हि माम् अभिभाषते
transliteration: aprasannamanāḥ kim nu sadā māṃ prati vatsalaḥ
vivarṇa vadano dīno na hi mām abhibhāṣate
english: Why is his mind so aggrieved who was so kind to me, and why does he look poorly and of pale countenance who used to welcome me always with kind words?

sanskrit: शारीरः मानसो वा अपि कच्चित् एनम् न बाधते
सम्तापो वा अभितापो वा दुर्लभम् हि सदा सुखम्
transliteration: śārīraḥ mānaso vā api kaccit enam na bādhate
samtāpo vā abhitāpo vā durlabham hi sadā sukham
english: Is he subject to any physical or mental disturbance? Oh! happiness uninterrupted is very dear.

sanskrit: कच्चिन् न किम्चित् भरते कुमारे प्रिय दर्शने
शत्रुघ्ने वा महा सत्त्वे मात्RRणाम् वा मम अशुभम्
transliteration: kaccin na kimcit bharate kumāre priya darśane
śatrughne vā mahā sattve mātṇām vā mama aśubham
english: Has any evil befallen the good-looking Bharata or high-souled Śatrughna? Is it not all well with my mothers.

sanskrit: अतोषयन् महा राजम् अकुर्वन् वा पितुर् वचः
मुहूर्तम् अपि न इच्चेयम् जीवितुम् कुपिते न्Rपे
transliteration: atoṣayan mahā rājam akurvan vā pitur vacaḥ
muhūrtam api na icceyam jīvitum kupite npe
english: Dissatisfying the king, disregarding his words and offending him, I do not want to breathe for a single moment.

sanskrit: यतः मूलम् नरः पश्येत् प्रादुर्भावम् इह आत्मनः
कथम् तस्मिन् न वर्तेत प्रत्यक्षे सति दैवते
transliteration: yataḥ mūlam naraḥ paśyet prādurbhāvam iha ātmanaḥ
katham tasmin na varteta pratyakṣe sati daivate
english: How can a man disregard him who is god himself seen and felt, and who is looked upon as a cause from whom he has sprung.

sanskrit: कच्चित् ते परुषम् किम्चित् अभिमानात् पिता मम
उक्तः भवत्या कोपेन यत्र अस्य लुलितम् मनः
transliteration: kaccit te paruṣam kimcit abhimānāt pitā mama
uktaḥ bhavatyā kopena yatra asya lulitam manaḥ
english: Oh mother, have you spoken any harsh word to my father either through anger or through haughtiness for which his mind is thus pulled down?

sanskrit: एतत् आचक्ष्व मे देवि तत्त्वेन परिप्Rच्चतः
किम् निमित्तम् अपूर्वो अयम् विकारः मनुज अधिपे
transliteration: etat ācakṣva me devi tattvena paripccataḥ
kim nimittam apūrvo ayam vikāraḥ manuja adhipe
english: Oh worshipful one, tell me all this, who am exceedingly anxious to get at the real truth. Why has this unforeseen sorrow overtaken the heart of the lord of men?
Being thus addressed by the high-souled Rāghava, that exceedingly shameless Kaikeyī spoke to him the following impudent words, fraught with her self-interest.

sanskrit: न राजा कुपितो राम व्यसनम् नास्य किम्चन
transliteration: na rājā kupito rāma vyasanam nāsya kimcana
english: Oh Rāma, the monarch is not angry nor has any danger befallen him. He has got something in his mind which he cannot speak out through your fear.
You are his most beloved son and word does not proceed from his mouth to speak you things unpleasant. But it behoves you to carry out what the monarch has promised to me.

sanskrit: एष मह्यम् वरम् दत्त्वा पुरा मामभिपूज्य च
transliteration: eṣa mahyam varam dattvā purā māmabhipūjya ca
english: Formerly regarding me very highly he conferred on me two boons and he now repents for that like a common person.
Promising 'I give you the lord of earth granted me these boons; in vain he wishes to set up a dyke when all the water has passed away.

Oh Rāma, it is known to you that truth is the root of all religion and may he not renounce that for you, being angry with me. If do you carry out all that the king will speak to you, good or evil, then I shall relate to you every thing.

sanskrit: यदि तद्वक्ष्यते राजा शुभम् वा यदि वाऽशुभम्
transliteration: yadi tadvakṣyate rājā śubham vā yadi vā'śubham
english: Oh Rāma, it is known to you that truth is the root of all religion and may he not renounce that for you, being angry with me. If do you carry out all that the king will speak to you, good or evil, then I shall relate to you every thing.

sanskrit: यदि त्वभिहितं राज्ञा त्वयि तन्न विपत्स्यते
transliteration: yadi tvabhihitaṃ rājñā tvayi tanna vipatsyate
english: If what I, with the king's permission, speak to you, does not go useless, I shall speak to you all; the king will not speak any thing.
Hearing these words uttered by Kaikeyī, Rāma, pained at heart, spoke to her in the presence of the king in the following way:

sanskrit: अहो धिङ्नार्हसे देवि पक्तुं मामीदृशं वचः
अहम् हि वचनात् राज्ञः पतेयम् अपि पावके
transliteration: aho dhiṅnārhase devi paktuṃ māmīdṛśaṃ vacaḥ
aham hi vacanāt rājñaḥ pateyam api pāvake

sanskrit: भक्षयेयम् विषम् तीक्ष्णम् मज्जेयम् अपि च अर्णवे
नियुक्तः गुरुणा पित्रा न्Rपेण च हितेन च
transliteration: bhakṣayeyam viṣam tīkṣṇam majjeyam api ca arṇave
niyuktaḥ guruṇā pitrā npeṇa ca hitena ca

sanskrit: तत् ब्रूहि वचनम् देवि राज्ञो यद् अभिकान्क्षितम्
करिष्ये प्रतिजाने च रामः द्विर् न अभिभाषते
transliteration: tat brūhi vacanam devi rājño yad abhikānkṣitam
kariṣye pratijāne ca rāmaḥ dvir na abhibhāṣate

sanskrit: तम् आर्जव समायुक्तम् अनार्या सत्य वादिनम्
उवाच रामम् कैकेयी वचनम् भ्Rश दारुणम्
transliteration: tam ārjava samāyuktam anāryā satya vādinam
uvāca rāmam kaikeyī vacanam bhśa dāruṇam
english: Then that wicked Kaikeyi spoke these highly cruel words to Rāma, simple and truthful.

sanskrit: पुरा देव असुरे युद्धे पित्रा ते मम राघव
रक्षितेन वरौ दत्तौ सशल्येन महा रणे
transliteration: purā deva asure yuddhe pitrā te mama rāghava
rakṣitena varau dattau saśalyena mahā raṇe
english: Foremerly in a great war between the gods and Asuras, your father, being wounded with shafts was tended by me for which he conferred upon me two boons.

sanskrit: तत्र मे याचितः राजा भरतस्य अभिषेचनम्
गमनम् दण्डक अरण्ये तव च अद्य एव राघव
transliteration: tatra me yācitaḥ rājā bharatasya abhiṣecanam
gamanam daṇḍaka araṇye tava ca adya eva rāghava
english: Of these two boons I have asked of the king the installation of Bharata, and the departure of Rāghava into the Dandaka forest even this very day.

sanskrit: यदि सत्य प्रतिज्ञम् त्वम् पितरम् कर्तुम् इच्चसि
आत्मानम् च नर रेष्ठ मम वाक्यम् इदम् श्Rणु
