transliteration: yadi satya pratijñam tvam pitaram kartum iccasi
ātmānam ca nara reṣṭha mama vākyam idam śṇu
english: Oh you best among men, if do you wish to keep your father's vows as well as yours, hear what I say.

sanskrit: स निदेशे पितुस् तिष्ठ यथा तेन प्रतिश्रुतम्
त्वया अरण्यम् प्रवेष्टव्यम् नव वर्षाणि पन्च च
transliteration: sa nideśe pitus tiṣṭha yathā tena pratiśrutam
tvayā araṇyam praveṣṭavyam nava varṣāṇi panca ca
english: Your father is bound to me by promise, obeying therefore your father's mandate, do you repair to the forest for nine years and five.

sanskrit: त्वदर्थे विहितम् राज्ञा तेन सर्वेण राघव
transliteration: tvadarthe vihitam rājñā tena sarveṇa rāghava
english: Bharata shall be installed, Ch Rāghava, by all those articles which have been brought by the monarch for your installation.

sanskrit: सप्त सप्त च वर्षाणि दण्डक अरण्यम् आश्रितः
अभिषेकम् इमम् त्यक्त्वा जटा चीर धरः वस
transliteration: sapta sapta ca varṣāṇi daṇḍaka araṇyam āśritaḥ
abhiṣekam imam tyaktvā jaṭā cīra dharaḥ vasa
english: Forsaking this installation, do you repair to Dandaka forest for seven and seven years and wear bark and matted hair.

sanskrit: भरतः कोसल पुरे प्रशास्तु वसुधाम् इमाम्
नाना रत्न समाकीर्णम् सवाजि रथ कुन्जराम्
transliteration: bharataḥ kosala pure praśāstu vasudhām imām
nānā ratna samākīrṇam savāji ratha kunjarām
english: And here in this Kosala let Bharata govern the world, adorned with many pearls and diamonds, with elephants, horses and chariots.
The king, filled with pity and having his face marked with the affliction of sorrow, cannot cast a glance upon you.
Oh you descendant of Raghu, do you carry out these words of the Lord of men and save him by redeeming these great vows of his.

sanskrit: तत् अप्रियम् अमित्रघ्नः वचनम् मरण उपमम्
श्रुत्वा न विव्यथे रामः कैकेयीम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tat apriyam amitraghnaḥ vacanam maraṇa upamam
śrutvā na vivyathe rāmaḥ kaikeyīm ca idam abravīt
english: Hearing these unpleasant words like to death, Rama, the destroyer of foes, was not pained, and spoke thus to Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: एवम् अस्तु गमिष्यामि वनम् वस्तुम् अहम् तु अतः
जटा चीर धरः राज्ञः प्रतिज्ञाम् अनुपालयन्
transliteration: evam astu gamiṣyāmi vanam vastum aham tu ataḥ
jaṭā cīra dharaḥ rājñaḥ pratijñām anupālayan
english: Be it what you say; carrying out the promise of the king, I shall repair to the forest from this place wearing bark and matted hair.

sanskrit: इदम् तु ज्ञातुम् इच्चामि किम् अर्थम् माम् मही पतिः
न अभिनन्दति दुर्धर्षो यथा पुरम् अरिम् दमः
transliteration: idam tu jñātum iccāmi kim artham mām mahī patiḥ
na abhinandati durdharṣo yathā puram arim damaḥ
english: Now I want to know only why that lord of the earth, invincible and the conqueror of foes, does not receive me in the same way as he used to do on previous occasions.

sanskrit: मन्युर् न च त्वया कार्यो देवि ब्रूहि तव अग्रतः
यास्यामि भव सुप्रीता वनम् चीर जटा धरः
transliteration: manyur na ca tvayā kāryo devi brūhi tava agrataḥ
yāsyāmi bhava suprītā vanam cīra jaṭā dharaḥ
english: be not angry, Oh worshipful one, I speak before you, be you propitiated well, and I shall go to the forest wearing bark and matted hair.

sanskrit: हितेन गुरुणा पित्रा क्Rतज्ञेन न्Rपेण च
नियुज्यमानो विश्रब्धम् किम् न कुर्यात् अहम् प्रियम्
transliteration: hitena guruṇā pitrā ktajñena npeṇa ca
niyujyamāno viśrabdham kim na kuryāt aham priyam
english: What is there that I cannot perform, considering it good without suspicion, if I am ordered so by my well-wisher, spiritual leader, father and king, who acknowledges your service (rendered in time of danger).* *The epithet Krtajñena may as well as be rendered into general terms; such as 'who acknowledges services rendered to him.' Here in translation I have followed the commentator who has restricted it to the special sense suitable to the occasion.

sanskrit: अलीकम् मानसम् तु एकम् ह्Rदयम् दहति इव मे
स्वयम् यन् न आह माम् राजा भरतस्य अभिषेचनम्
transliteration: alīkam mānasam tu ekam hdayam dahati iva me
svayam yan na āha mām rājā bharatasya abhiṣecanam
english: But this one sorrow burns my heart, why king did not tell me personally of the installation of Bharata.

sanskrit: अहम् हि सीताम् राज्यम् च प्राणान् इष्टान् धनानि च
ह्Rष्टः भ्रात्रे स्वयम् दद्याम् भरताय अप्रचोदितः
transliteration: aham hi sītām rājyam ca prāṇān iṣṭān dhanāni ca
hṣṭaḥ bhrātre svayam dadyām bharatāya apracoditaḥ
english: What of the command of the king, my father, I shall even at your mandate joyfully make over to Bharata, my kingdom, Sītā, wealth and even my life, thereby satisfying you, and fulfilling my promise.

sanskrit: किम् पुनर् मनुज इन्द्रेण स्वयम् पित्रा प्रचोदितः
तव च प्रिय काम अर्थम् प्रतिज्ञाम् अनुपालयन्
transliteration: kim punar manuja indreṇa svayam pitrā pracoditaḥ
tava ca priya kāma artham pratijñām anupālayan
english: What of the command of the king, my father, I shall even at your mandate joyfully make over to Bharata, my kingdom, Sītā, wealth and even my life, thereby satisfying you, and fulfilling my promise.

sanskrit: तत् आश्वासय हि इमम् त्वम् किम् न्व् इदम् यन् मही पतिः
वसुधा आसक्त नयनो मन्दम् अश्रूणि मुन्चति
transliteration: tat āśvāsaya hi imam tvam kim nv idam yan mahī patiḥ
vasudhā āsakta nayano mandam aśrūṇi muncati
english: Do you now console the bashful king; why has he, with his eyes steadily fixed on the ground, been shedding tears slowly?

sanskrit: गच्चन्तु च एव आनयितुम् दूताः शीघ्र जवैः हयैः
भरतम् मातुल कुलात् अद्य एव न्Rप शासनात्
transliteration: gaccantu ca eva ānayitum dūtāḥ śīghra javaiḥ hayaiḥ
bharatam mātula kulāt adya eva npa śāsanāt
english: Let messengers, with fast going steeds go today at the command of the king to fetch Bharata from his maternal uncle's house.

sanskrit: दण्डक अरण्यम् एषो अहम् इतः गच्चामि सत्वरः
अविचार्य पितुर् वाक्यम् समावस्तुम् चतुर् दश
transliteration: daṇḍaka araṇyam eṣo aham itaḥ gaccāmi satvaraḥ
avicārya pitur vākyam samāvastum catur daśa
english: I shall, not even judging the propriety of my father's words, speedily repair to the forest of Dandaka for fourteen years.

sanskrit: सा ह्Rष्टा तस्य तत् वाक्यम् श्रुत्वा रामस्य कैकयी
प्रस्थानम् श्रद्दधाना हि त्वरयाम् आस राघवम्
transliteration: sā hṣṭā tasya tat vākyam śrutvā rāmasya kaikayī
prasthānam śraddadhānā hi tvarayām āsa rāghavam
english: Hearing those words of Rāma, Kaikeyi was pleased, and being certain about his departure, hurried on Raghava.

sanskrit: एवम् भवतु यास्यन्ति दूताः शीघ्र जवैः हयैः
transliteration: evam bhavatu yāsyanti dūtāḥ śīghra javaiḥ hayaiḥ
english: Let it be that messengers with fast going steeds shall go to bring Bharata from his maternal uncle's residence.

sanskrit: तव तु अहम् क्षमम् मन्ये न उत्सुकस्य विलम्बनम्
राम तस्मात् इतः शीघ्रम् वनम् त्वम् गन्तुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: tava tu aham kṣamam manye na utsukasya vilambanam
rāma tasmāt itaḥ śīghram vanam tvam gantum arhasi
english: I do not think it proper for you, O Rāma, to delay, when you are so anxious; it behoves you therefore to depart from this place speedily to the forest.

sanskrit: व्रीडा अन्वितः स्वयम् यच् च न्Rपः त्वाम् न अभिभाषते
न एतत् किम्चिन् नर श्रेष्ठ मन्युर् एषो अपनीयताम्
transliteration: vrīḍā anvitaḥ svayam yac ca npaḥ tvām na abhibhāṣate
na etat kimcin nara śreṣṭha manyur eṣo apanīyatām
english: The king being abashed, does not himself address you, there is nothing else than this. Do you, Oh best of men, dispel this wretchedness of his.

sanskrit: यावत् त्वम् न वनम् यातः पुरात् अस्मात् अभित्वरन्
पिता तावन् न ते राम स्नास्यते भोक्ष्यते अपि वा
transliteration: yāvat tvam na vanam yātaḥ purāt asmāt abhitvaran
pitā tāvan na te rāma snāsyate bhokṣyate api vā
english: As long as you shall not hurriedly depart from his presence, Oh Rāma, your father shall not bathe, or eat anything.

sanskrit: धिक् कष्टम् इति निह्श्वस्य राजा शोक परिप्लुतः
मूर्चितः न्यपतत् तस्मिन् पर्यन्के हेम भूषिते
transliteration: dhik kaṣṭam iti nihśvasya rājā śoka pariplutaḥ
mūrcitaḥ nyapatat tasmin paryanke hema bhūṣite
english: 'Oh fie!' 'what affliction' sobbing hard with these words, the monarch, filled with sorrow, swooned away and fell down upon the sofa, embellished with gold.

sanskrit: रामः अपि उत्थाप्य राजानम् कैकेय्या अभिप्रचोदितः
कशया इव आहतः वाजी वनम् गन्तुम् क्Rत त्वरः
transliteration: rāmaḥ api utthāpya rājānam kaikeyyā abhipracoditaḥ
kaśayā iva āhataḥ vājī vanam gantum kta tvaraḥ
english: Raising the king up, Rāma, being directed by Kaikeyī, began to hurry on his departure to the forest, like to a steed struck sharp with a whip.

sanskrit: तत् अप्रियम् अनार्याया वचनम् दारुण उदरम्
श्रुत्वा गत व्यथो रामः कैकेयीम् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tat apriyam anāryāyā vacanam dāruṇa udaram
śrutvā gata vyatho rāmaḥ kaikeyīm vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing those cruel and unpleasant words of the wicked Kaikeyi, Rama, not being distressed, began to address her with the following words.

sanskrit: न अहम् अर्थ परः देवि लोकम् आवस्तुम् उत्सहे
विद्धि माम् Rषिभिस् तुल्यम् केवलम् धर्मम् आस्थितम्
transliteration: na aham artha paraḥ devi lokam āvastum utsahe
viddhi mām ṣibhis tulyam kevalam dharmam āsthitam
english: Oh worshipful one, being addicted to wealth do I not long for living in this world; like to Rșis, know me, to be well established in pure religion.

sanskrit: यद् अत्रभवतः किम्चित् शक्यम् कर्तुम् प्रियम् मया
प्राणान् अपि परित्यज्य सर्वथा क्Rतम् एव तत्
transliteration: yad atrabhavataḥ kimcit śakyam kartum priyam mayā
prāṇān api parityajya sarvathā ktam eva tat
english: If I can, even at the sacrifice of my own life, satisfy my worshipful father, rest assured it is to be done first in all manner.

sanskrit: न हि अतः धर्म चरणम् किम्चित् अस्ति महत्तरम्
यथा पितरि शुश्रूषा तस्य वा वचन क्रिया
transliteration: na hi ataḥ dharma caraṇam kimcit asti mahattaram
yathā pitari śuśrūṣā tasya vā vacana kriyā
english: There is no virtue greater than the serving of the father and carrying out his words.

sanskrit: अनुक्तः अपि अत्रभवता भवत्या वचनात् अहम्
वने वत्स्यामि विजने वर्षाणि इह चतुर् दश
transliteration: anuktaḥ api atrabhavatā bhavatyā vacanāt aham
vane vatsyāmi vijane varṣāṇi iha catur daśa
english: Even though not commanded by him, I shall, for your words, live in a solitary forest for fourteen years.

sanskrit: न नूनम् मयि कैकेयि किम्चित् आशम्ससे गुणम्
यद् राजानम् अवोचः त्वम् मम ईश्वरतरा सती
transliteration: na nūnam mayi kaikeyi kimcit āśamsase guṇam
yad rājānam avocaḥ tvam mama īśvaratarā satī
english: Oh Kaikeyī, certain it is that you are not acquainted with my foremost virtues, inasmuch as possessing full authority to rule me, you have requested the monarch for this.

sanskrit: यावन् मातरम् आप्Rच्चे सीताम् च अनुनयाम्य् अहम्
ततः अद्य एव गमिष्यामि दण्डकानाम् महद् वनम्
transliteration: yāvan mātaram āpcce sītām ca anunayāmy aham
tataḥ adya eva gamiṣyāmi daṇḍakānām mahad vanam
english: Excuse me until I ask my mother, and comfort Sītā; even this very day shall I wend my way to the great forest of Dandaka.

sanskrit: भरतः पालयेद् राज्यम् शुश्रूषेच् च पितुर् यथा
तहा भवत्या कर्तव्यम् स हि धर्मः सनातनः
transliteration: bharataḥ pālayed rājyam śuśrūṣec ca pitur yathā
tahā bhavatyā kartavyam sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: If behoves you to do that by which Bharata may govern the kingdom and tend our father, for this is the virtue eternal.

sanskrit: स रामस्य वचः श्रुत्वा भ्Rशम् दुह्ख हतः पिता
शोकात् अशक्नुवन् बाष्पम् प्ररुरोद महा स्वनम्
transliteration: sa rāmasya vacaḥ śrutvā bhśam duhkha hataḥ pitā
śokāt aśaknuvan bāṣpam praruroda mahā svanam
english: Hearing these words of Rāma, his father, greatly afflicted and incapable of speaking anything on account of sorrow, began to cry aloud.

sanskrit: वन्दित्वा चरणौ रामः विसम्ज्ञस्य पितुस् तदा
कैकेय्याः च अपि अनार्याया निष्पपात महा द्युतिः
transliteration: vanditvā caraṇau rāmaḥ visamjñasya pitus tadā
kaikeyyāḥ ca api anāryāyā niṣpapāta mahā dyutiḥ
english: Worshipping the feet of the king lying insensible, and those of vicious Kaikeyi, that greatly effulgent one went out.

sanskrit: स रामः पितरम् क्Rत्वा कैकेयीम् च प्रदक्षिणम्
निष्क्रम्य अन्तः पुरात् तस्मात् स्वम् ददर्श सुह्Rज् जनम्
transliteration: sa rāmaḥ pitaram ktvā kaikeyīm ca pradakṣiṇam
niṣkramya antaḥ purāt tasmāt svam dadarśa suhj janam
english: And reverentially going round his father and Kaikeyi, and issuing out of the female apartment, Rāma saw his own friends and relatives.

sanskrit: तम् बाष्प परिपूर्ण अक्षः प्Rष्ठतः अनुजगाम ह
लक्ष्मणः परम क्रुद्धः सुमित्र आनन्द वर्धनः
transliteration: tam bāṣpa paripūrṇa akṣaḥ pṣṭhataḥ anujagāma ha
lakṣmaṇaḥ parama kruddhaḥ sumitra ānanda vardhanaḥ
english: Then followed him Lakşmaņa, the enhance of Sumitra's joy, greatly angry and with his eyes full of tears.

sanskrit: शनैः जगाम सापेक्षो द्Rष्टिम् तत्र अविचालयन्
transliteration: śanaiḥ jagāma sāpekṣo dṣṭim tatra avicālayan
english: Going round with reverence the house of installation full of necessary articles, not turning away from it his wistful look, Rāma began to proceed slowly.

sanskrit: न च अस्य महतीम् लक्ष्मीम् राज्य नाशो अपकर्षति
लोक कान्तस्य कान्तत्वम् शीत रश्मेर् इव क्षपा
transliteration: na ca asya mahatīm lakṣmīm rājya nāśo apakarṣati
loka kāntasya kāntatvam śīta raśmer iva kṣapā
english: Loss of kingdom could not diminish the great beauty of that beloved of the people on account of its everlasting pleasantness, like to the wane of the moon.

sanskrit: न वनम् गन्तु कामस्य त्यजतः च वसुम्धराम्
सर्व लोक अतिगस्य इव लक्ष्यते चित्त विक्रिया
transliteration: na vanam gantu kāmasya tyajataḥ ca vasumdharām
sarva loka atigasya iva lakṣyate citta vikriyā
english: There was manifest in his no change of mind, who was about to fly as an exile to the forest and leave the world, like to one emancipated while yet living.

sanskrit: प्रतिषिद्ध्य शुभम् छत्रं व्यजने च स्वलंकृते
transliteration: pratiṣiddhya śubham chatraṃ vyajane ca svalaṃkṛte
english: Leaving aside the excellent umbrella and well adorned chowries, forsaking his relatives, chariot, citizens and other people, calmly bearing the affliction in mind and not manifesting the outward signs of sorrow, Rāma, with a view to communicate this unpleasant news to his mother, entered her abode.

sanskrit: धारयन् मनसा दुह्खम् इन्द्रियाणि निग्Rह्य च
प्रविवेश आत्मवान् वेश्म मातुर प्रिय शम्सिवान्
transliteration: dhārayan manasā duhkham indriyāṇi nighya ca
praviveśa ātmavān veśma mātura priya śamsivān
english: Leaving aside the excellent umbrella and well adorned chowries, forsaking his relatives, chariot, citizens and other people, calmly bearing the affliction in mind and not manifesting the outward signs of sorrow, Rāma, with a view to communicate this unpleasant news to his mother, entered her abode.
All persons, who were present there and who adorned themselves on account of the installation, did not perceive any sign of mental agony on the face of Rāma.
Like to the rays of the fully brilliant autumnal moon, that hero of mighty arms, having control over himself, did not forsake his native cheerfulness.

sanskrit: वाचा मधुरया रामः स्र्वं सम्मानयन् जनम्
transliteration: vācā madhurayā rāmaḥ srvaṃ sammānayan janam
english: The pious Rāma, having high fame, entered into the presence of his mother, manifesting great regards for the people with sweet speech.
Then followed him, the son of Sumitrā, of mighty prowess, of equal accomplishments with his brother, and bearing the mental sorrow. Rāma, entering the abode of his mother.

sanskrit: समीक्ष्य ताम् च अर्थ विपत्तिम् आगताम्
न चैव रामः अत्र जगाम विक्रियाम्
transliteration: samīkṣya tām ca artha vipattim āgatām
na caiva rāmaḥ atra jagāma vikriyām
english: Saw it filled with all sorts of amusements; and even though his mind was not agitated with any mental disturbance seeing the impending calamity of loss of wealth, he was anxious lest the lives of his dear relatives mighty be in danger.

sanskrit: आर्तशच्दो महान् जज्ञे स्त्रीणाम न्तःपुरे तदा
transliteration: ārtaśacdo mahān jajñe strīṇāma ntaḥpure tadā
english: There arose a great uproar of cry in the apartment of the females, when that best of men went out with clasped hands.

sanskrit: गतिर्यः शरणम् चासीत् स रोओमोऽद्य प्रवत्स्यति
transliteration: gatiryaḥ śaraṇam cāsīt sa roomo'dya pravatsyati
english: That Rāma, who used to serve all the females in all matters even without his father's permission, who was our stay and protector, is going to the forest.

sanskrit: कौसल्यायाम् यथा युक्तो जनन्याम् वर्तते सदा
transliteration: kausalyāyām yathā yukto jananyām vartate sadā
english: Raghava from his birth pays as much attention to us as to his mother Kausalya.

sanskrit: कृद्धान् प्रसादयन् सर्वान् स इतोऽद्य प्रवत्स्यति
transliteration: kṛddhān prasādayan sarvān sa ito'dya pravatsyati
english: He, who being cursed, does not get angry, pacifies the wrathful and studiously avoids words and deeds that excite anger in others, will repair hence this day to the forest.
Senseless is our king, who forsakes Rāghava who is the stay of all people, and thus kills his subjects.

sanskrit: इति सर्वा महिष्यस्ता विवत्सा इव धेनवः
transliteration: iti sarvā mahiṣyastā vivatsā iva dhenavaḥ
english: Thus the queens of Dasaratha, like to the cows that have lost their young ones, began to blame him and cry aloud.

sanskrit: स हि चान्तः पुरे घोरमार्तशब्धम् महीपतिः
transliteration: sa hi cāntaḥ pure ghoramārtaśabdham mahīpatiḥ
english: Hearing this terrible uproar of cry in the female apartment, that lord of earth, racked with sorrow on account of his son, hid himself in the seat (with head hanging downwards).

sanskrit: रामः तु भ्Rशम् आयस्तः निह्श्वसन्न् इव कुन्जरः
जगाम सहितः भ्रात्रा मातुर् अन्तः पुरम् वशी
transliteration: rāmaḥ tu bhśam āyastaḥ nihśvasann iva kunjaraḥ
jagāma sahitaḥ bhrātrā mātur antaḥ puram vaśī
english: Rāma too, having control over his own self, experiencing sorrow (for his relatives) and sobbing like an (enchained) elephant, entered into his mother's apartment, together with his brother.

sanskrit: सो अपश्यत् पुरुषम् तत्र व्Rद्धम् परम पूजितम्
उपविष्टम् ग्Rह द्वारि तिष्ठतः च अपरान् बहून्
transliteration: so apaśyat puruṣam tatra vddham parama pūjitam
upaviṣṭam gha dvāri tiṣṭhataḥ ca aparān bahūn
english: He saw a venerable old man, sitting at the gate and many other persons.

sanskrit: द्R^ष्ट्वै तु तदा रामं ते सर्वे सहसोत्थिताः
जयेन जयताम् श्रेष्ठम् वर्धयन्ति स्म राघवम्
transliteration: dṣṭvai tu tadā rāmaṃ te sarve sahasotthitāḥ
jayena jayatām śreṣṭham vardhayanti sma rāghavam
english: All those present, seeing Rāma, began to shower benedictions on him, the best of all victorious heroes, saying,"Victory to you".

sanskrit: प्रविश्य प्रथमाम् कक्ष्याम् द्वितीयायाम् ददर्श सः
ब्राह्मणान् वेद सम्पन्नान् व्Rद्धान् राज्ञा अभिसत्क्Rतान्
transliteration: praviśya prathamām kakṣyām dvitīyāyām dadarśa saḥ
brāhmaṇān veda sampannān vddhān rājñā abhisatktān
english: Having passed through the first apartment he saw in the second, many.old Brahmanas, versed in the Vedas and honoured by the king.

sanskrit: प्रणम्य रामः तान् व्Rद्धाम्स् त्Rतीयायाम् ददर्श सः
स्त्रियो व्Rद्धाः च बालाः च द्वार रक्षण तत्पराः
transliteration: praṇamya rāmaḥ tān vddhāms ttīyāyām dadarśa saḥ
striyo vddhāḥ ca bālāḥ ca dvāra rakṣaṇa tatparāḥ
english: Having bowed down to them, Rāma saw in the third apartment, women, boys, and old men, all engaged in watching the gate.

sanskrit: वर्धयित्वा प्रह्Rष्टाः ताः प्रविश्य च ग्Rहम् स्त्रियः
न्यवेदयन्त त्वरिता राम मातुः प्रियम् तदा
transliteration: vardhayitvā prahṣṭāḥ tāḥ praviśya ca gham striyaḥ
nyavedayanta tvaritā rāma mātuḥ priyam tadā
english: The female warders honoured Rāma rejoicing, and entering his mother's apartment, communicated to her speedily this pleasant news.

sanskrit: कौसल्या अपि तदा देवी रात्रिम् स्थित्वा समाहिता
प्रभाते तु अकरोत् पूजाम् विष्णोह् पुत्र हित एषिणी
transliteration: kausalyā api tadā devī rātrim sthitvā samāhitā
prabhāte tu akarot pūjām viṣṇoh putra hita eṣiṇī
english: Worshipful Kausalyā, seeking her son's welfare, kept up the whole night being absorbed in meditation, and was, in the morning, worshipping the God Vişņu.

sanskrit: सा क्षौम वसना ह्Rष्टा नित्यम् व्रत परायणा
अग्निम् जुहोति स्म तदा मन्त्रवत् क्Rत मन्गला
transliteration: sā kṣauma vasanā hṣṭā nityam vrata parāyaṇā
agnim juhoti sma tadā mantravat kta mangalā
english: Wearing silk-cloth, pleased, and accustomed to the performance of religious rites every day, she, performing benedictory ceremonies, was offering oblation to the fire.

sanskrit: प्रविश्य च तदा रामः मातुर् अन्तः पुरम् शुभम्
ददर्श मातरम् तत्र हावयन्तीम् हुत अशनम्
transliteration: praviśya ca tadā rāmaḥ mātur antaḥ puram śubham
dadarśa mātaram tatra hāvayantīm huta aśanam
english: Rāma entering the auspicious abode of his mother, beheld her thus engaged in the sacrifice to the fire.

The descendant of Raghu saw there, brought for the service of the celestials, curd, grains, clarified butter, sweetmeats, things fit for oblations to the fire, fried paddy, white garlands, rice boiled in milk and sugar, rice sesamum and pea mixtures, sacrificial fuels and jars full of water.

sanskrit: लाजान् माल्यानि शुक्लानि पायसम् कृसरम् तथा
transliteration: lājān mālyāni śuklāni pāyasam kṛsaram tathā
english: The descendant of Raghu saw there, brought for the service of the celestials, curd, grains, clarified butter, sweetmeats, things fit for oblations to the fire, fried paddy, white garlands, rice boiled in milk and sugar, rice sesamum and pea mixtures, sacrificial fuels and jars full of water.

He saw his virtuous mother wearing white silk, pulled down by the austere performance of religious rites, and engaged in propitiating the deities with the offering of water. She seeing her son, ever advancing the joy of his mother, approach, became pleased, and stepped forward like unto a mare beholding her young one.

sanskrit: सा चिरस्य आत्मजम् द्Rष्ट्वा मात्R नन्दनम् आगतम्
transliteration: sā cirasya ātmajam dṣṭvā māt nandanam āgatam

english: Seeing his mother approach, Rāghava bowed low, and (Kausalyā) embracing him in her arms smelt his head.

sanskrit: तम् उवाच दुराधर्षम् राघवम् सुतम् आत्मनः
कौसल्या पुत्र वात्सल्यात् इदम् प्रिय हितम् वचः
transliteration: tam uvāca durādharṣam rāghavam sutam ātmanaḥ
kausalyā putra vātsalyāt idam priya hitam vacaḥ
english: Kausalya, out of motherly affection, spoke these sweet and beneficent words to her own invincible son, Rāghava.

sanskrit: प्राप्नुहि आयुः च कीर्तिम् च धर्मम् च उपहितम् कुले
transliteration: prāpnuhi āyuḥ ca kīrtim ca dharmam ca upahitam kule
english: May you obtain the life and fame of the pious, old Rājarşis, and the virtue worthy of your family.

sanskrit: सत्य प्रतिज्ञम् पितरम् राजानम् पश्य राघव
अद्य एव हि त्वाम् धर्म आत्मा यौवराज्ये अभिषेक्ष्यति
transliteration: satya pratijñam pitaram rājānam paśya rāghava
adya eva hi tvām dharma ātmā yauvarājye abhiṣekṣyati

sanskrit: मातरम् राघवः किम्चित् प्रसार्य अन्जलिम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: mātaram rāghavaḥ kimcit prasārya anjalim abravīt

sanskrit: स स्वभाव विनीतः च गौरवाच् च तदा आनतः
transliteration: sa svabhāva vinītaḥ ca gauravāc ca tadā ānataḥ

sanskrit: देवि नूनम् न जानीषे महद् भयम् उपस्थितम्
इदम् तव च दुह्खाय वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणस्य च
transliteration: devi nūnam na jānīṣe mahad bhayam upasthitam
idam tava ca duhkhāya vaidehyā lakṣmaṇasya ca
english: O worshipful one, certain it is that you know not the great impending calamity; It is for the distress of yours, Laksmana and Vaidehi, that shall I wend my way to the Daņdaka forest. What is the use of a seat to me then? Now is the time come when I deserve a seat made of Kusa grass.

O worshipful one, certain it is that you know not the great impending calamity; It is for the distress of yours, Laksmana and Vaidehi, that shall I wend my way to the Daņdaka forest. What is the use of a seat to me then? Now is the time come when I deserve a seat made of Kusa grass.

sanskrit: चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि वत्स्यामि विजने वने
मधु मूल फलैः जीवन् हित्वा मुनिवद् आमिषम्
transliteration: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vatsyāmi vijane vane
madhu mūla phalaiḥ jīvan hitvā munivad āmiṣam
english: I shall live in the forest for fourteen years abstaining from animal food and living on tuberous roots and fruits like to the ascetics.

sanskrit: माम् पुनर् दण्डक अरण्यम् विवासयति तापसम्
transliteration: mām punar daṇḍaka araṇyam vivāsayati tāpasam
english: The king shall confer upon Bharata the heirapparentship and shall banish me as an ascetic into the forest.

sanskrit: स ष्ट्चाअष्टौ च वर्षाणि वत्स्यामि विजने वने
transliteration: sa ṣṭcāaṣṭau ca varṣāṇi vatsyāmi vijane vane
english: And I shall live in that solitary forest for eight and six years, feasting on roots, and fruits and performing the duties of a hermit.

sanskrit: सा निकृत्तैव सालस्य यष्टिः परशुना वने
transliteration: sā nikṛttaiva sālasya yaṣṭiḥ paraśunā vane
english: Like to the stem of a sāla tree cut asunder by an axe in a wood, like to a female celestial fallen down from the abode of the gods, she fell down suddenly (hearing these heart-rending words.)

sanskrit: ताम् अदुह्ख उचिताम् द्Rष्ट्वा पतिताम् कदलीम् इव
रामः तु उत्थापयाम् आस मातरम् गत चेतसम्
transliteration: tām aduhkha ucitām dṣṭvā patitām kadalīm iva
rāmaḥ tu utthāpayām āsa mātaram gata cetasam

sanskrit: उपाव्Rत्य उत्थिताम् दीनाम् वडवाम् इव वाहिताम्
पाम्शु गुण्ठित सर्व अग्नीम् विममर्श च पाणिना
transliteration: upāvtya utthitām dīnām vaḍavām iva vāhitām
pāmśu guṇṭhita sarva agnīm vimamarśa ca pāṇinā
english: Rāma seeing his mother, who deserved no distress, fall down like a plantain tree and insensible, raised her up, and finding her covered with dust all over her body like to a mare risen up after rolling on the ground on account of toil of bearing heavy burden, wiped off (her body) gently with his hand.

sanskrit: सा राघवम् उपासीनम् असुख आर्ता सुख उचिता
transliteration: sā rāghavam upāsīnam asukha ārtā sukha ucitā
english: She, deserving happiness, being racked with the destruction of her delight, spoke thus to Rāghava, that best of men, in the presence of Laksmana.

sanskrit: यदि पुत्र न जायेथा मम शोकाय राघव
न स्म दुह्खम् अतः भूयः पश्येयम् अहम् अप्रजा
transliteration: yadi putra na jāyethā mama śokāya rāghava
na sma duhkham ataḥ bhūyaḥ paśyeyam aham aprajā
english: Oh! my son, Oh! Rāghava, had you not been born for my grief I would have been sonless only, but would not have been subject to this greater grief.

sanskrit: एकएव हि वन्ध्यायाः शोको भवति मानवः
अप्रजा अस्मि इति सम्तापो न हि अन्यः पुत्र विद्यते
transliteration: ekaeva hi vandhyāyāḥ śoko bhavati mānavaḥ
aprajā asmi iti samtāpo na hi anyaḥ putra vidyate
english: A sonless woman has only one cause of mental affliction. Her only sorrow is “I have no child" and nothing else my son.

sanskrit: न द्Rष्ट पूर्वम् कल्याणम् सुखम् वा पति पौरुषे
अपि पुत्रे विपश्येयम् इति राम आस्थितम् मया
transliteration: na dṣṭa pūrvam kalyāṇam sukham vā pati pauruṣe
api putre vipaśyeyam iti rāma āsthitam mayā
english: I have not experienced in my life that blessing and pleasure which women generally feel when their husbands are devoted to them. I have sustained my life so long, O Rāma, only with the hope that I shall witness this and other happiness when I shall have a son.

sanskrit: अहम् श्रोष्ये सपत्नीनाम् अवराणाम् वरा सती
transliteration: aham śroṣye sapatnīnām avarāṇām varā satī
english: Myself, being the eldest of all the queens, shall have to hear unpleasant and heart-rending words from the co-wives who are all younger than I.

sanskrit: अतः दुह्खतरम् किम् नु प्रमदानाम् भविष्यति
त्वयि सम्निहिते अपि एवम् अहम् आसम् निराक्Rता
transliteration: ataḥ duhkhataram kim nu pramadānām bhaviṣyati
tvayi samnihite api evam aham āsam nirāktā

sanskrit: किम् पुनः प्रोषिते तात ध्रुवम् मरणम् एव मे
transliteration: kim punaḥ proṣite tāta dhruvam maraṇam eva me
english: You being present, they have reduced me to this miserable plight, I do not know what else they will do, you being away; there is death certain for me, Oh my darling! Being disregarded by my husband I have been greatly insulted, I am equal to the maid-servants of Kaikeyi or even inferior to them.

You being present, they have reduced me to this miserable plight, I do not know what else they will do, you being away; there is death certain for me, Oh my darling! Being disregarded by my husband I have been greatly insulted, I am equal to the maid-servants of Kaikeyi or even inferior to them.

sanskrit: यो हि माम् सेवते कश्चित् अथ वा अपि अनुवर्तते
कैकेय्याः पुत्रम् अन्वीक्ष्य स जनो न अभिभाषते
transliteration: yo hi mām sevate kaścit atha vā api anuvartate
kaikeyyāḥ putram anvīkṣya sa jano na abhibhāṣate
english: Those who serve me or are obedient to me, shall not even speak with me when they will see the son of Kaikeyi (installed).

sanskrit: नित्यक्रोधतया तस्याः कथं नु खरवादि तत्
कैकेय्या वदनम् द्रष्टुम् पुत्र शक्ष्यामि दुर्गता
transliteration: nityakrodhatayā tasyāḥ kathaṃ nu kharavādi tat
kaikeyyā vadanam draṣṭum putra śakṣyāmi durgatā
english: She is always of fretful temper, how shall I, reduced to misery (on account of your exile), eye the face of Kaikeyī, uttering harsh words.

sanskrit: दश सप्त च वर्षाणि तव जातस्य राघव
transliteration: daśa sapta ca varṣāṇi tava jātasya rāghava
english: I have spent, Oh Rāghava, ten years and seven from your (second) birth* birth* expecting a termination of my sorrow. Even though worn out, Oh Rāghava, shall not be able to suffer this great misery consequent upon your unending exile and the contempt of the co-wives. *Here the commentators differ in fixing the age of Rāma at the time of his going to the forest Rāma's age was under sixteen at the time of marriage, and after he has married to Sită he enjoyed her company for twelve years, when the proposal of installation was made. This makes totally age of twenty-seven. In the text ‘dasa sapta ca' (ten and seven) ten years fall short which are to be made up by taking into account the age of ten being left out, preceding Rāma's entering into the second birth which begins at maunjibandhana or initiation into the mysteries of the Vedic literature. Following the example of Bhāșyakāra Patañjali, the commentator, Rāmānuju, has in the sentence ‘daśa supta ca' supplied another (dasa) (ten) by means of ellipsis, thus giving an age of twentyseven. This, however, contradicts the statement of Sītā to Rāvana in guise of an anchorite, informing him of the age of her husband being twenty-five. A modern annotator with great ingenuity has devised ways to make up this discrepancy. The age of Rāma was under sixteen, when Visvamitra asked his assistance in destroying Taraka. 'Under sixteen' may mean fifteen or twelve as well. After marriage at twelve, Rāma enjoyed twelve years more the pleasure of home. This giving in total twenty-four, it is to be supposed that when he was exiled he stepped at twenty-five. The text dasa sapta ca' is correct, considering the age of eight being left out preceding his second birth at the initiation into the mysteries of the Veda.

I have spent, Oh Rāghava, ten years and seven from your (second) birth* birth* expecting a termination of my sorrow. Even though worn out, Oh Rāghava, shall not be able to suffer this great misery consequent upon your unending exile and the contempt of the co-wives. *Here the commentators differ in fixing the age of Rāma at the time of his going to the forest Rāma's age was under sixteen at the time of marriage, and after he has married to Sită he enjoyed her company for twelve years, when the proposal of installation was made. This makes totally age of twenty-seven. In the text ‘dasa sapta ca' (ten and seven) ten years fall short which are to be made up by taking into account the age of ten being left out, preceding Rāma's entering into the second birth which begins at maunjibandhana or initiation into the mysteries of the Vedic literature. Following the example of Bhāșyakāra Patañjali, the commentator, Rāmānuju, has in the sentence ‘daśa supta ca' supplied another (dasa) (ten) by means of ellipsis, thus giving an age of twentyseven. This, however, contradicts the statement of Sītā to Rāvana in guise of an anchorite, informing him of the age of her husband being twenty-five. A modern annotator with great ingenuity has devised ways to make up this discrepancy. The age of Rāma was under sixteen, when Visvamitra asked his assistance in destroying Taraka. 'Under sixteen' may mean fifteen or twelve as well. After marriage at twelve, Rāma enjoyed twelve years more the pleasure of home. This giving in total twenty-four, it is to be supposed that when he was exiled he stepped at twenty-five. The text dasa sapta ca' is correct, considering the age of eight being left out preceding his second birth at the initiation into the mysteries of the Veda.
How shall I, of miserable life, pass my days in grief not seeing your face, effulgent like to the full-moon.

sanskrit: उपवासैः च योगैः च बहुभिः च परिश्रमैः
दुह्खम् सम्वर्धितः मोघम् त्वम् हि दुर्गतया मया
transliteration: upavāsaiḥ ca yogaiḥ ca bahubhiḥ ca pariśramaiḥ
duhkham samvardhitaḥ mogham tvam hi durgatayā mayā
english: Wretched as I am, in vain have I brought you up with fasts, contemplation's and many other toilsome austerities.

sanskrit: स्थिरम् तु हृदयम् मन्ये मम इदम् यन् न दीर्यते
प्रावृषि इव महा नद्याः स्पृष्टम् कूलम् नव अम्भसा
transliteration: sthiram tu hṛdayam manye mama idam yan na dīryate
prāvṛṣi iva mahā nadyāḥ spṛṣṭam kūlam nava ambhasā
english: Surely, I consider my heart is very hard, as it does not rend like to the bank of a great river in contact with new water in the rainy season.

sanskrit: मम एव नूनम् मरणम् न विद्यते
न च अवकाशो अस्ति यम क्षये मम
यद् अन्तको अद्य एव न माम् जिहीर्षति
transliteration: mama eva nūnam maraṇam na vidyate
na ca avakāśo asti yama kṣaye mama
yad antako adya eva na mām jihīrṣati
english: There is no death for me, no vacant place in the abode of Yama; otherwise why does not Death take me away like to a lion snatching away a weeping hind; certain it is that my heart is made of iron, as it does not rend nor does my body being pressed down with this sorrow and (falling) down on earth, break into pieces; verily have I no death before time.

sanskrit: स्थिरम् हि नूनम् हृदयम् मम आयसम्
न भिद्यते यद् भुवि न अवदीर्यते
ध्रुवम् हि अकाले मरणम् न विद्यते
transliteration: sthiram hi nūnam hṛdayam mama āyasam
na bhidyate yad bhuvi na avadīryate
dhruvam hi akāle maraṇam na vidyate
english: There is no death for me, no vacant place in the abode of Yama; otherwise why does not Death take me away like to a lion snatching away a weeping hind; certain it is that my heart is made of iron, as it does not rend nor does my body being pressed down with this sorrow and (falling) down on earth, break into pieces; verily have I no death before time.

sanskrit: इदम् तु दुःखम् यद् अनर्थकानि मे
व्रतानि दानानि च सम्यमाः च हि
तपः च तप्तम् यद् अपत्य कारणात्
transliteration: idam tu duḥkham yad anarthakāni me
vratāni dānāni ca samyamāḥ ca hi
tapaḥ ca taptam yad apatya kāraṇāt
english: This distresses me that all my religious vows, alms giving, self-restraint and austerity, performed with a view of obtaining a son, have been fruitless, like to the seeds thrown on a barren soil.

sanskrit: यदि हि अकाले मरणम् स्वया इच्चया
गता अहम् अद्य एव परेत सम्सदम्
विना त्वया धेनुर् इव आत्मजेन वै
transliteration: yadi hi akāle maraṇam svayā iccayā
gatā aham adya eva pareta samsadam
vinā tvayā dhenur iva ātmajena vai
english: If any body in this life, being pressed down with some great calamity, could meet with death of his own accord, I would have instantly gone to the abode of death, being cut off from you like to a cow from her young one.

sanskrit: अथापि किम् जीवित मद्य मे वृथा
transliteration: athāpi kim jīvita madya me vṛthā
english: Oh, you, having a countenance of moon-like splendour, wretched indeed is my life without you, I shall follow you to the forest out of great affection, like to an enfeebled cow following her young one.
Kausalyā like a Kinnarī unable to bear this great calamity, anticipating great misfortune and seeing Rāma bound (with a great vow), began to lament in various ways. some

sanskrit: तथा तु विलपन्तीम् ताम् कौसल्याम् राम मातरम्
उवाच लक्ष्मणो दीनः तत् काल सदृशम् वचः
transliteration: tathā tu vilapantīm tām kausalyām rāma mātaram
uvāca lakṣmaṇo dīnaḥ tat kāla sadṛśam vacaḥ
english: At this time Laksmana, sorely distressed, addressed the weeping Kausalyā, the mother of Rāma with the following words suitable to that occasion.

sanskrit: न रोचते मम अपि एतत् आर्ये यद् राघवो वनम्
त्यक्त्वा राज्य श्रियम् गच्चेत् स्त्रिया वाक्य वशम् गतः
transliteration: na rocate mama api etat ārye yad rāghavo vanam
tyaktvā rājya śriyam gaccet striyā vākya vaśam gataḥ
english: I like it not, Oh worshipful one, that Räghava, should repair to the forest, renouncing this grandeur of sovereignty. The king is uxorious, old and therefore of perverted judgement and is addicted to worldly affairs; being under the influence of his wife and passion what could he not speak?

sanskrit: विपरीतः च वृद्धः च विषयैः च प्रधर्षितः
नृपः किम् इव न ब्रूयाच् चोद्यमानः समन्मथः
transliteration: viparītaḥ ca vṛddhaḥ ca viṣayaiḥ ca pradharṣitaḥ
nṛpaḥ kim iva na brūyāc codyamānaḥ samanmathaḥ
english: I like it not, Oh worshipful one, that Räghava, should repair to the forest, renouncing this grandeur of sovereignty. The king is uxorious, old and therefore of perverted judgement and is addicted to worldly affairs; being under the influence of his wife and passion what could he not speak?

sanskrit: न अस्य अपराधम् पश्यामि न अपि दोषम् तथा विधम्
येन निर्वास्यते राष्ट्रात् वन वासाय राघवः
transliteration: na asya aparādham paśyāmi na api doṣam tathā vidham
yena nirvāsyate rāṣṭrāt vana vāsāya rāghavaḥ
english: I do not see any such fault or sin in Rāma that he should be banished from the kingdom to range in the wood.

sanskrit: न तम् पश्याम्य् अहम् लोके परोक्षम् अपि यो नरः
transliteration: na tam paśyāmy aham loke parokṣam api yo naraḥ
english: I do not find any such man in this world, even amongst great enemies, who, forsaken for heinous sins, can cite, even in his absence, any fault of him.

sanskrit: देव कल्पम् ऋजुम् दान्तम् रिपूणाम् अपि वत्सलम्
अवेक्षमाणः को धर्मम् त्यजेत् पुत्रम् अकारणात्
transliteration: deva kalpam ṛjum dāntam ripūṇām api vatsalam
avekṣamāṇaḥ ko dharmam tyajet putram akāraṇāt
english: Observing what law of righteousness does the monarch, without any cause, renounce such a son who is like to celestials, simple, well disciplined and beloved even of the enemies?

sanskrit: तत् इदम् वचनम् राज्ञः पुनर् बाल्यम् उपेयुषः
पुत्रः को हृदये कुर्यात् राज व्Rत्तम् अनुस्मरन्
transliteration: tat idam vacanam rājñaḥ punar bālyam upeyuṣaḥ
putraḥ ko hṛdaye kuryāt rāja vttam anusmaran
english: What son, remembering his father's conduct, shall carry in his heart these words of the king, who has again gone back to childhood?

sanskrit: यावद् एव न जानाति कश्चित् अर्थम् इमम् नरः
तावद् एव मया साधम् आत्मस्थम् कुरु शासनम्
transliteration: yāvad eva na jānāti kaścit artham imam naraḥ
tāvad eva mayā sādham ātmastham kuru śāsanam
english: Ere people come to know this proposal of exile, do you secure the government of the kingdom to yourself with me.

sanskrit: मया पार्श्वे सधनुषा तव गुप्तस्य राघव
कः समर्थो अधिकम् कर्तुम् कृत अन्तस्य इव तिष्ठतः
transliteration: mayā pārśve sadhanuṣā tava guptasya rāghava
kaḥ samartho adhikam kartum kṛta antasya iva tiṣṭhataḥ
english: Who can disturb the installation, Oh Rāghava, myself protecting you by your side with my bows, like to Death himself.

sanskrit: निर्मनुष्याम् इमाम् सर्वाम् अयोध्याम् मनुज ऋषभ
करिष्यामि शरैअः तीक्ष्णैः यदि स्थास्यति विप्रिये
transliteration: nirmanuṣyām imām sarvām ayodhyām manuja ṛṣabha
kariṣyāmi śaraiaḥ tīkṣṇaiḥ yadi sthāsyati vipriye
english: If any body stands here as an enemy, surely shall I, Oh best of men, depopulate the whole city of Ayodhyā with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: भरतस्य अथ पक्ष्यो वा यो वा अस्य हितम् इच्चति
सर्वान् एतान् वधिष्यामि मृदुर् हि परिभूयते
transliteration: bharatasya atha pakṣyo vā yo vā asya hitam iccati
sarvān etān vadhiṣyāmi mṛdur hi paribhūyate
english: I shall immolate all who shall stand by Bharata or wish him well, certainly mildness brings about discomfiture.

sanskrit: प्रोत्साहितोऽयम् कैकेय्या स दुष्टो यदिः पिता
transliteration: protsāhito'yam kaikeyyā sa duṣṭo yadiḥ pitā
english: If father being propitiated and excited by Kaikeyi, turns out to be our enemy, he shall be slain, without any hesitation.
Even a spiritual leader deserves chastisement if he is puffed up with pride, and is devoid of the power of judging good actions and bad, and when he is gone astray.
Tell me, Oh best of men, by what law of virtue and what reason does he purpose to confer this kingdom upon Kaikeyi, which has devolved upon you (by the law of inheritance).

sanskrit: त्वया चैव मया चैव कृत्वा वैरम् अनुत्तमम्
कस्य शक्तिः श्रियम् दातुम् भरताय अरि शासन
transliteration: tvayā caiva mayā caiva kṛtvā vairam anuttamam
kasya śaktiḥ śriyam dātum bharatāya ari śāsana
english: Who dares conferring on on Bharata the kingdom, carrying hostility with me and you?

sanskrit: अनुरक्तः अस्मि भावेन भ्रातरम् देवि तत्त्वतः
सत्येन धनुषा चैव दत्तेन इष्टेन ते शपे
transliteration: anuraktaḥ asmi bhāvena bhrātaram devi tattvataḥ
satyena dhanuṣā caiva dattena iṣṭena te śape
english: Oh worshipful one, verily am I attached at heart to my brother.

sanskrit: दीप्तम् अग्निम् अरण्यम् वा यदि रामः प्रवेक्ष्यते
प्रविष्टम् तत्र माम् देवि त्वम् पूर्वम् अवधारय
transliteration: dīptam agnim araṇyam vā yadi rāmaḥ pravekṣyate
praviṣṭam tatra mām devi tvam pūrvam avadhāraya
english: By truth, bow, gifts and things dear to me, do I swear to you; if Rāma shall enter into the wood, know me, Oh worshipful one, to have entered into the fire before that.

sanskrit: हरामि वीर्यात् दुह्खम् ते तमः सूर्यैव उदितः
देवी पश्यतु मे वीर्यम् राघवः चैव पश्यतु
transliteration: harāmi vīryāt duhkham te tamaḥ sūryaiva uditaḥ
devī paśyatu me vīryam rāghavaḥ caiva paśyatu
english: Like to the sun dispelling darkness, shall I remove your sorrow by dint of my power; may your worshipful self and Rāghava witness it. Readily shall I despatch my father, whose heart is unduly attached to Kaikeyſ and who is therefore vile and being old contemptibly playing the child.

sanskrit: एतत् तु वचनम् श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणस्य महात्मनः
उवाच रामम् कौसल्या रुदन्ती शोक लालसा
transliteration: etat tu vacanam śrutvā lakṣmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ
uvāca rāmam kausalyā rudantī śoka lālasā
english: Hearing these words of the high-souled Laks maņa, Kausaly, weeping and being pressed with sorrow spoke these words to Rāma.

sanskrit: भ्रातुस् ते वदतः पुत्र लक्ष्मणस्य श्रुतम् त्वया
यद् अत्र अनन्तरम् तत् त्वम् कुरुष्व यदि रोचते
transliteration: bhrātus te vadataḥ putra lakṣmaṇasya śrutam tvayā
yad atra anantaram tat tvam kuruṣva yadi rocate
english: You have heard, Oh my son, what your brother Laksmana said; and if you like, do what seems reasonable to you.

sanskrit: न च अधर्म्यम् वचः श्रुत्वा सपत्न्या मम भाषितम्
विहाय शोक सम्तप्ताम् गन्तुम् अर्हसि माम् इतः
transliteration: na ca adharmyam vacaḥ śrutvā sapatnyā mama bhāṣitam
vihāya śoka samtaptām gantum arhasi mām itaḥ
english: It does not behove you, hearing the sinful words given vent to by the co-wife, to repair hence, leaving me who is sore distressed with sorrow.

sanskrit: धर्मज्ञ यदि धर्मिष्ठो धर्मम् चरितुम् इच्चसि
शुश्रूष माम् इहस्थः त्वम् चर धर्मम् अनुत्तमम्
transliteration: dharmajña yadi dharmiṣṭho dharmam caritum iccasi
śuśrūṣa mām ihasthaḥ tvam cara dharmam anuttamam
english: Oh you pious one, having knowledge of religion, if do you wish to acquire righteousness, serve me here and continue practising the best of all virtues.

sanskrit: शुश्रूषुर् जननीम् पुत्र स्व गृहे नियतः वसन्
परेण तपसा युक्तः काश्यपः त्रिदिवम् गतः
transliteration: śuśrūṣur jananīm putra sva gṛhe niyataḥ vasan
pareṇa tapasā yuktaḥ kāśyapaḥ tridivam gataḥ
english: Hear, Oh my son, the great ascetic Kasyapa, lived in his house, serving his mother continually and being crowned with best moral merit reached heaven.

sanskrit: यथा एव राजा पूज्यः ते गौरवेण तथा हि अहम्
त्वाम् न अहम् अनुजानामि न गन्तव्यम् इतः वनम्
transliteration: yathā eva rājā pūjyaḥ te gauraveṇa tathā hi aham
tvām na aham anujānāmi na gantavyam itaḥ vanam
english: As the monarch is worshipful to you in veneration so am I. I do not permit you, to repair hence to the forest.

sanskrit: त्वद् वियोगान् न मे कार्यम् जीवितेन सुखेन वा
त्वया सह मम श्रेयः तृणानाम् अपि भक्षणम्
transliteration: tvad viyogān na me kāryam jīvitena sukhena vā
tvayā saha mama śreyaḥ tṛṇānām api bhakṣaṇam
english: Separated from you I do not need life or happiness; with you I would prefer faring on grass.

sanskrit: यदि त्वम् यास्यसि वनम् त्यक्त्वा माम् शोक लालसाम्
अहम् प्रायम् इह आसिष्ये न हि शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्
transliteration: yadi tvam yāsyasi vanam tyaktvā mām śoka lālasām
aham prāyam iha āsiṣye na hi śakṣyāmi jīvitum
english: If do you depart to the forest leaving me troubled with sorrow, I shall resort to the vow of fasting and shall not be able to sustain my life.

sanskrit: ततः स्त्वम् प्राप्स्यसे पुत्र निरयम् लोक विश्रुतम्
ब्रह्म हत्याम् इव अधर्मात् समुद्रः सरिताम् पतिः
transliteration: tataḥ stvam prāpsyase putra nirayam loka viśrutam
brahma hatyām iva adharmāt samudraḥ saritām patiḥ
english: And then you shall receive the penalty of hell, well-known to the people, as did the ocean, the lord of rivers, for like unrighteousness, suffer the agony of Brahmanicide".* *The text has been here a little freely translated to make it compatible with the legend to which it refers. The ocean, thus goes the story, caused the grief of his mother. Upon which, Maharși Pippalāda, through magical power, subjected him to agony of hell. This agony the mother of Rāma relates as the same that follows the sin of Brahminicide.

sanskrit: विलपन्तीम् तथा दीनाम् कौसल्याम् जननीम् ततः
उवाच रामः धर्म अत्मा वचनम् धर्म सम्हितम्
transliteration: vilapantīm tathā dīnām kausalyām jananīm tataḥ
uvāca rāmaḥ dharma atmā vacanam dharma samhitam
english: Whereupon to his mother Kausalyä, sorrowful and weeping, spoke Răma, virtuous-souled these words of righteousness.

sanskrit: न अस्ति शक्तिः पितुर् वाक्यम् समतिक्रमितुम् मम
प्रसादये त्वाम् शिरसा गन्तुम् इच्चाम्य् अहम् वनम्
transliteration: na asti śaktiḥ pitur vākyam samatikramitum mama
prasādaye tvām śirasā gantum iccāmy aham vanam
english: There is no power in me to transgress my father's behest's; bend low I my head to you, I want to proceed to the forest.

sanskrit: ऋषिणा च पितुर् वाक्यम् कुर्वता व्रत चारिणा
गौर् हता जानता धर्मम् कण्डुना अपि विपश्चिता
transliteration: ṛṣiṇā ca pitur vākyam kurvatā vrata cāriṇā
gaur hatā jānatā dharmam kaṇḍunā api vipaścitā
english: The learned Rși Kandu, who lived in the forest keeping the word of his father, killed a cow, knowing it to be unrighteousness.

sanskrit: अस्माकम् च कुले पूर्वम् सगरस्य आज्ञया पितुः
खनद्भिः सागरैः भूतिम् अवाप्तः सुमहान् वधः
transliteration: asmākam ca kule pūrvam sagarasya ājñayā pituḥ
khanadbhiḥ sāgaraiḥ bhūtim avāptaḥ sumahān vadhaḥ
english: In our line the descendants of Sagara, at the command of their father, met with signal destruction, while digging the earth.

sanskrit: कृत्ता परशुना अरण्ये पितुर् वचन कारिणा
transliteration: kṛttā paraśunā araṇye pitur vacana kāriṇā
english: Rāma the son of Jamadagni, at his father's words, decapitated his mother in the forest.
These and other god-like personages, Oh worshipful one, obeyed heroically the orders of their father; and I shall do my father's welfare therefore,

sanskrit: न खल्व् एतन् मया एकेन क्रियते पितृ शासनम्
एतैरपि कृतम् देवि ये मया तव कीर्तिताः
transliteration: na khalv etan mayā ekena kriyate pitṛ śāsanam
etairapi kṛtam devi ye mayā tava kīrtitāḥ
english: It is not I alone who am carrying out my father's command; those whom I have mentioned now, O worshipful one, have done so.

sanskrit: पूर्वैः अयम् अभिप्रेतः गतः मार्गो अनुगम्यते
transliteration: pūrvaiḥ ayam abhipretaḥ gataḥ mārgo anugamyate
english: I am not introducing some such righteousness, unfavourable to you, that has been never practised before.

sanskrit: तत् एतत् तु मया कार्यम् क्रियते भुवि न अन्यथा
पितुर् हि वचनम् कुर्वन् न कश्चिन् नाम हीयते
transliteration: tat etat tu mayā kāryam kriyate bhuvi na anyathā
pitur hi vacanam kurvan na kaścin nāma hīyate
english: I am simply treading the path, that has been upheld and followed by worthies gone before. Surely shall I accomplish that which is worthy of being performed in this world and nothing else, one going by his father's behest's is not certainly degraded."

sanskrit: ताम् एवम् उक्त्वा जननीम् लक्ष्मणम् पुनर् अब्रवीत्
तव लक्ष्मण जानामि मयि स्नेहम् अनुत्तमम्
transliteration: tām evam uktvā jananīm lakṣmaṇam punar abravīt
tava lakṣmaṇa jānāmi mayi sneham anuttamam

sanskrit: विक्रमम् चैव सत्यम् च तेजश्च सुदुरासदम्
transliteration: vikramam caiva satyam ca tejaśca sudurāsadam
english: I know full well, Oh, Laksmana, your affection towards me and your power, strength • and unconquerable force.

sanskrit: अभिप्रायम् अविज्ञाय सत्यस्य च शमस्य च
transliteration: abhiprāyam avijñāya satyasya ca śamasya ca
english: Not knowing my settled conviction in regard to truth and peace, my mother, Oh beautiful Lakşmaņa, is so disturbed with incomparable sorrow.

sanskrit: धर्मः हि परमः लोके धर्मे सत्यम् प्रतिष्ठितम्
धर्म सम्श्रितम् एतच् च पितुर् वचनम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: dharmaḥ hi paramaḥ loke dharme satyam pratiṣṭhitam
dharma samśritam etac ca pitur vacanam uttamam
english: Righteousness is the prime object in this world and in righteousness is established truth, and this excellent utterance of my father is in keeping with righteousness.

sanskrit: सम्श्रुत्य च पितुर् वाक्यम् मातुर् वा ब्राह्मणस्य वा
न कर्तव्यम् वृथा वीर धर्मम् आश्रित्य तिष्ठता
transliteration: samśrutya ca pitur vākyam mātur vā brāhmaṇasya vā
na kartavyam vṛthā vīra dharmam āśritya tiṣṭhatā
english: It does not become them, O hero, who abide in righteousness to fail to carry out the commands of father, mother or a Brahmin.

sanskrit: सो अहम् न शक्ष्यामि पितुर् नियोगम् अतिवर्तितुम्
पितुर् हि वचनात् वीर कैकेय्या अहम् प्रचोदितः
transliteration: so aham na śakṣyāmi pitur niyogam ativartitum
pitur hi vacanāt vīra kaikeyyā aham pracoditaḥ
english: While I have been, Oh warrior, ordered by Kaikeyi at my father's words, I shall not be able to transgress those behest's again.

sanskrit: तत् एनाम् विसृज अनार्याम् क्षत्र धर्म आश्रिताम् मतिम्
धर्मम् आश्रय मा तैक्ष्ण्यम् मद् बुद्धिर् अनुगम्यताम्
transliteration: tat enām visṛja anāryām kṣatra dharma āśritām matim
dharmam āśraya mā taikṣṇyam mad buddhir anugamyatām
english: Do you relinquish therefore this unrighteous purpose of your consequent to the virtues of the Kșatriyas; do you abide by righteousness but not cruelty, and follow my decision.

sanskrit: तम् एवम् उक्त्वा सौहार्दात् भ्रातरम् लक्ष्मण अग्रजः
उवाच भूयः कौसल्याम् प्रान्जलिः शिरसा आनतः
transliteration: tam evam uktvā sauhārdāt bhrātaram lakṣmaṇa agrajaḥ
uvāca bhūyaḥ kausalyām prānjaliḥ śirasā ānataḥ
english: Saying these words to Lakşmaņa out of fraternal affection, spoke again Rāma to Kausalyā with clasped hands and with his head bending low.

sanskrit: अनुमन्यस्व माम् देवि गमिष्यन्तम् इतः वनम्
शापिता असि मम प्राणैः कुरु स्वस्त्ययनानि मे
transliteration: anumanyasva mām devi gamiṣyantam itaḥ vanam
śāpitā asi mama prāṇaiḥ kuru svastyayanāni me
english: I do bind you with an oath of my life, Oh venerable one, to allow me to wander away hence into the wood. Do you perform benedictory ceremonies for my welfare.

sanskrit: तीर्ण प्रतिज्ञः च वनात् पुनर् एष्याम्य् अहम् पुरीम्
transliteration: tīrṇa pratijñaḥ ca vanāt punar eṣyāmy aham purīm
english: Like to the royal saint Yayāti, in the days of yore once falling on earth going again to the abode of celestials, I shall, fulfilling my vows, again return home from the forest.
Do you, Oh mother, assuage your grief within your heart; lament not you, I shall return home again from the wood after making good my father's words.

sanskrit: त्वया मया च वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन सुमित्रया
transliteration: tvayā mayā ca vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena sumitrayā
english: Myself, Laksmana, Vaidehi, Sumitra and yourself shall abide by father's words, and this is the virtue eternal.

sanskrit: अम्ब सम्हृत्य सम्भारान् दुःखम् हृदि निगृह्य च
transliteration: amba samhṛtya sambhārān duḥkham hṛdi nigṛhya ca
english: Desisting from the ceremonies of installation and allaying your sorrow in your heart do you, Oh my mother, follow my pious decision about retiring to the forest.
Hearing those pious, sober and reasonable words of Rāma, the venerable mother, regaining her sense like to the dead, and casting her look upon him, spoke to him again the following words.

I am equally worshipful to you, Oh my son, with your father, for like him have I brought you up with pains and like him do I love you. I shall not allow you to repair to the forest and it does not behove you to go leaving me behind sore distressed with grief.

Without you, of what avail to me is my life, my relatives, the worship of the manes and the deities and the knowledge of divine truth on this earth? Prefer do I your company even for a moment to the presence of all creation.

Hearing these sorrowful words of his mother, Rāma was again inflamed with ire, like to an clephant goaded with a fire-brand, when entering into darkness. He, abiding in righteousness spoke such pious words to his mother, almost insensible, and to the son of Sumitrā, bewailing and racked with sorrow, as he was justified to utter on that occasion.

Hearing these sorrowful words of his mother, Rāma was again inflamed with ire, like to an clephant goaded with a fire-brand, when entering into darkness. He, abiding in righteousness spoke such pious words to his mother, almost insensible, and to the son of Sumitrā, bewailing and racked with sorrow, as he was justified to utter on that occasion.
I know, Oh Laksmana, your deep respects to me and your power. It is not proper for you to pain me along with my mother, not being cognizant of my intention.

Righteousness, wealth, and the objects of desire are looked upon with great esteem in this world of the created, but when the occasion for obtaining the result consequent upon the virtuous deeds of a prior life appears, all these three, I have no doubt, are doubt, are fulfilled in righteousness, as the wife alone, obedient, charming and having a son (fulfils them all).

It is not becoming for us to perform all those things where these three do not combine, whence results righteousness that we should resort to. A man seeking wealth become despicable, and one subject to desires is not admired by any (why bereft of righteousness).

sanskrit: गुरुश्च राजा च पिता च वृद्धः
transliteration: guruśca rājā ca pitā ca vṛddhaḥ
english: Who of us, having no tendency to wickedness, shall not obey the command of our father knowing it to be righteousness, who is old, our monarch and preceptor in military training, be it an outcome of his desires, anger or joy.

For this it is that I am unable to act against my father's vow, he is our father and therefore can command us both like a master; and he is the husband of this venerable one, therefore her stay and righteousness itself.
The righteousness monarch is still living and continues in his own path when ready to redeem his vow-even by renouncing me, how can this worshipful one accompany me like other insignificant widows?
Do you permit me therefore, to repair to the forest and perform benedictory ceremonies for me so that I may again return home like to Yayāti regaining heaven by truth.

I cannot neglect eminent fame being impelled by avarice for kingdom alone. Life is but of short duration, Oh worshipful one, and as such I do not long for acquiring this nether earth by means unrighteous.

Rāma, that foremost of men, with a view to range into the forest Dandaka after patiently propitiating his mother and instructing fully his younger brother the mysteries of righteousness, went round his mother with reverence and made up his mind to repair to the forest.

sanskrit: अथ तम् व्यथया दीनम् सविशेषम् अमर्षितम्
श्वसन्तम् इव नाग इन्द्रम् रोष विस्फारित ईक्षणम्
transliteration: atha tam vyathayā dīnam saviśeṣam amarṣitam
śvasantam iva nāga indram roṣa visphārita īkṣaṇam

sanskrit: आसद्य रामः सौमित्रिम् सुह्Rदम् भ्रातरम् प्रियम्
उवाच इदम् स धैर्येण धारयन् सत्त्वम् आत्मवान्
transliteration: āsadya rāmaḥ saumitrim suhdam bhrātaram priyam
uvāca idam sa dhairyeṇa dhārayan sattvam ātmavān
english: Here after holding the equanimity of mind with patience self-possessed Răma spoke thus to the son of Sumitrā, his dear brother, and friend, who was greatly sorry, had lost his patience and was pressed down with this misfortune of Rāma, and had his eyes inflated with anger like to an infuriated elephant.

sanskrit: निगृह्य रोषं शोकं च खैर्यमाश्रित्य केवलम्
transliteration: nigṛhya roṣaṃ śokaṃ ca khairyamāśritya kevalam
english: Subduing this anger and sorrow, taking recourse to patience only, brooking the insult and resorting to joy, do you set aside all those things that have been collected here for my installation and make preparations speedily for my repairing to the forest.

sanskrit: स्र्वम् विसर्जय क्षिप्रम् कुरु कार्यम् निरत्ययम्
transliteration: srvam visarjaya kṣipram kuru kāryam niratyayam

sanskrit: सौमित्रे यो अभिषेक अर्थे मम सम्भार सम्भ्रमः
अभिषेक निवृत्ति अर्थे सो अस्तु सम्भार सम्भ्रमः
transliteration: saumitre yo abhiṣeka arthe mama sambhāra sambhramaḥ
abhiṣeka nivṛtti arthe so astu sambhāra sambhramaḥ
english: Oh son of Sumitrā, do you take that amount of trouble for preventing now the collection of materials for installation, as did you take beforehand for collecting them.

sanskrit: यस्या मद् अभिषेक अर्थम् मानसम् परितप्यते
माता नः सा यथा न स्यात् सविशन्का तथा कुरु
transliteration: yasyā mad abhiṣeka artham mānasam paritapyate
mātā naḥ sā yathā na syāt saviśankā tathā kuru
english: Do you act therefore in such a way as will remove the apprehension from the mind of our mother (Kaikeyi), who is troubled at heart so greatly on hearing of my installation.

sanskrit: तस्याः शन्कामयम् दुह्खम् मुहूर्तम् अपि न उत्सहे
transliteration: tasyāḥ śankāmayam duhkham muhūrtam api na utsahe
english: Oh, son of Sumitra, I cannot neglect for a moment the trouble which has arisen in her mind on account of this fear.

sanskrit: न बुद्धि पूर्वम् न अबुद्धम् स्मरामि इह कदाचन
मातृणाम् वा पितुर् वाहम् कृतम् अल्पम् च विप्रियम्
transliteration: na buddhi pūrvam na abuddham smarāmi iha kadācana
mātṛṇām vā pitur vāham kṛtam alpam ca vipriyam
english: I do not remember to have done on any occasion wilfully or unwilfully any thing that is displeasing to my father or mothers.

sanskrit: सत्यः सत्य अभिसम्धः च नित्यम् सत्य पराक्रमः
पर लोक भयात् भीतः निर्भयो अस्तु पिता मम
transliteration: satyaḥ satya abhisamdhaḥ ca nityam satya parākramaḥ
para loka bhayāt bhītaḥ nirbhayo astu pitā mama
english: My father is of truthful words and vows and he has been greatly terrified by the fear of the next world; may his fear disappear now.

sanskrit: तस्य अपि हि भवेद् अस्मिन् कर्मणि अप्रतिसम्ह्Rते
सत्यम् न इति मनः तापः तस्य तापः तपेच् च माम्
transliteration: tasya api hi bhaved asmin karmaṇi apratisamhte
satyam na iti manaḥ tāpaḥ tasya tāpaḥ tapec ca mām
english: If this work of installation be not stopped, my father shall be greatly pained at heart thinking that his vows shall not be fulfilled and his sorrow will also ache me.

sanskrit: अभिषेक विधानम् तु तस्मात् सम्हृत्य लक्ष्मण
अन्वग् एव अहम् इच्चामि वनम् गन्तुम् इतः पुनः
transliteration: abhiṣeka vidhānam tu tasmāt samhṛtya lakṣmaṇa
anvag eva aham iccāmi vanam gantum itaḥ punaḥ
english: And it is for this reason, Oh Laksmana, that I purpose speedily to retire from this city to the forest, renouncing the preparations for my installation.

sanskrit: मम प्रव्राजनात् अद्य कृत कृत्या नृपात्मजा
transliteration: mama pravrājanāt adya kṛta kṛtyā nṛpātmajā
english: On my wandering away to the forest to-day, the daughter of Kekaya shall have her ends attained and shall install Bharata on the throne without any disturbance whatsoever,

sanskrit: मयि चीर अजिन धरे जटा मण्डल धारिणि
गते अरण्यम् च कैकेय्या भविष्यति मनः सुखम्
transliteration: mayi cīra ajina dhare jaṭā maṇḍala dhāriṇi
gate araṇyam ca kaikeyyā bhaviṣyati manaḥ sukham
english: Myself going to the forest, wearing. bark, tiger-skin and matted hair, Kaikeyi shall attain the happiness of her mind.

sanskrit: बुद्धिः प्रणीता येन इयम् मनः च सुसमाहितम्
तत् तु न अर्हामि सम्क्लेष्टुम् प्रव्रजिष्यामि माचिरम्
transliteration: buddhiḥ praṇītā yena iyam manaḥ ca susamāhitam
tat tu na arhāmi samkleṣṭum pravrajiṣyāmi māciram
english: That great One, who' has inspired Kaikeyi with this mode of mind and has kept it firm, I cannot offend. I shall repair hence without any delay.

sanskrit: कृत अन्तः तु एव सौमित्रे द्रष्टव्यो मत् प्रवासने
राज्यस्य च वितीर्णस्य पुनर् एव निवर्तने
transliteration: kṛta antaḥ tu eva saumitre draṣṭavyo mat pravāsane
rājyasya ca vitīrṇasya punar eva nivartane
english: Do you regard, Oh Laksmana, destiny as the only cause of this transfer of the kingdom, although attained, and of my banishment.

sanskrit: कैकेय्याः प्रतिपत्तिर् हि कथम् स्यान् मम पीडने
यदि भावो न दैवो अयम् कृत अन्त विहितः भवेत्
transliteration: kaikeyyāḥ pratipattir hi katham syān mama pīḍane
yadi bhāvo na daivo ayam kṛta anta vihitaḥ bhavet
english: Had not destiny been instrumental; in bringing about this; determination in Kaikeyi, she would not have been so much persevering in the infliction of misery upon me.

sanskrit: जानासि हि यथा सौम्य न मातृषु मम अन्तरम्
भूत पूर्वम् विशेषो वा तस्या मयि सुते अपि वा
transliteration: jānāsi hi yathā saumya na mātṛṣu mama antaram
bhūta pūrvam viśeṣo vā tasyā mayi sute api vā
english: Do you know, Oh gentle Laksmana, that I have never made any distinction in my mind between my mothers, nor did Kaikeyi make any such thing before between me and her son; consequently it is destiny only that has made her press for the prevention of my installation and for my exile with harsh and cruel words, or else why should she, a daughter of a king and possessed of an excellent temper and high accomplishments, speak painful words to me in the presence of her husband like to an ordinary woman.

sanskrit: सो अभिषेक निवृत्ति अर्थैः प्रवास अर्थैः च दुर्वचैः
उग्रैः वाक्यैः अहम् तस्या न अन्यद् दैवात् समर्थये
transliteration: so abhiṣeka nivṛtti arthaiḥ pravāsa arthaiḥ ca durvacaiḥ
ugraiḥ vākyaiḥ aham tasyā na anyad daivāt samarthaye
english: Do you know, Oh gentle Laksmana, that I have never made any distinction in my mind between my mothers, nor did Kaikeyi make any such thing before between me and her son; consequently it is destiny only that has made her press for the prevention of my installation and for my exile with harsh and cruel words, or else why should she, a daughter of a king and possessed of an excellent temper and high accomplishments, speak painful words to me in the presence of her husband like to an ordinary woman.

sanskrit: कथम् प्रकृति सम्पन्ना राज पुत्री तथा अगुणा
ब्रूयात् सा प्राकृता इव स्त्री मत् पीडाम् भर्तृ सम्निधौ
transliteration: katham prakṛti sampannā rāja putrī tathā aguṇā
brūyāt sā prākṛtā iva strī mat pīḍām bhartṛ samnidhau
english: That which is above comprehension is Destiny and it is beyond the power of creatures to avert its consequences; and evidently it is through this Destiny that have sprung up this distemper of Kaikeyi and my loss of kingdom.

sanskrit: यद् अचिन्त्यम् तु तत् दैवम् भूतेष्व् अपि न हन्यते
व्यक्तम् मयि च तस्याम् च पतितः हि विपर्ययः
transliteration: yad acintyam tu tat daivam bhūteṣv api na hanyate
vyaktam mayi ca tasyām ca patitaḥ hi viparyayaḥ
english: What man dares wiinstand Oh son of Sumitrā, this (terrible) destiny bidden from our view until known by the consequences of action destiny is the prime source of all those inconceivable causes which occur with reference to happiness misery, fear, and anger, profit and loss, birth and deliverance.

sanskrit: कश्चित् दैवेन सौमित्रे योद्धुम् उत्सहते पुमान्
यस्य न ग्रहणम् किम्चित् कर्मणो अन्यत्र दृश्यते
transliteration: kaścit daivena saumitre yoddhum utsahate pumān
yasya na grahaṇam kimcit karmaṇo anyatra dṛśyate
english: What man dares wiinstand Oh son of Sumitrā, this (terrible) destiny bidden from our view until known by the consequences of action destiny is the prime source of all those inconceivable causes which occur with reference to happiness misery, fear, and anger, profit and loss, birth and deliverance.

sanskrit: सुख दुह्खे भय क्रोधौ लाभ अलाभौ भव अभवौ
यस्य किम्चित् तथा भूतम् ननु दैवस्य कर्म तत्
transliteration: sukha duhkhe bhaya krodhau lābha alābhau bhava abhavau
yasya kimcit tathā bhūtam nanu daivasya karma tat
english: Seers of great austerity being influenced by this Destiny, succumb to the attack of anger and desire, renouncing all their hard disciplines.
Seers of great austerity being influenced by this Destiny, succumb to the attack of anger and desire, renouncing all their hard disciplines.
The hindrance in this world to the completion of works taken in hand, and the origination of an unthought of event in its stead is nothing but the action of this Destiny.

sanskrit: व्याहते अपि अभिषेके मे परितापो न विद्यते
transliteration: vyāhate api abhiṣeke me paritāpo na vidyate
english: The mind being brought under discipline by this true rationale, there remains no cause of sorrow regarding my installation being put a stop to.

sanskrit: तस्मात् अपरितापः सम्स् त्वम् अपि अनुविधाय माम्
transliteration: tasmāt aparitāpaḥ sams tvam api anuvidhāya mām
english: Do you therefore assuage your grief and follow me and intercept speedily the collection of materials for my installation.
The bathing ceremony, necessary before taking the vows of asceticism, shall be performed, Oh Laksmana, with all these jars full of water brought for my installation.

sanskrit: उद्धृतम् मे स्वयम् तो यम् व्रतादेशम् करिष्यति
transliteration: uddhṛtam me svayam to yam vratādeśam kariṣyati
english: Or what necessity have I with all these articles of installation; water drawn from the well by myself shall do for entering into the vow of exile.

sanskrit: मा च लक्ष्मण सम्तापम् कार्षीर्लक्ष्म्या विपर्यये
राज्यम् वा वनवासो वा वनवासो महोदयः
transliteration: mā ca lakṣmaṇa samtāpam kārṣīrlakṣmyā viparyaye
rājyam vā vanavāso vā vanavāso mahodayaḥ
english: Do you not grieve, Oh Laksmana, for this loss of kingdom. Of kingdom and exile into the forest, exile is fraught with glorious results.

sanskrit: न लक्ष्मण अस्मिन् मम राज्य विघ्ने
transliteration: na lakṣmaṇa asmin mama rājya vighne
english: Know you now the mighty power of destiny and do you not blame therefore my younger mother and my father labouring under the influence of Destiny.

sanskrit: इति ब्रुवति रामे तु लक्ष्मणो अधः शिरा मुहुः
श्रुत्वा मध्यम् जगाम इव मनसा दुह्ख हर्षयोह्
transliteration: iti bruvati rāme tu lakṣmaṇo adhaḥ śirā muhuḥ
śrutvā madhyam jagāma iva manasā duhkha harṣayoh

sanskrit: तदा तु बद्ध्वा भ्रुकुटीम् भ्रुवोर् मध्ये नर ऋषभ
transliteration: tadā tu baddhvā bhrukuṭīm bhruvor madhye nara ṛṣabha

sanskrit: तस्य दुष्प्रतिवीक्ष्यम् तत् भ्रुकुटी सहितम् तदा
बभौ क्रुद्धस्य सिम्हस्य मुखस्य सदृशम् मुखम्
transliteration: tasya duṣprativīkṣyam tat bhrukuṭī sahitam tadā
babhau kruddhasya simhasya mukhasya sadṛśam mukham

sanskrit: अग्रहः तम् विधुन्वम्स् तु हस्ती हस्तम् इवात्मनः
तिर्यग् ऊर्ध्वम् शरीरे च पातयित्वा शिरः धराम्
transliteration: agrahaḥ tam vidhunvams tu hastī hastam ivātmanaḥ
tiryag ūrdhvam śarīre ca pātayitvā śiraḥ dharām
english: Moving the extremities of his hands like to the trunk of an elephant, variously altering the altitude of the neck above his frame, glancing a look awry, thus spoke he to his brother.

sanskrit: अग्र अक्ष्णा वीक्षमाणः तु तिर्यग् भ्रातरम् अब्रवीत्
अस्थाने सम्भ्रमः यस्य जातः वै सुमहान् अयम्
transliteration: agra akṣṇā vīkṣamāṇaḥ tu tiryag bhrātaram abravīt
asthāne sambhramaḥ yasya jātaḥ vai sumahān ayam

sanskrit: कथम् हि एतत् असम्भ्रान्तः त्वद् विधो वक्तुम् अर्हति
transliteration: katham hi etat asambhrāntaḥ tvad vidho vaktum arhati

sanskrit: यथा दैवम् अशौण्डीरम् शौण्डीरः क्षत्रिय ऋषभः
किम् नाम कृपणम् दैवम् अशक्तम् अभिशम्सति
पापयोस् तु कथम् नाम तयोह् शन्का न विद्यते
transliteration: yathā daivam aśauṇḍīram śauṇḍīraḥ kṣatriya ṛṣabhaḥ
kim nāma kṛpaṇam daivam aśaktam abhiśamsati
pāpayos tu katham nāma tayoh śankā na vidyate

sanskrit: सन्ति धर्म उपधाः श्लक्ष्णा धर्मात्मन् किम् न बुध्यसे
transliteration: santi dharma upadhāḥ ślakṣṇā dharmātman kim na budhyase

sanskrit: यदि नैवम् व्यवसितम् स्याद्धि प्राग्रेव राघव
तयोः प्रागेव दत्तश्च स्याद्वरः प्रकृतश्च सः
transliteration: yadi naivam vyavasitam syāddhi prāgreva rāghava
tayoḥ prāgeva dattaśca syādvaraḥ prakṛtaśca saḥ
english: With a desire to renounce you by fraud, they simulate piety which is but selfishness. Had they not purposed thus, Oh, Rāghava, things would not have taken such a turn. If this story of the vows be true, then why had it not been declared before Surely has the monarch engaged in an action hateful to the people, namely the installation of a younger brother neglecting you (the eldest one). Pray, pardon me, oh great hero, I cannot brook all this.

sanskrit: लोक विद्विष्टम् आरब्धम् त्वद् अन्यस्य अभिषेचनम्
नोत्सहे सहितुम् वीर तत्र मे क्षन्तुमर्हसि
transliteration: loka vidviṣṭam ārabdham tvad anyasya abhiṣecanam
notsahe sahitum vīra tatra me kṣantumarhasi

sanskrit: येन इयम् आगता द्वैधम् तव बुद्धिर् मही पते
स हि धर्मः मम द्वेष्यः प्रसन्गात् यस्य मुह्यसि
transliteration: yena iyam āgatā dvaidham tava buddhir mahī pate
sa hi dharmaḥ mama dveṣyaḥ prasangāt yasya muhyasi
english: Even that so called virtue do I loathe, which has, O high-souled one, fascinated you, and made your mind run from one extreme to another. *Formerly the mind was for accepting the kingdom, and now for going to the forest as an exile. These are the two extremes here meant.
Why shall you, being capable of work, conform to these impious and cursed words of your father, who is sadly under the influence of Kaikeyi.

sanskrit: यद्य् अपि प्रतिपत्तिस् ते दैवी च अपि तयोः मतम्
तथा अपि उपेक्षणीयम् ते न मे तत् अपि रोचते
transliteration: yady api pratipattis te daivī ca api tayoḥ matam
tathā api upekṣaṇīyam te na me tat api rocate

sanskrit: तथा प्युपेक्षणीयम् ते न मे तदपि रोचते
transliteration: tathā pyupekṣaṇīyam te na me tadapi rocate

sanskrit: विक्लवो वीर्य हीनो यः स दैवम् अनुवर्तते
वीराः सम्भावित आत्मानो न दैवम् पर्युपासते
transliteration: viklavo vīrya hīno yaḥ sa daivam anuvartate
vīrāḥ sambhāvita ātmāno na daivam paryupāsate

sanskrit: दैवम् पुरुष कारेण यः समर्थः प्रबाधितुम्
न दैवेन विपन्न अर्थः पुरुषः सो अवसीदति
transliteration: daivam puruṣa kāreṇa yaḥ samarthaḥ prabādhitum
na daivena vipanna arthaḥ puruṣaḥ so avasīdati
english: He, who can avert the consequences of destiny by dint of his manliness, does not lose heart even in the face of his interest being endangered by it.

sanskrit: द्रक्ष्यन्ति तु अद्य दैवस्य पौरुषम् पुरुषस्य च
दैव मानुषयोः अद्य व्यक्ता व्यक्तिर् भविष्यति
transliteration: drakṣyanti tu adya daivasya pauruṣam puruṣasya ca
daiva mānuṣayoḥ adya vyaktā vyaktir bhaviṣyati
english: People shall witness to-day the power of destiny and manliness; this day shall appear which of them is more powerful. Those who have witness before the prevention of your installation by the evil agency of destiny, shall see it defeated, even this very day, by my manliness.

sanskrit: अद्य मत् पौरुष हतम् दैवम् द्रक्ष्यन्ति वै जनाः
यद् दैवात् आहतम् ते अद्य द्Rष्टम् राज्य अभिषेचनम्
transliteration: adya mat pauruṣa hatam daivam drakṣyanti vai janāḥ
yad daivāt āhatam te adya dṣṭam rājya abhiṣecanam

sanskrit: अत्यन्कुशम् इव उद्दामम् गजम् मद बल उद्धतम्
transliteration: atyankuśam iva uddāmam gajam mada bala uddhatam
english: Thwart shall I that assailing destiny by my prowess like to a terrible elephant, freed of its shackles, past the restraining power of a goading hook and inflamed with the juice issuing out of its temples.

sanskrit: लोक पालाः समस्ताः ते न अद्य राम अभिषेचनम्
न च क्Rत्स्नाः त्रयो लोका विहन्युः किम् पुनः पिता
transliteration: loka pālāḥ samastāḥ te na adya rāma abhiṣecanam
na ca ktsnāḥ trayo lokā vihanyuḥ kim punaḥ pitā
english: What of the father, not even all the protectors of the regions nor the entire population of the three worlds shall be able to present any obstacle in the way of Rāma's installation.

sanskrit: यैः विवासः तव अरण्ये मिथो राजन् समर्थितः
अरण्ये तु विवत्स्यन्ति चतुर् दश समाः तथा
transliteration: yaiḥ vivāsaḥ tava araṇye mitho rājan samarthitaḥ
araṇye tu vivatsyanti catur daśa samāḥ tathā
english: Those who have, with one voice oh king, settled about your exile to the forest, shall be banished to-day for fourteen years.

sanskrit: अहम् तदा आशाम् चेत्स्यामि पितुस् तस्याः च या तव
transliteration: aham tadā āśām cetsyāmi pitus tasyāḥ ca yā tava
english: Burn shall I down that hope of my father and Kaikeyi that they want to place Bharata on the throne by hindering your installation.

sanskrit: मद् बलेन विरुद्धाय न स्यात् दैव बलम् तथा
प्रभविष्यति दुह्खाय यथा उग्रम् पौरुषम् मम
transliteration: mad balena viruddhāya na syāt daiva balam tathā
prabhaviṣyati duhkhāya yathā ugram pauruṣam mama
english: Influence of destiny shall not bring my opponents that amount happiness, as the misery inflicted on them by my terrible prowess.

sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वम् वर्ष सहस्र अन्ते प्रजा पाल्यम् अनन्तरम्
आर्य पुत्राः करिष्यन्ति वन वासम् गते त्वयि
transliteration: ūrdhvam varṣa sahasra ante prajā pālyam anantaram
ārya putrāḥ kariṣyanti vana vāsam gate tvayi
english: Yourself retiring to the forest after governing the people for a thousand years, your sons shall resume the administration.

sanskrit: पूर्व राज Rषि व्Rत्त्या हि वन वासो विधीयते
transliteration: pūrva rāja ṣi vttyā hi vana vāso vidhīyate
english: Dwelling into the forest is permitted after making over(the charge of) the subjects to (the hands of the) sons, as did the Rājarsis of old.

sanskrit: स चेद् राजनि अनेक अग्रे राज्य विभ्रम शन्कया
न एवम् इच्चसि धर्मात्मन् राज्यम् राम त्वम् आत्मनि
transliteration: sa ced rājani aneka agre rājya vibhrama śankayā
na evam iccasi dharmātman rājyam rāma tvam ātmani
english: The monarch changing his mind, the kingdom shall be transferred into another's hands, do you, being afraid of this, want to fly as an exile to the forest? And is it for this, that you Oh virtuous souled Rāma, do not wish to have kingdom for you.

sanskrit: प्रतिजाने च ते वीर मा भूवम् वीर लोक भाक्
राज्यम् च तव रक्षेयम् अहम् वेला इव सागरम्
transliteration: pratijāne ca te vīra mā bhūvam vīra loka bhāk
rājyam ca tava rakṣeyam aham velā iva sāgaram
english: I do promise to you, Oh great hero, that I shall protect your kingdom like to shore protecting the sea, or else I shall not attain to the region of heroes.

sanskrit: मन्गलैः अभिषिन्चस्व तत्र त्वम् व्याप्Rतः भव
अहम् एको मही पालान् अलम् वारयितुम् बलात्
transliteration: mangalaiḥ abhiṣincasva tatra tvam vyāptaḥ bhava
aham eko mahī pālān alam vārayitum balāt
english: Do you perform the rites of installation with things necessary for benediction, do you engage in these affairs, myself alone shall be able by force to thwart the opposition of the kings.

sanskrit: न शोभ अर्थाव् इमौ बाहू न धनुर् भूषणाय मे
न असिरा बन्धन अर्थाय न शराः स्तम्भ हेतवः
transliteration: na śobha arthāv imau bāhū na dhanur bhūṣaṇāya me
na asirā bandhana arthāya na śarāḥ stambha hetavaḥ

sanskrit: अमित्र दमन अर्थम् मे सर्वम् एतच् चतुष्टयम्
न च अहम् कामये अत्यर्थम् यः स्यात् शत्रुर् मतः मम
transliteration: amitra damana artham me sarvam etac catuṣṭayam
na ca aham kāmaye atyartham yaḥ syāt śatrur mataḥ mama

sanskrit: असिना तीक्ष्ण धारेण विद्युच् चलित वर्चसा
प्रग्Rहीतेन वै शत्रुम् वज्रिणम् वा न कल्पये
transliteration: asinā tīkṣṇa dhāreṇa vidyuc calita varcasā
praghītena vai śatrum vajriṇam vā na kalpaye

sanskrit: खड्ग निष्पेष निष्पिष्टैः गहना दुश्चरा च मे
हस्ति अश्व नर हस्त ऊरु शिरोभिर् भविता मही
transliteration: khaḍga niṣpeṣa niṣpiṣṭaiḥ gahanā duścarā ca me
hasti aśva nara hasta ūru śirobhir bhavitā mahī
english: Cover thick shall I the field of battle and make it impassable by cutting asunder the trunks of the elephants, thighs of the horses and heads of the infantry.

sanskrit: खड्ग धारा हता मे अद्य दीप्यमानाइव अद्रयः
transliteration: khaḍga dhārā hatā me adya dīpyamānāiva adrayaḥ
english: Being beheaded by my swords like to the flaming fire and besmeared with blood resembling the clouds with lightning, my enemies shall fall down to the ground.

sanskrit: बद्ध गोधा अन्गुलि त्राणे प्रगृहीत शर आसने
कथम् पुरुष मानी स्यात् पुरुषाणाम् मयि स्थिते
transliteration: baddha godhā anguli trāṇe pragṛhīta śara āsane
katham puruṣa mānī syāt puruṣāṇām mayi sthite
english: Who is there, proud of his own prowess, that ! shall be able to withstand me when I shall appear at the battle field with bows and leathern fences of fingers.

sanskrit: बहुभिः च एकम् अत्यस्यन्न् एकेन च बहून् जनान्
विनियोक्ष्याम्य् अहम् बाणान् नृ वाजि गज मर्मसु
transliteration: bahubhiḥ ca ekam atyasyann ekena ca bahūn janān
viniyokṣyāmy aham bāṇān nṛ vāji gaja marmasu
english: Killing one with a number of arrows, and sometimes many with a single one, I shall drive shafts into the vital organs of men, horses and elephants.

sanskrit: अद्य मे अस्त्र प्रभावस्य प्रभावः प्रभविष्यति
राज्ञः च अप्रभुताम् कर्तुम् प्रभुत्वम् च तव प्रभो
transliteration: adya me astra prabhāvasya prabhāvaḥ prabhaviṣyati
rājñaḥ ca aprabhutām kartum prabhutvam ca tava prabho
english: Today shall I display my skill in arms in destroying the supremacy of the monarch and establishing you.

sanskrit: अद्य चन्दन सारस्य केयूरा मोक्षणस्य च
वसूनाम् च विमोक्षस्य सुह्Rदाम् पालनस्य च
transliteration: adya candana sārasya keyūrā mokṣaṇasya ca
vasūnām ca vimokṣasya suhdām pālanasya ca
english: That hand, which is fit for the smearing of the Sandal, for wearing armlets, distributing wealth and maintaining relations, shall be engaged today, Oh Rāma, in performing its worthy action, the discomfiture of them who want to throw obstacles in the way of your installation.

sanskrit: अनुरूपाव् इमौ बाहू राम कर्म करिष्यतः
transliteration: anurūpāv imau bāhū rāma karma kariṣyataḥ
english: That hand, which is fit for the smearing of the Sandal, for wearing armlets, distributing wealth and maintaining relations, shall be engaged today, Oh Rāma, in performing its worthy action, the discomfiture of them who want to throw obstacles in the way of your installation.

sanskrit: ब्रवीहि को अद्य एव मया वियुज्यताम्
तव असुह्Rद् प्राण यशः सुह्Rज् जनैः
यथा तव इयम् वसुधा वशे भवेत्
तथा एव माम् शाधि तव अस्मि किम्करः
transliteration: bravīhi ko adya eva mayā viyujyatām
tava asuhd prāṇa yaśaḥ suhj janaiḥ
yathā tava iyam vasudhā vaśe bhavet
tathā eva mām śādhi tava asmi kimkaraḥ
english: Pray tell me now, which of your enemies shall be cut off by me from wealth, life and relatives? I am your servant: do you give me instruction that the whole earth may be brought under your subjection.

sanskrit: निबोध माम् एष हि सौम्य सत् पथः
transliteration: nibodha mām eṣa hi saumya sat pathaḥ
english: That descendant of Raghu, wiping tears off the eyes of Lakşmaņa and consoling him repeatedly, spoke to him saying “Oh gentle one, I have thought it to be the best way by all means that I shall abide by my father's orders."

sanskrit: तम् समीक्ष्य तु अवहितम् पितुर् निर्देश पालने
कौसल्या बाष्प सम्रुद्धा वचो धर्मिष्ठम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tam samīkṣya tu avahitam pitur nirdeśa pālane
kausalyā bāṣpa samruddhā vaco dharmiṣṭham abravīt
english: Seeing Räma determined upon carrying out his father's behest's, Kausalya with her voice choked with vapour begot of tears, spoke to him the following pious words.

sanskrit: अदृष्ट दुह्खो धर्मात्मा सर्व भूत प्रियम् वदः
मयि जातः दशरथात् कथम् उन्चेन वर्तयेत्
transliteration: adṛṣṭa duhkho dharmātmā sarva bhūta priyam vadaḥ
mayi jātaḥ daśarathāt katham uncena vartayet
english: How shall this virtuous-souled one, beloved of people and who has never experienced misfortune before, live on grains gleaned, being born of me to Dasaratha?

sanskrit: यस्य भृत्याः च दासाः च मृष्टानि अन्नानि भुन्जते
कथम् स भोक्ष्यते नाथो वने मूल फलानि अयम्
transliteration: yasya bhṛtyāḥ ca dāsāḥ ca mṛṣṭāni annāni bhunjate
