सुयज्ञम् स तदा उवाच रामः सीता प्रचोदितः
transliteration: anyaiḥ ca ratnaiḥ bahubhiḥ kākutsthaḥ pratyapūjayat
suyajñam sa tadā uvāca rāmaḥ sītā pracoditaḥ

sanskrit: हारम् च हेम सूत्रम् च भार्यायै सौम्य हारय
रशनाम् च अधुना सीता दातुम् इच्चति ते सखे
transliteration: hāram ca hema sūtram ca bhāryāyai saumya hāraya
raśanām ca adhunā sītā dātum iccati te sakhe

sanskrit: पर्यन्कम् अग्र्य आस्तरणम् नाना रत्न विभूषितम्
transliteration: paryankam agrya āstaraṇam nānā ratna vibhūṣitam

sanskrit: तम् अपि इच्चति वैदेही प्रतिष्ठापयितुम् त्वयि
transliteration: tam api iccati vaidehī pratiṣṭhāpayitum tvayi
english: Vaidehi wishes to present you with this fine bed-stead with its coverlet studded with various precious jewels.

sanskrit: नागः शत्रुम् जयो नाम मातुलो यम् ददौ मम
तम् ते गज सहस्रेण ददामि द्विज पुम्गव
transliteration: nāgaḥ śatrum jayo nāma mātulo yam dadau mama
tam te gaja sahasreṇa dadāmi dvija pumgava
english: I offer you, o great ascetic, with a thousand gold coins, this excellent elephant, called the destroyer of foes, which had been bestowed upon me by my maternal uncle.

sanskrit: इति उक्तः स हि रामेण सुयज्ञः प्रतिगृह्य तत्
राम लक्ष्मण सीतानाम् प्रयुयोज आशिषः शिवाः
transliteration: iti uktaḥ sa hi rāmeṇa suyajñaḥ pratigṛhya tat
rāma lakṣmaṇa sītānām prayuyoja āśiṣaḥ śivāḥ
english: Being addressed thus by Rāma, Sujajña accepted all those offers, and showered benedictions upon Rāma, Sītā, and Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: अथ भ्रातरम् अव्यग्रम् प्रियम् रामः प्रियम् वदः
सौमित्रिम् तम् उवाच इदम् ब्रह्मा इव त्रिदश ईश्वरम्
transliteration: atha bhrātaram avyagram priyam rāmaḥ priyam vadaḥ
saumitrim tam uvāca idam brahmā iva tridaśa īśvaram
english: Thereupon Rāma spoke to his beloved considerate and fair-speaking brother, the son of Sumitrā, the following pleasant words, like to Brahma addressing the Lord of celestials.

sanskrit: अगस्त्यम् कौशिकम् चैव ताव् उभौ ब्राह्मण उत्तमौ
अर्चय आहूय सौमित्रे रत्नैः सस्यम् इव अम्बुभिः
transliteration: agastyam kauśikam caiva tāv ubhau brāhmaṇa uttamau
arcaya āhūya saumitre ratnaiḥ sasyam iva ambubhiḥ
english: O son of Sumiträ, do you invite the excellent Brāhmaṇas, Agastya and Viśvāmitra, and adore them, O Raghava, by conferring upon them gems, as people cherish corn with water.
And, O mighty armed one, do you worship them, O Raghava, with a thousand cows, gold, silver, and various precious jewels.

Do you confer upon that good Brāhmaṇa, the preceptor of the Tittirīya portion of the Vedas, who crowns Kausalyā with blessings every day, silk cloth, conveyances, maid-servants, and such other things, till the twice-born one is satisfied.

sanskrit: तस्य यानम् च दासीः च सौमित्रे सम्प्रदापय
कौशेयानि च वस्त्राणि यावत् तुष्यति स द्विजः
transliteration: tasya yānam ca dāsīḥ ca saumitre sampradāpaya
kauśeyāni ca vastrāṇi yāvat tuṣyati sa dvijaḥ
english: Do you confer upon that good Brāhmaṇa, the preceptor of the Tittirīya portion of the Vedas, who crowns Kausalyā with blessings every day, silk cloth, conveyances, maid-servants, and such other things, till the twice-born one is satisfied.

sanskrit: सूतः चित्र रथः च आर्यः सचिवः सुचिर उषितः
तोषय एनम् महा अर्हैः च रत्नैः वस्त्रैः धनैअः तथा
transliteration: sūtaḥ citra rathaḥ ca āryaḥ sacivaḥ sucira uṣitaḥ
toṣaya enam mahā arhaiḥ ca ratnaiḥ vastraiḥ dhanaiaḥ tathā

sanskrit: शालि वाह सहस्रम् च द्वे शते भद्रकाम्स् तथा
व्यन्जन अर्थम् च सौमित्रे गो सहस्रम् उपाकुरु
transliteration: śāli vāha sahasram ca dve śate bhadrakāms tathā
vyanjana artham ca saumitre go sahasram upākuru

sanskrit: अम्बा यथा च सा नन्देत्कौसल्या मम दक्षिणाम्
transliteration: ambā yathā ca sā nandetkausalyā mama dakṣiṇām

sanskrit: ततः स पुरुष व्याघ्रः तत् धनम् लक्ष्मणः स्वयम्
यथा उक्तम् ब्राह्मण इन्द्राणाम् अददात् धनदो यथा
transliteration: tataḥ sa puruṣa vyāghraḥ tat dhanam lakṣmaṇaḥ svayam
yathā uktam brāhmaṇa indrāṇām adadāt dhanado yathā
english: Thereupon Laksmana, that best of men, distributed amongst all these Brāhmaṇas all the entire riches as ordered by Rāma like to the Lord of wealth.

sanskrit: अथ अब्रवीद् बाष्प कलाम्स् तिष्ठतः च उपजीविनः
transliteration: atha abravīd bāṣpa kalāms tiṣṭhataḥ ca upajīvinaḥ
english: Seeing his dependants in a wretched plight, shedding tears continually, Rāma proffered to them various articles for their maintenance, and said, Do you occupy in turn until our return my rooms as well as Laksmana's.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणस्य च यद् वेश्म गृहम् च यद् इदम् मम
अशून्यम् कार्यम् एकैकम् यावद् आगमनम् मम
transliteration: lakṣmaṇasya ca yad veśma gṛham ca yad idam mama
aśūnyam kāryam ekaikam yāvad āgamanam mama

sanskrit: इति उक्त्वा दुह्खितम् सर्वम् जनम् तम् उपजीविनम्
उवाच इदम् धन ध्यक्षम् धनम् आनीयताम् इति
transliteration: iti uktvā duhkhitam sarvam janam tam upajīvinam
uvāca idam dhana dhyakṣam dhanam ānīyatām iti
english: Having spoken thus to all those dependants who were racked with great sorrow, Rāma ordered the Treasury officer to bring his riches there.

sanskrit: ततः अस्य धनम् आजह्रुः सर्वम् एव उपजीविनः
transliteration: tataḥ asya dhanam ājahruḥ sarvam eva upajīvinaḥ
english: There at, the servants brought all his riches and collected them in great heaps.

sanskrit: ततः स पुरुष व्याघ्रः तत् धनम् सह लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: tataḥ sa puruṣa vyāghraḥ tat dhanam saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Rāma, the best of men, together with Laksmana, distributed them amongst the Brahmanas, boys, the old, and the poor.

sanskrit: तत्र आसीत् पिन्गलो गार्ग्यः त्रिजटः नाम वै द्विजः
transliteration: tatra āsīt pingalo gārgyaḥ trijaṭaḥ nāma vai dvijaḥ
english: There lived in that quarter a Brāhmaṇa of a tawny colour, by name Trijata, descended from the line of Garga, earning his live-hood by digging the earth with spades and ploughs.

sanskrit: तम् वृद्धम् तरुणी भार्या बालानादाय दारकान्
transliteration: tam vṛddham taruṇī bhāryā bālānādāya dārakān
english: His young wife with her little children, struggling with poverty, spoke thus to the old Brāhmaṇa. “Throwing aside your spades and ploughs, do you hear my words. Go and see the virtuous-souled Rāma, and you are sure to get something from him now."

sanskrit: अपास्य फालम् कुद्दालम् कुरुष्व वचनम् ममम्
transliteration: apāsya phālam kuddālam kuruṣva vacanam mamam

english: Hearing these words of his wife. Trijata, shining in effulgence like to Bhſgu and Angirā, covering his body with a torn piece of cloth, proceeded towards Rāma's abode with his wife, and going on in a speedy and uninterrupted course, reached at last the royal abode and spoke to Rama thus:

sanskrit: आ पन्चमायाः कक्ष्याया न एनम् कश्चित् अवारयत्
transliteration: ā pancamāyāḥ kakṣyāyā na enam kaścit avārayat
english: Hearing these words of his wife. Trijata, shining in effulgence like to Bhſgu and Angirā, covering his body with a torn piece of cloth, proceeded towards Rāma's abode with his wife, and going on in a speedy and uninterrupted course, reached at last the royal abode and spoke to Rama thus:

sanskrit: स राज पुत्रम् आसाद्य त्रिजटः वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
निर्धनो बहु पुत्रः अस्मि राज पुत्र महा यशः
transliteration: sa rāja putram āsādya trijaṭaḥ vākyam abravīt
nirdhano bahu putraḥ asmi rāja putra mahā yaśaḥ
english: O mighty son of the King! a poor man am I, having a number of children. I maintain my family by digging the earth; do you therefore look upon me mercifully.

sanskrit: गवाम् सहस्रमप्येकम् न च विश्राणितम् मया
transliteration: gavām sahasramapyekam na ca viśrāṇitam mayā
english: Whereupon Rāma replied laughing: "I have not distributed as yet even one thousand of my cows. Do you hurl this rod, and you are the master of all those cows occupying the space at the extremely of which this rod shall fall."

sanskrit: स शाटीम् त्वरितः कट्याम् सम्ब्रान्तः परिवेष्ट्य ताम्
transliteration: sa śāṭīm tvaritaḥ kaṭyām sambrāntaḥ pariveṣṭya tām
english: Upon this, swiftly tightening the cloth around his waist, Trijața firmly grasping the rod hurled it with a mighty force.
The rod, hurled off his hands, fell on the other side of the river Sarayū in the midst of many thousand bullocks.

Seeing this, the virtuous-souled Rāma despatched to the hermitage of Trijata all the cows that lay extending up to the banks of the river Sarayū, and consoling him afterwards accosted him with the following words. “Be not offended."

sanskrit: मन्युर्न खलु कर्तव्यः परिहासो ह्ययम् मम
transliteration: manyurna khalu kartavyaḥ parihāso hyayam mama
english: Seeing this, the virtuous-souled Rāma despatched to the hermitage of Trijata all the cows that lay extending up to the banks of the river Sarayū, and consoling him afterwards accosted him with the following words. “Be not offended."
I acted thus only as a matter of joke. I asked you to do this only with the object of knowing whether you had the power to hurl this rod. Do you ask of me now anything you like.

Truly do I speak that you should not hesitate. I am ready to devote my wealth to the services of the Brāhmanas. And the wealth I have earned will conduce to my favour, if I can apply it to your service.
Then Trijata, being pleased with the accession of cows, went away along with his wife, showering happiness and joy.

Rama of great manliness afterwards distributed with proper respect and due welcome all his wealth amassed by righteous means amongst the Brāhmaṇas, friends, servants and the poor, according to the recommendation of his friends.

Rama of great manliness afterwards distributed with proper respect and due welcome all his wealth amassed by righteous means amongst the Brāhmaṇas, friends, servants and the poor, according to the recommendation of his friends.

sanskrit: दत्त्वा तु सह वैदेह्या ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनम् बहु
जग्मतुः पितरम् द्रष्टुम् सीतया सह राघवौ
transliteration: dattvā tu saha vaidehyā brāhmaṇebhyo dhanam bahu
jagmatuḥ pitaram draṣṭum sītayā saha rāghavau
english: Having distributed much wealth to the Brāhmaṇas, the Rāghavas set out with $ītā for the purpose of seeing their father.
The two looked beautiful with a couple of handmaids (following them), taking the weapons that had been decked by Sītā with flowery wreaths.

sanskrit: ततः प्रासाद हर्म्याणि विमान शिखराणि च
transliteration: tataḥ prāsāda harmyāṇi vimāna śikharāṇi ca
english: Then crowds of elegantly-attired citizens, mounting on the terraces of three-storied and seven-storied houses, looked on the scene with hearts filled with sorrow.

sanskrit: न हि रथ्याः स्म शक्यन्ते गन्तुम् बहु जन आकुलाः
आरुह्य तस्मात् प्रासादान् दीनाः पश्यन्ति राघवम्
transliteration: na hi rathyāḥ sma śakyante gantum bahu jana ākulāḥ
āruhya tasmāt prāsādān dīnāḥ paśyanti rāghavam
english: Unable to thread the streets because of a vast concourse, they ascending the terraces of the buildings, eyed Rāghava with woebegone eyes.

sanskrit: पदातिम् वर्जितच् चत्रम् रामम् दृष्ट्वा तदा जनाः
ऊचुर् बहु विधा वाचः शोक उपहत चेतसः
transliteration: padātim varjitac catram rāmam dṛṣṭvā tadā janāḥ
ūcur bahu vidhā vācaḥ śoka upahata cetasaḥ
english: And deprived of their senses by grief, the multitudes,* beholding Rāma proceeding on foot in company with Sītā and his younger brother, said. *Another reading i.e., Beholding Rāma without his umbrella and walking a foot.

sanskrit: यम् यान्तम् अनुयाति स्म चतुर् अन्ग बलम् महत्
तम् एकम् सीतया सार्धम् अनुयाति स्म लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: yam yāntam anuyāti sma catur anga balam mahat
tam ekam sītayā sārdham anuyāti sma lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: He that used to be followed by the vast body of the four-fold forces, proceeds now along with Sita, followed by Laksmana alone.

sanskrit: ऐश्वर्यस्य रसज्ञः सन् कामिनाम् चैव कामदः
न इच्चति एव अनृतम् कर्तुम् पितरम् धर्म गौरवात्
transliteration: aiśvaryasya rasajñaḥ san kāminām caiva kāmadaḥ
na iccati eva anṛtam kartum pitaram dharma gauravāt
english: Knowing every kind of enjoyment, that magnanimous one who has tasted of every luxury, for maintaining the dignity of morality, does not wish to falsify (his father's) word.

sanskrit: या न शक्या पुरा द्रष्टुम् भूतैः आकाशगैः अपि
ताम् अद्य सीताम् पश्यन्ति राज मार्ग गता जनाः
transliteration: yā na śakyā purā draṣṭum bhūtaiḥ ākāśagaiḥ api
tām adya sītām paśyanti rāja mārga gatā janāḥ
english: And that Sītā whom formerly the very rangers of the sky could not see, is to-day beheld by the passers-by.

sanskrit: अङ्ग राग उचिताम् सीताम् रक्त चन्दन सेविनीम्
वर्षम् उष्णम् च शीतम् च नेष्यति आशु विवर्णताम्
transliteration: aṅga rāga ucitām sītām rakta candana sevinīm
varṣam uṣṇam ca śītam ca neṣyati āśu vivarṇatām
english: Now summer's heat and winter's cold and the rains of the wet season wil speedily stain Sītā, whose person is worthy of being dyed, and who used to daub her limbs with red sandal paste.

sanskrit: अद्य नूनम् दशरथः सत्त्वम् आविश्य भाषते
न हि राजा प्रियम् पुत्रम् विवासयितुम् अर्हति
transliteration: adya nūnam daśarathaḥ sattvam āviśya bhāṣate
na hi rājā priyam putram vivāsayitum arhati
english: Surely to-day Dasaratha speaks thus, possessed by some evil spirit; for the king ought by no means to banish his beloved son.

sanskrit: निर्गुणस्य अपि पुत्रस्या काथम् स्यात् विप्रवासनम्
किम् पुनर् यस्य लोको अयम् जितः वृत्तेन केवलम्
transliteration: nirguṇasya api putrasyā kātham syāt vipravāsanam
kim punar yasya loko ayam jitaḥ vṛttena kevalam
english: Who ever exiles his son, albeit he be worthless? And what is to be said concerning a son that has fast secured all men's hearts by his behaviour?

sanskrit: आनृशम्स्यम् अनुक्रोशः श्रुतम् शीलम् दमः शमः
राघवम् शोभयन्ति एते षड् गुणाः पुरुष उत्तमम्
transliteration: ānṛśamsyam anukrośaḥ śrutam śīlam damaḥ śamaḥ
rāghavam śobhayanti ete ṣaḍ guṇāḥ puruṣa uttamam
english: Universal benevolence, kindness, learning, goodness, the restraint of the senses, and the control of the faculties, these six qualities adorn that best of men, Rāghava.

sanskrit: तस्मात् तस्य उपघातेन प्रजाः परम पीडिताः
औदकानि इव सत्त्वानि ग्रीष्मे सलिल सम्क्षयात्
transliteration: tasmāt tasya upaghātena prajāḥ parama pīḍitāḥ
audakāni iva sattvāni grīṣme salila samkṣayāt
english: Therefore the subjects will be afflicted in consequence of his separation, even as aquatic animals are, when summer dries up the waters of a tank.

sanskrit: पीडया पीडितम् सर्वम् जगद् अस्य जगत् पतेः
मूलस्य इव उपघातेन वृक्षः पुष्प फल उपगः
transliteration: pīḍayā pīḍitam sarvam jagad asya jagat pateḥ
mūlasya iva upaghātena vṛkṣaḥ puṣpa phala upagaḥ
english: The entire earth is distressed on account of the distress of this lord of the earth, even like a tree bearing blossoms and fruits, when its roots have been severed.

sanskrit: पुष्पम् फलम् च पत्रम् च शाखाश्चा स्येतरे जनाः
transliteration: puṣpam phalam ca patram ca śākhāścā syetare janāḥ
english: Surely this highly effulgent one with virtue for his chief good, is the root of humanity, and the latter represents its flowers, fruits, foliage, and boughs.

sanskrit: ते लक्ष्मणैव क्षिप्रम् सपत्न्यः सह बान्धवाः
transliteration: te lakṣmaṇaiva kṣipram sapatnyaḥ saha bāndhavāḥ
english: Therefore, accompanied by our wives and friends will we like Lakşmaņa follow the departing Rāghava by the same way that he takes.

sanskrit: उद्यानानि परित्यज्य क्षेत्राणि च गृहाणि च
एक दुह्ख सुखा रामम् अनुगच्चाम धार्मिकम्
transliteration: udyānāni parityajya kṣetrāṇi ca gṛhāṇi ca
eka duhkha sukhā rāmam anugaccāma dhārmikam
english: And leaving aside our gardens and fields and abodes, will we, making the righteous Rāma's happiness and misery our own, follow him.

sanskrit: उपात्त धन धान्यानि हृत साराणि सर्वशः
transliteration: upātta dhana dhānyāni hṛta sārāṇi sarvaśaḥ

sanskrit: वनम् नगरम् एव अस्तु येन गच्चति राघवः
अस्माभिः च परित्यक्तम् पुरम् सम्पद्यताम् वनम्
transliteration: vanam nagaram eva astu yena gaccati rāghavaḥ
asmābhiḥ ca parityaktam puram sampadyatām vanam
english: Let the forest to which Rāghava repairs resemble a city, and let this city renounced by as be converted into a wilderness.

sanskrit: बिलानि दम्ष्ट्रिणः सर्वे सानूनि मृग पक्षिणः
अस्मत् त्यक्तम् प्रपद्यन्ताम् सेव्यमानम् त्यजन्तु च
transliteration: bilāni damṣṭriṇaḥ sarve sānūni mṛga pakṣiṇaḥ
asmat tyaktam prapadyantām sevyamānam tyajantu ca

sanskrit: इति एवम् विविधा वाचो नाना जन समीरिताः
transliteration: iti evam vividhā vāco nānā jana samīritāḥ

sanskrit: राघावेण वने सर्वे सह वत्स्याम निर्वृताः
transliteration: rāghāveṇa vane sarve saha vatsyāma nirvṛtāḥ
english: Let them occupy the tracts left behind by us, and let them renounce such abounding in serpents, beasts, and birds, as yield grass, meat, and fruits. Let Kaikeyi (reign in this realm) along with her sons sons and adherents; we, renouncing homes, will dwell in the forest with Raghava.

sanskrit: शुश्राव रामः श्रुत्वा च न विचक्रे अस्य मानसम्
transliteration: śuśrāva rāmaḥ śrutvā ca na vicakre asya mānasam
english: Rāghava heard various words uttered thus by the populace; and having heard them he did not suffer his mind to be agitated. And that righteous one of the prowess of a mad elephant, form a distance began to make for the residence of his father resembiing in brightness a summit of the Kailasa mountain.

Rāghava heard various words uttered thus by the populace; and having heard them he did not suffer his mind to be agitated. And that righteous one of the prowess of a mad elephant, form a distance began to make for the residence of his father resembiing in brightness a summit of the Kailasa mountain.
Entering the king's mansion, he drawing nigh found the heroic Sumantra seated in dejected mood.
Seeing that well-wisher of his thus depressed, Rāma endeavouring by all means to do his father's bidding, cheerfully went on, desirous of beholding his sire.

And with the view of meeting the aggrieved king before repairing to the forest, the magnanimous son of the Ikşvāku race, seeing Sumantra, stayed there, so that that nobleminded one might inform his father of his visit.
And making up his mind to go to the woods in accordance with the command of his father, Rāghava seeing Sumantra, said to him; “Do you inform the king of my arrival. to

Then the mighty and incomparable Rāma of eyes resembling lotus-petals said the charioteer, "Do you announce me to my father.” Thus commissioned by Rāma, the charioteer entering the apartment, found the king heaving sighs, his senses overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: स राम प्रेषितः क्षिप्रम् सम्ताप कलुष इन्द्रियः
प्रविश्य नृपतिम् सूतः निह्श्वसन्तम् ददर्श ह
transliteration: sa rāma preṣitaḥ kṣipram samtāpa kaluṣa indriyaḥ
praviśya nṛpatim sūtaḥ nihśvasantam dadarśa ha
english: Then the mighty and incomparable Rāma of eyes resembling lotus-petals said the charioteer, "Do you announce me to my father.” Thus commissioned by Rāma, the charioteer entering the apartment, found the king heaving sighs, his senses overwhelmed with grief.

And he saw the monarch like the sun afflicted by Rāhu, or like fire enveloped in ashes, or like a i tank deprived of its waters. Thereupon concluding that the king agitated by sorrow was bewailing Rāma, the charioteer said with joined hands.

sanskrit: आलोक्य तु महा प्राज्ञः परम आकुल चेतसम्
रामम् एव अनुशोचन्तम् सूतः प्रान्जलिर् आसदत्
transliteration: ālokya tu mahā prājñaḥ parama ākula cetasam
rāmam eva anuśocantam sūtaḥ prānjalir āsadat

sanskrit: तम् वर्धयित्वा राजानम् सूतः पूर्वम् जयाशिषा
transliteration: tam vardhayitvā rājānam sūtaḥ pūrvam jayāśiṣā
english: And first paying homage to the king, invoking victory upon him, the charioteer, perplexed with fear, softly and sweetly addressed the monarch thus:

sanskrit: अयम् स पुरुष व्याघ्र द्वारि तिष्ठति ते सुतः
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो धनम् दत्त्वा सर्वम् चैव उपजीविनाम्
transliteration: ayam sa puruṣa vyāghra dvāri tiṣṭhati te sutaḥ
brāhmaṇebhyo dhanam dattvā sarvam caiva upajīvinām

sanskrit: स त्वा पश्यतु भद्रम् ते रामः सत्य पराक्रमः
transliteration: sa tvā paśyatu bhadram te rāmaḥ satya parākramaḥ

sanskrit: गमिष्यति महा अरण्यम् तम् पश्य जगती पते
वृतम् राज गुणैः सर्वैः आदित्यम् इव रश्मिभिः
transliteration: gamiṣyati mahā araṇyam tam paśya jagatī pate
vṛtam rāja guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ ādityam iva raśmibhiḥ

sanskrit: स सत्य वादी धर्म आत्मा गाम्भीर्यात् सागर उपमः
आकाशैव निष्पन्को नर इन्द्रः प्रत्युवाच तम्
transliteration: sa satya vādī dharma ātmā gāmbhīryāt sāgara upamaḥ
ākāśaiva niṣpanko nara indraḥ pratyuvāca tam
english: Thereupon, that virtuous and truthful (king) resembling the ocean by virtue of his gravity, and motionless like the welkin, answered Sumantra, saying.

sanskrit: सुमन्त्र आनय मे दारान् ये केचित् इह मामकाः
दारैः परिवृतः सर्वैः द्रष्टुम् इच्चामि राघवम्
transliteration: sumantra ānaya me dārān ye kecit iha māmakāḥ
dāraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvaiḥ draṣṭum iccāmi rāghavam
english: O Sumantra, you bring hither my wives. who are here. I wish to see Rāma accompained with my wives.

sanskrit: सो अन्तः पुरम् अतीत्य एव स्त्रियः ता वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
आर्यो ह्वयति वो राजा गम्यताम् तत्र माचिरम्
transliteration: so antaḥ puram atītya eva striyaḥ tā vākyam abravīt
āryo hvayati vo rājā gamyatām tatra māciram
english: Reaching the inner apartment, the charioteer said to the ladies, “The worshipful king calls you. Do you come speedily."

sanskrit: एवम् उक्ताः स्त्रियः सर्वाः सुमन्त्रेण नृप आज्ञया
प्रचक्रमुस् तत् भवनम् भर्तुर् आज्ञाय शासनम्
transliteration: evam uktāḥ striyaḥ sarvāḥ sumantreṇa nṛpa ājñayā
pracakramus tat bhavanam bhartur ājñāya śāsanam
english: Thus addressed by Sumantra at the mandate of the monarch, the ladies in a body, informed of their husband's command, went to the king's apartment.

sanskrit: अर्ध सप्त शताः ताः तु प्रमदाः ताम्र लोचनाः
कौसल्याम् परिवार्य अथ शनैः जग्मुर् धृत व्रताः
transliteration: ardha sapta śatāḥ tāḥ tu pramadāḥ tāmra locanāḥ
kausalyām parivārya atha śanaiḥ jagmur dhṛta vratāḥ
english: And three hundred and fifty females furnished with coppery eyes and observing vows, surrounding Kausalyā, proceeded slowly.

sanskrit: आगतेषु च दारेषु समवेक्ष्य मही पतिः
उवाच राजा तम् सूतम् सुमन्त्र आनय मे सुतम्
transliteration: āgateṣu ca dāreṣu samavekṣya mahī patiḥ
uvāca rājā tam sūtam sumantra ānaya me sutam
english: On the females coming there, the monarch seeing this, said to the charioteer, “O Sumantra, do you bring hither my son."

sanskrit: स सूतः रामम् आदाय लक्ष्मणम् मैथिलीम् तदा
जगाम अभिमुखः तूर्णम् सकाशम् जगती पतेः
transliteration: sa sūtaḥ rāmam ādāya lakṣmaṇam maithilīm tadā
jagāma abhimukhaḥ tūrṇam sakāśam jagatī pateḥ
english: Thereat the charioteer taking Răma, Lakşmaņa an Mithila's daughter, speedily came before the lord of earth.

sanskrit: स राजा पुत्रम् आयान्तम् दृष्ट्वा दूरात् कृत अन्जलिम्
उत्पपात आसनात् तूर्णम् आर्तः स्त्री जन सम्वृतः
transliteration: sa rājā putram āyāntam dṛṣṭvā dūrāt kṛta anjalim
utpapāta āsanāt tūrṇam ārtaḥ strī jana samvṛtaḥ
english: The king seeing his son drawing nigh with joined hands, nastily rose up from his seat in company with his wives.

sanskrit: सो अभिदुद्राव वेगेन रामम् दृष्ट्वा विशाम् पतिः
तम् असम्प्राप्य दुह्ख आर्तः पपात भुवि मूर्चितः
transliteration: so abhidudrāva vegena rāmam dṛṣṭvā viśām patiḥ
tam asamprāpya duhkha ārtaḥ papāta bhuvi mūrcitaḥ
english: And casting his eyes on Rāma, the king rushed towards him, but before reaching his son, the aggrieved monarch fell down to the earth in a Swoon.

sanskrit: तम् रामः अभ्यपातत् क्षिप्रम् लक्ष्मणः च महा रथः
विसम्ज्ञम् इव दुह्खेन सशोकम् नृपतिम् तदा
transliteration: tam rāmaḥ abhyapātat kṣipram lakṣmaṇaḥ ca mahā rathaḥ
visamjñam iva duhkhena saśokam nṛpatim tadā
english: Rāma and that mighty car-warrior Lakşmaņa swiftly neared the king stricken with grief and rendered senseless by sorrow.

sanskrit: स्त्री सहस्र निनादः च सम्जज्ञे राज वेश्मनि
हाहा राम इति सहसा भूषण ध्वनि मूर्चितः
transliteration: strī sahasra ninādaḥ ca samjajñe rāja veśmani
hāhā rāma iti sahasā bhūṣaṇa dhvani mūrcitaḥ
english: And there arose in the palace cries of women by thousands of "Ah Rāma,” mingled with the tinkling of ornaments.

sanskrit: तम् परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्याम् ताव् उभौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: tam pariṣvajya bāhubhyām tāv ubhau rāma lakṣmaṇau
english: Then both Rāma and Lakşmaņa along with Sītā took the king up with their arms, and with tears in their eyes laid him upon the couch.

sanskrit: अथ रामः मुहूर्तेन लब्ध सम्ज्ञम् मही पतिम्
उवाच प्रान्जलिर् भूत्वा शोक अर्णव परिप्लुतम्
transliteration: atha rāmaḥ muhūrtena labdha samjñam mahī patim
uvāca prānjalir bhūtvā śoka arṇava pariplutam
english: When the lord of the earth oppressed with the vapour begot of grief and overwhelmed with emotion, had regained his senses, Rāma with joined palms said.

sanskrit: आपृच्चे त्वाम् महा राज सर्वेषाम् ईश्वरः असि नः
प्रस्थितम् दण्डक अरण्यम् पश्य त्वम् कुशलेन माम्
transliteration: āpṛcce tvām mahā rāja sarveṣām īśvaraḥ asi naḥ
prasthitam daṇḍaka araṇyam paśya tvam kuśalena mām
english: I ask you, O mighty monarch, as you are the lord of us all. Do you see me safely despatched to the forest of Dandaka.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणम् च अनुजानीहि सीता च अन्वेति माम् वनम्
कारणैः बहुभिस् तथ्यैः वार्यमाणौ न च इच्चतः
transliteration: lakṣmaṇam ca anujānīhi sītā ca anveti mām vanam
kāraṇaiḥ bahubhis tathyaiḥ vāryamāṇau na ca iccataḥ
english: Do you permit Lakşmaņa, and let Sītā also follow me to the woods; for although prohibited by me with various reasons, they do not wish to be left behind. Do you O bestower of honour, permit us all, renouncing sorrow, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā and me, like Prajāpati permitting his sons.

sanskrit: अनुजानीहि सर्वान् नः शोकम् उत्सृज्य मानद
लक्ष्मणम् माम् च सीताम् च प्रजापतिर् इव प्रजाः
transliteration: anujānīhi sarvān naḥ śokam utsṛjya mānada
lakṣmaṇam mām ca sītām ca prajāpatir iva prajāḥ

sanskrit: उवाच रर्जा सम्प्रेक्ष्य वन वासाय राघवम्
transliteration: uvāca rarjā samprekṣya vana vāsāya rāghavam
english: Seeing Rāghava about to set out for the forest, the lord of earth said to the calm Rāma waiting for his orders.

sanskrit: अहम् राघव कैकेय्या वर दानेन मोहितः
अयोध्यायाः त्वम् एव अद्य भव राजा निगृह्य माम्
transliteration: aham rāghava kaikeyyā vara dānena mohitaḥ
ayodhyāyāḥ tvam eva adya bhava rājā nigṛhya mām
english: O Rāghava, I have been deprived of my senses in consequence of my having conferred boons on Kaikeyi. Do you therefore confining me to-day become king in Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः नृपतिना रामः धर्मभृताम् वरः
प्रत्युवाच अन्जलिम् कृत्वा पितरम् वाक्य कोविदः
transliteration: evam uktaḥ nṛpatinā rāmaḥ dharmabhṛtām varaḥ
pratyuvāca anjalim kṛtvā pitaram vākya kovidaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the monarch, Rāma, the best of the righteous, well versed in speech, with joined hands addressed his father thus.

sanskrit: भवान् वर्ष सहस्राय पृथिव्या नृपते पतिः
अहम् तु अरण्ये वत्स्यामि न मे कार्यम् त्वया अनृतम्
transliteration: bhavān varṣa sahasrāya pṛthivyā nṛpate patiḥ
aham tu araṇye vatsyāmi na me kāryam tvayā anṛtam
english: O king, do you rule this earth for a thousand years, I will reside in the forest. I do not wish for the kingdom.

sanskrit: नव पञ्च च वर्षाणि वनवासे विहृत्य ते
transliteration: nava pañca ca varṣāṇi vanavāse vihṛtya te
english: Having spent five and nine years in the woods, I shall again embrace your feet, O lord of men, after fulfilling your vow.
Fettered in the net of promise, the king bewailing his beloved son, secretly spurred on by Kaikeyi, said.

sanskrit: श्रेयसे वृद्धये तात पुनर् आगमनाय च
गच्चस्व अरिष्टम् अव्यग्रः पन्थानम् अकुतः भयम्
transliteration: śreyase vṛddhaye tāta punar āgamanāya ca
gaccasva ariṣṭam avyagraḥ panthānam akutaḥ bhayam
english: Do you, my darling, with the view of attaining welfare here and hereafter and auspicious fortune, go calmly your fearless way, so that you may return hither (in time.)

I dare not, O descendant of the Raghu race, forbid you who are established in truth and who are bent upon discharging your duty. But, O son, do not by any means depart to night: beholding you even for a single day, I shall feed with you.

sanskrit: अद्य तु इदानीम् रजनीम् पुत्र मा गच्च सर्वथा
मातरम् माम् च सम्पश्यन् वस इमाम् अद्य शर्वरीम्
transliteration: adya tu idānīm rajanīm putra mā gacca sarvathā
mātaram mām ca sampaśyan vasa imām adya śarvarīm

sanskrit: मातरं माम् च सम्पश्यन् वसेमामद्य शर्वरीम्
transliteration: mātaraṃ mām ca sampaśyan vasemāmadya śarvarīm
english: Do you, seeing me as well as your mother, stay here to-night, Then ministered to every way, you will set out to-morrow.

sanskrit: दुष्करम् क्रियते पुत्र सर्वथा राघव तया
transliteration: duṣkaram kriyate putra sarvathā rāghava tayā
english: O son, O beloved Rāghava, difficult is the task that you are going to perform, for compassing my good in the next world, you are ready to repair to the very woods!

sanskrit: न चैतन्मे प्रियम् पुत्र शपे सत्येन राघव
transliteration: na caitanme priyam putra śape satyena rāghava
english: But, O Raghava, I swear to you, this is anything but agreeable to me, my son. I have been made to swerve from my purpose by the crafty Kaikeyi resembling a fire hidden under ashes. You are going to give effect to the deceit that has been practised upon me by this woman intent upon sullying her line.

sanskrit: पञ्चना या तु लब्धा मे तां त्वम् निस्तर्तुमिच्छसि
transliteration: pañcanā yā tu labdhā me tāṃ tvam nistartumicchasi
english: But, O Raghava, I swear to you, this is anything but agreeable to me, my son. I have been made to swerve from my purpose by the crafty Kaikeyi resembling a fire hidden under ashes. You are going to give effect to the deceit that has been practised upon me by this woman intent upon sullying her line.
And as you are my eldest son, it is no wonder, O son, that you should wish to maintain your father's truth.

sanskrit: अथ रामः तथा श्रुत्वा पितुर् आर्तस्य भाषितम्
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा दीनो वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: atha rāmaḥ tathā śrutvā pitur ārtasya bhāṣitam
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā dīno vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing these words of his distressed father, the humble Rāma, along with his brother Laksmana, said.

sanskrit: प्राप्स्यामि यान् अद्य गुणान् को मे श्वस्तान् प्रदास्यति
अपक्रमणम् एव अतः सर्व कामैः अहम् वृणे
transliteration: prāpsyāmi yān adya guṇān ko me śvastān pradāsyati
apakramaṇam eva ataḥ sarva kāmaiḥ aham vṛṇe
english: Who will confer on me the merit to-morrow that I shall reap by going to-day? Therefore, I prefer even the journey to the woods to enjoying comforts here.

sanskrit: इयम् सराष्ट्रा सजना धन धान्य समाकुला
transliteration: iyam sarāṣṭrā sajanā dhana dhānya samākulā

sanskrit: यस्तुष्टेन वरो दत्तः कैकेय्यै वरद त्वया
transliteration: yastuṣṭena varo dattaḥ kaikeyyai varada tvayā
english: Do you bestow upon Bharata this earth renounced by me, this kingdom abounding in corn and kine and filled with people; my mind determined upon dwelling in the forest, does not waver. Do you, O bestower of boons, grant Kaikeyi everything that you had promised to her at the time of the war* Another reading is, The boon that you had well-pleased conferred., Another reading, Nor Mithila's daughter., Another reading is, Nor any of these worlds., (you had waged against the Dänavas), and thereby do you follow truth.

sanskrit: चतुर्दश समा वत्स्ये वने वनचरैः सह
transliteration: caturdaśa samā vatsye vane vanacaraiḥ saha
english: Obeying the mandate that you have issued, I will dwell in the forest for fourteen years in the company of the rangers of the woods. Do you without feeling any compunction confer the earth on Bharata.

sanskrit: न हि मे काम्क्षितम् राज्यम् सुखमात्मनि वा प्रियम्
यथा निदेशम् कर्तुम् वै तवैव रघुनन्धन
transliteration: na hi me kāmkṣitam rājyam sukhamātmani vā priyam
yathā nideśam kartum vai tavaiva raghunandhana
english: Mine is not the desire to obtain the kingdom for enjoying happiness or attaining any benefit. I will, O descendant of the Raghu race, do your bidding.

sanskrit: अपगच्चतु ते दुह्खम् मा भूर् बाष्प परिप्लुतः
न हि क्षुभ्यति दुर्धर्षः समुद्रः सरिताम् पतिः
transliteration: apagaccatu te duhkham mā bhūr bāṣpa pariplutaḥ
na hi kṣubhyati durdharṣaḥ samudraḥ saritām patiḥ
english: Banish your grief, and suppress your tears. That lord of streams, the irresistible ocean, never forsakes his own magnanimity.

sanskrit: न एव अहम् राज्यम् इच्चामि न सुखम् न च मैथिलीम्
त्वाम् अहम् सत्यम् इच्चामि न अनृतम् पुरुष ऋषभ
transliteration: na eva aham rājyam iccāmi na sukham na ca maithilīm
tvām aham satyam iccāmi na anṛtam puruṣa ṛṣabha

sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षम् तव सत्येन सुकृतेन च ते शपे
transliteration: pratyakṣam tava satyena sukṛtena ca te śape
english: O foremost of men, all I wish for is that you may not come by falsehood, and abide by truth. I truly and in good sooth swear before you that I cannot, O lord, remain here for a moment longer, O my father. Do you bear this grief. I cannot for certain act contrary to my promise.

sanskrit: न च शख्यम् मया तात स्थातुम् क्षणमपि प्रभो
स शोकम् ध्रारयस्वेमम् न हि मेऽस्ति विपर्ययः
transliteration: na ca śakhyam mayā tāta sthātum kṣaṇamapi prabho
sa śokam dhrārayasvemam na hi me'sti viparyayaḥ
english: O foremost of men, all I wish for is that you may not come by falsehood, and abide by truth. I truly and in good sooth swear before you that I cannot, O lord, remain here for a moment longer, O my father. Do you bear this grief. I cannot for certain act contrary to my promise.

sanskrit: अर्थितो ह्यस्मि कैकेय्या वनम् गच्छेति राघव
transliteration: arthito hyasmi kaikeyyā vanam gaccheti rāghava
english: Directed by Kaikeyi saying, 'Do you, O Rāghava, go to the forest,' I had said, 'I will go,', That promise I must accomplish.

sanskrit: मा चोत्कण्थां कृथा देव वने रम्स्यामहे वयम्
transliteration: mā cotkaṇthāṃ kṛthā deva vane ramsyāmahe vayam
english: Do you not, O revered one, feel aggrieved. We will abide in the forest abounding in mild deer and resounding with the notes of various birds.

sanskrit: पिता हि दैवतम् तात देवतानामपि स्मृतम्
transliteration: pitā hi daivatam tāta devatānāmapi smṛtam
english: The father is a very God, even the celestials say this. Therefore will I look upon your word in the light of divinity.
O best of monarchs, after the fourteen years have been spent, you will see me again by your side, therefore do you banish this grief.

sanskrit: स त्वम् पुरुषशार्दूल किमर्थम् विक्रियाम् गतः
transliteration: sa tvam puruṣaśārdūla kimartham vikriyām gataḥ
english: Why do you, O foremost of men, who will suppress other's grief, undergo this alteration?

sanskrit: पुरम् च राष्ट्रम् च मही च केवला
transliteration: puram ca rāṣṭram ca mahī ca kevalā
english: Do upon Bharata this city and this kingdom and the earth renounced by me. Doing your behest, I will repair to the forest, sojourning there for a long time.

sanskrit: त्वया यद् उक्तम् नृपते यथा अस्तु तत्
transliteration: tvayā yad uktam nṛpate yathā astu tat
english: Staying at the auspicious frontiers, let Bharata barely rule this earth furnished with watery expanses, cities and forests, when it has been renounced by me. O king, let what you have said be as you wish it.

sanskrit: न मे तथा पार्थिव धीयते मनो
महत्सु कामेषु न च आत्मनः प्रिये
व्यपैतु दुह्खम् तव मत् कृते अनघ
transliteration: na me tathā pārthiva dhīyate mano
mahatsu kāmeṣu na ca ātmanaḥ priye
vyapaitu duhkham tava mat kṛte anagha
english: You confer I do not, O king, set my heart upon any great object of desire, nor do I seek my own behoof, as I am bent upon, O you beloved of the good, working out your will. O sinless one, you will not therefore reap any evil on my account.

sanskrit: तत् अद्य न एव अनघ राज्यम् अव्ययम्
न सर्व कामान् न सुखम् न मैथिलीम्
वृणीय सत्यम् व्रतम् अस्तु ते तथा
transliteration: tat adya na eva anagha rājyam avyayam
na sarva kāmān na sukham na maithilīm
vṛṇīya satyam vratam astu te tathā
english: Associating you with untruth, I would not, O sinless one, wish even for your company who are agitated with anxiety,* or this entire kingdom, or every object of desire, or the earth, or Mithilā's daughter. Even this is my truthful vow, let also your vow prove true. *Some texts, Living.

sanskrit: गिरीमः च पश्यन् सरितः सराम्सि च
transliteration: girīmaḥ ca paśyan saritaḥ sarāmsi ca
english: Living upon fruits and roots in the forest, and surveying mountains and tanks and streams and graceful trees, I shall be happy on entering the forest. Do you cease to lament.
Thus benetted with calamities and exercised with grief and anguish, the king embraced his son, and then deprived of his consciousness, fell down on the ground and became motionless.

sanskrit: हा हा कृतम् तत्र बभूव सर्वम्
transliteration: hā hā kṛtam tatra babhūva sarvam
english: Thereat all the queens save that wife of the monarch (Kaikeyi) bewailed together; and crying Sumantra also went into a swoon. And the place was filled all around with exclamations of “O” and “Alas"

sanskrit: ततो निर्धूय सहसा शिरो निःश्वस्व चासकृत्
पाणौ पाणिम् विनिष्पिष्य दन्तान् कटकटाय्य च
transliteration: tato nirdhūya sahasā śiro niḥśvasva cāsakṛt
pāṇau pāṇim viniṣpiṣya dantān kaṭakaṭāyya ca

sanskrit: भर्ता सर्वस्य जगतः स्थावरस्य चरश्य च
transliteration: bhartā sarvasya jagataḥ sthāvarasya caraśya ca
english: O worshipful one, since you have forsaken king Dasaratha, the maintainer of this world and the mobile and the immobile that it contains, there is nothing that is incapable of being done by you. I consider you the murderess of your husband and as one that has finally exterminated one's line.

sanskrit: न ह्यकार्यतमम् किम्चित् तव देवीह विद्यते
transliteration: na hyakāryatamam kimcit tava devīha vidyate
english: O worshipful one, since you have forsaken king Dasaratha, the maintainer of this world and the mobile and the immobile that it contains, there is nothing that is incapable of being done by you. I consider you the murderess of your husband and as one that has finally exterminated one's line.
Inasmuch as you have by your act afflicted the Monarch invincible like Indra, firm as a hill and imperturbable like the deep itself.
You ought not to bring down your boonbestowing lord and husband Daśaratha; for surely the wish of a husband to a wife outweighs a koti of sons.
The princes will obtain the kingdom one after another according to age;, this custom it is your study to render nugatory even when the lord of the Ikşvāku race is still alive.

sanskrit: राजा भवतु ते पुत्रो भरतश्शास्तु मेदिनीम्
वयम् तत्र गमिष्यामो रामो यत्र गमिष्यति
transliteration: rājā bhavatu te putro bharataśśāstu medinīm
vayam tatra gamiṣyāmo rāmo yatra gamiṣyati
english: Let your son be king; let Bharata rule the earth: we, however, will go where goes Ráma.

sanskrit: न हि ते विषये कश्चिद्ब्राह्मणो वस्तुमर्हति
transliteration: na hi te viṣaye kaścidbrāhmaṇo vastumarhati
english: No Brāhmaṇa will dwell in your dominion, such is the ungracious deed you are going to do. [Surely we will go the way that is wended by Rama.
And what happiness, O revered one, will you, forsaken by friends, Brāhmaṇas and the saintly, reap by remaining here, allured by the lust of dominion? And you are going to do such an act!]

sanskrit: का प्रीती राज्यलाभेन तव देवि भविष्यति
transliteration: kā prītī rājyalābhena tava devi bhaviṣyati
english: And what happiness, O revered one, will you, forsaken by friends, Brāhmaṇas and the saintly, reap by remaining here, allured by the lust of dominion? And you are going to do such an act!]

sanskrit: आचरन्त्या न विदृता सद्यो भवति मेदिनी
transliteration: ācarantyā na vidṛtā sadyo bhavati medinī
english: A wonder it is that I perceive, viz., that the carth hid by a character like you is not riven this very day.
Why does not the flaming and dreadful censure uttered by the mighty Brahmarşis destroy you who are bent upon banishing Rāma?

sanskrit: आम्रम् चित्वा कुठारेन निम्बम् परिचरेत्तु यः
transliteration: āmram citvā kuṭhārena nimbam paricarettu yaḥ
english: Who having hewn a mango tree by his axe, tend a Nimba? It never turns sweet for him that waters it.

sanskrit: अभिजात्यम् हि ते मन्ये यथा मातुस्तथैव च
न हि निम्बात्स्रवेत्क्षौद्रम् लोके निगदितम् वचः
transliteration: abhijātyam hi te manye yathā mātustathaiva ca
na hi nimbātsravetkṣaudram loke nigaditam vacaḥ
english: Your birth is noble indeed; it is as much so as is your mother's. They say that sweet is never extracted from Nimba.
I remember what I have heard from old men concerning the vicious inclinations of your mother. Some one intent upon conferring boons conferred an excellent one on your father.

sanskrit: तेन तिर्यग्गतानाम् च भूतानाम् विदितम् वचः
transliteration: tena tiryaggatānām ca bhūtānām viditam vacaḥ
english: In virtue of this, that lord of earth could understand the import of sounds emitted by all beings, and it is in consequence of this that he could understand the speech even of birds and beasts.

sanskrit: पितुस्ते विदितो भावः स तत्र बहुधाऽहसत्
transliteration: pituste vidito bhāvaḥ sa tatra bahudhā'hasat
english: One day as your father was lying down, he, understanding the thoughts of a gold-hued Jrmbha bird, from its cries, laughed heartily.

sanskrit: हासम् ते नृपते सौम्य जिज्ञासामीति भाब्रवीत्
transliteration: hāsam te nṛpate saumya jijñāsāmīti bhābravīt
english: Thereat your mother getting angry, wishing for the noose of death, said, 'O king, O placid one, I ask you for the reason of your daughter.'

sanskrit: नृपश्चोवाच ताम् देवीम् देवि शम्सामि ते यदि
ततो मे मरणम् सद्यो भविष्यति न सम्शयः
transliteration: nṛpaścovāca tām devīm devi śamsāmi te yadi
tato me maraṇam sadyo bhaviṣyati na samśayaḥ
english: The king replied, 'O worshipful lady, if I unfold to you the reason of my laugh, then I shall without doubt die to day.'

sanskrit: माता ते पितरम् देवि ततह् केकयमब्रवीत्
शम्स मे जीव वा मा वा न मामपहसिष्यसि
transliteration: mātā te pitaram devi tatah kekayamabravīt
śamsa me jīva vā mā vā na māmapahasiṣyasi
english: But that revered one, your mother, again urged Kekaya, saying, 'Tell it to me, whether you live or die; for (when I have learnt all about it), you will not be able to laugh at me again.

sanskrit: प्रियया च तथोक्तः सन् केकयः पृथीवीपतिः
transliteration: priyayā ca tathoktaḥ san kekayaḥ pṛthīvīpatiḥ
english: Thus addressed by his beloved spouse, that lord of earth Kekaya went to the saint that had conferred the boon on him and related to him everything faithfully.

sanskrit: ततः स वरदह् साधु राजानम् प्रत्यभाषत
म्रियताम् ध्वम्सताम् वेयम् मा कृथास्त्वम् महीपते
transliteration: tataḥ sa varadah sādhu rājānam pratyabhāṣata
mriyatām dhvamsatām veyam mā kṛthāstvam mahīpate
english: Thereupon that boon-giving saint said to the king; “Whether this one kills herself or be destroyed, do you not, O king, reveal it."
Hearing these words of his, the king well pleased summarily forsook your mother and began to divert himself like Kuvera.
Even in the same way, you, O you that see only evil, staying in an unrighteous course, befouling the king's sense, endeavour to make him commit this wrong.
In this connection I remember a saying, viz., men take after their fathers, and women their mothers.
Do not be so, do you even accept what the lord of earth says. Doing the will of your lord, do you become the refuge of us all.
Do not incited by evil propensities, make your husband, the lord of men endued with the prowess of the celestial chief, perpetrate an unrighteous deed.

sanskrit: न हि मिथ्या प्रतिज्ञातम् करिष्यति तवानघः
transliteration: na hi mithyā pratijñātam kariṣyati tavānaghaḥ

sanskrit: परिवादो हि ते देवि महान्लोके चरिष्यति
यदि रामो वनम् याति विहाय पितरम् नृपम्
transliteration: parivādo hi te devi mahānloke cariṣyati
yadi rāmo vanam yāti vihāya pitaram nṛpam

sanskrit: स राज्यम् राघवः पातु भवत्वम् विगतज्वरा
न हि ते राघवादन्यः क्षमः पुरवरे वसेत्
transliteration: sa rājyam rāghavaḥ pātu bhavatvam vigatajvarā
na hi te rāghavādanyaḥ kṣamaḥ puravare vaset
english: Let therefore Rāghava govern his kingdom; and do you remove your agitation. Surely save Rāghava none residing in the kingdom will prove friendly to you.

sanskrit: रामे हि यौवराज्यस्थे राजा दशरथो वनम्
transliteration: rāme hi yauvarājyasthe rājā daśaratho vanam
english: On Rāma being installed as the heir-apparent, that best of bowmen, king Dasaratha, will depart for the forest, remembering ancient examples.

sanskrit: नैवसाक्षुभ्यते देवी न च स्म परिदूयते
न चास्या मुखवर्णस्य विक्रिया लक्ष्यते तदा
transliteration: naivasākṣubhyate devī na ca sma paridūyate
na cāsyā mukhavarṇasya vikriyā lakṣyate tadā
english: Thus in presence of the king, Sumantra with clasped palms, with soft yet cutting words endeavoured to strike Kaikeyi with regret. But that noble dame did not feel any compunction, nor was she touched 'with regret. And the complexion of her countenance remained as it was before.

sanskrit: ततः सुमन्त्रम् ऐक्ष्वाकः पीडितः अत्र प्रतिज्ञया
सबाष्पम् अतिनिह्श्वस्य जगाद इदम् पुनः पुनः
transliteration: tataḥ sumantram aikṣvākaḥ pīḍitaḥ atra pratijñayā
sabāṣpam atinihśvasya jagāda idam punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then that descendant of Ikṣvāku afflicted because of his promise, sighing and his heart filled with the vapour begot of sorrow, again addressed Sumantra, saying.

sanskrit: सूत रत्न सुसम्पूर्णा चतुर् विध बला चमूः
transliteration: sūta ratna susampūrṇā catur vidha balā camūḥ
english: O charioteer, do you speedily Marshall the army consisting of the four kinds of forces for following Rāghava.

sanskrit: रूप आजीवा च शालिन्यो वणिजः च महा धनाः
transliteration: rūpa ājīvā ca śālinyo vaṇijaḥ ca mahā dhanāḥ
english: Let sweet-speeched courtesans and opulent traders grace the extensive army of the prince.

sanskrit: ये च एनम् उपजीवन्ति रमते यैः च वीर्यतः
तेषाम् बहु विधम् दत्त्वा तान् अपि अत्र नियोजय
transliteration: ye ca enam upajīvanti ramate yaiḥ ca vīryataḥ
teṣām bahu vidham dattvā tān api atra niyojaya
english: Giving them immense wealth, do you also send with him those that depend on Rāma, as well as those with whom he delights to wrestle.

sanskrit: आयुधानि च मुख्यानि नागराः शकटानि च
transliteration: āyudhāni ca mukhyāni nāgarāḥ śakaṭāni ca
english: Let the foremost weapons, and the citizens, and cars, and fowlers well acquainted with the forest go in the wake of Käkutstha.

sanskrit: निघ्नन् मृगान् कुन्जरामः च पिबमः च आरण्यकम् मधु
नदीः च विविधाः पश्यन् न राज्यम् सम्स्मरिष्यति
transliteration: nighnan mṛgān kunjarāmaḥ ca pibamaḥ ca āraṇyakam madhu
nadīḥ ca vividhāḥ paśyan na rājyam samsmariṣyati
english: Killing deer and elephants, and drinking wild honey, and beholding various rivers, they will ultimately forget this kingdom.

sanskrit: धान्य कोशः च यः कश्चित् धन कोशः च मामकः
तौ रामम् अनुगच्चेताम् वसन्तम् निर्जने वने
transliteration: dhānya kośaḥ ca yaḥ kaścit dhana kośaḥ ca māmakaḥ
tau rāmam anugaccetām vasantam nirjane vane
english: And let our granary and treasury follow Rāma who is to reside in the forest.

sanskrit: यजन् पुण्येषु देशेषु विसृजमः च आप्त दक्षिणाः
ऋषिभिः च समागम्य प्रवत्स्यति सुखम् वने
transliteration: yajan puṇyeṣu deśeṣu visṛjamaḥ ca āpta dakṣiṇāḥ
ṛṣibhiḥ ca samāgamya pravatsyati sukham vane
english: Performing sacrifices at holy spots, and dispensing the prescribed Dakşiņās, let Rāma happily reside in the forest in the company of saints.

sanskrit: भरतः च महा बाहुर् अयोध्याम् पालयिष्यति
सर्व कामैः पुनः श्रीमान् रामः सम्साध्यताम् इति
transliteration: bharataḥ ca mahā bāhur ayodhyām pālayiṣyati
sarva kāmaiḥ punaḥ śrīmān rāmaḥ samsādhyatām iti
english: The mighty-armed Bharata will govern Ayodhyā. Therefore, do you furnish the auspicious Rāma with every object of enjoyment.

sanskrit: एवम् ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे कैकेय्या भयम् आगतम्
मुखम् च अपि अगमात् शेषम् स्वरः च अपि न्यरुध्यत
transliteration: evam bruvati kākutsthe kaikeyyā bhayam āgatam
mukham ca api agamāt śeṣam svaraḥ ca api nyarudhyata
english: When that descendant of Kākutstha said this, Kaikeyi was inspired with apprehension: her countenance became blank, and her utterance was choked.

sanskrit: सा विषण्णा च सम्त्रस्ता कैकेयी वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sā viṣaṇṇā ca samtrastā kaikeyī vākyam abravīt
english: Losing her complexion and agitated with fear, with her countenance fallen, Kaikeyi faced the king and said.

sanskrit: राज्यम् गत जनम् साधो पीत मण्डाम् सुराम् इव
transliteration: rājyam gata janam sādho pīta maṇḍām surām iva
english: O righteous one, like to a liquor whose lees alone have been left, Bharata will not receive the kingdom tasteless and denuded of all substance.

sanskrit: राजा दशरथो वाक्यम् उवाच आयत लोचनाम्
transliteration: rājā daśaratho vākyam uvāca āyata locanām
english: While the shameless Kaikeyi was speaking thus sternly, king Dasaratha said to that one of expansive eyes.

sanskrit: वहन्तम् किम् तुदसि माम् नियुज्य धुरि मा आहिते
transliteration: vahantam kim tudasi mām niyujya dhuri mā āhite
english: O worker of mischief, why having laid the load upon me, do you torment me? O ignoble one, why did you not ask for this, when you did first solicit the boon?

sanskrit: कैकेयी द्वि गुणम् क्रुद्धा राजानम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: kaikeyī dvi guṇam kruddhā rājānam idam abravīt
english: Hearing these wrathful words of the king, that beauteous one, Kaikeyi, waxing doubly wroth, addressed the monarch, saying.

sanskrit: तव एव वम्शे सगरः ज्येष्ठम् पुत्रम् उपारुधत्
असमन्जैति ख्यातम् तथा अयम् गन्तुम् अर्हति
transliteration: tava eva vamśe sagaraḥ jyeṣṭham putram upārudhat
asamanjaiti khyātam tathā ayam gantum arhati
english: Even in this line of yours, Sagara deprived his eldest son Asamañja by name of the enjoyment of the kingdom. In this way this one deserves to go to the forest.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः धिग् इति एव राजा दशरथो अब्रवीत्
व्रीडितः च जनः सर्वः सा च तन् न अवबुध्यत
transliteration: evam uktaḥ dhig iti eva rājā daśaratho abravīt
vrīḍitaḥ ca janaḥ sarvaḥ sā ca tan na avabudhyata
english: Thus addressed, king Dasaratha said, "O fire!" and all present were afflicted with shame: but Kaikeyi feigned not to understand all this.

sanskrit: तत्र वृद्धो महा मात्रः सिद्ध अर्थो नाम नामतः
शुचिर् बहु मतः राज्ञः कैकेयीम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tatra vṛddho mahā mātraḥ siddha artho nāma nāmataḥ
śucir bahu mataḥ rājñaḥ kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: Then a notable, aged, pure-spirited personage held in high esteem by the monarch, named Siddhartha, addressed Kaikeyi, saying.

sanskrit: असमन्जो गृहीत्वा तु क्रीडितः पथि दारकान्
सरय्वाः प्रक्षिपन्न् अप्सु रमते तेन दुर्मतिः
transliteration: asamanjo gṛhītvā tu krīḍitaḥ pathi dārakān
sarayvāḥ prakṣipann apsu ramate tena durmatiḥ
english: Asamañja by way of sport catching people on the way, used to throw them into the waters of the Sarayū, and that wicked-minded wretch made merry over the same.

sanskrit: तम् दृष्ट्वा नागरः सर्वे क्रुद्धा राजानम् अब्रुवन्
असमन्जम् वृषीण्व एकम् अस्मान् वा राष्ट्र वर्धन
transliteration: tam dṛṣṭvā nāgaraḥ sarve kruddhā rājānam abruvan
asamanjam vṛṣīṇva ekam asmān vā rāṣṭra vardhana
english: Seeing him do so, the citizens in a body, waxing wroth spoke to the monarch, 'O enhancer of the kingdom's prosperity, do you either banish Asamañja or us.'

sanskrit: तान् उवाच ततः राजा किम् निमित्तम् इदम् भयम्
ताः च अपि राज्ञा सम्पृष्टा वाक्यम् प्रकृतयो अब्रुवन्
transliteration: tān uvāca tataḥ rājā kim nimittam idam bhayam
tāḥ ca api rājñā sampṛṣṭā vākyam prakṛtayo abruvan
english: To them he replied, 'Whence is this fear of yours?' Thus asked by the monarch, the subjects said.

sanskrit: क्रीडितः तु एष नः पुत्रान् बालान् उद्भ्रान्त चेतनः
सरय्वाम् प्रक्षिपन् मौर्ख्यात् अतुलाम् प्रीतिम् अश्नुते
transliteration: krīḍitaḥ tu eṣa naḥ putrān bālān udbhrānta cetanaḥ
sarayvām prakṣipan maurkhyāt atulām prītim aśnute
english: “Through his impudence this one of perverted sense by way of diversion throwing our sons into the Sarayū, finds extreme delight.'

sanskrit: स तासाम् वचनम् श्रुत्वा प्रकृतीनाम् नर अधिप
तम् तत्याज अहितम् पुत्रम् तासाम् प्रिय चिकीर्षया
transliteration: sa tāsām vacanam śrutvā prakṛtīnām nara adhipa
tam tatyāja ahitam putram tāsām priya cikīrṣayā
english: Hearing these words of his subjects, that lord of men, with the intention of doing good to them, forsook that mischievous son of his.
Then swiftly causing a car to be yoked, he said to his men, “This one is to be banished for life in proper garb along with his wife.

Thereupon that worker of iniquity went to the forest and went about seeing mountain fastnesses. Thus did the virtuous king Sagara renounce his son. But what offence has Rāma committed that he is to be banished?

sanskrit: इति एवम् अत्यजद् राजा सगरः वै सुधार्मिकः
रामः किम् अकरोत् पापम् येन एवम् उपरुध्यते
transliteration: iti evam atyajad rājā sagaraḥ vai sudhārmikaḥ
rāmaḥ kim akarot pāpam yena evam uparudhyate
english: Thereupon that worker of iniquity went to the forest and went about seeing mountain fastnesses. Thus did the virtuous king Sagara renounce his son. But what offence has Rāma committed that he is to be banished?

sanskrit: न हि कम्चन पश्यामो राघवस्यागुणम् वयम्
transliteration: na hi kamcana paśyāmo rāghavasyāguṇam vayam
english: We do not find any fault whatever in Rāghava. Rare is his fault even like the spot on the Moon. Or it may be, O exalted lady, that you perceive some fault in Rāghava. Do you, if so, unfold it; and then let Rāma be banished,

sanskrit: अथवा देवि दोषम् त्वं कंचित्पश्यसि राघवे
तमद्य ब्रूहि तत्वैन तदा रोमो विवास्यताम्
transliteration: athavā devi doṣam tvaṃ kaṃcitpaśyasi rāghave
tamadya brūhi tatvaina tadā romo vivāsyatām
english: We do not find any fault whatever in Rāghava. Rare is his fault even like the spot on the Moon. Or it may be, O exalted lady, that you perceive some fault in Rāghava. Do you, if so, unfold it; and then let Rāma be banished,

sanskrit: अदुष्टस्य हि सम्त्यागः सत्पथे निरतस्य च
transliteration: aduṣṭasya hi samtyāgaḥ satpathe niratasya ca
english: But the renunciation of the honest ever constant in a righteous course, in consequence of its being opposed to virtue, destroys the splendour of Sakra himself.

sanskrit: तदलम् देवि रामस्य श्रिया विहतया त्वया
लोकतोऽप् हि ते रक्ष्यः परिवादः शुभानने
transliteration: tadalam devi rāmasya śriyā vihatayā tvayā
lokato'p hi te rakṣyaḥ parivādaḥ śubhānane
english: Therefore, O noble one, cease to persevere in this, for what good would the marring of Rāma's good fortune bring you? And, O you of a fair countenance, you will by such a course, escape odium.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु सिद्ध अर्थ वचो राजा श्रान्ततर स्वनः
शोक उपहतया वाचा कैकेयीम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: śrutvā tu siddha artha vaco rājā śrāntatara svanaḥ
śoka upahatayā vācā kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: Hearing Siddhārtha's words, the king, his voice waxing exceedingly feeble, addressed Kaikeyī in words surcharged with emotion.

O Personation of sin, you relish not this speech. You know not either your own good or mine. This wicked endeavour of yours, O you that strive after harm, which you put forth adopting a narrow path, is surely divorced from the course of the good.

sanskrit: सह एव राज्ञा भरतेन च त्वम्
transliteration: saha eva rājñā bharatena ca tvam
english: Forsaking my kingdom, forsaking happiness and treasures, I will to-day follow Rāma. Do you with Bharata for the king, forever enjoy dominion according to your heart's desire.

sanskrit: महा मात्र वचः श्रुत्वा रामः दशरथम् तदा
transliteration: mahā mātra vacaḥ śrutvā rāmaḥ daśaratham tadā
english: Hearing the words of that worthy, Rāma conversant with modesty, humbly addressed Dasaratha, saying.

sanskrit: त्यक्त भोगस्य मे राजन् वने वन्येन जीवतः
किम् कार्यम् अनुयात्रेण त्यक्त सन्गस्य सर्वतः
transliteration: tyakta bhogasya me rājan vane vanyena jīvataḥ
kim kāryam anuyātreṇa tyakta sangasya sarvataḥ
english: What O king, have I, that am renouncing everything and am going to dwell in the forest subsisting on what the forest yields, to do with a following?

sanskrit: यो हि दत्त्वा द्विप श्रेष्ठम् कक्ष्यायाम् कुरुते मनः
रज्जु स्नेहेन किम् तस्य त्यजतः कुन्जर उत्तमम्
transliteration: yo hi dattvā dvipa śreṣṭham kakṣyāyām kurute manaḥ
rajju snehena kim tasya tyajataḥ kunjara uttamam
english: Of what avail is a person's attachment for the tether of a goodly elephant, when the elephant itself is renounced by him?

sanskrit: तथा मम सताम् श्रेष्ठ किम् ध्वजिन्या जगत् पते
सर्वाणि एव अनुजानामि चीराणि एव आनयन्तु मे
transliteration: tathā mama satām śreṣṭha kim dhvajinyā jagat pate
sarvāṇi eva anujānāmi cīrāṇi eva ānayantu me
english: Thus it is with me, O foremost of righteous ones. What shal! I do with the army, O lord of men? I will confer everything on Bharata. Let them bring me a venture of bark.

sanskrit: खनित्र पिटके च उभे मम आनयत गच्चतः
चतुर् दश वने वासम् वर्षाणि वसतः मम
transliteration: khanitra piṭake ca ubhe mama ānayata gaccataḥ
catur daśa vane vāsam varṣāṇi vasataḥ mama
english: And for me who will go to the forest and reside there for fourteen years, bring a hoe and a basket.

sanskrit: अथ चीराणि कैकेयी स्वयम् आहृत्य राघवम्
उवाच परिधत्स्व इति जन ओघे निरपत्रपा
transliteration: atha cīrāṇi kaikeyī svayam āhṛtya rāghavam
uvāca paridhatsva iti jana oghe nirapatrapā
english: Thereupon Kaikeyi herself brought a bark dress and that shameless one said to Rāghava in the presence of all, “Do you wear this.”

sanskrit: स चीरे पुरुष व्याघ्रः कैकेय्याः प्रतिगृह्य ते
सूक्ष्म वस्त्रम् अवक्षिप्य मुनि वस्त्राणि अवस्त ह
transliteration: sa cīre puruṣa vyāghraḥ kaikeyyāḥ pratigṛhya te
sūkṣma vastram avakṣipya muni vastrāṇi avasta ha
english: On this, that foremost of men taking those two pieces of bark from Kaikeyi, left his fine attire and put on the ascetic garb.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणः च अपि तत्र एव विहाय वसने शुभे
तापसाच् चादने चैव जग्राह पितुर् अग्रतः
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaḥ ca api tatra eva vihāya vasane śubhe
tāpasāc cādane caiva jagrāha pitur agrataḥ
english: And Lakşmaņa also, renouncing his choice raiment, put on the dress of an anchorite before his father.

sanskrit: अथ आत्म परिधान अर्थम् सीता कौशेय वासिनी
समीक्ष्य चीरम् सम्त्रस्ता पृषती वागुराम् इव
transliteration: atha ātma paridhāna artham sītā kauśeya vāsinī
samīkṣya cīram samtrastā pṛṣatī vāgurām iva

sanskrit: सा व्यपत्रपमाणा इव प्रतिगृह्य च दुर्मनाः
गन्धर्व राज प्रतिमम् भर्तारम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sā vyapatrapamāṇā iva pratigṛhya ca durmanāḥ
gandharva rāja pratimam bhartāram idam abravīt

sanskrit: कथम् नु चीरम् बध्नन्ति मुनयो वन वासिनः
transliteration: katham nu cīram badhnanti munayo vana vāsinaḥ

sanskrit: कृत्वा कण्ठे च सा चीरम् एकम् आदाय पाणिना
तस्थौ हि अकुषला तत्र व्रीडिता जनक आत्मज
transliteration: kṛtvā kaṇṭhe ca sā cīram ekam ādāya pāṇinā
tasthau hi akuṣalā tatra vrīḍitā janaka ātmaja
english: Putting on one piece on her neck and holding the other in her hand, the daughter of Janaka, feeling uneasy, stood overpowered with shame.

sanskrit: तस्याः तत् क्षिप्रम् आगम्य रामः धर्मभृताम् वरः
चीरम् बबन्ध सीतायाः कौशेयस्य उपरि स्वयम्
transliteration: tasyāḥ tat kṣipram āgamya rāmaḥ dharmabhṛtām varaḥ
cīram babandha sītāyāḥ kauśeyasya upari svayam
english: Thereupon that best of righteous persons, Rāma, speedily coming up to her, fastened the monastic garb over Sītā's silk attire.

sanskrit: रामम् प्रेक्ष्य तु सीतायाः बध्नन्तम् चीरमुत्तमम्
transliteration: rāmam prekṣya tu sītāyāḥ badhnantam cīramuttamam
english: Beholding Rāma fastening that goodly garb on Sītā, the females of the inner apartment began to shed tears.
And waxing exceedingly aggrieved, they spoke to Rāma flaming in effulgence:, Child, do not take this virtuous one to the forest.
So long as you will reside in the forest in accordance with the wishes of your father, we shall behold her; and by this means let our lives attain their object, o lord.
O son, taking Lakşmaņa for your help, go you to the forest. This auspicious one does not deserve to live in the woods like an ascetic.

sanskrit: कुरु नो याचनाम् पुत्र! सीता तिष्ठतु भामिनी
धर्मनित्यः स्वयम् स्थातुम् न हीदानीम् त्वमिच्छसि
transliteration: kuru no yācanām putra! sītā tiṣṭhatu bhāminī
dharmanityaḥ svayam sthātum na hīdānīm tvamicchasi
english: O son, grant our prayer. Let the fair Sita remain. Ever steady in virtue, you do not yourself intend to stay here.

Hearing these words, Dasaratha's son tied the dress on Sītā having a similar character with himself. When she had put on the upper and under garments, the preceptor of the king, Vasiştha, his voice choked with the vapour of sorrow, dissuading Sita, said to Kaikeyi.

sanskrit: चीरे गृहीते तु तया समीक्ष्य नृपतेर्गुरुः
transliteration: cīre gṛhīte tu tayā samīkṣya nṛpaterguruḥ
english: Hearing these words, Dasaratha's son tied the dress on Sītā having a similar character with himself. When she had put on the upper and under garments, the preceptor of the king, Vasiştha, his voice choked with the vapour of sorrow, dissuading Sita, said to Kaikeyi.
O you whose desires outrun your sense of honour, O you of perverted understanding, O befouler of your line, deceiving the monarch, you stay not within the pale of the promise.

sanskrit: न गन्तव्यम् वनम् देव्या सीतया शीलवर्जिते
transliteration: na gantavyam vanam devyā sītayā śīlavarjite
english: O you bereft of good behaviour, that noble lady, Sītā, should not go to the forest, Sītā will occupy Rāma's seat.
Of all those that marry, the wife is the (other) soul. Șītā will govern the earth, as she is Rāma's self.

sanskrit: अथ यास्यति वैदेही वनम् रामेण सम्गता
transliteration: atha yāsyati vaidehī vanam rāmeṇa samgatā
english: But if Vaidehī goes to the forest with Rāma, we will follow him, and the inhabitants of the city will also repair thither. And the warders of the inner apartment, and the people of the kingdom and the city taking with them their necessaries and servants will accompany Rāghava and his wife.

sanskrit: सहोपजीव्यम् राष्ट्रम् च पुरम् च सपरिच्छदम्
transliteration: sahopajīvyam rāṣṭram ca puram ca saparicchadam
english: But if Vaidehī goes to the forest with Rāma, we will follow him, and the inhabitants of the city will also repair thither. And the warders of the inner apartment, and the people of the kingdom and the city taking with them their necessaries and servants will accompany Rāghava and his wife.
Bharata and Śatrughna wearing ascetic clothes and ranging the forest will live like their elder brother resident in the woods.

sanskrit: ततह् शून्याम् गतजनाम् वसुधाम् पादपैः सह
transliteration: tatah śūnyām gatajanām vasudhām pādapaiḥ saha
english: Then alone you of vile ways and intent upon harming the people will govern this empty earth deserted by the inhabitants, along with the trees.

sanskrit: न हि तद्भविता राष्ट्रम् यत्र रामो न भूपतिः
तद्वनम् भविता राष्ट्रम् यत्र रामो निवत्स्यति
transliteration: na hi tadbhavitā rāṣṭram yatra rāmo na bhūpatiḥ
tadvanam bhavitā rāṣṭram yatra rāmo nivatsyati
english: That can never be a kingdom where Rāma is not the monarch, and that forest where Rāma will reside will flourish into a monarchy.

sanskrit: न ह्यदत्ताम् महीम् पित्रा भरतः शास्तुमर्हति
त्वयि वा पुत्रवद्वस्तुम् यदि जातो महीपतेः
transliteration: na hyadattām mahīm pitrā bharataḥ śāstumarhati
tvayi vā putravadvastum yadi jāto mahīpateḥ
english: Bharata never wishes to govern a kingdom that has not been conferred upon him by his father; nor, if he has really been begotten by the monarch, will he any further act by you as a son.
Even if you leaving the earth fly to the air, that one cognizant of the character of his ancestry, will never act otherwise.

sanskrit: लोके हि स न विद्येत यो न राममनुव्रतः
transliteration: loke hi sa na vidyeta yo na rāmamanuvrataḥ
english: Therefore although intent on advancing your son, you have really brought about his injury. There exists not a person in the world that is not partial to Rāma.
O Kaikeyi, do you to-day behold beasts and snakes and birds journeying in the wake of Rāma, and even the trees stand with their heads turned towards him.
Do you, O noble lady, removing the ascetic guise, confer elegant ornaments on your daughter-in-law, for such a dress suits not this one, Saying this Vasistha prevented Kaikeyi.
O daughter of king Kekaya, you have asked for the abode of Rāma in the woods, and decked out in ornaments let Sītā daily engaged in adorning herself, reside in the forest with Rāghava.

And let the daughter of the king go to the forest, surrounded by excellent cars and servants, and taking with her attires and other necessary things. When you demanded the (fulfilment of the) promise, you had not your eye on Sita.

When that foremost of Brāhmaṇas, that preceptor of the king possessed of unparalleled potency had said this, Sītā, desirous of serving her beloved lord, did not turn from the ascetic dress (presented by Kaikeyi.) preceptor of the king possessed of unparalleled potency had said this, Sītā, desirous of serving her beloved lord, did not turn from the ascetic dress (presented by Kaikeyi.)

sanskrit: प्रचुक्रोश जनः सर्वो धिग् त्वाम् दशरथम् तु इति
transliteration: pracukrośa janaḥ sarvo dhig tvām daśaratham tu iti
english: When Şītā, having a husband although seeming as if she had none, was putting on the ascetic guise, the people got into a wrath and exclaimed, “O Dasaratha, fie on you!"

sanskrit: चिच्छेद जीविते श्रद्धाम् धर्मे यशसि चात्मनः
transliteration: ciccheda jīvite śraddhām dharme yaśasi cātmanaḥ
english: Aggrieved at the uproar that arose there in consequence, the lord of earth banished from his heart all regard for life, virtue, and fame. And sighing hot, that descendant of Ikşvāku spoke to that wife of his, saying, O Kaikeyi, Sītā deserves not to go in a Kuća dress.

sanskrit: स निह्श्वस्य उष्णम् ऐक्ष्वाकः ताम् भार्याम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
कैकेयि कुश चीरेण न सीता गन्तुम् अर्हति
transliteration: sa nihśvasya uṣṇam aikṣvākaḥ tām bhāryām idam abravīt
kaikeyi kuśa cīreṇa na sītā gantum arhati
english: Aggrieved at the uproar that arose there in consequence, the lord of earth banished from his heart all regard for life, virtue, and fame. And sighing hot, that descendant of Ikşvāku spoke to that wife of his, saying, O Kaikeyi, Sītā deserves not to go in a Kuća dress.

sanskrit: सुकुमारी च बाला च सततम् च सुखोचिता
transliteration: sukumārī ca bālā ca satatam ca sukhocitā
english: Tender, and youthful, and worthy of happiness, she is by no means capable of living in the forest. My spiritual guide has spoken the truth.

Whom has this one injured that, being the daughter of the foremost of kings, she like a female ascetic, wearing a meagre garb in the presence of all, will (repair to the woods and) remain there like a beggar destitute of everything?
Let Janaka's daughter leave off her ascetic guise. This is not the promise that I had made to you before. Let the princess go to the forest in comfort, furnished with all sorts of gems.

My sands run out; by me has this cruel promise been made with an oath. But this (exile of Sītä) has been thought of by you through your ignorance. Let it not, however, consume you like a bamboo flower destroying the bamboo.

sanskrit: रामेण यदि ते पा पे किम्चित्कृतमशोभनम्
अपकारः क इह ते वैदेह्या दर्शितोऽधमे
transliteration: rāmeṇa yadi te pā pe kimcitkṛtamaśobhanam
apakāraḥ ka iha te vaidehyā darśito'dhame
english: If, O wicked woman, Rāma has happened to do you something unbeautiful, what wrong, O base wretch, has Vaidehi done you in the world?
Of eyes expanded like those of a doe, endued with a mild temperament, and virtuous, what harm has Janaka's daughter done you.

sanskrit: ननु पर्याप्तम् एतत् ते पापे राम विवासनम्
किम् एभिः कृपणैः भूयः पातकैः अपि ते कृतैः
transliteration: nanu paryāptam etat te pāpe rāma vivāsanam
kim ebhiḥ kṛpaṇaiḥ bhūyaḥ pātakaiḥ api te kṛtaiḥ
english: Surely, O nefarious one, the banishment of Ráma is enough for you. Why then do you bend your mind to perpetrate these atrocious sins?

sanskrit: प्रतिज्ञातम् मया तावत् त्वयोक्तम् देवि शृण्वता
transliteration: pratijñātam mayā tāvat tvayoktam devi śṛṇvatā
english: O noble dame, having heard you asking for the banishment of Rāma, who had at first been intended by me for being installed, and who came here afterwards, I had promised you (his exile alone.)

sanskrit: मैथिलीमपि या हि त्व मीक्षसे चीरवासिनीम्
transliteration: maithilīmapi yā hi tva mīkṣase cīravāsinīm
english: But since, going beyond that promise of mine, you behold Mithala's daughter dressed in mendicant garb, surely you wish to find your way to hell.

sanskrit: एवम् ब्रुवन्तम् पितरम् रामः सम्प्रस्थितः वनम्
अवाक् शिरसम् आसीनम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: evam bruvantam pitaram rāmaḥ samprasthitaḥ vanam
avāk śirasam āsīnam idam vacanam abravīt
english: Thus commissioned to the forest, Räma who was seated sealing his lips, said.

sanskrit: इयम् धार्मिक कौसल्या मम माता यशस्विनी
वृद्धा च अक्षुद्र शीला च न च त्वाम् देव गर्हिते
transliteration: iyam dhārmika kausalyā mama mātā yaśasvinī
vṛddhā ca akṣudra śīlā ca na ca tvām deva garhite
english: O righteous one, this my mother is aged and famous and of lofty spirit. May she not meet with improper treatment at your hands! It behoves you, O bestower of boons, to show greater honour to her when she shall be deprived of me and be plunged into a sea of grief and afflicted with unprecedented woe.

sanskrit: मया विहीनाम् वरद प्रपन्नाम् शोक सागरम्
अदृष्ट पूर्व व्यसनाम् भूयः सम्मन्तुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: mayā vihīnām varada prapannām śoka sāgaram
adṛṣṭa pūrva vyasanām bhūyaḥ sammantum arhasi
english: O righteous one, this my mother is aged and famous and of lofty spirit. May she not meet with improper treatment at your hands! It behoves you, O bestower of boons, to show greater honour to her when she shall be deprived of me and be plunged into a sea of grief and afflicted with unprecedented woe.

sanskrit: माम् हि सम्चिन्तयन्ती सा त्वयि जीवेत् तपस्विनी
transliteration: mām hi samcintayantī sā tvayi jīvet tapasvinī
english: O you comparable to the mighty Indra, you should so behove with my mother smitten with my separation, that exercised by grief in consequence of my residence in the forest, she may not, renouncing life, repair to the mansions of Yama.

sanskrit: इमाम् महा इन्द्र उपम जात गर्भिनीम्
न जीवितम् न्यस्य यम क्षयम् व्रजेत्
transliteration: imām mahā indra upama jāta garbhinīm
na jīvitam nyasya yama kṣayam vrajet
english: O you comparable to the mighty Indra, you should so behove with my mother smitten with my separation, that exercised by grief in consequence of my residence in the forest, she may not, renouncing life, repair to the mansions of Yama.

sanskrit: रामस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा मुनि वेष धरम् च तम्
समीक्ष्य सह भार्याभी राजा विगत चेतनः
transliteration: rāmasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā muni veṣa dharam ca tam
samīkṣya saha bhāryābhī rājā vigata cetanaḥ
english: Hearing Rāma's words, and seeing him dressed like an ascetic, the king in the midst of his wives was deprived of his senses.

sanskrit: न एनम् दुह्खेन सम्तप्तः प्रत्यवैक्षत राघवम्
न च एनम् अभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य प्रत्यभाषत दुर्मनाः
transliteration: na enam duhkhena samtaptaḥ pratyavaikṣata rāghavam
na ca enam abhisamprekṣya pratyabhāṣata durmanāḥ
english: And burning in grief, the king could not eye Rāghava, nor seeing him could that one of arilicted mind answer anything.

sanskrit: स मुहूर्तम् इव असम्ज्ञो दुह्खितः च मही पतिः
विललाप महा बाहू रामम् एव अनुचिन्तयन्
transliteration: sa muhūrtam iva asamjño duhkhitaḥ ca mahī patiḥ
vilalāpa mahā bāhū rāmam eva anucintayan
english: Then remaining unconscious for a while, the mighty-armed lord of earth oppressed by grief began to bewail, thinking of Rāma.

sanskrit: मन्ये खलु मया पूर्वम् विवत्सा बहवः कृताः
प्राणिनो हिम्सिता वा अपि तस्मात् इदम् उपस्थितम्
transliteration: manye khalu mayā pūrvam vivatsā bahavaḥ kṛtāḥ
prāṇino himsitā vā api tasmāt idam upasthitam
english: I conclude that formerly I deprived many a cow of her calf, and took the life of many creature, and it is for this that the present calamity has befallen me.

sanskrit: न तु एव अनागते काले देहाच् च्यवति जीवितम्
कैकेय्या क्लिश्यमानस्य मृत्युर् मम न विद्यते
transliteration: na tu eva anāgate kāle dehāc cyavati jīvitam
kaikeyyā kliśyamānasya mṛtyur mama na vidyate
english: (I infer) that life never departs from the body unless the time comes, for although sore tried by Kaikeyſ, my life does not go out of me, and for I can see before me this one resembling fire, clad in the dress of an ascetic, having left his fine venture.

sanskrit: मो अहम् पावक सम्काशम् पश्यामि पुरतः स्थितम्
विहाय वसने सूक्ष्मे तापस आच्चादम् आत्मजम्
transliteration: mo aham pāvaka samkāśam paśyāmi purataḥ sthitam
vihāya vasane sūkṣme tāpasa āccādam ātmajam
english: (I infer) that life never departs from the body unless the time comes, for although sore tried by Kaikeyſ, my life does not go out of me, and for I can see before me this one resembling fire, clad in the dress of an ascetic, having left his fine venture.

sanskrit: एकस्याः खलु कैकेय्याः कृते अयम् क्लिश्यते जनः
स्व अर्थे प्रयतमानायाः सम्श्रित्य निकृतिम् त्विमाम्
transliteration: ekasyāḥ khalu kaikeyyāḥ kṛte ayam kliśyate janaḥ
sva arthe prayatamānāyāḥ samśritya nikṛtim tvimām
english: These people are in trouble in consequence of Kaikeyi alone striving by help of this craftiness to secure her interest.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा तु वचनम् बाष्पेण पिहित ईक्ष्णह
राम इति सकृद् एव उक्त्वा व्याहर्तुम् न शशाक ह
transliteration: evam uktvā tu vacanam bāṣpeṇa pihita īkṣṇaha
rāma iti sakṛd eva uktvā vyāhartum na śaśāka ha
english: Having said these words, Dasaratha, his senses overpowered by the vapour of sorrow, exclaimed "Rāma!” and could not proceed further.

sanskrit: सम्ज्ञाम् तु प्रतिलभ्य एव मुहूर्तात् स मही पतिः
नेत्राभ्याम् अश्रु पूर्णाभ्याम् सुमन्त्रम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: samjñām tu pratilabhya eva muhūrtāt sa mahī patiḥ
netrābhyām aśru pūrṇābhyām sumantram idam abravīt
english: Then soon regaining consciousness, the lord of earth with tearful eyes, addressed Sumantra, saying.

sanskrit: औपवाह्यम् रथम् युक्त्वा त्वम् आयाहि हय उत्तमैः
प्रापय एनम् महा भागम् इतः जन पदात् परम्
transliteration: aupavāhyam ratham yuktvā tvam āyāhi haya uttamaiḥ
prāpaya enam mahā bhāgam itaḥ jana padāt param
english: Yoking a riding car with excellent horses, do you come hither; and take the exalted one to the south of the kingdom.

sanskrit: एवम् मन्ये गुणवताम् गुणानाम् फलम् उच्यते
पित्रा मात्रा च यत् साधुर् वीरः निर्वास्यते वनम्
transliteration: evam manye guṇavatām guṇānām phalam ucyate
pitrā mātrā ca yat sādhur vīraḥ nirvāsyate vanam
english: The virtuous and heroic Rāma is being banished by his father and, mother Even this methinks will be asserted as the fruit of the virtues possessed by the pious.

sanskrit: राज्ञो वचनम् आज्ञाय सुमन्त्रः शीघ्र विक्रमः
योजयित्वा आययौ तत्र रथम् अश्वैः अलम्कृतम्
transliteration: rājño vacanam ājñāya sumantraḥ śīghra vikramaḥ
yojayitvā āyayau tatra ratham aśvaiḥ alamkṛtam
english: Receiving the mandate of the sovereign, Sumantra endued with fleet vigour, yoking a car adorned with horses, came there.

sanskrit: तम् रथम् राज पुत्राय सूतः कनक भूषितम्
आचचक्षे अन्जलिम् कृत्वा युक्तम् परम वाजिभिः
transliteration: tam ratham rāja putrāya sūtaḥ kanaka bhūṣitam
ācacakṣe anjalim kṛtvā yuktam parama vājibhiḥ
english: Then the charioteer with joined hands announced to the prince that the car adorned with gold was ready, yoked with excellent horses.

sanskrit: राजा सत्वरम् आहूय व्यापृतम् वित्त सम्चये
उवाच देश कालज्ञो निश्चितम् सर्वतः शुचि
transliteration: rājā satvaram āhūya vyāpṛtam vitta samcaye
uvāca deśa kālajño niścitam sarvataḥ śuci
english: The king, versed in time and place, and pure, speedily summoning his treasurer, said to him these words firmly.

sanskrit: वासाम्सि च महा अर्हाणि भूषणानि वराणि च
वर्षाणि एतानि सम्ख्याय वैदेह्याः क्षिप्रम् आनय
transliteration: vāsāmsi ca mahā arhāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca
varṣāṇi etāni samkhyāya vaidehyāḥ kṣipram ānaya
english: Do you without delay bring to Vaidehī excellent and costly attires and noble ornaments, counting these (ten and four) years.

sanskrit: नर इन्द्रेण एवम् उक्तः तु गत्वा कोश गृहम् ततः
प्रायच्चत् सर्वम् आहृत्य सीतायै क्षिप्रम् एव तत्
transliteration: nara indreṇa evam uktaḥ tu gatvā kośa gṛham tataḥ
prāyaccat sarvam āhṛtya sītāyai kṣipram eva tat
english: Thus desired by the foremost of men, that officer repairing to the treasury, procuring all those, speedily presented them to Sītā.

sanskrit: सा सुजाता सुजातानि वैदेही प्रस्थिता वनम्
भूषयाम् आस गात्राणि तैः विचित्रैः विभूषणैः
transliteration: sā sujātā sujātāni vaidehī prasthitā vanam
bhūṣayām āsa gātrāṇi taiḥ vicitraiḥ vibhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: Thereupon that pure-sprung one, Vaidehi, ordered to the forest, adorned her goodly limbs with those rare ornaments.

sanskrit: उद्यतः अम्शुमतः काले खम् प्रभा इव विवस्वतः
transliteration: udyataḥ amśumataḥ kāle kham prabhā iva vivasvataḥ
english: Thus decked out, Vaidehī graced that chamber like the effulgence of the Sun irradiating the welkin with his rays.

sanskrit: ताम् भुजाभ्याम् परिष्वज्य श्वश्रूर् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tām bhujābhyām pariṣvajya śvaśrūr vacanam abravīt
english: Then embracing with her arms Mithila's daughter of noble behaviour, and smelling the crown of her head, Sītā's mother-in-law said.

sanskrit: असत्यः सर्व लोके अस्मिन् सततम् सत्कृताः प्रियैः
भर्तारम् न अनुमन्यन्ते विनिपात गतम् स्त्रियः
transliteration: asatyaḥ sarva loke asmin satatam satkṛtāḥ priyaiḥ
bhartāram na anumanyante vinipāta gatam striyaḥ
english: Those women that although having always been carefully tended by their husbands, do not regard them during the incident of adversity, are in this world reckoned as unchaste.

Even this is the nature of women: having formerly tasted happiness (at the hands of their husbands), they, on the accession of an inconsiderable misfortune, take them to task, nay, forsake them utterly.
Those women that are untruthful, unmindful, of evil ways heartless, intent on unrighteous acts, and whose love is evanescent. are unchaste.

sanskrit: न कुलम् न कृतम् विद्या न दत्तम् नापि सम्ग्रहः
transliteration: na kulam na kṛtam vidyā na dattam nāpi samgrahaḥ
english: Neither lineage, no benefit, nor learning, nor gift, nor forbearance of faults, can secure the hearts of females, surely their hearts are unstable.

sanskrit: साध्वीनाम् हि स्थितानाम् तु शीले सत्ये श्रुते शमे
transliteration: sādhvīnām hi sthitānām tu śīle satye śrute śame
english: But chaste women of good character, abiding in truth, acting in accordance with the precepts of superiors, and maintaining the dignity of their race, single out their lords as the prime means of compassing their spiritual welfare.

sanskrit: स त्वया न अवमन्तव्यः पुत्रः प्रव्राजितः मम
तव दैवतम् अस्तु एष निर्धनः सधनो अपि वा
transliteration: sa tvayā na avamantavyaḥ putraḥ pravrājitaḥ mama
tava daivatam astu eṣa nirdhanaḥ sadhano api vā
english: Therefore although my son is going to be banished to the woods, you should by no means disregard him. Whether he be wealthy or poor, he is to you like a god.

sanskrit: विज्ञाय वचनम् सीता तस्या धर्म अर्थ सम्हितम्
कृत अन्जलिर् उवाच इदम् श्वश्रूम् अभिमुखे स्थिता
transliteration: vijñāya vacanam sītā tasyā dharma artha samhitam
kṛta anjalir uvāca idam śvaśrūm abhimukhe sthitā
english: Hearing her mother-in-law's words fraught with virtue and interest, Sītā facing that lady, said with joined palms.

sanskrit: करिष्ये सर्वम् एव अहम् आर्या यद् अनुशास्ति माम्
अभिज्ञा अस्मि यथा भर्तुर् वर्तितव्यम् श्रुतम् च मे
transliteration: kariṣye sarvam eva aham āryā yad anuśāsti mām
abhijñā asmi yathā bhartur vartitavyam śrutam ca me
english: I will do all that the noble one says. I know how I should act by my husband. I have heard all about that (from my parents.)

sanskrit: न माम् असज् जनेन आर्या समानयितुम् अर्हति
धर्मात् विचलितुम् न अहम् अलम् चन्द्रात् इव प्रभा
transliteration: na mām asaj janena āryā samānayitum arhati
dharmāt vicalitum na aham alam candrāt iva prabhā
english: The worshipful one ought not to place me on the same footing with unrighteous persons. As brightness does not depart from the moon, so I cannot swerve from virtue.

sanskrit: न अतन्त्री वाद्यते वीणा न अचक्रः वर्तते रथः
न अपतिः सुखम् एधते या स्यात् अपि शत आत्मजा
transliteration: na atantrī vādyate vīṇā na acakraḥ vartate rathaḥ
na apatiḥ sukham edhate yā syāt api śata ātmajā
english: The Viņā without strings does not sound; and the car without wheels does not move, so although having an hundred sons, a woman without her husband cannot attain happiness.

sanskrit: मितम् ददाति हि पिता मितम् माता मितम् सुतः
अमितस्य हि दातारम् भर्तारम् का न पूजयेत्
transliteration: mitam dadāti hi pitā mitam mātā mitam sutaḥ
amitasya hi dātāram bhartāram kā na pūjayet
english: The father gives in measure, the father and the son give in measure, but who does not worship that bestower of riches fineless', the husband?

sanskrit: सा अहम् एवम् गता श्रेष्ठा श्रुत धर्म पर अवरा
