आर्ये किम् अवमन्येयम् स्त्रीणाम् भर्ता हि दैवतम्
transliteration: sā aham evam gatā śreṣṭhā śruta dharma para avarā
ārye kim avamanyeyam strīṇām bhartā hi daivatam
english: O exalted one, having learnt from my superiors the principal as well the minor duties, shall I disregard (my lord)? A husband is a deity to the wife.

sanskrit: सीताया वचनम् श्रुत्वा कौसल्या हृदयम् गमम्
शुद्ध सत्त्वा मुमोच अश्रु सहसा दुह्ख हर्षजम्
transliteration: sītāyā vacanam śrutvā kausalyā hṛdayam gamam
śuddha sattvā mumoca aśru sahasā duhkha harṣajam
english: Hearing Sītā's words which went directly to the heart, Kausalyā endued with purity of spirit, out of fullness of bliss and bale suddenly shed tears.

sanskrit: ताम् प्रान्जलिर् अभिक्रम्य मातृ मध्ये अतिसत्कृताम्
रामः परम धर्मज्ञो मातरम् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tām prānjalir abhikramya mātṛ madhye atisatkṛtām
rāmaḥ parama dharmajño mātaram vākyam abravīt
english: Then with joined hands that foremost of virtuous ones addressed his mother, who, duly honoured by all, was seated in the midst of his other mothers, saying.

sanskrit: अम्ब मा दुह्खिता भूस् त्वम् पश्य त्वम् पितरम् मम
क्षयो हि वन वासस्य क्षिप्रम् एव भविष्यति
transliteration: amba mā duhkhitā bhūs tvam paśya tvam pitaram mama
kṣayo hi vana vāsasya kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati
english: O mother, without indulging in grief, you should minister to my father, and the term of my abode in the woods will shortly expire.

sanskrit: सुप्तायाः ते गमिष्यन्ति नव वर्षाणि पन्च च
सा समग्रम् इह प्राप्तम् माम् द्रक्ष्यसि सुहृद् वृतम्
transliteration: suptāyāḥ te gamiṣyanti nava varṣāṇi panca ca
sā samagram iha prāptam mām drakṣyasi suhṛd vṛtam
english: You will find these five and nine years pass away as if in a sleep. Then again, getting me, you will see me surrounded by my friends and relatives.

sanskrit: एतावद् अभिनीत अर्थम् उक्त्वा स जननीम् वचः
त्रयः शत शत अर्धा हि ददर्श अवेक्ष्य मातरः
transliteration: etāvad abhinīta artham uktvā sa jananīm vacaḥ
trayaḥ śata śata ardhā hi dadarśa avekṣya mātaraḥ
english: Having spoken out his mind to his mother, Rāma attentively eyed his three hundred and fifty mothers. And with joined hands Daśaratha's son spoke words fraught with virtue to his mothers afflicted like Kausalyā herself.

sanskrit: ताः च अपि स तथैव आर्ता मातृऋर् दशरथ आत्मजः
धर्म युक्तम् इदम् वाक्यम् निजगाद कृत अन्जलिः
transliteration: tāḥ ca api sa tathaiva ārtā mātṛṛr daśaratha ātmajaḥ
dharma yuktam idam vākyam nijagāda kṛta anjaliḥ
english: Having spoken out his mind to his mother, Rāma attentively eyed his three hundred and fifty mothers. And with joined hands Daśaratha's son spoke words fraught with virtue to his mothers afflicted like Kausalyā herself.

sanskrit: सम्वासात् परुषम् किम्चित् अज्ञानात् वा अपि यत् कृतम्
तन् मे समनुजानीत सर्वाः च आमन्त्रयामि वः
transliteration: samvāsāt paruṣam kimcit ajñānāt vā api yat kṛtam
tan me samanujānīta sarvāḥ ca āmantrayāmi vaḥ
english: If have said anything harsh to you in consequence of familiarity, or done any wrong through ignorance, do you forgive the same. I salute you all.
These calm words of Rāghava informed with piety were heard by the ladies overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: जज्ञे अथ तासाम् सम्नादः क्रौन्चीनाम् इव निह्स्वनः
मानव इन्द्रस्य भार्याणाम् एवम् वदति राघवे
transliteration: jajñe atha tāsām samnādaḥ krauncīnām iva nihsvanaḥ
mānava indrasya bhāryāṇām evam vadati rāghave
english: As Rāghava was speaking thus, there arose a loud wail proceeding from those wives of that chief of men, like to the cries of Krauncis.
And the abode of Dasaratha which formerly resounded with Murajas, Panavas, meghas,* was now filled with cries of distress and lamentations. *Musical instruments.

sanskrit: अथ रामः च सीता च लक्ष्मणः च कृत अन्जलिः
transliteration: atha rāmaḥ ca sītā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ ca kṛta anjaliḥ
english: Then exceedingly distressed, Rāma, Sītā and Lakşmaņa, bowing down to the king, circumambulated him.

sanskrit: तम् च अपि समनुज्ञाप्य धर्मज्ञः सीतया सह
transliteration: tam ca api samanujñāpya dharmajñaḥ sītayā saha
english: Then with the king's permission, the righteous Rāghava, stupefied with sorrow, in company with Sītā, paid respects to his mother.

sanskrit: अथ मातुः सुमित्राया जग्राह चरणौ पुनः
transliteration: atha mātuḥ sumitrāyā jagrāha caraṇau punaḥ
english: Following his brother, Lakşmaņa saluted Kausalyā; then he again took hold of his mother Sumitrā's feet.

sanskrit: तम् वन्दमानम् रुदती माता सौमित्रिम् अब्रवीत्
हित कामा महा बाहुम् मूर्ध्नि उपाघ्राय लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: tam vandamānam rudatī mātā saumitrim abravīt
hita kāmā mahā bāhum mūrdhni upāghrāya lakṣmaṇam
english: As the son of Sumitrā was thus engaged in honouring his mother, his mother smelling the crown of his head, thus spoke to the mightyarmed Laksmana.

sanskrit: सृष्टः त्वम् वन वासाय स्वनुरक्तः सुहृज् जने
रामे प्रमादम् मा कार्षीः पुत्र भ्रातरि गच्चति
transliteration: sṛṣṭaḥ tvam vana vāsāya svanuraktaḥ suhṛj jane
rāme pramādam mā kārṣīḥ putra bhrātari gaccati
english: Although attached to your friends here, you have my permission to go to the forest. When Rama shall have gone (to the woods), do not, O son, show any negligence to him.

sanskrit: व्यसनी वा समृद्धो वा गतिर् एष तव अनघ
एष लोके सताम् धर्मः यज् ज्येष्ठ वशगो भवेत्
transliteration: vyasanī vā samṛddho vā gatir eṣa tava anagha
eṣa loke satām dharmaḥ yaj jyeṣṭha vaśago bhavet
english: O sinless one, whether in prosperity or in adversity, even this one is your way. That a younger brother should follow his elder is in this world the duty of the righteous.

sanskrit: इदम् हि वृत्तम् उचितम् कुलस्य अस्य सनातनम्
दानम् दीक्षा च यज्ञेषु तनु त्यागो मृधेषु च
transliteration: idam hi vṛttam ucitam kulasya asya sanātanam
dānam dīkṣā ca yajñeṣu tanu tyāgo mṛdheṣu ca
english: These are the legitimate duties ever observed by this race, charity, initiation into sacrifice, and renunciation of the body in the field of battle,

sanskrit: सुमित्रा गच्छ गच्छेति पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्
transliteration: sumitrā gaccha gaccheti punaḥ punaruvāca tam
english: Do you consider Rāma as Daśaratha, and Janaka's own-begotten as myself; do you regard Ayodhyā as a wilderness, go my son, at your sweet pleasure. Having thus spoken to that dear descendant of Raghu, who had made up his mind (to journey to the forest), Sumitra again and again said to him, “Go! Go!"

sanskrit: रामम् दशरथम् विद्धि माम् विद्धि जनक आत्मजाम्
अयोध्याम् अटवीम् विद्धि गच्च तात यथा सुखम्
transliteration: rāmam daśaratham viddhi mām viddhi janaka ātmajām
ayodhyām aṭavīm viddhi gacca tāta yathā sukham
english: Do you consider Rāma as Daśaratha, and Janaka's own-begotten as myself; do you regard Ayodhyā as a wilderness, go my son, at your sweet pleasure. Having thus spoken to that dear descendant of Raghu, who had made up his mind (to journey to the forest), Sumitra again and again said to him, “Go! Go!"

sanskrit: ततः सुमन्त्रः काकुत्स्थम् प्रान्जलिर् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
विनीतः विनयज्ञः च मातलिर् वासवम् यथा
transliteration: tataḥ sumantraḥ kākutstham prānjalir vākyam abravīt
vinītaḥ vinayajñaḥ ca mātalir vāsavam yathā
english: Then like to Mātali addressing Väsava, that one understanding humility, Sumantra, with joined hands humbly said to Kākutstha.

sanskrit: रथम् आरोह भद्रम् ते राज पुत्र महा यशः
क्षिप्रम् त्वाम् प्रापयिष्यामि यत्र माम् राम वक्ष्यसि
transliteration: ratham āroha bhadram te rāja putra mahā yaśaḥ
kṣipram tvām prāpayiṣyāmi yatra mām rāma vakṣyasi
english: O illustrious prince, good betide you: do you ascend the car. O Rāma, I will speedily take you to wherever you will tell me.

sanskrit: चतुर् दश हि वर्षाणि वस्तव्यानि वने त्वया
तानि उपक्रमितव्यानि यानि देव्या असि चोदितः
transliteration: catur daśa hi varṣāṇi vastavyāni vane tvayā
tāni upakramitavyāni yāni devyā asi coditaḥ
english: You will have to spend fourteen years in the forest, and your stay must commence from this very day. So the noble lady has ordered.

sanskrit: तम् रथम् सूर्य सम्काशम् सीता हृष्टेन चेतसा
आरुरोह वर आरोहा कृत्वा अलम्कारम् आत्मनः
transliteration: tam ratham sūrya samkāśam sītā hṛṣṭena cetasā
āruroha vara ārohā kṛtvā alamkāram ātmanaḥ
english: Then having adorned her person, that best of her sex, Sītā, with a glad heart ascended the car resembling the sun.

sanskrit: तथैव आयुध जातानि भ्रातृभ्याम् कवचानि च
रथ उपस्थे प्रतिन्यस्य सचर्म कठिनम् च तत्
transliteration: tathaiva āyudha jātāni bhrātṛbhyām kavacāni ca
ratha upasthe pratinyasya sacarma kaṭhinam ca tat
english: And then he placed in front of the car various weapons, coats of mail, a basket bound in hide and a hoe, At length the brothers Rama and Laks maņa swiftly ascended the flaming car garnished with gold.
Counting the term of their stay in the woods, her father-in-law furnished Sītā following her lord with attires and ornaments.

sanskrit: रथोपस्थे प्रतिन्यस्य सचर्म कठिनम् च तत्
transliteration: rathopasthe pratinyasya sacarma kaṭhinam ca tat
english: And then he placed in front of the car various weapons, coats of mail, a basket bound in hide and a hoe, At length the brothers Rama and Laks maņa swiftly ascended the flaming car garnished with gold.

sanskrit: सीता तृतीयान् आरूढान् दृष्ट्वा धृष्टम् अचोदयत्
सुमन्त्रः सम्मतान् अश्वान् वायु वेग समान् जवे
transliteration: sītā tṛtīyān ārūḍhān dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭam acodayat
sumantraḥ sammatān aśvān vāyu vega samān jave
english: And seeing them with Sītā for the third, mounted, Sumantra drove the car yoked with goodly horses resembling the wind in celerity.

sanskrit: प्रयाते तु महा अरण्यम् चिर रात्राय राघवे
बभूव नगरे मूर्च्चा बल मूर्च्चा जनस्य च
transliteration: prayāte tu mahā araṇyam cira rātrāya rāghave
babhūva nagare mūrccā bala mūrccā janasya ca
english: On Rāghava having left for the forest to stay there for a long period, the men and beasts within the city were deprived of their senses (by grief).

sanskrit: तत् समाकुल सम्भ्रान्तम् मत्त सम्कुपित द्विपम्
हय शिन्जित निर्घोषम् पुरम् आसीन् महा स्वनम्
transliteration: tat samākula sambhrāntam matta samkupita dvipam
haya śinjita nirghoṣam puram āsīn mahā svanam
english: And in the city there arose a mighty tumult in consequence of the hurrying of people, the elephants waxing mad and furious, and the neighings of horses.

sanskrit: ततः सबाल वृद्धा सा पुरी परम पीडिता
रामम् एव अभिदुद्राव घर्म आर्तः सलिलम् यथा
transliteration: tataḥ sabāla vṛddhā sā purī parama pīḍitā
rāmam eva abhidudrāva gharma ārtaḥ salilam yathā
english: And the entire city containing, young and old, extremely afflicted, rushed after Rāma, like persons oppressed with the heat of the sun rushing towards water.

sanskrit: पार्श्वतः पृष्ठतः च अपि लम्बमानाः तत् उन्मुखाः
बाष्प पूर्ण मुखाः सर्वे तम् ऊचुर् भृश दुह्खिताः
transliteration: pārśvataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ ca api lambamānāḥ tat unmukhāḥ
bāṣpa pūrṇa mukhāḥ sarve tam ūcur bhṛśa duhkhitāḥ
english: As his side and back, the people bending forward with their faces covered with the vapour of grief, and sighing hard, said to he charioteer.

sanskrit: सम्यच्च वाजिनाम् रश्मीन् सूत याहि शनैः शनैः
मुखम् द्रक्ष्यामि रामस्य दुर्दर्शम् नो भविष्यति
transliteration: samyacca vājinām raśmīn sūta yāhi śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
mukham drakṣyāmi rāmasya durdarśam no bhaviṣyati
english: O charioteer, rein in the horses, do you proceed softly. We will see the countenance of Rāma, which we shall never see again.

sanskrit: आयसम् हृदयम् नूनम् राम मातुर् असम्शयम्
यद् देव गर्भ प्रतिमे वनम् याति न भिद्यते
transliteration: āyasam hṛdayam nūnam rāma mātur asamśayam
yad deva garbha pratime vanam yāti na bhidyate
english: Surely the heart of Rāma's mother is made of iron, for it does not burst on witnessing her son resembling Skanda repairing to the forest.

sanskrit: कृत कृत्या हि वैदेही चाया इव अनुगता पतिम्
न जहाति रता धर्मे मेरुम् अर्क प्रभा यथा
transliteration: kṛta kṛtyā hi vaidehī cāyā iva anugatā patim
na jahāti ratā dharme merum arka prabhā yathā
english: Vaidehī, attaining her desire, follows her husband, like a shadow, attached to virtue, she does not forsake him, even as the Sun forsakes not Meru.

sanskrit: अहो लक्ष्मण सिद्ध अर्थः सतताम् प्रिय वादिनम्
भ्रातरम् देव सम्काशम् यः त्वम् परिचरिष्यसि
transliteration: aho lakṣmaṇa siddha arthaḥ satatām priya vādinam
bhrātaram deva samkāśam yaḥ tvam paricariṣyasi
english: O Laksmana, you are blessed, since you will serve your god-like brother ever speaking fair.

sanskrit: महति एषा हि ते सिद्धिर् एष च अभ्युदयो महान्
एष स्वर्गस्य मार्गः च यद् एनम् अनुगच्चसि
transliteration: mahati eṣā hi te siddhir eṣa ca abhyudayo mahān
eṣa svargasya mārgaḥ ca yad enam anugaccasi
english: This design of yours is great; this is your mighty good fortune; this is the way to heaven that you are following him.

sanskrit: एवम् वदन्तः ते सोढुम् न शेकुर् बाष्पम् आगतम्
अथ राजा वृतः स्त्रीभिर् दीनाभिर् दीन चेतनः
transliteration: evam vadantaḥ te soḍhum na śekur bāṣpam āgatam
atha rājā vṛtaḥ strībhir dīnābhir dīna cetanaḥ
english: Saying this; they could not suppress their fears; and the men followed the beloved descendant of Ikşvāku.

sanskrit: निर्जगाम प्रियम् पुत्रम् द्रक्ष्यामि इति ब्रुवन् गृहात्
transliteration: nirjagāma priyam putram drakṣyāmi iti bruvan gṛhāt
english: Then the king, his sense overcome by grief, surrounded by his distressed wives, went out of his house, saying, “I will behold my dear son.”

sanskrit: शुश्रुवे च अग्रतः स्त्रीनाम् रुदन्तीनाम् महा स्वनः
यथा नादः करेणूनाम् बद्धे महति कुन्जरे
transliteration: śuśruve ca agrataḥ strīnām rudantīnām mahā svanaḥ
yathā nādaḥ kareṇūnām baddhe mahati kunjare
english: He heard before him a mighty noise proceeding from weeping women, like to the roars of she-elephants, when a great elephant has been taken captive.

sanskrit: पिता च राजा काकुत्स्थः श्रीमान् सन्नः तदा बभौ
परिपूर्णः शशी काले ग्रहेण उपप्लुतः यथा
transliteration: pitā ca rājā kākutsthaḥ śrīmān sannaḥ tadā babhau
paripūrṇaḥ śaśī kāle graheṇa upaplutaḥ yathā
english: Thereupon Rāma's father, the graceful Kākutstha, became shorn of his splendour, like to the full-moon enveloped at the appointed time during the eclipse.
Then the auspicious son of Daśaratha of soul incapable of being comprehended, ordered the charioteer, saying, "Do you proceed more speedily."

sanskrit: रामो याहीति सूतम् तम् तिष्ठेति स जनस्तदा
transliteration: rāmo yāhīti sūtam tam tiṣṭheti sa janastadā
english: Rāma saying to the charioteer, “Go," and the people, "Stay,” Thus desired on the way, the charioteer could not act both ways at once.
As the mighty-armed Rāma proceeded, the dust of the earth raised by the car-wheels were laid by the tears of the citizens showering down.
And in consequence of Rāghava's departure, the entire city filled with despair, and uttering with their senses lost exclamations of "Oh" and "Alas," became exceedingly afflicted.
And the tears begot of heart's grief that flowed from the eyes of the females, resembled rain-drops scattered around from lotuses shaken by the movements of fish.
And beholding the citizens absorbed in one thought, the auspicious monarch fell down in grief like a tree whose roots have been severed.

sanskrit: ततओ हल हला शब्दो जज्ञे रामस्य पृष्ठतः
नराणाम् प्रेक्ष्य राजानम् सीदन्तम् भृश दुह्खितम्
transliteration: tatao hala halā śabdo jajñe rāmasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
narāṇām prekṣya rājānam sīdantam bhṛśa duhkhitam
english: Then seeing the sovereign senseless and stricken with exceeding sorrow, the multitudes at the rear of Rāma broke out into a loud tumult.

sanskrit: हा राम इति जनाः केचित् राम माता इति च अपरे
अन्तः पुरम् समृद्धम् च क्रोशन्तम् पर्यदेवयन्
transliteration: hā rāma iti janāḥ kecit rāma mātā iti ca apare
antaḥ puram samṛddham ca krośantam paryadevayan
english: And seeing the king weeping aloud with the inmates of the inner apartment, some exclaiming "Oh Rama," and others, “O Rāma's mother," began to be-wail.

sanskrit: अन्वीक्षमाणो रामः तु विषण्णम् भ्रान्त चेतसम्
राजानम् मातरम् चैव ददर्श अनुगतौ पथि
transliteration: anvīkṣamāṇo rāmaḥ tu viṣaṇṇam bhrānta cetasam
rājānam mātaram caiva dadarśa anugatau pathi
english: Then turning back, Rāna saw that his sorrowstricken and bewildered father along with his mother, was following his track.

sanskrit: स बद्ध इव पाशेन किशोरो मातरम् यथा
transliteration: sa baddha iva pāśena kiśoro mātaram yathā
english: As a colt fastened in a snare cannot see its mother, so Rāma fastened in the bonds of virtue could not look at his mother openly.

sanskrit: पदातिनौ च यान अर्हाव् अदुह्ख अर्हौ सुख उचितौ
दृष्ट्वा सम्चोदयाम् आस शीघ्रम् याहि इति सारथिम्
transliteration: padātinau ca yāna arhāv aduhkha arhau sukha ucitau
dṛṣṭvā samcodayām āsa śīghram yāhi iti sārathim
english: And seeing his parents deserving of comfort and worthy of going in a carriage, going on foot, Rāma said to the charioteer, "Go you swiftly.”

sanskrit: न हि तत् पुरुष व्याघ्रः दुह्खदम् दर्शनम् पितुः
मातुः च सहितुम् शक्तः तोत्र अर्दितैव द्विपः
transliteration: na hi tat puruṣa vyāghraḥ duhkhadam darśanam pituḥ
mātuḥ ca sahitum śaktaḥ totra arditaiva dvipaḥ
english: And that foremost of men was incapable of bearing the looks of his father and mother, like to an elephant afflicted with the hook, (not being able to look at what is placed on its back.)
Rāma's mother rushed after him like a cow having a calf which has been fettered, rushing towards the fold, for the purpose of seeing it.

sanskrit: तथा रुदन्तीम् कौसल्याम् रथम् तम् अनुधावतीम्
क्रोशन्तीम् राम राम इति हा सीते लक्ष्मण इति च
transliteration: tathā rudantīm kausalyām ratham tam anudhāvatīm
krośantīm rāma rāma iti hā sīte lakṣmaṇa iti ca
english: Rāma beheld his mother Kausalyā running after the car, bewailing aloud, “Rāma, Rāma, Ah Sītā, Lakşmaņa,” shedding tears for Rāma, Laks maņa and Sītā, and appearing as if she had been dancing incessantly.

sanskrit: असकृत् प्रैक्षत तदा नृत्यन्तीम् इव मातरम्
transliteration: asakṛt praikṣata tadā nṛtyantīm iva mātaram
english: Rāma beheld his mother Kausalyā running after the car, bewailing aloud, “Rāma, Rāma, Ah Sītā, Lakşmaņa,” shedding tears for Rāma, Laks maņa and Sītā, and appearing as if she had been dancing incessantly.

sanskrit: तिष्ठ इति राजा चुक्रोष याहि याहि इति राघवः
सुमन्त्रस्य बभूव आत्मा चक्रयोः इव च अन्तरा
transliteration: tiṣṭha iti rājā cukroṣa yāhi yāhi iti rāghavaḥ
sumantrasya babhūva ātmā cakrayoḥ iva ca antarā
english: The king exclaimed, "Stay,” Rāghava said, "On, On." Sumantra's mind vacillated like that of one placed between two hosts burning to encounter each other.

sanskrit: न अश्रौषम् इति राजानम् उपालब्धो अपि वक्ष्यसि
चिरम् दुह्खस्य पापिष्ठम् इति रामः तम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: na aśrauṣam iti rājānam upālabdho api vakṣyasi
ciram duhkhasya pāpiṣṭham iti rāmaḥ tam abravīt
english: Rāma said to him, “When taxed by the monarch (on your return), you will say, 'I did not hear you.' But delay will impart me terrible pain."

sanskrit: रामस्य स वचः कुर्वन्न् अनुज्ञाप्य च तम् जनम्
व्रजतः अपि हयान् शीघ्रम् चोदयाम् आस सारथिः
transliteration: rāmasya sa vacaḥ kurvann anujñāpya ca tam janam
vrajataḥ api hayān śīghram codayām āsa sārathiḥ
english: Thereupon, doing Rāma's bidding, the charioteer, telling the people to desist, made the horses already coursing, run faster.

sanskrit: न्यवर्तत जनो राज्ञो रामम् कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम्
मनसा अपि अश्रु वेगैः च न न्यवर्तत मानुषम्
transliteration: nyavartata jano rājño rāmam kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam
manasā api aśru vegaiḥ ca na nyavartata mānuṣam
english: The retainers of the king stopped after circumambulating Rāma, but their minds did not turn back. But the others did not return either bodily or mentally.

sanskrit: यम् इच्चेत् पुनर् आयान्तम् न एनम् दूरम् अनुव्रजेत्
इति अमात्या महा राजम् ऊचुर् दशरथम् वचः
transliteration: yam iccet punar āyāntam na enam dūram anuvrajet
iti amātyā mahā rājam ūcur daśaratham vacaḥ

english: Then the courtiers said to that mighty monarch, Dasaratha, “He that is expected back should not be followed far". Hearing their words, the king endued with every virtue, with his body covered with perspiration and his countenance woebegone, and exceedingly distressed, stopped short and stood with his wife looking at his son
When that foremost of men had gone out of the city with joined hands, there arose a chorus of cries proceeding from the females residing in the inner apartment.

sanskrit: यो गतिम् शरणम् च आसीत् स नाथः क्व नु गच्चति
transliteration: yo gatim śaraṇam ca āsīt sa nāthaḥ kva nu gaccati
english: Where goes he that was the stay and refuge of the friendless, the feeble, and the helpless.

sanskrit: न क्रुध्यति अभिशस्तः अपि क्रोधनीयानि वर्जयन्
क्रुद्धान् प्रसादयन् सर्वान् सम दुह्खः क्व गच्चति
transliteration: na krudhyati abhiśastaḥ api krodhanīyāni varjayan
kruddhān prasādayan sarvān sama duhkhaḥ kva gaccati
english: He that although falsely accused, used not to be moved by anger, who pacified every enraged person by renouncing things calculated to fan anger and who felt equally for all, where goes he?

sanskrit: कौसल्यायाम् महा तेजा यथा मातरि वर्तते
तथा यो वर्तते अस्मासु महात्मा क्व नु गच्चति
transliteration: kausalyāyām mahā tejā yathā mātari vartate
tathā yo vartate asmāsu mahātmā kva nu gaccati
english: Where goes that highly energetic and magnanimous one who conducted himself with us as he did with his mother Kausalyā

sanskrit: परित्राता जनस्य अस्य जगतः क्व नु गच्चति
transliteration: paritrātā janasya asya jagataḥ kva nu gaccati
english: Afflicted by Kaikeyſ and commissioned by the monarch to the woods, where goes the deliverer of these people, of the entire world

sanskrit: अहो निश्चेतनो राजा जीव लोकस्य सम्प्रियम्
धर्म्यम् सत्य व्रतम् रामम् वन वासो प्रवत्स्यति
transliteration: aho niścetano rājā jīva lokasya sampriyam
dharmyam satya vratam rāmam vana vāso pravatsyati
english: Ah! the senseless monarch is sending to the woods the stay of all creatures, the righteous and truthful Rāma.

sanskrit: इति सर्वा महिष्यः ता विवत्साइव धेनवः
रुरुदुः चैव दुह्ख आर्ताः सस्वरम् च विचुक्रुशुः
transliteration: iti sarvā mahiṣyaḥ tā vivatsāiva dhenavaḥ
ruruduḥ caiva duhkha ārtāḥ sasvaram ca vicukruśuḥ
english: Thus all the queens, oppressed with grief, burst out into lamentations like kine bereft of calves, and loud was the sound of their wailing.

sanskrit: स तम् अन्तः पुरे घोरम् आर्त शब्दम् मही पतिः
पुत्र शोक अभिसम्तप्तः श्रुत्वा च आसीत् सुदुह्खितः
transliteration: sa tam antaḥ pure ghoram ārta śabdam mahī patiḥ
putra śoka abhisamtaptaḥ śrutvā ca āsīt suduhkhitaḥ
english: Hearing the loud tumult of lamentation in the inner apartment, the lord of earth burning in grief for his son was stricken with sorrow.

sanskrit: न अग्नि होत्राणि अहूयन्त सूर्यः च अन्तर् अधीयत
व्यसृजन् कवलान् नागा गावो वत्सान् न पाययन्
transliteration: na agni hotrāṇi ahūyanta sūryaḥ ca antar adhīyata
vyasṛjan kavalān nāgā gāvo vatsān na pāyayan
english: And oblations to the fire had not been offered; and the Sun set; and elephants forsook their forage; and the kine did not suckle their calves.

sanskrit: त्रिशन्कुर् लोहित अन्गः च बृहस्पति बुधाव् अपि
दारुणाः सोमम् अभ्येत्य ग्रहाः सर्वे व्यवस्थिताः
transliteration: triśankur lohita angaḥ ca bṛhaspati budhāv api
dāruṇāḥ somam abhyetya grahāḥ sarve vyavasthitāḥ
english: Trisanku, Lohitanga, Brhaspati, Budha and the other Grahas getting at the Moon, remained with fierce aspects.

sanskrit: नक्षत्राणि गत अर्चीम्षि ग्रहाः च गत तेजसः
विशाखाः च सधूमाः च नभसि प्रचकाशिरे
transliteration: nakṣatrāṇi gata arcīmṣi grahāḥ ca gata tejasaḥ
viśākhāḥ ca sadhūmāḥ ca nabhasi pracakāśire
english: The stars are shorn of their brightness; the Grahas deprived of sheen; and Viśākhā appeared enveloped in haze.

sanskrit: रामे वनम् प्रव्रजिते नगरम् प्रचचाल तत्
transliteration: rāme vanam pravrajite nagaram pracacāla tat
english: And clouds driven by the wind resembled the sea mounting the welkin; and the city shook on Rāma having departed for the forest.

sanskrit: न ग्रहो नापि नक्षत्रं प्रचकाशे न किंचन
transliteration: na graho nāpi nakṣatraṃ pracakāśe na kiṃcana
english: And the cardinal points are distressed, and appear enveloped in darkness. And no planet or star is to be seen.

sanskrit: अकस्मान् नागरः सर्वो जनो दैन्यम् उपागमत्
आहारे वा विहारे वा न कश्चित् अकरोन् मनः
transliteration: akasmān nāgaraḥ sarvo jano dainyam upāgamat
āhāre vā vihāre vā na kaścit akaron manaḥ
english: And all of a sudden the citizens have been stricken with poverty: and no one turns his thoughts to eating or drinking.
And ceaselessly burning in grief and heaving sighs, the people in Ayodhyā rage at the monarch.

sanskrit: बाष्प पर्याकुल मुखो राज मार्ग गतः जनः
न हृष्टः लक्ष्यते कश्चित् सर्वः शोक परायणः
transliteration: bāṣpa paryākula mukho rāja mārga gataḥ janaḥ
na hṛṣṭaḥ lakṣyate kaścit sarvaḥ śoka parāyaṇaḥ
english: And with their faces washed in tears, the wayfarers betoken no delight, but all are being exercised with grief.

sanskrit: न वाति पवनः शीतः न शशी सौम्य दर्शनः
न सूर्यः तपते लोकम् सर्वम् पर्याकुलम् जगत्
transliteration: na vāti pavanaḥ śītaḥ na śaśī saumya darśanaḥ
na sūryaḥ tapate lokam sarvam paryākulam jagat
english: The cool air does not blow, and no moon of mild appearance is seen, and no sun heats the world, all the entire Earth is overwhelmed with woe.

sanskrit: अनर्थिनः सुताः स्त्रीणाम् भर्तारः भ्रातरः तथा
सर्वे सर्वम् परित्यज्य रामम् एव अन्वचिन्तयन्
transliteration: anarthinaḥ sutāḥ strīṇām bhartāraḥ bhrātaraḥ tathā
sarve sarvam parityajya rāmam eva anvacintayan
english: Sons depend not upon their parents, husbands on their wives, and brothers on brothers, and all forsaking each other, think of Rāma only.

sanskrit: ये तु रामस्य सुहृदः सर्वे ते मूढ चेतसः
शोक भारेण च आक्रान्ताः शयनम् न जुहुस् तदा
transliteration: ye tu rāmasya suhṛdaḥ sarve te mūḍha cetasaḥ
śoka bhāreṇa ca ākrāntāḥ śayanam na juhus tadā
english: And deprived of sense, and oppressed by the load of sorrow, the friends of Rāma forsook their rest.

sanskrit: सनाग योध अश्व गणा ननाद च
transliteration: sanāga yodha aśva gaṇā nanāda ca
english: Like the Earth with her mountains bereft of Purandara, Ayodhya, bereft of Rama, shook, agitated by fear and grief; and the citizens with elephants and warriors uttered exclamations of distress.

sanskrit: यावत् तु निर्यतः तस्य रजो रूपम् अदृश्यत
न एव इक्ष्वाकु वरः तावत् सम्जहार आत्म चक्षुषी
transliteration: yāvat tu niryataḥ tasya rajo rūpam adṛśyata
na eva ikṣvāku varaḥ tāvat samjahāra ātma cakṣuṣī
english: So long as he could see the dust raised by the car of Rāma setting out for the forest, so long that best of the Ikşvāku race did not turn his eyes from that direction.

sanskrit: यावद् राजा प्रियम् पुत्रम् पश्यति अत्यन्त धार्मिकम्
तावद् व्यवर्धत इव अस्य धरण्याम् पुत्र दर्शने
transliteration: yāvad rājā priyam putram paśyati atyanta dhārmikam
tāvad vyavardhata iva asya dharaṇyām putra darśane
english: And so long as the king could discover his exceedingly virtuous and favourite son, so long he raised himself (on his toes) on the earth with the view of beholding him.

sanskrit: न पश्यति रजो अपि अस्य यदा रामस्य भूमिपः
तदा आर्तः च विषण्णः च पपात धरणी तले
transliteration: na paśyati rajo api asya yadā rāmasya bhūmipaḥ
tadā ārtaḥ ca viṣaṇṇaḥ ca papāta dharaṇī tale
english: When the ruler of earth could no longer perceive even the dust raised by Rāma's car, then pierced with sorrow, and in heaviness of heart, he fell down to the ground.

sanskrit: तस्य दक्षिणम् अन्वगात् कौसल्या बाहुम् अन्गना
वामम् च अस्य अन्वगात् पार्श्वम् कैकेयी भरत प्रिया
transliteration: tasya dakṣiṇam anvagāt kausalyā bāhum anganā
vāmam ca asya anvagāt pārśvam kaikeyī bharata priyā
english: Then (raising him up), Kausalyā held his right arm and walked with him, while the slenderwaisted Kaikeyi walked by his left.

sanskrit: ताम् नयेन च सम्पन्नो धर्मेण निवयेन च
उवाच राजा कैकेयीम् समीक्ष्य व्यथित इन्द्रियः
transliteration: tām nayena ca sampanno dharmeṇa nivayena ca
uvāca rājā kaikeyīm samīkṣya vyathita indriyaḥ
english: Endowed with a sense of justice and with virtue and humility, the king with afflicted senses steadily eyeing Kaikeyī, thus spoke to her.

sanskrit: कैकेयि मा मम अन्गानि स्प्राक्षीस् त्वम् दुष्ट चारिणी
न हि त्वाम् द्रष्टुम् इच्चामि न भार्या न च बान्धवी
transliteration: kaikeyi mā mama angāni sprākṣīs tvam duṣṭa cāriṇī
na hi tvām draṣṭum iccāmi na bhāryā na ca bāndhavī

sanskrit: ये च त्वाम् उपजीवन्ति न अहम् तेषाम् न ते मम
केवल अर्थ पराम् हि त्वाम् त्यक्त धर्माम् त्यजाम्य् अहम्
transliteration: ye ca tvām upajīvanti na aham teṣām na te mama
kevala artha parām hi tvām tyakta dharmām tyajāmy aham
english: O Kaikeyī, that have decided for following sin, do you not touch my person, nor do I wish to see you. You are no wife of mine, not even a maid-servant of a friend sharing his good graces. I am none to those that subsist on your favour, nor are they anything to me. I renounce you who solely seek your interest and have abandoned virtue.

sanskrit: अगृह्णाम् यच् च ते पाणिम् अग्निम् पर्यणयम् च यत्
अनुजानामि तत् सर्वम् अस्मिम्ल् लोके परत्र च
transliteration: agṛhṇām yac ca te pāṇim agnim paryaṇayam ca yat
anujānāmi tat sarvam asmiml loke paratra ca
english: I renounce all the advantages pertaining either to this world or the next which I am entitled to by virtue of having obtained your hand and having made you circumambulate the sacrificial fire.

sanskrit: भरतः चेत् प्रतीतः स्यात् राज्यम् प्राप्य इदम् अव्ययम्
यन् मे स दद्यात् पित्र् अर्थम् मा मा तत् दत्तम् आगमत्
transliteration: bharataḥ cet pratītaḥ syāt rājyam prāpya idam avyayam
yan me sa dadyāt pitr artham mā mā tat dattam āgamat
english: If Bharata is satisfied with receiving this entire kingdom, let not what he spends on account of my funeral obsequies find its way to me.

sanskrit: अथ रेणु समुध्वस्तम् तम् उत्थाप्य नर अधिपम्
न्यवर्तत तदा देवी कौसल्या शोक कर्शिता
transliteration: atha reṇu samudhvastam tam utthāpya nara adhipam
nyavartata tadā devī kausalyā śoka karśitā
english: Then raising the lord of men covered with dust, the noble Kausalyā pierced with grief, stopped (along with the monarch.)

sanskrit: हत्वा इव ब्राह्मणम् कामात् स्पृष्ट्वा अग्निम् इव पाणिना
अन्वतप्यत धर्म आत्मा पुत्रम् सम्चिन्त्य तापसम्
transliteration: hatvā iva brāhmaṇam kāmāt spṛṣṭvā agnim iva pāṇinā
anvatapyata dharma ātmā putram samcintya tāpasam
english: The righteous one remembering Rāghava repented himself, as if he had slain a Brāhmaṇa through inordinate desire, or as if he had placed his hand in fire.

sanskrit: निवृत्य एव निवृत्य एव सीदतः रथ वर्त्मसु
राज्ञो न अतिबभौ रूपम् ग्रस्तस्य अम्शुमतः यथा
transliteration: nivṛtya eva nivṛtya eva sīdataḥ ratha vartmasu
rājño na atibabhau rūpam grastasya amśumataḥ yathā
english: Having stopped again and again, the visage of the monarch lamenting on beholding the track of the car, appeared dim like the Moon invaded by Rāhu,

sanskrit: विललाप च दुह्ख आर्तः प्रियम् पुत्रम् अनुस्मरन्
नगर अन्तम् अनुप्राप्तम् बुद्ध्वा पुत्रम् अथ अब्रवीत्
transliteration: vilalāpa ca duhkha ārtaḥ priyam putram anusmaran
nagara antam anuprāptam buddhvā putram atha abravīt
english: And stricken with grief, he lamented, remembering his beloved son, and thinking that by this time he had reached the precincts of the city, he broke out into the following.

sanskrit: वाहनानाम् च मुख्यानाम् वहताम् तम् मम आत्मजम्
पदानि पथि दृश्यन्ते स महात्मा न दृश्यते
transliteration: vāhanānām ca mukhyānām vahatām tam mama ātmajam
padāni pathi dṛśyante sa mahātmā na dṛśyate
english: On the way are traced the foot-prints of those foremost of bearers that are carrying my son away; but that magnanimous one I do not find.

sanskrit: स नूनम् क्वचित् एव अद्य वृक्ष मूलम् उपाश्रितः
काष्ठम् वा यदि वा अश्मानम् उपधाय शयिष्यते
transliteration: sa nūnam kvacit eva adya vṛkṣa mūlam upāśritaḥ
kāṣṭham vā yadi vā aśmānam upadhāya śayiṣyate
english: And that meritorious son of mine, who, daubed with sandal, used to rest his head pleasantly upon a pillow, fanned by beauteous damsels decked in ornaments, will to-day surely take refuge underneath a tree, and lay his head on a wooden plank or a stone.

sanskrit: उत्थास्यति च मेदिन्याः कृपणः पाम्शु गुण्ठितः
transliteration: utthāsyati ca medinyāḥ kṛpaṇaḥ pāmśu guṇṭhitaḥ
english: Covered with dust, he heaving sighs will rise from the ground in sad guise, like a leader of she-elephants rising from the side of a mountain.
Covered with dust, he heaving sighs will rise from the ground in sad guise, like a leader of she-elephants rising from the side of a mountain.

sanskrit: द्रक्ष्यन्ति नूनम् पुरुषा दीघ बाहुम् वने चराः
रामम् उत्थाय गच्चन्तम् लोक नाथम् अनाथवत्
transliteration: drakṣyanti nūnam puruṣā dīgha bāhum vane carāḥ
rāmam utthāya gaccantam loka nātham anāthavat
english: The rangers of the woods will now see the long-armed Rāma resembling the lord himself of the worlds, rising from the ground and going like one forlorn.

sanskrit: सकामा भव कैकेयि विधवा राज्यम् आवस
transliteration: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi vidhavā rājyam āvasa
english: That one so dearly loved by Janaka, worthy of being constantly ministered to with comforts, is to-day going to the forest, fatigued in consequence of having been pierced with thorns.
Unacquainted with the forest, she is certainly afflicted with fright on hearing the deep roars of ferocious beasts, capable of making one's hair stand erect.

sanskrit: न हि तम् पुरुष व्याघ्रम् विना जीवितुम् उत्सहे
transliteration: na hi tam puruṣa vyāghram vinā jīvitum utsahe
english: O Kaikeyi, do you realise your desire, do you becoming a widow, rule this kingdom. Without that best of men I cannot live.

sanskrit: इति एवम् विलपन् राजा जन ओघेन अभिसम्वृतः
transliteration: iti evam vilapan rājā jana oghena abhisamvṛtaḥ
english: Thus lamenting, the king surrounded by the multitude, like one that had performed his bath after death, entered that best of cities filled with people enfeebled and smitten with grief, with its streets thinned of men and its stalls closed.

sanskrit: शून्य चत्वर वेश्म अन्ताम् सम्वृत आपण देवताम्
क्लान्त दुर्बल दुह्ख आर्ताम् न अत्याकीर्ण महा पथाम्
ताम् अवेक्ष्य पुरीम् सर्वाम् रामम् एव अनुचिन्तयन्
विलपन् प्राविशद् राजा गृहम् सूर्यैव अम्बुदम्
transliteration: śūnya catvara veśma antām samvṛta āpaṇa devatām
klānta durbala duhkha ārtām na atyākīrṇa mahā pathām
tām avekṣya purīm sarvām rāmam eva anucintayan
vilapan prāviśad rājā gṛham sūryaiva ambudam

sanskrit: महा ह्रदम् इव अक्षोभ्यम् सुपर्णेन हृत उरगम्
रामेण रहितम् वेश्म वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च
transliteration: mahā hradam iva akṣobhyam suparṇena hṛta uragam
rāmeṇa rahitam veśma vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca

english: Then with tears in his eyes, the lord of earth, lamenting, in unintelligible accents said these sad and broken words.

sanskrit: कौसल्याया गृहम् शीघ्रम् राम मातुर् नयन्तु माम्
इति ब्रुवन्तम् राजानम् अनयन् द्वार दर्शितः
transliteration: kausalyāyā gṛham śīghram rāma mātur nayantu mām
iti bruvantam rājānam anayan dvāra darśitaḥ
english: Do you speedily take me to the room of Rāma's mother, Kausalyā; for in no other place shall I find rest for my heart.
When the king had spoken thus, the ushers taking him to Kausalyā's chamber, made his lie down in lowly plight.

sanskrit: अधिरुह्य अपि शयनम् बभूव लुलितम् मनः
transliteration: adhiruhya api śayanam babhūva lulitam manaḥ
english: Having entered Kausalyā's apartment, the king having laid himself on the bed, was overwhelmed with emotion.
The king surveyed the mansion deprived of his two sons as well as his daughter-in-law, like to the welkin deprived of the Moon.

sanskrit: तच् च दृष्ट्वा महा राजो भुजम् उद्यम्य वीर्यवान्
उच्चैः स्वरेण चुक्रोश हा राघव जहासि माम्
transliteration: tac ca dṛṣṭvā mahā rājo bhujam udyamya vīryavān
uccaiḥ svareṇa cukrośa hā rāghava jahāsi mām
english: Beholding this, the puissant sovereign raising up his arm, burst out into lamentations, saying, “Ah! Rāma, you forsakes us both! Ah me! surely those blessed people are happy, who having passed this gap of time, will behold Rāma returned and will embrace him."

sanskrit: सुखिता बत तम् कालम् जीविष्यन्ति नर उत्तमाः
परिष्वजन्तः ये रामम् द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुनर् आगतम्
transliteration: sukhitā bata tam kālam jīviṣyanti nara uttamāḥ
pariṣvajantaḥ ye rāmam drakṣyanti punar āgatam
english: Beholding this, the puissant sovereign raising up his arm, burst out into lamentations, saying, “Ah! Rāma, you forsakes us both! Ah me! surely those blessed people are happy, who having passed this gap of time, will behold Rāma returned and will embrace him."
Then when the night had come like to his own fatal night, Dasaratha at mid-night addressed Kausalyā.

sanskrit: न त्वाम् पश्यामि कौसल्ये साधु माम् पाणिना स्पृश
transliteration: na tvām paśyāmi kausalye sādhu mām pāṇinā spṛśa

english: Then seeing that foremost of men absorbed in the contemplation of Rāma, that noble dame sat by him, and afflicted with greater grief, began to indulge in sorrow,* sighing heavily. *Another text reads vinisvasantam, joining it to narendram, foremost of men.

sanskrit: ततः समीक्ष्य शयने सन्नम् शोकेन पार्थिवम्
कौसल्या पुत्र शोक आर्ता तम् उवाच मही पतिम्
transliteration: tataḥ samīkṣya śayane sannam śokena pārthivam
kausalyā putra śoka ārtā tam uvāca mahī patim
english: Then seeing the king lying down stupified with grief, Kausalya, aggrieved for her son, spoke to the lord of earth, saying.

sanskrit: राघवो नर शार्दूल विषम् उप्त्वा द्विजिह्ववत्
विचरिष्यति कैकेयी निर्मुक्ता इव हि पन्नगी
transliteration: rāghavo nara śārdūla viṣam uptvā dvijihvavat
vicariṣyati kaikeyī nirmuktā iva hi pannagī
english: O best of men, having vented her venom upon Rāghava, the crooked Kaikeyi will go about like a she serpent that has cast off her slough.

sanskrit: विवास्य रामम् सुभगा लब्ध कामा समाहिता
त्रासयिष्यति माम् भूयो दुष्ट अहिर् इव वेश्मनि
transliteration: vivāsya rāmam subhagā labdha kāmā samāhitā
trāsayiṣyati mām bhūyo duṣṭa ahir iva veśmani
english: And that fortunate one having by her endeavours attained her end, will frighten me the more like a wicked serpent in one's house.

sanskrit: अथ स्म नगरे रामः चरन् भैक्षम् गृहे वसेत्
काम कारः वरम् दातुम् अपि दासम् मम आत्मजम्
transliteration: atha sma nagare rāmaḥ caran bhaikṣam gṛhe vaset
kāma kāraḥ varam dātum api dāsam mama ātmajam
english: If Rāma had stayed in this city subsisting himself by alms, or had I made my son as Kaikeyi's slave, even that would have been preferable (before his retirement to the woods.)

sanskrit: पातयित्वा तु कैकेय्या रामम् स्थानात् यथा इष्टतः
प्रदिष्टः रक्षसाम् भागः पर्वणि इव आहित अग्निना
transliteration: pātayitvā tu kaikeyyā rāmam sthānāt yathā iṣṭataḥ
pradiṣṭaḥ rakṣasām bhāgaḥ parvaṇi iva āhita agninā
english: Like to the sacrificial share cast to the Rākşasas by the sacrificers on the occasions of Parvas that wielder of the bow, the mightyarmed Rāma, gifted with the gait of the prince of elephants, cast off by Kaikeyī, takes refuge in the forest in company with his wife and Laks mana.

sanskrit: गज राज गतिर् वीरः महा बाहुर् धनुर् धरः
वनम् आविशते नूनम् सभार्यः सह लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: gaja rāja gatir vīraḥ mahā bāhur dhanur dharaḥ
vanam āviśate nūnam sabhāryaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Like to the sacrificial share cast to the Rākşasas by the sacrificers on the occasions of Parvas that wielder of the bow, the mightyarmed Rāma, gifted with the gait of the prince of elephants, cast off by Kaikeyī, takes refuge in the forest in company with his wife and Laks mana.

sanskrit: वने तु अदृष्ट दुह्खानाम् कैकेय्या अनुमते त्वया
त्यक्तानाम् वन वासाय का न्व् अवस्था भविष्यति
transliteration: vane tu adṛṣṭa duhkhānām kaikeyyā anumate tvayā
tyaktānām vana vāsāya kā nv avasthā bhaviṣyati
english: Despatched by you to the woods at the command of Kaikeyi, to what a plight will they, not inured to the privations of a forest-life, be reduced!

sanskrit: ते रत्न हीनाः तरुणाः फल काले विवासिताः
कथम् वत्स्यन्ति कृपणाः फल मूलैः कृत अशनाः
transliteration: te ratna hīnāḥ taruṇāḥ phala kāle vivāsitāḥ
katham vatsyanti kṛpaṇāḥ phala mūlaiḥ kṛta aśanāḥ
english: And bereft of elegant apparel, how will they of tender years, exiled in this time of enjoyment, pass their lives in misery, subsisting on fruits and roots!

sanskrit: अपि इदानीम् स कालः स्यान् मम शोक क्षयः शिवः
सभार्यम् यत् सह भ्रात्रा पश्येयम् इह राघवम्
transliteration: api idānīm sa kālaḥ syān mama śoka kṣayaḥ śivaḥ
sabhāryam yat saha bhrātrā paśyeyam iha rāghavam
english: Will such a time present itself now that my grief removed and my desire attained, I shall here behold Rāghava along with his wife and brother?

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा एव उपस्थितौ वीरौ कदा अयोध्या भविष्यति
यशस्विनी हृष्ट जना सूच्च्रित ध्वज मालिनी
transliteration: śrutvā eva upasthitau vīrau kadā ayodhyā bhaviṣyati
yaśasvinī hṛṣṭa janā sūccrita dhvaja mālinī
english: When, hearing that those heroes have come, will Ayodhyā adorned with standards and garlands, attain fame, with her populace filled with joy?

sanskrit: कदा प्रेक्ष्य नर व्याघ्राव् अरण्यात् पुनर् आगतौ
transliteration: kadā prekṣya nara vyāghrāv araṇyāt punar āgatau
english: When, seeing those foremost of men returned from the forest, will the city overflow with delight, like the ocean on the occasion of a Parva?

sanskrit: कदा अयोध्याम् महा बाहुः पुरीम् वीरः प्रवेक्ष्यति
पुरः कृत्य रथे सीताम् वृषभो गो वधूम् इव
transliteration: kadā ayodhyām mahā bāhuḥ purīm vīraḥ pravekṣyati
puraḥ kṛtya rathe sītām vṛṣabho go vadhūm iva
english: When will the mighty-armed hero enter the city of Ayodhyā, placing Sītā before him on the car, like to a bull having his bovine mate before him?

sanskrit: कदा प्राणि सहस्राणि राज मार्गे मम आत्मजौ
transliteration: kadā prāṇi sahasrāṇi rāja mārge mama ātmajau
english: When will people by thousands shower fried paddy upon my sons on the road, as those repressors of foes will enter the city?
When shall I behold those (two) wearing burnished ear-rings, entering Ayodhyā, placing before them their weapons and swords, like unto two hills furnished with their summits?

sanskrit: कदा सुमनसः कन्या द्विजातीनाम् फलानि च
transliteration: kadā sumanasaḥ kanyā dvijātīnām phalāni ca
english: When accepting flowers from girls and fruits from Brahmanas, will they, filled with delight, go round the palace?

sanskrit: कदा परिणतः बुद्ध्या वयसा च अमर प्रभः
transliteration: kadā pariṇataḥ buddhyā vayasā ca amara prabhaḥ
english: When with his intelligence ripened by time, although resembling a celestial in age, will that righteous-souled one come here, rejoicing people like a Trivarsa?* *Three consecutive showers, favourable tot he erops.

sanskrit: निह्सम्शयम् मया मन्ये पुरा वीर कदर्यया
पातु कामेषु वत्सेषु मातृऋणाम् शातिताः स्तनाः
transliteration: nihsamśayam mayā manye purā vīra kadaryayā
pātu kāmeṣu vatseṣu mātṛṛṇām śātitāḥ stanāḥ
english: Doubtless, O hero, formerly of vile ways that I was, I had cut off the paps of kine and thus prevented their calves hungering after their mothers' milk, from drinking it.

sanskrit: सा अहम् गौर् इव सिम्हेन विवत्सा वत्सला कृता
कैकेय्या पुरुष व्याघ्र बाल वत्सा इव गौर् बलात्
transliteration: sā aham gaur iva simhena vivatsā vatsalā kṛtā
kaikeyyā puruṣa vyāghra bāla vatsā iva gaur balāt
english: And it is for this sin that, О foremost of men, have I, attached to my son, been forcibly deprived of him by Kaikeyi, like a cow deprived of her calf by a lion.

sanskrit: न हि तावद् गुणैः जुष्टम् सर्व शास्त्र विशारदम्
एक पुत्रा विना पुत्रम् अहम् जीवितुम् उत्सहे
transliteration: na hi tāvad guṇaiḥ juṣṭam sarva śāstra viśāradam
eka putrā vinā putram aham jīvitum utsahe
english: Having an only son, I dare not live without him endowed with every virtue and versed in every branch of learning.

sanskrit: न हि मे जीविते किम्चित् सामर्थम् इह कल्प्यते
अपश्यन्त्याः प्रियम् पुत्रम् महा बाहुम् महा बलम्
transliteration: na hi me jīvite kimcit sāmartham iha kalpyate
apaśyantyāḥ priyam putram mahā bāhum mahā balam
english: Not seeing my beloved son and the mighty Lakşmaņa, I cannot live at all.
As in summer the divine Sun furnished with fierce rays burns this earth, even so this raging fire of grief of account of my son consumes me.

sanskrit: विलपन्तीम् तथा ताम् तु कौसल्याम् प्रमद उत्तमाम्
इदम् धर्मे स्थिता धर्म्यम् सुमित्रा वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: vilapantīm tathā tām tu kausalyām pramada uttamām
idam dharme sthitā dharmyam sumitrā vākyam abravīt
english: As that best of ladies, Kausalyā, was thus lamenting, Sumitrā ever abiding in virtue, spoke to her these words consistent with righteousness.

sanskrit: तव आर्ये सद् गुणैः युक्तः पुत्रः स पुरुष उत्तमः
किम् ते विलपितेन एवम् कृपणम् रुदितेन वा
transliteration: tava ārye sad guṇaiḥ yuktaḥ putraḥ sa puruṣa uttamaḥ
kim te vilapitena evam kṛpaṇam ruditena vā
english: O worshipful one, your son is crowned with all qualities, and is the best of men. Why then do you bewail thus, or weep bitterly?

sanskrit: यः तव आर्ये गतः पुत्रः त्यक्त्वा राज्यम् महा बलः
साधु कुर्वन् महात्मानम् पितरम् सत्य वादिनाम्
transliteration: yaḥ tava ārye gataḥ putraḥ tyaktvā rājyam mahā balaḥ
sādhu kurvan mahātmānam pitaram satya vādinām
english: Since, O revered one, renouncing the kingdom, your mighty son wendeth (to the woods) with the view of fulfiling the intention of his high-souled and truthful sire, the worthy Rāma staying in the duty that is completely observed by the good and the performance of which always bringeth welfare in the next world, should by no means be lamented.

sanskrit: शिष्टैः आचरिते सम्यक् शश्वत् प्रेत्य फल उदये
रामः धर्मे स्थितः श्रेष्ठो न स शोच्यः कदाचन
transliteration: śiṣṭaiḥ ācarite samyak śaśvat pretya phala udaye
rāmaḥ dharme sthitaḥ śreṣṭho na sa śocyaḥ kadācana
english: Since, O revered one, renouncing the kingdom, your mighty son wendeth (to the woods) with the view of fulfiling the intention of his high-souled and truthful sire, the worthy Rāma staying in the duty that is completely observed by the good and the performance of which always bringeth welfare in the next world, should by no means be lamented.

sanskrit: वर्तते च उत्तमाम् वृत्तिम् लक्ष्मणो अस्मिन् सदा अनघः
दयावान् सर्व भूतेषु लाभः तस्य महात्मनः
transliteration: vartate ca uttamām vṛttim lakṣmaṇo asmin sadā anaghaḥ
dayāvān sarva bhūteṣu lābhaḥ tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: That sinless one, Laksmana, kind to all creatures, will minister to Rāma in the best way possible, and this is to the advantage of that high-souled one.

sanskrit: अरण्य वासे यद् दुह्खम् जानती वै सुख उचिता
अनुगच्चति वैदेही धर्म आत्मानम् तव आत्मजम्
transliteration: araṇya vāse yad duhkham jānatī vai sukha ucitā
anugaccati vaidehī dharma ātmānam tava ātmajam
english: And experiencing the hardships that come of living in the forest, Vaidehi deserving of happiness follows your righteous son.

sanskrit: कीर्ति भूताम् पताकाम् यो लोके भ्रामयति प्रभुः
दम सत्य व्रत परः किम् न प्राप्तः तव आत्मजः
transliteration: kīrti bhūtām patākām yo loke bhrāmayati prabhuḥ
dama satya vrata paraḥ kim na prāptaḥ tava ātmajaḥ
english: What is wanting to that maintainer of all, your son of subdued senses, intent upon truth and the observance of vows, who is spreading his banner of fame over the world?

sanskrit: व्यक्तम् रामस्य विज्ञाय शौचम् माहात्म्यम् उत्तमम्
न गात्रम् अम्शुभिः सूर्यः सम्तापयितुम् अर्हति
transliteration: vyaktam rāmasya vijñāya śaucam māhātmyam uttamam
na gātram amśubhiḥ sūryaḥ samtāpayitum arhati
english: Acquainted with Rāma's manifest purity and high magnanimity, the Sun himself will not dare burn his body with his rays.

sanskrit: राघवम् युक्त शीत उष्णः सेविष्यति सुखो अनिलः
transliteration: rāghavam yukta śīta uṣṇaḥ seviṣyati sukho anilaḥ
english: And issuing from the woods at all hours, the delicious air impregnated with heat and cold will serve Raghava.

sanskrit: शयानम् अनघम् रात्रौ पिता इव अभिपरिष्वजन्
transliteration: śayānam anagham rātrau pitā iva abhipariṣvajan
english: And when he will lie down at night, the Moon touching him with his beams and embracing him even like his own father, will gladden his heart.

sanskrit: ददौ च अस्त्राणि दिव्यानि यस्मै ब्रह्मा महा ओजसे
दानव इन्द्रम् हतम् दृष्ट्वा तिमि ध्वज सुतम् रणे
transliteration: dadau ca astrāṇi divyāni yasmai brahmā mahā ojase
dānava indram hatam dṛṣṭvā timi dhvaja sutam raṇe
english: That hero of mighty energy on whom Brahma had conferred celestial weapons, seeing that foremost of the Dānavas, the son of Timidhvaja, slain in battle, that tiger-like one, relying on the native strength of his arms, will fearlessly abide in the forest as if in his own home.

That hero of mighty energy on whom Brahma had conferred celestial weapons, seeing that foremost of the Dānavas, the son of Timidhvaja, slain in battle, that tiger-like one, relying on the native strength of his arms, will fearlessly abide in the forest as if in his own home.

sanskrit: कथम् न प्R^थिवी तस्य शासने स्थातुमर्हति
transliteration: katham na pthivī tasya śāsane sthātumarhati
english: And why should not the earth remain in the sway of him coming within the range of whose arms enemies find destruction?

sanskrit: या श्रीःशौर्यम् च रामस्य या च कल्याणसत्वता
transliteration: yā śrīḥśauryam ca rāmasya yā ca kalyāṇasatvatā
english: Considering Rāma's grace, heroism and auspiciousness, (there cannot be any doubt that) returning from the forest, he will speedily regain his own kingdom.

He is the sun of the sun, the lord of the lord, he is the auspiciousness of priine auspiciousness, the fame of fame, the forbearance of forbearance, the god of the gods, and the foremost of creatures. What evil qualities, O noble lady, will be perceived in him, whether he remains in the city or in the forest?

sanskrit: तस्य केह्यगुणा देवि वने वा प्यथवा पुरे
transliteration: tasya kehyaguṇā devi vane vā pyathavā pure

sanskrit: पृथिव्या सह वैदेह्या श्रिया च पुरुष ऋषभः
क्षिप्रम् तिसृभिर् एताभिः सह रामः अभिषेक्ष्यते
transliteration: pṛthivyā saha vaidehyā śriyā ca puruṣa ṛṣabhaḥ
kṣipram tisṛbhir etābhiḥ saha rāmaḥ abhiṣekṣyate
english: And that best of men, Räma, will soon be installed in the kingdom, in company with these three, the Earth, Vaidehī, and the goddess of victory.

sanskrit: दुह्खजम् विसृजन्ति अस्रम् निष्क्रामन्तम् उदीक्ष्य यम्
transliteration: duhkhajam visṛjanti asram niṣkrāmantam udīkṣya yam

english: Although overwhelmed with grief, the people of Ayodhyā, seeing that noble unvanquished one retiring to the woods clad in Kuśa and bark, are shedding tears begot of sorrow; yet accompanied by that Lakşmī, what is there that is incapable of being attained by him?

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणोव्रजति ह्यग्रे तस्य किम् नाम दुर्लभम्
transliteration: lakṣmaṇovrajati hyagre tasya kim nāma durlabham
english: And what is there that is incapable of being obtained by him before whom goes that foremost of bowmen himself bearing arrows, swords and other weapons?

sanskrit: जहिशोकम् च मोहम् च देवि सत्यम् ब्रवीमि ते
transliteration: jahiśokam ca moham ca devi satyam bravīmi te
english: You will again see him returned from the forest. O exalted one, chase your grief and sadness.
I tell you this truly. O blameless one, you will again, O auspicious lady, see your son, like to the new-risen moon, paying homage to your feet with his head.
And again seeing him returned and crowned with great auspiciousness, you will speedily shed the dew of delight.

sanskrit: मा शोको देवि दुःखम् वा न राअमे दृअह्य्RWऽशिवम्
क्षिप्रम् द्रक्ष्यसि पुत्रम् त्वम् ससीतम् सह लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: mā śoko devi duḥkham vā na rāame dṛahy'śivam
kṣipram drakṣyasi putram tvam sasītam saha lakṣmaṇam
english: O noble lady, do not grieve or lament. Evil cannot touch Räma. You will soon behold your son along with Sītā and Lakşmaņa.
O sinless one, it is for you to console these people. Why then, O revered one, do you suffer your heart to be thus overpowered?

sanskrit: नार्हा त्वम् शोचितुम् देवि यस्यास्ते राघवस्सुतः
न हि रामात्परो लोके विद्यते सत्पथे स्थितः
transliteration: nārhā tvam śocitum devi yasyāste rāghavassutaḥ
na hi rāmātparo loke vidyate satpathe sthitaḥ
english: O eminent one, you ought not to bewail, inasmuch as Rāghava is your son. In this world there is not another residing in honesty that is superior to Rāma.

sanskrit: मुदा अश्रु मोक्ष्यसे क्षिप्रम् मेघ लेका इव वार्षिकी
transliteration: mudā aśru mokṣyase kṣipram megha lekā iva vārṣikī
english: Beholding your son surrounded by his friends, bowing to you, you will soon shed blissful tears, even like a rain-cloud.

sanskrit: पुत्रः ते वरदः क्षिप्रम् अयोध्याम् पुनर् आगतः
transliteration: putraḥ te varadaḥ kṣipram ayodhyām punar āgataḥ
english: And soon will your son conferring boons, returning (to this place), press your feet with those soft and plump hands of his.
And even as a Chain of clouds speaks to a hill, you will speak to your worshipful and heroic son, surrounded by his friends. bowing to you.
Having thus addressed Rāma's mother and inspired her with hope in various words, the noble and pleasant and blameless Sumitrā, clever in speech, paused.
Hearing those words of Laksmana's mother, the wife of the best of men, Rāma's mother, had her sorrow destroyed in her person, even like and autumnal cloud surcharged with slight rain.

sanskrit: अनुजग्मुः प्रयान्तम् तम् वन वासाय मानवाः
transliteration: anujagmuḥ prayāntam tam vana vāsāya mānavāḥ
english: The people, who yarned after Rāma having truth for prowess, followed him repairing to the forest.

sanskrit: निवर्तिते अपि च बलात् सुहृद् वर्गे च राजिनि
न एव ते सम्न्यवर्तन्त रामस्य अनुगता रथम्
transliteration: nivartite api ca balāt suhṛd varge ca rājini
na eva te samnyavartanta rāmasya anugatā ratham
english: Even when the king in the interests of his son had with much ado restrained himself, these, following Răma's car, did not desist.

sanskrit: अयोध्या निलयानाम् हि पुरुषाणाम् महा यशाः
बभूव गुण सम्पन्नः पूर्ण चन्द्रैव प्रियः
transliteration: ayodhyā nilayānām hi puruṣāṇām mahā yaśāḥ
babhūva guṇa sampannaḥ pūrṇa candraiva priyaḥ
english: That illustrious one crowned with every perfection was dear to the inhabitants of Ayodhyā like to the full moon himself.

sanskrit: स याच्यमानः काकुत्स्थः स्वाभिः प्रकृतिभिस् तदा
कुर्वाणः पितरम् सत्यम् वनम् एव अन्वपद्यत
transliteration: sa yācyamānaḥ kākutsthaḥ svābhiḥ prakṛtibhis tadā
kurvāṇaḥ pitaram satyam vanam eva anvapadyata
english: Although besought by the subjects, the truthful Käkutstha having pledged his word to his father, kept on going to the forest.

sanskrit: उवाच रामः स्नेहेन ताः प्रजाः स्वाः प्रजाइव
transliteration: uvāca rāmaḥ snehena tāḥ prajāḥ svāḥ prajāiva
english: And affectionately eyeing them as if drinking them with his sight, Rāma touchingly addressed those subjects as if they were his own, The love and regard which the inhabitants of Ayodhyā have for me, let them, for pleasing me, extend in full measure towards Bharata.

sanskrit: या प्रीतिर् बहुमानः च मय्य् अयोध्या निवासिनाम्
मत् प्रिय अर्थम् विशेषेण भरते सा निवेश्यताम्
transliteration: yā prītir bahumānaḥ ca mayy ayodhyā nivāsinām
mat priya artham viśeṣeṇa bharate sā niveśyatām
english: And affectionately eyeing them as if drinking them with his sight, Rāma touchingly addressed those subjects as if they were his own, The love and regard which the inhabitants of Ayodhyā have for me, let them, for pleasing me, extend in full measure towards Bharata.

sanskrit: स हि कल्याण चारित्रः कैकेय्या आनन्द वर्धनः
करिष्यति यथावद् वः प्रियाणि च हितानि च
transliteration: sa hi kalyāṇa cāritraḥ kaikeyyā ānanda vardhanaḥ
kariṣyati yathāvad vaḥ priyāṇi ca hitāni ca
english: That enhancer of Kaikeyi's delight bearing an auspicious character, will duly compass your happiness and welfare.

sanskrit: ज्ञान वृद्धो वयो बालो मृदुर् वीर्य गुण अन्वितः
अनुरूपः स वो भर्ता भविष्यति भय अपहः
transliteration: jñāna vṛddho vayo bālo mṛdur vīrya guṇa anvitaḥ
anurūpaḥ sa vo bhartā bhaviṣyati bhaya apahaḥ
english: Aged by virtue of his wisdom, although young in years, and mild albeit furnished with heroic virtue, that remover of fear will make a fit ruler for you. son

sanskrit: स हि राज गुणैः युक्तः युव राजः समीक्षितः
अपि च अपि मया शिष्टैः कार्यम् वो भर्तृ शासनम्
transliteration: sa hi rāja guṇaiḥ yuktaḥ yuva rājaḥ samīkṣitaḥ
api ca api mayā śiṣṭaiḥ kāryam vo bhartṛ śāsanam
english: Crowned with every regal virtue and selected as the heir-apparent (by the monarch), he is more meritorious by far than I am. I behove you to obey the order of your master.

sanskrit: न च तप्येद् यथा च असौ वन वासम् गते मयि
महा राजः तथा कार्यो मम प्रिय चिकीर्षया
transliteration: na ca tapyed yathā ca asau vana vāsam gate mayi
mahā rājaḥ tathā kāryo mama priya cikīrṣayā
english: And seeking my good, it beloves you to act so that when I shall have gone to the forest, the king may not grieve.

sanskrit: यथा यथा दाशरथिर् धर्मम् एव आस्थितः अभवत्
तथा तथा प्रकृतयो रामम् पतिम् अकामयन्
transliteration: yathā yathā dāśarathir dharmam eva āsthitaḥ abhavat
tathā tathā prakṛtayo rāmam patim akāmayan
english: But as Daśaratha's son was bringing home to the people that their duty lay in obeying the royal Mandata, they desried that even Rāma should rule them.

sanskrit: बाष्पेण पिहितम् दीनम् रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
चकर्ष इव गुणैः बद्ध्वा जनम् पुनर् इव आसनम्
transliteration: bāṣpeṇa pihitam dīnam rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
cakarṣa iva guṇaiḥ baddhvā janam punar iva āsanam
english: Rāma in company with Sumitrā's attracted the inhabitants of the city subdued by his virtues, who stood with tears in their eyes.

sanskrit: ते द्विजाः त्रिविधम् वृद्धा ज्ञानेन वयसा ओजसा
वयः प्रकम्प शिरसो दूरात् ऊचुर् इदम् वचः
transliteration: te dvijāḥ trividham vṛddhā jñānena vayasā ojasā
vayaḥ prakampa śiraso dūrāt ūcur idam vacaḥ
english: The three kinds of the twice-born ones, viz., those old by virtue, respectively, of age, wisdom, and ascetic energy, the old folks with their heads shaking through length of years, cried from a distance.

sanskrit: वहन्तः जवना रामम् भो भो जात्याः तुरम् गमाः
निवर्तध्वम् न गन्तव्यम् हिता भवत भर्तरि
transliteration: vahantaḥ javanā rāmam bho bho jātyāḥ turam gamāḥ
nivartadhvam na gantavyam hitā bhavata bhartari
english: O you fleet coursers boasting of exalted extraction that bear Rāma away, do you desist, do not go; do you do even what is for the good of your master.
And more pareicularly being creatures furnished with ears, do you, your horses, knowing our prayer, desist.

sanskrit: उपवाह्यः तु वो भर्ता न अपवाह्यः पुरात् वनम्
transliteration: upavāhyaḥ tu vo bhartā na apavāhyaḥ purāt vanam
english: Pure of spirit and heroic and ever firm in noble promises, that master of yours should in justice be carried (to the city) and not to the forest away from it.

sanskrit: एवम् आर्त प्रलापाम्स् तान् वृद्धान् प्रलपतः द्विजान्
अवेक्ष्य सहसा रामः रथात् अवततार ह
transliteration: evam ārta pralāpāms tān vṛddhān pralapataḥ dvijān
avekṣya sahasā rāmaḥ rathāt avatatāra ha
english: Suddenly seeing those old Brāhmaṇas thus lamenting distressfully, Rāma speedily descended from his car.

sanskrit: पद्भ्याम् एव जगाम अथ ससीतः सह लक्ष्मणः
सम्निकृष्ट पद न्यासो रामः वन परायणः
transliteration: padbhyām eva jagāma atha sasītaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
samnikṛṣṭa pada nyāso rāmaḥ vana parāyaṇaḥ
english: Along with Lakşmaņa and Sitā, Rāma bound for the forest, began to walk near them on foot.

sanskrit: द्विजातीम्स् तु पदातीम्स् तान् रामः चारित्र वत्सलः
न शशाक घृणा चक्षुः परिमोक्तुम् रथेन सः
transliteration: dvijātīms tu padātīms tān rāmaḥ cāritra vatsalaḥ
na śaśāka ghṛṇā cakṣuḥ parimoktum rathena saḥ
english: Endowed with kindness, that friend of the good, Rāma, could not by proceeding on his car bear to pare with the Brāhmaṇas that were following on foot.

sanskrit: गच्चन्तम् एव तम् दृष्ट्वा रामम् सम्भ्रान्त मानसाः
ऊचुः परम सम्तप्ता रामम् वाक्यम् इदम् द्विजाः
transliteration: gaccantam eva tam dṛṣṭvā rāmam sambhrānta mānasāḥ
ūcuḥ parama samtaptā rāmam vākyam idam dvijāḥ
english: Seeing him thus going, the Brāhamaņas with agitated hearts, and burning in grief, addressed Rāma in these words.

sanskrit: ब्राह्मण्यम् कृत्स्नम् एतत् त्वाम् ब्रह्मण्यम् अनुगच्चति
द्विज स्कन्ध अधिरूढाः त्वाम् अग्नयो अपि अनुयान्ति अमी
transliteration: brāhmaṇyam kṛtsnam etat tvām brahmaṇyam anugaccati
dvija skandha adhirūḍhāḥ tvām agnayo api anuyānti amī
english: The Brāhmaṇas in a body are following you ever seeking their good, and mounting on the shoulders of the regenerate ones, the (sacrificial) Fires are walking in your wake.

sanskrit: वाजपेय समुत्थानि चत्राणि एतानि पश्य नः
पृष्ठतः अनुप्रयातानि हम्सान् इव जल अत्यये
transliteration: vājapeya samutthāni catrāṇi etāni paśya naḥ
pṛṣṭhataḥ anuprayātāni hamsān iva jala atyaye
english: And behold these raised umbrellas of ours got from the Vājapeya sacrifice, that like to autumnal clouds follow at your back.

sanskrit: एभिः चायाम् करिष्यामः स्वैः चत्रैः वाजपेयिकैः
transliteration: ebhiḥ cāyām kariṣyāmaḥ svaiḥ catraiḥ vājapeyikaiḥ
english: With these umbrellas got at the Vājapeya sacrifice, we will afford shade to Rāma destitute of his own white umbrella, when he shall feel the heat of the (solar) rays.

sanskrit: या हि नः सततम् बुद्धिर् वेद मन्त्र अनुसारिणी
त्वत् कृते सा कृता वत्स वन वास अनुसारिणी
transliteration: yā hi naḥ satatam buddhir veda mantra anusāriṇī
tvat kṛte sā kṛtā vatsa vana vāsa anusāriṇī
english: That intelligence of ours which ever follows the Vedic Mantras, is now, O child, ready to follow you to the forest in your interests.

sanskrit: हृदयेष्व् अवतिष्ठन्ते वेदा ये नः परम् धनम्
वत्स्यन्ति अपि गृहेष्व् एव दाराः चारित्र रक्षिताः
transliteration: hṛdayeṣv avatiṣṭhante vedā ye naḥ param dhanam
vatsyanti api gṛheṣv eva dārāḥ cāritra rakṣitāḥ
english: That best of treasurers, the Vedas, resides in our bosoms; and our wives protected by their chastity shall abide in our homes.

sanskrit: न पुनर् निश्चयः कार्यः त्वद् गतौ सुकृता मतिः
त्वयि धर्म व्यपेक्षे तु किम् स्यात् धर्मम् अवेक्षितुम्
transliteration: na punar niścayaḥ kāryaḥ tvad gatau sukṛtā matiḥ
tvayi dharma vyapekṣe tu kim syāt dharmam avekṣitum
english: As we have already made up our minds to follow you, it is useless to fix our hearts afresh. But if you overlooks virtues, what becomes of abiding by righteousness?* *Another reading is; What becomes of the virtue that we expect at your hands?

sanskrit: याचितः नो निवर्तस्व हम्स शुक्ल शिरः रुहैः
शिरोभिर् निभृत आचार मही पतन पाम्शुलैः
transliteration: yācitaḥ no nivartasva hamsa śukla śiraḥ ruhaiḥ
śirobhir nibhṛta ācāra mahī patana pāmśulaiḥ
english: O you that are ever firm in virtue, we beseech you by humbling to the dust our heads covered with hair white-hued like cranes, do you desist.

sanskrit: बहूनाम् वितता यज्ञा द्विजानाम् यैह आगताः
तेषाम् समाप्तिर् आयत्ता तव वत्स निवर्तने
transliteration: bahūnām vitatā yajñā dvijānām yaiha āgatāḥ
teṣām samāptir āyattā tava vatsa nivartane
english: These numerous Brāhmaṇas that have come hither have entered upon many a sacrifice. The completion of these, O child, depends upon your return.

sanskrit: भक्तिमन्ति हि भूतानि जम्गम अजम्गमानि च
याचमानेषु तेषु त्वम् भक्तिम् भक्तेषु दर्शय
transliteration: bhaktimanti hi bhūtāni jamgama ajamgamāni ca
yācamāneṣu teṣu tvam bhaktim bhakteṣu darśaya
english: All creatures mobile and immobile cherish you with high regard. All these beseech you. Do you show consideration to those that regard you.

sanskrit: अनुगम्तुम् अशक्ताः त्वाम् मूलैः उद्धिऋत वेगिभिः
उन्नता वायु वेगेन विक्रोशन्ति इव पादपाः
transliteration: anugamtum aśaktāḥ tvām mūlaiḥ uddhiṛta vegibhiḥ
unnatā vāyu vegena vikrośanti iva pādapāḥ
english: Tall trees deprived of motion in consequence of being fast rooted to the earth and incapable of following you, are prohibiting you by sounding with the wind.

sanskrit: निश्चेष्ट आहार सम्चारा वृक्ष एक स्थान विष्ठिताः
पक्षिणो अपि प्रयाचन्ते सर्व भूत अनुकम्पिनम्
transliteration: niśceṣṭa āhāra samcārā vṛkṣa eka sthāna viṣṭhitāḥ
pakṣiṇo api prayācante sarva bhūta anukampinam
english: And birds staying upon trees and neither manifesting any motion nor seeking for their food, beseech you to have compassion upon all creatures.

sanskrit: ददृशे तमसा तत्र वारयन्ति इव राघवम्
transliteration: dadṛśe tamasā tatra vārayanti iva rāghavam
english: While the Brāhmaṇas were loudly demanding the return of Rāma, he found the darkness to descend as if forbidding him.
Then Sumantra unyoked the fatigued horses from the car, which at once fell to rolling in the dust. And then bathing and making them drink, he soon as the dusk set in, set fare before them.

sanskrit: ततः तु तमसा तीरम् रम्यम् आश्रित्य राघवः
सीताम् उद्वीक्ष्य सौमित्रिम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tataḥ tu tamasā tīram ramyam āśritya rāghavaḥ
sītām udvīkṣya saumitrim idam vacanam abravīt
english: Then Rāghava pausing on the banks of the Tamasā, looked at Sītā and spoke to Sumitrā's son, saying.

sanskrit: इयम् अद्य निशा पूर्वा सौमित्रे प्रस्थिता वनम्
वन वासस्य भद्रम् ते स न उत्कण्ठितुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: iyam adya niśā pūrvā saumitre prasthitā vanam
vana vāsasya bhadram te sa na utkaṇṭhitum arhasi
english: O son of Sumitrā, this is the first night of our exile into the forest. From this day it behoveth you not, good betide you, to suffer your mind to grieve (by dwelling on past joys.)

sanskrit: पश्य शून्यानि अरण्यानि रुदन्ति इव समन्ततः
यथा निलयम् आयद्भिर् निलीनानि मृग द्विजैः
transliteration: paśya śūnyāni araṇyāni rudanti iva samantataḥ
yathā nilayam āyadbhir nilīnāni mṛga dvijaiḥ
english: The empty forest resounding with the cries of beasts and birds returned to their abodes, covered with gloom, seems to weep on all sides.

sanskrit: अद्य अयोध्या तु नगरी राज धानी पितुर् मम
सस्त्री पुम्सा गतान् अस्मान् शोचिष्यति न सम्शयः
transliteration: adya ayodhyā tu nagarī rāja dhānī pitur mama
sastrī pumsā gatān asmān śociṣyati na samśayaḥ
english: Doubtless to-day the men and women of Ayodhyā, the metropolis of my father, are bewailing us retired to the forest.

sanskrit: त्वाम् च माम् च नरव्याघ्र शत्रघ्नभरतौ तथा
transliteration: tvām ca mām ca naravyāghra śatraghnabharatau tathā
english: O foremost of men, the people are attached to yourself, the monarch, Bharata, Satrughna, and myself, because of our various good qualities.

sanskrit: अपि वानौध भवेताम् तु रुदन्तौ तावभीक्ष्णशः
transliteration: api vānaudha bhavetām tu rudantau tāvabhīkṣṇaśaḥ
english: I bewail our father as well as my illustrious mother. I fear lest lamenting ceaselessly, they become blind.

sanskrit: भरतः खलु धर्म आत्मा पितरम् मातरम् च मे
धर्म अर्थ काम सहितैः वाक्यैः आश्वासयिष्यति
transliteration: bharataḥ khalu dharma ātmā pitaram mātaram ca me
dharma artha kāma sahitaiḥ vākyaiḥ āśvāsayiṣyati
english: But surely the virtuous Bharata will console our father and mother with words fraught with virtuc, interest and profit.

sanskrit: भरतस्य आनृशम्सत्वम् सम्चिन्त्य अहम् पुनः पुनः
न अनुशोचामि पितरम् मातरम् च अपि लक्ष्मण
transliteration: bharatasya ānṛśamsatvam samcintya aham punaḥ punaḥ
na anuśocāmi pitaram mātaram ca api lakṣmaṇa
english: Reflecting again and again on Bharata's sincerity of soul, I do not, O mighty-armed one, bewail either my mother or my father.

sanskrit: त्वया कार्यम् नर व्याघ्र माम् अनुव्रजता कृतम्
अन्वेष्टव्या हि वैदेह्या रक्षण अर्थे सहायता
transliteration: tvayā kāryam nara vyāghra mām anuvrajatā kṛtam
anveṣṭavyā hi vaidehyā rakṣaṇa arthe sahāyatā
english: foremost of men, that you have followed me in what is your duty. (If you had not done so), I should have to seek elsewhere for the protection of Vaidehī.

sanskrit: अद्भिर् एव तु सौमित्रे वत्स्याम्य् अद्य निशाम् इमाम्
एतद्द् हि रोचते मह्यम् वन्ये अपि विविधे सति
transliteration: adbhir eva tu saumitre vatsyāmy adya niśām imām
etadd hi rocate mahyam vanye api vividhe sati
english: foremost of men, that you have followed me in what is your duty. (If you had not done so), I should have to seek elsewhere for the protection of Vaidehī.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा तु सौमित्रम् सुमन्त्रम् अपि राघवः
अप्रमत्तः त्वम् अश्वेषु भव सौम्य इति उवाच ह
transliteration: evam uktvā tu saumitram sumantram api rāghavaḥ
apramattaḥ tvam aśveṣu bhava saumya iti uvāca ha
english: O Sumitrā's son, I will spend here this night, subsisting alone. Even this recommends itself to me, although the forest yields various kinds of fruits.

sanskrit: सो अश्वान् सुमन्त्रः सम्यम्य सूर्ये अस्तम् समुपागते
transliteration: so aśvān sumantraḥ samyamya sūrye astam samupāgate
english: Having said this to Sumitrā's son, Raghava spoke to Sumantra, saying, “O mild one, do you now heedfully tend the horses.” Then at sunset, fastening the horses, Sumantra fed them plentifully with grass, and then came back.

sanskrit: उपास्यतु शिवाम् सम्ध्याम् दृष्ट्वा रात्रिम् उपस्थिताम्
रामस्य शयनम् चक्रे सूतः सौमित्रिणा सह
transliteration: upāsyatu śivām samdhyām dṛṣṭvā rātrim upasthitām
rāmasya śayanam cakre sūtaḥ saumitriṇā saha
english: Then seeing the night arrived, the charioteer worshipped the beneficent Sandhyā, and then in company with Sumitrā's son, prepared Rāma's bed. on water

sanskrit: ताम् शय्याम् तमसा तीरे वीक्ष्य वृक्ष दलैः कृताम्
रामः सौमित्रिणाम् सार्धम् सभार्यः सम्विवेश ह
transliteration: tām śayyām tamasā tīre vīkṣya vṛkṣa dalaiḥ kṛtām
rāmaḥ saumitriṇām sārdham sabhāryaḥ samviveśa ha
english: And looking at that bed on the shores of the Tamasā surrounded by trees, Rāma along with his wife and the son of Sumitrā, lay down,

sanskrit: सभार्यम् सम्प्रसुप्तम् तम् भ्रातरम् वीक्ष्य लक्ष्मणः
कथयाम् आस सूताय रामस्य विविधान् गुणान्
transliteration: sabhāryam samprasuptam tam bhrātaram vīkṣya lakṣmaṇaḥ
kathayām āsa sūtāya rāmasya vividhān guṇān
english: When Lakşmaņa found that Rāma afflicted with fatigue had slept together with his spouse, he began to speak to the charioteer concerning the various qualities of Rāma.

sanskrit: जाग्रतः हि एव ताम् रात्रिम् सौमित्रेर् उदितः रविः
सूतस्य तमसा तीरे रामस्य ब्रुवतः गुणान्
transliteration: jāgrataḥ hi eva tām rātrim saumitrer uditaḥ raviḥ
sūtasya tamasā tīre rāmasya bruvataḥ guṇān
english: As remaining awake in the night, Sumitrā's son was engaged in expatiating to the charioteer on the virtues of Rāma on the banks of the Tamasă, the sun arose.

sanskrit: गो कुल आकुल तीरायाः तमसायाः विदूरतः
अवसत् तत्र ताम् रात्रिम् रामः प्रकृतिभिः सह
transliteration: go kula ākula tīrāyāḥ tamasāyāḥ vidūrataḥ
avasat tatra tām rātrim rāmaḥ prakṛtibhiḥ saha
english: Rāma abode that night along with the subjects at some distance from the banks of the Tamasā filled with kine.

sanskrit: उत्थाय तु महा तेजाः प्रकृतीस् ता निशाम्य च
अब्रवीद् भ्रातरम् रामः लक्ष्मणम् पुण्य लक्षणम्
transliteration: utthāya tu mahā tejāḥ prakṛtīs tā niśāmya ca
abravīd bhrātaram rāmaḥ lakṣmaṇam puṇya lakṣaṇam
english: Rising (from his bed), that highly energetic one, Rāma, viewing the subjects (asleep), addressed his brother Lakşmana graced with auspicious marks.

sanskrit: अस्मद् व्यपेक्षान् सौमित्रे निरपेक्षान् गृहेष्व् अपि
वृक्ष मूलेषु सम्सुप्तान् पश्य लक्ष्मण साम्प्रतम्
transliteration: asmad vyapekṣān saumitre nirapekṣān gṛheṣv api
vṛkṣa mūleṣu samsuptān paśya lakṣmaṇa sāmpratam
english: O son of Sumitrā, these that for our sake have disregarded their own homes, are still asleep beneath the trees.

sanskrit: यथा एते नियमम् पौराः कुर्वन्ति अस्मन् निवर्तने
अपि प्राणान् असिष्यन्ति न तु त्यक्ष्यन्ति निश्चयम्
transliteration: yathā ete niyamam paurāḥ kurvanti asman nivartane
api prāṇān asiṣyanti na tu tyakṣyanti niścayam
english: These citizens have determined upon making me turn back from the forest, they would rather renounce their lives than give up their resolve.

sanskrit: यावद् एव तु सम्सुप्ताः तावद् एव वयम् लघु
रथम् आरुह्य गच्चामः पन्थानम् अकुतः भयम्
transliteration: yāvad eva tu samsuptāḥ tāvad eva vayam laghu
ratham āruhya gaccāmaḥ panthānam akutaḥ bhayam
english: Let us while they are asleep ascending on our car, swiftly go our way without fear of molestation.

sanskrit: अतः भूयो अपि न इदानीम् इक्ष्वाकु पुर वासिनः
स्वपेयुर् अनुरक्ता माम् वृष्क मूलानि सम्श्रिताः
transliteration: ataḥ bhūyo api na idānīm ikṣvāku pura vāsinaḥ
svapeyur anuraktā mām vṛṣka mūlāni samśritāḥ
english: Attached to me, the denizons of Ikşvāku's city will not again indulge in sleep underneath trees.

sanskrit: पौरा हि आत्म कृतात् दुह्खात् विप्रमोच्या नृप आत्मजैः
न तु खल्व् आत्मना योज्या दुह्खेन पुर वासिनः
transliteration: paurā hi ātma kṛtāt duhkhāt vipramocyā nṛpa ātmajaiḥ
na tu khalv ātmanā yojyā duhkhena pura vāsinaḥ
english: A prince should deliver citizens from the calamity they bring upon themselves; but he should by no means drag them into those which he himself has brought on.

sanskrit: अब्रवील् लक्ष्मणो रामम् साक्षात् धर्मम् इव स्थितम्
रोचते मे महा प्राज्ञ क्षिप्रम् आरुह्यताम् इति
transliteration: abravīl lakṣmaṇo rāmam sākṣāt dharmam iva sthitam
rocate me mahā prājña kṣipram āruhyatām iti
english: Then Lakşmana spoke to Rāma like to manifest Virtue on earth, "O wise one, even this is relished also by me. Do you speedily ascend (the car.)"
Rāma said to the charioteer, "Do you at once yoke the car. I will repair to the forest. Do you, my master, swiftly go hence."

sanskrit: सूतः ततः सम्त्वरितः स्यन्दनम् तैः हय उत्तमैः
transliteration: sūtaḥ tataḥ samtvaritaḥ syandanam taiḥ haya uttamaiḥ
english: Thereupon the charioteer bestirring himself, yoking the excellent horses to the car, said to Rāma with joined hands.

sanskrit: अयम् युक्तो महाबाहो रथस्ते रथिनाम् वर
transliteration: ayam yukto mahābāho rathaste rathinām vara
english: Here, O mighty-armed one, is your car ready yoked, O foremost of car-warriors. Do you speedily ascend, good betide you, along with Sītā and Laksmaņa.
Ascending the car after equipping himself, Rāghava crossed the rapidly-rushing Tamasā abounding in eddies.
Having crossed (the stream), the auspicious and mighty-armed one came upon a safe and goodly-high way capable of inspiring even timid people with confidence.

sanskrit: मोहन अर्थम् तु पौराणाम् सूतम् रामः अब्रवीद् वचः
उदन् मुखः प्रयाहि त्वम् रथम् आस्थाय सारथे
transliteration: mohana artham tu paurāṇām sūtam rāmaḥ abravīd vacaḥ
udan mukhaḥ prayāhi tvam ratham āsthāya sārathe

sanskrit: मुहूर्तम् त्वरितम् गत्वा निर्गतय रथम् पुनः
यथा न विद्युः पौरा माम् तथा कुरु समाहितः
transliteration: muhūrtam tvaritam gatvā nirgataya ratham punaḥ
yathā na vidyuḥ paurā mām tathā kuru samāhitaḥ
english: But with the view of deluding the citizens, Rāma said to the charioteer, "O charioteer, do you ascending the car proceed northwards; and having proceeded swiftly for a while, do you turn the car. Do you carefully act so that the citizens nay not perceive this."

sanskrit: रामस्य वचनम् श्रुत्वा तथा चक्रे स सारथिः
transliteration: rāmasya vacanam śrutvā tathā cakre sa sārathiḥ
english: Hearing Rāma's words, the charioteer did accordingly, and having returned said to Rāma to ascend the car.
Then on those perpetuators of the Raghu race having along with Sītā been seated on the car, the charioteer drove the horses by that road which conducted to the hermitage.

sanskrit: उदङ्मुखम् तम् तु रथम् चकार स
transliteration: udaṅmukham tam tu ratham cakāra sa
english: Then placing the car with its face northwards for the purpose of invoking auspiciousness on their journey, that mighty charioteer, Dasaratha's son established on the vehicle, set out for the forest.

sanskrit: प्रभातायाम् तु शर्वर्याम् पौराः ते राघवो विना
शोक उपहत निश्चेष्टा बभूवुर् हत चेतसः
transliteration: prabhātāyām tu śarvaryām paurāḥ te rāghavo vinā
śoka upahata niśceṣṭā babhūvur hata cetasaḥ
english: When the night had departed an day dawned, the citizens not finding Rāghava, overwhelmed with grief and were deprived of their senses. were

sanskrit: शोकज अश्रु परिद्यूना वीक्षमाणाः ततः ततः
आलोकम् अपि रामस्य न पश्यन्ति स्म दुह्खिताः
transliteration: śokaja aśru paridyūnā vīkṣamāṇāḥ tataḥ tataḥ
ālokam api rāmasya na paśyanti sma duhkhitāḥ
english: With tears of grief and afflicted with distress, they looked hither and thither, but they could not discover even the dust raised by Rāma's car.

sanskrit: कृपणाः करुणा वाचो वदन्ति स्म मनस्विनः
transliteration: kṛpaṇāḥ karuṇā vāco vadanti sma manasvinaḥ
english: And those intelligent ones, extremely distressed on being deprived of Rāma endowed with understanding, with countenance betokening sorrow, spoke these piteous words.
Oh! fie on that sleep through which having been deprived of senses, well shall not to-day behold Rāma of broad chest and mighty arms.

sanskrit: भक्तम् जनम् परित्यज्य प्रवासम् राघवो गतः
transliteration: bhaktam janam parityajya pravāsam rāghavo gataḥ
english: How could Rāma of mighty arms, resorting to this undesirable course, has gone into exile as an ascetic, leaving behind those that regard him dearly?

sanskrit: यो नः सदा पालयति पिता पुत्रानिवौरसान्
कथम् रघूणाम् स श्रेष्ठस्त्यक्त्वा नो विपिनम् गतः
transliteration: yo naḥ sadā pālayati pitā putrānivaurasān
katham raghūṇām sa śreṣṭhastyaktvā no vipinam gataḥ
english: Why has that foremost of Raghus, who has always cherished us even as a father cherishes his sons begot by his own loins, forsaking us, betaken himself to the forest?

sanskrit: रामेण रहितानाम् हि किमर्थम् जीवितम् हि नः
transliteration: rāmeṇa rahitānām hi kimartham jīvitam hi naḥ
english: Here will we either renounce our lives, or direct our course to the north to meet death. Of what good are our lives, when we have been deprived of Rāma?

sanskrit: सन्ति शुष्काणि काष्ठानि प्रभूतानि महान्ति च
तैः प्रज्वाल्य चिताम् सर्वे प्रविशामोऽथ पावकम्
transliteration: santi śuṣkāṇi kāṣṭhāni prabhūtāni mahānti ca
taiḥ prajvālya citām sarve praviśāmo'tha pāvakam
english: There are nuge trunks of dry wood to be got here in plenty. Lighting the pile of woods will we all enter the fire.

sanskrit: नीतः स राघवोऽस्माभिर्ति वक्तुम् कथम् क्षमम्
transliteration: nītaḥ sa rāghavo'smābhirti vaktum katham kṣamam
english: What shall we say (when people ask us?) How can we say, 'We took hence the mightyarmed, sweet-speeched and unavenging Rāma?

sanskrit: सा नूनम् नगरी दीना दृष्ट्वाऽस्मान् राघवम् विना
transliteration: sā nūnam nagarī dīnā dṛṣṭvā'smān rāghavam vinā
english: Surely seeing us without Rāghava, the forlorn city with her women, children and grown up folks will be plunged in grief.

sanskrit: विहिनास्तेन च पुनः कथम् पश्याम ताम् पुरीम्
transliteration: vihināstena ca punaḥ katham paśyāma tām purīm
english: We had issued with that high-souled hero. Deprived of him, how shall we behold that city again?

sanskrit: इतीव बहुधा वाचो बाहुमुद्यम्य ते जनाः
transliteration: itīva bahudhā vāco bāhumudyamya te janāḥ
english: Thus raising up their arms, they stricken with grief, indulged in lamentations, like to kine deprived of their calves.

sanskrit: ततः मार्ग अनुसारेण गत्वा किम्चित् क्षणम् पुनःमार्ग नाशात् विषादेन महता समभिप्लुतः
transliteration: tataḥ mārga anusāreṇa gatvā kimcit kṣaṇam punaḥmārga nāśāt viṣādena mahatā samabhiplutaḥ
english: Then following for a while the track of the car, they, missing the track, became overwhelmed with woe.

sanskrit: किम् इदम् किम् करिष्यामः दैवेन उपहताइति
transliteration: kim idam kim kariṣyāmaḥ daivena upahatāiti
english: And then those intelligent ones came back by the track of the car. "What is this? What shall we do? We have been foiled by some supernatural agency."

sanskrit: ततः यथा आगतेन एव मार्गेण क्लान्त चेतसः
अयोध्याम् अगमन् सर्वे पुरीम् व्यथित सज्जनाम्
transliteration: tataḥ yathā āgatena eva mārgeṇa klānta cetasaḥ
ayodhyām agaman sarve purīm vyathita sajjanām
english: Then they returned to the city of Ayodhyā with its good people oppressed with grief, by the self-same way by which they had come.

And entering their wealthy mansions, they deprived of their senses by grief, could not recognize them for their own, nor could they with their hearts rendered absolutely cheerless, although looking at them minutely, distinguish their own from others.

sanskrit: स्वम् स्वम् निलयम् आगम्य पुत्र दारैः समावृताः
अश्रूणि मुमुचुः सर्वे बाष्पेण पिहित आननाः
transliteration: svam svam nilayam āgamya putra dāraiḥ samāvṛtāḥ
aśrūṇi mumucuḥ sarve bāṣpeṇa pihita ānanāḥ

sanskrit: न च आहृष्यन् न च अमोदन् वणिजो न प्रसारयन्
न च अशोभन्त पण्यानि न अपचन् गृह मेधिनः
transliteration: na ca āhṛṣyan na ca amodan vaṇijo na prasārayan
na ca aśobhanta paṇyāni na apacan gṛha medhinaḥ
english: They forgot to rejoice or make merry, and the traders did not spread (their stores), and stalls did not grace the place, and the householders did not cook, and people did not rejoice on recovering lost property or gaining a profuse accession of wealth, and mothers did not feel any delight on beholding their first-born.

sanskrit: नष्टम् दृष्ट्वा न अभ्यनन्दन् विपुलम् वा धन आगमम्
पुत्रम् प्रथमजम् लब्ध्वा जननी न अभ्यनन्दत
transliteration: naṣṭam dṛṣṭvā na abhyanandan vipulam vā dhana āgamam
putram prathamajam labdhvā jananī na abhyanandata
