english: They forgot to rejoice or make merry, and the traders did not spread (their stores), and stalls did not grace the place, and the householders did not cook, and people did not rejoice on recovering lost property or gaining a profuse accession of wealth, and mothers did not feel any delight on beholding their first-born.

sanskrit: गृहे गृहे रुदन्त्यः च भर्तारम् गृहम् आगतम्
व्यगर्हयन्तः दुह्ख आर्ता वाग्भिस् तोत्रैः इव द्विपान्
transliteration: gṛhe gṛhe rudantyaḥ ca bhartāram gṛham āgatam
vyagarhayantaḥ duhkha ārtā vāgbhis totraiḥ iva dvipān
english: And in every home females afflicted with woe, weeping child their husbands coming home, with the following words as (drivers) spur elephants with hooks.

sanskrit: किम् नु तेषाम् गृहैः कार्यम् किम् दारैः किम् धनेन वा
पुत्रैः वा किम् सुखैः वा अपि ये न पश्यन्ति राघवम्
transliteration: kim nu teṣām gṛhaiḥ kāryam kim dāraiḥ kim dhanena vā
putraiḥ vā kim sukhaiḥ vā api ye na paśyanti rāghavam
english: Of what use are their houses, and wives, and wealth, and sons, and comforts, to those who see not Rāghava (in their midst?)

sanskrit: एकः सत् पुरुषो लोके लक्ष्मणः सह सीतया
यो अनुगच्चति काकुत्स्थम् रामम् परिचरन् वने
transliteration: ekaḥ sat puruṣo loke lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā
yo anugaccati kākutstham rāmam paricaran vane
english: There is one only good man in this world even Lakşmaņa, who along with Sītā is following Käkutstha Rāma to the woods.

sanskrit: आपगाः कृत पुण्याः ताः पद्मिन्यः च सराम्सि च
येषु स्नास्यति काकुत्स्थो विगाह्य सलिलम् शुचि
transliteration: āpagāḥ kṛta puṇyāḥ tāḥ padminyaḥ ca sarāmsi ca
yeṣu snāsyati kākutstho vigāhya salilam śuci
english: Those streams, assemblage of lotuses, and pools are blessed by which bathing in the sacred waters, Kakutstha will pass.

sanskrit: आपगाः च महा अनूपाः सानुमन्तः च पर्वताः
transliteration: āpagāḥ ca mahā anūpāḥ sānumantaḥ ca parvatāḥ
english: And romantic forests and woods, watery expanses of mighty volume, and mountains with flat spaces, will grace Kākutstha.

sanskrit: काननम् वा अपि शैलम् वा यम् रामः अभिगमिष्यति
प्रिय अतिथिम् इव प्राप्तम् न एनम् शक्ष्यन्ति अनर्चितुम्
transliteration: kānanam vā api śailam vā yam rāmaḥ abhigamiṣyati
priya atithim iva prāptam na enam śakṣyanti anarcitum
english: And forests and hills to which will repair Rāma cannot go without paying him homage like to a welcome guest.

sanskrit: विचित्र कुसुम आपीडा बहु मन्जलि धारिणः
अकाले च अपि मुख्यानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च
transliteration: vicitra kusuma āpīḍā bahu manjali dhāriṇaḥ
akāle ca api mukhyāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca

sanskrit: अकाले चापि मुख्यानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च
transliteration: akāle cāpi mukhyāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca
english: And hills from regard will show to Rāma arrived there the choicest flowers and fruits even out of season and will supply him with fountains of pure water.

sanskrit: विदर्शयन्तः विविधान् भूयः चित्रामः च निर्झरान्
transliteration: vidarśayantaḥ vividhān bhūyaḥ citrāmaḥ ca nirjharān
english: And hills from regard will show to Rāma arrived there the choicest flowers and fruits even out of season and will supply him with fountains of pure water.

sanskrit: यत्र रामः भयम् न अत्र न अस्ति तत्र पराभवः
transliteration: yatra rāmaḥ bhayam na atra na asti tatra parābhavaḥ
english: And presenting him with many a charming fountain, trees will delight Rāma at the tops of mountains.* Where Rama is, there is nor fear or failure. That mighty-armed son of Dasaratha is heroic. Let us while he is yet ahead within a short distance of us, follow Rāghava. *The meaning is, Trees will please Rāghava by spreading for him a bed of leaves and flowers.

sanskrit: स हि शूरः महा बाहुः पुत्रः दशरथस्य च
पुरा भवति नो दूरात् अनुगच्चाम राघवम्
transliteration: sa hi śūraḥ mahā bāhuḥ putraḥ daśarathasya ca
purā bhavati no dūrāt anugaccāma rāghavam
english: And presenting him with many a charming fountain, trees will delight Rāma at the tops of mountains.* Where Rama is, there is nor fear or failure. That mighty-armed son of Dasaratha is heroic. Let us while he is yet ahead within a short distance of us, follow Rāghava. *The meaning is, Trees will please Rāghava by spreading for him a bed of leaves and flowers.

sanskrit: पादच् चाया सुखा भर्तुस् तादृशस्य महात्मनः
स हि नाथो जनस्य अस्य स गतिः स परायणम्
transliteration: pādac cāyā sukhā bhartus tādṛśasya mahātmanaḥ
sa hi nātho janasya asya sa gatiḥ sa parāyaṇam
english: Even the shadow of the feet of our master, so high-souled, would bring us happiness. He is the lord of all these, he is the refuge, he is the accomplishment of our religious duties.

sanskrit: वयम् परिचरिष्यामः सीताम् यूयम् तु राघवम्
इति पौर स्त्रियो भर्तृऋन् दुह्ख आर्ताः तत् तत् अब्रुवन्
transliteration: vayam paricariṣyāmaḥ sītām yūyam tu rāghavam
iti paura striyo bhartṛṛn duhkha ārtāḥ tat tat abruvan
english: We and you, will serve Sītā, and Rāghava. Thus afflicted with grief, the women of the city spoke to their husbands.

sanskrit: युष्माकम् राघवो अरण्ये योग क्षेमम् विधास्यति
सीता नारी जनस्य अस्य योग क्षेमम् करिष्यति
transliteration: yuṣmākam rāghavo araṇye yoga kṣemam vidhāsyati
sītā nārī janasya asya yoga kṣemam kariṣyati
english: In the forest Rāghava will attain for you the unattainable and protect what is attained; and Sītā being a female will do the same for these (women.)

sanskrit: को न्व् अनेन अप्रतीतेन स उत्कण्ठित जनेन च
transliteration: ko nv anena apratītena sa utkaṇṭhita janena ca
english: Who will take pleasure in residing in a dwelling where the heart dies within itself, which is devoid of delight, where the people are always agitated with anxiety and which is exceedingly disagreeable?

sanskrit: कैकेय्या यदि चेद् राज्यम् स्यात् अधर्म्यम् अनाथवत्
न हि नो जीवितेन अर्थः कुतः पुत्रैः कुतः धनैः
transliteration: kaikeyyā yadi ced rājyam syāt adharmyam anāthavat
na hi no jīvitena arthaḥ kutaḥ putraiḥ kutaḥ dhanaiḥ
english: If this kingdom devolves on Kaikeyi it will be divested of all virtues and will be like to one without a master. And of what avail then is our life itself, not to speak of sons and wealth.

sanskrit: यया पुत्रः च भर्ता च त्यक्ताव् ऐश्वर्य कारणात्
कम् सा परिहरेद् अन्यम् कैकेयी कुल पाम्सनी
transliteration: yayā putraḥ ca bhartā ca tyaktāv aiśvarya kāraṇāt
kam sā parihared anyam kaikeyī kula pāmsanī
english: Whom else will that stainer of her line, Kaikeyī, forsake now, who for the sake of wealth has forsaken her son and her lord?

sanskrit: कैकेय्या न वयम् राज्ये भृतका निवसेमहि
जीवन्त्या जातु जीवन्त्यः पुत्रैः अपि शपामहे
transliteration: kaikeyyā na vayam rājye bhṛtakā nivasemahi
jīvantyā jātu jīvantyaḥ putraiḥ api śapāmahe
english: We swear by our sons that so long as Kaikeyi is alive, we living will never stay in her kingdom, although we may be maintained by her.

sanskrit: या पुत्रम् पार्थिव इन्द्रस्य प्रवासयति निर्घृणा
कः ताम् प्राप्य सुखम् जीवेद् अधर्म्याम् दुष्ट चारिणीम्
transliteration: yā putram pārthiva indrasya pravāsayati nirghṛṇā
kaḥ tām prāpya sukham jīved adharmyām duṣṭa cāriṇīm
english: What happiness can be ours by living with that wicked and unrighteous one who lost to every sense of shame is bent upon exiling the son of the foremost of kings?
Troubled by disturbances, with all its sacrifices stopped, and having no master over it, the entire (kingdom) will meet with destruction because of Kaikeyi.

sanskrit: न हि प्रव्रजिते रामे जीविष्यति मही पतिः
मृते दशरथे व्यक्तम् विलोपः तत् अनन्तरम्
transliteration: na hi pravrajite rāme jīviṣyati mahī patiḥ
mṛte daśarathe vyaktam vilopaḥ tat anantaram
english: On Rāma retiring to the forest, the lord of earth will surely not live; and Dasaratha dying, it is evident everything will come to naught.

sanskrit: ते विषम् पिबत आलोड्य क्षीण पुण्याः सुदुर्गताः
राघवम् वा अनुगच्चध्वम् अश्रुतिम् वा अपि गच्चत
transliteration: te viṣam pibata āloḍya kṣīṇa puṇyāḥ sudurgatāḥ
rāghavam vā anugaccadhvam aśrutim vā api gaccata
english: Do you, your virtue exhausted, and oppressed with grief, pounding poison, take it, or follow Rāghava, or remove to such a place that the very name of Kaikeyī may not reach your ears.

sanskrit: मिथ्या प्रव्राजितः रामः सभार्यः सह लक्ष्मणः
भरते सम्निषृष्टाः स्मः सौनिके पशवो यथा
transliteration: mithyā pravrājitaḥ rāmaḥ sabhāryaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
bharate samniṣṛṣṭāḥ smaḥ saunike paśavo yathā
english: Rāma has been deceitfully exiled along with his wife and Lakşmaņa; and we are bound to Bharata like to a (sacrificial) beast before one that is to slaughter it.

Surely that mighty car warrior, with deepest collar-bones having a countenance resembling the full-moon, sable-hued, repressing his foes, with this arms reaching to his knees and lotuslike eyes, Rāma the elder brother of Laksmana, always speaking first (to a visitor,) suave, truthtelling, endowed with prowess, amiable to all men, and lovely like the moon himself, surely that foremost of men gifted with the strength of a mad elephant, will grace the forests, ranging it around.

Surely that mighty car warrior, with deepest collar-bones having a countenance resembling the full-moon, sable-hued, repressing his foes, with this arms reaching to his knees and lotuslike eyes, Rāma the elder brother of Laksmana, always speaking first (to a visitor,) suave, truthtelling, endowed with prowess, amiable to all men, and lovely like the moon himself, surely that foremost of men gifted with the strength of a mad elephant, will grace the forests, ranging it around.
Thus lamenting in the city, the females thereof burning in grief became distressed like people stricken with panic on the occasion of a plague.
Thus lamenting in the city, the females thereof burning in grief became distressed like people stricken with panic on the occasion of a plague.
As the women were thus bewailing Rāghava in their homes, the Sun set and night came on.
The city became enveloped in darkness, and the light of the sacrificial fires) extinguished, and the sounds of study and edifying discourse ceased.
The shops of the tradesmen being closed, and festive mirth having disappeared, and people becoming defenceless, the city of Ayodhyā resembled the firmament deprived of the stars.

sanskrit: सुतैः हि तासाम् अधिको हि सो अभवत्
transliteration: sutaiḥ hi tāsām adhiko hi so abhavat
english: Distressed for the sake of Rāma as if it was a was son or a brother of theirs that was banished, the women weeping forlorn, lamented with senses lost; and Rāma was to them more than a son.

And the voice of song and festal glee and dance and sounds of instruments having died away, and mirth having disappeared, and the shops not displaying their wares, Ayodhyā then resembled the mighty ocean emptied of its waters.

sanskrit: रामः अपि रात्रि शेषेण तेन एव महद् अन्तरम्
जगाम पुरुष व्याघ्रः पितुर् आज्ञाम् अनुस्मरन्
transliteration: rāmaḥ api rātri śeṣeṇa tena eva mahad antaram
jagāma puruṣa vyāghraḥ pitur ājñām anusmaran
english: That best of men, Rāma, remembering his father's commanded cleared a large tract of country before the night terminated.

sanskrit: तथैव गच्चतः तस्य व्यपायात् रजनी शिवा
उपास्य स शिवाम् सम्ध्याम् विषय अन्तम् व्यगाहत
transliteration: tathaiva gaccataḥ tasya vyapāyāt rajanī śivā
upāsya sa śivām samdhyām viṣaya antam vyagāhata
english: And as he went on, the auspicious night was spent. And then having offered up his devotions to the beneficent Sandhyā, Rāma entered into another country.

sanskrit: ग्रामान् विकृष्ट सीमान् तान् पुष्पितानि वनानि च
पश्यन्न् अतिययौ शीघ्रम् शरैः इव हय उत्तमैः
transliteration: grāmān vikṛṣṭa sīmān tān puṣpitāni vanāni ca
paśyann atiyayau śīghram śaraiḥ iva haya uttamaiḥ
english: And seeing villages having ploughed fields on their skirts, and powering woods, he by means of those excellent horses, proceeded very fast although seeming to go slowly.

sanskrit: शृण्वन् वाचो मनुष्याणाम् ग्राम सम्वास वासिनाम्
राजानम् धिग् दशरथम् कामस्य वशम् आगतम्
transliteration: śṛṇvan vāco manuṣyāṇām grāma samvāsa vāsinām
rājānam dhig daśaratham kāmasya vaśam āgatam
english: And as Rāma proceeded,* he heard the villagers speaking to each other, saying, Fie on king Dasaratha, who has yielded himself up to lust! *The N.W.P. text has an additional couplet:, How will that exalted lady, Janaka's daughter, ever engaged in enjoyment, bear misery?

sanskrit: हा नृशम्स अद्य कैकेयी पापा पाप अनुबन्धिनी
तीक्ष्णा सम्भिन्न मर्यादा तीक्ष्णे कर्मणि वर्तते
transliteration: hā nṛśamsa adya kaikeyī pāpā pāpa anubandhinī
tīkṣṇā sambhinna maryādā tīkṣṇe karmaṇi vartate
english: Ah! the rebutless, fell and sinful Kaikeyi intent upon impiety, having put by her honour, has resolved upon an exceedingly atrocious deed, she that exiles into the woods such a virtuous son of the monarch, endowed with high wisdom, kind, and having his senses under control.* *The N.W.P. text has an additional line: And of the reprehensible Kaikeyi intent upon cruel deeds.

sanskrit: या पुत्रम् ईदृशम् राज्ञः प्रवासयति धार्मिकम्
वन वासे महा प्राज्ञम् सानुक्रोशम् अतन्द्रितम्
transliteration: yā putram īdṛśam rājñaḥ pravāsayati dhārmikam
vana vāse mahā prājñam sānukrośam atandritam
english: Ah! the rebutless, fell and sinful Kaikeyi intent upon impiety, having put by her honour, has resolved upon an exceedingly atrocious deed, she that exiles into the woods such a virtuous son of the monarch, endowed with high wisdom, kind, and having his senses under control.* *The N.W.P. text has an additional line: And of the reprehensible Kaikeyi intent upon cruel deeds.
Alas! king Daſaratha has no affection for his own son, since wishes to dismiss from hence Rāma sinless and dear to the subjects.

sanskrit: अहो दशरथो राजा निस्नेहः स्वसुत प्रियम्
transliteration: aho daśaratho rājā nisnehaḥ svasuta priyam
english: Alas! king Daſaratha has no affection for his own son, since wishes to dismiss from hence Rāma sinless and dear to the subjects.

sanskrit: एता वाचो मनुष्याणाम् ग्राम सम्वास वासिनाम्
शृण्वन्न् अति ययौ वीरः कोसलान् कोसल ईश्वरः
transliteration: etā vāco manuṣyāṇām grāma samvāsa vāsinām
śṛṇvann ati yayau vīraḥ kosalān kosala īśvaraḥ
english: Hearing these words of the villagers, that hero, the lord of Kosala, left Kosala behind him. Then crossing the river Vedaśruti of sacred waters, Rāma went in the direction of the quarter in which Agastya resided. (South)

sanskrit: ततः वेद श्रुतिम् नाम शिव वारि वहाम् नदीम्
उत्तीर्य अभिमुखः प्रायात् अगस्त्य अध्युषिताम् दिशम्
transliteration: tataḥ veda śrutim nāma śiva vāri vahām nadīm
uttīrya abhimukhaḥ prāyāt agastya adhyuṣitām diśam
english: Hearing these words of the villagers, that hero, the lord of Kosala, left Kosala behind him. Then crossing the river Vedaśruti of sacred waters, Rāma went in the direction of the quarter in which Agastya resided. (South)

sanskrit: गत्वा तु सुचिरम् कालम् ततः शीत जलाम् नदीम्
गोमतीम् गोयुत अनूपाम् अतरत् सागरम् गमाम्
transliteration: gatvā tu suciram kālam tataḥ śīta jalām nadīm
gomatīm goyuta anūpām atarat sāgaram gamām
english: Then proceeding for a good while, he crossed the cool flowing stream Gomati running in the direction of the ocean, with its banks filled with kine and inundating its edge.

sanskrit: गोमतीम् च अपि अतिक्रम्य राघवः शीघ्रगैः हयैः
मयूर हम्स अभिरुताम् ततार स्यन्दिकाम् नदीम्
transliteration: gomatīm ca api atikramya rāghavaḥ śīghragaiḥ hayaiḥ
mayūra hamsa abhirutām tatāra syandikām nadīm
english: Having passed the Gomatī, Rāghava by means of fleet-coursing horses next crossed over the river Sandika resounding with the cries of cranes and peacocks.

sanskrit: स महीम् मनुना राज्ञा दत्ताम् इक्ष्वाकवे पुरा
स्फीताम् राष्ट्र आवृताम् रामः वैदेहीम् अन्वदर्शयत्
transliteration: sa mahīm manunā rājñā dattām ikṣvākave purā
sphītām rāṣṭra āvṛtām rāmaḥ vaidehīm anvadarśayat
english: Here Rāma showed to Vaidehi those flourishing regions that had formerly been conferred by king Manu on Ikşvāku, and which teemed with populous tracts.

sanskrit: सूतैति एव च आभाष्य सारथिम् तम् अभीक्ष्णशः
हम्स मत्त स्वरः श्रीमान् उवाच पुरुष ऋषभः
transliteration: sūtaiti eva ca ābhāṣya sārathim tam abhīkṣṇaśaḥ
hamsa matta svaraḥ śrīmān uvāca puruṣa ṛṣabhaḥ
english: Then frequently addressing the charioteer, saying, "O Suta", that best of men furnished with grace and endowed with a voice like that of a mad swan, spoke.

sanskrit: कदा अहम् पुनर् आगम्य सरय्वाः पुष्पिते वने
मृगयाम् पर्याटष्यामि मात्रा पित्रा च सम्गतः
transliteration: kadā aham punar āgamya sarayvāḥ puṣpite vane
mṛgayām paryāṭaṣyāmi mātrā pitrā ca samgataḥ
english: When shall I coming back, range a hunting the blossoming groves of the Sarayū, along with my father and mother?

sanskrit: न अत्यर्थम् अभिकान्क्षामि मृगयाम् सरयू वने
रतिर् हि एषा अतुला लोके राज ऋषि गण सम्मता
transliteration: na atyartham abhikānkṣāmi mṛgayām sarayū vane
ratir hi eṣā atulā loke rāja ṛṣi gaṇa sammatā
english: I do not so much long for hunting in the woods of the Sarayū; but a relish (for the pastime) is considered as beyond compare being held in esteem by the Rājarşis.

sanskrit: राजर्षीणाम् हि लोकेऽस्मिन् रत्यर्थम् मृगया वने
transliteration: rājarṣīṇām hi loke'smin ratyartham mṛgayā vane
english: Hunting in the forest was introduced for the recreation of Rāghavas. Yet do I not take beyond measure to the chase which has been followed in season by the descendants of Manu and which is ever coveted by bowmen.

sanskrit: स तम् अध्वानम् ऐक्ष्वाकः सूतम् मधुरया गिरातम् तम् अर्थम् अभिप्रेत्य ययौवाक्यम् उदीरयन्
transliteration: sa tam adhvānam aikṣvākaḥ sūtam madhurayā girātam tam artham abhipretya yayauvākyam udīrayan
english: Taking this subject, the descendant of Ikşvāku passed the way, addressing sweet words to the charioteer.

sanskrit: विशालान् कोसलान् रम्यान् यात्वा लक्ष्मण पूर्वजः
transliteration: viśālān kosalān ramyān yātvā lakṣmaṇa pūrvajaḥ
english: Having passed the extensive and romantic Kosala, the intelligent elder brother of Lakşmaņa facing Ayodhyā said with joined hands.

sanskrit: दैवतानि च यानि त्वाम् पालयन्त्यावसन्ति च
transliteration: daivatāni ca yāni tvām pālayantyāvasanti ca
english: O best of cities, governed by Kākutstha, I address you as well as the deities that inhabit and guard you.

sanskrit: पुनर्ध्रक्ष्यामि मात्रा च पित्रा च सह सम्गतः
transliteration: punardhrakṣyāmi mātrā ca pitrā ca saha samgataḥ
english: Returning from my abode in the woods, I will, freed from my debt to the lord of earth, behold you again along with my father and mother.
Then he furnished with graceful coppery eyes raising his right hand, with tears in his eyes and in forlorn guise addressed the people of the provinces, saying.

sanskrit: अनुक्रोशो दया चैव यथार्हम् मयि वह् कृतः
transliteration: anukrośo dayā caiva yathārham mayi vah kṛtaḥ
english: You have shown due compassion and regret for me. To grieve long is not fit. do you therefore repair to look after your interests.

sanskrit: विलपन्तो नरा घोरम् व्यतिष्ठन्त क्वचित् क्वचित्
transliteration: vilapanto narā ghoram vyatiṣṭhanta kvacit kvacit
english: Thereupon saluting that high-souled one and going round him, bewailing all the while in heaviness of heart, they at times stopped on their way.
And as they kept lamenting, unsatiated in beholding him, Rāghava went beyond the range of their sight, like the Sun disappearing at nightfall.

sanskrit: राज्यम् भोग्यम् नरेन्द्राणाम् ययौ धृतिमताम् वरः
transliteration: rājyam bhogyam narendrāṇām yayau dhṛtimatām varaḥ
english: Proceeding at a middling pace, that best of those endowed with fortitude, passed through lands smiling cheerfully, prosperous, and crowded with elegant villas, realms worthy of being covered by the foremost of kings.

sanskrit: तत्र त्रिपथगाम् दिव्याम् शिव तोयाम् अशैवलाम्
ददर्श राघवो गन्गाम् पुण्याम् ऋषि निसेविताम्
transliteration: tatra tripathagām divyām śiva toyām aśaivalām
dadarśa rāghavo gangām puṇyām ṛṣi nisevitām

sanskrit: हम्स सरस सम्घुष्टाम् चक्र वाक उपकूजिताम्
transliteration: hamsa sarasa samghuṣṭām cakra vāka upakūjitām

sanskrit: शिम्शुमरैः च नक्रैः च भुजम्गैः च निषेविताम्
transliteration: śimśumaraiḥ ca nakraiḥ ca bhujamgaiḥ ca niṣevitām

sanskrit: ताम् ऊर्मि कलिल आवर्ताम् अन्ववेक्ष्य महा रथः
सुमन्त्रम् अब्रवीत् सूतम् इह एव अद्य वसामहे
transliteration: tām ūrmi kalila āvartām anvavekṣya mahā rathaḥ
sumantram abravīt sūtam iha eva adya vasāmahe
english: And beholding (the river) with her surging eddies, that mighty car-warrior said to the charioteer, Sumantra, We will rest here to day.

sanskrit: अविदूरात् अयम् नद्या बहु पुष्प प्रवालवान्
सुमहान् इन्गुदी वृक्षो वसामः अत्र एव सारथे
transliteration: avidūrāt ayam nadyā bahu puṣpa pravālavān
sumahān ingudī vṛkṣo vasāmaḥ atra eva sārathe
english: There is hard by the river a gigantic Ingudī tree, bearing a profusion of flowers and fresh leaves. Here, O charioteer, will we stay to-day.
I see (before me) the foremost of streams, whose waters are honoured (by all) and which is sacred to celestials and men and Gandharvas and beasts and serpents and fowls.

sanskrit: लक्षणः च सुमन्त्रः च बाढम् इति एव राघवम्
उक्त्वा तम् इन्गुदी वृक्षम् तदा उपययतुर् हयैः
transliteration: lakṣaṇaḥ ca sumantraḥ ca bāḍham iti eva rāghavam
uktvā tam ingudī vṛkṣam tadā upayayatur hayaiḥ
english: Thereupon saying to Rāghava, “Very well,” Lakşinana and Sumantra with the horses went to the Ingudi tree.

sanskrit: रामः अभियाय तम् रम्यम् वृक्षम् इक्ष्वाकु नन्दनः
रथात् अवातरत् तस्मात् सभार्यः सह लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: rāmaḥ abhiyāya tam ramyam vṛkṣam ikṣvāku nandanaḥ
rathāt avātarat tasmāt sabhāryaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: And reaching the tree, that descendant of Ikşvāku alighted from the car along with his wife and Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: सुमन्त्रः अपि अवतीर्य एव मोचयित्वा हय उत्तमान्
वृक्ष मूल गतम् रामम् उपतस्थे कृत अन्जलिः
transliteration: sumantraḥ api avatīrya eva mocayitvā haya uttamān
vṛkṣa mūla gatam rāmam upatasthe kṛta anjaliḥ
english: Then descending, Sumantra relieved those excellent horses, and with joined hands stood before Rāma seated at the foot of the tree.

sanskrit: तत्र राजा गुहो नाम रामस्य आत्म समः सखा
निषाद जात्यो बलवान् स्थपतिः च इति विश्रुतः
transliteration: tatra rājā guho nāma rāmasya ātma samaḥ sakhā
niṣāda jātyo balavān sthapatiḥ ca iti viśrutaḥ
english: There lived at the place a king named Guha, a friend to Răma, dear as his own self, a Nişāda by birth, powerful and famed as the lord of the Nişādas.

sanskrit: स श्रुत्वा पुरुष व्याघ्रम् रामम् विषयम् आगतम्
वृद्धैः परिवृतः अमात्यैः ज्ञातिभिः च अपि उपागतः
transliteration: sa śrutvā puruṣa vyāghram rāmam viṣayam āgatam
vṛddhaiḥ parivṛtaḥ amātyaiḥ jñātibhiḥ ca api upāgataḥ
english: Hearing that thai foremost of men, Răma, had arrived at the place, he (Guha) surrounded by his aged counsellors and kindred came to him.

sanskrit: ततः निषाद अधिपतिम् दृष्ट्वा दूरात् अवस्थितम्
सह सौमित्रिणा रामः समागच्चद् गुहेन सः
transliteration: tataḥ niṣāda adhipatim dṛṣṭvā dūrāt avasthitam
saha saumitriṇā rāmaḥ samāgaccad guhena saḥ
english: Seeing the lord of the Nişādhas at a distance, Rāma came up to him in company with Sumitra's son.

sanskrit: तम् आर्तः सम्परिष्वज्य गुहो राघवम् अब्रवीत्
यथा अयोध्या तथा इदम् ते राम किम् करवाणि ते
transliteration: tam ārtaḥ sampariṣvajya guho rāghavam abravīt
yathā ayodhyā tathā idam te rāma kim karavāṇi te
english: Thereat touched, Guha embracing Rāghava said to him, "O Rāma, as Ayodhyā this kingdom is to you. What shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: ईदृशम् हि महाबाहो कः प्रप्स्यत्यतिथिम् प्रियम्
ततः गुणवद् अन्न अद्यम् उपादाय पृथग् विधम्
अर्घ्यम् च उपानयत् क्षिप्रम् वाक्यम् च इदम् उवाच ह
transliteration: īdṛśam hi mahābāho kaḥ prapsyatyatithim priyam
tataḥ guṇavad anna adyam upādāya pṛthag vidham
arghyam ca upānayat kṣipram vākyam ca idam uvāca ha

sanskrit: स्वागतम् ते महा बाहो तव इयम् अखिला मही
वयम् प्रेष्या भवान् भर्ता साधु राज्यम् प्रशाधि नः
transliteration: svāgatam te mahā bāho tava iyam akhilā mahī
vayam preṣyā bhavān bhartā sādhu rājyam praśādhi naḥ

sanskrit: भक्ष्यम् भोज्यम् च पेयम् च लेह्यम् च इदम् उपस्थितम्
शयनानि च मुख्यानि वाजिनाम् खादनम् च ते
transliteration: bhakṣyam bhojyam ca peyam ca lehyam ca idam upasthitam
śayanāni ca mukhyāni vājinām khādanam ca te

sanskrit: गुहम् एव ब्रुवाणम् तम् राघवः प्रत्युवाच ह
transliteration: guham eva bruvāṇam tam rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha

sanskrit: अर्चिताः चैव हृष्टाः च भवता सर्वथा वयम्
पद्भ्याम् अभिगमाच् चैव स्नेह सम्दर्शनेन च
transliteration: arcitāḥ caiva hṛṣṭāḥ ca bhavatā sarvathā vayam
padbhyām abhigamāc caiva sneha samdarśanena ca
english: When Guha had said this, Rāghava answered him, saying, “We have been well received by you and are well pleased with you, since coming here on foot you have shown us affection."

sanskrit: भुजाभ्याम् साधु वृत्ताभ्याम् पीडयन् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
दिष्ट्या त्वाम् गुह पश्यामिअरोगम् सह बान्धवैः
transliteration: bhujābhyām sādhu vṛttābhyām pīḍayan vākyam abravīt
diṣṭyā tvām guha paśyāmiarogam saha bāndhavaiḥ
english: Then pressing Guha hard with his arms, Rāma said, O Guha, it is by good luck that I see you whole along with your friends. Is your kingdom in peace both as regards your friends and the forest?

sanskrit: अपि ते कूशलम् राष्ट्रे मित्रेषु च धनेषु च
यत् तु इदम् भवता किम्चित् प्रीत्या समुपकल्पितम्
सर्वम् तत् अनुजानामि न हि वर्ते प्रतिग्रहे
transliteration: api te kūśalam rāṣṭre mitreṣu ca dhaneṣu ca
yat tu idam bhavatā kimcit prītyā samupakalpitam
sarvam tat anujānāmi na hi varte pratigrahe
english: The things that you have presented me with out of love I accept but can not enjoy.

sanskrit: कुश चीर अजिन धरम् फल मूल अशनम् च माम्
विद्धि प्रणिहितम् धर्मे तापसम् वन गोचरम्
transliteration: kuśa cīra ajina dharam phala mūla aśanam ca mām
viddhi praṇihitam dharme tāpasam vana gocaram
english: Do you know me as assuming an ascetic mode of life in the woods, in which I am to wear Kusa and bark and live upon fruits and roots.

sanskrit: अश्वानाम् खादनेन अहम् अर्थी न अन्येन केनचित्
transliteration: aśvānām khādanena aham arthī na anyena kenacit
english: So, with the single exception of the food for the horses, things require I none; and these horses being well kept, I shall consider myself as entertained by you.

sanskrit: एते हि दयिता राज्ञः पितुर् दशरथस्य मे
एतैः सुविहितैः अश्वैः भविष्याम्य् अहम् अर्चितः
transliteration: ete hi dayitā rājñaḥ pitur daśarathasya me
etaiḥ suvihitaiḥ aśvaiḥ bhaviṣyāmy aham arcitaḥ
english: These are the favourites of my father, Dasaratha, and on these horses being well provided for, I shall be well received.

sanskrit: अश्वानाम् प्रतिपानम् च खादनम् चैव सो अन्वशात्
गुहः तत्र एव पुरुषाम्स् त्वरितम् दीयताम् इति
transliteration: aśvānām pratipānam ca khādanam caiva so anvaśāt
guhaḥ tatra eva puruṣāms tvaritam dīyatām iti
english: Thereupon Guha on the spot commanded the men, saying, Let the horses have without delay meats and drinks.

sanskrit: ततः चीर उत्तर आसन्गः सम्ध्याम् अन्वास्य पश्चिमाम्
जलम् एव आददे भोज्यम् लक्ष्मणेन आहृतम् स्वयम्
transliteration: tataḥ cīra uttara āsangaḥ samdhyām anvāsya paścimām
jalam eva ādade bhojyam lakṣmaṇena āhṛtam svayam
english: Then putting his sheet over his person, he (Rāma) performed his evening devotions. Having done this, he took as his sustenance the water that had been procured by Lakşmaņa himself.

sanskrit: तस्य भूमौ शयानस्य पादौ प्रक्षाल्य लक्ष्मणः
सभार्यस्य ततः अभ्येत्य तस्थौ वृष्कम् उपाश्रितः
transliteration: tasya bhūmau śayānasya pādau prakṣālya lakṣmaṇaḥ
sabhāryasya tataḥ abhyetya tasthau vṛṣkam upāśritaḥ
english: On Rāma having lain down on the ground along with his wife, Lakşmaņa washed their feet, and then remained stationed under the tree.

sanskrit: गुहो अपि सह सूतेन सौमित्रिम् अनुभाषयन्
अन्वजाग्रत् ततः रामम् अप्रमत्तः धनुर् धरः
transliteration: guho api saha sūtena saumitrim anubhāṣayan
anvajāgrat tataḥ rāmam apramattaḥ dhanur dharaḥ
english: Then bow in hand and with his wits about him, conversing with Sumitra's son along with the charioteer, Guha remained awake, watching Rama.
Thus the livelong night passed away with that illustrious, intelligent and high-souled son of Daśaratha, unacquainted with troubles and worthy of happiness.

sanskrit: तम् जाग्रतम् अदम्भेन भ्रातुर् अर्थाय लक्ष्मणम्
गुहः सम्ताप सम्तप्तः राघवम् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tam jāgratam adambhena bhrātur arthāya lakṣmaṇam
guhaḥ samtāpa samtaptaḥ rāghavam vākyam abravīt
english: As for the purpose of protecting his brother, Lakṣmaṇa was watching him out of sincere affection, Guha burning in grief addressed that descendant of Raghu, saying.

sanskrit: इयम् तात सुखा शय्या त्वद् अर्थम् उपकल्पिता
प्रत्याश्वसिहि साध्व् अस्याम् राज पुत्र यथा सुखम्
transliteration: iyam tāta sukhā śayyā tvad artham upakalpitā
pratyāśvasihi sādhv asyām rāja putra yathā sukham
english: This O child, is the easeful bed that has been prepared for you. O prince, do you as you listen, lie down upon it.

sanskrit: उचितः अयम् जनः सर्वः क्लेशानाम् त्वम् सुख उचितः
गुप्ति अर्थम् जागरिष्यामः काकुत्स्थस्य वयम् निशाम्
transliteration: ucitaḥ ayam janaḥ sarvaḥ kleśānām tvam sukha ucitaḥ
gupti artham jāgariṣyāmaḥ kākutsthasya vayam niśām
english: These (foresters) are inured to this hardship; but you are worthy of ease. We will wake up during the night for guarding Kākutstha.

sanskrit: न हि रामात् प्रियतरः मम अस्ति भुवि कश्चन
ब्रवीम्य् एतत् अहम् सत्यम् सत्येन एव च ते शपे
transliteration: na hi rāmāt priyataraḥ mama asti bhuvi kaścana
bravīmy etat aham satyam satyena eva ca te śape
english: There is none on earth dearer to me than Răma. This I tell you truly and I swear by truth itself.

sanskrit: अस्य प्रसादात् आशम्से लोके अस्मिन् सुमहद् यशः
धर्म अवाप्तिम् च विपुलाम् अर्थ अवाप्तिम् च केवलाम्
transliteration: asya prasādāt āśamse loke asmin sumahad yaśaḥ
dharma avāptim ca vipulām artha avāptim ca kevalām
english: Through his grace I hope in this world to attain high fame, and great religious merit as well as completely secure profit and pleasure.

sanskrit: सो अहम् प्रिय सखम् रामम् शयानम् सह सीतया
रक्षिष्यामि धनुष् पाणिः सर्वतः ज्ञातिभिः सह
transliteration: so aham priya sakham rāmam śayānam saha sītayā
rakṣiṣyāmi dhanuṣ pāṇiḥ sarvataḥ jñātibhiḥ saha
english: I will bow in hand in company with my kindred adequately guard my dear friend reposing with Sītā.

sanskrit: न हि मे अविदितम् किम्चित् वने अस्मिमः चरतः सदा
चतुर् अन्गम् हि अपि बलम् सुमहत् प्रसहेमहि
transliteration: na hi me aviditam kimcit vane asmimaḥ carataḥ sadā
catur angam hi api balam sumahat prasahemahi
english: Always ranging in this forest, nothing herein is unknown to me. I shall vanquish even any mighty body of fourfold forces (that may come up against us.)

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणः तम् तदा उवाच रक्ष्यमाणाः त्वया अनघ
न अत्र भीता वयम् सर्वे धर्मम् एव अनुपश्यता
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaḥ tam tadā uvāca rakṣyamāṇāḥ tvayā anagha
na atra bhītā vayam sarve dharmam eva anupaśyatā
english: Thereupon Laksmana said, O sinless one, protected by you ever having your sight fixed on virtue, we do not fear to live in this place. But how with Dasaratha's son lying down on the ground along with Sītă can I indulge in sleep or what is the use of my living and enjoying happiness?

sanskrit: कथम् दाशरथौ भूमौ शयाने सह सीतया
शक्या निद्रा मया लब्धुम् जीवितम् वा सुखानि वा
transliteration: katham dāśarathau bhūmau śayāne saha sītayā
śakyā nidrā mayā labdhum jīvitam vā sukhāni vā
english: Thereupon Laksmana said, O sinless one, protected by you ever having your sight fixed on virtue, we do not fear to live in this place. But how with Dasaratha's son lying down on the ground along with Sītă can I indulge in sleep or what is the use of my living and enjoying happiness?

sanskrit: यो न देव असुरैः सर्वैः शक्यः प्रसहितुम् युधि
तम् पश्य सुख सम्विष्टम् तृणेषु सह सीतया
transliteration: yo na deva asuraiḥ sarvaiḥ śakyaḥ prasahitum yudhi
tam paśya sukha samviṣṭam tṛṇeṣu saha sītayā

sanskrit: यो मन्त्र तपसा लब्धो विविधैः च परिश्रमैः
एको दशरथस्य एष पुत्रः सदृश लक्षणः
transliteration: yo mantra tapasā labdho vividhaiḥ ca pariśramaiḥ
eko daśarathasya eṣa putraḥ sadṛśa lakṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: अस्मिन् प्रव्रजितः राजा न चिरम् वर्तयिष्यति
विधवा मेदिनी नूनम् क्षिप्रम् एव भविष्यति
transliteration: asmin pravrajitaḥ rājā na ciram vartayiṣyati
vidhavā medinī nūnam kṣipram eva bhaviṣyati

sanskrit: विनद्य सुमहा नादम् श्रमेण उपरताः स्त्रियः
निर्घोष उपरतम् तात मन्ये राज निवेशनम्
transliteration: vinadya sumahā nādam śrameṇa uparatāḥ striyaḥ
nirghoṣa uparatam tāta manye rāja niveśanam
english: Having bewailed aloud, the women have, methinks, (by this time) ceased through fatigue, and the king's residence is still.

sanskrit: कौसल्या चैव राजा च तथैव जननी मम
न आशम्से यदि जीवन्ति सर्वे ते शर्वरीम् इमाम्
transliteration: kausalyā caiva rājā ca tathaiva jananī mama
na āśamse yadi jīvanti sarve te śarvarīm imām
english: I can not hope that Kausalyā, the king, and my mother (Sumitrā) all those are yet alive.

sanskrit: जीवेद् अपि हि मे माता शत्रुघ्नस्य अन्ववेक्षया
तत् दुह्खम् यत् तु कौसल्या वीरसूर् विनशिष्यति
transliteration: jīved api hi me mātā śatrughnasya anvavekṣayā
tat duhkham yat tu kausalyā vīrasūr vinaśiṣyati
english: If they are, it is for this night only. Even if my mother live looking up to Satrughna, yet this is my grief that that mother of a hero, Kausalyā will breathe her last.

sanskrit: अनुरक्त जन आकीर्णा सुख आलोक प्रिय आवहा
राज व्यसन सम्सृष्टा सा पुरी विनशिष्यति
transliteration: anurakta jana ākīrṇā sukha āloka priya āvahā
rāja vyasana samsṛṣṭā sā purī vinaśiṣyati
english: And that palace filled with people attached to Rāma and flooded with the light of delight, will, visited with the calamity that will befall the king meet with destruction.
How will the life of that high-souled king not seeing his magnanimous son, his eldest son, remain in this body?
When the king is dead, Kausalyā will die after him and then my mother will depart this life.

sanskrit: राज्ये रामम् अनिक्षिप्य पिता मे विनशिष्यति
transliteration: rājye rāmam anikṣipya pitā me vinaśiṣyati
english: Frustrated in his desire, my father, foiled in his endeavours to confer the kingdom on Rāma, will, exclaiming 'All is lost,' 'All is lost,' give up the ghost.

sanskrit: सिद्ध अर्थाः पितरम् वृत्तम् तस्मिन् काले हि उपस्थिते
transliteration: siddha arthāḥ pitaram vṛttam tasmin kāle hi upasthite
english: Surely they are blessed that when the time shall come when the king will die, will perform the funeral rites of that descendant of Raghu.

sanskrit: रम्य चत्वर सम्स्थानाम् सुविभक्त महा पथाम्
हर्म्य प्रसाद सम्पन्नाम् गणिका वर शोभिताम्
transliteration: ramya catvara samsthānām suvibhakta mahā pathām
harmya prasāda sampannām gaṇikā vara śobhitām

sanskrit: रथ अश्व गज सम्बाधाम् तूर्य नाद विनादिताम्
सर्व कल्याण सम्पूर्णाम् हृष्ट पुष्ट जन आकुलाम्
transliteration: ratha aśva gaja sambādhām tūrya nāda vināditām
sarva kalyāṇa sampūrṇām hṛṣṭa puṣṭa jana ākulām

sanskrit: आराम उद्यान सम्पन्नाम् समाज उत्सव शालिनीम्
सुखिता विचरिष्यन्ति राज धानीम् पितुर् मम
transliteration: ārāma udyāna sampannām samāja utsava śālinīm
sukhitā vicariṣyanti rāja dhānīm pitur mama

english: If Dasaratha live we shall returning from the forest, behold that high-souled one observing noble vows.

sanskrit: अपि सत्य प्रतिज्ञेन सार्धम् कुशलिना वयम्
निवृत्ते वन वासे अस्मिन्न् अयोध्याम् प्रविशेमहि
transliteration: api satya pratijñena sārdham kuśalinā vayam
nivṛtte vana vāse asminn ayodhyām praviśemahi
english: If we remain in peace, we shall returning from the forest with that one firm in promise, enter Ayodhyā?

sanskrit: तिष्ठतः राज पुत्रस्य शर्वरी सा अत्यवर्तत
transliteration: tiṣṭhataḥ rāja putrasya śarvarī sā atyavartata
english: As the high-souled son of the king oppressed with grief was thus lamenting sitting up, the day broke.

sanskrit: तथा हि सत्यम् ब्रुवति प्रजा हिते
नर इन्द्र पुत्रे गुरु सौहृदात् गुहः
transliteration: tathā hi satyam bruvati prajā hite
nara indra putre guru sauhṛdāt guhaḥ
english: When that son of the foremost of men, intent on the welfare of the subjects had spoken thus truly, Guha, out of extreme affection for (Rāma), shed tears afflicted with grief and hurt like an elephant suffering from fever.

sanskrit: प्रभातायाम् तु शर्वर्याम् पृथु वृक्षा महा यशाः
उवाच रामः सौमित्रिम् लक्ष्मणम् शुभ लक्षणम्
transliteration: prabhātāyām tu śarvaryām pṛthu vṛkṣā mahā yaśāḥ
uvāca rāmaḥ saumitrim lakṣmaṇam śubha lakṣaṇam
english: When the morning broke, that illustrious one having a spacious chest, Rāma, addressed Sumitrā's son, Laksmana, graced with auspicious marks.

sanskrit: भास्कर उदय कालो अयम् गता भगवती निशा
असौ सुकृष्णो विहगः कोकिलः तात कूजति
transliteration: bhāskara udaya kālo ayam gatā bhagavatī niśā
asau sukṛṣṇo vihagaḥ kokilaḥ tāta kūjati
english: This is the time of sunrise: the reverend Night has departed. O child, this gracefully sable-hued bird, the Coel, has began to warble, and I hear the cries of peacocks uttering notes in the woods. O amiable one, we will cross the Jāhnavī, fast rushing to the ocean.

sanskrit: बर्हिणानाम् च निर्घोषः श्रूयते नदताम् वने
तराम जाह्नवीम् सौम्य शीघ्रगाम् सागरम् गमाम्
transliteration: barhiṇānām ca nirghoṣaḥ śrūyate nadatām vane
tarāma jāhnavīm saumya śīghragām sāgaram gamām
english: This is the time of sunrise: the reverend Night has departed. O child, this gracefully sable-hued bird, the Coel, has began to warble, and I hear the cries of peacocks uttering notes in the woods. O amiable one, we will cross the Jāhnavī, fast rushing to the ocean.

sanskrit: विज्ञाय रामस्य वचः सौमित्रिर् मित्र नन्दनः
गुहम् आमन्त्र्य सूतम् च सो अतिष्ठद् भ्रातुर् अग्रतः
transliteration: vijñāya rāmasya vacaḥ saumitrir mitra nandanaḥ
guham āmantrya sūtam ca so atiṣṭhad bhrātur agrataḥ
english: Hearing Rāma's words, that enhancer of the delight of friends, Sumitra's son, conveyed them to Guha and the charioteer; and then stood before his brother.

sanskrit: स तु रामस्य वचनम् निशम्य प्रतिगृह्य च
transliteration: sa tu rāmasya vacanam niśamya pratigṛhya ca
english: Hearing of Rāma's speech and accepting it, that lord of the Nişādas speedily summoning his counsellors spoke to them saying.
Do you without delay bring to this bathingplace a strong and elegant boat furnished with a rudder and steered by a helmsman, such as is capable of ferrying (people) comfortably.

Hearing this mandate of Guha, his potent counsellors procuring goodly boat, informed him of it. Then with joined hands, Guha spoke to Rāghava, saying, The boat is ready, worshipful one. What more shall I do in your behalf?

sanskrit: उपस्थितेयम् नौर्देव भूयः किम् करवाणि ते
transliteration: upasthiteyam naurdeva bhūyaḥ kim karavāṇi te
english: Hearing this mandate of Guha, his potent counsellors procuring goodly boat, informed him of it. Then with joined hands, Guha spoke to Rāghava, saying, The boat is ready, worshipful one. What more shall I do in your behalf?
O you that resembles the son of a celestial, here is the boat for you, O foremost of men, to cross over the river that goes after the ocean. O you of excellent vows, do you ascend it.
Thereupon the highly energetic Rāma said to Guha the following words, “I have attained my end through you. Do you at once get on board the baggage." son

sanskrit: ततः कलापान् सम्नह्य खड्गौ बद्ध्वा च धन्विनौ
जग्मतुर् येन तौ गन्गाम् सीतया सह राघवौ
transliteration: tataḥ kalāpān samnahya khaḍgau baddhvā ca dhanvinau
jagmatur yena tau gangām sītayā saha rāghavau
english: Then donning on their mail and equipped with their bows, quivers and swords, the Rāghavas along with Sītā descended to the Gangā.

sanskrit: रामम् एव तु धर्मज्ञम् उपगम्य विनीतवत्
किम् अहम् करवाणि इति सूतः प्रान्जलिर् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: rāmam eva tu dharmajñam upagamya vinītavat
kim aham karavāṇi iti sūtaḥ prānjalir abravīt
english: Then coming forward in humble guise before Rāma cognizant of virtue, the charioteer said with joined hands, "What shall I do (now)?"
Thereupon Dasaratha's touching Sumantra by his goodly right hand, said, “O Sumantra, do you again repair to the monarch, but let your senses be unclouded.”

sanskrit: निवर्तस्व इति उवाच एनम् एतावद्द् हि कृतम् मम
रथम् विहाय पद्भ्याम् तु गमिष्यामि महावनम्
transliteration: nivartasva iti uvāca enam etāvadd hi kṛtam mama
ratham vihāya padbhyām tu gamiṣyāmi mahāvanam
english: “Do you” said he to the charioteer, "turn back, So far I have come (in obedience to the order of the monarch.) Now, renouncing the car, will I repair to the mighty forest on foot."

sanskrit: आत्मानम् तु अभ्यनुज्ञातम् अवेक्ष्य आर्तः स सारथिः
सुमन्त्रः पुरुष व्याघ्रम् ऐक्ष्वाकम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: ātmānam tu abhyanujñātam avekṣya ārtaḥ sa sārathiḥ
sumantraḥ puruṣa vyāghram aikṣvākam idam abravīt
english: Finding himself thus commanded, the charioteer, Sumantra grieved at heart spoke to that best of men, the descendant of Ikşvāku.

sanskrit: न अतिक्रान्तम् इदम् लोके पुरुषेण इह केनचित्
तव सभ्रातृ भार्यस्य वासः प्राकृतवद् वने
transliteration: na atikrāntam idam loke puruṣeṇa iha kenacit
tava sabhrātṛ bhāryasya vāsaḥ prākṛtavad vane
english: That Destiny owing to which you will have to pass your days in the forest like a low person, along with your brother and wife, has in this world been withstood by none.

sanskrit: न मन्ये ब्रह्म चर्ये अस्ति स्वधीते वा फल उदयः
मार्दव आर्जवयोः वा अपि त्वाम् चेद् व्यसनम् आगतम्
transliteration: na manye brahma carye asti svadhīte vā phala udayaḥ
mārdava ārjavayoḥ vā api tvām ced vyasanam āgatam
english: I deem the Brahmacarya mode of life, or study, or meekness or sincerity as attended with no fruit, since you have come by calamity.

sanskrit: सह राघव वैदेह्या भ्रात्रा चैव वने वसन्
त्वम् गतिम् प्राप्स्यसे वीर त्रीम्ल् लोकाम्स् तु जयन्न् इव
transliteration: saha rāghava vaidehyā bhrātrā caiva vane vasan
tvam gatim prāpsyase vīra trīml lokāms tu jayann iva
english: O Rāghava, living in the forest with Vaidehi and your brother, you, O Lord, attain a state (of supreme excellence), having, as it were, conquered the three worlds.

sanskrit: वयम् खलु हता राम ये तया अपि उपवन्चिताः
कैकेय्या वशम् एष्यामः पापाया दुह्ख भागिनः
transliteration: vayam khalu hatā rāma ye tayā api upavancitāḥ
kaikeyyā vaśam eṣyāmaḥ pāpāyā duhkha bhāginaḥ
english: O Rāma, it is we, wretched that we are, that are undone, as we, deprived of your company, shall come under the sinful Kaikeyi expressing great misery.

sanskrit: इति ब्रुवन्न् आत्म समम् सुमन्त्रः सारथिस् तदा
दृष्ट्वा दुर गतम् रामम् दुह्ख आर्तः रुरुदे चिरम्
transliteration: iti bruvann ātma samam sumantraḥ sārathis tadā
dṛṣṭvā dura gatam rāmam duhkha ārtaḥ rurude ciram
english: Having said this, the charioteer, Sumantra, seeing Rāma intent upon going to a distant land, wept for a long while in heaviness of heart.

sanskrit: ततः तु विगते बाष्पे सूतम् स्पृष्ट उदकम् शुचिम्
रामः तु मधुरम् वाक्यम् पुनः पुनर् उवाच तम्
transliteration: tataḥ tu vigate bāṣpe sūtam spṛṣṭa udakam śucim
rāmaḥ tu madhuram vākyam punaḥ punar uvāca tam
english: Then when he had dried up his tears, and sanctified himself by touching the water of the Gangā, Rāma again addressed the charioteer in sweet words, saying.

sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकूणाम् त्वया तुल्यम् सुहृदम् न उपलक्षये
यथा दशरथो राजा माम् न शोचेत् तथा कुरु
transliteration: ikṣvākūṇām tvayā tulyam suhṛdam na upalakṣaye
yathā daśaratho rājā mām na śocet tathā kuru
english: I do not find any one that is a friend of the sons of Ikşvāku like to you. Do you so act that king Dasaratha may not grieve (for me.)

sanskrit: शोक उपहत चेताः च वृद्धः च जगती पतिः
काम भार अवसन्नः च तस्मात् एतत् ब्रवीमि ते
transliteration: śoka upahata cetāḥ ca vṛddhaḥ ca jagatī patiḥ
kāma bhāra avasannaḥ ca tasmāt etat bravīmi te
english: The lord of earth has been deprived of his senses by grief, has grown old, and is oppressed by the weight of desires (thwarted.) Therefore it is that I tell you this.

sanskrit: यद् यद् आज्ञापयेत् किम्चित् स महात्मा मही पतिः
कैकेय्याः प्रिय काम अर्थम् कार्यम् तत् अविकान्क्षया
transliteration: yad yad ājñāpayet kimcit sa mahātmā mahī patiḥ
kaikeyyāḥ priya kāma artham kāryam tat avikānkṣayā
english: Whatever that noble-minded lord of earth commands for the pleasure of Kaikeyi, should by us be done with alacrity.

sanskrit: एतत् अर्थम् हि राज्यानि प्रशासति नर ईश्वराः
यद् एषाम् सर्व कृत्येषु मनो न प्रतिहन्यते
transliteration: etat artham hi rājyāni praśāsati nara īśvarāḥ
yad eṣām sarva kṛtyeṣu mano na pratihanyate
english: It is for this that those lords of men, kings, govern, viz., that others may not thwart their purposes.)

sanskrit: यद्यथा स महा राजो न अलीकम् अधिगच्चति
न च ताम्यति दुह्खेन सुमन्त्र कुरु तत् तथा
transliteration: yadyathā sa mahā rājo na alīkam adhigaccati
na ca tāmyati duhkhena sumantra kuru tat tathā
english: O Sumantra, do you act so, that the mighty monarch may not come across anything unpleasant, or be attacked with chagrin through grief.

sanskrit: अदृष्ट दुह्खम् राजानम् वृद्धम् आर्यम् जित इन्द्रियम्
ब्रूयाः त्वम् अभिवाद्य एव मम हेतोर् इदम् वचः
transliteration: adṛṣṭa duhkham rājānam vṛddham āryam jita indriyam
brūyāḥ tvam abhivādya eva mama hetor idam vacaḥ
english: Do you saluting him for me say these words to the aged monarch who has his senses under complete control, and who has never seen misfortune before.

sanskrit: न एव अहम् अनुशोचामि लक्ष्मणो न च मैथिली
अयोध्यायाः च्युताः च इति वने वत्स्यामह इति वा (महेति!)
transliteration: na eva aham anuśocāmi lakṣmaṇo na ca maithilī
ayodhyāyāḥ cyutāḥ ca iti vane vatsyāmaha iti vā (maheti!)
english: Neither I nor Lakşmaņa grieve for being ejected out of Ayodhyā, or that we shall have to abide in the forest.

sanskrit: चतुर् दशसु वर्षेषु निवृत्तेषु पुनः पुनः
लक्ष्मणम् माम् च सीताम् च द्रक्ष्यसि क्षिप्रम् आगतान्
transliteration: catur daśasu varṣeṣu nivṛtteṣu punaḥ punaḥ
lakṣmaṇam mām ca sītām ca drakṣyasi kṣipram āgatān
english: After these fourteen years have gone by, you will see Lakşmaņa, Sītā and myself come to you speedily.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा तु राजानम् मातरम् च सुमन्त्र मे
अन्याः च देवीः सहिताः कैकेयीम् च पुनः पुनः
transliteration: evam uktvā tu rājānam mātaram ca sumantra me
anyāḥ ca devīḥ sahitāḥ kaikeyīm ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Having thus, O Sumantra, in my name again and again spoken to the king, to iny mother and to Kaikeyi along with the other revered ladies, do you communicate to Kausalyā our welfare conveying to her at the same time Şītā's and Lakşmana's salutations to her feet as well those of myself who am her eldest son.

sanskrit: आरोग्यम् ब्रूहि कौसल्याम् अथ पाद अभिवन्दनम्
सीताया मम च आर्यस्य वचनाल् लक्ष्मणस्य च
transliteration: ārogyam brūhi kausalyām atha pāda abhivandanam
sītāyā mama ca āryasya vacanāl lakṣmaṇasya ca
english: Having thus, O Sumantra, in my name again and again spoken to the king, to iny mother and to Kaikeyi along with the other revered ladies, do you communicate to Kausalyā our welfare conveying to her at the same time Şītā's and Lakşmana's salutations to her feet as well those of myself who am her eldest son.

sanskrit: ब्रूयाः च हि महा राजम् भरतम् क्षिप्रम् आनय
आगतः च अपि भरतः स्थाप्यो नृप मते पदे
transliteration: brūyāḥ ca hi mahā rājam bharatam kṣipram ānaya
āgataḥ ca api bharataḥ sthāpyo nṛpa mate pade
english: Do you also tell the king, 'Do you speedily bring Bharata; and when Bharata has come, let him be the invested with royalty.

sanskrit: भरतम् च परिष्वज्य यौवराज्ये अभिषिच्य च
अस्मत् सम्तापजम् दुह्खम् न त्वाम् अभिभविष्यति
transliteration: bharatam ca pariṣvajya yauvarājye abhiṣicya ca
asmat samtāpajam duhkham na tvām abhibhaviṣyati
english: When you have embraced Bharata and installed him in the kingdom, you no longer be overpowered with grief on our account.'

sanskrit: भरतः च अपि वक्तव्यो यथा राजनि वर्तसे
तथा मातृषु वर्तेथाः सर्वास्व् एव अविशेषतः
transliteration: bharataḥ ca api vaktavyo yathā rājani vartase
tathā mātṛṣu vartethāḥ sarvāsv eva aviśeṣataḥ
english: And tell Bharata, “As you bear yourself to the king so it behoves you to bear yourself to all your mothers, without making any distinction at hall. As Kaikeyi is unto you, so without distinction is Sumitrā.'

sanskrit: यथा च तव कैकेयी सुमित्रा च अविशेषतः
तथैव देवी कौसल्या मम माता विशेषतः
transliteration: yathā ca tava kaikeyī sumitrā ca aviśeṣataḥ
tathaiva devī kausalyā mama mātā viśeṣataḥ
english: And tell Bharata, “As you bear yourself to the king so it behoves you to bear yourself to all your mothers, without making any distinction at hall. As Kaikeyi is unto you, so without distinction is Sumitrā.'
Governing the kingdom as the heir-apparent with the view of compassing the pleasure of our father, he will be able to secure happiness both in this world and the next.

sanskrit: तत् सर्वम् वचनम् श्रुत्वा स्नेहात् काकुत्स्थम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tat sarvam vacanam śrutvā snehāt kākutstham abravīt
english: Told by Rāma to go back and instructed in this wise, Sumantra having heard everything, addressed Kākutstha from affection, saying.

sanskrit: यद् अहम् न उपचारेण ब्रूयाम् स्नेहात् अविक्लवः
भक्तिमान् इति तत् तावद् वाक्यम् त्वम् क्षन्तुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: yad aham na upacāreṇa brūyām snehāt aviklavaḥ
bhaktimān iti tat tāvad vākyam tvam kṣantum arhasi
english: It behoves you to forgive what I say plainly from affection, without letting myself by overwhelmed with emotion, and with due reverence for you. How can I, O child, without you return to that city, which seems as it afflicted with the grief incident to the loss of a son?

sanskrit: कथम् हि त्वद् विहीनो अहम् प्रतियास्यामि ताम् पुरीम्
तव तात वियोगेन पुत्र शोक आकुलाम् इव
transliteration: katham hi tvad vihīno aham pratiyāsyāmi tām purīm
tava tāta viyogena putra śoka ākulām iva

sanskrit: सरामम् अपि तावन् मे रथम् दृष्ट्वा तदा जनः
विना रामम् रथम् दृष्ट्वा विदीर्येत अपि सा पुरी
transliteration: sarāmam api tāvan me ratham dṛṣṭvā tadā janaḥ
vinā rāmam ratham dṛṣṭvā vidīryeta api sā purī
english: Having then seen my car with Rāma on it, the hearts of the people and the palace will in all likelihood burst when they shall see it without Rāma. Surely the city will be distressed on beholding this empty car, like a host seeing car with its ro slain and the charioteer alone left in the field.

sanskrit: दैन्यम् हि नगरी गच्चेद् दृष्ट्वा शून्यम् इमम् रथम्
सूत अवशेषम् स्वम् सैन्यम् हत वीरम् इव आहवे
transliteration: dainyam hi nagarī gacced dṛṣṭvā śūnyam imam ratham
sūta avaśeṣam svam sainyam hata vīram iva āhave
english: Having then seen my car with Rāma on it, the hearts of the people and the palace will in all likelihood burst when they shall see it without Rāma. Surely the city will be distressed on beholding this empty car, like a host seeing car with its ro slain and the charioteer alone left in the field.

sanskrit: दूरे अपि निवसन्तम् त्वाम् मानसेन अग्रतः स्थितम्
चिन्तयन्त्यो अद्य नूनम् त्वाम् निराहाराः कृताः प्रजाः
transliteration: dūre api nivasantam tvām mānasena agrataḥ sthitam
cintayantyo adya nūnam tvām nirāhārāḥ kṛtāḥ prajāḥ
english: Thinking in their minds that you although actually at a great distance from them, are before them, the subjects (not finding you) will renounce food (and thus destroy themselves.)

sanskrit: दृष्टं तद्धि त्वया राम! यादृशम् त्वत्प्रवासने
transliteration: dṛṣṭaṃ taddhi tvayā rāma! yādṛśam tvatpravāsane
english: You yourself witnessed how the subjects overwhelmed with grief on your account, conducted themselves when you were being banished to the woods.

sanskrit: आर्त नादो हि यः पौरैः मुक्तः तत् विप्रवासने
रथस्थम् माम् निशाम्य एव कुर्युः शत गुणम् ततः
transliteration: ārta nādo hi yaḥ pauraiḥ muktaḥ tat vipravāsane
rathastham mām niśāmya eva kuryuḥ śata guṇam tataḥ
english: They will on seeing me with the car, burst out into lamentations exceeding a hundred times in bitterness those in which they indulged when you set out for the forest.

sanskrit: अहम् किम् च अपि वक्ष्यामि देवीम् तव सुतः मया
नीतः असौ मातुल कुलम् सम्तापम् मा कृथाइति
transliteration: aham kim ca api vakṣyāmi devīm tava sutaḥ mayā
nītaḥ asau mātula kulam samtāpam mā kṛthāiti

sanskrit: असत्यम् अपि न एव अहम् ब्रूयाम् वचनम् ईदृशम्
कथम् अप्रियम् एव अहम् ब्रूयाम् सत्यम् इदम् वचः
transliteration: asatyam api na eva aham brūyām vacanam īdṛśam
katham apriyam eva aham brūyām satyam idam vacaḥ

sanskrit: मम तावन् नियोगस्थाः त्वद् बन्धु जन वाहिनः
कथम् रथम् त्वया हीनम् प्रवक्ष्यन्ति हय उत्तमाः
transliteration: mama tāvan niyogasthāḥ tvad bandhu jana vāhinaḥ
katham ratham tvayā hīnam pravakṣyanti haya uttamāḥ
english: And ever abiding by my command and used to carry your friends, how can these excellent horses bear this car without you?
Therefore, O şinless one, I shall not be able to go to Ayodhyā without you; and it behoves you to permit me to follow you to the forest.

sanskrit: यदि मे याचमानस्य त्यागम् एव करिष्यसि
सरथो अग्निम् प्रवेक्ष्यामि त्यक्त मात्रैह त्वया
transliteration: yadi me yācamānasya tyāgam eva kariṣyasi
saratho agnim pravekṣyāmi tyakta mātraiha tvayā
english: But if you forsake me who beseech you, I will as soon as left by you, enter into fire along with the car.

sanskrit: भविष्यन्ति वने यानि तपो विघ्न कराणि ते
transliteration: bhaviṣyanti vane yāni tapo vighna karāṇi te
english: I shall, O Rāghava, by means of this car, withstand all those impediments that shall present themselves against your ascetic austerities in the forest.

sanskrit: तत् कृतेन मया प्राप्तम् रथ चर्या कृतम् सुखम्
आशम्से त्वत् कृतेन अहम् वन वास कृतम् सुखम्
transliteration: tat kṛtena mayā prāptam ratha caryā kṛtam sukham
āśamse tvat kṛtena aham vana vāsa kṛtam sukham
english: I have through your favour experienced the pleasure of driving the car. I expect at your hands the pleasure of living in the woods.

sanskrit: प्रसीद इच्चामि ते अरण्ये भवितुम् प्रत्यनन्तरः
प्रीत्या अभिहितम् इच्चामि भव मे पत्यनन्तरः
transliteration: prasīda iccāmi te araṇye bhavitum pratyanantaraḥ
prītyā abhihitam iccāmi bhava me patyanantaraḥ
english: Be you propitious. It is my wish to remain in the forest with you, and do you say, affectionately, 'Do you remain by my side.'

sanskrit: इमे चापि हया वीर यदि ते वनवासिनः
transliteration: ime cāpi hayā vīra yadi te vanavāsinaḥ
english: And these horses, O hero, will attain to a supreme state if your serve you during your abode in the forest.

sanskrit: तव शुश्रूषणम् मूर्ध्ना करिष्यामि वने वसन्
अयोध्याम् देव लोकम् वा सर्वथा प्रजहाम्य् अहम्
transliteration: tava śuśrūṣaṇam mūrdhnā kariṣyāmi vane vasan
ayodhyām deva lokam vā sarvathā prajahāmy aham
english: Living in the forest, I will serve you with the crown of my head; and I will entirely renounce Ayodhyā or the celestial regions themselves.

sanskrit: न हि शक्या प्रवेष्टुम् सा मया अयोध्या त्वया विना
राज धानी महा इन्द्रस्य यथा दुष्कृत कर्मणा
transliteration: na hi śakyā praveṣṭum sā mayā ayodhyā tvayā vinā
rāja dhānī mahā indrasya yathā duṣkṛta karmaṇā
english: Even as a doer of evil deeds cannot enter the metropolis of the mighty Indra, I am incapable of entering Ayodhyā without you.

sanskrit: वन वासे क्षयम् प्राप्ते मम एष हि मनो रथः
यद् अनेन रथेन एव त्वाम् वहेयम् पुरीम् पुनः
transliteration: vana vāse kṣayam prāpte mama eṣa hi mano rathaḥ
yad anena rathena eva tvām vaheyam purīm punaḥ
english: This is my desire that the term of exile over, I may carry you back to the palace on this very car.

sanskrit: चतुर् दश हि वर्षाणि सहितस्य त्वया वने
क्षण भूतानि यास्यन्ति शतशः तु ततः अन्यथा
transliteration: catur daśa hi varṣāṇi sahitasya tvayā vane
kṣaṇa bhūtāni yāsyanti śataśaḥ tu tataḥ anyathā
english: Remaining with you in the forest the fourteen years will pass away dwindled into a moment, but without you, they shall the proportions of an hundred years. assume

sanskrit: भृत्य वत्सल तिष्ठन्तम् भर्तृ पुत्र गते पथि
भक्तम् भृत्यम् स्थितम् स्थित्याम् त्वम् न माम् हातुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: bhṛtya vatsala tiṣṭhantam bhartṛ putra gate pathi
bhaktam bhṛtyam sthitam sthityām tvam na mām hātum arhasi
english: O you bearing affection towards your servants, it does not behove you to forsake your servant having regard for you, ever abiding by the way that is wended by the son of his master, and observing the duties of his position.

sanskrit: एवम् बहु विधम् दीनम् याचमानम् पुनः पुनः
रामः भृत्य अनुकम्पी तु सुमन्त्रम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: evam bahu vidham dīnam yācamānam punaḥ punaḥ
rāmaḥ bhṛtya anukampī tu sumantram idam abravīt
english: Thereupon Rāma kind towards servants, said these words to Sumantra as he besought him thus humbly in various ways, O you that bear attachment to your master, I know that you regard me highly. But do you listen as to why I send you to the city from hence.

sanskrit: जानामि परमाम् भक्तिम् मयि ते भर्तृ वत्सल
शृणु च अपि यद् अर्थम् त्वाम् प्रेषयामि पुरीम् इतः
transliteration: jānāmi paramām bhaktim mayi te bhartṛ vatsala
śṛṇu ca api yad artham tvām preṣayāmi purīm itaḥ
english: Thereupon Rāma kind towards servants, said these words to Sumantra as he besought him thus humbly in various ways, O you that bear attachment to your master, I know that you regard me highly. But do you listen as to why I send you to the city from hence.

sanskrit: नगरीम् त्वाम् गतम् दृष्ट्वा जननी मे यवीयसी
कैकेयी प्रत्ययम् गच्चेद् इति रामः वनम् गतः
transliteration: nagarīm tvām gatam dṛṣṭvā jananī me yavīyasī
kaikeyī pratyayam gacced iti rāmaḥ vanam gataḥ
english: Seeing you returned to the city, my youngest mother Kaikeyi will believe that Rāma has gone to the woods.

sanskrit: परितुष्टा हि सा देवि वन वासम् गते मयि
राजानम् न अतिशन्केत मिथ्या वादी इति धार्मिकम्
transliteration: parituṣṭā hi sā devi vana vāsam gate mayi
rājānam na atiśanketa mithyā vādī iti dhārmikam
english: Then well pleased on my having repaired to the woods, she will not entertain any apprehension anent the righteous monarch, thinking that he is intruthful.

sanskrit: एष मे प्रथमः कल्पो यद् अम्बा मे यवीयसी
भरत आरक्षितम् स्फीतम् पुत्र राज्यम् अवाप्नुयात्
transliteration: eṣa me prathamaḥ kalpo yad ambā me yavīyasī
bharata ārakṣitam sphītam putra rājyam avāpnuyāt
english: This is my first wish that my youngest mother may obtain her son's kingdom, prosperous and well protected by Bharata.

sanskrit: मम प्रिय अर्थम् राज्ञः च सरथः त्वम् पुरीम् व्रज
सम्दिष्टः च असि या अनर्थाम्स् ताम्स् तान् ब्रूयाः तथा तथा
transliteration: mama priya artham rājñaḥ ca sarathaḥ tvam purīm vraja
samdiṣṭaḥ ca asi yā anarthāms tāms tān brūyāḥ tathā tathā
english: Do you, O Sumantra, bear yourself to the palace to compass the end of both the king and myself, and do you communicate in the desired way what I have said to the respective parties.

sanskrit: इति उक्त्वा वचनम् सूतम् सान्त्वयित्वा पुनः पुनः
गुहम् वचनम् अक्लीबम् रामः हेतुमद् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: iti uktvā vacanam sūtam sāntvayitvā punaḥ punaḥ
guham vacanam aklībam rāmaḥ hetumad abravīt
english: Having said this to the charioteer and consoled him again and again, the energetic Rāma spoke to Guha the following words fraught with reason.

sanskrit: नेदानीम् गुह योग्योऽयम् वसो मे सजने वने
transliteration: nedānīm guha yogyo'yam vaso me sajane vane
english: O Guha, I should not now reside in a forest inhabited by men. I should certainly now abide in an asylum in proper guise.

In harmony with the wishes of Sītā and Laks maņa, I, imposing on myself in the interests of my father self-denial and wearing that ornament of ascetics, a head of matted hair, will go (to the forest). Do you therefore bring me starch from the banian.” Thereupon Guha speedily brought the starch for the prince. And prepared matted locks for himself, Rāma and Laksmana.

sanskrit: जटाः कृत्वा गमिष्यामि न्यग्रोध क्षीरम् आनय
तत् क्षीरम् राज पुत्राय गुहः क्षिप्रम् उपाहरत्
transliteration: jaṭāḥ kṛtvā gamiṣyāmi nyagrodha kṣīram ānaya
tat kṣīram rāja putrāya guhaḥ kṣipram upāharat
english: In harmony with the wishes of Sītā and Laks maņa, I, imposing on myself in the interests of my father self-denial and wearing that ornament of ascetics, a head of matted hair, will go (to the forest). Do you therefore bring me starch from the banian.” Thereupon Guha speedily brought the starch for the prince. And prepared matted locks for himself, Rāma and Laksmana.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणस्य आत्मनः चैव रामः तेन अकरोज् जटाः
transliteration: lakṣmaṇasya ātmanaḥ caiva rāmaḥ tena akaroj jaṭāḥ
english: And that mighty-armed chief of men wore matted locks. And those brothers Rāma and Lakş maņa dressed as mendicants, and wearing heads of matted hair, appeared like saints.

sanskrit: तौ तदा चीर वसनौ जटा मण्डल धारिणौ
अशोभेताम् ऋषि समौ भ्रातरौ राम रक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: tau tadā cīra vasanau jaṭā maṇḍala dhāriṇau
aśobhetām ṛṣi samau bhrātarau rāma rakṣmaṇau
english: And that mighty-armed chief of men wore matted locks. And those brothers Rāma and Lakş maņa dressed as mendicants, and wearing heads of matted hair, appeared like saints.

sanskrit: ततः वैखानसम् मार्गम् आस्थितः सह लक्ष्मणः
व्रतम् आदिष्टवान् रामः सहायम् गुहम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tataḥ vaikhānasam mārgam āsthitaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
vratam ādiṣṭavān rāmaḥ sahāyam guham abravīt
english: Then entering upon the Vānaprastha mode of life, Rāma along with Lakşmaņa assuming the vow of that life, observed to that adherent of his, Guha.

sanskrit: अप्रमत्तः बले कोशे दुर्गे जन पदे तथा
भवेथा गुह राज्यम् हि दुरारक्षतमम् मतम्
transliteration: apramattaḥ bale kośe durge jana pade tathā
bhavethā guha rājyam hi durārakṣatamam matam
english: Do you, my friend, vigilantly protect the army, the exchequer, the fort and the provinces; for a kingdom demands all the exertions (of the king thereof).

sanskrit: ततः तम् समनुज्ञाय गुहम् इक्ष्वाकु नन्दनः
जगाम तूर्णम् अव्यग्रः सभार्यः सह लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: tataḥ tam samanujñāya guham ikṣvāku nandanaḥ
jagāma tūrṇam avyagraḥ sabhāryaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Then taking the permission of Guha, the descendant of Ikşvāku, holding his soul in calmness, set out with his wife and Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: स तु दृष्ट्वा नदी तीरे नावम् इक्ष्वाकु नन्दनः
तितीर्षुः शीघ्रगाम् गन्गाम् इदम् लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sa tu dṛṣṭvā nadī tīre nāvam ikṣvāku nandanaḥ
titīrṣuḥ śīghragām gangām idam lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: Seeing a boat at the river-side, that son of Ikşvāku desirous of crossing the swift-coursing Garigā, spoke these words.

sanskrit: आरोह त्वम् नर व्याघ्र स्थिताम् नावम् इमाम् शनैः
सीताम् च आरोपय अन्वक्षम् परिगृह्य मनस्विनीम्
transliteration: āroha tvam nara vyāghra sthitām nāvam imām śanaiḥ
sītām ca āropaya anvakṣam parigṛhya manasvinīm
english: Do you ascend, gently, O foremost of men, the boat that stay here, after the making the virtuous Sītā ascend by taking her by the hand.

sanskrit: स भ्रातुः शासनम् श्रुत्वा सर्वम् अप्रतिकूलयन्
आरोप्य मैथिलीम् पूर्वम् आरुरोह आत्मवाम्स् ततः
transliteration: sa bhrātuḥ śāsanam śrutvā sarvam apratikūlayan
āropya maithilīm pūrvam āruroha ātmavāms tataḥ
english: Hearing his brother's command, that strongwilled one, furthering everything, having made Mithila's daughter ascend, ascended himself.

sanskrit: अथ आरुरोह तेजस्वी स्वयम् लक्ष्मण पूर्वजः
ततः निषाद अधिपतिर् गुहो ज्ञातीन् अचोदयत्
transliteration: atha āruroha tejasvī svayam lakṣmaṇa pūrvajaḥ
tataḥ niṣāda adhipatir guho jñātīn acodayat
english: That energetic elder brother of Lakşmaņa next ascended himself. Then the lord of the Nişadas, Guha, incited his kinsfolk.
Having got on board the boat, the exceedingly puissant Rāghava for securing his welfare, recited mantras fit to be recited by Kștriyas and Brahmanas.

sanskrit: आचम्य च यथाशास्त्रम् नदीम् ताम् सह सीतया
transliteration: ācamya ca yathāśāstram nadīm tām saha sītayā
english: Then that mighty car-warrior, Laksmana, sipping water from the river as laid down in the scriptures, bowed down to it along with Sītā in gladness of heart.

sanskrit: अनुज्ञाय सुमन्त्रम् च सबलम् चैव तम् गुहम्
आस्थाय नावम् रामः तु चोदयाम् आस नाविकान्
transliteration: anujñāya sumantram ca sabalam caiva tam guham
āsthāya nāvam rāmaḥ tu codayām āsa nāvikān
english: Then telling Sumantra, Guha, and the forces, Rāma ascending the boat, ordered the boatmen (to proceed).

sanskrit: ततः तैः चोदिता सा नौः कर्ण धार समाहिता
शुभ स्फ्य वेग अभिहता शीघ्रम् सलिलम् अत्यगात्
transliteration: tataḥ taiḥ coditā sā nauḥ karṇa dhāra samāhitā
śubha sphya vega abhihatā śīghram salilam atyagāt
english: Then the boat decked out by the heimsman, moved by them, and urged on by the pulls of the goodly roars, proceeded apace in the water.

sanskrit: मध्यम् तु समनुप्राप्य भागीरथ्याः तु अनिन्दिता
वैदेही प्रान्जलिर् भूत्वा ताम् नदीम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: madhyam tu samanuprāpya bhāgīrathyāḥ tu aninditā
vaidehī prānjalir bhūtvā tām nadīm idam abravīt
english: Having arrived at the middle of the Bhagirathi, that blameless one, Vaidehi, with joined hands, addressed the river, saying.

sanskrit: पुत्रः दशरथस्य अयम् महा राजस्य धीमतः
निदेशम् पालयतु एनम् गन्गे त्वद् अभिरक्षितः
transliteration: putraḥ daśarathasya ayam mahā rājasya dhīmataḥ
nideśam pālayatu enam gange tvad abhirakṣitaḥ
english: O Ganga, protected by you, may the son of the intelligent and mighty monarch, Dasaratha, execute the mandate (of the latter.)

sanskrit: चतुर् दश हि वर्षाणि समग्राणि उष्य कानने
भ्रात्रा सह मया चैव पुनः प्रत्यागमिष्यति
transliteration: catur daśa hi varṣāṇi samagrāṇi uṣya kānane
bhrātrā saha mayā caiva punaḥ pratyāgamiṣyati
english: Having spent complete fourteen years in the forest, he will return in company with his brother and myself.

sanskrit: ततः त्वाम् देवि सुभगे क्षेमेण पुनर् आगता
यक्ष्ये प्रमुदिता गन्गे सर्व काम समृद्धये
transliteration: tataḥ tvām devi subhage kṣemeṇa punar āgatā
yakṣye pramuditā gange sarva kāma samṛddhaye
english: Then, O worshipful one, O you of auspicious fortune, having returned safely, I will, O Gangā, worship you, you that crown every desire.

sanskrit: त्वम् हि त्रिपथगा देवि ब्रह्म लोकम् समीक्षसे
भार्या च उदधि राजस्य लोके अस्मिन् सम्प्रदृश्यसे
transliteration: tvam hi tripathagā devi brahma lokam samīkṣase
bhāryā ca udadhi rājasya loke asmin sampradṛśyase
english: O you that wend in three ways, O revered one, you envelope the regions of Brahma. You appear in this world as the spouse of the Ocean-king.

sanskrit: सा त्वाम् देवि नमस्यामि प्रशम्सामि च शोभने
प्राप्त राज्ये नर व्याघ्र शिवेन पुनर् आगते
transliteration: sā tvām devi namasyāmi praśamsāmi ca śobhane
prāpta rājye nara vyāghra śivena punar āgate
english: I will, O respected one, bow down to you, O beauteous one, I will hymn you, when, with good fortune returned, the foremost of men has obtained the kingdom, I will to please you give away to Brāhmaṇas hundreds and thousands of kine, cloths, sapid rice, and vessels of wine by thousands, and pillaos.

sanskrit: गवाम् शत सहस्राणि वस्त्राणि अन्नम् च पेशलम्
transliteration: gavām śata sahasrāṇi vastrāṇi annam ca peśalam
english: I will, O respected one, bow down to you, O beauteous one, I will hymn you, when, with good fortune returned, the foremost of men has obtained the kingdom, I will to please you give away to Brāhmaṇas hundreds and thousands of kine, cloths, sapid rice, and vessels of wine by thousands, and pillaos.

sanskrit: यक्ष्ये त्वाम् प्रयता देवि पुरीम् पुनरुपागता
transliteration: yakṣye tvām prayatā devi purīm punarupāgatā

sanskrit: यानि त्वत्तीरवासीनि दैवतानि च सन्ति हि
transliteration: yāni tvattīravāsīni daivatāni ca santi hi
english: O worshipful one, I will worship you on Rāma having returned to the city. And I will worship all the gods that dwell on your banks, as well as the holy spots and fanes, as soon as, O sinless one, that mighty-armed one without sin will, coming back from his abode in the forest, enter Ayodhyā in company with his brother and myself.

sanskrit: तथा सम्भाषमाणा सा सीता गन्गाम् अनिन्दिता
दक्षिणा दक्षिणम् तीरम् क्षिप्रम् एव अभ्युपागमत्
transliteration: tathā sambhāṣamāṇā sā sītā gangām aninditā
dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇam tīram kṣipram eva abhyupāgamat
english: Having thus addressed the Gangā, that blameless one ever obedient to her husband, swiftly went to the south bank (of the river).

sanskrit: तीरम् तु समनुप्राप्य नावम् हित्वा नर ऋषभः
प्रातिष्ठत सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या च परम् तपः
transliteration: tīram tu samanuprāpya nāvam hitvā nara ṛṣabhaḥ
prātiṣṭhata saha bhrātrā vaidehyā ca param tapaḥ
english: Going to the (other) bank of the stream, that best of men, and subduer of foes stood along with his brother and Vaidehī.

sanskrit: अथ अब्रवीन् महा बाहुः सुमित्र आनन्द वर्धनम्
transliteration: atha abravīn mahā bāhuḥ sumitra ānanda vardhanam

sanskrit: अग्रतः गच्च सौमित्रे सीता त्वाम् अनुगच्चतु
transliteration: agrataḥ gacca saumitre sītā tvām anugaccatu

sanskrit: पृष्ठतः अहम् गमिष्यामि त्वाम् च सीताम् च पालयन्
अद्य दुह्खम् तु वैदेही वन वासस्य वेत्स्यति
transliteration: pṛṣṭhataḥ aham gamiṣyāmi tvām ca sītām ca pālayan
adya duhkham tu vaidehī vana vāsasya vetsyati

sanskrit: न हि तावदतिक्रान्ता सुकरा काचन क्रिया
अद्य दुःखम् तु वैदेही वनवासस्य वेत्स्यति
transliteration: na hi tāvadatikrāntā sukarā kācana kriyā
adya duḥkham tu vaidehī vanavāsasya vetsyati
english: We have not yet performed any of the arduous tasks. To day Vaidehi will know the grief of a life in the woods.

sanskrit: विषमम् च प्रपातम् च वनमद्य प्रवेक्ष्यति
transliteration: viṣamam ca prapātam ca vanamadya pravekṣyati
english: And to day she will enter the forest destitute of the concourse of men, devoid of fields and gardens, uneven, and containing pits, etc.
Hearing Rama's words, Laksmana went ahead; that descendant of Raghu, Rāma, followed Sita.

sanskrit: गतम् तु गन्गा पर पारम् आशु
transliteration: gatam tu gangā para pāram āśu
english: On Rāma having speedily crossed the Gangā, the distressed Sumantra who had been gazing at him steadfastly, being no longer able to discern him, turned away his eyes and, overcome with grief, shed tears.

And having crossed that mighty river, that high-souled one, that bestower of boons, resembling in prowess a Lokapăla, without delay entered the flourishing and smiling Vatsas crowned with goodly crops.

sanskrit: तौ तत्र हत्वा चतुरः महा मृगान्
transliteration: tau tatra hatvā caturaḥ mahā mṛgān
english: And then the two (brothers) having slain the four kinds of beasts, viz., boars, rsyas, prsatas and maharurus,* and taking their flesh, in the evening took refuge under a mighty tree, feeling the demands of appetite. *Varieties of deer.

sanskrit: स तम् वृक्षम् समासाद्य सम्ध्याम् अन्वास्य पश्चिमाम्
रामः रमयताम् श्रेष्ठैति ह उवाच लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: sa tam vṛkṣam samāsādya samdhyām anvāsya paścimām
rāmaḥ ramayatām śreṣṭhaiti ha uvāca lakṣmaṇam
english: Having taken refuge under the tree and performed his evening devotions, that foremost of those capable of charming others. Rāma, addressed Laksmana, saying.

sanskrit: अद्य इयम् प्रथमा रात्रिर् याता जन पदात् बहिः
या सुमन्त्रेण रहिता ताम् न उत्कण्ठितुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: adya iyam prathamā rātrir yātā jana padāt bahiḥ
yā sumantreṇa rahitā tām na utkaṇṭhitum arhasi
english: To day is the first night (which we must spend) outside the inhabited tracts without the company of Sumantra.. You ought not to suffer your mind to be uneasy on that score.

sanskrit: योग क्षेमः हि सीताया वर्तते लक्ष्मण आवयोह्
transliteration: yoga kṣemaḥ hi sītāyā vartate lakṣmaṇa āvayoh
english: From to night forth, we shall have to guard her vigilantly, for, O Laksmana, the preservation of what she has as well as the securing to her of what she has not, rests with us.

sanskrit: रात्रिम् कथम्चित् एव इमाम् सौमित्रे वर्तयामहे
transliteration: rātrim kathamcit eva imām saumitre vartayāmahe
english: We will, O son of Sumitrā, anyhow pass the night; let us ourselves procuring (leaves) and spreading them on the ground, anyhow lie down on it.

sanskrit: स तु सम्विश्य मेदिन्याम् महा अर्ह शयन उचितः
इमाः सौमित्रये रामः व्याजहार कथाः शुभाः
transliteration: sa tu samviśya medinyām mahā arha śayana ucitaḥ
imāḥ saumitraye rāmaḥ vyājahāra kathāḥ śubhāḥ
english: Saying this, Rāma lying down on the ground although worthy of a costly bed, spoke these excellent words to Sumitrā's son.

sanskrit: ध्रुवम् अद्य महा राजो दुह्खम् स्वपिति लक्ष्मण
कृत कामा तु कैकेयी तुष्टा भवितुम् अर्हति
transliteration: dhruvam adya mahā rājo duhkham svapiti lakṣmaṇa
kṛta kāmā tu kaikeyī tuṣṭā bhavitum arhati
english: O Lakşmaņa, surely the king sleeps uneasily to day, and Kaikeyi having attained her end ought to be satisfied.

sanskrit: सा हि देवी महा राजम् कैकेयी राज्य कारणात्
अपि न च्यावयेत् प्राणान् दृष्ट्वा भरतम् आगतम्
transliteration: sā hi devī mahā rājam kaikeyī rājya kāraṇāt
api na cyāvayet prāṇān dṛṣṭvā bharatam āgatam
english: Will not that revered lady, for the purpose of having Bharata established in the kingdom, take the king's life, when she shall see Bharata arrived?

sanskrit: अनाथः चैव वृद्धः च मया चैव विनाकृतः
किम् करिष्यति काम आत्मा कैकेय्या वशम् आगतः
transliteration: anāthaḥ caiva vṛddhaḥ ca mayā caiva vinākṛtaḥ
kim kariṣyati kāma ātmā kaikeyyā vaśam āgataḥ
english: Forlorn and old and deprived of me. I do not know what he will do, his soul possessed by desire, and having come under the influence of Kaikeyi.

sanskrit: इदम् व्यसनम् आलोक्य राज्ञः च मति विभ्रमम्
कामएव अर्ध धर्माभ्याम् गरीयान् इति मे मतिः
transliteration: idam vyasanam ālokya rājñaḥ ca mati vibhramam
kāmaeva ardha dharmābhyām garīyān iti me matiḥ
english: Viewing this calamity that has overtaken us) and the disorder that has taken place in the senses of the monarch, I deem even lust as more potent than either virtue or interest.

sanskrit: को हि अविद्वान् अपि पुमान् प्रमदायाः कृते त्यजेत्
चन्द अनुवर्तिनम् पुत्रम् तातः माम् इव लक्ष्मण
transliteration: ko hi avidvān api pumān pramadāyāḥ kṛte tyajet
canda anuvartinam putram tātaḥ mām iva lakṣmaṇa
english: O Lakşmana, what man is there ignorant though he be, who for the sake of a female forsake as my father has done me, his son following his foot-steps?

sanskrit: सुखी बत सभार्यः च भरतः केकयी सुतः
मुदितान् कोसलान् एको यो भोक्ष्यति अधिराजवत्
transliteration: sukhī bata sabhāryaḥ ca bharataḥ kekayī sutaḥ
muditān kosalān eko yo bhokṣyati adhirājavat
english: Ah! Kaikeyi's son Bharata with his wife is really happy, he that enjoys the sole sovereignty of the delighted Kosalas.

sanskrit: स हि सर्वस्य राज्यस्य मुखम् एकम् भविष्यति
ताते च वयसा अतीते मयि च अरण्यम् आश्रिते
transliteration: sa hi sarvasya rājyasya mukham ekam bhaviṣyati
tāte ca vayasā atīte mayi ca araṇyam āśrite
english: Now that our father has grown old and I have taken refuge in the forest, he will alone experience the supreme felicity in the kingdom.

sanskrit: अर्थ धर्मौ परित्यज्य यः कामम् अनुवर्तते
एवम् आपद्यते क्षिप्रम् राजा दशरथो यथा
transliteration: artha dharmau parityajya yaḥ kāmam anuvartate
evam āpadyate kṣipram rājā daśaratho yathā
english: He that renouncing interest and virtue, follows lust, speedily gets himself involved in troubles even like king Dasaratha.

sanskrit: मन्ये दशरथ अन्ताय मम प्रव्राजनाय च
कैकेयी सौम्य सम्प्राप्ता राज्याय भरतस्य च
transliteration: manye daśaratha antāya mama pravrājanāya ca
kaikeyī saumya samprāptā rājyāya bharatasya ca
english: O amiable one, I think that Kaikeyi has been born for making an end of Dasaratha, sending me into exile, and conferring the kingdom on Bharata.

sanskrit: अपि इदानीम् न कैकेयी सौभाग्य मद मोहिता
कौसल्याम् च सुमित्राम् च सम्प्रबाधेत मत् कृते
transliteration: api idānīm na kaikeyī saubhāgya mada mohitā
kausalyām ca sumitrām ca samprabādheta mat kṛte
english: At present for impareing me pain, Kaikeyi intoxicated by the tide of good fortune, will afflict Kausalya and Sumitrā.

sanskrit: मा स्म मत् कारणात् देवी सुमित्रा दुह्खम् आवसेत्
अयोध्याम् इतएव त्वम् काले प्रविश लक्ष्मण
transliteration: mā sma mat kāraṇāt devī sumitrā duhkham āvaset
ayodhyām itaeva tvam kāle praviśa lakṣmaṇa
english: Your mother, the reversed Sumitrā, will be smitten with grief on our account. Do you, Laks maņa, tomorrow morning repair to Ayodhyā:

sanskrit: अहम् एको गमिष्यामि सीतया सह दण्डकान्
अनाथाया हि नाथः त्वम् कौसल्याया भविष्यसि
transliteration: aham eko gamiṣyāmi sītayā saha daṇḍakān
anāthāyā hi nāthaḥ tvam kausalyāyā bhaviṣyasi
english: I alone will go to Dandaka along with Sītā. You will be the protector of the helpless Kausalya.

sanskrit: क्षुद्र कर्मा हि कैकेयी द्वेषात् अन्याय्यम् आचरेत्
परिदद्या हि धर्मज्ञे भरते मम मातरम्
transliteration: kṣudra karmā hi kaikeyī dveṣāt anyāyyam ācaret
paridadyā hi dharmajñe bharate mama mātaram
english: Kaikeyi is surely mean-minded, she perpetrates wrongs from malice. O you cognizant of virtue, she may administer poison to my mother.

sanskrit: नूनम् जाति अन्तरे कस्मिम्स् स्त्रियः पुत्रैः वियोजिताः
जनन्या मम सौमित्रे तत् अपि एतत् उपस्थितम्
transliteration: nūnam jāti antare kasmims striyaḥ putraiḥ viyojitāḥ
jananyā mama saumitre tat api etat upasthitam
english: Surely, O child, in a former birth, women were bereft of their sons by my mother, O son of Sumitrā; and it is for this that this misfortune has befallen her.

sanskrit: मया हि चिर पुष्टेन दुह्ख सम्वर्धितेन च
विप्रायुज्यत कौसल्या फल काले धिग् अस्तु माम्
transliteration: mayā hi cira puṣṭena duhkha samvardhitena ca
viprāyujyata kausalyā phala kāle dhig astu mām
english: Having been brought up and reared with great pains by Kausalyä, I have left her at the time when her labours ought to have borne fruit, Fie on me.

sanskrit: मा स्म सीमन्तिनी काचिज् जनयेत् पुत्रम् ईदृशम्
सौमित्रे यो अहम् अम्बाया दद्मि शोकम् अनन्तकम्
transliteration: mā sma sīmantinī kācij janayet putram īdṛśam
saumitre yo aham ambāyā dadmi śokam anantakam
english: Let on woman, O son of Sumitrā, gibe birth to a son like me who have imparted such infinite pain to my mother.

sanskrit: मन्ये प्रीति विशिष्टा सा मत्तः लक्ष्मण सारिका
यस्याः तत् श्रूयते वाक्यम् शुक पादम् अरेर् दश
transliteration: manye prīti viśiṣṭā sā mattaḥ lakṣmaṇa sārikā
yasyāḥ tat śrūyate vākyam śuka pādam arer daśa
english: O Laksmana, I consider my mother's female parrot as more sharing her affection, since she is heard to say, 'O Śuka, do you bite the foot of the foe?

sanskrit: शोचन्त्याः च अल्प भाग्याया न किम्चित् उपकुर्वता
पुर्त्रेण किम् अपुत्राया मया कार्यम् अरिम् दम
transliteration: śocantyāḥ ca alpa bhāgyāyā na kimcit upakurvatā
purtreṇa kim aputrāyā mayā kāryam arim dama
english: What am I, O repressor of foes, now to do for her, bewailing, of slender fortune, she that has not profited in the least by her son, and who stands in no further need of his good offices ? Surely my unfortunate mother, Kausalyā, bereft of me, lies down on the ground, overwhelmed with woe, and plunged in an ocean of grief..

sanskrit: अल्प भाग्या हि मे माता कौसल्या रहिता मया
शेते परम दुह्ख आर्ता पतिता शोक सागरे
transliteration: alpa bhāgyā hi me mātā kausalyā rahitā mayā
śete parama duhkha ārtā patitā śoka sāgare
english: What am I, O repressor of foes, now to do for her, bewailing, of slender fortune, she that has not profited in the least by her son, and who stands in no further need of his good offices ? Surely my unfortunate mother, Kausalyā, bereft of me, lies down on the ground, overwhelmed with woe, and plunged in an ocean of grief..

sanskrit: एको हि अहम् अयोध्याम् च पृथिवीम् च अपि लक्ष्मण
तरेयम् इषुभिः क्रुद्धो ननु वीर्यम् अकारणम्
transliteration: eko hi aham ayodhyām ca pṛthivīm ca api lakṣmaṇa
tareyam iṣubhiḥ kruddho nanu vīryam akāraṇam
english: O Laksmana, enraged, I alone without doubt, can rid Ayodhyā, the Earth herself, by means of my arrows. But improper is the display of prowess for no reason,

sanskrit: अधर्म भय भीतः च पर लोकस्य च अनघ
तेन लक्ष्मण न अद्य अहम् आत्मानम् अभिषेचये
transliteration: adharma bhaya bhītaḥ ca para lokasya ca anagha
tena lakṣmaṇa na adya aham ātmānam abhiṣecaye
english: O sinless one, I am afraid of unrighteousness and of the next life; and for this it is that, O Lakşmaņa, I do not install myself in the kingdom.

sanskrit: एतत् अन्यच् च करुणम् विलप्य विजने बहु
अश्रु पूर्ण मुखो रामः निशि तूष्णीम् उपाविशत्
transliteration: etat anyac ca karuṇam vilapya vijane bahu
aśru pūrṇa mukho rāmaḥ niśi tūṣṇīm upāviśat
english: Having in solitude for a long while piteously bewailed thus and in other ways, Rāma sat silent in the night with tears in his eyes.

sanskrit: विलप्य उपरतम् रामम् गत अर्चिषम् इव अनलम्
transliteration: vilapya uparatam rāmam gata arciṣam iva analam
english: Thereupon Lakşmaņa consoled Rāma spent with lamentation, like to fire deprived of its radiance or the ocean of its tide.

sanskrit: ध्रुवम् अद्य पुरी रामायोध्या युधिनाम् वर
निष्प्रभा त्वयि निष्क्रान्ते गत चन्द्रा इव शर्वरी
transliteration: dhruvam adya purī rāmāyodhyā yudhinām vara
niṣprabhā tvayi niṣkrānte gata candrā iva śarvarī
english: Surely, O Rama, O foremost of warriors, on your having come out, the city of Ayodhyā is shorn of its splendour like the night deprived of the moon.

sanskrit: न एतत् औपयिकम् राम यद् इदम् परितप्यसे
विषादयसि सीताम् च माम् चैव पुरुष ऋषभ
