transliteration: na etat aupayikam rāma yad idam paritapyase
viṣādayasi sītām ca mām caiva puruṣa ṛṣabha
english: This is not fit that you should grieve; for thereby, O foremost of men, you make both Sītā and myself grieve.

sanskrit: न च सीता त्वया हीना न च अहम् अपि राघव
मुहूर्तम् अपि जीवावो जलान् मत्स्याव् इव उद्धृतौ
transliteration: na ca sītā tvayā hīnā na ca aham api rāghava
muhūrtam api jīvāvo jalān matsyāv iva uddhṛtau
english: O Rāghava, deprived of you neither Sītā nor I can live for a moment, like fish taken out of water : without you.

sanskrit: न हि तातम् न शत्रुघ्नम् न सुमित्राम् परम् तप
द्रष्टुम् इच्चेयम् अद्य अहम् स्वर्गम् वा अपि त्वया विना
transliteration: na hi tātam na śatrughnam na sumitrām param tapa
draṣṭum icceyam adya aham svargam vā api tvayā vinā
english: O repressor of foes, I wish to see neither my father, nor Satrughna, nor Sumitrā, nor heaven itself.
Then viewing from where they sat at ease their well-laid bed under the banian tree, those virtuous ones (Rāma and Sītā) went to it.

sanskrit: निशम्य च एवम् वन वासम् आदरात्
transliteration: niśamya ca evam vana vāsam ādarāt
english: Hearing Lakşmaņa's excellent and appropriate words with which he gladly assumed a life in the woods, that subduer of foes, Rāghava, in the name of righteousness, at once fully granted him the permission to dwell with him for the entire fourteen years.
Then like to a couple of lions dwelling on a mountain-summit, at that lone spot of the extensive forest, those powerful perpetuators of the Raghu race, began to dwell without fear.

sanskrit: ते तु तस्मिन् महा वृक्षौषित्वा रजनीम् शिवाम्
विमले अभ्युदिते सूर्ये तस्मात् देशात् प्रतस्थिरे
transliteration: te tu tasmin mahā vṛkṣauṣitvā rajanīm śivām
vimale abhyudite sūrye tasmāt deśāt pratasthire
english: Having passed the auspicious night underneath that might tree, they, when the sun had risen in unclouded splendour, went away from that place.

sanskrit: जग्मुस् तम् देशम् उद्दिश्य विगाह्य सुमहद् वनम्
transliteration: jagmus tam deśam uddiśya vigāhya sumahad vanam
english: Then dividing into a mighty forest, they proceeded in the direction in which the Bhāgirathi Gangå meets with the Yamunā.

sanskrit: ते भूमिम् आगान् विविधान् देशामः च अपि मनो रमान्
अदृष्ट पूर्वान् पश्यन्तः तत्र तत्र यशस्विनः
transliteration: te bhūmim āgān vividhān deśāmaḥ ca api mano ramān
adṛṣṭa pūrvān paśyantaḥ tatra tatra yaśasvinaḥ
english: Those illustrious ones went on, viewing at intervals various fields and delightful lands which they had never seen before.

sanskrit: यथा क्षेमेण गच्चन् स पश्यमः च विविधान् द्रुमान्
निवृत्त मात्रे दिवसे रामः सौमित्रिम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: yathā kṣemeṇa gaccan sa paśyamaḥ ca vividhān drumān
nivṛtta mātre divase rāmaḥ saumitrim abravīt
english: And going on beholding various kinds of blossoming trees, Rāma when the day had declined, spoke to Sumitrā's son saying.

sanskrit: प्रयागम् अभितः पश्य सौमित्रे धूमम् उन्नतम्
अग्नेर् भगवतः केतुम् मन्ये सम्निहितः मुनिः
transliteration: prayāgam abhitaḥ paśya saumitre dhūmam unnatam
agner bhagavataḥ ketum manye samnihitaḥ muniḥ
english: O son of Sumitrā, do you behold the beautiful wreath of smoke that rises in front of Prayāga, sign of the worshipful Fire, and I infer some ascetic to be near.

sanskrit: नूनम् प्राप्ताः स्म सम्भेदम् गन्गा यमुनयोः वयम्
तथा हि श्रूयते शम्ब्दो वारिणा वारि घट्टितः
transliteration: nūnam prāptāḥ sma sambhedam gangā yamunayoḥ vayam
tathā hi śrūyate śambdo vāriṇā vāri ghaṭṭitaḥ
english: For certain we have arrived at the confluence of the Gangā and the Yamunā; and it is for this that we hear the roar of the waters produced by the rushing of them.

sanskrit: भरद्वाज आश्रमे च एते दृश्यन्ते विविधा द्रुमाः
transliteration: bharadvāja āśrame ca ete dṛśyante vividhā drumāḥ
english: All these various trees with their wood hewn away by foresters are seen in the asylums.

sanskrit: धन्विनौ तौ सुखम् गत्वा लम्बमाने दिवा करे
गन्गा यमुनयोह् सम्धौ प्रापतुर् निलयम् मुनेः
transliteration: dhanvinau tau sukham gatvā lambamāne divā kare
gangā yamunayoh samdhau prāpatur nilayam muneḥ
english: Thus having proceeded at ease, you bowmen when the sun stood aslant, arrived in the vicinity of the ascetic's residence on the delta of the Yamunā and the Gangā.

sanskrit: रामः तु आश्रमम् आसाद्य त्रासयन् मृग पक्षिणः
transliteration: rāmaḥ tu āśramam āsādya trāsayan mṛga pakṣiṇaḥ
english: Proceeding awhile on the way, Rāma, in presence of the asylum, came up to Bharadvāja's place, frightening beasts and birds.

sanskrit: ततः तु आश्रमम् आसाद्य मुनेर् दर्शन कान्क्षिणौ
सीतया अनुगतौ वीरौ दूरात् एव अवतस्थतुः
transliteration: tataḥ tu āśramam āsādya muner darśana kānkṣiṇau
sītayā anugatau vīrau dūrāt eva avatasthatuḥ
english: Arriving at the hermitage, the heroes desirous of seeing the ascetic, stood at a distance with Sītā behind them.

And as soon as entering in, that exalted one saw that high-souled anchoret of accomplished vows, who had attained spiritual insight through austerities, sitting surrounded by his disciples after having finished the Agnihotra, Rāma with joined hands saluted him along with Sumitra's son and Sita.

sanskrit: हुत अग्नि होत्रम् दृष्ट्वा एव महा भागम् कृत अन्जलिः
रामः सौमित्रिणा सार्धम् सीतया च अभ्यवादयत्
transliteration: huta agni hotram dṛṣṭvā eva mahā bhāgam kṛta anjaliḥ
rāmaḥ saumitriṇā sārdham sītayā ca abhyavādayat
english: And as soon as entering in, that exalted one saw that high-souled anchoret of accomplished vows, who had attained spiritual insight through austerities, sitting surrounded by his disciples after having finished the Agnihotra, Rāma with joined hands saluted him along with Sumitra's son and Sita.

sanskrit: न्यवेदयत च आत्मानम् तस्मै लक्ष्मण पूर्वजः
पुत्रौ दशरथस्य आवाम् भगवन् राम लक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: nyavedayata ca ātmānam tasmai lakṣmaṇa pūrvajaḥ
putrau daśarathasya āvām bhagavan rāma lakṣmaṇau

sanskrit: भार्या मम इयम् वैदेही कल्याणी जनक आत्मजा
माम् च अनुयाता विजनम् तपो वनम् अनिन्दिता
transliteration: bhāryā mama iyam vaidehī kalyāṇī janaka ātmajā
mām ca anuyātā vijanam tapo vanam aninditā

sanskrit: पित्रा प्रव्राज्यमानम् माम् सौमित्रिर् अनुजः प्रियः
अयम् अन्वगमद् भ्राता वनम् एव दृढ व्रतः
transliteration: pitrā pravrājyamānam mām saumitrir anujaḥ priyaḥ
ayam anvagamad bhrātā vanam eva dṛḍha vrataḥ

sanskrit: पित्रा नियुक्ता भगवन् प्रवेष्यामः तपो वनम्
धर्मम् एव आचरिष्यामः तत्र मूल फल अशनाः
transliteration: pitrā niyuktā bhagavan praveṣyāmaḥ tapo vanam
dharmam eva ācariṣyāmaḥ tatra mūla phala aśanāḥ
english: O revered one, commissioned by my father, I will enter the forest of asceticism, and there subsisting on fruits and roots will practise virtue.

sanskrit: तस्य तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा राज पुत्रस्य धीमतः
उपानयत धर्म आत्मा गाम् अर्घ्यम् उदकम् ततः
transliteration: tasya tat vacanam śrutvā rāja putrasya dhīmataḥ
upānayata dharma ātmā gām arghyam udakam tataḥ
english: Hearing those words of the intelligent prince, that righteous (ascetic) brought a bull* as well as Arghya and water and divers kinds of edibles consisting of wild fruits and roots. *When an eminent guest came to a person's house, as he offered madhuparka, with a bull which was killed for his entertainment
And that one of fiery austerities assigned quarters, along with beasts and birds as well as ascetics, for Rāma.

sanskrit: मृग पक्षिभिर् आसीनो मुनिभिः च समन्ततः
रामम् आगतम् अभ्यर्च्य स्वागतेन आह तम् मुनिः
transliteration: mṛga pakṣibhir āsīno munibhiḥ ca samantataḥ
rāmam āgatam abhyarcya svāgatena āha tam muniḥ
english: Then paying homage to Rāma he proceeded by short stages, and asking him, Has your journey been a pleasant one?, the ascetic sat down. And when Rāghava had sat down after receiving the homage, Bharadvāja spoke to him these words fraught with virtue.

sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य च ताम् अर्चाम् उपविष्टम् स राघवम्
भरद्वाजो अब्रवीद् वाक्यम् धर्म युक्तम् इदम् तदा
transliteration: pratigṛhya ca tām arcām upaviṣṭam sa rāghavam
bharadvājo abravīd vākyam dharma yuktam idam tadā
english: Then paying homage to Rāma he proceeded by short stages, and asking him, Has your journey been a pleasant one?, the ascetic sat down. And when Rāghava had sat down after receiving the homage, Bharadvāja spoke to him these words fraught with virtue.

sanskrit: चिरस्य खलु काकुत्स्थ पश्यामि त्वाम् इह आगतम्
श्रुतम् तव मया च इदम् विवासनम् अकारणम्
transliteration: cirasya khalu kākutstha paśyāmi tvām iha āgatam
śrutam tava mayā ca idam vivāsanam akāraṇam
english: O Kākutstha, I behold you come after a long time. I have heard of your causeless exile.

sanskrit: अवकाशो विविक्तः अयम् महा नद्योह् समागमे
पुण्यः च रमणीयः च वसतु इह भगान् सुखम्
transliteration: avakāśo viviktaḥ ayam mahā nadyoh samāgame
puṇyaḥ ca ramaṇīyaḥ ca vasatu iha bhagān sukham
english: This spot at the meeting of the mighty rivers is lonely, sacred and charming. Do you dwell here happily.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः तु वचनम् भरद्वाजेन राघवः
प्रत्युवाच शुभम् वाक्यम् रामः सर्व हिते रतः
transliteration: evam uktaḥ tu vacanam bharadvājena rāghavaḥ
pratyuvāca śubham vākyam rāmaḥ sarva hite rataḥ
english: Thus addressed by Bharadvāja, that descendant of Raghu, Rāma intent on the welfare of all, answered in auspicious words.

O reverend one, I apprehend that, living hard by, the inhabitants of the city and the provinces, thinking me as easily to be seen, will come to this asylum desirous of beholding me and Vaidehī. It is for this reason that living at this place does not recommended itself to me.

sanskrit: आगमिष्यति वैदेहीम् माम् च अपि प्रेक्षको जनः
अनेन कारणेन अहम् इह वासम् न रोचये
transliteration: āgamiṣyati vaidehīm mām ca api prekṣako janaḥ
anena kāraṇena aham iha vāsam na rocaye
english: O reverend one, I apprehend that, living hard by, the inhabitants of the city and the provinces, thinking me as easily to be seen, will come to this asylum desirous of beholding me and Vaidehī. It is for this reason that living at this place does not recommended itself to me.

sanskrit: एक अन्ते पश्य भगवन्न् आश्रम स्थानम् उत्तमम्
रमते यत्र वैदेही सुख अर्हा जनक आत्मजा
transliteration: eka ante paśya bhagavann āśrama sthānam uttamam
ramate yatra vaidehī sukha arhā janaka ātmajā
english: Do you, O worshipful one, hit upon a retired and agreeable asylum where Janaka's daughter worthy of happiness, will pass her days pleasantly.

sanskrit: एतत् श्रुत्वा शुभम् वाक्यम् भरद्वाजो महा मुनिः
राघवस्य ततः वाक्यम् अर्थ ग्राहकम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: etat śrutvā śubham vākyam bharadvājo mahā muniḥ
rāghavasya tataḥ vākyam artha grāhakam abravīt
english: Hearing this auspicious speech of Rāghava, that eminent anchoret Bharadvāja said these words calculated to serve Rāma's purpose.

sanskrit: दश क्रोशैतः तात गिरिर् यस्मिन् निवत्स्यसि
महर्षि सेवितः पुण्यः सर्वतः सुख दर्शनः
transliteration: daśa krośaitaḥ tāta girir yasmin nivatsyasi
maharṣi sevitaḥ puṇyaḥ sarvataḥ sukha darśanaḥ

sanskrit: गो लान्गूल अनुचरितः वानर ऋष्क निषेवितः
चित्र कूटैति ख्यातः गन्ध मादन सम्निभः
transliteration: go lāngūla anucaritaḥ vānara ṛṣka niṣevitaḥ
citra kūṭaiti khyātaḥ gandha mādana samnibhaḥ
english: Ten Krosas hence, my child, is the mountain where you shall dwell. it is inhabited by maharsis, and is sacred, and picturesque throughout, abounding in Golāngulas, monkeys, and bears, known by the name of Citrakuta, resembling Gandhamädana.

sanskrit: यावता चित्र कूटस्य नरः शृन्गाणि अवेक्षते
कल्याणानि समाधत्ते न पापे कुरुते मनः
transliteration: yāvatā citra kūṭasya naraḥ śṛngāṇi avekṣate
kalyāṇāni samādhatte na pāpe kurute manaḥ
english: On beholding the peaks of Citrakuța, one reaps welfare, and ignorance does not envelope one's mind.

sanskrit: ऋषयः तत्र बहवो विहृत्य शरदाम् शतम्
तपसा दिवम् आरूधाः कपाल शिरसा सह
transliteration: ṛṣayaḥ tatra bahavo vihṛtya śaradām śatam
tapasā divam ārūdhāḥ kapāla śirasā saha
english: There innumerable saints with the hair of their heads rendered white like skulls, having spent hundreds of years, have through austerities ascended heaven.

sanskrit: प्रविविक्तम् अहम् मन्ये तम् वासम् भवतः सुखम्
इह वा वन वासाय वस राम मया सह
transliteration: praviviktam aham manye tam vāsam bhavataḥ sukham
iha vā vana vāsāya vasa rāma mayā saha
english: That solitary spot I deem as one which will make a happy residence for you. O Rāma, do you, for living out the term of your banishment, dwell either here or with me.

sanskrit: स रामम् सर्व कामैअः तम् भरद्वाजः प्रिय अतिथिम्
सभार्यम् सह च भ्रात्रा प्रतिजग्राह धर्मवित्
transliteration: sa rāmam sarva kāmaiaḥ tam bharadvājaḥ priya atithim
sabhāryam saha ca bhrātrā pratijagrāha dharmavit
english: Bharadvāja entertained his welcome guest, Rāma, along with his wife and brother by extending towards them every rite of hospitality.

sanskrit: तस्य प्रयागे रामस्य तम् महर्षिम् उपेयुषः
प्रपन्ना रजनी पुण्या चित्राः कथयतः कथाः
transliteration: tasya prayāge rāmasya tam maharṣim upeyuṣaḥ
prapannā rajanī puṇyā citrāḥ kathayataḥ kathāḥ
english: At Prayāga Rāma having obtained the company of that Maharși, and discoursing on a variety of sacred topics, the night came on.
And with Sītā for the third, Kåkutstha brought up in luxury, being fatigued, pleasantly spent that night at the romantic hermitage of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: उवाच नर शार्दूलो मुनिम् ज्वलित तेजसम्
transliteration: uvāca nara śārdūlo munim jvalita tejasam
english: When the night had passed away and day dawned, (Rāma) approached Bharadvāja, and that chief of men addressed that ascetic of flaming energy.

sanskrit: शर्वरीम् भवनन्न् अद्य सत्य शील तव आश्रमे
उषिताः स्म इह वसतिम् अनुजानातु नो भवान्
transliteration: śarvarīm bhavanann adya satya śīla tava āśrame
uṣitāḥ sma iha vasatim anujānātu no bhavān
english: O reverend sire of truthful character, we have here in your asylum spent the night. Do you now permit us to set forward (for Citrakuta).

sanskrit: रात्र्याम् तु तस्याम् व्युष्टायाम् भरद्वाजो अब्रवीद् इदम्
मधु मूल फल उपेतम् चित्र कूटम् व्रज इति ह
transliteration: rātryām tu tasyām vyuṣṭāyām bharadvājo abravīd idam
madhu mūla phala upetam citra kūṭam vraja iti ha

sanskrit: तत्र कुन्जर यूथानि मृग यूथानि च अभितः
transliteration: tatra kunjara yūthāni mṛga yūthāni ca abhitaḥ

sanskrit: विचरन्ति वन अन्तेषु तानि द्रक्ष्यसि राघव
transliteration: vicaranti vana anteṣu tāni drakṣyasi rāghava
english: Do you repair to the famed Citrakuţa, holy, fair to the view, and abounding in countless fruits and roots. And in those forests range herds of elephants and deer; and these, O Rāghava, you will behold. And ranging with Sītā rivers and rills and plateau's, caverns and fountains, your mind will experience delight.

sanskrit: मृगैः च मत्तैः बहुभिः च कुन्जरैः
transliteration: mṛgaiḥ ca mattaiḥ bahubhiḥ ca kunjaraiḥ

english: Having spent the night there, those princes, repressors of their foes, after paying their obeisance to the Maharși, set out for the mountain.

sanskrit: तेषाम् चैव स्वस्त्ययनम् महर्षिः स चकार ह
transliteration: teṣām caiva svastyayanam maharṣiḥ sa cakāra ha
english: Seeing them about to set forth, that Maharși performed a propitiatory ceremony for them, even as a father does on behalf of the sons begot from his own loins.

sanskrit: ततः प्रचक्रमे वक्तुम् वचनम् स महामुनिः
transliteration: tataḥ pracakrame vaktum vacanam sa mahāmuniḥ
english: And that mighty ascetic, Bharadvāja having truth for his prowess, addressed them, saying.
O best of men, do you coming to the confluence of the Gangā and the Yamunā proceed along the Kalindi river flowing westwards.

Arriving at the Kalindi running in a contrary direction, you will, O Rāghava, behold a goodly bathing place well-worn by foot-passengers. There constructing a raft, do you cross over the river who is the daughter of the Sun.

sanskrit: तत्र यूयम् प्लवम् कृत्वा तरताम्शुमतीम् नदीम्
transliteration: tatra yūyam plavam kṛtvā taratāmśumatīm nadīm

sanskrit: समासाद्य तु तम् वृक्षम् वसेद्वातिक्रमेत वा
क्रोशमात्रम् ततो गत्वा नीलम् द्रक्ष्यथ काननम्
transliteration: samāsādya tu tam vṛkṣam vasedvātikrameta vā
krośamātram tato gatvā nīlam drakṣyatha kānanam

sanskrit: अथा साद्य तु काLइन्दीम् शीघ्रस्रोतोवहाम् नदीम्
transliteration: athā sādya tu kāindīm śīghrasrotovahām nadīm

english: Then with heaps of dry wild wood covered with grass, they constructed a large raft. And the puissant Lakşmaņa tearing twigs from the ratan and the rose-apple, made a comfortable seat for Sita.

sanskrit: पार्श्वे च तत्र वैदेह्या वसने चूष्णानि च
transliteration: pārśve ca tatra vaidehyā vasane cūṣṇāni ca

sanskrit: आरोप्य प्रथमम् सीताम् सम्घाटम् प्रतिगृह्य तौ
transliteration: āropya prathamam sītām samghāṭam pratigṛhya tau

sanskrit: स्वस्ति देवि तरामि त्वाम् पार्येन्मे पतिर्वतम्
transliteration: svasti devi tarāmi tvām pāryenme patirvatam
english: Having come near the middle of the Kalindi, Sītā prayed to her, saying, 'Hail to you, O goddess! I cross you. If my husband can successfully perform his vow, I will worship you with a thousand cows and an hundred vessels of wine, hail to you, upon Rāma's return to the city ruled by Ikşvāki

sanskrit: कौसल्याम् चैव पश्येयम् सुमित्राम् च यशस्विनीम्
transliteration: kausalyām caiva paśyeyam sumitrām ca yaśasvinīm
english: On coming to the banian, Vaidehī saluted it saying, “O mighty tree, I bow to you. May my husband fulfil his vow; and may we behold Kausalyā and the illustrious Sumitrā.” Having thus prayed with joined hands, the intelligent Sītā went away.

sanskrit: दयिताम् च विधेयम् च रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
transliteration: dayitām ca vidheyam ca rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt

sanskrit: एकैकम् पादपम् गुल्मम् लताम् वा पुष्पशालिनीम्
transliteration: ekaikam pādapam gulmam latām vā puṣpaśālinīm

sanskrit: रेमे जनकराजस्य तदा प्रेक्ष्य सुता नदीम्
transliteration: reme janakarājasya tadā prekṣya sutā nadīm

english: And having disported in the beautiful woods resounding with multitudes of peacocks and inhabited by elephants and monkeys, they looking as lively as ever, coming to the level banks of the river, took up their quarters there.

sanskrit: प्रबोधयाम् आस शनैः लक्ष्मणम् रघु नन्दनः
transliteration: prabodhayām āsa śanaiḥ lakṣmaṇam raghu nandanaḥ
english: When the night had been spent, that best of Raghus gently awakened Lakşmaņa from his light sleep.

sanskrit: सौमित्रे शृणु वन्यानाम् वल्गु व्याहरताम् स्वनम्
transliteration: saumitre śṛṇu vanyānām valgu vyāharatām svanam
english: O Sumiträ's son, do you hear the dulcet notes of the birds in the woods. Let us proceed. O repressor of foes, the time of our departure is present.

sanskrit: स सुप्तः समये भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणः प्रतिबोधितः
जहौ निद्राम् च तन्द्रीम् च प्रसक्तम् च पथि श्रमम्
transliteration: sa suptaḥ samaye bhrātrā lakṣmaṇaḥ pratibodhitaḥ
jahau nidrām ca tandrīm ca prasaktam ca pathi śramam
english: Awakened at the proper time, Rāma's brother left off sleep and drowsiness and clinging fatigue.

sanskrit: ततौत्थाय ते सर्वे स्पृष्ट्वा नद्याः शिवम् जलम्
पन्थानम् ऋषिणा उद्दिष्टम् चित्र कूटस्य तम् ययुः
transliteration: tatautthāya te sarve spṛṣṭvā nadyāḥ śivam jalam
panthānam ṛṣiṇā uddiṣṭam citra kūṭasya tam yayuḥ
english: Then they all arising touched the sacred waters of the river, and began to proceed on the way to Citrakuța inhabited by ascetics.

sanskrit: ततः सम्प्रस्थितः काले रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
सीताम् कमल पत्र अक्षीम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tataḥ samprasthitaḥ kāle rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
sītām kamala patra akṣīm idam vacanam abravīt
english: Setting out in season with Sumitra's son, he of eyes resembling lotus-petais spoke these words to Sītā.

sanskrit: आदीप्तान् इव वैदेहि सर्वतः पुष्पितान् नगान्
स्वैः पुष्पैः किम्शुकान् पश्य मालिनः शिशिर अत्यये
transliteration: ādīptān iva vaidehi sarvataḥ puṣpitān nagān
svaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kimśukān paśya mālinaḥ śiśira atyaye
english: O Vaidehi, behold these flowering trees, the Kinsukas in spring appearing engarlanded with their own flowers, and as if flaming., Do you behold the Bhallatakas and Bilvas bending beneath their fruits and flowers, with no man to enjoy them. Surely, we: shall be able to live here.

sanskrit: फल पत्रैः अवनतान् नूनम् शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्
transliteration: phala patraiḥ avanatān nūnam śakṣyāmi jīvitum
english: O Vaidehi, behold these flowering trees, the Kinsukas in spring appearing engarlanded with their own flowers, and as if flaming., Do you behold the Bhallatakas and Bilvas bending beneath their fruits and flowers, with no man to enjoy them. Surely, we: shall be able to live here.

sanskrit: मधूनि मधु कारीभिः सम्भृतानि नगे नगे
transliteration: madhūni madhu kārībhiḥ sambhṛtāni nage nage
english: Behold, O Laksmana, these honeycombs measuring about a Droņa have been hung up on trees by the bees.

sanskrit: एष क्रोशति नत्यूहः तम् शिखी प्रतिकूजति
रमणीये वन उद्देशे पुष्प सम्स्तर सम्कटे
transliteration: eṣa krośati natyūhaḥ tam śikhī pratikūjati
ramaṇīye vana uddeśe puṣpa samstara samkaṭe
english: In the charming woods overarched by flowers, the Datyuha cries, and is responded to by the peacock.

sanskrit: मातम्ग यूथ अनुसृतम् पक्षि सम्घ अनुनादितम्
चित्र कूटम् इमम् पश्य प्रवृद्ध शिखरम् गिरिम्
transliteration: mātamga yūtha anusṛtam pakṣi samgha anunāditam
citra kūṭam imam paśya pravṛddha śikharam girim
english: Do you behold Citrakuta frequented by mad elephants and resonant with the voice of multitudes of birds, the mountain with its towering summits.
O child, we will disport in the sacred woods of Citrakuta with fine level plains, and covered with divers trees.

sanskrit: ततः तौ पाद चारेण गच्चन्तौ सह सीतया
रम्यम् आसेदतुः शैलम् चित्र कूटम् मनो रमम्
transliteration: tataḥ tau pāda cāreṇa gaccantau saha sītayā
ramyam āsedatuḥ śailam citra kūṭam mano ramam
english: Then they proceeding on foot along with Sītā, arrived at the charming and beautiful mountain Citrakuta.

sanskrit: तम् तु पर्वतम् आसाद्य नाना पक्षि गण आयुतम्
transliteration: tam tu parvatam āsādya nānā pakṣi gaṇa āyutam
english: Arriving at the mountain inhabited by birds of various kinds, abounding in fruits and roots, and furnished with watery expanses, (Răma) said.
O amiable one, methinks this beautiful hill furnished with innumerable fruits and roots, is fraught with subsistence.

sanskrit: अयम् वासो भवेत् तावद् अत्र सौम्य रमेमहि
transliteration: ayam vāso bhavet tāvad atra saumya ramemahi
english: And the hill is inhabited by high-souled ascetics. Let this, O child, be our abode. We will dwell here.

sanskrit: इति सीता च रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च कृताञ्जलिः
transliteration: iti sītā ca rāmaśca lakṣmaṇaśca kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Then Ráma, Lakşmana and Sītā with joined hands presented themselves at the asylum of Vālmīki and saluted him.

sanskrit: आस्यतामिति चोवाच स्वागतम् तु निवेद्य च
transliteration: āsyatāmiti covāca svāgatam tu nivedya ca
english: Thereat the Maharși cognizant of morality said to them, "Be seated!” and addressed Rāma, saying, “Has your journey been a pleasant one?”
Then having duly acquainted the saint with matters pertaining to himself, that lord, the mighty-armed elder brother of Laksmana, said to the latter.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मण आनय दारूणि दृढानि च वराणि च
कुरुष्व आवसथम् सौम्य वासे मे अभिरतम् मनः
transliteration: lakṣmaṇa ānaya dārūṇi dṛḍhāni ca varāṇi ca
kuruṣva āvasatham saumya vāse me abhiratam manaḥ
english: O Lakşmaņa, bring you wood good and strong. O amiable one, construct a dwelling. My mind is set upon staying here.

sanskrit: तस्य तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा सौमित्रिर् विविधान् द्रुमान्
आजहार ततः चक्रे पर्ण शालाम् अरिम् दम
transliteration: tasya tat vacanam śrutvā saumitrir vividhān drumān
ājahāra tataḥ cakre parṇa śālām arim dama
english: Hearing his words, Sumitra's son procured woods of various descriptions, and then that subduer of foes reared a cottage thatched with leaves.

sanskrit: ताम् निष्ठताम् बद्धकटाम् दृष्ट्वा रमः सुदर्शनाम्
शुश्रूषमाणम् एक अग्रम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tām niṣṭhatām baddhakaṭām dṛṣṭvā ramaḥ sudarśanām
śuśrūṣamāṇam eka agram idam vacanam abravīt
english: Beholding that goodly dwelling walled with wood furnished with doors, Rāma addressed these words and Lakşmaņa, intent upon ministering to his brother.

sanskrit: ऐणेयम् माम्सम् आहृत्य शालाम् यक्ष्यामहे वयम्
transliteration: aiṇeyam māmsam āhṛtya śālām yakṣyāmahe vayam
english: Procuring meat, we will worship the deity presiding over this dwelling. O Sumitrā's son, those who wish to live long, should pacify the household gods.

sanskrit: मृगम् हत्वाऽऽनय क्षिप्रम् लक्ष्मणेह शुभेक्षणकर्तव्यः शास्त्रदृष्टो हि विधिर्दर्ममनुस्मर
transliteration: mṛgam hatvā''naya kṣipram lakṣmaṇeha śubhekṣaṇakartavyaḥ śāstradṛṣṭo hi vidhirdarmamanusmara
english: O Lakşmaņa graced with auspicious eyes, do you killing deer, swiftly bring it here. It behoves us to observe the rules prescribed by the scriptures. Do you follow the ordinance.

sanskrit: चकार स यथोक्तम् च तम् रामः पुनरब्रवीत्
transliteration: cakāra sa yathoktam ca tam rāmaḥ punarabravīt
english: Acquainted with the words of his brother, Lakşmaņa, slayer of hostile heroes did as he was told. Thereupon Rāma addressed him again.
Do you cook this meat. We will worship the presiding deities of this mansion. Bestir yourself, the moment is mild and the day is styled Dhruva.

sanskrit: स लक्ष्मणः कृष्ण मृगम् हत्वा मेध्यम् पतापवान्
अथ चिक्षेप सौमित्रिः समिद्धे जात वेदसि
transliteration: sa lakṣmaṇaḥ kṛṣṇa mṛgam hatvā medhyam patāpavān
atha cikṣepa saumitriḥ samiddhe jāta vedasi
english: Then Lakşmana the son of Sumitrā endowed with vigour, having slain a sacred black deer, threw it into flaming fire.

sanskrit: तम् तु पक्वम् समाज्ञाय निष्टप्तम् चिन्न शोणितम्
लक्ष्मणः पुरुष व्याघ्रम् अथ राघवम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tam tu pakvam samājñāya niṣṭaptam cinna śoṇitam
lakṣmaṇaḥ puruṣa vyāghram atha rāghavam abravīt
english: And seeing it well scorched and hot and free from blood, Lakşmaņa spoke to that foremost of men, Rāghava, saying.

sanskrit: अयम् कृष्णः समाप्त अन्गः शृतः कृष्ण मृगो यथा
देवता देव सम्काश यजस्व कुशलो हि असि
transliteration: ayam kṛṣṇaḥ samāpta angaḥ śṛtaḥ kṛṣṇa mṛgo yathā
devatā deva samkāśa yajasva kuśalo hi asi

sanskrit: रामः स्नात्वा तु नियतः गुणवान् जप्य कोविदः
transliteration: rāmaḥ snātvā tu niyataḥ guṇavān japya kovidaḥ

english: And (this having been done), Rāma of immeasurable energy rejoiced exceedingly. And sacrificing to Vaisva, Rudra and Visnu, he performed some ceremonies for removing malign influences from the abode.

sanskrit: जपम् च न्यायतः कृत्वा स्नात्वा नद्याम् यथाविधि
पाप सम्शमनम् रामः चकार बलिम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: japam ca nyāyataḥ kṛtvā snātvā nadyām yathāvidhi
pāpa samśamanam rāmaḥ cakāra balim uttamam
english: Having duly performed Japa and bathed is consonance with the ordinance, Rāma made an excellent sacrifice for removing sin. And then Rāghava established a dais, and a Caitya proportionate to the abode.* The N.W.P. text reads:, "And in that romantic. forest abounding in various kinds of beast and birds, with trees bearing a profusion of variegated flowers, and resounding with the roars of beasts and serpents, those ones and, who had conquered their senses, began to live happily.",

Having duly performed Japa and bathed is consonance with the ordinance, Rāma made an excellent sacrifice for removing sin. And then Rāghava established a dais, and a Caitya proportionate to the abode.* The N.W.P. text reads:, "And in that romantic. forest abounding in various kinds of beast and birds, with trees bearing a profusion of variegated flowers, and resounding with the roars of beasts and serpents, those ones and, who had conquered their senses, began to live happily.",

And having with garlands made of wild flowers, fruits roots, meat cooked according to the ordinance, water, Fapa as prescribed by the Veda, grass, and faggot, worshipped the spirits, those descendants of Raghu, the auspicious Rāma and Lakşmaņa, in company with Sītă entered the graceful mansion.]

sanskrit: तौ तर्पयित्वा भूतानि राघवौ सह सीतया
transliteration: tau tarpayitvā bhūtāni rāghavau saha sītayā
english: And having with garlands made of wild flowers, fruits roots, meat cooked according to the ordinance, water, Fapa as prescribed by the Veda, grass, and faggot, worshipped the spirits, those descendants of Raghu, the auspicious Rāma and Lakşmaņa, in company with Sītă entered the graceful mansion.]

And as the celestials enter the hall entitled Sudharmă, they together with the view of dwelling in it, entered the mansion beautiful to behold, thatched with the leaves of trees, built at a convenient site, well-made, and keeping out the wind.

And having come to the charming Citrakuta and the river Mālyavatī furnished with excellent bathing places, and haunted by beasts and fowls, they rejoiced with glad hearts, and forsook the grief incident to their exile from the city.

sanskrit: कथयित्वा सुदुह्ख आर्तः सुमन्त्रेण चिरम् सह
रामे दक्षिण कूलस्थे जगाम स्व गृहम् गुहः
transliteration: kathayitvā suduhkha ārtaḥ sumantreṇa ciram saha
rāme dakṣiṇa kūlasthe jagāma sva gṛham guhaḥ
english: Having for a long time conversed with Sumantra, Guha distressed at heart on Rāma reaching the southern bank, retraced his steps homewards.

Learning from envoys at (Śrngaverapura) all about Rāma's visit to Bharadvāja at Prayāga and his reception (at Bharadvāja's place) as well as their destined journey (to Citrakuta), Sumantra, taking the permission (of Guha), yoked those excellent horses and with a heavy heart directed his course to the city of Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: अनुज्ञातः सुमन्त्रः अथ योजयित्वा हय उत्तमान्
अयोध्याम् एव नगरीम् प्रययौ गाढ दुर्मनाः
transliteration: anujñātaḥ sumantraḥ atha yojayitvā haya uttamān
ayodhyām eva nagarīm prayayau gāḍha durmanāḥ
english: Learning from envoys at (Śrngaverapura) all about Rāma's visit to Bharadvāja at Prayāga and his reception (at Bharadvāja's place) as well as their destined journey (to Citrakuta), Sumantra, taking the permission (of Guha), yoked those excellent horses and with a heavy heart directed his course to the city of Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: स वनानि सुगन्धीनि सरितः च सराम्सि च
पश्यन्न् अतिययौ शीघ्रम् ग्रामाणि नगराणि च
transliteration: sa vanāni sugandhīni saritaḥ ca sarāmsi ca
paśyann atiyayau śīghram grāmāṇi nagarāṇi ca
english: And beholding perfumed woods and rivers and watery expanses and towns and villages, he eagerly proceeded on his way.

sanskrit: ततः साय अह्न समये तृतीये अहनि सारथिः
transliteration: tataḥ sāya ahna samaye tṛtīye ahani sārathiḥ
english: And on the third day at dusk the charioteer arriving at Ayodhyā saw it bereft of happiness.

sanskrit: स शून्याम् इव निह्शब्दाम् दृष्ट्वा परम दुर्मनाः
सुमन्त्रः चिन्तयाम् आस शोक वेग समाहतः
transliteration: sa śūnyām iva nihśabdām dṛṣṭvā parama durmanāḥ
sumantraḥ cintayām āsa śoka vega samāhataḥ
english: And beholding it empty and still, Sumantra afflicted with exceeding sorrow, and overwhelmed with grief, thought, “Perhaps the city with her elephants and horses and men and king has been consumed by the fire of grief on account of Rāma."

sanskrit: कच्चिन् न सगजा साश्वा सजना सजन अधिपा
राम सम्ताप दुह्खेन दग्धा शोक अग्निना पुरी
transliteration: kaccin na sagajā sāśvā sajanā sajana adhipā
rāma samtāpa duhkhena dagdhā śoka agninā purī
english: And beholding it empty and still, Sumantra afflicted with exceeding sorrow, and overwhelmed with grief, thought, “Perhaps the city with her elephants and horses and men and king has been consumed by the fire of grief on account of Rāma."

sanskrit: इति चिन्ता परः सूतः वाजिभिः श्रीघ्रपातिभिः
transliteration: iti cintā paraḥ sūtaḥ vājibhiḥ śrīghrapātibhiḥ
english: Having thus reflected, the charioteer drawing up to the city-gate by means of those fleetcoursing horses, speedily entered the city.

sanskrit: सुमन्त्रम् अभियान्तम् तम् शतशो अथ सहस्रशः
क्व रामैति पृच्चन्तः सूतम् अभ्यद्रवन् नराः
transliteration: sumantram abhiyāntam tam śataśo atha sahasraśaḥ
kva rāmaiti pṛccantaḥ sūtam abhyadravan narāḥ
english: Thereupon, people by hundreds and thousands rushed after the charioteer, Sumantra, asking, "Where is Rāma?”

sanskrit: तेषाम् शशम्स गङ्गायाम् अहम् आपृच्च्य राघवम्
transliteration: teṣām śaśamsa gaṅgāyām aham āpṛccya rāghavam

sanskrit: ते तीर्णाइति विज्ञाय बाष्प पूर्ण मुखा जनाः
अहो धिग् इति निश्श्वस्य हा राम इति च चुक्रुशुः
transliteration: te tīrṇāiti vijñāya bāṣpa pūrṇa mukhā janāḥ
aho dhig iti niśśvasya hā rāma iti ca cukruśuḥ

sanskrit: शुश्राव च वचः तेषाम् बृन्दम् बृन्दम् च तिष्ठताम्
हताः स्म खलु ये न इह पश्यामैति राघवम्
transliteration: śuśrāva ca vacaḥ teṣām bṛndam bṛndam ca tiṣṭhatām
hatāḥ sma khalu ye na iha paśyāmaiti rāghavam

sanskrit: दान यज्ञ विवाहेषु समाजेषु महत्सु च
न द्रक्ष्यामः पुनर् जातु धार्मिकम् रामम् अन्तरा
transliteration: dāna yajña vivāheṣu samājeṣu mahatsu ca
na drakṣyāmaḥ punar jātu dhārmikam rāmam antarā
english: We shall no longer see the righteous Rāma in the midst of mighty assemblies engaged in charity, sacrifice or nuptial rites.

sanskrit: किम् समर्थम् जनस्य अस्य किम् प्रियम् किम् सुख आवहम्
transliteration: kim samartham janasya asya kim priyam kim sukha āvaham
english: What was necessary for this body? What was dear to them and what did they delight in?, (constantly revolving all this in his mind), Rāma ruled this city even as father.

sanskrit: वात अयन गतानाम् च स्त्रीणाम् अन्वन्तर आपणम्
transliteration: vāta ayana gatānām ca strīṇām anvantara āpaṇam
english: Then proceeding past the stalls, Sumantra heard the lamentations of females at windows, burning in grief for Rāma.

sanskrit: स राज मार्ग मध्येन सुमन्त्रः पिहित आननः
यत्र राजा दशरथः तत् एव उपययौ गृहम्
transliteration: sa rāja mārga madhyena sumantraḥ pihita ānanaḥ
yatra rājā daśarathaḥ tat eva upayayau gṛham
english: With his face muffled, Sumantra proceeded on the highway towards the palace of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: सो अवतीर्य रथात् शीघ्रम् राज वेश्म प्रविश्य च
कक्ष्याः सप्त अभिचक्राम महा जन समाकुलाः
transliteration: so avatīrya rathāt śīghram rāja veśma praviśya ca
kakṣyāḥ sapta abhicakrāma mahā jana samākulāḥ
english: Swiftly alighting from the car and entering the royal residence, he went past seven apartments thronged with people.
And beholding Sumantra returned to the city crowned with edifices, seven-storied houses, and palatial mansions, the women, stricken with the absence of Rama, set up a cry of "Oh" and "Alas."

Waxing still more aggrieved, the females looked at each other with their expansive and transparent eyes fast flooded with tears. And then he heard the talk, as toned down it proceeded from the royal mansions, of the wives of Dasaratha afflicted with grief for Rāma.

sanskrit: ततः दशरथ स्त्रीणाम् प्रासादेभ्यः ततः ततः
राम शोक अभितप्तानाम् मन्दम् शुश्राव जल्पितम्
transliteration: tataḥ daśaratha strīṇām prāsādebhyaḥ tataḥ tataḥ
rāma śoka abhitaptānām mandam śuśrāva jalpitam

sanskrit: सह रामेण निर्यातः विना रामम् इह आगतः
सूतः किम् नाम कौसल्याम् शोचन्तीम् प्रति वक्ष्यति
transliteration: saha rāmeṇa niryātaḥ vinā rāmam iha āgataḥ
sūtaḥ kim nāma kausalyām śocantīm prati vakṣyati
english: Going in company with Rāma, and returning without him, what will the charioteer answer Kausalya bewailing (for her son)?

sanskrit: यथा च मन्ये दुर्जीवम् एवम् न सुकरम् ध्रुवम्
आच्चिद्य पुत्रे निर्याते कौसल्या यत्र जीवति
transliteration: yathā ca manye durjīvam evam na sukaram dhruvam
āccidya putre niryāte kausalyā yatra jīvati
english: Surely life is miserable, yet is incapable of being renounced, since, although her son leaving (the installation) has gone away, yet Kausalyā still lives.

sanskrit: सत्य रूपम् तु तत् वाक्यम् राज्ञः स्त्रीणाम् निशामयन्
प्रदीप्तम् इव शोकेन विवेश सहसा गृहम्
transliteration: satya rūpam tu tat vākyam rājñaḥ strīṇām niśāmayan
pradīptam iva śokena viveśa sahasā gṛham
english: Having heard those words of the queens, fraught with truth, Sumantra burning as it were in grief, at once entered the (next) apartment.

sanskrit: स प्रविश्य अष्टमीम् कक्ष्याम् राजानम् दीनम् आतुलम्
पुत्र शोक परिम्लानम् अपश्यत् पाण्डुरे गृहे
transliteration: sa praviśya aṣṭamīm kakṣyām rājānam dīnam ātulam
putra śoka parimlānam apaśyat pāṇḍure gṛhe
english: And entering the eighth apartment he beheld in a gloomy chamber the king distressed and in a pitiable plight, woe-begone for grief for his son.

sanskrit: अभिगम्य तम् आसीनम् नर इन्द्रम् अभिवाद्य च
सुमन्त्रः राम वचनम् यथा उक्तम् प्रत्यवेदयत्
transliteration: abhigamya tam āsīnam nara indram abhivādya ca
sumantraḥ rāma vacanam yathā uktam pratyavedayat
english: Thereupon presenting himself before the monarch, Sumantra saluted him and then conveyed to the king the words of Rāma as he had uttered them.

sanskrit: स तूष्णीम् एव तत् श्रुत्वा राजा विभ्रान्त चेतनः
मूर्चितः न्यपतत् भूमौ राम शोक अभिपीडितः
transliteration: sa tūṣṇīm eva tat śrutvā rājā vibhrānta cetanaḥ
mūrcitaḥ nyapatat bhūmau rāma śoka abhipīḍitaḥ
english: Hearing them silently, the monarch with his mind exceedingly wrought, dropped down to the ground in a swoon, afflicted with grief for Rāma.

sanskrit: ततः अन्तः पुरम् आविद्धम् मूर्चिते पृथिवी पतौ
उद्धृत्य बाहू चुक्रोश नृपतौ पतिते क्षितौ
transliteration: tataḥ antaḥ puram āviddham mūrcite pṛthivī patau
uddhṛtya bāhū cukrośa nṛpatau patite kṣitau
english: On the lord of earth swooning away and falling to the ground, the inmates of the inner apartment raising their burst into lamentations. arms of an

sanskrit: सुमित्रया तु सहिता कौसल्या पतितम् पतिम्
उत्थापयाम् आस तदा वचनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sumitrayā tu sahitā kausalyā patitam patim
utthāpayām āsa tadā vacanam ca idam abravīt
english: Kausalyā availing herself of the aid of Sumantra, raised up her fallen lord and addressed him, saying.

sanskrit: इमम् तस्य महा भाग दूतम् दुष्कर कारिणः
वन वासात् अनुप्राप्तम् कस्मान् न प्रतिभाषसे
transliteration: imam tasya mahā bhāga dūtam duṣkara kāriṇaḥ
vana vāsāt anuprāptam kasmān na pratibhāṣase
english: This, O eminently virtuous one, is the envoy of that one an exceedingly arduous achievement returned from the forest. Why do you not accost him?

sanskrit: अद्य इमम् अनयम् कृत्वा व्यपत्रपसि राघव
उत्तिष्ठ सुकृतम् ते अस्तु शोके न स्यात् सहायता
transliteration: adya imam anayam kṛtvā vyapatrapasi rāghava
uttiṣṭha sukṛtam te astu śoke na syāt sahāyatā
english: O descendant of Raghu, you are ashamed today, having done this wrong. Do you rise: merit be yours (arising from this act.) Let not your adherents come to naught (because of your sorrow).

sanskrit: देव यस्या भयात् रामम् न अनुपृच्चसि सारथिम्
न इह तिष्ठति कैकेयी विश्रब्धम् प्रतिभाष्यताम्
transliteration: deva yasyā bhayāt rāmam na anupṛccasi sārathim
na iha tiṣṭhati kaikeyī viśrabdham pratibhāṣyatām
english: O worshipful one, she from fear of whom you do not speak to the charioteer, Kaikeyi, is not here. Do you therefore speak to him without fear.

sanskrit: सा तथा उक्त्वा महा राजम् कौसल्या शोक लालसा
धरण्याम् निपपात आशु बाष्प विप्लुत भाषिणी
transliteration: sā tathā uktvā mahā rājam kausalyā śoka lālasā
dharaṇyām nipapāta āśu bāṣpa vipluta bhāṣiṇī
english: Having said this to the monarch, Kausalyā overwhelmed with grief, with her voice oppressed with the vapour begot of emotion, all on a sudden fell to the earth.

sanskrit: एवम् विलपतीम् दृष्ट्वा कौसल्याम् पतिताम् भुवि
पतिम् च अवेक्ष्य ताः सर्वाः सुस्वरम् रुरुदुः स्त्रियः
transliteration: evam vilapatīm dṛṣṭvā kausalyām patitām bhuvi
patim ca avekṣya tāḥ sarvāḥ susvaram ruruduḥ striyaḥ
english: Behoiding Kausalyā fallen on the ground bewailing, as also their husband, the ladies seated around, began to Lament,

sanskrit: ततः तम् अन्तः पुर नादम् उत्थितम्
पुरम् तदा आसीत् पुनर् एव सम्कुलम्
transliteration: tataḥ tam antaḥ pura nādam utthitam
puram tadā āsīt punar eva samkulam
english: Hearing the sounds of wailing arise from the inner apartment, old and young as well as females, set up lamentations all round; and the city was again filled with them.

sanskrit: प्रत्याश्वस्तः यदा राजा मोहात् प्रत्यागतः पुनः
थाजुहाव तम् सूतम् राम वृत्त अन्त कारणात्
transliteration: pratyāśvastaḥ yadā rājā mohāt pratyāgataḥ punaḥ
thājuhāva tam sūtam rāma vṛtta anta kāraṇāt
english: When having been ministered to and when his senses has returned after the swoon, the king summoned Sumantra for hearing tidings of Rama.

sanskrit: वृद्धम् परम सम्तप्तम् नव ग्रहम् इव द्विपम्
transliteration: vṛddham parama samtaptam nava graham iva dvipam

sanskrit: राजा तु रजसा सूतम् ध्वस्त अङ्गम् समुपस्थितम्
अश्रु पूर्ण मुखम् दीनम् उवाच परम आर्तवत्
transliteration: rājā tu rajasā sūtam dhvasta aṅgam samupasthitam
aśru pūrṇa mukham dīnam uvāca parama ārtavat

sanskrit: क्व नु वत्स्यति धर्म आत्मा वृक्ष मूलम् उपाश्रितः
सो अत्यन्त सुखितः सूत किम् अशिष्यति राघवः
transliteration: kva nu vatsyati dharma ātmā vṛkṣa mūlam upāśritaḥ
so atyanta sukhitaḥ sūta kim aśiṣyati rāghavaḥ
english: Where stays that righteous one, taking refuge under a tree? lapped in luxury, what, O charioteer, will Rāghava feed on?

sanskrit: भूमि पाल आत्मजो भूमौ शेते कथम् अनाथवत्
transliteration: bhūmi pāla ātmajo bhūmau śete katham anāthavat
english: Unworthy of privations, and worthy of excellent beds, how, O Sumantra, a king's son, he is sleeping on the ground like one forlorn?

sanskrit: यम् यान्तम् अनुयान्ति स्म पदाति रथ कुण्Jजराः
स वत्स्यति कथम् रामः विजनम् वनम् आश्रितः
transliteration: yam yāntam anuyānti sma padāti ratha kuṇjarāḥ
sa vatsyati katham rāmaḥ vijanam vanam āśritaḥ
english: How is Rāma passing his days in the lone forest, he who when he went out used to be followed by foot-men and elephants?

sanskrit: व्याLऐः मृगैः आचरितम् कृष्ण सर्प निषेवितम्
कथम् कुमारौ वैदेह्या सार्धम् वनम् उपस्थितौ
transliteration: vyāaiḥ mṛgaiḥ ācaritam kṛṣṇa sarpa niṣevitam
katham kumārau vaidehyā sārdham vanam upasthitau
english: How are the princes in company with Vaidehi living in the woods, ranged by serpents and beasts and inhabited by black snakes?

sanskrit: राज पुत्रौ कथम् पादैः अवरुह्य रथात् गतौ
transliteration: rāja putrau katham pādaiḥ avaruhya rathāt gatau
english: How, O Sumantra, having descended from the car, the princes along with the tender and unfortunate Sītā are proceeding on foot?

sanskrit: सिद्ध अर्थः खलु सूत त्वम् येन दृष्टौ मम आत्मजौ
वन अन्तम् प्रविशन्तौ ताव् अश्विनाव् इव मन्दरम्
transliteration: siddha arthaḥ khalu sūta tvam yena dṛṣṭau mama ātmajau
vana antam praviśantau tāv aśvināv iva mandaram
english: O charioteer, surely you are blessed, for you have beheld my sons enter the forest, like the Asvins entering the Mandāra hill.

sanskrit: किम् उवाच वचो रामः किम् उवाच च लक्ष्मणः
सुमन्त्र वनम् आसाद्य किम् उवाच च मैथिली
transliteration: kim uvāca vaco rāmaḥ kim uvāca ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
sumantra vanam āsādya kim uvāca ca maithilī
english: And what did Rāma say? And what did Laks mana? And, O Sumantra, arriving at the forest what did Mithila's daughter?

sanskrit: आसितम् शयितम् भुक्तम् सूत रामस्य कीर्तय
transliteration: āsitam śayitam bhuktam sūta rāmasya kīrtaya
english: Do you, O charioteer, describe to me what Rāma lives on and where he lies down. Hearing this, I shall live, like Yayati in the midst of saints.

sanskrit: इति सूतः नर इन्द्रेण चोदितः सज्जमानया
उवाच वाचा राजानम् स बाष्प परिर्बद्धया
transliteration: iti sūtaḥ nara indreṇa coditaḥ sajjamānayā
uvāca vācā rājānam sa bāṣpa parirbaddhayā
english: Thus urged by the king, the charioteer spoke to the king with his voice faltering and suppressed with the vapour of grief.

sanskrit: अब्रवीन् माम् महा राज धर्मम् एव अनुपालयन्
अन्जलिम् राघवः कृत्वा शिरसा अभिप्रणम्य च
transliteration: abravīn mām mahā rāja dharmam eva anupālayan
anjalim rāghavaḥ kṛtvā śirasā abhipraṇamya ca

sanskrit: सूत मद्वचनात् तस्य तातस्य विदित आत्मनः
transliteration: sūta madvacanāt tasya tātasya vidita ātmanaḥ

sanskrit: सर्वम् अन्तः पुरम् वाच्यम् सूत मद्वचनात्त्वया
आरोग्यम् अविशेषेण यथा अर्हम् च अभिवादनम्
transliteration: sarvam antaḥ puram vācyam sūta madvacanāttvayā
ārogyam aviśeṣeṇa yathā arham ca abhivādanam

sanskrit: माता च मम कौसल्या कुशलम् च अभिवादनम्
transliteration: mātā ca mama kausalyā kuśalam ca abhivādanam
english: Having saluted my mother Kausalyā and conveyed to her news of my welfare, as well as of my unswerving adherence to morality, do you tell her these words, Do you remaining steady in virtue, at the proper hour bestir yourself in behalf of the chamber of sacrificial fire. And, O revered one, do you minister to the feet of that worshipful one, (the king), as if they were very deities.

sanskrit: देवि देवस्य पादौ च देववत् परिपालय
transliteration: devi devasya pādau ca devavat paripālaya
english: Having saluted my mother Kausalyā and conveyed to her news of my welfare, as well as of my unswerving adherence to morality, do you tell her these words, Do you remaining steady in virtue, at the proper hour bestir yourself in behalf of the chamber of sacrificial fire. And, O revered one, do you minister to the feet of that worshipful one, (the king), as if they were very deities.

sanskrit: अभिमानम् च मानम् च त्यक्त्वा वर्तस्व मातृषु
अनु राजान मार्याम् च कैकेयीमम्ब कारय
transliteration: abhimānam ca mānam ca tyaktvā vartasva mātṛṣu
anu rājāna māryām ca kaikeyīmamba kāraya
english: Banishing pride and self-love, do you bear yourself towards my mothers. And, O mother, do you show respect to Kaikeyi, who is followed by the king himself.
You should behave towards Bharata as one should towards one's king. Kings (although juveline), are really senior by virtue of their royalty; and do you remember the duties touching sovereigns.

sanskrit: भरतः कुशलम् वाच्यो वाच्यो मद् वचनेन च
सर्वास्व एव यथा न्यायम् वृत्तिम् वर्तस्व मातृषु
transliteration: bharataḥ kuśalam vācyo vācyo mad vacanena ca
sarvāsva eva yathā nyāyam vṛttim vartasva mātṛṣu
english: Do you communicate to Bharata news of my welfare and say in my name, Do you behave properly with all your mothers.

sanskrit: वक्तव्यः च महा बाहुर् इक्ष्वाकु कुल नन्दनः
transliteration: vaktavyaḥ ca mahā bāhur ikṣvāku kula nandanaḥ
english: And to that delight of the Ikṣvāku line do you further say, Having been installed as the heirapparent, be you, looking upon the king as the supreme authority in the state, obedient to him.
Do you not deprive the king of authority, as he has grown old. O Prince, do you grant him satisfaction in the kingdom and do you proclaim his mandates.

sanskrit: मातेव मम माता ते द्रष्टव्या पुत्रगर्धिनी
transliteration: māteva mama mātā te draṣṭavyā putragardhinī
english: And shedding copious tears, he again addressed me, saying, Do you look upon my mother as on your own proud of her son. Having said this, the mighty-armed and illustrious Rāma furnished with eyes resembling lotus-petals, shed plenteous tears.

sanskrit: इति एवम् माम् महाराज बृवन्न् एव महा यशाः
रामः राजीव ताम्र अक्षो भृशम् अश्रूणि अवर्तयत्
transliteration: iti evam mām mahārāja bṛvann eva mahā yaśāḥ
rāmaḥ rājīva tāmra akṣo bhṛśam aśrūṇi avartayat

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणः तु सुसम्क्रुद्धो निह्श्वसन् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
केन अयम् अपराधेन राज पुत्रः विवासितः
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaḥ tu susamkruddho nihśvasan vākyam abravīt
kena ayam aparādhena rāja putraḥ vivāsitaḥ
english: Thereupon Lakşmaņa waxing wroth, breathing hard, said, For what fault of his has the Prince been banished?

sanskrit: राज्ञा तु खलु कैकेय्या लघु त्वाश्रित्य शासनम्
transliteration: rājñā tu khalu kaikeyyā laghu tvāśritya śāsanam
english: Observing the worthless command of Kaikeyſ, whether the king has done well or ill, we have been exceedingly pained thereby.

sanskrit: यदि प्रव्राजितः रामः लोभ कारण कारितम्
वर दान निमित्तम् वा सर्वथा दुष्कृतम् कृतम्
transliteration: yadi pravrājitaḥ rāmaḥ lobha kāraṇa kāritam
vara dāna nimittam vā sarvathā duṣkṛtam kṛtam
english: Whether Rāma has been exiled through Kaikeyi's lust for dominion or through the exigencies of the bestowal of the boon, there cannot be any doubt that the king has acted most unrighteously.

sanskrit: रामस्य तु परित्यागे न हेतुम् उपलक्षये
transliteration: rāmasya tu parityāge na hetum upalakṣaye
english: Even if this has been done in harmony with the wish of the Lord, I do not perceive any reason for the banishment of Rāma.
The king through lack of sense has done herulessly what is opposed to morality; and this banishment of Rāma will but bring upon him woe here and hereafter.

sanskrit: अहम् तावन् महा राजे पितृत्वम् न उपलक्षये
भ्राता भर्ता च बन्धुः च पिता च मम राघवः
transliteration: aham tāvan mahā rāje pitṛtvam na upalakṣaye
bhrātā bhartā ca bandhuḥ ca pitā ca mama rāghavaḥ
english: Fatherhood find I none in the monarch. My brother and feeder and friend and father is even Rāghava.

sanskrit: सर्व लोक प्रियम् त्यक्त्वा सर्व लोक हिते रतम्
सर्व लोको अनुरज्येत कथम् त्वा अनेन कर्मणा
transliteration: sarva loka priyam tyaktvā sarva loka hite ratam
sarva loko anurajyeta katham tvā anena karmaṇā
english: Renouncing one that is universally dear, and that is ever engaged in the good of all, how by such an act will the king please the people?
How by banishing the righteous Rāma dear to all the subjects, and thus withstanding the wishes of all, will he retain his royalty?

sanskrit: जानकी तु महा राज निःश्वसन्ती तपस्विनी
भूत उपहत चित्ता इव विष्ठिता वृष्मृता स्थिता
transliteration: jānakī tu mahā rāja niḥśvasantī tapasvinī
bhūta upahata cittā iva viṣṭhitā vṛṣmṛtā sthitā
english: O mighty monarch, Janaki also, unfortunate that she is, sighing heavily, stood wildered like one that had been possessed.

sanskrit: अदृष्ट पूर्व व्यसना राज पुत्री यशस्विनी
तेन दुह्खेन रुदती न एव माम् किम्चित् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: adṛṣṭa pūrva vyasanā rāja putrī yaśasvinī
tena duhkhena rudatī na eva mām kimcit abravīt
english: And not having experienced any calamity before, the famed princes weeping because of this misfortune, told me nothing.

sanskrit: मुमोच सहसा बाष्पम् माम् प्रयान्तम् उदीक्ष्य सा
transliteration: mumoca sahasā bāṣpam mām prayāntam udīkṣya sā
english: Looking up to her lord with a blank countenance, she suddenly let fall tears, perceiving the destruction of the subject.

sanskrit: तथैव रामः अश्रु मुखः कृत अन्जलिः
स्थितः अभवल् लक्ष्मण बाहु पालितः स्थितः
transliteration: tathaiva rāmaḥ aśru mukhaḥ kṛta anjaliḥ
sthitaḥ abhaval lakṣmaṇa bāhu pālitaḥ sthitaḥ
english: Thus said Rāma ministered to by Lakşmaņa, with a tearful countenance; and thus stood the unfortunate and weeping Sītå beholding the royal car and myself.

sanskrit: मम तु अश्वा निवृत्तस्य न प्रावर्तन्त वर्त्मनि
उष्णम् अश्रु विमुन्चन्तः रामे सम्प्रस्थिते वनम्
transliteration: mama tu aśvā nivṛttasya na prāvartanta vartmani
uṣṇam aśru vimuncantaḥ rāme samprasthite vanam
english: On Rāma having gone to the forest, my horses as I turned away, did not proceed vigorously on the way, and shed warm tears. And having (done homage) to both the princes by joining my hands, I turned my back, bearing as best I could that load of sorrow.

sanskrit: उभाभ्याम् राज पुत्राभ्याम् अथ कृत्वा अहम् ज्ञलिम्
प्रस्थितः रथम् आस्थाय तत् दुह्खम् अपि धारयन्
transliteration: ubhābhyām rāja putrābhyām atha kṛtvā aham jñalim
prasthitaḥ ratham āsthāya tat duhkham api dhārayan
english: On Rāma having gone to the forest, my horses as I turned away, did not proceed vigorously on the way, and shed warm tears. And having (done homage) to both the princes by joining my hands, I turned my back, bearing as best I could that load of sorrow.

sanskrit: गुहा इव सार्धम् तत्र एव स्थितः अस्मि दिवसान् बहून्
आशया यदि माम् रामः पुनः शब्दापयेद् इति
transliteration: guhā iva sārdham tatra eva sthitaḥ asmi divasān bahūn
āśayā yadi mām rāmaḥ punaḥ śabdāpayed iti
english: Indulging in the hope that Rāma might again summon me by any of the envoys (of Guha left there), I stayed there with Guha for many days.

sanskrit: विषये ते महा राज माम व्यसन कर्शिताः
अपि वृक्षाः परिम्लानः सपुष्प अन्कुर कोरकाः
transliteration: viṣaye te mahā rāja māma vyasana karśitāḥ
api vṛkṣāḥ parimlānaḥ sapuṣpa ankura korakāḥ
english: In your dominions, O monarch, exercised by the calamity that has befallen Rāma, even trees bearing blossoms and buds and sprouts look sad; the rivers and pools and liquid lapses have their waters dried up; and the woods and groves have their foliage withered.

In your dominions, O monarch, exercised by the calamity that has befallen Rāma, even trees bearing blossoms and buds and sprouts look sad; the rivers and pools and liquid lapses have their waters dried up; and the woods and groves have their foliage withered.

sanskrit: न च सर्पन्ति सत्त्वानि व्याला न प्रसरन्ति च
राम शोक अभिभूतम् तन् निष्कूजम् अभवद् वनम्
transliteration: na ca sarpanti sattvāni vyālā na prasaranti ca
rāma śoka abhibhūtam tan niṣkūjam abhavad vanam
english: Creatures do not move and beasts of prey cease to range about; and the forest appears to be dumb, stupefied by grief on account of Rāma.

sanskrit: लीन पुष्कर पत्राः च नर इन्द्र कलुष उदकाः
सम्तप्त पद्माः पद्मिन्यो लीन मीन विहम्गमाः
transliteration: līna puṣkara patrāḥ ca nara indra kaluṣa udakāḥ
samtapta padmāḥ padminyo līna mīna vihamgamāḥ
english: Streams containing lotuses with their leaves shrivelled, have their waters stained; and lotuses have their leaves burnt; and fished and (aquatic) birds have grown lean. And flowers both on land and water have been deprived of their freshness and fragrance; and they no longer retain their former condition.

sanskrit: जलजानि च पुष्पाणि माल्यानि स्थलजानि च
न अद्य भान्ति अल्प गन्धीनि फलानि च यथा पुरम्
transliteration: jalajāni ca puṣpāṇi mālyāni sthalajāni ca
na adya bhānti alpa gandhīni phalāni ca yathā puram
english: Streams containing lotuses with their leaves shrivelled, have their waters stained; and lotuses have their leaves burnt; and fished and (aquatic) birds have grown lean. And flowers both on land and water have been deprived of their freshness and fragrance; and they no longer retain their former condition.
The gardens are idle with their birds drooping. And, O best of men, I do not find the bowers beautiful (as before).

sanskrit: प्रविशन्तम् अयोध्याम् माम् न कश्चित् अभिनन्दति
नरा रामम् अपश्यन्तः निह्श्वसन्ति मुहुर् मुहुः
transliteration: praviśantam ayodhyām mām na kaścit abhinandati
narā rāmam apaśyantaḥ nihśvasanti muhur muhuḥ
english: When I entered Ayodhyā, none greeted me. And not seeing Rāma, the people sigh momentarily.
And, O revered one, seeing the royal car returned hither without Rāma, the people on the highways from grief appear with tearful countenance.

sanskrit: हर्म्यैः विमानैः प्रासादैः अवेक्ष्य रथम् आगतम्
हाहा कार कृता नार्यो राम अदर्शन कर्शिताः
transliteration: harmyaiḥ vimānaiḥ prāsādaiḥ avekṣya ratham āgatam
hāhā kāra kṛtā nāryo rāma adarśana karśitāḥ
english: And from mansions, cars, and lordly edifices, ladies seeing the car come back, set up a chorus of 'Ah' and 'Alas,' afflicted with the absence of Rama.

sanskrit: आयतैः विमलैः नेत्रैः अश्रु वेग परिप्लुतैः
transliteration: āyataiḥ vimalaiḥ netraiḥ aśru vega pariplutaiḥ
english: And becoming more distressed that ever, the fair sex with their expansive and clear eyes filled with tears, began to eye each other indistinctly.

sanskrit: न अमित्राणाम् न मित्राणाम् उदासीन जनस्य च
अहम् आर्ततया कम्चित् विशेषम् न उपलक्षये
transliteration: na amitrāṇām na mitrāṇām udāsīna janasya ca
aham ārtatayā kamcit viśeṣam na upalakṣaye
english: And in consequence of the general grief that prevailed, I could not perceive any difference between friends and foes and persons indifferent.

sanskrit: अप्रहृष्ट मनुष्या च दीन नाग तुरम्गमा
transliteration: aprahṛṣṭa manuṣyā ca dīna nāga turamgamā
english: O mighty monarch, distressed in consequence of the exile of Rāma, men appear sunk in dejection, and elephants and horses are spiritless; and seized with cheerlessness, they utter doleful sounds and heave profound sighs. Ayodhyā appears to me joyless like Kausalyă deprived of her son.

sanskrit: निरानन्दा महा राज राम प्रव्राजन आतुला
कौसल्या पुत्र हीना इवायोध्या प्रतिभाति मा मा
transliteration: nirānandā mahā rāja rāma pravrājana ātulā
kausalyā putra hīnā ivāyodhyā pratibhāti mā mā
english: O mighty monarch, distressed in consequence of the exile of Rāma, men appear sunk in dejection, and elephants and horses are spiritless; and seized with cheerlessness, they utter doleful sounds and heave profound sighs. Ayodhyā appears to me joyless like Kausalyă deprived of her son.

sanskrit: सूतस्य वचनम् श्रुत्वा वाचा परम दीनया
बाष्प उपहतया राजा तम् सूतम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sūtasya vacanam śrutvā vācā parama dīnayā
bāṣpa upahatayā rājā tam sūtam idam abravīt
english: Hearing the words of the charioteer, the king like an exceedingly forlorn, addressed the former in words lost in the vapour of sorrow.

sanskrit: मया न मन्त्र कुशलैः वृद्धैः सह समर्थितम्
transliteration: mayā na mantra kuśalaiḥ vṛddhaiḥ saha samarthitam
english: Exhorted by Kaikeyi of a sinful country, born in a sinful race and cherishing sinful designs, I did not take counsel with aged people capable of offering advice.

sanskrit: न सुहृद्भिर् न च अमात्यैः मन्त्रयित्वा न नैगमैः
मया अयम् अर्थः सम्मोहात् स्त्री हेतोह् सहसा कृतः
transliteration: na suhṛdbhir na ca amātyaiḥ mantrayitvā na naigamaiḥ
mayā ayam arthaḥ sammohāt strī hetoh sahasā kṛtaḥ
english: Without consulting with friends or courtiers or persons versed in the Vedas, I have in the interest of a woman rashly done this thing through ignorance.

sanskrit: भवितव्यतया नूनम् इदम् वा व्यसनम् महत्
कुलस्य अस्य विनाशाय प्राप्तम् सूत यदृच्चया
transliteration: bhavitavyatayā nūnam idam vā vyasanam mahat
kulasya asya vināśāya prāptam sūta yadṛccayā
english: Meseems, O charioteer, for the purpose of destroying this line entirely, this mighty disaster has surely befallen us through the influence of Destiny.

sanskrit: सूत यद्य् अस्ति ते किम्चिन् मया अपि सुकृतम् कृतम्
त्वम् प्रापय आशु माम् रामम् प्राणाः सम्त्वरयन्ति माम्
transliteration: sūta yady asti te kimcin mayā api sukṛtam kṛtam
tvam prāpaya āśu mām rāmam prāṇāḥ samtvarayanti mām
english: O charioteer, if I have ever done you any good do you immediately take me to Rāma: my life urges me on (in this direction).

sanskrit: यद् यद् या अपि मम एव आज्ञा निवर्तयतु राघवम्
न शक्ष्यामि विना राम मुहूर्तम् अपि जीवितुम्
transliteration: yad yad yā api mama eva ājñā nivartayatu rāghavam
na śakṣyāmi vinā rāma muhūrtam api jīvitum
english: Or let my command make Rāghava turn back. I cannot live for a moment without Rāma.

sanskrit: अथवा अपि महा बाहुर् गतः दूरम् भविष्यति
माम् एव रथम् आरोप्य शीघ्रम् रामाय दर्शय
transliteration: athavā api mahā bāhur gataḥ dūram bhaviṣyati
mām eva ratham āropya śīghram rāmāya darśaya
english: But if that mighty-armed one has proceeded far, do you placing me on a car speedily show me to Rāma.

sanskrit: वृत्त दम्ष्ट्रः महा इष्वासः क्व असौ लक्ष्मण पूर्वजः
यदि जीवामि साध्व् एनम् पश्येयम् सह सीतया
transliteration: vṛtta damṣṭraḥ mahā iṣvāsaḥ kva asau lakṣmaṇa pūrvajaḥ
yadi jīvāmi sādhv enam paśyeyam saha sītayā
english: Where is that elder brother of Lakşmaņa of a mighty bow, furnished with teeth resembling Kunda flowers? If I live so long, I will behold him in company with Sītā.

sanskrit: लोहित अक्षम् महा बाहुम् आमुक्त मणि कुण्डलम्
रामम् यदि न पश्यामि गमिष्यामि यम क्षयम्
transliteration: lohita akṣam mahā bāhum āmukta maṇi kuṇḍalam
rāmam yadi na paśyāmi gamiṣyāmi yama kṣayam
english: What can be sadder than this, that reduced to such a pass, I cannot see here that descendant of Ikşvāku, Rāghava?

sanskrit: अतः नु किम् दुह्खतरम् यो अहम् इक्ष्वाकु नन्दनम्
इमाम् अवस्थाम् आपन्नो न इह पश्यामि राघवम्
transliteration: ataḥ nu kim duhkhataram yo aham ikṣvāku nandanam
imām avasthām āpanno na iha paśyāmi rāghavam
english: What can be sadder than this, that reduced to such a pass, I cannot see here that descendant of Ikşvāku, Rāghava?

sanskrit: हा राम राम अनुज हा हा वैदेहि तपस्विनी
न माम् जानीत दुह्खेन म्रियमाणम् अनाथवत्
transliteration: hā rāma rāma anuja hā hā vaidehi tapasvinī
na mām jānīta duhkhena mriyamāṇam anāthavat
english: Ah Rāma! Ah you younger brother of Rāma! Ah you unfortunate Vaidehī! You do not know that I am through grief lamenting like one deserted.
Deprived of his consciousness through that sorrow of his, the king said.

sanskrit: यस्मिन् बत निमग्नोऽहम् कौसल्ये राघवम् विना
दुस्तरः जीवता देवि मया अयम् शोक सागरः
transliteration: yasmin bata nimagno'ham kausalye rāghavam vinā
dustaraḥ jīvatā devi mayā ayam śoka sāgaraḥ

sanskrit: अशोभनम् यो अहम् इह अद्य राघवम्
दिदृक्षमाणो न लभे सलक्ष्मणम्इति इव राजा विलपन् महा यहाशःपपात तूर्णम् शयने स मूर्चितः
transliteration: aśobhanam yo aham iha adya rāghavam
didṛkṣamāṇo na labhe salakṣmaṇamiti iva rājā vilapan mahā yahāśaḥpapāta tūrṇam śayane sa mūrcitaḥ

sanskrit: भयम् अगमत् पुनर् एव राम माता
transliteration: bhayam agamat punar eva rāma mātā

sanskrit: ततः भूत उपसृष्टा इव वेपमाना पुनः पुनः
धरण्याम् गत सत्त्वा इव कौसल्या सूतम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tataḥ bhūta upasṛṣṭā iva vepamānā punaḥ punaḥ
dharaṇyām gata sattvā iva kausalyā sūtam abravīt
english: Then like one possessed by an evil spirit, and trembling again and again, Kausalyä lying down on the ground like one dead, spoke to the charioteer, saying.

sanskrit: नय माम् यत्र काकुत्स्थः सीता यत्र च लक्ष्मणः
तान् विना क्षणम् अपि अत्र जीवितुम् न उत्सहे हि अहम्
transliteration: naya mām yatra kākutsthaḥ sītā yatra ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
tān vinā kṣaṇam api atra jīvitum na utsahe hi aham
english: Do you take me where Kākutstha is and Sītā and Lakşınaņa: without them, I cannot live for a moment.

sanskrit: निवर्तय रथम् शीघ्रम् दण्डकान् नय माम् अपि
अथ तान् न अनुगच्चामि गमिष्यामि यम क्षयम्
transliteration: nivartaya ratham śīghram daṇḍakān naya mām api
atha tān na anugaccāmi gamiṣyāmi yama kṣayam
english: Do you without delay turn the car. Do you take me also to Dandaka. If I do not follow them, I shall repair to the mansion of Yama.

sanskrit: इदम् आश्वासयन् देवीम् सूतः प्रान्जलिर् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: idam āśvāsayan devīm sūtaḥ prānjalir abravīt
english: Thereat the cahrioteer with joined hands comforted that exalted lady with ready words faltering and choked with rising vapour, "Do you leave grief and sorrow and the violent emotion. Renouncing grief, Rāghava is living in the woods."

sanskrit: त्यज शोकम् च मोहम् च सम्भ्रमम् दुह्खजम् तथा
व्यवधूय च सम्तापम् वने वत्स्यति राघवः
transliteration: tyaja śokam ca moham ca sambhramam duhkhajam tathā
vyavadhūya ca samtāpam vane vatsyati rāghavaḥ
english: Thereat the cahrioteer with joined hands comforted that exalted lady with ready words faltering and choked with rising vapour, "Do you leave grief and sorrow and the violent emotion. Renouncing grief, Rāghava is living in the woods."

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणः च अपि रामस्य पादौ परिचरन् वने
आराधयति धर्मज्ञः पर लोकम् जित इन्द्रियः
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaḥ ca api rāmasya pādau paricaran vane
ārādhayati dharmajñaḥ para lokam jita indriyaḥ
english: And in the forest, the righteous Laksmara, having his senses under control, is ministering to Răma's feet and is thus adoring the gods for happiness in the next world.

sanskrit: विजने अपि वने सीता वासम् प्राप्य गृहेष्व् इव
विस्रम्भम् लभते अभीता रामे सम्न्यस्त मानसा
transliteration: vijane api vane sītā vāsam prāpya gṛheṣv iva
visrambham labhate abhītā rāme samnyasta mānasā
english: And even in the lonely woods, Sītā as if remaining at home, having fixed her thoughts on Rāma, is living a life of love.

sanskrit: न अस्या दैन्यम् कृतम् किम्चित् सुसूक्ष्मम् अपि लक्षये
उचिता इव प्रवासानाम् वैदेही प्रतिभाति मा
transliteration: na asyā dainyam kṛtam kimcit susūkṣmam api lakṣaye
ucitā iva pravāsānām vaidehī pratibhāti mā
english: And there appears not the least trace of any distress afflicting her; and Vaidehi seems to me as if she were meant (by Nature) for a life away from home.

sanskrit: नगर उपवनम् गत्वा यथा स्म रमते पुरा
तथैव रमते सीता निर्जनेषु वनेष्व् अपि
transliteration: nagara upavanam gatvā yathā sma ramate purā
tathaiva ramate sītā nirjaneṣu vaneṣv api
english: And as forinerly going to urban villas she disported, she disports now even in the lonely forest.

sanskrit: बाला इव रमते सीता बाल चन्द्र निभ आनना
रामा रामे हि अदीन आत्मा विजने अपि वने सती
transliteration: bālā iva ramate sītā bāla candra nibha ānanā
rāmā rāme hi adīna ātmā vijane api vane satī
english: And although living in the lone forest, that one of a countenance resembling the infant moon, sports merrily like a girl, in the garden represented by Rāma's self.

sanskrit: तत् गतम् हृदयम् हि अस्याः तत् अधीनम् च जीवितम्
अयोध्या अपि भवेत् तस्या राम हीना तथा वनम्
transliteration: tat gatam hṛdayam hi asyāḥ tat adhīnam ca jīvitam
ayodhyā api bhavet tasyā rāma hīnā tathā vanam
english: Ayodhyā without Rāma would have seemed a wilderness to her whose heart is fixed on him and whose very life depends upon him.

sanskrit: परि पृच्चति वैदेही ग्रामामः च नगराणि च
गतिम् दृष्ट्वा नदीनाम् च पादपान् विविधान् अपि
transliteration: pari pṛccati vaidehī grāmāmaḥ ca nagarāṇi ca
gatim dṛṣṭvā nadīnām ca pādapān vividhān api
english: Vaidehī is now asking (Rāma) concerning the villages and towns (in their way); and observing various trees and the courses of the rivers, Jānaki, asking Råma Laksmana (for information), is learning all about them. And Sītā sports as she used to do in arbours stationed at the distance of only one krosa from Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: रामम् हि लक्ष्मनम् वापि पृष्ट्वा जानाति जानती
transliteration: rāmam hi lakṣmanam vāpi pṛṣṭvā jānāti jānatī
english: Vaidehī is now asking (Rāma) concerning the villages and towns (in their way); and observing various trees and the courses of the rivers, Jānaki, asking Råma Laksmana (for information), is learning all about them. And Sītā sports as she used to do in arbours stationed at the distance of only one krosa from Ayodhyā.
This only I remember; but all that she had from sudden impulse communicated to me or concerning Kaikeyſ, does not rise into consciousness.
Suppressing this topic which had come up through heedlessness, the charioteer spoke sweet words cheering up that noble lady.

sanskrit: अध्वना वात वेगेन सम्भ्रमेण आतपेन च
न हि गच्चति वैदेह्याः चन्द्र अम्शु सदृशी प्रभा
transliteration: adhvanā vāta vegena sambhrameṇa ātapena ca
na hi gaccati vaidehyāḥ candra amśu sadṛśī prabhā
english: Neither through the fatigue of travel, nor the influence of the wind, nor excitement, nor the sun, has Vaidehi's lustre resembling the lunar light suffered any diminution.

sanskrit: सदृशम् शत पत्रस्य पूर्ण चन्द्र उपम प्रभम्
वदनम् तत् वदान्याया वैदेह्या न विकम्पते
transliteration: sadṛśam śata patrasya pūrṇa candra upama prabham
vadanam tat vadānyāyā vaidehyā na vikampate
english: The countenance of that fair-speaking one resembling the lotus and comparable to the full moon in splendour, has not waxed pale.

sanskrit: अलक्त रस रक्त अभाव् अलक्त रस वर्जितौ
अद्य अपि चरणौ तस्याः पद्म कोश सम प्रभौ
transliteration: alakta rasa rakta abhāv alakta rasa varjitau
adya api caraṇau tasyāḥ padma kośa sama prabhau
english: Her feet now without your dye of the liquid lac, but naturally furnished with the roseate hue of the same, are gorgeous like lotus buds.

sanskrit: नूपुर उद्घुष्ट हेला इव खेलम् गच्चति भामिनी
इदानीम् अपि वैदेही तत् रागा न्यस्त भूषणा
transliteration: nūpura udghuṣṭa helā iva khelam gaccati bhāminī
idānīm api vaidehī tat rāgā nyasta bhūṣaṇā
english: Still Vaidehī decked in ornaments from affection for Rāma, goes gracefully rebuking with her bangles the wavy gait (of cranes).

sanskrit: गजम् वा वीक्ष्य सिम्हम् वा व्याघ्रम् वा वनम् आश्रिता
न आहारयति सम्त्रासम् बाहू रामस्य सम्श्रिता
transliteration: gajam vā vīkṣya simham vā vyāghram vā vanam āśritā
na āhārayati samtrāsam bāhū rāmasya samśritā
english: Supporting herself on Rāma's arm, Sītă arrived at the forest, is not inspired with fear on beholding either an elephant, or a lion, or a tiger.

sanskrit: न शोच्याः ते न च आत्मा ते शोच्यो न अपि जन अधिपः
इदम् हि चरितम् लोके प्रतिष्ठास्यति शाश्वतम्
transliteration: na śocyāḥ te na ca ātmā te śocyo na api jana adhipaḥ
idam hi caritam loke pratiṣṭhāsyati śāśvatam
english: Therefore they are not to be bewailed, nor your own self, nor the lord of men. This history of Rāma will endure for ever in this world.

sanskrit: वने रता वन्य फल अशनाः पितुः
transliteration: vane ratā vanya phala aśanāḥ pituḥ
english: Renouncing grief and with cheerful hearts, well established in the life led by the Maharşis, they living in the forest on wild fruits as their sustenance, are maintaining the noble promise of their sire.

sanskrit: प्रिय इति पुत्र इति च राघव इति च
transliteration: priya iti putra iti ca rāghava iti ca
english: Consoled by the truth-telling yet sweetspeeched charioteer, that lady oppressed with grief for her son, ceased not to wail loudly, "My beloved,” “My son," "Rāghava."

sanskrit: वनम् गते धर्म परे रामे रमयताम् वरे
कौसल्या रुदती स्वार्ता भर्तारम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: vanam gate dharma pare rāme ramayatām vare
kausalyā rudatī svārtā bhartāram idam abravīt
english: On that foremost of those capable of charming people, the righteous Rāma, repairing to the forest, Kausalyā crying in grief said to her husband.

sanskrit: यद्यपि त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रथितम् ते मयद् यशः
सानुक्रोशो वदान्यः च प्रिय वादी च राघवः
transliteration: yadyapi triṣu lokeṣu prathitam te mayad yaśaḥ
sānukrośo vadānyaḥ ca priya vādī ca rāghavaḥ
english: Your great fame has spread over the three worlds; and the descendant of Raghu is kind, munificent and fair-speaking.

sanskrit: कथम् नर वर श्रेष्ठ पुत्रौ तौ सह सीतया
दुह्खितौ सुख सम्वृद्धौ वने दुह्खम् सहिष्यतः
transliteration: katham nara vara śreṣṭha putrau tau saha sītayā
duhkhitau sukha samvṛddhau vane duhkham sahiṣyataḥ
english: Why then have you forsaken those foremost of men along with Sītā? Brought up in happiness, and now brought to misery, how can they bear it?

sanskrit: सा नूनम् तरुणी श्यामा सुकुमारी सुख उचिता
कथम् उष्णम् च शीतम् च मैथिली प्रसहिष्यते
transliteration: sā nūnam taruṇī śyāmā sukumārī sukha ucitā
katham uṣṇam ca śītam ca maithilī prasahiṣyate
english: How can the youthful daughter of Mithilā of slender make, tender, and deserving of happiness, bear heat and cold?

sanskrit: भुक्त्वा अशनम् विशाल अक्षी सूप दम्श अन्वितम् शुभम्
वन्यम् नैवारम् आहारम् कथम् सीता उपभोक्ष्यते
transliteration: bhuktvā aśanam viśāla akṣī sūpa damśa anvitam śubham
vanyam naivāram āhāram katham sītā upabhokṣyate
english: Having formerly partaken of (excellent) rice with curries, how will Sita feed on wild rice?

sanskrit: गीत वादित्र निर्घोषम् श्रुत्वा शुभम् अनिन्दिता
कथम् क्रव्य अद सिम्हानाम् शब्दम् श्रोष्यति अशोभनम्
transliteration: gīta vāditra nirghoṣam śrutvā śubham aninditā
katham kravya ada simhānām śabdam śroṣyati aśobhanam
english: Having heard excellent vocal and instrumental music, how will Sītă hear the frightful cries of carnivorous lions?

sanskrit: महा इन्द्र ध्वज सम्काशः क्व नु शेते महा भुजः
भुजम् परिघ सम्काशम् उपधाय महा बलः
transliteration: mahā indra dhvaja samkāśaḥ kva nu śete mahā bhujaḥ
bhujam parigha samkāśam upadhāya mahā balaḥ
english: Resembling the gonfalon of the great Indra, where sleeps the mighty-armed and exceedingly powerful Råma, making his arm like to a mace his pillow?

sanskrit: पद्म वर्णम् सुकेश अन्तम् पद्म निह्श्वासम् उत्तमम्
कदा द्रक्ष्यामि रामस्य वदनम् पुष्कर ईक्षणम्
transliteration: padma varṇam sukeśa antam padma nihśvāsam uttamam
kadā drakṣyāmi rāmasya vadanam puṣkara īkṣaṇam
english: When shall I behold Rāma's countenance hued like the lotus, with his hair ending beautifully (in curls), and his breath impregnated with the fine perfume of the lotus, and his eyes resembling lotus leaves?

sanskrit: वज्र सारमयम् नूनम् हृदयम् मे न सम्शयः
अपश्यन्त्या न तम् यद् वै फलति इदम् सहस्रधा
transliteration: vajra sāramayam nūnam hṛdayam me na samśayaḥ
apaśyantyā na tam yad vai phalati idam sahasradhā
english: Surely my heart, without doubt, is made of the essence of the thunderbolt, since not beholding him, it is not cracked in a thousand fragments.

sanskrit: यत्त्वया करुणम् कर्म व्यपोह्य मम बान्धवाः
transliteration: yattvayā karuṇam karma vyapohya mama bāndhavāḥ
english: It is because of your sad act that mine own, being thwarted, although worthy of happiness, are miserably ranging the wilderness.

sanskrit: जह्याद्राज्यम् च कोशम् च भरतो नोपल्स्ख्यते
transliteration: jahyādrājyam ca kośam ca bharato nopalskhyate
english: If after the expiration of the five and ten years, Rāghava does return, it does not appear likely that Bharata will renounce the kingdom and the exchequer.

Some on the occasions of the Sradha (first) feast their own friends, and having done this, they mind the choice Brāhmaṇas. But those twice-born ones that are meritorious, learned, and like to celestials, do not at the last moment regard even viands resembling ambrosia.

Some on the occasions of the Sradha (first) feast their own friends, and having done this, they mind the choice Brāhmaṇas. But those twice-born ones that are meritorious, learned, and like to celestials, do not at the last moment regard even viands resembling ambrosia.
Brāhmaṇas of high respectability endowed with wisdom never bear being entertained after the other twice-born ones have been feasted, even as bulls never quietly bear to have their horns cut off.

sanskrit: एवम् कनीयसा भ्रात्रा भुक्तम् राज्यम् विशाम् पते
भ्राता ज्येष्ठा वरिष्ठाः च किम् अर्थम् न अवमम्स्यते
transliteration: evam kanīyasā bhrātrā bhuktam rājyam viśām pate
bhrātā jyeṣṭhā variṣṭhāḥ ca kim artham na avamamsyate
english: Why will not an elder brother and one who has sterling merits, O monarch, disregard a kingdom which has been thus enjoyed by his younger brother?

sanskrit: न परेण आहृतम् भक्ष्यम् व्याघ्रः खादितुम् इच्चति
एवम् एव नर व्याघ्रः पर लीढम् न मम्स्यते
transliteration: na pareṇa āhṛtam bhakṣyam vyāghraḥ khāditum iccati
evam eva nara vyāghraḥ para līḍham na mamsyate
english: A tiger does not like to feed on food procured by others. Even so that tiger-like personage does not regard anything that has come to be tasted by another.

sanskrit: हविर् आज्यम् पुरोडाशाः कुशा यूपाः च खादिराः
न एतानि यात यामानि कुर्वन्ति पुनर् अध्वरे
transliteration: havir ājyam puroḍāśāḥ kuśā yūpāḥ ca khādirāḥ
na etāni yāta yāmāni kurvanti punar adhvare
english: Clarified butter, sacrificial cakes, Kusa, stakes of catechu having been used in one sacrifice cannot be used in another.

sanskrit: तथा हि आत्तम् इदम् राज्यम् हृत साराम् सुराम् इव
न अभिमन्तुम् अलम् रामः नष्ट सोमम् इव अध्वरम्
transliteration: tathā hi āttam idam rājyam hṛta sārām surām iva
na abhimantum alam rāmaḥ naṣṭa somam iva adhvaram
english: Even so this kingdom which has been already enjoyed, like to liquor deprived of its essence or a sacrifice whose soma has been eaten, cannot be accepted by Rāma.

sanskrit: न एवम् विधम् असत्कारम् राघवो मर्षयिष्यति
transliteration: na evam vidham asatkāram rāghavo marṣayiṣyati
english: Such an ill treatment Rāghava will not put up with, even as a powerful tiger cannot bear the rubbing of its tail (by another).

sanskrit: अधर्मम् त्विह धर्मात्मा लोकम् धर्मेण योजयेत्
transliteration: adharmam tviha dharmātmā lokam dharmeṇa yojayet
english: This world aided by the gods fear to encounter him in high conflict; but he restrains himself, thinking any such action on his part as unrighteous. Indeed, that righteous one brings back people to morality.
Surely, that mighty-armed one endowed with exceeding prowess, can with his golden shafts burn all creatures and the oceans, like the Day at the dissolution of all.

sanskrit: स तादृशः सिम्ह बलो वृषभ अक्षो नर ऋषभः
स्वयम् एव हतः पित्रा जलजेन आत्मजो यथा
transliteration: sa tādṛśaḥ simha balo vṛṣabha akṣo nara ṛṣabhaḥ
svayam eva hataḥ pitrā jalajena ātmajo yathā
english: But such a man of men, possessed of leonine strength, and graced with the eyes of a bull, has been destroyed by his father, like a fish destroying his offspring.

sanskrit: द्विजाति चरितः धर्मः शास्त्र दृष्टः सनातनः
यदि ते धर्म निरते त्वया पुत्रे विवासिते
transliteration: dvijāti caritaḥ dharmaḥ śāstra dṛṣṭaḥ sanātanaḥ
yadi te dharma nirate tvayā putre vivāsite
english: If you had believed in the morality prescribed in the scriptures, and which is followed by the twice-born ones, you would not have banished your son. But disregarding such morality, you have banished your virtuous son.

sanskrit: गतिर् एवाक् पतिर् नार्या द्वितीया गतिर् आत्मजः
तृतीया ज्ञातयो राजमः चतुर्थी न इह विद्यते
transliteration: gatir evāk patir nāryā dvitīyā gatir ātmajaḥ
tṛtīyā jñātayo rājamaḥ caturthī na iha vidyate
english: One of the refuges of a woman is her husband, a second is her son, and a third is her relatives; and a fourth she has none.

sanskrit: तत्र त्वम् चैव मे न अस्ति रामः च वनम् आश्रितः
न वनम् गन्तुम् इच्चामि सर्वथा हि हता त्वया
transliteration: tatra tvam caiva me na asti rāmaḥ ca vanam āśritaḥ
na vanam gantum iccāmi sarvathā hi hatā tvayā
english: But you cease to be mine; and Rāma has been sent to the woods. I do not like to go into the forest; so I am entirely undone by you.

sanskrit: हतः तथा आत्मा सह मन्त्रिभिः च
हता सपुत्रा अस्मि हताः च पौराः
सुतः च भार्या च तव प्रहृष्टौ
transliteration: hataḥ tathā ātmā saha mantribhiḥ ca
hatā saputrā asmi hatāḥ ca paurāḥ
sutaḥ ca bhāryā ca tava prahṛṣṭau
english: This kingdom, your own kingdom, has been destroyed by you; destroyed are all along with the counsellors; destroyed am I with my son; and destroyed are the citizens: your son and your wife are alone delighted.

sanskrit: स्वदुष्कृतम् च अपि पुनः तदा अस्मरत्
transliteration: svaduṣkṛtam ca api punaḥ tadā asmarat
english: Hearing these words uttered in heart-rending accents, Dasaratha exceedingly distressed, became senseless. And being afflicted with grief, he again remembered his evil act.

sanskrit: एवम् तु क्रुद्धया राजा राम मात्रा सशोकया
श्रावितः परुषम् वाक्यम् चिन्तयाम् आस दुह्खितः
transliteration: evam tu kruddhayā rājā rāma mātrā saśokayā
śrāvitaḥ paruṣam vākyam cintayām āsa duhkhitaḥ
english: Thus harshly addressed by the indignant mother of Rāma, the king aggrieved was plunged in thought. Having thought for a long while, that repressor of foes, the king, who had lost his senses through grief, regained consciousness.

sanskrit: चिन्तयित्वा स च नृपो मुमोह व्याकुलेन्द्रियः
transliteration: cintayitvā sa ca nṛpo mumoha vyākulendriyaḥ
english: Thus harshly addressed by the indignant mother of Rāma, the king aggrieved was plunged in thought. Having thought for a long while, that repressor of foes, the king, who had lost his senses through grief, regained consciousness.
Having regained his senses, he sighing hot and hard, seeing Kausalyā beside him, was again lost in thought.

sanskrit: यद् अनेन कृतम् पूर्वम् अज्ञानात् शब्द वेधिना
transliteration: yad anena kṛtam pūrvam ajñānāt śabda vedhinā
english: As he was thinking, the sinful act which he had through ignorance formerly committed by means of the shaft which hits by sounds, rose up in his recollection,

sanskrit: अमनाः तेन शोकेन राम शोकेन च प्रभुः
transliteration: amanāḥ tena śokena rāma śokena ca prabhuḥ
english: Afflicted with this grief as well as that on account of Rāma, that lord, the king, burned in these two several griefs.

sanskrit: दह्यमानः तु शोकाभ्याम् कौसल्याम् आह भू पतिः
transliteration: dahyamānaḥ tu śokābhyām kausalyām āha bhū patiḥ
english: Burning in grief and distressed, he trembling and with joined hands, with his head hanging down, addressed Kausalyā, with the view of pacifying her.

sanskrit: प्रसादये त्वाम् कौसल्ये रचितः अयम् मया अन्जलिः
वत्सला च आनृशम्सा च त्वम् हि नित्यम् परेष्व् अपि
transliteration: prasādaye tvām kausalye racitaḥ ayam mayā anjaliḥ
vatsalā ca ānṛśamsā ca tvam hi nityam pareṣv api
english: I deprecate your displeasure. O Kausalyä with joined hands. You are ever affectionate and did not treat harshly even enemies.

sanskrit: भर्ता तु खलु नारीणाम् गुणवान् निर्गुणो अपि वा
transliteration: bhartā tu khalu nārīṇām guṇavān nirguṇo api vā
english: Verily to women cognizant of virtue, a husband, whether he has any merits or not, is a very deity.

sanskrit: सा त्वम् धर्म परा नित्यम् दृष्ट लोक पर अवर
न अर्हसे विप्रियम् वक्तुम् दुह्खिता अपि सुदुह्खितम्
transliteration: sā tvam dharma parā nityam dṛṣṭa loka para avara
na arhase vipriyam vaktum duhkhitā api suduhkhitam
english: Ever virtuous, you, that have seen both the virtuous and the vicious, although aggrieved, ought not to say anything unpleasant to me who am weighed down with woe.

sanskrit: तत् वाक्यम् करुणम् राज्ञः श्रुत्वा दीनस्य भाषितम्
कौसल्या व्यसृजद् बाष्पम् प्रणाली इव नव उदकम्
transliteration: tat vākyam karuṇam rājñaḥ śrutvā dīnasya bhāṣitam
kausalyā vyasṛjad bāṣpam praṇālī iva nava udakam
english: Having heard these piteous words of the distressed king, Kausalyā uttered words even as a water-way lets out fresh accession of rain.
