english: Thus asked by his friend, Bharata answered, “Listen why this depression has overtaken me. In a dream I beheld my father, pale, with his hair loosely flowing about, plunging from the summit of a mountain into a dirty pool filled with cowdung.”

sanskrit: स्वप्ने पितरम् अद्राक्षम् मलिनम् मुक्त मूर्धजम्
पतन्तम् अद्रि शिखरात् कलुषे गोमये ह्रदे
transliteration: svapne pitaram adrākṣam malinam mukta mūrdhajam
patantam adri śikharāt kaluṣe gomaye hrade
english: Thus asked by his friend, Bharata answered, “Listen why this depression has overtaken me. In a dream I beheld my father, pale, with his hair loosely flowing about, plunging from the summit of a mountain into a dirty pool filled with cowdung.”

sanskrit: प्लवमानः च मे दृष्टः स तस्मिन् गोमय ह्रदे
पिबन्न् अन्जलिना तैलम् हसन्न् इव मुहुर् मुहुः
transliteration: plavamānaḥ ca me dṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmin gomaya hrade
pibann anjalinā tailam hasann iva muhur muhuḥ
english: And I saw him floating on a sink of cowdung, and yet with a momentary laugh drinking oil by means of his joined hands.

sanskrit: ततः तिलोदनम् भुक्त्वा पुनः पुनर् अधः शिराः
तैलेन अभ्यक्त सर्व अन्गः तैलम् एव अवगाहत
transliteration: tataḥ tilodanam bhuktvā punaḥ punar adhaḥ śirāḥ
tailena abhyakta sarva angaḥ tailam eva avagāhata
english: Then feeding on rice mixed with sesame, he again and again hanging his head down, dives into oil with his limbs rubbed with oil.

sanskrit: स्वप्ने अपि सागरम् शुष्कम् चन्द्रम् च पतितम् भुवि
सहसा च अपि सम्शन्तम् ज्वलितम् जात वेदसम्
transliteration: svapne api sāgaram śuṣkam candram ca patitam bhuvi
sahasā ca api samśantam jvalitam jāta vedasam

sanskrit: अवदीर्णाम् च पृथिवीम् शुष्कामः च विविधान् द्रुमान्
अहम् पश्यामि विध्वस्तान् सधूमामः चैव पार्वतान्
transliteration: avadīrṇām ca pṛthivīm śuṣkāmaḥ ca vividhān drumān
aham paśyāmi vidhvastān sadhūmāmaḥ caiva pārvatān

sanskrit: पीठे कार्ष्णायसे च एनम् निषण्णम् कृष्ण वाससम्
प्रहसन्ति स्म राजानम् प्रमदाः कृष्ण पिन्गलाः
transliteration: pīṭhe kārṣṇāyase ca enam niṣaṇṇam kṛṣṇa vāsasam
prahasanti sma rājānam pramadāḥ kṛṣṇa pingalāḥ
english: I saw the king seated on a sable seat of iron, clad in a sable garb; and women black and yellow beating him.

sanskrit: त्वरमाणः च धर्म आत्मा रक्त माल्य अनुलेपनः
रथेन खर युक्तेन प्रयातः दक्षिणा मुखः
transliteration: tvaramāṇaḥ ca dharma ātmā rakta mālya anulepanaḥ
rathena khara yuktena prayātaḥ dakṣiṇā mukhaḥ
english: And bearing a garland of red flowers, with his body daubed with red sandal, he was fast proceeding to the south in a car yoked with asses.
And women clad in red garment were laughing at him, and a grim-visaged Rākşasa was seen by me as dragging him.

sanskrit: एवम् एतन् मया दृष्टम् इमाम् रात्रिम् भय आवहाम्
अहम् रामः अथ वा राजा लक्ष्मणो वा मरिष्यति
transliteration: evam etan mayā dṛṣṭam imām rātrim bhaya āvahām
aham rāmaḥ atha vā rājā lakṣmaṇo vā mariṣyati
english: This was the dream that I saw this terrible night. Either I, or Rama, or the king, or Lakşmaņa is to breathe our last.

sanskrit: नरः यानेन यः स्वप्ने खर युक्तेन याति हि
अचिरात् तस्य धूम अग्रम् चितायाम् सम्प्रदृश्यते
transliteration: naraḥ yānena yaḥ svapne khara yuktena yāti hi
acirāt tasya dhūma agram citāyām sampradṛśyate
english: The smoke of the funeral pyre of him will be shortly visible that goes in the car yoked with asses. It is for this reason that I am poor of spirit, and that I do not respond to your words. Further, my throat is parched, and my mind ill at ease.

sanskrit: एतन् निमित्तम् दीनो अहम् तन् न वः प्रतिपूजये
शुष्यति इव च मे कण्ठो न स्वस्थम् इव मे मनः
transliteration: etan nimittam dīno aham tan na vaḥ pratipūjaye
śuṣyati iva ca me kaṇṭho na svastham iva me manaḥ
english: The smoke of the funeral pyre of him will be shortly visible that goes in the car yoked with asses. It is for this reason that I am poor of spirit, and that I do not respond to your words. Further, my throat is parched, and my mind ill at ease.

sanskrit: भ्रष्टश्च स्वरयोगो मे चाया चोपहता मम
transliteration: bhraṣṭaśca svarayogo me cāyā copahatā mama
english: Ground of fear find I none, yet am I subject to fear. My voice is untuned, and my grace fled, and I begin to despise my life, nor know I the reason why.

sanskrit: जुगुप्सन्न् इव च आत्मानम् न च पश्यामि कारणम्
इमाम् हि दुह्स्वप्न गतिम् निशाम्य ताम्
भयम् महत् तद्द् हृदयान् न याति मे
transliteration: jugupsann iva ca ātmānam na ca paśyāmi kāraṇam
imām hi duhsvapna gatim niśāmya tām
bhayam mahat tadd hṛdayān na yāti me
english: Bringing to mind this various-looking dream which I had not thought of before, and remembering the king of incomprehensible presence, this fear goes not from my heart.

sanskrit: भरते ब्रुवति स्वप्नम् दूताः ते क्लान्त वाहनाः
प्रविश्य असह्य परिखम् रम्यम् राज गृहम् पुरम्
transliteration: bharate bruvati svapnam dūtāḥ te klānta vāhanāḥ
praviśya asahya parikham ramyam rāja gṛham puram
english: Bharata was speaking thus when the envoys with their vehicles fatigued, entered the splendid royal residence surrounded by a strong rampart.

sanskrit: समागम्य तु राज्ञा च राज पुत्रेण च अर्चिताः
राज्ञः पादौ गृहीत्वा तु तम् ऊचुर् भरतम् वचः
transliteration: samāgamya tu rājñā ca rāja putreṇa ca arcitāḥ
rājñaḥ pādau gṛhītvā tu tam ūcur bharatam vacaḥ
english: Presenting themselves before the king, they, well received by him as well as the prince, bowed down to the feet of the monarch.

sanskrit: पुरोहितः त्वा कुशलम् प्राह सर्वे च मन्त्रिणः
त्वरमाणः च निर्याहि कृत्यम् आत्ययिकम् त्वया
transliteration: purohitaḥ tvā kuśalam prāha sarve ca mantriṇaḥ
tvaramāṇaḥ ca niryāhi kṛtyam ātyayikam tvayā
english: Then they addressed Bharata, saying, The priest and the counsellors have enquired after your welfare. Do you set out speedily. A business is on hand that Brooke no delay on your part.
And, O you of expansive eyes, do you take these costly raiment's and ornaments, and present them to your maternal uncle and grandfather.

sanskrit: अत्र विम्शति कोट्यः तु नृपतेर् मातुलस्य ते
दश कोट्यः तु सम्पूर्णाः तथैव च नृप आत्मज
transliteration: atra vimśati koṭyaḥ tu nṛpater mātulasya te
daśa koṭyaḥ tu sampūrṇāḥ tathaiva ca nṛpa ātmaja
english: Twenty Kotis are intended for the king and complete ten for your maternal uncle, O son of the monarch.

sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य च तत् सर्वम् स्वनुरक्तः सुहृज् जने
दूतान् उवाच भरतः कामैः सम्प्रतिपूज्य तान्
transliteration: pratigṛhya ca tat sarvam svanuraktaḥ suhṛj jane
dūtān uvāca bharataḥ kāmaiḥ sampratipūjya tān
english: Taking all these, Bharata attached to his relatives, made the articles over to them; and receiving the envoys with goodly gifts, spoke to them.

sanskrit: कच्चित् सुकुशली राजा पिता दशरथो मम
कच्चिच् च अरागता रामे लक्ष्मणे वा महात्मनि
transliteration: kaccit sukuśalī rājā pitā daśaratho mama
kaccic ca arāgatā rāme lakṣmaṇe vā mahātmani
english: Is my father, king Dasaratha, well? And is it well with Rama and the high-souled Laksmana?

sanskrit: आर्या च धर्म निरता धर्मज्ञा धर्म दर्शिनी
अरोगा च अपि कौसल्या माता रामस्य धीमतः
transliteration: āryā ca dharma niratā dharmajñā dharma darśinī
arogā ca api kausalyā mātā rāmasya dhīmataḥ
english: And is the mother of the intelligent Rāma, the revered Kausalyā, conversant with virtue and ever practising it, well?

sanskrit: कच्चित् सुमित्रा धर्मज्ञा जननी लक्ष्मणस्य या
शत्रुघ्नस्य च वीरस्य सारोगा च अपि मध्यमा
transliteration: kaccit sumitrā dharmajñā jananī lakṣmaṇasya yā
śatrughnasya ca vīrasya sārogā ca api madhyamā
english: Is the virtuous Sumitrā, mother of Lakşmaņa and of the heroic Śatrughna, well?

sanskrit: आत्म कामा सदा चण्डी क्रोधना प्राज्ञ मानिनी
अरोगा च अपि कैकेयी माता मे किम् उवाच ह
transliteration: ātma kāmā sadā caṇḍī krodhanā prājña māninī
arogā ca api kaikeyī mātā me kim uvāca ha
english: And that wrathful one ever intent on her interest and setting immense store by her wisdom, my mother Kaikeyī, is it also well with her?

sanskrit: एवम् उक्ताः तु ते दूता भरतेन महात्मना
ऊचुः सम्प्रश्रितम् वाक्यम् इदम् तम् भरतम् तदा
transliteration: evam uktāḥ tu te dūtā bharatena mahātmanā
ūcuḥ sampraśritam vākyam idam tam bharatam tadā
english: Thus addressed by the magnanimous Bharata, the envoys spoke to him these humble and brief words.

sanskrit: कुशलाः ते नर व्याघ्र येषाम् कुशलम् इच्चसि
श्रीश्च त्वाम् वृणुते पद्मा युज्यताम् चापि ते रकः
transliteration: kuśalāḥ te nara vyāghra yeṣām kuśalam iccasi
śrīśca tvām vṛṇute padmā yujyatām cāpi te rakaḥ
english: Those of whose welfare you are enquiring after, are, O foremost of men, all well. Śrī seated on the lotus asks for you. Let your car be yoked.

sanskrit: भरतः च अपि तान् दूतान् एवम् उक्तः अभ्यभाषत
आपृच्चे अहम् महा राजम् दूताः सम्त्वरयन्ति माम्
transliteration: bharataḥ ca api tān dūtān evam uktaḥ abhyabhāṣata
āpṛcce aham mahā rājam dūtāḥ samtvarayanti mām
english: Thus addressed, Bharata said to the envoys, “Let me tell the king that the envoys are urging speed on me.”

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा तु तान् दूतान् भरतः पार्थिव आत्मजः
दूतैः सम्चोदितः वाक्यम् मातामहम् उवाच ह
transliteration: evam uktvā tu tān dūtān bharataḥ pārthiva ātmajaḥ
dūtaiḥ samcoditaḥ vākyam mātāmaham uvāca ha
english: Having said this, that son of the king, Bharata, communicated to his maternal grand-father what the envoys had told him.

sanskrit: राजन् पितुर् गमिष्यामि सकाशम् दूत चोदितः
पुनर् अपि अहम् एष्यामि यदा मे त्वम् स्मरिष्यसि
transliteration: rājan pitur gamiṣyāmi sakāśam dūta coditaḥ
punar api aham eṣyāmi yadā me tvam smariṣyasi
english: Asked by the envoys, I shall, O monarch, go to my father. I shall come again whenever you will remember me.

sanskrit: भरतेन एवम् उक्तः तु नृपो मातामहः तदा
तम् उवाच शुभम् वाक्यम् शिरस्य् आघ्राय राघवम्
transliteration: bharatena evam uktaḥ tu nṛpo mātāmahaḥ tadā
tam uvāca śubham vākyam śirasy āghrāya rāghavam
english: Thus accosted by Bharata, his maternal grandfather, the king, smelling Bharata's head, spoke these auspicious words to that descendant of Raghu.

sanskrit: गच्च तात अनुजाने त्वाम् कैकेयी सुप्रजाः त्वया
मातरम् कुशलम् ब्रूयाः पितरम् च परम् तप
transliteration: gacca tāta anujāne tvām kaikeyī suprajāḥ tvayā
mātaram kuśalam brūyāḥ pitaram ca param tapa
english: Go, my child; I permit you. Kaikeyi is mother of a worthy son through you. Do you O subduer of foes, communicate our welfare to both your father and your mother.

sanskrit: पुरोहितम् च कुशलम् ये च अन्ये द्विज सत्तमाः
तौ च तात महा इष्वासौ भ्रातरु राम लक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: purohitam ca kuśalam ye ca anye dvija sattamāḥ
tau ca tāta mahā iṣvāsau bhrātaru rāma lakṣmaṇau
english: Do you likewise communicate the same to the priest and the other principal Brāhmaṇas; as also, my child, to those mighty bowmen, the brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: तस्मै हस्ति उत्तमामः चित्रान् कम्बलान् अजिनानि च
transliteration: tasmai hasti uttamāmaḥ citrān kambalān ajināni ca
english: Then honouring Bharata, king Kekaya conferred on Bharata wealth consisting of choice elephants maintained (at the palace) and woollen sheets and deerskins.

sanskrit: रुक्म निष्क सहस्रे द्वे षोडश अश्व शतानि च
सत्कृत्य कैकेयी पुत्रम् केकयो धनम् आदिशत्
transliteration: rukma niṣka sahasre dve ṣoḍaśa aśva śatāni ca
satkṛtya kaikeyī putram kekayo dhanam ādiśat
english: Honouring the son of Kaikeyi, Kekaya gave him two thousand nishkas and six hundred : horses.

sanskrit: तथा अमात्यान् अभिप्रेतान् विश्वास्यामः च गुण अन्वितान्
ददाव् अश्व पतिः शीघ्रम् भरताय अनुयायिनः
transliteration: tathā amātyān abhipretān viśvāsyāmaḥ ca guṇa anvitān
dadāv aśva patiḥ śīghram bharatāya anuyāyinaḥ
english: And for following Bharata, Aśvapati without delay assigned a number of goodly, trustworthy, and qualified courtiers.

sanskrit: ऐरावतान् ऐन्द्र शिरान् नागान् वै प्रिय दर्शनान्
खरान् शीघ्रान् सुसम्युक्तान् मातुलो अस्मै धनम् ददौ
transliteration: airāvatān aindra śirān nāgān vai priya darśanān
kharān śīghrān susamyuktān mātulo asmai dhanam dadau
english: Bharata's maternal uncle conferred on Bharata wealth in the shape of graceful elephants sprung in the īrāvat mountain and the country called Indrasira; as well as fleet and well-broken horses.

sanskrit: अन्तः पुरे अतिसम्वृद्धान् व्याघ्र वीर्य बल अन्वितान्
दम्ष्ट्र आयुधान् महा कायान् शुनः च उपायनम् ददौ
transliteration: antaḥ pure atisamvṛddhān vyāghra vīrya bala anvitān
damṣṭra āyudhān mahā kāyān śunaḥ ca upāyanam dadau
english: The king presented him with dogs brought up in the inner apartment, resembling tigers in strength and prowess, furnished with teeth representing weapons, and large of body.

sanskrit: स मातामहम् आपृच्च्य मातुलम् च युधा जितम्
रथम् आरुह्य भरतः शत्रुघ्न सहितः ययौ
transliteration: sa mātāmaham āpṛccya mātulam ca yudhā jitam
ratham āruhya bharataḥ śatrughna sahitaḥ yayau
english: Then after speaking with his maternal grandfather and uncle, Yudhajit, Bharata ascending a car, set out with Satrughna.

sanskrit: बभूव ह्यस्य हृदते चिन्ता सुमहती तदा
त्वरया चापि दूतानाम् स्वप्नस्यापि च दर्शनात्
transliteration: babhūva hyasya hṛdate cintā sumahatī tadā
tvarayā cāpi dūtānām svapnasyāpi ca darśanāt
english: Owing to his having seen the dream and the post haste speed of the envoys, a mighty anxiety was present in his heart.
Then issuing from his abode, that one possessed of exceeding grace passed the goodly thoroughfare thronged with men, horses, and elephants.
Having left it behind, Bharata saw (before him) the inner apartment (of the king); and thereupon the handsome Bharata entered it without let.

sanskrit: स माता महमापृच्च्य मातुलम् च युधाजितम्
transliteration: sa mātā mahamāpṛccya mātulam ca yudhājitam
english: Then after speaking with his maternal grandfather and uncle, Yudhajit, Bharata ascending a car, set out with Satrughna.

sanskrit: रथान् मण्डल चक्रामः च योजयित्वा परः शतम्
उष्ट्र गो अश्व खरैः भृत्या भरतम् यान्तम् अन्वयुः
transliteration: rathān maṇḍala cakrāmaḥ ca yojayitvā paraḥ śatam
uṣṭra go aśva kharaiḥ bhṛtyā bharatam yāntam anvayuḥ
english: Thereat servants by means of an hundred cars, furnished with circular wheels, and yoked with camels, oxen, horses, and asses, followed Bharata.

Protected by the forces and the courtiers of his maternal grandfather dear to him like his ownself, the magnanimous Bharata who had his foes removed, taking with him his brother, Śatrughna, departed from the abode (of the king), like Siddha issuing from the regions of Indra.

sanskrit: स प्रान् मुखो राज गृहात् अभिनिर्याय वीर्यवान्
ततः सुदामाम् द्युतिमान् सम्तीर्वावेक्ष्य ताम् नदीम्
transliteration: sa prān mukho rāja gṛhāt abhiniryāya vīryavān
tataḥ sudāmām dyutimān samtīrvāvekṣya tām nadīm
english: Issuing from the palace, the blazing Bharata endowed with prowess went in an easterly direction, and seeing before him the river called Sudāmā, crossed it. Then the auspicious descendant of Iksvāku crossed the broad Hrādinſ coursing westwards, as also the river Satadru.

sanskrit: ह्लादिनीम् दूर पाराम् च प्रत्यक् स्रोतः तरन्गिणीम्
शतद्रूम् अतरत् श्रीमान् नदीम् इक्ष्वाकु नन्दनः
transliteration: hlādinīm dūra pārām ca pratyak srotaḥ tarangiṇīm
śatadrūm atarat śrīmān nadīm ikṣvāku nandanaḥ
english: Issuing from the palace, the blazing Bharata endowed with prowess went in an easterly direction, and seeing before him the river called Sudāmā, crossed it. Then the auspicious descendant of Iksvāku crossed the broad Hrādinſ coursing westwards, as also the river Satadru.

sanskrit: एल धाने नदीम् तीर्त्वा प्राप्य च अपर पर्पटान्
transliteration: ela dhāne nadīm tīrtvā prāpya ca apara parpaṭān
english: Then crossing a river at Eladhana,' and coming to Aparaparvata”, he crossed the Sila? and the Akurvatī, and arrived at Agneya* and Salyakarsanam. 1. Some read Eladhani. 2. Some read Apharaparyata. 3. The river, according to some is so named because it transforms the surrounding objects to stone. 4. Some make Agneya an epithet to Salyakarsana, meaning, relating to the south-east.

sanskrit: सत्य सम्धः शुचिः श्रीमान् प्रेक्षमाणः शिला वहाम्
अत्ययात् स महा शैलान् वनम् चैत्र रथम् प्रति
transliteration: satya samdhaḥ śuciḥ śrīmān prekṣamāṇaḥ śilā vahām
atyayāt sa mahā śailān vanam caitra ratham prati
english: And having purified himself and seen Silavaha,' that one of truthful purposes passed the Mahacailas,' and entered the forest of Caitraratha. 1. According to Tirtha, Silavaha is a strcam having Āgneya on one side and Salyakarşaņa on the other. 2. Lit, mighty mountains.

sanskrit: सरस्वतीम् च गङ्गाम् च उग्मेन प्रतिपद्य च
transliteration: sarasvatīm ca gaṅgām ca ugmena pratipadya ca
english: Then coming upon the confluence of the Ganga and the Sarasvati, Bharata entered the forest of Bhārunda lying to the north* of Vīramatsya. *Uttarān, lit. north. Some text read uttaram. It would mean countries lying to the north of Viramatsya.

sanskrit: वेगिनीम् च कुलिन्ग आख्याम् ह्रादिनीम् पर्वत आवृताम्
यमुनाम् प्राप्य सम्तीर्णो बलम् आश्वासयत् तदा
transliteration: veginīm ca kulinga ākhyām hrādinīm parvata āvṛtām
yamunām prāpya samtīrṇo balam āśvāsayat tadā
english: Next crossing the rapid river Kulingā and the Hrādinſ surrounded by hills, as well as the Yamunā, he ordered the forces to halt.

sanskrit: शीतीकृत्य तु गात्राणि क्लान्तान् आश्वास्य वाजिनः
तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च प्रायात् आदाय च उदकम्
transliteration: śītīkṛtya tu gātrāṇi klāntān āśvāsya vājinaḥ
tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca prāyāt ādāya ca udakam
english: Then cooling the limbs of the fatigued horses (with water) and refreshing them, Bharata himself bathed there and drank of the water; and then resumed the march, furnished with the water. Then the gentle prince by means of an excellent car, like to the wind-god himself, entered the mighty forest inhabited by various races of men.

sanskrit: राज पुत्रः महा अरण्यम् अनभीक्ष्ण उपसेवितम्
भद्रः भद्रेण यानेन मारुतः खम् इव अत्ययात्
transliteration: rāja putraḥ mahā araṇyam anabhīkṣṇa upasevitam
bhadraḥ bhadreṇa yānena mārutaḥ kham iva atyayāt
english: Then cooling the limbs of the fatigued horses (with water) and refreshing them, Bharata himself bathed there and drank of the water; and then resumed the march, furnished with the water. Then the gentle prince by means of an excellent car, like to the wind-god himself, entered the mighty forest inhabited by various races of men.
Seeing that the mighty river Gangā was hard to cross at Ansudhāna, Bharata speedily went to the famous city of Prāgvața.
Having crossed the Gangă at Prāgvața, he went over to the Kuţikoșthika. Having with his forces crossed that river, he proceeded to Dharmavardhana.

sanskrit: तोरणम् दक्षिण अर्धेन जम्बू प्रस्थम् उपागमत्
वरूथम् च ययौ रम्यम् ग्रामम् दशरथ आत्मजः
transliteration: toraṇam dakṣiṇa ardhena jambū prastham upāgamat
varūtham ca yayau ramyam grāmam daśaratha ātmajaḥ
english: Then proceeding by the south of Toraņa, he came to Jambuprastha. Then Dasaratha's son went to the beautiful village of Varūtha.

sanskrit: तत्र रम्ये वने वासम् कृत्वा असौ प्रान् मुखो ययौ
transliteration: tatra ramye vane vāsam kṛtvā asau prān mukho yayau
english: Having for a while stayed at that romantic wood, he proceeded eastwards, and presented himself at the villa of Ujjihānāya, where abound trees (called) Priyaka.

sanskrit: सालाम्स् तु प्रियकान् प्राप्य शीघ्रान् आस्थाय वाजिनः
अनुज्ञाप्य अथ भरतः वाहिनीम् त्वरितः ययौ
transliteration: sālāms tu priyakān prāpya śīghrān āsthāya vājinaḥ
anujñāpya atha bharataḥ vāhinīm tvaritaḥ yayau
english: Coming to the Priyakas, Bharata speedily yoking the horses, set out without delay, issuing his orders to the forces.

sanskrit: वासम् कृत्वा सर्व तीर्थे तीर्त्वा च उत्तानकाम् नदीम्
अन्या नदीः च विविधाः पार्वतीयैअः तुरम् गमैः
transliteration: vāsam kṛtvā sarva tīrthe tīrtvā ca uttānakām nadīm
anyā nadīḥ ca vividhāḥ pārvatīyaiaḥ turam gamaiḥ

sanskrit: ततार च नर व्याघ्रः लौहित्ये स कपीवतीम्
transliteration: tatāra ca nara vyāghraḥ lauhitye sa kapīvatīm

sanskrit: एक साले स्थाणुमतीम् विनते गोमतीम् नदीम्
कलिन्ग नगरे च अपि प्राप्य साल वनम् तदा
transliteration: eka sāle sthāṇumatīm vinate gomatīm nadīm
kalinga nagare ca api prāpya sāla vanam tadā

sanskrit: वनम् च समतीत्य आशु शर्वर्याम् अरुण उदये
transliteration: vanam ca samatītya āśu śarvaryām aruṇa udaye

sanskrit: अयोध्याम् मनुना राज्ञा निर्मिताम् स ददर्श ह
ताम् पुरीम् पुरुष व्याघ्रः सप्त रात्र उषिटः पथि
transliteration: ayodhyām manunā rājñā nirmitām sa dadarśa ha
tām purīm puruṣa vyāghraḥ sapta rātra uṣiṭaḥ pathi

sanskrit: अयोध्याम् अग्रतः दृष्ट्वा रथे सारथिम् अब्रवीत्
एषा न अतिप्रतीता मे पुण्य उद्याना यशस्विनी
transliteration: ayodhyām agrataḥ dṛṣṭvā rathe sārathim abravīt
eṣā na atipratītā me puṇya udyānā yaśasvinī

sanskrit: अयोध्या दृश्यते दूरात् सारथे पाण्डु मृत्तिका
यज्वभिर् गुण सम्पन्नैः ब्राह्मणैः वेद पारगैः
transliteration: ayodhyā dṛśyate dūrāt sārathe pāṇḍu mṛttikā
yajvabhir guṇa sampannaiḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ veda pāragaiḥ

sanskrit: भूयिष्ठम् ऋषैः आकीर्णा राज ऋषि वर पालिता
अयोध्यायाम् पुरा शब्दः श्रूयते तुमुलो महान्
transliteration: bhūyiṣṭham ṛṣaiḥ ākīrṇā rāja ṛṣi vara pālitā
ayodhyāyām purā śabdaḥ śrūyate tumulo mahān

sanskrit: समन्तान् नर नारीणाम् तम् अद्य न शृणोम्य् अहम्
उद्यानानि हि साय अह्ने क्रीडित्वा उपरतैः नरैः
transliteration: samantān nara nārīṇām tam adya na śṛṇomy aham
udyānāni hi sāya ahne krīḍitvā uparataiḥ naraiḥ

sanskrit: तानि अद्य अनुरुदन्ति इव परित्यक्तानि कामिभिः
transliteration: tāni adya anurudanti iva parityaktāni kāmibhiḥ
english: The gardens where from persons having sported in the evening used to rush out (at day break) wear a different aspect now. Forsaken by the pleasure-seekers, the garden appear to weep.

sanskrit: अरण्य भूता इव पुरी सारथे प्रतिभाति मे
न हि अत्र यानैः दृश्यन्ते न गजैः न च वाजिभिः
transliteration: araṇya bhūtā iva purī sārathe pratibhāti me
na hi atra yānaiḥ dṛśyante na gajaiḥ na ca vājibhiḥ
english: O charioteer, the city appears to me like a wilderness. And I do not as formerly behold the flower of the city leaving or entering her on cars or elephants or horses.

sanskrit: निर्यान्तः वा अभियान्तः वा नर मुख्या यथा पुरम्
transliteration: niryāntaḥ vā abhiyāntaḥ vā nara mukhyā yathā puram

english: Gardens which, frequented by people inebriated with the honey of love, met together for purposes of sport, looked charmingly blooming, I find as utterly void of cheerfulness, with the trees as if lamenting with tremulous leaves.

sanskrit: सम्रक्ताम् मधुराम् वाणीम् कलम् व्याहरताम् बहु
transliteration: samraktām madhurām vāṇīm kalam vyāharatām bahu

sanskrit: प्रवाति पवनः श्रीमान् किम् नु नाद्य यथापुरम्
transliteration: pravāti pavanaḥ śrīmān kim nu nādya yathāpuram

sanskrit: अनिष्टानि च पापानि पश्यामि विविधानि च
transliteration: aniṣṭāni ca pāpāni paśyāmi vividhāni ca

sanskrit: निमित्तानि अमनोज्ञानि तेन सीदति ते मनः
सर्वथा कुशलम् सूत दुर्लभम् मम बन्धुषु
transliteration: nimittāni amanojñāni tena sīdati te manaḥ
sarvathā kuśalam sūta durlabham mama bandhuṣu

sanskrit: तथा ह्यसति सम्मोहे हृदयम् सीदतीव मे
transliteration: tathā hyasati sammohe hṛdayam sīdatīva me

sanskrit: द्वाह्स्थैः उत्थाय विजयम् पृष्टः तैः सहितः ययौ
स तु अनेक अग्र हृदयो द्वाह्स्थम् प्रत्यर्च्य तम् जनम्
transliteration: dvāhsthaiḥ utthāya vijayam pṛṣṭaḥ taiḥ sahitaḥ yayau
sa tu aneka agra hṛdayo dvāhstham pratyarcya tam janam

sanskrit: सूतम् अश्व पतेः क्लान्तम् अब्रवीत् तत्र राघवः
transliteration: sūtam aśva pateḥ klāntam abravīt tatra rāghavaḥ
english: Then courteously telling the warders to desist, he with an agitated heart spoke to the tired charioteer of Aśvapati, “O sinless one, why have I been brought in this haste without any (adequate) reason?" My heart apprehended some evil; and my disposition gives way.

sanskrit: अशुभाशङ्कि हृदयम् शीलम् च पततीव मे
श्रुता नो यादृशाः पूर्वम् नृपतीनाम् विनाशने
transliteration: aśubhāśaṅki hṛdayam śīlam ca patatīva me
śrutā no yādṛśāḥ pūrvam nṛpatīnām vināśane

sanskrit: आकाराः तान् अहम् सर्वान् इह पश्यामि सारथे
transliteration: ākārāḥ tān aham sarvān iha paśyāmi sārathe

sanskrit: माल्यापणेषु राजन्ते नाद्य पण्यानि वा तथा
transliteration: mālyāpaṇeṣu rājante nādya paṇyāni vā tathā
english: The images are not worshipped; and the places of sacrifice are in a like condition. And garlands are not displayed in the shops where they are sold. And traders looking anxious, with their business stopped, do not look as before.

The images are not worshipped; and the places of sacrifice are in a like condition. And garlands are not displayed in the shops where they are sold. And traders looking anxious, with their business stopped, do not look as before.

sanskrit: मलिनम् च अश्रु पूर्ण अक्षम् दीनम् ध्यान परम् कृशम्
सस्त्री पुम्सम् च पश्यामि जनम् उत्कण्ठितम् पुरे
transliteration: malinam ca aśru pūrṇa akṣam dīnam dhyāna param kṛśam
sastrī pumsam ca paśyāmi janam utkaṇṭhitam pure
english: And in temples and Caityas birds and beasts appear dispirited. And in the city I behold men and women pale and woe-begone and emaciated and anxious, with tears filling their eyes.

sanskrit: इति एवम् उक्त्वा भरतः सूतम् तम् दीन मानसः
तानि अनिष्टानि अयोध्यायाम् प्रेक्ष्य राज गृहम् ययौ
transliteration: iti evam uktvā bharataḥ sūtam tam dīna mānasaḥ
tāni aniṣṭāni ayodhyāyām prekṣya rāja gṛham yayau
english: Having said this to the charioteer, Bharata, beholding these inauspicious sights, entered the palace of the king with a depressed heart.

sanskrit: ताम् शून्य शृन्ग अटक वेश्म रथ्याम्
transliteration: tām śūnya śṛnga aṭaka veśma rathyām
english: Beholding the city resembling the city of Indra, with her crossings and houses and roads void of people, and the doors and hinges covered with dust, Bharata was filled with greater grief.

sanskrit: यानि अन्न्यदा न अस्य पुरे बभूवुः
transliteration: yāni annyadā na asya pure babhūvuḥ
english: And witnessing many unpleasant things which he had never seen during the life of the monarch, that high-souled one entered the mansion of his father, bending his head, depressed in spirits, and with his mind extremely aggrieved.

sanskrit: अपश्यम्स् तु ततः तत्र पितरम् पितुर् आलये
जगाम भरतः द्रष्टुम् मातरम् मातुर् आलये
transliteration: apaśyams tu tataḥ tatra pitaram pitur ālaye
jagāma bharataḥ draṣṭum mātaram mātur ālaye
english: Not having seen his father in his father's quarters, Bharata went to his mother's apartment for seeing her. *The text is evidently corrupt. From the sequel it appears that Bharata has not seen the king at that time. That commentator, however, passes over the point in silence, which is to be accounted for by the slovenliness of the way of though characterising the Sanskrit commentators in general. An English commentator would have considered the matter as of very great importance, but his Hindu brother takes it quietly, and passes on with indifference.

sanskrit: अनुप्राप्तम् तु तम् दृष्ट्वा कैकेयी प्रोषितम् सुतम्
उत्पपात तदा हृष्टा त्यक्त्वा सौवर्ण मानसम्
transliteration: anuprāptam tu tam dṛṣṭvā kaikeyī proṣitam sutam
utpapāta tadā hṛṣṭā tyaktvā sauvarṇa mānasam
english: On seeing her son before her after his sojourn from home, Kaikeyi delighted, rose up from her golden seat.

sanskrit: स प्रविश्य एव धर्म आत्मा स्व गृहम् श्री विवर्जितम्
भरतः प्रेक्ष्य जग्राह जनन्याः चरणौ शुभौ
transliteration: sa praviśya eva dharma ātmā sva gṛham śrī vivarjitam
bharataḥ prekṣya jagrāha jananyāḥ caraṇau śubhau
english: On entering his own quarter which he found deprived of grace, the virtuous Bharata took hold of his mother's auspicious feet.

sanskrit: सा तम् मूर्ध्नि समुपाघ्राय परिष्वज्य यशस्विनम्
transliteration: sā tam mūrdhni samupāghrāya pariṣvajya yaśasvinam
english: Then smelling the crown of his head and embracing him and taking that illustrious one on her lap, Kaikeyi addressed him, saying.

sanskrit: अद्य ते कतिचित् रात्र्यः च्युतस्य आर्यक वेश्मनः
अपि न अध्व श्रमः शीघ्रम् रथेन आपततः तव
transliteration: adya te katicit rātryaḥ cyutasya āryaka veśmanaḥ
api na adhva śramaḥ śīghram rathena āpatataḥ tava
english: How many days hence did you leave the residence of the revered one? Have you felt any fatigue on the way incident to the car proceeding swiftly?

sanskrit: आर्यकः ते सुकुशलो युधा जिन् मातुलः तव
प्रवासाच् च सुखम् पुत्र सर्वम् मे वक्तुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: āryakaḥ te sukuśalo yudhā jin mātulaḥ tava
pravāsāc ca sukham putra sarvam me vaktum arhasi
english: And is the revered one will, and your maternal uncle, Yuddhajit? And, my son, have you passed your time pleasantly during your sojourn? It behoves you to tell me all this.

sanskrit: एवम् पृष्ठः तु कैकेय्या प्रियम् पार्थिव नन्दनः
आचष्ट भरतः सर्वम् मात्रे राजीव लोचनः
transliteration: evam pṛṣṭhaḥ tu kaikeyyā priyam pārthiva nandanaḥ
ācaṣṭa bharataḥ sarvam mātre rājīva locanaḥ
english: Thus asked that son of the king, Bharata, furnished with eyes resembling lotuses, told his mother that all was well.

sanskrit: अद्य मे सप्तमी रात्रिः च्युतस्य आर्यक वेश्मनः
अम्बायाः कुशली तातः युधाजिन् मातुलः च मे
transliteration: adya me saptamī rātriḥ cyutasya āryaka veśmanaḥ
ambāyāḥ kuśalī tātaḥ yudhājin mātulaḥ ca me
english: Seven nights hence I took leave of that revered one's residence. My mother's sire is well, as also my maternal uncle, Yuddhajit.

sanskrit: यन् मे धनम् च रत्नम् च ददौ राजा परम् तपः
परिश्रान्तम् पथि अभवत् ततः अहम् पूर्वम् आगतः
transliteration: yan me dhanam ca ratnam ca dadau rājā param tapaḥ
pariśrāntam pathi abhavat tataḥ aham pūrvam āgataḥ

sanskrit: राज वाल्य हरैः दूतैअः त्वर्यमाणो अहम् आगतः
यद् अहम् प्रष्टुम् इच्चामि तत् अम्बा वक्तुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: rāja vālya haraiḥ dūtaiaḥ tvaryamāṇo aham āgataḥ
yad aham praṣṭum iccāmi tat ambā vaktum arhasi
english: My vehicles had got tired in consequence of bearing the wealth and jewels which that subduer of foes, the king, had bestowed on me. And it is for this reason that I have come in advance of them. Urged by the royal emissaries, I have come here so swiftly. But it behoves my mother to tell me what I wish to ask.

sanskrit: शून्यो अयम् शयनीयः ते पर्यन्को हेम भूषितः
न च अयम् इक्ष्वाकु जनः प्रहृष्टः प्रतिभाति मे
transliteration: śūnyo ayam śayanīyaḥ te paryanko hema bhūṣitaḥ
na ca ayam ikṣvāku janaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ pratibhāti me
english: This sleeping bedstead of yours adorned with gold is empty. I do not see the race of Ikşvāku in their usual good spirits.

sanskrit: राजा भवति भूयिष्ठ्गम् इह अम्बाया निवेशने
तम् अहम् न अद्य पश्यामि द्रष्टुम् इच्चन्न् इह आगतः
transliteration: rājā bhavati bhūyiṣṭhgam iha ambāyā niveśane
tam aham na adya paśyāmi draṣṭum iccann iha āgataḥ
english: The king generally remains in this apartment of my mother. But coming here with the desire of seeing him, I do not today find him at this place.

sanskrit: पितुर् ग्रहीष्ये चरणौ तम् मम आख्याहि पृच्चतः
transliteration: pitur grahīṣye caraṇau tam mama ākhyāhi pṛccataḥ
english: I would take the feet of my father. Do you tell me who ask you. Is he in the apartment of my eldest mother, Kausalya?

sanskrit: तम् प्रत्युवाच कैकेयी प्रियवद् घोरम् अप्रियम्
transliteration: tam pratyuvāca kaikeyī priyavad ghoram apriyam
english: Blinded by the lust of dominion, and looking upon that as desirable (to Bharata) which was exceedingly disagreeable (to him), Kaikeyi replied to him, who did not know what had transpired.

sanskrit: या गतिः सर्व भूतानाम् ताम् गतिम् ते पिता गतः
राजा महात्मा तेजस्वी यायजूकः सताम् गतिः
transliteration: yā gatiḥ sarva bhūtānām tām gatim te pitā gataḥ
rājā mahātmā tejasvī yāyajūkaḥ satām gatiḥ
english: That high-souled and energetic one ever engaged in sacrifice, the refuge of the good, your father, the king, has come by the state which pertains to all creatures.

sanskrit: तत् श्रुत्वा भरतः वाक्यम् धर्म अभिजनवान् शुचिः
पपात सहसा भूमौ पितृ शोक बल अर्दितः
transliteration: tat śrutvā bharataḥ vākyam dharma abhijanavān śuciḥ
papāta sahasā bhūmau pitṛ śoka bala arditaḥ
english: Hearing these words, Bharata of pure ways sprung from a righteous race, smite with the vehemence of sorrow on account of his father, suddenly fell down to the earth. And exclaiming in the anguish of spirit and in the excess of grief, the words, "Ah me! I am undone!" that mightyarmed one endowed with prowess, fell down, tossing about his arms.

Hearing these words, Bharata of pure ways sprung from a righteous race, smite with the vehemence of sorrow on account of his father, suddenly fell down to the earth. And exclaiming in the anguish of spirit and in the excess of grief, the words, "Ah me! I am undone!" that mightyarmed one endowed with prowess, fell down, tossing about his arms.

sanskrit: ततः शोकेन सम्वीतः पितुर् मरण दुह्खितः
विललाप महा तेजा भ्रान्त आकुलित चेतनः
transliteration: tataḥ śokena samvītaḥ pitur maraṇa duhkhitaḥ
vilalāpa mahā tejā bhrānta ākulita cetanaḥ
english: Then, overwhelmed with and distressed at the death of his father, that highly sorrow energetic one, with his senses distracted, indulged in lamentations.

sanskrit: एतत् सुरुचिरम् भाति पितुर् मे शयनम् पुरा
transliteration: etat suruciram bhāti pitur me śayanam purā
english: This bed of my father used to look like the speckless welkin at night crowned with the moon, after the clouds have gone off. But to-day, deprived of that intellignet one, it ceases to shine, like the firmament without the moon or the sea devoid of its waters.

sanskrit: तत् इदम् न विभाति अद्य विहीनम् तेन धीमता
transliteration: tat idam na vibhāti adya vihīnam tena dhīmatā
english: This bed of my father used to look like the speckless welkin at night crowned with the moon, after the clouds have gone off. But to-day, deprived of that intellignet one, it ceases to shine, like the firmament without the moon or the sea devoid of its waters.
Exclaiming with tears trickling down, that foremost of victorious ones, extremely afflicted at heart, wept, muffling his graceful countenance.

sanskrit: तम् आर्तम् देव सम्काशम् समीक्ष्य पतितम् भुवि
transliteration: tam ārtam deva samkāśam samīkṣya patitam bhuvi
english: Seeing that one resembling a celestial fallen to the earth, stricken with sorrow, like to a bough of the Sāla that had been severed in the wood by an axe, his mother raising up he distressed son like a mad elephant or the sun or the moon, addressed him.

sanskrit: उत्थापयित्वा शोक आर्तम् वचनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: utthāpayitvā śoka ārtam vacanam ca idam abravīt
english: Seeing that one resembling a celestial fallen to the earth, stricken with sorrow, like to a bough of the Sāla that had been severed in the wood by an axe, his mother raising up he distressed son like a mad elephant or the sun or the moon, addressed him.

sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठ उत्तिष्ठ किम् शेषे राज पुत्र महा यशः
त्वद् विधा न हि शोचन्ति सन्तः सदसि सम्मताः
transliteration: uttiṣṭha uttiṣṭha kim śeṣe rāja putra mahā yaśaḥ
tvad vidhā na hi śocanti santaḥ sadasi sammatāḥ
english: Arise, arise. Why do you lie down, O illustrious son of the king? Persons like you having their senses under perfect control, and approved by men of culture, do not grieve.
O you endo!. ed with understanding, like the halo of the Sun in the solar disc, your sense, entitled to dispensing gifts and celebrating sacrifices, ever follows morals your Śruti and asceticism.

sanskrit: स रुदत्या चिरम् कालम् भूमौ विपरिवृत्य च
जननीम् प्रत्युवाच इदम् शोकैः बहुभिर् आवृतः
transliteration: sa rudatyā ciram kālam bhūmau viparivṛtya ca
jananīm pratyuvāca idam śokaiḥ bahubhir āvṛtaḥ
english: Having wept for a long while with his body rolling on the earth, Bharata afflicted with manifold grief, answered his mother, saying.

sanskrit: अभिषेक्ष्यति रामम् तु राजा यज्ञम् नु यक्ष्यति
इति अहम् कृत सम्कल्पो हृष्टः यात्राम् अयासिषम्
transliteration: abhiṣekṣyati rāmam tu rājā yajñam nu yakṣyati
iti aham kṛta samkalpo hṛṣṭaḥ yātrām ayāsiṣam
english: The king will install Rāma and celebrate a sacrifice' concluding this for certain, I had joyfully gone from hence.

sanskrit: तत् इदम् हि अन्यथा भूतम् व्यवदीर्णम् मनो मम
पितरम् यो न पश्यामि नित्यम् प्रिय हिते रतम्
transliteration: tat idam hi anyathā bhūtam vyavadīrṇam mano mama
pitaram yo na paśyāmi nityam priya hite ratam
english: But it has fallen out otherwise. That I do not behold my father ever engaged in the dear welfare (of his subjects) cleaves my heart mother.

sanskrit: अम्ब केन अत्यगात् राजा व्याधिना मय्य् अनागते
धन्या राम आदयः सर्वे यैः पिता सम्स्कृतः स्वयम्
transliteration: amba kena atyagāt rājā vyādhinā mayy anāgate
dhanyā rāma ādayaḥ sarve yaiḥ pitā samskṛtaḥ svayam
english: Of what ailment has the king breathed his last during my absence? Blessed are Rāma and others who have personally performed my sire's last rites.

sanskrit: न नूनम् माम् महा राजः प्राप्तम् जानाति कीर्तिमान्
उपजिघ्रेद्द् हि माम् मूर्ध्नि तातः सम्नम्य सत्वरम्
transliteration: na nūnam mām mahā rājaḥ prāptam jānāti kīrtimān
upajighredd hi mām mūrdhni tātaḥ samnamya satvaram
english: Surely the renowned monarch does not know that I have come. (If he had done so), pressing down my head, my father would at once have smelt it.

sanskrit: क्व स पाणिः सुख स्पर्शः तातस्य अक्लिष्ट कर्मणः
येन माम् रजसा ध्वस्तम् अभीक्ष्णम् परिमार्जति
transliteration: kva sa pāṇiḥ sukha sparśaḥ tātasya akliṣṭa karmaṇaḥ
yena mām rajasā dhvastam abhīkṣṇam parimārjati
english: Where is now the soft hand of that energetic one which used to rub my person when it was covered with dust?

sanskrit: यो मे भ्राता पिता बन्धुर् यस्य दासो अस्मि धीमतः
तस्य माम् शीघ्रम् आख्याहि रामस्य अक्लिष्ट कर्मणः
transliteration: yo me bhrātā pitā bandhur yasya dāso asmi dhīmataḥ
tasya mām śīghram ākhyāhi rāmasya akliṣṭa karmaṇaḥ
english: Do you now without delay convey the news of my arrival to the vigorous Rāma, who is at once my father, brother and friend, and whose beloved servant I am.

sanskrit: पिता हि भवति ज्येष्ठो धर्मम् आर्यस्य जानतः
तस्य पादौ ग्रहीष्यामि स हि इदानीम् गतिर् मम
transliteration: pitā hi bhavati jyeṣṭho dharmam āryasya jānataḥ
tasya pādau grahīṣyāmi sa hi idānīm gatir mama
english: The eldest brother of one that is noble and cognisant of morality, becomes his father. I shall take hold of his feet: he is now my refuge.

sanskrit: आर्ये किम् अब्रवीद् राजा पिता मे सत्य विक्रमः
transliteration: ārye kim abravīd rājā pitā me satya vikramaḥ
english: And, O noble lady, what did that virtuous one cognizant of virtue, that pre-eminently pious one, firm in his vow, and having truth for prowess, even my father, say? I wish to hear news concerning us relative to the last moments of the monarch.

sanskrit: पश्चिमम् साधु सम्देशम् इच्चामि श्रोतुम् आत्मनः
इति पृष्टा यथा तत्त्वम् कैकेयी वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: paścimam sādhu samdeśam iccāmi śrotum ātmanaḥ
iti pṛṣṭā yathā tattvam kaikeyī vākyam abravīt

sanskrit: राम इति राजा विलपन् हा सीते लक्ष्मण इति च
स महात्मा परम् लोकम् गतः गतिमताम् वरः
transliteration: rāma iti rājā vilapan hā sīte lakṣmaṇa iti ca
sa mahātmā param lokam gataḥ gatimatām varaḥ

sanskrit: इमाम् तु पश्चिमाम् वाचम् व्याजहार पिता तव
काल धर्म परिक्षिप्तः पाशैः इव महा गजः
transliteration: imām tu paścimām vācam vyājahāra pitā tava
kāla dharma parikṣiptaḥ pāśaiḥ iva mahā gajaḥ

sanskrit: सिद्ध अर्थाः तु नरा रामम् आगतम् सीतया सह
लक्ष्मणम् च महा बाहुम् द्रक्ष्यन्ति पुनर् आगतम्
transliteration: siddha arthāḥ tu narā rāmam āgatam sītayā saha
lakṣmaṇam ca mahā bāhum drakṣyanti punar āgatam
english: Your father like a mighty elephant fast bound with a cord, said to me these words during his last moments, "Blessed are they that shall see Rāma and the mighty-armed Lakşmaņa returned along with Sītā.”

sanskrit: तत् श्रुत्वा विषसाद एव द्वितीया प्रिय शम्सनात्
विषण्ण वदनो भूत्वा भूयः पप्रच्च मातरम्
transliteration: tat śrutvā viṣasāda eva dvitīyā priya śamsanāt
viṣaṇṇa vadano bhūtvā bhūyaḥ papracca mātaram
english: Hearing this, Bharata apprehending a second misfortune was deeply moved; and with a sad countenance, he again asked his mother.

sanskrit: क्व च इदानीम् स धर्म आत्मा कौसल्य आनन्द वर्धनः
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया च समम् गतः
transliteration: kva ca idānīm sa dharma ātmā kausalya ānanda vardhanaḥ
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā ca samam gataḥ
english: Where has gone that righteous-souled one, the enchancer of Kausalya's joy, along with Laks maņa and Sītā?

sanskrit: तथा पृष्टा यथा तत्त्वम् आख्यातुम् उपचक्रमे
माता अस्य युगपद् वाक्यम् विप्रियम् प्रिय शन्कया
transliteration: tathā pṛṣṭā yathā tattvam ākhyātum upacakrame
mātā asya yugapad vākyam vipriyam priya śankayā
english: Thus questioned, his mother at the same time duly said in words which although highly unwelcome, she took as agreeable to Bharata.

sanskrit: स हि राज सुतः पुत्र चीर वासा महा वनम्
दण्डकान् सह वैदेह्या लक्ष्मण अनुचरः गतः
transliteration: sa hi rāja sutaḥ putra cīra vāsā mahā vanam
daṇḍakān saha vaidehyā lakṣmaṇa anucaraḥ gataḥ
english: O son, that son of the king wearing bark has repaired to the forest of Dandaka, along with Vaidehi and followed by Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: तत् श्रुत्वा भरतः त्रस्तः भ्रातुः चारित्र शन्कया
transliteration: tat śrutvā bharataḥ trastaḥ bhrātuḥ cāritra śankayā
english: Hearing this, Bharata apprehending some moral lapse on the part of his brother from the dignity of his race, asked in agitation.

sanskrit: कच्चिन् न ब्राह्मण वधम् हृतम् रामेण कस्यचित्
कच्चिन् न आढ्यो दरिद्रः वा तेन अपापो विहिम्सितः
transliteration: kaccin na brāhmaṇa vadham hṛtam rāmeṇa kasyacit
kaccin na āḍhyo daridraḥ vā tena apāpo vihimsitaḥ
english: Has Rāma deprived any Brāhmaṇa of his wealth? Or has he wronged any innocent person, whether rich or poor?

sanskrit: कच्चिन् न पर दारान् वा राज पुत्रः अभिमन्यते
कस्मात् स दण्डक अरण्ये भ्रूणहा इव विवासितः
transliteration: kaccin na para dārān vā rāja putraḥ abhimanyate
kasmāt sa daṇḍaka araṇye bhrūṇahā iva vivāsitaḥ
english: Has the fancy of the prince gone after the wife of another? For what reason has brother Rāma been banished?

sanskrit: अथ अस्य चपला माता तत् स्व कर्म यथा तथम्
तेन एव स्त्री स्वभावेन व्याहर्तुम् उपचक्रमे
transliteration: atha asya capalā mātā tat sva karma yathā tatham
tena eva strī svabhāvena vyāhartum upacakrame
english: Thereat his volatile mother, influenced by her feminine nature, related faithfully to him her own doings.
Thus asked by the magnanimous Bharata, Kaikeyi vainly pluming herself on her wisdom, joyfully said.

sanskrit: न ब्राह्मण धनम् किम्चिद्द् हृतम् रामेण कस्यचित्
कश्चिन् न आढ्यो दरिद्रः वा तेन अपापो विहिम्सितः
transliteration: na brāhmaṇa dhanam kimcidd hṛtam rāmeṇa kasyacit
kaścin na āḍhyo daridraḥ vā tena apāpo vihimsitaḥ

sanskrit: न रामः पर दारामः च चक्षुर्भ्याम् अपि पश्यति
मया तु पुत्र श्रुत्वा एव रामस्य एव अभिषेचनम्
transliteration: na rāmaḥ para dārāmaḥ ca cakṣurbhyām api paśyati
mayā tu putra śrutvā eva rāmasya eva abhiṣecanam

sanskrit: याचितः ते पिता राज्यम् रामस्य च विवासनम्
स स्व वृत्तिम् समास्थाय पिता ते तत् तथा अकरोत्
transliteration: yācitaḥ te pitā rājyam rāmasya ca vivāsanam
sa sva vṛttim samāsthāya pitā te tat tathā akarot

sanskrit: रामः च सह सौमित्रिः प्रेषितः सह सीतया
तम् अपश्यन् प्रियम् पुत्रम् मही पालो महा यशाः
transliteration: rāmaḥ ca saha saumitriḥ preṣitaḥ saha sītayā
tam apaśyan priyam putram mahī pālo mahā yaśāḥ
english: Thereupon, he, staying by his promise, did accordingly: Rāma has been banished along with Sumitrā's son and Sītā. Not seeing his beloved son, the illustrious lord of earth, stricken by grief on his account, has breathed his last.

sanskrit: त्वया तु इदानीम् धर्मज्ञ राजत्वम् अवलम्ब्यताम्
transliteration: tvayā tu idānīm dharmajña rājatvam avalambyatām

sanskrit: त्वत् कृते हि मया सर्वम् इदम् एवम् विधम् कृतम्
मा शोकम् मा च सम्तापम् धैर्यमाश्रय पुत्रक
transliteration: tvat kṛte hi mayā sarvam idam evam vidham kṛtam
mā śokam mā ca samtāpam dhairyamāśraya putraka

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु पितरम् वृत्तम् भ्रातरु च विवासितौ
transliteration: śrutvā tu pitaram vṛttam bhrātaru ca vivāsitau
english: Hearing of his father's death and the exile of his brothers, Bharata burning in grief, said these words.

sanskrit: किम् नुण्कार्यम् हतस्य इह मम राज्येन शोचतः
विहीनस्य अथ पित्रा च भ्रात्रा पितृ समेन च
transliteration: kim nuṇkāryam hatasya iha mama rājyena śocataḥ
vihīnasya atha pitrā ca bhrātrā pitṛ samena ca
english: Deprived of my father as well as my brother like to a father, what shall I bewailing them and undone by you do with the kingdom?

sanskrit: दुह्खे मे दुह्खम् अकरोर् व्रणे क्षारम् इव आदधाः
राजानम् प्रेत भावस्थम् कृत्वा रामम् च तापसम्
transliteration: duhkhe me duhkham akaror vraṇe kṣāram iva ādadhāḥ
rājānam preta bhāvastham kṛtvā rāmam ca tāpasam
english: You, like one throwing alkali on a sore, have, by bringing about the death of the king and making Rāma an ascetic, heaped grief on grief.

sanskrit: कुलस्य त्वम् अभावाय काल रात्रिर् इव आगता
अन्गारम् उपगूह्य स्म पिता मे न अवबुद्धवान्
transliteration: kulasya tvam abhāvāya kāla rātrir iva āgatā
angāram upagūhya sma pitā me na avabuddhavān
english: You have come like the fatal night for the destruction of this race. Not under-standing it, my father embraced live coal.
O you that have your gaze fixed on sin, it is through you that my sovereign has come by death; and that, O stainer of the line, this race has by your infatuation been deprived of its happiness.

sanskrit: त्वाम् प्राप्य हि पिता मे.द्य सत्यसन्धो महायशाः
transliteration: tvām prāpya hi pitā me.dya satyasandho mahāyaśāḥ
english: Having got you, my illustrious sire intent upon truth, king Dasaratha, afflicted by extreme sorrow, has departed this life.
Why has the king, my father, ever loving virtue, been deprived of life? Why has Rāma been banished; and wherefore has he gone to the woods?

sanskrit: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च पुत्र शोक अभिपीडिते
दुष्करम् यदि जीवेताम् प्राप्य त्वाम् जननीम् मम
transliteration: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca putra śoka abhipīḍite
duṣkaram yadi jīvetām prāpya tvām jananīm mama
english: Afflicted with grief for their son, even if Kausalya and Sumitrā live, it will be hard for them to do so in the presence of you, my mother.

sanskrit: ननु तु आर्यो अपि धर्म आत्मा त्वयि वृत्तिम् अनुत्तमाम्
वर्तते गुरु वृत्तिज्ञो यथा मातरि वर्तते
transliteration: nanu tu āryo api dharma ātmā tvayi vṛttim anuttamām
vartate guru vṛttijño yathā mātari vartate
english: Surely the noble and virtuous Råma, well knowing his duties towards his superiors, regards you as highly as he does his own mother.

sanskrit: तथा ज्येष्ठा हि मे माता कौसल्या दीर्घ दर्शिनी
त्वयि धर्मम् समास्थाय भगिन्याम् इव वर्तते
transliteration: tathā jyeṣṭhā hi me mātā kausalyā dīrgha darśinī
tvayi dharmam samāsthāya bhaginyām iva vartate
english: In the same way, my eldest mother, the farsighted Kausalyā, doing her duties by you, bears herself like a sister.

sanskrit: तस्याः पुत्रम् कृत आत्मानम् चीर वल्कल वाससम्
प्रस्थाप्य वन वासाय कथम् पापे न शोचसि
transliteration: tasyāḥ putram kṛta ātmānam cīra valkala vāsasam
prasthāpya vana vāsāya katham pāpe na śocasi
english: Why, O sinful one, having sent to the woods her magnanimous son, clad in bark, do you not grieve?

sanskrit: अपाप दर्शिनम् शूरम् कृत आत्मानम् यशस्विनम्
प्रव्राज्य चीर वसनम् किम् नु पश्यसि कारणम्
transliteration: apāpa darśinam śūram kṛta ātmānam yaśasvinam
pravrājya cīra vasanam kim nu paśyasi kāraṇam
english: Having exiled the famous and heroic Rāma seeing no sin, clad in bark, what benefit do you perceive as yours?

sanskrit: लुब्धाया विदितः मन्ये न ते अहम् राघवम् प्रति
तथा हि अनर्थो राज्य अर्थम् त्वया नीतः महान् अयम्
transliteration: lubdhāyā viditaḥ manye na te aham rāghavam prati
tathā hi anartho rājya artham tvayā nītaḥ mahān ayam
english: I deem that you did not know how very highly I regarded Rāghava; and therefore it is that you have brought this mighty calamity.

sanskrit: अहम् हि पुरुष व्याघ्राव् अपश्यन् राम लक्ष्मणौ
केन शक्ति प्रभावेन राज्यम् रक्षितुम् उत्सहे
transliteration: aham hi puruṣa vyāghrāv apaśyan rāma lakṣmaṇau
kena śakti prabhāvena rājyam rakṣitum utsahe
english: Not seeing those chiefs of men, Rāma and Lakşmaņa, by virtue of whose energy can I venture to rule the kingdom?

sanskrit: तम् हि नित्यम् महा राजो बलवन्तम् महा बलः
उअपाश्रितः अभूद् धर्म आत्मा मेरुर् मेरु वनम् यथा
transliteration: tam hi nityam mahā rājo balavantam mahā balaḥ
uapāśritaḥ abhūd dharma ātmā merur meru vanam yathā
english: The monarch was ever protected by that powerful one possessed of mighty energy, as Meru is protected by its forest.

sanskrit: सो अहम् कथम् इमम् भारम् महा धुर्य समुद्यतम्
दम्यो धुरम् इव आसाद्य सहेयम् केन च ओजसा
transliteration: so aham katham imam bhāram mahā dhurya samudyatam
damyo dhuram iva āsādya saheyam kena ca ojasā
english: Like a calf burdened with a load capable of being borne by a mighty ox, by what energy shall I bear this burden which was borne by an exceedingly strong person?

sanskrit: अथ वा मे भवेत् शक्तिर् योगैः बुद्धि बलेन वा
सकामाम् न करिष्यामि त्वाम् अहम् पुत्र गर्धिनीम्
transliteration: atha vā me bhavet śaktir yogaiḥ buddhi balena vā
sakāmām na kariṣyāmi tvām aham putra gardhinīm
english: And even if this strength be mine through yoga or vigour of intellect, I will not crown with success the hopes of you, proud of your son.

sanskrit: न मे विकाङ्खा जायेत त्यक्तुम् त्वाम् पापनिश्चयाम्
transliteration: na me vikāṅkhā jāyeta tyaktum tvām pāpaniścayām
english: Nor, had Rāma not always regarded you as his mother, would I hesitate to renounce you, whose heart has been set on sin.
O you that views unrighteousness, O you that have fallen off from the way of the good, how could such thoughts unworthy of our line, arise in your mind?

sanskrit: अस्मिन् कुले हि सर्वेषाम् ज्येष्ठो राज्येऽभिषिच्यते
transliteration: asmin kule hi sarveṣām jyeṣṭho rājye'bhiṣicyate
english: In this race, the eldest brother of al} is installed in the kingdom: the other brothers remain under him.

sanskrit: न हि मन्ये नृशसे त्वम् राजधर्ममवेक्षसे
गतिम् वा न विजानासि राजवृत्तस्य शाश्वतीम्
transliteration: na hi manye nṛśase tvam rājadharmamavekṣase
gatim vā na vijānāsi rājavṛttasya śāśvatīm
english: O fell one, you did not, I think, know the morality of kings, or the consequence that attends its faithful observance.
Of all the princes, the eldest is always installed as the king. Even this is the accepted principle of all sovereigns, specially the descendants of Ikşvāku.

But to-day the pride of character of those whose virtue was their sole concern,* and who shone in the character of their line, has been humbled through they instrumentality. *Another interpretation is;, Whose virtue is their sole protector.
And how, O highly exalted lady, O you that born in a royal race, could such reprehensible fatuity take possession of your senses?

sanskrit: न तु कामम् करिष्यामि तवाऽह्म् पापनिश्चये
transliteration: na tu kāmam kariṣyāmi tavā'hm pāpaniścaye
english: But, O you bent upon sin, I will by no means fulfil the wish of you by whom has been brought in the first instance this calamity calculated to end my existence.
Further, O sinless one, I will do this at present was to displease you: I will bring from the forest my brother dear to his relatives.
And having brought back Rāma, I will in a perfectly contented spirit, became the slave of that one of flaming energy.

sanskrit: प्रिय इतरैः वाक्य गणैअः तुदम्स् ताम्
शोक आतुरः च अपि ननाद भूयः
transliteration: priya itaraiḥ vākya gaṇaiaḥ tudams tām
śoka āturaḥ ca api nanāda bhūyaḥ
english: The high-souled Bharata afflicted (his mother) with multitudes of words causing pain; and distressed with grief, emitted sounds like to a lion in the cave of Mandāra.

sanskrit: ताम् तथा गर्हयित्वा तु मातरम् भरतः तदा
रोषेण महता आविष्टः पुनर् एव अब्रवीद् वचः
transliteration: tām tathā garhayitvā tu mātaram bharataḥ tadā
roṣeṇa mahatā āviṣṭaḥ punar eva abravīd vacaḥ
english: Having thus reproved his mother in great wrath, Bharata said again.

sanskrit: राज्यात् भ्रम्शस्व कैकेयि नृशम्से दुष्ट चारिणि
परित्यक्ता च धर्मेण मा मृतम् रुदती भव
transliteration: rājyāt bhramśasva kaikeyi nṛśamse duṣṭa cāriṇi
parityaktā ca dharmeṇa mā mṛtam rudatī bhava
english: Do you bear yourself from this kingdom, O heartless and wicked Kaikeyī. Having been lost to righteousness, do not you lament me dead.

sanskrit: किम् नु ते अदूषयद् राजा रामः वा भृश धार्मिकः
ययोः मृत्युर् विवासः च त्वत् कृते तुल्यम् आगतौ
transliteration: kim nu te adūṣayad rājā rāmaḥ vā bhṛśa dhārmikaḥ
yayoḥ mṛtyur vivāsaḥ ca tvat kṛte tulyam āgatau
english: What qualities of yours were taxed by the king or the exceedingly virtuous Rāma, that both of them simultaneously have come by death and exile respectively through your agency?

sanskrit: भ्रूणहत्याम् असि प्राप्ता कुलस्य अस्य विनाशनात्
कैकेयि नरकम् गच्च मा च भर्तुः सलोकताम्
transliteration: bhrūṇahatyām asi prāptā kulasya asya vināśanāt
kaikeyi narakam gacca mā ca bhartuḥ salokatām
english: O Kaikeyī, you have been guilty of homicide in consequence of the destruction of this race. Do you go to hell, never to the world attained by my father.

sanskrit: यत्त्वया हीदृशम् पापम् कृतम् घोरेण कर्मणा
transliteration: yattvayā hīdṛśam pāpam kṛtam ghoreṇa karmaṇā
english: Since, renouncing Rāma dear to all, you have committed this sin by your grim act and brought me into fear.

sanskrit: त्वत् कृते मे पिता वृत्तः रामः च अरण्यम् आश्रितः
अयशो जीव लोके च त्वया अहम् प्रतिपादितः
transliteration: tvat kṛte me pitā vṛttaḥ rāmaḥ ca araṇyam āśritaḥ
ayaśo jīva loke ca tvayā aham pratipāditaḥ
english: Through you has my father met with his end, and Rāma has taken refuge in the woods; and it is through you that I have come to ignominy among all creatures.

sanskrit: मातृ रूपे मम अमित्रे नृशम्से राज्य कामुके
न ते अहम् अभिभाष्यो अस्मि दुर्वृत्ते पति घातिनि
transliteration: mātṛ rūpe mama amitre nṛśamse rājya kāmuke
na te aham abhibhāṣyo asmi durvṛtte pati ghātini
english: O you enemy of mine in the guise of a mother! O fell one! O you that covetest the kingdom! do you not speak to me, O wicked wretch!

sanskrit: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च याः च अन्या मम मातरः
दुह्खेन महता आविष्टाः त्वाम् प्राप्य कुल दूषिणीम्
transliteration: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca yāḥ ca anyā mama mātaraḥ
duhkhena mahatā āviṣṭāḥ tvām prāpya kula dūṣiṇīm
english: O slayer of your husband! it is because of you, stainer of your race, that Kausalyā, Sumiträ, and other mothers of mine have been overwhelmed with a mighty sorrow.

sanskrit: न त्वम् अश्व पतेः कन्या धर्म राजस्य धीमतः
राक्षसी तत्र जाता असि कुल प्रध्वम्सिनी पितुः
transliteration: na tvam aśva pateḥ kanyā dharma rājasya dhīmataḥ
rākṣasī tatra jātā asi kula pradhvamsinī pituḥ

sanskrit: यत् त्वया धार्मिको रामः नित्यम् सत्य परायणः
वनम् प्रस्थापितः दुह्खात् पिता च त्रिदिवम् गतः
transliteration: yat tvayā dhārmiko rāmaḥ nityam satya parāyaṇaḥ
vanam prasthāpitaḥ duhkhāt pitā ca tridivam gataḥ

sanskrit: यत् प्रधाना असि तत् पापम् मयि पित्रा विना कृते
भ्रातृभ्याम् च परित्यक्ते सर्व लोकस्य च अप्रिये
transliteration: yat pradhānā asi tat pāpam mayi pitrā vinā kṛte
bhrātṛbhyām ca parityakte sarva lokasya ca apriye

sanskrit: कौसल्याम् धर्म सम्युक्ताम् वियुक्ताम् पाप निश्चये
कृत्वा कम् प्राप्स्यसे तु अद्य लोकम् निरय गामिनी
transliteration: kausalyām dharma samyuktām viyuktām pāpa niścaye
kṛtvā kam prāpsyase tu adya lokam niraya gāminī
english: O you of sinful ways, having separated the virtuous Kausalya (from her son), what world, O you that repairest to hell, shall be your portion?

sanskrit: किम् न अवबुध्यसे क्रूरे नियतम् बन्धु सम्श्रयम्
ज्येष्ठम् पितृ समम् रामम् कौसल्याय आत्म सम्भवम्
transliteration: kim na avabudhyase krūre niyatam bandhu samśrayam
jyeṣṭham pitṛ samam rāmam kausalyāya ātma sambhavam
english: Does you not, O tortuous one, know that that one sprung from Kucalya's, self, my eldest brother Räma, who is like a father to me, has ever been the refuge of his friends?

sanskrit: अन्ग प्रत्यन्गजः पुत्रः हृदयाच् च अपि जायते
तस्मात् प्रियतरः मातुः प्रियत्वान् न तु बान्धवः
transliteration: anga pratyangajaḥ putraḥ hṛdayāc ca api jāyate
tasmāt priyataraḥ mātuḥ priyatvān na tu bāndhavaḥ
english: A son born from all the limbs of his mother, comes out from her heart, and therefore it is that he is far dearer to his mother, albeit her friends are dear to her.* *Angapratyangaja: at., born from the limbs principal and minor. The commentator recounts the face, the breast, the abdomen, the hands and the feet as constituting the former; and eyes, fingers, etc., as the latter.

sanskrit: अन्यदा किल धर्मज्ञा सुरभिः सुर सम्मता
वहमानौ ददर्श उर्व्याम् पुत्रौ विगत चेतसौ
transliteration: anyadā kila dharmajñā surabhiḥ sura sammatā
vahamānau dadarśa urvyām putrau vigata cetasau
english: Once on a time, it is related by persons cognizant of morality, Surabhi regarded by the celestials, beheld two of her sons toiling on earth and seeming to be deprived of their senses.

sanskrit: ताव् अर्ध दिवसे श्रान्तौ दृष्ट्वा पुत्रौ मही तले
रुरोद पुत्र शोकेन बाष्प पर्याकुल ईक्षणा
transliteration: tāv ardha divase śrāntau dṛṣṭvā putrau mahī tale
ruroda putra śokena bāṣpa paryākula īkṣaṇā
english: And, when the day had been half spent, seeing her sons fatigued on earth, she stricken with grief for them, began to weep with tears flooding her eyes.

sanskrit: अधस्तात् व्रजतः तस्याः सुर राज्ञो महात्मनः
बिन्दवः पतिता गात्रे सूक्ष्माः सुरभि गन्धिनः
transliteration: adhastāt vrajataḥ tasyāḥ sura rājño mahātmanaḥ
bindavaḥ patitā gātre sūkṣmāḥ surabhi gandhinaḥ
english: And it came to pass that as the magnanimous sovereign of the celestials was passing below, her fine and fragrant tear drops fell on his person.

sanskrit: सुरभिम् मन्यते दृष्ट्वा भूयसीम् ताम् सुरेश्वरः
transliteration: surabhim manyate dṛṣṭvā bhūyasīm tām sureśvaraḥ
english: And that lord, Indra, also considered Surabhi of a person breathing a sacred odour, whose tears had dropped on his body, as the foremost being on earth.
Turning his eyes up, Śakra found Surabhi stationed in the sky, distressed and weeping in extreme anguish of spirit.

sanskrit: ताम् दृष्ट्वा शोक सम्तप्ताम् वज्र पाणिर् यशस्विनीम्
इन्द्रः प्रान्जलिर् उद्विग्नः सुर राजो अब्रवीद् वचः
transliteration: tām dṛṣṭvā śoka samtaptām vajra pāṇir yaśasvinīm
indraḥ prānjalir udvignaḥ sura rājo abravīd vacaḥ
english: Seeing that illustrious one burning in grief, the wielder of the thunder-bolt, Indra the lord of the celestials, waxing anxious, with joined hands said.

sanskrit: भयम् कच्चिन् न च अस्मासु कुतश्चित् विद्यते महत्
कुतः निमित्तः शोकः ते ब्रूहि सर्व हित एषिणि
transliteration: bhayam kaccin na ca asmāsu kutaścit vidyate mahat
kutaḥ nimittaḥ śokaḥ te brūhi sarva hita eṣiṇi
english: Is there any great danger in any quarter? Do you, O you that are intent on the welfare of all, say, whence is this grief of yours?

sanskrit: एवम् उक्ता तु सुरभिः सुर राजेन धीमता
पत्युवाच ततः धीरा वाक्यम् वाक्य विशारदा
transliteration: evam uktā tu surabhiḥ sura rājena dhīmatā
patyuvāca tataḥ dhīrā vākyam vākya viśāradā
english: Thus addressed by the intelligent king of the celestials, that one well skilled in speech, the sedate Surabhi answered.

sanskrit: शान्तम् पातम् न वः किम्चित् कुतश्चित् अमर अधिप
अहम् तु मग्नौ शोचामि स्व पुत्रौ विषमे स्थितौ
transliteration: śāntam pātam na vaḥ kimcit kutaścit amara adhipa
aham tu magnau śocāmi sva putrau viṣame sthitau
english: Auspiciousness, O lord of celestials ! No sin is yours. But I mourn my sons fallen into evil plight, having seen them lean, distressed, and burnt by the rays of the sun, Balivardas afflicted by the wicked-minded ploughman.

sanskrit: एतौ दृष्ट्वा कृषौ दीनौ सूर्य रश्मि प्रतापिनौ
अर्ध्यमानौ बली वर्दौ कर्षकेण सुर अधिप
transliteration: etau dṛṣṭvā kṛṣau dīnau sūrya raśmi pratāpinau
ardhyamānau balī vardau karṣakeṇa sura adhipa

sanskrit: मम कायात् प्रसूतौ हि दुह्खितौ भार पीडितौ
यौ दृष्ट्वा परितप्ये अहम् न अस्ति पुत्र समः प्रियः
transliteration: mama kāyāt prasūtau hi duhkhitau bhāra pīḍitau
yau dṛṣṭvā paritapye aham na asti putra samaḥ priyaḥ
english: Seeing those that have been born of my body, cast down and in trouble, I grieve: there is none that is dear like to a son.

sanskrit: यस्याः पुत्र सहस्त्रैस्तु कृत्स्नम् व्याप्तमिदम् जगत्
ताम् दृष्ट्वा रुदतीम् शक्रो न सुतान्मन्यते परम्
transliteration: yasyāḥ putra sahastraistu kṛtsnam vyāptamidam jagat
tām dṛṣṭvā rudatīm śakro na sutānmanyate param
english: Seeing her the whole earth is filled with whose sons by thousands, weeping, Indra understood that none is an object of greater affection than a son.

Even that one yielding whatever is asked, auspicious, crowned with the choicest virtues,। although having all natural functions, showing equal kindness to all, and of unequalled character, who maintain all creatures, she who has a thousand sons, grieves (for her sons). How can then Kausalyā carry on existence without Rāma?

sanskrit: किम् पुनर् या विना रामम् कौसल्या वर्तयिष्यति
transliteration: kim punar yā vinā rāmam kausalyā vartayiṣyati
english: Even that one yielding whatever is asked, auspicious, crowned with the choicest virtues,। although having all natural functions, showing equal kindness to all, and of unequalled character, who maintain all creatures, she who has a thousand sons, grieves (for her sons). How can then Kausalyā carry on existence without Rāma?

sanskrit: एक पुत्रा च साध्वी च विवत्सा इयम् त्वया कृता
तस्मात् त्वम् सततम् दुह्खम् प्रेत्य च इह च लप्स्यसे
transliteration: eka putrā ca sādhvī ca vivatsā iyam tvayā kṛtā
tasmāt tvam satatam duhkham pretya ca iha ca lapsyase
english: Chaste and having an only son, that lady has through you been separated from her son, (like a cow separated from her calf). For this, you will always have to suffer misery alike in this world and the next.

sanskrit: अहम् हि अपचितिम् भ्रातुः पितुः च सकलाम् इमाम्
वर्धनम् यशसः च अपि करिष्यामि न सम्शयः
transliteration: aham hi apacitim bhrātuḥ pituḥ ca sakalām imām
vardhanam yaśasaḥ ca api kariṣyāmi na samśayaḥ
english: I shall for my part completely minister to my brother and father, and shall without doubt, increase my fame.

sanskrit: स्वयम् एव प्रवेक्ष्यामि वनम् मुनि निषेवितम्
transliteration: svayam eva pravekṣyāmi vanam muni niṣevitam
english: Bringing hither the mighty-armed lord of Kosala endowed with immense strength, I myself will repair to the forest inhabited by ascetics.

sanskrit: न ह्यहम् पापसम्कल्पे पापे पापम् त्वया कृतम्
transliteration: na hyaham pāpasamkalpe pāpe pāpam tvayā kṛtam
english: O you that have delivered yourself over to iniquity, I, looked at by the citizens with their throats oppressed with the vapour grief, cannot bear this (burden of) sin heaped on my by you.

sanskrit: सा त्वमग्निम् प्रविश वा स्वयम् वा दण्डकान्विश
रज्जुम् बधान वा कण्ठे न हि तेऽन्यत्परायणम्
transliteration: sā tvamagnim praviśa vā svayam vā daṇḍakānviśa
rajjum badhāna vā kaṇṭhe na hi te'nyatparāyaṇam
english: Do you enter fire, or dive into Dandaka, or wound a cord round your neck: other desirable way there is none for you.
On Rāma having truth for prowess, obtaining the earth, I, my disgrace removed, shall be blest.

sanskrit: इति नागैव अरण्ये तोमर अन्कुश चोदितः
पपात भुवि सम्क्रुद्धो निह्श्वसन्न् इव पन्नगः
transliteration: iti nāgaiva araṇye tomara ankuśa coditaḥ
papāta bhuvi samkruddho nihśvasann iva pannagaḥ
english: Grieving thus, Bharata, like an elephant in the forest afflicted with a tomara or ankusa,* fell to the earth sighing like an enraged snake. *Names of instruments.

sanskrit: शची पतेः केतुर् इव उत्सव क्षये
transliteration: śacī pateḥ ketur iva utsava kṣaye
english: With his eyes reddened, and his cloth falling off, and his ornaments cast away, that subduer of foes, the king's son fallen on the earth, resembled a banner of Sakra after the festival is over.

sanskrit: राज्यम् न कामये जातु मन्त्रये नापि मातरम्
transliteration: rājyam na kāmaye jātu mantraye nāpi mātaram

english: I did not know the banishment of the magnanimous Rāma to the woods, or the exile of Sumitra's son; nor did I know how Sītā came to be banished.

sanskrit: कौसल्या शब्दम् आज्ञाय सुमित्राम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: kausalyā śabdam ājñāya sumitrām idam abravīt
english: As the high-souled Bharata was thus wailing, Kausalyā recognizing his voice spoke to Sumitra.

sanskrit: आगतः क्रूर कार्यायाः कैकेय्या भरतः सुतः
तम् अहम् द्रष्टुम् इच्चामि भरतम् दीर्घ दर्शिनम्
transliteration: āgataḥ krūra kāryāyāḥ kaikeyyā bharataḥ sutaḥ
tam aham draṣṭum iccāmi bharatam dīrgha darśinam
english: Come is Bharata, the son of that one of crooked ways. I am desirous of seeing the farsighted Bharata.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा सुमित्राम् सा विवर्णा मलिन अम्बरा
transliteration: evam uktvā sumitrām sā vivarṇā malina ambarā

sanskrit: स तु राम अनुजः च अपि शत्रुघ्न सहितः तदा
transliteration: sa tu rāma anujaḥ ca api śatrughna sahitaḥ tadā
english: Having said this to Sumitrā, that one emaciated and with a pallid countenance, trembling and almost deprived of sensation, went to where Bharata, was. And it came to pass that the king's son, Bharata, along with Śatrughna had just then by the way that led to the same, been proceeding to Kausalyā's quarter.

sanskrit: ततः शत्रुघ्न भरतौ कौसल्याम् प्रेक्ष्य दुह्खितौ
पर्यष्वजेताम् दुह्ख आर्ताम् पतिताम् नष्ट चेतनाम्
transliteration: tataḥ śatrughna bharatau kausalyām prekṣya duhkhitau
paryaṣvajetām duhkha ārtām patitām naṣṭa cetanām
english: Then Śatrughna and Bharata seeing the aggrieved Kausalyā, embraced the stricken and fallen lady wellnigh deprived of her senses. Thereupon, weeping from grief, the noble and intelligent Kausalyà exceedingly afflicted, embracing them as they indulged in sorrow, said to Bharata.

sanskrit: भरतम् प्रत्युवाच इदम् कौसल्या भृश दुह्खिता
transliteration: bharatam pratyuvāca idam kausalyā bhṛśa duhkhitā
english: Then Śatrughna and Bharata seeing the aggrieved Kausalyā, embraced the stricken and fallen lady wellnigh deprived of her senses. Thereupon, weeping from grief, the noble and intelligent Kausalyà exceedingly afflicted, embracing them as they indulged in sorrow, said to Bharata.

sanskrit: इदम् ते राज्य कामस्य राज्यम् प्राप्तम् अकण्टकम्
सम्प्राप्तम् बत कैकेय्या शीघ्रम् क्रूरेण कर्मणा
transliteration: idam te rājya kāmasya rājyam prāptam akaṇṭakam
samprāptam bata kaikeyyā śīghram krūreṇa karmaṇā
english: Thus have you, that had desired the kingdom, received it rid of its thorn. Alas! it has been speedily obtained through the crooked act of Kaikeyi.

sanskrit: प्रस्थाप्य चीर वसनम् पुत्रम् मे वन वासिनम्
कैकेयी कम् गुणम् तत्र पश्यति क्रूर दर्शिनी
transliteration: prasthāpya cīra vasanam putram me vana vāsinam
kaikeyī kam guṇam tatra paśyati krūra darśinī
english: What is the good that is perceived by Kaikeyi of tortuous sight in sending away my son clad in bark to the woods?

sanskrit: क्षिप्रम् माम् अपि कैकेयी प्रस्थापयितुम् अर्हति
हिरण्य नाभो यत्र आस्ते सुतः मे सुमहा यशाः
transliteration: kṣipram mām api kaikeyī prasthāpayitum arhati
hiraṇya nābho yatra āste sutaḥ me sumahā yaśāḥ
english: It behoves Kaikeyi to send me also speedily to where is staying my illustrious son furnished with a gold-gleaming navel.

sanskrit: अथवा स्वयम् एव अहम् सुमित्र अनुचरा सुखम्
अग्नि होत्रम् पुरः कृत्य प्रस्थास्ये यत्र राघवः
transliteration: athavā svayam eva aham sumitra anucarā sukham
agni hotram puraḥ kṛtya prasthāsye yatra rāghavaḥ
english: Or first performing the fire-sacrifice, I followed by Sumitrā, will myself happily seek the way by which Rāghava (has gone to the woods).

sanskrit: कामम् वा स्वयम् एव अद्य तत्र माम् नेतुम् अर्हसि
यत्र असौ पुरुष व्याघ्रः तप्यते मे तपः सुतः
transliteration: kāmam vā svayam eva adya tatra mām netum arhasi
yatra asau puruṣa vyāghraḥ tapyate me tapaḥ sutaḥ
english: Or it behoves you to yourself bring me to the place where that foremost of men, my son, is performing austerities.

sanskrit: इदम् हि तव विस्तीर्णम् धन धान्य समाचितम्
हस्ति अश्व रथ सम्पूर्णम् राज्यम् निर्यातितम् तया
transliteration: idam hi tava vistīrṇam dhana dhānya samācitam
hasti aśva ratha sampūrṇam rājyam niryātitam tayā
english: This spacious kingdom abounding in corn and wealth, and filled with elephants, horses, and cars, is yours, having been conferred on you (by Kaikeyi).
Thus reproached by many a harsh word, the sinless Bharata felt exceeding pain like to that produced by pricking a sore with a needle.

Exceedingly agitated, he fell at Kausalya's feet, lamenting much, and well nigh deprived of his Bharata then regained his consciousness, and with joined hands answered Kausalya lamenting thus and overcome with excess of sorrow, saying.

sanskrit: एवम् विलपमानाम् ताम् भरतः प्रान्जलिस् तदा
कौसल्याम् प्रत्युवाच इदम् शोकैः बहुभिर् आवृताम्
transliteration: evam vilapamānām tām bharataḥ prānjalis tadā
kausalyām pratyuvāca idam śokaiḥ bahubhir āvṛtām

sanskrit: आर्ये कस्मात् अजानन्तम् गर्हसे माम् अकिल्बिषम्
विपुलाम् च मम प्रीतिम् स्थिराम् जानासि राघवे
transliteration: ārye kasmāt ajānantam garhase mām akilbiṣam
vipulām ca mama prītim sthirām jānāsi rāghave
english: O noble lady, what for do you censure me who am without sin and who know nothing of this? You know that profuse is my delight in Rāghava.

sanskrit: कृता शास्त्र अनुगा बुद्धिर् मा भूत् तस्य कदाचन
सत्य सम्धः सताम् श्रेष्ठो यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: kṛtā śāstra anugā buddhir mā bhūt tasya kadācana
satya samdhaḥ satām śreṣṭho yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May the sense of him never follow scripture, that had approved the exile into the woods of that foremost of the good, the noble Rāma intent senses. on truth!

sanskrit: प्रैष्यम् पापीयसाम् यातु सूर्यम् च प्रति मेहतु
हन्तु पादेन गाम् सुप्ताम् यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: praiṣyam pāpīyasām yātu sūryam ca prati mehatu
hantu pādena gām suptām yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May such a person as had approved the exile to the woods of the noble one undergo servitude at the hands of the sinful, answer the calls of nature facing the Sun, and kick a sleeping cow with his feet!

sanskrit: कारयित्वा महत् कर्म भर्ता भृत्यम् अनर्थकम्
अधर्मः यो अस्य सो अस्याः तु यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: kārayitvā mahat karma bhartā bhṛtyam anarthakam
adharmaḥ yo asya so asyāḥ tu yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods come by the sin that is reaped by a master who withholds salary from servants after the ceremony is over!

sanskrit: ततः तु द्रुह्यताम् पापम् यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: tataḥ tu druhyatām pāpam yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May that one that had approved the exile of the noble Rāma to the woods, be guilty of the sin that is his that injures a sovereign engaged in ruling his subjects like sons!

sanskrit: बलि षड् भागम् उद्धृत्य नृपस्य अरक्षतः प्रजाः
अधर्मः यो अस्य सो अस्य अस्तु यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: bali ṣaḍ bhāgam uddhṛtya nṛpasya arakṣataḥ prajāḥ
adharmaḥ yo asya so asya astu yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May the person that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods, reap the sin of his that having taken a sixth pare of their incomes, does not protect his subjects!

sanskrit: सम्श्रुत्य च तपस्विभ्यः सत्रे वै यज्ञ दक्षिणाम्
ताम् विप्रलपताम् पापम् यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: samśrutya ca tapasvibhyaḥ satre vai yajña dakṣiṇām
tām vipralapatām pāpam yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods, come by the demerit that is his that denies Dakșiņās to ascetics in a sacrifice, after having promised them the same!

sanskrit: हस्ति अश्व रथ सम्बाधे युद्धे शस्त्र समाकुले
मा स्म कार्षीत् सताम् धर्मम् यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: hasti aśva ratha sambādhe yuddhe śastra samākule
mā sma kārṣīt satām dharmam yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May he that had approved the exile into the woods of the noble one, never discharge the duty of the good in the field thronged with elephants and horses and cars, and bristling with arms!

sanskrit: उपदिष्टम् सुसूक्ष्म अर्थम् शास्त्रम् यत्नेन धीमता
स नाशयतु दुष्ट आत्मा यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: upadiṣṭam susūkṣma artham śāstram yatnena dhīmatā
sa nāśayatu duṣṭa ātmā yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May the wicked wight that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods bring to naught the subtle scriptural knowledge which has been carefully taught him by his intelligent preceptor!
May that one that had approved the exile of the noble (Rāma) to the woods never behold the long-armed and broad-shouldered (Rāghava) resembling the Sun and the Moon in energy (on the throne)!

sanskrit: पायसम् कृसरम् चागम् वृथा सो अश्नातु निर्घृणः
गुरूमः च अपि अवजानातु यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: pāyasam kṛsaram cāgam vṛthā so aśnātu nirghṛṇaḥ
gurūmaḥ ca api avajānātu yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May that one void of aversion, that had approved of the exile of the noble one to the woods feed on Payasa, Krsara, and goat's flesh, which have not been offered in sacrifice; and may he insult his spiritual precept.
Or! May he that had approved the exile of the noble one to the woods touch a cow with his feet, revile his superiors, and injure his friends!
May that one of wicked soul that had approved of the exile of the noble one into the woods divulge any defects (of another's character) that have been communicated to him in strict confidence!
May he that had approved the exile of Rāma to the woods, never repay any good act, be ungrateful, abandoned by all, the object of universal execration.

sanskrit: पुत्रैः दारैः च भृत्यैः च स्व गृहे परिवारितः
स एको मृष्टम् अश्नातु यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: putraiḥ dāraiḥ ca bhṛtyaiḥ ca sva gṛhe parivāritaḥ
sa eko mṛṣṭam aśnātu yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May he that had approved of the exile into the woods of the noble one, eat alone in his home, although surrounded by sons and wives and servitors!
May he that haå approved of the exile of the noble one, die without obtaining wives worthy of him, without sons, without any good works performed!
May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods, never see his own offspring, and not attaining ripe age, may he mourn his wives!

sanskrit: राज स्त्री बाल वृद्धानाम् वधे यत् पापम् उच्यते
भृत्य त्यागे च यत् पापम् तत् पापम् प्रतिपद्यताम्
transliteration: rāja strī bāla vṛddhānām vadhe yat pāpam ucyate
bhṛtya tyāge ca yat pāpam tat pāpam pratipadyatām
english: And may he come by the sin that is reaped by slaying a king, a woman, a boy, or an old man, or by renouncing those who have claims on his maintenance!

sanskrit: लाक्षया मधुमाम्सेन लोहेन च विषेण च
transliteration: lākṣayā madhumāmsena lohena ca viṣeṇa ca
english: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods always feed his family with lac, honey, meat, iron, and poison!
May that one that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods, while flying from the engagement while it is waxing furious with the foe, come to be killed !
May he that had approved of the exile of the noble one into the woods, clad in tatters with a skuil in hand, like a madman range the earth abegging!

sanskrit: पाने प्रसक्तो भवतु स्त्रीष्वक्षेषु च नित्यशः
transliteration: pāne prasakto bhavatu strīṣvakṣeṣu ca nityaśaḥ
english: May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods, be always addicted to wine, to women, and to dice; and may he be swayed by lust, anger, etc!

sanskrit: यस्य धर्मे मनो भूयादधर्मम् स निषेवताम्
transliteration: yasya dharme mano bhūyādadharmam sa niṣevatām
english: May he that had approved of the exile of that noble one into the woods, never relish virtue, and go after unrighteousness; and may he shower his wealth on the unworthy!
May he that had approved the exile of the noble one into the woods, have his various accumulated riches by thousand carried off by robbers!

sanskrit: उभे सम्ध्ये शयानस्य यत् पापम् परिकल्प्यते
तच् च पापम् भवेत् तस्य यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: ubhe samdhye śayānasya yat pāpam parikalpyate
tac ca pāpam bhavet tasya yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May he that had approved of the exile into the woods of that noble one, come by the demerit that is his who sleeps during both the twilight's! May he reap the sin that is reaped by an incendiary or him that Leith with his preceptor's wife; or him that wrongs his friend!

sanskrit: यद् अग्नि दायके पापम् यत् पापम् गुरु तल्पगे
मित्र द्रोहे च यत् पापम् तत् पापम् प्रतिपद्यताम्
transliteration: yad agni dāyake pāpam yat pāpam guru talpage
mitra drohe ca yat pāpam tat pāpam pratipadyatām

sanskrit: देवतानाम् पितृऋणाम् च माता पित्रोस् तथैव च
मा स्म कार्षीत् स शुश्रूषाम् यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: devatānām pitṛṛṇām ca mātā pitros tathaiva ca
mā sma kārṣīt sa śuśrūṣām yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: May he that had approved the exile of that noble one into the woods, never serve the gods or the manes of the ancestors or his father and mother!

sanskrit: सताम् लोकात् सताम् कीर्त्याः सज् जुष्टात् कर्मणः तथा
भ्रश्यतु क्षिप्रम् अद्य एव यस्य आर्यो अनुमते गतः
transliteration: satām lokāt satām kīrtyāḥ saj juṣṭāt karmaṇaḥ tathā
bhraśyatu kṣipram adya eva yasya āryo anumate gataḥ
english: may he that had approved the exile of that noble one into the woods, be speedily shut out from the world of the good, from their fame, and from their acts!
May he that had approved the exile of that long armed and broad breasted one, renouncing the ministration of his mother, turn his thoughts to evil!

May he that had approved the exile of the noble one, becoming improved the exile of the noble one, becoming impoverished yet having to support a large family, and suffering from fever, be always miserable! an
May he that had approved the exile of that noble one render fruitless the hopes of poor people cherishing them and looking up (wistfully).

May he that had approved the exile into the woods of the noble one remaining (always) wicked, cruel and impure, leading unrighteous life and being in (continual) fear of his sovereign, maintain himself by deceit for ever and a day!
May that wicked person that had approved the exile into the woods of that noble one disregard his chaste wife remaining near, after she has performed her ablutions at the end of her season.
May that foolish person that had approved the exile of that noble one forsaking all pleasure in virtue, seek others wives, renouncing his own wedded with sacred rites!
May his that had approved the banishment into the woods of that noble one be the sin that is incurred by a Brāhmana that has rendered himself sonless.
May he that had approved the exile into the woods of that noble one come by the sin that attaches to a wine biber or one that administers poison to another!

sanskrit: बालवत्साम् च गाम् दोग्दु यस्यर्योऽनुमते गतः
transliteration: bālavatsām ca gām dogdu yasyaryo'numate gataḥ
english: May that one of befouled senses that had approved of the exile into the woods of that noble one disturb the worship of Brāhmaṇa and milch a cow that has a calf.
May he that had approved of the exile into the woods of the noble one bear the sin that is his that serves a thirsty soul with deceit.

May he that had approved the exile into the woods of that noble one reap the demerit of them that from devotion to their respective faiths wrangle from their own points of view, as well as that of them that listen to the disputation!

sanskrit: विहीनाम् पति पुत्राभ्याम् कौसल्याम् पार्थिव आत्मजः
एवम् आश्वसयन्न् एव दुह्ख आर्तः निपपात ह
transliteration: vihīnām pati putrābhyām kausalyām pārthiva ātmajaḥ
evam āśvasayann eva duhkha ārtaḥ nipapāta ha

sanskrit: तथा तु शपथैः कष्टैः शपमानम् अचेतनम्
भरतम् शोक सम्तप्तम् कौसल्या वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tathā tu śapathaiḥ kaṣṭaiḥ śapamānam acetanam
bharatam śoka samtaptam kausalyā vākyam abravīt
english: Then Kausalyā addressed the aggrieved Bharaia (well-nigh) deprived of his senses, swearing strong oaths, saying.

sanskrit: मम दुह्खम् इदम् पुत्र भूयः समुपजायते
शपथैः शपमानो हि प्राणान् उपरुणत्सि मे
transliteration: mama duhkham idam putra bhūyaḥ samupajāyate
śapathaiḥ śapamāno hi prāṇān uparuṇatsi me
english: O son, it grieves me more that you are afflicting my heart by taking oaths.

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या न चलितः धर्मात् आत्मा ते सह लक्ष्मणः
वत्स सत्य प्रतिज्ञो मे सताम् लोकान् अवाप्स्यसि
transliteration: diṣṭyā na calitaḥ dharmāt ātmā te saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
vatsa satya pratijño me satām lokān avāpsyasi
english: Lucky it is that graced with auspicious marks, you swerves not from virtue. My child, for this reason you will attain the regions of pious person, drawing into her lap Bharata attached to his brother, and embracing the mighty armed one, gave way to grief.

Lucky it is that graced with auspicious marks, you swerves not from virtue. My child, for this reason you will attain the regions of pious person, drawing into her lap Bharata attached to his brother, and embracing the mighty armed one, gave way to grief.

sanskrit: मोहाच् च शोक सम्रोधात् बभूव लुलितम् मनः
