english: And in that habitation, Bharata saw great heaps of dry dung of deer and buffaloes, gathered for preventing cold.
As he proceeded, the intelligent and mightyarmed Bharata with a cheerful heart remarked to Śatrughna and all the courtiers.

sanskrit: मन्ये प्राप्ता: स्म तं देशं भरद्वाजो यमब्रवीत्
transliteration: manye prāptā: sma taṃ deśaṃ bharadvājo yamabravīt
english: I conceive, we have reached the tract that was mentioned by Bharadvāja. Hard by this spot, I fancy, is the river Mandākini.
On high are barks set up by Lakşmaņa. Having to pass by the way at unusual hours, (Laksmana) has marked it with signs.
On the side of the hill is the way by which long-tusked elephants pass to and fro with vehemence, roaring at each other.
Here is seen the dense and dark smoke of that which the anchorets are ever anxious to preserve in the forest, fire.
Even here shall I with a delighted heart see that foremost of men, the noble Rāghava resembling a Maharși, ever engaged in serving his superiors.

sanskrit: अथ गत्वा मुहूर्तं तु चित्रकूटं स राघव:
transliteration: atha gatvā muhūrtaṃ tu citrakūṭaṃ sa rāghava:
english: Then going to Citrakuta, that descendant of Raghu, coming to the Mandakini, said to the men.

sanskrit: जनेन्द्रो निर्जनं प्राप्य धिङ्मे जन्म सजीवितम्
transliteration: janendro nirjanaṃ prāpya dhiṅme janma sajīvitam
english: That foremost of men in all the world, the lord of all, coming into seclusion, is in his yoga posture. O fie upon my birth and my life!

sanskrit: सर्वान् कामान् परित्यज्य वने वसति राघव:
transliteration: sarvān kāmān parityajya vane vasati rāghava:
english: For me, having come by misfortune, and renounced every comfort, the effulgent lord of men, Rāghava, is dwelling in the woods.
I shall be taxed of men on the score. To-day (first) pacifying him, I will fall at the feet of Rāma as well as of Sitã and Lakşmaņa.
Having thus bewailed, Dasaratha's son saw a splendid, charming, and holy dwelling in that forest, composed of leaves.

And Bharata beheld in Rāma's habitation a sacred structure made of leaves, covered with a profusion of Sāla, palm, and Aśvakarņa leaves; spread with soft Kuśa, like a dais in a sacrifice; adorned with bows resembling the iris, plaited on the back with gold, of mighty force, and capable of achieving arduous feets and destroying foes; and garnished with arrows in quivers, seeming like the rays of the sun, with flaming mouths, like to the Bhogavatī with serpents; and exceedingly beautified with golden sheaths and scimitars and shields spangled with gold and nice guana finger-fences decked with gold; inaccessible to foes like a lion's den to deer; and furnished with a spacious dais inclined on the north-east, with a fire flaming on it.

And Bharata beheld in Rāma's habitation a sacred structure made of leaves, covered with a profusion of Sāla, palm, and Aśvakarņa leaves; spread with soft Kuśa, like a dais in a sacrifice; adorned with bows resembling the iris, plaited on the back with gold, of mighty force, and capable of achieving arduous feets and destroying foes; and garnished with arrows in quivers, seeming like the rays of the sun, with flaming mouths, like to the Bhogavatī with serpents; and exceedingly beautified with golden sheaths and scimitars and shields spangled with gold and nice guana finger-fences decked with gold; inaccessible to foes like a lion's den to deer; and furnished with a spacious dais inclined on the north-east, with a fire flaming on it.

sanskrit: निरीक्ष्य स मुहूर्त्तं तु ददर्श भरतो गुरम्
transliteration: nirīkṣya sa muhūrttaṃ tu dadarśa bharato guram

english: And looking around, anon Bharata saw his superior Rāma seated in the cottage bearing a head of matted locks, clad in a black deer-skin, and having tattered cloth and bark for his garment. And he saw Råma seated like to a flame, with leonine shoulders, mighty arms, and eyes resembling lotuses, the righteous lord of this world bounded by the seas, saw the mightyarmed on like to the eternal Brahma, seated on a skin-seat on the ground along with Sītā and Lakş mana.
And seeing him, overwhelmed with grief and affliction, the righteous and graceful son of Kaikeyi, Bharata, rushed (towards him).
And soon as Bharata saw Rāma, he, exceedingly distressed, broke out into lamentations in words choked with sorrow. And incapable of holding himself in patience, he said.
That elder brother of mine, who (seated) in court should be surrounded by the subjects intent upon paying him homage, is now surrounded by wild deer.
He that used to adorn his person with attire worth many thousands (of things), engaged in observing morality, is clad in deer-skin.

sanskrit: अधारयद्यो विविधाश्चित्रा: सुमनसस्तदा सोऽयं जटाभारमिमं वहते राघव: कथम्
transliteration: adhārayadyo vividhāścitrā: sumanasastadā so'yaṃ jaṭābhāramimaṃ vahate rāghava: katham
english: Why does he that always wore variegated blossoms, Rāghava, bears this burthen of matted locks?
He who is worthy of acquiring religious merit by celebrating sacrifices according to the ordinance, is now following morality by afflicting his person.
How is the person of that one whose body used to be daubed with costly sandal, covered with dust.
It is for me that Rama, although deserving of comfort, has come by this misfortune. Wicked that I am, fie upon my life despised of men!
Thus lamenting in woeful guise, with the lotus of his countenance covered with sweat, Bharata coming at Rāma's feet, fell at them bewailing.
And inflamed with grief, the exceedingly powerful prince Bharata, having in distress of spirit uttered, O noble one, again said nothing.
And beholding the illustrious Rāma, Bharata with his utterance choked with emotion, exclaimed, O noble one, and was unable to say anything further.

Then Śatrughna also weeping paid homage unto the feet of Rāma. And shedding tears, Rāma embraced them both. Then as in the sky, the Sun and the Moon meet with śukra and Brhaspati, those two princes (Rāma and Laks mana) met with Sumantra and Guha in the forest.

sanskrit: तत: सुमन्त्रेण गुहेन चैव समीयतू राजसुतावरण्ये
transliteration: tata: sumantreṇa guhena caiva samīyatū rājasutāvaraṇye
english: Then Śatrughna also weeping paid homage unto the feet of Rāma. And shedding tears, Rāma embraced them both. Then as in the sky, the Sun and the Moon meet with śukra and Brhaspati, those two princes (Rāma and Laks mana) met with Sumantra and Guha in the forest.

And beholding those kings resembling leaders of elephant-herds met together in that mighty forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears. forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears.

sanskrit: ददर्श रामो दुर्दर्शं युगान्ते भास्करं यथा
transliteration: dadarśa rāmo durdarśaṃ yugānte bhāskaraṃ yathā

sanskrit: आघ्राय रामस्तं मूर्ध्नि परिष्वज्य च राघव:
transliteration: āghrāya rāmastaṃ mūrdhni pariṣvajya ca rāghava:

sanskrit: क्व नु ते ऽभूत् पिता तात यदरण्यं त्वमागत:
transliteration: kva nu te 'bhūt pitā tāta yadaraṇyaṃ tvamāgata:
english: Where was your father, child, that you have come to the forest? It certainly behoves you not to come to the forest while he is living.
Ah! I see you come from far after a long time. Why, my child, have you come to this gloomy forest?

sanskrit: कच्चिन्न दीन: सहसा राजा लोकान्तरं गत:
transliteration: kaccinna dīna: sahasā rājā lokāntaraṃ gata:
english: Is the king alive, my child, seeing that you have come hither; or, afflicted with grief, has he suddenly gone to the other world?

sanskrit: कच्चित् सौम्य न ते राज्यं भ्रष्टं बालस्य शाश्वतम्
transliteration: kaccit saumya na te rājyaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ bālasya śāśvatam
english: O mild one, child that you are, your kingdom ever yours has not been wrested from you? And, O you having truth for prowess, do you, my child, minister to our sire?
Is that truthful one, that performer of Rajasüya and Aśvamedha, ever devoted to righteousness, king Dasaratha, well?

sanskrit: स कच्चिद् ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् धर्मनित्यो महाद्युति:
transliteration: sa kaccid brāhmaṇo vidvān dharmanityo mahādyuti:
english: My child, is that exceedingly effulgent and learned Brāhmaṇa ever steady in morality, the priest of the Iksvākus, duly honoured?

sanskrit: सा तात कच्चित्कौसल्या सुमित्रा च प्रजावती
सुखिनी कच्चिदार्य्या च देवी नन्दति कैकयी
transliteration: sā tāta kaccitkausalyā sumitrā ca prajāvatī
sukhinī kaccidāryyā ca devī nandati kaikayī
english: And, my child, are Kausalyā, and Sumitrā having a son, in happiness? And is the noble Kaikeyi in spirits?

And is that one, sprung from a mighty line, humble and versed in various lore, your priest, who performs every ceremony, who bears no ill will, and whose gaze is ever fixed upon our welfare, honoured?

sanskrit: हुतं च होष्यमाणं च काले वेदयते सदा
transliteration: hutaṃ ca hoṣyamāṇaṃ ca kāle vedayate sadā
english: Do intelligent and sincere people cognizant of the rules, look after the sacrificial fire? And do they regularly inform you of the proper seasons for performing the fire-sacrifice?
Do you regard the deities, the ancestral manes, the preceptors like to predecessors, the physicians, the Brahmanas, and the servants?
And do not disregard the preceptor Sudhanvā versed in excellent arms whether inspired with mantras or not, and accomplished in the knowledge of polity?
And, my child, have you employed as your controlled, well-born, and understanding signs, who are like your own self?

sanskrit: मन्त्रो विजयमूलं हि राज्ञां भवति राघव
transliteration: mantro vijayamūlaṃ hi rājñāṃ bhavati rāghava
english: O descendant of Raghu, counsel well kept by clever councillors versed in lore, is the root of victory with kings.
You have not come under the sway of sleep? and you awake at the proper hour? And do you during the short hours revolve the means of acquiring wealth?

sanskrit: कच्चित्ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति
transliteration: kaccitte mantrito mantro rāṣṭraṃ na paridhāvati
english: And you did not take counsel either with yourself alone, or (on the other hand) with a multiplicity of counsellors? and your counsel does not range the kingdom (i.e. does not take air)?
O descendant of Raghu, having determined upon a course costing small effort but fraught with a mighty result, you set about it sharply and delay not?
Do the (auxiliary) kings know only those acts of yours that have been accomplished or those that are well nigh so, and not those that you intend to set yours hand to?

sanskrit: त्वया वा वा ऽमात्यैर्बुध्यते तात मन्त्रितम्
english: Do others through inference or appearances come at a knowledge of your counsels, although undivulged to others by yourself or your counsellors; and (do you and your ministers) attain to a knowledge of others' counsels?
And passing by a thousand dunces, do you set your heart on having a single wise man? In times of pecuniary stress, a wise man stands in excellent stead.
And although a king might be surrounded by a thousand or ten thousand fools, yet he can count upon no assistance (at their hands).
And a single able counsellor, intelligent, heroic, and sagacious, bring great prosperity upon a king or a prince.
And, my child, do you employ the best servants upon the best offices, the middling upon middling, and the worst upon the worst?
And did you employ upon the most worthy offices counsellors who are above bribery, who have served your father and grand-father, and who are pure?
And do the subjects visited with condign, punishment, as well as the ministers, disregard you, O son of Kaikeyi?
Do the priests scorn you like a fallen one, even as females do those lascivious folks who use force towards the former?

sanskrit: शूरमैश्वर्यकामं च यो न हन्ति स वध्यते
transliteration: śūramaiśvaryakāmaṃ ca yo na hanti sa vadhyate
english: He that does not slay a physician skilled in ways and means, a servant given to enlisting the sympathies of his fellow-servants against his master, or a hero that covets riches, is slain (by them).
And had you chosen for your general one that is confident, is endowed with intelligence and fortitude, sprung in a respectable race, and attached and able?
And do you practically honour your foremost warriors possessed of prowess, who have already given evidence of their manliness?

sanskrit: कच्चिद्बलस्य भक्तं च वेतनं च यथोचितम्
transliteration: kaccidbalasya bhaktaṃ ca vetanaṃ ca yathocitam
english: And do you at the proper time grant your soldiers what you should, provision and pay; and do not delay in doing this?

sanskrit: भर्त्तु: कुप्यन्ति दुष्यन्ति सो ऽनर्थ: सुमहान् स्मृत:
transliteration: bharttu: kupyanti duṣyanti so 'nartha: sumahān smṛta:
english: If the proper time for granting provision and pay be passed, the servants get wroth with their master and tax him; and great is the evil that springs herefrom.
And are the principal descendants of our race attached to you; and are they, when enlisted on your side with concentrated minds, ready to lay down their lives?
O Bharata, are your spies persons coming from the provinces, and learned, upright, endowed with presence of mind, representing the truth, and possessed of wisdon?

And do you acquire intelligence of the expedients, eighteen* in respect of others, and fifteen in respect of the own self, by means of every three spies appointed in connection with each of these expedients, men quite ignorant of each other's counsels? *1. Minister. 2. Priest. 3. Heir-apparent. 4. General. 5. Warder. 6. Gatekeeper of the inner-apartment. 7. Jailer. 8. Treasurer. 9. Conveyer of the royal orders. 10. Pleaders. 11. Judges. 12. Members of the council. 13. Distributor of pay and provision to the army. 14. Journeymen. 15. Justice of the peace. 16. Protector of the frontiers of the kingdom. 17. Magistrate. 18. Guards of rivers, hills, and fortresses.
And do you not contemn those. weak ones that, O destroyer of your. foes, having been expelled, have come again (to you)?

And, my child, you did not minister to atheistical Brāhmaṇas? These childish persons proud of their learning are only fit for bringing evils upon others. While there are excellent scriptures, these people of subtle intellects, having acquired a knowledge of dialectics, speak vanities.

And, my child, you did not minister to atheistical Brāhmaṇas? These childish persons proud of their learning are only fit for bringing evils upon others. While there are excellent scriptures, these people of subtle intellects, having acquired a knowledge of dialectics, speak vanities.
And do agriculturists and cow herds find favour in your sight? And remaining in their respective vocations, do they enjoy happiness?

sanskrit: रक्ष्या हि राज्ञा धर्मेण सर्वे विषयवासिन:
transliteration: rakṣyā hi rājñā dharmeṇa sarve viṣayavāsina:
english: And do you maintain them by securing to them what they wish for and removing from them what they wish away? All the dwellers in his dominions should be protected by the king.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्न श्रद्दधास्यासां कच्चिद् गुह्यं न भाषसे
transliteration: kaccinna śraddadhāsyāsāṃ kaccid guhyaṃ na bhāṣase
english: And do you conciliate the females; and are they well protected by you? And do you not regard them; and do you not open to them your mind?
And are the woods where elephants breed, kept by you; and have you kine? And do you not foster mares and female-elephants?
And do you show yourself daily in the court, well robed? And rising in the morning, do you show yourself in the high-ways?
And do your servants boldly present themselves before you; or do they all keep away? A middle course contributes to their good fortune.
Are all the forts furnished with wealth, corn, arms water, machines, artisans, and bowmen?

sanskrit: अपात्रेषु न ते कच्चित्कोशो गच्छति राघव
transliteration: apātreṣu na te kaccitkośo gacchati rāghava
english: And are your incomings great and outgoings slender? And, O Raghu's descendant, you do not give away your coffers to the undeserving?
And did you spend your wealth in the interests of the deities, or the pitris, or the Brāhmaṇas who have come to you, or warriors, or friends?

If any respectable, pure-spirited and clean person happen to be accused by some one of theft or other crimes, do you from covetousness punish him without first having him tried by persons versed in scripture?
And, O best of men, is a thief, that has been caught, interrogated (as to his guilt), and found with the stolen property on his person, set free (by your men) from motives of gain.
And do your counsellors, o descendant of Raghu, accomplished in various lore, uninfluenced by greed, consider the conduct of both the rich and the poor involved in peril?

O son of the Raghu race, the tears of those who have been falsely charged with any offence, (and who have failed to obtain justice), dropping, destroy the sons as well as the beasts of the ruler that minds his own comfort only.
And do you with these three, gifts, mind and word, try to win over aged people, boys, physicians, and the principal ones?
And do you salute spiritual preceptors, aged persons, ascetics, gods, guests, Caityas, emancipated one, and Brāhmaṇās?

sanskrit: कच्चिदर्थेन वा धर्ममर्थं धर्मेण वा पुन:
उभौ वा प्रीतिलोभेन कामेन च न बाधसे
transliteration: kaccidarthena vā dharmamarthaṃ dharmeṇa vā puna:
ubhau vā prītilobhena kāmena ca na bādhase
english: And you do not oppose righteousness by interest, or interest by virtue, or both by desire, intent on gratifying the senses?

sanskrit: कच्चिदर्थं च धर्मं च कामं च जयतां वर
विभज्य काले कालज्ञ सर्वान् वरद सेवसे
transliteration: kaccidarthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca jayatāṃ vara
vibhajya kāle kālajña sarvān varada sevase
english: And, O foremost of conquerors, do you, O you cognisant of time, in season resorting to interest, desire, and virtue respectively, attain them, O bestower of boons?
And do Brāhmaṇas versed in all religious lore and knowing interest, together with the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces wish for your happiness, O highly wise one?

Atheism, untruthfulness, inattention, anger, procrastination, companionship with evil persons, indolence, gratification of the senses, consultation with a single person concerning the needs of a kingdom, taking counsel with those that are cognisant of evils alone, omission to take in hand a task that has been decided upon, divulgence of counsel, non-commencement of a course in the morning, and marching against all the foes at one and the same time, have you eschewed these ten and four faults?

Atheism, untruthfulness, inattention, anger, procrastination, companionship with evil persons, indolence, gratification of the senses, consultation with a single person concerning the needs of a kingdom, taking counsel with those that are cognisant of evils alone, omission to take in hand a task that has been decided upon, divulgence of counsel, non-commencement of a course in the morning, and marching against all the foes at one and the same time, have you eschewed these ten and four faults?

sanskrit: दश पञ्च चतुर्वर्गान् सप्तवर्गं च तत्त्वत:
transliteration: daśa pañca caturvargān saptavargaṃ ca tattvata:

english: And, O wise one, do you, as laid down in the ordinance, take counsel, severally and in a body with three or four men?

sanskrit: कच्चित्ते सफला वेदा: कच्चित्ते सफला: क्रिया:
कच्चित्ते सफला दारा: कच्चित्ते सफलं श्रुतम्
transliteration: kaccitte saphalā vedā: kaccitte saphalā: kriyā:
kaccitte saphalā dārā: kaccitte saphalaṃ śrutam
english: And do you observe the Vedas? And do you perceive the fruit of your acts? And have your wives borne children? And has your knowledge of scripture borne fruit?
O descendant of Raghu, is your intellect going the way that I have indicated above? This course is conducive to long life, and fame; and virtue, desire and interest.

sanskrit: यां वृत्तिं वर्त्तते तातो यां च न: प्रपितामहा:
तां वृत्तिं वर्त्तसे कच्चिद्या च सत्पथगा शुभा
transliteration: yāṃ vṛttiṃ varttate tāto yāṃ ca na: prapitāmahā:
tāṃ vṛttiṃ varttase kaccidyā ca satpathagā śubhā
english: O child, are you following the course that was followed by our ancestors? And are you maintaining the conduct that is excellent and passes along pious ways?

sanskrit: कच्चित् स्वादु कृतं भोज्यमेको नाश्नासि राघव
transliteration: kaccit svādu kṛtaṃ bhojyameko nāśnāsi rāghava
english: And, O son of Raghu, you do not alone partake of sapid meats yourself alone? And do you share them with those friends who expect it?

sanskrit: राजा तु धर्मेण हि पालयित्वा महामतिर्दण्डधर: प्रजानाम्
अवाप्य कृत्स्नां वसुधां यथावदितश्च्युत: स्वर्गमुपैति विद्वान्
transliteration: rājā tu dharmeṇa hi pālayitvā mahāmatirdaṇḍadhara: prajānām
avāpya kṛtsnāṃ vasudhāṃ yathāvaditaścyuta: svargamupaiti vidvān
english: The learned king ruling (all) righteously, that chastiser of the subjects, the monarch attaining duly the entire earth, going away from hence, acquires the celestial regions.

sanskrit: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरत: प्रत्युवाच ह
transliteration: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā bharata: pratyuvāca ha

sanskrit: शाश्वतो ऽयं सदा धर्म्म: स्थितो ऽस्मासु नरर्षभ
ज्येष्ठपुत्रे स्थिते राजन्न कनीयान् नृपो भवेत्
transliteration: jyeṣṭhaputre sthite rājanna kanīyān nṛpo bhavet

sanskrit: स समृद्धां मया सार्द्धमयोध्यां गच्छ राघव
transliteration: sa samṛddhāṃ mayā sārddhamayodhyāṃ gaccha rāghava

sanskrit: राजानं मानुषं प्राहुर्देवत्वे स मतो मम
transliteration: rājānaṃ mānuṣaṃ prāhurdevatve sa mato mama

sanskrit: केकयस्थे च मयि तु त्वयि चारण्यमाश्रिते
दिवमार्यो गतो राजा यायजूक: सतां मत:
transliteration: kekayasthe ca mayi tu tvayi cāraṇyamāśrite

ahaṃ cāyaṃ ca śatrughna: pūrvameva kṛtodakau

transliteration: priyeṇa khalu dattaṃ hi pitṛlokeṣu rāghava

sanskrit: त्वया विहीनस्तव शोकरुग्णस्त्वां संस्मरन्नस्तमित: पिता ते
transliteration: tvayā vihīnastava śokarugṇastvāṃ saṃsmarannastamita: pitā te

sanskrit: प्रगृह्य बाहू रामो वै पुष्पिताग्रो यथा द्रुम:

transliteration: pragṛhya bāhū rāmo vai puṣpitāgro yathā druma:
vane paraśunā kṛttastathā bhuvi papāta ha

transliteration: rudanta: saha vaidehyā siṣicu: salilena vai

sanskrit: स राम: स्वर्गतं श्रुत्वा पितरं पृथिवीपतिम्
transliteration: sa rāma: svargataṃ śrutvā pitaraṃ pṛthivīpatim

sanskrit: किं करिष्याम्ययोध्यायां ताते दिष्टां गतिं गते
transliteration: kiṃ kariṣyāmyayodhyāyāṃ tāte diṣṭāṃ gatiṃ gate

transliteration: kiṃ nu tasya mayā kāryyaṃ durjātena mahātmana:
yo mṛto mama śokena mayā cāpi na saṃskṛta:

transliteration: ko nu śāsiṣyati punastāte lokāntaraṃ gate

sanskrit: पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन्
transliteration: purā prekṣya suvṛttaṃ māṃ pitā yānyāha sāntvayan

उवाच लक्ष्मणं तत्र दु:खितो दु:खितं वच:
transliteration: sāntvayitvā tu tāṃ rāmo rudantīṃ janakātmajām

transliteration: idaṃ bhuṅkṣva mahārāja prīto yadaśanā vayam

transliteration: atha vāsān parityajya taṃ sarve 'bhimukhā: svanam

transliteration: tathā puṃskokilā: krauñcā visaṃjñā bhejire diśa:

sanskrit: आसीनं स्थण्डिले रामं ददर्श सहसा जन:
transliteration: āsīnaṃ sthaṇḍile rāmaṃ dadarśa sahasā jana:

sanskrit: स तत्र कांच्चित् परिषस्वजे नरान्नराश्च केचित्तु तमभ्यवादयन्
चकार सर्वान् सवयस्य बान्धवान् यथार्हमासाद्य तदा नृपात्मज:

cakāra sarvān savayasya bāndhavān yathārhamāsādya tadā nṛpātmaja:

गुहा गिरीणां च दिशश्च सन्ततं मृदङ्गघोषप्रतिम: प्रशुश्रुवे
transliteration: sa tatra teṣāṃ rudatāṃ mahātmanāṃ bhuvaṃ ca khaṃ cānuninādayan svana:
guhā girīṇāṃ ca diśaśca santataṃ mṛdaṅgaghoṣapratima: praśuśruve

sanskrit: वसिष्ठ: पुरत: कृत्वा दारान् दशरथस्य च
transliteration: vasiṣṭha: purata: kṛtvā dārān daśarathasya ca

transliteration: vane prākkevalaṃ tīrthaṃ ye te nirviṣayīkṛtā:

sanskrit: जघन्यमपि ते पुत्र: कृतवान्न तु गर्हित:
transliteration: jaghanyamapi te putra: kṛtavānna tu garhita:

transliteration: taṃ bhūmau piturārtena nyastaṃ rāmeṇa vīkṣya sā

sanskrit: अतो दु:खतरं लोके न किञ्चित् प्रतिभाति मा
transliteration: ato du:khataraṃ loke na kiñcit pratibhāti mā

sanskrit: कथं दु:खेन हृदयं न स्फोटति सहस्रधा
transliteration: kathaṃ du:khena hṛdayaṃ na sphoṭati sahasradhā

transliteration: śrutistu khalviyaṃ satyā laukikī pratibhāti mā
english: O mighty monarch! do you well pleased feed on this, which we also live upon. That which is the fare of an individual, is also the fare of his divinities.

transliteration: saumitrirapi tā: sarvā: māta': samprekṣya du:khita:

sanskrit: यथा रामे तथा तस्मिन् सर्वा ववृतिरे स्त्रिय:
transliteration: yathā rāme tathā tasmin sarvā vavṛtire striya:

sanskrit: तां परिष्वज्य दु:खार्त्तां माता दुहितरं यथा
transliteration: tāṃ pariṣvajya du:khārttāṃ mātā duhitaraṃ yathā

sanskrit: रामपत्नी कथं दु:खं सम्प्राप्ता निर्जने वने
transliteration: rāmapatnī kathaṃ du:khaṃ samprāptā nirjane vane

sanskrit: मुखं ते प्रेक्ष्य मां शोको दहत्यग्निरिवाश्रयम् भृशं मनसि वैदेहि व्यसनारणिसम्भव:
transliteration: mukhaṃ te prekṣya māṃ śoko dahatyagnirivāśrayam bhṛśaṃ manasi vaidehi vyasanāraṇisambhava:

sanskrit: प्रगृह्य पादौ सुसमृद्धतेजस: सहैव तेनोपविवेश राघव:
transliteration: pragṛhya pādau susamṛddhatejasa: sahaiva tenopaviveśa rāghava:

sanskrit: उपोपविष्टस्तु तथा स वीर्यवांस्तपस्विवेषेण समीक्ष्य राघवम्
श्रिया ज्वलन्तं भरत: कृताञ्जलिर्यथा महेन्द्र: प्रयत: प्रजापतिम्
transliteration: upopaviṣṭastu tathā sa vīryavāṃstapasviveṣeṇa samīkṣya rāghavam
śriyā jvalantaṃ bharata: kṛtāñjaliryathā mahendra: prayata: prajāpatim

sanskrit: किमेष वाक्यं भरतो ऽद्य राघवं प्रणम्य सत्कृत्य च साधु वक्ष्यति
इतीव तस्यार्यजनस्य तत्त्वतो बभूव कौतूहलमुत्तमं तदा
transliteration: kimeṣa vākyaṃ bharato 'dya rāghavaṃ praṇamya satkṛtya ca sādhu vakṣyati
itīva tasyāryajanasya tattvato babhūva kautūhalamuttamaṃ tadā

sanskrit: स राघव: सत्यधृतिश्च लक्ष्मणो महानुभवो भरतश्च धार्मिक:
वृता: सुहृद्भिश्च विरेजुरध्वरे यथा सदस्यै: सहितास्त्रयो ऽग्नय:
transliteration: sa rāghava: satyadhṛtiśca lakṣmaṇo mahānubhavo bharataśca dhārmika:
vṛtā: suhṛdbhiśca virejuradhvare yathā sadasyai: sahitāstrayo 'gnaya:

sanskrit: तं तु राम: समाज्ञाय भ्रातरं गुरुवत्सलम्
transliteration: taṃ tu rāma: samājñāya bhrātaraṃ guruvatsalam

sanskrit: आर्य्यं तात: परित्यज्य कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम्
transliteration: āryyaṃ tāta: parityajya kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram

transliteration: striyā niyukta: kaikeyyā mama mātrā parantapa

sanskrit: इमा: प्रकृतय: सर्वा विधवा मातरश्च या:
transliteration: imā: prakṛtaya: sarvā vidhavā mātaraśca yā:

sanskrit: तदानुपूर्व्या युक्तं च युक्तं चात्मनि मानद
राज्यं प्राप्नुहि धर्मेण सकामान् सुहृद: कुरु
transliteration: tadānupūrvyā yuktaṃ ca yuktaṃ cātmani mānada
rājyaṃ prāpnuhi dharmeṇa sakāmān suhṛda: kuru

sanskrit: एभिश्च सचिवै: सार्द्धं शिरसा याचितो मया
transliteration: ebhiśca sacivai: sārddhaṃ śirasā yācito mayā

sanskrit: वयमस्य यथा लोके सङ्ख्याता: सौम्य साधुभि:
transliteration: vayamasya yathā loke saṅkhyātā: saumya sādhubhi:

sanskrit: व्यादिश्य च महातेजा दिवं दशरथो गत:
transliteration: vyādiśya ca mahātejā divaṃ daśaratho gata:

sanskrit: स च प्रमाणं धर्मात्मा राजा लोकगुरुस्तव
transliteration: sa ca pramāṇaṃ dharmātmā rājā lokagurustava

sanskrit: उपभोक्ष्ये त्वहं दत्तं भागं पित्रा महात्मना
transliteration: upabhokṣye tvahaṃ dattaṃ bhāgaṃ pitrā mahātmanā

sanskrit: तदेव मन्ये परमात्मनो हितं न सर्वलोकेश्वरभावमप्यहम्
transliteration: tadeva manye paramātmano hitaṃ na sarvalokeśvarabhāvamapyaham

english: As those foremost of persons surrounded by their friends indulged in lamentations, the night passed away in grief. On the night being succeeded by an auspicious morning, those brothers surrounded by their friends, having performed Homa and Japa on the Mandākinī, returned to Rāma.

As those foremost of persons surrounded by their friends indulged in lamentations, the night passed away in grief. On the night being succeeded by an auspicious morning, those brothers surrounded by their friends, having performed Homa and Japa on the Mandākinī, returned to Rāma.
And sitting silent, no one said anything. Then Bharata addressed Rāma in the midst of those friends, saying.

sanskrit: सान्त्विता मामिका माता दत्तं राज्यमिदं मम
transliteration: sāntvitā māmikā mātā dattaṃ rājyamidaṃ mama
english: My mother was (first) pacified (by grant to the kingdom.) The kingdom is (now) mine. I grant the same to you. Do you enjoy the kingdom rid of its thorns.
Like to a dyke forced by a torrent during the rains, this mighty monarchy is difficult of being protected save by you.

sanskrit: अनुगन्तुं न शक्तिर्मे गतिं तव महीपते
transliteration: anugantuṃ na śaktirme gatiṃ tava mahīpate
english: As a mule is incapable of imitating the course of a horse, or as birds, that of Tarksya, I, O Lord of earth, lack the strength to imitate you.

sanskrit: राम तेन तु दुर्जीवं य: परानुपजीवति
transliteration: rāma tena tu durjīvaṃ ya: parānupajīvati
english: O Rāma, ever happy is the life of him that others depend upon for subsistence: unhappy is the life of the person that depends upon others for support.

sanskrit: यथा तु रोपितो वृक्ष: पुरुषेण विवर्द्धित:
transliteration: yathā tu ropito vṛkṣa: puruṣeṇa vivarddhita:

sanskrit: स यथा पुष्पितो भूत्वा फलानि न विदर्शयेत्
स तां नानुभवेत्प्रीतिं यस्य हेतो: प्ररोपित:
transliteration: sa yathā puṣpito bhūtvā phalāni na vidarśayet
sa tāṃ nānubhavetprītiṃ yasya heto: praropita:

sanskrit: यदि त्वमस्मान् वृषभो भर्त्ता भृत्यान्न शाधि हि
transliteration: yadi tvamasmān vṛṣabho bharttā bhṛtyānna śādhi hi

english: Let the principal orders, O monarch, behold you, represser of foes, established in the kingdom, like the powerful sun himself.

sanskrit: तवा ऽनुयाने काकुत्स्थ मत्ता नर्दन्तु कुञ्जरा:
english: O Kākutstha, let mad elephants roar, with the view of following you; and let the women of the inner apartments with concentrated rainds utter jubilation.
On hearing the words of Bharata, who was beseeching Rāma, many of the citizens expressed their approbation by exclaiming, “Excellent well!"
Seeing the illustrious Bharata aggrieved and engaged in lamentation, the calm and considerate Rāma consoled him, saying.
No creature is endowed with the power of exercising any control over the course of events, man has no independent status (in nature).

The Destroyer draw him both here and hereafter. Those that increase, are destined to deteriorate; those that go upward, ultimately fall, those that come together, separate in the end; and life at length meet with death.
As a ripe fruit has no other fear than fall, so man who is born, has no other fear than death.
Even as a stout-pillared edifice, getting dilapidated, waxes weak, so men coming under the sway of decrepitude and death, get enfeebled.

sanskrit: अत्येति रजनी या तु सा न प्रतिनिवर्त्तते
transliteration: atyeti rajanī yā tu sā na pratinivarttate
english: A night that has gone by, does not return, as the full Yamunā, when she has entered the ocean, does not come back.
In this world, days and nights pass away with creatures, and speedily impair their lives, even as in summer the rays (of the sun) (dry up) the waters.

sanskrit: आयुस्ते हीयते यस्य स्थितस्य च गतस्य च
transliteration: āyuste hīyate yasya sthitasya ca gatasya ca
english: Do you therefore deplore yourself. Why do you lament any thing else? Every one's life is decreasing, whether he sits or moves.
Death goes with one, sits down with one, and after having gone a long way, returns with one.

sanskrit: जरया पुरुषो जीर्ण: किं हि कृत्वा प्रभावयेत्
transliteration: jarayā puruṣo jīrṇa: kiṃ hi kṛtvā prabhāvayet
english: The person is filled with folds in the skin, the hair has grown hoary, the individual is enfeebled because of age, by doing what, can be prevent this?
People rejoice on the rising of the sun; they feel delighted at the approach of night, but they do not understand that their lives have (meanwhile) been shortened.
People are exhilarated at the commencement of a new season of novel fashion; creatures get their lives shortened at the change of season.

sanskrit: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे
transliteration: yathā kāṣṭhaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca sameyātāṃ mahārṇave
english: As on the mighty ocean, one piece of wood comes in contact with another; so, a person, having been in association with another, is separated from him in time. In this way, wives and sons and kindred and wealth, having been in association, go away; their separation is certain.

sanskrit: एवं भार्याश्च पुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च घनानि च
transliteration: evaṃ bhāryāśca putrāśca jñātayaśca ghanāni ca
english: As on the mighty ocean, one piece of wood comes in contact with another; so, a person, having been in association with another, is separated from him in time. In this way, wives and sons and kindred and wealth, having been in association, go away; their separation is certain.
There exists not one in this world that can change one's nature as received. A person lamenting a dead individual, has no power to prevent his own death.

sanskrit: यथा हि सार्थं गच्छन्तं ब्रूयात् कश्चित् पथि स्थित:
transliteration: yathā hi sārthaṃ gacchantaṃ brūyāt kaścit pathi sthita:

sanskrit: आत्मा सुखे नियोक्तव्य: सुखभाज: प्रजा: स्मृता:
transliteration: ātmā sukhe niyoktavya: sukhabhāja: prajā: smṛtā:

sanskrit: धूतपापो गत: स्वर्गं पिता न: पृथिवीपति:
transliteration: dhūtapāpo gata: svargaṃ pitā na: pṛthivīpati:
english: My child, our righteous sire, who, after having performed excellent and entire sacrifices, accompanied with Dakșiņās, has repaired to heaven, honoured of he good, should not be mourned.* *The N.W.P. text has seven additional lines here, wanting in the other texts:, “That lord of the earth, our father Dasaratha, has gone to heaven. On account of having adequately maintained his servants and governed his subjects, and virtuously given away wealth, our sire has gone to heaven. And by virtue of supremely excellent and desirable acts, and sacrifices accompanied with Dakşiņā, that master of this world, our father Dasaratha, has ascended heaven. And having celebrated many sacrifices and enjoyed luxuries, that lord of the earth, having attained a goodly age, has gone to heaven."
Having renounced his human frame wasted and worn out with age, our father has attained celestial state, which exists in the regions of Brahma.

sanskrit: स्वर्गं दशरथ: प्राप्त: पिता न: पृथिवीपति:
transliteration: svargaṃ daśaratha: prāpta: pitā na: pṛthivīpati:
english: My child, our righteous sire, who, after having performed excellent and entire sacrifices, accompanied with Dakșiņās, has repaired to heaven, honoured of he good, should not be mourned.* *The N.W.P. text has seven additional lines here, wanting in the other texts:, “That lord of the earth, our father Dasaratha, has gone to heaven. On account of having adequately maintained his servants and governed his subjects, and virtuously given away wealth, our sire has gone to heaven. And by virtue of supremely excellent and desirable acts, and sacrifices accompanied with Dakşiņā, that master of this world, our father Dasaratha, has ascended heaven. And having celebrated many sacrifices and enjoyed luxuries, that lord of the earth, having attained a goodly age, has gone to heaven."

sanskrit: स न शोच्य: पिता तात: स्वर्गत: सत्कृत: सताम्
transliteration: sa na śocya: pitā tāta: svargata: satkṛta: satām

sanskrit: स जीर्णं मानुषं देहं परित्यज्य पिता हि न:
transliteration: sa jīrṇaṃ mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ parityajya pitā hi na:

sanskrit: तं तु नैवंविध: कश्चित् प्राज्ञ: शोचितुमर्हति
transliteration: taṃ tu naivaṃvidha: kaścit prājña: śocitumarhati

sanskrit: स स्वस्थो भव माशोचीर्यात्वा चावस तां पुरीम्
तथा पित्रा नियुक्तो ऽसि वशिना वदतां वर
transliteration: sa svastho bhava māśocīryātvā cāvasa tāṃ purīm
tathā pitrā niyukto 'si vaśinā vadatāṃ vara

sanskrit: न मया शासनं तस्य त्यक्तुं न्याय्यमरिन्दम
तत् त्वयापि सदा मान्यं स वै बन्धु: स न: पिता
transliteration: na mayā śāsanaṃ tasya tyaktuṃ nyāyyamarindama
tat tvayāpi sadā mānyaṃ sa vai bandhu: sa na: pitā
english: O subduer foes, it is not proper for me to pass by his orders. So they are also worthy of being honoured by you. He is our friend and father.
O descendant of Raghu, that mandate of our righteous father, acceptable to me, will I obey by abiding in the woods.
O foremost of men, (good in the next world is capable of being attained by an honest and pious person crowned with sterling virtues, ever following his superiors.

sanskrit: निशाम्य तु शुभं वृत्तं पितुर्दशरथस्य न:
transliteration: niśāmya tu śubhaṃ vṛttaṃ piturdaśarathasya na:
english: O best of men, thinking that our father Dasaratha has attained excellent state, do you, resorting to all noble qualities, seek your welfare in the next world.
Having said these significant words to his younger brother, with the view of making him obey the injuctions of their father, that lord, the magnanimous Rāma, paused.

On Rāma having stopped after speaking these pregnant words, the virtuous Bharata addressed the righteous Rāma attached to him subjects in an excellent speech on the banks of the Mandākinī, saying, “O vanquisher of foes, who is there is this world like to you?"

sanskrit: न त्वां प्रव्यथयेद्दु:खं प्रीतिर्वा न प्रहर्षयेत्
transliteration: na tvāṃ pravyathayeddu:khaṃ prītirvā na praharṣayet

english: Pain does not afflict you, nor does pleasure exhilarate. Yourself the exemplar of even aged people, you refer to them on doubtful point (of morality).

sanskrit: यथा मृतस्तथा जीवन् यथा ऽसति तथा सति
transliteration: yathā mṛtastathā jīvan yathā 'sati tathā sati
english: ‘Living like to dead and existing like to nonexisting', what shall make a person that has attained this intellectual state, grieve?

sanskrit: स एवं व्यसनं प्राप्य न विषीदितुमर्हति
transliteration: sa evaṃ vyasanaṃ prāpya na viṣīditumarhati
english: O lord of men, he that like to you understands the nature of the soul and its environment coming by any calamity, ought not to despond.

You resemble, O Rāghava, the god in strength, and are magnanimous, and truthful in promise, and know every thing and are endued with intelligence, Calamity, however unbearable it may be, should not overpower a person like yourself furnished with such virtues and cognizant of life and death.

You resemble, O Rāghava, the god in strength, and are magnanimous, and truthful in promise, and know every thing and are endued with intelligence, Calamity, however unbearable it may be, should not overpower a person like yourself furnished with such virtues and cognizant of life and death.
The sin that in my absence from home has been perpetrated by my mean-minded mother does not find favour in my sight. Be you therefore propitious to me.

sanskrit: धर्मबन्धेन बद्धो ऽस्मि तेनेमां नेह मातरम्
english: I am bound by the fetters of religion. For this it is that I do not by a severe penalty slay my wicked mother deserving of chastisement.
How having sprung from Dasaratha of righteous deeds and born of immaculate race, and knowing virtue and vice, can I commit such a reprehensible action?

sanskrit: गुरु: क्रियावान् वृद्धश्च राजा प्रेत: पितेति च
तातं न परिगर्हेयं दैवतं चेति संसदि
transliteration: guru: kriyāvān vṛddhaśca rājā preta: piteti ca
tātaṃ na parigarheyaṃ daivataṃ ceti saṃsadi
english: Dasaratha is our superior, of meritorious acts, aged our king, a departed spirit, and our father, it is on account of this that I do not censure our father who is a deity to us.

sanskrit: स्त्रिया: प्रियं चिकीर्षु: सन् कुर्याद्धर्मज्ञ धर्मवित्
transliteration: striyā: priyaṃ cikīrṣu: san kuryāddharmajña dharmavit
english: O cognizant of virtue, what virtuous person conversant in morality, should, seeking the pleasure of his wife, commit such a sinful act devoid of both righteousness and interest?

sanskrit: राज्ञैवं कुर्वता लोके प्रत्यक्षं सा श्रुति: कृता
transliteration: rājñaivaṃ kurvatā loke pratyakṣaṃ sā śruti: kṛtā
english: 'Creatures, as their end approaches, lose their sense this ancient adage has been illustrated in the world by the course the king has taken.
Do you, intent upon bringing about good, redeem the wrong that has been done by our sire through anger, ignorance and recklessness.

sanskrit: तदपत्यं भवानस्तु मा भवान् दुष्कृतं पितु:
transliteration: tadapatyaṃ bhavānastu mā bhavān duṣkṛtaṃ pitu:
english: Be you that (real) son (of the monarch). Do you not approve the action of your father, since what he has done is divorced from righteousness and is blameworthy.

sanskrit: कैकेयीं मां च तातं च सुहृदो बान्धवांश्च न:
transliteration: kaikeyīṃ māṃ ca tātaṃ ca suhṛdo bāndhavāṃśca na:
english: Do you rescue all these, Kaikeyī, myself, my father, our friends and adherents, and the whole body of the citizens as well as the inhabitants of the provinces.

sanskrit: क्व चारण्यं क्व च क्षात्ऺत्र क्व जटा: क्व च पालनम्
ईदृशं व्याहतं कर्म न भवान् कर्तुमर्हति
transliteration: kva cāraṇyaṃ kva ca kṣāttra kva jaṭā: kva ca pālanam
īdṛśaṃ vyāhataṃ karma na bhavān kartumarhati
english: Where is the forest? And where is Ksatriya morality? Where are matted locks? And where is your government of the country? It behoves you not to act in such an untoward way.
Even this is the first duty of a Ksatriya, viz., getting oneself installed, by means of which, O highly wise one, he can compass the government of the people.
What base Ksatriya setting aside this indubitable morality, resorts to a dubious and inauspicious course, which should be followed by the old alone?
But if you be bent upon practising this austere morality, do you undergo this trouble, after having righteously ruled the four orders.
O you cognizant of morality, those versed in duty say that of the four modes of life, the life of the householder is the foremost. Why then do you wish to renounce the same?

sanskrit: श्रुतेन बाल: स्थानेन जन्मना भवतो ह्यहम्
स कथं पालयिष्यामि भूमिं भवति तिष्ठति
transliteration: śrutena bāla: sthānena janmanā bhavato hyaham
sa kathaṃ pālayiṣyāmi bhūmiṃ bhavati tiṣṭhati
english: I am inferior to you in learning, in position, and in birth. How can I then govern the earth, you existing?
Void of sense and quality, a body, and inferior to you in point of years, I, deprived of you, can not live.
O you cognizant of morality, do you, along with your friends, according to your proper morality rule this entire ancestral kingdom rid of its thorns and enjoying tranquillity.

sanskrit: इहैव त्वा ऽभिषिञ्चन्तु सर्वा: प्रकृतय: सह
english: Even here, O you cognizant of the Mantras, let all the subjects and the Rtvijas with Vasiștha, versed in the Mantras, install you.

Having been installed, go to Ayodhyā for the purpose of governing it, having with our assistance conquered your enemies by they strength, like Vāsava conquering (his foes) with the help of the Maruts.
Having freed yourself from the threefold debts, do you govern me, repressing your foes, and propitiating your friends with every gratification.

sanskrit: अद्य भीता: पलायन्तां दुर्हृदस्ते दिशो दश
transliteration: adya bhītā: palāyantāṃ durhṛdaste diśo daśa
english: O noble one, to-day let your friends rejoice in consequence of your coronation. To day let those that intend to do you harm, being frightened, fly to the ten cardinal points.

sanskrit: अद्य तत्रभवन्तं च पितरं रक्ष किल्बिषात्
transliteration: adya tatrabhavantaṃ ca pitaraṃ rakṣa kilbiṣāt
english: O foremost of men, wiping out the disgrace of my mother, do you emancipate our sire from sin.

sanskrit: शिरसा त्वा ऽभियाचे ऽहं कुरुष्व करुणां मयि
english: I beseech you with bent head. Be you merciful to me, to all our friends, and, O great lord, to all creatures in general.
But, if disregarding my solicitations, you wend from here to the forest, I shall go along with you.

sanskrit: तथाहि रामो भरतेन ताम्यता प्रसाद्यमान: शिरसा महीपति:
न चैव चक्रे गमनाय सत्त्ववान् मतिं पितुस्तद्वचने व्यवस्थित:
transliteration: tathāhi rāmo bharatena tāmyatā prasādyamāna: śirasā mahīpati:
na caiva cakre gamanāya sattvavān matiṃ pitustadvacane vyavasthita:
english: Although thus besought and propitiated by Bharata with bent head, that lord of the earth, Rāma, possessed of strength, established in the words of his father, did not decide for going.

sanskrit: तदद्भुतं स्थैर्यमवेक्ष्य राघवे समं जनो हर्षमवाप दु:खित:
न यात्ययोध्यामिति दु:खितो ऽभवत् स्थिरप्रतिज्ञत्वमवेक्ष्य हर्षित:
transliteration: tadadbhutaṃ sthairyamavekṣya rāghave samaṃ jano harṣamavāpa du:khita:
english: Witnessing that wonderful firmness in Rāghava, the people were at one and the same time delighted and depressed. They were aggrieved because he would not go to Ayodhyā; they rejoiced on seeing his firm resolution.

sanskrit: तथा ब्रुवाणं भरतं प्रतुष्टुवु: प्रणम्य रामं च ययाचिरे सह
transliteration: tathā bruvāṇaṃ bharataṃ pratuṣṭuvu: praṇamya rāmaṃ ca yayācire saha
english: Then the Rtvijas, the citizens, and their leaders, and the mothers with their senses lost and with tears in their eyes, extolled Bharata as he was speaking thus; and, bowing down to Rāma, they directed their solicitations together.
As Bharata was again ng in this strain, his graceful elder brother, having been highly honoured, answered Bharata in the midst of his relatives, saying.
Having been born as a son to Daśaratha, foremost of monarchs, by Kaikeyſ, this speech of yours is worthy of you.

sanskrit: पुरा भ्रात: पिता न: स मातरं ते समुद्वहन्
transliteration: purā bhrāta: pitā na: sa mātaraṃ te samudvahan
english: O brother, formerly when our father espoused the hand of your mother, he promised her the kingdom as her marriage portion.

sanskrit: दैवासुरे च सङ्ग्रामे जनन्यै तव पार्थिव:
transliteration: daivāsure ca saṅgrāme jananyai tava pārthiva:
english: Then on the occasion of the war between the gods and the Asuras, that master, the king, well pleased (with her), being besought, granted her a boon.

sanskrit: तत: सा सम्प्रतिश्राव्य तव माता यशस्विनी
transliteration: tata: sā sampratiśrāvya tava mātā yaśasvinī
english: Having been thus promised, that virtuous lady, your illustrious mother, O foremost of men, asked for two boons (of the king), viz., your enthronement, O best of men, and my banishment. Thus besought by her, the king conferred on her the boon.

sanskrit: तव राज्यं नरव्याघ्र मम प्रव्राजनं तथा
तौ च राजा तदा तस्यै नियुक्त: प्रददौ वरौ
transliteration: tava rājyaṃ naravyāghra mama pravrājanaṃ tathā
tau ca rājā tadā tasyai niyukta: pradadau varau
english: Having been thus promised, that virtuous lady, your illustrious mother, O foremost of men, asked for two boons (of the king), viz., your enthronement, O best of men, and my banishment. Thus besought by her, the king conferred on her the boon.
And, you foremost of men, I have been enjoyed by my sire to stay in the woods for fourteen years, in consequence of his having granted her the boon.

sanskrit: सो ऽहं वनमिदं प्राप्तो निर्जनं लक्ष्मणान्वित:
english: And, having, in company with Laksmana and Sītā, come to the lone forest, I in humble guise am staying in the truthful speech of my father.
You too, you foremost of kings, should in the same way speedily render our father truthful, by getting yourself installed.
O Bharata, for my sake, do you free that lord, the king, from his debts. Do you, O you cognizant of morality, deliver our father and gladden your mother.

sanskrit: श्रूयते हि पुरा तात श्रुतिर्गीता यशस्विना
transliteration: śrūyate hi purā tāta śrutirgītā yaśasvinā
english: O child, we hear that in Gaya, formerly the famous Gaya, engaged in a sacrifice, chanted this Vedic hymn, for pleasing his departed ancestors.

sanskrit: तस्मात् पुत्र इति प्रोक्त: पितऽन् यत्पाति वा सुत:
transliteration: tasmāt putra iti prokta: pita'n yatpāti vā suta:
english: Since a son delivers his sire form the hell named Put, a son goes by the appellation of putra, he protecting his (departed) ancestors in every way.
One should wish for many sons crowned with qualities and versed in various lore, for the chance is that one at least of these may repair to Gayā.

sanskrit: तस्मात् त्राहि नरश्रेष्ठ पितरं नरकात् प्रभो
transliteration: tasmāt trāhi naraśreṣṭha pitaraṃ narakāt prabho
english: O son of the Raghu race, the Rājarşis have delivered their decision on the point. Therefore, you foremost of men, do you, O lord, rescue your sire from hell.
O Bharata, go to Ayodhyā, and please the subjects, in company with Śatrughna, O hero, and all the regenerate ones.

sanskrit: आभ्यां तु सहितो राजन् वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च
transliteration: ābhyāṃ tu sahito rājan vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca
english: I also, O hero, without delay shall have to enter the forest of Dandaka in company with Lakşmaņa and Sītā.

sanskrit: त्वं राजा भरत भव स्वयं नराणां वन्यानामहमपि राजराण्मृगाणाम्
गच्छत्वं पुरवरमद्य सम्प्रहृष्ट: संहृष्टस्त्वहमपि दण्डकान् प्रवेक्ष्ये
transliteration: tvaṃ rājā bharata bhava svayaṃ narāṇāṃ vanyānāmahamapi rājarāṇmṛgāṇām
gacchatvaṃ puravaramadya samprahṛṣṭa: saṃhṛṣṭastvahamapi daṇḍakān pravekṣye
english: O Bharata, be you yourself the monarch of men. I shall become the king of kings of deer. Go you to that foremost of cities with a glad heart: with a glad heart will I enter Dandaka.

sanskrit: छायां ते दिनकरभा: प्रबाधमानं वर्षत्रं भरत करोतु मूर्ध्नि शीताम्
एतेषामहमपि काननद्रुमाणां छायां तामति शयिनीं सुखी श्रयिष्ये
transliteration: chāyāṃ te dinakarabhā: prabādhamānaṃ varṣatraṃ bharata karotu mūrdhni śītām
eteṣāmahamapi kānanadrumāṇāṃ chāyāṃ tāmati śayinīṃ sukhī śrayiṣye
english: O Bharata, let the umbrella barring out the rays of the sun, afford cool shade to your head: I shall happily seek the dense shade of these forest trees.

sanskrit: शत्रुघ्न: कुशलमतिस्तु ते सहाय: सौमित्रिर्मम विदित: प्रधानमित्रम्
चत्वारस्तनयवरा वयं नरेन्द्रं सत्यस्थं भरत चराम मा विषादम्
transliteration: śatrughna: kuśalamatistu te sahāya: saumitrirmama vidita: pradhānamitram
catvārastanayavarā vayaṃ narendraṃ satyasthaṃ bharata carāma mā viṣādam
english: Śatrughna endued with cleverness is your helper: Sumitrā's son is well known as my best friend. We four worthy sons of that foremost of monarchs will keep him established in truth, O Bharata. Let not your mind despond.
As Rāma cognizant of righteousness was thus encouraging Bharata, Jābāli, best of Brāhmaṇas, addressed him in words divorced from morality, saying.
O Rāghava, endowed with a noble understanding and leading a life of asceticism, do not suffer your intellect to entertain inanities, like any low person.

sanskrit: क: कस्य पुरुषो बन्धु: किमाप्यं कस्य केनचित्
transliteration: ka: kasya puruṣo bandhu: kimāpyaṃ kasya kenacit
english: Who is whose friend ? And to what is one entitled and by virtue of what relation? And who is such ? Since a creature is born alone and dies alone, a person that cherishes his father and mother with affection, must, O Rāma, be looked upon as a madman.

sanskrit: तस्मान्माता पिता चेति राम सज्जेतयो नर:
उन्मत्त इव स ज्ञेयो नास्ति कश्चिद्धि कस्यचित्
transliteration: tasmānmātā pitā ceti rāma sajjetayo nara:
unmatta iva sa jñeyo nāsti kaściddhi kasyacit
english: Who is whose friend ? And to what is one entitled and by virtue of what relation? And who is such ? Since a creature is born alone and dies alone, a person that cherishes his father and mother with affection, must, O Rāma, be looked upon as a madman.

sanskrit: यथा ग्रामान्तरं गच्छन् नर: कश्चित् क्वचिद्वसेत्
transliteration: yathā grāmāntaraṃ gacchan nara: kaścit kvacidvaset
english: No individual has any one (in the world). As on the eve of setting out for another country, a person stays somewhere (outside the village he lives in), and the next day goes away, renouncing that abode, even such are a man's father and mother, house and wealth. O Kākutstha, worthy people never bear affection towards a mere abode.

sanskrit: एवमेव मनुष्याणां पिता माता गृहं वसु
transliteration: evameva manuṣyāṇāṃ pitā mātā gṛhaṃ vasu
english: No individual has any one (in the world). As on the eve of setting out for another country, a person stays somewhere (outside the village he lives in), and the next day goes away, renouncing that abode, even such are a man's father and mother, house and wealth. O Kākutstha, worthy people never bear affection towards a mere abode.

sanskrit: पित्र्यं राज्यं परित्यज्य स नार्हसि नरोत्तम
transliteration: pitryaṃ rājyaṃ parityajya sa nārhasi narottama
english: Therefore, O best of men, leaving your ancestral kingdom, you ought not to abide in the disagreeable forest filled with dangers and difficulties.

sanskrit: एकवेणी धरा हि त्वां नगरी सम्प्रतीक्षते
transliteration: ekaveṇī dharā hi tvāṃ nagarī sampratīkṣate
english: Do you get yourself sprinkled in the prosperous Ayodhyā. The city expects you wearing a single woven braid.
O king's son, enjoying costly regal pleasures, do you sport in Ayodhyā, like Sakra in the celestial regions.

sanskrit: न ते कश्चिद्दशरथस्त्वं च तस्य न कश्चन
अन्यो राजा त्वमन्य: स तस्मात् कुरु यदुच्यते
transliteration: na te kaściddaśarathastvaṃ ca tasya na kaścana
anyo rājā tvamanya: sa tasmāt kuru yaducyate
english: Dasaratha is none to you, and you too are none's to Dasaratha. He is quite other than your sire; and you have no connection with him. Therefore, do you act as I tell you.

sanskrit: बीजमात्रं पिता जन्तो: शुक्लं रुधिरमेव च
transliteration: bījamātraṃ pitā janto: śuklaṃ rudhirameva ca
english: A father is merely an instrumental cause (touching the generation of his child). A father's semen coming in contact with a mother's blood, at the time befitting conception, a person is brought into being.

sanskrit: गत: स नृपतिस्तत्र गन्तव्यं यत्र तेन वै
प्रवृत्तिरेषा मर्त्त्यानां त्वं तु मिथ्या विहन्यसे
transliteration: gata: sa nṛpatistatra gantavyaṃ yatra tena vai
pravṛttireṣā marttyānāṃ tvaṃ tu mithyā vihanyase
english: The king has gone the way he should. This is the nature of all creatures. But you for naught deny yourself (the manliness of monarchical power).

sanskrit: अर्थधर्मपरा ये ये तांस्तान् शोचामि नेतरान्
ते हि दु:खमिह प्राप्य विनाशं प्रेत्य भेजिरे
transliteration: arthadharmaparā ye ye tāṃstān śocāmi netarān
te hi du:khamiha prāpya vināśaṃ pretya bhejire
english: Those that disregarding interest are devoted to virtue, do I mourn, and not others; for having suffered misery here, they in the end meet with extinction.
People engage in Aştaka* in behalf of ancestors and deities. Behold the waste of edibles. Does any dead person feed? *The lunar days and months for propitiating the manes.

sanskrit: दद्यात् प्रवसत: श्राद्धं न तत् पथ्यशनं भवेत्
transliteration: dadyāt pravasata: śrāddhaṃ na tat pathyaśanaṃ bhavet
english: If food partaken by one is transferred to the body of another, offer Śrāddha to one going to a distant and, that shall serve for his provender on the way.
Works (on morality) enjoining, Worship,' 'Give away,' 'Be initiated,' 'Observe rites,' "Renounce', have been composed by intelligent persons, for inducing people to be charitable.

sanskrit: स नास्ति परमित्येव कुरु बुद्धिं महामते
transliteration: sa nāsti paramityeva kuru buddhiṃ mahāmate
english: O magnanimous one, assure yourself there is no hereafter. Do you remain grounded in the evident, turning your back on what is beyond our ken.
Placing in front the intellect of the good, and approved by all, do you, propitiated by Bharata, accept the monarchy.

sanskrit: जाबालेस्तु वच: श्रुत्वा राम: सत्यात्मनां वर:
transliteration: jābālestu vaca: śrutvā rāma: satyātmanāṃ vara:
english: Hearing Jāvāli's words, Rāma having truth for prowess, by help of an exceedingly subtle intellect uninfluenced (under the exhortations of that sage), said.
What you, wishing for my welfare, have dwelt upon, though wearing the guise of a good action, is really not such; and though appearing to be beneficent, is really calculated to entail misery.

The person that with his sinful acts sticking to him, walk astray, as well as he that hold up (to others) different patterns of character (from those recommended by scripture), does not win honour with the good.

sanskrit: चारित्रमेव व्याख्याति शुचिं वा यदि वा ऽशुचिम्
transliteration: cāritrameva vyākhyāti śuciṃ vā yadi vā 'śucim
english: One's character (fashioned according to scripture) shows whether one is high-born or base, heroic or vainly priding himself on his manliness, pure or impure.

(But by adopting the code of conduct inculcated by you), a mean character may appear as a noble one, one bereft of purity may appear pure, an inauspicious individual may seem auspicious, and one of vile ways may appear honest.

If I adopt this unrighteous course, calculated to produce confusion of castes, and do acts not recognized by scripture, I shall, renouncing good, have to reap only evil. Then what man possessed of consciousness and capable of discriminating between right and wrong, shall honour me, given to wicked ways and deserving of universal reprehension?

If I adopt this unrighteous course, calculated to produce confusion of castes, and do acts not recognized by scripture, I shall, renouncing good, have to reap only evil. Then what man possessed of consciousness and capable of discriminating between right and wrong, shall honour me, given to wicked ways and deserving of universal reprehension?

sanskrit: कस्य धास्याम्यहं वृत्तं केन वा स्वर्गमाप्नुयाम्
transliteration: kasya dhāsyāmyahaṃ vṛttaṃ kena vā svargamāpnuyām
english: Whose is this course (that you asked me to follow)? And by what way shall I attain heaven, by following the present course, which would make me give up my vow?

sanskrit: यद्वृत्ता: सन्ति राजानस्तद्वृत्ता: सन्ति हि प्रजा:
transliteration: yadvṛttā: santi rājānastadvṛttā: santi hi prajā:
english: When I have (first) myself set up desire as my standard of action, the entire body of the people shall follow me: subjects take to the ways that have been adopted by their sovereigns.
This eternal regal morality founded in kindness towards the subjects, is verily true. Hence a kingdom is essentially based upon truth; and this world itself is established in truth.

sanskrit: सत्यवादी हि लोके ऽस्मिन् परमं गच्छति क्षयम्
transliteration: satyavādī hi loke 'smin paramaṃ gacchati kṣayam
english: Saints and celestials for certain regard truth alone. In this world a truthful person attains the regions of Brahma.

sanskrit: धर्म: सत्यं परो लोके मूलं स्वर्गस्य चोच्यते
transliteration: dharma: satyaṃ paro loke mūlaṃ svargasya cocyate
english: Untruthful persons harass people as much as serpents. In this world virtue, which is said to be the root of everything, is itself established in truth.

sanskrit: सत्यमेवेश्वरो लोके सत्यं पद्मा श्रिता सदा
transliteration: satyameveśvaro loke satyaṃ padmā śritā sadā
english: In this world, truth is the Lord; in truth is established righteousness. Everything has truth for its basis. No condition is superior to truth.

sanskrit: दत्तमिष्टं हुतं चैव तप्तानि च तपांसि च
transliteration: dattamiṣṭaṃ hutaṃ caiva taptāni ca tapāṃsi ca
english: The Veda, which inculcates gift, sacrifice homa, and asceticism, is based on truth. I never or

sanskrit: मज्जत्येको हि निरय एक: स्वर्गे महीयते
transliteration: majjatyeko hi niraya eka: svarge mahīyate
english: One protects men, another his family; one is plunged in hell, another is honoured in heaven.

Why should I not then obey the mandate of my father? My father was of truthful promise and of righteous ways and with the object of observing his promise, he laid on me this (for faithful performance).
Having promised to my superior with an oath, shall through covetousness forgetfulness or pride rive the bridge of truth.

sanskrit: नैव देवा न पितर: प्रतीच्छन्तीति न: श्रुतम्
transliteration: naiva devā na pitara: pratīcchantīti na: śrutam
english: We have heard that the gods and the Pitrs do not accept offerings from one inclined to untruth, or who is unsteady and of volatile faculties.

This duty of maintaining truth, whose influence radiates all over one's soul, I certainly find to be the prime one; and this burthen has (ere this) been borne by worthy people. And it is for this that I reverence the same.
I abjure that Ksatriya morality which, wearing the garb of righteousness, is in fact impiety, and which is pursued by the low-minded, or the wicked, or the covetous, or the sinful.

sanskrit: कायेन कुरुते पापं मनसा सम्प्रधार्य च
अनृतं जिह्वया चाह त्रिविधं कर्म पातकम्
transliteration: kāyena kurute pāpaṃ manasā sampradhārya ca
anṛtaṃ jihvayā cāha trividhaṃ karma pātakam
english: A person commits a sin by means of his physique, but after he has accurately cast it in his mind; and he has also spoken an untruth with his tongue. Thus a sin is threefold.

sanskrit: भूमि: कीर्त्तिर्यशो लक्ष्मी: पुरुषं प्रार्थयन्ति हि
transliteration: bhūmi: kīrttiryaśo lakṣmī: puruṣaṃ prārthayanti hi
english: The earth and fame and renown and auspiciousness pay court to the truthful person. The good follow truth, therefore even truth is to be sought by all).
Therefore the seemingly excellent thing that you, after having well ascertained it, have said to me in words informed with reason, 'You had rather do this', appears to me wanting in nobility.
How, after having promised to my superior this exile of mine, shall I act up to Bharata's words, setting aside those of my superior?
I having remained firm in the promise I had made to my superior, that noble lady, Kaikeyi, became exceedingly delighted.

sanskrit: मूलै: पुष्पै: फलै: पुण्यै: पितऽन् देवांश्च तर्पयन्
transliteration: mūlai: puṣpai: phalai: puṇyai: pita'n devāṃśca tarpayan
english: Living in the forest, pure, with regulated fare, I shall, propitiating the gods and the Pits with fruits, flowers and roots, (fulfil my vow).

Satisfying the five classes,* I shall, retaining my simplicity and my religious faith and being able to distinguish between right and wrong, pass away the term (of banishment). * Prakrāmam, The commentator says that the word means, Cāndrāyaṇa and other rites.
Having come to this scene of action, one should do that which is proper. Even Agni and Vāyu and Soma reap the fruits of their own acts.
Having acquired the appellation of Satakratu, the sovereign of the celestials has gone to heaven; and, having performed rigid austerities, the Maharșis have attained the celestial regions.'

Having heard of the reasons couched in that atheristical speech which he could not allow to pass without stricture, that one of fierce energy, the king's son, censuring what Jāvāli had said, again spoke.

sanskrit: सत्यं च धर्मं च पराक्रमं च भूतानुकम्पां प्रियवादिताञ्च
transliteration: satyaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca parākramaṃ ca bhūtānukampāṃ priyavāditāñca
english: Truth, righteousness, prowess, kindness to creatures, fair spokeness, and worship of the twice-born ones, gods and guests, these have by the pious been styled the ways to heaven.

sanskrit: धर्मं चरन्त: सकलं यथावत् कांक्षन्ति लोकागममप्रमत्ता:
transliteration: dharmaṃ caranta: sakalaṃ yathāvat kāṃkṣanti lokāgamamapramattā:
english: Having duly heard that these are capable of conferring the summum bonum, and also come to the same conclusion by reasoning, Vipras, adequately and competely observing morality with the utmost care, are eagerly desirous of attaining those regions.

I blame this act of my father's, viz., that he took (for his (for his priest) one of perverse understanding, who range by help of such an intellect, who is frightfully atheistic, and who has swerved from the path of righteousness.

sanskrit: यथा हि चोर: स तथा हि बुद्धस्तथागतं नास्तिकमत्र विद्धि
तस्माद्धि य: शङ्क्यतम: प्रजानां न नास्तिकेनाभिमुखो बुध: स्यात्
transliteration: yathā hi cora: sa tathā hi buddhastathāgataṃ nāstikamatra viddhi
tasmāddhi ya: śaṅkyatama: prajānāṃ na nāstikenābhimukho budha: syāt
english: As a thief is, so is a Buddha, and know that in this matter, an atheist is in a like predicament. Therefore, such an one, when capable of being punished like a thief for the good of the people, should be punished like a thief; and let no Brāhamaņa ever speak with an atheist.

sanskrit: त्वत्तो जना: पूर्वतरे वराश्च शुभानि कर्माणि बहूनि चक्रु:
जित्वा सदेमं च परञ्च लोकं तस्माद्द्विजा: स्वस्ति हुतं कृतं च
transliteration: tvatto janā: pūrvatare varāśca śubhāni karmāṇi bahūni cakru:
jitvā sademaṃ ca parañca lokaṃ tasmāddvijā: svasti hutaṃ kṛtaṃ ca
english: Other Brāhmaṇas than yourself, superior to you, have, severing this world as well as the next, performed various excellent acts.

sanskrit: अहिंसका वीतमलाश्च लोके भवन्ति पूज्या मुनय: प्रधाना:
transliteration: ahiṃsakā vītamalāśca loke bhavanti pūjyā munaya: pradhānā:
english: Therefore those Brahmanas, a men, who have spared life and in other ways practised morality, and have also given away in charity, performed austerities and served others, (perform sacrifices in consonance with Vedas). And principal ascetics engaged in religion, surrounded by the good, possessed of energy, having charity for their foremost attribute, void of envy, and their hearts free from all stain, are honoured in this world.

sanskrit: इति ब्रुवन्तं वचनं सरोषं रामं महात्मानमदीनसत्त्वम्
उवाच तथ्यं पुनरास्तिकं च सत्यं वच: सानुनयं च विप्र:
transliteration: iti bruvantaṃ vacanaṃ saroṣaṃ rāmaṃ mahātmānamadīnasattvam
uvāca tathyaṃ punarāstikaṃ ca satyaṃ vaca: sānunayaṃ ca vipra:
english: When the magnanimous Rama of undiminished strength had wrathfully said this, that Vipra with supplications again spoke words fraught with morality and high spiritual truth.

sanskrit: न नास्तिकानां वचनं ब्रवीम्यहं न नास्तिकोऽहं न च नास्ति किञ्चन
समीक्ष्य कालं पुनरास्तिकोऽभवं भवेय काले पुनरेव नास्तिकः
transliteration: na nāstikānāṃ vacanaṃ bravīmyahaṃ na nāstiko'haṃ na ca nāsti kiñcana
samīkṣya kālaṃ punarāstiko'bhavaṃ bhaveya kāle punareva nāstikaḥ
english: I do not speak the language of atheists; nor am I an atheist; nor yet is it true that there is nothing (hereafter). On the occasion of things having reference to the next world being performed, I am again a believer, and on the occasion of things' connection with this world being taken in hand, I am an atheist once again.

sanskrit: स चापि कालो ऽयमुपागत: शनैर्यथा मया नास्तिकवागुदीरिता
निवर्त्तनार्थं तव राम कारणात् प्रसादनार्थं तु मयैतदीरितम्
transliteration: sa cāpi kālo 'yamupāgata: śanairyathā mayā nāstikavāgudīritā
nivarttanārthaṃ tava rāma kāraṇāt prasādanārthaṃ tu mayaitadīritam
english: O Rāma, the time has gradually drawn nigh when for the purpose of making you turn back, it is necessary that I should speak the language of atheism. But pacifying you, I have (again) spoken this (i.e. I am a believer).

sanskrit: क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय रामं तं वसिष्ठ: प्रत्युवाच ह
transliteration: kruddhamājñāya rāmaṃ taṃ vasiṣṭha: pratyuvāca ha
english: Knowing that Rāma was wroth, Vasiştha said, Jābāli knows the departure of the creature to the next world and their return thence.
Anxious of making the turn back, he had spoken thus. Do you now, O lord of the world, learn the genesis of creatures from me.
Water was everywhere. The earth was constructed therein. Then sprang the self-create Brahmā along with all the celestials.

sanskrit: असृजच्च जगत् सर्वं सह पुत्रै: कृतात्मभि:
transliteration: asṛjacca jagat sarvaṃ saha putrai: kṛtātmabhi:

english: Brahma eternal, existing through all time and incapable of decay, sprang from the sky. From him Marici came into being, and Kaśyapa is Marici's son.

sanskrit: स तु प्रजापति: पूर्वमिक्ष्वाकुस्तु मनो: सुत:
transliteration: sa tu prajāpati: pūrvamikṣvākustu mano: suta:
english: Vivasvat drew his birth from Kaśyapa, and Manu from Vivasvat. Manu was formerly known as Prajāpati. Ikṣvāku is son to Manu; and this world was first conferred upon Ikşvāku by Manu. Do you know Ikşvāku as the first kind in Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: यस्येयं प्रथमं दत्ता समृद्धा मनुना मही
transliteration: yasyeyaṃ prathamaṃ dattā samṛddhā manunā mahī
english: Vivasvat drew his birth from Kaśyapa, and Manu from Vivasvat. Manu was formerly known as Prajāpati. Ikṣvāku is son to Manu; and this world was first conferred upon Ikşvāku by Manu. Do you know Ikşvāku as the first kind in Ayodhyā.
The graceful Kukşi is known as the son of Iksvāku. And, O hero, Kuksi's son was Vikuksi.
Vikukși had the powerful Bāņa possessed of exceeding energy for his son. Bāna had the mighty-armed Anaranya of high austerities for his son.
During the time of that foremost of righteous person, the monarch Anaranya, drought or famine did not occur (in Ayodhyā); nor were there any thieves at that time.
O mighty king, from Anaranya sprang king Pșthu. From Pệthu sprang Trišanku of mighty energy.
Dhruvasandhi had the illustrious Bharata, destroyer of foes (for his son) From Bharata sprang Asita, to whom sprang these hostile kings as foes, Haihayas, Tālajanghas and Sasabindus, heroes all.

sanskrit: तांस्तु सर्वान् प्रतिव्यूह्य युद्धे राजा प्रवासित:
स च शैलवरे रम्ये बभूवाभिरतो मुनि:
transliteration: tāṃstu sarvān prativyūhya yuddhe rājā pravāsita:
sa ca śailavare ramye babhūvābhirato muni:
english: Having engaged with them in battle, the king was excited (by them). And on the romantic Himavat, he become engaged in asceticism.

sanskrit: द्वे चास्य भार्ये गर्भिण्यौ बभूवतुरिति श्रुति:
transliteration: dve cāsya bhārye garbhiṇyau babhūvaturiti śruti:
english: It is said that at the time, his two wives were gone with child. There one of the exalted ladies having eyes resembling lotus petals saluted Bhrgu's son furnished with the splendour of a celestial, desirous of having an excellent son. Another administered poison to the other for destroying her foetus.
Bhrgu's son named Cyavana was at that time staying in Himavat. Appearing before the sage, Kalindi saluted him.

Thereupon he returned the greeting that had been made by that lady anxious to secure a boon for the birth of a son. You, shall, O lady get a son of mighty soul, who shall be celebrated among men; and who shall be pious and powerful, the perpetuator of his race and destroyer of enemies

sanskrit: कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं हृष्टा मुनिं तमनुमान्य च
तत: सा गृहमागम्य देवी पुत्रं व्यजायत
transliteration: kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ hṛṣṭā muniṃ tamanumānya ca
tata: sā gṛhamāgamya devī putraṃ vyajāyata
english: Hearing this, that noble lady having gone round him and paid in respect to the ascetic went to her home and gave birth to a son furnished with eyes resembling lotus petals, and of sheen like that of the inside of a lotus.

sanskrit: गरेण सह तेनैव जात: स सगरो ऽभवत्
transliteration: gareṇa saha tenaiva jāta: sa sagaro 'bhavat
english: And because her co-wife, had given her poison for destroying her foetus, and as in consequence of this, he had come in contact with poison, he came to be allied Sagara.

sanskrit: स राजा सगरो नाम य: समुद्रमखानयत्
transliteration: sa rājā sagaro nāma ya: samudramakhānayat
english: The name of that king is Sagara, who having been initiated in a sacrifice excavated the ocean, frightening the people with the vehemence of his operations.

sanskrit: जीवन्नेव स पित्रा तु निरस्त: पापकर्मकृत्
transliteration: jīvanneva sa pitrā tu nirasta: pāpakarmakṛt
english: Asamañja is known to have been the son of Sagara. This wicked man while yet in life, was banished by his father.
Asamanja's son was the puissant Ansumat. Dilipa is the son of Ansumat and Dilipa's son is Bhagiratha.

sanskrit: ककुत्स्थस्य च पुत्रो ऽभूद्रघुर्येन तु राघवा:
english: From Bhagiratha sprang Kakutstha; from whom the Kākutsthas came to be well known. Kakutstha had Raghu for his son; after whom have been named the Rāghavas.
Raghu's son is the energetic Pravědha, who are human beings. He is known on earth under such names as Kalmāşapāda, Saudāsa.
We have heard that Kalmāșapāda's son was Śarkhaņa, who having been endowed with prowess, found destruction along with his forces.

sanskrit: शङ्खणस्य च पुत्रो ऽभूच्छूर: श्रीमान् सुदर्शन:
english: Sarkhana's son was the beautiful and heroic Sudarśana. Sudarśana's son was Agnivarṇa and Agnivarna's, Sighraga.

sanskrit: शीघ्रगस्य मरु: पुत्रो मरो: पुत्र: प्रशुश्रुक:
transliteration: śīghragasya maru: putro maro: putra: praśuśruka:
english: Śighraga's son was Maru, and Maru's Praśuśruva. Praśuśruva's son the magnanimous Ambarisa.
Ambarīşa's son was Nahuşa having truth for his prowess. Nahușa's son was the exceedingly virtuous Nābhaga.

sanskrit: अजस्य चैव धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथ: सुत:
transliteration: ajasya caiva dharmātmā rājā daśaratha: suta:
english: Nābhāga had two sons, Aja and Suvrata. Aja's son was the virtuous king Dasaratha.

sanskrit: तस्य ज्येष्ठो ऽसि दायादो राम इत्यभिविश्रुत:
english: His eldest son are you celebrated under the name of Rāma. Do you receive your own kingdom and look after the world.

sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकूणां हि सर्वेषां राजा भवति पूर्वज:
पूर्वजे नावर: पुत्रो ज्येष्ठो राज्ये ऽभिषिच्यते
transliteration: ikṣvākūṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ rājā bhavati pūrvaja:
english: Among the Ikșwākus, the first born becomes the sovereign. The first born existing, an inferior son cannot be installed in the kingdom.

sanskrit: स राघवाणां कुलधर्ममात्मन: सनातनं नाद्य विहन्तुमर्हसि
transliteration: sa rāghavāṇāṃ kuladharmamātmana: sanātanaṃ nādya vihantumarhasi
english: It therefore does not today behove you to depart from the ever existing morality of the descendants of Raghu. Do you rule this earth filled with gems, and furnished with high fame, do you like to a father govern her containing many kingdoms.
Having thus addressed Rāma, the royal priest Vasiștha again spoke to him words fraught with righteousness, saying.

sanskrit: आचार्य्यश्चैव काकुत्स्थ पिता माता च राघव
transliteration: ācāryyaścaiva kākutstha pitā mātā ca rāghava
english: To a man born there are three superiors, viz, the preceptor, O Kakutstha, and father and mother, O Raghava.
Oforemost of men, the father begets a person, the preceptor imparts wisdom and therefore is he called a superior.

sanskrit: सो ऽहं ते पितुराचार्य्यस्तव चैव परन्तप
मम त्वं वचनं कुर्वन् नातिवर्त्ते: सताङ्गतिम्
transliteration: mama tvaṃ vacanaṃ kurvan nātivartte: satāṅgatim
english: I, O subduer of foes, have been the preceptor of both yourself and your father. By doing what I say, you will not lose the state of the righteous.

sanskrit: इमा हि ते परिषद: श्रेणयश्च द्विजास्तथा
एषु तात चरन् धर्मं नातिवर्त्ते: सताङ्गतिम्
transliteration: imā hi te pariṣada: śreṇayaśca dvijāstathā
eṣu tāta caran dharmaṃ nātivartte: satāṅgatim

english: These courtiers of yours, these relatives, and these kings;, by protecting them virtuously you will not lose the state of the righteous. It does not behove you to disregard the words of your aged and virtuous mother. By doing her bidding you will not lose the state of the righteous.
O Rāghava, by acting as Bharata, who is soliciting you, says, you having the morality of truth for your prowess, will not be frustrated of the state of the pious.
Thus sweetly addressed by his preceptor personally, that foremost of men, Rāghava, replied to Vasistha, seated with him, saying.

sanskrit: न सुप्रतिकरं तत्तु मात्रा पित्रा च यत्कृतम्
transliteration: na supratikaraṃ tattu mātrā pitrā ca yatkṛtam
english: What his father and mother always do in behalf of their son, and what they effect by way of provision and sleep and clothing and constant sweet speech, and sport, is difficult of being repaid.

sanskrit: नित्यं च प्रियवादेन तथा संवर्द्धनेन च
transliteration: nityaṃ ca priyavādena tathā saṃvarddhanena ca
english: What his father and mother always do in behalf of their son, and what they effect by way of provision and sleep and clothing and constant sweet speech, and sport, is difficult of being repaid.

sanskrit: स हि राजा जनयिता पिता दशरथो मम
आज्ञातं यन्मया तस्य न तन्मिथ्या भविष्यति
transliteration: sa hi rājā janayitā pitā daśaratho mama
ājñātaṃ yanmayā tasya na tanmithyā bhaviṣyati
english: Therefore, what my father, king Dasaratha has commanded me to do, must not be falsified.
Rāma having said this, the broad-breasted Bharata, extremely depressed spoke to the charioteer who was by, saying.

sanskrit: इह मे स्थण्डिले शीघ्रं कुशानास्तर सारथे
transliteration: iha me sthaṇḍile śīghraṃ kuśānāstara sārathe
english: O charioteer, do you speedily spread Kuša on the ground here. I will remain near the noble one until he be kindly disposed (towards me). Even as a twice born one deprived of his wealth Leith down (at the door of an unrighteous person), eschewing food and in darkness, will I lie down in front of this cottage, until he betakes himself back (to Ayodhyā)

O charioteer, do you speedily spread Kuša on the ground here. I will remain near the noble one until he be kindly disposed (towards me). Even as a twice born one deprived of his wealth Leith down (at the door of an unrighteous person), eschewing food and in darkness, will I lie down in front of this cottage, until he betakes himself back (to Ayodhyā)

sanskrit: स तु राममवेक्षन्तं सुमन्त्रं प्रेक्ष्य दुर्मना:
transliteration: sa tu rāmamavekṣantaṃ sumantraṃ prekṣya durmanā:
english: Then with a dispirited heart finding Sumantra looking up to Rāma, Bharata himself spread Kuśa and lay down upon it.

sanskrit: किं मां भरत कुर्वाणं तात प्रत्युपवेक्ष्यसि
transliteration: kiṃ māṃ bharata kurvāṇaṃ tāta pratyupavekṣyasi
english: To him spoke that foremost of Rājarşis, the highly energetic Rāma, O Bharata, my dear brother, what have I done that you have down by me?

It is a Brāhmaṇa who alone can obstruct a person by lying down beside him; but there is no rule by which a member of the military class* can lie down (in this wise). *Murdhabhisikta, Murdha, the head; Abhisikta, sprinkled; kings being consecrated by having poured on their heads, while seated on a throne, prepared for the purpose, water from some sacred stream, mixed with honey, clarified butter, and spirituous liquor, as well as two sorts of grass and sprouts of corn; the term applies to the Kșetriya as identified with the king, the duties of royalty belonging specially to the military caste.
O best of men, arise, renouncing this difficult vow; and, O descendant of Raghu, do you from hence take yourself to that best of cities, Ayodhyā,
Being seated, Bharata, eyeing the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces, remarked, What for do you not solicit the noble one?

Thereupon the citizens and the dwellers of the provinces answered that high-souled one, saying, We perceive that the descendant of Raghu says to Kākutstha what is fit; and this exceedingly virtuous one stay by the words of his sire. Therefore we are incapable of suddenly saying anything.

sanskrit: एषो ऽपि हि महाभाग: पितुर्वचसि तिष्ठति
अत एव न शक्ता: स्मो व्यावर्त्तयितुमञ्जसा
transliteration: ata eva na śaktā: smo vyāvarttayitumañjasā
english: Thereupon the citizens and the dwellers of the provinces answered that high-souled one, saying, We perceive that the descendant of Raghu says to Kākutstha what is fit; and this exceedingly virtuous one stay by the words of his sire. Therefore we are incapable of suddenly saying anything.
Hearing their speech, Rāma said, “Listen to the words of these friends having morality for their vision."

sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठ त्वं महाबाहो मां च स्पृश तथोदकम्
transliteration: uttiṣṭha tvaṃ mahābāho māṃ ca spṛśa tathodakam
english: And, O scion of the Raghu race, hearing their utterances as regards both yourself and me, do you decide. Arise, you mighty-armed one. Touch me and then water.

Thereat arising, Bharata, having touched water, said, You courtiers, and you ministers, listen to me! I did not wish for my paternal kingdom; nor did I sway my mother (towards obtaining the same); nor did I know that the exceedingly righteous Rāghava was to seek the woods.

sanskrit: न याचे पितरं राज्यं नानुशासामि मातरम्
transliteration: na yāce pitaraṃ rājyaṃ nānuśāsāmi mātaram
english: Thereat arising, Bharata, having touched water, said, You courtiers, and you ministers, listen to me! I did not wish for my paternal kingdom; nor did I sway my mother (towards obtaining the same); nor did I know that the exceedingly righteous Rāghava was to seek the woods.

sanskrit: यदि त्ववश्यं वस्तव्यं कर्त्तव्यं च पितुर्वच:
transliteration: yadi tvavaśyaṃ vastavyaṃ karttavyaṃ ca piturvaca:
english: But if he must dwell here, and thus act out the mandate of our father, I also will abide in the forest for fourteen years.
Astonished at the determination of Bharata, the righteous Rāma eyeing the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces, said.

sanskrit: विक्रीतमाहितं क्रीतं यत् पित्रा जीवता मम
न तल्लोपयितुं शक्यं मया वा भरतेन वा
transliteration: vikrītamāhitaṃ krītaṃ yat pitrā jīvatā mama
na tallopayituṃ śakyaṃ mayā vā bharatena vā
english: Neither Bharata nor I can annual any sale or pledge or purchase effected by our father during his life.

sanskrit: युक्तमुक्तं च कैकेय्या पित्रा मे सुकृतं कृतम्
