transliteration: yuktamuktaṃ ca kaikeyyā pitrā me sukṛtaṃ kṛtam
english: Therefore I ought not to accept any substitute for living in the woods, who can but contribute to my censure. Kaikeyi has spoken what is proper; and my father has acted well.
I know Bharata to be forgiving, and given to serving superiors. Everything in that high-souled one intent on truth appear beneficial.
Having returned from the forest, I will in company with this brother of virtuous character become the worthy master of this earth.

sanskrit: वृतो राजा हि कैकेय्या मया तद्वचनं कृतम्
transliteration: vṛto rājā hi kaikeyyā mayā tadvacanaṃ kṛtam

english: Observing the meeting of the two brothers of unparalleled energy, capable of making one's hair stand on end, the Maharsis struck with surprise came to the scene.

sanskrit: तौ भ्रातरौ महात्मानौ महात्मानौ काकुत्स्थौ प्रशशंसिरे
transliteration: tau bhrātarau mahātmānau mahātmānau kākutsthau praśaśaṃsire
english: And remaining invisible, the ascetics, Siddhas and prime saints admired those brothers, the virtuous Käkutsthas.

sanskrit: स धन्यो यस्य पुत्रौ द्वौ धर्मज्ञौ धर्मविक्रमौ
transliteration: sa dhanyo yasya putrau dvau dharmajñau dharmavikramau
english: Blessed is he whose sons these, two cognizant of virtue and having truth for prowess are. Having heard their converse, we are delighted.
Then the saints, desirous of the destruction of the ten-headed one, having become unanimous, speedily addressed that foremost of monarchs, Bharata, saying.

sanskrit: ग्राह्यं रामस्य वाक्यं ते पितरं यद्यवेक्षसे
transliteration: grāhyaṃ rāmasya vākyaṃ te pitaraṃ yadyavekṣase
english: Born in an illustrious line, endued with high wisdom, of high character and high fame, you should accept Rāma's words, in you have a care for the happiness of your sire.
We wish that Rāma may always act truthfully in respect of his father. By virtue of this truth connected with Kaikeyi, Dasaratha has gone to heaven.

sanskrit: राजर्षयश्चैव तदा सर्वे स्वांस्वां गतिं गता:
transliteration: rājarṣayaścaiva tadā sarve svāṃsvāṃ gatiṃ gatā:
english: Having said this, the Gandharvas, Maharsis, and Rājarșis each went to his proper quarter.
Having paid homage to those saints, Rāma possessed of a gracious presence, hearing their words, was filled with joy, and looked lovely with his delightful countenance.
But with his frame agitated (with emotion), Bharata with joined hands again addressed Rāghava in words faltering (with feeling).
O Rāma, taking into account the morality of this race, it behoves you to act in accordance with the solicitations of my mother (and yours).
I do not venture to govern this vast kingdom alone, or please the citizens and the inhabitants of the provinces attached to you.

sanskrit: ज्ञातयश्च हि योधाश्च मित्राणि सुहृदश्च न:
transliteration: jñātayaśca hi yodhāśca mitrāṇi suhṛdaśca na:
english: And as husbandmen remain expecting rain, our kindred, and warriors and friends and adherents wait in expectation of you.

sanskrit: इदं राज्यं महाप्राज्ञ स्थापय प्रतिपद्य हि
transliteration: idaṃ rājyaṃ mahāprājña sthāpaya pratipadya hi
english: O exceedingly wise one, accepting the kingdom, do you place it in the hands of some person. O Kākutstha, whomsoever you will chose for performing this office, will surely prove strong enough to govern the people.
Having said this, Bharata fell at his brother's feet; and sweetly addressing him, O Rāghava, solicited him once again.
Taking on his lap that sable-hued on furnished with eyes resembling lotus-leaves, Rāma with a voice like that of a mad swan, spoke to (Bharata).

sanskrit: आगता त्वामियं बुद्धि: स्वजा वैनयिकी च या
transliteration: āgatā tvāmiyaṃ buddhi: svajā vainayikī ca yā
english: You have at length attained the mental attitude that is natural and that also comes of the training one receives at the hands of his preceptor. And brother you venture greatly to protect the earth.
Taking counsel with courtiers, adherents and intelligent ministers, do you achieve grand tasks.

sanskrit: अतीयात् सागरो वेलां न प्रतिज्ञामहं पितु:
transliteration: atīyāt sāgaro velāṃ na pratijñāmahaṃ pitu:
english: Even if beauty forsake the moon, or Himavat his snow, or the ocean overleaps its shores, I shall not forsake the promise of my sire.

sanskrit: कामाद्वा तात लोभाद्वा मात्रा तुभ्यमिदं कृतम्
न तन्मनसि कर्त्तव्यं वर्त्तितव्यं च मातृवत्
transliteration: kāmādvā tāta lobhādvā mātrā tubhyamidaṃ kṛtam
na tanmanasi karttavyaṃ varttitavyaṃ ca mātṛvat
english: My brother, you ought not to cherish in your mind what your mother incited by covetousness or affection for you has done; and you should act by her as one should by one's mother.
When Rāma resembling the sun in energy and like the moon of Pratipat in appearance, had said this, Bharata said to the son of Kausalya.
O noble one, do you take off your feet your sandals adorned with gold. These shall protect what the people have got and secure to you what they lack.

sanskrit: सो ऽधिरुह्य नरव्याघ्र: पादुके ह्यवरुह्य च
english: Thereupon taking off his sandals, that highly energetic one gave them to the magnanimous Bharata.

Bharata, bowing down to the sandals, said, O hero, for, four and ten years shall I, wearing matted locks and bark, and subsisting upon fruits and roots, O scion of the Raghu race, expecting your arrival, remain outside the city, having, O subduer of foes, made over the task of government to your sandals.

sanskrit: चतुर्दशे हि सम्पूर्णे वर्षे ऽहनि रघूत्तम
न द्रक्ष्यामि यदि त्वां तु प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम्
transliteration: na drakṣyāmi yadi tvāṃ tu pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam
english: O foremost of Raghus, if after the completion of the fourteen year, I do not see you, I shall enter into fire.

sanskrit: तथेति च प्रतिज्ञाय तं परिष्वज्य सादरम्
transliteration: tatheti ca pratijñāya taṃ pariṣvajya sādaram

sanskrit: मातरं रक्ष कैकेयीं मा रोषं कुरु तां प्रति
मया च सीतया चैव शप्तो ऽसि रघुसत्तम
transliteration: mātaraṃ rakṣa kaikeyīṃ mā roṣaṃ kuru tāṃ prati
mayā ca sītayā caiva śapto 'si raghusattama

sanskrit: स पादुके ते भरत: प्रतापवान् स्वलङ्कृते सम्परिपूज्य धर्मवित्
प्रदक्षिणं चैव चकार राघवं चकार चैवोत्तमनागमूर्द्धनि
transliteration: sa pāduke te bharata: pratāpavān svalaṅkṛte samparipūjya dharmavit
pradakṣiṇaṃ caiva cakāra rāghavaṃ cakāra caivottamanāgamūrddhani
english: Then accepting those burnished and garnished sandals, Bharata versed in morality circumabulated Rāghava, and placed the sandals on the head of an excellent elephant.

sanskrit: अथानुपूर्व्यात् प्रतिनन्द्य तं जनं गुरूंश्च मन्त्रिप्रकृतीस्तथानुजौ
transliteration: athānupūrvyāt pratinandya taṃ janaṃ gurūṃśca mantriprakṛtīstathānujau
english: Then having one by one honoured that assembly, and his preceptor and the counsellors, and the subjects and his younger brothers, perpetuator of the Raghu race, steady in his own duty like. Himavat itself, took leave of them.

sanskrit: तं मातरो बाष्पगृहीतकण्ठ्यो दु:खेन नामन्त्रयितुं हि शेकु:
स त्वेव मातऽरभिवाद्य सर्वा रुदन् कुटीं स्वां प्रविवेश राम:
transliteration: taṃ mātaro bāṣpagṛhītakaṇṭhyo du:khena nāmantrayituṃ hi śeku:
sa tveva māta'rabhivādya sarvā rudan kuṭīṃ svāṃ praviveśa rāma:
english: His mothers with their throats invaded by the vapour of grief could not from distress of heart say ought to him. And Rāma also having paid homage to all of them, weeping entered his own cottage.

sanskrit: तत: शिरसि कृत्वा तु पादुके भरतस्तदा
transliteration: tata: śirasi kṛtvā tu pāduke bharatastadā
english: Then taking the pair of sandals on his head, Bharata in company with Śatrughna well pleased, ascended the car.
And Vasiştha, and Vāmadeva and Jāvāli steady his vow as well as the minister, honoured on account of their counsels, went before.
And going round the charming Mandākinī, they went eastwards, circumambulating (at the same time) the mighty hill, Citrakuta.
And beholding various kinds of beautiful minerals by thousand. Bharata accompanied by his army went by the side (of the hill).
At a short distance from Citrakuța, Bharata beheld the spot where the ascetic Bharadvāja had built his habitation.
Approaching the asylum, the puissant Bharata descended from the car, and the son of Raghu then paid homage to the saint's feet.

sanskrit: अपि कृत्यं कृतं तात रामेण च समागतम्
transliteration: api kṛtyaṃ kṛtaṃ tāta rāmeṇa ca samāgatam
english: Thereat Bharadvāja well pleased said, Have you, my child, on meeting with Rama, done what it behoved you to do?

sanskrit: एवमुक्त: स तु ततो भरद्वाजेन धीमता
transliteration: evamukta: sa tu tato bharadvājena dhīmatā
english: Thus addressed by the intelligent Bharadvāja, Bharata attached to righteousness answered the former, saying.

sanskrit: स याच्यमानो गुरुणा मया च दृढविक्रम:
transliteration: sa yācyamāno guruṇā mayā ca dṛḍhavikrama:
english: Solicited by our preceptor as well as by myself, Rāghava of steady prowess highly pleased spoke to Vasiștha.

sanskrit: चतुर्दश हि वर्षाणि या प्रतिज्ञा पितुर्मम
transliteration: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi yā pratijñā piturmama
english: I would faithfully perform my father's promise for fourteen years; for even this is the promise of my father.
Thus accosted, the eminently wise Vasiștha skilled in speech replied to Rāghava in these pregnant words.
Do you well pleased confer (on Bharata) your sandals decked in gold. Thereby, exceedingly wise one, you will be able to protect what the people have and secure to them what they have not.

sanskrit: पादुके अधिरुह्यैते मम राज्याय वै ददौ
transliteration: pāduke adhiruhyaite mama rājyāya vai dadau
english: Thus addressed by Vasiştha, Rāghava facing the east, conferred on me his sandals decked in gold, in order that I mighty carry on the government of the kingdom.
Commanded by the magnanimous Rāma, I retrace my steps. I will go to Ayodhyā, taking the sandals along with me.
Hearing these auspicious words of the highsouled Bharata, the ascetic Bharadvāja said to Bharata.
It is no wonder that Rāma has acted nobly by you, foremost among men and possessed of an (excellent) character and disposition, even as water poured out, flow downwards.
Your father Dasaratha has become freed from his debts, since he has a son like to you, righteous and attached to virtue.
When the ascetic had said this, Bharata with joined palms paid his respects to that highly wise one, by taking hold of his feet.
And after having again and again gone round Bharadvāja, the graceful Bharata went to Ayodhyā accompanied by his counsellors.
And returning by means of cars and carts, horses and elephants, that army marching in the wake of Bharata, spread wide.

sanskrit: ददृशुस्तां पुन: सर्वे गङ्गां शुभजलां नदीम्
transliteration: dadṛśustāṃ puna: sarve gaṅgāṃ śubhajalāṃ nadīm
english: And after having crossed the beautiful river Yamunā flowing in waves, they again beheld the river Gangā of auspicious waters.
And having along with his friend crossed over that river filled with beautiful waters, Bharata together with his army entered the charming city of Srigavera.

sanskrit: अयोध्यां च ततो दृष्ट्वा पित्रा भ्रात्रा विवर्जिताम्
transliteration: ayodhyāṃ ca tato dṛṣṭvā pitrā bhrātrā vivarjitām
english: And from the city of Śộngava he went to Ayodhyā and again beheld it. And seeing Ayodhyā bereft of his father and mother, Bharata burning in grief, said to the charioteer.

sanskrit: सारथे पश्य विध्वस्ता सायोध्या न प्रकाशते
transliteration: sārathe paśya vidhvastā sāyodhyā na prakāśate
english: O charioteer, behold that Ayodhyā, which shorn of its splendour and decorations, and plunged in grief, forlorn and silent, does not appear delightful.
Arriving by means of a car emitting a low and solemn sound, that lord, the highly famous Bharata speedily entered Ayodhyā.

Ranged by cats and owls, with the doors of the people's dwellings remaining closed; like a night enveloped in darkness gloomy; and invisible; resembling the beloved wife of Rāhu's enemy, Rohini, brilliant with the lustre of the latter, when she is forlorn in consequence of her lover being afflicted by that planet.

Ranged by cats and owls, with the doors of the people's dwellings remaining closed; like a night enveloped in darkness gloomy; and invisible; resembling the beloved wife of Rāhu's enemy, Rohini, brilliant with the lustre of the latter, when she is forlorn in consequence of her lover being afflicted by that planet.
Like to a mountain stream shrunk up, having its waters turbid and slightly heated, and its fowls burning in the heat; and with its fishes, alligators and other aquatic animals rendered lean.
Resembling a flame of fire devoid of smoke and streaming up in golden splendour, next sprinkled with clarified butter, and lastly appearing with its crest extinguished.
With armour scattered all round, and sick elephants and horses and cars and standards, and heroes lying dead, in distress.

Like to an army in a mighty encounter; resembling the silent ripples of the ocean raised by the gentle breeze which ere now (in the shapes of surges) were heaving, brimming over with foam and sending forth roars.
Like a silent dais after the sacrifice is over, without the sacrificial appurtenances, without worthy priests.
Like to the wife of a youthful ox, exercised with anxiety on having been forsaken by her favourite ox, staying in distress in a pen, abstaining from fresh grass.
Like to a string of new pearls divorced from noble, mild-gleaming rubies and other excellent gems.
Like a star on the expiration of its virtue, moving from its place and dislodged from heaven, dropping to the earth with its brightness contracted.
Like a blossoming creeper at the end of spring with maddened Bhramaras* suddenly rendered nerveless in consequence of being caught by a forest fire. *Black bees.
With her merchants plunged in grief, and her shops and stalls closed; like the welkin covered with clouds, and having its moon and stars hid.
Like an unclean, uncovered spot used for drinking, with all the wine drained, and scattered with broken bowls, and with the tipplers lying dead.

Like to a reservoir with its terrace riven, filled with broken pots, and lying with its pillars crushed; like a long strong bow-string fixed on a bow furnished with nooses, falling off the bow to the ground, being snapped in consequence of the pressure of the arrow.

Like to a reservoir with its terrace riven, filled with broken pots, and lying with its pillars crushed; like a long strong bow-string fixed on a bow furnished with nooses, falling off the bow to the ground, being snapped in consequence of the pressure of the arrow.
Like a mare, suddenly urged on by a rider skilled in battle, lying (on the ground), having been slain by the hostile forces.
That son of Dasaratha, the beauteous Bharata, while proceeding on his car, addressed the charioteer as he drove that best of cars, saying.

sanskrit: किं नु खल्वद्य गम्भीरो मूर्च्छितो न निशम्यते
transliteration: kiṃ nu khalvadya gambhīro mūrcchito na niśamyate
english: Why do I not hear as formerly the solemn sounds of song and instrumental music spreading on all sides in Ayodhyā?
And there does not breathe around the aroma of liquor, or the perfume of garlands, or the incense of aguru and sandal.
And on Rāma being banished, in this city is not heard the mild neighing of steeds, the rattle of vehicles, the roar of mad elephants, or the mighty clatter of arms.

sanskrit: गते हि रामे तरुणा: सन्तप्ता नोपभुञ्जते
transliteration: gate hi rāme taruṇā: santaptā nopabhuñjate
english: And on Rāma having repaired to the forest, youthful folk stricken with sorrow do not enjoy the incense of aguru and sandal, or costly fresh chaplets. And persons bearing variegated garlands do not walk abroad; and no festivities are celebrated in the city stricken with grief on account of Rāma.

Surely, the grace of the city has gone away with my brother. Surely, that Ayodhyā does not look beautiful like an autumnal night with showers pouring down. When shall my brother, coming hither like a carnival, gladden all hearts in Ayodhyā like rain in summer?

sanskrit: कदा नु खलु मे भ्राता महोत्सव इवागत:
transliteration: kadā nu khalu me bhrātā mahotsava ivāgata:

english: And the highways shall be graced with young people elegantly attired and bearing themselves bravely in Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: एवं बहुविधं जल्पन् विवेश वसतिं पितु:
transliteration: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ jalpan viveśa vasatiṃ pitu:
english: Having said this in grief, Bharata in company with the charioteer entered Ayodhyā and immediately went to the residence of his father, bereft of that foremost of men, like a cavern bereft of its lion.

sanskrit: निरीक्ष्य सर्वन्तु विविक्तमात्मवान् मुमोच बाष्पं भरत: सुदु:खित:
transliteration: nirīkṣya sarvantu viviktamātmavān mumoca bāṣpaṃ bharata: sudu:khita:
english: Seeing the inner apartment shorn of its splendour, like a day deprived of the sun, mouisted by the deities, and everywhere unclean, the self-possessed Bharata, moved by grief, began to drop tears. to his

sanskrit: ततो निक्षिप्य मातऽ: स अयोध्यायां दृढव्रत:
transliteration: tato nikṣipya māta': sa ayodhyāyāṃ dṛḍhavrata:
english: Having placed his mothers in Ayodhyā, Bharata steady in his vow, kindling in grief, said preceptors.

sanskrit: तत्र दु:खमिदं सर्वं सहिष्ये राघवं विना
transliteration: tatra du:khamidaṃ sarvaṃ sahiṣye rāghavaṃ vinā
english: I shall go to Nandigrāma, and therefore greet you all. There I shall suffer all this grief on account of Rāma's absence.

sanskrit: गतश्च हि दिवं राजा वनस्थश्च गुरुर्मम
रामं प्रतीक्षे राज्याय स हि राजा महायशा:
transliteration: gataśca hi divaṃ rājā vanasthaśca gururmama
rāmaṃ pratīkṣe rājyāya sa hi rājā mahāyaśā:
english: The king has gone to heaven, and my superior is staying in the woods. I shall remain in expectation of Rāma, assuming the reins of government. Verily that illustrious one is the king.
Hearing this excellent speech of the highsouled Bharata the counsellors as well as the priest Vasiştha said.

sanskrit: सुभृशं श्लाघनीयं च यदुक्तं भरत त्वया
transliteration: subhṛśaṃ ślāghanīyaṃ ca yaduktaṃ bharata tvayā
english: What, О Bharata, influenced by affection for your brother you say, is worthy of you and is highly commendable.
Who will not endorse what has fallen from you, ever engaged in serving your friends, established in fraternal love, and who have entered upon a noble course?
Having heard the words of the counsellors acceptable and welcome, Bharata said to the charioteer, Do you yoke my car.
Then with a cheerful countenance having spoken to his mothers, that graceful one ascended the car in company with Satrughna.
Having swiftly ascended the car, both Satrughna and Bharata, right glad at heart, set out surrounded by counsellors and priests.

sanskrit: प्रययु: प्राङ्मुखा: सर्वे नन्दिग्रामो यतो ऽभवत्
english: And going ahead, all the preceptors headed by Vasiştha proceeded eastwards, in which direction lay Nandigrāma.

sanskrit: प्रययौ भरते याते सर्वे च पुरवासिन:
transliteration: prayayau bharate yāte sarve ca puravāsina:
english: And the forces, filled with elephants and horses and cars, although not called, set out on Bharata proceeding, as well as all the citizens.

sanskrit: रथस्थ: स हि धर्मात्मा भरतो भ्रातृवत्सल:
transliteration: rathastha: sa hi dharmātmā bharato bhrātṛvatsala:
english: And ascending the car, the virtuous Bharata attached to his brother, speedily went to Nandigrāma, holding the sandals (of Rāma) on his head.

sanskrit: ततस्तु भरत: क्षिप्रं नन्दिग्रामं प्रविश्य स:
transliteration: tatastu bharata: kṣipraṃ nandigrāmaṃ praviśya sa:
english: Then entering Nandigrāma in a short time, Bharata swiftly alighted from the car and addressed his preceptors, saying.

sanskrit: एतद्राज्यं मम भ्रात्रा दत्तं संन्यासवत् स्वयम्
transliteration: etadrājyaṃ mama bhrātrā dattaṃ saṃnyāsavat svayam
english: This monarchy has been consigned to me as a trust; and these gold-decked sandals shall carry on the work of government, protecting what the people have and securing to them what they have not.

sanskrit: भरत: शिरसा कृत्वा संन्यासं पादुके तत:
transliteration: bharata: śirasā kṛtvā saṃnyāsaṃ pāduke tata:
english: Then bowing to the sandals which represented the trust. Bharata burning in grief addressed the entire body of the subjects, saying.

sanskrit: आभ्यां राज्ये स्थितो धर्म: पादुकाभ्यां गुरोर्मम
transliteration: ābhyāṃ rājye sthito dharma: pādukābhyāṃ gurormama
english: Do you speedily bold the umbrella (over these sandals). These represent the dear feet. of the exalted one. Through these sandals of my superior, will be established the regal morality (of the kingdom).

sanskrit: भ्रात्रा हि मयि संन्यासो निक्षिप्त: सौहृदादयम्
transliteration: bhrātrā hi mayi saṃnyāso nikṣipta: sauhṛdādayam
english: This kingdom from love has been conferred on me as a trust; therefore I shall govern it until Rāghava comes.

sanskrit: क्षिप्रं संयोजयित्वा तु राघवस्य पुन: स्वयम्
चरणौ तौ तु रामस्य द्रक्ष्यामि सहपादुकौ
transliteration: kṣipraṃ saṃyojayitvā tu rāghavasya puna: svayam
caraṇau tau tu rāmasya drakṣyāmi sahapādukau
english: Again speedily putting these sandals on Raghava's feet, I shall behold them with the sandals on.
On Rāghava coming (back), I shall, my burden being cast upon him, making over the kingdom to him, engage myself in serving my superior.

sanskrit: राघवाय च संन्यासं दत्त्वे मे वरपादुके
राज्यं चेदमयोध्यां च धूतपापो भवामि च
transliteration: rāghavāya ca saṃnyāsaṃ dattve me varapāduke
rājyaṃ cedamayodhyāṃ ca dhūtapāpo bhavāmi ca
english: And having rendered to Rāghava the trust in the shape of these sandals, this kingdom, and Ayodhyā, I shall be washed form my sin.

sanskrit: एवं तु विलपन् दीनो भरत: स महायशा:
transliteration: evaṃ tu vilapan dīno bharata: sa mahāyaśā:

sanskrit: तदा हि यत्कार्य्यमुपैति किञ्चिदुपायनं चोपहृतं महार्हम्
स पादुकाभ्यां प्रथमं निवेद्य चकार पश्चाद्भरतो यथावत्
transliteration: tadā hi yatkāryyamupaiti kiñcidupāyanaṃ copahṛtaṃ mahārham
sa pādukābhyāṃ prathamaṃ nivedya cakāra paścādbharato yathāvat

english: On Bharata having returned, while Rāma was dwelling in the woods, he noticed affright among the ascetics, added to a desire to remove to another place.
And those ascetic that were living happily in the asylum in Citrakuța, relying upon Rāma (for their protection), he found to be wrought up with anxiety.
And by means of signs by the eye and contractions of the brow, they, afflicted with fear, were, alluding to Răma, slowly speaking to each other.
Perceiving their anxiety, Rāma apprehensive of himself, with joined hands addressed the patriarchal ascetic, saying.
O reverend one, do you find me deviating from the path of former sovereigns, or acting contrary to their practice, which has perplexed (the minds of) these ascetics?
Have the sages seen my younger (brother), the high-souled Lakṣmaṇa, do anything from inadvertence that in unworthy of him?

sanskrit: प्र(म)मादाभ्युचितां वृत्तिं सीता युक्तं न वर्तते
transliteration: pra(ma)mādābhyucitāṃ vṛttiṃ sītā yuktaṃ na vartate
english: Does not Sītā engaged in serving you, having to serve me, now minister to you as a woman should?
Thereat a certain aged and decrepit ascetic, with his frame trembling said to Rāma ever kind towards creatures.
Where is the falling off of that one of excellent character, engaged in offices of beneficence,-more specially with reference to ascetics?
This fear arising from Rākşasas afflicts the ascetics because of you; and they, extremely agitated, converse with each other (on the subject).

sanskrit: अवलिप्तश्च पापश्च त्वां च तात न मृष्यते
transliteration: avaliptaśca pāpaśca tvāṃ ca tāta na mṛṣyate

english: A Rākşasa named Khara, a younger brother of Rāvana, has been harassing the ascetics dwelling in Janasthāna. And Dhrsta also a fearless and wicked Rākṣasa feeding on human beings, and the unrighteous Avalipta, cannot bear you, my child. As long, my child, as you have been residing in this asylum, the Rākşasas have been plaguing the ascetics.

And they show themselves sometimes in disgusting shapes, sometimes in horrible and dreadful ones, in various frightful forms capable of frightening folks. And they throw execrable and unclean things among the anchorets, and torment those that happen to come before them.

And they show themselves sometimes in disgusting shapes, sometimes in horrible and dreadful ones, in various frightful forms capable of frightening folks. And they throw execrable and unclean things among the anchorets, and torment those that happen to come before them.
And they take delight in approaching asylums unperceived, and slaughtering ascetics, after having bound them by means of their arms.
And on the occasion of sacrifices, they throw away the vessels containing sacrificial articles, pour water on the sacrificial fire and break vessels containing water.
Eager to renounce this asylum infested by those wicked ones, and removing to another place, the sages today have been exhorting me (on the subject).
And, O Rama, ere this, those wicked ones have slain ascetics. Therefore would renounce this asylum.
Not far from here is a picturesque wood abounding in fruits and roots. Thither shall I betake myself together with my own folks.
Khara shall also annoy you. If you think it proper, go hence in company with us. we
O Rāghava, although you are vigilant, able, and in all ways capable, it would be unpleasant for you to dwell here now in doubt.
When the anxious ascetic had said this, Rāma could not console him by his words.

sanskrit: स जगामाश्रमं त्यक्त्वा कुलै: कुलपति: सह
transliteration: sa jagāmāśramaṃ tyaktvā kulai: kulapati: saha
english: Then having paid homage to Rāma, and spoken to him and encouraged Rāghava, the patriach ascetic renouncing the asylum, went away along with his own people.

And Rāma having (for a time) followed the sage who was departing from that place, and having paid him respects, being permitted by them, well-pleased, and advised (as to what it behoved him to do), came to his quarters reposing there.

sanskrit: आश्रमं त्वृषिविरहितं प्रभु: क्षणमपि न विजहौ स राघव:
transliteration: āśramaṃ tvṛṣivirahitaṃ prabhu: kṣaṇamapi na vijahau sa rāghava:
english: (Thenceforth) Rāghava never for a moment left that asylum forsaken by the sages., Rāghava having such qualities in his character as were likely to stand the sages in stead, the ascetics (that remained behind) ever followed Rāghava.
When the ascetics had gone away, Rāghava reflected (as to his stay at that place); and from diverse reasons, he did not relish remaining there any further.

sanskrit: इह मे भरतो दृष्टो मातरश्च सनागरा:
transliteration: iha me bharato dṛṣṭo mātaraśca sanāgarā:
english: Here have I seen Bharata and my mother in company with the citizens. Overwhelmed with grief on my account, they ever recur to my memory.
And in consequence of the troops of that highsouled one having quartered here as well as the dung discharged by his elephants and horses, this place has got exceedingly dirty.

sanskrit: प्रातिष्ठत स वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च सङ्गत:
transliteration: prātiṣṭhata sa vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca saṅgata:
english: Therefore will I go to another quarter. Having settled this in his mind, Rāghava departed along with Videha's daughter and Laksmana.
And having arrived at Atri's asylum, that renowned one paid obeisance (to the sage); and the reverend Atri also on his pare received Rāma asason.

sanskrit: सौमित्रिं च महाभागां सीतां च समसान्त्वयत्
transliteration: saumitriṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ sītāṃ ca samasāntvayat
english: And having personally given Rāma respectful reception and entertainment, the ascetic regarded the exalted Lakşmaņa and Sītā with a gracious eye.

And his aged wife having come there, Atri greeted her; and after she had been paid homage, the sage cognizant of virtue ever engaged in the good of all creatures, gladdened her (by presenting Sītā to her.) And that best of sages said to the pious female ascetic, Anasüyā, engaged in offices of virtue, “Do you accept Videha's daughter."

sanskrit: यया मूलफले सृष्टे जाह्नवी च प्रवर्त्तिता
transliteration: yayā mūlaphale sṛṣṭe jāhnavī ca pravarttitā

sanskrit: दशरात्रं कृता रात्रि: सेयं मातेव ते ऽनघ
transliteration: daśarātraṃ kṛtā rātri: seyaṃ māteva te 'nagha

english: Let Vaidehī always resort to this aged ascetic devoid of anger, who is worthy of being bowed down to by all creatures.

sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवाणं तमृषिं तथेत्युक्त्वा स राघव:
transliteration: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tamṛṣiṃ tathetyuktvā sa rāghava:
english: When the saint had spoken thus, Rāghava saying, “So be it," turned his eyes to Sītā, and thus spoke to that one knowing morality.

O princess, you have heard what has been uttered by the ascetic. For the sake of your own welfare, do you speedily resort to the female anchoret. Do you without delay resort to the ascetic Anasuya, who is worthy of being associated with, and who has by virtue of her acts attained renown among men.f
Hearing these words of Rāghava Mithila's daughter, the illustrious Sītā, drew near the righteous wife of Atri.

Thereupon Sītā, announcing her name, saluted the pious and chaste Anasuyā old with slackened joints, with folds all over her skin, and her hair hoary from age, whose frame shook perpetually, like a plantain-leaf in the wind.

Thereupon Sītā, announcing her name, saluted the pious and chaste Anasuyā old with slackened joints, with folds all over her skin, and her hair hoary from age, whose frame shook perpetually, like a plantain-leaf in the wind.
Having paid homage to that ascetic with her senses subdued, Vaidehi glad at heart, with joined hands, enquired after her welfare.

sanskrit: तत: सीतां महाभागां दृष्ट्वा तां धर्मचारिणीम्
transliteration: tata: sītāṃ mahābhāgāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ dharmacāriṇīm
english: Seeing the virtuous Sītā engaged in righteous acts, the old lady consoling her, said "By luck it is that you regard righteousness."

sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा ज्ञातिजनं सीते मानमृद्धिं च भामिनि
transliteration: tyaktvā jñātijanaṃ sīte mānamṛddhiṃ ca bhāmini
english: O Sita, having left your kindred, and banishing pride, you have o honoured lady, followed Rāma staying in the woods.

sanskrit: नगरस्थो वनस्थो वा पापो वा यदि वा शुभ:
यासां स्त्रीणां प्रियो भर्ता तासां लोका महोदया:
transliteration: nagarastho vanastho vā pāpo vā yadi vā śubha:
yāsāṃ strīṇāṃ priyo bhartā tāsāṃ lokā mahodayā:
english: They that love their husbands, whether living in the city or the forest, whether well or ill disposed towards them, attain great state.
Wicked, ur libidinous, or indigent, a husband is a supreme deity to a wife of noble character.
Than the husband a greater friend find I none, O Vaidehī, who is worthy of being served both in this world and the next, and who is like imperishable asceticism.
But bad women whose hearts hunger after carnality, and who lord over their husbands, do not get acquainted with the virtues and demerits (of their husbands); and range at their will.
O Mithilā's daughter, surely women of this sort who are given to doing evil acts, reap infamy and fall off from righteousness.
But worthy women like you furnished with excellence, see a superior and better world, and range the celestial regions, like pious people.

sanskrit: भवस्व भर्त्तु: सहधर्मचारिणी यशश्च धर्मं च तत: समाप्स्यसि
transliteration: bhavasva bharttu: sahadharmacāriṇī yaśaśca dharmaṃ ca tata: samāpsyasi
english: Therefore following this one, and adopting the course of chaste women, do you prove the associate in virtue of your husband, and then shall you attain both fame and religious merit.
Thus addressed by Anasūyā, Vaidehī devoid of malice, honouring her words, began, “That you should instruct me is no wonder in you."
I know that a woman's spiritual guide is her husband. Even if a husband should be poor and of a disreputable character, he should be ungiudgingly obeyed by the like of me. one
I know that a woman's spiritual guide is her husband. Even if a husband should be poor and of a disreputable character, he should be ungiudgingly obeyed by the like of me. one

sanskrit: किं पुनर्यो गुण: श्लाघ्य: सानुक्रोशो जितेन्द्रिय:
transliteration: kiṃ punaryo guṇa: ślāghya: sānukrośo jitendriya:
english: And to be said of one that is crowned with qualities, kind, self-controlled, of steady affection, righteous-souled, and who is dear as a father or a mother?

sanskrit: यां वृत्तिं वर्त्तते राम: कौसल्यायां महाबल:
transliteration: yāṃ vṛttiṃ varttate rāma: kausalyāyāṃ mahābala:
english: The exceedingly strong Rāma bear himself towards the other wives of the monarch as he does towards Kausalyā herself.
Renouncing sense of self-importance that heroic conversant with righteousness, devoted to his king, regards as his mothers those on whom the monarch once cast his eyes.

sanskrit: समाहितं मे श्वश्र्वा च हृदये तद्धृतं महत्
transliteration: samāhitaṃ me śvaśrvā ca hṛdaye taddhṛtaṃ mahat
english: What my mother-in-law instructed me at the time that I was leaving for the lonely and fearful forest, is constantly present in my mind.

sanskrit: अनुशिष्टा जनन्या ऽस्मि वाक्यं तदपि मे धृतम्
transliteration: anuśiṣṭā jananyā 'smi vākyaṃ tadapi me dhṛtam
english: And what also my mother taught me in presence of fire on the occasion of the bestowal of my hand, is also remembered by me.

And, O you engaged in acts of righteousness, I have not forgotten the words that my relatives said to me, viz, the asceticism of a woman is ministering to her husband. They did not teach any thing else.
Having served her lord. Sāvitri is highly honoured in heaven; and you also, following the same course, by virtue of having served your husband, has secured heaven.

sanskrit: रोहिणी न विना चन्द्रं मुहूर्त्तमपि दृश्यते
transliteration: rohiṇī na vinā candraṃ muhūrttamapi dṛśyate
english: And this foremost of females, this goddess of heaven, Rohiņi, is not seen for a moment without the moon.
And prime women of this sort, firm in their husbands, are highly respected in the celestial regions by virtue of their pious acts.

sanskrit: ततो ऽनसूया संहृष्टा श्रुत्वोक्तं सीतया वच:
english: Hearing Sītā's words, Anasuyā, exceedingly delighted, smelling her head, spoke thus, pleasing Maithili.

sanskrit: तत्संश्रित्य बलं सीते छन्दये त्वां शुचिस्मिते
transliteration: tatsaṃśritya balaṃ sīte chandaye tvāṃ śucismite
english: By observing restrictions, I have earned great asceticism. By resorting to that energy, I would, O Sīta, confer a boon upon you, O you of pure vows.

sanskrit: उपपन्नं मनोज्ञं च वचनं तव मैथिलि
प्रीता चास्म्युचितं किं ते करवाणि ब्रवीहि मे
transliteration: upapannaṃ manojñaṃ ca vacanaṃ tava maithili
prītā cāsmyucitaṃ kiṃ te karavāṇi bravīhi me
english: O Maithili, your words are just and proper. I am well pleased (with you). Tell me, O Sītā, what good shall I do you?
Hearing her words, Sītā, surprised, said with a smile, to that lady equipped with ascetic strength, “All this has been done by you."

sanskrit: सा त्वेवमुक्ता धर्मज्ञा तया प्रीततरा ऽभवत्
सफलं च प्रहर्षं ते हन्त सीते करोम्यहम्
transliteration: saphalaṃ ca praharṣaṃ te hanta sīte karomyaham
english: Thus accosted, that one cognizant of virtue, was still more pleased, and said, “I am exceedingly pleased (with your words). I will attain a desire of mine."

sanskrit: इदं दिव्यं वरं माल्यं वस्त्रमाभरणानि च
transliteration: idaṃ divyaṃ varaṃ mālyaṃ vastramābharaṇāni ca
english: This noble and grand garland, this apparel, these ornaments, and this precious paste for adorning the person, presented by me, let these, O Sītā, grace your person. These, worthy of you will never be tarnished.

sanskrit: मया दत्तमिदं सीते तव गात्राणि शोभयेत्
transliteration: mayā dattamidaṃ sīte tava gātrāṇi śobhayet
english: This noble and grand garland, this apparel, these ornaments, and this precious paste for adorning the person, presented by me, let these, O Sītā, grace your person. These, worthy of you will never be tarnished.
O daughter of Janaka, daubing your person with this excellent paint, you will grace your husband even as Śrī does the undeteriorating Visnu.

Thereupon Mithila's daughter accepted those things presented to her out of love, viz., the apparel, the paint, the ornaments and the garland. Having accepted those accepted those presents conferred on her from love, that illustrious one, Sītā, quietly sat beside the female ascetic with joined hands.

sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य च तत् सीता प्रीतिदानं यशस्विनी
transliteration: pratigṛhya ca tat sītā prītidānaṃ yaśasvinī
english: Thereupon Mithila's daughter accepted those things presented to her out of love, viz., the apparel, the paint, the ornaments and the garland. Having accepted those accepted those presents conferred on her from love, that illustrious one, Sītā, quietly sat beside the female ascetic with joined hands.
Then as Sītā was sitting, Anasūyā firm in vow asked her concerning a thing that was near her heart, saying.
I have heard, O Sītā, that you were won by the renowned Rāghava on the occasion of a selfchoice.

sanskrit: तां कथां श्रोतुमिच्छामि विस्तरेण च मैथिलि
transliteration: tāṃ kathāṃ śrotumicchāmi vistareṇa ca maithili
english: O Maithili, that story I should like to hear, related at length. It therefore, behoves you to relate that to me in detail.

sanskrit: एवमुक्ता तु सा सीता तां ततो धर्मचारिणीम्
श्रूयतामिति चोक्त्वा वै कथयामास तां कथाम्
transliteration: evamuktā tu sā sītā tāṃ tato dharmacāriṇīm
śrūyatāmiti coktvā vai kathayāmāsa tāṃ kathām
english: Thus address, Sītā, saying to the ascetic engaged in pious acts, "Listen!" began to tell the story.
Mithila's lord, the heroic Janaka, justly rule the earth, engaged in observing the duties of Ks atriyas.

sanskrit: अहं किलोत्थिता भित्त्वा जगतीं नृपते: सुता
transliteration: ahaṃ kilotthitā bhittvā jagatīṃ nṛpate: sutā
english: As he was ploughing a plain intended for a sacrifice, I rose from under the earth; and (in this sense) I am the daughter of that king.
Tending me, with my body covered with dust, Janaka, engaged in throwing handfuls of dust (to level hollow spots), was struck with amazement.
Being childless, he took me on his lap from affection, and saying, 'This is my daughter', conceived affection for me.

sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षे च वागुक्ता प्रति मा ऽमानुषी किल
transliteration: antarikṣe ca vāguktā prati mā 'mānuṣī kila
english: Then there were uttered words in the welkin, resembling those of a human being,! 'O king, in all righteousness, this is your daughter'.

sanskrit: तत: प्रहृष्टो धर्मात्मा पिता मे मिथिलाधिप:
transliteration: tata: prahṛṣṭo dharmātmā pitā me mithilādhipa:
english: Then well-pleased, my righteous father, the king, lord of Mithilā, receiving me, attained mighty good fortune.
Consigned to the pious eldest noble one (queen), desirous of having offspring, I was brought up by that mild lady, with the tenderness of a mother.

sanskrit: पतिसंयोगसुलभं वयो दृष्ट्वा तु मे पिता
transliteration: patisaṃyogasulabhaṃ vayo dṛṣṭvā tu me pitā
english: (In time) seeing me fit for the company of a husband, my father in distress was plunged in thought, like a poor man that has lost his wealth.
Even if the father of a girl be like to ſakra himself on earth he reaps odium at the hands of his equals and inferiors.
Perceiving this obloquy at a short distance, the king was plunged in a sea of anxiety, but could not cross it, like one that has no raft.

sanskrit: सदृशं चानुरूपं च महीपाल: पतिं मम
transliteration: sadṛśaṃ cānurūpaṃ ca mahīpāla: patiṃ mama
english: Knowing me as unborn from any female vessel, the lord of earth reflecting upon it, could not come upon a suitable and fit husband for me.
Then as he reflected, this thought occurred to him 'I will righteously celebrate the self-choice of my daughters'.
In the great sacrifice of Daksa, the highsouled Varuna had well-pleased conferred on Devarata an excellent bow with inexhaustible arrows and a couple of quivers.
Incapable of being moved on account of its weight, the kings could not even dream of bending the bow.

sanskrit: तद्धनु: प्राप्य मे पित्रा व्याहृतं सत्यवादिना
transliteration: taddhanu: prāpya me pitrā vyāhṛtaṃ satyavādinā
english: Having obtained the bow, my truthful father said, 'No fear!' inviting at the same time the kings to an assembly of sovereigns.

sanskrit: इदं च धनुरुद्यम्य सज्यं य: कुरुते नर:
तस्य मे दुहिता भार्या भविष्यति न संशय:
transliteration: idaṃ ca dhanurudyamya sajyaṃ ya: kurute nara:
tasya me duhitā bhāryā bhaviṣyati na saṃśaya:
english: He that, raising the bow, shall string it, shall doubtless receive my daughter for his wife.
Seeing that best of bows in weight resembling a hill, the kings saluting it, go away, unable to move it.

sanskrit: सुदीर्घस्य तु कालस्य राघवो ऽयं महाद्युति:
english: It came to pass that after a long time, this highly effulgent Rāghava came to witness the sacrifice in company with Viśvāmitra. And Rāma having truth for his prowess, and the righteous Viśvāmitra were respectfully received by my sire.
Thus accosted by the Vipra, my father brought the bow, and showed that celestial bow to the princes.
Thus accosted by the Vipra, my father brought the bow, and showed that celestial bow to the princes.
Thereupon, in the twinkling of an eye, bending it, the powerful (Raghava) stringed the bow and drew it.

sanskrit: तेन पूरयता वेगान्मध्ये भग्नं द्विधा धनु:
transliteration: tena pūrayatā vegānmadhye bhagnaṃ dvidhā dhanu:
english: And as he drew it vehemently, it broke in the middle in twain. And the sound of it was dreadful like to the bursting of a thunder-bolt.

sanskrit: ततो ऽहं तत्र रामाय पित्रा सत्याभिसन्धिना
english: Then raising an excellent vessel of water, my truthful father prepared to bestow me on Rāghava.

sanskrit: दीयमानां न तु तदा प्रतिजग्राह राघव:
transliteration: dīyamānāṃ na tu tadā pratijagrāha rāghava:
english: And bestowed on Rāghava, I was accepted of him, after he had consulted the wish of his father, that lord, the master of Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: मम पित्रा त्वहं दत्ता रामाय विदितात्मने
transliteration: mama pitrā tvahaṃ dattā rāmāya viditātmane
english: And inviting my father-in-law, the old king Dasaratha, my father bestowed me on Rāma having knowledge of self.

sanskrit: भार्य्यार्थे लक्ष्मणस्यापि दत्ता पित्रा मम स्वयम्
transliteration: bhāryyārthe lakṣmaṇasyāpi dattā pitrā mama svayam

sanskrit: एवं दत्तास्मि रामाय तदा तस्मिन् स्वयम्वरे
transliteration: evaṃ dattāsmi rāmāya tadā tasmin svayamvare

sanskrit: अनसूया तु धर्मज्ञा श्रुत्वा तां महतीं कथाम्
transliteration: anasūyā tu dharmajñā śrutvā tāṃ mahatīṃ kathām
english: Having heard this grand story, Anasāyā cognizant of righteousness, smelling the head of Mithilā's daughter, embraced Sītā with her arms.

sanskrit: यथा स्वयम्वरं वृत्तं तत्सर्वं हि श्रुतं मया
रमे ऽहं कथया ते तु दृढं मधुरभाषिणि
transliteration: yathā svayamvaraṃ vṛttaṃ tatsarvaṃ hi śrutaṃ mayā
rame 'haṃ kathayā te tu dṛḍhaṃ madhurabhāṣiṇi
english: I have heard all that you, describing the selfchoice, have spoken sweetly and beautifully in articulated letters and feet.

O sweet-speeched one, I have been delighted with your narration. But ushering in the auspicious night, the graceful Sun has set. And there are heard the notes of feathered ones, which, after having gone about in search of food, are resting now for the purpose of sleeping.
And these ascetics having bathed, are wending their way in a body, carrying waterpitchers, their barks drenched with water.
The smoke arising from the fire-sacrifice duly performed by the ascetics, reddish like the hue of the pigeon's neck, is seen, wafted by the wind.

sanskrit: विप्रकृष्टेपि देशे ऽस्मिन्न प्रकाशन्ति वै दिश:
english: And trees of spare foliage appear dense (on all sides); and distance is no longer perceptible.
And animals ranging in the night are going about all round; and those deer of the asylum are reposing on the daises.
O Sītā, the night crested by the stars has arrived; and, veiled in moonlight, appears the moon in the heavens.
Go you; I permit you. Do you seek the society of Rāma. I have been pleased with your sweet converse.

sanskrit: अलङ्कुरु च तावत्त्वं प्रत्यक्षं मम मैथिलि
transliteration: alaṅkuru ca tāvattvaṃ pratyakṣaṃ mama maithili
english: O daughter of Mithilā, do you deck yourself before me. Do you thus please me, my child, you that look beautiful with excellent ornaments.

sanskrit: प्रणम्य शिरसा तस्यै रामं त्वभिमुखी ययौ
transliteration: praṇamya śirasā tasyai rāmaṃ tvabhimukhī yayau
english: Thereat, having adorned herself, Sītā, resembling the daughter of a celestial, bowing down to the feet (of the female ascetic), directed her steps towards Rāma.

sanskrit: तथा तु भूषितां सीतां ददर्श वदतां वर:
transliteration: tathā tu bhūṣitāṃ sītāṃ dadarśa vadatāṃ vara:
english: And that best of speakers, Raghava, saw Sita, decked with the ornaments affectionately presented by the ascetic; and he rejoiced thereat.
Then Mithila's daughter, Sita, related to Rama all about her having been affectionately presented by the ascetic with attire, ornaments and the garland.
Thereupon, witnessing the honour that had been accorded to Maithili, rare among men, Rāma became well pleased, as also that mighty car-warrior, Laksmana.
Then Raghu's son, ministered to by the ascetic, happily spent the delightful night there, with her face resembling the moon.
On the night having passed away, those foremost of men, after performing their ablutions, enquired of the ascetics performing fire sacrifices, who lived in the forest.

Thereat the righteous ascetics ranging the forest said that all the sides of the forest were infested by Rākşasas. “Ferocious beasts feasting on blood, and Rākşasas, O Rāghava, living on human beings, wearing various shapes, abide in this mighty forest."

Thereat the righteous ascetics ranging the forest said that all the sides of the forest were infested by Rākşasas. “Ferocious beasts feasting on blood, and Rākşasas, O Rāghava, living on human beings, wearing various shapes, abide in this mighty forest."

sanskrit: उच्छिष्टं वा प्रमत्तं वा तापसं धर्मचारिणम्
transliteration: ucchiṣṭaṃ vā pramattaṃ vā tāpasaṃ dharmacāriṇam
english: These eat up ascetics leading the Brahmacarya mode of life, who happen to be unclean or heedless. Do you, therefore, O Raghava, let them.

sanskrit: अनेन तु वनं दुर्गं गन्तुं राघव ते क्षमम्
transliteration: anena tu vanaṃ durgaṃ gantuṃ rāghava te kṣamam
english: This is the path of the Maharșis, who procure fruits in the forest. By this way you will be able to enter the impracticable wild, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: इतीव तै: प्राञ्जलिभिस्तपस्विभिर्द्विजै: कृत: स्वस्त्ययन: परं तप:
वनं सभार्य्य: प्रविऺवेश राघव: सलक्ष्मण: सूर्य्यमिवाभ्रमण्डलम्
transliteration: itīva tai: prāñjalibhistapasvibhirdvijai: kṛta: svastyayana: paraṃ tapa:
vanaṃ sabhāryya: praviveśa rāghava: salakṣmaṇa: sūryyamivābhramaṇḍalam
english: Thus addressed by the ascetic twice-born ones, and having been blessed by them, that repressor of foes, Rāghava, entered the forest in company with his wife and Lakşmaņa, like the sun entering a mass of clouds.

sanskrit: रामो ददर्श दुर्धर्ष तापस आश्रम मण्डलम्
transliteration: rāmo dadarśa durdharṣa tāpasa āśrama maṇḍalam

sanskrit: कुश चीर परिक्षिप्तम् ब्राह्म्या लक्ष्म्या समावृतम्
यथा प्रदीप्तम् दुर्दर्शम् गगने सूर्य मण्डलम्
transliteration: kuśa cīra parikṣiptam brāhmyā lakṣmyā samāvṛtam
yathā pradīptam durdarśam gagane sūrya maṇḍalam

sanskrit: शरण्यम् सर्व भूतानाम् सु संमृष्ट अजिरम् सदा
मृगैः बहुभिः आकीर्णम् पक्षि सन्घैः समावृतम्
transliteration: śaraṇyam sarva bhūtānām su saṃmṛṣṭa ajiram sadā
mṛgaiḥ bahubhiḥ ākīrṇam pakṣi sanghaiḥ samāvṛtam

sanskrit: पूजितम् च उपनृत्तम् च नित्यम् अप्सरसाम् गणैः
विशालैः अग्नि शरणैः स्रुक् भाण्डैः अजिनैः कुशैः
transliteration: pūjitam ca upanṛttam ca nityam apsarasām gaṇaiḥ
viśālaiḥ agni śaraṇaiḥ sruk bhāṇḍaiḥ ajinaiḥ kuśaiḥ

sanskrit: समिद्भिः तोय कलशैः फल मूलैः च शोभितम्
आरण्यैः च महा वृक्षैः पुण्यैः स्वादु फलैर् वृतम्
transliteration: samidbhiḥ toya kalaśaiḥ phala mūlaiḥ ca śobhitam
āraṇyaiḥ ca mahā vṛkṣaiḥ puṇyaiḥ svādu phalair vṛtam

sanskrit: बलि होम अर्चितम् पुण्यम् ब्रह्म घोष निनादितम्
पुष्पैः च अन्यैः परिक्षिप्तम् पद्मिन्या च स पद्मया
transliteration: bali homa arcitam puṇyam brahma ghoṣa nināditam
puṣpaiḥ ca anyaiḥ parikṣiptam padminyā ca sa padmayā

sanskrit: फलमूल अशनैः दान्तैः चीर कृष्णाजिन अम्बरैः
सूर्य वैश्वानर आभैः च पुराणैः मुनिभिर् युतम्
transliteration: phalamūla aśanaiḥ dāntaiḥ cīra kṛṣṇājina ambaraiḥ
sūrya vaiśvānara ābhaiḥ ca purāṇaiḥ munibhir yutam

sanskrit: पुण्यैः च नियत आहारैः शोभितम् परम ऋषिभिः
तत् ब्रह्म भवन प्रख्यम् ब्रह्म घोष निनादितम्
transliteration: puṇyaiḥ ca niyata āhāraiḥ śobhitam parama ṛṣibhiḥ
tat brahma bhavana prakhyam brahma ghoṣa nināditam

sanskrit: ब्रह्म विद्भिः महा भागैः ब्राह्मणैः उपशोभितम्
तत् दृष्ट्वा राघवः श्रीमान् तापस आश्रम मण्डलम्
transliteration: brahma vidbhiḥ mahā bhāgaiḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ upaśobhitam
tat dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ śrīmān tāpasa āśrama maṇḍalam

sanskrit: अभ्यगच्छत् महातेजा विज्यम् कृत्वा महद् धनुः
दिव्य ज्ञान उपपन्नाः ते रामम् दृष्ट्वा महर्षयः
transliteration: abhyagacchat mahātejā vijyam kṛtvā mahad dhanuḥ
divya jñāna upapannāḥ te rāmam dṛṣṭvā maharṣayaḥ

sanskrit: अभिजग्मुः तदा प्रीता वैदेहीम् च यशस्विनीम्
ते तु सोमम् इव उद्यन्तम् दृष्ट्वा वै धर्मचारिणम्
transliteration: abhijagmuḥ tadā prītā vaidehīm ca yaśasvinīm
te tu somam iva udyantam dṛṣṭvā vai dharmacāriṇam

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणम् च एव दृष्ट्वा तु वैदेहीम् च यशश्विनीम्
transliteration: lakṣmaṇam ca eva dṛṣṭvā tu vaidehīm ca yaśaśvinīm

sanskrit: ददृशुर् विस्मित आकारा रामस्य वन वासिनः
transliteration: dadṛśur vismita ākārā rāmasya vana vāsinaḥ
english: And those dwellers of the wood, struck with wonder, beheld Rāma's tender grace and loveliness and elegance of dress.

sanskrit: वैदेहीम् लक्ष्मणम् रामम् नेत्रैर् अनिमिषैर् इव
आश्चर्य भूतान् ददृशुः सर्वे ते वन वासिनः
transliteration: vaidehīm lakṣmaṇam rāmam netrair animiṣair iva
āścarya bhūtān dadṛśuḥ sarve te vana vāsinaḥ
english: And struck with astonishment, those inhabitants of the woods of pre-eminent piety saw Vaidehī, Lakşmaņa and Rāma, with winkless eyes.

sanskrit: अत्र एनम् हि महाभागाः सर्व भूत हिते रताः
transliteration: atra enam hi mahābhāgāḥ sarva bhūta hite ratāḥ
english: And those persons of exalted virtue, engaged in the welfare of all creatures, made Rāghava, their guest, sit down in their thatched cottage.

sanskrit: ततो रामस्य सत्कृत्य विधिना पावक उपमाः
transliteration: tato rāmasya satkṛtya vidhinā pāvaka upamāḥ
english: Then, having received Rāma respectfully according to scriptural prescription, those virtuous ones of eminent piety, resembling fire, procured water (for Rāma).

sanskrit: मूलम् पुष्पम् फलम् सर्वम् आश्रमम् च महात्मनः
transliteration: mūlam puṣpam phalam sarvam āśramam ca mahātmanaḥ

sanskrit: धर्मपालो जनस्य अस्य शरण्यः च महायशाः
transliteration: dharmapālo janasya asya śaraṇyaḥ ca mahāyaśāḥ

sanskrit: पूजनीयः च मान्यः च राजा दण्डधरो गुरुः
इन्द्रस्य एव चतुर्भागः प्रजा रक्षति राघव
transliteration: pūjanīyaḥ ca mānyaḥ ca rājā daṇḍadharo guruḥ
indrasya eva caturbhāgaḥ prajā rakṣati rāghava

sanskrit: राजा तस्माद् वरान् भोगान् रम्यान् भुङ्क्ते नमस्कृतः
ते वयम् भवता रक्ष्या भवद् विषय वासिनः
नगरस्थो वनस्थो वा त्वम् नः राजा जनेश्वरः
transliteration: rājā tasmād varān bhogān ramyān bhuṅkte namaskṛtaḥ
te vayam bhavatā rakṣyā bhavad viṣaya vāsinaḥ
nagarastho vanastho vā tvam naḥ rājā janeśvaraḥ
english: And we, being in your dominions, ought to be protected by you. Whether living in the city or in the woods, you, lord of men, are our sovereign.

sanskrit: न्यस्त दण्डा वयम् राजन् जित क्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः
रक्षणीयाः त्वया शश्वद् गर्भ भूताः तपोधनाः
transliteration: nyasta daṇḍā vayam rājan jita krodhā jitendriyāḥ
rakṣaṇīyāḥ tvayā śaśvad garbha bhūtāḥ tapodhanāḥ
english: We have renounced chastising others; and, O monarch, we have conquered our anger, and subdued our passions. Therefore, even as a child in its mother's womb (should be protected by her), should we be protected by you."

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा फलैर् मूलैः पुष्पैर् अन्यैः च राघवम्
वन्यैः च विविध आहारैः स लक्ष्मणम् अपूजयन्
transliteration: evam uktvā phalair mūlaiḥ puṣpair anyaiḥ ca rāghavam
vanyaiḥ ca vividha āhāraiḥ sa lakṣmaṇam apūjayan
english: Having said this, they entertained Rāghava, along with Laksmana, with fruits and roots and flowers and diverse other edibles procurable in the woods.

sanskrit: तथाऽन्ये तापसाः सिद्धा रामम् वैश्वानर उपमाः
न्याय वृत्ता यथा न्यायम् तर्पयामासुर् ईश्वरम्
transliteration: tathā'nye tāpasāḥ siddhā rāmam vaiśvānara upamāḥ
nyāya vṛttā yathā nyāyam tarpayāmāsur īśvaram
english: In the same way, other ascetics of accomplished purposes, living lives of integrity, duly pleased that lord, Rāma, resembling Vaisvānara.

sanskrit: कृत आतिथ्योऽथ रामस्तु सूर्यस्य उदयनम् प्रति
आमंत्र्य स मुनीम् तत् सर्वान् वनम् एव अन्वगाहत
transliteration: kṛta ātithyo'tha rāmastu sūryasya udayanam prati
āmaṃtrya sa munīm tat sarvān vanam eva anvagāhata
english: Having received the homage of the ascetics, Rāma about sun-rise, having greeted them all, entered into the forest.

sanskrit: नाना मृग गण आकीर्णम् ऋक्ष शार्दूल सेवितम्
ध्वस्त वृक्ष लता गुल्मम् दुर्दर्श सलिलाशयम्
transliteration: nānā mṛga gaṇa ākīrṇam ṛkṣa śārdūla sevitam
dhvasta vṛkṣa latā gulmam durdarśa salilāśayam
english: And Rāma, followed by Lakṣmaṇa, saw the heart of the forest abounding in various kinds of beasts, ranged by bears and tigers, with its trees and shrubs torn and trampled, its pools turbid, and its birds crying.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मण अनुचरोओ रामो वन मध्यम् ददर्श ह
transliteration: lakṣmaṇa anucaroo rāmo vana madhyam dadarśa ha
english: And Rāma, followed by Lakṣmaṇa, saw the heart of the forest abounding in various kinds of beasts, ranged by bears and tigers, with its trees and shrubs torn and trampled, its pools turbid, and its birds crying.

sanskrit: सीताया सह काकुत्स्थः तस्मिन् घोर मृग आयुते
ददर्श गिरि शृङ्ग आभम् पुरुषादम् महास्वनम्
transliteration: sītāyā saha kākutsthaḥ tasmin ghora mṛga āyute
dadarśa giri śṛṅga ābham puruṣādam mahāsvanam

sanskrit: बीभत्सम् विषमम् दीर्घम् विकृतम् घोर दर्शनम्
transliteration: bībhatsam viṣamam dīrgham vikṛtam ghora darśanam

sanskrit: वसानम् चर्म वैयाघ्रम् वस आर्द्रम् रुधिरोक्षितम्
त्रासनम् सर्व भूतानाम् व्यादितास्यम् इव अन्तकम्
transliteration: vasānam carma vaiyāghram vasa ārdram rudhirokṣitam
trāsanam sarva bhūtānām vyāditāsyam iva antakam

sanskrit: त्रीन् सिंहान् चतुरो व्याघ्रान् द्वौ वृकौ पृषतान् दश
सविषाणम् वसादिग्धम् गजस्य च शिरो महत्
transliteration: trīn siṃhān caturo vyāghrān dvau vṛkau pṛṣatān daśa
saviṣāṇam vasādigdham gajasya ca śiro mahat

sanskrit: स रामम् लक्ष्मणम् चैव सीताम् दृष्ट्वा च मैथिलीम्
transliteration: sa rāmam lakṣmaṇam caiva sītām dṛṣṭvā ca maithilīm

sanskrit: अभ्य धावत् सुसंक्रुद्धो प्रजाः काल इव अन्तकः
स कृत्वा भैरवम् नादम् चालयन् इव मेदिनीम्
transliteration: abhya dhāvat susaṃkruddho prajāḥ kāla iva antakaḥ
sa kṛtvā bhairavam nādam cālayan iva medinīm
english: Having seen Rāma and Laksmana as well as Sītā the daughter of Mithilā, he growing angry, rushed (against them), like the Destroyer himself rushing against creatures at the universal dissolution.

sanskrit: अङ्केन आदाय वैदेहीम् अपक्रम्य तदा अब्रवीत्
युवाम् जटा चीर धरौ सभार्यौ क्षीण जीवितौ
transliteration: aṅkena ādāya vaidehīm apakramya tadā abravīt
yuvām jaṭā cīra dharau sabhāryau kṣīṇa jīvitau
english: Uttering a dreadful yell, and, as if making the earth tremble, he took Vaidehi on his waist, and, going a little distance, said, “O you wearing bark and matted locks, O you of feeble strength, that accompanied by your (common) wife, have entered the forest of Dandaka, bearing bows and arrows and scimitars, why, being ascetics, do you wish to associate with a (single) woman?

sanskrit: प्रविष्टौ दण्डकारण्यम् शर चाप असि पाणिनौ
कथम् तापसयोः युवाम् च वासः प्रमदया सह
transliteration: praviṣṭau daṇḍakāraṇyam śara cāpa asi pāṇinau
katham tāpasayoḥ yuvām ca vāsaḥ pramadayā saha

sanskrit: अधर्म चारिणौ पापौ कौ युवाम् मुनि दूषकौ
अहम् वनम् इदम् दुर्गम् विराघो नाम राक्षसः
transliteration: adharma cāriṇau pāpau kau yuvām muni dūṣakau
aham vanam idam durgam virāgho nāma rākṣasaḥ

sanskrit: चरामि सायुधो नित्यम् ऋषि मांसानि भक्षयन्
इयम् नारी वरारोहा मम भार्या भविष्यति
transliteration: carāmi sāyudho nityam ṛṣi māṃsāni bhakṣayan
iyam nārī varārohā mama bhāryā bhaviṣyati

sanskrit: युवयोः पापयोः च अहम् पास्यामि रुधिरम् मृधे
तस्य एवम् ब्रुवतो दुष्टम् विराधस्य दुरात्मनः
transliteration: yuvayoḥ pāpayoḥ ca aham pāsyāmi rudhiram mṛdhe
tasya evam bruvato duṣṭam virādhasya durātmanaḥ

sanskrit: सीता प्रावेपिता उद्वेगात् प्रवाते कदली यथा
transliteration: sītā prāvepitā udvegāt pravāte kadalī yathā
english: Hearing the wicked and vaunting speech of the impious Virādha, as he said this, Janaka's daughter, Sītā, began to tremble from fear, like a plantain tree shaken by the wind.

sanskrit: ताम् दृष्ट्वा राघवः सीताम् विराध अङ्कगताम् शुभाम्
transliteration: tām dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ sītām virādha aṅkagatām śubhām
english: Seeing the graceful Sītā on the waist of Virādha, Rāghava with a blank countenance said to Laksmana,

sanskrit: पश्य सौम्य नरेन्द्रस्य जनकस्य अत्म संभवाम्
transliteration: paśya saumya narendrasya janakasya atma saṃbhavām
english: O amiable one, behold the daughter of king Janaka, my wife of pure ways, an illustrious princess brought up in luxury, on Virādha's waist.

sanskrit: यत् अभिप्रेतम् अस्मासु प्रियम् वर वृतम् च यत्
transliteration: yat abhipretam asmāsu priyam vara vṛtam ca yat

sanskrit: कैकेय्यास्तु सुसंवृत्तम् क्षिप्रम् अद्य एव लक्ष्मण
या न तुष्यति राज्येन पुत्रार्थे दीर्घ दर्शिनी
transliteration: kaikeyyāstu susaṃvṛttam kṣipram adya eva lakṣmaṇa
yā na tuṣyati rājyena putrārthe dīrgha darśinī

sanskrit: अद्य इदानीम् सकामा सा या माता मम मध्यमा
transliteration: adya idānīm sakāmā sā yā mātā mama madhyamā

sanskrit: पर स्पर्शात् तु वैदेह्या न दुःखतरम् अस्ति मे
पितुर् विनाशात् सौमित्रे स्व राज्य हरणात् तथा
transliteration: para sparśāt tu vaidehyā na duḥkhataram asti me
pitur vināśāt saumitre sva rājya haraṇāt tathā
english: O Sumitra's son, nothing can impart to me greater anguish than the touching of Vaidehi by another, which surpasses my father's demise and my having been deprived of the kingdom.”'

sanskrit: इति ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे बाष्प शोक परिप्लुतः
अब्रवीत् लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धो रुद्धो नाग इव श्वसन्
transliteration: iti bruvati kākutsthe bāṣpa śoka pariplutaḥ
abravīt lakṣmaṇaḥ kruddho ruddho nāga iva śvasan
english: As Kākutstha with his eyes flooded with tears was speaking thus, Lakşmaņa flying into a rage, spoke like to a confined elephant:

sanskrit: अनाथ इव भूतानाम् नाथः त्वम् वासवोपमः
मया प्रेष्येण काकुत्स्थः किम् अर्थम् परितप्यसे
transliteration: anātha iva bhūtānām nāthaḥ tvam vāsavopamaḥ
mayā preṣyeṇa kākutsthaḥ kim artham paritapyase
english: Why do you, O Kākutstha, being the lord of all creatures and resembling Väsava himself, and also backed by myself, your servant, grieve like one forlorn ?

sanskrit: शरेण निहतस्य अद्य मया क्रुद्धेन रक्षसः
विराधस्य गत असोः हि मही पास्यति शोणितम्
transliteration: śareṇa nihatasya adya mayā kruddhena rakṣasaḥ
virādhasya gata asoḥ hi mahī pāsyati śoṇitam
english: The earth shall drink the gore of this Rākşasa, Virādha, when deprived of life, after he has been slain with a shaft by my angry self.

sanskrit: राज्य कामे मम क्रोधो भरते यो बभूव ह
तम् विराधे विमोक्ष्यामि वज्री वज्रम् इव अचले
transliteration: rājya kāme mama krodho bharate yo babhūva ha
tam virādhe vimokṣyāmi vajrī vajram iva acale
english: That ire of mine which I had conceived against Bharata hankering after the kingdom, will I discharge on Virādha; even as the wielder of the thunder-bolt hurls his weapon at a hi!l.

sanskrit: मम भुज बल वेग वेगितःपततु शरोऽस्य महान् महोरसि
व्यपनयतु तनोः च जीवितम्पततु ततः च महीम् विघूर्णितः
transliteration: mama bhuja bala vega vegitaḥpatatu śaro'sya mahān mahorasi
vyapanayatu tanoḥ ca jīvitampatatu tataḥ ca mahīm vighūrṇitaḥ
english: Let my mighty arrow acquiring velocity from the speed imparted to it through the energy of my arms, light on his huge breast, and force his life from forth his body; and let him whirling (at length) fall down to the earth.

sanskrit: अथ उवाच पुनर् वाक्यम् विराधः पूरयन् वनम्
पृच्छतो मम हि ब्रूतम् कौ युवाम् क्व गमिष्यथः
transliteration: atha uvāca punar vākyam virādhaḥ pūrayan vanam
pṛcchato mama hi brūtam kau yuvām kva gamiṣyathaḥ
english: Then Virādha again spoke filling the forest, Do you tell me who ask you, who are you and whither are you going? The North-West Provinces text has additional Sloka : Having said this, the graceful Lakşmaņa spoke to Virādha as if jestingly, Who are you that coming to the forest, are ranging it pleasantly?-

sanskrit: तम् उवाच ततो रामो राक्षसम् ज्वलित आननम्
transliteration: tam uvāca tato rāmo rākṣasam jvalita ānanam
english: Thereupon, the highly energetic Rāma answered the Rākşasa with a flaming face, when he had thus asked (Rāma) that he belonged to the Iksvaku race. Know us that are in the forest, for Kșatriyas of respectable character. I also am anxious of knowing who you are, wandering in the Dandakas.

sanskrit: क्षत्रियौ वृत्त संपन्नौ विद्धि नौ वनगोचरौ
त्वाम् तु वेदितुम् इच्छावः कः त्वम् चरसि दण्डकान्
transliteration: kṣatriyau vṛtta saṃpannau viddhi nau vanagocarau
tvām tu veditum icchāvaḥ kaḥ tvam carasi daṇḍakān
english: Thereupon, the highly energetic Rāma answered the Rākşasa with a flaming face, when he had thus asked (Rāma) that he belonged to the Iksvaku race. Know us that are in the forest, for Kșatriyas of respectable character. I also am anxious of knowing who you are, wandering in the Dandakas.

sanskrit: तम् उवाच विराधः तु रामम् सत्य पराक्रमम्
हन्त वक्ष्यामि ते राजन् निबोध मम राघव
transliteration: tam uvāca virādhaḥ tu rāmam satya parākramam
hanta vakṣyāmi te rājan nibodha mama rāghava
english: Virădha answered Råma having truth for his prowess, Ah! I will tell you, O king. Do you,O Răghava understand!

sanskrit: पुत्रः किल जवस्य अहम् माता मम शतह्रदा
विराध इति माम् आहुः पृथिव्याम् सर्व राक्षसाः
transliteration: putraḥ kila javasya aham mātā mama śatahradā
virādha iti mām āhuḥ pṛthivyām sarva rākṣasāḥ
english: I am son of Java, and my mother is Satahradā. All the Rāksasas of the earth have called me Virādha.

sanskrit: तपसा च अभि संप्राप्ता ब्रह्मणो हि प्रसादजा
शस्त्रेण अवध्यता लोके अच्छेद्य अभेद्यत्वम् एव च
transliteration: tapasā ca abhi saṃprāptā brahmaṇo hi prasādajā
śastreṇa avadhyatā loke acchedya abhedyatvam eva ca
english: Having gratified Brahmă by my asceticism, IⓇreceived (this boon) that none in the world would be able to slay me by mangling my body with weapons.

sanskrit: उत्सृज्य प्रमदाम् एनाम् अनपेक्षौ यथा आगतम्
त्वरमाणौ पलायेथाम् न वाम् जीवितम् आददे
transliteration: utsṛjya pramadām enām anapekṣau yathā āgatam
tvaramāṇau palāyethām na vām jīvitam ādade
english: Forsaking this fair one, do you, renouncing all hope (of either recovering her or vanquishing me), speedily flee away to that place whence you had come; else I shall deprive you of your lives. Thereat, Rāma with his eyes reddened through wrath replied to that Rākşasa of a deformed shape, the wicked Viradha.

sanskrit: तम् रामः प्रति उवाच इदम् कोप संरक्त लोचनः
राक्षसम् विकृत आकारम् विराधम् पाप चेतसम्
transliteration: tam rāmaḥ prati uvāca idam kopa saṃrakta locanaḥ
rākṣasam vikṛta ākāram virādham pāpa cetasam
english: Forsaking this fair one, do you, renouncing all hope (of either recovering her or vanquishing me), speedily flee away to that place whence you had come; else I shall deprive you of your lives. Thereat, Rāma with his eyes reddened through wrath replied to that Rākşasa of a deformed shape, the wicked Viradha.

sanskrit: क्षुद्र धिक्त्वाम् तु हीनार्थम् मृत्युम् अन्वेषसे ध्रुवम्
रणे प्राप्स्यसि संतिष्ठ न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे
transliteration: kṣudra dhiktvām tu hīnārtham mṛtyum anveṣase dhruvam
raṇe prāpsyasi saṃtiṣṭha na me jīvan vimokṣyase
english: Little! shame on you of base purposes! You surely seek your own death; and (death) you shall get in battle. Stay! You escapist me not with life.

sanskrit: ततः सज्यम् धनुः कृत्वा रामः सुनिशितान् शरान्
सु शीघ्रम् अभिसंधाय राक्षसम् निजघान ह
transliteration: tataḥ sajyam dhanuḥ kṛtvā rāmaḥ suniśitān śarān
su śīghram abhisaṃdhāya rākṣasam nijaghāna ha
english: Then stringing his bow, Rāma, speedily aiming at the Rākşasa, pierced him with sharpened shafts; and (then) from his bow-string let go seven shafts, having their feathered parts plaited with good, furnished with great velocity, and coursing like Suparna or the wind.

sanskrit: धनुषा ज्या गुणवता सप्त बाणान् मुमोच ह
रुक्म पुंखान् महावेगान् सुपर्ण अनिल तुल्य गान्
transliteration: dhanuṣā jyā guṇavatā sapta bāṇān mumoca ha
rukma puṃkhān mahāvegān suparṇa anila tulya gān
english: Then stringing his bow, Rāma, speedily aiming at the Rākşasa, pierced him with sharpened shafts; and (then) from his bow-string let go seven shafts, having their feathered parts plaited with good, furnished with great velocity, and coursing like Suparna or the wind.

sanskrit: ते शरीरम् विराधस्य भित्त्वा बर्हिण वाससः
transliteration: te śarīram virādhasya bhittvā barhiṇa vāsasaḥ
english: Thereat, resembling flames, those arrows furnished with peacocks, feathers, pierced. Viradha's body, and fell to the earth, covered with blood.

sanskrit: स विद्धो न्यस्य वैदेहीम् शूलम् उद्यम्य राक्षसः
अभ्यद्रवत् सुसंक्रुद्धः तदा रामम् स लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: sa viddho nyasya vaidehīm śūlam udyamya rākṣasaḥ
abhyadravat susaṃkruddhaḥ tadā rāmam sa lakṣmaṇam
english: On being thus pierced, the Rākṣasa set Vaidehi down, and, upraising a dart, rushed in wrath towards Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: स विनद्य महानादम् शूलम् शक्र ध्वज उपमम्
प्रगृह्य अशोभत तदा व्यात्तानन इव अंतकः
transliteration: sa vinadya mahānādam śūlam śakra dhvaja upamam
pragṛhya aśobhata tadā vyāttānana iva aṃtakaḥ
english: And sending forth a mighty roar, he took up a dart resembling the banner of Sakra and he then appeared like the Destroyer* with opening mouth.

sanskrit: अथ तौ भ्रातरौ दीप्तम् शर वर्षम् ववर्षतुः
विराधे राक्षसे तस्मिन् कालांतक अयम् उपमे
transliteration: atha tau bhrātarau dīptam śara varṣam vavarṣatuḥ
virādhe rākṣase tasmin kālāṃtaka ayam upame
english: Then the brothers showered a blazing volley of shafts on that Rākşasa, resembling the Destroyer himself. The text has Kalāntakayamopame-abl..~~ resembling Kala, Antaka, or Yama. The commentator cites a sloka, which assigns three several functions to the three, Kāla execute his office on the occasion of the separation of life from the body; Antaka compasses the end; and Yama finally sits in judgement upon the departed soul. But this strikes me as misplaced erudition. I, however, give the commonsense rendering,

sanskrit: स प्रहस्य महा रौद्रः स्थित्वा अजृम्भत राक्षसः
जृंभमाणस्य ते बाणाः कायात् निष्पेतुर् अशुगाः
transliteration: sa prahasya mahā raudraḥ sthitvā ajṛmbhata rākṣasaḥ
jṛṃbhamāṇasya te bāṇāḥ kāyāt niṣpetur aśugāḥ
english: Stationing himself at a spot, the Rākşasa, laughing terribly, yawned, and as he yawned the flest-coursing shafts fell off from his person, a

sanskrit: स्पर्शात् तु वर दानेन प्राणान् संरोध्य राक्षसः
transliteration: sparśāt tu vara dānena prāṇān saṃrodhya rākṣasaḥ
english: And by virtue of the bestowal of the boon (by Brahmā), the Rākşasa Virādha drew up his vital energies, and, lifting up a pike, darted at the descendants of Raghu.

sanskrit: तत् शूलम् वज्र संकाशम् गगने ज्वलन उपमम्
द्वाभ्याम् शराभ्याम् चिच्छेद रामः शस्त्रभृताम् वरः
transliteration: tat śūlam vajra saṃkāśam gagane jvalana upamam
dvābhyām śarābhyām ciccheda rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtām varaḥ
english: That best of those bearing arms cut off with two arrows that dart resembling the thunder-bolt and flaming in the sky.

sanskrit: तत् राम विशिखैः छिन्नम् शूलम् तस्य आपतत् भुविः
पपात अशनिना चिन्नम् मेरोर् इव शिला तलम्
transliteration: tat rāma viśikhaiḥ chinnam śūlam tasya āpatat bhuviḥ
papāta aśaninā cinnam meror iva śilā talam
english: And the dart severed by the shafts of Rāma, fell to the earth, as falls a crag severed by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: तौ खड्गौ क्षिप्रम् उद्यम्य कृष्ण सर्पौ इव उद्यतौ
तूर्णम् आपेततुः तस्य तदा प्रहारताम् बलात्
transliteration: tau khaḍgau kṣipram udyamya kṛṣṇa sarpau iva udyatau
tūrṇam āpetatuḥ tasya tadā prahāratām balāt
english: Thereat, swiftly raising up sword, resembling a black snake, each (of the Rāghavas) approached his antagonist, and began to assail him hastily.

sanskrit: स वध्यमान सुभृशम् भुजाभ्याम् परिगृह्य तौ
transliteration: sa vadhyamāna subhṛśam bhujābhyām parigṛhya tau
english: Thus hard beset, that terrible one, seizing them both with his arms, attempted to make away with those foremost of men, who, however, retained their calmness.

sanskrit: तस्य अभिप्रायम् अज्ञाय रामो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
वहतु अयम् अलम् तावत् पथानेन तु राक्षसः
transliteration: tasya abhiprāyam ajñāya rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
vahatu ayam alam tāvat pathānena tu rākṣasaḥ
english: Reading his purpose, Rāma spoke to Lakşmana, Let the Rākşasa bear us by this way. Not use of letting him. O Sumitra's son let the Rākşasa bear us wherever he likes. Even this, by which the ranger of the night is proceeding, is our way.

sanskrit: यथा च इच्छति सोउमित्रे तथा वहतु राक्षसः
अयम् एव हि नः पन्था येन याति निशाचरः
transliteration: yathā ca icchati soumitre tathā vahatu rākṣasaḥ
ayam eva hi naḥ panthā yena yāti niśācaraḥ
english: Reading his purpose, Rāma spoke to Lakşmana, Let the Rākşasa bear us by this way. Not use of letting him. O Sumitra's son let the Rākşasa bear us wherever he likes. Even this, by which the ranger of the night is proceeding, is our way.

sanskrit: स तु स्व बल वीर्येण समुत्क्षिप्य निशाचरः
बालाः इव स्कन्ध गतौ चकार अति बलोद्धतः
transliteration: sa tu sva bala vīryeṇa samutkṣipya niśācaraḥ
bālāḥ iva skandha gatau cakāra ati baloddhataḥ
english: And lifting up (Rāma and Lakşmana) by his might and. prowess, as if they were striplings, that haughty ranger of the night laid them on his shoulders.

sanskrit: तौ आरोप्य ततः स्कन्धम् राघवो रजनी चरः
विराधो विनदन् घोरम् जगाम अभिमुखो वनम्
transliteration: tau āropya tataḥ skandham rāghavo rajanī caraḥ
virādho vinadan ghoram jagāma abhimukho vanam
english: And having deposited the Rāghavas on his shoulders, Virādha-ranger* of night-sending up dreadful shouts, directed his course towards the forest. Another reading is:-That ranger of the night laid on his shoulders, those ones, who were puffed up with their exceeding prowess.

sanskrit: वनम् महा मेघ निभम् प्रविष्टोद्रुमैः महद्भिः विविधैः उपेतम्
नाना विधैः पक्षि कुलैः विचित्रम्शिव आयुतम् व्याल मृगैः विकीर्णम्
transliteration: vanam mahā megha nibham praviṣṭodrumaiḥ mahadbhiḥ vividhaiḥ upetam
nānā vidhaiḥ pakṣi kulaiḥ vicitramśiva āyutam vyāla mṛgaiḥ vikīrṇam
english: And he at length entered the forest resembling a mighty mass of clouds, furnished with various kinds of trees, picturesque with diverse species of birds, and abounding in jackals, serpents and beasts.

sanskrit: ह्रियमाणौ तु काकुत्स्थौ दृष्ट्वा सीता रघूत्तमौ
उच्चैः स्वरेण चुक्रोश प्रगृह्य सु महाभुजौ
transliteration: hriyamāṇau tu kākutsthau dṛṣṭvā sītā raghūttamau
uccaiḥ svareṇa cukrośa pragṛhya su mahābhujau
english: Seeing those foremost of Raghus, the Kākutsthas, carried away, Sītā carried in a loud voice, raising up her arms. * *Another reading is Subhujābhujau-That one of elegant arms (raising) them up.

sanskrit: एष दाशरथी रामः सत्यवान् शीलवान् शुचिः
रक्षसा रौद्र रूपेण ह्रियते सह लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: eṣa dāśarathī rāmaḥ satyavān śīlavān śuciḥ
rakṣasā raudra rūpeṇa hriyate saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Rāma, the son of Dasaratha, the strong, the truthful and the pure, is, along with Laksmana, being carried away by you, Rākşasa of a terrible appearance.

sanskrit: माम् ऋका भक्ष इष्यन्ति शार्दूल द्वीपिनः तथा
माम् हरः उत्सृज्य काकुत्स्थौ नमस्ते राक्षसोत्तमः
transliteration: mām ṛkā bhakṣa iṣyanti śārdūla dvīpinaḥ tathā
mām haraḥ utsṛjya kākutsthau namaste rākṣasottamaḥ
english: Me bears will devour and tigers and panthers. Renouncing the Kākutsthas, do you carry me away. I bow to you, O best of Raksasas.

sanskrit: तस्याः तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा वैदेह्याः राम लक्ष्मणौ
वेगम् प्रचक्रतुर् वीरौ वधे तस्य दुरात्मनः
transliteration: tasyāḥ tat vacanam śrutvā vaidehyāḥ rāma lakṣmaṇau
vegam pracakratur vīrau vadhe tasya durātmanaḥ
english: Hearing these words of Vaidehi, Rāma and Lakşmaņa bestirred themselves for compassing the death of that wicked one.

sanskrit: तस्य रौद्रस्य सोउमित्रिः सव्यम् बाहुम् बभञ्ज ह
रामः तु दक्षिणम् बाहुम् तरसा तस्य रक्षसः
transliteration: tasya raudrasya soumitriḥ savyam bāhum babhañja ha
rāmaḥ tu dakṣiṇam bāhum tarasā tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: And Sumitra's son broke his left arm; while Rāma at once broke the Rākşasa's right one.

sanskrit: सः भग्न बहुः संविग्नः पपात आशु विमूर्छितः
धरण्याम् मेघ संकाशो वज्र भिन्न इव अचलः
transliteration: saḥ bhagna bahuḥ saṃvignaḥ papāta āśu vimūrchitaḥ
dharaṇyām megha saṃkāśo vajra bhinna iva acalaḥ
english: On his arms being broken, the Raksasa resembling a mass of clouds, growing weak, sank down on the ground in a swoon, like a hill riven by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: मुष्टिभिर् बाहुभिर् पद्भिः सूदयन्तौ तु राक्षसम्
उद्यम्योद्यम्य च अपि एनम् स्थण्डिले निष्पिपेषतुः
transliteration: muṣṭibhir bāhubhir padbhiḥ sūdayantau tu rākṣasam
udyamyodyamya ca api enam sthaṇḍile niṣpipeṣatuḥ
english: Thereupon, They assailed the Rākṣasa with their fists, arms and feet; and lifting him up once and again, and pressing him, they trod on him over the ground.

sanskrit: स विद्धो बहुभिर् बाणैः खड्गाभ्याम् च परिक्षतः
निष्पिष्टो बहुधा भूमौ न ममार स राक्षसः
transliteration: sa viddho bahubhir bāṇaiḥ khaḍgābhyām ca parikṣataḥ
niṣpiṣṭo bahudhā bhūmau na mamāra sa rākṣasaḥ
english: Although he was sore pierced by full many an arrow and cut shortly by scimitars, and pressed down on the earth in various ways, yet the Rākşasa expired not.

sanskrit: तम् प्रेक्ष्य रामः सुभृशम् अवध्यम् अचल उपमम्
भयेषु अभय दः श्रीमान् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tam prekṣya rāmaḥ subhṛśam avadhyam acala upamam
bhayeṣu abhaya daḥ śrīmān idam vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing him utterly incapable of being killed, and resembling a hill, that inspirer of hope in times of peril, the graceful (Rama), said, O foreinost of men, in consequence of his austerities, yon Rākşasa cannot be vanquished with weapons in conflict. Therefore, let us cast him into a pit.

Seeing him utterly incapable of being killed, and resembling a hill, that inspirer of hope in times of peril, the graceful (Rama), said, O foreinost of men, in consequence of his austerities, yon Rākşasa cannot be vanquished with weapons in conflict. Therefore, let us cast him into a pit.

sanskrit: कुंजर्स्य इव रौद्रस्य राक्षसस्य अस्य लक्ष्मण!
वने अस्मिन् सुमहद् श्वभ्रम् खन्यताम् रौद्रवर्चसः
transliteration: kuṃjarsya iva raudrasya rākṣasasya asya lakṣmaṇa!
vane asmin sumahad śvabhram khanyatām raudravarcasaḥ
english: O Lakşmaņa, dig a capacious pit in this forest* for this Rākşhasa resembling an elephant, terrible, and of a grim presence. *The reading slightly varies in some texts.-T

sanskrit: इति उक्त्वा लक्ष्मणम् रामः प्रदरः खन्यताम् इति
तस्थौ विराधम् आक्र्म्य कण्ठे पादेन वीर्यवान्
transliteration: iti uktvā lakṣmaṇam rāmaḥ pradaraḥ khanyatām iti
tasthau virādham ākrmya kaṇṭhe pādena vīryavān

sanskrit: तत् श्रुत्वा राघवेण उक्तम् राक्षसः प्रश्रितम् वचः
transliteration: tat śrutvā rāghaveṇa uktam rākṣasaḥ praśritam vacaḥ
english: Having heard Rāghava's words, the Rākşasa Virādha, spoke gently to the descendant of Kākutstha, the best among the men.

sanskrit: हतोऽहम् पुरुषव्याघ्रः शक्र तुल्य बलेन वै
मया तु पूर्वम् त्वम् मोहान् न ज्ञातः पुरुषर्षभः
transliteration: hato'ham puruṣavyāghraḥ śakra tulya balena vai
mayā tu pūrvam tvam mohān na jñātaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Slain am I, O chief of men, by you possessed of strength equal to that of Śakra. Through ignorance, O foremost of men, I could not before know you.

sanskrit: कौसल्या सुप्रजातः तात रामः त्वम् विदितो मया
वैदेही च महाभागा लक्ष्मणः च महायशाः
transliteration: kausalyā suprajātaḥ tāta rāmaḥ tvam vidito mayā
vaidehī ca mahābhāgā lakṣmaṇaḥ ca mahāyaśāḥ
english: Now I know you that are Rāma, the worthy Son of Kausalyā, my child; as well as the highly virtuous Vaidehi and the renowned Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: अभि शापाद् अहम् घोरम् प्रविष्टो राक्ष्सीम् तनुम्
तुंबुरुः नाम गन्धर्वः शप्तो वैश्रवणेन हि
transliteration: abhi śāpād aham ghoram praviṣṭo rākṣsīm tanum
tuṃburuḥ nāma gandharvaḥ śapto vaiśravaṇena hi
english: By virtue of a curse, I entered this dreadful Räkşasi form, I a Gandharva, having been cursed by Vaisravaņa.

sanskrit: प्रसाद्यमानः च मया सोऽब्रवीत् माम् महायशाः
यदा दाशरथी रमः त्वाम् वधिष्यति संयुगे
transliteration: prasādyamānaḥ ca mayā so'bravīt mām mahāyaśāḥ
yadā dāśarathī ramaḥ tvām vadhiṣyati saṃyuge
english: Being propitiated by me, that greatly famous one said, 'When Rāma the son of Dasaratha, shall slay you in encounter, you, attaining your natural condition, shall repair to the celestial regions.'

sanskrit: तदा प्रकृतिम् आपन्नो भवान् स्वर्गम् गमिष्यति
अनुपस्थीयमानो माम् स क्रुद्धो व्याजहार ह
transliteration: tadā prakṛtim āpanno bhavān svargam gamiṣyati
anupasthīyamāno mām sa kruddho vyājahāra ha

sanskrit: इति वैश्रवणो राजा रंभ आसक्तम् उवाच ह
तव प्रसादान् मुक्तो अहम् अभिशापात् सु दारुणात्
transliteration: iti vaiśravaṇo rājā raṃbha āsaktam uvāca ha
tava prasādān mukto aham abhiśāpāt su dāruṇāt

sanskrit: भुवनम् स्वम् गमिष्यामि स्वस्ति वोऽस्तु परंतप
transliteration: bhuvanam svam gamiṣyāmi svasti vo'stu paraṃtapa

sanskrit: अध्यर्थ योजने तातः महर्षिः सूर्य संनिभः
तम् क्षिप्रम् अभिगच्छ त्वम् स ते श्रेयो अभिधास्यति
transliteration: adhyartha yojane tātaḥ maharṣiḥ sūrya saṃnibhaḥ
tam kṣipram abhigaccha tvam sa te śreyo abhidhāsyati
english: Half a Yojana hence, my child, dwells the righteous and potent Maharși, Śarabharga, resembling the Sun. Seek him speedily: he will bring about your good. Casting me (into this pit) in the wood, do you, O Rama, peacefully go your way. Even this is the eternal usage of the Raksasas.

sanskrit: अवटे च अपि माम् राम निक्षिप्य कुशली व्रज
रक्षसाम् गत सत्त्वानाम् एष धर्मः सनातनः
transliteration: avaṭe ca api mām rāma nikṣipya kuśalī vraja
rakṣasām gata sattvānām eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ

sanskrit: अवटे ये निधीयन्ते तेषाम् लोकाः सनातनाः
एवम् उक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थम् विराधः शर पीडितः
transliteration: avaṭe ye nidhīyante teṣām lokāḥ sanātanāḥ
evam uktvā tu kākutstham virādhaḥ śara pīḍitaḥ
english: Those that die in the forest, attain eternal regions. Having said this to Kākutstha, the mighty Viradha, afflicted with arrows, having his body deposited (in the pit), attained heaven.

sanskrit: बभूव स्वर्ग संप्राप्तो न्यस्त देहो महाबलः
तत् श्रुत्वा राघवः वाक्यम् लक्ष्मणम् व्यादिदेश ह
transliteration: babhūva svarga saṃprāpto nyasta deho mahābalaḥ
tat śrutvā rāghavaḥ vākyam lakṣmaṇam vyādideśa ha

sanskrit: कुंजर्स्य इव रौद्रस्य राक्षसस्य अस्य लक्ष्मण!
वने अस्मिन् सुमहत् श्वभ्रम् खन्यताम् रौद्रकर्मणः
transliteration: kuṃjarsya iva raudrasya rākṣasasya asya lakṣmaṇa!
vane asmin sumahat śvabhram khanyatām raudrakarmaṇaḥ
english: O Lakşmaņa, dig a capacious pit in this forest* for this Rākşhasa resembling an elephant, terrible, and of a grim presence. *The reading slightly varies in some texts.-T

sanskrit: इति उक्त्वा लक्ष्मणम् रामः प्रदरः खन्यताम् इति
तस्थौ विराधम् आक्रम्य कण्ठे पादेन वीर्यवान्
transliteration: iti uktvā lakṣmaṇam rāmaḥ pradaraḥ khanyatām iti
tasthau virādham ākramya kaṇṭhe pādena vīryavān

sanskrit: ततः खनित्रम् आदाय लक्ष्मणः श्वभ्रम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: tataḥ khanitram ādāya lakṣmaṇaḥ śvabhram uttamam
english: Then taking a hoe, Lakşmaņa dug a spacious pit by the side of the huge-bodied* Virādha. *Mahātmānam-lit.-high-souled. The poet may have applied the epithet in this sense in view of Virādha being really a Gandharva. I have, however, preferred the other sense, as being more in harmony with the character of Virādha as a Rākşasa; and have accordingly rendered the word, huge bodied.

sanskrit: तम् मुक्त कण्ठम् उत्क्षिप्य शङ्कु कर्णम् महास्वनम्
विराधम् प्राक्षिपत् श्वभ्रे नदन्तम् भैरव स्वनम्
transliteration: tam mukta kaṇṭham utkṣipya śaṅku karṇam mahāsvanam
virādham prākṣipat śvabhre nadantam bhairava svanam
english: Then when his throat had been freed (Laks maņa) cast into the pit Virādha having ears resembling javelins, sending loud and dreadful sounds.

sanskrit: तम् आहवे दारुणम् आशु विक्रमौस्थिरौ उभौ संयति राम लक्ष्मणौ
मुदान्वितौ चिक्षिपतुर् भयावहम्नदन्तम् उत्क्षिप्य बिलेन राक्ष्सम्
