english: Thereat taking his bow from Lakşmaņa and holding it fast, the effulgent Rāma, the conqueror of foes, fixed flaming arrows to it like so many serpents and said being exercised with ire like to fire on the eve of dissolution.

sanskrit: संदधे धनुषि श्रीमान् रामः पर पुरंजयः
युग अन्त अग्निः इव क्रुद्धः इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: saṃdadhe dhanuṣi śrīmān rāmaḥ para puraṃjayaḥ
yuga anta agniḥ iva kruddhaḥ idam vacanam abravīt
english: Thereat taking his bow from Lakşmaņa and holding it fast, the effulgent Rāma, the conqueror of foes, fixed flaming arrows to it like so many serpents and said being exercised with ire like to fire on the eve of dissolution.

sanskrit: यथा जरा यथा मृत्युः यथा कालो यथा विधिः
नित्यम् न प्रतिहन्यन्ते सर्व भूतेषु लक्ष्मण
तथा अहम् क्रोध संयुक्तो न निवार्यो अस्मि असंशयम्
transliteration: yathā jarā yathā mṛtyuḥ yathā kālo yathā vidhiḥ
nityam na pratihanyante sarva bhūteṣu lakṣmaṇa
tathā aham krodha saṃyukto na nivāryo asmi asaṃśayam
english: O Lakşınaņa none shall be able to withstand me, who am inflamed with rage, as debility consequent on old age, death, time, duty are incapable of being averted from their destined ends by the animals.

sanskrit: पुरा इव मे चारु दतीम् अनिन्दिताम्दिशन्ति सीताम् यदि न अद्य मैथिलीम्
सदेव गन्धर्व मनुष्य पन्नगम्जगत् स शैलम् परिवर्तयामि अहम्
transliteration: purā iva me cāru datīm aninditāmdiśanti sītām yadi na adya maithilīm
sadeva gandharva manuṣya pannagamjagat sa śailam parivartayāmi aham
english: I shall bring about a mighty revolution in the world containing the celestials Gandharvas, human beings, Pannagas and the mountains, if I do not get back, in her pristine beauty, my Sītā, the daughter of the King of Mithilā.

sanskrit: तप्यमानम् तथा रामम् सीता हरण कर्शितम्
लोकानाम् अभवे युक्तम् सांवर्तकम् इव अनलम्
transliteration: tapyamānam tathā rāmam sītā haraṇa karśitam
lokānām abhave yuktam sāṃvartakam iva analam

sanskrit: वीक्षमाणम् धनुः सज्यम् निःश्वसंतम् पुनः पुनः
दग्धु कामम् जगत् सर्वम् युग अन्ते च यथा हरम्
transliteration: vīkṣamāṇam dhanuḥ sajyam niḥśvasaṃtam punaḥ punaḥ
dagdhu kāmam jagat sarvam yuga ante ca yathā haram

sanskrit: अदृष्ट पूर्वम् संक्रुद्धम् दृष्ट्वा रामम् स लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: adṛṣṭa pūrvam saṃkruddham dṛṣṭvā rāmam sa lakṣmaṇaḥ

sanskrit: पुरा भूत्वा मृदुः दांतः सर्व भूत हिते रतः
न क्रोध वशम् आपन्नः प्रकृतिम् हातुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: purā bhūtvā mṛduḥ dāṃtaḥ sarva bhūta hite rataḥ
na krodha vaśam āpannaḥ prakṛtim hātum arhasi
english: Ere this you had been gently, self-controlled and engaged in the welfare of all beings. It dose not behove you now to renounce your natural temper being influenced by ire.

sanskrit: चन्द्रे लक्ष्मीः प्रभा सूर्ये गतिः वायौ भुवि क्षमा
एतत् च नियतम् सर्वम् त्वयि च अनुत्तमम् यशः
transliteration: candre lakṣmīḥ prabhā sūrye gatiḥ vāyau bhuvi kṣamā
etat ca niyatam sarvam tvayi ca anuttamam yaśaḥ
english: Ever manifested itself in you, glory Par excellence like to splendour in the Moon, lustre in the Sun, motion in the wind and forgiveness in the Earth.

sanskrit: एकस्य न अपराधेन लोकान् हन्तुम् त्वम् अर्हसि
न तु जानामि कस्य अयम् भग्नः सांग्रामिको रथः
transliteration: ekasya na aparādhena lokān hantum tvam arhasi
na tu jānāmi kasya ayam bhagnaḥ sāṃgrāmiko rathaḥ
english: It become you not to devastate the whole world for the crime of an individual being. Methinks for certain, this shattered car must be the property of an individual person, not of many.

sanskrit: केन वा कस्य वा हेतोः स आयुधः स परिच्छदः
खुर नेमि क्षतः च अयम् सिक्तो रुधिर बिन्दुभिः
transliteration: kena vā kasya vā hetoḥ sa āyudhaḥ sa paricchadaḥ
khura nemi kṣataḥ ca ayam sikto rudhira bindubhiḥ

sanskrit: देशो निवृत्त संग्रामः सु घोरः पार्थिव आत्मज
एकस्य तु विमर्दो अयम् न द्वयोः वदताम् वर
transliteration: deśo nivṛtta saṃgrāmaḥ su ghoraḥ pārthiva ātmaja
ekasya tu vimardo ayam na dvayoḥ vadatām vara

sanskrit: न हि वृत्तम् हि पश्यामि बलस्य महतः पदम्
न एकस्य तु कृते लोकान् विनाशयितुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: na hi vṛttam hi paśyāmi balasya mahataḥ padam
na ekasya tu kṛte lokān vināśayitum arhasi

sanskrit: युक्त दण्डा हि मृदवः प्रशान्ता वसुधा अधिपाः
सदा त्वम् सर्व भूतानाम् शरण्यः परमा गतिः
transliteration: yukta daṇḍā hi mṛdavaḥ praśāntā vasudhā adhipāḥ
sadā tvam sarva bhūtānām śaraṇyaḥ paramā gatiḥ
english: Kings, gentle and mild by nature, do always administer punishment, proportionate to the amount of offence. You are always the stay and the best refuge of all animals.

sanskrit: को नु दार प्रणाशम् ते साधु मन्येत राघव
सरितः सागराः शैला देव गन्धर्व दानवाः
transliteration: ko nu dāra praṇāśam te sādhu manyeta rāghava
saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailā deva gandharva dānavāḥ
english: Who shall think well, O Raghava, of the destruction of your wife? The celestials, Danavas, Gandharvas, rivers, seas, and mountains-none can act unfriendly by you as the learned priests cannot act improperly towards those initiated by them.

sanskrit: न अलम् ते विप्रियम् कर्तुम् दीक्षितस्य इव साधवः
येन राजन् हृता सीता तम् अन्वेषितुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: na alam te vipriyam kartum dīkṣitasya iva sādhavaḥ
yena rājan hṛtā sītā tam anveṣitum arhasi

sanskrit: मद् द्वितीयो धनुष् पाणिः सहायैः परम ऋषिभिः
समुद्रम् च विचेष्यामः पर्वतान् च वनानि च
transliteration: mad dvitīyo dhanuṣ pāṇiḥ sahāyaiḥ parama ṛṣibhiḥ
samudram ca viceṣyāmaḥ parvatān ca vanāni ca

sanskrit: गुहाः च विविधा घोरा पद्मिन्यो विविधाः थथा
देव गन्धर्व लोकान् च विचेष्यामः समाहिताः
transliteration: guhāḥ ca vividhā ghorā padminyo vividhāḥ thathā
deva gandharva lokān ca viceṣyāmaḥ samāhitāḥ

sanskrit: यावत् न अधिगमिष्यामः तव भार्या अपहारिणम्
न चेत् साम्ना प्रदास्यन्ति पत्नीम् ते त्रिदश ईश्वराः
कोसल इन्द्र ततः पश्चात् प्राप्त कालम् करिष्यसि
transliteration: yāvat na adhigamiṣyāmaḥ tava bhāryā apahāriṇam
na cet sāmnā pradāsyanti patnīm te tridaśa īśvarāḥ
kosala indra tataḥ paścāt prāpta kālam kariṣyasi

sanskrit: शीलेन साम्ना विनयेन सीताम्नयेन न प्राप्स्यसि चेत् नरेन्द्र
ततः समुत्सादय हेम पुंखैःमहेन्द्र वज्र प्रतिमैः शर ओघैः
transliteration: śīlena sāmnā vinayena sītāmnayena na prāpsyasi cet narendra
tataḥ samutsādaya hema puṃkhaiḥmahendra vajra pratimaiḥ śara oghaiḥ
english: You shall then uproot the whole world, O lord of men, with your gold-feathered arrows resembling the thunderbolt of Mahendra, if you do not come by your wife by resorting to good conduct, self-control, lowliness and polity.

sanskrit: तम् तथा शोक संतप्तम् विलपंतम् अनाथवत्
transliteration: tam tathā śoka saṃtaptam vilapaṃtam anāthavat

sanskrit: ततः सौमित्रिः आश्वास्य मुहूर्तात् इव लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: tataḥ saumitriḥ āśvāsya muhūrtāt iva lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Rāma bewailing thus like one helpless being stricken with grief, overwhelmed with sorrow and losing control over himself, Lakşmaņa touched his feet and consoling him instantly began.

sanskrit: महता तपसा राम महता च अपि कर्मणा
राज्ञा दशरथेन असि लब्धो अमृतम् इव अमरैः
transliteration: mahatā tapasā rāma mahatā ca api karmaṇā
rājñā daśarathena asi labdho amṛtam iva amaraiḥ
english: By constant asceticism and manifold pious observances king Dasaratha obtained you like to the celestials obtaining ambrosia.

sanskrit: तव चैव गुणैः बद्धः त्वत् वियोगात् महिपतिः
राजा देवत्वम् आपन्नो भरतस्य यथा श्रुतम्
transliteration: tava caiva guṇaiḥ baddhaḥ tvat viyogāt mahipatiḥ
rājā devatvam āpanno bharatasya yathā śrutam
english: As I have heard from Bharata, king Dasaratha died for your separation, attached as he was to you for your accomplishments.

sanskrit: यदि दुःखम् इदम् प्राप्तम् काकुत्स्थ न सहिष्यसे
प्राकृतः च अल्प सत्त्वः च इतरः कः सहिष्यति
transliteration: yadi duḥkham idam prāptam kākutstha na sahiṣyase
prākṛtaḥ ca alpa sattvaḥ ca itaraḥ kaḥ sahiṣyati
english: O Kākutstha, if do you not bear patiently this impending peril what little-minded person else shall bear it?

sanskrit: आश्वसिहि नरश्रेष्ठ प्राणिनः कस्य न आपद
संस्पृशन्ति अग्निवत् राजन् क्षणेन व्यपयान्ति च
transliteration: āśvasihi naraśreṣṭha prāṇinaḥ kasya na āpada
saṃspṛśanti agnivat rājan kṣaṇena vyapayānti ca
english: Compose yourself, O you best of men. Peril overtake everybody like to fire but vanish in no time.

sanskrit: दुःखितो हि भवान् लोकान् तेजसा यदि धक्ष्यते
आर्ताः प्रजा नर व्याघ्र क्व नु यास्यन्ति निर्वृतिम्
transliteration: duḥkhito hi bhavān lokān tejasā yadi dhakṣyate
ārtāḥ prajā nara vyāghra kva nu yāsyanti nirvṛtim

sanskrit: लोक स्वभाव एव एष ययातिः नहुष आत्मजः
गतः शक्रेण सालोक्यम् अनयः तम् समस्पृशत्
transliteration: loka svabhāva eva eṣa yayātiḥ nahuṣa ātmajaḥ
gataḥ śakreṇa sālokyam anayaḥ tam samaspṛśat
english: This is the nature of men. Yayati, the son of king Nahusa, though attained to the state of celestials, was however thrown down for an iniquitous deed.

sanskrit: महाऋषि यः वसिष्ठः तु यः पितुः नः पुरोहितः
अह्ना पुत्र शतम् जज्ञे तथैव अस्य पुनर् हतम्
transliteration: mahāṛṣi yaḥ vasiṣṭhaḥ tu yaḥ pituḥ naḥ purohitaḥ
ahnā putra śatam jajñe tathaiva asya punar hatam
english: The hundred sons, that had been born to our ancestral priest Vasiştha, were all killed in one day.

sanskrit: या च इयम् जगतो माता सर्व लोक नमस्कृता
अस्याः च चलनम् भूमेः दृश्यते कोसलेश्वर
transliteration: yā ca iyam jagato mātā sarva loka namaskṛtā
asyāḥ ca calanam bhūmeḥ dṛśyate kosaleśvara
english: O lord of Kosala, even Vasumati, the mother of the world, adored of all beings, meet with misery consequent upon earth-quake.

sanskrit: यौ धर्मौ जगताम् नेत्रे यत्र सर्वम् प्रतिष्ठितम्
transliteration: yau dharmau jagatām netre yatra sarvam pratiṣṭhitam
english: Even the mighty Sun and Moon witness eclipse who are the eyes of the world and the very images of virtue and in whom the whole world is stationed.

sanskrit: सुमहान्ति अपि भूतानि देवाः च पुरुष ऋषभ
न दैवस्य प्रमुंचन्ति सर्व भूतानि देहिनः
transliteration: sumahānti api bhūtāni devāḥ ca puruṣa ṛṣabha
na daivasya pramuṃcanti sarva bhūtāni dehinaḥ
english: O you best of men, what of insignificant beings cased in this frail body, even the mighty creatures and celestials are subject to the influence of destiny.

sanskrit: शक्र आदिषु अपि देवेषु वर्तमानौ नय अनयौ
श्रूयेते नर शार्दूल न त्वम् व्यथितुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: śakra ādiṣu api deveṣu vartamānau naya anayau
śrūyete nara śārdūla na tvam vyathitum arhasi
english: I have heard, O best of men, even the celestials headed by Indra are subject to happiness or misery. So it dose not behove you to bewail thus.

sanskrit: हृतायाम् अपि वैदेह्याम् नष्टायाम् अपि राघव
शोचितुम् न अर्हसे वीर यथा अन्यः प्राकृतः तथा
transliteration: hṛtāyām api vaidehyām naṣṭāyām api rāghava
śocitum na arhase vīra yathā anyaḥ prākṛtaḥ tathā
english: O descendant of Raghu, it become you not to lament like an ordinary person even if Janakí is dead or has been carried away.

sanskrit: त्वत् विधा नहि शोचन्ति सततम् सर्व दर्शिनः
सुमहत्सु अपि कृच्छ्रेषु राम अनिर्विण्ण दर्शनाः
transliteration: tvat vidhā nahi śocanti satatam sarva darśinaḥ
sumahatsu api kṛcchreṣu rāma anirviṇṇa darśanāḥ
english: O Rāma, persons, highly experienced and ascertaining right or wrong without being moved, do not lament even in the face of mighty perils.

sanskrit: बुद्ध्या युक्ता महाप्राज्ञा विजानन्ति शुभ अशुभे
transliteration: buddhyā yuktā mahāprājñā vijānanti śubha aśubhe
english: O you best of men, do you, after due consideration, ascertain what is proper or improper; persons of your vast wisdom are cognizant of the right or wrong by dint of their understanding.

sanskrit: अदृष्ट गुण दोषाणाम् अधृवाणाम् च कर्मणाम्
न अंतरेण क्रियाम् तेषाम् फलम् इष्टम् च वर्तते
transliteration: adṛṣṭa guṇa doṣāṇām adhṛvāṇām ca karmaṇām
na aṃtareṇa kriyām teṣām phalam iṣṭam ca vartate
english: Without proper exercise, actions, of unknown merit and uncertain issue do not bear fruits.

sanskrit: माम् एवम् हि पुरा वीर त्वम् एव बहुशो उक्तवान्
अनुशिष्यात् हि को नु त्वाम् अपि साक्षात् बृहस्पतिः
transliteration: mām evam hi purā vīra tvam eva bahuśo uktavān
anuśiṣyāt hi ko nu tvām api sākṣāt bṛhaspatiḥ
english: O hero, many a time and oft ere this, you had given me the self-same counsel. Who is capable of counselling you who are the very preceptor of the gods?

sanskrit: बुद्धिः च ते महाप्राज्ञ देवैः अपि दुर्अन्वया
शोकेन अभिप्रसुप्तम् ते ज्ञानम् सम्बोधयामि अहम्
transliteration: buddhiḥ ca te mahāprājña devaiḥ api duranvayā
śokena abhiprasuptam te jñānam sambodhayāmi aham
english: O you of great intellect, even the celestials cannot measure your mental acumen. Greatly benumbed is your wisdom with the slumber of grief, and I am to rouse it.

sanskrit: दिव्यम् च मानुषम् च एवम् आत्मनः च पराक्रमम्
इक्ष्वाकु वृषभ अवेक्ष्य यतस्व द्विषताम् वधे
transliteration: divyam ca mānuṣam ca evam ātmanaḥ ca parākramam
ikṣvāku vṛṣabha avekṣya yatasva dviṣatām vadhe
english: O you the best of lkşvākus, do you engage in the destruction of your foes considering well your celestial and human prowess.

sanskrit: किम् ते सर्व विनाशेन कृतेन पुरुष ऋषभ
तम् एव तु रिपुम् पापम् विज्ञाय उद्धर्तुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: kim te sarva vināśena kṛtena puruṣa ṛṣabha
tam eva tu ripum pāpam vijñāya uddhartum arhasi
english: O you best of men, what necessity have you to destroy the whole world? Do you rescue Sītā after finding out your vicious enemy.

sanskrit: पूर्वजो अपि उक्त मात्रः तु लक्ष्मणेन सुभाषितम्
transliteration: pūrvajo api ukta mātraḥ tu lakṣmaṇena subhāṣitam
english: After Laksmana had spoken these highly sound and pleasant words, Rāma, ever taking to what is sound, accepted them.

sanskrit: स निगृह्य महाबाहुः प्रवृद्धम् रोषम् आत्मनः
अवष्टभ्य धनुः चित्रम् रामो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sa nigṛhya mahābāhuḥ pravṛddham roṣam ātmanaḥ
avaṣṭabhya dhanuḥ citram rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: Thereupon that one, of mighty arms, slaking his flaming ire and reclining himself upon his beautiful bow, addressed Laksmana.

sanskrit: किम् करिष्यावहे वत्स क्व वा गच्छाव लक्ष्मण
केन उपायेन पश्येयम् सीताम् इह विचिन्तय
transliteration: kim kariṣyāvahe vatsa kva vā gacchāva lakṣmaṇa
kena upāyena paśyeyam sītām iha vicintaya
english: Do you ponder over, O brother, where shall we repair, what shall we do and by what means shall we come by Sītā?

sanskrit: तम् तथा परिताप आर्तम् लक्ष्मणो रामम् अब्रवीत्
इदम् एव जनस्थानम् त्वम् अन्वेषितुम् अर्हसि
transliteration: tam tathā paritāpa ārtam lakṣmaṇo rāmam abravīt
idam eva janasthānam tvam anveṣitum arhasi

sanskrit: राक्षसैः बहुभिः कीर्णम् नाना द्रुम लता आयुतम्
सन्ति इह गिरि दुर्गाणि निर्दराः कंदराणि च
transliteration: rākṣasaiḥ bahubhiḥ kīrṇam nānā druma latā āyutam
santi iha giri durgāṇi nirdarāḥ kaṃdarāṇi ca
english: Whereto Lakşmaņa replied saying to the highly aggrieved Råma, It is proper for you to search this Janasthāna filled with a multitude of Rākṣasas and covered with diverse trees and creepers. Here are many strongholds in the midst of mountains, clefts of rocks, many caves and numerous cavities filled with various animals.

sanskrit: गुहाः च विविधा घोरा नाना मृग गण आकुलाः
आवासाः किन्नराणाम् च गन्धर्व भवनानि च
transliteration: guhāḥ ca vividhā ghorā nānā mṛga gaṇa ākulāḥ
āvāsāḥ kinnarāṇām ca gandharva bhavanāni ca

sanskrit: तानि युक्तो मया सार्धम् समन्वेषितुम् अर्हसि
त्वत् विधा बुद्धि संपन्ना माहात्मानो नरर्षभ
transliteration: tāni yukto mayā sārdham samanveṣitum arhasi
tvat vidhā buddhi saṃpannā māhātmāno nararṣabha
english: Many are the abodes here belonging to the Kinnaras and Gandharvas. Do you, along with me, search all these places. Great men, of your calibre, do remain unagitated even in the midst of difficulties like to mountains never shaken by the velocity of the wind.

sanskrit: आपत्सु न प्रकंपन्ते वायु वेगैः इव अचलाः
इति उक्तः तत् वनम् सर्वम् विचचार स लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: āpatsu na prakaṃpante vāyu vegaiḥ iva acalāḥ
iti uktaḥ tat vanam sarvam vicacāra sa lakṣmaṇaḥ

sanskrit: क्रुद्धो रामः शरम् घोरम् संधाय धनुषि क्षुरम्
ततः पर्वत कूट आभम् महा भागम् द्विज उत्तमम्
transliteration: kruddho rāmaḥ śaram ghoram saṃdhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram
tataḥ parvata kūṭa ābham mahā bhāgam dvija uttamam

sanskrit: ददर्श पतितम् भूमौ क्षतज आर्द्रम् जटायुषम्
तम् दृष्ट्वा गिरि शृंग आभम् रामो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: dadarśa patitam bhūmau kṣataja ārdram jaṭāyuṣam
tam dṛṣṭvā giri śṛṃga ābham rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: Thereupon he beheld, fallen on ground, having his person bathed in blood, the king of birds-Jatayu, resembling a mountain peak, and spoke to Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: अनेन सीता वैदेही भक्षिता न अत्र संशयः
गृध्र रूपम् इदम् व्यक्तम् रक्षो भ्रमति काननम्
transliteration: anena sītā vaidehī bhakṣitā na atra saṃśayaḥ
gṛdhra rūpam idam vyaktam rakṣo bhramati kānanam
english: It is clear and beyond all doubt that Vaidehī has been devoured by this Rākşasa, assuming the shape of a vulture and ranging the forest.

sanskrit: भक्षयित्वा विशालाक्षीम् आस्ते सीताम् यथा सुखम्
एनम् वधिष्ये दीप्त अग्रैः घोरैः बाणैः अजिह्मगैः
transliteration: bhakṣayitvā viśālākṣīm āste sītām yathā sukham
enam vadhiṣye dīpta agraiḥ ghoraiḥ bāṇaiḥ ajihmagaiḥ
english: This Rākşasa has been reposing at ease after devouring that one of expansive eyes; I shall kill him with terrible straight coursing arrows, having flaming points.

sanskrit: इति उक्त्वा अभ्यपतत् गृध्रम् सन्धाय धनुषि क्षुरम्
क्रुद्धो रामः समुद्र अन्ताम् चालयन् इव मेदिनीम्
transliteration: iti uktvā abhyapatat gṛdhram sandhāya dhanuṣi kṣuram
kruddho rāmaḥ samudra antām cālayan iva medinīm
english: Fixing sharpened shafts to his bow, Rāma, enraged, darted towards the vulture, as if moving the sea-girt earth.

sanskrit: तम् दीन दीनया वाचा स फेनम् रुधिरम् वमन्
अभ्यभाषत पक्षी तु रामम् दशरथ आत्मजम्
transliteration: tam dīna dīnayā vācā sa phenam rudhiram vaman
abhyabhāṣata pakṣī tu rāmam daśaratha ātmajam
english: Vomiting frothy blood Jațāyu, the king of vultures, spoke to Rāma, the son of Dasaratha.

sanskrit: याम् ओषधिम् इव आयुष्मन् अन्वेषसि महा वने
सा देवी मम च प्राणा रावणेन उभयम् हृतम्
transliteration: yām oṣadhim iva āyuṣman anveṣasi mahā vane
sā devī mama ca prāṇā rāvaṇena ubhayam hṛtam
english: O you of long life, that goddess, whom you have been searching in this vast forest like to Os adhi, and my life have been carried away by Rāvana.

sanskrit: त्वया विरहिता देवी लक्ष्मणेन च राघव
transliteration: tvayā virahitā devī lakṣmaṇena ca rāghava
english: I saw her, O Rāghava, carried away stealthily by the powerful Rāvaņa, in your absence as well as that of Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: सीताम् अभ्यवपन्नो अहम् रावणः च रणे मया
विध्वंसित रथः च अत्र पातितो धरणी तले
transliteration: sītām abhyavapanno aham rāvaṇaḥ ca raṇe mayā
vidhvaṃsita rathaḥ ca atra pātito dharaṇī tale
english: Myself nearing Sītā, for her rescue, O Lord, Rāvaņa was thrown down on earth by me in conflict having his car and umbrella shattered.

sanskrit: एतत् अस्य धनुः भग्नम् एतत् अस्य शरावरम्
अयम् अस्य रणे राम भग्नः सांग्रामिको रथः
transliteration: etat asya dhanuḥ bhagnam etat asya śarāvaram
ayam asya raṇe rāma bhagnaḥ sāṃgrāmiko rathaḥ
english: This is his snapped bow and these are his broken shafts. And this is his war-car, O Rāma shattered in fight.

sanskrit: अयम् तु सारथिः तस्य मत् पक्ष निहतो भुविः
परिश्रान्तस्य मे पक्षौ छित्त्वा खड्गेन रावणः
transliteration: ayam tu sārathiḥ tasya mat pakṣa nihato bhuviḥ
pariśrāntasya me pakṣau chittvā khaḍgena rāvaṇaḥ
english: This is his charioteer lying on earth being killed by the velocity of my wings. Having sundered my wings with his dagger, who had been exhausted, Rāvana taking Sītā, rose high up in the welkin. It behove you not to kill me who had been wounded before by the Rākşasa.

sanskrit: रक्षसा निहतम् पूर्वम् न माम् हन्तुम् त्वम् अर्हसि
transliteration: rakṣasā nihatam pūrvam na mām hantum tvam arhasi
english: This is his charioteer lying on earth being killed by the velocity of my wings. Having sundered my wings with his dagger, who had been exhausted, Rāvana taking Sītā, rose high up in the welkin. It behove you not to kill me who had been wounded before by the Rākşasa.

sanskrit: रामः तस्य तु विज्ञाय सीता सक्ताम् प्रियाम् कथाम्
गृध्र राजम् परिष्वज्य परित्यज्य महत् धनुः
transliteration: rāmaḥ tasya tu vijñāya sītā saktām priyām kathām
gṛdhra rājam pariṣvajya parityajya mahat dhanuḥ
english: Hearing from him pleasant words relating to Sītā, Rāma, leaving aside, instantly, his mighty bow, embraced him, and rolling on earth having lost self-control through grief, began to lament with Lakşmaņa. Though highly composed by nature, he was overwhelmed with doubled grief.

sanskrit: निपपात अवशो भूमौ रुरोद सह लक्ष्मण
द्विगुणीकृत ताप आर्तो रामो धीरतरो अपि सन्
transliteration: nipapāta avaśo bhūmau ruroda saha lakṣmaṇa
dviguṇīkṛta tāpa ārto rāmo dhīrataro api san
english: Hearing from him pleasant words relating to Sītā, Rāma, leaving aside, instantly, his mighty bow, embraced him, and rolling on earth having lost self-control through grief, began to lament with Lakşmaņa. Though highly composed by nature, he was overwhelmed with doubled grief.

sanskrit: एकम् एक अयने कृच्छ्रे निःश्वसन्तम् मुहुर् मुहुः
समीक्ष्य दुःखितो रामः सौमित्रिम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: ekam eka ayane kṛcchre niḥśvasantam muhur muhuḥ
samīkṣya duḥkhito rāmaḥ saumitrim idam abravīt
english: And beholding Jațāyu, sigh again and again and breathing with difficulty in a helpless plight, Rāma, highly aggrieved, spoke to Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: राज्यम् भ्रष्टम् वने वासः सीता नष्टा मृते द्विजः
ईदृशी इयम् मम अलक्ष्मीः दहेत् अपि पावकम्
transliteration: rājyam bhraṣṭam vane vāsaḥ sītā naṣṭā mṛte dvijaḥ
īdṛśī iyam mama alakṣmīḥ dahet api pāvakam
english: I have lost my kingdom and have been living in this forest. My Sītā has been carried away and this bird has been killed (on my account). This misfortune of mine can burn even the very fire.

sanskrit: संपूर्णम् अपि चेत् अद्य प्रतरेयम् महोदधिम्
सो अपि नूनम् मम अलक्ष्म्या विशुष्येत् सरिताम् पतिः
transliteration: saṃpūrṇam api cet adya pratareyam mahodadhim
so api nūnam mama alakṣmyā viśuṣyet saritām patiḥ
english: If for assuaging my grief I do enter the mighty ocean, verily shall that misfortune dry up even that lord of rivers.

sanskrit: न अस्ति अभाग्यतरो लोके मत्तो अस्मिन् स चराचरे
येन इयम् महती प्राप्ता मया व्यसन वागुरा
transliteration: na asti abhāgyataro loke matto asmin sa carācare
yena iyam mahatī prāptā mayā vyasana vāgurā
english: There is none so unfortunate as I, throughout this earth, mobile or immobile, and it is for this bad luck that I have confronted this mighty disaster.

sanskrit: अयम् पितृ वयस्यो मे गृध्र राजो जरा अन्वितः
शेते विनिहतो भूमौ मम भाग्य विपर्ययात्
transliteration: ayam pitṛ vayasyo me gṛdhra rājo jarā anvitaḥ
śete vinihato bhūmau mama bhāgya viparyayāt
english: This mighty king of vultures is our father's friend and he Leith on earth, killed through the evil turn of my fortune.

sanskrit: इति एवम् उक्त्वा बहुशो राघवः सह लक्ष्मणः
जटायुषम् च पस्पर्श पितृ स्नेहम् निदर्शयन्
transliteration: iti evam uktvā bahuśo rāghavaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
jaṭāyuṣam ca pasparśa pitṛ sneham nidarśayan
english: Uttering these and various other words, Rāghava, along with Lakşmaņa touched his body manifesting his paternal affection.

sanskrit: निकृत्त पक्षम् रुधिर अवसिक्तम्तम् गृध्र राजम् परिरभ्य रामः
क्व मैथिलि प्राण समा मम इतिविमुच्य वाचम् निपपात भूमौ
transliteration: nikṛtta pakṣam rudhira avasiktamtam gṛdhra rājam parirabhya rāmaḥ
kva maithili prāṇa samā mama itivimucya vācam nipapāta bhūmau
english: Embracing the king of vultures, bathed in blood, having its wings cut off, Rāghava, fell on the ground, exclaiming where has Maithili gone like to my life?

sanskrit: रामः प्रेक्ष्य तु तम् गृध्रम् भुवि रौद्रेण पातितम्
सौमित्रिम् मित्र संपन्नम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: rāmaḥ prekṣya tu tam gṛdhram bhuvi raudreṇa pātitam
saumitrim mitra saṃpannam idam vacanam abravīt

sanskrit: मम अयम् नूनम् अर्थेषु यतमानो विहंगमः
राक्षसेन हतः संख्ये प्राणान् त्यजति मत् कृते
transliteration: mama ayam nūnam artheṣu yatamāno vihaṃgamaḥ
rākṣasena hataḥ saṃkhye prāṇān tyajati mat kṛte

sanskrit: अति खिन्नः शरीरे अस्मिन् प्राणो लक्ष्मण विद्यते
तथा स्वर विहीनो अयम् विक्लवम् समुदीक्षते
transliteration: ati khinnaḥ śarīre asmin prāṇo lakṣmaṇa vidyate
tathā svara vihīno ayam viklavam samudīkṣate

sanskrit: जटायो यदि शक्नोषि वाक्यम् व्याहरितुम् पुनः
सीताम् आख्याहि भद्रम् ते वधम् आख्याहि च आत्मनः
transliteration: jaṭāyo yadi śaknoṣi vākyam vyāharitum punaḥ
sītām ākhyāhi bhadram te vadham ākhyāhi ca ātmanaḥ
english: May good betide you, O Jatayu; if you are capable of speaking again, do you relate how Sītā has been carried away and you have been killed.

sanskrit: किम् निमित्तो जहार आर्याम् रावणः तस्य किम् मया
अपराधम् तु यम् दृष्ट्वा रावणेन हृता प्रिया
transliteration: kim nimitto jahāra āryām rāvaṇaḥ tasya kim mayā
aparādham tu yam dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇena hṛtā priyā
english: Why has Rāvaņa taken away by stealth the worshipful Jānki? What offence did I commit by him that he has carried away my dear one?

sanskrit: कथम् तत् चन्द्र संकाशम् मुखम् आसीत् मनोहरम्
सीतया कानि च उक्तानि तस्मिन् काले द्विजोत्तम
transliteration: katham tat candra saṃkāśam mukham āsīt manoharam
sītayā kāni ca uktāni tasmin kāle dvijottama
english: O you best of birds, how looked the moonlike, pleasant countenance of Sītā at the time of her being carried away? What did she speak then?

sanskrit: कथम् वीर्यः कथम् रूपः किम् कर्मा स च राक्षसः
क्व च अस्य भवनम् तात ब्रूहि मे परिपृच्छतः
transliteration: katham vīryaḥ katham rūpaḥ kim karmā sa ca rākṣasaḥ
kva ca asya bhavanam tāta brūhi me paripṛcchataḥ
english: What is the prowess, appearance and action of that Raksasa? Where dose he live, O reverend Sir? Pray tell me, I do ask you.

sanskrit: तम् उद्वीक्ष्य सः धर्मात्मा विलपन्तम् अनाथवत्
वाचा विक्लवया रामम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tam udvīkṣya saḥ dharmātmā vilapantam anāthavat
vācā viklavayā rāmam idam vacanam abravīt
english: Beholding Rāma, lament like one helpless, the virtuous-souled Jațăyu spoke in faltering accents.

sanskrit: मायाम् आस्थाय विपुलाम् वात दुर्दिन संकुलाम्
transliteration: māyām āsthāya vipulām vāta durdina saṃkulām
english: Sītā has been carried away by Rāvana, the lord of Rākşasas, creating a mighty illusion producing wind and showers.

sanskrit: परिक्लांतस्य मे तात पक्षौ चित्त्वा निशाचरः
सीताम् आदाय वैदेहीम् प्रयातो दक्षिणा मुखः
transliteration: pariklāṃtasya me tāta pakṣau cittvā niśācaraḥ
sītām ādāya vaidehīm prayāto dakṣiṇā mukhaḥ
english: O darling, myself being worn out that nightranger, having sundered my wings, fled away with Sītā to the southerly direction.

sanskrit: उपरुध्यन्ति मे प्राणा दृष्टिर् भ्रमति राघव
पश्यामि वृक्षान् सौवर्णान् उशीर कृत मूर्धजान्
transliteration: uparudhyanti me prāṇā dṛṣṭir bhramati rāghava
paśyāmi vṛkṣān sauvarṇān uśīra kṛta mūrdhajān
english: O Rāghava, my life is about to expire, my eye-sight has grown of mistaken perception, I see trees before me made of gold having hair resembling Usira.

sanskrit: येन याति मुहूर्तेन सीताम् आदाय रावणः
विप्रनष्टम् धनम् क्षिप्रम् तत् स्वामि प्रतिपद्यते
transliteration: yena yāti muhūrtena sītām ādāya rāvaṇaḥ
vipranaṣṭam dhanam kṣipram tat svāmi pratipadyate
english: Rāvana has taken away Sītā at a moment when a person regains soon his lost property. O Kākutstha, this moment is called Vindya, which Rāvana has not been able to perceive. (At this moment) the person who takes away (a thing) is soon destroyed like to a fish devouring a hook. This refers to Jatāyu's astrological knowledge. Vindya is derived from the root Vid-to gain. Thus this moment is favourable to the laser and unfavourable to the taker. Hence Rāvana carrying away Sītā at this moment shall meet with destruction.

sanskrit: विन्दो नाम मुहूर्तो असौ स च काकुत्स्थ न अबुधत्
त्वत् प्रियाम् जानकीम् हृत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वर
झषवत् बडिशम् गृह्य क्षिप्रम् एव विनश्यति
transliteration: vindo nāma muhūrto asau sa ca kākutstha na abudhat
tvat priyām jānakīm hṛtvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvara
jhaṣavat baḍiśam gṛhya kṣipram eva vinaśyati

sanskrit: न च त्वया व्यथा कार्या जनकस्य सुताम् प्रति
वैदेह्या रंस्यसे क्षिप्रम् हत्वा तम् रणमूर्धनि
transliteration: na ca tvayā vyathā kāryā janakasya sutām prati
vaidehyā raṃsyase kṣipram hatvā tam raṇamūrdhani
english: Do not therefore entertain the least doubt about your coming by Janakī. Destroying him at the head of the battle you shall soon sport with Vaidehi.

sanskrit: आस्यात् सुस्राव रुधिरम् म्रियमाणस्य स अमिषम्
transliteration: āsyāt susrāva rudhiram mriyamāṇasya sa amiṣam
english: Thereupon flesh and gore began to come out of the mouth of Jatayu, the king of vultures, not loosing his sense even while treading the verge of death.

sanskrit: पुत्रो विश्रवसः साक्षात् भ्राता वैश्रवणस्य च
इति उक्त्वा दुर्लभान् प्राणान् मुमोच पतगेश्वरः
transliteration: putro viśravasaḥ sākṣāt bhrātā vaiśravaṇasya ca
iti uktvā durlabhān prāṇān mumoca patageśvaraḥ
english: Thereupon the king of birds gave up his dear life uttering only-Rāvana is the son of Visravā and brother to Vaisravana (the lord of wealth).

sanskrit: ब्रूहि ब्रूहि इति रामस्य ब्रुवाणस्य कृतांजलेः
त्यक्त्वा शरीरम् गृध्रस्य जग्मुः प्राणा विहायसम्
transliteration: brūhi brūhi iti rāmasya bruvāṇasya kṛtāṃjaleḥ
tyaktvā śarīram gṛdhrasya jagmuḥ prāṇā vihāyasam
english: Rāma again and again addressed him with joined palms saying, Do you speak! Do you speak. And instantly Jatayu's vital spark rose up in the sky, leaving his bodily frame.

sanskrit: स निक्षिप्य शिरो भूमौ प्रसार्य चरणौ तदा
विक्षिप्य च शरीरम् स्वम् पपात धरणी तले
transliteration: sa nikṣipya śiro bhūmau prasārya caraṇau tadā
vikṣipya ca śarīram svam papāta dharaṇī tale
english: Thereupon the king of vultures fell down on the earth by stretching forth his legs, body and head on the ground.

sanskrit: तम् गृध्रम् प्रेक्ष्य ताम्र अक्षम् गत असुम् अचलोपमम्
रामः सु बहुभिः दुह्खैः दीनः सौमित्रिम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tam gṛdhram prekṣya tāmra akṣam gata asum acalopamam
rāmaḥ su bahubhiḥ duhkhaiḥ dīnaḥ saumitrim abravīt
english: Beholding the vulture dead, of huge proportions, resembling a hill and having red eyes, Rama, aggrieved, spoke piteously to Saumitri.

sanskrit: बहूनि रक्षसाम् वासे वर्षाणि वसता सुखम्
transliteration: bahūni rakṣasām vāse varṣāṇi vasatā sukham
english: Living happily, for years, in this forest of Dandaka inhabited by the Rākşasas, Jațāyu has, at last, given up his life.

sanskrit: अनेक वार्षिको यः तु चिर काल समुत्थितः
सो अयम् अद्य हतः शेते कालो हि दुर्अतिक्रमः
transliteration: aneka vārṣiko yaḥ tu cira kāla samutthitaḥ
so ayam adya hataḥ śete kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: He lived for a long time, of an uplifted person, and has now laid low on the earth. None can withstand the course of destiny.

sanskrit: पश्य लक्ष्मण गृध्रो अयम् उपकारी हतः च मे
transliteration: paśya lakṣmaṇa gṛdhro ayam upakārī hataḥ ca me
english: Observe, O Laksmana, this vulture for my benefaction, has been killed by the powerful Rāvaņa in his attempt to rescue Sītā.

sanskrit: गृध्र राज्यम् परित्यज्य पितृ पैतामहम् महत्
मम हेतोः अयम् प्राणान् मुमोच पतगेश्वरः
transliteration: gṛdhra rājyam parityajya pitṛ paitāmaham mahat
mama hetoḥ ayam prāṇān mumoca patageśvaraḥ
english: For me, has this Lord of birds, breathed his last, renouncing his large ancestral kingdom.

sanskrit: सर्वत्र खलु दृश्यन्ते साधवो धर्म चारिणः
शूराः शरण्याः सौमित्रे तिर्यक् योनि गतेषु अपि
transliteration: sarvatra khalu dṛśyante sādhavo dharma cāriṇaḥ
śūrāḥ śaraṇyāḥ saumitre tiryak yoni gateṣu api
english: In every status of animal creation, the heroic, the righteous and the honest, affording refuge to all, are to be found, even among the birds.

sanskrit: सीता हरणजं दुःखम् न मे सौम्य तथा गतम्
यथा विनाशो गृध्रस्य मत् कृते च परंतप
transliteration: sītā haraṇajaṃ duḥkham na me saumya tathā gatam
yathā vināśo gṛdhrasya mat kṛte ca paraṃtapa
english: I do not feel so much affliction, O hero, for Sītā's ravishment as I do for this vulture, who has been killed for me.

sanskrit: राजा दशरथः श्रीमान् यथा मम मया यशाः
पूजनीयः च मान्यः च तथा अयम् पतगेश्वरः
transliteration: rājā daśarathaḥ śrīmān yathā mama mayā yaśāḥ
pūjanīyaḥ ca mānyaḥ ca tathā ayam patageśvaraḥ
english: Like to the highly famous, effulgent king Dasaratha, this King of birds is worthy of being adored and worshipped by me.

sanskrit: गृध्र राजम् दिधक्षामि मत् कृते निधनम् गतम्
transliteration: gṛdhra rājam didhakṣāmi mat kṛte nidhanam gatam
english: O Saumitri, do you bring fuels; I shall produce fire there-with and burn the dead body of this king of birds who has been killed on my account.

sanskrit: नाथम् पतग लोकस्य चिताम् आरोपयामि अहम्
इमम् धक्ष्यामि सौमित्रे हतम् रौद्रेण रक्षसा
transliteration: nātham pataga lokasya citām āropayāmi aham
imam dhakṣyāmi saumitre hatam raudreṇa rakṣasā
english: Placing on a funeral pile, I shall cremate, O Saumitrī, the dead body of this king of birds who has been destroyed by the grim-visaged Raksasas.

sanskrit: या गतिः यज्ञ शीलानाम् आहित अग्नेः च या गतिः
अ पर आवर्तिनाम् या च या च भूमि प्रदायिनाम्
transliteration: yā gatiḥ yajña śīlānām āhita agneḥ ca yā gatiḥ
a para āvartinām yā ca yā ca bhūmi pradāyinām
english: Being consecrated and commanded by me, do you, O highly powerful king of birds, attain to that excellent state of existence, which is reached by persons ever performing pious observance, by Āhilāgnis by heroes who are not afraid of entering a battle-field and by persons who confer grants of land.

sanskrit: मया त्वम् समनुज्ञातो गच्छ लोकान् अनुत्तमान्
गृध्र राज महा सत्त्व संस्कृतः च मया व्रज
transliteration: mayā tvam samanujñāto gaccha lokān anuttamān
gṛdhra rāja mahā sattva saṃskṛtaḥ ca mayā vraja
english: Being consecrated and commanded by me, do you, O highly powerful king of birds, attain to that excellent state of existence, which is reached by persons ever performing pious observance, by Āhilāgnis by heroes who are not afraid of entering a battle-field and by persons who confer grants of land.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा चिताम् दीप्ताम् आरोप्य पतगेश्वरम्
ददाह रामो धर्मात्मा स्व बन्धुम् इव दुःखितः
transliteration: evam uktvā citām dīptām āropya patageśvaram
dadāha rāmo dharmātmā sva bandhum iva duḥkhitaḥ
english: Saying this the virtuous-souled Rāma, afflicted with sorrow, burned the body of the king of birds, placing it on the funeral pile, like to his own kinsman.

sanskrit: रामो अथ सह सौमित्रिः वनम् यात्वा स वीर्यवान्
स्थूलान् हत्वा महा रोहीन् अनु तस्तार तम् द्विजम्
transliteration: rāmo atha saha saumitriḥ vanam yātvā sa vīryavān
sthūlān hatvā mahā rohīn anu tastāra tam dvijam
english: Entering the forest with Saumitrī, Rāma gifted with prowess, killed plump high deer and stretched forth grass and twigs for offering oblation to that bird. Taking off the flesh of those high deer and clustering it, Rāma, of great renown, offered it to the vultures in that pleasant forest-land, abounding in green grass.

sanskrit: रोहि मांसानि च उद्धृत्य पेशी कृत्वा महायशाः
शकुनाय ददौ रामो रम्ये हरित शाद्वले
transliteration: rohi māṃsāni ca uddhṛtya peśī kṛtvā mahāyaśāḥ
śakunāya dadau rāmo ramye harita śādvale
english: Entering the forest with Saumitrī, Rāma gifted with prowess, killed plump high deer and stretched forth grass and twigs for offering oblation to that bird. Taking off the flesh of those high deer and clustering it, Rāma, of great renown, offered it to the vultures in that pleasant forest-land, abounding in green grass.

sanskrit: यत् तत् प्रेतस्य मर्त्यस्य कथयन्ति द्विजातयः
तत् स्वर्ग गमनम् पित्र्यम् क्षिप्रम् रामो जजाप ह
transliteration: yat tat pretasya martyasya kathayanti dvijātayaḥ
tat svarga gamanam pitryam kṣipram rāmo jajāpa ha
english: Thereupon for his speedy arrival at the abode of celestials, Rāma recited those Mantras which are being uttered by the twice-born ones.

sanskrit: ततो गोदावरीम् गत्वा नदीम् नर वर आत्मजौ
उदकम् चक्रतुः तस्मै गृध्र राजाय तौ उभौ
transliteration: tato godāvarīm gatvā nadīm nara vara ātmajau
udakam cakratuḥ tasmai gṛdhra rājāya tau ubhau
english: Afterwards repairing to the river Godāverī the two princes offered water to that kingly vulture.

sanskrit: शास्त्र दृष्टेन विधिना जले गृधाय राघवौ
स्नात्वा तौ गृध्र राजाय उदकम् चक्रुः तदा
transliteration: śāstra dṛṣṭena vidhinā jale gṛdhāya rāghavau
snātvā tau gṛdhra rājāya udakam cakruḥ tadā
english: And offering yater to him according to the prescribed rites of the Śástras, those two descendants of Raghu, after bathing, perforined the Udaka ceremony for that king of vultures. Presentation of water specially to the manes as a religious or obsequal rite.

sanskrit: स गृध्र राजः कृतवान् यशस्करम्सु दुष्करम् कर्म रणे निपातितः
महर्षि कल्पेन च संस्कृतः तदाजगाम पुण्याम् गतिम् आत्मनः शुभाम्
transliteration: sa gṛdhra rājaḥ kṛtavān yaśaskaramsu duṣkaram karma raṇe nipātitaḥ
maharṣi kalpena ca saṃskṛtaḥ tadājagāma puṇyām gatim ātmanaḥ śubhām
english: Having been killed in battle for an arduous but glorious work, that king of vultures, consecrated by the ascetic-like Rāma, attained to an excellent state.

sanskrit: कृतोदकौ तौ अपि पक्षि सत्तमेस्थिराम् च बुद्धिम् प्रणिधाय जग्मुतुः
प्रवेश्य सीता अधिगमने ततो मनोवनम् सुरेन्द्रौ इव विष्णु वासवौ
transliteration: kṛtodakau tau api pakṣi sattamesthirām ca buddhim praṇidhāya jagmutuḥ
praveśya sītā adhigamane tato manovanam surendrau iva viṣṇu vāsavau
english: Having performed the Udaka ceremony for that best of birds and considering him in the light of a father they went away and entered the forest in quest of Sītā like to the two best of celestials-Visnu and Vasava. glorious work, that king of vultures, consecrated by the ascetic-like Rāma, attained to an excellent state.

sanskrit: कृत्वा एवम् उदकम् तस्मै प्रस्थितौ राघवौ तदा
अवेक्षन्तौ वने सीताम् जग्मतुः पश्चिमाम् दिशम्
transliteration: kṛtvā evam udakam tasmai prasthitau rāghavau tadā
avekṣantau vane sītām jagmatuḥ paścimām diśam
english: Having offered him the gift of water, those two descendants of Raghu wended their way in that forest in quest of Sītā and proceeded towards the south-west*. In this sloka west is mentioned and in the next one there is reference to their turning to the south and hence west here refers to south-west.

sanskrit: ताम् दिशम् दक्षिणाम् गत्वा शर चाप असि धारिणौ
transliteration: tām diśam dakṣiṇām gatvā śara cāpa asi dhāriṇau
english: Then turning to the south, with bow and arrows in hand, they reached a track not wended by the people.

sanskrit: गुल्मैः वृक्षैः च बहुभिः लताभिः च प्रवेष्टितम्
आवृतम् सर्वतो दुर्गम् गहनम् घोर दर्शनम्
transliteration: gulmaiḥ vṛkṣaiḥ ca bahubhiḥ latābhiḥ ca praveṣṭitam
āvṛtam sarvato durgam gahanam ghora darśanam
english: It was a ghastly, impenetrable forest, covered on all sides with groves, trees and creepers,

sanskrit: व्यतिक्रम्य तु वेगेन गृहीत्वा दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
सु भीमम् तन् महाअरण्यम् व्यतियातौ महाबलौ
transliteration: vyatikramya tu vegena gṛhītvā dakṣiṇām diśam
su bhīmam tan mahāaraṇyam vyatiyātau mahābalau
english: Proceeding by the southerly direction, those two mighty ones, passed hastily by that terrible, dreary forest.

sanskrit: ततः परम् जनस्थानात् त्रि क्रोशम् गम्य राघवौ
क्रौंच अरण्यम् विविशतुः गहनम् तौ महौजसौ
transliteration: tataḥ param janasthānāt tri krośam gamya rāghavau
krauṃca araṇyam viviśatuḥ gahanam tau mahaujasau
english: Thereupon, the highly effulgent descendants of Raghu entered the dense forest of Krauñca, situated at a distance of six miles from Janasthāna.

sanskrit: नाना मेघ घन प्रख्यम् प्रहृष्टम् इव सर्वतः
नाना वर्णैः शुभैः पुष्पैः मृग पक्षि गणैः युतम्
transliteration: nānā megha ghana prakhyam prahṛṣṭam iva sarvataḥ
nānā varṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ puṣpaiḥ mṛga pakṣi gaṇaiḥ yutam
english: It was a dense forest like to a collection of clouds, as if smiling on all sides blooming with charming flowers of diverse hues and frequented by various animals and birds.

sanskrit: दिदृक्षमाणौ वैदेहीम् तत् वनम् तौ विचिक्यतुः
तत्र तत्र अवतिष्ठन्तौ सीता हरण दुःखितौ
transliteration: didṛkṣamāṇau vaidehīm tat vanam tau vicikyatuḥ
tatra tatra avatiṣṭhantau sītā haraṇa duḥkhitau
english: Waiting for sometime here and there they, exercised with Sītā's ravishment, explored the entire forest in quest of Vaidehi.

sanskrit: ततः पूर्वेण तौ गत्वा त्रि क्रोसम् भ्रातरु तदा
transliteration: tataḥ pūrveṇa tau gatvā tri krosam bhrātaru tadā
english: Proceeding three Kośas towards the East and passing by the forest of Krauñca the two brothers descried on their way the asylum of Matanga.

sanskrit: दृष्टा तु तद् वनम् घोरम् बहु भीम मृग द्विजम्
नाना वृक्ष समाकीर्णम् सर्वम् गहन पादपम्
transliteration: dṛṣṭā tu tad vanam ghoram bahu bhīma mṛga dvijam
nānā vṛkṣa samākīrṇam sarvam gahana pādapam
english: Having seen that dreary forest frequented by various animals and birds and covered with diverse trees and dense groves, the two sons of Dasaratha beheld a cave in the mountain deep as the region under the earth and ever enveloped with darkness.

sanskrit: ददृशाः ते गिरौ तत्र दरीम् डशरथ आत्मजौ
पाताल सम गम्भीराम् तमसा नित्य संवृताम्
transliteration: dadṛśāḥ te girau tatra darīm ḍaśaratha ātmajau
pātāla sama gambhīrām tamasā nitya saṃvṛtām
english: Having seen that dreary forest frequented by various animals and birds and covered with diverse trees and dense groves, the two sons of Dasaratha beheld a cave in the mountain deep as the region under the earth and ever enveloped with darkness.

sanskrit: आसाद्य च नरव्याघ्रौ दर्याः तस्या अविदूरतः
ददर्श तु महारूपाम् रक्षसीम् विकृत आननाम्
transliteration: āsādya ca naravyāghrau daryāḥ tasyā avidūrataḥ
dadarśa tu mahārūpām rakṣasīm vikṛta ānanām

sanskrit: भयदाम् अल्प सत्त्वानाम् भीभत्साम् रौद्र दर्शनाम्
लंबोदरीम् तीक्ष्ण दंष्ट्राम् करालीम् परुष त्वचम्
transliteration: bhayadām alpa sattvānām bhībhatsām raudra darśanām
laṃbodarīm tīkṣṇa daṃṣṭrām karālīm paruṣa tvacam

sanskrit: भक्षयन्तीम् मृगान् भीमान् विकटाम् मुक्त मूर्धजाम्
अवैक्षताम् तु तौ तत्र भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: bhakṣayantīm mṛgān bhīmān vikaṭām mukta mūrdhajām
avaikṣatām tu tau tatra bhrātarau rāma lakṣmaṇau

sanskrit: सा समासाद्य तौ वीरौ व्रजन्तम् भ्रातुः अग्रतः
एहि रंस्यावहे इति उक्त्वा समालंबत लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: sā samāsādya tau vīrau vrajantam bhrātuḥ agrataḥ
ehi raṃsyāvahe iti uktvā samālaṃbata lakṣmaṇam
english: Beholding there the two brothers, Rāma and Laksmana, she neared the heroes and saying, 'come, we shall sport' assailed Laksmana who had been going before his brother.

sanskrit: उवाच च एनम् वचनम् सौमित्रिम् उपगुह्य सा
अहम् तु अयोमुखी नाम लाभः ते त्वम् असि प्रियः
transliteration: uvāca ca enam vacanam saumitrim upaguhya sā
aham tu ayomukhī nāma lābhaḥ te tvam asi priyaḥ
english: And embracing him she spoke to Saumitrī the following words:-My name is Ayomukhi; it is a great gain to you that you have becoine my beloved one, O my lord.

sanskrit: नाथ पर्वत दुर्गेषु नदीनाम् पुलिनेषु च
आयुः चिरम् इदम् वीर त्वम् मया सह रंस्यसे
transliteration: nātha parvata durgeṣu nadīnām pulineṣu ca
āyuḥ ciram idam vīra tvam mayā saha raṃsyase
english: Do you sport with me, for ever, O hero, in these mountainous strongholds and on the banks of the rivers.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः तु कुपितः खडगम् उद्धृत्य लक्ष्मणः
कर्ण नास स्तनम् तस्या निचकर्ता अरिसूदनः
transliteration: evam uktaḥ tu kupitaḥ khaḍagam uddhṛtya lakṣmaṇaḥ
karṇa nāsa stanam tasyā nicakartā arisūdanaḥ
english: Thereat, exercised with ire, Laksmana, the subduer of foes, uplifting his dagger, chopped off her nose, ears and breast.

sanskrit: कर्ण नासे निकृत्ते तु विस्वरम् विननाद सा
यथा आगतम् प्रदुद्राव राक्षसी घोर दर्शना
transliteration: karṇa nāse nikṛtte tu visvaram vinanāda sā
yathā āgatam pradudrāva rākṣasī ghora darśanā
english: Having her nose and ears cut off, that terriblelooking Räkşasi, emitting fearful cries, fled away whence she had come.

sanskrit: तस्याम् गतायाम् गहनम् व्रजन्तौ वनम् ओजसा
आसेदतुः अरि मित्र घ्नौ भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: tasyām gatāyām gahanam vrajantau vanam ojasā
āsedatuḥ ari mitra ghnau bhrātarau rāma lakṣmaṇau
english: On her departure, proceeding quickly, the two brothers, Rāma and Lakşmaņa, the conquerors of foes, reached a dense forest.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणः तु महातेजाः सत्त्ववान् शीलवान् शुचिः
अब्रवीत् प्रांजलिः वाक्यम् भ्रातरम् दीप्त तेजसम्
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaḥ tu mahātejāḥ sattvavān śīlavān śuciḥ
abravīt prāṃjaliḥ vākyam bhrātaram dīpta tejasam
english: There upon the highly effulgent and truthful Laksmana, possessing a pure character, spoke, with folded hands, to his brother of flaming energy.

sanskrit: स्पंदन्ते मे दृढम् बाहुः उद्विग्नम् इव मे मनः
प्रायशः च अपि अनिष्टानि निमित्तानि उपलक्षये
transliteration: spaṃdante me dṛḍham bāhuḥ udvignam iva me manaḥ
prāyaśaḥ ca api aniṣṭāni nimittāni upalakṣaye
english: My left arm is throbbing, my mind is filled with anxiety and I perceive before me many a bad omen. Do you put on your habiliments, O worshipful one, and act by what I say for your well-being. Methinks from these bad omens some calamity shall soon befall us.

sanskrit: तस्मात् सज्जी भव आर्य त्वम् कुरुष्व वचनम् हितम्
मम एव हि निमित्तानि सद्यः शंसन्ति संभ्रमम्
transliteration: tasmāt sajjī bhava ārya tvam kuruṣva vacanam hitam
mama eva hi nimittāni sadyaḥ śaṃsanti saṃbhramam
english: My left arm is throbbing, my mind is filled with anxiety and I perceive before me many a bad omen. Do you put on your habiliments, O worshipful one, and act by what I say for your well-being. Methinks from these bad omens some calamity shall soon befall us.

sanskrit: एष वंजुलको नाम पक्षी परम दारुणः
आवयोः विजयम् युद्धे शंसन् इव विनर्दति
transliteration: eṣa vaṃjulako nāma pakṣī parama dāruṇaḥ
āvayoḥ vijayam yuddhe śaṃsan iva vinardati
english: O Rāma, this terrible bird Vanjulaka is emitting fearful cries as if announcing our victory in the conflict.

sanskrit: तयोः अन्वेषतोः एवम् सर्वम् तत् वनम् ओजसा
संजज्ञे विपुलः शब्दः प्रभंजन् इव तत् वनम्
transliteration: tayoḥ anveṣatoḥ evam sarvam tat vanam ojasā
saṃjajñe vipulaḥ śabdaḥ prabhaṃjan iva tat vanam
english: Thereupon while they began to explore the entire forest with their prowess there arose a terrible sound as if breaking down the wood.

sanskrit: वनस्य तस्य शब्दो अभूत् दिवम् आपूरयन् इव
transliteration: vanasya tasya śabdo abhūt divam āpūrayan iva
english: The forest was enveloped on all sides with a mighty wind and everywhere was audible a roar filling the wood-land.

sanskrit: तम् शब्दम् कांक्षमाणः तु रामः खड्गी सह अनुजः
ददर्श सु महा कायम् राक्षसम् विपुल उरसम्
transliteration: tam śabdam kāṃkṣamāṇaḥ tu rāmaḥ khaḍgī saha anujaḥ
dadarśa su mahā kāyam rākṣasam vipula urasam
english: With a view to ascertain whence the sound proceeded, Rāma, with a dagger in hand, along with his younger brother, espied a Rākşasha of huge proportions, having big thighs.

sanskrit: आसेदतुः च तत् रक्षः तौ उभौ प्रमुखे स्थितम्
विवृद्धम् अ-शिरो ग्रीवम् कबंधम् उदरे मुखम्
transliteration: āsedatuḥ ca tat rakṣaḥ tau ubhau pramukhe sthitam
vivṛddham a-śiro grīvam kabaṃdham udare mukham
english: The two brothers beheld that Rākşasa stationed before them, having a huge body, devoid of head and neck and therefore a headless demon and having its mouth on its belly.

sanskrit: रोमभिर्निश्चितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्महागिरिमिवोच्छ्रितम् - यद्वा -रोमभिः निचितैः तीक्ष्णैः महागिरिम् इव उच्छ्रितम्
नील मेघ निभम् रौद्रम् मेघ स्तनित निःस्वनम्
transliteration: romabhirniścitaistīkṣṇairmahāgirimivocchritam - yadvā -romabhiḥ nicitaiḥ tīkṣṇaiḥ mahāgirim iva ucchritam
nīla megha nibham raudram megha stanita niḥsvanam
english: Its body resembled a huge mountain and was covered with sharpened down; its look was terrible like to sable cloud and its roar resembled the muttering where of.

Its one terrible, expansive eye, seeing all, was on the fore-head placed on its breast and shone forth like to the flaming fire and it had huge yellow eye-lashes. Its mouth was greatly widened and covered with rows of huge teeth and it was again and again licking that terrible mouth.

sanskrit: एकेन उरसि घोरेण नयनेन आशु दर्शिना
महा दंष्ट्र उपपन्नम् तम् लेलिहानम् महा मुखम्
transliteration: ekena urasi ghoreṇa nayanena āśu darśinā
mahā daṃṣṭra upapannam tam lelihānam mahā mukham
english: Its one terrible, expansive eye, seeing all, was on the fore-head placed on its breast and shone forth like to the flaming fire and it had huge yellow eye-lashes. Its mouth was greatly widened and covered with rows of huge teeth and it was again and again licking that terrible mouth.

sanskrit: भक्षयंतम् महा घोरान् ऋक्ष सिम्ह मृग द्विपान्
घोरौ भुजौ विकुर्वाणम् उभौ योजनम् आयतौ
transliteration: bhakṣayaṃtam mahā ghorān ṛkṣa simha mṛga dvipān
ghorau bhujau vikurvāṇam ubhau yojanam āyatau

sanskrit: कराभ्याम् विविधान् गृह्य ऋक्षान् पक्षि गणान् मृगान्
transliteration: karābhyām vividhān gṛhya ṛkṣān pakṣi gaṇān mṛgān
english: And stretching forth its two huge arms extending over a Yojana it was devouring bears, lions and deer. It was catching and throwing with its huge hands many an animal, bird and bear.

sanskrit: स्थितम् आवृत्य पन्थानम् तयोः भ्रात्रोः प्रपन्नयोः
अथ तम् समतिक्रम्य क्रोश मात्रम् ददर्शतुः
transliteration: sthitam āvṛtya panthānam tayoḥ bhrātroḥ prapannayoḥ
atha tam samatikramya krośa mātram dadarśatuḥ
english: Hindering the way-fare it was awaiting those two brothers. And proceeding a Krosa, they espied that fearful, grim-visaged, headless demon, hindering all creatures with its arms, terrible-looking and appearing like a kabandha from its very situation,

sanskrit: महान्तम् दारुणम् भीमम् कबंधम् भुज संवृतम्
कबंधम् इव संस्थानत् अति घोर प्रदशनम्
transliteration: mahāntam dāruṇam bhīmam kabaṃdham bhuja saṃvṛtam
kabaṃdham iva saṃsthānat ati ghora pradaśanam

sanskrit: स महा बाहुः अत्यर्थम् प्रसार्य विपुलौ भुजौ
जग्राह सहितौ एव राघवौ पीडयन् बलात्
transliteration: sa mahā bāhuḥ atyartham prasārya vipulau bhujau
jagrāha sahitau eva rāghavau pīḍayan balāt
english: Thereupon that one, of huge arms, stretching them forth, got hold of those two descendants of Raghu crushing them with its strength.

sanskrit: खड्गिनौ दृढ धन्वानौ तिग्म तेजौ महा भुजौ
भ्रातरौ विवशम् प्राप्तौ कृष्यमाणौ महा बलौ
transliteration: khaḍginau dṛḍha dhanvānau tigma tejau mahā bhujau
bhrātarau vivaśam prāptau kṛṣyamāṇau mahā balau
english: Those two highly powerful brothers, of mighty arms, with daggers and bows in their hands, were assailed and got hold of by that Raksasha.

sanskrit: तत्र धैर्यात् च शूराः तु राघवो न एव विव्यधे
बाल्यात् अनाश्रयत्वात् च एव लक्ष्मणः तु अतिविव्यधे
transliteration: tatra dhairyāt ca śūrāḥ tu rāghavo na eva vivyadhe
bālyāt anāśrayatvāt ca eva lakṣmaṇaḥ tu ativivyadhe
english: Rāma was heroic and patient by nature and consequently was not much afflicted; but Laks maņa was a mere boy and impatient by nature and was consequently greatly afflicted.

sanskrit: उवाच च विषण्णम् सन् राघवम् राघव अनुजः
पश्य माम् विवशम् वीर राक्षसस्य वशम् गतम्
transliteration: uvāca ca viṣaṇṇam san rāghavam rāghava anujaḥ
paśya mām vivaśam vīra rākṣasasya vaśam gatam
english: Being greatly distressed, the younger brother of Răghava spoke to him, saying Do you behold me, O hero, brought under the hold of this Raks asha, and renouncing me only, O Rāghava, do you get yourself cff. And offering me as sacrifice, do you escape at your ease.

sanskrit: मया एकन तु निर्युक्तः परिमुच्यस्व राघव
माम् हि भूत बलिम् दत्त्वा पलास्व यथा सुखम्
transliteration: mayā ekana tu niryuktaḥ parimucyasva rāghava
mām hi bhūta balim dattvā palāsva yathā sukham
english: Being greatly distressed, the younger brother of Răghava spoke to him, saying Do you behold me, O hero, brought under the hold of this Raks asha, and renouncing me only, O Rāghava, do you get yourself cff. And offering me as sacrifice, do you escape at your ease.

sanskrit: अधिगंता असि वैदेहीम् अचिरेण इति मे मतिः
प्रति लभ्य च काकुत्स्थ पितॄ पैतामहम् महीम्
transliteration: adhigaṃtā asi vaidehīm acireṇa iti me matiḥ
prati labhya ca kākutstha pitṝ paitāmaham mahīm
english: Methinks for certain, O Kākutstha, you shall soon come by Vaidehi and regain your ancestral kingdom. But remember me always, O Rāma, when you shall find yourself placed on the throne.

sanskrit: तत्र माम् राम राज्यस्थः स्मर्तुम् अर्हसि सर्वदा
लक्ष्मणेन एवम् उक्तः तु रामः सौमित्रिम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tatra mām rāma rājyasthaḥ smartum arhasi sarvadā
lakṣmaṇena evam uktaḥ tu rāmaḥ saumitrim abravīt

sanskrit: मा स्म त्रासम् वृथा वीर न हि त्वा दृक् विषीदति
एतस्मिन् अन्तरे क्रूरो भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: mā sma trāsam vṛthā vīra na hi tvā dṛk viṣīdati
etasmin antare krūro bhrātarau rāma lakṣmaṇau

sanskrit: तौ उवाच महाबाहुः कबन्धो दानव उत्तमः
कौ युवाम् वृषभ स्कन्धौ महा खड्ग धनुर् धरौ
transliteration: tau uvāca mahābāhuḥ kabandho dānava uttamaḥ
kau yuvām vṛṣabha skandhau mahā khaḍga dhanur dharau

sanskrit: घोरम् देशम् इमम् प्राप्तौ दैवेन मम चाक्षुषौ
वदतम् कार्यम् इह वाम् किम् अर्थम् च आगतौ युवाम्
transliteration: ghoram deśam imam prāptau daivena mama cākṣuṣau
vadatam kāryam iha vām kim artham ca āgatau yuvām

sanskrit: इमम् देशम् अनुप्राप्तौ क्षुधा आर्तस्य इह तिष्ठतः
स बाण चाप खड्गौ च तीक्ष्ण शृंगौ इव ऋषभौ
transliteration: imam deśam anuprāptau kṣudhā ārtasya iha tiṣṭhataḥ
sa bāṇa cāpa khaḍgau ca tīkṣṇa śṛṃgau iva ṛṣabhau

sanskrit: मम तूर्णम् उपसंप्राप्तौ दुर्लभम् जीवितम् वाम्
तस्य तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा कबंधस्य दुरात्मनः
transliteration: mama tūrṇam upasaṃprāptau durlabham jīvitam vām
tasya tat vacanam śrutvā kabaṃdhasya durātmanaḥ

sanskrit: कृच्छ्रात् कृच्छ्रतरम् प्राप्य दारुणम् सत्य विक्रम
transliteration: kṛcchrāt kṛcchrataram prāpya dāruṇam satya vikrama
english: Hearing those words of the vicious-souled Kabandha, Rāma having his countenance dried up, bespoke Laksmana-O you, having truth for your prowess, again and again, greater and worse calamities have been threatening us. We have already met with a dire disaster leading to our death, consequent on my separation from my dear one.

sanskrit: व्यसनम् जीवित अन्ताय प्राप्तम् अप्राप्य ताम् प्रियाम्
कालस्य सुमहत् वीर्यम् सर्व भूतेषु लक्ष्मण
transliteration: vyasanam jīvita antāya prāptam aprāpya tām priyām
kālasya sumahat vīryam sarva bhūteṣu lakṣmaṇa

sanskrit: त्वाम् च माम् च नरव्याघ्र व्यसनैः पश्य मोहितौ
न हि भारो अस्ति दैवस्य सर्व भुतेषु लक्ष्मण
transliteration: tvām ca mām ca naravyāghra vyasanaiḥ paśya mohitau
na hi bhāro asti daivasya sarva bhuteṣu lakṣmaṇa
english: Mighty is the course of Destiny in all creatures, O Lakşmaņa. Do you O best of men, behold even yourself and me stricken with calamity. But O Lakşmaņa it is not very difficult for destiny to afflict all creatures.

sanskrit: शूराः च बलवंतः च कृत अस्त्राः च रण आजिरे
काल अभिपन्नाः सीदन्ति यथा वालुक सेतवः
transliteration: śūrāḥ ca balavaṃtaḥ ca kṛta astrāḥ ca raṇa ājire
kāla abhipannāḥ sīdanti yathā vāluka setavaḥ
english: Under the influence of destiny even the mighty heroes, well habited in armours are distressed like to a bridge of sands.

sanskrit: इति ब्रुवाणो दृढ सत्य विक्रमोमहायशा दाशरथिः प्रतापवान्
अवेक्ष्य सौमित्रिम् उदग्र विक्रमम्स्थिराम् तदा स्वाम् मतिम् आत्मना अकरोत्
transliteration: iti bruvāṇo dṛḍha satya vikramomahāyaśā dāśarathiḥ pratāpavān
avekṣya saumitrim udagra vikramamsthirām tadā svām matim ātmanā akarot
english: Addressing these words to Saumitrī, the resolute, powerful and highly famous son of Dasaratha, having truth for his prowess, composed himself by dint of his own understanding.

sanskrit: तौ तु तत्र स्थितौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
बाहु पाश परिक्षिप्तौ कबन्धो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tau tu tatra sthitau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau rāma lakṣmaṇau
bāhu pāśa parikṣiptau kabandho vākyam abravīt
english: Beholding both the brothers, Rāma and Laks maņa, clasping each other with their arms, the headless demon spoke:

sanskrit: तिष्ठतः किम् नु माम् दृष्ट्वा क्षुधा आर्तम् क्षत्रिय ऋषभौ
आहार अर्थम् तु सन्दिष्टौ दैवेन गत चेतसौ
transliteration: tiṣṭhataḥ kim nu mām dṛṣṭvā kṣudhā ārtam kṣatriya ṛṣabhau
āhāra artham tu sandiṣṭau daivena gata cetasau
english: O two best of Ksatryas, are you waiting here beholding me hungry? O you having lost your sense, you have been chosen by Destiny as my food.

sanskrit: तत् श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणो वाक्यम् प्राप्त कालम् हितम् तदा
उवाच आर्तिम् समापन्नो विक्रमे कृत निश्चयः
transliteration: tat śrutvā lakṣmaṇo vākyam prāpta kālam hitam tadā
uvāca ārtim samāpanno vikrame kṛta niścayaḥ
english: Hearing those words Laksmana, sore, distressed and determined to display his valour, addressed Rāma with words worthy of being said on that occasion.

sanskrit: त्वाम् च माम् च पुरा तूर्णम् आदत्ते राक्षस अधमः
तस्मात् असिभ्याम् अस्य आशु बाहू चिन्दावहे गुरू
transliteration: tvām ca mām ca purā tūrṇam ādatte rākṣasa adhamaḥ
tasmāt asibhyām asya āśu bāhū cindāvahe gurū
english: This vile Rākṣasa shall seize both of us; let us sunder soon its two huge arms with our daggers.

sanskrit: भिषणो अयम् महाकायो राक्षसो भुज विक्रमः
लोकम् हि अति जितम् कृत्वा हि अवाम् हन्तुम् इह इच्छति
transliteration: bhiṣaṇo ayam mahākāyo rākṣaso bhuja vikramaḥ
lokam hi ati jitam kṛtvā hi avām hantum iha icchati
english: This grim-visaged Raksasas, of huge proportions, gifted only with the strength of arms, defeating all other persons, has addressed itself at last to destroy us.

sanskrit: निश्चेष्टानाम् वधो राजन् कुत्स्तितो जगती पतेः
क्रतु मध्य उपनीतानाम् पशूनाम् इव राघव
transliteration: niśceṣṭānām vadho rājan kutstito jagatī pateḥ
kratu madhya upanītānām paśūnām iva rāghava
english: It is odious for the Kșatriyas to make away with those who cannot defend themselves like to animals brought for sacrifice.* The purport is : Lakṣmaṇa wanted to chop off the arms of Kabandha and not to put an end to its life as it was not capable of fighting, being a headless demon. And it is not proper for the Ks atryas to destroy those who cannot fight.

sanskrit: एतत् संजल्पितम् श्रुत्वा तयोः क्रुद्धः तु राक्षसः
विदार्य आस्यम् ततो रौद्रम् तौ भक्षयितुम् आरभत्
transliteration: etat saṃjalpitam śrutvā tayoḥ kruddhaḥ tu rākṣasaḥ
vidārya āsyam tato raudram tau bhakṣayitum ārabhat
english: Hearing their conversation, the Raksasa, inflamed with rage, widening its terrible mouth, prepared to devour them up. This has a special significance here-meaning to get hold of them by stretching forth its arms.

sanskrit: ततः तौ देश कालज्ञौ खड्गाभ्याम् एव राघवौ
अच्छिन्दताम् सुसंहृष्टौ बाहू तस्य अंस देशतः
transliteration: tataḥ tau deśa kālajñau khaḍgābhyām eva rāghavau
acchindatām susaṃhṛṣṭau bāhū tasya aṃsa deśataḥ
english: Thereat Rāma and Lakşmana, cognizant of time and place, pleased+, sundered its arms off its shoulders with their daggers. They were pleased because they cut off its arms with ease like to the trunks of a plantain tree.

sanskrit: दक्षिणो दक्षिणम् बाहुम् असक्तम् असिना ततः
चिच्छेद रामो वेगेन सव्यम् वीरः तु लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: dakṣiṇo dakṣiṇam bāhum asaktam asinā tataḥ
ciccheda rāmo vegena savyam vīraḥ tu lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Rāma, stationed on the right side cut off in no time its right arm with his dagger and the heroic Laksmana, the left one. It may mean also expert.

sanskrit: स पपात महाबाहुः चिन्न बाहुः महा स्वनः
खम् च गाम् च दिशः चैव नादयन् जलदो यथा
transliteration: sa papāta mahābāhuḥ cinna bāhuḥ mahā svanaḥ
kham ca gām ca diśaḥ caiva nādayan jalado yathā
english: Having got its arms dissevered, the terriblevoiced, Kabandha, of huge arms, roaring like to the muttering of clouds and resounding the heaven, earth and all the quarters, fell flat on the ground.

sanskrit: स निकृत्तौ भुजौ दृष्ट्वा शोणित ओघ परिप्लुतः
दीनः पप्रच्छ तौ वीरौ कौ युवाम् इति दानवः
transliteration: sa nikṛttau bhujau dṛṣṭvā śoṇita ogha pariplutaḥ
dīnaḥ papraccha tau vīrau kau yuvām iti dānavaḥ
english: Beholding both its arms cut off, the demon, with its person bathed in blood, asked them poorly Who are you?

sanskrit: इति तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य लक्ष्मणः शुभ लक्षणः
transliteration: iti tasya bruvāṇasya lakṣmaṇaḥ śubha lakṣaṇaḥ
english: Being thus accosted by Kabandha, the mighty Lakşmana, gifted with auspicious marks, spoke to it, about Kākutstha.

sanskrit: अयम् इक्ष्वाकु दायादो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः
तस्य एव अवरजम् विद्धि भ्रातरम् माम् च लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: ayam ikṣvāku dāyādo rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ
tasya eva avarajam viddhi bhrātaram mām ca lakṣmaṇam
english: He is a descendant of the Ikşvākus known on earth by the name of Rāma, and know me as his younger brother, by name-Laksmana.

sanskrit: मात्रा प्रतिहतो राज्ये रामः प्रवाजितो वनम्
मया सह चरति एष भार्यया च महत् वनम्
transliteration: mātrā pratihato rājye rāmaḥ pravājito vanam
mayā saha carati eṣa bhāryayā ca mahat vanam
english: Being thwarted by mother (Kaikeyi) in his accession of kingdom, he, renouncing all, has fled as an exile to woods, and has, along with me and his spouse, been ranging this forest. While living in the dense forest the wife of Răma, effulgent like to the celestials has been ravished by a Raksasa. Searching her, have we come here.

sanskrit: अस्य देव प्रभावस्य वसतो विजने वने
रक्षसा अपहृता भार्या याम् इच्छन्तौ इह आगतौ
transliteration: asya deva prabhāvasya vasato vijane vane
rakṣasā apahṛtā bhāryā yām icchantau iha āgatau
english: Being thwarted by mother (Kaikeyi) in his accession of kingdom, he, renouncing all, has fled as an exile to woods, and has, along with me and his spouse, been ranging this forest. While living in the dense forest the wife of Răma, effulgent like to the celestials has been ravished by a Raksasa. Searching her, have we come here.

sanskrit: त्वम् तु को वा किम् अर्थम् वा कबन्ध सदृशो वने
आस्येन उरसि दीप्तेन भग्न जन्घो विचेष्टसे
transliteration: tvam tu ko vā kim artham vā kabandha sadṛśo vane
āsyena urasi dīptena bhagna jangho viceṣṭase
english: Who are you? And what for are you ranging this forest like to a headless demon, having your thighs broken and your flaming face placed on your breast?

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः कबंधः तु लक्ष्मणेन उत्तरम् वचः
उवाच परम प्रीतः तत् इन्द्र वचनम् स्मरन्
transliteration: evam uktaḥ kabaṃdhaḥ tu lakṣmaṇena uttaram vacaḥ
uvāca parama prītaḥ tat indra vacanam smaran
english: Being thus addressed by Lakṣmaṇa with these goodly words, Kabandha, pleased, recollecting the words of Indra, bespoke him,

sanskrit: स्वागतम् वाम् नरव्याघ्रौ दिष्ट्या पश्यामि वाम् अहम्
दिष्ट्या च इमौ निकृत्तौ मे युवाभ्याम् बाहु बन्धनौ
transliteration: svāgatam vām naravyāghrau diṣṭyā paśyāmi vām aham
diṣṭyā ca imau nikṛttau me yuvābhyām bāhu bandhanau
english: O two best of men, you are welcome! By my good luck it is that I do behold you. By my good fortune you have dissevered my shoulders today.

sanskrit: विरूपम् यत् च मे रूपम् प्राप्तम् हि अविनयात् यथा
तत् मे शृणु नरव्याघ्र तत्त्वतः शंसतः तव
transliteration: virūpam yat ca me rūpam prāptam hi avinayāt yathā
tat me śṛṇu naravyāghra tattvataḥ śaṃsataḥ tava
english: Do you hear; I shall relate truly to you how have I, by my haughtiness, come by this unsightly shape.

sanskrit: रूपम् आसीत् मम अचिंत्यम् त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्
transliteration: rūpam āsīt mama aciṃtyam triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam

sanskrit: यथा सूर्यस्य सोमस्य शक्रस्य च यथा वपुः
सो अहम् रूपम् इदम् कृत्वा लोक वित्रासनम् महत्
transliteration: yathā sūryasya somasya śakrasya ca yathā vapuḥ
so aham rūpam idam kṛtvā loka vitrāsanam mahat

sanskrit: ऋषीन् वन गतान् राम त्रासयामि ततः ततः
ततः स्थूलशिरा नाम महर्षिः कोपितो मया
transliteration: ṛṣīn vana gatān rāma trāsayāmi tataḥ tataḥ
tataḥ sthūlaśirā nāma maharṣiḥ kopito mayā

sanskrit: संचिन्वन् विविधम् वन्यम् रूपेण अनेन धर्षितः
तेन अहम् उक्तः प्रेक्ष्य एवम् घोर शाप अभिधायिना
transliteration: saṃcinvan vividham vanyam rūpeṇa anena dharṣitaḥ
tena aham uktaḥ prekṣya evam ghora śāpa abhidhāyinā
english: Once on a time assuming this terrible shape I assailed and enraged the great ascetic Sthulasira collecting diverse wild fruits. Thereupon he imprecated curses upon me.

sanskrit: एतत् एव नृशंसम् ते रूपम् अस्तु विगर्हितम्
स मया याचितः क्रुद्धः शापस्य अन्तो भवेत् इति
transliteration: etat eva nṛśaṃsam te rūpam astu vigarhitam
sa mayā yācitaḥ kruddhaḥ śāpasya anto bhavet iti
english: Do you retain this ghastly shape hated of all mankind. Upon my praying to that angry ascetic for my relief from that curse, he said.

sanskrit: अभिशाप कृतस्य इति तेन इदम् भाषितम् वचः
यदा छित्त्वा भुजौ रामः त्वाम् दहेत् विजने वने
transliteration: abhiśāpa kṛtasya iti tena idam bhāṣitam vacaḥ
yadā chittvā bhujau rāmaḥ tvām dahet vijane vane

sanskrit: तदा त्वम् प्राप्स्यसे रूपम् स्वम् एव विपुलम् शुभम्
श्रिया विराजितम् पुत्रम् दनोः त्वम् विद्धि लक्ष्मण
transliteration: tadā tvam prāpsyase rūpam svam eva vipulam śubham
śriyā virājitam putram danoḥ tvam viddhi lakṣmaṇa
english: You shall regain your stalwart and beautiful shape when you shall be burnt by Rāma in a dense forest having got your arms dissevered by him.

sanskrit: इन्द्र कोपात् इदम् रूपम् प्राप्तम् एवम् रण आजिरे
अहम् हि तपसा उग्रेण पितामहम् अतोषयम्
transliteration: indra kopāt idam rūpam prāptam evam raṇa ājire
aham hi tapasā ugreṇa pitāmaham atoṣayam

sanskrit: दीर्घम् आयुः स मे प्रादात् ततो माम् विभ्रमो अस्पृशत्
दीर्घम् आयुः मया प्राप्तम् किम् मे शक्रः करिष्यति
transliteration: dīrgham āyuḥ sa me prādāt tato mām vibhramo aspṛśat
dīrgham āyuḥ mayā prāptam kim me śakraḥ kariṣyati
english: O Lakşmaņa, know me to be the beautiful son of Danu. Through Indra's curse in the battle field I have been metamorphosed into my present shape. After I had pleased him with hard austerites, the Grand-Father of the celestials conferred on me a long life. And therefore I was inflamed with pride assailed Indra in a conflict, thinking within me, 'I have gained a long life-what can Indra do me?'

sanskrit: इति एवम् बुद्धिम् आस्थाय रणे शक्रम् अधर्षयम्
तस्य बाहु प्रमुक्तेन वज्रेण शत पर्वणा
transliteration: iti evam buddhim āsthāya raṇe śakram adharṣayam
tasya bāhu pramuktena vajreṇa śata parvaṇā
english: Thereupon by his thunderbolt, having hundred edges hurled off his hands, my thighs were shattered and my head thrusted into my body.

sanskrit: सक्थिनी च शिरः चैव शरीरे संप्रवेशितम्
स मया याच्यमानः सन् न आनयत् यम सादनम्
transliteration: sakthinī ca śiraḥ caiva śarīre saṃpraveśitam
sa mayā yācyamānaḥ san na ānayat yama sādanam

sanskrit: पितामह वचः सत्यम् तत् अस्ति इति मम अब्रवीत्
अनाहारः कथम् शक्तो भग्न सक्थि शिरो मुखः
transliteration: pitāmaha vacaḥ satyam tat asti iti mama abravīt
anāhāraḥ katham śakto bhagna sakthi śiro mukhaḥ

sanskrit: वज्रेण अभिहतः कालम् सु दीर्घम् अपि जीवितुम्
स एवम् उक्तः मे शक्रो बाहू योजनम् आयतौ
transliteration: vajreṇa abhihataḥ kālam su dīrgham api jīvitum
sa evam uktaḥ me śakro bāhū yojanam āyatau
english: Where to I replied 'How shall I live long without any food, being smitten by you having a thunderbolt in your hand, and having my head, thighs and mouth crushed down?' Thereat Indra made my hands extending over a Yojana and placed my mouth, having sharpened teeth, on my belly.

sanskrit: तदा च आस्यम् च मे कुक्षौ तीक्ष्ण दंष्ट्रम् अकल्पयत्
सो अहम् भुजाभ्याम् दीर्घाभ्याम् संकृष्य अस्मिन् वने चरान्
transliteration: tadā ca āsyam ca me kukṣau tīkṣṇa daṃṣṭram akalpayat
so aham bhujābhyām dīrghābhyām saṃkṛṣya asmin vane carān

sanskrit: सिंह द्विपि मृग व्याघ्रान् भक्षयामि समंततः
स तु माम् अब्रवीत् इन्द्रो यदा रामः स लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: siṃha dvipi mṛga vyāghrān bhakṣayāmi samaṃtataḥ
sa tu mām abravīt indro yadā rāmaḥ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ

sanskrit: छेत्स्यते समरे बाहू तदा स्वर्गम् गमिष्यसि
अनेन वपुषा तात वने अस्मिन् राजसत्तम
transliteration: chetsyate samare bāhū tadā svargam gamiṣyasi
anena vapuṣā tāta vane asmin rājasattama

sanskrit: यत् यत् पश्यामि सर्वस्य ग्रहणम् साधु रोचये
अवश्यम् ग्रहणम् रामो मन्ये अहम् समुपैष्यति
transliteration: yat yat paśyāmi sarvasya grahaṇam sādhu rocaye
avaśyam grahaṇam rāmo manye aham samupaiṣyati

sanskrit: इमाम् बुद्धिम् पुरस्कृत्य देह न्यास कृत श्रमः
स त्वम् रामो असि भद्रम् ते न अहम् अन्येन राघव
transliteration: imām buddhim puraskṛtya deha nyāsa kṛta śramaḥ
sa tvam rāmo asi bhadram te na aham anyena rāghava

sanskrit: शक्यो हन्तुम् यथा तत्त्वम् एवम् उक्तम् महर्षिणा
अहम् हि मति साचिव्यम् करिष्यामि नर ऋषभ
transliteration: śakyo hantum yathā tattvam evam uktam maharṣiṇā
aham hi mati sācivyam kariṣyāmi nara ṛṣabha

sanskrit: मित्रम् चैव उपदेक्ष्यामि युवाभ्याम् संस्कृतो अग्निना
एवम् उक्तः तु धर्मात्मा दनुना तेन राघवः
transliteration: mitram caiva upadekṣyāmi yuvābhyām saṃskṛto agninā
evam uktaḥ tu dharmātmā danunā tena rāghavaḥ

sanskrit: रावणेन हृता सीता मम भार्या यशस्विनी
transliteration: rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā mama bhāryā yaśasvinī

sanskrit: निष्क्रांतस्य जनस्थानात् सह भ्रात्रा यथा सुखम्
नाम मात्रम् तु जानामि न रूपम् तस्य रक्षसः
transliteration: niṣkrāṃtasya janasthānāt saha bhrātrā yathā sukham
nāma mātram tu jānāmi na rūpam tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: My renowned spouse Sītā was easily ravished by Rāvaņa after I had gone out of Janasthana along with my brother. I know that Raksasa's name only—but do not know his whereabouts, his figure and his prowess.

sanskrit: निवासम् वा प्रभावम् वा वयम् तस्य न विद्महे
transliteration: nivāsam vā prabhāvam vā vayam tasya na vidmahe
english: It behove you to show proper compassion for us, who have been stricken with grief, who are helpless, have been ranging this forest in this way and are, ever engaged in the well-being of others*. This sloka may be rendered in another way:Do you continue benefiting us by showing proper compassion for us, who are stricken with grief helpless and ranging the forest in this way. We have however adopted here the commentator Rāmāņaya's explanation.

sanskrit: कारुण्यम् सदृशम् कर्तुम् उपकारे च वर्तताम्
काष्ठानि आनीय भग्नानि काले शुष्काणि कुंजरैः
transliteration: kāruṇyam sadṛśam kartum upakāre ca vartatām
kāṣṭhāni ānīya bhagnāni kāle śuṣkāṇi kuṃjaraiḥ

sanskrit: धक्ष्यामः त्वाम् वयम् वीर श्वभ्रे महति कल्पिते
स त्वम् सीताम् समाचक्ष्व येन वा यत्र वा हृता
transliteration: dhakṣyāmaḥ tvām vayam vīra śvabhre mahati kalpite
sa tvam sītām samācakṣva yena vā yatra vā hṛtā

sanskrit: कुरु कल्याणम् अत्यर्थम् यदि जानासि तत्त्वतः
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण वाक्यम् दनुः अनुत्तमम्
transliteration: kuru kalyāṇam atyartham yadi jānāsi tattvataḥ
evam uktaḥ tu rāmeṇa vākyam danuḥ anuttamam

sanskrit: प्रोवाच कुशलो वक्तुम् वक्तारम् अपि राघवम्
दिव्यम् अस्ति न मे ज्ञानम् न अभिजानामि मैथिलीम्
transliteration: provāca kuśalo vaktum vaktāram api rāghavam
divyam asti na me jñānam na abhijānāmi maithilīm

sanskrit: यः ताम् ज्ञास्यति तम् वक्ष्ये दग्धः स्वम् रूपम् आस्थितः
यो अभिजानाति तद् रक्षः तद् वक्ष्ये राम तत् परम्
transliteration: yaḥ tām jñāsyati tam vakṣye dagdhaḥ svam rūpam āsthitaḥ
yo abhijānāti tad rakṣaḥ tad vakṣye rāma tat param
english: I am not gifted with divine fore-sight and therefore do not know where Maithilī is. I shall let you know of him who shall be able to tell you all about her, after I resume my original shape, being burnt (by you). I shall furthermore tell you, O Rāma, who knows that Räksasa.

sanskrit: अदग्धस्य हि विज्ञातुम् शक्तिः अस्ति न मे प्रभो
राक्षसम् तम् महावीर्यम् सीता येन हृता तव
transliteration: adagdhasya hi vijñātum śaktiḥ asti na me prabho
rākṣasam tam mahāvīryam sītā yena hṛtā tava
english: Without being burnt I am incapable of being cognizant of that highly powerful Rākṣasa who has carried away your Sītā.

sanskrit: विज्ञानम् हि महत् भ्रष्टम् शाप दोषेण राघव
स्वकृतेन मया प्राप्तम् रूपम् लोक विगर्हितम्
transliteration: vijñānam hi mahat bhraṣṭam śāpa doṣeṇa rāghava
svakṛtena mayā prāptam rūpam loka vigarhitam
english: By the influence of curse, I have lost my foresight and by my own improper actions I have been transformed into this ugly figure.

sanskrit: किम् तु यावत् न याति अस्तम् सविता श्रान्त वाहनः
तावत् माम् अवटे क्षिप्त्वा दह राम यथा विधि
transliteration: kim tu yāvat na yāti astam savitā śrānta vāhanaḥ
tāvat mām avaṭe kṣiptvā daha rāma yathā vidhi
english: Do you cremate me according to the prescribed rites after throwing me into the ditch before the sun, with his worn out carriers descends into the western horizon.

sanskrit: दग्धः त्वया अहम् अवटे न्यायेन रघुनंदन
वक्ष्यामि तम् महावीर यः तम् वेत्स्यति राक्षसम्
transliteration: dagdhaḥ tvayā aham avaṭe nyāyena raghunaṃdana
vakṣyāmi tam mahāvīra yaḥ tam vetsyati rākṣasam
english: Being burnt by you in the ditch, with due ceremonials, O descendant of Raghu, I shall inention, to you, one who knows that Rāksasa.

sanskrit: तेन सख्यम् च कर्तव्यम् न्याय्य वृत्तेन राघव
कल्पयिष्यति ते प्रीतः साहाय्यम् लघु विक्रमः
transliteration: tena sakhyam ca kartavyam nyāyya vṛttena rāghava
kalpayiṣyati te prītaḥ sāhāyyam laghu vikramaḥ
english: O Raghava, O fleet-footed hero, do you contract friendship with him gifted with good qualities and he shall assist you.

sanskrit: न हि तस्य अस्ति अविज्ञातम् त्रिषु लोकेषु राघव
सर्वान् परिवृतो लोकान् पुरा वै कारण अन्तरे
transliteration: na hi tasya asti avijñātam triṣu lokeṣu rāghava
sarvān parivṛto lokān purā vai kāraṇa antare
english: There is nothing unknown to him, O Rāghava is the three worlds. Formerly for some reasons he had travelled all over them.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तौ तु तौ वीरौ कबन्धेन नर ईश्वरौ
transliteration: evam uktau tu tau vīrau kabandhena nara īśvarau
english: After Kabandha had spoken thus, the two best of men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa took him to a mountain-cave and placed on fire.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणः तु महा उल्काभिः ज्वलिताभिः समन्ततः
transliteration: lakṣmaṇaḥ tu mahā ulkābhiḥ jvalitābhiḥ samantataḥ
english: Laksmana kindled the funeral pile, which was ablaze on all sides. Thereupon the fire began to burn down slowly the huge and corpulent body of Kabandha like to a lump of clarified butter.

sanskrit: तत् शरीरम् कबन्धस्य घृत पिण्ड उपमम् महत्
transliteration: tat śarīram kabandhasya ghṛta piṇḍa upamam mahat
english: Laksmana kindled the funeral pile, which was ablaze on all sides. Thereupon the fire began to burn down slowly the huge and corpulent body of Kabandha like to a lump of clarified butter.

sanskrit: स विधूय चिताम् आशु विधूमो अग्निर् इव उत्थितः
अरजे वाससी बिभ्रत् मालाम् दिव्याम् महाबलः
transliteration: sa vidhūya citām āśu vidhūmo agnir iva utthitaḥ
araje vāsasī bibhrat mālām divyām mahābalaḥ
english: Afterwards the highly powerful demon, shaking the funeral pile, rose up quickly like a smokeless flame of fire, wearing a clean cloth and a celestial garland.

sanskrit: ततः चिताया वेगेन भास्वरो विरज अंबरः
उत्पपात आशु संहृष्टः सर्व प्रत्यंग भूषणः
transliteration: tataḥ citāyā vegena bhāsvaro viraja aṃbaraḥ
utpapāta āśu saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sarva pratyaṃga bhūṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: विमाने भास्वरे तिष्ठन् हंस युक्ते यशस् करे
प्रभया च महातेजा दिशो दश विराजयन्
transliteration: vimāne bhāsvare tiṣṭhan haṃsa yukte yaśas kare
prabhayā ca mahātejā diśo daśa virājayan
english: And the graceful demon, wearing an unsullied cloth and having all its limbs crested with diverse ornaments, rose from the pile high up in the welkin with a delighted heart. Thereupon mounting on a famed car, brilliant and drawn by swans* and lighting up all the quarters with the effulgence of his person, that highly powerful one, stationing himself in the heaven, addressed Rāma. By virtue of the pious observances performed by him in his previous existence and for his being burnt by Rāma that celestial car appeared there.

sanskrit: सो अन्तरिक्ष गतो वाक्यम् कबन्धो रामम् अब्रवीत्
शृणु राघव तत्त्वेन यथा सीमाम् अवाप्स्यसि
transliteration: so antarikṣa gato vākyam kabandho rāmam abravīt
śṛṇu rāghava tattvena yathā sīmām avāpsyasi

sanskrit: राम षड् युक्तयो लोके याभिः सर्वम् विमृश्यते
परिमृष्टो दश अन्तेन दश आभागेन सेव्यते
transliteration: rāma ṣaḍ yuktayo loke yābhiḥ sarvam vimṛśyate
parimṛṣṭo daśa antena daśa ābhāgena sevyate
english: Do you hear truly, O Rāghava, of the means by which you shall come by Sīta. There are six expedients. O Rāma, by virtue of which kings acquire all objects. He, in whom misfortune has culminated, should seek the company of one such+. The six expedients are as follow—(1) Sandhi, peace. (2) Vigraha war-fare. (3) Yāna, military expedition against an enemy. (4) Asana-halting. (5) Daidhibhava-sowing dissension. (6) Samaşraya seeking protection. This is a moral law referring to the sixth to or expedient, to be resorted by the kings-namely Samasrarya seeking protection.

sanskrit: दश आभाग गतो हीनः त्वम् राम सह लक्ष्मणः
यत् कृते व्यसनम् प्राप्तम् त्वया दार प्रधर्षणम्
transliteration: daśa ābhāga gato hīnaḥ tvam rāma saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
yat kṛte vyasanam prāptam tvayā dāra pradharṣaṇam
english: You have, O Rāma along with Laksmana, met with the culmination of misfortune and for which you have been assailed with such a disaster as the ravishment of your spouse.

sanskrit: तत् अवश्यम् त्वया कार्यः स सुहृत् सुहृदाम् वर
अकृत्वा न हि ते सिद्धिम् अहम् पश्यामि चिन्तयन्
transliteration: tat avaśyam tvayā kāryaḥ sa suhṛt suhṛdām vara
akṛtvā na hi te siddhim aham paśyāmi cintayan
english: O you best of my friends, it behove you, therefore to make friends with such a person. Or else I do not find any means for your success.

sanskrit: श्रूयताम् राम वक्ष्यामि सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः
भ्रात्रा निरस्तः क्रुद्धेन वालिना शक्र सूनुना
transliteration: śrūyatām rāma vakṣyāmi sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ
bhrātrā nirastaḥ kruddhena vālinā śakra sūnunā
english: Do you hear, O Rāma, what I relate. There live with four monkeys a heroic, self-controlled monkey by name Sugrīva, on that best of mountains Rşyamūka, situated on the banks of the lake Pampā, being driven by his enraged brother Vāli, the son of Indra.

sanskrit: ऋष्यमूके गिरि वरे पंपा पर्यन्त शोभिते
निवसति आत्मवान् वीरः चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः
transliteration: ṛṣyamūke giri vare paṃpā paryanta śobhite
nivasati ātmavān vīraḥ caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ
english: Do you hear, O Rāma, what I relate. There live with four monkeys a heroic, self-controlled monkey by name Sugrīva, on that best of mountains Rşyamūka, situated on the banks of the lake Pampā, being driven by his enraged brother Vāli, the son of Indra.

sanskrit: सत्य संधो विनीतः च धृतिमान् मतिमान् महान्
transliteration: satya saṃdho vinītaḥ ca dhṛtimān matimān mahān

sanskrit: दक्षः प्रगल्भो द्युतिमान् महा बल पराक्रमः
भ्राता विवासितो वीर राज्य हेतो महात्मना
transliteration: dakṣaḥ pragalbho dyutimān mahā bala parākramaḥ
bhrātā vivāsito vīra rājya heto mahātmanā

sanskrit: स ते सहायो मित्रम् च सीतायाः परिमार्गणे
भविष्यति हि ते राम मा च शोके मनः कृधाः
transliteration: sa te sahāyo mitram ca sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇe
bhaviṣyati hi te rāma mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛdhāḥ

sanskrit: भवितव्यम् हि यत् च अपि न तत् शक्यम् इह अन्यथा
कर्तुम् इक्ष्वाकु शार्दूल कालो हि दुर्रक्रमः
transliteration: bhavitavyam hi yat ca api na tat śakyam iha anyathā
kartum ikṣvāku śārdūla kālo hi durrakramaḥ
english: O you best of Ikşvākus, none can withstand destiny on this earth, truly unavoidable is it course.

sanskrit: गच्छ शीघ्रम् इतो वीर सुग्रीवम् तम् महाबलम्
वयस्यम् तम् कुरु क्षिप्रम् इतो गत्वा अद्य राघव
transliteration: gaccha śīghram ito vīra sugrīvam tam mahābalam
vayasyam tam kuru kṣipram ito gatvā adya rāghava
english: Do you proceed soon, O hero, to Sugriva of mighty prowess, and repairing hence even to-day do you contract friendship with him, taking vow in the presence of flaming fire* that you shall not envy each other. This refers to the the oriental custom of performing every sacred rite in the presence of fire as witness. The Hindus regard the fire with sacred reverence and for this in all their social and religious ceremonials fire plays, a very prominent and sacred part.

sanskrit: न च ते सो अवमन्तव्यः सुग्रीवो वानर अधिपः
transliteration: na ca te so avamantavyaḥ sugrīvo vānara adhipaḥ
english: Do you proceed soon, O hero, to Sugriva of mighty prowess, and repairing hence even to-day do you contract friendship with him, taking vow in the presence of flaming fire* that you shall not envy each other. This refers to the the oriental custom of performing every sacred rite in the presence of fire as witness. The Hindus regard the fire with sacred reverence and for this in all their social and religious ceremonials fire plays, a very prominent and sacred part.

sanskrit: कृतज्ञः काम रूपी च सहाय अर्थी च वीर्यवान्
शक्तौ हि अद्य युवाम् कर्तुम् कार्यम् तस्य चिकीर्षितम्
transliteration: kṛtajñaḥ kāma rūpī ca sahāya arthī ca vīryavān
śaktau hi adya yuvām kartum kāryam tasya cikīrṣitam
english: Despise not that kingly monkey Sugrīva, because he is grateful, capable of assuming shapes at will, seeking protection and powerful. You too are able to accomplish his wished-for object.

sanskrit: कृतार्थो वा अकृतार्थो वा तव कृत्यम् करिष्यति
स ऋक्षरजसः पुत्रः पंपाम् अटति शन्कितः
transliteration: kṛtārtho vā akṛtārtho vā tava kṛtyam kariṣyati
sa ṛkṣarajasaḥ putraḥ paṃpām aṭati śankitaḥ

sanskrit: भास्करस्य औरसः पुत्रो वालिना कृत किल्बिषः
संनिधाय आयुधम् क्षिप्रम् ऋष्यमूक आलयम् कपिम्
transliteration: bhāskarasya aurasaḥ putro vālinā kṛta kilbiṣaḥ
saṃnidhāya āyudham kṣipram ṛṣyamūka ālayam kapim

sanskrit: कुरु राघव सत्येन वयस्यम् वन चारिणम्
