बलात् अस्मिन् समागम्य मंत्रिभिः पुर वासिभिः
transliteration: yāce tvām śirasā rājan mayā baddho ayam aṃjaliḥ
balāt asmin samāgamya maṃtribhiḥ pura vāsibhiḥ

sanskrit: राजभावे नियुक्तो अहम् शून्य देश जिगीषया
स्निग्धम् एवम् ब्रुवाणम् माम् स विनिर्भर्त्स्य वानरः
transliteration: rājabhāve niyukto aham śūnya deśa jigīṣayā
snigdham evam bruvāṇam mām sa vinirbhartsya vānaraḥ

sanskrit: धिक् त्वाम् इति च माम् उक्त्वा बहु तत् तत् उवाच ह
प्रकृतीः च समानीय मंत्रिणः चैव सम्मतान्
transliteration: dhik tvām iti ca mām uktvā bahu tat tat uvāca ha
prakṛtīḥ ca samānīya maṃtriṇaḥ caiva sammatān

sanskrit: माम् आह सुहृदाम् मध्ये वाक्यम् परम गर्हितम्
विदितम् वो मया रात्रौ मायावी स महाअसुरः
transliteration: mām āha suhṛdām madhye vākyam parama garhitam
viditam vo mayā rātrau māyāvī sa mahāasuraḥ

sanskrit: माम् समाह्वयत क्रुद्धो युद्ध कांक्षी तदा पुरा
तस्य तद् भाषितम् श्रुत्वा निःसृतः अहम् नृपाअलयात्
transliteration: mām samāhvayata kruddho yuddha kāṃkṣī tadā purā
tasya tad bhāṣitam śrutvā niḥsṛtaḥ aham nṛpāalayāt

sanskrit: अनुयातः च माम् तूर्णम् अयम् भ्राता सुदारुणः
स तु दृष्ट्वा एव माम् रात्रौ स द्वितीयम् महाबलः
transliteration: anuyātaḥ ca mām tūrṇam ayam bhrātā sudāruṇaḥ
sa tu dṛṣṭvā eva mām rātrau sa dvitīyam mahābalaḥ

sanskrit: प्राद्रवत् भय संत्रस्तो वीक्ष्य आवाम् समुपागतौ
अभिद्रुतः तु वेगेन विवेश स महाबिलम्
transliteration: prādravat bhaya saṃtrasto vīkṣya āvām samupāgatau
abhidrutaḥ tu vegena viveśa sa mahābilam
english: Thereat seeing me with one to assist me, and finding that we had come upon him, that mighty Asura, fled, seized with fear. And fleeing on, he (at length) swiftly entered a huge hole.

sanskrit: तम् प्रविष्टम् विदित्वा तु सुघोरम् सुमहद् बिलम्
अयम् उक्तो अथ मे भ्राता मया तु क्रूर दर्शनः
transliteration: tam praviṣṭam viditvā tu sughoram sumahad bilam
ayam ukto atha me bhrātā mayā tu krūra darśanaḥ
english: Knowing that he had entered that dreadful and large cave, I spoke to my brother of a crooked presence.

sanskrit: अहत्वा न अस्ति मे शक्तिः प्रति गन्तुम् इतः पुरीम्
बिल द्वारि प्रतीक्ष त्वम् यावत् एनम् निहन्मि अहम्
transliteration: ahatvā na asti me śaktiḥ prati gantum itaḥ purīm
bila dvāri pratīkṣa tvam yāvat enam nihanmi aham
english: Without slaying (this Asura) I cannot return to the palace. Do you wait at the mouth of the cave while I slay him.

sanskrit: स्थितोऽयम् इति मत्वा अहम् प्रविष्टः तु दुरासदम्
तम् मे मार्गयतः तत्र गतः संवत्सरः तदा
transliteration: sthito'yam iti matvā aham praviṣṭaḥ tu durāsadam
tam me mārgayataḥ tatra gataḥ saṃvatsaraḥ tadā
english: This one is stationed here-thinking thus, I entered that inaccessible cave. And as I searched (for the Asura), one entire year passed away.

sanskrit: स तु दृष्टो मया शत्रुः अनिर्वेदात् भयाअवहः
निहतः च मया सद्यः सः सर्वैः सह बन्धुभिः
transliteration: sa tu dṛṣṭo mayā śatruḥ anirvedāt bhayāavahaḥ
nihataḥ ca mayā sadyaḥ saḥ sarvaiḥ saha bandhubhiḥ
english: That wicked wight who had roused my alarm in consequence of his disappearance, was (at length) slain by me in one day, along with his friends.

sanskrit: तस्य आस्यात् तु प्रवृत्तेन रुधिरौघेण तद् बिलम्
पूर्णम् आसीत् दुराक्रामम् स्वनतः तस्य भूतले
transliteration: tasya āsyāt tu pravṛttena rudhiraugheṇa tad bilam
pūrṇam āsīt durākrāmam svanataḥ tasya bhūtale
english: Then as he emitted yells in the subterranean region, the cave was filled with his blood and it became difficult to come out of it.

sanskrit: सूदयित्वा तु तम् शत्रुम् विक्रान्तम् तम् अहम् सुखम्
निष्क्रामम् न एव पश्यामि बिलस्य पिहितम् मुखम्
transliteration: sūdayitvā tu tam śatrum vikrāntam tam aham sukham
niṣkrāmam na eva paśyāmi bilasya pihitam mukham
english: Having with ease slain my powerful foe, I could not find the outlet of the cavern, its mouth having been closed.

sanskrit: विक्रोशमानस्य तु मे सुग्रीव इति पुनः पुनः
यतः प्रतिवचो नास्ति ततः अहम् भृश दुःखितः
transliteration: vikrośamānasya tu me sugrīva iti punaḥ punaḥ
yataḥ prativaco nāsti tataḥ aham bhṛśa duḥkhitaḥ
english: Then as I again and again cried Sugrīva, Sugrīva, I became exceedingly sorry for not receiving any reply.

sanskrit: पाद प्रहारैः तु मया बहुभिः परिपातितम्
ततः अहम् तेन निष्क्रम्य पथा पुरम् उपागतः
transliteration: pāda prahāraiḥ tu mayā bahubhiḥ paripātitam
tataḥ aham tena niṣkramya pathā puram upāgataḥ
english: Thereat I threw down the stone after striking it many times with my legs. Then coming out by its mouth, I have come to this city.

sanskrit: तत्र अनेन अस्मि सम्रुद्धः राज्यम् मृगयत आत्मनः
transliteration: tatra anena asmi samruddhaḥ rājyam mṛgayata ātmanaḥ
english: Seeking my kingdom, the crafty Sugrīva had shut me up there forgetting fraternal love.'

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा तु माम् तत्र वस्त्रेण एकेन वानरः
transliteration: evam uktvā tu mām tatra vastreṇa ekena vānaraḥ
english: Saying this, that monkey, the shameless Vali, exiled me with a single cloth on.

sanskrit: तेन अहम् अपविद्धः च हृत दारः च राघव
तत् भयात् च महीम् सर्वान् क्रान्तवान् स वन अर्णवाम्
transliteration: tena aham apaviddhaḥ ca hṛta dāraḥ ca rāghava
tat bhayāt ca mahīm sarvān krāntavān sa vana arṇavām
english: O Rāghava, I have been discomfited by him, and been deprived of my wife. And from fear of him, I have wandered over the whole earth having forest and seas. And aggrieved in consequence of my having been deprived of my wife. I have (at length) entered this best of mountains, Rsyamuka, which for a certain reason* is incapable of being approached by Vali. *In consequence of Matanga's curse.

sanskrit: ऋश्यमूकम् गिरि वरम् भार्या हरण दुःखितः
transliteration: ṛśyamūkam giri varam bhāryā haraṇa duḥkhitaḥ
english: O Rāghava, I have been discomfited by him, and been deprived of my wife. And from fear of him, I have wandered over the whole earth having forest and seas. And aggrieved in consequence of my having been deprived of my wife. I have (at length) entered this best of mountains, Rsyamuka, which for a certain reason* is incapable of being approached by Vali. *In consequence of Matanga's curse.

sanskrit: एतत् ते सर्वम् आख्यातम् वैर अनुकथनम् महत्
अनागसा मया प्राप्तम् व्यसनम् पश्य राघव
transliteration: etat te sarvam ākhyātam vaira anukathanam mahat
anāgasā mayā prāptam vyasanam paśya rāghava
english: Thus have I mentioned to you the great cause of this hostility, O Rāghava, innocent as I am, I have come by this mighty misfortune.

sanskrit: वालिनः च भयात् तस्य सर्वलोक भयापह
कर्तुम् अर्हसि मे वीर प्रसादम् तस्य निग्रहात्
transliteration: vālinaḥ ca bhayāt tasya sarvaloka bhayāpaha
kartum arhasi me vīra prasādam tasya nigrahāt
english: O you that inspirest the fear of all creatures, by chastising Vāli it behoveth you to grant your grace to me, who am tormented with fear in connection with Vali, O hero.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः स तेजस्वी धर्मज्ञो धर्म संहितम्
वचनम् वक्तुम् आरेभे सुग्रीवम् प्रहसन् इव
transliteration: evam uktaḥ sa tejasvī dharmajño dharma saṃhitam
vacanam vaktum ārebhe sugrīvam prahasan iva
english: Thus accosted, that energetic one knowing righteousness, smiling, began to address Sugrīva in words fraught with morality.

sanskrit: अमोघाः सूर्य संकाशा निशिता मे शरा इमे
तस्मिन् वालिनि दुर्वृत्ते पतिष्यन्ति रुष अन्विताः
transliteration: amoghāḥ sūrya saṃkāśā niśitā me śarā ime
tasmin vālini durvṛtte patiṣyanti ruṣa anvitāḥ
english: These sharpened shafts of mine, resembling the sun, and never missing, shall furiously fall upon the wicked Vāli.

sanskrit: यावत् तम् न हि पश्येयम् तव भार्य अपहारिणम्
तावत् स जीवेत् पापात्मा वाली चारित्र दूषकः
transliteration: yāvat tam na hi paśyeyam tava bhārya apahāriṇam
tāvat sa jīvet pāpātmā vālī cāritra dūṣakaḥ
english: So long as you did not see that stealer of your wife, so long only shall the impious Väli of vile character, live.

sanskrit: आत्म अनुमानात् पश्यामि मग्नः त्वाम् शोक सागरे
त्वाम् अहम् तारयिष्यामि बाढम् प्राप्स्यसि पुष्कलम्
transliteration: ātma anumānāt paśyāmi magnaḥ tvām śoka sāgare
tvām aham tārayiṣyāmi bāḍham prāpsyasi puṣkalam
english: By what I myself feel, I see that you had sunk in a sea of sorrow. But I will deliver you; and you shall attain both your wife as well as this kingdom.

sanskrit: तस्य तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा हर्ष पौरुष वर्धनम्
सुग्रीवः परम प्रीतः सु महत् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tasya tat vacanam śrutvā harṣa pauruṣa vardhanam
sugrīvaḥ parama prītaḥ su mahat vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing that speech of his capable of enhancing joy and manliness, Sugrīva overjoyed, spoke those words informed with high sense.
Hearing Rāma's words capable of enhancing joy and manliness, Sugrīva highly honoured the former and extolled him, saying.

sanskrit: त्वं दहेः कुपितो लोकान्युगान्त इव भास्करः
transliteration: tvaṃ daheḥ kupito lokānyugānta iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Enraged, you, with your sharp and flaming shafts, capable of piercing into the vitals, canst burn up the worlds, like the sun at the universal dissolution.

sanskrit: वालिनः पौरुषं यत्तद्यच्च वीर्यं धृतिश्च या
transliteration: vālinaḥ pauruṣaṃ yattadyacca vīryaṃ dhṛtiśca yā
english: Heedfully hearing from me of Vali's strength, prowess and fortitude, do you afterwards, ascertain what is fit.
Before the sun rises, Vāli can easily range the ocean from west to east and from south to north.
Ascending the tops of mountains, Vāli possessed of prowess throws up their summits, and then again swiftly holds them.
And displaying his strength, Vāli vehemently crushes in the woods various stout trees.
There was one assuming the shape of buffalo named Dundubhi, resembling in splendour the summit of Kailasa. That one possessed of prowess had the strength of an hundred elephants.
That wicked one of a gigantic body inflated by his prowess and blinded by the boon he had received once went to that lord of streams—the Sea.
Passing beyond the Sea, with waves upon him, and containing heaps of gemsji e said to the mighty deep-Grant me battle.
Thereat the righteous-souled and mighty Ocean arose and, O king, said these words to that Asura, who had been urged by Death.

sanskrit: समर्थो नास्मि ते दातुं युद्धं युद्धविशारद
transliteration: samartho nāsmi te dātuṃ yuddhaṃ yuddhaviśārada
english: O you that are skilled in fight, I am not competent to offer you fight; but lister to me who will tell you who shall offer the fight.

There is a monarch of mountains in a mighty forest,—the great refuge of asceticism, the worker of the weal (of all), an Asura, celebrated by the name of Himavān containing great cascades and furnished with many fountains and caves. He can compass your incomparable pleasure.

There is a monarch of mountains in a mighty forest,—the great refuge of asceticism, the worker of the weal (of all), an Asura, celebrated by the name of Himavān containing great cascades and furnished with many fountains and caves. He can compass your incomparable pleasure.

Concluding that the ocean was afraid, that foremost of Asuras, presented himself in the wood of Himavān, like a shaft shot from a bow. Thereupon Dundhubhi began to throw down many white crags resembling the foremost of elephants; and sent up shouts.

Concluding that the ocean was afraid, that foremost of Asuras, presented himself in the wood of Himavān, like a shaft shot from a bow. Thereupon Dundhubhi began to throw down many white crags resembling the foremost of elephants; and sent up shouts.
Then resembling white clouds, mild and possessed of a pleasing shape, Himavan, stationed on the summit, spoke,

sanskrit: क्लेष्टुमर्हसि मां न त्वं दुन्दुभे धर्मवत्सल
transliteration: kleṣṭumarhasi māṃ na tvaṃ dundubhe dharmavatsala
english: O Dundhubhi, O you that are attached to righteousness, it behoveth you not to distress me. I am the refuge of all those ascetics who are not expert in military arts.
Hearing those words of that intelligent lord of mountains Dundhubhi, with reddened eyes, said.
Afraid of me and hence void of energy if you are incapable of fighting with me, do you name him who is ready to fight with me who am desirous of entering into conflict.
Hearing these words the virtuous-souled Himavān, skilled in speech, spoke to that great Asura, exercised with ire.
O greatly wise one, there lives in Kişkindhā, of incomparable beauty, the mighty and highly graceful monkey—the son of Sakra, by name Vali.
That mighty wise one, skilled in warfare, is capable of fighting with you on equal terms like to Namuci with Vasava.
Do you speedily repair to him if did you wish for a conflict. He is always expert in military exploits and is hard to repress.

sanskrit: जगाम तां पुरीं तस्य किष्किन्धां वालिनस्तदा
transliteration: jagāma tāṃ purīṃ tasya kiṣkindhāṃ vālinastadā
english: Hearing Himavān's Himavān's words, Dundhubhi, inflamed with ire, went to Kişkindhā—Vāli's capital.

Assuming the figure of a terrible buffalo, with sharpened horns like to a cloud big with water, ranging on the sky in the rainy season, and approaching the gate of Kişkindhā that highly powerful one set up a terrible roar, shaking the earth like to the sound of a kettle-drum.

Assuming the figure of a terrible buffalo, with sharpened horns like to a cloud big with water, ranging on the sky in the rainy season, and approaching the gate of Kişkindhā that highly powerful one set up a terrible roar, shaking the earth like to the sound of a kettle-drum.
Like to an elephant he felled, out of haughtiness, the trees around, and rent the earth with his hoofs scraping it with his horns.
Vāli was in the female-apartment at that time, and unable to bear the sound came out with his wives like to the Moon with stars.
Thereupon thạt lord of monkeys and other wild anànals, spoke openly to Dundhubhi, saying,
O Dundhubhi, obstructing this my city-gate, why did you set up a terrible roar? Did you know my mighty strength? Do you save your own life.
Hearing those words of that intelligent lord of monkeys, Dundhubhi, with reddened eyes spoke.

sanskrit: न त्वं स्त्रीसन्निधौ वीर वचनं वक्तुमर्हसि
मम युद्धं प्रयच्छाद्य ततो ज्ञास्यामि ते बलम्
transliteration: na tvaṃ strīsannidhau vīra vacanaṃ vaktumarhasi
mama yuddhaṃ prayacchādya tato jñāsyāmi te balam
english: O hero, it becomes you not to speak thus before your wives. Do you enter into conflict with me and your prowess shall be ascertained thereafter.
Or I shall suppress my wrath for this night and do you, O monkey, enjoy till the rise of the Sun.

sanskrit: दीयतां सम्प्रदानं च परिष्वज्य च वानरान्
transliteration: dīyatāṃ sampradānaṃ ca pariṣvajya ca vānarān
english: Embracing all the monkeys, inviting all your friends, do you, that are the lord of the monkey herds, honour them with gifts.

sanskrit: क्रीडस्व च सह स्त्रीभिरहं ते दर्पनाशनः
transliteration: krīḍasva ca saha strībhirahaṃ te darpanāśanaḥ
english: Do you survey Kişkindhã and make your children kings. And do you enjoy with your wives-it is me that shall crush down your pride.

sanskrit: यो हि मत्तं प्रमत्तं वा सुप्तं वा रहितं भृशम्
transliteration: yo hi mattaṃ pramattaṃ vā suptaṃ vā rahitaṃ bhṛśam
english: He, who destroyeth a person who is given up to drinking, reckless, emaciated and deprived of weapons, and one like you, sunk in the abyss of voluptuousness, committeth the sin consequent upon the destruction of an embryo,
Where to replied Vāli, laughing, to that wicked lord of Asuras, leaving aside all his wives, headed by Tārā.
If you are not afraid of fighting, do not consider me as one given up to drinking only. Do you regard this my attachment as a draught in this conflict, to be drunk by the heroes.
Saying this, Vāli, taking his golden garland, conferred on him by his father Mahendra, addressed himself for the conflict.
Holding him by the horns, Vāli, that lord of monkeys, setting up a terrible roar, hurled Dundhubhi resembling a mountain.

sanskrit: श्रोत्राभ्यामथ रक्तं तु तस्य सुस्राव पात्यतः
transliteration: śrotrābhyāmatha raktaṃ tu tasya susrāva pātyataḥ
english: Alha beliowing a thundering voice, Vali crushed (him) down. And blood began to trickle down from the pores of his ears.
Both of them desired to subdue each other and thus there arose a terrible conflict between Vali and Dundhubhi.
Thereupon fought Väli equalling Śakra in prowess, by fists knees, legs, stones and trees.
Thus there was a skirmish between the monkey chief and the Asura. And in this conflict Asura's strength was greatly reduced, while that of Sakra's son was highly enhanced.
And taking up with his arms that lifeless one, the mighty Vāli hurled him with great force at distance of a Yojana.
While thus thrown down by force, drops of blood, falling from his mouth, driven by the wind, fell upon the asylum of the great Saint Matanga.
O great one, beholding the drops of blood there, the great ascetic, angered, thought within himself-Who might be the author of this sprinkling of blood?
Who is that wicked-souled, vicious-minded, stupid person, who has all on a sudden sprinkled me with blood?
Saying this, that best of saints issued out (of the hermitage) and surveyed a lifeless buffalo lying on the earth, like to a huge mountain.

sanskrit: स तु विज्ञाय तपसा वानरेण कृतं हि तत्
transliteration: sa tu vijñāya tapasā vānareṇa kṛtaṃ hi tat
english: And apprehending by virtue of his asceticism, that this has been committed by a monkey, he imprecated a mighty curse on the perpetrator (of that iniquitous deed).
He shall not enter here who has spoiled the sanctity of my forest with showers of blood. And surely he shall be killed (on entering).
Forsooth shall that wicked one cease to exist if he strideth within a Yojana around my asylum, who has felled these trees by throwing the body of the Asura.

sanskrit: ये चापि सचिवाः स्तस्य संश्रिता मामकं वनम्
transliteration: ye cāpi sacivāḥ stasya saṃśritā māmakaṃ vanam
english: His counsellors or any one related to him, who shall resort to this my forest (shall meet with the self-same fate). They shall not live here; hearing this from me let them take their own ways. And even if they live here, forsooth, shall I curse them too.

sanskrit: न च तैरिह वस्तव्यं श्रुत्वा यान्तु यथासुखम्
यदि तेऽपी ह तिष्ठन्ति शपिष्ये तानपि ध्रुवम्
transliteration: na ca tairiha vastavyaṃ śrutvā yāntu yathāsukham
yadi te'pī ha tiṣṭhanti śapiṣye tānapi dhruvam
english: His counsellors or any one related to him, who shall resort to this my forest (shall meet with the self-same fate). They shall not live here; hearing this from me let them take their own ways. And even if they live here, forsooth, shall I curse them too.
This my forest is being protected by me every day like to my own son—and the monkeys are always used to destroy its leaves, trees and roots.

sanskrit: दिवसश्चास्य मर्यादा यं द्रष्टा श्वोऽस्मि वानरम्
transliteration: divasaścāsya maryādā yaṃ draṣṭā śvo'smi vānaram
english: Forgive them I to-day-but if I find any tomorrow, he shall be turned into stone for many thousand years.
Hearing those words of the saint, the monkey herd issued out (of the forest). And beholding them (coming out of the forest) Vāli spoke.
Why have you all-the dwellers of the Matanga forest approached me-Is it all well with you?

sanskrit: ततस्ते कारणं सर्वं तदा शापं च वालिनः
transliteration: tataste kāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ tadā śāpaṃ ca vālinaḥ
english: Thereupon they related to Vāli, wearing a golden garland, the cause of the Saint's curse by him and other monkeys.61
Hearing those words, Vāli approached that great ascetic and solicited him with folded hands.
Disregarding him, the ascetic entered into his asylum and Vāli was overwhelmed with the fear of curse.

O Lord of men, afraid of the curse that monkey chief purposed to repair to the mount Rş yamuka. Knowing for certain, O Rāma, that he shall not enter this forest, I have been living here with my ministers, devoid of fear and grief.

O Lord of men, afraid of the curse that monkey chief purposed to repair to the mount Rş yamuka. Knowing for certain, O Rāma, that he shall not enter this forest, I have been living here with my ministers, devoid of fear and grief.
Here is the collection of Dundhuvi's bones, killed on account of his own haughtiness, resembling a huge mountain.
These are the seven huge Sāla trees, clothed in branches, which Vāli could simultaneously divest of leaves by virtue of his prowess.

sanskrit: कथं तं वालिनं हन्तुं समरे शक्ष्यसे नृप
transliteration: kathaṃ taṃ vālinaṃ hantuṃ samare śakṣyase nṛpa
english: I have related to you, O Rāma, the incomparable prowess of his. Do you tell me now, O hero, how canst you destroy him in the conflict?
Unto Sugrīva speaking thus, Lakşmaņa smiling replied:-Performing what shall you confide in (Rāma's ability) to destroy Vāli?

sanskrit: वालिनं निहतं मन्ये दृष्ट्वा रामस्य विक्रमम्
transliteration: vālinaṃ nihataṃ manye dṛṣṭvā rāmasya vikramam

english: Having addressed Rāma thus, Sugrīva, having blood-red eyes, thought aside for a moment and again spoke to Kākutstha.
He is heroic and proud of his prowess-his heroism and strength are known all over the world. He is a mighty monkey and incapable of being repressed in a battle.
His actions are such as are above the power of the celestials. Revolving them within myself and terrified I have repaired to this mount Rșyamuka.
And thinking of that lord of monkeys, unconquerable and irrepressible I dare not leave this Rsymuka.
And exercised with fear and anxiety, therefore, I have been wandering in this mighty forest along with my devoted counsellors, headed by Hanumān.

sanskrit: उपलब्धं च मे श्लाघ्यं सन्मित्रं मित्रवत्सल
transliteration: upalabdhaṃ ca me ślāghyaṃ sanmitraṃ mitravatsala
english: And having secured in you a worthy and sincere friend, O best of men, O you that are loving to your friends, I have taken your shelter like to Himăvat himself.

sanskrit: अप्रत्यक्षं तु मे वीर्यं समरे तव राघव
transliteration: apratyakṣaṃ tu me vīryaṃ samare tava rāghava
english: Cognizant am í of the prowess of my highly powerful and wicked brother, but I have never witnessed thine in a conflict, O Raghava.

sanskrit: न खल्वहं त्वां तुलये नावमन्ये न भीषये
transliteration: na khalvahaṃ tvāṃ tulaye nāvamanye na bhīṣaye
english: I do not compare you with Vāli, nor do I disregard or frighten you—forsooth have I greatly been alarmed by his terrible actions.

sanskrit: कामं राघव ते वाणी प्रमाणं धैर्यमाकृतिः
transliteration: kāmaṃ rāghava te vāṇī pramāṇaṃ dhairyamākṛtiḥ
english: O Rāghava, your words, patience and figure are the proofs of your heroism—truly do they bespeak of your valour like to fire hidden by ashes.
Hearing those words of the high-souled Sugrīva, Rāma, smiling, spoke to that monkey, saying.

sanskrit: यदि न प्रत्ययोऽस्मासु विक्रमे तव वानर
transliteration: yadi na pratyayo'smāsu vikrame tava vānara
english: O monkey, if you does not confide in my valour, soon shall I create your confidence about my war-like abilities.

Having thus addressed Sugrīva and consoling him, the highly powerful Raghava, of mighty arms-Laksmana's elder brother, lifting up easily with his thumb the dried frame of that Asura-Dundhubhi-hurled it at a distance of ten Yojanas.

Having thus addressed Sugrīva and consoling him, the highly powerful Raghava, of mighty arms-Laksmana's elder brother, lifting up easily with his thumb the dried frame of that Asura-Dundhubhi-hurled it at a distance of ten Yojanas.

sanskrit: क्षिप्तं दृष्ट्वा ततः कायं सुग्रीवः पुनरब्रवीत्
transliteration: kṣiptaṃ dṛṣṭvā tataḥ kāyaṃ sugrīvaḥ punarabravīt
english: Beholding that Asura's body thrown thus, Sugrīva, again addressed to the heroic Rāma, before Lakşmaņa and the monkey herd, the following pregnant words.

sanskrit: आर्द्रस्समांसः प्रत्यग्रः क्षिप्तः कायः पुरा सखे
transliteration: ārdrassamāṃsaḥ pratyagraḥ kṣiptaḥ kāyaḥ purā sakhe
english: Friend, formerly this body was wet and corpulent, and it was thrown with great difficulty by my brother Vāli, mad with voluptuousness.

sanskrit: परिश्रान्तेन मत्तेन भ्रात्रा मे वालिना तदा
transliteration: pariśrāntena mattena bhrātrā me vālinā tadā
english: And O Rāghava, it is now divested of flesh and hence light like to grass and consequently it has been hurled by you with ease, O descendant of Raghu.

sanskrit: नात्र शक्यं बलं ज्ञातुं तव वा तस्य वाऽधिकम्
transliteration: nātra śakyaṃ balaṃ jñātuṃ tava vā tasya vā'dhikam
english: And unable am I to ascertain who is the mightier? There is a good deal of difference, O Rāghava, between a body, wet and dried.

sanskrit: स एव संशयस्तात तव तस्य च यद्बले
transliteration: sa eva saṃśayastāta tava tasya ca yadbale
english: There is still doubt, O worshipful one, which of you is the mightier? Truly shall your strength be manifested in the piercing of one of these Sala trees.
Having stringed your bow like to the trunk of an elephant and stretching it to your ears, do you shoot this mighty arrow.

sanskrit: इमं हि सालं सहित स्त्वया शरो
transliteration: imaṃ hi sālaṃ sahita stvayā śaro
english: Doubt there is none that this arrow flung by you shall bore this Sāla tree. There is no need of discussion any more; do you perform, O king, what do you think proper for me, contracted, as you had, friendship with me, with a solemn vow.
Like to the sun among the planets, like to the Himālaya among the mountains, like to the lion among the quadrupeds you are the foremost of men in prowess.

sanskrit: एतच् च वचनम् श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य सुभाषितम्
transliteration: etac ca vacanam śrutvā sugrīvasya subhāṣitam
english: Hearing those pleasant words of Sugrīva, the highly effulgent Rāma, to create his confidence, took up his bow.

sanskrit: स गृहीत्वा धनुर् घोरम् शरम् एकम् च मानदः
सालम् उद्दिश्य चिक्षेप पूरयन् स रवैः दिशः
transliteration: sa gṛhītvā dhanur ghoram śaram ekam ca mānadaḥ
sālam uddiśya cikṣepa pūrayan sa ravaiḥ diśaḥ
english: That one, conferring honours upon others, holding his terrible bow and a shaft, darted it towards the Sāla, filling all the quarters with a sound,

sanskrit: स विसृष्टो बलवता बाणः स्वर्ण परिष्कृतः
भित्त्वा सालान् गिरि प्रस्थम् सप्त भूमिम् विवेश ह
transliteration: sa visṛṣṭo balavatā bāṇaḥ svarṇa pariṣkṛtaḥ
bhittvā sālān giri prastham sapta bhūmim viveśa ha
english: The arrow, clear as the gold itself, hurled by that one of mighty strength, perforating the trees, entered into the mountainous expanse and the sevenfold regions of the earth.

sanskrit: सायकः तु मुहूर्तेन सालान् भित्त्वा महाजवः
निष्पत्य च पुनः तूर्णम् तम् एव प्रविवेश ह
transliteration: sāyakaḥ tu muhūrtena sālān bhittvā mahājavaḥ
niṣpatya ca punaḥ tūrṇam tam eva praviveśa ha
english: And that shaft, gifted with wonderful velocity, piercing all the trees entered again into the quiver.

sanskrit: तान् दृष्ट्वा सप्त निर्भिन्नान् सालान् वानरपुंगवः
रामस्य शर वेगेन विस्मयम् परमम् गतः
transliteration: tān dṛṣṭvā sapta nirbhinnān sālān vānarapuṃgavaḥ
rāmasya śara vegena vismayam paramam gataḥ
english: Having beheld those seven trees bored by Rāma's arrow, that monkey chief attained to an excess of surprise.

sanskrit: स मूर्ध्ना न्यपतत् भूमौ प्रलंबीकृत भूषणः
transliteration: sa mūrdhnā nyapatat bhūmau pralaṃbīkṛta bhūṣaṇaḥ
english: Thereupon Sugrīva, exceedingly glad, and delighted with his actions, bowing down his head on the earth and stretching his ornamented person on the ground, addressed with clasped hands, that heroic descendant of Raghu.

sanskrit: इदम् च उवाच धर्मज्ञम् कर्मणा तेन हर्षितः
रामम् सर्व अस्त्र विदुषाम् श्रेष्ठम् शूरम् अवस्थितम्
transliteration: idam ca uvāca dharmajñam karmaṇā tena harṣitaḥ
rāmam sarva astra viduṣām śreṣṭham śūram avasthitam
english: Rāma, the foremost of those conversant with religious lore, with the following pious words.

sanskrit: स इन्द्रान् अपि सुरान् सर्वाम् त्वम् बाणैः पुरुषर्षभ
समर्थः समरे हन्तुम् किम् पुनर् वालिनम् प्रभो
transliteration: sa indrān api surān sarvām tvam bāṇaiḥ puruṣarṣabha
samarthaḥ samare hantum kim punar vālinam prabho
english: O best of men, O lord, what of Vali, you are capable of destroying with your arrows, in the conflict, even the celestials headed by Indra.

sanskrit: येन सप्त महा साला गिरिर् भूमिः च दारिताः
बाणेन एकेन काकुत्स्थ स्थाता ते को रण अग्रतः
transliteration: yena sapta mahā sālā girir bhūmiḥ ca dāritāḥ
bāṇena ekena kākutstha sthātā te ko raṇa agrataḥ
english: O Kākutstha, who can stand before you in a battle, who has pierced the seven trees, and the mountain, and the earth with one arrow?

sanskrit: अद्य मे विगतः शोकः प्रीतिर् अद्य परा मम
transliteration: adya me vigataḥ śokaḥ prītir adya parā mama
english: Obtaining you as my friend like to Mahendra and Varuņa, my grief has been removed and I have attained to an excess of delight.

sanskrit: तम् अद्य एव प्रियार्थम् मे वैरिणम् भ्रातृ रूपिणम्
वालिनम् जहि काकुत्स्थ मया बद्धो अयम् अंजलिः
transliteration: tam adya eva priyārtham me vairiṇam bhrātṛ rūpiṇam
vālinam jahi kākutstha mayā baddho ayam aṃjaliḥ
english: Do you, O Kākutstha, even to-day destroy, for my welfare, my brother Vāli. This I do pray to you with folded hands.

sanskrit: ततो रामः परिष्वज्य सुग्रीवम् प्रिय दर्शनम्
transliteration: tato rāmaḥ pariṣvajya sugrīvam priya darśanam
english: Thereupon embracing Sugrīva, of a pleasant countenance and like to Lakşmaņa, the highly wise Rāma spoke to him, saying,

sanskrit: अस्माद् गच्छाम किष्किन्धाम् क्षिप्रम् गच्छ त्वम् अग्रतः
गत्वा च आह्वय सुग्रीव वालिनम् भ्रातृ गन्धिनम्
transliteration: asmād gacchāma kiṣkindhām kṣipram gaccha tvam agrataḥ
gatvā ca āhvaya sugrīva vālinam bhrātṛ gandhinam
english: Soon shall we repair to Kiskindha.-Do you go before, O Sugriva, and invite your false brother, Vali, to battle.

sanskrit: सर्वे ते त्वरितम् गत्वा किष्किन्धाम् वालिनः पुरीम्
वृक्षैः आत्मानम् आवृत्य हि अतिष्ठन् गहने वने
transliteration: sarve te tvaritam gatvā kiṣkindhām vālinaḥ purīm
vṛkṣaiḥ ātmānam āvṛtya hi atiṣṭhan gahane vane
english: Thereupon proceeding quickly to Kişkindhā, Väli's capital—they all stood waiting in that dense forest, hiding themselves under the trees.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवो अपि व्यनदद् घोरम् वालिनो ह्वान कारणात्
गाढम् परिहितो वेगान् नादैः भिन्दन् इव अंबरम्
transliteration: sugrīvo api vyanadad ghoram vālino hvāna kāraṇāt
gāḍham parihito vegān nādaiḥ bhindan iva aṃbaram
english: With a view to call Vāli, Sugrīva, tying fast his cloth (around the waist) set up a terrible roar, as if rending the sky (therewith).

sanskrit: तम् श्रुत्वा निनदम् भ्रातुः क्रुद्धो वाली महाबलः
निष्पपात सुसंरब्धो भास्करो अस्त तटात् इव
transliteration: tam śrutvā ninadam bhrātuḥ kruddho vālī mahābalaḥ
niṣpapāta susaṃrabdho bhāskaro asta taṭāt iva
english: Hearing the terrible uproar of his brother, the mighty Vāli, highly angered, issued out of his city, like to the Sun from the western shores (where he sets).

sanskrit: ततः सुतुमुलम् युद्धम् वालि सुग्रीवयोः अभूत्
गगने ग्रहयोः घोरम् बुध अंगारकयोः इव
transliteration: tataḥ sutumulam yuddham vāli sugrīvayoḥ abhūt
gagane grahayoḥ ghoram budha aṃgārakayoḥ iva
english: Thereupon there arose a mighty conflict between Vāli and Sugrīva like to the planets Mercury and Mars fighting with each other on the sky.

sanskrit: तलैः अशनि कल्पैः च वज्र कल्पैः च मुष्टिभिः
जघ्नतुः समरे अन्योन्यम् भ्रातरौ क्रोध मूर्च्छितौ
transliteration: talaiḥ aśani kalpaiḥ ca vajra kalpaiḥ ca muṣṭibhiḥ
jaghnatuḥ samare anyonyam bhrātarau krodha mūrcchitau
english: The two brothers, exercised with ire, struck each other with palms like to Asani and with fists resembling adamant.

sanskrit: ततो रामो धनुष् पाणिः तौ उभौ समुदैक्षत
अन्योन्य सदृशौ वीरौ उभौ देवौ इव अश्विनौ
transliteration: tato rāmo dhanuṣ pāṇiḥ tau ubhau samudaikṣata
anyonya sadṛśau vīrau ubhau devau iva aśvinau
english: Thereupon Rāma, with bow in hand, beheld those two heroes resembling each other, like to two Aświns.

sanskrit: यत् न अवगच्छत् सुग्रीवम् वालिनम् वा अपि राघवः
ततो न कृतवान् बुद्धिम् मोक्तुम् अन्तकरम् शरम्
transliteration: yat na avagacchat sugrīvam vālinam vā api rāghavaḥ
tato na kṛtavān buddhim moktum antakaram śaram
english: And Rāghava did not discharge that mortal shaft until he could perfectly ascertain who was Vāli and who was Sugriva.

sanskrit: एतस्मिन् अन्तरे भग्नः सुग्रीवः तेन वालिना
transliteration: etasmin antare bhagnaḥ sugrīvaḥ tena vālinā
english: In the mean time, being defeated by Vāli, Sugrīva fled away and not beholding Rāghava, proceeded towards Rșyamuka.

sanskrit: क्लान्तो रुधिर सिक्त अंगो प्रहारैः जर्जरी कृतः
transliteration: klānto rudhira sikta aṃgo prahāraiḥ jarjarī kṛtaḥ
english: And wearied, worn out with blows, and having his person bathed in blood, he, followed by Vāli, angered, entered that mighty forest.

sanskrit: तम् प्रविष्टम् वनम् दृष्ट्वा वाली शाप भयात् ततः
मुक्तो हि असि त्वम् इति उक्त्वा स निवृत्तो महाबलः
transliteration: tam praviṣṭam vanam dṛṣṭvā vālī śāpa bhayāt tataḥ
mukto hi asi tvam iti uktvā sa nivṛtto mahābalaḥ
english: Beholding him enter that forest, the highly powerful Vâli could not pursue him there for fear of the curse but said:-You are released today

sanskrit: राघवो अपि सह भ्रात्रा सह चैव हनूमता
तदेव वनम् आगच्छत् सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः
transliteration: rāghavo api saha bhrātrā saha caiva hanūmatā
tadeva vanam āgacchat sugrīvo yatra vānaraḥ
english: And Rāghava too, with his brother and Hanumān, entered that forest, where the monkey chief Sugrīva was.

sanskrit: तम् समीक्ष्य आगतम् रामम् सुग्रीवः सह लक्ष्मणम्
ह्रीमान् दीनम् उवाच इदम् वसुधाम् अवलोकयन्
transliteration: tam samīkṣya āgatam rāmam sugrīvaḥ saha lakṣmaṇam
hrīmān dīnam uvāca idam vasudhām avalokayan
english: Beholding Rāma approach with Lakşmaņa, Sugrīva, stricken with shame and casting his looks on the earth, addressed him poorly, with the following words.

sanskrit: आह्वयस्व इति माम् उक्त्वा दर्शयित्वा च विक्रमम्
वैरिणा घातयित्वा च किम् इदानीम् त्वया कृतम्
transliteration: āhvayasva iti mām uktvā darśayitvā ca vikramam
vairiṇā ghātayitvā ca kim idānīm tvayā kṛtam
english: Accosting me with 'do you call (Vāli),' displaying your valour and making me struck by the enemy, what improper, conduct have you shown by me? You should have spoken me then truly, O Rāghava,-I shall not destroy Vali and I would not have gone there.

sanskrit: ताम् एव वेलाम् वक्तव्यम् त्वया राघव तत्त्वतः
वालिनम् न निहन्मि इति ततो न अहम् इतो व्रजे
transliteration: tām eva velām vaktavyam tvayā rāghava tattvataḥ
vālinam na nihanmi iti tato na aham ito vraje
english: Accosting me with 'do you call (Vāli),' displaying your valour and making me struck by the enemy, what improper, conduct have you shown by me? You should have spoken me then truly, O Rāghava,-I shall not destroy Vali and I would not have gone there.

sanskrit: तस्य च एवम् ब्रुवाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
करुणम् दीनया वाचा राघवः पुनर् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tasya ca evam bruvāṇasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
karuṇam dīnayā vācā rāghavaḥ punar abravīt
english: The high-souled Sugrīva speaking thus poorly, Rāghava again spoke to him, saying:

sanskrit: सुग्रीव श्रूयताम् तात क्रोधः च व्यपनीयताम्
कारणम् येन बाणो अयम् स मया न विसर्जितः
transliteration: sugrīva śrūyatām tāta krodhaḥ ca vyapanīyatām
kāraṇam yena bāṇo ayam sa mayā na visarjitaḥ
english: Do you hear, O Sugriva, O worshipful one, why I did not discharge my arrow then.

sanskrit: त्वम् च सुग्रीव वाली च सदृशौ स्थः परस्परम्
transliteration: tvam ca sugrīva vālī ca sadṛśau sthaḥ parasparam
english: By ornaments, dress, stature and movements yourself and Vali are just the same, O Sugriva.

sanskrit: स्वरेण वर्चसा च एव प्रेक्षितेन च वानर
विक्रमेण च वाक्यैः च व्यक्तिम् वाम् न उपलक्षये
transliteration: svareṇa varcasā ca eva prekṣitena ca vānara
vikrameṇa ca vākyaiḥ ca vyaktim vām na upalakṣaye
english: By voice, by words, by looks or by valour, O monkey, I could not make out any distinction.

sanskrit: ततो अहम् रूप सादृश्यात् मोहितो वानरोत्तम
न उत्सृजामि महावेगम् शरम् शत्रु निबर्हणम्
transliteration: tato aham rūpa sādṛśyāt mohito vānarottama
na utsṛjāmi mahāvegam śaram śatru nibarhaṇam
english: O best of monkeys, being thus surprised by the similarity of your countenances I could not discharge that foe-destroying and quick-coursing shaft.

sanskrit: जीवित अन्तकरम् घोरम् सादृश्यात् तु विशंकितः
मूलघातो न नौ स्याद्धि द्वयोः इति कृतो मया
transliteration: jīvita antakaram ghoram sādṛśyāt tu viśaṃkitaḥ
mūlaghāto na nau syāddhi dvayoḥ iti kṛto mayā
english: I was so afraid of your resemblance with Vāli that I thought that lest the mortal shaft might destroy you.

sanskrit: त्वयि वीर विपन्ने हि अज्ञान् लाघवान् मया
मौढ्यम् च मम बाल्यम् च ख्यापितम् स्यात् कपीस्वर
transliteration: tvayi vīra vipanne hi ajñān lāghavān mayā
mauḍhyam ca mama bālyam ca khyāpitam syāt kapīsvara
english: O hero, O lord of monkeys, if any disaster befalleth you, who are already overwhelmed with miseries, through my ignorance childishness, they shall be known all over the world.

sanskrit: दत्त अभय वधो नाम पातकम् महत् अद्भुतम्
अहम् च लक्ष्मणः च एव सीत च वरवर्णिनी
transliteration: datta abhaya vadho nāma pātakam mahat adbhutam
aham ca lakṣmaṇaḥ ca eva sīta ca varavarṇinī

sanskrit: त्वत् अधीना वयम् सर्वे वने अस्मिन् शरणम् भवान्
तस्मात् युध्यस्व भूयस्त्वम् मा शंकी च वानर
transliteration: tvat adhīnā vayam sarve vane asmin śaraṇam bhavān
tasmāt yudhyasva bhūyastvam mā śaṃkī ca vānara
english: Mighty is the sin that ariseth from the destruction of one who has been offered shelter. Myself, Laksmana, and that exquisitely fine damsel-Sita-are all at your service-you or are our only refuge in this forest. Do you again enter into conflict, therefore, and do not fear, O monkey.

sanskrit: एतन् मुहूर्ते तु मया पश्य वालिनम् आहवे
transliteration: etan muhūrte tu mayā paśya vālinam āhave
english: And do you behold even, in this very moment, Vāli, moving restlessly on the breast of the earth, wounded by my shaft.

sanskrit: येन त्वाम् अभिजानीयाम् द्वन्द्व युद्धम् उपागतम्
transliteration: yena tvām abhijānīyām dvandva yuddham upāgatam
english: Do you make some mark on your person, O lord of monkeys, by which I shall be able to recognize you when engaged in a duel (with your brother).

sanskrit: गज पुष्पीम् इमाम् फुल्लाम् उत्पाट्य शुभ लक्षणाम्
कुरु लक्ष्मण कण्ठे अस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
transliteration: gaja puṣpīm imām phullām utpāṭya śubha lakṣaṇām
kuru lakṣmaṇa kaṇṭhe asya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
english: O Lakşmaņa, plucking this auspicious Gaja flower, do you put it round the neck of the highsouled Sugriva.

sanskrit: ततो गिरि तटे जाताम् उत्पाट्य कुसुमायुताम्
लक्ष्मणो गज पुष्पीम् ताम् तस्य कण्ठे व्यसर्जयत्
transliteration: tato giri taṭe jātām utpāṭya kusumāyutām
lakṣmaṇo gaja puṣpīm tām tasya kaṇṭhe vyasarjayat
english: Thereat that highly graceful one with the garland around his neck appeared like to a cloud.

sanskrit: स तथा शुशुभे श्रीमान् लतया कण्ठ सक्तया
मालया इव बलाकानाम् ससंध्य इव तोयदः
transliteration: sa tathā śuśubhe śrīmān latayā kaṇṭha saktayā
mālayā iva balākānām sasaṃdhya iva toyadaḥ
english: Thereat that highly graceful one with the garland around his neck appeared like to a cloud.

sanskrit: जगाम सह रामेण किष्किंधाम् पुनराप सः
transliteration: jagāma saha rāmeṇa kiṣkiṃdhām punarāpa saḥ
english: And appearing in a graceful person and attentive to Rāma's words he again entered Kiş kindhā with him.

sanskrit: ऋश्यमूकात् स धर्मात्मा किष्किन्धाम् लक्ष्मण अग्रजः
जगाम सह सुग्रीवो वालि विक्रम पालिताम्
transliteration: ṛśyamūkāt sa dharmātmā kiṣkindhām lakṣmaṇa agrajaḥ
jagāma saha sugrīvo vāli vikrama pālitām
english: Thereupon the high-souled Rāma, along with Sugrīva, proceeded from the mount Rșyamuka to Kiskindha, maintained by Vali's prowess, raising up his gold crested mighty bow and taking his battle arrows like to Aditya.

sanskrit: समुद्यम्य महत् चापम् रामः कांचन भूषितम्
शराम् च आदित्य संकाशान् गृहीत्वा रण साधकान्
transliteration: samudyamya mahat cāpam rāmaḥ kāṃcana bhūṣitam
śarām ca āditya saṃkāśān gṛhītvā raṇa sādhakān
english: Thereupon the high-souled Rāma, along with Sugrīva, proceeded from the mount Rșyamuka to Kiskindha, maintained by Vali's prowess, raising up his gold crested mighty bow and taking his battle arrows like to Aditya.

sanskrit: अग्रतः तु ययौ तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः
सुग्रीवः संहत ग्रीवो लक्ष्मणः च महाबलः
transliteration: agrataḥ tu yayau tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
sugrīvaḥ saṃhata grīvo lakṣmaṇaḥ ca mahābalaḥ
english: The mighty Sugrīva, bending low, proceeded before the high-souled Rama and Laksmana.

sanskrit: पृष्ठतो हनुमान् वीरो नलो नीलः च वीर्यवान्
तारः चैव महातेजा हरि यूथप यूथपाः
transliteration: pṛṣṭhato hanumān vīro nalo nīlaḥ ca vīryavān
tāraḥ caiva mahātejā hari yūthapa yūthapāḥ
english: They were followed by the heroic Hanumān, the mighty Nala and Neela, and the highly powerful Tārā, the leader of the monkey herd.

sanskrit: ते वीक्षमाणा वृक्षाम् च पुष्प भार अवलम्बिनः
प्रसन्न अंबुवहाः चैव सरितः सागरम् गमाः
transliteration: te vīkṣamāṇā vṛkṣām ca puṣpa bhāra avalambinaḥ
prasanna aṃbuvahāḥ caiva saritaḥ sāgaram gamāḥ
english: They beheld as they proceeded, trees, lowered down with the weight of flowers, rivers of clear water flowing to the ocean, mountain hollows, hills, caves, cavities, and principal peaks and charming rills.

sanskrit: कन्दराणि च शैलाम् च निर्दराणि गुहाः तथा
शिखराणि च मुख्यानि दरीः च प्रिय दर्शनाः
transliteration: kandarāṇi ca śailām ca nirdarāṇi guhāḥ tathā
śikharāṇi ca mukhyāni darīḥ ca priya darśanāḥ
english: They beheld as they proceeded, trees, lowered down with the weight of flowers, rivers of clear water flowing to the ocean, mountain hollows, hills, caves, cavities, and principal peaks and charming rills.

sanskrit: वैदूर्य विमलैः तोयैः पद्मैः च आकोश कुड्मलैः
शोभितान् सजलान् मार्गे तटाकान् च अवलोकयन्
transliteration: vaidūrya vimalaiḥ toyaiḥ padmaiḥ ca ākośa kuḍmalaiḥ
śobhitān sajalān mārge taṭākān ca avalokayan
english: They. beheld on their way, pools filled with water clear as Baidurya and beautified with lotuses-full blown and buds, and resounded with the cries of Kārandhabas, swans, geese, Banculas, water-fowls, Cakravākas, and various other birds.

sanskrit: यद्वा -कारण्डैः सारसैः हंसैः वंजुलैः जल कुक्कुटैः
चक्रवाकैः तथा च अन्यैः शकुनैः प्रतिनादितान्
transliteration: yadvā -kāraṇḍaiḥ sārasaiḥ haṃsaiḥ vaṃjulaiḥ jala kukkuṭaiḥ
cakravākaiḥ tathā ca anyaiḥ śakunaiḥ pratināditān

sanskrit: यद्वा -मृदु शष्प अंकुर आहारान् निर्भयान् वन गोचरान्
चरताम् सर्वतो अपश्यन् स्थलीषु हरिणान् स्थितान्
transliteration: yadvā -mṛdu śaṣpa aṃkura āhārān nirbhayān vana gocarān
caratām sarvato apaśyan sthalīṣu hariṇān sthitān
english: They surveyed all around in the forest-land, deer ranging fearlessly at large and grazing on tender grass.

sanskrit: तटाक वैरिणः च अपि शुक्ल दन्त विभूषितान्
घोरान् एकचरान् वन्यान् द्विरदान् कूल घातिनः
transliteration: taṭāka vairiṇaḥ ca api śukla danta vibhūṣitān
ghorān ekacarān vanyān dviradān kūla ghātinaḥ

sanskrit: मत्तन् गिरि तट उद्घुष्टान् पर्वतान् इव जंगमान्
वानरान् द्विरद प्रख्यान् मही रेणु समुक्षितान्
transliteration: mattan giri taṭa udghuṣṭān parvatān iva jaṃgamān
vānarān dvirada prakhyān mahī reṇu samukṣitān

sanskrit: वने वन चराम् च अन्यान् खेचराम् च विहंगमान्
पश्यन्तः त्वरिता जग्मुः सुग्रीव वश वर्तिनः
transliteration: vane vana carām ca anyān khecarām ca vihaṃgamān
paśyantaḥ tvaritā jagmuḥ sugrīva vaśa vartinaḥ

sanskrit: तेषाम् तु गच्छताम् तत्र त्वरितम् रघुनंदनः
द्रुम षण्ड वनम् दृष्ट्वा रामः सुग्रीवम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: teṣām tu gacchatām tatra tvaritam raghunaṃdanaḥ
druma ṣaṇḍa vanam dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ sugrīvam abravīt
english: They proceeding quickly, Rama, the descendant of Raghu, beholding the forest filled with trees, spoke to Sugrīva, saying.

sanskrit: एष मेघ इव आकाशे वृक्ष षण्डः प्रकाशते
मेघ संघात विपुलः पर्यन्त कदली वृतः
transliteration: eṣa megha iva ākāśe vṛkṣa ṣaṇḍaḥ prakāśate
megha saṃghāta vipulaḥ paryanta kadalī vṛtaḥ
english: These trees skirted by plantain groves, dense as a collection of clouds, appear as clouds in the sky. Great is my curiosity, O friend, to learn what are these. 'And I wish to have my curiosity removed by you.

sanskrit: किम् एतत् ज्ञातुम् इच्छामि सखे कौतूहलम् मम
कौतूहल अपनयनम् कर्तुम् इच्छामि अहम् त्वया
transliteration: kim etat jñātum icchāmi sakhe kautūhalam mama
kautūhala apanayanam kartum icchāmi aham tvayā
english: These trees skirted by plantain groves, dense as a collection of clouds, appear as clouds in the sky. Great is my curiosity, O friend, to learn what are these. 'And I wish to have my curiosity removed by you.

sanskrit: तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः
गच्छन्न् एव आचचक्षे अथ सुग्रीवः तत् महद् वनम्
transliteration: tasya tad vacanam śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
gacchann eva ācacakṣe atha sugrīvaḥ tat mahad vanam
english: Hearing the words of the high-souled Rāghava, Sugrīva began to describe that great forest.

sanskrit: एतद् राघव विस्तीर्णम् आश्रमम् श्रम नाशनम्
उद्यान वन संपन्नम् स्वादु मूल फल उदकम्
transliteration: etad rāghava vistīrṇam āśramam śrama nāśanam
udyāna vana saṃpannam svādu mūla phala udakam

sanskrit: अत्र सप्तजना नाम मुनयः संशित व्रताः
सप्त एव आसन् अधः शीर्षा नियतम् जल शायिनः
transliteration: atra saptajanā nāma munayaḥ saṃśita vratāḥ
sapta eva āsan adhaḥ śīrṣā niyatam jala śāyinaḥ

sanskrit: सप्त रात्रे कृत आहारा वायुना अचल वासिनः
दिवम् वर्ष शतैः याताः सप्तभिः सकलेवराः
transliteration: sapta rātre kṛta āhārā vāyunā acala vāsinaḥ
divam varṣa śataiḥ yātāḥ saptabhiḥ sakalevarāḥ

sanskrit: तेषाम् एतत् प्रभावेण द्रुम प्राकार संवृतम्
आश्रमम् सुदुराधर्षम् अपि स इन्द्रैः सुर असुरैः
transliteration: teṣām etat prabhāveṇa druma prākāra saṃvṛtam
āśramam sudurādharṣam api sa indraiḥ sura asuraiḥ
english: By virtue of their asceticism, this asylum is walled by trees and incapable of being conquered even by Indra, the celestials and the Asuras.

sanskrit: पक्षिणो वर्जयन्ति एतत् तथा अन्ये वनचारिणः
विशन्ति मोहाद् ये अपि अत्र न निवर्तन्ते ते पुनः
transliteration: pakṣiṇo varjayanti etat tathā anye vanacāriṇaḥ
viśanti mohād ye api atra na nivartante te punaḥ
english: Birds or other wild animals do not enter this asylum; whoever entereth this by mistake never returneth.

sanskrit: विभूषण रवाअः च अत्र श्रूयंते सकलाक्षराः
तूर्य गीत स्वनाअः च अपि गन्धो दिव्यः च राघव
transliteration: vibhūṣaṇa ravāaḥ ca atra śrūyaṃte sakalākṣarāḥ
tūrya gīta svanāaḥ ca api gandho divyaḥ ca rāghava
english: There is audible, O Rāghava, the sound of the dressing of Apsarās, their sweet-winged accents and that of their music and drums; and herçin pervadeth the celestial fragrance.

sanskrit: त्रेताग्नयो अपि दीप्यन्ते धूमो हि एष प्रदृश्यते
वेष्टयन् इव वृक्ष अग्रान् कपोत अंग अरुणो घनः
transliteration: tretāgnayo api dīpyante dhūmo hi eṣa pradṛśyate
veṣṭayan iva vṛkṣa agrān kapota aṃga aruṇo ghanaḥ
english: Here burneth the fire Tretā; and the smoke and cloud sable like to the wings of a pigeon envelope the tops of the trees.

sanskrit: एते वृक्षाः प्रकाशन्ते धूम संसक्त मस्तकाः
मेघ जाल प्रतिच्छन्ना वैदूर्य गिरयो यथा
transliteration: ete vṛkṣāḥ prakāśante dhūma saṃsakta mastakāḥ
megha jāla praticchannā vaidūrya girayo yathā
english: And there appear the trees, having their tops saturated with smoke and cloaked with clouds, like to so many Baidurya hills.

sanskrit: कुरु प्रणामम् धर्मात्मन् तेषाम् उद्दिश्य राघवः
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रयतः संयत अंजलिः
transliteration: kuru praṇāmam dharmātman teṣām uddiśya rāghavaḥ
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā prayataḥ saṃyata aṃjaliḥ
english: Do you, O Rāghava, O virtuous-souled one, make obeisance to them along with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, with concentrated heart and folded palms.

sanskrit: प्रणमन्ति हि ये तेषाम् ऋषीणाम् भावित आत्मनाम्
न तेषाम् अशुभम् किंचित् शरीरे राम दृश्यते
transliteration: praṇamanti hi ye teṣām ṛṣīṇām bhāvita ātmanām
na teṣām aśubham kiṃcit śarīre rāma dṛśyate
english: There resteth no sin in their persons, O Rāma, who bow to those self-controlled Saints.

sanskrit: ततो रामः सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन कृतांजलिः
transliteration: tato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena kṛtāṃjaliḥ
english: Thereupon Rāma, along with his younger brother Lakşmaņa, made obeisance to those high-souled ones.

sanskrit: अभिवाद्य च धर्मात्मा रामो भ्राता च लक्ष्मणः
सुग्रीवो वानराअः चैव जग्मुः संहृष्ट मानसाः
transliteration: abhivādya ca dharmātmā rāmo bhrātā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
sugrīvo vānarāaḥ caiva jagmuḥ saṃhṛṣṭa mānasāḥ
english: Having paid homage (to the sacred memory of those great ones) the virtuous-souled Rāma his (younger) brother Laksmana, Sugriva and other monkeys, proceeded with delighted hearts.

sanskrit: ते गत्वा दूरम् अध्वानम् तस्मात् सप्त जन आश्रमात्
ददृशुः ताम् दुराधर्षाम् किष्किन्धाम् वालि पालिताम्
transliteration: te gatvā dūram adhvānam tasmāt sapta jana āśramāt
dadṛśuḥ tām durādharṣām kiṣkindhām vāli pālitām
english: And wending a distant way from that hermitage of the seven great ones, they beheld Kişkindhä, hard to conquer and occupied by Vali.

sanskrit: ततस्तु रामानुज राम वानराःप्रगृह्य शस्त्राणि उदित उग्र तेजसा
पुरीम् सुरेश आत्मज वीर्य पालिताम्वधाय शत्रोः पुनर् आगताः इह
transliteration: tatastu rāmānuja rāma vānarāḥpragṛhya śastrāṇi udita ugra tejasā
purīm sureśa ātmaja vīrya pālitāmvadhāya śatroḥ punar āgatāḥ iha
english: Thereupon, Rāma, his younger brother and the monkeys taking their weapons, entered, to encompass the destruction of their enemies, the city (of Kişkindhā) reared by the prowess of Indra's son.

sanskrit: सर्वे ते त्वरितम् गत्वा किष्किन्धाम् वालिनः पालिताम्
वृक्षैर् आत्मानम् आवृत्य व्यतिष्ठन् गहने वने
transliteration: sarve te tvaritam gatvā kiṣkindhām vālinaḥ pālitām
vṛkṣair ātmānam āvṛtya vyatiṣṭhan gahane vane
english: They all, repairing quickly to Kiskindha, Vāli's capital stood waiting in the dense forest, hiding themselves behind the trees.

sanskrit: विसार्य सर्वतो दृष्टिम् कानने कानन प्रियः
सुग्रीवो विपुल ग्रीवः क्रोधम् आहारयद् भृशम्
transliteration: visārya sarvato dṛṣṭim kānane kānana priyaḥ
sugrīvo vipula grīvaḥ krodham āhārayad bhṛśam
english: Casting his looks all around in the forest, Sugrīva, having a huge neck and fond of woods, became exceedingly enraged.

sanskrit: ततः तु निनदम् घोरम् कृत्वा युद्धाय च आह्वयत्
परिवारैः परिवृतो नादैर् भिन्दन् इव अंबरम्
transliteration: tataḥ tu ninadam ghoram kṛtvā yuddhāya ca āhvayat
parivāraiḥ parivṛto nādair bhindan iva aṃbaram
english: Setting up a terrible uproar and rending the sky with his cry (Sugrīva) encircled by his kinsmen, invited (Vāli) to battle.

sanskrit: गर्जन् इव महामेघो वायु वेग पुरस्सरः
अथ बालार्क सदृशो दृप्त सिम्ह गतिः ततः
transliteration: garjan iva mahāmegho vāyu vega purassaraḥ
atha bālārka sadṛśo dṛpta simha gatiḥ tataḥ
english: Thereupon roaring like to a huge cloud, preceded by a mighty wind, Sugrīva, gifted with leonine motion and resembling the newly risen Sun, finding Rāma expert in business, spoke to him, saying.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा रामम् क्रिया दक्षम् सुग्रीवो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
हरि वागुरया व्याप्तम् तप्त कांचन तोरणाम्
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā rāmam kriyā dakṣam sugrīvo vākyam abravīt
hari vāgurayā vyāptam tapta kāṃcana toraṇām
english: You have reached Kiskindhā, Vāli's capital, adorned with gold, filled with pennons and instruments and surrounded by monkeys. Do you make good your promise, O hero, you hadst made before to encompass the destruction of Vāli like to the season making the creepers filled with fruits.

sanskrit: प्राप्ताः स्म ध्वज यंत्र आढ्याम् किष्किन्धाम् वालिनः पुरीम्
प्रतिज्ञा या कृता वीर त्वया वालि वधे पुरा
transliteration: prāptāḥ sma dhvaja yaṃtra āḍhyām kiṣkindhām vālinaḥ purīm
pratijñā yā kṛtā vīra tvayā vāli vadhe purā
english: You have reached Kiskindhā, Vāli's capital, adorned with gold, filled with pennons and instruments and surrounded by monkeys. Do you make good your promise, O hero, you hadst made before to encompass the destruction of Vāli like to the season making the creepers filled with fruits.

sanskrit: सफलाम् कुरु ताम् क्षिप्रम् लताम् काल इव आगतः
एवम् उक्तः तु धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवेण स राघवः
transliteration: saphalām kuru tām kṣipram latām kāla iva āgataḥ
evam uktaḥ tu dharmātmā sugrīveṇa sa rāghavaḥ
english: Being thus accosted by Sugrīva, the virtuoussouled Rāghava, the slayer of foes, addressed him with the following words.

sanskrit: तम् एव उवाच वचनम् सुग्रीवम् शत्रु सूदनः
कृत अभिज्ञान चिह्नः त्वम् अनया गज साह्वया
transliteration: tam eva uvāca vacanam sugrīvam śatru sūdanaḥ
kṛta abhijñāna cihnaḥ tvam anayā gaja sāhvayā
english: Uprooting the Gaja creeper, Laksmana, has placed it around your neck as an emblem (to distinguish you). You does appear beautiful, O hero, with this creeper around your neck like to the sun on the sky engarlanded by the stars.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणेन समुत्पाट्य एषा कण्ठे कृता तव
सोभासे अपि अधिकम् वीर लतया कण्ठसक्तया
transliteration: lakṣmaṇena samutpāṭya eṣā kaṇṭhe kṛtā tava
sobhāse api adhikam vīra latayā kaṇṭhasaktayā

sanskrit: विपरीत इव आकाशे सूर्यो नक्षत्र मालया
अद्य वालि समुत्थम् ते भयम् वैरम् च वानर
transliteration: viparīta iva ākāśe sūryo nakṣatra mālayā
adya vāli samuttham te bhayam vairam ca vānara
english: I shall, O monkey, by the discharge of one shaft in the conflict, destroy your fear and enmity proceeding from Vāli.

sanskrit: एकेन अहम् प्रमोक्ष्यामि बाण मोक्षेण संयुगे
मम दर्शय सुग्रीव वैरिणम् भ्रातृ रूपिणम्
transliteration: ekena aham pramokṣyāmi bāṇa mokṣeṇa saṃyuge
mama darśaya sugrīva vairiṇam bhrātṛ rūpiṇam

sanskrit: वाली विनिहतो यावद् वने पांसुषु चेष्टते
यदि दृष्टि पथम् प्राप्तो जीवन् स विनिवर्तते
transliteration: vālī vinihato yāvad vane pāṃsuṣu ceṣṭate
yadi dṛṣṭi patham prāpto jīvan sa vinivartate

sanskrit: ततो दोषेण मा गच्छेत् सद्यो गर्हेच्च माम् भवान्
प्रत्यक्षम् सप्त ते साला मया बाणेन दारिताः
transliteration: tato doṣeṇa mā gacchet sadyo garhecca mām bhavān
pratyakṣam sapta te sālā mayā bāṇena dāritāḥ

sanskrit: ततो वेत्सि बलेन अद्य वालिनम् निहतम् मया
अनृतम् न उक्त पूर्वम् मे चिरम् कृच्छ्रे अपि तिष्ठता
transliteration: tato vetsi balena adya vālinam nihatam mayā
anṛtam na ukta pūrvam me ciram kṛcchre api tiṣṭhatā

sanskrit: धर्म लोभ परीतेन न च वक्ष्ये कथंचन
सफलाम् च करिष्यामि प्रतिज्ञाम् जहि संभ्रमम्
transliteration: dharma lobha parītena na ca vakṣye kathaṃcana
saphalām ca kariṣyāmi pratijñām jahi saṃbhramam

sanskrit: तद् आह्वान निमित्तम् च वालिनो हेममालिनः
transliteration: tad āhvāna nimittam ca vālino hemamālinaḥ

sanskrit: सुग्रीव कुरु तम् शब्दम् निष्पतेद् येन वानरः
जितकाशी जयश्लाघी त्वया च अधर्षितः पुरात्
transliteration: sugrīva kuru tam śabdam niṣpated yena vānaraḥ
jitakāśī jayaślāghī tvayā ca adharṣitaḥ purāt

sanskrit: रिपूणाम् धर्षितम् श्रुत्वा मर्षयन्ति न संयुगे
transliteration: ripūṇām dharṣitam śrutvā marṣayanti na saṃyuge
english: He has subdued his breath, is proud of victory and fond of warfare; you could not repress him before. Forsooth that Vāli shall come out, leaving the company (of his wives). Hearing the war cry of his enemy, he shall never put up with it, specially, as he boasteth of his prowess before his wives.

sanskrit: जानन्तः तु स्वकम् वीर्यम् स्त्री समक्षम् विशेषतः
स तु राम वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो हेमपिंगलः
transliteration: jānantaḥ tu svakam vīryam strī samakṣam viśeṣataḥ
sa tu rāma vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo hemapiṃgalaḥ

sanskrit: ननर्द क्रूर नादेन विनिर्भिन्दन् इव अम्बरम्
तत्र शब्देन वित्रस्ता गावो यान्ति हतप्रभाः
transliteration: nanarda krūra nādena vinirbhindan iva ambaram
tatra śabdena vitrastā gāvo yānti hataprabhāḥ

sanskrit: द्रवन्ति च मृगाः शीघ्रम् भग्ना;इव रणे हयाः
पतन्ति च खगा भूमौ क्षीण पुण्या इव ग्रहाः
transliteration: dravanti ca mṛgāḥ śīghram bhagnā;iva raṇe hayāḥ
patanti ca khagā bhūmau kṣīṇa puṇyā iva grahāḥ
english: And the deer fly away like to the horses defeated in a warfare. And the birds fall down on the earth, like to planets, losing their purity.

sanskrit: ततः स जीमूत कृत प्रणादोनादम् हि अमुंचत् त्वरया प्रतीतः
सूर्यात्मजः शौर्य विवृद्ध तेजाःसरित् पतिर्वा अनिल चंचल ऊर्मिः
transliteration: tataḥ sa jīmūta kṛta praṇādonādam hi amuṃcat tvarayā pratītaḥ
sūryātmajaḥ śaurya vivṛddha tejāḥsarit patirvā anila caṃcala ūrmiḥ
english: Thereupon confiding in Rāma's words, that son, of Suryya (Sun) having his energy enhanced by means of his prowess resembling the ocean agitated by the wind, began to roar like to cloud.

sanskrit: अथ तस्य निनादम् तम् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
शुश्राव अन्तःपुर गतो वाली भ्रातुर् अमर्षणः
transliteration: atha tasya ninādam tam sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ
śuśrāva antaḥpura gato vālī bhrātur amarṣaṇaḥ
english: While residing in the female apartment, Vāli heard the uproar of that high-souled Sugriva-his wrathful brother.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु तस्य निनदम् सर्वभूत प्रकंपनम्
मदः च एकपदे नष्टः क्रोधः च आपादितो महान्
transliteration: śrutvā tu tasya ninadam sarvabhūta prakaṃpanam
madaḥ ca ekapade naṣṭaḥ krodhaḥ ca āpādito mahān
english: And hearing that mighty roar, shaking the whole world of creation, his pride was in no time, crushed and he attained to an excess of ire.

sanskrit: ततो रोष परीत अंगो वाली स कनक प्रभः
उपरक्त इव आदित्यः सद्यो निष्प्रभताम् गतः
transliteration: tato roṣa parīta aṃgo vālī sa kanaka prabhaḥ
uparakta iva ādityaḥ sadyo niṣprabhatām gataḥ
english: Thereupon, Vāli, having a golden hue, greatly exercised with wrath, instantly lost the effulgence of his person like to the sun possessed by Rāhu.

sanskrit: वाली दंष्ट्रा करालः तु क्रोधाद् दीप्त अग्नि लोचनः
भाति उत्पतित पद्माभः समृणाल इव ह्रदः
transliteration: vālī daṃṣṭrā karālaḥ tu krodhād dīpta agni locanaḥ
bhāti utpatita padmābhaḥ samṛṇāla iva hradaḥ
english: And looking terrible by his teeth and having eyes resembling burning fire in consequence of ire he appeared like to a pond, having the lotuses thereof uprooted with their stalks and fibres.

sanskrit: शब्दम् दुर्मर्षणम् श्रुत्वा निष्पपात ततो हरिः
वेगेन च पद न्यासैर् दारयन् इव मेदिनीम्
transliteration: śabdam durmarṣaṇam śrutvā niṣpapāta tato hariḥ
vegena ca pada nyāsair dārayan iva medinīm
english: And hearing that unbearable sound, the 'monkey, issued out speedily, as if riving the earth with his foot marks.

sanskrit: तम् तु तारा परिष्वज्य स्नेहाद् दर्शित सौहृदा
उवाच त्रस्त संभ्रांता हित उदर्कम् इदम् वचः
transliteration: tam tu tārā pariṣvajya snehād darśita sauhṛdā
uvāca trasta saṃbhrāṃtā hita udarkam idam vacaḥ
english: Embracing him warmly and showing her affection, Tara, afraid and mortified, addressed him with the following words, presaging his future welfare.

sanskrit: साधु क्रोधम् इमम् वीर नदी वेगम् इव आगतम्
शयनाद् उत्थितः काल्यम् त्यज भुक्ताम् इव स्रजम्
transliteration: sādhu krodham imam vīra nadī vegam iva āgatam
śayanād utthitaḥ kālyam tyaja bhuktām iva srajam
english: Do you renounce, O hero, this your ire, coming like the course of a river, like to one, leaving aside the garland, which he used in the night, after rising from bed.

sanskrit: काल्यम् एतेन संग्रामम् करिष्यसि च वानर
वीर ते शत्रु बाहुल्यम् फल्गुता वा न विद्यते
transliteration: kālyam etena saṃgrāmam kariṣyasi ca vānara
vīra te śatru bāhulyam phalgutā vā na vidyate
english: O monkey chief, do you engage with him in conflict, tomorrow. O hero, your enemy is very insignificant and hence there will be no deterioration on your part. Your hastily issuing out does not please me; do you hear, why I do prevent you.

sanskrit: सहसा तव निष्क्रामो मम तावत् न रोचते
transliteration: sahasā tava niṣkrāmo mama tāvat na rocate
english: O monkey chief, do you engage with him in conflict, tomorrow. O hero, your enemy is very insignificant and hence there will be no deterioration on your part. Your hastily issuing out does not please me; do you hear, why I do prevent you.

sanskrit: पूर्वम् आपतितः क्रोधात् स त्वाम् आह्वयते युधि
निष्पत्य च निरस्तः ते हन्यमानो दिशो गतः
transliteration: pūrvam āpatitaḥ krodhāt sa tvām āhvayate yudhi
niṣpatya ca nirastaḥ te hanyamāno diśo gataḥ
english: Formerly this Sugrīva invited you angrily to battle and being defeated and wounded by you fled away.

sanskrit: इह एत्य पुनर् आह्वानम् शंकाम् जनयति इव मे
transliteration: iha etya punar āhvānam śaṃkām janayati iva me
english: That one, who had been defeated and harassed by you formerly, is now calling you. Indeed it has excited my fear.

sanskrit: दर्पः च व्यवसायः च यादृशः तस्य नर्दतः
निनादस्य च संरंभो न एतत् अल्पम् हि कारणम्
transliteration: darpaḥ ca vyavasāyaḥ ca yādṛśaḥ tasya nardataḥ
ninādasya ca saṃraṃbho na etat alpam hi kāraṇam
english: His pride, his energy, and his terrible uproar do indicate that there is nothing insignificant (at the bottom).

sanskrit: न असहायम् अहम् मन्ये सुग्रीवम् तम् इह आगतम्
अवष्टब्ध सहायः च यम् आश्रित्य एष गर्जति
transliteration: na asahāyam aham manye sugrīvam tam iha āgatam
avaṣṭabdha sahāyaḥ ca yam āśritya eṣa garjati
english: I do not think Sugrīva has come here without any to assist him. Forsooth he has taken shelter of some body, and securing which he has been setting up such a terrible uproar.

sanskrit: प्रकृत्या निपुणः चैव बुद्धिमान् चैव वानरः
न अपरीक्षित वीर्येण सुग्रीवः सख्यम् एष्यति
transliteration: prakṛtyā nipuṇaḥ caiva buddhimān caiva vānaraḥ
na aparīkṣita vīryeṇa sugrīvaḥ sakhyam eṣyati
english: That monkey is clever by nature and gifted with intellect. And Sugrīva shall not desire friendship with any one without having a test of his prowess.

sanskrit: पूर्वम् एव मया वीर श्रुतम् कथयतो वचः
अंगदस्य कुमारस्य वक्ष्यामि अद्य हितम् वचः
transliteration: pūrvam eva mayā vīra śrutam kathayato vacaḥ
aṃgadasya kumārasya vakṣyāmi adya hitam vacaḥ
english: Hearken, O hero, I shall relate to you today, the auspicious words, I heard ere this, from the prince Angada.

sanskrit: अंगदः तु कुमरो अयम् वनांतम् उपनिर्गतः
प्रवृत्तिः तेन कथिता चारैः असीत् निवेदिता
transliteration: aṃgadaḥ tu kumaro ayam vanāṃtam upanirgataḥ
pravṛttiḥ tena kathitā cāraiḥ asīt niveditā
english: He has related to me all about Sugrīva, what he heard from his emmissaries while journeying in the forest.

sanskrit: अयोध्य अधिपतेः पुत्रौ शूरौ समर दुर्जयौ
इक्ष्वाकूणाम् कुले जातौ प्रथितौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: ayodhya adhipateḥ putrau śūrau samara durjayau
ikṣvākūṇām kule jātau prathitau rāma lakṣmaṇau
english: The two heroic sons of the king of Ayodhyá— Rāma and Lakşmaņa, incapable of being defeated in a battle and born in the race of Iksawkus, have repaired to woods.

sanskrit: सुग्रीव प्रिय कामार्थम् प्राप्तौ तत्र दुरासदौ
स ते भ्रातुर् हि विख्यातः सहायो रण कर्मणि
transliteration: sugrīva priya kāmārtham prāptau tatra durāsadau
sa te bhrātur hi vikhyātaḥ sahāyo raṇa karmaṇi
english: To accomplish Sugrīva's welfare, those two heroes, hard to repress, have come here. He is the main stay of your brother in the battle. Rāma has sprung up like to the fire of dissolution and is the repressor of enemy's prowess. He is the refuge of the saints and the prime shelter of the afflicted.

sanskrit: रामः पर बलमर्दी युगान्त अग्निः इव उत्थितः
निवास वृक्षः साधूनाम् आपन्नानाम् परा गतिः
transliteration: rāmaḥ para balamardī yugānta agniḥ iva utthitaḥ
nivāsa vṛkṣaḥ sādhūnām āpannānām parā gatiḥ
english: To accomplish Sugrīva's welfare, those two heroes, hard to repress, have come here. He is the main stay of your brother in the battle. Rāma has sprung up like to the fire of dissolution and is the repressor of enemy's prowess. He is the refuge of the saints and the prime shelter of the afflicted.

sanskrit: आर्तानाम् संश्रयः चैव यशसः च एक भाजनम्
ज्ञान विज्ञान संपन्नो निदेशो निरतः पितुः
transliteration: ārtānām saṃśrayaḥ caiva yaśasaḥ ca eka bhājanam
jñāna vijñāna saṃpanno nideśo nirataḥ pituḥ
english: He is the protector of those grinded by their enemies and is the only possessor of fame. He is gifted with knowledge and intellect and ever abideth by his sire's commandments,

sanskrit: धातूनाम् इव शैलेन्द्रो गुणानाम् आकरो महान्
तत् क्षमो न विरोधः ते सह तेन महात्मना
transliteration: dhātūnām iva śailendro guṇānām ākaro mahān
tat kṣamo na virodhaḥ te saha tena mahātmanā
english: Like to Himālaya, the king of mountains, containing diverse metals, he is the mine of various accomplishments. It does not behove you therefore to enter into conflict with that high-souled Răma, incomparable in prowess and hard to conquer in battle.

sanskrit: शूर वक्ष्यामि ते किंचिन् न च इच्छामि अभ्यसूयितुम्
transliteration: śūra vakṣyāmi te kiṃcin na ca icchāmi abhyasūyitum

sanskrit: श्रूयताम् क्रियताम् चैव तव वक्ष्यामि यद् हितम्
transliteration: śrūyatām kriyatām caiva tava vakṣyāmi yad hitam
english: Hearken, O hero, I desire to speak something more-I do not wish to excite your wrath. Do you instantly confer upon Sugrīva, the dignity of heir apparent (to your throne). O hero, O king, do not quarrel with your younger brother.

sanskrit: विग्रहम् मा कृथा वीर भ्रात्रा राजन् यवीयसा
अहम् हि ते क्षमम् मन्ये तेन रामेण सौहृदम्
transliteration: vigraham mā kṛthā vīra bhrātrā rājan yavīyasā
aham hi te kṣamam manye tena rāmeṇa sauhṛdam

sanskrit: सुग्रीवेण च संप्रीतिम् वैरम् उत्सृज्य दूरतः
लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयान् एष वानरः
transliteration: sugrīveṇa ca saṃprītim vairam utsṛjya dūrataḥ
lālanīyo hi te bhrātā yavīyān eṣa vānaraḥ

sanskrit: तत्र वा सन्निहस्थो वा सर्वथा बन्धुः एव ते
नहि तेन समम् बन्धुम् भुवि पश्यामि किंचन
transliteration: tatra vā sannihastho vā sarvathā bandhuḥ eva te
nahi tena samam bandhum bhuvi paśyāmi kiṃcana
english: This your younger brother, even when remaining at a distance, should always be maintained by you. Whether by you, or at a distance, he is always your best friend—I do not find his equal on earth.

sanskrit: वैरम् एतत् सम् उत्स्रृज्य तव पार्श्वे स तिष्ठतु
transliteration: vairam etat sam utsrṛjya tava pārśve sa tiṣṭhatu
english: By conferring on him gifts and honours do you receive him back. And do you renounce your enmity and let him sit by you.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवो विपुल ग्रीवो महाबन्धुः मतः तव
भ्रातृ सौहृदम् आलंब्य न अन्या गति इह अस्ति ते
transliteration: sugrīvo vipula grīvo mahābandhuḥ mataḥ tava
bhrātṛ sauhṛdam ālaṃbya na anyā gati iha asti te
english: Methinks, that large-necked Sugrīva is your best friend-there is no other resource for you than to secure your brother's friendship.

sanskrit: यदि ते मत् प्रियम् कार्यम् यदि च अवैषि माम् हिताम्
याच्यमानः प्रियत्वेन साधु वाक्यम् कुरुष्व मे
transliteration: yadi te mat priyam kāryam yadi ca avaiṣi mām hitām
yācyamānaḥ priyatvena sādhu vākyam kuruṣva me
english: If you does wish to go by my desire, if you does regard me as your well-wisher, do you perform what I do request you for your welfare. Be pleased and hear my beneficial words.

sanskrit: प्रसीद पथ्यम् श्रुणु जल्पितम् हि मेन रोषम् एव अनुविधातुम् अर्हसि
क्षमो हि ते कोशल राज सूनुनान विग्रहः शक्र सम तेजसा
transliteration: prasīda pathyam śruṇu jalpitam hi mena roṣam eva anuvidhātum arhasi
kṣamo hi te kośala rāja sūnunāna vigrahaḥ śakra sama tejasā
english: It does not behove you to yield to the influence of ire your conflict with that son of the king of Kosala, gifted with the prowess of Sakra, will not conduce to your welfare.

sanskrit: तदा हि तारा हितम् एव वाक्यम्तम् वालिनम् पथ्यम् इदम् बभाषे
न रोचते तद् वचनम् हि तस्यकाल अभिपन्नस्य विनाश काले
transliteration: tadā hi tārā hitam eva vākyamtam vālinam pathyam idam babhāṣe
na rocate tad vacanam hi tasyakāla abhipannasya vināśa kāle
english: Thereupon Tārā spoke to Väli these suitable and well-meaning words—but they did not satisfy him, possessed by Kāla, as he was, on the eve of his destruction.

sanskrit: ताम् एवम् ब्रुवतीम् ताराम् ताराधिप निभ आननाम्
वाली निर्भर्त्सयामास वचनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tām evam bruvatīm tārām tārādhipa nibha ānanām
vālī nirbhartsayāmāsa vacanam ca idam abravīt
english: After Tārā, having a moon-like countenance, had spoken thus, Vāli, remonstrated with her and said.

sanskrit: गर्जतो अस्य च सुसंरब्धम् भ्रातुः शत्रोर् विशेषतः
transliteration: garjato asya ca susaṃrabdham bhrātuḥ śatror viśeṣataḥ
english: O you of exquisite loveliness, my brother, and specially my enemy, is roaring lowly and haughtily-and how shall I put up with it?
O timid damsel, heroes, who have never been defeated and have never fled away from the battle field, had rather meet with death than put up with this ignominy.

sanskrit: सोढुम् न च समर्थो अहम् युद्ध कामस्य संयुगे
सुग्रीवस्य च संरंभम् हीन ग्रीवस्य गर्जतम्
transliteration: soḍhum na ca samartho aham yuddha kāmasya saṃyuge
sugrīvasya ca saṃraṃbham hīna grīvasya garjatam
english: I am incapable of bearing this proud uproar of Sugrīva, having a defective neck and desirous of entering into conflict with me.

sanskrit: न च कार्यो विषादः ते राघवम् प्रति मत् कृते
धर्मज्ञः च कृतज्ञः च कथम् पापम् करिष्यति
transliteration: na ca kāryo viṣādaḥ te rāghavam prati mat kṛte
dharmajñaḥ ca kṛtajñaḥ ca katham pāpam kariṣyati
english: Fearing danger from Rāghava, you needst not entertain any anxiety on my account. Why shall that virtuous-souled and grateful Rāma perpetrate iniquity?

sanskrit: निवर्तस्व सह स्त्रीभिः कथम् भूयो अनुगच्छसि
सौहृदम् दर्शितम् तावत् मयि भक्तिः त्वया कृता
transliteration: nivartasva saha strībhiḥ katham bhūyo anugacchasi
sauhṛdam darśitam tāvat mayi bhaktiḥ tvayā kṛtā
english: Do you therefore return with my other wives. Why do you follow me again? You have already shown your friendship and respect for me. I shall repairing thither, only fight with Sugrīva. I shall crush down his pride and not destroy him.

sanskrit: प्रति योत्स्यामि अहम् गत्वा सुग्रीवम् जहि संभ्रमम्
दर्पम् च अस्य विनेष्यामि न च प्राणैर् वियोक्ष्यते
transliteration: prati yotsyāmi aham gatvā sugrīvam jahi saṃbhramam
darpam ca asya vineṣyāmi na ca prāṇair viyokṣyate
english: Do you therefore return with my other wives. Why do you follow me again? You have already shown your friendship and respect for me. I shall repairing thither, only fight with Sugrīva. I shall crush down his pride and not destroy him.

sanskrit: अहम् हि अजि स्थितस्य अस्य करिष्यामि यत् ईप्सितम्
वृक्षैः मुष्टि प्रहारैः च पीडितः प्रति यास्यति
transliteration: aham hi aji sthitasya asya kariṣyāmi yat īpsitam
vṛkṣaiḥ muṣṭi prahāraiḥ ca pīḍitaḥ prati yāsyati
english: I shall deal with him mercifully in the battle as you does wish and being struck with fists and trees he shall fly away.

sanskrit: न मे गर्वितम् आयस्तम् सहिष्यति दुरात्मवान्
कृतम् तारे सहायत्वम् दर्शितम् सौहृदम् मयि
transliteration: na me garvitam āyastam sahiṣyati durātmavān
kṛtam tāre sahāyatvam darśitam sauhṛdam mayi
english: Forsooth, that vicious-souled one shall not be able to withstand my pride and proficient skill in warfare. O Tārā, you had already displayed your attachment to me by giving me good counsels.

sanskrit: शापिता असि मम प्राणैः निवर्तस्व जनेन च
अलम् जित्वा निवर्तिष्ये तम् अहम् भ्रातरम् रणे
transliteration: śāpitā asi mama prāṇaiḥ nivartasva janena ca
alam jitvā nivartiṣye tam aham bhrātaram raṇe
english: By my life, do you go back with the other members of my household, I shall only return after bringing about the discomfiture of my brother in the battle.

sanskrit: तम् तु तारा परिष्वज्य वालिनम् प्रिय वादिनी
चकार रुदती मन्दम् दक्षिणा सा प्रदक्षिणम्
transliteration: tam tu tārā pariṣvajya vālinam priya vādinī
cakāra rudatī mandam dakṣiṇā sā pradakṣiṇam
english: Thereupon, Tārā, dextrous and of sweet accents, embracing Väli, went round him, with tears trickling from her eyes.

sanskrit: ततः स्वस्त्ययनम् कृत्वा मंत्रवित् विजय एषिणी
अंतःपुरम् सह स्त्रीभिः प्रविष्टा शोक मोहिता
transliteration: tataḥ svastyayanam kṛtvā maṃtravit vijaya eṣiṇī
aṃtaḥpuram saha strībhiḥ praviṣṭā śoka mohitā
english: Having performed Sastayana or the ceremony of benediction, that one gifted with a knowledge of Mantras, and desirous of Vāli's success, went, overwhelmed with grief, to the inner-apartment in the company of other females.

sanskrit: प्रविष्टायाम् तु तारायाम् सह स्त्रीभिः स्वम् आलयम्
नगर्या निर्ययौ क्रुद्धो महा सर्प इव श्वसन्
transliteration: praviṣṭāyām tu tārāyām saha strībhiḥ svam ālayam
nagaryā niryayau kruddho mahā sarpa iva śvasan
english: After Tārā had departed to her own quarters with her female companions, he issued out of the city sighing like an enraged serpent.

sanskrit: स निःश्वस्य महारोषो वाली परम वेगवान्
सर्वतः चारयन् दृष्टिम् शत्रु दर्शन कांक्षया
transliteration: sa niḥśvasya mahāroṣo vālī parama vegavān
sarvataḥ cārayan dṛṣṭim śatru darśana kāṃkṣayā
english: And the quick-paced Vali, exceedingly wroth, sighing, cast his looks around with a view to behold his enemy.

sanskrit: स ददर्श ततः श्रीमान् सुग्रीवम् हेम पिङ्गलम्
transliteration: sa dadarśa tataḥ śrīmān sugrīvam hema piṅgalam
english: And that highly effulgent one espied Sugrīva, having a golden yellow hue, tightly clothed, standing firm on the earth and shining like to burning gold.

sanskrit: तम् स दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुः सुग्रीवम् पर्यवस्थितम्
गाढम् परिदधे वासो वाली परम कोपिनः
transliteration: tam sa dṛṣṭvā mahābāhuḥ sugrīvam paryavasthitam
gāḍham paridadhe vāso vālī parama kopinaḥ
english: And beholding Sugrīva stationed thus, the greatly enraged Vāli, of mighty arms, put on his clothes tightly well.

sanskrit: स वाली गाढ संवीतो मुष्टिम् उद्यम्य वीर्यवान्
सुग्रीवम् एव अभिमुखो ययौ योद्धुम् कृत क्षणः
transliteration: sa vālī gāḍha saṃvīto muṣṭim udyamya vīryavān
sugrīvam eva abhimukho yayau yoddhum kṛta kṣaṇaḥ
english: Highly powerful and closely habited, he, clinching his fists, proceeded towards Sugriva, and waited for the action.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवो अपि समुद्दिश्य वालिनम् हेम मालिनम्
transliteration: sugrīvo api samuddiśya vālinam hema mālinam
english: Sugrīva too, clinching his fist and exceedingly wroth, proceeded towards Vāli, wearing a golden garland.

sanskrit: तम् वाली क्रोध ताम्राक्षः सुग्रीवम् रण कोविदम्
आपतंतम् महा वेगम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tam vālī krodha tāmrākṣaḥ sugrīvam raṇa kovidam
āpataṃtam mahā vegam idam vacanam abravīt
english: And beholding Sugrīva, adept in warfare having his eyes reddened with ire, advance quickly, Vāli spoke.

sanskrit: एष मुष्टिर् महान् बद्धो गाढः सुनियत अंगुलिः
मया वेग विमुक्तः ते प्राणान् आदाय यास्यति
transliteration: eṣa muṣṭir mahān baddho gāḍhaḥ suniyata aṃguliḥ
mayā vega vimuktaḥ te prāṇān ādāya yāsyati
english: Behold, I have clinched this terrible fist, arranging close my fingers; and one blow from me will take away your life.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः तु सुग्रीवः क्रुद्धो वालिनम् अब्रवीत्
तव च एष हरन् प्राणान् मुष्टिः पततु मूर्धनि
transliteration: evam uktaḥ tu sugrīvaḥ kruddho vālinam abravīt
tava ca eṣa haran prāṇān muṣṭiḥ patatu mūrdhani
english: Being accosted thus by Vāli, Sugrīva, exercised with wrath, spoke to him, saying,—This my fist shall strike you on your head taking away your life.

sanskrit: ताडितः तेन तम् क्रुद्धः समभिक्रम्य वेगतः
अभवत् शोणित उद्गारी सापीड इव पर्वतः
transliteration: tāḍitaḥ tena tam kruddhaḥ samabhikramya vegataḥ
abhavat śoṇita udgārī sāpīḍa iva parvataḥ
english: Thereupon being struck by Vāli, waxing worth and approaching him quickly he began to vomit out gore like to a mountain having springs.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवेण तु निःशंकम् सालम् उत्पाट्य तेजसा
गात्रेषु अभिहतो वाली वज्रेण इव महा गिरिः
transliteration: sugrīveṇa tu niḥśaṃkam sālam utpāṭya tejasā
gātreṣu abhihato vālī vajreṇa iva mahā giriḥ
english: And Vāli too was struck down by Sugrīva, fearlessly taking up a Sāla tree, like to a mountain clapped by a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: स तु वृक्षेण निर्भग्नः साल ताडन विह्वलः
गुरु भार भर आक्रान्ता नौः ससार्था इव सागरे
transliteration: sa tu vṛkṣeṇa nirbhagnaḥ sāla tāḍana vihvalaḥ
guru bhāra bhara ākrāntā nauḥ sasārthā iva sāgare
english: Being thus smitten by the tree and overwhelmed with the strike of Sāla he was troubled like to a heavily laden boat in the midst of an ocean.

sanskrit: तौ भीम बल विक्रान्तौ सुपर्ण सम वेगिनौ
प्रयुद्धौ घोर वपुषौ चन्द्र सूर्यौ इव अंबरे
transliteration: tau bhīma bala vikrāntau suparṇa sama veginau
prayuddhau ghora vapuṣau candra sūryau iva aṃbare
english: And these (two brothers) gifted with mighty strength and prowess and motion of Suparna, and having huge persons fought with each other like to the Sun and Moon on the sky.

sanskrit: परस्परम् अमित्र घ्नौ च्छिद्र अन्वेषण तत्परौ
ततो अवर्धत वाली तु बल वीर्य समन्वितः
transliteration: parasparam amitra ghnau cchidra anveṣaṇa tatparau
tato avardhata vālī tu bala vīrya samanvitaḥ
english: They were inimical to each other and intent on finding their mutual dark sides. And Vāli, gifted with strength and prowess, fared better in the conflict, and that highly powerful son of Sun-Sugrīva, was worsted.

sanskrit: वालिना भग्न दर्पः तु सुग्रीवो मन्द विक्रमः
transliteration: vālinā bhagna darpaḥ tu sugrīvo manda vikramaḥ

sanskrit: वृक्षैः स शाखैः शिखरैः वज्र कोटि निभैः नखैः
transliteration: vṛkṣaiḥ sa śākhaiḥ śikharaiḥ vajra koṭi nibhaiḥ nakhaiḥ

sanskrit: मुष्टिभिः जानुभिः पद्भिः बाहुभिः च पुनः पुनः
तयोः युद्द्धम् अभूत् घोरम् वृत्र वासवोः इव
transliteration: muṣṭibhiḥ jānubhiḥ padbhiḥ bāhubhiḥ ca punaḥ punaḥ
tayoḥ yudddham abhūt ghoram vṛtra vāsavoḥ iva
english: Thereupon there took place a mighty conflict between them like to Vitra and Vāsava by means of trees with branches, hills, nails, hard as thunderbolts, fists, knees, legs and arms.

sanskrit: तौ शोणितात्कौ युध्येताम् वानारौ वन् चारिणौ
मेघौ इव महा शब्दैः तर्जमानौ परस्परम्
transliteration: tau śoṇitātkau yudhyetām vānārau van cāriṇau
meghau iva mahā śabdaiḥ tarjamānau parasparam
english: And these two monkeys ranging in the forest, fought with each other, having their persons bathed in blood, and roaring like to clouds.

sanskrit: प्रेक्षमाणम् दिशः च एव राघवः स मुहुर् मुहुर्
transliteration: prekṣamāṇam diśaḥ ca eva rāghavaḥ sa muhur muhur
english: Rāghava again and again beheld the weak points of that monkey chief Sugrīva, losing his strength by and by.

sanskrit: ततो रामो महातेजा आर्तम् दृष्ट्वा हरीश्वरम्
स शरम् वीक्षते वीरो वालिनो वध कांक्षया
transliteration: tato rāmo mahātejā ārtam dṛṣṭvā harīśvaram
sa śaram vīkṣate vīro vālino vadha kāṃkṣayā
english: And beholding that chief of monkeys greatly distressed, the highly powerful and heroic Rāma cast his looks upon his shaft, having the destruction of Väli in view.

sanskrit: ततो धनुषि संधाय शरम् आशी विष उपमम्
पूरयामास तत् चापम् काल चक्रम् इव अन्तकः
transliteration: tato dhanuṣi saṃdhāya śaram āśī viṣa upamam
pūrayāmāsa tat cāpam kāla cakram iva antakaḥ
english: And fixing on his bow an arrow resembling a serpent, he stretched it like to Death drawing out his cycle of time.

sanskrit: प्रदुद्रुवुर् मृगाः च एव युगांत इव मोहिताः
transliteration: pradudruvur mṛgāḥ ca eva yugāṃta iva mohitāḥ
english: Being terrified by the sound of his stringing of the bow the birds and beasts, dismayed as on the eve of dissolution, fied away into different quarters.

sanskrit: मुक्तस्तु वज्र निर्घोषः प्रदीप्त अशनि संनिभः
राघवेण महा बाणो वालि वक्षसि पातितः
transliteration: muktastu vajra nirghoṣaḥ pradīpta aśani saṃnibhaḥ
rāghaveṇa mahā bāṇo vāli vakṣasi pātitaḥ
english: And a mighty shaft, like to thunderbolt and resembling flaming fire, being hurled by Rāma, alighted on the breast of Väli.

sanskrit: ततः तेन महातेजा वीर्य युक्तः कपीश्वरः
वेगेन अभिहतो वाली निपपात मही तले
transliteration: tataḥ tena mahātejā vīrya yuktaḥ kapīśvaraḥ
vegena abhihato vālī nipapāta mahī tale
english: Being wounded by that shaft that highly powerful chief of monkeys, gifted with prowess fell down on the earth.

sanskrit: इन्द्र ध्वज इव उद्धूत पौर्ण मास्याम् महीतले
अश्वयुक् समये मासि गत सत्त्वो विचेतनः
बाष्प संरुद्ध कण्ठस्तु वाली च आर्त स्वरः शनैः
transliteration: indra dhvaja iva uddhūta paurṇa māsyām mahītale
aśvayuk samaye māsi gata sattvo vicetanaḥ
bāṣpa saṃruddha kaṇṭhastu vālī ca ārta svaraḥ śanaiḥ
english: Like to ſakra's banner in the full-moon of Asvin, Vali, with his throat choked with vapour, losing all sense and sighing hard, fell dead down to the ground.

sanskrit: नरोत्तमः काल युगांतकोपमम् शरोत्तमम् कांचन रूप्यभूषितम्
ससर्ज दीप्तम् तम् अमित्र मर्दनम् स धूममग्निम् मुखतो यथा हरः
transliteration: narottamaḥ kāla yugāṃtakopamam śarottamam kāṃcana rūpyabhūṣitam
sasarja dīptam tam amitra mardanam sa dhūmamagnim mukhato yathā haraḥ
english: As the great God Hara emitted forth fire with smoke from his mouth, so that best of men like to Death hurled an excellent, flaming and foedestroying shaft, resembling gold and death itself.

sanskrit: अथ उक्षितः शोणित तोय विस्रवैःसुपुष्पित अशोक इव अचलोद्गतः
विचेतनो वासव सूनुर् आहवेप्रभ्रञ्शित इन्द्र ध्वजवत् क्षितिम् गतः
transliteration: atha ukṣitaḥ śoṇita toya visravaiḥsupuṣpita aśoka iva acalodgataḥ
vicetano vāsava sūnur āhaveprabhrañśita indra dhvajavat kṣitim gataḥ
english: Thereupon being bathed in blood that son of Vasava, fell senseless on the ground, in the conflict like to a blossoming Asoka growing on a hill and Sakra's banner struck down on the earth.

sanskrit: ततः शरेण अभिहतो रामेण रण कर्कशः
transliteration: tataḥ śareṇa abhihato rāmeṇa raṇa karkaśaḥ
english: Thereupon Vāli, adept in warfare, wounded by Rāma's shaft, fell down to the ground like to a felled tree.

sanskrit: स भूमौ न्यस्त सर्वांगः तप्त कांचन भूषणः
