english: (And thought I), 'Mahisa, unable to issue out, needs must meet his end.' And despairing of his (Vali's) life, I retraced my steps to Kiskindha.

sanskrit: राज्यम् च सुमहत् प्राप्य ताराम् च रुमया सह
मित्रैः च सहितः तत्र वसामि विगत ज्वरः
transliteration: rājyam ca sumahat prāpya tārām ca rumayā saha
mitraiḥ ca sahitaḥ tatra vasāmi vigata jvaraḥ
english: And obtaining the spacious kingdom along with Tãrã and Umā, I began to pass my days in peace in company with his counsellors.

sanskrit: आजगाम ततो वाली हत्वा तम् दानवर्षभः
ततो अहम् अददाम् राज्यम् गौरवात् भय यंत्रितः
transliteration: ājagāma tato vālī hatvā tam dānavarṣabhaḥ
tato aham adadām rājyam gauravāt bhaya yaṃtritaḥ

sanskrit: स माम् जिघांसुः दुष्टात्मा वाली प्रव्यथित इन्द्रियः
transliteration: sa mām jighāṃsuḥ duṣṭātmā vālī pravyathita indriyaḥ
english: Then came that foremost of monkeys, having slain him (Mahisa). Thereupon I, influenced by fear, in consideration of his dignity, made over to him his monarchy. But Vali, his senses exercised with sorrow, anxious to slay me, in company with his counsellors, pursued me, who heels.

sanskrit: ततो अहम् वालिना तेन सानुबन्धः प्रधावितः
नदीः च विविधाः पश्यन् वनानि नगराणि च
transliteration: tato aham vālinā tena sānubandhaḥ pradhāvitaḥ
nadīḥ ca vividhāḥ paśyan vanāni nagarāṇi ca
english: Hotly pursued and chased by Vāli, I surveyed various streams and woods and cities. And I surveyed the earth like the hoof-print of a cow, or the image reflected from a mirror, or a firebrand whirled (in the air).* *The commentator remarks that like the hoof-print of a cow expresses the case with which Sugrīva travelled the earth; like a fire brand whirled conveys his vehement speed; and like the image reflected on a mirror signifies the lucidity of his perception.

sanskrit: आदर्श तल संकाशा ततो वै पृथिवी मया
अलात चक्र प्रतिमा दृष्टा गोष्पदवत् तदा - कृता
transliteration: ādarśa tala saṃkāśā tato vai pṛthivī mayā
alāta cakra pratimā dṛṣṭā goṣpadavat tadā - kṛtā
english: Hotly pursued and chased by Vāli, I surveyed various streams and woods and cities. And I surveyed the earth like the hoof-print of a cow, or the image reflected from a mirror, or a firebrand whirled (in the air).* *The commentator remarks that like the hoof-print of a cow expresses the case with which Sugrīva travelled the earth; like a fire brand whirled conveys his vehement speed; and like the image reflected on a mirror signifies the lucidity of his perception.

sanskrit: पूर्वम् दिशाम् ततो गत्वा पश्यामि विविधान् द्रुमान्
पर्वतान् स दरीन् रम्यान् सरांसि विविधानि च
transliteration: pūrvam diśām tato gatvā paśyāmi vividhān drumān
parvatān sa darīn ramyān sarāṃsi vividhāni ca
english: Then repairing to the East, I see various trees, and mountains, and charming caves, and diverse tanks.

sanskrit: उदयम् तत्र पश्यामि पर्वतम् धातु मण्डितम्
क्षीरोदम् सागरम् चैव नित्यम् अप्सर आलयम्
transliteration: udayam tatra paśyāmi parvatam dhātu maṇḍitam
kṣīrodam sāgaram caiva nityam apsara ālayam
english: And there I behold the Ascending mountain decked with gold,—and that daily abode of Apsarās-the sea of milk.

sanskrit: परिकाल्यमानः तदा वालिना अभिद्रुतः हि अहम्
पुनः आवृत्य सहसा प्रस्थितो अहम् तदा विभो
transliteration: parikālyamānaḥ tadā vālinā abhidrutaḥ hi aham
punaḥ āvṛtya sahasā prasthito aham tadā vibho
english: And chased by Vāli, and flying on, I suddenly veered round, and then again, O master, off I went.

sanskrit: दिशः तस्याः ततो भूयः प्रस्थितो दक्षिणम् दिशम्
विन्ध्य पादप संकीर्णाम् चन्दन द्रुम शोभिताम्
transliteration: diśaḥ tasyāḥ tato bhūyaḥ prasthito dakṣiṇam diśam
vindhya pādapa saṃkīrṇām candana druma śobhitām
english: And changing that direction, I again made for the South crowded with trees belonging to Vindhya, and embellished with sandal woods.

sanskrit: द्रुम शैल अन्तरे पश्यन् भूयो दक्षिणतो अपराअम्
अपराम् च दिशम् प्राप्तो वालिना समभिद्रुतः
transliteration: druma śaila antare paśyan bhūyo dakṣiṇato aparāam
aparām ca diśam prāpto vālinā samabhidrutaḥ
english: Then seeing Văli in the mountain among trees, from the south I, pursued by Vāli, betook myself to the western quarter.

sanskrit: स पश्यन् विविधान् देशान् अस्तम् च गिरि सत्तमम्
प्राप्य च अस्तम् गिरि श्रेष्ठम् उत्तरम् संप्रधावितः
transliteration: sa paśyan vividhān deśān astam ca giri sattamam
prāpya ca astam giri śreṣṭham uttaram saṃpradhāvitaḥ

sanskrit: हिमवंतम् च मेरुम् च समुद्रम् च तथा उत्तरम्
यदा न विन्दे शरणम् वालिना समभिद्रुतः
transliteration: himavaṃtam ca merum ca samudram ca tathā uttaram
yadā na vinde śaraṇam vālinā samabhidrutaḥ

sanskrit: ततो माम् बुद्धि संपन्नो हनुमान् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
इदानीम् मे स्मृतम् राजन् यथा वाली हरीश्वरः
transliteration: tato mām buddhi saṃpanno hanumān vākyam abravīt
idānīm me smṛtam rājan yathā vālī harīśvaraḥ

sanskrit: मतंगेन तदा शप्तो हि अस्मिन् आश्रम मण्डले
प्रविशेत् यदि वै वाली मूर्धा अस्य शतधा भवेत्
transliteration: mataṃgena tadā śapto hi asmin āśrama maṇḍale
praviśet yadi vai vālī mūrdhā asya śatadhā bhavet
english: 'O king, now, I remember me how that lord of monkeys, Vāli, was cursed by Matanga in this very hermitage. If Vāli enters (into this asylum), his head becomes cleft in hundred.

sanskrit: तत्र वासः सुखो अस्माकम् निर्उद्विग्नो भविष्यति
transliteration: tatra vāsaḥ sukho asmākam nirudvigno bhaviṣyati
english: There shall dwell happily without anxiety.' O king's son, thereupon, we went to the Rișyamuka mountain, nor did then Vāli enter we there from fear of Matanga.

sanskrit: न विवेश तदा वाली मतंगस्य भयात् तदा
एवम् मया तदा राजन् प्रत्यक्षम् उपलक्षितम्
पृथिवी मण्डलम् सर्वम् गुहाम् अस्मि आगतः ततः
transliteration: na viveśa tadā vālī mataṃgasya bhayāt tadā
evam mayā tadā rājan pratyakṣam upalakṣitam
pṛthivī maṇḍalam sarvam guhām asmi āgataḥ tataḥ
english: Thus, O king, did I actually see all the world. And from that place I came to this cave.

sanskrit: दर्शनार्थम् तु वैदेह्याः सर्वतः कपि कुंजराः
व्यादिष्टाः कपि राजेन यथा उक्तम् जग्मुर् अंजसा
transliteration: darśanārtham tu vaidehyāḥ sarvataḥ kapi kuṃjarāḥ
vyādiṣṭāḥ kapi rājena yathā uktam jagmur aṃjasā
english: The principal monkeys, having been ordered by the monkey-king, speedily went in all directions to their destinations for the purpose of seeing Vaidehi.

sanskrit: ते सरांसि सरित् कक्षान् आकाशम् नगराणि च
नदी दुर्गान् तथा शैलान् विचिन्वन्ति समन्ततः
transliteration: te sarāṃsi sarit kakṣān ākāśam nagarāṇi ca
nadī durgān tathā śailān vicinvanti samantataḥ
english: And on all sides they explore watery expanses, and streams, and lawns, and commons, and cities, and tracts rendered impassable by torrents.

sanskrit: तत्र देशान् प्रविचिन्वन्ति स शैल वन काननान्
transliteration: tatra deśān pravicinvanti sa śaila vana kānanān
english: And the leaders of monkey-herds search all those countries, countries, described described by Sugrīva,-containing mountains, woods and forests.

sanskrit: विचिन्त्य दिवसम् सर्वे सीता अधिगमने धृताः
समायान्ति स्म मेदिन्याम् निशा कालेषु वानराः
transliteration: vicintya divasam sarve sītā adhigamane dhṛtāḥ
samāyānti sma medinyām niśā kāleṣu vānarāḥ
english: Engaged during the day in search of Sītā, at night the monkeys seek the ground (for sleep).

sanskrit: सर्व ऋतुकान् च देशेषु वानराः स फलान् द्रुमान्
आसाद्य रजनीम् शय्याम् चक्रुः सर्वेषु अहस्सु ते
transliteration: sarva ṛtukān ca deśeṣu vānarāḥ sa phalān drumān
āsādya rajanīm śayyām cakruḥ sarveṣu ahassu te
english: In every place, by day coming to trees aye enjoying every season, and crowned with fruits, the monkeys prepared their beds at night.* *The sense is rather obscure, it being difficult to understand the relation their beds bore to the neighbouring trees.

sanskrit: तत् अहः प्रथमम् कृत्वा मासे प्रस्रवणम् गताः
कपि राजेन संगम्य निराशाः कपि कुंजराः
transliteration: tat ahaḥ prathamam kṛtvā māse prasravaṇam gatāḥ
kapi rājena saṃgamya nirāśāḥ kapi kuṃjarāḥ
english: Counting that day* as the first, the principal monkeys, after the month had run out, resigning all hope, came to the Fountain and met with the monkey-king. *i.e. the day of their departure.

sanskrit: विचित्य तु दिशम् पूर्वाम् यथा उक्ताम् सचिवैः सह
transliteration: vicitya tu diśam pūrvām yathā uktām sacivaiḥ saha
english: And having explored the Eastern regions, as directed, the exceedingly strong Vinata not having been able to see Sītā, came back, in company with his counsellors.

sanskrit: दिशम् अपि उत्तराम् सर्वाम् विविच्य स महाकपिः
आगतः सह सैन्येन वीरः शतबलिः तदा
transliteration: diśam api uttarām sarvām vivicya sa mahākapiḥ
āgataḥ saha sainyena vīraḥ śatabaliḥ tadā
english: And then that mighty ape, Satavali, daunted in spirits, arrived with his forces, after having searched all through the North.

sanskrit: सुषेणः पश्चिमाम् आशाम् विविच्य सह वानरैः
समेत्य मासे पूर्णे तु सुग्रीवम् उपचक्रमे
transliteration: suṣeṇaḥ paścimām āśām vivicya saha vānaraiḥ
sametya māse pūrṇe tu sugrīvam upacakrame
english: And having searched the West in company with his monkeys, Sușeņa, on the month being complete, presented himself before Sugrīva.

sanskrit: तम् प्रस्रवण पृष्ठस्थम् समासाद्य अभिवाद्य च
आसीनम् सह रामेण सुग्रीवम् इदम् अब्रुवन्
transliteration: tam prasravaṇa pṛṣṭhastham samāsādya abhivādya ca
āsīnam saha rāmeṇa sugrīvam idam abruvan
english: And coming to Sugrīva seated along with Rāma behind the Fountain, and saluting the former, Susena said to Sugriva.

sanskrit: विचिताः पर्वताः सर्वे वनानि गहनानि च
निम्नगाः सागर अन्ताः च सर्वे जनपदाः तथा
transliteration: vicitāḥ parvatāḥ sarve vanāni gahanāni ca
nimnagāḥ sāgara antāḥ ca sarve janapadāḥ tathā

sanskrit: गुहाः च विचिताः सर्वा याः च ते परिकीर्तिताः
विचिताः च महागुल्मा लता वितत संतताः
transliteration: guhāḥ ca vicitāḥ sarvā yāḥ ca te parikīrtitāḥ
vicitāḥ ca mahāgulmā latā vitata saṃtatāḥ

sanskrit: गहनेषु च देशेषु दुर्गेषु विषमेषु च
ये चैव गहना देशा विचिताः ते पुनः पुनः
transliteration: gahaneṣu ca deśeṣu durgeṣu viṣameṣu ca
ye caiva gahanā deśā vicitāḥ te punaḥ punaḥ

sanskrit: उदार सत्त्व अभिजनो हनूमान्स मैथिलीम् ज्ञास्यसि वानरेन्द्र
दिशम् तु याम् एव गता तु सीताताम् आस्थितो वायु सुतो हनूमान्
transliteration: udāra sattva abhijano hanūmānsa maithilīm jñāsyasi vānarendra
diśam tu yām eva gatā tu sītātām āsthito vāyu suto hanūmān
english: O lord of monkeys, possessed of great strength and nobly born, it is Hanumān who will be able to ascertain the whereabouts of Mithila's daughter. And the Wind's son, Hanumān, has followed even the has by which Sītā has gone.

sanskrit: सह तार अंगदाभ्याम् तु सहसा हनुमान् कपिः
सुग्रीवेण यथा उद्दिष्टम् तम् देशम् उपचक्रमे
transliteration: saha tāra aṃgadābhyām tu sahasā hanumān kapiḥ
sugrīveṇa yathā uddiṣṭam tam deśam upacakrame
english: The monkey Hanumān in company with Tārā and Angada swiftly set out for the quarter assigned by Sugrīva.

sanskrit: स तु दूरम् उपागम्य सर्वैः तैः कपि सत्तमैः
ततो विचित्य विन्ध्यस्य गुहाः च गहनानि च
transliteration: sa tu dūram upāgamya sarvaiḥ taiḥ kapi sattamaiḥ
tato vicitya vindhyasya guhāḥ ca gahanāni ca

sanskrit: पर्वताग्र नदी दुर्गान् सरांसि विपुल द्रुमान्
वृक्ष खण्डान् च विविधान् पर्वतान् वन पादपान्
transliteration: parvatāgra nadī durgān sarāṃsi vipula drumān
vṛkṣa khaṇḍān ca vividhān parvatān vana pādapān

sanskrit: अन्वेषमाणाः ते सर्वे वानराः सर्वतो दिशम्
न सीताम् ददृशुर् वीरा मैथिलीम् जनक आत्मजाम्
transliteration: anveṣamāṇāḥ te sarve vānarāḥ sarvato diśam
na sītām dadṛśur vīrā maithilīm janaka ātmajām

sanskrit: ते भक्षयन्तो मूलानि फलानि विविधानि अपि
अन्वेषमाणा दुर्धर्षा न्यवसन् तत्र तत्र ह
transliteration: te bhakṣayanto mūlāni phalāni vividhāni api
anveṣamāṇā durdharṣā nyavasan tatra tatra ha

sanskrit: स तु देशो दुर्अन्वेषो गुहा गहनवान् महान्
निर्जलम् निर्जनम् शून्यम् गहनम् घोर दर्शनम्
transliteration: sa tu deśo duranveṣo guhā gahanavān mahān
nirjalam nirjanam śūnyam gahanam ghora darśanam

sanskrit: ता दृशानि अन्या अपि अरण्यानि विचित्य भृइश पीडिताः
स देशः च दुर्अन्वेष्यो गुहा गहनवान् महान्
transliteration: tā dṛśāni anyā api araṇyāni vicitya bhṛiśa pīḍitāḥ
sa deśaḥ ca duranveṣyo guhā gahanavān mahān

sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा तु तम् ततः देशम् सर्वे वै हरि यूथपाः
देशम् अन्यम् दुराधर्षम् विविशुः च अकुतो भयाः
transliteration: tyaktvā tu tam tataḥ deśam sarve vai hari yūthapāḥ
deśam anyam durādharṣam viviśuḥ ca akuto bhayāḥ

sanskrit: यत्र वन्ध्य फला वृक्षा विपुष्पाः पर्ण वर्जिताः
निस्तोयाः सरितो यत्र मूलम् यत्र सुदुर्लभम्
transliteration: yatra vandhya phalā vṛkṣā vipuṣpāḥ parṇa varjitāḥ
nistoyāḥ sarito yatra mūlam yatra sudurlabham

sanskrit: न सन्ति महिषा यत्र न मृगा न च हस्तिनः
शार्दूलाः पक्षिणो वा अपि ये च अन्ये वन गोचराः
transliteration: na santi mahiṣā yatra na mṛgā na ca hastinaḥ
śārdūlāḥ pakṣiṇo vā api ye ca anye vana gocarāḥ

sanskrit: न च अत्र वृक्षा न ओषध्यो न वल्ल्यो न अपि वीरुधः
स्निग्ध पत्राः स्थले यत्र पद्मिन्यः फुल्ल पंकजाः
transliteration: na ca atra vṛkṣā na oṣadhyo na vallyo na api vīrudhaḥ
snigdha patrāḥ sthale yatra padminyaḥ phulla paṃkajāḥ
english: And there are there neither trees, nor annual plants, nor creepers, nor herbs,-and in that place there are no pleasant pools, with cool leaves, and filled with blown lotuses, and it has been renounced by the black-bees.

sanskrit: प्रेक्षणीयाः सुगन्धाः च भ्रमरैः च वर्जिताः
कण्डुर् नाम महाभागः सत्य वादी तपो धनः
transliteration: prekṣaṇīyāḥ sugandhāḥ ca bhramaraiḥ ca varjitāḥ
kaṇḍur nāma mahābhāgaḥ satya vādī tapo dhanaḥ

sanskrit: तस्य तस्मिन् वने पुत्रो बालको दश वार्षिकः
transliteration: tasya tasmin vane putro bālako daśa vārṣikaḥ

sanskrit: प्रणष्टो जीवित अन्ताय क्रुद्धः तेन महामुनिः
तेन धर्माअत्मना शप्तम् कृत्स्नम् तत्र महद् वनम्
transliteration: praṇaṣṭo jīvita antāya kruddhaḥ tena mahāmuniḥ
tena dharmāatmanā śaptam kṛtsnam tatra mahad vanam

sanskrit: तस्य ते कानन अन्तान् तु गिरीणाम् कन्दराणि च
transliteration: tasya te kānana antān tu girīṇām kandarāṇi ca

sanskrit: तत्र च अपि महात्मानो न अपश्यन् जनक आत्मजाम्
transliteration: tatra ca api mahātmāno na apaśyan janaka ātmajām
english: They carefully search the skirts of its woods, mountain-caves, and the sources of its streams. And those high-souled ones, devoted to the good of Sugrīva, did not find Janaka's daughter, or her ravisher, Rāvaņa.

sanskrit: हर्तारम् रावणम् वा अपि सुग्रीव प्रिय कारिणः
ते प्रविश्य तु तम् भीमम् लता गुल्म समावृतम्
transliteration: hartāram rāvaṇam vā api sugrīva priya kāriṇaḥ
te praviśya tu tam bhīmam latā gulma samāvṛtam

sanskrit: ददृशुः भीम कर्माणम् असुरम् सुर निर्भयम्
तम् दृष्ट्वा वनरा घोरम् स्थितम् शैलम् इव असुरम्
transliteration: dadṛśuḥ bhīma karmāṇam asuram sura nirbhayam
tam dṛṣṭvā vanarā ghoram sthitam śailam iva asuram

sanskrit: गाढम् परिहिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा तम् पर्वत उपमम्
सो अपि तान् वानरान् सर्वान् नष्टाः स्थ इति अब्रवीत् बली
transliteration: gāḍham parihitāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā tam parvata upamam
so api tān vānarān sarvān naṣṭāḥ stha iti abravīt balī

sanskrit: तम् आपतन्तम् सहसा वालि पुत्रो अंगदः तदा
transliteration: tam āpatantam sahasā vāli putro aṃgadaḥ tadā

sanskrit: रावणो अयम् इति ज्ञात्वा तलेन अभिजघान ह
स वालि पुत्र अभिहतो वक्त्रात् शोणितम् उद्वमन्
transliteration: rāvaṇo ayam iti jñātvā talena abhijaghāna ha
sa vāli putra abhihato vaktrāt śoṇitam udvaman

sanskrit: असुरो न्यपतत् भूमौ पर्यस्त इव पर्वतः
ते तु तस्मिन् निर् उच्छ्वासे वानरा जित काशिनः
transliteration: asuro nyapatat bhūmau paryasta iva parvataḥ
te tu tasmin nir ucchvāse vānarā jita kāśinaḥ
english: Struck by Vāli's son, that Asura, his mouth vomiting blood, fell down to the earth like a hill toppled down. And on his having breathed his last, the monkeys, elated with victory, thoroughly searched that mountain cavern.

sanskrit: व्यचिन्वन् प्रायशः तत्र सर्वम् तत् गिरि गह्वरम्
विचितम् तु ततः सर्वम् सर्वे ते कानन ओकसः
transliteration: vyacinvan prāyaśaḥ tatra sarvam tat giri gahvaram
vicitam tu tataḥ sarvam sarve te kānana okasaḥ

sanskrit: अन्यत् एव अपरम् घोरम् विविशुर् गिरि गह्वरम्
ते विचित्य पुनः खिन्ना विनिष्पत्य समागताः
एकांते वृक्ष मूले तु निषेदुर् दीन मानसाः
transliteration: anyat eva aparam ghoram viviśur giri gahvaram
te vicitya punaḥ khinnā viniṣpatya samāgatāḥ
ekāṃte vṛkṣa mūle tu niṣedur dīna mānasāḥ
english: And after having searched (that place) also, they came out fatigued; and with desponding hearts sat them down at a distance under the shade of a tree. they came out fatigued; and with desponding hearts sat them down at a distance under the shade of a tree.

sanskrit: अथ अंगदः तदा सर्वान् वानरान् इदम् अब्रवीत्
परिश्रान्तो महा प्राज्ञः समाश्वास्य शनैर् वचः
transliteration: atha aṃgadaḥ tadā sarvān vānarān idam abravīt
pariśrānto mahā prājñaḥ samāśvāsya śanair vacaḥ
english: Then the eminently wise Angada, fatigued, spoke to all the monkeys, cheering them.

sanskrit: वनानि गिरयो नद्यो दुर्गाणि गहनानि च
दरी गिरि गुहाः चैव विचिता नः समंततः
transliteration: vanāni girayo nadyo durgāṇi gahanāni ca
darī giri guhāḥ caiva vicitā naḥ samaṃtataḥ
english: Woods, and mountains, and rivers, and impenetrable wilds, and valleys, and mountain caverns have been thoroughly searched. But Jānakī we have failed to find anywhere,—or that wicked wight, the Rākṣasa that has ravished Sītā.

sanskrit: तत्र तत्र सह अस्माभिः जानकी न च दृश्यते
तथा रक्षः अपहर्ता च सीतायाः चैव दुष्कृती
transliteration: tatra tatra saha asmābhiḥ jānakī na ca dṛśyate
tathā rakṣaḥ apahartā ca sītāyāḥ caiva duṣkṛtī
english: Woods, and mountains, and rivers, and impenetrable wilds, and valleys, and mountain caverns have been thoroughly searched. But Jānakī we have failed to find anywhere,—or that wicked wight, the Rākṣasa that has ravished Sītā.

sanskrit: कालः च नः महान् यातः सुग्रीवः च उग्र शासनः
transliteration: kālaḥ ca naḥ mahān yātaḥ sugrīvaḥ ca ugra śāsanaḥ
english: We have spent a great part of the term that had been assigned by Sugrīva of stern commands. Therefore, banishing languor, sadness, and invading drowsiness, do you together search all round.

sanskrit: विहाय तन्द्रीम् शोकम् च निद्राम् चैव समुत्थिताम्
विचिनुध्वम् तथा सीताम् पश्यामो जनक आत्मजाम्
transliteration: vihāya tandrīm śokam ca nidrām caiva samutthitām
vicinudhvam tathā sītām paśyāmo janaka ātmajām
english: Do you so search Sītā, that she may be found out (by us). High spirits, ability and forwardness in action, are said to conduce to success. Therefore it is that I speak thus to you.

sanskrit: अनिर्वेदम् च दाक्ष्यम् च मनसः च अपराजयम्
कार्य सिद्धि कराणि आहुः तस्मात् एतत् ब्रवीमि अहम्
transliteration: anirvedam ca dākṣyam ca manasaḥ ca aparājayam
kārya siddhi karāṇi āhuḥ tasmāt etat bravīmi aham

sanskrit: अद्य अपि इदम् वनम् दुर्गम् विचिन्वन्तु वन ओकसः
खेदम् त्यक्त्वा पुनः सर्वम् वनम् एतत् विचिन्वताम्
transliteration: adya api idam vanam durgam vicinvantu vana okasaḥ
khedam tyaktvā punaḥ sarvam vanam etat vicinvatām
english: You dwellers of the wood, do you to day rummage this impenetrable wood; renouncing grief, do you again search through this forest.

sanskrit: परम् निर्वेदम् आगम्य न हि नः मीलनम् क्षमम्
transliteration: param nirvedam āgamya na hi naḥ mīlanam kṣamam
english: Those who act, for certain behold the fruit of their endeavours; but if people once give way to grief, they cannot again attain vigour.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवः क्रोधनो राजा तीक्ष्ण दण्डः च वानराः
भेतव्यम् तस्य सततम् रामस्य च महात्मनः
transliteration: sugrīvaḥ krodhano rājā tīkṣṇa daṇḍaḥ ca vānarāḥ
bhetavyam tasya satatam rāmasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: You monkeys, king Sugrīva is irascible; and inflicteth sharp punishments. He should be always feared, as also the magnanimous Rāma.

sanskrit: हितार्थम् एतत् उक्तम् वः क्रियताम् यदि रोचते
उच्यताम् हि क्षमम् यत् तत् सर्वेषाम् एव वानराः
transliteration: hitārtham etat uktam vaḥ kriyatām yadi rocate
ucyatām hi kṣamam yat tat sarveṣām eva vānarāḥ
english: I tell you this for your good. Act accordingly, if you list. And do you also express what else you are capable of.

sanskrit: उवाच व्यक्तया वाचा पिपासा श्रम खिन्नया
transliteration: uvāca vyaktayā vācā pipāsā śrama khinnayā
english: Hearing Angada's words Gandhamādana said in candid words faint from thirst and fatigue,

sanskrit: सदृशम् खलु वः वाक्यम् अंगदो यत् उवाच ह
हितम् च एव अनुकूलम् च क्रियताम् अस्य भाषितम्
transliteration: sadṛśam khalu vaḥ vākyam aṃgado yat uvāca ha
hitam ca eva anukūlam ca kriyatām asya bhāṣitam
english: What Angada has said to us is worthy of him, and is beneficial and good. Do you follow his speech.

sanskrit: पुनः मार्गामहे शैलान् कन्दराम् च शिलान् तथा
काननानि च शून्यानि गिरि प्रस्रवणानि च
transliteration: punaḥ mārgāmahe śailān kandarām ca śilān tathā
kānanāni ca śūnyāni giri prasravaṇāni ca
english: Let us afresh search hills, caves and rocks, vacant forests and mountain cascades,-in accordance with what the high-souled Sugrīva has laid down. Let all in a body rummage the wood, and the mountain caverns.

sanskrit: विचिन्वन्तु वनम् सर्वे गिरि दुर्गाणि संगताः
transliteration: vicinvantu vanam sarve giri durgāṇi saṃgatāḥ
english: Let us afresh search hills, caves and rocks, vacant forests and mountain cascades,-in accordance with what the high-souled Sugrīva has laid down. Let all in a body rummage the wood, and the mountain caverns.

sanskrit: ततः समुत्थाय पुनः वानराः ते महाबलाः
विन्ध्य कानन संकीर्णाम् विचेरुर् दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
transliteration: tataḥ samutthāya punaḥ vānarāḥ te mahābalāḥ
vindhya kānana saṃkīrṇām vicerur dakṣiṇām diśam
english: There rising up, the mighty monkeys again began to range the South close with forests belonging to Vindhya.

sanskrit: ते शारद अभ्र प्रतिमम् श्रीमत् रजत पर्वतम्
transliteration: te śārada abhra pratimam śrīmat rajata parvatam
english: And the monkeys ascended the Silvern Hill resembling the autumnal welkin, graceful, and furnished with summits and valleys.

sanskrit: तत्र लोध्र वनम् रम्यम् सप्त पर्ण वनानि च
विचिन्वन्तो हरि वराः सीता दर्शन कान्क्षिणः
transliteration: tatra lodhra vanam ramyam sapta parṇa vanāni ca
vicinvanto hari varāḥ sītā darśana kānkṣiṇaḥ
english: And eager to behold Sītā, those excellent monkeys began to search the Lodhra wood, and the Saptaparņa forests.

sanskrit: तस्य अग्रम् अधिरूढाः ते श्रान्ता विपुल विक्रमाः
न पश्यन्ति स्म वैदेहीम् रामस्य महिषीम् प्रियाम्
transliteration: tasya agram adhirūḍhāḥ te śrāntā vipula vikramāḥ
na paśyanti sma vaidehīm rāmasya mahiṣīm priyām
english: And ascending its top*, those ones endued with immense prowess, experiencing fatigue, could not find Vaidehi, the beloved spouse of Rama. *i.e. the top of the Silvern Hill.

sanskrit: ते तु दृष्टि गतम् दृष्ट्वा तम् शैलम् बहु कंदरम्
transliteration: te tu dṛṣṭi gatam dṛṣṭvā tam śailam bahu kaṃdaram
english: And having surveyed that hill having many a grot, so far as the eye could range, the monkeys looking all round, descended (the eminence).

sanskrit: अवरुह्य ततो भूमिम् श्रान्ता विगत चेतसः
स्थित्वा मुहूर्तम् तत्र अथ वृक्ष मूलम् उपाश्रिताः
transliteration: avaruhya tato bhūmim śrāntā vigata cetasaḥ
sthitvā muhūrtam tatra atha vṛkṣa mūlam upāśritāḥ
english: And having descended to the earth, the monkeys, bewildered, and losing their consciousness, rested for a while at the foot of a tree.

sanskrit: ते मुहूर्तम् समाश्वस्ताः किंचित् भग्न परिश्रमाः
पुनर् एव उद्यताः कृत्स्नाम् मार्गितुम् दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
transliteration: te muhūrtam samāśvastāḥ kiṃcit bhagna pariśramāḥ
punar eva udyatāḥ kṛtsnām mārgitum dakṣiṇām diśam
english: And their fatigue having gone off a little, the monkeys, having been refreshed for a while, again prepared to explore the whole South.

sanskrit: हनुमत् प्रमुखाः ते तु प्रस्थिताः प्लवग ऋषभाः
विंध्यम् एव आदितः कृत्वा विचेरुः ते समंततः
transliteration: hanumat pramukhāḥ te tu prasthitāḥ plavaga ṛṣabhāḥ
viṃdhyam eva āditaḥ kṛtvā viceruḥ te samaṃtataḥ
english: And the monkey chiefs, headed by Hanumān, having set out (on the search), began to range all through Vindhya.

sanskrit: सह तारा अंगदाभ्याम् तु संगम्य हनुमान् कपिः
विचिनोति च विन्ध्यस्य गुहाः च गहनानि च
transliteration: saha tārā aṃgadābhyām tu saṃgamya hanumān kapiḥ
vicinoti ca vindhyasya guhāḥ ca gahanāni ca
english: The monkey, Hanumān, in company with Tārā and Angada searcheth the caves and woods of Vindhya, caverns all around haunted by lions and tigers, and in vast inaccessible cascades in that foremost of mountains.

sanskrit: सिंह शार्दूल जुष्टाः च गुहाः च परितः तथा
विषमेषु नग इन्द्रस्य महा प्रस्रवणेषु च
transliteration: siṃha śārdūla juṣṭāḥ ca guhāḥ ca paritaḥ tathā
viṣameṣu naga indrasya mahā prasravaṇeṣu ca
english: The monkey, Hanumān, in company with Tārā and Angada searcheth the caves and woods of Vindhya, caverns all around haunted by lions and tigers, and in vast inaccessible cascades in that foremost of mountains.

sanskrit: आसेदुः तस्य शैलस्य कोटिम् दक्षिण पस्चिमाम्
तेषाम् तत्र एव वसताम् स कालो व्यत्यवर्तत
transliteration: āseduḥ tasya śailasya koṭim dakṣiṇa pascimām
teṣām tatra eva vasatām sa kālo vyatyavartata
english: And they came to the south-western summit of the inountain. And when they sojourned there, their (appointed) term had not expired.

sanskrit: स हि देशो दुरन्वेष्यो गुहा गहनवान् महान्
तत्र वायु सुतः सर्वम् विचिनोति स्म पर्वतम्
transliteration: sa hi deśo duranveṣyo guhā gahanavān mahān
tatra vāyu sutaḥ sarvam vicinoti sma parvatam
english: And that spacious country, consisting as it did, of caves and grots and woods, was difficult to search. And there the wind-god's offspring searched all over the mountain.

sanskrit: मैन्दः च द्विविदः चैव हनुमान् जांबवान् अपि
अंगदो युव राजः च तारः च वनगोचरः
transliteration: maindaḥ ca dvividaḥ caiva hanumān jāṃbavān api
aṃgado yuva rājaḥ ca tāraḥ ca vanagocaraḥ

sanskrit: गिरि जाल आवृतान् देशान् मार्गित्वा दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
विचिन्वन्तः ततः तत्र ददृशुः विवृतम् बिलम्
transliteration: giri jāla āvṛtān deśān mārgitvā dakṣiṇām diśam
vicinvantaḥ tataḥ tatra dadṛśuḥ vivṛtam bilam
english: Having explored the South, (containing) countries enveloped with mountain chains, we have all got fatigued, but we have failed to find Mithila's daughter.

sanskrit: दुर्गम् ऋक्ष बिलम् नाम दानवेन अभिरक्षितम्
क्षुत् पिपासा परीताः तु श्रान्ताः तु सलिल अर्थिनः
transliteration: durgam ṛkṣa bilam nāma dānavena abhirakṣitam
kṣut pipāsā parītāḥ tu śrāntāḥ tu salila arthinaḥ

sanskrit: अवकीर्णम् लता वृक्षैः ददृशुः ते महा बिलम्
तत्र क्रौन्चाः च हंसाः च सारसाः च अपि निष्क्रमन्
transliteration: avakīrṇam latā vṛkṣaiḥ dadṛśuḥ te mahā bilam
tatra krauncāḥ ca haṃsāḥ ca sārasāḥ ca api niṣkraman

sanskrit: जल आर्द्राः चक्रवाकाः च रक्त अंगाः पद्म रेणुभिः
ततः तत् बिलम् आसाद्य सुगन्धि दुरतिक्रमम्
transliteration: jala ārdrāḥ cakravākāḥ ca rakta aṃgāḥ padma reṇubhiḥ
tataḥ tat bilam āsādya sugandhi duratikramam

sanskrit: संजात परिशंकाः ते तत् बिलम् प्लवग उत्तमाः
transliteration: saṃjāta pariśaṃkāḥ te tat bilam plavaga uttamāḥ
english: And drawing nigh to that fragrant and inaccessible cave, those superior monkeys were struck with amaze, and became eager (to enter into it).

sanskrit: नाना सत्त्व समाकीर्णाम् दैत्य इन्द्र निलय उपमम्
transliteration: nānā sattva samākīrṇām daitya indra nilaya upamam
english: And with their minds filled with doubt, those vigorous foremost of monkeys gladly approached that cave; abounding in diverse animals, resembling the residence of the lord of Daityas, dazzling, and dreadful, and impenetrable on all sides. Then Hanuman the son of the wind-god, possessed of the splendour of a mountain-summit, cognizant of woods and forests, said to the grim-visaged apes,

sanskrit: दुर्दर्शम् इव घोरम् च दुर्विगाह्यम् च सर्वशः
ततः पर्वत कूट आभो हनुमान् मारुत आत्मजः
transliteration: durdarśam iva ghoram ca durvigāhyam ca sarvaśaḥ
tataḥ parvata kūṭa ābho hanumān māruta ātmajaḥ

sanskrit: अब्रवीत् वानरान् घोरान् कान्तार वन कोविदः
गिरि जाल आवृतान् देशान् मार्गित्वा दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
transliteration: abravīt vānarān ghorān kāntāra vana kovidaḥ
giri jāla āvṛtān deśān mārgitvā dakṣiṇām diśam

sanskrit: वयम् सर्वे परिश्रांता न च पश्याम मैथिलीम्
अस्मात् च अपि बिलात् हंसाः क्रौन्चाः च सह सारसैः
transliteration: vayam sarve pariśrāṃtā na ca paśyāma maithilīm
asmāt ca api bilāt haṃsāḥ krauncāḥ ca saha sārasaiḥ

sanskrit: जल आर्द्राः चक्रवाकाः च निष्पतन्ति स्म सर्वशः
नूनम् सलिलवान् अत्र कूपो वा यदि वा ह्रदः
transliteration: jala ārdrāḥ cakravākāḥ ca niṣpatanti sma sarvaśaḥ
nūnam salilavān atra kūpo vā yadi vā hradaḥ
english: And from yonder cave come out swarms of and and kraunchas and chakravākas, drenched with water. For certain here is a well or a watery expanse. And at the mouth of the cave there are these cool trees.'

sanskrit: तथा च इमे बिल द्वारे स्निग्धाः तिष्ठन्ति पादपाः
इति उक्ताः तत् बिलम् सर्वे विविशुः तिमिर आवृतम्
transliteration: tathā ca ime bila dvāre snigdhāḥ tiṣṭhanti pādapāḥ
iti uktāḥ tat bilam sarve viviśuḥ timira āvṛtam

sanskrit: अचन्द्र सूर्यम् हरयो ददृशू रोम हर्षणम्
निशम्य तस्मात् सिंहाः च तान् तान् च मृग पक्षिणः
transliteration: acandra sūryam harayo dadṛśū roma harṣaṇam
niśamya tasmāt siṃhāḥ ca tān tān ca mṛga pakṣiṇaḥ

sanskrit: प्रविष्टा हरि शार्दूला बिलम् तिमिर आवृतम्
न तेषाम् सज्जते दृष्टिः न तेजः न पराक्रमः
transliteration: praviṣṭā hari śārdūlā bilam timira āvṛtam
na teṣām sajjate dṛṣṭiḥ na tejaḥ na parākramaḥ

sanskrit: वायोः इव गतिः तेषाम् दृष्टिः तम् अपि वर्तते
ते प्रविष्टाः तु वेगेन तत् बिलम् कपि कुंजराः
transliteration: vāyoḥ iva gatiḥ teṣām dṛṣṭiḥ tam api vartate
te praviṣṭāḥ tu vegena tat bilam kapi kuṃjarāḥ

sanskrit: प्रकाशम् च अभिरामम् च ददृशुः देशम् उत्तमम्
ततः तस्मिन् बिले भीमे नाना पादप संकुले
transliteration: prakāśam ca abhirāmam ca dadṛśuḥ deśam uttamam
tataḥ tasmin bile bhīme nānā pādapa saṃkule
english: And those foremost of monkeys rushed into the cavity; and beheld displayed (before them) an excellent and charming scene. And embracing each other in that fearful cave rife with various trees, they passed over an hundred Yojanas.

sanskrit: ते नष्ट संज्ञाः तृषिताः संभ्रांताः सलिल अर्थिनः
transliteration: te naṣṭa saṃjñāḥ tṛṣitāḥ saṃbhrāṃtāḥ salila arthinaḥ

sanskrit: परिपेतुर् बिले तस्मिन् कंचित् कालम् अतन्द्रिताः
ते कृशा दीन वदनाः परिश्रान्ताः प्लवंगमाः
transliteration: paripetur bile tasmin kaṃcit kālam atandritāḥ
te kṛśā dīna vadanāḥ pariśrāntāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: And deprived of their sense, and tried with thirst, and bewildered, and thirsting for water, they for a time vigilantly descended in darkness down the cave. And emaciated, with woebegone faces, and spent, those monkeys despairing of their lives, (at last) saw light.

sanskrit: आलोकम् ददृशुः वीरा निराशा जीविते यदा
ततः तम् देशम् आगम्य सौम्याः वितिमिरम् वनम्
transliteration: ālokam dadṛśuḥ vīrā nirāśā jīvite yadā
tataḥ tam deśam āgamya saumyāḥ vitimiram vanam

sanskrit: ददृशुः कान्चनान् वृक्षान् दीप्त वैश्वानर प्रभान्
सालान् तालान् तमालान् च पुन्नागान् वंजुलान् धवान्
transliteration: dadṛśuḥ kāncanān vṛkṣān dīpta vaiśvānara prabhān
sālān tālān tamālān ca punnāgān vaṃjulān dhavān

sanskrit: चंपकान् नाग वृक्षान् च कर्णिकारान् च पुष्पितान्
स्तबकैः कांचनैः चित्रैः रक्तैः किसलयैः तथा
transliteration: caṃpakān nāga vṛkṣān ca karṇikārān ca puṣpitān
stabakaiḥ kāṃcanaiḥ citraiḥ raktaiḥ kisalayaiḥ tathā

sanskrit: आपीडैः च लताभिः च हेम आभरण भूषितैः
transliteration: āpīḍaiḥ ca latābhiḥ ca hema ābharaṇa bhūṣitaiḥ

sanskrit: नील वैदूर्य वर्णाः च पद्मिनीः पतगैः आवृताः
transliteration: nīla vaidūrya varṇāḥ ca padminīḥ patagaiḥ āvṛtāḥ

sanskrit: महद्भिः कांचनैः वृक्षैः वृता बाल अर्क संनिभैः
जातरूपमयैः मत्स्यैः महद्भिः च अथ पन्कजैः
transliteration: mahadbhiḥ kāṃcanaiḥ vṛkṣaiḥ vṛtā bāla arka saṃnibhaiḥ
jātarūpamayaiḥ matsyaiḥ mahadbhiḥ ca atha pankajaiḥ

sanskrit: नलिनीः तत्र ददृशुः प्रसन्न सलिल आयुताः
कांचनानि विमानानि राजतानि तथा एव च
transliteration: nalinīḥ tatra dadṛśuḥ prasanna salila āyutāḥ
kāṃcanāni vimānāni rājatāni tathā eva ca

sanskrit: तपनीय गवाक्षाणि मुक्ता जाल आवृतानि च
हैम राजत भौमानि वैदूर्य मणिमन्ति च
transliteration: tapanīya gavākṣāṇi muktā jāla āvṛtāni ca
haima rājata bhaumāni vaidūrya maṇimanti ca

sanskrit: ददृशुः तत्र हरयो गृह मुख्यानि सर्वशः
पुष्पितान् फलिनो वृक्षान् प्रवाल मणि संनिभान्
transliteration: dadṛśuḥ tatra harayo gṛha mukhyāni sarvaśaḥ
puṣpitān phalino vṛkṣān pravāla maṇi saṃnibhān

sanskrit: कांचन भ्रमरान् चैव मधूनि च समन्ततः
मणि कांचन चित्राणि शयनानि आसनानि च
transliteration: kāṃcana bhramarān caiva madhūni ca samantataḥ
maṇi kāṃcana citrāṇi śayanāni āsanāni ca

sanskrit: हेम रजत कांस्यानाम् भाजनानाम् च राशयः
transliteration: hema rajata kāṃsyānām bhājanānām ca rāśayaḥ

sanskrit: अगुरूणाम् च दिव्यानाम् चंदनानाम् च संचयम्
शुचीनि अभ्यवहाराणि मूलानि च फलानि च
transliteration: agurūṇām ca divyānām caṃdanānām ca saṃcayam
śucīni abhyavahārāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca

sanskrit: महा अर्हाणि च पानानि मधूनि रसवन्ति च
दिव्यानाम् अम्बराणाम् च महा अर्हाणाम् च संचयान्
transliteration: mahā arhāṇi ca pānāni madhūni rasavanti ca
divyānām ambarāṇām ca mahā arhāṇām ca saṃcayān

sanskrit: कंबलानाम् च चित्राणाम् अजिनानाम् च संचयान्
तत्र तत्र विन्यस्तान् दीप्तान् वैश्वानर प्रभान्
transliteration: kaṃbalānām ca citrāṇām ajinānām ca saṃcayān
tatra tatra vinyastān dīptān vaiśvānara prabhān

sanskrit: तत्र तत्र विचिन्वन्तो बिले तत्र महा प्रभाः
transliteration: tatra tatra vicinvanto bile tatra mahā prabhāḥ

sanskrit: ददृशुः वानराः शूराः स्त्रियम् कांचित् अदूरतः
ताम् च ते ददृशुः तत्र चीर कृष्ण अजिन अम्बराम्
transliteration: dadṛśuḥ vānarāḥ śūrāḥ striyam kāṃcit adūrataḥ
tām ca te dadṛśuḥ tatra cīra kṛṣṇa ajina ambarām

sanskrit: तापसीम् नियत आहाराम् ज्वलंतीम् इव तेजसा
प्रपच्छ हनुमान् तत्र का असि त्वम् कस्य वा बिलम्
transliteration: tāpasīm niyata āhārām jvalaṃtīm iva tejasā
prapaccha hanumān tatra kā asi tvam kasya vā bilam

sanskrit: ततो हनूमान् गिरि सन्निकाशःकृत अंजलिः ताम् अभिवाद्य वृद्धाम्
पप्रच्छ का त्वम् भवनम् बिलम् चरत्नानि च इमानि वदस्व कस्य
transliteration: tato hanūmān giri sannikāśaḥkṛta aṃjaliḥ tām abhivādya vṛddhām
papraccha kā tvam bhavanam bilam caratnāni ca imāni vadasva kasya
english: And-Hanumān like to a hill, bowing down to the old women with joined hands, asked her, saying,-Who are you? And tell me, to whom belong this edifice and the cave as well as all these jewels.

sanskrit: इति उक्त्वा हनुमान् तत्र पुनः कृष्ण अजिन अंबराम्
अब्रवीत् ताम् महाभागाम् तापसीम् धर्म चारिणीम्
transliteration: iti uktvā hanumān tatra punaḥ kṛṣṇa ajina aṃbarām
abravīt tām mahābhāgām tāpasīm dharma cāriṇīm
english: Having said this to that female clad in a piece of black deer-skin, Hanumān asked that highly religious ascetic practising pious offices,

sanskrit: इदम् प्रविष्टाः सहसा बिलम् तिमिर संवृतम्
क्षुत् पिपासा परिश्रांताः परिखिन्नाः च सर्वशः
transliteration: idam praviṣṭāḥ sahasā bilam timira saṃvṛtam
kṣut pipāsā pariśrāṃtāḥ parikhinnāḥ ca sarvaśaḥ

sanskrit: महत् धरण्या विवरम् प्रविष्टाः स्म पिपासिताः
इमाम् तु एवम् विधान् भावान् विविधान् अद्भुत उपमान्
transliteration: mahat dharaṇyā vivaram praviṣṭāḥ sma pipāsitāḥ
imām tu evam vidhān bhāvān vividhān adbhuta upamān

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा वयम् प्रव्यथिताः संभ्रांता नष्ट चेतसः
कस्य एते कांचना वृक्षाः तरुण आदित्य सन्निभाः
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā vayam pravyathitāḥ saṃbhrāṃtā naṣṭa cetasaḥ
kasya ete kāṃcanā vṛkṣāḥ taruṇa āditya sannibhāḥ

sanskrit: शुचीनि अभ्यवहार्याणि मूलानि च फलानि च
transliteration: śucīni abhyavahāryāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca

sanskrit: तपनीय गव अक्षाणि मणि जाल आवृतानि च
पुष्पिताः फालवन्तः च पुण्याः सुरभि गन्धयः
transliteration: tapanīya gava akṣāṇi maṇi jāla āvṛtāni ca
puṣpitāḥ phālavantaḥ ca puṇyāḥ surabhi gandhayaḥ

sanskrit: कांचनानि च पद्मानि जातानि विमले जले
transliteration: kāṃcanāni ca padmāni jātāni vimale jale

sanskrit: कथम् मत्स्याः च सौवर्णा दृश्यन्ते सह कच्छपैः
आत्मानः अनुभावात् वा कस्य वै एतत् तपो बलम्
transliteration: katham matsyāḥ ca sauvarṇā dṛśyante saha kacchapaiḥ
ātmānaḥ anubhāvāt vā kasya vai etat tapo balam
english: And golden lotuses spring in in lucent water,-how golden fishes are discovered in it along with tortoises! Have these sprung from your power; or do they owe their existence to the ascetic energy of any other? It behoves you to relate all this to us who are ignorant of everything.

sanskrit: अजानताम् नः सर्वेषाम् सर्वम् आख्यातुम् अर्हसि
एवम् उक्ता हनुमता तापसी धर्म चारिणी
transliteration: ajānatām naḥ sarveṣām sarvam ākhyātum arhasi
evam uktā hanumatā tāpasī dharma cāriṇī

sanskrit: प्रति उवाच हनूमंतम् सर्व भूत हिते रता
transliteration: prati uvāca hanūmaṃtam sarva bhūta hite ratā

sanskrit: तेन इदम् निर्मितम् सर्वम् मायया कांचनम् वनम्
पुरा दानव मुख्यानाम् विश्वकर्मा बभूव ह
transliteration: tena idam nirmitam sarvam māyayā kāṃcanam vanam
purā dānava mukhyānām viśvakarmā babhūva ha

sanskrit: येन इदम् कांचनम् दिव्यम् निर्मितम् भवन उत्तमम्
स तु वर्ष सहस्राणि तपः तप्त्वा महत् वने
transliteration: yena idam kāṃcanam divyam nirmitam bhavana uttamam
sa tu varṣa sahasrāṇi tapaḥ taptvā mahat vane

sanskrit: पितामहात् वरम् लेभे सर्वम् औशसनम् धनम्
विधाय सर्वम् बलवान् सर्व काम ईश्वरः तदा
transliteration: pitāmahāt varam lebhe sarvam auśasanam dhanam
vidhāya sarvam balavān sarva kāma īśvaraḥ tadā

sanskrit: उवास सुखितः कालम् कंचित् अस्मिन् महावने
तम् अप्सरसि हेमायाम् सक्तम् दानव पुंगवम्
transliteration: uvāsa sukhitaḥ kālam kaṃcit asmin mahāvane
tam apsarasi hemāyām saktam dānava puṃgavam

sanskrit: विक्रम्य एव अशनिम् गृह्य जघान ईशः पुरंदरः
इदम् च ब्रह्मणा दत्तम् हेमायै वनम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: vikramya eva aśanim gṛhya jaghāna īśaḥ puraṃdaraḥ
idam ca brahmaṇā dattam hemāyai vanam uttamam

sanskrit: शाश्वतः काम भोगः च गृहम् च इदम् हिरण्मयम्
transliteration: śāśvataḥ kāma bhogaḥ ca gṛham ca idam hiraṇmayam

sanskrit: मम प्रिय सखी हेमा नृत्त गीत विशारदा
transliteration: mama priya sakhī hemā nṛtta gīta viśāradā

sanskrit: तया दत्त वरा च अस्मि रक्षामि भवनम् महान्
किम् कार्यम् कस्य वा हेतोः कांताराणि प्रपद्यथ
transliteration: tayā datta varā ca asmi rakṣāmi bhavanam mahān
kim kāryam kasya vā hetoḥ kāṃtārāṇi prapadyatha

sanskrit: कथम् च इदम् वनम् दुर्गम् युष्माभिः उपलक्षितम्
शुचीनि अभ्यवहार्याणि मूलानि च फलानि च
भुक्त्वा पीत्वा च पानीयम् सर्वम् मे वक्तुम् अर्हथ
transliteration: katham ca idam vanam durgam yuṣmābhiḥ upalakṣitam
śucīni abhyavahāryāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca
bhuktvā pītvā ca pānīyam sarvam me vaktum arhatha
english: Having partaken of these fruits and roots intended for use, and drunk, do you detail all this to me.

sanskrit: अथ तान् अब्रवीत् सर्वान् विश्रांतान् हरि यूथपान्
इदम् वचनम् एकाग्रा तापसी धर्म चारिणी
transliteration: atha tān abravīt sarvān viśrāṃtān hari yūthapān
idam vacanam ekāgrā tāpasī dharma cāriṇī
english: Then to all the monkey-chiefs, after they had rested, the female ascetic, engaged in righteous practices, eagerly said these words,

sanskrit: वानरा यदि वः खेदः प्रनष्टः फल भक्षणात्
यदि च एतत् मया श्राव्यम् श्रोतुम् इच्छामि कथताम्
transliteration: vānarā yadi vaḥ khedaḥ pranaṣṭaḥ phala bhakṣaṇāt
yadi ca etat mayā śrāvyam śrotum icchāmi kathatām
english: You monkeys, if your pain has gone off in consequence of the fare of fruits which you have partaken, and also if it be fit to be heard by me, I would listen to your narration.

sanskrit: तस्याः तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा हनुमान् मारुत आत्मजः
transliteration: tasyāḥ tat vacanam śrutvā hanumān māruta ātmajaḥ
english: Hearing her words, Hanumān, the son of the wind-god, in all candour began to relate everything faithfully.

sanskrit: राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य महेन्द्र वरुण उपमः
रामो दाशरथिः श्रीमान् प्रविष्टो दण्डका वनम्
transliteration: rājā sarvasya lokasya mahendra varuṇa upamaḥ
rāmo dāśarathiḥ śrīmān praviṣṭo daṇḍakā vanam
english: The Sovereign of all this world, resembling Mahendra or Varuna, Rāma, the graceful son of Dasaratha, entered the woods of Dandaka, in company with his brother, Laksmana, as well as his spouse, Vaidehi. His wife has been forcibly carried of by Rāvana.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या च अपि भार्यया
तस्य भार्या जनस्थानात् रावणेन हृता बलात्
transliteration: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā ca api bhāryayā
tasya bhāryā janasthānāt rāvaṇena hṛtā balāt
english: The Sovereign of all this world, resembling Mahendra or Varuna, Rāma, the graceful son of Dasaratha, entered the woods of Dandaka, in company with his brother, Laksmana, as well as his spouse, Vaidehi. His wife has been forcibly carried of by Rāvana.

sanskrit: वीरः तस्य सखा राज्ञः सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः
राजा वानर मुख्यानाम् येन प्रस्थापिता वयम्
transliteration: vīraḥ tasya sakhā rājñaḥ sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ
rājā vānara mukhyānām yena prasthāpitā vayam
english: His friend is that heroic king, the monkey named Sugrīva. By that monarch of the foremnost monkeys have we been despatched (hither). And we have, joining company with these prime monkeys headed by Angada, come to the South, protected by Yama, and inhabited by Agastya.

sanskrit: अगस्त्य चरिताम् आशाम् दक्षिणाम् यम रक्षिताम्
सहैभिर्वानरैमुख्यैरङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वयम् - यद्वा -सह एभिः वानरैः मुख्यैः अंगद प्रमुखैः वयम्
transliteration: agastya caritām āśām dakṣiṇām yama rakṣitām
sahaibhirvānaraimukhyairaṅgadapramukhairvayam - yadvā -saha ebhiḥ vānaraiḥ mukhyaiḥ aṃgada pramukhaiḥ vayam

sanskrit: रावणम् सहिताः सर्वे राक्षसम् काम रूपिणम्
सीतया सह वैदेह्या मार्गध्वम् इति चोदिताः
transliteration: rāvaṇam sahitāḥ sarve rākṣasam kāma rūpiṇam
sītayā saha vaidehyā mārgadhvam iti coditāḥ
english: And we have been commissioned, 'Do you all search for the Rākşasa Rāvana, wearing forms at will, along with Videha's daughter, Sītā.'

sanskrit: विचित्य तु वयम् सर्वे समग्रम् - समुद्रम् - दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
वयम् बुभुक्षिताः सर्वे वृक्ष मूलम् उपाश्रिताः
transliteration: vicitya tu vayam sarve samagram - samudram - dakṣiṇām diśam
vayam bubhukṣitāḥ sarve vṛkṣa mūlam upāśritāḥ
english: Having searched through the forest as well as the ocean on the South, we becoming hungry, sat down at the foot of a tree.

sanskrit: विवर्ण वदनाः सर्वे सर्वे ध्यान परायणाः
न अधिगच्छामहे पारम् मग्नाः चिन्ता महाअर्णवे
transliteration: vivarṇa vadanāḥ sarve sarve dhyāna parāyaṇāḥ
na adhigacchāmahe pāram magnāḥ cintā mahāarṇave
english: And with pallid countenance, we all, absorbed in thought, sank in a wide sea of anxiety, which we could not cross.

sanskrit: चारयन्तः ततः चक्षुः दृष्टवन्तो महद् बिलम्
transliteration: cārayantaḥ tataḥ cakṣuḥ dṛṣṭavanto mahad bilam
english: And casting our eyes around, we spyed a huge cave covered with trees and plants and enveloped in gloom.

sanskrit: अस्मात् हंसा जल क्लिन्नाः पक्षैः सलिल रेणुभिः
transliteration: asmāt haṃsā jala klinnāḥ pakṣaiḥ salila reṇubhiḥ
english: And (it came to pass that) from this (cave) came out swans, drenched with water, with drops of water on their wings,-and plumed kuravas and cranes.

sanskrit: साधु अत्र प्रविशाम इति मया तु उक्ताः प्लवंगमाः
तेषाम् अपि हि सर्वेषाम् अनुमानम् उपागतम्
transliteration: sādhu atra praviśāma iti mayā tu uktāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
teṣām api hi sarveṣām anumānam upāgatam

sanskrit: अस्मिन् निपतिताः सर्वे अपि अथ कार्य त्वरान्विताः
ततो गाढम् निपतिता गृह्य हस्तौ परस्परम्
transliteration: asmin nipatitāḥ sarve api atha kārya tvarānvitāḥ
tato gāḍham nipatitā gṛhya hastau parasparam

sanskrit: इदम् प्रविष्टाः सहसा बिलम् तिमिर संवृतम्
एतत् नः कार्यम् एतेन कृत्येन वयम् आगताः
transliteration: idam praviṣṭāḥ sahasā bilam timira saṃvṛtam
etat naḥ kāryam etena kṛtyena vayam āgatāḥ

sanskrit: त्वाम् च एव उपगताः सर्वे परिद्यूना बुभुक्षिताः
आतिथ्य धर्म दत्तानि मूलानि च फलानि च
transliteration: tvām ca eva upagatāḥ sarve paridyūnā bubhukṣitāḥ
ātithya dharma dattāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca
english: Having come to you, hungry, and exhausted, we, who had been sore tried by hunger, have been entertained with fruits and roots, agreeably to the code regulating hospitality.

sanskrit: यत् त्वया रक्षिताः सर्वे म्रियमाणा बुभुक्षया
transliteration: yat tvayā rakṣitāḥ sarve mriyamāṇā bubhukṣayā

sanskrit: ब्रूहि प्रत्युपकार अर्थम् किम् ते कुर्वन्तु वानराः
एवम् उक्ता तु सर्वज्ञा वानरैः तैः स्वयंप्रभा
transliteration: brūhi pratyupakāra artham kim te kurvantu vānarāḥ
evam uktā tu sarvajñā vānaraiḥ taiḥ svayaṃprabhā

sanskrit: प्रत्युवाच ततः सर्वान् इदम् वानर यूथपान्
transliteration: pratyuvāca tataḥ sarvān idam vānara yūthapān

sanskrit: चरंत्या मम धर्मेण न कार्यम् इह केनचित्
एवम् उक्तः शुभम् वाक्यम् तापस्या धर्म संहितम्
transliteration: caraṃtyā mama dharmeṇa na kāryam iha kenacit
evam uktaḥ śubham vākyam tāpasyā dharma saṃhitam

sanskrit: उवाच हनुमान् वाक्यम् ताम् अनिन्दित लोचनाम्
शरणम् त्वाम् प्रपन्नाः स्मः सर्वे वै धर्मचारिणिम्
transliteration: uvāca hanumān vākyam tām anindita locanām
śaraṇam tvām prapannāḥ smaḥ sarve vai dharmacāriṇim

sanskrit: यः कृतः समयो अस्माकम् सुग्रीवेण महात्मना
स तु कालो व्यतिक्रान्तो बिले च परिवर्तताम्
transliteration: yaḥ kṛtaḥ samayo asmākam sugrīveṇa mahātmanā
sa tu kālo vyatikrānto bile ca parivartatām
english: We all take refuge in you, practising piety. the term that had been fixed by the high-souled Sugrīva in respect of us, shall all be spent in this cave. Therefore it behoveth you to deliver us from this place.

sanskrit: सा त्वम् अस्मात् बिलात् अस्मान् उत्तारयितुम् अर्हसि
तस्मात् सुग्रीव वचनात् अतिक्रान्तान् गत आयुषः
transliteration: sā tvam asmāt bilāt asmān uttārayitum arhasi
tasmāt sugrīva vacanāt atikrāntān gata āyuṣaḥ
english: It behove you to save us, exercised with fear for Sugriva,-who, happening to override Sugriva's command, shall lose our lives. And, further, O you that practisest righteousness, great is the task that is to be performed by us.

sanskrit: त्रातुम् अर्हसि नः सर्वान् सुग्रीव भय शन्कितान्
महत् च कार्यम् अस्माभिः कर्तव्यम् धर्मचारिणि
transliteration: trātum arhasi naḥ sarvān sugrīva bhaya śankitān
mahat ca kāryam asmābhiḥ kartavyam dharmacāriṇi

sanskrit: तत् च अपि न कृतम् कार्यम् अस्माभिः इह वासिभिः
एवम् उक्ता हनुमता तापसी वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tat ca api na kṛtam kāryam asmābhiḥ iha vāsibhiḥ
evam uktā hanumatā tāpasī vākyam abravīt

english: Thus addressed by Hanumān, the ascetic said, Once entering, hard it is for any one to return (hence) alive. But by the potency of my asceticism acquired through self-discipline, I shall deliver all the monkeys from this den.

sanskrit: सर्वान् एव बिलात् अस्मात् तारयिष्यामि वानरान्
transliteration: sarvān eva bilāt asmāt tārayiṣyāmi vānarān

sanskrit: न हि निष्क्रमितुम् शक्यम् अनिमीलित लोचनैः
ततो निमीलिताः सर्वे सुकुमार अंगुलैः करैः
transliteration: na hi niṣkramitum śakyam animīlita locanaiḥ
tato nimīlitāḥ sarve sukumāra aṃgulaiḥ karaiḥ

sanskrit: सहसा पिदधुः दृष्टिम् हृष्टा गमन कान्क्षिणः
वानराः तु महात्मानो हस्त रुद्ध मुखाः तदा
transliteration: sahasā pidadhuḥ dṛṣṭim hṛṣṭā gamana kānkṣiṇaḥ
vānarāḥ tu mahātmāno hasta ruddha mukhāḥ tadā

sanskrit: निमेष अन्तर मात्रेण बिलात् उत्तारिताः तथा
उवाच सर्वान् तान् तत्र तापसी धर्म चारिणी
transliteration: nimeṣa antara mātreṇa bilāt uttāritāḥ tathā
uvāca sarvān tān tatra tāpasī dharma cāriṇī

sanskrit: निःसृतान् विषमात् तस्मात् समाश्वास्य इदम् अब्रवीत्
एष विन्ध्यो गिरिः श्रीमान् नाना द्रुम लता आयुतः
transliteration: niḥsṛtān viṣamāt tasmāt samāśvāsya idam abravīt
eṣa vindhyo giriḥ śrīmān nānā druma latā āyutaḥ

sanskrit: एष प्रसवणः शैलः सागरो अयम् महा उदधिः
स्वस्ति वो अस्तु गमिष्यामि भवनम् वानरर्षभाः
इति उक्त्वा तत् बिलम् श्रीमत् प्रविवेश स्वयम्प्रभा
transliteration: eṣa prasavaṇaḥ śailaḥ sāgaro ayam mahā udadhiḥ
svasti vo astu gamiṣyāmi bhavanam vānararṣabhāḥ
iti uktvā tat bilam śrīmat praviveśa svayamprabhā
english: This is the fair Vindhya mountain filled with various trees and herbs. This is the Praśravaņa hill; and this is the great deep. Fair Fortune! I go to my abode, you foremost of monkeys. Having spokea thus, Svayamprabhā entered that captivating cave.

sanskrit: ततः ते ददृशुः घोरम् सागरम् वरुण आलयम्
transliteration: tataḥ te dadṛśuḥ ghoram sāgaram varuṇa ālayam
english: Then they saw the ocean—abode of Varuņashoreless, resounding, rife with dreadful billows.

sanskrit: मयस्य माया विहितम् गिरि दुर्गम् विचिन्वताम्
तेषाम् मासो व्यतिक्रान्तो यो राज्ञा समयः कृतः
transliteration: mayasya māyā vihitam giri durgam vicinvatām
teṣām māso vyatikrānto yo rājñā samayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: Exploring the mountain fateness of Maya*, they spent the month that had been set by the king. *Named Rhiksavila.

sanskrit: विन्ध्यस्य तु गिरेः पादे संप्रपुष्पित पादपे
transliteration: vindhyasya tu gireḥ pāde saṃprapuṣpita pādape
english: Then sitting down at the foot of the Vindhya mountain, containing blossoming trees, at that time* those high-souled ones indulged-in reflections. *i.e. at the beginning of winter.

sanskrit: ततः पुष्पातिभाराग्राँल्ल्ताशतसमावृतान् -यद्वा -ततः पुष्प अतिभार अग्रान् लता शत समावृतान्
द्रुमान् वासन्तिकान् दृष्ट्वा बभूवुः भय शन्किताः
transliteration: tataḥ puṣpātibhārāgrām̐lltāśatasamāvṛtān -yadvā -tataḥ puṣpa atibhāra agrān latā śata samāvṛtān
drumān vāsantikān dṛṣṭvā babhūvuḥ bhaya śankitāḥ
english: Beholding vernal trees bending beneath the load of flowers, and environed by hundreds of plants, they were inspired with apprehension.

sanskrit: नष्ट संदेश काल अर्था निपेतुर् धरणी तले
transliteration: naṣṭa saṃdeśa kāla arthā nipetur dharaṇī tale
english: And each knowing that spring had appeared, they, the term appointed for their task having run out, dropped down on the ground.

sanskrit: ततः तान् कपि वृद्धान् च शिष्टान् चैव वनौकसः
वाचा मधुरया अभाष्य यथावत् अनुमान्य च
transliteration: tataḥ tān kapi vṛddhān ca śiṣṭān caiva vanaukasaḥ
vācā madhurayā abhāṣya yathāvat anumānya ca
english: Thereat, with bland words properly honouring the aged apes and the rest dwelling in the woods, that monkey having the shoulders of a lion or a bull, and plump and broad arms-the youthful prince Angada, endowed with high wisdom, spoke,

sanskrit: स तु सिंह ऋषभ स्कंधः पीन आयत भुजः कपिः
transliteration: sa tu siṃha ṛṣabha skaṃdhaḥ pīna āyata bhujaḥ kapiḥ
english: Thereat, with bland words properly honouring the aged apes and the rest dwelling in the woods, that monkey having the shoulders of a lion or a bull, and plump and broad arms-the youthful prince Angada, endowed with high wisdom, spoke,

sanskrit: शासनात् कपि राजस्य वयम् सर्वे विनिर्गताः
मासः पूर्णो बिलस्थानाम् हरयः किम् न बुध्यते
transliteration: śāsanāt kapi rājasya vayam sarve vinirgatāḥ
māsaḥ pūrṇo bilasthānām harayaḥ kim na budhyate
english: We have come out at the mandate of the monarch of monkeys. While we sojourned in the cave, a full month had passed away, you monkeys. Why do you not understand this? We set out, engaging that our term of search should reach no further than the end of Kärtika;* but that has expired. Now, what next is to be done? *October.

sanskrit: वयम् आश्वयुजे मासि काल संख्या व्यवस्थिताः
प्रस्थिताः सो अपि च अतीतः किम् अतः कार्यम् उत्तरम्
transliteration: vayam āśvayuje māsi kāla saṃkhyā vyavasthitāḥ
prasthitāḥ so api ca atītaḥ kim ataḥ kāryam uttaram
english: We have come out at the mandate of the monarch of monkeys. While we sojourned in the cave, a full month had passed away, you monkeys. Why do you not understand this? We set out, engaging that our term of search should reach no further than the end of Kärtika;* but that has expired. Now, what next is to be done? *October.

sanskrit: भवन्त प्रत्ययम् प्राप्ता नीति मार्ग विशारदाः
हितेषु अभिरता भर्त्तुः निसृष्टाः सर्व कर्मसु
transliteration: bhavanta pratyayam prāptā nīti mārga viśāradāḥ
hiteṣu abhiratā bharttuḥ nisṛṣṭāḥ sarva karmasu

sanskrit: कर्मसु अप्रतिमाः सर्वे दिक्षु विश्रुत पौरुषाः
transliteration: karmasu apratimāḥ sarve dikṣu viśruta pauruṣāḥ

sanskrit: इदानीम् अकृत अर्थानाम् मर्तव्यम् न अत्र संशयः
हरि राजस्य संदेशम् अकृत्वा कः सुखी भवेत्
transliteration: idānīm akṛta arthānām martavyam na atra saṃśayaḥ
hari rājasya saṃdeśam akṛtvā kaḥ sukhī bhavet

sanskrit: आस्मिन् अतीते काले तु सुग्रीवेण कृते स्वयम्
प्रायोपवेशनम् युक्तम् सर्वेषाम् च वन ओकसाम्
transliteration: āsmin atīte kāle tu sugrīveṇa kṛte svayam
prāyopaveśanam yuktam sarveṣām ca vana okasām

sanskrit: तीक्ष्णः प्रकृत्या सुग्रीवः स्वामि भावे व्यवस्थितः
न क्षमिष्यति नः सर्वान् अपराध कृतो गतान्
transliteration: tīkṣṇaḥ prakṛtyā sugrīvaḥ svāmi bhāve vyavasthitaḥ
na kṣamiṣyati naḥ sarvān aparādha kṛto gatān
english: Naturally stern, Sugrīva, established as our master, shall not forgive us, when we repair there, after having transgressed thus.

sanskrit: अप्रवृत्तौ च सीतायाः पापम् एव करिष्यति
तस्मात् क्षमम् इह अद्य एव गंतुम् प्रायोपविशनम्
transliteration: apravṛttau ca sītāyāḥ pāpam eva kariṣyati
tasmāt kṣamam iha adya eva gaṃtum prāyopaviśanam
english: Sītā not having been found out, Sugrīva, for certain, shall commit this sin.* Therefore it is fit that, forsaking our sons, and wives, and wealth, and homes, we this very day sit down to starve ourselves to death. *i.e. slay us.

sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा पुत्रन् च दारान् च धनानि च गृहाणि च
ध्रुवम् नः हिंसते राजा सर्वान् प्रतिगतान् इतः
transliteration: tyaktvā putran ca dārān ca dhanāni ca gṛhāṇi ca
dhruvam naḥ hiṃsate rājā sarvān pratigatān itaḥ

sanskrit: वधेन अप्रतिरूपेण श्रेयान् मृत्युः इह एव नः
न च अहम् यौवराज्येन सुग्रीवेण अभिषेचितः
transliteration: vadhena apratirūpeṇa śreyān mṛtyuḥ iha eva naḥ
na ca aham yauvarājyena sugrīveṇa abhiṣecitaḥ

sanskrit: नरेन्द्रेण अभिषिक्तो अस्मि रामेण अक्लिष्ट कर्मणा
स पूर्वम् बद्ध वैरो माम् राजा दृष्ट्वा व्यतिक्रमम्
transliteration: narendreṇa abhiṣikto asmi rāmeṇa akliṣṭa karmaṇā
sa pūrvam baddha vairo mām rājā dṛṣṭvā vyatikramam

sanskrit: किम् मे सुहृद्भिः व्यसनम् पश्यद्भिः जीवितांतरे
इह एव प्रायम् आसिष्ये पुण्ये सागर रोधसि
transliteration: kim me suhṛdbhiḥ vyasanam paśyadbhiḥ jīvitāṃtare
iha eva prāyam āsiṣye puṇye sāgara rodhasi
english: What is the use of suffering my friends to look on my disaster at the last moment of my existence? Therefore even on this sacred shore of the sea shall I sit down to starve myself.

sanskrit: एतत् श्रुत्वा कुमारेण युव राजेन भाषितम्
सर्वे ते वानर श्रेष्ठाः करुणम् वाक्यम् अब्रुवन्
transliteration: etat śrutvā kumāreṇa yuva rājena bhāṣitam
sarve te vānara śreṣṭhāḥ karuṇam vākyam abruvan
english: Hearing the tender prince speak thus, all those principal monkeys pathetically observed,

sanskrit: तीक्ष्णः प्रकृत्या सुग्रीवः प्रिया रक्तः च राघवः
समीक्ष्य अकृत कार्यान् तु तस्मिन् च समये गते
transliteration: tīkṣṇaḥ prakṛtyā sugrīvaḥ priyā raktaḥ ca rāghavaḥ
samīkṣya akṛta kāryān tu tasmin ca samaye gate
english: Sugrīva is harsh by nature, and Rāghava loveth his wife dearly. The time appointed having passed by, seeing us (come) without attaining success in the task, and seeing us arrive without obtaining a sight of Vaidehi, (Sugrīva) shall certainly slay us from the desire of doing what is agreeable to Rāghava.

sanskrit: अदृष्टायाम् च वैदेह्याम् दृष्ट्वा चैव समागतान्
transliteration: adṛṣṭāyām ca vaidehyām dṛṣṭvā caiva samāgatān
english: Sugrīva is harsh by nature, and Rāghava loveth his wife dearly. The time appointed having passed by, seeing us (come) without attaining success in the task, and seeing us arrive without obtaining a sight of Vaidehi, (Sugrīva) shall certainly slay us from the desire of doing what is agreeable to Rāghava.

sanskrit: न क्षमम् च अपराद्धानाम् गमनम् स्वामि पार्श्वतः
transliteration: na kṣamam ca aparāddhānām gamanam svāmi pārśvataḥ
english: Those who have transgressed, cannot come to the side of their master. Having come hither as the principal servants of Sugrīva, we shall either see Sītā or obtain information concerning her, or else, O hero, we shall repair to the mansion of Yama.

sanskrit: इह एव सीताम् अन्वीक्ष्य प्रवृत्तिम् उपलभ्य वा
नः चेत् गच्छाम तम् वीरम् गमिष्यामो यम क्षयम्
transliteration: iha eva sītām anvīkṣya pravṛttim upalabhya vā
naḥ cet gacchāma tam vīram gamiṣyāmo yama kṣayam
english: Those who have transgressed, cannot come to the side of their master. Having come hither as the principal servants of Sugrīva, we shall either see Sītā or obtain information concerning her, or else, O hero, we shall repair to the mansion of Yama.

sanskrit: प्लवंगमानाम् तु भय अर्दितानाम्श्रुत्वा वचः तार इदम् बभाषे
अलम् विषादेन बिलम् प्रविश्यवसाम सर्वे यदि रोचते वः
transliteration: plavaṃgamānām tu bhaya arditānāmśrutvā vacaḥ tāra idam babhāṣe
alam viṣādena bilam praviśyavasāma sarve yadi rocate vaḥ
english: Hearing the speeches of the monkeys afflicted with fear, Tārā said,-No use of indulging in grief. If you relish it, let us all entering the cave, dwell there.

sanskrit: इदम् हि माया विहितम् सुदुर्गमम्प्रभूत वृक्ष उदक भोज्य पेयम्
इह अस्ति नः न एव भयम् पुरंदरात्न राघवात् वानर राजतो अपि वा
transliteration: idam hi māyā vihitam sudurgamamprabhūta vṛkṣa udaka bhojya peyam
iha asti naḥ na eva bhayam puraṃdarātna rāghavāt vānara rājato api vā
english: This place abounding in flowers and waters, meats and drinks,—which has been brought forth by the power of ilusion, is incapable of being approached. Here we have no fear from Purandara, or Rāghava, or the king of monkeys.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा अंगदस्य अपि वचो अनुकूलम्ऊचुः च सर्वे हरयः प्रतीताः
यथा न हन्येम तथा विधानम्असक्तम् अद्य एव विधीयताम् नः
transliteration: śrutvā aṃgadasya api vaco anukūlamūcuḥ ca sarve harayaḥ pratītāḥ
yathā na hanyema tathā vidhānamasaktam adya eva vidhīyatām naḥ

sanskrit: तथा ब्रुवति तारे तु तारा अधिपति वर्चसि
अथ मेने हृतम् राज्यम् हनुमान् अंगदेन तत्
transliteration: tathā bruvati tāre tu tārā adhipati varcasi
atha mene hṛtam rājyam hanumān aṃgadena tat
english: When Tārā, bright as the moon, had spoken thus, Hanumān felt as if Angada had already deprived (Sugrīva) of his kingdom.* The sense is very obscure. One meaning is: Hanumān thought that Argada acquiescing in what Tārā had said, must remain there,-and ultimately endeavour to wrest the kingdom from Sugriva. Another meaning is: Hanumān conceived that remaining there in peace, Angada would consider his position as enviable as if he had extorted the kingdom from Sugrīva.

sanskrit: बुद्ध्या हि अष्ट अंगया युक्तम् चतुर् बल समन्वितम्
चतुर् दश गुणम् मेने हनुमान् वालिनः सुतम्
transliteration: buddhyā hi aṣṭa aṃgayā yuktam catur bala samanvitam
catur daśa guṇam mene hanumān vālinaḥ sutam

sanskrit: आपूर्यमाणम् शश्वत् च तेजो बल पराक्रमैः
शशिनम् शुक्ल पक्ष आदौ वर्धमानम् इव श्रिया
transliteration: āpūryamāṇam śaśvat ca tejo bala parākramaiḥ
śaśinam śukla pakṣa ādau vardhamānam iva śriyā

sanskrit: बृहस्पति समम् बुद्ध्या विक्रमे सदृशम् पितुः
transliteration: bṛhaspati samam buddhyā vikrame sadṛśam pituḥ

sanskrit: भर्तुः अर्थे परिश्रान्तम् सर्व शास्त्र विशारदः
transliteration: bhartuḥ arthe pariśrāntam sarva śāstra viśāradaḥ
english: And Hanumān versed in all branches of learning, finding Angada backward in the affair of his master, began inspire him with fear.* *Touching Tārā.

sanskrit: भेदयामास तान् सर्वान् वानरान् वाक्य संपदा
transliteration: bhedayāmāsa tān sarvān vānarān vākya saṃpadā
english: He, wealthy in words, laying under contribution the second of the four means,* had created division among those monkeys. *Referred to above.

sanskrit: तेषु सर्वेषु भिन्नेषु ततो अभीषय अंगदम्
भीषणैः विविधैः वाक्यैः कोप उपाय समन्वितैः
transliteration: teṣu sarveṣu bhinneṣu tato abhīṣaya aṃgadam
bhīṣaṇaiḥ vividhaiḥ vākyaiḥ kopa upāya samanvitaiḥ
english: On their being divided, he (Hanuman) set about raising Angada's apprehension by various fear-fraught speech, referring to punishments.

sanskrit: त्वम् समर्थ तरः पित्रा युद्धे तारेय वै ध्रुवम्
दृढम् धारयितुम् शक्तः कपि राज्यम् यथा पिता
transliteration: tvam samartha taraḥ pitrā yuddhe tāreya vai dhruvam
dṛḍham dhārayitum śaktaḥ kapi rājyam yathā pitā
english: O Tārā's son, you are for certain more capable of fight than even your sire; and you are also able to hold the monkey-kingdom as firmly as he.

sanskrit: नित्यम् अस्थिर चित्ता हि कपयो हरि पुंगव
न आज्ञाप्यम् विषहिष्यन्ति पुत्र दारान् विना त्वया
transliteration: nityam asthira cittā hi kapayo hari puṃgava
na ājñāpyam viṣahiṣyanti putra dārān vinā tvayā
english: But, O foremost of monkeys, the monkeys are always inconstant in character. Bereft of their wives and sons, they shall not bear your behest.

sanskrit: त्वाम् न एते हि अनुयुंजेयुः प्रत्यक्षम् प्रवदामि ते
यथा अयम् जांबवान् नीलः सुहोत्रः च महाकपिः
transliteration: tvām na ete hi anuyuṃjeyuḥ pratyakṣam pravadāmi te
yathā ayam jāṃbavān nīlaḥ suhotraḥ ca mahākapiḥ
english: They shall never take to you. This I tell you in presence of all. And I will tell you what. You neither by the virtues of conciliation, charity and the rest, nor by chastisement, shall succeed in drawing to your side this Jāmbavān, or Nīla, or the mighty ape Suhotra, or myself.

sanskrit: न हि अहम् ते इमे सर्वे साम दान आदिभिः गुणैः
दण्डेन न त्वया शक्याः सुग्रीवात् अपकर्षितुम्
transliteration: na hi aham te ime sarve sāma dāna ādibhiḥ guṇaiḥ
daṇḍena na tvayā śakyāḥ sugrīvāt apakarṣitum
english: They shall never take to you. This I tell you in presence of all. And I will tell you what. You neither by the virtues of conciliation, charity and the rest, nor by chastisement, shall succeed in drawing to your side this Jāmbavān, or Nīla, or the mighty ape Suhotra, or myself.

sanskrit: विगृह्य आसनम् अपि आहुः दुर्बलेन बलीयसा
आत्म रक्षा करः तस्मात् न विगृह्णीत दुर्बलः
transliteration: vigṛhya āsanam api āhuḥ durbalena balīyasā
ātma rakṣā karaḥ tasmāt na vigṛhṇīta durbalaḥ
english: A strong one wronging another that is weak, can live; therefore a weak person anxious for self-preservation, should never wrong (a strong individual).

sanskrit: याम् च इमाम् मन्यसे धात्रीम् एतत् बिलम् इति श्रुतम्
एतत् लक्ष्मण बाणानाम् ईषत् कार्यम् विदारणे
transliteration: yām ca imām manyase dhātrīm etat bilam iti śrutam
etat lakṣmaṇa bāṇānām īṣat kāryam vidāraṇe
english: You considerest that this cave may serve for your protectress,* having heard of it (said by Tārā); but to rive the same is but light work for the shafts of Laksmana. *The word meaning cave is feminine in Sanskrit.

sanskrit: स्वल्पम् हि कृतम् इन्द्रेण क्षिपता हि अशनिम् पुरा
लक्ष्मणो निशितैः बाणैः भिन्द्यात् पत्र पुटम् यथा
transliteration: svalpam hi kṛtam indreṇa kṣipatā hi aśanim purā
lakṣmaṇo niśitaiḥ bāṇaiḥ bhindyāt patra puṭam yathā
english: Formerly this was cleft a little by Indra, with his thunderbolt hurled (against it);* but now Lakṣmaṇa would pierce it like a leaf-stalk, by means of his keen arrows. *The commentator interprets the passage differently: Formerly Indra did a little damage herein-i.e. merely slew Maya, the architect of the mansion. This is ingenuity. I give the plain sense.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणस्य च नाराचा बहवः सन्ति तत् विधाः
वज्र अशनि सम स्पर्शा गिरीणाम् अपि दारकाः
transliteration: lakṣmaṇasya ca nārācā bahavaḥ santi tat vidhāḥ
vajra aśani sama sparśā girīṇām api dārakāḥ
english: Lakşmaņa has many an iron arrow like Indra's thunderbolt or that of the sky,* capable of riving even mountains. 15 *Vajrasani-Vajra is the thunder-bolt in the hand of Indra, and Asani—the thunder-bolt produced by clouds.

sanskrit: अवस्थाने यदा एव त्वम् आसिष्यसि परंतप
तदा एव हरयः सर्वे त्यक्ष्यन्ति कृत निश्चयाः
transliteration: avasthāne yadā eva tvam āsiṣyasi paraṃtapa
tadā eva harayaḥ sarve tyakṣyanti kṛta niścayāḥ
english: O subduer of enemies, soon as you shall set up here, the monkeys, making up their minds, shall forsake you.

sanskrit: स्मरंतः पुत्र दाराणाम् नित्य उद्विग्ना बुभुक्षिताः
खेदिता दुःख शय्याभिः त्वाम् करिष्यन्ति पृष्ठतः
transliteration: smaraṃtaḥ putra dārāṇām nitya udvignā bubhukṣitāḥ
kheditā duḥkha śayyābhiḥ tvām kariṣyanti pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Remembering their wives and sons, ever anxious (on account of Sugrīva, pining for domestic happiness, ad aggrieved (at their pitiable plight), they shall turn their backs upon you.

sanskrit: स त्वम् हीनः सुहृद्भिः च हित कामैः च बंधुभिः
तृणात् अपि भृश उद्विग्नः स्पंदमानात् भविष्यसि
transliteration: sa tvam hīnaḥ suhṛdbhiḥ ca hita kāmaiḥ ca baṃdhubhiḥ
tṛṇāt api bhṛśa udvignaḥ spaṃdamānāt bhaviṣyasi
english: Then forsaken by the kindred as well as friends seeking your welfare, you shall be struck with affright even at a quaking blade of grass. If you make head (against Sugriva), the sharpened shafts of Laksmana, terrible, of exceeding impetuosity and mighty vehemence, and incapable of being baffled, shall be eager to slay you.

sanskrit: अति उग्र वेगा निशिता घोरा लक्ष्मण सायकाः
transliteration: ati ugra vegā niśitā ghorā lakṣmaṇa sāyakāḥ
english: Then forsaken by the kindred as well as friends seeking your welfare, you shall be struck with affright even at a quaking blade of grass. If you make head (against Sugriva), the sharpened shafts of Laksmana, terrible, of exceeding impetuosity and mighty vehemence, and incapable of being baffled, shall be eager to slay you.

sanskrit: अस्माभिः तु गतम् सार्धम् विनीतवत् उपस्थितम्
आनुपूर्व्यात् तु सुग्रीवो राज्ये त्वाम् स्थापयिष्यति
transliteration: asmābhiḥ tu gatam sārdham vinītavat upasthitam
ānupūrvyāt tu sugrīvo rājye tvām sthāpayiṣyati
english: On the contrary, if you in humble guise present yourself (before him) along with us, he shall-establish you in the kingdom, in consideration of your being the next heir.

sanskrit: धर्म राजः पितृव्यः ते प्रीति कामो दृढ व्रतः
शुचिः सत्य प्रतिज्ञः च स त्वाम् जातु न नाशयेत्
transliteration: dharma rājaḥ pitṛvyaḥ te prīti kāmo dṛḍha vrataḥ
śuciḥ satya pratijñaḥ ca sa tvām jātu na nāśayet
english: A righteous sovereign, steady in vow, clean, and truthful in promise, your uncle, who cherishes affection for you shall not by any mears chastise. Ju.

sanskrit: प्रिय कामः च ते मातुः तत् अर्थम् च अस्य जीवितम्
तस्य अपत्यम् च न अस्ति अन्यत् तस्मात् अंगद गम्यताम्
transliteration: priya kāmaḥ ca te mātuḥ tat artham ca asya jīvitam
tasya apatyam ca na asti anyat tasmāt aṃgada gamyatām
english: He loves your mother, and his life is for her; and she has no other son. Therefore, O Angada, go along with us.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यम् प्रश्रितम् धर्म संहितम्
स्वामि सत्कार संयुक्तम् अंगदो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: śrutvā hanumato vākyam praśritam dharma saṃhitam
svāmi satkāra saṃyuktam aṃgado vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing Hanuman's speech, uttered meekly, fraught with morality, and reflecting honour upon Sugriva, Angada said,

sanskrit: स्थैर्यमात्ममनःशौचमानृशंस्यमथाअर्जवम् - यद्व -स्थैर्यम् आत्म मनः शौचम् आनृशंस्यम् अथ आर्जवम्
विक्रमः चैव धैर्यम् च सुग्रीवे न उपपद्यते
transliteration: sthairyamātmamanaḥśaucamānṛśaṃsyamathāarjavam - yadva -sthairyam ātma manaḥ śaucam ānṛśaṃsyam atha ārjavam
vikramaḥ caiva dhairyam ca sugrīve na upapadyate
english: Firmness, and mental sanctity, mercy, candour, prowess, and patience, are not in Sugriva.

sanskrit: भ्रातुः ज्येष्ठस्य यो भार्याम् जीवितो महिषीम् प्रियाम्
धर्मेण मातरम् यः तु स्वीकरोति जुगुप्सितः
transliteration: bhrātuḥ jyeṣṭhasya yo bhāryām jīvito mahiṣīm priyām
dharmeṇa mātaram yaḥ tu svīkaroti jugupsitaḥ
english: He that, while her son is living, appropriateth the beloved queen of his elder brother, mother to him by morality, is hated (of all beings). How can he that could cover up the mouth of the cave, when he had been desired by his brother gone on martial mission, to guard the same,—(how can he) know morality?

sanskrit: कथम् स धर्मम् जानीते येन भ्रात्रा दुरात्मना
transliteration: katham sa dharmam jānīte yena bhrātrā durātmanā
english: He that, while her son is living, appropriateth the beloved queen of his elder brother, mother to him by morality, is hated (of all beings). How can he that could cover up the mouth of the cave, when he had been desired by his brother gone on martial mission, to guard the same,—(how can he) know morality?

sanskrit: सत्यात् पाणि गृहीतः च कृत कर्मा महायशाः
विस्मृतो राघवो येन स कस्य सुकृतम् स्मरेत्
transliteration: satyāt pāṇi gṛhītaḥ ca kṛta karmā mahāyaśāḥ
vismṛto rāghavo yena sa kasya sukṛtam smaret
english: Whose good office remembereth he who could forget the renowned Räghava himself of mighty deeds, after having, in the name of truth, taken his hand? How can he reap religious merit that directed us to search Sītā here, from fear of Laksmana, and not from fear of unrighteousness?

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणस्य भयेन इह न अधर्म भय भीरुणा
आदिष्टा मार्गितुम् सीताम् धर्मः तस्मिन् कथम् भवेत्
transliteration: lakṣmaṇasya bhayena iha na adharma bhaya bhīruṇā
ādiṣṭā mārgitum sītām dharmaḥ tasmin katham bhavet
english: Whose good office remembereth he who could forget the renowned Räghava himself of mighty deeds, after having, in the name of truth, taken his hand? How can he reap religious merit that directed us to search Sītā here, from fear of Laksmana, and not from fear of unrighteousness?

sanskrit: तस्मिन् पापे कृतघ्ने तु स्मृति भिन्ने चल आत्मनि
आर्यः को विश्वसेत् जातु तत् कुलीनो विशेषतः
transliteration: tasmin pāpe kṛtaghne tu smṛti bhinne cala ātmani
āryaḥ ko viśvaset jātu tat kulīno viśeṣataḥ
english: What noble person, in especial, sprung in his race, shall any longer repose confidence in that impious one of unstable soul who has run amuck of morality?

sanskrit: राज्ये पुत्रः प्रतिष्ठाप्यः स गुणो निर्गुणो अपि वा
कथम् शत्रु कुलीनम् माम् सुग्रीवो जीवयिष्यति
transliteration: rājye putraḥ pratiṣṭhāpyaḥ sa guṇo nirguṇo api vā
katham śatru kulīnam mām sugrīvo jīvayiṣyati
english: Meritorious or otherwise, how can Sugriva, having installed in the kingdom me, son (of his enemy) and the enemy sprung in his race, suffer me to live?

sanskrit: भिन्न मन्त्रो अपराद्धः च हीन शक्तिः कथम् हि अहम्
किष्किन्धाम् प्राप्य जीवेयम् अनाथ इव दुर्बलः
transliteration: bhinna mantro aparāddhaḥ ca hīna śaktiḥ katham hi aham
kiṣkindhām prāpya jīveyam anātha iva durbalaḥ
english: How can I, whose counsels have been revealed, who have transgressed, and who have been deprived of my power, repairing to Kiş kindhā like one forlorn and feeble, live?

sanskrit: उपांशु दण्डेन हि माम् बंधनेन उपपादयेत्
शठः क्रूरो नृशंसः च सुग्रीवो राज्य कारणात्
transliteration: upāṃśu daṇḍena hi mām baṃdhanena upapādayet
śaṭhaḥ krūro nṛśaṃsaḥ ca sugrīvo rājya kāraṇāt
english: For the sake of his kingdom, Sugrīva, wily, cunning and cruel, shall put me in solitary confinement.

sanskrit: बंधनात् च अवसादात् मे श्रेयः प्रायोपवेशनम्
अनुजानंतु माम् सर्वे गृहम् गच्छंतु वानराः
transliteration: baṃdhanāt ca avasādāt me śreyaḥ prāyopaveśanam
anujānaṃtu mām sarve gṛham gacchaṃtu vānarāḥ
english: For me fasting to death is better than being confined-and suffering the consequent misery. Do you grant me your permission; and go to your homes, you monkeys.

sanskrit: अहम् वः प्रतिजानामि न गमिष्यामि अहम् पुरीम्
इह एव प्रायम् आसिष्ये श्रेयो मरणम् एव मे
transliteration: aham vaḥ pratijānāmi na gamiṣyāmi aham purīm
iha eva prāyam āsiṣye śreyo maraṇam eva me
english: I vow before you, to the palace I will never repair. At this very spot will I fast for death; as death is good for me.

sanskrit: अभिवादन पूर्वम् तु राजा कुशलम् एव च
transliteration: abhivādana pūrvam tu rājā kuśalam eva ca
english: Bowing to the king as well as to the powerful Rāghava, you should communicate my wellbeing to Sugriva— lord of my health and peace to my mother Umā.

sanskrit: वाच्यः तातः यवीयान् मे सुग्रीवो वानर ईश्वरः
आरोग्य पूर्वम् कुशलम् वाच्या माता रुमा च मे
transliteration: vācyaḥ tātaḥ yavīyān me sugrīvo vānara īśvaraḥ
ārogya pūrvam kuśalam vācyā mātā rumā ca me
english: Bowing to the king as well as to the powerful Rāghava, you should communicate my wellbeing to Sugriva— lord of my health and peace to my mother Umā.

sanskrit: मातरम् चैव मे ताराम् आश्वासयितुम् अर्हथ
प्रकृत्या प्रिय पुत्रा सा सानुक्रोशा तपस्विनी
transliteration: mātaram caiva me tārām āśvāsayitum arhatha
prakṛtyā priya putrā sā sānukrośā tapasvinī

sanskrit: विनष्टम् माम् इह श्रुत्वा व्यक्तम् हास्यति जीवितम्
एतावत् उक्त्वा वचनम् वृद्धान् तान् अभिवाद्य च
transliteration: vinaṣṭam mām iha śrutvā vyaktam hāsyati jīvitam
etāvat uktvā vacanam vṛddhān tān abhivādya ca

sanskrit: विवेश अंगदो भूमौ रुदन् दर्भेषु दुर्मनाः
तस्य संविशतः तत्र रुदन्तो वानर ऋषभाः
transliteration: viveśa aṃgado bhūmau rudan darbheṣu durmanāḥ
tasya saṃviśataḥ tatra rudanto vānara ṛṣabhāḥ

sanskrit: नयनेभ्यः प्रमुमुचुः उष्णम् वै वारि दुःखिताः
सुग्रीवम् चैव निन्दन्तः प्रशंसन्तः च वालिनम्
transliteration: nayanebhyaḥ pramumucuḥ uṣṇam vai vāri duḥkhitāḥ
sugrīvam caiva nindantaḥ praśaṃsantaḥ ca vālinam
english: When he had entered, those foremost monkeys, stricken with sorrow, weeping shed warm tears from their eyes. And censuring Sugrīva and praising Vāli, they, surrounding Angada, determined to starve themselves to death.

sanskrit: परिवार्य अंगदम् सर्वे व्यवस्यन् प्रायम् आसितुम्
तत् वाक्यम् वालि पुत्रस्य विज्ञाय प्लवग ऋषभाः
transliteration: parivārya aṃgadam sarve vyavasyan prāyam āsitum
tat vākyam vāli putrasya vijñāya plavaga ṛṣabhāḥ

sanskrit: उपस्पृश्य उदकम् सर्वे प्राक् मुखाः समुपाविशन्
दक्षिण अग्रेषु दर्भेषु उदक् तीरम् समाश्रिताः
transliteration: upaspṛśya udakam sarve prāk mukhāḥ samupāviśan
dakṣiṇa agreṣu darbheṣu udak tīram samāśritāḥ
english: Taking to heart the speech of Väli's son, those prime monkeys, sipping water, sat down facing the East. And sitting on the edge of the water on grass pointing to the south, the foremost monkeys, wishing for surcease, thought within themselves,-Even this is fit for us.

sanskrit: मुमूर्षवओ हरिश्रेष्टा एतत् क्षमम् इति स्म ह
रामस्य वन वासम् च क्षयम् दशरथस्य च
transliteration: mumūrṣavao hariśreṣṭā etat kṣamam iti sma ha
rāmasya vana vāsam ca kṣayam daśarathasya ca

sanskrit: जनस्थान वधम् चैव वधम् चैव जटायुषः
हरणम् चैव वैदेह्या वालिनः च वधम् तथा
राम कोपम् च वदताम् हरीणाम् भयम् आगतः
transliteration: janasthāna vadham caiva vadham caiva jaṭāyuṣaḥ
haraṇam caiva vaidehyā vālinaḥ ca vadham tathā
rāma kopam ca vadatām harīṇām bhayam āgataḥ
english: And as they spoke of the exile of Rāma and the demise of Daſaratha, the carnage in Janasthāna, the slaying of Jațāyu, the ravishment of Vaidehī, the slaughter of Vāli, and the ire of Rāma, the monkeys were seized with fear.

sanskrit: स संविशद्भिः बहुभिः महीधरोमहाअद्रि कूट प्रमितैः प्लवंगमैः
बभूव सन्नादित निर्दर अन्तरोभृशम् नदद्भिः जलदैः इव अंबरम्
transliteration: sa saṃviśadbhiḥ bahubhiḥ mahīdharomahāadri kūṭa pramitaiḥ plavaṃgamaiḥ
babhūva sannādita nirdara antarobhṛśam nadadbhiḥ jaladaiḥ iva aṃbaram
english: When those monkeys resembling mountainsummits had entered in, they set up cries, which, like to the rumbling of clouds, making the sky resound, made that mountain with its rills reverberate.

sanskrit: उपविष्टाः तु ते सर्वे यस्मिन् प्रायम् गिरि स्थले
हरयो गृध्र राजः च तम् देशम् उपचक्रमे
transliteration: upaviṣṭāḥ tu te sarve yasmin prāyam giri sthale
harayo gṛdhra rājaḥ ca tam deśam upacakrame
english: When the monkeys had been seated in that mountain, with the intention of putting a period to their existence through fasting a king of vultures happened to come to that quarter. And that long-lived bird was named Sampāti, the beautiful brother of Jaţāyu, famous for his strength and prowess.

sanskrit: सांपातिः नाम नाम्ना तु चिर जीवी विहंगमः
भ्राता जटायुषः श्रीमान् प्रख्यात बल पौरुषः
transliteration: sāṃpātiḥ nāma nāmnā tu cira jīvī vihaṃgamaḥ
bhrātā jaṭāyuṣaḥ śrīmān prakhyāta bala pauruṣaḥ
english: When the monkeys had been seated in that mountain, with the intention of putting a period to their existence through fasting a king of vultures happened to come to that quarter. And that long-lived bird was named Sampāti, the beautiful brother of Jaţāyu, famous for his strength and prowess.

sanskrit: उपविष्टान् हरीन् दृष्ट्वा हृष्टात्मा गिरम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: upaviṣṭān harīn dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭātmā giram abravīt
english: Issuing from a cavern of the mighty mountain Vindhya, he, seeing the monkeys seated, well pleased, said.

sanskrit: विधिः किल नरम् लोके विधानेन अनुवर्तते
यथा अयम् विहितो भक्ष्यः चिरात् मह्यम् उपागतः
transliteration: vidhiḥ kila naram loke vidhānena anuvartate
yathā ayam vihito bhakṣyaḥ cirāt mahyam upāgataḥ
english: Verily man reapeth the fruit of his former acts; and therefore it is that this food ordained to that end, comes to me after a long time. I shall feed on these monkeys, one by one, slaying them one after another. Eyeing those apes, the bird expressed himself thus.

sanskrit: उवाच एतत् वचः पक्षी तान् निरीक्ष्य प्लवंगमान्
transliteration: uvāca etat vacaḥ pakṣī tān nirīkṣya plavaṃgamān
english: Verily man reapeth the fruit of his former acts; and therefore it is that this food ordained to that end, comes to me after a long time. I shall feed on these monkeys, one by one, slaying them one after another. Eyeing those apes, the bird expressed himself thus.

sanskrit: तस्य तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा भक्ष लुब्धस्य पक्षिणः
अंगदः परम् आयस्तो हनूमंतम् अथ अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tasya tat vacanam śrutvā bhakṣa lubdhasya pakṣiṇaḥ
aṃgadaḥ param āyasto hanūmaṃtam atha abravīt
english: Hearing this speech of the bird coveting his food, Argada faintly spoke to Hanumān.

sanskrit: पश्य सीता - गृध्रा - अपदेशेन साक्षात् वैवस्वतो यमः
transliteration: paśya sītā - gṛdhrā - apadeśena sākṣāt vaivasvato yamaḥ
english: Behold! through Sita's simplicity* this onethe very son of the Sun, Yama-has come to this place, to exterminate the monkeys. *Another reading is Gridhra padesana— through the vultur's cunning. This the commentator consider as preferrable.

sanskrit: रामस्य न कृतम् कार्यम् न कृतम् राज शाशनम्
हरीणाम् इयम् अज्ञाता विपत्तिः सहसा आगता
transliteration: rāmasya na kṛtam kāryam na kṛtam rāja śāśanam
harīṇām iyam ajñātā vipattiḥ sahasā āgatā
english: Rāma's work has not been done; nor the royal mandate. And this disaster has arrived unthought of by the monkeys.

sanskrit: वैदेह्याः प्रिय कामेन कृतम् कर्म जटायुषा
गृध्र राजेन यत् तत्र श्रुतम् वः तत् अशेषतः
transliteration: vaidehyāḥ priya kāmena kṛtam karma jaṭāyuṣā
gṛdhra rājena yat tatra śrutam vaḥ tat aśeṣataḥ
english: You have in detail heard all that, inspired with the desire of doing what is good to Vaidehi, that king of vultures, Jatayu, did here.

sanskrit: तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि तिर्यक् योनि गतानि अपि
प्रियम् कुर्वन्ति रामस्य त्यक्त्वा प्राणान् यथा वयम्
transliteration: tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni tiryak yoni gatāni api
priyam kurvanti rāmasya tyaktvā prāṇān yathā vayam
english: In this way, all creatures, even the brute species, compass the welfare of Rāma, renouncing their lives, as we do.

sanskrit: ततः तस्य उपकार अर्थम् त्यजत आत्मानम् आत्मना
transliteration: tataḥ tasya upakāra artham tyajata ātmānam ātmanā
english: It is because of the love and tenderness* they bear towards (Rāma), that people do good to each other. *The commentator explains in pure orthodox fashion: Because every-thing is in Rama, people serve each other from the love and tenderness, which partain to him.

sanskrit: प्रियम् कृत्वा हि रामस्य धर्मज्ञेन जटायुषा
राघव अर्थे परिश्रान्ता वयम् संत्यक्त जीविताः
transliteration: priyam kṛtvā hi rāmasya dharmajñena jaṭāyuṣā
rāghava arthe pariśrāntā vayam saṃtyakta jīvitāḥ
english: Therefore the righteous Jațãyu, of his own accord laying down his life, has done the pleasure of Rāma. We also, overcome with fatigue and (almost) dying, have come to this forest; but Mithila's daughter we find not.

sanskrit: कांताराणि प्रपन्नाः स्म न च पश्याम मैथिलीम्
स सुखी गृध्र राजः तु रावणेन हतो रणे
मुक्तः च सुग्रीव भयात् गतः च परमाम् गतिम्
transliteration: kāṃtārāṇi prapannāḥ sma na ca paśyāma maithilīm
sa sukhī gṛdhra rājaḥ tu rāvaṇena hato raṇe
muktaḥ ca sugrīva bhayāt gataḥ ca paramām gatim
english: Happy is that king of vultures, having been slain by Rāvaņa in battle. He has got quit of the fear of Sugrīva, and has also attained supreme state.

sanskrit: हरणेन च वैदेह्याः संशयम् हरयो गताः
transliteration: haraṇena ca vaidehyāḥ saṃśayam harayo gatāḥ
english: In consequence of the death of Jațāyu and that of king Dasaratha, as well as owing to the ravishment of Vaidehi, (the lives of) the monkeys have come into jeopardy.

sanskrit: राम लक्ष्मणयोः वासाम् अरण्ये सह सीतया
राघवस्य च बाणेन वालिनः च तथा वधः
transliteration: rāma lakṣmaṇayoḥ vāsām araṇye saha sītayā
rāghavasya ca bāṇena vālinaḥ ca tathā vadhaḥ
english: Rama's and Laksmana's abode in the forest with Sītā, Rāghava's slaying of Vāli with a shaft, the slaughter of innumerable Räksasas by the enraged Rama, and (finally) this mishap-all these owe their origin to the bestowal of the boon on Kaikeyi.

sanskrit: राम कोपात् अशेषाणाम् राक्षसाम् च तथा वधम्
कैकेय्या वर दानेन इदम् च विकृतम् कृतम्
transliteration: rāma kopāt aśeṣāṇām rākṣasām ca tathā vadham
kaikeyyā vara dānena idam ca vikṛtam kṛtam
english: Rama's and Laksmana's abode in the forest with Sītā, Rāghava's slaying of Vāli with a shaft, the slaughter of innumerable Räksasas by the enraged Rama, and (finally) this mishap-all these owe their origin to the bestowal of the boon on Kaikeyi.

sanskrit: तत् असुखम् अनुकीर्तितम् वचोभुवि पतितान् च निरीक्ष्य वानरान्
भृश चकित मतिः महामतिःकृपणम् उदाहृतवान् स गृध्रराजः
transliteration: tat asukham anukīrtitam vacobhuvi patitān ca nirīkṣya vānarān
bhṛśa cakita matiḥ mahāmatiḥkṛpaṇam udāhṛtavān sa gṛdhrarājaḥ
english: Seeing the monkeys stretched on the earth, and hearing their piteous words describing their grief, that magnanimous king of vultures, with his mind agitated said (this).
