kṣiptam indreṇa te vajram kopa āviṣṭena tejasā
english: And, seeing you shing through the heavens, O mighty monkey, Indra, owing wrath, hurled his thunder-bolt at you.

sanskrit: तदा शैलाग्र शिखरे वामो हनुर् अभज्यत
ततो हि नाम धेयम् ते हनुमान् इति कीर्तितम्
transliteration: tadā śailāgra śikhare vāmo hanur abhajyata
tato hi nāma dheyam te hanumān iti kīrtitam
english: Thereat, breaking your left jaw, you (didst fall) on the mountain From this circumstance, your name has been known Hanuman.

sanskrit: ततः त्वाम् निहतम् दृष्ट्वा वायुः गन्ध वहः स्वयम्
त्रैलोक्यम् भृश संक्रुद्धो न ववौ वै प्रभंजनः
transliteration: tataḥ tvām nihatam dṛṣṭvā vāyuḥ gandha vahaḥ svayam
trailokyam bhṛśa saṃkruddho na vavau vai prabhaṃjanaḥ
english: Witnessing you beaten back, that bearer of fumes himself, the Wind, that breaketh everything before in wrath did not blow through the three worlds.

sanskrit: संभ्रांताः च सुराः सर्वे त्रैलोक्ये क्षुभिते सति
transliteration: saṃbhrāṃtāḥ ca surāḥ sarve trailokye kṣubhite sati
english: Thereat, all gods-lords of the universeinfluenced by fear in consequence of the triune world waxing agitated, began to path the wrathful Wind.

sanskrit: प्रसादिते च पवने ब्रह्मा तुभ्यम् वरम् ददौ
अशस्त्र वध्यताम् तात समरे सत्य विक्रम
transliteration: prasādite ca pavane brahmā tubhyam varam dadau
aśastra vadhyatām tāta samare satya vikrama
english: And on the Wind being mollified, Bra conferred on him a boon, saying,–O child, O you of prowess, (your son) shall be incapable of being slain in be by means of weapons.'

sanskrit: वज्रस्य च निपातेन विरुजम् त्वाम् समीक्ष्य च
सहस्र नेत्रः प्रीत आत्मा ददौ ते वरम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: vajrasya ca nipātena virujam tvām samīkṣya ca
sahasra netraḥ prīta ātmā dadau te varam uttamam
english: And seeing him sustain (serious) injury consequent on the impact of the thunder. He of a thousand eyes, pleased in his soul, also confer on (you) and excellent boon, O lord, saying, 'Your death: take place according to your will.' *Hanuman.

sanskrit: स्वच्छंदतः च मरणम् तव स्यात् इति वै प्रभो
स त्वम् केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीम विक्रमः
transliteration: svacchaṃdataḥ ca maraṇam tava syāt iti vai prabho
sa tvam kesariṇaḥ putraḥ kṣetrajo bhīma vikramaḥ

sanskrit: मारुतस्य औरसः पुत्रः तेजसा च अपि तत् समः
त्वम् हि वायु सुतो वत्स प्लवने च अपि तत् समः
transliteration: mārutasya aurasaḥ putraḥ tejasā ca api tat samaḥ
tvam hi vāyu suto vatsa plavane ca api tat samaḥ

sanskrit: वयम् अद्य गत प्राणा भवान् अस्मासु सांप्रतम्
दाक्ष्य विक्रम संपन्नः कपि राज इव अपरः
transliteration: vayam adya gata prāṇā bhavān asmāsu sāṃpratam
dākṣya vikrama saṃpannaḥ kapi rāja iva aparaḥ
english: The are the son of the Wind, my child-equal to him in power of leaping. Now we are without our lives. And you, endowed with dexterity and vigour, and like another I of the monkeys,+ are before us. *Sugriva.

sanskrit: त्रिविक्रमे मया तात स शैल वन कानना
त्रिः सप्त कृत्वः पृथिवी परिक्रान्ता प्रदक्षिणम्
transliteration: trivikrame mayā tāta sa śaila vana kānanā
triḥ sapta kṛtvaḥ pṛthivī parikrāntā pradakṣiṇam
english: On the occasion of Vişnu enveloping the earth with three steps, I, O child, had circa ambulated the earth with her mountains, woods and fore one and twenty times.

sanskrit: तथा च ओषधयो अस्माभिः संचिता देव शासनात्
निर्मथ्यम् अमृतम् याभिः तदा तदानीम् नो महत् बलम्
transliteration: tathā ca oṣadhayo asmābhiḥ saṃcitā deva śāsanāt
nirmathyam amṛtam yābhiḥ tadā tadānīm no mahat balam
english: Then, commissioned by the gods, had gathered annuals, which (bcing cast on the deep), cat ambrosia to come out after churning. At that time, god was our strength.

sanskrit: स इदानीम् अहम् वृद्धः परिहीन पराक्रमः
साम्प्रतम् कालम् अस्माकम् भवान् सर्व गुण अन्वितः
transliteration: sa idānīm aham vṛddhaḥ parihīna parākramaḥ
sāmpratam kālam asmākam bhavān sarva guṇa anvitaḥ
english: But now I have grown old, and prowess has left me. At present we have you, furnish with every virtue.

sanskrit: तत् विजृंभस्व विक्रांतः प्लवताम् उत्तमो हि असि
त्वत् वीर्यम् द्रष्टु कामा इयम् सर्वा वानर वाहिनी
transliteration: tat vijṛṃbhasva vikrāṃtaḥ plavatām uttamo hi asi
tvat vīryam draṣṭu kāmā iyam sarvā vānara vāhinī
english: Therefore, possessed of vigour, do I bestir yourself, and bound over (the main). You are the qualified of all. This entire monkey host is eager to bell your prowess.

sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठ हरि शार्दूल लंघयस्व महा अर्णवम्
परा हि सर्व भूतानाम् हनुमन् या गतिः तव
transliteration: uttiṣṭha hari śārdūla laṃghayasva mahā arṇavam
parā hi sarva bhūtānām hanuman yā gatiḥ tava
english: O redoubtable monkey, do you arise! leap over the mighty ocean. Your motion, Hanumān, asseth that of all beings.

sanskrit: विषाण्णा हरयः सर्वे हनुमन् किम् उपेक्षसे
विक्रमस्व महावेग विष्णुः त्रीन् विक्रमान् इव
transliteration: viṣāṇṇā harayaḥ sarve hanuman kim upekṣase
vikramasva mahāvega viṣṇuḥ trīn vikramān iva
english: All the monkeys are depressed. O Hanuman, did you overlook this? Put forth your you endowed with mighty vehemence, like Vişnu sing over the three worlds in three steps.

sanskrit: ततः कपीनाम् ऋषभेण चोदितःप्रतीत वेगः पवन आत्मजः कपिः
प्रहर्षयन् ताम् हरि वीर वाहिनीम्चकार रूपम् महत् आत्मनः तदा
transliteration: tataḥ kapīnām ṛṣabheṇa coditaḥpratīta vegaḥ pavana ātmajaḥ kapiḥ
praharṣayan tām hari vīra vāhinīmcakāra rūpam mahat ātmanaḥ tadā
english: Exhorted by foremost of monkeys, that one famed for has speech, that key, the offspring of the Wind-god, gladdening the monkey-chiefs, wore (a fit) shape for crossing the ocean.* *Another epithet of Hanumān, Pavanātmaja-son to the Wind?? on the score of Redundency.

sanskrit: तम् दृष्ट्वा जृंभमाणम् ते क्रमितुम् शत योजनम्
transliteration: tam dṛṣṭvā jṛṃbhamāṇam te kramitum śata yojanam
english: Seeing that foremost of monkeys enlarge his person for bossing over an hundred Yojanas, and suddenly filled with energy, (the monkeys) at once renounced sorrow, and, filled with light, set up ululations and fell to eulogizing the mighty Hanuman.

sanskrit: विनेदुः तुष्टुवुः च अपि हनूमन्तम् महाबलम्
transliteration: vineduḥ tuṣṭuvuḥ ca api hanūmantam mahābalam
english: Seeing that foremost of monkeys enlarge his person for bossing over an hundred Yojanas, and suddenly filled with energy, (the monkeys) at once renounced sorrow, and, filled with light, set up ululations and fell to eulogizing the mighty Hanuman.

sanskrit: प्रहृष्टा विस्मिताः च अपि ते वीक्षन्ते समंततः
त्रिविक्रम कृत उत्साहम् नारायणम् इव प्रजाः
transliteration: prahṛṣṭā vismitāḥ ca api te vīkṣante samaṃtataḥ
trivikrama kṛta utsāham nārāyaṇam iva prajāḥ
english: And, struck with amazement, they, (staying) all round, joyfully gazed (at him); even as creatures beheld Nārāyaṇa, then stretching forth his three steps, he prepared him (for the succeeding feat). And, eulogized by them, the odorous mighty Hanuman increased; and, flourishing his tail me joy, attained strength.

sanskrit: समाविद्ध्य च लांगूलम् हर्षात् बलम् उपेयिवान्
transliteration: samāviddhya ca lāṃgūlam harṣāt balam upeyivān
english: And, struck with amazement, they, (staying) all round, joyfully gazed (at him); even as creatures beheld Nārāyaṇa, then stretching forth his three steps, he prepared him (for the succeeding feat). And, eulogized by them, the odorous mighty Hanuman increased; and, flourishing his tail me joy, attained strength.
As, extolled by the principal derly monkeys, he became fraught with effulgence, his beauty as great. .

sanskrit: यथा विजृंभते सिंहो विवृते गिरि गह्वरे

transliteration: yathā vijṛṃbhate siṃho vivṛte giri gahvare

english: As a lion fills himself with vigour in an open we, so the son of the Wind-god filled himself with energy.

english: The face of him, as that intelligent one was filling, himself has force was aflame like a frying-pan, or like to themeless fire.

english: Rising in the midst of the monkeys, Hanumān has his down standing on end through joy, saluting the monkeys, said,

sanskrit: तस्य अहम् शीघ्र वेगस्य शीघ्र गस्य महात्मनः
मारुतस्य औरसः पुत्रः प्लवने च अस्मि तत् समः
transliteration: tasya aham śīghra vegasya śīghra gasya mahātmanaḥ

Begot from his loins, I am the son of fast-coursing and high-souled Wind, coursing swiftly am his equal in all these accomplishments.* *i.e. pertaining to leaping.

english: Resembling Mahāmeru, me shall behold, you monkeys, making my way, covering up sky, as if devouring up the heavens. I shall, leaping concentrating my energy, scatter the clouds, shake the I and suck up the ocean.

ऋते सुपर्ण राजानम् मारुतम् वा महाबलम्

english: The strength of Vinata's son the Wind-god's, or mine, (surpasses that of every creature). None save the sovereign of birds, or the exceeding mighty Wind, can follow me in flight.

english: In the twing an eye I shall spread through the unsupported lightning darting from clouds.

विष्णोः प्रक्रममाणस्य तदा त्रीन् विक्रमान् इव

english: And at the time of leaping over the ocean, my form shall resemble that of the energizing Vişņu, when He had assumed the triune energy.

english: In vehemence like to Garura, I shall, I conceive, go an Ayuta yojanas.

विक्रम्य सहसा हस्तात् अमृतम् तत् इह आनये

english: I can, suddenly summoning energy, bring hither ambrosia from the very grasp of Vāsava or Brahmā himself. I shall leap sheer over Lankā. Even this is my impression.

ṛṣīṇām ca prasādena kapi vṛddha matena ca

sīdan mahati kāṃtāre sārtha hīna iva adhva gaḥ

मनः समाधाय महाअनुभावोजगाम लंकाम् मनसा मनस्वी
transliteration: sa vegavān vega samāhita ātmāhari pravīraḥ para vīra hantā
manaḥ samādhāya mahāanubhāvojagāma laṃkām manasā manasvī
english: That intelligent, magnanimous and heroic monkey-destroyer of hostile heroes, endowed with speed, concentrating his soul on his energy, mentally went to Lankā.
Hanumăn then resolved to travel through the air or the path of Cāraņas (heavens), in quest of Jānaki who had taken away by Rävaņa.
In order to perform that arduous task he raised his head and stiffened his neck quite erect, for which he looked like a bull.

Then he, wise and mighty monkey walked over the earth, green with grass, with irresistible steps. At that time, he brushed aside all animals like a lion and crushed down many trees, and thereby scared away the feathered denizens of the forest.

Then he, wise and mighty monkey walked over the earth, green with grass, with irresistible steps. At that time, he brushed aside all animals like a lion and crushed down many trees, and thereby scared away the feathered denizens of the forest.
After this, he bowed down to the Sun, Indra, Svayambhu, Wind-god, and all beings with joined palms and then facing the west he saluted his father and then began to increase in dimension like the sea.

sanskrit: ततो हि ववृधे गन्तुं दक्षिणो दक्षिणां दिश्म्
transliteration: tato hi vavṛdhe gantuṃ dakṣiṇo dakṣiṇāṃ diśm
english: After this, he bowed down to the Sun, Indra, Svayambhu, Wind-god, and all beings with joined palms and then facing the west he saluted his father and then began to increase in dimension like the sea.
The foremost of the Vānaras at this stared at him, he swelled in size for the purpose of Rāma as the ocean swells on the full-moon days.
Hanumān got ready for crossing the ocean having grown his body immensely. He caught hold tightly of the mountain with his hands and feet.

sanskrit: सर्वतः संवृतः शैलो बभौ पुष्पमयो यथा
transliteration: sarvataḥ saṃvṛtaḥ śailo babhau puṣpamayo yathā

transliteration: salilaṃ saṃprasusrāva madaṃ matta iva dvipaḥ

transliteration: mumoca ca śilāḥ śailo viśālāḥ samanaḥśilāḥ

english: Big rocks bit by those snakes crumbled into pieces and those fragments began to burn with fire-like venom.

sanskrit: विषघ्नान्यपि नागानां न शेकुः शमितुं विषम्
transliteration: viṣaghnānyapi nāgānāṃ na śekuḥ śamituṃ viṣam
english: Although there were many medical herbs, capable of counteracting poison, which had sprung up on that mountain, could not neutralise that poison of the snakes.

At this sudden convulsion, the hermits thought that they were being driven by the Rākşasas. The Vidyādharas with their woman ran away from their drinking haunts, leaving their golden seats, goblets, bowls, delicious articles for chewing, various kinds of meat, oxen, hides and swords with golden hilts. Fair damsels wearing necklaces, bracelets, anklets and carnation garlands, besmeared with red sandal paste and with their eyes red with wine dallying in amorous sports being startled by this strange occurrence, with their lovers, rose in the sky and watched the thing with delightful curiosity from above.

Looking like a mountain, the hermits thought about Hanumān, son of wind-god, undertaken for the benefit of Rāma and Vānaras in general, and blessed that he would be able to cross the ocean, the abode of Varuņa easily.
Hearing this from the hermits, the Vidyādharas were struck with wonder and they repeatedly looked at Hanumān.

sanskrit: दुधुवे च स रोमाणि चकम्पे चाचलोपमः
transliteration: dudhuve ca sa romāṇi cakampe cācalopamaḥ
english: Meanwhile the fire-like mighty hero trembled in his limbs and his hairs stood on their ends, and he roared like the rumbling of a cloud.
He lashed his roundish tail covered with down and again on his back just to get ready for the spring. It seemed as if Garuda, the king of the birds, was flying off with a huge snake.
He lashed his roundish tail covered with down and again on his back just to get ready for the spring. It seemed as if Garuda, the king of the birds, was flying off with a huge snake.

sanskrit: ससाद च कपिः क्ट्यां चरणौ संचुकोच च
transliteration: sasāda ca kapiḥ kṭyāṃ caraṇau saṃcukoca ca
english: The monkey firmly planted his arins like bolts, on the mountain; then crouched at the waist and contracted his legs. Contracting his arms, neck and abdomen He, the glorious and powerful Hanumān then, mustered his strengh.

sanskrit: संहृत्य च भुजौ श्रीमांस्तथैव च शिरोधराम्
तेजः स्त्त्वं तथा वीर्यमाविवेश स वीर्यवान्
transliteration: saṃhṛtya ca bhujau śrīmāṃstathaiva ca śirodharām
tejaḥ sttvaṃ tathā vīryamāviveśa sa vīryavān
english: The monkey firmly planted his arins like bolts, on the mountain; then crouched at the waist and contracted his legs. Contracting his arms, neck and abdomen He, the glorious and powerful Hanumān then, mustered his strengh.

He looked up to survey the distance, he suspended his breath in the heart while looking into sky. Then doing firm his feet and contracting his ears in order to spring, addressing other Vanaras, mighty Hanuman said.

He looked up to survey the distance, he suspended his breath in the heart while looking into sky. Then doing firm his feet and contracting his ears in order to spring, addressing other Vanaras, mighty Hanuman said.
I shall reach Lankā with the velocity of wind, just like an arrow shot by Rāma and if I do not find Jānakī there I shall, at the same speed, go to the region of the gods.

sanskrit: न हि द्रक्ष्यामि यदि तां लङ्कायां जनकात्मजाम्
transliteration: na hi drakṣyāmi yadi tāṃ laṅkāyāṃ janakātmajām
english: I shall reach Lankā with the velocity of wind, just like an arrow shot by Rāma and if I do not find Jānakī there I shall, at the same speed, go to the region of the gods.

sanskrit: यदि वा त्रिदिवे सीतां न द्रक्ष्याम्यकृतश्रमः
transliteration: yadi vā tridive sītāṃ na drakṣyāmyakṛtaśramaḥ
english: If I do not see Sītā in heaven even after exerting myself, I shall bring Ravana, the ruler of Raksasas, in bondage. At anyway with success, I shall come with Sītā or then I shall bring Lankā uprooting it with Rāvana.

If I do not see Sītā in heaven even after exerting myself, I shall bring Ravana, the ruler of Raksasas, in bondage. At anyway with success, I shall come with Sītā or then I shall bring Lankā uprooting it with Rāvana.

With these words, Hanumān who was full of vigour, sprang into the air accounted himself like a compeer of Garuda. As he flew up with vehemence, trees growing on the mountain, were uprooted from all sides.

Hanumān thus being covered with buds and blossoms looked like a hill lit up with glowworms. Then the heavy trees being deprived of their flowers by the velocity of the flight began to drop down into the sea like mountains bode, afflicted with the fear of Mahendra.

Hanumān thus being covered with buds and blossoms looked like a hill lit up with glowworms. Then the heavy trees being deprived of their flowers by the velocity of the flight began to drop down into the sea like mountains bode, afflicted with the fear of Mahendra.
And strewn with various sprouts and buds and blossoms, the monkey resembling a mass of clouds, looked lovely like a bill filled with glowworms.

sanskrit: विमुक्तास्तस्य वेगेन मुक्त्वा पुष्पाणि ते द्रुमाः
transliteration: vimuktāstasya vegena muktvā puṣpāṇi te drumāḥ
english: And uprooted by the force of his rush, mose trees, their flowers fallen off, plunged into the sea, like friends returning to their homes (after having accompanied their friend some way).

And blown by the wind caused by the a monkey, the various variegated flowers of the trees the consequence of their lightness, showered down on the sea. And covered with heaps of fragrant flowers of diverse hues, the monkey resembled a mass of clouds embellished by lines of lightning

The waters of the ocean) strewn with blossoms carried off by his motion, operated like the sky garnished with charming stars (cresting the same). His arms stretched in the sky, seemed like five-hooded snakes issuing from mountain.
As he coursed the orbit of air, his eyes flashing like lightning, resembled two craters a glow on a mountain.

Beside his coppery nose, his face looked coppery, as looks the solar disc on the approach of eve. And the uplifted tail of the Wind-god's offspring engaged in bounding, appeared beautiful in the sky like the raised standard of Sakra.

sanskrit: दृश्यते सानुबन्धा च तथा स कपिकुञ्जरः
transliteration: dṛśyate sānubandhā ca tathā sa kapikuñjaraḥ

english: As he coursed above, on account of the reflection cast by his body (on the boson of the deep), the monkey* by his progress, looked link a bark swayed by the breeze. *Under water.

sanskrit: यं यं देशं समुद्रस्य जगाम स महाकपिः
स स तस्योरुवेगेन सोन्माद इव लक्ष्यते
transliteration: yaṃ yaṃ deśaṃ samudrasya jagāma sa mahākapiḥ
sa sa tasyoruvegena sonmāda iva lakṣyate
english: And wherever that mighty monkey went about the sea, the state of things appeared to undergo a violent convulsion owing to impetus imparted by his body.
That mighty monkey possessed of exceeding speed rushed on, raising multitudes of surges on the sea by his breast resembling rock.
And the wind begot of the monkey as well as that of the clouds, issuing out, made the dreadsounding ocean roll violently.
Pushing up multitudes of high-heaving billows from the salt waters, that tiger-like monkey rushed on separating earth and heaven.
And that one endued with vehement speed passed over surges in the mighty main resembling Mandara or Meru; as if counting them.
The waters lashed up to the clouds by the force (of his speed), looked like autumnal clouds overspreading the sky.
Then whales and alligators and fishes and tortoises appeared plainly visible, like the persons of individuals, when the cloth has been taken off then.

sanskrit: व्योम्नि तं कपिशार्दूलं सुपर्ण इति मेनिरे
transliteration: vyomni taṃ kapiśārdūlaṃ suparṇa iti menire
english: And sea-serpents, seeing that tiger-like monkey proceeding in the sky, took him for Suparna himself.
The shadow the leonine monkey, measuring ten Yojanas in width and thirty in length, seemed the handsome in consequence of his speed.

sanskrit: तस्य सा शुशुभे छाया वितता लवणाम्भसि
transliteration: tasya sā śuśubhe chāyā vitatā lavaṇāmbhasi
english: That shadow resembling masses of white clouds, rallying on the salt waters and following the wind-god's son, seemed exceedingly beautiful. on more
And that exceedingly energetic highly monkey possessed of a gigantic body, appeared splendid in the unsupported aerial way, like a winged mountain.

And the deep beside the course that was being vehemently pursued by that elephantine monkey, was suddenly urned into a water-course.* *The sense is hard to hit. The commentator says, that agitated by Hanuman's peed, the clouds began to pour down showers on the ocean.
And coursing through the regions of fowls like the monarch of the feathered race, Hanuman, pushing away masses of clouds, resembled the wind himself.
And colossal clouds scattered by the monkey, pale and crimson and blue and mangistha-hued, looked exceedingly lovely.
And now entering into the clouds, and now emerging from them, he looked like the moon, sometimes hid and sometimes visible.

sanskrit: प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा प्लवङ्गं त्वरितं तदा
transliteration: plavamānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā plavaṅgaṃ tvaritaṃ tadā
english: Beholding that monkey engaged in bounding with celerity, gods, Gandharvas and Dānavas began to strew blossoms (on him).

sanskrit: तताप न हि तं सूर्यः प्लवन्तं वानरोत्तमम्
transliteration: tatāpa na hi taṃ sūryaḥ plavantaṃ vānarottamam
english: As he was leaping, the Sun did not burn him; and the Wind ministered to him, for the success of Rāma's work.
And the saints hymned his praises, as he was leaping on in the sky. And applauding the ranger of forests, they raised the voice of song.
Nagas and Yaksas, and various (races of) Raksasas, eulogized (him), on beholding that tiger-like monkey, Hanumān, in the act of bounding.

sanskrit: तथा मया विधातव्यं विश्रमेत यथा कपिः
transliteration: tathā mayā vidhātavyaṃ viśrameta yathā kapiḥ

english: To golden summits of that mountain being thus lifted up, the dark-blue sky assumed the golden hue. And by those highly resplendent golden peaks that best of mountains assumed the brilliance of a thousand suns.

sanskrit: बुद्ध्वा तस्य कपेर्वेगं जहर्ष च ननन्द च
transliteration: buddhvā tasya kapervegaṃ jaharṣa ca nananda ca

english: Thereupon, with a glad heart assuming the semblance of a man ånd stationing himself upon his own summit, that mountain-chief addressed Hanumān, saying.
O best of monkeys, forsooth had you been engaged in this arduous task. Coming down on my peak do you take rest.

sanskrit: स त्वां रामहिते युक्तं प्रत्यर्चयति सागरः
transliteration: sa tvāṃ rāmahite yuktaṃ pratyarcayati sāgaraḥ
english: This ocean was reared by one born in the family of Raghus. And beholding you engaged on Rāma's behoof he is worshipping you.
The best and everlasting virtue consists in returning benefits to one who has benefited us. Bent on returning benefits to Raghu's race, he deserve respect from you.

And to welcome you properly I have been despatched by him with the message-traversing over a hundred yojans this monkey has been worn out with fatigue; let him voyage to the remaining way after resting for a while on your summit.

sanskrit: तिष्ठ त्वं हरिशार्दूल मयि विश्रम्य गम्यताम्
transliteration: tiṣṭha tvaṃ hariśārdūla mayi viśramya gamyatām

english: Do you therefore, O best of monkeys, remain here and take rest. And feasting on these many fragrant and sweet fruits and roots, O foremost of monkeys, do you relieve yourself of the toil and proceed.
O leader of monkeys, my relation with you is replete with many virtues and known all over the three worlds.
O Son of Maruta, O best of monkeys, I know you to be the foremost of all monkeys.
Even an ordinary guest should be adored by him who abide by virtue, what of you great as you are?
O you lion among monkeys, you are the son of Māruta, the foremost of celestials and are his equal in speed.

sanskrit: पूजिते त्वयि धर्मज्ञ पूजां प्राप्नोति मारुतः
तस्मात्त्वं पूजनीयो मे शृणु चाप्यत्र कारणम्
transliteration: pūjite tvayi dharmajña pūjāṃ prāpnoti mārutaḥ
tasmāttvaṃ pūjanīyo me śṛṇu cāpyatra kāraṇam
english: You that are conversant with virtue, being worshipped, Maruta himself receive offerings. You are therefore worth of my adoration. Hearken, there is another reason for it.
O worshipful one, in olden times, the mountains, gifted with wings, began to range all quarters with velocity like to Garuda.
They moving thus, the celestials, the ascetics, and all creatures became almost faint with fear of their falling down.

sanskrit: पक्षान् चिच्छेद वज्रेण तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः
transliteration: pakṣān ciccheda vajreṇa tatra tatra sahasraśaḥ
english: Highly enraged therefore, the thousand-eyed Deity, the performer of hundred sacrifices, hundred with his thunderbolt, the wings of hundreds and thousands of them.
When with his thunderbolt, the Lord of celestials, wroth, approached me, I was all on a sudden thrown down by the high-souled Wind.
O best of monkeys I was these cast done in this salt ocean and preserved unhurt by your ancestors having my wings hid.

sanskrit: ततोऽहं मानयामि त्वां मान्यो हि मम मारुतः
त्वया मे ह्येष संबन्धः कपिमुख्य महागुणः
transliteration: tato'haṃ mānayāmi tvāṃ mānyo hi mama mārutaḥ
tvayā me hyeṣa saṃbandhaḥ kapimukhya mahāguṇaḥ
english: I shall therefore adore you and you are object of my worship O Maruta! And this my relation with you, O foremost of monkeys, is pregnant with many virtues.
The time for returning benefits having arrived, O high-souled one, it behove you to afford me and the ocean, satisfaction with a blessed heart.

sanskrit: श्रमं मोक्षय पूजां च गृहाण कपिसत्तम
प्रीतिं च बहुमन्यस्व प्रीतोऽस्मि तव दर्शनात्
transliteration: śramaṃ mokṣaya pūjāṃ ca gṛhāṇa kapisattama
prītiṃ ca bahumanyasva prīto'smi tava darśanāt
english: best of monkeys, relieve yourself of the fatigue and accept my affectionate offering, who am worthy of your respect. For his relationship with Wind whose son was Pitupanthānam-the text means "his father's path”-Wind being Hanumān's father the passage means-"aerial way."-Happy am I to see you. *Wrath in consequence of his inability to accept his offerings.
Being thus accosted by Maināka, the best of mountains, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys said, saying: Pleased am I and you had shown me enough of hospitality. Do you give up your wrath.

sanskrit: प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता न स्थातव्यमिहान्त्तरे
transliteration: pratijñā ca mayā dattā na sthātavyamihānttare
english: Business wants me to go soon and the time is well-nigh spent. Besides I have promised that I shall not halt at any intermediate place.
Thereupon touching the hill with his hand that highly energetic monkey wended, smiling his aerial way. Ocean
Thereat the and the mountain respectfully looked towards him and adored and welcomed him with blessings worthy of the occasion.
Leaving the mountain and the ocean and rising his up, he proceeded in the clear welkin traversing the aerial way.
Rising high up and casting his look down on the hill, that foremost of monkeys proceeded by the unsupported aerial track.
Beholding this singularly arduous work of Hanumān the celestials, the Siddhas and the ascetics all praised him.
All the celestials and others living on its summit, were highly pleased with the mountain arrayed in gold and having beautiful sides.
And the thousand-eyed Vásava was also pleased. And greatly pleased that highly intelligent Saci's lord, himself, addressed that best of mountains having picturesque sides, saying.

sanskrit: अभयं ते प्रयच्छामि तिष्ठ सौम्य यथासुखम्
transliteration: abhayaṃ te prayacchāmi tiṣṭha saumya yathāsukham
english: Greatly delighted am I, O lord of mountains, O you having golden peaks. 'No fear' I do declare to you. Proceedest you therefore, at your ease, O gently one!
Greatly had you hoped Hanumān, crossin fearlessly an unceasingly, over hundred yojanas so that he might not fall in danger.

sanskrit: सत्क्रियां कुर्वता तस्य तोषितोऽस्मि दृढं त्वया
transliteration: satkriyāṃ kurvatā tasya toṣito'smi dṛḍhaṃ tvayā
english: This monkey, is going in the interests of Rāma, Dasaratha's son—and you had welcomed him to the best of your mighty. Therefore I am greatly pleased with you.
Beholding that lord of celestials the performer of an hundred sacrifices, highly gratified, that best of mountains attained to an excess of joy.
Having received boons (from Indra) the Mountain occupied again its pristine place. And Hanumān in a short time crossed over the main.
Thereupon the celestial along with Gandharvas, Siddhas and the ascetics, spake to Surasā the mother of serpents, resembling the Sun, saying.
The highly effulgent son of Wind named Hanumān is crossing over the main. You are required to throw obstacles in his way for a while.
Assuming therefore the semblance of a terrible, grim-visaged Rāksasa, resembling a huge mountain and having terrible teeth and a face with coppery eyes, do you touch the welkin.
We are anxious to learn if he defeat you by some means or comes by grief."

Thus addressed the worshipful Surasā, having been honoured by the celestials, deformed and horrible and capable of exciting the fear of all beings, and obstructing Hanumān as he was coursing on, said.

sanskrit: विकृतं च विरूपं च सर्वस्य च भयावहम्
transliteration: vikṛtaṃ ca virūpaṃ ca sarvasya ca bhayāvaham
english: Thus addressed the worshipful Surasā, having been honoured by the celestials, deformed and horrible and capable of exciting the fear of all beings, and obstructing Hanumān as he was coursing on, said.
O foremost of monkeys, you had been ordained as my fare by the gods themselves. I will eat you up, do you enter my mouth.

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या चापि भार्यया
transliteration: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā
english: Thus accosted by Surasā, (Hanumān) with a glad countenance, said, Rama, son to Dasaratha, had entered the Dandaka forest in company with his brother, Lakşmaņa, and his wife, Vaidehi.

sanskrit: तस्य सीत हृता भार्या रावणेन यशस्विनी
transliteration: tasya sīta hṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena yaśasvinī
english: He having created hostility with the Rākṣasas, his illustrious wife, Sītā, while he was engrossed in some work, was carried away by Ravana.
At Rāma's command, I go to her as his envoy. It behove you, living in (Rāma's) dominions, to lend him your help.

sanskrit: आगमिष्यामि ते वक्त्रं सत्यं प्रतिशृणोमि ते
transliteration: āgamiṣyāmi te vaktraṃ satyaṃ pratiśṛṇomi te
english: Or having seen Mithila's daughter, as well as Rāma of untiring deeds, I will enter your mouth. This I promise you truly."
Thus addressed by Hanumān, Surasā, capable of wearing forms at will, said, “None shall pass me without being devoured by me, even this is the boon that I have received."
Then seeing him go away, the mother of the Nāgās, Surasā, desirous of essaying the strength of Hanuman, spoke.

sanskrit: वर एष पुरा दत्तो मम धात्रेति सत्वरा
transliteration: vara eṣa purā datto mama dhātreti satvarā
english: O best of monkeys, you shall have to go, today after entering my mouth. Even this is the boon that was conferred on me by the Deity. Having said this swiftly, she extending her capacious mouth wide, stood in front of the wind-god's son.

sanskrit: व्यादाय विपुलं वक्त्रं स्थिता सा मारुतेः पुरः
transliteration: vyādāya vipulaṃ vaktraṃ sthitā sā māruteḥ puraḥ

sanskrit: अब्रवीत्कुरु वै वक्त्रं येन मां विषहिष्यसे
वर एष पुरा दत्तो ममम् ध्रात्रेति सत्वरा
transliteration: abravītkuru vai vaktraṃ yena māṃ viṣahiṣyase
vara eṣa purā datto mamam dhrātreti satvarā
english: O best of monkeys, you shall have to go, today after entering my mouth. Even this is the boon that was conferred on me by the Deity. Having said this swiftly, she extending her capacious mouth wide, stood in front of the wind-god's son.

sanskrit: व्यादाय विपुलं वक्त्रं स्थिता सा मरुतेः पुरः
transliteration: vyādāya vipulaṃ vaktraṃ sthitā sā maruteḥ puraḥ

english: Threat, Surasă, extended her mouth forty yojanas, and thereupon the heroic Hanuman attained the altitude of fifty yojanas. Surasā enlarged her mouth sixty yojanas; and the heroic Hanumān anon heightened himself seventy yojanas. Şurasā widened her mouth eighty yoyanas; and Hanumān like to Fire raised himself ninety yojanas. And Surasā enlarged her mouth an hundred yojanas.

sanskrit: प्रविष्टोऽस्मि हि ते वक्त्रं दाक्षायणि नमोऽस्तु ते
transliteration: praviṣṭo'smi hi te vaktraṃ dākṣāyaṇi namo'stu te
english: O descendant of Dakşa, I have entered into your mouth. I bow down to you. I will repair to where Vaidehi is Your boon has proved trve.
Seeing him out of her mouth like the Moon out of the mouth of Rāhu, the venerable Surasā spoke to the monkey in her native form, saying.
For compassing your end, go, O foremost of monkeys, O mild one, at yours ease. And bringing to Vaidehī tidings touching the highsouled Rāghava do you meet her.

Witnessing that third act* The third feat, remarks Rāmānuja, is Hanuman's issuing out of Surasā's mouth. The preceding two are not mentioned. — of Hanumān's hard to perform, all beings extolled the monkey exclaiming, "Excellent! Excellent!" *A kind of also or agallochum.-Wilson.

Then he, resembling the wind in rush, arrived at the irrepressible ocean-abode of Varuņawent on, enveloping the welkin, on the aerial way, visited by showers, ranged by fowls and Gandharvas, graced by the rşis; embellished by shining vehicles rolling on, drawn by lions, or elephants, or tigers, or bird-serpents; presided over by eminently pious and righteous persons who have won the regions of heaven; and therefore appearing as if adorned by the (five) Fires; of the touch of Asani or Havya; (ever) served by Fire bearing sacrificial oblations; garnished by planets and stars and astral luminaries, and the Sun and the Moon; thronged with Maharsis, and Gandharvas and Nāgas, and Yaksas; and pure, and speckless;-the support of the universe-inhabited by Viswavasu; lorded over by the elephants of the king of the celestials; the orbit of the Sun and Moon, endowed with auspiciousness constituting the canopy of this live world blameless; and made by Brahmā; crowded with countless heroes, and Vidyādharas. And the wind-god's son Hanumnān, scattering clouds like the very Wind himself, coursed on in the aerial way like Garuda.

Then he, resembling the wind in rush, arrived at the irrepressible ocean-abode of Varuņawent on, enveloping the welkin, on the aerial way, visited by showers, ranged by fowls and Gandharvas, graced by the rşis; embellished by shining vehicles rolling on, drawn by lions, or elephants, or tigers, or bird-serpents; presided over by eminently pious and righteous persons who have won the regions of heaven; and therefore appearing as if adorned by the (five) Fires; of the touch of Asani or Havya; (ever) served by Fire bearing sacrificial oblations; garnished by planets and stars and astral luminaries, and the Sun and the Moon; thronged with Maharsis, and Gandharvas and Nāgas, and Yaksas; and pure, and speckless;-the support of the universe-inhabited by Viswavasu; lorded over by the elephants of the king of the celestials; the orbit of the Sun and Moon, endowed with auspiciousness constituting the canopy of this live world blameless; and made by Brahmā; crowded with countless heroes, and Vidyādharas. And the wind-god's son Hanumnān, scattering clouds like the very Wind himself, coursed on in the aerial way like Garuda.
And everywhere Hanumān, son to the wind god coursing through the unsupported sky, looked like the monarch of mountains furnished with wings.

sanskrit: प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा सिंहिका नाम राक्षसी
transliteration: plavamānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā siṃhikā nāma rākṣasī
english: And it came to pass that beholding him in the act of bounding, a Rākşasi named Sinhikā, of great age, and capable of wearing forms at will, thought herself.

sanskrit: इदं हि मे महत्सत्त्वं चिरस्य वशमागतम्
transliteration: idaṃ hi me mahatsattvaṃ cirasya vaśamāgatam
english: Today after a long lapse of time I shall have my fare. This mighty creature has after a long time come within my power.

Seeing that one of a distorted countenance, the wind-god's son thought, This one is, without doubt, the creature of wonderful form, possessed of exceeding prowess, given to securing its prey by means of its shadow, which had been described by the monkey-king.
And concluding her to be Sinhikā from her act, the intelligent monkey attaining a gigantic body, increased himself, like a mass of clouds during the rains.
Seeing the enlarged body of the mighty monkey, she extended her mouth measuring the sky and the nether regions. And roaring like to a mass of clouds, she rushed against the monkey.
Seeing the enlarged body of the mighty monkey, she extended her mouth measuring the sky and the nether regions. And roaring like to a mass of clouds, she rushed against the monkey.

sanskrit: कायमात्रं च मेधावी मर्माणि च महाकपिः
transliteration: kāyamātraṃ ca medhāvī marmāṇi ca mahākapiḥ
english: Thereat, that intelligent and mighty monkey marked her deformed and huge mouth, her body and its asticulated members.

sanskrit: स तस्या विवृते वक्त्रे वज्रसंहननः कपिः
transliteration: sa tasyā vivṛte vaktre vajrasaṃhananaḥ kapiḥ
english: And the redoubtable monkey hard as the thunderbolt, contracting himself in a moment, threw himself into her mouth.

sanskrit: ग्रस्यमानं यथा चन्द्रं पूर्णं पर्वणि राहुणा
transliteration: grasyamānaṃ yathā candraṃ pūrṇaṃ parvaṇi rāhuṇā
english: And the Siddhas and Chāraņas saw him sink in her mouth, as the full Moon is taken by Rāhu during a Parva.
Then tearing her limits by means of his sharp claws, the monkey, endowed with the celerity of thought, vehemently sprang forward.

sanskrit: तां तु दृष्ट्वा च धऋत्या च दाक्षिण्येन निपात्य च
transliteration: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā ca dhaṛtyā ca dākṣiṇyena nipātya ca
english: Then slaying her by his acuteness of sight, endurance and skill, that heroic, self-controlled monkey again began to swell himself amain.

sanskrit: तां हतां वानरेणाशु पतितां वीक्ष्य सिंहिकाम्
transliteration: tāṃ hatāṃ vānareṇāśu patitāṃ vīkṣya siṃhikām

sanskrit: भीममद्य कृतं कर्म महत्सत्त्वं त्वया हतम्
transliteration: bhīmamadya kṛtaṃ karma mahatsattvaṃ tvayā hatam

sanskrit: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव
transliteration: yasya tvetāni catvāri vānarendra yathā tava

sanskrit: कायवृद्धिं प्रवेगं च मम दृष्ट्वव राक्षसाः
transliteration: kāyavṛddhiṃ pravegaṃ ca mama dṛṣṭvava rākṣasāḥ

english: Thus wearing various graceful forms, that one, acting after reflection, having come to the other shore of the ocean incapable of being reached by others, on looking over his (immensely magnified person), reduced his body (to its former size).

That high-souled one resembling a cloudy pavilion, alighted on the (foremost) summit of the splendid mountain, Samva; crested with picturesque peaks; and abounding in ketakas, uddalakas and cocoanuts.
And reaching the shore of the sea, and beholding Lankā on the top of that foremost of mountains, the monkeys renouncing his native form, fell on that mountain, agitating birds and beasts.

sanskrit: त्रिकूटशिखरे लङ्कां स्थितां स्वस्थो ददर्श ह
transliteration: trikūṭaśikhare laṅkāṃ sthitāṃ svastho dadarśa ha
english: Having crossed over the ocean incapable of being repressed, that one endowed with great strength, staying at the plateau of Chitrakūta, and having refreshed himself, cast his eyes on Laukā.
And covered with showers of blossoms poured down by the trees, that monkey possessed of prowess then appeared there like Puspamaya.* *A monkey so named.
Having cleared an hundred Yoyanas, that monkey gifted with first-rate prowess, did not heave sighs or feel any fatigue.
I am competent to bound over many hundreds of Yojanas. What then is this end of the ocean measuring an hundred Yojanas only?

sanskrit: स तु वीर्यवतां श्रेष्ठः प्लवतामपि चोत्तमः
transliteration: sa tu vīryavatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ plavatāmapi cottamaḥ
english: That foremost of those endowed with energy and the prime of monkeys, gifted with speed, went to Laikā,* having crossed over the mighty main. *Descending, remarks the commentator, from the mountain-summit.

sanskrit: शाद्वलानि च नीलानि गन्धवन्ति वनानि च
गण्डवन्ति च मध्येन जगाम नगवन्ति च
transliteration: śādvalāni ca nīlāni gandhavanti vanāni ca
gaṇḍavanti ca madhyena jagāma nagavanti ca
english: Seeing blue lawns, and perfumed woods, replete with honey and filled with mountains, he held his way by the central thoroughfare.
That foremost of monkeys, the energetic Hanumān, went by hills filled with trees, and ranges of blossoming woods.

sanskrit: स नगाग्रे च तां लङ्कां ददर्श पवनात्मजः
transliteration: sa nagāgre ca tāṃ laṅkāṃ dadarśa pavanātmajaḥ
english: And stationing himself in that mountain, the offspring of the Wind-god beheld woods and groves and Lankā established at the brow of the mountain.

sanskrit: ददर्श हनुमान् लङ्कां दिवि देवपुरीं यथा
transliteration: dadarśa hanumān laṅkāṃ divi devapurīṃ yathā

english: And that graceful monkey saw Lankā situated on the top of the mountain, filled with splendid yellow-white palaces, like to a city stationed in the sky ruled by the lord of Rākşasas and reared by Viśvakarmā himself. And the monkey, Hanumān, beheld Lankā, as if moving in the sky: with her walls furnished with daises for her hips, the immense waters and woods for her cloth, Śataghnīs and darts for her hair ends: and pennons on her walls for earrings, built as if by the agency of the Mind; and constructed by Viśvakarmā himself.

sanskrit: तस्याश्च महतीं गुप्तिं सागरं च निरीक्ष्य सः
रावणं च रिपुं घोरं चिन्तयामास वानरः
transliteration: tasyāśca mahatīṃ guptiṃ sāgaraṃ ca nirīkṣya saḥ
rāvaṇaṃ ca ripuṃ ghoraṃ cintayāmāsa vānaraḥ
english: And arriving at the Northern gate resembling the mansion of Kailāsa, and cleaving, as it were, the welkin, and as if holding the firmament with lofty and glorious edifices, and observing the sea; his dreadful enemy, Ravana; the city teeming with poisonous snakes, as well as the method of defence (displayed in it)-the monkeys reflected, Even if the monkeys came here, they should fail to achieve success; for Lankā is incapable of being taken in battle by the celestials themselves.

sanskrit: न हि युद्धेन व लङ्का शक्या जेतुं सुरैरपि
transliteration: na hi yuddhena va laṅkā śakyā jetuṃ surairapi

sanskrit: इमां तु विषमां दुर्गां लङ्कां रावणपालिताम्
प्राप्यापि स महाबाहुः किम् करिष्यति राघवः
transliteration: imāṃ tu viṣamāṃ durgāṃ laṅkāṃ rāvaṇapālitām
prāpyāpi sa mahābāhuḥ kim kariṣyati rāghavaḥ
english: Even if the mighty-armed Rāghava should reach this terrible-looking and impregnable Lankā reared by Rāvana, what could he do?

sanskrit: न दानस्य न भेदस्य नैव युद्धस्य दृश्यते
transliteration: na dānasya na bhedasya naiva yuddhasya dṛśyate
english: Opportunity find I none either for conciliation with the Raksasas, or for (winning them over) by gifts, or for sowing dissensions among them, or for conquering them in fight.
Of all the monkeys, four only endowed with (exceptional) celerity, viz., Vāli's son, Nīla, the intelligent king, and myself, heave the power to come over here.

sanskrit: यावज्जानामि वैदेहीं यदि जीवति वा न वा
transliteration: yāvajjānāmi vaidehīṃ yadi jīvati vā na vā
english: When I have ascertained whether Vaidehī is alive or not, I shall, after interviewing Janaka's daughter, think about this.
Then that elephantine monkey, stationed on the summit of that mountain, for a while bethought himself as the success of Rāma.* *About rescuing his wife.

sanskrit: अनेन रूपेण मया न शक्या रक्षसां पुरी
transliteration: anena rūpeṇa mayā na śakyā rakṣasāṃ purī
english: I cannot in this form succeed in entering the city of the Rākşasas, guarded by wily and powerful Rākṣasas.
I should, while engaged in searching for Jānaki, deceive all the strong and highly energetic Rākşasas gifted with prowess.

sanskrit: लक्ष्यालक्ष्येण रूपेण रात्रौ लङ्का पुरी मया
प्रवेष्टुं प्राप्तकालं मे कृत्यं साधयितुं महत्
transliteration: lakṣyālakṣyeṇa rūpeṇa rātrau laṅkā purī mayā
praveṣṭuṃ prāptakālaṃ me kṛtyaṃ sādhayituṃ mahat
english: For attaining this mighty object, it behove me to enter Lankā at night in a shape invisible yet well suited to the end in view.

sanskrit: तां पुरीं तादृशीं दृष्ट्वा दुराधर्शां सुरासुरैः
transliteration: tāṃ purīṃ tādṛśīṃ dṛṣṭvā durādharśāṃ surāsuraiḥ
english: Beholding the city in that state, difficult of being subdued by the celestials and Asuras (combined), Hanumān, sighing moment arily, thought within himself,
How can I, without being discovered by the impious lord of Rākşasas, Rāvana, succeed in seeing Janaka's daughter, Maithili?
How can the work of Rāma cognizant of self (be so managed that it) may not be brought to naught? How can I see Janaka's daughter singly in secret?
Action on the very eve of success, on being obstructed by adverse season and place, and through the agency of unreflecting envoys come to nought, even as darkness is dispelled on sunrise.

In respect of what should he undertaken and what not, even the certain decision (of a master assisted by his counsellors), because of a heedless messenger, dose not appear in all its beauty: messengers (foolish) yet proud of their knowledge, bring every business to nought.

sanskrit: न विनश्येत्कथं कार्यं वैक्लब्यम् न कथं भवेत्
लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य कथं नु न वृथा भवेत्
transliteration: na vinaśyetkathaṃ kāryaṃ vaiklabyam na kathaṃ bhavet
laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya kathaṃ nu na vṛthā bhavet
english: How can I so manage that my business may not suffer? How can I avoid recklessness? How can my bounding over the deep bear fruit?

sanskrit: मयि दृष्टे तु रक्षोभी रामस्य विदितात्मनः
transliteration: mayi dṛṣṭe tu rakṣobhī rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
english: On my being seen by the Rākşasas, the work of Rāma cognizant of self, desirous of the destruction of Ravana, shall be marred.

sanskrit: न हि शक्यं क्वचित् स्थातुमविज्ञातेन राक्षसैः
transliteration: na hi śakyaṃ kvacit sthātumavijñātena rākṣasaiḥ
english: Even if I wear a Rākşasa form, I cannot anywhere remain undiscovered by the Rākṣasas.
What shall I say of any other form? Even the wind, I conceive dose not stray here, unperceived. Nothing whatever is here that is unknown to the Räkşasas of redoubtable deeds.

sanskrit: इहाहं यदि तिष्ठामि स्वेन रूपेण संवृतः
transliteration: ihāhaṃ yadi tiṣṭhāmi svena rūpeṇa saṃvṛtaḥ
english: Should I stay here embodied in my native form, I shall come by destruction; and the interest also of my master shall suffer.

sanskrit: तदहं स्वेन रूपेण रजन्यां ह्रस्वतां गतः
transliteration: tadahaṃ svena rūpeṇa rajanyāṃ hrasvatāṃ gataḥ
english: Therefore, diminishing myself, I shall at night, for compassing the welfare of Rāghava, enter Lankā is my own form.
Entering at night Råvaņa's capital difficult of access, I shall, obtaining entry into every dwelling seek Janaka's daughter.'
Having made up his mind thus, the heroic Hanumān, extremely eager to see Vaidehi, wished for the setting of the sun.

sanskrit: सूर्ये चास्तं गते रात्रौ देहं संक्षिप्य मारुतिः
transliteration: sūrye cāstaṃ gate rātrau dehaṃ saṃkṣipya mārutiḥ
english: On the sun having set, at night the Windgod's son, contracting his person, reducing himself to the dimensions of a cat, became wonderful to behold.

At dusk, the powerful Hanumān, springing up, entered the charming city of Lankā with its well divided highways; furnished with rows of edifices having golden pillars, and net-works, resembling the metropolis of the Gandharvas.

At dusk, the powerful Hanumān, springing up, entered the charming city of Lankā with its well divided highways; furnished with rows of edifices having golden pillars, and net-works, resembling the metropolis of the Gandharvas.
He saw that splendid city containing sevenstoried and eight-storied edifices, studded with crystal and adorned with gold. And the dwellings of the Rākṣasas were embellished with these (ornaments).
He saw that splendid city containing sevenstoried and eight-storied edifices, studded with crystal and adorned with gold. And the dwellings of the Rākṣasas were embellished with these (ornaments).

sanskrit: काञ्चनानि च चित्राणि तोरणानि च रक्षसाम्
transliteration: kāñcanāni ca citrāṇi toraṇāni ca rakṣasām
english: And graceful golden gateways belonging to the Rākṣasas everywhere lent splendour to Lankā adorned all over.
Beholding Lankā, wonderful and of inconceivable loveliness, the mighty monkey, desirous of beholding Vaidehī, became depressed and delighted at the same time.

And he (entered Lankā) engarlanded with yellow edifices joined together, with the ornamented arches of her gateways furnished with nets of precious gold; famed (all over the world); ruled by the arm of Ravana, and vigilantly guarded by night-rangers of dreadful strength.
As if ministering to him,* the Moon furnished with many thousands of rays arose with the stars in the midst of the sky, spreading lunar light over all creatures. * Hanuman.
And that heroic monkey behold the Moon possessing the sheen of a conch, and hued like milk or the lotus-stalk, arisen and afloat (in the welkin), like a swan swimming in a tank.

sanskrit: स लम्ब शिखरे लम्बे लम्ब तोयद सम्निभे
सत्त्वम् आस्थाय मेधावी हनुमान् मारुत आत्मजः
transliteration: sa lamba śikhare lambe lamba toyada samnibhe
sattvam āsthāya medhāvī hanumān māruta ātmajaḥ

sanskrit: निशि लन्काम् महा सत्त्वः विवेश कपि कुन्जरः
रम्य कानन तोय आढ्याम् पुरीम् रावण पालिताम्
transliteration: niśi lankām mahā sattvaḥ viveśa kapi kunjaraḥ
ramya kānana toya āḍhyām purīm rāvaṇa pālitām

sanskrit: शारद अम्बु धर प्रख्यैः भवनैः उपशोभिताम्
सागर उपम निर्घोषाम् सागर अनिल सेविताम्
transliteration: śārada ambu dhara prakhyaiḥ bhavanaiḥ upaśobhitām
sāgara upama nirghoṣām sāgara anila sevitām

sanskrit: चारु तोरण निर्यूहाम् पाण्डुर द्वार तोरणाम्
transliteration: cāru toraṇa niryūhām pāṇḍura dvāra toraṇām

sanskrit: भुजग आचरिताम् गुप्ताम् शुभाम् भोगवतीम् इव
ताम् सविद्युत् घन आकीर्णाम् ज्योतिः मार्ग निषेविताम्
transliteration: bhujaga ācaritām guptām śubhām bhogavatīm iva
tām savidyut ghana ākīrṇām jyotiḥ mārga niṣevitām

sanskrit: चण्ड मारुत निर्ह्रादाम् यथा इन्द्रस्य अमरावतीम्
transliteration: caṇḍa māruta nirhrādām yathā indrasya amarāvatīm

sanskrit: विस्मय आविष्ट हृदयः पुरीम् आलोक्य सर्वतः
transliteration: vismaya āviṣṭa hṛdayaḥ purīm ālokya sarvataḥ

sanskrit: मणि स्फटिक मुक्ताभिः मणि कुट्टिम भूषितैः
तप्त हाटक निर्यूहैः राजत अमल पाण्डुरैः
transliteration: maṇi sphaṭika muktābhiḥ maṇi kuṭṭima bhūṣitaiḥ
tapta hāṭaka niryūhaiḥ rājata amala pāṇḍuraiḥ

sanskrit: वैदूर्य तल सोपानैः स्फाटिक अन्तर पाम्सुभिः
चारु सम्जवन उपेतैः खम् इव उत्पतितैः शुभैः
transliteration: vaidūrya tala sopānaiḥ sphāṭika antara pāmsubhiḥ
cāru samjavana upetaiḥ kham iva utpatitaiḥ śubhaiḥ

sanskrit: क्रौन्च बर्हिण सम्घुष्टे राज हम्स निषेवितैः
transliteration: kraunca barhiṇa samghuṣṭe rāja hamsa niṣevitaiḥ
english: Resounding with Krauñca as and peacocks; frequented by swans, and everywhere resonant with the sounds of trumpets and ornaments.

sanskrit: खम् इव उत्पतिताम् लन्काम् जहर्ष हनुमान् कपिः
transliteration: kham iva utpatitām lankām jaharṣa hanumān kapiḥ
english: And then beholding the city Lankā, resembling Vasvokasāra,* and appearing to mount to the welkin, the monkey Hanumān was filled with rapture. *Alaka.

sanskrit: ताम् समीक्ष्य पुरीम् लन्काम् राक्षस अधिपतेः शुभाम्
अनुत्तमाम् ऋद्धि युताम् चिन्तयाम् आस वीर्यवान्
transliteration: tām samīkṣya purīm lankām rākṣasa adhipateḥ śubhām
anuttamām ṛddhi yutām cintayām āsa vīryavān
english: And seeing the delightful, . divine and prosperous city of Lankā belonging to the lord of Rākşasas, that one endowed with prowess thought within himself,

sanskrit: न इयम् अन्येन नगरी शक्या धर्षयितुम् बलात्
रक्षिता रावण बलैः उद्यत आयुध धारिभिः
transliteration: na iyam anyena nagarī śakyā dharṣayitum balāt
rakṣitā rāvaṇa balaiḥ udyata āyudha dhāribhiḥ
english: This city protected by the forces of Rãvaņa with their hands holding upraised arms, is incapable of being forcibly subdued by any other.

sanskrit: कुमुद अन्गदयोः वा अपि सुषेणस्य महा कपेः
प्रसिद्धा इयम् भवेत् भूमिः मैन्द द्विविदयोः अपि
transliteration: kumuda angadayoḥ vā api suṣeṇasya mahā kapeḥ
prasiddhā iyam bhavet bhūmiḥ mainda dvividayoḥ api
english: This place can be easily entered by Kumuda, and Angada, as well as by that mighty monkey, Suşeņa; and also by Mainda and Dvivida. And there is way also for the offspring of the Sun, and that monkey, Kuśaparva, as well as of that foremost of monkeys, Rksya, and myself."

sanskrit: विवस्वतः तनूजस्य हरेः च कुश पर्वणः
ऋक्षस्य केतु मालस्य मम चैव गतिः भवेत्
transliteration: vivasvataḥ tanūjasya hareḥ ca kuśa parvaṇaḥ
ṛkṣasya ketu mālasya mama caiva gatiḥ bhavet

sanskrit: समीक्ष्य तु महा बाहः राघवस्य पराक्रमम्
लक्ष्मणस्य च विक्रान्तम् अभवत् प्रीतिमान् कपिः
transliteration: samīkṣya tu mahā bāhaḥ rāghavasya parākramam
lakṣmaṇasya ca vikrāntam abhavat prītimān kapiḥ
english: Having witnessed the prowess of Rāghava, as well as the vigour of Lakşmaņa, the monkey was filled with joy.

sanskrit: ताम् रत्न वसन उपेताम् कोष्ठ आगार अवतम्सकाम्
यन्त्र अगार स्तनीम् ऋद्धाम् प्रमदाम् इव भूषिताम्
transliteration: tām ratna vasana upetām koṣṭha āgāra avatamsakām
yantra agāra stanīm ṛddhām pramadām iva bhūṣitām

sanskrit: ताम् नष्ट तिमिराम् दीपैः भास्वरैः च महा गृहैः
नगरीम् राक्षस इन्द्रस्य ददर्श स महा कपिः
transliteration: tām naṣṭa timirām dīpaiḥ bhāsvaraiḥ ca mahā gṛhaiḥ
nagarīm rākṣasa indrasya dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ

sanskrit: सा तम् हरिवरम् दृष्ट्वा लङ्का रावणपालिता
transliteration: sā tam harivaram dṛṣṭvā laṅkā rāvaṇapālitā
english: Seeing that best of monkeys, Lankā, ruled by Rāvana arising of herself with her countenance rendered deformed, stood before the heroic son of the Wind and, emitting a tremendous roar, addressed the offspring of the Wind-god, saying,

Seeing that best of monkeys, Lankā, ruled by Rāvana arising of herself with her countenance rendered deformed, stood before the heroic son of the Wind and, emitting a tremendous roar, addressed the offspring of the Wind-god, saying,

sanskrit: कस्त्वम् केन च कार्येण इह प्राप्तो वनालय
कथय स्वेह यत्तत्त्वम् यावत्प्राणा धरन्ति ते
transliteration: kastvam kena ca kāryeṇa iha prāpto vanālaya
kathaya sveha yattattvam yāvatprāṇā dharanti te
english: O you that had the woods for the home, who are you? And on what errand had you come hither? Tell me while yet you had your vital powers left in you.

sanskrit: न शक्यम् खल्वियम् लङ्का प्रवेष्टुम् वानर त्वया
transliteration: na śakyam khalviyam laṅkā praveṣṭum vānara tvayā
english: O monkey, for certain you are unable to obtain entry into this Laňkā, protected by the forces of Rāvaņa, and carefully guarded on all sides.

sanskrit: कथयिष्यामि ते तत्त्वम् यन्मम् त्वम् परिपृच्छसि
transliteration: kathayiṣyāmi te tattvam yanmam tvam paripṛcchasi
english: Thereat, the heroic Hanumān spoke to her staying in front of him, “I shall tell you all about that anent which you questionest me. Who are you that having deformed eyes stayest at the gate of this city? And what for, O frightful one, do you rail at me in wrath?"

sanskrit: किमर्थम् चापि माम् रुद्ध्वा निर्भर्त्सयसि दारुणा
transliteration: kimartham cāpi mām ruddhvā nirbhartsayasi dāruṇā
english: Thereat, the heroic Hanumān spoke to her staying in front of him, “I shall tell you all about that anent which you questionest me. Who are you that having deformed eyes stayest at the gate of this city? And what for, O frightful one, do you rail at me in wrath?"
Hearing Hanumān's speech, Lankā, capable of wearing forms at will, waxing wroth addressed the Wind-god's offspring, saying,
I, who am incapable of being repressed, abiding by the mandate of the high-souled sovereign of the Rākşasas, protect this city.

sanskrit: न शक्या मामवज्ञाय प्रवेष्टुम् नगरी त्वया
अद्य प्राणैः परित्यक्तः स्वप्स्यसे निहतो मया
transliteration: na śakyā māmavajñāya praveṣṭum nagarī tvayā
adya prāṇaiḥ parityaktaḥ svapsyase nihato mayā
english: You are unable to enter this city, passing me by. You shall to-day, losing your life and slain by me, sleep (the sleep of death).

sanskrit: अहम् हि नगरी लङ्का स्वयमेव प्लवङ्गम
transliteration: aham hi nagarī laṅkā svayameva plavaṅgama
english: O monkey, I am the City of Lankā myself. I every way guard (all that is here.) that I told you.
Hearing Lankā's words, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, foremost of monkeys-exerting himself (to secure victory), stood like another hill.
Seeing her appear in the form of a deformed female, that foremost and best-of monkeys endued with intelligence, possessed of prowess, said.

sanskrit: इत्यर्थमिह सम्प्राप्तः परम् कौतूहलम् हि मे
transliteration: ityarthamiha samprāptaḥ param kautūhalam hi me
english: I will behold the city of Lanká, crowned with turrets, walls and ornamented arches. It is for this that I have come here, Great is my curiosity.
I come forsooth to see the woods and groves and gardens of Lankā here, as well as her principle edifices.

sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनम् श्रुत्वा लङ्का सा कामरूपिणी
transliteration: tasya tadvacanam śrutvā laṅkā sā kāmarūpiṇī
english: Hearing these words of his, Lankā capable of wearing forms at will, again addressed him in a speech fraught with dissonant letters:

sanskrit: न शक्यमद्य ते द्रष्टुम् पुरीयम् वनराधम
transliteration: na śakyamadya te draṣṭum purīyam vanarādhama
english: you of perverse understanding, O worst of monkeys, without in the first instance) vanquishing me, you cannot to-day behold this city ruled by the monarch of the Rākşasas.
Thereat that tiger of a monkey said to that female ranger of the night. After seeing this city, O gentle one, I shall go away even a I have come.

sanskrit: ततः कृत्वा महानादम् सा वै लङ्का भयावहम्
transliteration: tataḥ kṛtvā mahānādam sā vai laṅkā bhayāvaham
english: Thereupon, setting up a mighty and terrible roar, Laikā filled with vehemence, struck at Hanumān with her palm.

sanskrit: ततः स कपिशार्दुलो लङ्काया ताडितो भृशम्
transliteration: tataḥ sa kapiśārdulo laṅkāyā tāḍito bhṛśam
english: That tiger-like monkey, the energetic offspring of the wind-god, on being lustily struck by Larkā, emitted a tremendous roars.
And (Hanuman) fastened the fingers of his left hand into a box, and transported with rage, dealt it to her.

sanskrit: स्त्री चेति मन्यमानेन नातिक्रोधः स्वयम् कृतः
सा तु तेन प्रहारेण विह्वलाङ्गी नीशाचरी
transliteration: strī ceti manyamānena nātikrodhaḥ svayam kṛtaḥ
sā tu tena prahāreṇa vihvalāṅgī nīśācarī
english: Considering that she was a female he did not give way to excessive wrath. And struck at (by Hanumān), that ranger of the night, of a deformed face, her body overcome, suddenly dropped to the earth.

sanskrit: कृपाम् चकार तेजस्वी मन्यमानः स्त्रियम् तु ताम्
transliteration: kṛpām cakāra tejasvī manyamānaḥ striyam tu tām

sanskrit: अहं तु नगरी लङ्का स्वयमेव प्लवङ्गम
transliteration: ahaṃ tu nagarī laṅkā svayameva plavaṅgama

sanskrit: इदम् तु तथ्यम् शृणु वै ब्रुवन्त्य मे हरीश्वर
transliteration: idam tu tathyam śṛṇu vai bruvantya me harīśvara

sanskrit: स्वयम्भुवा पुरा दत्तम् वरदानम् यथा मम
transliteration: svayambhuvā purā dattam varadānam yathā mama

sanskrit: तदा त्वया हि विज्ञेयम् रक्षसाम् भयामागतम्
स हि म् समयः सौम्य प्राप्तोऽय तव द्र्शनात्
transliteration: tadā tvayā hi vijñeyam rakṣasām bhayāmāgatam
sa hi m samayaḥ saumya prāpto'ya tava drśanāt
english: When a certain monkey shall by his prowess, bring you under his sway, then shall you understand that a fear is come to me, in consequence of my meeting with you. The truth ordained by the self-create know no turning.
Entering this splendid city lying under an imprecation, governed by the chief of the Rāks asas, do you at your will happily repairing everywhere, search for the chaste daughter of Janaka. .

sanskrit: स निर्जत्य पुरीम् लण्का श्रेष्ठाम् ताम् कामरूपिणीम्
transliteration: sa nirjatya purīm laṇkā śreṣṭhām tām kāmarūpiṇīm
english: Having by his vigour vanquished the excellent City of Lankā capable of wearing forms at will, that exceedingly energetic foremost of monkeys, Hanumān, endued with prodigious prowess, Ieaped sheer over a wall, where doorway there was none; and that elephantine monkey gifted with great strength entered Lankā by night.

sanskrit: चक्रेणाऽथ पदम् सव्यम् शत्रूणाम् स तु मूर्धनि
transliteration: cakreṇā'tha padam savyam śatrūṇām sa tu mūrdhani

sanskrit: ततस्तु ताम् पुरीम् लङ्काम् रम्यामभिययौ कपिः
transliteration: tatastu tām purīm laṅkām ramyāmabhiyayau kapiḥ

sanskrit: हसित उद्घुष्ट निनदैः तूर्य घोष पुरः सरैः
वज्र अन्कुश निकाशैः च वज्र जाल विभूषितैः
transliteration: hasita udghuṣṭa ninadaiḥ tūrya ghoṣa puraḥ saraiḥ
vajra ankuśa nikāśaiḥ ca vajra jāla vibhūṣitaiḥ

sanskrit: गृह मेधैः पुरी रम्या बभासे द्यौः इव अम्बुदैः
प्रजज्वाल तदा लन्का रक्षः गण गृहैः शुभैः
transliteration: gṛha medhaiḥ purī ramyā babhāse dyauḥ iva ambudaiḥ
prajajvāla tadā lankā rakṣaḥ gaṇa gṛhaiḥ śubhaiḥ

sanskrit: सित अभ्र सदृशैः चित्रैः पद्म स्वस्तिक सम्स्थितैः
वर्धमान गृहैः च अपि सर्वतः सुविभाषितैः
transliteration: sita abhra sadṛśaiḥ citraiḥ padma svastika samsthitaiḥ
vardhamāna gṛhaiḥ ca api sarvataḥ suvibhāṣitaiḥ
english: Then Lankā, with handsome and variegated mansions of Rākṣasas, resembling white clouds and arranged like lotus-leaves; and adorned on all sides with structures superscribed 'Vardhamāna,' shone forth in all it glory.

sanskrit: ताम् चित्र माल्य आभरणाम् कपि राज हितम् करः
राघव अर्थम् चरन् श्रीमान् ददर्श च ननन्द च
transliteration: tām citra mālya ābharaṇām kapi rāja hitam karaḥ
rāghava artham caran śrīmān dadarśa ca nananda ca
english: And that graceful one serving in the interests of the king of monkeys, ranging for Rāma's behoof, beheld (Lankā) adorned with variegated wreaths; and was highly delighted.

sanskrit: शुश्राव मधुरम् गीतम् त्रि स्थान स्वर भूषितम्
स्त्रीणाम् मद समृद्धानाम् दिवि च अप्सरसाम् इव
transliteration: śuśrāva madhuram gītam tri sthāna svara bhūṣitam
strīṇām mada samṛddhānām divi ca apsarasām iva

transliteration: śuśrāva kāncī ninadam nūpurāṇām ca nihsvanam

transliteration: āsphoṭita ninādāmaḥ ca kṣveḍitāmaḥ ca tataḥ tataḥ
śuśrāva japatām tatra mantran rakṣogṛheṣu vai

रावण स्तव सम्युक्तान् गर्जतः राक्षसान् अपि

rāvaṇa stava samyuktān garjataḥ rākṣasān api

ददर्श मध्यमे गुल्मे राक्षसस्य चरान् बहून्
transliteration: rāja mārgam samāvṛtya sthitam rakṣaḥ balam mahat
dadarśa madhyame gulme rākṣasasya carān bahūn

sanskrit: दीक्षितान् जटिलान् मुण्डान् गः अजिन अम्बर वाससः
दर्भ मुष्टि प्रहरणान् अग्नि कुण्ड आयुधामः तथा
transliteration: dīkṣitān jaṭilān muṇḍān gaḥ ajina ambara vāsasaḥ
darbha muṣṭi praharaṇān agni kuṇḍa āyudhāmaḥ tathā

sanskrit: कूट मुद्गर पाणीमः च दण्ड आयुध धरान् अपि
एक अक्ष अनेक कर्णामः च चलल् लम्ब पयः धरान्
transliteration: kūṭa mudgara pāṇīmaḥ ca daṇḍa āyudha dharān api
eka akṣa aneka karṇāmaḥ ca calal lamba payaḥ dharān

sanskrit: करालान् भुग्न वक्त्रामः च विकटान् वामनामः तथा
धन्विनः खड्गिनः चैव शतघ्नी मुसल आयुधान्
transliteration: karālān bhugna vaktrāmaḥ ca vikaṭān vāmanāmaḥ tathā
dhanvinaḥ khaḍginaḥ caiva śataghnī musala āyudhān

transliteration: parigha uttama hastāmaḥ ca vicitra kavaca ujjvalān

transliteration: virūpān bahu rūpāmaḥ ca surūpāmaḥ ca suvarcasaḥ

transliteration: śakti vṛkṣa āyudhāmaḥ caiva paṭṭiśa aśani dhāriṇaḥ

स्रग्विणः त्व् अनुलिप्तामः च वर आभरण भूषितान्
transliteration: kṣepaṇī pāśa hastāmaḥ ca dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ
sragviṇaḥ tv anuliptāmaḥ ca vara ābharaṇa bhūṣitān
english: And (Hanuman) saw also various weapons; and those having for their arms darts and vrikshas, or bearing patticas and asanis, or having Kshepanis* and nooses in their hands, saw that mighty monkey, or wearing wreaths, or having their persons daubed with pastes, or adorned with nobel ornaments, or clad in various kinds of raiment; and many a one ranging wherever he listed. *A short arrow thrown from the hand, or shot

sanskrit: तीक्ष्ण शूल धरामः चैव वज्रिणः च महा बलान्
transliteration: tīkṣṇa śūla dharāmaḥ caiva vajriṇaḥ ca mahā balān

sanskrit: शत साहस्रम् अव्यग्रम् आरक्षम् मध्यमम् कपिः
transliteration: śata sāhasram avyagram ārakṣam madhyamam kapiḥ
english: And those holding sharpened javelins; and mighty ones bearing Vajras; and hundreds and thousands of warriors garrisoned in the central courtyard and engaged in vigilantly guarding the central courtyard and engaged in vigilantly guarding the interior, having been directed by the lord of the Raksas, saw the monkey.

sanskrit: प्राकार आवृतम् अत्यन्तम् ददर्श स महा कपिः
transliteration: prākāra āvṛtam atyantam dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ

sanskrit: त्रिविष्टप निभम् दिव्यम् दिव्य नाद विनादितम्
वाजि हेषित सम्घुष्टम् नादितम् भूषणैः तथा
transliteration: triviṣṭapa nibham divyam divya nāda vināditam
vāji heṣita samghuṣṭam nāditam bhūṣaṇaiḥ tathā

sanskrit: रथैः यानैः विमानैः च तथा गज हयैः शुभैः
वारणैः च चतुः दन्तैः श्वेत अभ्र निचय उपमैः
transliteration: rathaiḥ yānaiḥ vimānaiḥ ca tathā gaja hayaiḥ śubhaiḥ
vāraṇaiḥ ca catuḥ dantaiḥ śveta abhra nicaya upamaiḥ

sanskrit: भूषितम् रुचिर द्वारम् मत्तैः च मृग पक्षिभिः
राक्षस अधिपतेः गुप्तम् आविवेश गृहम् कपिः
transliteration: bhūṣitam rucira dvāram mattaiḥ ca mṛga pakṣibhiḥ
rākṣasa adhipateḥ guptam āviveśa gṛham kapiḥ

english: He (Hanumān) entered Rāvana's inner apartment girt round with a wall consisting of blazing gold and Jambúnada;* having its top decorated with costly gems and pearls; and worshipped with excellent black Aguru and sandal. * Jambunada is a kind of gold having sixteen diverse colours.
Like a swan in a silver cage, like a lion in a cave in Mandara, like a hero on a haughty elephant, appeared the Moon in the middle of the sky.

the Moon resembled a sharp-horned bull, or a mighty white-hued hill with towering summits, or an elephant with his horns plated with gold. And with (the mark of) the horn.* *The sun. It is a planet in Hindu cosmogony.

And, with his dirt composed of particles of cool water removed; and the darkness dispelled in consequence of the vicinity of the mighty planet; and with his spots appearing clcar because of his shining appearance, appeared (the hare-marked worshipful Moon in full splendour.
Like a lion on coming out of his cavern, or a lordly elephant on entering into the thick of a mighty encounter, or a monarch on obtaining a kingdom, appeared the Moon in full splendour.

And now appeared the revered Mid-night, chasing away darkness with the Moon displayed, when flesh-eating (Raksasas) lend full liberty to their vicious appetite for flesh; and when disputes between lovers cease, and which bring down heaven itself.

The sounds of strings sweet to the ear spread around; females sleep besides their husbands; and night-rangers, given to astounding and terrible acts, are, in the same way, out, indulging in their sports.

The intelligent monkey saw mansions crowded with (Raksasas), some inebriate with wine and other with wealth, and abounding in cars and horses and golden seats; and fraught with the grace got of heroism.
And (Raksasas) were parleying, moving about their plump arms, railing at each other; and throwing intemperate speeches at each other.
(Hanumān saw) Raksasas striking at their chests (by way of challenge). sinking on the persons of their beloved, wearing diverse habiliments, or stretching their tough bows.
And (he) saw debonair damsels daubing their frames with pastes; and others, again, sleeping, and fair-faced wenches smiling, and others sighing hard under the influence of anger.
And with gigantic elephants roaring, (the place), honoured by pious persons, with its heroes heaving sighs looked exceedingly beautiful like a lake in which serpents are sighing forth.

In that apartment (Hanumān) saw persons of commanding understandings, endowed with a tongue, instinct with the spirit of reverence-the foremost men of all this world, and bearing euphonious appellations, and clad in diverse attires.

sanskrit: ननन्द दृष्ट्वा स च तान् सुरूपा
transliteration: nananda dṛṣṭvā sa ca tān surūpā
english: And beholding those well-formed people, whose conduct was of a piece with their many virtues, (Hanumān) rejoiced exceedingly. And he saw some having beautiful forms, and others deformed, and both possessed of splendour.

And (Hanumān) saw there their wives worthy of noble ornaments and endowed with eminent beauty; of spotless character; possessing great potency; like to stars in point of excellency of conduct, displaying side-glances and other tokens of dalliance, engaged in dear driking.
At dead of night Hanuman saw some females blazing in beauty affected simultaneously with bashfulness and bliss, on being embraced by their paramours, like birds embracing their mates.

The sensible Hanumān saw there other females scated in stately halls, lying in happiness on the laps of their lovers, beloved of their lords-intent on virtue, married women, under the influence of Madana.
Hanumān saw some without sheets, like to golden streaks, paragons among women of the hue of molten gold, and some of a moon-like complexion, endued with lovelines, bereft of their beloved.

That exceedingly heroic monkey saw females in their homes experiencing the height of joy in the company of their beloved dear to their souls; charming with blossoms; filled with gladness; and enchaining the hearts of their lords with their loveiness
And Hanumān saw crowds of faces like to the Moon displayed, with elegant eyes furnished with lovely lashes, and side-long looks; an multitudes of ornaments resembling beautiful lines of lighting.

But Hanumān saw not Sītā, of the highest lineage, ever abiding by the way of righteousness; born in a royal line, like to a delightful and well-begot plant, of a slender frame, sprung from the mind (of Brahmä himself);

sanskrit: स निकामम् विमानेषु विषण्णः काम रूपधृत्
transliteration: sa nikāmam vimāneṣu viṣaṇṇaḥ kāma rūpadhṛt
english: Wending about at will on the roofs of sevenstoried edifices, that monkey capable of assuming any form that he chose, began Lankā with speed.

sanskrit: आससाद अथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षस इन्द्र निवेशनम्
transliteration: āsasāda atha lakṣmīvān rākṣasa indra niveśanam
english: And (at length) that auspicious one arrived at the mansion of the Rākṣasa chief, surrounded by a shining wall hued like the Sun;

sanskrit: रक्षितम् राक्षसैर् भीमैः सिम्हैर् इव महद् वनम्
transliteration: rakṣitam rākṣasair bhīmaiḥ simhair iva mahad vanam

sanskrit: रूप्य कोप हितैः चित्रैः तोरणैर् हेम भूषितैः
विचित्राभिः च कक्ष्याभिर् द्वारैः च रुचिरैर् व्Rतम्
transliteration: rūpya kopa hitaiḥ citraiḥ toraṇair hema bhūṣitaiḥ
vicitrābhiḥ ca kakṣyābhir dvāraiḥ ca rucirair vtam

sanskrit: गज आस्थितैर् महा मात्रैः शूरैः च विगत श्रमैः
transliteration: gaja āsthitair mahā mātraiḥ śūraiḥ ca vigata śramaiḥ

sanskrit: सिम्ह व्याघ्र तनु त्राणैर् दान्त कान्चन राजतैः
घोषवद्भिर् विचित्रैः च सदा विचरितम् रथैः
transliteration: simha vyāghra tanu trāṇair dānta kāncana rājataiḥ
ghoṣavadbhir vicitraiḥ ca sadā vicaritam rathaiḥ

sanskrit: बहु रत्न समाकीर्णम् पर अर्ध्य आसन भाजनम्
महा रथ समावासम् महा रथ महा आसनम्
transliteration: bahu ratna samākīrṇam para ardhya āsana bhājanam
mahā ratha samāvāsam mahā ratha mahā āsanam

sanskrit: दृश्यैः च परम उदारैः तैः तैः च मृग पक्षिभिः
transliteration: dṛśyaiḥ ca parama udāraiḥ taiḥ taiḥ ca mṛga pakṣibhiḥ

sanskrit: विनीतैर् अन्त पालैः च रक्षोभिः च सुरक्षितम्
मुख्याभिः च वर स्त्रीभिः परिपूर्णम् समन्ततः
transliteration: vinītair anta pālaiḥ ca rakṣobhiḥ ca surakṣitam
mukhyābhiḥ ca vara strībhiḥ paripūrṇam samantataḥ

sanskrit: मुदित प्रमदा रत्नम् राक्षस इन्द्र निवेशनम्
वर आभरण निर्ह्रादैः समुद्र स्वन निह्स्वनम्
transliteration: mudita pramadā ratnam rākṣasa indra niveśanam
vara ābharaṇa nirhrādaiḥ samudra svana nihsvanam

sanskrit: तद् राज गुण सम्पन्नम् मुख्यैः च वर चन्दनैः
भेरी म्Rदन्ग अभिरुतम् शन्ख घोष विनादितम्
transliteration: tad rāja guṇa sampannam mukhyaiḥ ca vara candanaiḥ
bherī mdanga abhirutam śankha ghoṣa vināditam

sanskrit: नित्य अर्चितम् पर्व हुतम् पूजितम् राक्षसैः सदा
transliteration: nitya arcitam parva hutam pūjitam rākṣasaiḥ sadā
english: Resonant with trumpets and drums; and ringing with the blares of conchs; where the ever adored offspring of the Parvas was always worshipped by the Rākşasas;

sanskrit: समुद्रम् इव गम्भीरम् समुद्रम् इव निह्स्वनम्
महात्मानो महद् वेश्म महा रत्न परिच्चदम्
transliteration: samudram iva gambhīram samudram iva nihsvanam
mahātmāno mahad veśma mahā ratna pariccadam
english: Solemn like the sea; and resounding like the ocean itself, the mighty mansion of the highsouled (Rāvana); clad in costly jewels; scattered with precious gems-as that mighty monkey beheld (Ravana's residence), he set about searching for Sītā.

sanskrit: महा जन समाकीर्णम् ददर्श स महा कपिः
विराजमानम् वपुषा गज अश्व रथ सम्कुलम्
transliteration: mahā jana samākīrṇam dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ
virājamānam vapuṣā gaja aśva ratha samkulam
english: That mighty monkey concluded, “This is the ornament of Larikā bodied forth beautifully to the view, covered with elephants, steeds and chariots."

sanskrit: लन्का आभरणम् इति एव सो अमन्यत महा कपिः
transliteration: lankā ābharaṇam iti eva so amanyata mahā kapiḥ
english: That mighty monkey concluded, “This is the ornament of Larikā bodied forth beautifully to the view, covered with elephants, steeds and chariots."

sanskrit: गृहाद् गृहम् राक्षसानाम् उद्यानानि च वानरः
वीक्षमाणो हि असम्त्रस्तः प्रासादामः च चचार सः
transliteration: gṛhād gṛham rākṣasānām udyānāni ca vānaraḥ
vīkṣamāṇo hi asamtrastaḥ prāsādāmaḥ ca cacāra saḥ
english: There in the vicinity of Rāvana's mansion, Hanumān began to range the dwellings of the Rākṣasas from one to another, as well as all the gardens (located there). And without experiencing any agitation, he observing (everything), ranged the palaces. *Rāmānuja says that Hanumān began to range the dwelling about the wall environing Rāvana's mansion.

sanskrit: ततो अन्यत् पुप्लुवे वेश्म महा पार्श्वस्य वीर्यवान्
transliteration: tato anyat pupluve veśma mahā pārśvasya vīryavān
english: Then that one endowed with wondrous motion, with a bound entered Prahasta's palace; and then with another, that (monkey) possessed of energy entered the into of Mahaparcwa.

sanskrit: अथ मेघ प्रतीकाशम् कुम्भ कर्ण निवेशनम्
विभीषणस्य च तथा पुप्लुवे स महा कपिः
transliteration: atha megha pratīkāśam kumbha karṇa niveśanam
vibhīṣaṇasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahā kapiḥ
english: Then that inighty monkey entered into the abode of Kumbhakarna, resembling a mass of clouds; and thereafter that of Vibhisana;

sanskrit: महा उदरस्य च तथा विरूप अक्षस्य चैव हि
विद्युज् जिह्वस्य भवनम् विद्युन् मालेः तथैव च
transliteration: mahā udarasya ca tathā virūpa akṣasya caiva hi
vidyuj jihvasya bhavanam vidyun māleḥ tathaiva ca
english: And then that of Mahodara, and then that of Virupaksha; and then the abode of Vidyujjibha, and then that of Vidyunmala;

sanskrit: वज्र दम्ष्ट्रस्य च तथा पुप्लुवे स महा कपिः
शुकस्य च महा वेगः सारणस्य च धीमतः
तथा च इन्द्रजितो वेश्म जगाम हरि यूथपः
transliteration: vajra damṣṭrasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahā kapiḥ
śukasya ca mahā vegaḥ sāraṇasya ca dhīmataḥ
tathā ca indrajito veśma jagāma hari yūthapaḥ
english: And then that mighty monkey with a bound entered into the abode of Vahudanshtra. And then that leader of monkey-bands gifted with great speed leapt into the abode of Suka, and next into that of the intelligent Sarana.

sanskrit: जम्बु मालेः सुमालेः च जगाम हरि यूथपः
transliteration: jambu māleḥ sumāleḥ ca jagāma hari yūthapaḥ

sanskrit: रश्मि केतोः च भवनम् सूर्य शत्रोः तथैव च
वज्रकायस्य च तथा पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः
transliteration: raśmi ketoḥ ca bhavanam sūrya śatroḥ tathaiva ca
vajrakāyasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahākapiḥ
english: and (then) to the abode of Rashmiketu, and Suryyasachu. And (next) that powerful monkey leapt into the mansion of Vajrakaya;

sanskrit: धूम्र अक्षस्य च सम्पातेर् भवनम् मारुत आत्मजः
विद्युद् रूपस्य भीमस्य घनस्य विघनस्य च
transliteration: dhūmra akṣasya ca sampāter bhavanam māruta ātmajaḥ
vidyud rūpasya bhīmasya ghanasya vighanasya ca

sanskrit: शुक नाभस्य वक्रस्य शठस्य विकटस्य च
ह्रस्व कर्णस्य दम्ष्ट्रस्य रोमशस्य च रक्षसः
transliteration: śuka nābhasya vakrasya śaṭhasya vikaṭasya ca
hrasva karṇasya damṣṭrasya romaśasya ca rakṣasaḥ

sanskrit: युद्ध उन्मत्तस्य मत्तस्य ध्वज ग्रीवस्य नादिनः
विद्युज् जिह्व इन्द्र जिह्वानाम् तथा हस्ति मुखस्य च
transliteration: yuddha unmattasya mattasya dhvaja grīvasya nādinaḥ
vidyuj jihva indra jihvānām tathā hasti mukhasya ca

sanskrit: करालस्य पिशाचस्य शोणित अक्षस्य चैव हि
क्रममाणः क्रमेण एव हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः
transliteration: karālasya piśācasya śoṇita akṣasya caiva hi
kramamāṇaḥ krameṇa eva hanūmān māruta ātmajaḥ

sanskrit: तेषु तेषु महा अर्हेषु भवनेषु महा यशाः
तेषाम् R^द्धिमताम् ऋद्धिम् ददर्श स महा कपिः
transliteration: teṣu teṣu mahā arheṣu bhavaneṣu mahā yaśāḥ
teṣām ddhimatām ṛddhim dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ

sanskrit: आससाद अथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षस इन्द्र निवेशनम्
transliteration: āsasāda atha lakṣmīvān rākṣasa indra niveśanam
english: Having bounded over the mansions of all situated around, that blessed with one auspiciousness, at length came to the very mansion of the monarch of the Rākşasas.

sanskrit: विचरन् हरि शार्दूलो राक्षसीर् विकृत ईक्षणाः
transliteration: vicaran hari śārdūlo rākṣasīr vikṛta īkṣaṇāḥ
english: That tiger-like monkey-the best of his speciesranging around, saw Rākṣasis of frightful eyes, alternately mounting sentry over the couch of Rāvana-bearing darts and maces in their hands, and equipped with javelins and clubs.

sanskrit: शूल मुद्गल हस्ताः च शक्तो तोमर धारिणीः
ददर्श विविधान् गुल्मामः तस्य रक्षः पतेर् गृहे
transliteration: śūla mudgala hastāḥ ca śakto tomara dhāriṇīḥ
dadarśa vividhān gulmāmaḥ tasya rakṣaḥ pater gṛhe

sanskrit: रक्तान् श्वेतान् सितामः चैव हरीमः चैव महा जवान्
transliteration: raktān śvetān sitāmaḥ caiva harīmaḥ caiva mahā javān

sanskrit: कुलीनान् रूप सम्पन्नान् गजान् पर गज आरुजान्
निष्ठितान् गज शिखायाम् ऐरावत समान् युधि
transliteration: kulīnān rūpa sampannān gajān para gaja ārujān
niṣṭhitān gaja śikhāyām airāvata samān yudhi

sanskrit: निहन्त्RRन् पर सैन्यानाम् गृहे तस्मिन् ददर्श सः
क्षरतः च यथा मेघान् स्रवतः च यथा गिरीन्
transliteration: nihantn para sainyānām gṛhe tasmin dadarśa saḥ
kṣarataḥ ca yathā meghān sravataḥ ca yathā girīn

sanskrit: मेघ स्तनित निर्घोषान् दुर्धर्षान् समरे परैः
transliteration: megha stanita nirghoṣān durdharṣān samare paraiḥ

sanskrit: हेम जालैर् अविच्चिन्नाः तरुण आदित्य सम्निभाः
transliteration: hema jālair aviccinnāḥ taruṇa āditya samnibhāḥ
english: That monkey, son to the Wind-god, saw in the mansion of the lord of Rākşasas, Rāvana, hosts by thousands; and cars of various forms of glittering gold, furnished all over with golden net-works, resembling the risen sun.

sanskrit: शिबिका विविध आकाराः स कपिर् मारुत आत्मजः
लता गृहाणि चित्राणि चित्र शाला गृहाणि च
transliteration: śibikā vividha ākārāḥ sa kapir māruta ātmajaḥ
latā gṛhāṇi citrāṇi citra śālā gṛhāṇi ca

sanskrit: क्रीडा गृहाणि च अन्यानि दारु पर्वतकान् अपि
कामस्य गृहकम् रम्यम् दिवा गृहकम् एव च
transliteration: krīḍā gṛhāṇi ca anyāni dāru parvatakān api
kāmasya gṛhakam ramyam divā gṛhakam eva ca
english: And graceful grots; and picture galleries; and sporting saloons, mountains composed of wood, captivating structures dedicated to dalliance, and dwellings for day-dalliance,' saw he in the mansion of the Raksasa monarch. 1. Designed for sport. — 2. The conception of day-dalliance met with in Vidya Sundara of Bharata Chandra Roy, the Bengali poet, is found to have first originated with Vālimiki.

sanskrit: स मन्दर तल प्रख्यम् मयूर स्थान सम्कुलम्
transliteration: sa mandara tala prakhyam mayūra sthāna samkulam

sanskrit: ध्वज यष्टिभिर् आकीर्णम् ददर्श भवन उत्तमम्
अनन्त रत्न निचयम् निधि जालम् समन्ततः
transliteration: dhvaja yaṣṭibhir ākīrṇam dadarśa bhavana uttamam
ananta ratna nicayam nidhi jālam samantataḥ
english: He beheld that charming mansion resembling Mandara, filled with places for peacocks* thronged with pennons and flagstaffs, a very mine of countless gems, a field of treasures spread around, where persons of intrepid calmness were engaged in acts tending to the safety of the treasures, resembling the mansion herself of Kubera. *Sportive peacocks.

sanskrit: धीर निष्ठित कर्म अन्तम् गृहम् भूत पतेर् इव
अर्चिर्भिः च अपि रत्नानाम् तेजसा रावणस्य च
transliteration: dhīra niṣṭhita karma antam gṛham bhūta pater iva
arcirbhiḥ ca api ratnānām tejasā rāvaṇasya ca

sanskrit: विरराज अथ तद् वेश्म रश्मिमान् इव रश्मिभिः
जाम्बू नदमयानि एव शयनानि आसनानि च
transliteration: virarāja atha tad veśma raśmimān iva raśmibhiḥ
jāmbū nadamayāni eva śayanāni āsanāni ca

sanskrit: भाजनानि च शुभ्राणि ददर्श हरि यूथपः
मध्व् आसव कृत क्लेदम् मणि भाजन सम्कुलम्
transliteration: bhājanāni ca śubhrāṇi dadarśa hari yūthapaḥ
madhv āsava kṛta kledam maṇi bhājana samkulam

sanskrit: मनो रमम् असम्बाधम् कुबेर भवनम् यथा
