नूपुराणाम् च घोषेण कान्चीनाम् निनदेन च
transliteration: mano ramam asambādham kubera bhavanam yathā
nūpurāṇām ca ghoṣeṇa kāncīnām ninadena ca

sanskrit: मृदन्ग तल घोषैः च घोषवद्भिर् विनादितम्
प्रासाद सम्घात युतम् स्त्री रत्न शत सम्कुलम्
transliteration: mṛdanga tala ghoṣaiḥ ca ghoṣavadbhir vināditam
prāsāda samghāta yutam strī ratna śata samkulam

sanskrit: सुव्यूढ कक्ष्यम् हनुमान् प्रविवेश महा गृहम्
transliteration: suvyūḍha kakṣyam hanumān praviveśa mahā gṛham

english: And that one endowed with strength saw that row of structures fitted up with golden windows, studded with lapis lazulis, and containing birds; like to a mass of clouds in a season of great rains, crowned with lightning, and fraught with fowls.

sanskrit: मनो हराः च अपि पुनर् विशाला
transliteration: mano harāḥ ca api punar viśālā
english: He saw various structures close to one another to which excellent conchs, arms and bows lent lustre; as well as huge and splendid towers belonging to edifices resembling mountains.

The monkey beheld mansions, treasuring various kinds of wealth, which were held in regard by both gods and Asuras, devoid of every defect; and which had been won (by Rāvana) through his own might.* Swavalenarjitam. Another meaning is: (mansions) into which Hanumān found entry through his own might.

And (Hanumān) saw the mansions of the lord of Lankā, located in strict conformity with aesthetic laws, appearing as if they had been constructed by Maya himself, which had on the earth beneath every excellence.

sanskrit: यथा नग अग्रम् बहु धातु चित्रम्
यथा नभः च ग्रह चन्द्र चित्रम्
transliteration: yathā naga agram bahu dhātu citram
yathā nabhaḥ ca graha candra citram
english: And (Hanumān) saw the car variegated with countless gems; like unto the top of a mountain variegated with innumerable metals; or like the firmament with the moon and the planets, or like clouds of diverse hues fused into a homogeneous whole.

The place in the car designed as the seat of the many, was filled with rows of hills,* Composed of gold and gems. Its hills were filled with trees; its trees were filled flowers; and (finally) its flowers were filled with leaves and filaments.
And (in it), where white mansions were reared, there were tank's filed with fair flowers; and lotuses furnished with filaments; and picturesque woods; and liquid lapses.

sanskrit: वेश्म उत्तमानाम् अपि च उच्च मानम्
transliteration: veśma uttamānām api ca ucca mānam
english: And the mighty monkey beheld there the great chariot going after the name of Pushpa, appearing beautiful, wheeling round in the splendour of the gems—which had surpassed cven the cars pertaining to the abodes of the celestials.

And in that car) were birds made of lapis lazulis; and (other) birds composed of silver and coral; and variegated serpents made of various precious metals; and fair-bodied steeds resembling those of superior breeds; and there were constructed birds having graceful mouths; and fair, tapering, playful and contracted plumage, bearing blossoms made of coral and gold, like to the very plumage of Kama himself.

There were elephants possessed of graceful trunks, bearing filaments; and with their trunks bearing lotus leaves, engaged in showering water on Lakshmi); as well as the goddess, made with fair arms, seated on a pool with a lotus in her hand.

sanskrit: इति इव तद् ग्Rहम् अभिगम्य शोभनम्
पुनः च तत् परम सुगन्धि सुन्दरम्
हिम अत्यये नगम् इव चारु कन्दरम्
transliteration: iti iva tad gham abhigamya śobhanam
punaḥ ca tat parama sugandhi sundaram
hima atyaye nagam iva cāru kandaram
english: Thus entering that graceful mansion, like to a mountain containing charming caverns, (Hanumān) was seized with wonderment. And once again (entering that charming mansion), like to a taking and fragrant tree during spring furnished with holes, Hanumān was seized with wonderment.

sanskrit: ततः स ताम् कपिर् अभिपत्य पूजिताम्
चरन् पुरीम् दश मुख बाहु पालिताम्
transliteration: tataḥ sa tām kapir abhipatya pūjitām
caran purīm daśa mukha bāhu pālitām
english: Then ranging by bounds that honoured city ruled by the arms of the Ten faced one, he, not finding the highly regarded and extremely distressed daughter of Janaka, who had won over her grief by contemplating the virtues of her lord, (was affected with sorrow).

sanskrit: ततः तदा बहु विध भावित आत्मनः
transliteration: tataḥ tadā bahu vidha bhāvita ātmanaḥ
english: And, not seeing Janaka's daughter, then the heart of that high-souled one, honoured for his character by the entire world, of schooled self, ever ranging by the way chiming in with morality, and having the scriptures for his eyesight, as he ranged about, was oppressed with grief.
Staying in that mansion, that intelligent monkey, the offspring of the Wind-god, beheld that splendid aerial car, beauteous with excellent jewels, and furnished with windows of burnished gold.

And the car, embellished with transcendentally beautiful figures, belauded by Viśvakarmā himself as constituting the acme (of his art), which, mounting the welkin, looked like a mark of the Sun's orbit, appeared resplendent.

There was nothing in that car which was not made skilfully; nothing that did not look like a precious jewel (sprung spontaneously on its person), and the style displayed in its various parts surpassed anything that could be found in the car of the celestials themselves, and everything in that car was executed in the highest style of excellence,

That (car) obtained (by Ravana) in virtue of prowess sprung from asceticism and contemplation (of the Deity); capable of repairing wherever (the owner) wished to wend; displaying various kinds of constructive skill, composed of materials procured from diverse sources, such as were worthy of a celestial car.

Coursing through the firmament in a variety of ways, the congeries of all wonderful things, adorned with ranges of chambers; captivating to the mind; stainless as the autumnal Moon; furnished with splendid summits, like the crest of a mountain.

Which was borne by rangers of the night, given to mighty meals, ranging the sky, with faces graced with ear-rings; and by thousands of ghosts possessed of terrible speed, having expansive, winkless and rolling eyes. That heroic firs of monkeys saw that excellent car, beauteous with vernal blossoms, fairer than the month of spring and furnished with flowers.

Which was borne by rangers of the night, given to mighty meals, ranging the sky, with faces graced with ear-rings; and by thousands of ghosts possessed of terrible speed, having expansive, winkless and rolling eyes. That heroic firs of monkeys saw that excellent car, beauteous with vernal blossoms, fairer than the month of spring and furnished with flowers.

sanskrit: तस्य आलय वरिष्ठस्य मध्ये विपुलम् आयतम्
ददर्श भवन श्रेष्ठम् हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः
transliteration: tasya ālaya variṣṭhasya madhye vipulam āyatam
dadarśa bhavana śreṣṭham hanūmān māruta ātmajaḥ
english: And located within that excellent mansion, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, saw a superior and grand structure, stainless and spacious; half a Yojana in width and one in lenght, belonging to the lord of the Rākşasas, and abounding with many a palace.

sanskrit: अर्ध योजन विस्तीर्णम् आयतम् योजनम् हि तत्
भवनम् राक्षस इन्द्रस्य बहु प्रासाद सम्कुलम्
transliteration: ardha yojana vistīrṇam āyatam yojanam hi tat
bhavanam rākṣasa indrasya bahu prāsāda samkulam
english: And located within that excellent mansion, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, saw a superior and grand structure, stainless and spacious; half a Yojana in width and one in lenght, belonging to the lord of the Rākşasas, and abounding with many a palace.

sanskrit: मार्गमाणः तु वैदेहीम् सीताम् आयत लोचनाम्
transliteration: mārgamāṇaḥ tu vaidehīm sītām āyata locanām
english: Searching for Videha's daughter, the large eyed Sītā, that slayer of enemies, Hanumān, ranged all through (this edifice).

Hanumān beheld the goodly edifice where the Rāksasas used to dwell in common. And (at length) that one came upon the mansion itself of the lord of Rākşasas, having three-tusked and four-tusked elephants, and protected by persons with upraised arms, and covering a capacious area.

sanskrit: चतुर् विषाणैर् द्विरदैः त्रिविषाणैः तथैव च
transliteration: catur viṣāṇair dviradaiḥ triviṣāṇaiḥ tathaiva ca
english: Hanumān beheld the goodly edifice where the Rāksasas used to dwell in common. And (at length) that one came upon the mansion itself of the lord of Rākşasas, having three-tusked and four-tusked elephants, and protected by persons with upraised arms, and covering a capacious area.

sanskrit: आह्Rताभिः च विक्रम्य राज कन्याभिर् आव्Rतम्
transliteration: āhtābhiḥ ca vikramya rāja kanyābhir āvtam
english: And (Hanumān beheld) the residence of Rāvana thronged with his Rākṣasi wives, as well as with princesses forcibly brought thither (by him), like to the sea teeming with alligators and Makaras, abounding in timingilas and fishes and snakes, and agitated by the force of the wind.

sanskrit: तन् नक्र मकर आकीर्णम् तिमिम्गिल झष आकुलम्
वायु वेग समाधूतम् पन्नगैर् इव सागरम्
transliteration: tan nakra makara ākīrṇam timimgila jhaṣa ākulam
vāyu vega samādhūtam pannagair iva sāgaram
english: And (Hanumān beheld) the residence of Rāvana thronged with his Rākṣasi wives, as well as with princesses forcibly brought thither (by him), like to the sea teeming with alligators and Makaras, abounding in timingilas and fishes and snakes, and agitated by the force of the wind.

sanskrit: या हि वैश्वरणे लक्ष्मीर् या च इन्द्रे हरि वाहने
सा रावण ग्Rहे सर्वा नित्यम् एव अनपायिनी
transliteration: yā hi vaiśvaraṇe lakṣmīr yā ca indre hari vāhane
sā rāvaṇa ghe sarvā nityam eva anapāyinī
english: The same enchanting splendour that is in Vaiśravaņa or the ray-riding Moon, remained ever constant and abiding in, Rāvana's abode. And the prosperity of king Kubera, or Yama, or Varuna, was here present in the house of the Rākşas, or even surpassed by the prosperity (of Rāvana).

sanskrit: या च राज्ञः कुबेरस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च
ताद्Rशी तद् विशिष्टा वा Rद्धी रक्षो ग्Rहेष्व् इह
transliteration: yā ca rājñaḥ kuberasya yamasya varuṇasya ca
tādśī tad viśiṣṭā vā ddhī rakṣo gheṣv iha
english: The same enchanting splendour that is in Vaiśravaņa or the ray-riding Moon, remained ever constant and abiding in, Rāvana's abode. And the prosperity of king Kubera, or Yama, or Varuna, was here present in the house of the Rākşas, or even surpassed by the prosperity (of Rāvana).

sanskrit: तस्य हर्म्यस्य मध्यस्थम् वेश्म च अन्यत् सुनिर्मितम्
transliteration: tasya harmyasya madhyastham veśma ca anyat sunirmitam
english: In the midst of that mansion the Wind-god's offspring found another.* excellently constructed, having innumerable mad elephants; that noble car embellished with all gems, entitled Pushpaka, which had been constructed in heaven by Viśvakarmă for Brahmā himself. *The car Puspaka, according to Tirtha, whose view is accepted by Rāmānuja. According to Kataka, Vesma means a bedchamber of husband and wife.

sanskrit: ब्रह्मणो अर्थे क्Rतम् दिव्यम् दिवि यद् विश्व कर्मणा
विमानम् पुष्पकम् नाम सर्व रत्न विभूषितम्
transliteration: brahmaṇo arthe ktam divyam divi yad viśva karmaṇā
vimānam puṣpakam nāma sarva ratna vibhūṣitam
english: In the midst of that mansion the Wind-god's offspring found another.* excellently constructed, having innumerable mad elephants; that noble car embellished with all gems, entitled Pushpaka, which had been constructed in heaven by Viśvakarmă for Brahmā himself. *The car Puspaka, according to Tirtha, whose view is accepted by Rāmānuja. According to Kataka, Vesma means a bedchamber of husband and wife.

sanskrit: परेण तपसा लेभे यत् कुबेरः पितामहात्
कुबेरम् ओजसा जित्वा लेभे तद् राक्षस ईश्वरः
transliteration: pareṇa tapasā lebhe yat kuberaḥ pitāmahāt
kuberam ojasā jitvā lebhe tad rākṣasa īśvaraḥ
english: Which Kubera obtained for the Great-father through high austerities, and which, vanquishing Kubera by his prowess, the Rākṣasa chief god possession of.

sanskrit: ईहा म्Rग समायुक्तैः कार्य स्वर हिरण्मयैः
सुक्Rतैर् आचितम् स्तम्भैः प्रदीप्तम् इव च श्रिया
transliteration: īhā mga samāyuktaiḥ kārya svara hiraṇmayaiḥ
suktair ācitam stambhaiḥ pradīptam iva ca śriyā

sanskrit: मेरु मन्दर सम्काशैर् उल्लिखद्भिर् इव अम्बरम्
कूट अगारैः शुभ आकारैः सर्वतः समलम्क्Rतम्
transliteration: meru mandara samkāśair ullikhadbhir iva ambaram
kūṭa agāraiḥ śubha ākāraiḥ sarvataḥ samalamktam

sanskrit: ज्वलन अर्क प्रतीकाशम् सुक्Rतम् विश्व कर्मणा
हेम सोपान सम्युक्तम् चारु प्रवर वेदिकम्
transliteration: jvalana arka pratīkāśam suktam viśva karmaṇā
hema sopāna samyuktam cāru pravara vedikam

sanskrit: जाल वात अयनैर् युक्तम् कान्चनैः स्थाटिकैर् अपि
इन्द्र नील महा नील मणि प्रवरवेदिकम्
transliteration: jāla vāta ayanair yuktam kāncanaiḥ sthāṭikair api
indra nīla mahā nīla maṇi pravaravedikam

english: And the mighty monkey ascended the splendid car Pushpaka, containing figures of wolves, made of Karttasvara and Hiranya; graced with ranges of goodly pillars; as if blazing in splendour; throughout garnished with narrow secret rooms and saloons, piercing the heavens, and resembling Meru of Mandara, and like to the flaming Sun; skilfully reared by Viswakarmā; with golden staircases and graceful and grand raised seats, rows of golden and crystal windows, and daises composed of sapphires, emeralds and other superb gems; embellished with noble vidrumas, costly stones, and round pearls, as also with plastered terraces; pasted with red sandal, like to gold, and furnished with a sacred aroma; and resembling the sun new risen.

sanskrit: विमानम् पुष्पकम् दिव्यम् आरुरोह महा कपिः
transliteration: vimānam puṣpakam divyam āruroha mahā kapiḥ

sanskrit: तत्रस्थः स तदा गन्धम् पान भक्ष्य अन्न सम्भवम्
दिव्यम् सम्मूर्चितम् जिघ्रन् रूपवन्तम् इव अनिलम्
transliteration: tatrasthaḥ sa tadā gandham pāna bhakṣya anna sambhavam
divyam sammūrcitam jighran rūpavantam iva anilam

sanskrit: स गन्धः तम् महा सत्त्वम् बन्धुर् बन्धुम् इव उत्तमम्
इत एहि इति उवाच इव तत्र यत्र स रावणः
transliteration: sa gandhaḥ tam mahā sattvam bandhur bandhum iva uttamam
ita ehi iti uvāca iva tatra yatra sa rāvaṇaḥ

sanskrit: ततः ताम् प्रस्थितः शालाम् ददर्श महतीम् शुभाम्
रावणस्य मनः कान्ताम् कान्ताम् इव वर स्त्रियम्
transliteration: tataḥ tām prasthitaḥ śālām dadarśa mahatīm śubhām
rāvaṇasya manaḥ kāntām kāntām iva vara striyam

sanskrit: मणि सोपान विक्Rताम् हेम जाल विराजिताम्
स्फाटिकैर् आव्Rत तलाम् दन्त अन्तरित रूपिकाम्
transliteration: maṇi sopāna viktām hema jāla virājitām
sphāṭikair āvta talām danta antarita rūpikām

sanskrit: मुक्ताभिः च प्रवालैः च रूप्य चामी करैर् अपि
विभूषिताम् मणि स्तम्भैः सुबहु स्तम्भ भूषिताम्
transliteration: muktābhiḥ ca pravālaiḥ ca rūpya cāmī karair api
vibhūṣitām maṇi stambhaiḥ subahu stambha bhūṣitām

sanskrit: स्तम्भैः पक्षैर् इव अत्युच्चैर् दिवम् सम्प्रस्थिताम् इव
transliteration: stambhaiḥ pakṣair iva atyuccair divam samprasthitām iva

sanskrit: महत्या कुथय आस्त्रीणम् प्Rथिवी लक्षण अन्कया
पृथिवीम् इव विस्तीर्णाम् सराष्ट्र ग्Rह मालिनीम्
transliteration: mahatyā kuthaya āstrīṇam pthivī lakṣaṇa ankayā
pṛthivīm iva vistīrṇām sarāṣṭra gha mālinīm

sanskrit: नादिताम् मत्त विहगैर् दिव्य गन्ध अधिवासिताम्
पर अर्ध्य आस्तरण उपेताम् रक्षो अधिप निषेविताम्
transliteration: nāditām matta vihagair divya gandha adhivāsitām
para ardhya āstaraṇa upetām rakṣo adhipa niṣevitām

sanskrit: धूम्राम् अगरु धूपेन विमलाम् हम्स पाण्डुराम्
चित्राम् पुष्प उपहारेण कल्माषीम् इव सुप्रभाम्
transliteration: dhūmrām agaru dhūpena vimalām hamsa pāṇḍurām
citrām puṣpa upahāreṇa kalmāṣīm iva suprabhām

sanskrit: मनः सम्ह्लाद जननीम् वर्णस्य अपि प्रसादिनीम्
ताम् शोक नाशिनीम् दिव्याम् श्रियः सम्जननीम् इव
transliteration: manaḥ samhlāda jananīm varṇasya api prasādinīm
tām śoka nāśinīm divyām śriyaḥ samjananīm iva

sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि इन्द्रिय अर्थैः तु पन्च पन्चभिर् उत्तमैः
तर्पयाम् आस माता इव तदा रावण पालिता
transliteration: indriyāṇi indriya arthaiḥ tu panca pancabhir uttamaiḥ
tarpayām āsa mātā iva tadā rāvaṇa pālitā

sanskrit: स्वर्गो अयम् देव लोको अयम् इन्द्रस्य इयम् पुरी भवेत्
सिद्धिर् वा इयम् परा हि स्याद् इति अमन्यत मारुतिः
transliteration: svargo ayam deva loko ayam indrasya iyam purī bhavet
siddhir vā iyam parā hi syād iti amanyata mārutiḥ
english: This must be svarga, or the region of the immortals, or the city of Amarāvatī, or the supreme Siddhit thought the Wind-god's offspring Svarga is the region where persons reap the fruit of Jyotishtoma, etc. Siddhi is Illusion spread by Gandharvas.

sanskrit: प्रध्यायत इव अपश्यत् प्रदीपामः तत्र कान्चनान् (ःइअतुस्!)
धूर्तान् इव महा धूर्तैर् देवनेन पराजितान्
transliteration: pradhyāyata iva apaśyat pradīpāmaḥ tatra kāncanān (ḥiatus!)
dhūrtān iva mahā dhūrtair devanena parājitān
english: And he saw the golden lamps (shorn of their brightness),* like to gamblers worsted at dice by others exceedingly skilful, and, in consequence, plunged in thought. * By the superior splendour of Rāvaņa.

sanskrit: दीपानाम् च प्रकाशेन तेजसा रावणस्य च
अर्चिर्भिर् भूषणानाम् च प्रदीप्ता इति अभ्यमन्यत
transliteration: dīpānām ca prakāśena tejasā rāvaṇasya ca
arcirbhir bhūṣaṇānām ca pradīptā iti abhyamanyata
english: And (Hanumān) conceived that (Rāvana's sleeping apartment) was in a conflagration, on account of the display of the lamps, Rāvana's energy, and the splendour of the ornaments.

sanskrit: ततो अपश्यत् कुथा आसीनम् नाना वर्ण अम्बर स्रजम्
सहस्रम् वर नारीणाम् नाना वेष विभूषितम्
transliteration: tato apaśyat kuthā āsīnam nānā varṇa ambara srajam
sahasram vara nārīṇām nānā veṣa vibhūṣitam
english: And when the night had been half spent, (Hanuman) saw thousands of superb dames, adorned in various attires, and bearing apparels of diverse hues, and wreaths, who having given up sport, and come under the influence of wine and sleep, were fast asleep on woollen sheets.

sanskrit: परिव्Rत्ते अर्ध रात्रे तु पान निद्रा वशम् गतम्
क्रीडित्वा उपरतम् रात्रौ सुष्वाप बलवत् तदा
transliteration: parivtte ardha rātre tu pāna nidrā vaśam gatam
krīḍitvā uparatam rātrau suṣvāpa balavat tadā
english: And when the night had been half spent, (Hanuman) saw thousands of superb dames, adorned in various attires, and bearing apparels of diverse hues, and wreaths, who having given up sport, and come under the influence of wine and sleep, were fast asleep on woollen sheets.

sanskrit: तत् प्रसुप्तम् विरुरुचे निह्शब्द अन्तर भूषणम्
निह्शब्द हम्स भ्रमरम् यथा पद्म वनम् महत्
transliteration: tat prasuptam viruruce nihśabda antara bhūṣaṇam
nihśabda hamsa bhramaram yathā padma vanam mahat
english: And in consequence of the silence that reigned (in the apartment) embellished with (ornaments), it resembled a large lotus-grove, where the swans and the black bees are silent.

sanskrit: तासाम् सम्व्Rत दन्तानि मीलित अक्षाणि मारुतिः
transliteration: tāsām samvta dantāni mīlita akṣāṇi mārutiḥ
english: And the Wind-god's offspring beheld the countenance of those beauteous women, with closed eyes, having their lashes shut through languor; and odorous with lotus-perfume.

sanskrit: प्रबुद्धानि इव पद्मानि तासाम् भूत्वा क्षपा क्षये
पुनः सम्व्Rत पत्राणि रात्राव् इव बभुः तदा
transliteration: prabuddhāni iva padmāni tāsām bhūtvā kṣapā kṣaye
punaḥ samvta patrāṇi rātrāv iva babhuḥ tadā
english: And their faces appeared like lotuses blowing on the expire of night and closing their petals by night.

sanskrit: इमानि मुख पद्मानि नियतम् मत्त षट्पदाः
अम्बुजानि इव फुल्लानि प्रार्थयन्ति पुनः पुनः
transliteration: imāni mukha padmāni niyatam matta ṣaṭpadāḥ
ambujāni iva phullāni prārthayanti punaḥ punaḥ
english: “These lotus-faces like to very lotuses themselves, ever the six-footed ones* seek once and again.” Thus thought with discrimination the graceful, mighty. monkey; and on account of their perfections, he confessed those countenances to be equal to water-sprung (lotuses). * Şatpadā—six-footed—a name of the black bee. "Salitodbhavas, water spiung—a name of the lotus.

sanskrit: इति वा अमन्यत श्रीमान् उपपत्त्या महा कपिः
मेने हि गुणतः तानि समानि सलिल उद्भवैः
transliteration: iti vā amanyata śrīmān upapattyā mahā kapiḥ
mene hi guṇataḥ tāni samāni salila udbhavaiḥ
english: “These lotus-faces like to very lotuses themselves, ever the six-footed ones* seek once and again.” Thus thought with discrimination the graceful, mighty. monkey; and on account of their perfections, he confessed those countenances to be equal to water-sprung (lotuses). * Şatpadā—six-footed—a name of the black bee. "Salitodbhavas, water spiung—a name of the lotus.

sanskrit: सा तस्य शुशुभे शाला ताभिः स्त्रीभिर् विराजिता
शारदी इव प्रसन्ना द्यौः ताराभिर् अभिशोभिता
transliteration: sā tasya śuśubhe śālā tābhiḥ strībhir virājitā
śāradī iva prasannā dyauḥ tārābhir abhiśobhitā
english: And that apartment, in consequence of being graced by those women, appeared splendid, like the autumnal, complacent sky decorated with the stars.

sanskrit: स च ताभिः परिव्Rतः शुशुभे राक्षस अधिपः
यथा हि उडु पतिः श्रीमामः ताराभिर् अभिसम्व्Rतः
transliteration: sa ca tābhiḥ parivtaḥ śuśubhe rākṣasa adhipaḥ
yathā hi uḍu patiḥ śrīmāmaḥ tārābhir abhisamvtaḥ
english: And surrounded by them, the Rākṣasa chief resembled the fair Moon encircled by the stars.

sanskrit: याः च्यवन्ते अम्बरात् ताराः पुण्य शेष समाव्Rताः
इमाः ताः सम्गताः क्Rत्स्ना इति मेने हरिः तदा
transliteration: yāḥ cyavante ambarāt tārāḥ puṇya śeṣa samāvtāḥ
imāḥ tāḥ samgatāḥ ktsnā iti mene hariḥ tadā
english: “Those stars that drop from the firmament on their virtue deteriorating, have assembled here in a body," thus thought the monkey at that time.

sanskrit: ताराणाम् इव सुव्यक्तम् महतीनाम् शुभ अर्चिषाम्
प्रभा वर्ण प्रसादाः च विरेजुः तत्र योषिताम्
transliteration: tārāṇām iva suvyaktam mahatīnām śubha arciṣām
prabhā varṇa prasādāḥ ca virejuḥ tatra yoṣitām
english: And the shine, form, and splendour of those females resembled, forsooth those of magnificently displayed, noble and lustrous stars.

sanskrit: व्याव्Rत्त गुरु पीन स्रक् प्रकीर्ण वर भूषणाः
पान व्यायाम कालेषु निद्रा अपह्Rत चेतसः
transliteration: vyāvtta guru pīna srak prakīrṇa vara bhūṣaṇāḥ
pāna vyāyāma kāleṣu nidrā apahta cetasaḥ
english: And on account of their having been bereft of consciousness through sleep, induced by fatigue brought on by drink (and dance), their hair was dishevelled, and their full wreaths and goodly ornaments lay scattered about.

sanskrit: व्याव्Rत्त तिलकाः काश्चित् काश्चिद् उद्भ्रान्त नूपुराः
पार्श्वे गलित हाराः च काश्चित् परम योषितः
transliteration: vyāvtta tilakāḥ kāścit kāścid udbhrānta nūpurāḥ
pārśve galita hārāḥ ca kāścit parama yoṣitaḥ
english: And some of those paragons had got their beauty-spots, smudged; and some, their bangles loosening off, some, their chains running to one side.

sanskrit: मुखा हार व्Rताः च अन्याः काश्चित् प्रस्रस्त वाससः
व्याविद्ध रशना दामाः किशोर्य इव वाहिताः
transliteration: mukhā hāra vtāḥ ca anyāḥ kāścit prasrasta vāsasaḥ
vyāviddha raśanā dāmāḥ kiśorya iva vāhitāḥ
english: And others had their pearl necklaces burst, and their cloths getting away (from their persons), and the chains of their zones straying irregularly; resembling way-worn mares.

sanskrit: सुकुण्डल धराः च अन्या विच्चिन्न म्Rदित स्रजः
गज इन्द्र म्Rदिताः फुल्ला लता इव महा वने
transliteration: sukuṇḍala dharāḥ ca anyā viccinna mdita srajaḥ
gaja indra mditāḥ phullā latā iva mahā vane
english: And others again were without their ear-rings, and had their garlands torn and crushed; and resembled blossoming creepers, trodden down in a vast forest by mighty elephants.

sanskrit: चन्द्र अम्शु किरण आभाः च हाराः कासाम्चिद् उत्कटाः
हम्सा इव बभुः सुप्ताः स्तन मध्येषु योषिताम्
transliteration: candra amśu kiraṇa ābhāḥ ca hārāḥ kāsāmcid utkaṭāḥ
hamsā iva babhuḥ suptāḥ stana madhyeṣu yoṣitām
english: And the pearl chains of some shining females resembling moon beams, having got topsy-turvy, was lying like sleeping swans between the breasts of the damsels.

sanskrit: अपरासाम् च वैदूर्याः कादम्बा इव पक्षिणः
हेम सूत्राणि च अन्यासाम् चक्र वाका इव अभवन्
transliteration: aparāsām ca vaidūryāḥ kādambā iva pakṣiṇaḥ
hema sūtrāṇi ca anyāsām cakra vākā iva abhavan
english: And the lapis chains of some resembled water-crows;* and the fine golden chains turned upside down of other appeared like ruddy geese. *Kadamba-a drake; or, according to some, a teal; a gander; or the species gallinula porphyria.

sanskrit: हम्स कारण्डव आकीर्णाः चक्र वाक उपशोभिताः
आपगा इव ता रेजुर् जघनैः पुलिनैर् इव
transliteration: hamsa kāraṇḍava ākīrṇāḥ cakra vāka upaśobhitāḥ
āpagā iva tā rejur jaghanaiḥ pulinair iva
english: And those ladies resembled rivers having hips for banks; containing swans and Karandavas, and beautified with ruddy geese.

sanskrit: किन्किणी जाल सम्काशाः ता हेम विपुल अम्बुजाः
भाव ग्राहा यशः तीराः सुप्ता नद्य इव आबभुः
transliteration: kinkiṇī jāla samkāśāḥ tā hema vipula ambujāḥ
bhāva grāhā yaśaḥ tīrāḥ suptā nadya iva ābabhuḥ
english: Those sleeping females appeared like streams; having Kinkiņis for their ripples; and large gold lotuses;* marks* of amorous encounter on their persons for ferocious aquatic animals; and perfections,** for their banks. 'i.e. the faces of the females are meant. Another meaning is, gold for large lotuses. *Vilasa, may also mean arch displays by way of ecquetry. **Yasa, according to some, here means grace.

sanskrit: मृदुष्व् अन्गेषु कासाम्चित् कुच अग्रेषु च सम्स्थिताः
बभूवुर् भूषणानि इव शुभा भूषण राजयः
transliteration: mṛduṣv angeṣu kāsāmcit kuca agreṣu ca samsthitāḥ
babhūvur bhūṣaṇāni iva śubhā bhūṣaṇa rājayaḥ
english: On the tender frames, as well as on the tops of the breasts, of graceful scratches consequent pressure, appeared like ornaments.

sanskrit: अम्शु कान्ताः च कासाम्चिन् मुख मारुत कम्पिताः
उपरि उपरि वक्त्राणाम् व्याधूयन्ते पुनः पुनः
transliteration: amśu kāntāḥ ca kāsāmcin mukha māruta kampitāḥ
upari upari vaktrāṇām vyādhūyante punaḥ punaḥ
english: The scarf-ends of some stirred by the air that some on was blowing about their faces, flapped on them again and again.

sanskrit: ताः पाताका इव उद्धूताः पत्नीनाम् रुचिर प्रभाः
नाना वर्ण सुवर्णानाम् वक्त्र मूलेषु रेजिरे
transliteration: tāḥ pātākā iva uddhūtāḥ patnīnām rucira prabhāḥ
nānā varṇa suvarṇānām vaktra mūleṣu rejire
english: At the nether part of the faces of Rāvana's wives, they (the scarf-ends) appeared beauteous like uplifted streamers of exceeding elegance, composed of many-hued golden yarn.

sanskrit: ववल्गुः च अत्र कासाम्चित् कुण्डलानि शुभ अर्चिषाम्
मुख मारुत सम्सर्गान् मन्दम् मन्दम् सुयोषिताम्
transliteration: vavalguḥ ca atra kāsāmcit kuṇḍalāni śubha arciṣām
mukha māruta samsargān mandam mandam suyoṣitām
english: The ear-rings of some dames possessed of a pleasant sheen, stirred by the air that was breathing about their faces, were undulating gently.

sanskrit: शर्कर आसव गन्धः स प्रक्Rत्या सुरभिः सुखः
तासाम् वदन निह्श्वासः सिषेवे रावणम् तदा
transliteration: śarkara āsava gandhaḥ sa praktyā surabhiḥ sukhaḥ
tāsām vadana nihśvāsaḥ siṣeve rāvaṇam tadā
english: The sweet breath of their faces, naturally fragrani, and redolent of sugar and asava, was then rogaling Rāvana.

sanskrit: रावण आनन शन्काः च काश्चिद् रावण योषितः
मुखानि स्म सपत्नीनाम् उपाजिघ्रन् पुनः पुनः
transliteration: rāvaṇa ānana śankāḥ ca kāścid rāvaṇa yoṣitaḥ
mukhāni sma sapatnīnām upājighran punaḥ punaḥ
english: Out of fear sprung from sleep and intoxication, some of Rāvana's wives were again and again smelling the faces of those, co-wives with them, taking the faces to belong to Rāvaņa.

sanskrit: अत्यर्थम् सक्त मनसो रावणे ता वर स्त्रियः
अस्वतन्त्राः सपत्नीनाम् प्रियम् एव आचरमः तदा
transliteration: atyartham sakta manaso rāvaṇe tā vara striyaḥ
asvatantrāḥ sapatnīnām priyam eva ācaramaḥ tadā
english: From their hearts being firmly fixed on Ravana, those excellent women, having their sense of separateness removed, (albeit thus dealt with), did what was dear to them.* *The sense is very imperspicusous only by reason of he unskilful use of the pronouns. The damsels kissed did not resent the act; but kissed the kissers in turn.

sanskrit: अम्शुकानि च रम्याणि प्रमदाः तत्र शिश्यिरे
transliteration: amśukāni ca ramyāṇi pramadāḥ tatra śiśyire
english: Other females, making their gay scarf-ends (for their sheets), and making their arms, their pillows, were lying down there.

sanskrit: अन्या वक्षसि च अन्यस्याः तस्याः काचित् पुनर् भुजम्
अपरा त्व् अन्कम् अन्यस्याः तस्याः च अपि अपरा भुजौ
transliteration: anyā vakṣasi ca anyasyāḥ tasyāḥ kācit punar bhujam
aparā tv ankam anyasyāḥ tasyāḥ ca api aparā bhujau
english: And some were lying on others' bosoms; and others again, on the arms of the latter. And some lay on the laps of others; and others, again, on the breasts of the latter.

sanskrit: ऊरु पार्श्व कटी प्Rष्ठम् अन्योन्यस्य समाश्रिताः
परस्पर निविष्ट अन्ग्यो मद स्नेह वश अनुगाः
transliteration: ūru pārśva kaṭī pṣṭham anyonyasya samāśritāḥ
paraspara niviṣṭa angyo mada sneha vaśa anugāḥ
english: They reposed on each other's thighs, flanks, waists, and backs; and coming under the influence of wine and amour, they lay on each other's persons.

sanskrit: एकी क्Rत भुजाः सर्वाः सुषुपुः तत्र योषितःअन्योन्य भुज सूत्रेण स्त्री माला ग्रथिता हि सा
माला इव ग्रथिता सूत्रे शुशुभे मत्त षट्पदा
transliteration: ekī kta bhujāḥ sarvāḥ suṣupuḥ tatra yoṣitaḥanyonya bhuja sūtreṇa strī mālā grathitā hi sā
mālā iva grathitā sūtre śuśubhe matta ṣaṭpadā

sanskrit: लतानाम् माधवे मासि फुल्लानाम् वायु सेवनात्
अन्योन्य माला ग्रथितम् सम्सक्त कुसुम उच्चयम्
transliteration: latānām mādhave māsi phullānām vāyu sevanāt
anyonya mālā grathitam samsakta kusuma uccayam
english: That multitude of females in a mediey appeared like an assemblage of blooming plants in the month of Caitra,* with its wreaths formed in consequence of their coming in contact with one another, and of its clusters touching each other, on account of the breeze blowing; with the plants encircling the graceful (necks of the trees), and rife with Bhramaras chasing each other. 'March-April.

sanskrit: आसीद् वनम् इव उद्धूतम् स्त्री वनम् रावणस्य तत्
transliteration: āsīd vanam iva uddhūtam strī vanam rāvaṇasya tat
english: That multitude of females in a mediey appeared like an assemblage of blooming plants in the month of Caitra,* with its wreaths formed in consequence of their coming in contact with one another, and of its clusters touching each other, on account of the breeze blowing; with the plants encircling the graceful (necks of the trees), and rife with Bhramaras chasing each other. 'March-April.

sanskrit: उचितेष्व् अपि सुव्यक्तम् न तासाम् योषिताम् तदा
विवेकः शक्य आधातुम् भूषण अन्ग अम्बर स्रजाम्
transliteration: uciteṣv api suvyaktam na tāsām yoṣitām tadā
vivekaḥ śakya ādhātum bhūṣaṇa anga ambara srajām
english: Although the ornaments of those women wearing ornaments, attires and wreaths, were put on proper places; yet (on account of the profusion of the ornaments themselves, as well as because of the circumstance of the dames sleeping, * it was difficult to ascertain which ornament belonged to one damsel and which to another. *In consequence also, remarks the commentator, of the uniformity running through the ornaments, as well as of the close contact of the persons of the ladies.

sanskrit: रावणे सुख सम्विष्टे ताः स्त्रियो विविध प्रभाः
ज्वलन्तः कान्चना दीपाः प्रेक्षन्त अनिमिषा इव
transliteration: rāvaṇe sukha samviṣṭe tāḥ striyo vividha prabhāḥ
jvalantaḥ kāncanā dīpāḥ prekṣanta animiṣā iva
english: It seemed as if, Rāvana having attained rest (through sleep), the flaming golden lamps furnished with various rays, were gazing at the girls with winkless eyes.

sanskrit: राज Rषि पित्R दैत्यानाम् गन्धर्वाणाम् च योषितः
रक्षसाम् च अभवन् कन्याः तस्य काम वशम् गताः
transliteration: rāja ṣi pit daityānām gandharvāṇām ca yoṣitaḥ
rakṣasām ca abhavan kanyāḥ tasya kāma vaśam gatāḥ
english: Daughters of Rajarsis, of Vipras, of Daityas, of Gandharvas, and of Rākşasas, having come under the influence of desire, had become his wives.

sanskrit: युद्धकामेन ताः सर्वा रावणेन हृताः स्त्रियः
transliteration: yuddhakāmena tāḥ sarvā rāvaṇena hṛtāḥ striyaḥ
english: And all those women had been procured by Rāvana because he sought fight (with their relations) and some haughty dames, rapt with desire, had of themselves come to this place.

sanskrit: न च अन्य कामा अपि न च अन्य पूर्वा
विना वर अर्हाम् जनक आत्मजाम् तु
transliteration: na ca anya kāmā api na ca anya pūrvā
vinā vara arhām janaka ātmajām tu
english: There was no woman there, who had been won by force by (Rāvana), possessed as he was of prowess; but they had all been subdued by his qualities. And save the surpassingly worthy daughter of Janaka, no female (had been brought), who had set her heart on another, or who had known any other before.

sanskrit: न च अकुलीना न च हीन रूपा
भार्या अभवत् तस्य न हीन सत्त्वा
न च अपि कान्तस्य न कामनीया
transliteration: na ca akulīnā na ca hīna rūpā
bhāryā abhavat tasya na hīna sattvā
na ca api kāntasya na kāmanīyā
english: There was none who, being his wife, was not of high extraction; none who was defective in grace; none who was not an object of desire of her lover.

sanskrit: सुजातम् अस्य इति हि साधु बुद्धेः
transliteration: sujātam asya iti hi sādhu buddheḥ
english: as The lord of monkeys endowed with uprightness of sense, thought, “If the righteously wedded wife of Rāghava were one of the wives of the king of the Rākṣasas, it would well for him."

sanskrit: पुनः च सो अचिन्तयद् आर्त रूपो
transliteration: punaḥ ca so acintayad ārta rūpo

sanskrit: तत्र दिव्य उपमम् मुख्यम् स्फाटिकम् रत्न भूषितम्
transliteration: tatra divya upamam mukhyam sphāṭikam ratna bhūṣitam
english: And there Hanumán employed in looking around saw a grand dais made of crystal; and embellished with jewels; comparable to one belonging to the celestial regions; furnished with superb and costly sofas, having their parts painted and composed of ivory, gold, and lapis lazulis; with highly precious canopies.

And there Hanumán employed in looking around saw a grand dais made of crystal; and embellished with jewels; comparable to one belonging to the celestial regions; furnished with superb and costly sofas, having their parts painted and composed of ivory, gold, and lapis lazulis; with highly precious canopies.

sanskrit: तस्य च एकतमे देशे सो अग्र्य माल्य विभूषितम्
ददर्श पाण्डुरम् चत्रम् तारा अधिपति सम्निभम्
transliteration: tasya ca ekatame deśe so agrya mālya vibhūṣitam
dadarśa pāṇḍuram catram tārā adhipati samnibham
english: At one place thereof he saw a white umbrella, adorned with beautiful wreaths, resembling the lord of the stars himself.
And Hanuman saw a splendid sofa garnished with gold, bearing garlands of aśoka blossoms, flaming like fire;

sanskrit: गन्धैः च विविधैर् जुष्टम् वर धूपेन धूपितम्
transliteration: gandhaiḥ ca vividhair juṣṭam vara dhūpena dhūpitam
english: Around which persons kept waving with their hands chowris furnished with hair;* rife with perfumes of various kinds; odorous with rich dhupa, spread with excellent sheets; covered with the skins of rams; and decked on all sides with chaplets of gorgeous flowers. *The commentator throws out a conjecture that artificial figures are here meant; which mechanically performed the function herein assigned to them.

sanskrit: परम आस्तरण आस्तीर्णम् आविक अजिन सम्व्र्तम्
transliteration: parama āstaraṇa āstīrṇam āvika ajina samvrtam
english: Around which persons kept waving with their hands chowris furnished with hair;* rife with perfumes of various kinds; odorous with rich dhupa, spread with excellent sheets; covered with the skins of rams; and decked on all sides with chaplets of gorgeous flowers. *The commentator throws out a conjecture that artificial figures are here meant; which mechanically performed the function herein assigned to them.

sanskrit: तस्मिन् जीमूत सम्काशम् प्रदीप्त उत्तम कुण्डलम्
लोहित अक्षम् महा बाहुम् महा रजत वाससम्
transliteration: tasmin jīmūta samkāśam pradīpta uttama kuṇḍalam
lohita akṣam mahā bāhum mahā rajata vāsasam

sanskrit: सम्ध्या रक्तम् इव आकाशे तोयदम् सतडिद् गुणम्
transliteration: samdhyā raktam iva ākāśe toyadam sataḍid guṇam

sanskrit: वृतम् आभरणैर् दिव्यैः सुरूपम् काम रूपिणम्
सव्र्क्ष वन गुल्म आढ्यम् प्रसुप्तम् इव मन्दरम्
transliteration: vṛtam ābharaṇair divyaiḥ surūpam kāma rūpiṇam
savrkṣa vana gulma āḍhyam prasuptam iva mandaram

sanskrit: क्रीडित्वा उपरतम् रात्रौ वर आभरण भूषितम्
प्रियम् राक्षस कन्यानाम् राक्षसानाम् सुख आवहम्
transliteration: krīḍitvā uparatam rātrau vara ābharaṇa bhūṣitam
priyam rākṣasa kanyānām rākṣasānām sukha āvaham

sanskrit: पीत्वा अपि उपरतम् च अपि ददर्श स महा कपिः
भास्करे शयने वीरम् प्रसुप्तम् राक्षस अधिपम्
transliteration: pītvā api uparatam ca api dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ
bhāskare śayane vīram prasuptam rākṣasa adhipam

sanskrit: निह्श्वसन्तम् यथा नागम् रावणम् वानर उत्तमः
आसाद्य परम उद्विग्नः सो अपासर्पत् सुभीतवत्
transliteration: nihśvasantam yathā nāgam rāvaṇam vānara uttamaḥ
āsādya parama udvignaḥ so apāsarpat subhītavat
english: Respiring like a (hissing) serpent.* And reaching there, Hanumān, waxing wondrous agitated, shrank back, as if in fear. And then arriving at the staircase, the mighty monkey, stationing himself on a dais in the middle of the stairs, gazed at the inebriate, Raksasa, resembling a tiger. 'The commentator, however, interprets: like an elephant. Serpent is, I fancy, a happy rendering of Nāga.

sanskrit: अथ आरोहणम् आसाद्य वेदिका अन्तरम् आश्रितः
सुप्तम् राक्षस शार्दूलम् प्रेक्षते स्म महा कपिः
transliteration: atha ārohaṇam āsādya vedikā antaram āśritaḥ
suptam rākṣasa śārdūlam prekṣate sma mahā kapiḥ
english: Respiring like a (hissing) serpent.* And reaching there, Hanumān, waxing wondrous agitated, shrank back, as if in fear. And then arriving at the staircase, the mighty monkey, stationing himself on a dais in the middle of the stairs, gazed at the inebriate, Raksasa, resembling a tiger. 'The commentator, however, interprets: like an elephant. Serpent is, I fancy, a happy rendering of Nāga.

sanskrit: शुशुभे राक्षस इन्द्रस्य स्वपतः शयन उत्तमम्
गन्ध हस्तिनि सम्विष्टे यथा प्रस्रवणम् महत्
transliteration: śuśubhe rākṣasa indrasya svapataḥ śayana uttamam
gandha hastini samviṣṭe yathā prasravaṇam mahat
english: As the sovereign of the Rākșasas was sleeping, his graceful bed resembled a grand cascade, beside which stands an elephant breathing odour.

sanskrit: कान्चन अन्गद नद्धौ च ददर्श स महात्मनः
विक्षिप्तौ राक्षस इन्द्रस्य भुजाव् इन्द्र ध्वज उपमौ
transliteration: kāncana angada naddhau ca dadarśa sa mahātmanaḥ
vikṣiptau rākṣasa indrasya bhujāv indra dhvaja upamau
english: Hanuman saw the arms of the huge-bodied lord of Raksasas, fastened with bracelets, stretched (there), like to the banners of Indra;

sanskrit: ऐरावत विषाण अग्रैर् आपीडित क्र्त व्रणौ
वज्र उल्लिखित पीन अम्सौ विष्णु चक्र परिक्षितौ
transliteration: airāvata viṣāṇa agrair āpīḍita krta vraṇau
vajra ullikhita pīna amsau viṣṇu cakra parikṣitau
english: Which had been wounded by the tusk-ends of Airāvata, whose plump parts had been riven by vajra; and which had been torn by the discus of Visnu;

sanskrit: पीनौ समसुजात अम्सौ सम्गतौ बल सम्युतौ
सुलक्षण नख अन्गुष्ठौ स्वन्गुली तल लक्षितौ
transliteration: pīnau samasujāta amsau samgatau bala samyutau
sulakṣaṇa nakha anguṣṭhau svangulī tala lakṣitau
english: Well developed; having equal and elegant parts; with hard joints; fraught with strength; with thumbs having nails bearing auspicious marks; having rings (on the fingers); covered; formed like bludgeons; round; resembling the trunks of elephants; cast on the white bed like to five-hooded serpents;

sanskrit: सम्हतौ परिघ आकारौ व्र्त्तौ करि कर उपमौ
विक्षिप्तौ शयने शुभ्रे पन्च शीर्षाव् इव उरगौ
transliteration: samhatau parigha ākārau vrttau kari kara upamau
vikṣiptau śayane śubhre panca śīrṣāv iva uragau
english: Well developed; having equal and elegant parts; with hard joints; fraught with strength; with thumbs having nails bearing auspicious marks; having rings (on the fingers); covered; formed like bludgeons; round; resembling the trunks of elephants; cast on the white bed like to five-hooded serpents;

Smeared and adorned with cool, fragrant, and excellent sandal resembling the blood of hares; pressed by paragons; odorous with incense; resisting (in battle) Yaksas, and Pannagas, Gandharvas, gods and Dānavas.

sanskrit: उत्तम स्त्री विम्र्दितौ गन्ध उत्तम निषेवितौ
यक्ष पन्नग गन्धर्व देव दानव राविणौ
transliteration: uttama strī vimrditau gandha uttama niṣevitau
yakṣa pannaga gandharva deva dānava rāviṇau
english: Smeared and adorned with cool, fragrant, and excellent sandal resembling the blood of hares; pressed by paragons; odorous with incense; resisting (in battle) Yaksas, and Pannagas, Gandharvas, gods and Dānavas.

sanskrit: ददर्श स कपिः तस्य बाहू शयन सम्स्थितौ
मन्दरस्य अन्तरे सुप्तौ महा अर्ही रुषिताव् इव
transliteration: dadarśa sa kapiḥ tasya bāhū śayana samsthitau
mandarasya antare suptau mahā arhī ruṣitāv iva
english: That monkey saw his arms resting on the bed, like to two beautiful and mighty serpents sleeping in the entrails of Mandara.

sanskrit: ताभ्याम् स परिपूर्णाभ्याम् भुजाभ्याम् राक्षस अधिपः
शुशुभे अचल सम्काशः श्र्न्गाभ्याम् इव मन्दरः
transliteration: tābhyām sa paripūrṇābhyām bhujābhyām rākṣasa adhipaḥ
śuśubhe acala samkāśaḥ śrngābhyām iva mandaraḥ
english: With both those well developed arms of his, the lord of Rākṣasas resembling a hill, looked handsome like Mandara with its summits.

sanskrit: चूत पुम्नाग सुरभिर् बकुल उत्तम सम्युतः
मृष्ट अन्न रस सम्युक्तः पान गन्ध पुरः सरः
transliteration: cūta pumnāga surabhir bakula uttama samyutaḥ
mṛṣṭa anna rasa samyuktaḥ pāna gandha puraḥ saraḥ
english: And breath bearing the aroma of the mango, and the Punnāga, the sweet scent of the Bakula, the savour of viands fraught with the six kinds of tastes, and the perfume of wines, came out of the mighty mouth of the sovereign of the Rākşasas, filling as it were, that entire chamber.

sanskrit: तस्य राक्षस सिम्हस्य निश्चक्राम मुखान् महान्
शयानस्य विनिह्श्वासः पूरयन्न् इव तद् ग्र्हम्
transliteration: tasya rākṣasa simhasya niścakrāma mukhān mahān
śayānasya vinihśvāsaḥ pūrayann iva tad grham
english: And breath bearing the aroma of the mango, and the Punnāga, the sweet scent of the Bakula, the savour of viands fraught with the six kinds of tastes, and the perfume of wines, came out of the mighty mouth of the sovereign of the Rākşasas, filling as it were, that entire chamber.

sanskrit: रक्त चन्दन दिग्धेन तथा हारेण शोभिता
transliteration: rakta candana digdhena tathā hāreṇa śobhitā

sanskrit: महा अर्हेण सुसम्वीतम् पीतेन उत्तम वाससा
transliteration: mahā arheṇa susamvītam pītena uttama vāsasā

sanskrit: गान्गे महति तोय अन्ते प्रसुतमिव कुन्जरम्
transliteration: gānge mahati toya ante prasutamiva kunjaram

sanskrit: चतुर्भिः कान्चनैर् दीपैर् दीप्यमानैः चतुर् दिशम्
प्रकाशी क्र्त सर्व अन्गम् मेघम् विद्युद् गणैर् इव
transliteration: caturbhiḥ kāncanair dīpair dīpyamānaiḥ catur diśam
prakāśī krta sarva angam megham vidyud gaṇair iva

sanskrit: पाद मूल गताः च अपि ददर्श सुमहात्मनः
पत्नीः स प्रिय भार्यस्य तस्य रक्षः पतेर् ग्र्हे
transliteration: pāda mūla gatāḥ ca api dadarśa sumahātmanaḥ
patnīḥ sa priya bhāryasya tasya rakṣaḥ pater grhe
english: He (Hanumān) also saw in the mansion of the Rākşas chief, the wives of that huge bodied one dear to his wives, lying at his feet.

sanskrit: शशि प्रकाश वदना वर कुण्डल भूषिताः
अम्बाल माल्य आभरणा ददर्श हरि यूथपः
transliteration: śaśi prakāśa vadanā vara kuṇḍala bhūṣitāḥ
ambāla mālya ābharaṇā dadarśa hari yūthapaḥ
english: That protector of monkey-bands saw them, having countenances resembling the Moon displayed; decked out with elegant ear-rings; bearing unfading garlands* by way of ornamentation; lying on the arms and lap of the lord of the Räksasa. *i.e. celestial females.

sanskrit: नृत्त वादित्र कुशला राक्षस इन्द्र भुज अन्कगाः
वर आभरण धारिण्यो निषन्ना दद्र्शे कपिः
transliteration: nṛtta vāditra kuśalā rākṣasa indra bhuja ankagāḥ
vara ābharaṇa dhāriṇyo niṣannā dadrśe kapiḥ

sanskrit: वज्र वैदूर्य गर्भाणि श्रवण अन्तेषु योषिताम्
transliteration: vajra vaidūrya garbhāṇi śravaṇa anteṣu yoṣitām
english: The monkey saw women bearing noble ornaments, lying down. And he saw golden bracelets and ear-rings at the nether ends of the women's ears, set with diamonds and lapises.

sanskrit: तासाम् चन्द्र उपमैर् वक्त्रैः शुभैर् ललित कुण्डलैः
विरराज विमानम् तन् नभः तारा गणैर् इव
transliteration: tāsām candra upamair vaktraiḥ śubhair lalita kuṇḍalaiḥ
virarāja vimānam tan nabhaḥ tārā gaṇair iva
english: With their fair countenances resembling the Moon, graced with comely ear-rings, that terrace looked beautiful, like the welking embellished with stars.

sanskrit: मद व्यायाम खिन्नाः ताः राक्षस इन्द्रस्य योषितः
तेषु तेष्व् अवकाशेषु प्रसुप्ताः तनु मध्यमाः
transliteration: mada vyāyāma khinnāḥ tāḥ rākṣasa indrasya yoṣitaḥ
teṣu teṣv avakāśeṣu prasuptāḥ tanu madhyamāḥ
english: The slender-waisted wives of the sovereign of the Rākşasas, overcome with languor consequent on drink and amorous encounter, were fast asleep at the very places where they were seated.
And another transcendentally beautiful damsel possessed of lovely limbs, skilled in dance, was fast asleep, betraying comely movement (during sleep).

sanskrit: महा नदी प्रकीर्णा इव नलिनी पोतम् आश्रिता
transliteration: mahā nadī prakīrṇā iva nalinī potam āśritā
english: Another was seen asleep, embracing a Vīņā, like a lotus with spreading petals, resting by the side of a raft.

sanskrit: अन्या कक्ष गतेन एव मड्डुकेन असित ईक्षणा
प्रसुप्ता भामिनी भाति बाल पुत्रा इव वत्सला
transliteration: anyā kakṣa gatena eva maḍḍukena asita īkṣaṇā
prasuptā bhāminī bhāti bāla putrā iva vatsalā
english: And another dark-eyed which was asleep with her mudduka* on her lap, like a loving mother having a boy. *A kind of musical instrument.

sanskrit: पटहम् चारु सर्व अन्गी पीड्य शेते शुभ स्तनी
चिरस्य रमणम् लब्ध्वा परिष्वज्य इव कामिनी
transliteration: paṭaham cāru sarva angī pīḍya śete śubha stanī
cirasya ramaṇam labdhvā pariṣvajya iva kāminī
english: Another damsel possessed of graceful limbs and a shapely bust, was lying down, hugging her kettle-drum, like a woman embracing her lover obtained after a long time.

sanskrit: काचिद् अम्शम् परिष्वज्य सुप्ता कमल लोचना
रहः प्रियतमम् गृह्य सकामेव च कामिनी
transliteration: kācid amśam pariṣvajya suptā kamala locanā
rahaḥ priyatamam gṛhya sakāmeva ca kāminī
english: One lotus-eyed female was asleep, embracing her Vīņā; like an amorous dainsel hugging her fair paramour.

sanskrit: निद्रा वशम् अनुप्राप्ता सह कान्ता इव भामिनी
transliteration: nidrā vaśam anuprāptā saha kāntā iva bhāminī
english: And another girl of restrained self, given to dancing, had come under the sway of sleep embracing her vipanci* like a female sleeping with her lover. *A kind of Vina.

sanskrit: अन्या कनक सम्काशैर् म्र्दु पीनैर् मनो रमैः
मृदन्गम् परिपीड्य अन्गैः प्रसुप्ता मत्त लोचना
transliteration: anyā kanaka samkāśair mrdu pīnair mano ramaiḥ
mṛdangam paripīḍya angaiḥ prasuptā matta locanā
english: Another having inebriate eyes, was fast asleep, embracing her mridanga with her charming, plump, and tender limbs, resembling gold.

sanskrit: भुज पार्श्व अन्तरस्थेन कक्षगेन क्र्श उदरी
पणवेन सह अनिन्द्या सुप्ता मद क्र्त श्रमा
transliteration: bhuja pārśva antarasthena kakṣagena krśa udarī
paṇavena saha anindyā suptā mada krta śramā
english: Another female of faultless features, endued with a slender frame, having been overcome by lassitude consequent on drink, was asleep, with her panava on the ends of her lower garment, held fast with her hands.

sanskrit: डिण्डिमम् परिग्र्ह्य अन्या तथैव आसक्त डिण्डिमा
प्रसुप्ता तरुणम् वत्सम् उपगूह्य इव भामिनी
transliteration: ḍiṇḍimam parigrhya anyā tathaiva āsakta ḍiṇḍimā
prasuptā taruṇam vatsam upagūhya iva bhāminī
english: Another woman was sleeping soundly, embracing her dindima,* with another, bound at her back; like a female taking both her lover and her child. *A kind of musical instrument.

sanskrit: काचिद् आडम्बरम् नारी भुज सम्भोग पीडितम्
कृत्वा कमल पत्र अक्षी प्रसुप्ता मद मोहिता
transliteration: kācid āḍambaram nārī bhuja sambhoga pīḍitam
kṛtvā kamala patra akṣī prasuptā mada mohitā
english: Another damsel having eyes resembling lotuspetals, having come under the influence of liquor, was asleep, firmly holding her aramvara' with her hands. A kind of musical instrument.

sanskrit: कलशीम् अपविद्ध्य अन्या प्रसुप्ता भाति भामिनी
वसन्ते पुष्प शबला माला इव परिमार्जिता
transliteration: kalaśīm apaviddhya anyā prasuptā bhāti bhāminī
vasante puṣpa śabalā mālā iva parimārjitā
english: Another woman, intoxicated by wine, was discovered asleep, with her water-vessel upset; and, in consequence, appearing like a wellwashed variegated wreath in spring.

sanskrit: पाणिभ्याम् च कुचौ काचित् सुवर्ण कलश उपमौ
उपगूह्य अबला सुप्ता निद्रा बल पराजिता
transliteration: pāṇibhyām ca kucau kācit suvarṇa kalaśa upamau
upagūhya abalā suptā nidrā bala parājitā
english: Another, coming under the masterdom of slumber, was sleeping, holding with her hands her twin breasts resembling golden jars.

sanskrit: अन्या कमल पत्र अक्षी पूर्ण इन्दु सद्र्श आनना
अन्याम् आलिन्ग्य सुश्रोणी प्रसुप्ता मद विह्वला
transliteration: anyā kamala patra akṣī pūrṇa indu sadrśa ānanā
anyām ālingya suśroṇī prasuptā mada vihvalā
english: And another lotus-eyed and moon-faced fair one, coming under the governance of slumber, (was asleep), embracing another furnished with shapely hips.

sanskrit: निपीड्य च कुचैः सुप्ताः कामिन्यः कामुकान् इव
transliteration: nipīḍya ca kucaiḥ suptāḥ kāminyaḥ kāmukān iva
english: And eminently beautiful dames were asleep, embracing musical instruments; like wenches pressing lustful (lovers), with their breasts.

sanskrit: तासाम् एक अन्त विन्यस्ते शयानाम् शयने शुभे
ददर्श रूप सम्पन्नाम् अपराम् स कपिः स्त्रियम्
transliteration: tāsām eka anta vinyaste śayānām śayane śubhe
dadarśa rūpa sampannām aparām sa kapiḥ striyam
english: That monkey saw that lady, endued with beauty, lying down apart in an excellent bed; adorned with ornaments containing pearls and jewels; and as if decorating that charming mansion with her grace.

sanskrit: विभूषयन्तीम् इव च स्व श्रिया भवन उत्तमम्
transliteration: vibhūṣayantīm iva ca sva śriyā bhavana uttamam
english: That monkey saw that lady, endued with beauty, lying down apart in an excellent bed; adorned with ornaments containing pearls and jewels; and as if decorating that charming mansion with her grace.

sanskrit: गौरीम् कनक वर्ण आभाम् इष्टाम् अन्तः पुर ईश्वरीम्
कपिर् मन्द उदरीम् तत्र शयानाम् चारु रूपिणीम्
transliteration: gaurīm kanaka varṇa ābhām iṣṭām antaḥ pura īśvarīm
kapir manda udarīm tatra śayānām cāru rūpiṇīm

sanskrit: स ताम् दृष्ट्वा महा बाहुर् भूषिताम् मारुत आत्मजः
तर्कयाम् आस सीता इति रूप यौवन सम्पदा
transliteration: sa tām dṛṣṭvā mahā bāhur bhūṣitām māruta ātmajaḥ
tarkayām āsa sītā iti rūpa yauvana sampadā

sanskrit: हर्षेण महता युक्तो ननन्द हरि यूथपः
transliteration: harṣeṇa mahatā yukto nananda hari yūthapaḥ
english: Thereat, (Hanumăn) struck at his arms with his hands, kissed his tail, exhibited signs of glee, frolicked, sang, darted towards the pillars, shoot up to the top thereof, and jumbed down to the earth, manifesting his monkey-nature.

sanskrit: अवधूय च ताम् बुद्धिम् बभूव अवस्थितः तदा
जगाम च अपराम् चिन्ताम् सीताम् प्रति महा कपिः
transliteration: avadhūya ca tām buddhim babhūva avasthitaḥ tadā
jagāma ca aparām cintām sītām prati mahā kapiḥ
english: Then resigning that line of thought, that mighty monkey, regaining his equanimity, set out in another direction of thought touching Sītā.

sanskrit: न रामेण वियुक्ता सा स्वप्तुम् अर्हति भामिनी
न भोक्तुम् न अपि अलम्कर्तुम् न पानम् उपसेवितुम्
transliteration: na rāmeṇa viyuktā sā svaptum arhati bhāminī
na bhoktum na api alamkartum na pānam upasevitum
english: Separated from Rāma, that lady is incapable of sleeping, or eating, or decorating (her person), or drinking.

sanskrit: न अन्यम् नरम् उपस्थातुम् सुराणाम् अपि च ईश्वरम्
न हि राम समः कश्चिद् विद्यते त्रिदशेष्व् अपि
transliteration: na anyam naram upasthātum surāṇām api ca īśvaram
na hi rāma samaḥ kaścid vidyate tridaśeṣv api
english: She is incapable of associating with any other person, although he were the sovereign of the celestials himself. And even in all heaven there is none who is equal to Rāma.

sanskrit: अन्या इयम् इति निश्चित्य पान भूमौ चचार सः
क्रीडितेन अपराः क्लान्ता गीतेन च तथा पराः
transliteration: anyā iyam iti niścitya pāna bhūmau cacāra saḥ
krīḍitena aparāḥ klāntā gītena ca tathā parāḥ

sanskrit: नृत्तेन च अपराः क्लान्ताः पान विप्रहताः तथा
transliteration: nṛttena ca aparāḥ klāntāḥ pāna viprahatāḥ tathā

sanskrit: तथा आस्तरण मुख्य्येषु सम्विष्टाः च अपराः स्त्रियः
transliteration: tathā āstaraṇa mukhyyeṣu samviṣṭāḥ ca aparāḥ striyaḥ

sanskrit: रूप सम्ल्लाप शीलेन युक्त गीत अर्थ भाषिणा
देश काल अभियुक्तेन युक्त वाक्य अभिधायिना
transliteration: rūpa samllāpa śīlena yukta gīta artha bhāṣiṇā
deśa kāla abhiyuktena yukta vākya abhidhāyinā

sanskrit: रत अभिरत सम्सुप्तम् ददर्श हरि यूथपः
तासाम् मध्ये महा बाहुः शुशुभे राक्षस ईश्वरः
transliteration: rata abhirata samsuptam dadarśa hari yūthapaḥ
tāsām madhye mahā bāhuḥ śuśubhe rākṣasa īśvaraḥ

sanskrit: गोष्ठे महति मुख्यानाम् गवाम् मध्ये यथा वृषः
स राक्षस इन्द्रः शुशुभे ताभिः परिवृतः स्वयम्
transliteration: goṣṭhe mahati mukhyānām gavām madhye yathā vṛṣaḥ
sa rākṣasa indraḥ śuśubhe tābhiḥ parivṛtaḥ svayam

sanskrit: करेणुभिर् यथा अरण्यम् परिकीर्णो महा द्विपः
सर्व कामैर् उपेताम् च पान भूमिम् महात्मनः
transliteration: kareṇubhir yathā araṇyam parikīrṇo mahā dvipaḥ
sarva kāmair upetām ca pāna bhūmim mahātmanaḥ

sanskrit: ददर्श कपि शार्दूलः तस्य रक्षः पतेर् गृहे
मृगाणाम् महिषाणाम् च वराहाणाम् च भागशः
transliteration: dadarśa kapi śārdūlaḥ tasya rakṣaḥ pater gṛhe
mṛgāṇām mahiṣāṇām ca varāhāṇām ca bhāgaśaḥ
english: In the abode of the huge-bodied Rākşasa chief, that tiger like monkey saw that place of drinking, furnished with every object of desire.

sanskrit: तत्र न्यस्तानि माम्सानि पान भूमौ ददर्श सः
रौक्मेषु च विशलेषु भाजनेष्व् अर्ध भक्षितान्
transliteration: tatra nyastāni māmsāni pāna bhūmau dadarśa saḥ
raukmeṣu ca viśaleṣu bhājaneṣv ardha bhakṣitān

sanskrit: ददर्श कपि शार्दूल मयूरान् कुक्कुटामः तथा
transliteration: dadarśa kapi śārdūla mayūrān kukkuṭāmaḥ tathā

sanskrit: शल्यान् म्Rग मयूरामः च हनूमान् अन्ववैक्षत
कृकरान् विविधान् सिद्धामः चकोरान् अर्ध भक्षितान्
transliteration: śalyān mga mayūrāmaḥ ca hanūmān anvavaikṣata
kṛkarān vividhān siddhāmaḥ cakorān ardha bhakṣitān

sanskrit: महिषान् एक शल्यामः च चागामः च कृत निष्ठितान्
लेख्यम् उच्च अवचम् पेयम् भोज्यानि विविधानि च
transliteration: mahiṣān eka śalyāmaḥ ca cāgāmaḥ ca kṛta niṣṭhitān
lekhyam ucca avacam peyam bhojyāni vividhāni ca

sanskrit: तथा अम्ल लवण उत्तम्सैर् विविधै राग षाडवैः
हार नूपुर केयूरैर् अपविद्धैर् महा धनैः
transliteration: tathā amla lavaṇa uttamsair vividhai rāga ṣāḍavaiḥ
hāra nūpura keyūrair apaviddhair mahā dhanaiḥ

sanskrit: पान भाजन विक्षिप्तैः फलैः च विविधैर् अपि
कृत पुष्प उपहारा भूर् अधिकम् पुष्यति श्रियम्
transliteration: pāna bhājana vikṣiptaiḥ phalaiḥ ca vividhair api
kṛta puṣpa upahārā bhūr adhikam puṣyati śriyam
english: With large and costly stray bangles and bracelests; and scattered cans, and diverse kinds of fruit; and wreaths of flowers, the pavement attained exceeding beauty.

sanskrit: तत्र तत्र च विन्यस्तैः सुश्लिष्टैः शयन आसनैः
पान भूमिर् विना वह्निम् प्रदीप्ता इव उपलक्ष्यते
transliteration: tatra tatra ca vinyastaiḥ suśliṣṭaiḥ śayana āsanaiḥ
pāna bhūmir vinā vahnim pradīptā iva upalakṣyate
english: And with elegantly jointed bedsteads, arranged (around), the scene of wassail appeared aflame without fire.

sanskrit: बहु प्रकारैर् विविधैर् वर सम्स्कार सम्स्कृतैः
माम्सैः कुशल सम्युक्तैः पान भूमि गतैः पृथक्
transliteration: bahu prakārair vividhair vara samskāra samskṛtaiḥ
māmsaiḥ kuśala samyuktaiḥ pāna bhūmi gataiḥ pṛthak

sanskrit: दिव्याः प्रसन्ना विविधाः सुराः कृत सुरा अपि
शर्कर आसव माध्वीकाः पुष्प आसव फल आसवाः
transliteration: divyāḥ prasannā vividhāḥ surāḥ kṛta surā api
śarkara āsava mādhvīkāḥ puṣpa āsava phala āsavāḥ

sanskrit: वास चूर्णैः च विविधैर् मृष्टाः तैः तैः पृथक् पृथक्
सम्तता शुशुभे भूमिर् माल्यैः च बहु सम्स्थितैः
transliteration: vāsa cūrṇaiḥ ca vividhair mṛṣṭāḥ taiḥ taiḥ pṛthak pṛthak
samtatā śuśubhe bhūmir mālyaiḥ ca bahu samsthitaiḥ

sanskrit: हिरण्मयैः च करकैर् भाजनैः स्फाटिकैर् अपि
transliteration: hiraṇmayaiḥ ca karakair bhājanaiḥ sphāṭikair api

sanskrit: पान श्रेष्ठम् तदा भूरि कपिः तत्र ददर्श ह
transliteration: pāna śreṣṭham tadā bhūri kapiḥ tatra dadarśa ha
english: The monkey saw that foremost of all places set apart for drinking, containing silver and golden jars.

sanskrit: सो अपश्यत् शात कुम्भानि शीधोर् मणिमयानि च
राजतानि च पूर्णानि भाजनानि महा कपिः
transliteration: so apaśyat śāta kumbhāni śīdhor maṇimayāni ca
rājatāni ca pūrṇāni bhājanāni mahā kapiḥ
english: That mighty monkey saw golden wine-vessels studded with gems, all filled with wine; and some with half full of liquor, some with their wine entirely exhausted, and some full of liquor.

sanskrit: क्वचिद् अर्ध अवशेषाणि क्वचित् पीतानि सर्वशः
क्वचिन् न एव प्रपीतानि पानानि स ददर्श ह
transliteration: kvacid ardha avaśeṣāṇi kvacit pītāni sarvaśaḥ
kvacin na eva prapītāni pānāni sa dadarśa ha
english: That mighty monkey saw golden wine-vessels studded with gems, all filled with wine; and some with half full of liquor, some with their wine entirely exhausted, and some full of liquor.

sanskrit: क्वचिद् भक्ष्यामः च विविधान् क्वचित् पानानि भागशः
क्वचिद् अन्न अवशेषाणि पश्यन् वै विचचार ह
transliteration: kvacid bhakṣyāmaḥ ca vividhān kvacit pānāni bhāgaśaḥ
kvacid anna avaśeṣāṇi paśyan vai vicacāra ha
english: And (at some spots) he saw various kinds of viands, and at other wines ranged in rows, and at others the wine-vessels remaining half full.

sanskrit: क्वचित् प्रभिन्नैः करकैः क्वचिद् आलोडितैर् घटैः
क्वचित् सम्पृक्त माल्यानि जलानि च फलानि च
transliteration: kvacit prabhinnaiḥ karakaiḥ kvacid āloḍitair ghaṭaiḥ
kvacit sampṛkta mālyāni jalāni ca phalāni ca

sanskrit: शयनानि अत्र नारीणाम् शून्यानि बहुधा पुनः
परस्परम् समाश्लिष्य काश्चित् सुप्ता वर अन्गनाः
transliteration: śayanāni atra nārīṇām śūnyāni bahudhā punaḥ
parasparam samāśliṣya kāścit suptā vara anganāḥ
english: There were many bedsteads belonging to fair ones, remaining vacant; and at some places excellent women were sleeping touching each other.

sanskrit: काचिच् च वस्त्रम् अन्यस्या अपह्Rत्य उपगुह्य च
उपगम्य अबला सुप्ता निद्रा बल पराजिता
transliteration: kācic ca vastram anyasyā apahtya upaguhya ca
upagamya abalā suptā nidrā bala parājitā
english: And at one place, a female, borne down by the force of sleep, forcibly possessing herself of another's cloth, and wrapping herself there with, went to the bed of that one, and was indulging in sleep.

sanskrit: तासाम् उच्च्वास वातेन वस्त्रम् माल्यम् च गात्रजम्
न अत्यर्थम् स्पन्दते चित्रम् प्राप्य मन्दम् इव अनिलम्
transliteration: tāsām uccvāsa vātena vastram mālyam ca gātrajam
na atyartham spandate citram prāpya mandam iva anilam
english: And with their breath, their variegated wreaths and the cloth on their persons were stirring gently, as if with a mild-blowing breeze.

sanskrit: चन्दनस्य च शीतस्य शीधोर् मधु रसस्य च
विविधस्य च माल्यस्य पुष्पस्य विविधस्य च
transliteration: candanasya ca śītasya śīdhor madhu rasasya ca
vividhasya ca mālyasya puṣpasya vividhasya ca
english: Laden with the odours of cool sandal, and of sweet-tasting Sidhu; and of diverse wreaths and flowers, and with perfumes of various kinds, and entranced with (the aroma) of sandals suitable for use after ablution, and of dhupas, the air, impregnated with excellent scent, was there breathing around the car Puşpaka.

sanskrit: बहुधा मारुतः तत्र गन्धम् विविधम् उद्वहन्
स्नानानाम् चन्दनानाम् च धूपानाम् चैव मूर्चितः
प्रववौ सुरभिर् गन्धो विमाने पुष्पके तदा
transliteration: bahudhā mārutaḥ tatra gandham vividham udvahan
snānānām candanānām ca dhūpānām caiva mūrcitaḥ
pravavau surabhir gandho vimāne puṣpake tadā

sanskrit: श्याम अवदाताः तत्र अन्याः काश्चित् कृष्णा वर अन्गनाः
transliteration: śyāma avadātāḥ tatra anyāḥ kāścit kṛṣṇā vara anganāḥ

sanskrit: काश्चित् कान्चन वर्ण अन्ग्यः प्रमदा राक्षस आलये
तासाम् निद्रा वशत्वाच् च मदनेन विमूर्चितम्
transliteration: kāścit kāncana varṇa angyaḥ pramadā rākṣasa ālaye
tāsām nidrā vaśatvāc ca madanena vimūrcitam

sanskrit: पद्मिनीनाम् प्रसुप्तानाम् रूपम् आसीद् यथैव हि
एवम् सर्वम् अशेषेण रावण अन्तः पुरम् कपिः
transliteration: padminīnām prasuptānām rūpam āsīd yathaiva hi
evam sarvam aśeṣeṇa rāvaṇa antaḥ puram kapiḥ

sanskrit: ददर्श सुमहा तेजा न ददर्श च जानकीम्
निरीक्षमाणः च ततः ताः स्त्रियः स महा कपिः
transliteration: dadarśa sumahā tejā na dadarśa ca jānakīm
nirīkṣamāṇaḥ ca tataḥ tāḥ striyaḥ sa mahā kapiḥ

sanskrit: जगाम महतीम् चिन्ताम् धर्म साध्वस शन्कितः
transliteration: jagāma mahatīm cintām dharma sādhvasa śankitaḥ

sanskrit: इदम् खलु मम अत्यर्थम् धर्म लोपम् करिष्यति
न हि मे पर दाराणाम् दृष्टिर् विषय वर्तिनी
transliteration: idam khalu mama atyartham dharma lopam kariṣyati
na hi me para dārāṇām dṛṣṭir viṣaya vartinī

sanskrit: अयम् च अत्र मया दृष्टः पर दार परिग्रहः
तस्य प्रादुर् अभूच् चिन्ता पुनर् अन्या मनस्विनः
transliteration: ayam ca atra mayā dṛṣṭaḥ para dāra parigrahaḥ
tasya prādur abhūc cintā punar anyā manasvinaḥ

sanskrit: निश्चित एक अन्त चित्तस्य कार्य निश्चय दर्शिनी
कामम् दृष्ट्वा मया सर्वा विश्वस्ता रावण स्त्रियः
transliteration: niścita eka anta cittasya kārya niścaya darśinī
kāmam dṛṣṭvā mayā sarvā viśvastā rāvaṇa striyaḥ

sanskrit: न तु मे मनसः किम्चिद् वैकृत्यम् उपपद्यते
मनो हि हेतुः सर्वेषाम् इन्द्रियाणाम् प्रवर्तते
transliteration: na tu me manasaḥ kimcid vaikṛtyam upapadyate
mano hi hetuḥ sarveṣām indriyāṇām pravartate

sanskrit: शुभ अशुभास्व् अवस्थासु तच् च मे सुव्यवस्थितम्
न अन्यत्र हि मया शक्या वैदेही परिमार्गितुम्
transliteration: śubha aśubhāsv avasthāsu tac ca me suvyavasthitam
na anyatra hi mayā śakyā vaidehī parimārgitum

sanskrit: स्त्रियो हि स्त्रीषु द्Rश्यन्ते सदा सम्परिमार्गणे
यस्य सत्त्वस्य या योनिः तस्याम् तत् परिमार्ग्यते
transliteration: striyo hi strīṣu dśyante sadā samparimārgaṇe
yasya sattvasya yā yoniḥ tasyām tat parimārgyate

sanskrit: न शक्यम् प्रमदा नष्टा मृगीषु परिमार्गितुम्
तद् इदम् मार्गितम् तावत् शुद्धेन मनसा मया
transliteration: na śakyam pramadā naṣṭā mṛgīṣu parimārgitum
tad idam mārgitam tāvat śuddhena manasā mayā

sanskrit: रावण अन्तः पुरम् सरम् दृश्यते न च जानकी
देव गन्धर्व कन्याः च नाग कन्याः च वीर्यवान्
transliteration: rāvaṇa antaḥ puram saram dṛśyate na ca jānakī
deva gandharva kanyāḥ ca nāga kanyāḥ ca vīryavān

sanskrit: अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान् न एव अपश्यत जानकीम्
ताम् अपश्यन् कपिः तत्र पश्यमः च अन्या वर स्त्रियः
transliteration: avekṣamāṇo hanumān na eva apaśyata jānakīm
tām apaśyan kapiḥ tatra paśyamaḥ ca anyā vara striyaḥ

sanskrit: लता ग्Rहामः चित्र गृहान् निशा गृहान्
न च एव ताम् पश्यति चारु दर्शनाम्
transliteration: latā ghāmaḥ citra gṛhān niśā gṛhān
na ca eva tām paśyati cāru darśanām
english: Remaining in that mansion, (Hanuman) desirous of getting a sight of Sītā graced with a fair presence, went into bowers, and picture galleries, and night-houses;* but her he did not find. *Intended for stay at night.

sanskrit: स चिन्तयाम् आस ततो महा कपिः
ध्रुवम् नु सीता म्रियते यथा न मे
transliteration: sa cintayām āsa tato mahā kapiḥ
dhruvam nu sītā mriyate yathā na me
english: And not finding the beloved (spouse) of Raghu's son that mighty monkey reflected, “Surely Sītā is not alive, for although I have searched (through and through), yet Mithila's daughter I have failed to find."

sanskrit: स्व शील सम्रक्षण तत् परा सती
हता भवेद् आर्य पथे परे स्थिता
transliteration: sva śīla samrakṣaṇa tat parā satī
hatā bhaved ārya pathe pare sthitā
english: That girl solicitous for the preservation of her chastity, and staying in the prime path of virtuous woman, that chaste one has, for certain, been slain by this chief of the Rākṣasas, (ever) finding delight in iniquity.
Seeing the wives of the Rākṣasa inonarch, of frightful forms, monstrous; of lurid hue; having huge faces; with large horrid eyes, the daughter of Janaka has given up the ghost from fright.

sanskrit: न मे अस्ति सुग्रीव समीपगा गतिः
transliteration: na me asti sugrīva samīpagā gatiḥ
english: Failing to see Sītā, and (thereby) annulling my prowess, and having long spent the appointed space in company with the monkeys, way have I none to present myself before Sugrīva, that monkey being puissant and given to meting out sharp chastisement.

sanskrit: दृष्टम् अन्तः पुरम् सर्वम् दृष्ट्वा रावण योषितः
न सीता दृश्यते साध्वी वृथा जातो मम श्रमः
transliteration: dṛṣṭam antaḥ puram sarvam dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇa yoṣitaḥ
na sītā dṛśyate sādhvī vṛthā jāto mama śramaḥ
english: Having searched the inner apartment through, and seen the wives of the Rākṣasa, I do not see the chaste Sită. Therefore vain is the trouble that I take.

sanskrit: किम् नु माम् वानराः सर्वे गतम् वक्ष्यन्ति सम्गताः
गत्वा तत्र त्वया वीर किम् कृतम् तद् वदस्व नः
transliteration: kim nu mām vānarāḥ sarve gatam vakṣyanti samgatāḥ
gatvā tatra tvayā vīra kim kṛtam tad vadasva naḥ
english: What, alas! shall the monkeys assembled tell me when I shall go (to them)? 'O hero, tell us what you have done, repairing there.'

sanskrit: अदृष्ट्वा किम् प्रवक्ष्यामि ताम् अहम् जनक आत्मजाम्
transliteration: adṛṣṭvā kim pravakṣyāmi tām aham janaka ātmajām
english: And not having seen Janaka's daughter, what shall I answer? The term fixed (by Sugrīva) having been past, certainly meet it is that I should fast to death.

sanskrit: किम् वा वक्ष्यति व्Rद्धः च जाम्बवान् अन्गदः च सः
गतम् पारम् समुद्रस्य वानराः च समागताः
transliteration: kim vā vakṣyati vddhaḥ ca jāmbavān angadaḥ ca saḥ
gatam pāram samudrasya vānarāḥ ca samāgatāḥ
english: And what shall the aged Jambhavan, and what shall Angada, say? And what, again, shall the assembled monkeys say to me when I shall have crossed over the main.

sanskrit: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलम् अनिर्वेदः परम् सुखम्
अनिर्वेदो हि सततम् सर्व अर्थेषु प्रवर्तकः
transliteration: anirvedaḥ śriyo mūlam anirvedaḥ param sukham
anirvedo hi satatam sarva artheṣu pravartakaḥ
english: But perseverance is the source of good fortune; and perseverance bring about supreme happiness. Search again I will, where I have not yet searched.

sanskrit: करोति सफलम् जन्तोः कर्म यच् च करोति सः
तस्माद् अनिर्वेद क्Rतम् यत्नम् चेष्टे अहम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: karoti saphalam jantoḥ karma yac ca karoti saḥ
tasmād anirveda ktam yatnam ceṣṭe aham uttamam

sanskrit: अदृष्टामः च विचेष्यामि देशान् रावण पालितान्
आपान शाला विचिताः तथा पुष्प गृहाणि च
transliteration: adṛṣṭāmaḥ ca viceṣyāmi deśān rāvaṇa pālitān
āpāna śālā vicitāḥ tathā puṣpa gṛhāṇi ca

sanskrit: चित्र शालाः च विचिता भूयः क्रीडा गृहाणि च
निष्कुट अन्तर रथ्याः च विमानानि च सर्वशः
transliteration: citra śālāḥ ca vicitā bhūyaḥ krīḍā gṛhāṇi ca
niṣkuṭa antara rathyāḥ ca vimānāni ca sarvaśaḥ

sanskrit: इति सम्चिन्त्य भूयो अपि विचेतुम् उपचक्रमे
भूमी गृहामः चैत्य गृहान् गृह अतिगृहकान् अपि
transliteration: iti samcintya bhūyo api vicetum upacakrame
bhūmī gṛhāmaḥ caitya gṛhān gṛha atigṛhakān api

sanskrit: उत्पतन् निपतमः च अपि तिष्ठन् गच्चन् पुनः क्वचित्
transliteration: utpatan nipatamaḥ ca api tiṣṭhan gaccan punaḥ kvacit

sanskrit: प्रविशन् निष्पतमः च अपि प्रपतन्न् उत्पतन्न् अपि
सर्वम् अपि अवकाशम् स विचचार महा कपिः
transliteration: praviśan niṣpatamaḥ ca api prapatann utpatann api
sarvam api avakāśam sa vicacāra mahā kapiḥ

sanskrit: चतुर् अन्गुल मात्रो अपि न अवकाशः स विद्यते
रावण अन्तः पुरे तस्मिन् यम् कपिर् न जगाम सः
transliteration: catur angula mātro api na avakāśaḥ sa vidyate
rāvaṇa antaḥ pure tasmin yam kapir na jagāma saḥ
english: There was not even space measuring four fingers in that inner apartment of Rāvana, to which the monkey did not repair.

sanskrit: प्राकर अन्तर रथ्याः च वेदिकः चैत्य सम्श्रयाः
श्वभ्राः च पुष्करिण्यः च सर्वम् तेन अवलोकितम्
transliteration: prākara antara rathyāḥ ca vedikaḥ caitya samśrayāḥ
śvabhrāḥ ca puṣkariṇyaḥ ca sarvam tena avalokitam
english: And he saw the abodes of the nobility, the daises, the trees by the crossings, the holes, and the tanks.

sanskrit: राक्षस्यो विविध आकारा विरूपा विकृताः तथा
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न तु सा जनक आत्मजा
transliteration: rākṣasyo vividha ākārā virūpā vikṛtāḥ tathā
dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu sā janaka ātmajā
english: And Hanumān saw there Räksasas of various forms, frightful and deformed; but he saw not Janaka's daughter.

sanskrit: रूपेण अप्रतिमा लोके वरा विद्या धर स्त्रियः
दृटा हनूमता तत्र न तु राघव नन्दिनी
transliteration: rūpeṇa apratimā loke varā vidyā dhara striyaḥ
dṛṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu rāghava nandinī
english: Hanuman there the the foremost and beautiful wives of Vidyadharas; but he saw not Rāghava's beloved Sītā.

sanskrit: नाग कन्या वर आरोहाः पूर्ण चन्द्र निभ आननाः
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न तु सीता सुमध्यमा
transliteration: nāga kanyā vara ārohāḥ pūrṇa candra nibha ānanāḥ
dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na tu sītā sumadhyamā
english: Hanumān saw there transcendentally beautiful women, daughter of Nāgas, having countenances resembling the moon; but he saw not Janaka's daughter. saw

sanskrit: प्रमथ्य राक्षस इन्द्रेण नाग कन्या बलाद्द् हृताः
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न सा जनक नन्दिनी
transliteration: pramathya rākṣasa indreṇa nāga kanyā balādd hṛtāḥ
dṛṣṭā hanūmatā tatra na sā janaka nandinī
english: And Hanumān saw there daughter of Nāgas forcibly brought by the lord of the Rākşasas; but he saw not Janaka's daughter.

sanskrit: सो अपश्यमः ताम् महा बाहुः पश्यमः च अन्या वर स्त्रियः
विषसाद महा बाहुर् हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः
transliteration: so apaśyamaḥ tām mahā bāhuḥ paśyamaḥ ca anyā vara striyaḥ
viṣasāda mahā bāhur hanūmān māruta ātmajaḥ
english: Having seen other beauteous females, and not seeing her, the mighty-armed son of the Windgod was oppressed with sandness.

sanskrit: उद्योगम् वानर इन्द्राणम् प्लवनम् सागरस्य च
व्यर्थम् वीक्ष्य अनिल सुतः चिन्ताम् पुनर् उपागमत्
transliteration: udyogam vānara indrāṇam plavanam sāgarasya ca
vyartham vīkṣya anila sutaḥ cintām punar upāgamat
english: Seeing that the endeavours of the monarch of monkeys, as well as the bounding over the main, had come to nought, the offspring of the Windgod was plunged in thought.

sanskrit: अवतीर्य विमानाच् च हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः
चिन्ताम् उपजगाम अथ शोक उपहत चेतनः
transliteration: avatīrya vimānāc ca hanūmān māruta ātmajaḥ
cintām upajagāma atha śoka upahata cetanaḥ
english: Descending from the aerial car, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, his senses deprived by sorrow, was again wrought up with anxiety.

sanskrit: विमानात् तु सुसम्क्रम्य प्राकारम् हरि यूथपः
हनूमान् वेगवान् आसीद् यथा विद्युद् घन अन्तरे
transliteration: vimānāt tu susamkramya prākāram hari yūthapaḥ
hanūmān vegavān āsīd yathā vidyud ghana antare
english: Alighting from the car, Hanumān possessed of vigorous activity, leader of monkeybands-nearing the wall, looked like lightning within a mass of clouds.

sanskrit: अदृष्ट्वा जानकीम् सीताम् अब्रवीद् वचनम् कपिः
transliteration: adṛṣṭvā jānakīm sītām abravīd vacanam kapiḥ
english: And having gone round the mansions of Ravana, and not seeing Janaki, the monkey Hanuman said,

sanskrit: भूयिष्ठम् लोडिता लन्का रामस्य चरता प्रियम्
न हि पश्यामि वैदेहीम् सीताम् सर्व अन्ग शोभनाम्
transliteration: bhūyiṣṭham loḍitā lankā rāmasya caratā priyam
na hi paśyāmi vaidehīm sītām sarva anga śobhanām
english: Striving after Rāma's welfare, I have again searched through Lankā; but I do not see Vaidehi's daughter, Janaki, having all her limbs endeued with loveliness.

sanskrit: नद्यो अनूपवन अन्ताः च दुर्गाः च धरणी धराः
transliteration: nadyo anūpavana antāḥ ca durgāḥ ca dharaṇī dharāḥ
english: And I have explored pools, and watery expanses, and tanks, and rivers, and streams, and marshes, and and woods, and citadels, and mountains, yea, all this earth; but Janaki I do not fimd.

sanskrit: लोडिता वसुधा सर्वा न च पश्यामि जानकीम्
transliteration: loḍitā vasudhā sarvā na ca paśyāmi jānakīm

sanskrit: आख्याता गृध्र राजेन न च पश्यामि ताम् अहम्
किम् नु सीता अथ वैदेही मैथिली जनक आत्मजा
transliteration: ākhyātā gṛdhra rājena na ca paśyāmi tām aham
kim nu sītā atha vaidehī maithilī janaka ātmajā

sanskrit: क्षिप्रम् उत्पततो मन्ये सीताम् आदाय रक्षसः
transliteration: kṣipram utpatato manye sītām ādāya rakṣasaḥ

sanskrit: बिभ्यतो राम बाणानाम् अन्तरा पतिता भवेत्
transliteration: bibhyato rāma bāṇānām antarā patitā bhavet

sanskrit: मन्ये पतितम् आर्याया हृदयम् प्रेक्ष्य सागरम्
रावणस्य ऊरु वेगेन भुजाभ्याम् पीडितेन च
transliteration: manye patitam āryāyā hṛdayam prekṣya sāgaram
rāvaṇasya ūru vegena bhujābhyām pīḍitena ca

sanskrit: तया मन्ये विशाल अक्ष्या त्यक्तम् जीवितम् आर्यया
उपरि उपरि वा नूनम् सागरम् क्रमतः तदा
transliteration: tayā manye viśāla akṣyā tyaktam jīvitam āryayā
upari upari vā nūnam sāgaram kramataḥ tadā

sanskrit: आहो क्षुद्रेण च अनेन रक्षन्ती शीलम् आत्मनः
transliteration: āho kṣudreṇa ca anena rakṣantī śīlam ātmanaḥ

sanskrit: अथवा राक्षस इन्द्रस्य पत्नीभिर् असित ईक्षणा
transliteration: athavā rākṣasa indrasya patnībhir asita īkṣaṇā
english: Alas! trying to preserve her chastity, the forlorn Sītā, practising self-mortification, has been devoured by this abject-minded Rāvana. Or that darkeyed innocent one, has been eaten up by the wives of the Rākşasa chief, actuated by wicked motives.* *Jealously, according to the commentator.

sanskrit: अदुष्टा दुष्ट भावाभिर् भक्षिता सा भविष्यति
सम्पूर्ण चन्द्र प्रतिमम् पद्म पत्र निभ ईक्षणम्
transliteration: aduṣṭā duṣṭa bhāvābhir bhakṣitā sā bhaviṣyati
sampūrṇa candra pratimam padma patra nibha īkṣaṇam

sanskrit: रामस्य ध्यायती वक्त्रम् पन्चत्वम् कृपणा गता
हा राम लक्ष्मण इति एव हा अयोध्येति च मैथिली
transliteration: rāmasya dhyāyatī vaktram pancatvam kṛpaṇā gatā
hā rāma lakṣmaṇa iti eva hā ayodhyeti ca maithilī

sanskrit: विलप्य बहु वैदेही न्यस्त देहा भविष्यति
transliteration: vilapya bahu vaidehī nyasta dehā bhaviṣyati

sanskrit: नूनम् लालप्यते मन्दम् पन्जरस्था इव शारिका
जनकस्य कुले जाता राम पत्नी सुमध्यमा
transliteration: nūnam lālapyate mandam panjarasthā iva śārikā
janakasya kule jātā rāma patnī sumadhyamā

sanskrit: कथम् उत्पल पत्र अक्षी रावणस्य वशम् व्रजेत्
विनष्टा वा प्रनष्टा वा मृता वा जनक आत्मजा
transliteration: katham utpala patra akṣī rāvaṇasya vaśam vrajet
vinaṣṭā vā pranaṣṭā vā mṛtā vā janaka ātmajā

sanskrit: रामस्य प्रिय भार्यस्य न निवेदयितुम् क्षमम्
निवेद्यमाने दोषः स्याद् दोषः स्याद् अनिवेदने
transliteration: rāmasya priya bhāryasya na nivedayitum kṣamam
nivedyamāne doṣaḥ syād doṣaḥ syād anivedane

sanskrit: कथम् नु खलु कर्तव्यम् विषमम् प्रतिभाति मे
अस्मिन्न् एवम् गते कर्ये प्राप्त कालम् क्षमम् च किम्
transliteration: katham nu khalu kartavyam viṣamam pratibhāti me
asminn evam gate karye prāpta kālam kṣamam ca kim

sanskrit: भवेद् इति मतिम् भूयो हनुमान् प्रविचारयन्
यदि सीताम् अदृष्ट्वा अहम् वानर इन्द्र पुरीम् इतः
transliteration: bhaved iti matim bhūyo hanumān pravicārayan
yadi sītām adṛṣṭvā aham vānara indra purīm itaḥ
english: Thus thinking, Hanumān again reflected, "If without seeing Sītā, I repair to the abode of the lord of monkeys, what then shall I gain as the object of my exertions?

sanskrit: गमिष्यामि ततः को मे पुरुष अर्थो भविष्यति
मम इदम् लन्घनम् व्यर्थम् सागरस्य भविष्यति
transliteration: gamiṣyāmi tataḥ ko me puruṣa artho bhaviṣyati
mama idam langhanam vyartham sāgarasya bhaviṣyati

sanskrit: प्रवेशः चिव लन्काया राक्षसानाम् च दर्शनम्
किम् वा वक्ष्यति सुग्रीवो हरयो व समागताः
transliteration: praveśaḥ civa lankāyā rākṣasānām ca darśanam
kim vā vakṣyati sugrīvo harayo va samāgatāḥ

sanskrit: किष्किन्धाम् समनुप्राप्तौ तौ वा दशरथ आत्मजौ
गत्वा तु यदि काकुत्स्थम् वक्ष्यामि परम् अप्रियम्
transliteration: kiṣkindhām samanuprāptau tau vā daśaratha ātmajau
gatvā tu yadi kākutstham vakṣyāmi param apriyam

sanskrit: न दृष्टा इति मया सीता ततः त्यक्ष्यन्ति जीवितम्
परुषम् दारुणम् क्रूरम् तीक्ष्णम् इन्द्रिय तापनम्
transliteration: na dṛṣṭā iti mayā sītā tataḥ tyakṣyanti jīvitam
paruṣam dāruṇam krūram tīkṣṇam indriya tāpanam

sanskrit: सीता निमित्तम् दुर्वाक्यम् श्रुत्वा स न भविष्यति
तम् तु कृच्च्र गतम् दृष्ट्वा पन्चत्व गत मानसम्
transliteration: sītā nimittam durvākyam śrutvā sa na bhaviṣyati
tam tu kṛccra gatam dṛṣṭvā pancatva gata mānasam

sanskrit: भृश अनुरक्तो मेधावी न भविष्यति लक्ष्मणः
विनष्टौ भ्रातरौ श्रुत्वा भरतो अपि मरिष्यति
transliteration: bhṛśa anurakto medhāvī na bhaviṣyati lakṣmaṇaḥ
vinaṣṭau bhrātarau śrutvā bharato api mariṣyati

sanskrit: भरतम् च मृतम् दृष्ट्वा शत्रुघ्नो न भविष्यति
पुत्रान् मृतान् समीक्ष्य अथ न भविष्यन्ति मातरः
transliteration: bharatam ca mṛtam dṛṣṭvā śatrughno na bhaviṣyati
putrān mṛtān samīkṣya atha na bhaviṣyanti mātaraḥ

sanskrit: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च कैकेयी च न सम्शयः
कृतज्ञः सत्य सम्धः च सुग्रीवः प्लवग अधिपः
transliteration: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca kaikeyī ca na samśayaḥ
kṛtajñaḥ satya samdhaḥ ca sugrīvaḥ plavaga adhipaḥ

sanskrit: रामम् तथा गतम् दृष्ट्वा ततः त्यक्ष्यन्ति जीवितम्
transliteration: rāmam tathā gatam dṛṣṭvā tataḥ tyakṣyanti jīvitam

sanskrit: पीडिता भर्तृ शोकेन रुमा त्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्
वालिजेन तु दुह्खेन पीडिता शोक कर्शिता
transliteration: pīḍitā bhartṛ śokena rumā tyakṣyati jīvitam
vālijena tu duhkhena pīḍitā śoka karśitā

sanskrit: पन्चत्व गमने राज्ञः तारा अपि न भविष्यति
माता पित्रोर् विनाशेन सुग्रीव व्यसनेन च
transliteration: pancatva gamane rājñaḥ tārā api na bhaviṣyati
mātā pitror vināśena sugrīva vyasanena ca

sanskrit: कुमारो अपि अन्गदः कस्माद् धारयिष्यति जीवितम्
भर्तृजेन तु शोकेन अभिभूता वन ओकसः
transliteration: kumāro api angadaḥ kasmād dhārayiṣyati jīvitam
bhartṛjena tu śokena abhibhūtā vana okasaḥ

sanskrit: शिराम्सि अभिहनिष्यन्ति तलैर् मुष्टिभिर् एव च
transliteration: śirāmsi abhihaniṣyanti talair muṣṭibhir eva ca
english: The dwellers of the woods overwhelmed with grief got of (the decease of) their master, shall strike at their heads with their clenched fists and hands. And the monkeys affectionately cherished by the famous lord of the monkeys with soothing words gifts and regard, shall resign there lives.

sanskrit: लालिताः कपि राजेन प्राणामः त्यक्ष्यन्ति वानराः
न वनेषु न शैलेषु न निरोधेषु वा पुनः
transliteration: lālitāḥ kapi rājena prāṇāmaḥ tyakṣyanti vānarāḥ
na vaneṣu na śaileṣu na nirodheṣu vā punaḥ

sanskrit: सपुत्र दाराः सामात्या भर्तृ व्यसन पीडिताः
transliteration: saputra dārāḥ sāmātyā bhartṛ vyasana pīḍitāḥ

sanskrit: शैल अग्रेभ्यः पतिष्यन्ति समेत्य विषमेषु च
विषम् उद्बन्धनम् वा अपि प्रवेशम् ज्वलनस्य वा
transliteration: śaila agrebhyaḥ patiṣyanti sametya viṣameṣu ca
viṣam udbandhanam vā api praveśam jvalanasya vā

sanskrit: घोरम् आरोदनम् मन्ये गते मयि भविष्यति
transliteration: ghoram ārodanam manye gate mayi bhaviṣyati

sanskrit: इक्ष्वाकु कुल नाशः च नाशः चैव वन ओकसाम्
सो अहम् न एव गमिष्यामि किष्किन्धाम् नगरीम् इतः
transliteration: ikṣvāku kula nāśaḥ ca nāśaḥ caiva vana okasām
so aham na eva gamiṣyāmi kiṣkindhām nagarīm itaḥ

sanskrit: न हि शक्ष्यामि अहम् द्रष्टुम् सुग्रीवम् मैथिलीम् विना
मयि अगच्चति च इहस्थे धर्म आत्मानौ महा रथौ
transliteration: na hi śakṣyāmi aham draṣṭum sugrīvam maithilīm vinā
mayi agaccati ca ihasthe dharma ātmānau mahā rathau

sanskrit: आशया तौ धरिष्येते वनराः च मनस्विनः
हस्त आदानो मुख आदानो नियतो वृक्ष मूलिकः
transliteration: āśayā tau dhariṣyete vanarāḥ ca manasvinaḥ
hasta ādāno mukha ādāno niyato vṛkṣa mūlikaḥ
english: On my not going there and staying here, those righteous-souled Maharathas as well as the fastfleeting monkeys, shall preserve their lives through hope (of hearing tidings concerning Sītā). And not having seen Janaka's daughter, I will lead the Vānaprastha mode of life, partaking (of fruits) falling into my hands or mouth, restraining my senses, and staying at the foot of trees.

sanskrit: सागर अनूपजे देशे बहु मूल फल उदके
transliteration: sāgara anūpaje deśe bahu mūla phala udake

sanskrit: चिताम् कृत्वा प्रवेक्ष्यामि समिद्धम् अरणी सुतम्
transliteration: citām kṛtvā pravekṣyāmi samiddham araṇī sutam

sanskrit: इदम् अपि ऋषिभिर् दृष्टम् निर्याणम् इति मे मतिः
transliteration: idam api ṛṣibhir dṛṣṭam niryāṇam iti me matiḥ

sanskrit: सम्यग् आपः प्रवेक्ष्यामि न चेत् पश्यामि जानकीम्
सुजात मूला सुभगा कीर्ति माला यशस्विनी
transliteration: samyag āpaḥ pravekṣyāmi na cet paśyāmi jānakīm
sujāta mūlā subhagā kīrti mālā yaśasvinī

sanskrit: प्रभग्ना चिर रात्री इयम् मम सीताम् अपश्यतः
तापसो वा भविष्यामि नियतो वृक्ष मूलिकः
transliteration: prabhagnā cira rātrī iyam mama sītām apaśyataḥ
tāpaso vā bhaviṣyāmi niyato vṛkṣa mūlikaḥ

sanskrit: न इतः प्रतिगमिष्यामि ताम् अदृष्ट्वा असित ईक्षणाम्
यदि इतः प्रतिगच्चामि सीताम् अनधिगम्य ताम्
transliteration: na itaḥ pratigamiṣyāmi tām adṛṣṭvā asita īkṣaṇām
yadi itaḥ pratigaccāmi sītām anadhigamya tām
