sanskrit: अन्गदः सहितैः सर्वैर् वानरैर् न भविष्यति
विनाशे बहवो दोषा जीवन् प्राप्नोति भद्रकम्
transliteration: angadaḥ sahitaiḥ sarvair vānarair na bhaviṣyati
vināśe bahavo doṣā jīvan prāpnoti bhadrakam

sanskrit: तस्मात् प्राणान् धरिष्यामि ध्रुवो जीवति सम्गमः
एवम् बहु विधम् दुह्खम् मनसा धारयन् मुहुः
transliteration: tasmāt prāṇān dhariṣyāmi dhruvo jīvati samgamaḥ
evam bahu vidham duhkham manasā dhārayan muhuḥ

sanskrit: न अध्यगच्चत् तदा पारम् शोकस्य कपि कुन्जरः
रावणम् वा वधिष्यामि दशग्रीवम् महा बलम्
transliteration: na adhyagaccat tadā pāram śokasya kapi kunjaraḥ
rāvaṇam vā vadhiṣyāmi daśagrīvam mahā balam

sanskrit: कामम् अस्तु हृता सीता प्रत्याचीर्णम् भविष्यति
अथवा एनम् समुत्क्षिप्य उपरि उपरि सागरम्
transliteration: kāmam astu hṛtā sītā pratyācīrṇam bhaviṣyati
athavā enam samutkṣipya upari upari sāgaram

sanskrit: रामाय उपहरिष्यामि पशुम् पशु पतेर् इव
इति चिन्ता समापन्नः सीताम् अनधिगम्य ताम्
transliteration: rāmāya upahariṣyāmi paśum paśu pater iva
iti cintā samāpannaḥ sītām anadhigamya tām

sanskrit: ध्यान शोका परीत आत्मा चिन्तयाम् आस वानरः
यावत् सीताम् न पश्यामि राम पत्नीम् यशस्विनीम्
transliteration: dhyāna śokā parīta ātmā cintayām āsa vānaraḥ
yāvat sītām na paśyāmi rāma patnīm yaśasvinīm

sanskrit: तावद् एताम् पुरीम् लन्काम् विचिनोमि पुनः पुनः
सम्पाति वचनाच् च अपि रामम् यदि आनयामि अहम्
transliteration: tāvad etām purīm lankām vicinomi punaḥ punaḥ
sampāti vacanāc ca api rāmam yadi ānayāmi aham

sanskrit: अपश्यन् राघवो भार्याम् निर्दहेत् सर्व वानरान्
इह एव नियत आहारो वत्स्यामि नियत इन्द्रियः
transliteration: apaśyan rāghavo bhāryām nirdahet sarva vānarān
iha eva niyata āhāro vatsyāmi niyata indriyaḥ

sanskrit: न मत् कृते विनश्येयुः सर्वे ते नर वानराः
अशोक वनिका च अपि महती इयम् महा द्रुमा
transliteration: na mat kṛte vinaśyeyuḥ sarve te nara vānarāḥ
aśoka vanikā ca api mahatī iyam mahā drumā

sanskrit: इमाम् अभिगमिष्यामि न हि इयम् विचिता मया
वसून् रुद्रामः तथा आदित्यान् अश्विनौ मरुतो अपि च
transliteration: imām abhigamiṣyāmi na hi iyam vicitā mayā
vasūn rudrāmaḥ tathā ādityān aśvinau maruto api ca

sanskrit: नमः कृत्वा गमिष्यामि रक्षसाम् शोक वर्धनः
जित्वा तु राक्षसान् देवीम् इक्ष्वाकु कुल नन्दिनीम्
transliteration: namaḥ kṛtvā gamiṣyāmi rakṣasām śoka vardhanaḥ
jitvā tu rākṣasān devīm ikṣvāku kula nandinīm

sanskrit: स मुहूर्तम् इव ध्यात्वा चिन्ता विग्रथित इन्द्रियः
transliteration: sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā cintā vigrathita indriyaḥ

sanskrit: उदतिष्ठन् महा बाहुर् हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः
नमो अस्तु रुद्र इन्द्र यम अनिलेभ्यो
नमो अस्तु चन्द्र अर्क मरुद् गणेभ्यः
transliteration: udatiṣṭhan mahā bāhur hanūmān māruta ātmajaḥ
namo astu rudra indra yama anilebhyo
namo astu candra arka marud gaṇebhyaḥ
english: Having thus reflected for a space, the mightyarmed offspring of the Wind-god, his senses agitated with anxiety, arose. “I bow to Rāma with Lakşmaņa, and to the revered daughter of Janaka, I bow to Rudra, and Indra, and Yama, and Wind-god, and I bow to the Moon, to Fire and to the Maruts."

sanskrit: स तेभ्यः तु नमः कृत्वा सुग्रीवाय च मारुतिः
दिशः सर्वाः समालोक्य अशोक वनिकाम् प्रति
transliteration: sa tebhyaḥ tu namaḥ kṛtvā sugrīvāya ca mārutiḥ
diśaḥ sarvāḥ samālokya aśoka vanikām prati
english: Having bowed to them all, as also to Sugrīva, the offspring of the Wind-god, surveying all he cardinal points, mentally entered the Asoka wood.

sanskrit: स गत्वा मनसा पूर्वम् अशोक वनिकाम् शुभाम्
उत्तरम् चिन्तयाम् आस वानरो मारुत आत्मजः
transliteration: sa gatvā manasā pūrvam aśoka vanikām śubhām
uttaram cintayām āsa vānaro māruta ātmajaḥ
english: Having mentally entered the Asoka wood, that monkey, son to the Wind-god, reflected as to what he should do next.

sanskrit: ध्रुवम् तु रक्षो बहुला भविष्यति वन आकुला
अशोक वनिका चिन्त्या सर्व सम्स्कार सम्स्कृता
transliteration: dhruvam tu rakṣo bahulā bhaviṣyati vana ākulā
aśoka vanikā cintyā sarva samskāra samskṛtā
english: The sacred Asoka wood, sanctified with every purifying rite and abounding in woods, needs must be full of Rāksas.

sanskrit: रक्षिणः च अत्र विहिता नूनम् रक्षन्ति पादपान्
भगवान् अपि सर्व आत्मा न अतिक्षोभम् प्रवायति
transliteration: rakṣiṇaḥ ca atra vihitā nūnam rakṣanti pādapān
bhagavān api sarva ātmā na atikṣobham pravāyati
english: And warders, directed there to, forsooth, protect the trees, and that worshipful Soul of the universe does not breathe here vigorously.

sanskrit: सम्क्षिप्तो अयम् मया आत्मा च राम अर्थे रावणस्य च
सिद्धिम् मे सम्विधास्यन्ति देवाः सर्षि गणाः त्व् इह
transliteration: samkṣipto ayam mayā ātmā ca rāma arthe rāvaṇasya ca
siddhim me samvidhāsyanti devāḥ sarṣi gaṇāḥ tv iha
english: I contract my person in the interests of Rāma, and in order that Rāvana may not see me. May all the deities along with the saints confer success on me.

sanskrit: ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूर् भगवान् देवाः चैव दिशन्तु मे
सिद्धिम् अग्निः च वायुः च पुरु हूतः च वज्रधृत्
transliteration: brahmā svayambhūr bhagavān devāḥ caiva diśantu me
siddhim agniḥ ca vāyuḥ ca puru hūtaḥ ca vajradhṛt

sanskrit: वरुणः पाश हस्तः च सोम आदित्यै तथैव च
अश्विनौ च महात्मानौ मरुतः सर्व एव च
transliteration: varuṇaḥ pāśa hastaḥ ca soma ādityai tathaiva ca
aśvinau ca mahātmānau marutaḥ sarva eva ca

sanskrit: सिद्धिम् सर्वाणि भूतानि भूतानाम् चैव यः प्रभुः
दास्यन्ति मम ये च अन्ये अदृष्टाः पथि गोचराः
transliteration: siddhim sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhūtānām caiva yaḥ prabhuḥ
dāsyanti mama ye ca anye adṛṣṭāḥ pathi gocarāḥ

sanskrit: द्रक्ष्ये तद् आर्या वदनम् कदा न्व् अहम्
transliteration: drakṣye tad āryā vadanam kadā nv aham
english: When shall I behold the blameless face of that noble lady, with its protruding nose; having luminous smiles, having eyes resembling lotuspetals; and bright as the complacent lord of stars?

sanskrit: कथम् नु मे दृष्ट पथे अद्य सा भवेत्
transliteration: katham nu me dṛṣṭa pathe adya sā bhavet
english: Ah! today how shall feeble forlorn one that has been borne down by the force of the mean, abject and grim-visaged (Ravana), fierce yet wearing (at the time of the rape), a dress tending to inspire confidence, come in my sight?

sanskrit: स मुहूर्तम् इव ध्यत्वा मनसा च अधिगम्य ताम्
अवप्लुतो महा तेजाः प्राकारम् तस्य वेश्मनः
transliteration: sa muhūrtam iva dhyatvā manasā ca adhigamya tām
avapluto mahā tejāḥ prākāram tasya veśmanaḥ
english: Having reflected for a while and mentally met with her, that highly energetic one leapt from the wall of Rāvana's mansion on to that (of the Asoka wood).

sanskrit: स तु सम्हृष्ट सर्व अन्गः प्राकारस्थो महा कपिः
पुष्पित अग्रान् वसन्त आदौ ददर्श विविधान् द्रुमान्
transliteration: sa tu samhṛṣṭa sarva angaḥ prākārastho mahā kapiḥ
puṣpita agrān vasanta ādau dadarśa vividhān drumān

sanskrit: सालान् अशोकान् भव्यामः च चम्पकामः च सुपुष्पितान्
उद्दालकान् नाग वृक्षामः चूतान् कपि मुखान् अपि
transliteration: sālān aśokān bhavyāmaḥ ca campakāmaḥ ca supuṣpitān
uddālakān nāga vṛkṣāmaḥ cūtān kapi mukhān api

sanskrit: अथ आम्र वण सम्चन्नाम् लता शत समावृताम्
ज्या मुक्त इव नाराचः पुप्लुवे वृक्ष वाटिकाम्
transliteration: atha āmra vaṇa samcannām latā śata samāvṛtām
jyā mukta iva nārācaḥ pupluve vṛkṣa vāṭikām

sanskrit: स प्रविष्य विचित्राम् ताम् विहगैर् अभिनादिताम्
राजतैः कान्चनैः चैव पादपैः सर्वतो वृताम्
transliteration: sa praviṣya vicitrām tām vihagair abhināditām
rājataiḥ kāncanaiḥ caiva pādapaiḥ sarvato vṛtām

sanskrit: विहगैर् मृग सम्घैः च विचित्राम् चित्र काननाम्
उदित आदित्य सम्काशाम् ददर्श हनुमान् कपिः
transliteration: vihagair mṛga samghaiḥ ca vicitrām citra kānanām
udita āditya samkāśām dadarśa hanumān kapiḥ

sanskrit: वृताम् नाना विधैर् वृक्षैः पुष्प उपग फल उपगैः
कोकिलैर् भृन्ग राजैः च मत्तैर् नित्य निषेविताम्
transliteration: vṛtām nānā vidhair vṛkṣaiḥ puṣpa upaga phala upagaiḥ
kokilair bhṛnga rājaiḥ ca mattair nitya niṣevitām

sanskrit: प्रहृष्ट मनुजे कले मृग पक्षि समाकुले
मत्त बर्हिण सम्घुष्टाम् नाना द्विज गण आयुताम्
transliteration: prahṛṣṭa manuje kale mṛga pakṣi samākule
matta barhiṇa samghuṣṭām nānā dvija gaṇa āyutām

sanskrit: मार्गमाणो वर आरोहाम् राज पुत्रीम् अनिन्दिताम्
सुख प्रसुप्तान् विहगान् बोधयाम् आस वानरः
transliteration: mārgamāṇo vara ārohām rāja putrīm aninditām
sukha prasuptān vihagān bodhayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: As he was searching for that surpassingly beautiful and blameless daughter of the king, that monkey awakened the monkeys that were sleeping sweetly..

sanskrit: उत्पतद्भिर् द्विज गणैः पक्षैः सालाः समाहताः
अनेक वर्णा विविधा मुमुचुः पुष्प वृष्टयः
transliteration: utpatadbhir dvija gaṇaiḥ pakṣaiḥ sālāḥ samāhatāḥ
aneka varṇā vividhā mumucuḥ puṣpa vṛṣṭayaḥ
english: And blown against by the wind caused by the wings of the birds as they flew upwards, various and variegated trees showered down blossoms.

sanskrit: पुष्प अवकीर्णः शुशुभे हनुमान् मारुत आत्मजः
अशोक वनिका मध्ये यथा पुष्पमयो गिरिः
transliteration: puṣpa avakīrṇaḥ śuśubhe hanumān māruta ātmajaḥ
aśoka vanikā madhye yathā puṣpamayo giriḥ
english: And in the midst of the Asoka wood, Hanumān, son to the Wind-god, covered over with flowers, looked lovely like a hill strewn with blossoms.

sanskrit: दिशः सर्व अभिदावन्तम् वृक्ष षण्ड गतम् कपिम्
द्Rष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि वसन्त इति मेनिरे
transliteration: diśaḥ sarva abhidāvantam vṛkṣa ṣaṇḍa gatam kapim
dṣṭvā sarvāṇi bhūtāni vasanta iti menire
english: All creatures, beholding that monkey embosomed among trees and darting on all sides, took him for spring.

sanskrit: वृक्षेभ्यः पतितैः पुष्पैर् अवकीर्णा पृथग् विधैः
रराज वसुधा तत्र प्रमदा इव विभूषिता
transliteration: vṛkṣebhyaḥ patitaiḥ puṣpair avakīrṇā pṛthag vidhaiḥ
rarāja vasudhā tatra pramadā iva vibhūṣitā
english: And strewn with several masses of blossoms loosened from the trees, the Earth appeared breateous like a damsel dight with ornaments.
And shaken in diverse ways by the motion of the light fleeting monkey, the tree showered many-hued flowers.

sanskrit: निर्धूत पत्र शिखराः शीर्ण पुष्प फल द्रुमाः
निक्षिप्त वस्त्र आभरणा धूर्ता इव पराजिताः
transliteration: nirdhūta patra śikharāḥ śīrṇa puṣpa phala drumāḥ
nikṣipta vastra ābharaṇā dhūrtā iva parājitāḥ
english: With their leaves and tops torn, and their flowers and fruits shrivelled up, the trees looked like worsted gamblers bereft of their clothes.

sanskrit: हनूमता वेगवता कम्पिताः ते नग उत्तमाः
पुष्प पर्ण फलानि आशु मुमुचुः पुष्प शालिनः
transliteration: hanūmatā vegavatā kampitāḥ te naga uttamāḥ
puṣpa parṇa phalāni āśu mumucuḥ puṣpa śālinaḥ
english: And shaken by Hanumān vehemently moving about, those excellent trees crowned with fruits, speedily cast off fruits, flowers and foliage.

sanskrit: विहम्ग सम्घैर् हीनाः ते स्कन्ध मात्र आश्रया द्रुमाः
बभूवुर् अगमाः सर्वे मारुतेन इव निर्धुताः
transliteration: vihamga samghair hīnāḥ te skandha mātra āśrayā drumāḥ
babhūvur agamāḥ sarve mārutena iva nirdhutāḥ
english: And moved by the Wind god's offspring, the trees with their trunks left, and forsaken by the fowls were incapable of harbouring any creatures.

sanskrit: विधूत केशी युवतिर् यथा मृदित वर्णिका
निष्पीत शुभ दन्त ओष्ठी नखैर् दन्तैः च विक्षता
transliteration: vidhūta keśī yuvatir yathā mṛdita varṇikā
niṣpīta śubha danta oṣṭhī nakhair dantaiḥ ca vikṣatā
english: And like youthful fair ones with hair dishevelled, their paste worn off, their upper lips with fair teeth sucked of their moisture; and having their persons torn with nails, and teeth; appeared 'the Asoka wood with its trees shattered; and itself ground with the tail, hands and legs (of Hanumān).

sanskrit: तथा लान्गूल हस्तैः च चरणाभ्याम् च मर्दिता
बभूव अशोक वनिका प्रभग्न वर पादपा
transliteration: tathā lāngūla hastaiḥ ca caraṇābhyām ca marditā
babhūva aśoka vanikā prabhagna vara pādapā

sanskrit: महा लतानाम् दामानि व्यधमत् तरसा कपिः
यथा प्रावृषि विन्ध्यस्य मेघ जालानि मारुतः
transliteration: mahā latānām dāmāni vyadhamat tarasā kapiḥ
yathā prāvṛṣi vindhyasya megha jālāni mārutaḥ
english: That monkey with his vehemence scattered the clusters of shrubs, like the wind violently scattering clouds in the rainy reason.

sanskrit: स तत्र मणि भूमीः च राजतीः च मनो रमाः
तथा कान्चन भूमीः च विचरन् ददृशे कपिः
transliteration: sa tatra maṇi bhūmīḥ ca rājatīḥ ca mano ramāḥ
tathā kāncana bhūmīḥ ca vicaran dadṛśe kapiḥ
english: And ranging there, the monkey saw beautiful pavements, jewelled, silvern and golden.

sanskrit: वापीः च विविध आकाराः पूर्णाः परम वारिणा
महा अर्हैर् मणि सोपानैर् उपपन्नाः ततः ततः
transliteration: vāpīḥ ca vividha ākārāḥ pūrṇāḥ parama vāriṇā
mahā arhair maṇi sopānair upapannāḥ tataḥ tataḥ

sanskrit: मुक्ता प्रवाल सिकता स्फटिक अन्तर कुट्टिमाः
transliteration: muktā pravāla sikatā sphaṭika antara kuṭṭimāḥ
english: He saw there various pools filled with excellent water and having steps crusted with jewels. Their sandy soil was filled with pearls and corals, and the ground inside was made of crystal. And their banks were decked with diverse golden trees.

sanskrit: फुल्ल पद्म उत्पल वनाः चक्र वाक उपकूजिताः
नत्यूह रुत सम्घुष्टा हम्स सारस नादिताः
transliteration: phulla padma utpala vanāḥ cakra vāka upakūjitāḥ
natyūha ruta samghuṣṭā hamsa sārasa nāditāḥ
english: They were beautified with full blown lotuses, waterlilies, Chakravakas and Natyuhas* and filled with the notes of swans and Sarasas. *A gallinule.

sanskrit: दीर्घाभिर् द्रुम युक्ताभिः सरिद्भिः च समन्ततः
transliteration: dīrghābhir druma yuktābhiḥ saridbhiḥ ca samantataḥ
english: They were encircled on all sides with big tanks having trees on their banks and water, clear and sweet like to nectar.

sanskrit: नाना गुल्म आवृत वनाः कर वीर कृत अन्तराः
transliteration: nānā gulma āvṛta vanāḥ kara vīra kṛta antarāḥ
english: They were entwined with hundreds of creepers, covered with Santāna* flowers and filled with diverse groves and Karaviras serving the purpose of windows. *One of the trees of heaven. 'Literally the passages means "making a gap in that forest thickly filled with trees.” But Rāmānuja interprets thus and we have adopted his interpretaion.

sanskrit: ततो अम्बु धर सम्काशम् प्रव्Rद्ध शिखरम् गिरिम्
विचित्र कूटम् कूटैः च सर्वतः परिवारितम्
transliteration: tato ambu dhara samkāśam pravddha śikharam girim
vicitra kūṭam kūṭaiḥ ca sarvataḥ parivāritam
english: Thereupon that foremost of monkeys beheld there a mountain-the most picturesque in the world, resembling clouds, having high summits, covered on all sides with peaks and filled with hilly abodes and various trees.

sanskrit: शिला गृहैर् अवततम् नाना वृक्षैः समावृतम्
ददर्श कपि शार्दूलो रम्यम् जगति पर्वतम्
transliteration: śilā gṛhair avatatam nānā vṛkṣaiḥ samāvṛtam
dadarśa kapi śārdūlo ramyam jagati parvatam
english: Thereupon that foremost of monkeys beheld there a mountain-the most picturesque in the world, resembling clouds, having high summits, covered on all sides with peaks and filled with hilly abodes and various trees.

sanskrit: ददर्श च नगात् तस्मान् नदीम् निपतिताम् कपिः
अन्काद् इव समुत्पत्य प्रियस्य पतिताम् प्रियाम्
transliteration: dadarśa ca nagāt tasmān nadīm nipatitām kapiḥ
ankād iva samutpatya priyasya patitām priyām
english: That monkey beheld there a river falling down from the mountain like to a damsel falling down from the lap of her beloved. And the branches of the trees touching the water (of the stream) resembled a fair damsel prevented by her dear companions from forsaking the company of her beloved).

sanskrit: जले निपतित अग्रैः च पादपैर् उपशोभिताम्
वार्यमाणाम् इव क्रुद्धाम् प्रमदाम् प्रिय बन्धुभिः
transliteration: jale nipatita agraiḥ ca pādapair upaśobhitām
vāryamāṇām iva kruddhām pramadām priya bandhubhiḥ
english: That monkey beheld there a river falling down from the mountain like to a damsel falling down from the lap of her beloved. And the branches of the trees touching the water (of the stream) resembled a fair damsel prevented by her dear companions from forsaking the company of her beloved).

sanskrit: पुनर् आव्Rत्त तोयाम् च ददर्श स महा कपिः
प्रसन्नाम् इव कान्तस्य कान्ताम् पुनर् उपस्थिताम्
transliteration: punar āvtta toyām ca dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ
prasannām iva kāntasya kāntām punar upasthitām
english: And that great monkey beheld further down the stream turning back like to the damsel, pleased, going back to her dear one.

sanskrit: तस्य अदूरात् स पद्मिन्यो नाना द्विज गण आयुताः
ददर्श कपि शार्दूलो हनुमान् मारुत आत्मजः
transliteration: tasya adūrāt sa padminyo nānā dvija gaṇa āyutāḥ
dadarśa kapi śārdūlo hanumān māruta ātmajaḥ
english: That foremost of monkeys, Hanumăn, the son of Maruti, beheld, at some distance, ponds filled with lotuses and various birds.

sanskrit: कृत्रिमाम् दीर्घिकाम् च अपि पूर्णाम् शीतेन वारिणा
मणि प्रवर सोपानाम् मुख्ता सिकत शोभिताम्
transliteration: kṛtrimām dīrghikām ca api pūrṇām śītena vāriṇā
maṇi pravara sopānām mukhtā sikata śobhitām
english: He saw a big artificial pond full of cool water having stairs crusted with excellent jewels and its sandy banks filled with pearls.

sanskrit: विविधैर् मृग सम्घैः च विचित्राम् चित्र काननाम्
प्रासादैः सुमहद्भिः च निर्मितैर् विश्व कर्मणा
transliteration: vividhair mṛga samghaiḥ ca vicitrām citra kānanām
prāsādaiḥ sumahadbhiḥ ca nirmitair viśva karmaṇā
english: It was embellished on all sides) with various animals, diverse trees and big mansions made by Viśvakarmāt himself. It was adorned all around with artificial forests and all the trees there bore flowers and fruits, spreading their branches like to umbrellas and having golden and silvern pavements under them. 'The son of Brahma and artist of gods.

sanskrit: काननैः कॄत्रिमैः च अपि सर्वतः समलम्कृताम्
ये केचित् पादपाः तत्र पुष्प उपग फल उपगाः
transliteration: kānanaiḥ kṝtrimaiḥ ca api sarvataḥ samalamkṛtām
ye kecit pādapāḥ tatra puṣpa upaga phala upagāḥ

sanskrit: सच् चत्राः सवितर्दीकाः सर्वे सौवर्ण वेदिकाः
लता प्रतानैः बहुभिः पर्णैः च बहुभिर् व्Rताम्
transliteration: sac catrāḥ savitardīkāḥ sarve sauvarṇa vedikāḥ
latā pratānaiḥ bahubhiḥ parṇaiḥ ca bahubhir vtām

sanskrit: काञ्चनीम् शिम्शुपाम् एकाम् ददर्श स महा कपिः
transliteration: kāñcanīm śimśupām ekām dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ
english: And that great monkey beheld there one golden Singsapa* tree surrounded on all sides with golden pavements. 'A tree (Dalbergia Sisu).

sanskrit: सो अपश्यद् भूमि भागामः च गर्त प्रस्रवणानि च
सुवर्ण वृक्षान् अपरान् ददर्श शिखि सम्निभान्
transliteration: so apaśyad bhūmi bhāgāmaḥ ca garta prasravaṇāni ca
suvarṇa vṛkṣān aparān dadarśa śikhi samnibhān
english: And he saw the glebe, the hill streams and many a golden trees resembling the fire.

sanskrit: तेषाम् द्रुमाणाम् प्रभया मेरोर् इव महा कपिः
अमन्यत तदा वीरः कान्चनो अस्मि इति वानरः
transliteration: teṣām drumāṇām prabhayā meror iva mahā kapiḥ
amanyata tadā vīraḥ kāncano asmi iti vānaraḥ
english: By the lustre of all those trees that heroic monkey appeared as if made of gold like to the Sun by the touch of the mount Sumeru.

sanskrit: ताम् कान्चनैः तरु गणैर् मारुतेन च वीजिताम्
किन्किणी शत निर्घोषाम् दृष्ट्वा विस्मयम् आगमत्
transliteration: tām kāncanaiḥ taru gaṇair mārutena ca vījitām
kinkiṇī śata nirghoṣām dṛṣṭvā vismayam āgamat
english: Having seen those beautiful golden trees, shaken by the wind and making a sound like that of a Kinkini; having flowery tops and new leaves he was greatly amazed.

sanskrit: स पुष्पित अग्राम् रुचिराम् तरुण अन्कुर पल्लवाम्
ताम् आरुह्य महा वेगः शिम्शपाम् पर्ण सम्व्Rताम्
transliteration: sa puṣpita agrām rucirām taruṇa ankura pallavām
tām āruhya mahā vegaḥ śimśapām parṇa samvtām

sanskrit: इतो द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेहीम् राम दर्शन लालसाम्
इतः च इतः च दुह्ख आर्ताम् सम्पतन्तीम् यद्Rच्चया
transliteration: ito drakṣyāmi vaidehīm rāma darśana lālasām
itaḥ ca itaḥ ca duhkha ārtām sampatantīm yadccayā
english: And climbing that Singsapa tree enveloped with leaves that monkey, gifted with velocity, reflected— Perchance I may see Vaidehi, exercised with grief, anxious to behold Rāma and wandering hither and thither at her pleasure.

sanskrit: अशोक वनिका च इयम् दृढम् रम्या दुरात्मनः
चम्पकैः चन्दनैः च अपि बकुलैः च विभूषिता
transliteration: aśoka vanikā ca iyam dṛḍham ramyā durātmanaḥ
campakaiḥ candanaiḥ ca api bakulaiḥ ca vibhūṣitā

sanskrit: इयम् च नलिनी रम्या द्विज सम्घ निषेविता
इमाम् सा राम महिषी नूनम् एष्यति जानकी
transliteration: iyam ca nalinī ramyā dvija samgha niṣevitā
imām sā rāma mahiṣī nūnam eṣyati jānakī
english: Certainly this is the picturesque Asoka forest of that vicious-souled one, embellished with sandal Champakas and Bakulas. Here is a beautiful pond abounding in lotuses, thronged with birds and forsooth shall that royal spouse Jānaki repair hither.

sanskrit: सा राम राम महिषी राघवस्य प्रिया सदा
वन सम्चार कुशला नूनम् एष्यति जानकी
transliteration: sā rāma rāma mahiṣī rāghavasya priyā sadā
vana samcāra kuśalā nūnam eṣyati jānakī

sanskrit: अथवा मृग शाव अक्षी वनस्य अस्य विचक्षणा
वनम् एष्यति सा च इह राम चिन्ता अनुकर्शिता
transliteration: athavā mṛga śāva akṣī vanasya asya vicakṣaṇā
vanam eṣyati sā ca iha rāma cintā anukarśitā
english: She is the beloved queen of Rāghava and expert in walking in the garden. And separated from Rāma, certainly shall Jānakī repair hither. Or she having the eyes of a young antelope and adept in roaming in the forest, exercised with thought touching Rāma, shall come here.

sanskrit: राम शोक अभिसम्तप्ता सा देवी वाम लोचना
वन वास रता नित्यम् एष्यते वन चारिणी
transliteration: rāma śoka abhisamtaptā sā devī vāma locanā
vana vāsa ratā nityam eṣyate vana cāriṇī
english: Or she having beautiful eyes and fond of ranging in the forest, racked with sorrow in consequence of Rāma's separation, dose always frequent this forest.* *The commentator, Rāmānuja interprets this bloka as explaining the cause of Sītā's frequenting the Asoka forest.

sanskrit: वने चराणाम् सततम् नूनम् स्पृहयते पुरा
रामस्य दयिता भार्या जनकस्य सुता सती
transliteration: vane carāṇām satatam nūnam spṛhayate purā
rāmasya dayitā bhāryā janakasya sutā satī
english: Ere this, the chaste and worshipful spouse of Rāma–Janaka's daughter, used to love always the birds and animals of the forest.

sanskrit: सम्ध्या काल मनाः श्यामा ध्रुवम् एष्यति जानकी
नदीम् च इमाम् शिव जलाम् सम्ध्या अर्थे वर वर्णिनी
transliteration: samdhyā kāla manāḥ śyāmā dhruvam eṣyati jānakī
nadīm ca imām śiva jalām samdhyā arthe vara varṇinī
english: (The morning has set in) and surely the beautiful and graceful daughter of Janaka fond of performing morning ablutions, shall come to this river of pure water to perform them. "Sandhyā literally means the point of time which connect day and night. It however, generally means the period after sunset and before the night sets. But here with reference to the speech which Hanumān began by the end of night, it means the morning.

sanskrit: तस्याः च अपि अनुरूपेयम् अशोक वनिका शुभा
शुभा या पार्थिव इन्द्रस्य पत्नी रामस्य सम्मिता
transliteration: tasyāḥ ca api anurūpeyam aśoka vanikā śubhā
śubhā yā pārthiva indrasya patnī rāmasya sammitā
english: Truly is this beautiful forest of Asoka the worthy abode of the beloved and chaste spouse of Rāma, the lord of men.

sanskrit: यदि जिवति सा देवी तारा अधिप निभ आनना
आगमिष्यति सा अवश्यम् इमाम् शिव जलाम् नदीम्
transliteration: yadi jivati sā devī tārā adhipa nibha ānanā
āgamiṣyati sā avaśyam imām śiva jalām nadīm
english: If that one of moon-like countenance breathes forsooth shall she come to this river of cool water."

Having arrived there and anxiously expecting the appearance of the spouse of that lord of men, the high-souled Hanumān hiding himself (on the Singsapa tree) enveloped with flowers and leaves, beheld all.

sanskrit: स वीक्षमाणः तत्रस्थो मार्गमाणः च मैथिलीम्
अवेक्षमाणः च महीम् सर्वाम् ताम् अन्ववैक्षत
transliteration: sa vīkṣamāṇaḥ tatrastho mārgamāṇaḥ ca maithilīm
avekṣamāṇaḥ ca mahīm sarvām tām anvavaikṣata
english: Having stationed himself on the tree, casting his looks all around in quest of Sītā and looking down on the carth he surveyed the entire forest of (Asoka).

sanskrit: दिव्य गन्ध रस उपेताम् सर्वतः समलम्कृताम्
transliteration: divya gandha rasa upetām sarvataḥ samalamkṛtām
english: It was beautified with Santdaka creepers and various trees, fragrant with celestial odours and was embellished on all sides.

sanskrit: ताम् स नन्दन सम्काशाम् मृग पक्षिभिर् आवृताम्
हर्म्य प्रासाद सम्बाधाम् कोकिल आकुल निह्स्वनाम्
transliteration: tām sa nandana samkāśām mṛga pakṣibhir āvṛtām
harmya prāsāda sambādhām kokila ākula nihsvanām

sanskrit: बह्व आसन कुथा उपेताम् बहु भूमि गृह आयुताम्
transliteration: bahva āsana kuthā upetām bahu bhūmi gṛha āyutām

sanskrit: सर्व ऋतु कुसुमैः रम्यैः फलवद्भिः च पादपैः
पुष्पितानाम् अशोकानाम् श्रिया सूर्य उदय प्रभाम्
transliteration: sarva ṛtu kusumaiḥ ramyaiḥ phalavadbhiḥ ca pādapaiḥ
puṣpitānām aśokānām śriyā sūrya udaya prabhām

sanskrit: निष्पत्र शाखाम् विहगैः क्रियमाणाम् इव असकृत्
transliteration: niṣpatra śākhām vihagaiḥ kriyamāṇām iva asakṛt
english: And stationed there Maruti beheld trees as if devoid of leaves on account of the hundreds of birds, adorned with various flowers, resorting there.

sanskrit: आमूल पुष्प निचितैर् अशोकैः शोक नाशनैः
transliteration: āmūla puṣpa nicitair aśokaiḥ śoka nāśanaiḥ

sanskrit: पुष्प भार अतिभारैः च स्पृशद्भिर् इव मेदिनीम्
transliteration: puṣpa bhāra atibhāraiḥ ca spṛśadbhir iva medinīm
english: He saw there the earth touched by Asoka trees, the removers of grief, having flowers growing from the roots and lowered down with their weight. And the entire quarter was as if ablaze with the beauty of the flowery Karrikaras and Kingsukas.

sanskrit: स देशः प्रभया तेषाम् प्रदीप्त इव सर्वतः
पुम्नागाः सप्त पर्णाः च चम्पक उद्दालकाः तथा
transliteration: sa deśaḥ prabhayā teṣām pradīpta iva sarvataḥ
pumnāgāḥ sapta parṇāḥ ca campaka uddālakāḥ tathā

sanskrit: विवृद्ध मूला बहवः शोभन्ते स्म सुपुष्पिताः
शात कुम्भ निभाः केचित् केचिद् अग्नि शिख उपमाः
transliteration: vivṛddha mūlā bahavaḥ śobhante sma supuṣpitāḥ
śāta kumbha nibhāḥ kecit kecid agni śikha upamāḥ

sanskrit: नील अन्जन निभाः केचित् तत्र अशोकाः सहस्रशः
नन्दनम् विविध उद्यानम् चित्रम् चैत्ररथम् यथा
transliteration: nīla anjana nibhāḥ kecit tatra aśokāḥ sahasraśaḥ
nandanam vividha udyānam citram caitraratham yathā

sanskrit: अतिवृत्तम् इव अचिन्त्यम् दिव्यम् रम्यम् श्रिया वृतम्
द्वितीयम् इव च आकाशम् पुष्प ज्योतिर् गण आयुतम्
transliteration: ativṛttam iva acintyam divyam ramyam śriyā vṛtam
dvitīyam iva ca ākāśam puṣpa jyotir gaṇa āyutam

sanskrit: पुष्प रत्न शतैः चित्रम् पन्चमम् सागरम् यथा
सर्व ऋतु पुष्पैर् निचितम् पादपैर् मधु गन्धिभिः
transliteration: puṣpa ratna śataiḥ citram pancamam sāgaram yathā
sarva ṛtu puṣpair nicitam pādapair madhu gandhibhiḥ

sanskrit: नाना निनादैः उद्यानम् रम्यम् मृग गणैर् द्विजैः
अनेक गन्ध प्रवहम् पुण्य गन्धम् मनो रमम्
transliteration: nānā ninādaiḥ udyānam ramyam mṛga gaṇair dvijaiḥ
aneka gandha pravaham puṇya gandham mano ramam
english: And that garden was embellished with flowers of all seasons and honey-smelling trees, and filled with diverse notes and various animals and birds. And that fragrant garden was rendered more charming with various other fragrances. And that foremost of monkeys beheld in that garden of Asoka, a round palace, situated at a distance, fragrantas the Gandhamādana mountain and high as the lord of mountains.

sanskrit: शैल इन्द्रम् इव गन्ध आढ्यम् द्वितीयम् गन्ध मादनम्
अशोक वनिकायाम् तु तस्याम् वानर पुम्गवः
transliteration: śaila indram iva gandha āḍhyam dvitīyam gandha mādanam
aśoka vanikāyām tu tasyām vānara pumgavaḥ

sanskrit: स ददर्श अविदूरस्थम् चैत्य प्रासादम् ऊर्जितम्
मध्ये स्तम्भ सहस्रेण स्थितम् कैलास पाण्डुरम्
transliteration: sa dadarśa avidūrastham caitya prāsādam ūrjitam
madhye stambha sahasreṇa sthitam kailāsa pāṇḍuram

sanskrit: प्रवाल कृत सोपानम् तप्त कान्चन वेदिकम्
मुष्णन्तम् इव चक्षूम्षि द्योतमानम् इव श्रिया
transliteration: pravāla kṛta sopānam tapta kāncana vedikam
muṣṇantam iva cakṣūmṣi dyotamānam iva śriyā

sanskrit: विमलम् प्राम्शु भावत्वाद् उल्लिखन्तम् इव अम्बरम्
transliteration: vimalam prāmśu bhāvatvād ullikhantam iva ambaram

sanskrit: उपवास कृशाम् दीनाम् निह्श्वसन्तीम् पुनः पुनः
ददर्श शुक्ल पक्ष आदौ चन्द्र रेखाम् इव अमलाम्
transliteration: upavāsa kṛśām dīnām nihśvasantīm punaḥ punaḥ
dadarśa śukla pakṣa ādau candra rekhām iva amalām
english: Thereupon he beheld there (Sītā) wearing a soiled cloth, poorly, greatly reduced by fast, sighing again and again and encircled by a band of Räkşasīs. She was (however) spotless like to the rays of the moon on the first lunar day.

sanskrit: पिनद्धाम् धूम जालेन शिखाम् इव विभावसोः
transliteration: pinaddhām dhūma jālena śikhām iva vibhāvasoḥ
english: Her graceful beauty could with great difficulty be perceived lie to the flame of fire enveloped with smoke.

sanskrit: पीतेन एकेन सम्वीताम् क्लिष्टेन उत्तम वाससा
transliteration: pītena ekena samvītām kliṣṭena uttama vāsasā
english: And wearing a shattered and soiled yellow cloth and divested of all ornaments she appeared like a lotus stalk without lotuses.* *This passage has another meaning-Padmini has two meanings— (i) lotus (ii) Lakşmi or the goddess of wealth. The goddess of wealth is generally described as sitting on a lotus.

sanskrit: ग्रहेण अन्गारकेण एव पीडिताम् इव रोहिणीम्
transliteration: graheṇa angārakeṇa eva pīḍitām iva rohiṇīm
english: Oppressed, racked with grief, weakened and chaste as she was, she appeared like Rohini possessed by Ketu.

sanskrit: अश्रु पूर्ण मुखीम् दीनाम् कृशाम् अननशेन च
शोक ध्यान पराम् दीनाम् नित्यम् दुह्ख परायणाम्
transliteration: aśru pūrṇa mukhīm dīnām kṛśām ananaśena ca
śoka dhyāna parām dīnām nityam duhkha parāyaṇām
english: She was greatly reduced by fast, stricken with grief and anxious thoughts, disturbed with sorrow and was poorly and her eyes were always full of tears.

sanskrit: प्रियम् जनम् अपश्यन्तीम् पश्यन्तीम् राक्षसी गणम्
स्व गणेन मृगीम् हीनाम् श्व गण अभिवृताम् इव
transliteration: priyam janam apaśyantīm paśyantīm rākṣasī gaṇam
sva gaṇena mṛgīm hīnām śva gaṇa abhivṛtām iva
english: Separated from her kith and kin and not beholding Rāma and Lakşmaņa* but the Rāks asīs, she appeared like a hind surrounded by dogs. *Priyājanam-literally means dear ones—but here it refers to Rāma and Lakşmana.

sanskrit: नील नाग आभया वेण्या जघनम् गतया एकया
transliteration: nīla nāga ābhayā veṇyā jaghanam gatayā ekayā
english: Her braid of long hair resembling a black serpent falling on her back it appeared as if the Earth was filled with dark-blue forests on the disappearance of the rains.

sanskrit: सुख अर्हाम् दुह्ख सम्तप्ताम् व्यसनानाम् अकोदिवाम्
ताम् समीक्ष्य विशाल अक्षीम् अधिकम् मलिनाम् कृशाम्
transliteration: sukha arhām duhkha samtaptām vyasanānām akodivām
tām samīkṣya viśāla akṣīm adhikam malinām kṛśām

sanskrit: तर्कयाम् आस सीता इति कारणैः उपपादिभिः
ह्रियमाणा तदा तेन रक्षसा काम रूपिणा
transliteration: tarkayām āsa sītā iti kāraṇaiḥ upapādibhiḥ
hriyamāṇā tadā tena rakṣasā kāma rūpiṇā

sanskrit: यथा रूपा हि दृष्टा वै तथा रूपा इयम् अन्गना
पूर्ण चन्द्र आननाम् सुभ्रूम् चारु वृत्त पयो धराम्
transliteration: yathā rūpā hi dṛṣṭā vai tathā rūpā iyam anganā
pūrṇa candra ānanām subhrūm cāru vṛtta payo dharām

sanskrit: कुर्वन्तीम् प्रभया देवीम् सर्वा वितिमिरा दिशः
ताम् नील केशीम् बिम्ब ओष्ठीम् सुमध्याम् सुप्रतिष्ठिताम्
transliteration: kurvantīm prabhayā devīm sarvā vitimirā diśaḥ
tām nīla keśīm bimba oṣṭhīm sumadhyām supratiṣṭhitām
english: Having the countenance of the full-moon, beautiful eye brows, round breast, she is as if dispelling the darkness from all quarters by virtue of her grace. Her throat was yellow, and her lips were like Bimbas.* She was of middle stature and her limbs were all well built. *A circubituceous plant with red fruits.

sanskrit: सीताम् पद्म पलाश अक्षीम् मन्मथस्य रतिम् यथा
इष्टाम् सर्वस्य जगतः पूर्ण चन्द्र प्रभाम् इव
transliteration: sītām padma palāśa akṣīm manmathasya ratim yathā
iṣṭām sarvasya jagataḥ pūrṇa candra prabhām iva
english: She had eyes resembling lotus petals and was like the beloved wife of Manmatha-Rati and was adorable to the whole creation like the rays of the full-moon. That one having a graceful person was seated on the earth like a female ascetic having her senses restrained. And she was sighing again and again like the timid daughterin-law of the lord of serpents.* *The epithet has a special significance because through her the destruction of the race of Raksasas was brought about.

sanskrit: भूमौ सुतनुम् आसीनाम् नियताम् इव तापसीम्
निःश्वास बहुलाम् भीरुम् भुजग इन्द्र वधूम् इव
transliteration: bhūmau sutanum āsīnām niyatām iva tāpasīm
niḥśvāsa bahulām bhīrum bhujaga indra vadhūm iva
english: She had eyes resembling lotus petals and was like the beloved wife of Manmatha-Rati and was adorable to the whole creation like the rays of the full-moon. That one having a graceful person was seated on the earth like a female ascetic having her senses restrained. And she was sighing again and again like the timid daughterin-law of the lord of serpents.* *The epithet has a special significance because through her the destruction of the race of Raksasas was brought about.

sanskrit: शोक जालेन महता विततेन न राजतीम्
सम्सक्ताम् धूम जालेन शिखाम् इव विभावसोः
transliteration: śoka jālena mahatā vitatena na rājatīm
samsaktām dhūma jālena śikhām iva vibhāvasoḥ
english: Entangled by a mighty web of grief her grace was greatly lessened and she appeared like the flame of fire enveloped in smoke.

sanskrit: ताम् स्मृतीम् इव सम्दिघ्दाम् ऋद्धिम् निपतिताम् इव
विहताम् इव च श्रद्धाम् आशाम् प्रतिहताम् इव
transliteration: tām smṛtīm iva samdighdām ṛddhim nipatitām iva
vihatām iva ca śraddhām āśām pratihatām iva

sanskrit: स उपसर्गाम् यथा सिद्धिम् बुद्धिम् सकलुषाम् इव
transliteration: sa upasargām yathā siddhim buddhim sakaluṣām iva
english: She was like to Smrti of doubtful meanings, fallen wealth, lost respect, hope without any desire for gain, Siddhis of many troubles, sullied understanding and fame soiled with false rumours.

sanskrit: राम उपरोध व्यथिताम् रक्षो हरण कर्शिताम्
अबलाम् मृग शाव अक्षीम् वीक्षमाणाम् ततः ततः
transliteration: rāma uparodha vyathitām rakṣo haraṇa karśitām
abalām mṛga śāva akṣīm vīkṣamāṇām tataḥ tataḥ
english: That innocent one was greatly distressed for not being able to attend upon Rāma and she having the eyes of a young hind, being oppressed by the Rākṣasis was casting her looks hither and thither.

sanskrit: बाष्प अम्बु प्रतिपूर्णेन कृष्ण वक्त्र अक्षि पक्ष्मणा
transliteration: bāṣpa ambu pratipūrṇena kṛṣṇa vaktra akṣi pakṣmaṇā
english: With a displeased countenance, having darkblue and curling eye lashes, and eyes full of tears, she was sighing again and again.

sanskrit: मल पन्क धराम् दीनाम् मण्डन अर्हाम् अमण्डिताम्
प्रभाम् नक्षत्र राजस्य काल मेघैः इव आवृताम्
transliteration: mala panka dharām dīnām maṇḍana arhām amaṇḍitām
prabhām nakṣatra rājasya kāla meghaiḥ iva āvṛtām
english: Worthy of Wearing ornaments but now without any, poorly, crusted with execrations, she appeared like the rays of the stars enveloped by dark-blue clouds. And beholding Sītã in that pitiable plight like to learning for want of practice, (Hanumān) was Puzzled with doubts.

sanskrit: तस्य सम्दिदिहे बुद्धिः मुहुः सीताम् निरीक्ष्य तु
transliteration: tasya samdidihe buddhiḥ muhuḥ sītām nirīkṣya tu
english: Worthy of Wearing ornaments but now without any, poorly, crusted with execrations, she appeared like the rays of the stars enveloped by dark-blue clouds. And beholding Sītã in that pitiable plight like to learning for want of practice, (Hanumān) was Puzzled with doubts.

sanskrit: सम्स्कारेण यथा हीनाम् वाचम् अर्थ अन्तरम् गताम्
transliteration: samskāreṇa yathā hīnām vācam artha antaram gatām
english: Seeing her without ornaments he could with great difficulty make her out like to words having different meanings without the knowledge of grammar.

sanskrit: ताम् समीक्ष्य विशाल अक्षीम् राज पुत्रीम् अनिन्दिताम्
तर्कयाम् आस सीता इति कारणैः उपपादयन्
transliteration: tām samīkṣya viśāla akṣīm rāja putrīm aninditām
tarkayām āsa sītā iti kāraṇaiḥ upapādayan
english: And beholding that blameless daughter of the king, having expansive eyes, Hanumān, by various reasonings, reflected-“Forsooth she must be Sītā."

sanskrit: वैदेह्या यानि च अन्गेषु तदा रामो अन्वकीर्तयत्
तानि आभरण जालानि गात्र शोभीनि अलक्षयत्
transliteration: vaidehyā yāni ca angeṣu tadā rāmo anvakīrtayat
tāni ābharaṇa jālāni gātra śobhīni alakṣayat
english: I see at her person all these ornaments, of which Rāma mentioned to me at the time of my departure.

sanskrit: सुकृतौ कर्ण वेष्टौ च श्व दम्ष्ट्रौ च सुसम्स्थितौ
मणि विद्रुम चित्राणि हस्तेष्व् आभरणानि च
transliteration: sukṛtau karṇa veṣṭau ca śva damṣṭrau ca susamsthitau
maṇi vidruma citrāṇi hasteṣv ābharaṇāni ca
english: I behold on her ears excellent ear-rings and nicely placed Svadangstras and on her arms jewelled ornaments rendered dark-blue by dirt for constant use.

sanskrit: श्यामानि चिर युक्तत्वात् तथा सम्स्थानवन्ति च
तानि एव एतानि मन्ये अहम् यानि रामो अन्वकीर्तयत्
transliteration: śyāmāni cira yuktatvāt tathā samsthānavanti ca
tāni eva etāni manye aham yāni rāmo anvakīrtayat
english: Verily these are the ornaments Rāma mentioned to me. I do not perceive them which had been cast off by her. But these are the rest there is not the least doubt about it.

sanskrit: तत्र यानि अवहीनानि तानि अहम् न उपलक्षये
यानि अस्या न अवहीनानि तानि इमानि न सम्शयः
transliteration: tatra yāni avahīnāni tāni aham na upalakṣaye
yāni asyā na avahīnāni tāni imāni na samśayaḥ

sanskrit: पीतम् कनक पट्ट आभम् स्रस्तम् तद् वसनम् शुभम्
उत्तरीयम् नग आसक्तम् तदा दृष्टम् प्लवम् गमैः
transliteration: pītam kanaka paṭṭa ābham srastam tad vasanam śubham
uttarīyam naga āsaktam tadā dṛṣṭam plavam gamaiḥ
english: The monkeys had seen, her excellent yellow cloth made of golden fibres, on the hill. They had seen also her excellent ornaments, which cast off by her, fell on the earth with a sound.

sanskrit: भूषणानि च मुख्यानि दृष्टानि धरणी तले
अनया एव अपविद्धानि स्वनवन्ति महान्ति च
transliteration: bhūṣaṇāni ca mukhyāni dṛṣṭāni dharaṇī tale
anayā eva apaviddhāni svanavanti mahānti ca
english: The monkeys had seen, her excellent yellow cloth made of golden fibres, on the hill. They had seen also her excellent ornaments, which cast off by her, fell on the earth with a sound.

sanskrit: तथा हि नूनम् तद् वर्णम् तथा श्रीमद् यथा इतरत्
transliteration: tathā hi nūnam tad varṇam tathā śrīmad yathā itarat
english: Her cloth has been shattered by constant use but her grace has not been rendered worse than its colour.

sanskrit: इयम् कनक वर्ण अन्गी रामस्य महिषी प्रिया
प्रनष्टा अपि सती यस्य मनसो न प्रणश्यति
transliteration: iyam kanaka varṇa angī rāmasya mahiṣī priyā
pranaṣṭā api satī yasya manaso na praṇaśyati
english: This one having a golden countenance must be the beloved queen of Rāma who, albeit separated from him, has not disappeared from his mind.

sanskrit: इयम् सा यत् कृते रामः चतुर्भिः परितप्यते
transliteration: iyam sā yat kṛte rāmaḥ caturbhiḥ paritapyate
english: This is that damsel on whose account Rāma being simultaneously burnt by affection, pity, grief and amour, affection in consequence of his beloved spouse being ravished, pity for his inability to protect one dependent on him, grief for the loss of his beloved wife and amour for his dear one.

sanskrit: स्त्री प्रनष्टा इति कारुण्याद् आश्रिता इति आनृशम्स्यतः
पत्नी नष्टा इति शोकेन प्रियेति मदनेन च
transliteration: strī pranaṣṭā iti kāruṇyād āśritā iti ānṛśamsyataḥ
patnī naṣṭā iti śokena priyeti madanena ca
english: This is that damsel on whose account Rāma being simultaneously burnt by affection, pity, grief and amour, affection in consequence of his beloved spouse being ravished, pity for his inability to protect one dependent on him, grief for the loss of his beloved wife and amour for his dear one.

sanskrit: अस्या देव्या यथा रूपम् अन्ग प्रत्यन्ग सौष्ठवम्
रामस्य च यथा रूपम् तस्य इयम् असित ईक्षणा
transliteration: asyā devyā yathā rūpam anga pratyanga sauṣṭhavam
rāmasya ca yathā rūpam tasya iyam asita īkṣaṇā
english: Verily it appear from the grace of her person, from her well developed limbs and from Rāma's beauty that this worshipful damsel having darkblue eyes must be his spouse.

sanskrit: अस्या देव्या मनः तस्मिमः तस्य च अस्याम् प्रतिष्ठितम्
तेन इयम् स च धर्म आत्मा मुहूर्तम् अपि जीवति
transliteration: asyā devyā manaḥ tasmimaḥ tasya ca asyām pratiṣṭhitam
tena iyam sa ca dharma ātmā muhūrtam api jīvati
english: She has her mind fixed in him, and he in her and it is for this that she and the virtuous-souled (Rāma) have been still maintaining their being.

sanskrit: दुष्करम् कुरुते रामो इमाम् मत्त काशिनीम्
सीताम् विना महा बाहुः मुहूर्तम् अपि जीवति
transliteration: duṣkaram kurute rāmo imām matta kāśinīm
sītām vinā mahā bāhuḥ muhūrtam api jīvati

sanskrit: एवम् सीताम् तदा दृष्ट्वा हृष्टः पवन सम्भवः
जगाम मनसा रामम् प्रशशम्स च तम् प्रभुम्
transliteration: evam sītām tadā dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭaḥ pavana sambhavaḥ
jagāma manasā rāmam praśaśamsa ca tam prabhum
english: Having beheld Sītā in this plight, that son of the wind-god approached Rāma in mind and showered praises on his master.

sanskrit: प्रशस्य तु प्रशस्तव्याम् सीताम् ताम् हरि पुम्गवः
गुण अभिरामम् रामम् च पुनः चिन्ता परो अभवत्
transliteration: praśasya tu praśastavyām sītām tām hari pumgavaḥ
guṇa abhirāmam rāmam ca punaḥ cintā paro abhavat
english: Having eulogized Sītā, worthy of being praised and Rāma, endeared by accomplishments that foremost of monkeys again engaged in meditation.

sanskrit: स मुहूर्तम् इव ध्यात्वा बाष्प पर्याकुलेक्षणः
सीताम् आश्रित्य तेजस्वी हनुमान् विललाप ह
transliteration: sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā bāṣpa paryākulekṣaṇaḥ
sītām āśritya tejasvī hanumān vilalāpa ha
english: Having reflected for some time, the powerful Hanumān, having his eyes full of tears bewailed on Siita's account (in the following strain).

sanskrit: मान्या गुरु विनीतस्य लक्ष्मणस्य गुरु प्रिया
यदि सीता अपि दुह्ख आर्ता कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः
transliteration: mānyā guru vinītasya lakṣmaṇasya guru priyā
yadi sītā api duhkha ārtā kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: No one can withstand the course of destiny since Sītā, being the spouse of the worshipful brother of Laksmana, ever obedient to his elders, has been overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: न अत्यर्थम् क्षुभ्यते देवी गन्गा इव जलद आगमे
transliteration: na atyartham kṣubhyate devī gangā iva jalada āgame
english: The worshipful damsel is cognizant of the prowess of Rāma and the intelligent Laksmana and for this she is not entirely depressed like to the river Ganges at the approach of the rainy season,

sanskrit: तुल्य शील वयो वृत्ताम् तुल्य अभिजन लक्षणाम्
राघवो अर्हति वैदेहीम् तम् च इयम् असित ईक्षणा
transliteration: tulya śīla vayo vṛttām tulya abhijana lakṣaṇām
rāghavo arhati vaidehīm tam ca iyam asita īkṣaṇā
english: As regards their character, age, conduct, family and other auspicious marks they are equal and hence Rāghava deserve Vaidehi and this one of dark-blue eyes is his.

sanskrit: ताम् दृष्ट्वा नव हेम आभाम् लोक कान्ताम् इव श्रियम्
जगाम मनसा रामम् वचनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tām dṛṣṭvā nava hema ābhām loka kāntām iva śriyam
jagāma manasā rāmam vacanam ca idam abravīt
english: And having scen seen her, gold-hued and conducing to the happiness of the people like to the Goddess of wealth, Hanuman approached Rāma in his mind and said.

sanskrit: अस्या हेतोर् विशाल अक्ष्या हतो वाली महा बलः
रावण प्रतिमो वीर्ये कबन्धः च निपातितः
transliteration: asyā hetor viśāla akṣyā hato vālī mahā balaḥ
rāvaṇa pratimo vīrye kabandhaḥ ca nipātitaḥ
english: For this (damsel) was killed the mighty Vāli and Kabandha-Rāvana's equal in prowess.

sanskrit: विराधः च हतः सम्ख्ये राक्षसो भीम विक्रमः
वने रामेण विक्रम्य महा इन्द्रेण इव शम्बरः
transliteration: virādhaḥ ca hataḥ samkhye rākṣaso bhīma vikramaḥ
vane rāmeṇa vikramya mahā indreṇa iva śambaraḥ
english: For her (too) was destroyed in battle, the terribly powerful Rākşasa-Viradha, by Rāma putting forth his energy, like to ſambara killed by Mahendra.

sanskrit: चतुर् दश सहस्राणि रक्षसाम् भीम कर्मणाम्
निहतानि जन स्थाने शरैर् अग्नि शिख उपमैः
transliteration: catur daśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasām bhīma karmaṇām
nihatāni jana sthāne śarair agni śikha upamaiḥ
english: (It was for her) that fourteen thousand Rākşasas of terrible deeds were destroyed at Janasthāna with arrow resembling the flame of fire. And Khara was killed in battle, and Trisirā was discomfited and the mighty Dūşaņa by Rāma, knowing his ownself.

sanskrit: करः च निहतः सम्ख्ये त्रिशिराः च निपातितः
दूषणः च महा तेजा रामेण विदित आत्मना
transliteration: karaḥ ca nihataḥ samkhye triśirāḥ ca nipātitaḥ
dūṣaṇaḥ ca mahā tejā rāmeṇa vidita ātmanā
english: (It was for her) that fourteen thousand Rākşasas of terrible deeds were destroyed at Janasthāna with arrow resembling the flame of fire. And Khara was killed in battle, and Trisirā was discomfited and the mighty Dūşaņa by Rāma, knowing his ownself.

sanskrit: ऐश्वर्यम् वानराणाम् च दुर्लभम् वालि पालितम्
अस्या निमित्ते सुग्रीवः प्राप्तवान् लोक सत्कृतम्
transliteration: aiśvaryam vānarāṇām ca durlabham vāli pālitam
asyā nimitte sugrīvaḥ prāptavān loka satkṛtam
english: And it was on her account that Sugrīva, known all over the world, came by the wealth of the monkeys hard to acquire and amassed by Vali.

sanskrit: सागरः च मया क्रान्तः श्रीमान् नद नदी पतिः
अस्या हेतोर् विशाल अक्ष्याः पुरी च इयम् निरीक्षिता
transliteration: sāgaraḥ ca mayā krāntaḥ śrīmān nada nadī patiḥ
asyā hetor viśāla akṣyāḥ purī ca iyam nirīkṣitā
english: And it is for this (damsel) of expansive eyes that I have crossed the effulgent lord of rivers and have seen this city.

sanskrit: अस्याः कृते जगत् च अपि युक्तम् इति एव मे मतिः
transliteration: asyāḥ kṛte jagat ca api yuktam iti eva me matiḥ
english: And methinks it would have been all proper had Rāma turned on her account the whole earth bounded by oceans.

sanskrit: राज्यम् वा त्रिषु लोकेषु सीता वा जनक आत्मजा
त्रैलोक्य राज्यम् सकलम् सीताया न आप्नुयात् कलाम्
transliteration: rājyam vā triṣu lokeṣu sītā vā janaka ātmajā
trailokya rājyam sakalam sītāyā na āpnuyāt kalām
english: If the kingdom over the three worlds and the daughter of Janaka be compared together, the former is not equal to one hundredth part of Sītā.

sanskrit: इयम् सा धर्म शीलस्य जनकस्य महात्मनः
transliteration: iyam sā dharma śīlasya janakasya mahātmanaḥ
english: This Sītā, the daughter of the high-souled Janaka, the pious King of Mithilā, firmly attached to her husband, rose, covered with dust, out of the earth, in a field delved by a furrow.

sanskrit: उत्थिता मेदिनीम् भित्त्वा क्षेत्रे हल मुख क्षते
पद्म रेणु निभैः कीर्णा शुभैः केदार पाम्सुभिः
transliteration: utthitā medinīm bhittvā kṣetre hala mukha kṣate
padma reṇu nibhaiḥ kīrṇā śubhaiḥ kedāra pāmsubhiḥ
english: This Sītā, the daughter of the high-souled Janaka, the pious King of Mithilā, firmly attached to her husband, rose, covered with dust, out of the earth, in a field delved by a furrow.

sanskrit: स्नुषा दशरथस्य एषा ज्येष्ठा राज्ञो यशस्विनी
transliteration: snuṣā daśarathasya eṣā jyeṣṭhā rājño yaśasvinī
english: She is the well-known eldest daughter-in-law of the king Dasaratha, of an adorable character and unchecked prowess.

sanskrit: इयम् सा दयिता भार्या राक्षसी वशम् आगता
transliteration: iyam sā dayitā bhāryā rākṣasī vaśam āgatā
english: And She is the beloved spouse of the pious and grateful Rāma, knowing his ownself, and has been brought under the control of the Raksasis.

sanskrit: सर्वान् भोगान् परित्यज्य भर्तृ स्नेह बलात् कृता
transliteration: sarvān bhogān parityajya bhartṛ sneha balāt kṛtā
english: Renouncing all luxuries, and considering not the least about miseries, she actuated by her husband's love entered the solitary forest.

sanskrit: सम्तुष्टा फल मूलेन भर्तृ शुश्रूषणा परा
या पराम् भजते प्रीतिम् वने अपि भवने यथा
transliteration: samtuṣṭā phala mūlena bhartṛ śuśrūṣaṇā parā
yā parām bhajate prītim vane api bhavane yathā
english: And satisfied with fruits and roots and ever engaged in her husband's service, she lived in the forest as much delighted as she was in her house.

sanskrit: सा इयम् कनक वर्ण अन्गी नित्यम् सुस्मित भाषिणी
transliteration: sā iyam kanaka varṇa angī nityam susmita bhāṣiṇī
english: And that one of a golden hue, never used to afflictions and who was wont to converse always with a delighted countenance, has now been suffering incomparable miseries.

sanskrit: इमाम् तु शील सम्पन्नाम् द्रष्टुम् इच्चति राघवः
transliteration: imām tu śīla sampannām draṣṭum iccati rāghavaḥ
english: Like to a thirsty wight longing for an abode where he might get a drink, Rāghava pants after seeing her, gifted with an exalted character and oppressed by Rāvana.

sanskrit: अस्या नूनम् पुनर् लाभाद् राघवः प्रीतिम् एष्यति
राजा राज्य परिभ्रष्टः पुनः प्राप्य इव मेदिनीम्
transliteration: asyā nūnam punar lābhād rāghavaḥ prītim eṣyati
rājā rājya paribhraṣṭaḥ punaḥ prāpya iva medinīm
english: As a monarch who had lost his kingdom, is greatly delighted when he regain it, forsooth shall Rāghava, in like manner, be pleased when he shall come by her.

sanskrit: काम भोगैः परित्यक्ता हीना बन्धु जनेन च
धारयति आत्मनो देहम् तत् समागम कान्क्षिणी
transliteration: kāma bhogaiḥ parityaktā hīnā bandhu janena ca
dhārayati ātmano deham tat samāgama kānkṣiṇī
english: She too has been maintaining her being in the hope of seeing Rāma again, separated as she is from her friends and deprived of all comforts and luxuries.

sanskrit: न एषा पश्यति राक्षस्यो न इमान् पुष्प फल द्रुमान्
एकस्थ हृदया नूनम् रामम् एव अनुपश्यति
transliteration: na eṣā paśyati rākṣasyo na imān puṣpa phala drumān
ekastha hṛdayā nūnam rāmam eva anupaśyati
english: These Rākşasīs, and these trees enveloped with fruits and flowers-forsooth she dose not behold, but is engaged with all her heart in medidations only touching Rāma.

sanskrit: भर्ता नाम परम् नार्या भूषणम् भूषणाद् अपि
एषा हि रहिता तेन शोभन अर्हा न शोभते
transliteration: bhartā nāma param nāryā bhūṣaṇam bhūṣaṇād api
eṣā hi rahitā tena śobhana arhā na śobhate
english: Husband enhance the beauty of a female more than the dress (and therefore Sītā) beautiful as she is, dose not appear graceful, in her husband's absence.

sanskrit: दुष्करम् कुरुते रामो हीनो यद् अनया प्रभुः
धारयति आत्मनो देहम् न दुह्खेन अवसीदति
transliteration: duṣkaram kurute rāmo hīno yad anayā prabhuḥ
dhārayati ātmano deham na duhkhena avasīdati
english: Forsooth my master Rāma has performed a difficult act for he has been still keeping up his life in her separation without consuming himself in grief.

sanskrit: इमाम् असित केश अन्ताम् शत पत्र निभ ईक्षणाम्
सुख अर्हाम् दुःखिताम् ज्~आत्वा मम अपि व्यथितम् मनः
transliteration: imām asita keśa antām śata patra nibha īkṣaṇām
sukha arhām duḥkhitām jātvā mama api vyathitam manaḥ
english: My heart is greatly pained knowing that she, having dark-blue eyes, resembling lotus petals, worthy of happiness, has been possessed by grief.
She, patient as the Earth, having eyes resembling lotuses, who was ere this protected by Rāghava and Lakşmaņa, is now being guarded by Rākşasīs having terrible eyes, under the trees.

sanskrit: हिम हत नलिनी इव नष्ट शोभा
सह चर रहिता इव चक्र वाकी
transliteration: hima hata nalinī iva naṣṭa śobhā
saha cara rahitā iva cakra vākī
english: Being harassed with continued miseries, the daughter of Janaka has lost all her beauty like to a water-lily crushed with frost, and has come by a miserable plight like to a doe separated from her mate.

sanskrit: अस्या हि पुष्प अवनत अग्र शाखाः
transliteration: asyā hi puṣpa avanata agra śākhāḥ
english: The branches of the Asoka trees, lowered down with flowers are as if enhancing her grief as also the Moon of many thousand rays, at the expire of the winter."

sanskrit: सीता इयम् इति एव निविष्ट बुद्धिः
transliteration: sītā iyam iti eva niviṣṭa buddhiḥ
english: Having reflected thus and arrived at ine conclusion that she was Sītā, that powerful leader of monkeys gifted with velocity stationed himself on that tree.
Thereupon the Moon, white as water-lily and of clear appearance proceeded far down the welkin like to a goose traversing the blue waters.
With a view to befriend him, the Moon of clear rays, sprinkled the Wind-God's son, with cool beams.
And thereupon he beheld Sītā, having a moon-like countenance, plunged in grief like to a laden boat sunk in water.
While beholding Vaidehī, Hanumān, the son of Maruta, observed at some distance, a number of grim-visaged Raksasis.
Some had one ear, some one eye, some had big ears some was without ears; some had formidable ears and some had a nose projecting upwards.

And some had the upper part of their bodies unusually long and bulky, some had a long and slender neck, some had dishevelled hair, and some one's person was so thickly covered with hairs, that she appeared to have been cloaked in a blanket.

Some had long ears some had a long forehead, some had a long belly, some had long breasts; some had long lips; some had their lips and chins stuck together, some had a long countenance and some had long knees.

sanskrit: ह्रस्वाम् दीर्घाम् च कुब्जाम् विकटाम् वामनां तथा
transliteration: hrasvām dīrghām ca kubjām vikaṭām vāmanāṃ tathā
english: Some one was of-short stature, some was tall, some crooked, some grim-visaged, some dwarfish, some one was of terribly dark colour; some had a disfigured countenance; some had coppery eyes and a fearful face.
Some were terrible-looking, some coppercoloured, some black, some angry and some fond of quarrelling with each other; and some had iron darts, hammers and mallets in their hands.

Some had a face like that of a boar, some had a face like that of a deer, some like that of a tiger, some like that of a buffalo, some like that of a goat, and some like that of a jackal; some had legs like those of a camel, some had those of an elephant, some those of a horse and some had their heads placed on their breasts.

Some one had only one hand some had only one leg. Some had ears like those of a horse, some like those of a cow, some like those of an ass, some like those of an elephant and others had ears like those of a lion.
Some had very big noses, some had crooked and others were without any; some had noses like those of an elephant and others had their noses on their foreheads.

Some had their legs like those of elephants some had very huge legs; some and like those of a cow, some had on their legs locks of hair like to pillars, some had a terribly huge head, some had big breasts and others had spacious bellies, Some had faces and eyes beyond ordinary proportions.
Some had a long face and tongue. And some had the face of a goat, some that of an elephant some that of a cow, some that of a boar some that of a horse and some that of an ass.

sanskrit: पिबन्तीः सततं पानं सदा मां ससुराप्रियाः
transliteration: pibantīḥ satataṃ pānaṃ sadā māṃ sasurāpriyāḥ

english: And that foremost of monkeys found all these grim-visaged Rākşasīs seated around that mighty tree enveloped with branches. And the graceful Hanuman observed at the foot of that tree that worshipful and blameless daughter of the king Janaka. She was bereft of all effulgence, racked with grief and all her hairs were soiled with dirt. no

And that foremost of monkeys found all these grim-visaged Rākşasīs seated around that mighty tree enveloped with branches. And the graceful Hanuman observed at the foot of that tree that worshipful and blameless daughter of the king Janaka. She was bereft of all effulgence, racked with grief and all her hairs were soiled with dirt. no
She appeared like a star fallen down on the earth on the wane of virtue. And famed though she was all over the world for her chastity, it was difficult for her now to see her husband.

She had excellent ornaments-her attachment to her husband was the only ornament. She was imprisoned by the lord of Rākşasas and separated from all her friends, she appeared like a she elephant separated from her band and bound and attacked by a lion, and like the rays of the Moon enveloped with clouds at the expire of the rainy season,

She had excellent ornaments-her attachment to her husband was the only ornament. She was imprisoned by the lord of Rākşasas and separated from all her friends, she appeared like a she elephant separated from her band and bound and attacked by a lion, and like the rays of the Moon enveloped with clouds at the expire of the rainy season,

Her beauty was greatly faded (in consequence of her husband's separation) like to a stringed instrument for want of a player. And ever engaged in her husband's welfare she was thoroughly unworthy of being brought under the control of the Rākşasas. Being sunk in the abyss of grief and encircled by those Rākşasīs she appeared in the forest of Asoka like to Rohiņi possessed by Rāhu.

Her beauty was greatly faded (in consequence of her husband's separation) like to a stringed instrument for want of a player. And ever engaged in her husband's welfare she was thoroughly unworthy of being brought under the control of the Rākşasas. Being sunk in the abyss of grief and encircled by those Rākşasīs she appeared in the forest of Asoka like to Rohiņi possessed by Rāhu.
And Hanuman beheld her there like a creeper divested of flowers. And having her person soiled with dirt and shorn of all ornaments she appeared in her hidden grace like to a lotus covered with clay.

sanskrit: मृणाली पङ्कदिग्धेव विभाति च न भाति च
transliteration: mṛṇālī paṅkadigdheva vibhāti ca na bhāti ca

sanskrit: हर्षजानि च सोऽश्रूणि ताम् दृष्ट्वा मदिरेक्षणाम्
transliteration: harṣajāni ca so'śrūṇi tām dṛṣṭvā madirekṣaṇām
english: And beholding her having inebriate eyes, Hanumān shed tears of delight and bowed to Rāghava.
Having offered his obeisance to Räma and Lakşmaņa the powerful Hanumān, greatly delighted in seeing Sītā, remained there hidden.
Beholding the forest filled with flowery trees and desiring to have a full view of her, he, wellnigh, spent the night.

At that late hour of the night, he heard the chantings of the Vedas by the Rákşasas, conversant with the six supplementary parts of the Vedas,* engaged in the performance of sacrificial rites and knowing Brahmā. *Grammar, Prosody, astronomy, pronounciation, the meaning of the unusual terms and the ritual of the Hindu religion.
And thereupon the mighty Ten-headed Rākṣasa, having huge arms, awoke with the sounds of those auspicious instruments, pleasant to ears.
Awaking, that great and powerful lord of Rākşasas, having his cloth and garlands loosened, began to think of Vaidehi.

sanskrit: न स तं राक्षसः कामं शशाकात्मनि गूहितुम्
transliteration: na sa taṃ rākṣasaḥ kāmaṃ śaśākātmani gūhitum
english: That Raksasa, puffed up with pride, was passionately attached to her and so he could not restrain his amour in him.
And one hundred damsels followed in the train of the son of Pulastya like to the damsels of the celestials and Gandharvas following mahendra. 'Refers to Rāvana, Pulastya being his father.
There among those fair ones, some carried torches with gold handles, chowries and some fans.
Some carrying water in golden jars headed the train while others carrying the golden throne covered with a coverlet followed it.
And a favourite damsel carried in her right hand a jewelled drinking bowl filled with wine.
Another carrying the white umbrella having golden ribs resembling the full moon and goose, followed in the train.

sanskrit: अनुजग्मुः पतिं वीरम् घनम् विद्युल्लता इव
transliteration: anujagmuḥ patiṃ vīram ghanam vidyullatā iva
english: And in this wise the excellent wives, of Rāvaņa, having their eyes rendered sleepy with sleep and wine, followed their heroic husband like to lightings following the cloud.
Their necklaces and keyuras were displaced, paste fade, hair dishevelled and they had drops of sweat on their faces.
With sleep and intoxication, were reeling those fair ones of beautiful countenances, having their hairs with garlands disbanded and their persons wet with perspiration.
And in this way those beloved wives, (of Ravana) having inebriate eyes, followed, out of amour and reverence, their husband.
And their might husband, brought under the control of amour and having his mind firmly attached to Şītā, proceeded slowly.

sanskrit: ततः काञ्चीनिनादं च नूपुराणाम् च निस्वनम्
transliteration: tataḥ kāñcīninādaṃ ca nūpurāṇām ca nisvanam
english: And that monkey, son of Maruta, heard the sound of kāñcīs and nūpuras of those excellent damsels.
And the monkey Hanumān also beheld Rāvana, of extraordinary deeds and of inconceivable prowess and strength, at the gate.
His whole body was seen on all sides by the light of the lamps lighted with perfumed oil and carried by the Rākşasīs before.
He was inflamed with amour, pride and haughtiness and his expansive eyes were coppery and idle. And he appeared like Cupid himself just appearing in view, leaving behind his bow and arrows.
Holding his excellent robe, covered with flowers, washed, set with jewels and white as the foam of the churned nectar, he placed it in its proper place.
Hanumăn, hiding himself on the tree, in the midst of many leaves and flowers, tried to recognise him as he approached.
Beholding him, that foremost of monkeys saw that highly famous king Rāvana, surrounded by his excellently beautiful and youthful wives, enter that forest of enjoyment filled with birds and animals.
Beholding him, that foremost of monkeys saw that highly famous king Rāvana, surrounded by his excellently beautiful and youthful wives, enter that forest of enjoyment filled with birds and animals.

sanskrit: तेन विश्रवसः पुत्रः स दृष्टो राक्षसाधिपः
transliteration: tena viśravasaḥ putraḥ sa dṛṣṭo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: There was a warder by name Sankukarņa in that forest—highly powerful, wearing various ornaments and addicted to drinking. And by him was seen that lord of Rākşasas—the son of Visrava.

That highly energetic monkey beheld that effulgent (Rāvana) surrounded by excellent damsels like to moon encircled by stars. And beholding him the monkey reflected—“This must be Rāvana-for he is the person whom I saw sleeping in an excellent apartment in that city.” Thinking this, that highly effulgent son of Maruta-Hanuman leaped (high upon another branch).

That highly energetic monkey beheld that effulgent (Rāvana) surrounded by excellent damsels like to moon encircled by stars. And beholding him the monkey reflected—“This must be Rāvana-for he is the person whom I saw sleeping in an excellent apartment in that city.” Thinking this, that highly effulgent son of Maruta-Hanuman leaped (high upon another branch).
And effulgent as he was, that highly intelligent monkey hid himself on a branch covered with leaves, being unable to stand before the effulgence of that Rākșasa.
Rāvana proceeded in that way, being anxious to behold the blue-eyed Sītā, having spacious breast, excellent hips and a lock of black hair.

sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सीता रौद्रस्य रक्षसः
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sītā raudrasya rakṣasaḥ

sanskrit: निवर्तय मनो मत्तः स्वजने क्रियतां मनः
transliteration: nivartaya mano mattaḥ svajane kriyatāṃ manaḥ

sanskrit: न मां प्रार्थयितुं युक्तस्त्वं सिद्धिमिव पापकृत्
कुलं सम्प्राप्तया पुण्यं कुले महति जातया
transliteration: na māṃ prārthayituṃ yuktastvaṃ siddhimiva pāpakṛt
kulaṃ samprāptayā puṇyaṃ kule mahati jātayā

sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही रावणं तं यशस्विनी
transliteration: evamuktvā tu vaidehī rāvaṇaṃ taṃ yaśasvinī

sanskrit: यथा तव तथान्येषां रक्ष्या दारा निशाचर
transliteration: yathā tava tathānyeṣāṃ rakṣyā dārā niśācara

sanskrit: इह सन्तो न वा सन्ति सतो वा नानुवर्तसे
transliteration: iha santo na vā santi sato vā nānuvartase

sanskrit: तथेयं त्वां समासाद्य लङ्का रत्नौघ सङ्कुला
transliteration: tatheyaṃ tvāṃ samāsādya laṅkā ratnaugha saṅkulā

sanskrit: एवं त्वां पापकर्माणं वक्ष्यन्ति निकृता जनाः
transliteration: evaṃ tvāṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ vakṣyanti nikṛtā janāḥ

sanskrit: साधु रावण रामेण मां समानय दुःखिताम्
transliteration: sādhu rāvaṇa rāmeṇa māṃ samānaya duḥkhitām

sanskrit: त्वद्विधं न तु सङ्क्रुद्धो लोकनाथः स राघवः
transliteration: tvadvidhaṃ na tu saṅkruddho lokanāthaḥ sa rāghavaḥ

sanskrit: रामस्य धनुषः शब्दं श्रोष्यसि त्वं महास्वनम्
transliteration: rāmasya dhanuṣaḥ śabdaṃ śroṣyasi tvaṃ mahāsvanam

sanskrit: आश्रमं तु तयोः शून्यं प्रविश्य नरसिंहयोः
transliteration: āśramaṃ tu tayoḥ śūnyaṃ praviśya narasiṃhayoḥ

sanskrit: क्षिप्रं तव स नाथो मे रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
transliteration: kṣipraṃ tava sa nātho me rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha

sanskrit: यथा यथा सान्त्वयिता वश्यः स्त्रीणां तथा तथा
यथा यथा प्रियं वक्ता परिभूतस्तथा तथा
transliteration: yathā yathā sāntvayitā vaśyaḥ strīṇāṃ tathā tathā
yathā yathā priyaṃ vaktā paribhūtastathā tathā

sanskrit: संनियच्छति मे क्रोधं त्वयि कामः समुत्थितः
transliteration: saṃniyacchati me krodhaṃ tvayi kāmaḥ samutthitaḥ

sanskrit: परुषाणि हि वाक्यानि यानि यानि ब्रवीषि माम्
तेषु तेषु वधो युक्तस्तव मैथिलि दारुणः
transliteration: paruṣāṇi hi vākyāni yāni yāni bravīṣi mām
teṣu teṣu vadho yuktastava maithili dāruṇaḥ

sanskrit: द्वौ मासौ रक्षितव्यौ मे योऽवधिस्ते मया कृतः
transliteration: dvau māsau rakṣitavyau me yo'vadhiste mayā kṛtaḥ

sanskrit: नूनं न ते जनः कश्चिदसिन्निःश्रेयसे स्थितः
transliteration: nūnaṃ na te janaḥ kaścidasinniḥśreyase sthitaḥ

sanskrit: मां हि धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं शचीमिव शचीपतेः
transliteration: māṃ hi dharmātmanaḥ patnīṃ śacīmiva śacīpateḥ

sanskrit: यथा दृप्तश्च मातङ्गः शशश् च सहितौ वने
transliteration: yathā dṛptaśca mātaṅgaḥ śaśaś ca sahitau vane

sanskrit: स त्वमिक्ष्वाकुनाथं वै क्षिपन्निह न लज्जसे
transliteration: sa tvamikṣvākunāthaṃ vai kṣipanniha na lajjase

sanskrit: इमे ते नयने क्रूरे विरूपे कृष्णपिङ्गले
transliteration: ime te nayane krūre virūpe kṛṣṇapiṅgale

sanskrit: तस्य धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं स्नुषां दशरथस्य च
कथं व्याहरतो मां ते न जिह्वा पाप शीर्यते
transliteration: tasya dharmātmanaḥ patnīṃ snuṣāṃ daśarathasya ca
kathaṃ vyāharato māṃ te na jihvā pāpa śīryate

sanskrit: न त्वां कुर्मि दशग्रीव भस्म भस्मार्हतेजसा
transliteration: na tvāṃ kurmi daśagrīva bhasma bhasmārhatejasā

sanskrit: अपोह्य रामं कस्माद्धि दारचाउर्य.म् त्वया क्र्तम्
transliteration: apohya rāmaṃ kasmāddhi dāracāurya.m tvayā krtam

sanskrit: उवाच रावणः सीतां भुजङ्ग इव निःश्वसन्
transliteration: uvāca rāvaṇaḥ sītāṃ bhujaṅga iva niḥśvasan

sanskrit: यथा मद्वशगा सीता क्षिप्रं भवति जानकी
तथा कुरुत राक्षस्यः सर्वाः क्षिप्रं समेत्य च
transliteration: yathā madvaśagā sītā kṣipraṃ bhavati jānakī
tathā kuruta rākṣasyaḥ sarvāḥ kṣipraṃ sametya ca

sanskrit: विहाय सीतां मदनेन मोहितःस्वमेव वेश्म प्रविवेश भास्वरम्
transliteration: vihāya sītāṃ madanena mohitaḥsvameva veśma praviveśa bhāsvaram

sanskrit: सन्दिश्य च ततः सर्वा राक्षसीर्निर्जगाम ह
transliteration: sandiśya ca tataḥ sarvā rākṣasīrnirjagāma ha

sanskrit: दशग्रीवस्य भार्यात्वं सीते न बहु मन्यसे
transliteration: daśagrīvasya bhāryātvaṃ sīte na bahu manyase

sanskrit: प्रजापतीनां षण्णां तु चतुर्थो यः प्रजापतिः
मानसो ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः पुलस्त्य इति विश्रुतः
transliteration: prajāpatīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ tu caturtho yaḥ prajāpatiḥ
mānaso brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ pulastya iti viśrutaḥ

sanskrit: बलिनो वीर्ययुक्तस्या भार्यात्वं किं न लप्स्यसे
transliteration: balino vīryayuktasyā bhāryātvaṃ kiṃ na lapsyase

sanskrit: प्रियां बहुमतां भार्यां त्यक्त्वा राजा महाबलः
transliteration: priyāṃ bahumatāṃ bhāryāṃ tyaktvā rājā mahābalaḥ

sanskrit: निर्जिताः समरे येन स ते पार्श्वमुपागतः
transliteration: nirjitāḥ samare yena sa te pārśvamupāgataḥ

sanskrit: यस्य सूर्यो न तपति भीतो यस्य च मारुतः
न वाति स्मायतापाङ्गे किं त्वं तस्य न तिष्ठसि
transliteration: yasya sūryo na tapati bhīto yasya ca mārutaḥ
na vāti smāyatāpāṅge kiṃ tvaṃ tasya na tiṣṭhasi

sanskrit: पुष्पवृष्टिं च तरवो मुमुचुर्यस्य वै भयात्
शैलाश्च सुभ्रु पानीयं जलदाश् च यदेच्छति
transliteration: puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ ca taravo mumucuryasya vai bhayāt
śailāśca subhru pānīyaṃ jaladāś ca yadecchati

sanskrit: किं त्वं न कुरुषे बुद्धिं भार्यार्थे रावणस्य हि
transliteration: kiṃ tvaṃ na kuruṣe buddhiṃ bhāryārthe rāvaṇasya hi

sanskrit: साधु ते तत्त्वतो देवि कथितं साधु भामिनि
transliteration: sādhu te tattvato devi kathitaṃ sādhu bhāmini

sanskrit: प्रत्याहर मनो रामान्न त्वं जातु भविष्यसि
transliteration: pratyāhara mano rāmānna tvaṃ jātu bhaviṣyasi

sanskrit: मानुषी मानुषं तं तु राममिच्छसि शोभने
transliteration: mānuṣī mānuṣaṃ taṃ tu rāmamicchasi śobhane

sanskrit: कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः
दीनो वा राज्यहीनो वा यो मे भर्ता स मे गुरुः
transliteration: kāmaṃ khādata māṃ sarvā na kariṣyāmi vo vacaḥ
dīno vā rājyahīno vā yo me bhartā sa me guruḥ

sanskrit: परितुष्टास्मि भद्रं ते मानुषस्ते कृतो विधिः
ममापि तु वचः पथ्यं ब्रुवन्त्याः कुरु मैथिलि
transliteration: parituṣṭāsmi bhadraṃ te mānuṣaste kṛto vidhiḥ
mamāpi tu vacaḥ pathyaṃ bruvantyāḥ kuru maithili

sanskrit: अग्नेः स्वाहा यथा देवी शचीवेन्द्रस्य शोभने
transliteration: agneḥ svāhā yathā devī śacīvendrasya śobhane

sanskrit: किं ते रामेण वैदेहि कृपणेन गतायुषा
transliteration: kiṃ te rāmeṇa vaidehi kṛpaṇena gatāyuṣā

sanskrit: एतदुक्तं च मे वाक्यं यदि त्वं न करिष्यसि
transliteration: etaduktaṃ ca me vākyaṃ yadi tvaṃ na kariṣyasi

sanskrit: न च नः कुरुषे वाक्यं हितं कालपुरस्कृतम्
transliteration: na ca naḥ kuruṣe vākyaṃ hitaṃ kālapuraskṛtam

sanskrit: भज प्रीतिं प्रहर्षं च त्यजैतां नित्यदैन्यताम्
transliteration: bhaja prītiṃ praharṣaṃ ca tyajaitāṃ nityadainyatām

sanskrit: जानासि हि यथा भीरु स्त्रीणां यौवनमध्रुवम्
transliteration: jānāsi hi yathā bhīru strīṇāṃ yauvanamadhruvam

sanskrit: स्त्रीसहस्राणि ते सप्त वशे स्थास्यन्ति सुन्दरि
transliteration: strīsahasrāṇi te sapta vaśe sthāsyanti sundari

sanskrit: उत्पाट्य वा ते हृदयं भक्षयिष्यामि मैथिलि
यदि मे व्याहृतं वाक्यं न यथावत्करिष्यसि
transliteration: utpāṭya vā te hṛdayaṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi maithili
yadi me vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ na yathāvatkariṣyasi

sanskrit: रावणेन हृतां दृष्ट्वा दौर्हृदो मे महानभूत्
transliteration: rāvaṇena hṛtāṃ dṛṣṭvā daurhṛdo me mahānabhūt

sanskrit: अन्त्राण्यपि तथा शीर्षं खादेयमिति मे मतिः
transliteration: antrāṇyapi tathā śīrṣaṃ khādeyamiti me matiḥ

sanskrit: निवेद्यतां ततो राज्ञे मानुषी सा मृतेति ह
नात्र कश्चन सन्देहः खादतेति स वक्ष्यति
transliteration: nivedyatāṃ tato rājñe mānuṣī sā mṛteti ha
nātra kaścana sandehaḥ khādateti sa vakṣyati

sanskrit: विभजाम ततः सर्वा विवादो मे न रोचते
पेयमानीयतां क्षिप्रं माल्यं च विविधं बहु
transliteration: vibhajāma tataḥ sarvā vivādo me na rocate
peyamānīyatāṃ kṣipraṃ mālyaṃ ca vividhaṃ bahu

sanskrit: अजामुखा यदुक्तं हि तदेव मम रोचते
transliteration: ajāmukhā yaduktaṃ hi tadeva mama rocate

sanskrit: तथा तासां वदन्तीनां परुषं दारुणं बहु
transliteration: tathā tāsāṃ vadantīnāṃ paruṣaṃ dāruṇaṃ bahu

sanskrit: कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः
transliteration: kāmaṃ khādata māṃ sarvā na kariṣyāmi vo vacaḥ
english: A woman cannot be the wife of a Rākşasa. Eat me up if you will, I will never follow your words.

sanskrit: न शर्म लेभे दुःखार्ता रावणेन च तर्जिता
transliteration: na śarma lebhe duḥkhārtā rāvaṇena ca tarjitā

sanskrit: सा वेपमाना पतिता प्रवाते कदली यथा
transliteration: sā vepamānā patitā pravāte kadalī yathā

sanskrit: तस्या सा दीर्घविपुला वेपन्त्याः सीतया तदा
transliteration: tasyā sā dīrghavipulā vepantyāḥ sītayā tadā

sanskrit: हा रामेति च दुःखार्ता पुनर्हा लक्ष्मणेति च
हा श्वश्रु मम कौसल्ये हा सुमित्रेति भाविनि
transliteration: hā rāmeti ca duḥkhārtā punarhā lakṣmaṇeti ca
hā śvaśru mama kausalye hā sumitreti bhāvini

sanskrit: अकाले दुर्लभो मृत्युः स्त्रिया वा पुरुषस्य वा
transliteration: akāle durlabho mṛtyuḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā

sanskrit: सीदामि खलु शोकेन कूलं तोयहतं यथा
transliteration: sīdāmi khalu śokena kūlaṃ toyahataṃ yathā

sanskrit: धन्याः पश्यन्ति मे नाथं कृतज्ञं प्रियवादिनम्
transliteration: dhanyāḥ paśyanti me nāthaṃ kṛtajñaṃ priyavādinam

sanskrit: कीदृशं तु मया पापं पुरा देहान्तरे कृतम्
येनेदं प्राप्यते दुःखं मया घोरं सुदारुणम्
transliteration: kīdṛśaṃ tu mayā pāpaṃ purā dehāntare kṛtam
yenedaṃ prāpyate duḥkhaṃ mayā ghoraṃ sudāruṇam

sanskrit: न हि मे जीवितेनार्थो नैवार्थैर्न च भूषणैः
वसन्त्या राक्षसी मध्ये विना रामं महारथम्
transliteration: na hi me jīvitenārtho naivārthairna ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ
vasantyā rākṣasī madhye vinā rāmaṃ mahāratham

sanskrit: का च मे जीविते श्रद्धा सुखे वा तं प्रियं विना
transliteration: kā ca me jīvite śraddhā sukhe vā taṃ priyaṃ vinā

sanskrit: न चाप्यहं चिरं दुःखं सहेयं प्रियवर्जिता
transliteration: na cāpyahaṃ ciraṃ duḥkhaṃ saheyaṃ priyavarjitā

sanskrit: प्रत्याख्यातं न जानाति नात्मानं नात्मनः कुलम्
transliteration: pratyākhyātaṃ na jānāti nātmānaṃ nātmanaḥ kulam

sanskrit: छिन्ना भिन्ना विभक्ता वा दीप्ते वाग्नौ प्रदीपिता
रावणं नोपतिष्ठेयं किं प्रलापेन वश् चिरम्
transliteration: chinnā bhinnā vibhaktā vā dīpte vāgnau pradīpitā
rāvaṇaṃ nopatiṣṭheyaṃ kiṃ pralāpena vaś ciram

sanskrit: येनैकेन निरस्तानि स मां किं नाभिपद्यते
transliteration: yenaikena nirastāni sa māṃ kiṃ nābhipadyate

sanskrit: समर्थः खलु मे भर्ता रावणं हन्तुमाहवे
transliteration: samarthaḥ khalu me bhartā rāvaṇaṃ hantumāhave

sanskrit: रणे रामेण निहतः स मां किं नाभिपद्यते
transliteration: raṇe rāmeṇa nihataḥ sa māṃ kiṃ nābhipadyate

sanskrit: न तु राघवबाणानां गतिरोधी ह विद्यते
transliteration: na tu rāghavabāṇānāṃ gatirodhī ha vidyate

sanskrit: किं नु तत्कारणं येन रामो दृढपराक्रमः
transliteration: kiṃ nu tatkāraṇaṃ yena rāmo dṛḍhaparākramaḥ

sanskrit: इहस्थां मां न जानीते शङ्के लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः
transliteration: ihasthāṃ māṃ na jānīte śaṅke lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ

sanskrit: रावणस्य च नीचस्य कीर्तिं नाम च नाशयेत्
transliteration: rāvaṇasya ca nīcasya kīrtiṃ nāma ca nāśayet

sanskrit: यथाहमेवं रुदती तथा भूयो न संशयः
transliteration: yathāhamevaṃ rudatī tathā bhūyo na saṃśayaḥ

sanskrit: न हि ताभ्यां रिपुर्दृष्टो मुहूतमपि जीवति
transliteration: na hi tābhyāṃ ripurdṛṣṭo muhūtamapi jīvati

sanskrit: नूनं लङ्का हते पापे रावणे राक्षसाधिपे
शोषं यास्यति दुर्धर्षा प्रमदा विधवा यथा
transliteration: nūnaṃ laṅkā hate pāpe rāvaṇe rākṣasādhipe
śoṣaṃ yāsyati durdharṣā pramadā vidhavā yathā

sanskrit: यदि नाम स शूरो मां रामो रक्तान्तलोचनः
transliteration: yadi nāma sa śūro māṃ rāmo raktāntalocanaḥ

sanskrit: अकार्यं ये न जानन्ति नैरृताः पापकारिणः
transliteration: akāryaṃ ye na jānanti nairṛtāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ

sanskrit: साहं कथं करिष्यामि तं विना प्रियदर्शनम्
transliteration: sāhaṃ kathaṃ kariṣyāmi taṃ vinā priyadarśanam

sanskrit: क्षिप्रं वैवस्वतं देवं पश्येयं पतिना विना
transliteration: kṣipraṃ vaivasvataṃ devaṃ paśyeyaṃ patinā vinā

sanskrit: जानन्तौ तौ न कुर्यातां नोर्व्यां हि मम मार्गणम्
transliteration: jānantau tau na kuryātāṃ norvyāṃ hi mama mārgaṇam

sanskrit: नूनं ममैव शोकेन स वीरो लक्ष्मणाग्रजः
transliteration: nūnaṃ mamaiva śokena sa vīro lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ

sanskrit: मम पश्यन्ति ये नाथं रामं राजीवलोचनम्
transliteration: mama paśyanti ye nāthaṃ rāmaṃ rājīvalocanam

sanskrit: अथ वा न हि तस्यार्थे धर्मकामस्य धीमतः
transliteration: atha vā na hi tasyārthe dharmakāmasya dhīmataḥ

sanskrit: किं नु मे न गुणाः के चित्किं वा भाग्य क्षयो हि मे
याहं सीता वरार्हेण हीना रामेण भामिनी
transliteration: kiṃ nu me na guṇāḥ ke citkiṃ vā bhāgya kṣayo hi me
yāhaṃ sītā varārheṇa hīnā rāmeṇa bhāminī

sanskrit: श्रेयो मे जीवितान्मर्तुं विहीना या महात्मना
transliteration: śreyo me jīvitānmartuṃ vihīnā yā mahātmanā

sanskrit: अथ वा न्यस्तशस्त्रौ तौ वने मूलफलाशनौ
भ्रातरौ हि नर श्रेष्ठौ चरन्तौ वनगोचरौ
transliteration: atha vā nyastaśastrau tau vane mūlaphalāśanau
bhrātarau hi nara śreṣṭhau carantau vanagocarau

sanskrit: न च मे विहितो मृत्युरस्मिन्दुःखेऽपि वर्तति
transliteration: na ca me vihito mṛtyurasminduḥkhe'pi vartati

sanskrit: जितात्मानो महाभागा येषां न स्तः प्रियाप्रिये
transliteration: jitātmāno mahābhāgā yeṣāṃ na staḥ priyāpriye

sanskrit: ताभ्यां हि ये वियुज्यन्ते नमस्तेषां महात्मनाम्
transliteration: tābhyāṃ hi ye viyujyante namasteṣāṃ mahātmanām

sanskrit: तथा तासां वदन्तीनां परुषं दारुणं बहु
transliteration: tathā tāsāṃ vadantīnāṃ paruṣaṃ dāruṇaṃ bahu
english: Those hideous Rākşasīs thus threatening her with reproaches rude and rough, the daughter of the king Janaka began to weep.
And being thus addressed by those Rākşasīs, Vaidehi, of subdued soul, being greatly terrified, said, having her voice choked with vapour.

sanskrit: कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः
transliteration: kāmaṃ khādata māṃ sarvā na kariṣyāmi vo vacaḥ
english: A woman can never be the wife of a Räksasa. Eat ine up if you will, I shall never follow your words.

sanskrit: न शर्म लेभे दुःखार्ता रावणेन च तर्जिता
transliteration: na śarma lebhe duḥkhārtā rāvaṇena ca tarjitā
english: And being surrounded by the Rākṣasīs and threatened by Rāvana, Sītă, resembling the daughter of a celestial, stricken with grief, could not console herself.
And trembling, she shrank from their presence like to a strayed fawn surrounded by wolves.
And resorting to a flowery branch of an Asoka tree, she sunk in grief, thought upon her lord.
With tears she bathed her beautiful breast and oppressed with woe, she could not reach the other bank of the ocean of grief.

sanskrit: सा वेपमाना पतिता प्रवाते कदली यथा
transliteration: sā vepamānā patitā pravāte kadalī yathā
english: Like a plantain tree shaken by the breeze, she shook and fell down trembling (on the earth). And being afraid of the Rākşasīs, her cheeks forsook their native hue.

sanskrit: तस्याः सा दीर्घविपुला वेपन्त्या सीतया तदा
transliteration: tasyāḥ sā dīrghavipulā vepantyā sītayā tadā
english: And herself trembling, her pretty long lock of hair also shook and appeared like a serpent moving this way and that.

sanskrit: रा रामेति च दूःखार्ता हा पुनर्लक्ष्मणेति च
हा श्वश्रु मम कौसल्ये हा सुमित्रेति भामिनी
transliteration: rā rāmeti ca dūḥkhārtā hā punarlakṣmaṇeti ca
hā śvaśru mama kausalye hā sumitreti bhāminī

sanskrit: अकाले दुर्लभो मृत्युः स्त्रिया वा पुरुषस्य वा
transliteration: akāle durlabho mṛtyuḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā
english: Overwhelmed with grief and beside herself with ire, the daughter of the king of Mithilā, wept and exclaimed sorrowfully, O Rāma, and again, O Laksmana, O mother Kausalyā! O queen Sumitrā! true is the saying of the wise that death dose never approach untimely the male or the female.
Or else I would not have lived for a moment, separated from Rama and oppressed by the Raksasis as I am.
Limited is my virtue, and therefore I am to die the death of a poor deserted thing like to a bark driven by the blast in the midst of the ocean.

sanskrit: सीदामि खलु शोकेन कूलं तोयहतं यथा
transliteration: sīdāmi khalu śokena kūlaṃ toyahataṃ yathā
english: Debarred from my husband's sight and tortured by the hideous demons, I shall sink, oppressed with woes, like to the banks of a river, washed by the water.

sanskrit: धन्याः पश्यन्ति मे नाथं कृतज्ञं प्रियवादिनम्
transliteration: dhanyāḥ paśyanti me nāthaṃ kṛtajñaṃ priyavādinam
english: Oh blest are they who have been resting their eyes upon my grateful and sweet-speeched lord of leonine gaits, having eyes resembling lotus petals!
And separated from Rāma of subdued soul, it is as difficult for me to breathe as for him who has drank up virulent poison.

sanskrit: कीदृशं तु मया पापं पुरा जन्मान्तरे कृतम्
येनेदं प्राप्यते दुःखं मया घोरं सुदारुणम्
transliteration: kīdṛśaṃ tu mayā pāpaṃ purā janmāntare kṛtam
yenedaṃ prāpyate duḥkhaṃ mayā ghoraṃ sudāruṇam
english: What mighty iniquity had I perpetrated in my previous existence that I have met with this terrible disaster!
I wish to renounce my life under this load of grief-but alas! I am surrounded by the Raks asis and cannot meet Rāma.
Oh! cursed is this subject human life, that they cannot renounce it even at their pleasure!

Saying this, the daughter of the king Janaka, bathed her countenance with tears and hanging down her head began to lament. And she began to roll on the earth like to a colt as if she was mad, possessed by a devil and had lost her sense.

Saying this, the daughter of the king Janaka, bathed her countenance with tears and hanging down her head began to lament. And she began to roll on the earth like to a colt as if she was mad, possessed by a devil and had lost her sense.
I, the spouse of Rāma, who was drawn away at a distance by the Rākşasa (Mārīca) assuming shapes at will, was seized and borne away by Rāvana.
A captive of the Rākşasis, subject to their terrible threats and taunts, sunk in grief and anxiety, I desire not to keep my life.

sanskrit: नहि मे जीवितैरर्थो नैवार्थैर्न च भूषणैः
transliteration: nahi me jīvitairartho naivārthairna ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: Of what avail are wealth, ornament and life to me, who am living in the midst of the Răkşasas and separated from Ráma, of the mighty car?
Forsooth my my life is is made of stone, imperishable and immortal since it is not riven asunder even by this mighty grief.

sanskrit: धिङ्मामनार्यामसतीं या ऽहं तेन विना कृता
english: Woe to me! who am unchaste and vile and my life is vicious, since breathe I still in the absence of my lord.

sanskrit: का च मे जीविते श्रद्धा सुखे वा तं प्रियं विना
transliteration: kā ca me jīvite śraddhā sukhe vā taṃ priyaṃ vinā
