And beholding Dadhimukha greatly enraged, all the monkeys, headed by Hanumān, approached him with great vehemence.
And as the mighty Dadhimukha of huge arms, was proceeding towards them vehemently with a huge tree, Angada, wroth, caught him by the hand.

sanskrit: मदान्धश्च न वेदैनमार्यको ऽयं ममेति सः
english: He was beside himself with intoxication and therefore did not show him the least mercy, albeit he (Dadhimukha) was worshipful to him. And accordingly with great vehemence he ground him to the dust.
His arms and thighs were broken and his countenance was disfigured and that great hero, the foremost of the monkeys, bathed in a pool of blood, remained senseless for sometime.
And thereupon releasing himself from them by some device that leading monkey, proceeded to a nook, and addressed his attendants, saying.

sanskrit: एते तिष्ठन्तु गच्छामो भर्ता नो यत्र वानरः
transliteration: ete tiṣṭhantu gacchāmo bhartā no yatra vānaraḥ
english: Let us all proceed there where our lord, the spacious-necked Sugrīva live with Rāma.
I shall relate to him all the unfair dealings of Angada and forsooth shall that wrathful king punish all these monkeys
The picturesque Madhuvana is the most favourite orchard of the high-souled Sugrīva. It was enjoyed by his forefathers and is not even approached by the celestials.
And meting out punishment to these monkeys, eager to drink honey and almost half dead, Sugrīva shall slay them as will as their friends and relatives.
Those vicious-souled ones are worthy of being slain since they have transgressed the royal mandate. And then shall my wrath, arising out of impatience, bear fruits.
Having thus spoken to the guards of the forest the highly powerful Dadhimukha leaped high up in the welkin and went away with them.
And in no time he reached where the highly intelligent "Niether monkey/Sugriva, the offspring of the sun, was."

sanskrit: रामं च लक्ष्मणं चैव दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवमेव च
transliteration: rāmaṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā sugrīvameva ca
english: And beholding Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Sugrīva and the level ground he descended from the sky.

And descending from the sky that great and heroic Dabhimukha ,lord over all the monkeys engaged in protecting the forest, placing his folded palms on his forehead and with a poorly countenance, laid low his crown at Sugrīva's feet.

sanskrit: स दीनवदनो भूत्वा कृत्वा शिरसि चाञ्जलिम्
transliteration: sa dīnavadano bhūtvā kṛtvā śirasi cāñjalim
english: And descending from the sky that great and heroic Dabhimukha ,lord over all the monkeys engaged in protecting the forest, placing his folded palms on his forehead and with a poorly countenance, laid low his crown at Sugrīva's feet.
And beholding that monkey place his crown at his feet the monkey-chief, with an anxious mind, accosted him, saying.

sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ कस्मात् त्वं पादयोः पतितो मम
transliteration: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha kasmāt tvaṃ pādayoḥ patito mama
english: Rise up, rise up, why had you lain yourself at my feet? I declare you had you come here? It behove you to suggest the becoming procedure. Is it all well with my orchard Madhuvana? I long to know everything, O monkey.
Being thus addressed hopefully by the highsouled Sugrīva, Dadhimukha, gifted with an intelligence of a very high order, rose up and spoke.

sanskrit: वनं निसृष्टपूर्वं हि भक्षितं तच्च वानरैः
transliteration: vanaṃ nisṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hi bhakṣitaṃ tacca vānaraiḥ
english: Neither yourself, nor Vāli, the lord of the monkeys, O king, allowed that orchard to be freely used by the monkeys but that has been now laid waste by them.

sanskrit: निवार्यमाणास्ते सर्वे भ्रूवौ वै दर्शयन्ति हि
transliteration: nivāryamāṇāste sarve bhrūvau vai darśayanti hi
english: Some of them went beyond the pale of food conduct, others ate at their pleasure, and all frowned (at us).
When these attendants, being insulted by them, were greatly wroth, they were driven out of the garden, by those powerful and enraged monkeys.
They were greatly assailed by those many thousand heroic monkeys, worked up with ire and having reddened eyes.
Some had their arins broken, some had their knee-joints crushed and some of them were thrown up in the sky.

sanskrit: कृत्स्नं मधुवनं चैव प्रकामं तैः प्रभक्ष्यते
transliteration: kṛtsnaṃ madhuvanaṃ caiva prakāmaṃ taiḥ prabhakṣyate
english: Yourself their lord living, these heroes are beaten, and the entire Madhuvana is being freely enjoyed by them.
The highly intelligent Lakşmaņa, the slayer of foes, addressed Sugriva, the foremost O the monkeys, while he was thus being informed, saying.
O king, why has this monkey, the guard over the forest, come to you, and what sorrow has led him to give vent to these expressions?
Being thus addressed by the high-souled Laksmana, Sugriva, skilled in the art of speech, replied.

sanskrit: आर्य लक्ष्मण संप्राह वीरो दधिमुखः कपिः
transliteration: ārya lakṣmaṇa saṃprāha vīro dadhimukhaḥ kapiḥ
english: O worshipful Lakşmaņa, the heroic monkey Dadhimukha speaks that the war-like monkeys headed by Angada have drunk honey.

Forsooth that orchard has been laid waste by these heroes headed by Angada. And ransacking the southern quarter, those leading monkeys have come back and delightedly entered the Madhuvana. And the whole orchard has been explored and enjoyed by those monkeys and the attendants beaten and wounded on their kneejoints. To communicate to me this intelligence, this monkey of known prowess, and sweet accents, named Dhadimukha, has come here.

sanskrit: आगतैश्च प्रमथितं यथा मधुवनं हि तैः
transliteration: āgataiśca pramathitaṃ yathā madhuvanaṃ hi taiḥ

sanskrit: धर्षितं च वनं कृत्स्नमुपयुक्तं च वानरैः
transliteration: dharṣitaṃ ca vanaṃ kṛtsnamupayuktaṃ ca vānaraiḥ

sanskrit: दृष्टा देवी न सन्देहो न चान्येन हनूमता
न ह्यन्यः साधने हेतुः कर्मणो ऽस्य हनूमतः
transliteration: dṛṣṭā devī na sandeho na cānyena hanūmatā
na hyanyaḥ sādhane hetuḥ karmaṇo 'sya hanūmataḥ

sanskrit: व्यवसायश्च वीर्यं च श्रुतं चापि प्रतिष्ठितम्
transliteration: vyavasāyaśca vīryaṃ ca śrutaṃ cāpi pratiṣṭhitam
english: There is none else but Hanumān who is the instrumental of this work, for that best of monkeys has in him a high intellect, know the art of success, is gifted with courage, strength and prowess and is conversant with Śāstras.
That work is sure to succeed whose leading spirits are the mighty Jāmbavāna and Angada, and worker is Hanumăn.

Forsooth that orchard has been laid waste by these heroes headed by Angada. And ransacking the southern quarter, those leading monkeys have come back and delightedly entered the Madhuvana. And the whole orchard has been explored and enjoyed by those monkeys and the attendants beaten and wounded on their kneejoints. To communicate to me this intelligence, this monkey of known prowess, and sweet accents, named Dhadimukha, has come here.

sanskrit: दृष्टा सीता महाबाहो सौमित्रे पश्य तत्त्वतः
transliteration: dṛṣṭā sītā mahābāho saumitre paśya tattvataḥ
english: O you of mighty arms, O son of Sumitra, forsooth they have beheld Sītā, since the monkeys, just on their return, have engaged in drinking honey.
O best of men, they are all well-known monkeys and without espying Vaidehī they would not have engaged in the destruction of that orchard conferred on us as a gift by the celestials.
Hearing these words from Sugrīva, pleasant to ears, the virtuous-souled Lakşmaņa along with Rāghava, was greatly pleased.
And hearing this from Dadhimukha, Sugrīva, greatly gratified; addressed that lord of the for st, gain, Saying.

sanskrit: प्रीतो ऽस्मि सो ऽहं युद्भुक्तं वनं तैः कृतकर्मभिः
transliteration: prīto 'smi so 'haṃ yudbhuktaṃ vanaṃ taiḥ kṛtakarmabhiḥ
english: Greatly pleased I am, since, they, being successful, have explored this forest. And the insulting procedure of the successful is also pardonable. Do you soon go there and protect that orchards, and send here all those monkeys headed by Hanumān.

sanskrit: द्रष्टुं कृतार्थान् सह राघवाभ्यां श्रोतुं च सीताधिगमे प्रयत्नम्
transliteration: draṣṭuṃ kṛtārthān saha rāghavābhyāṃ śrotuṃ ca sītādhigame prayatnam
english: Along with these two descendants of Raghu, I long to know soon from these monkeys headed by Hanumān, and proud like lions, what they have settled for the regaining of Sītā.

sanskrit: प्रीतिस्पीताक्षौ सम्प्रहृष्टौ कुमारौ दृष्ट्वा सिद्धार्थौ वानराणां च राजा
अङ्गैः संहृष्टैः कर्मसिद्धिं विदित्वा बाह्वोरासन्नां सो ऽतिमात्रं ननन्द
transliteration: prītispītākṣau samprahṛṣṭau kumārau dṛṣṭvā siddhārthau vānarāṇāṃ ca rājā
aṅgaiḥ saṃhṛṣṭaiḥ karmasiddhiṃ viditvā bāhvorāsannāṃ so 'timātraṃ nananda
english: And beholding-these two princes greatly delighted and their eyes expanded with joy, the king of the monkeys, thought that the accomplishment of the great work was near at hand, and was accordingly greatly delighted."
Being thus addressed by Sugrīva, the monkey Dadhimuklia, delighted, bowed to him, Rāghava and Laksmana.

sanskrit: स प्रणम्य च सुग्रीवं राघवौ च महाबलौ
transliteration: sa praṇamya ca sugrīvaṃ rāghavau ca mahābalau
english: And adoring Sugrīva and the highly powerful descendants of Raghu, he along with other heroic monkeys, leaped up in the sky.

sanskrit: स यथैवागतः पूर्वं तथैव त्वरितं गतः
transliteration: sa yathaivāgataḥ pūrvaṃ tathaiva tvaritaṃ gataḥ
english: He went away with the same speed with which he came and leaping down on the earth from the sky, entered the orchard.
And entering that forest he beheld all the leaders of the monkeys spending the hours delightedly, having passed urine, the outcome of honey.
And approaching them, the hero, with folded hands and delighted, addressed Angada, with the following words.
O gentle one, do you not take offence, for these monkeys, protecting the garden enraged, unwittingly prevented you.

sanskrit: मौर्ख्यात् पूर्वं कृतो दोषस्तं भवान् क्षन्तुमर्हति
transliteration: maurkhyāt pūrvaṃ kṛto doṣastaṃ bhavān kṣantumarhati

sanskrit: आख्यातं हि मया गत्वा पितृव्यस्य तवानघ
transliteration: ākhyātaṃ hi mayā gatvā pitṛvyasya tavānagha
english: O innocent prince, I have related all about this to your uncle. When I described to him, the arrival of all these forest rangers, as well as of yours accompanied by them, and the destruction of this garden by you all, he was not the least offended, rather delighted.

sanskrit: प्रहृष्टो न तु रुष्टो ऽसौ वनं श्रुत्वा प्रधर्षितम्
transliteration: prahṛṣṭo na tu ruṣṭo 'sau vanaṃ śrutvā pradharṣitam
english: O innocent prince, I have related all about this to your uncle. When I described to him, the arrival of all these forest rangers, as well as of yours accompanied by them, and the destruction of this garden by you all, he was not the least offended, rather delighted.
And worked up with joy your uncle Sugrīva, the lord of earth and monkeys, said “Send them all here speedily."
Hearing those words from Dadhimukha, Angada, the foremost of the monkeys and skilled in speech, addressed them all, saying.

sanskrit: शङ्के श्रुतो ऽयं वृत्तान्तो रामेण हरियूथपाः
तत्क्षमं नेह नः स्थातुं कृते कार्ये परन्तपाः
transliteration: tatkṣamaṃ neha naḥ sthātuṃ kṛte kārye parantapāḥ
english: O you leaders of the monkey hosts, I fear, Rāma has heard all about this. Dadhimukha relates everything joyfully and hence I infer this. And our work finished, O slayer of foes, it dose not behove us to remain here (any longer).

sanskrit: किं शेषं गमनं तत्र सुग्रीवो यत्र मे गुरुः
transliteration: kiṃ śeṣaṃ gamanaṃ tatra sugrīvo yatra me guruḥ
english: You have all drunk honey at your pleasure and there is nothing left and you should now go where the monkey king Sugrīva is.

sanskrit: सर्वे यथा मां वक्ष्यन्ति समेत्य हरियूथपाः
तथा ऽस्मि कर्ता कर्तव्ये भवद्भिः परवानहम्
transliteration: sarve yathā māṃ vakṣyanti sametya hariyūthapāḥ
english: O leading monkeys, I shall follow what you will in a band desire me to do. In action I am subordinate to you all.
I am not justified to command although I am a prince. You are all of accomplished actions, it is not proper to repress you forcibly.
Hearing those sweet words of the prince Angada, the monkeys delightedly replied, saying.

sanskrit: एवं वक्ष्यति को राजन् प्रभुः सन् वानरर्षभ
transliteration: evaṃ vakṣyati ko rājan prabhuḥ san vānararṣabha
english: O king, O foremost of monkeys, who else can speak thus being a master? Any one else, we think, is proud of his wealth.

sanskrit: तव चेदं सुसदृशं वाक्यं नान्यस्य कस्यचित्
transliteration: tava cedaṃ susadṛśaṃ vākyaṃ nānyasya kasyacit
english: Such like words become you only and none else. Your humility speaks of your future greatness.
We are all anxious to go there, where Sugriva, the king of the monkeys, is.

sanskrit: क्वचिद्गन्तुं हरिश्रेष्ठ ब्रूमः सत्यमिदं तु ते
transliteration: kvacidgantuṃ hariśreṣṭha brūmaḥ satyamidaṃ tu te
english: Verily we speak to you, O foremost of monkeys, that without your permission, none among us, is capable of advancing a single step.”

They addressing him thus, Angada replied"All right, let us all go.” Saying this he leaped up in the sky and was followed by all those monkeys, clouding the welkin as if with stones thrown up by a tool.

sanskrit: कृत्वा ऽ ऽकाशं निराकाशं यन्त्रोत्क्षिप्ता इवाचलाः
english: They addressing him thus, Angada replied"All right, let us all go.” Saying this he leaped up in the sky and was followed by all those monkeys, clouding the welkin as if with stones thrown up by a tool.
And placing before them Angada and Hanumān, the monkeys leaping vehemently up in the sky roared like to clouds driven by the wind.
And Angada nearing, Sugrīva, the lord of the monkeys, spoke to the lotus-eyed Rāma, stricken with grief, saying.

sanskrit: समाश्वसिहि भद्र ते दृष्टा देवी न संशयः
नागन्तुमिह शक्यं तैरतीते समये हि नः
transliteration: samāśvasihi bhadra te dṛṣṭā devī na saṃśayaḥ
nāgantumiha śakyaṃ tairatīte samaye hi naḥ
english: May good betide you. Do you console yourself. The worshipful dame has been found out; there is not the least doubt about it. Or else they would not have come as the time is already past.

I (further more) infer this from Angada's joy, O you of auspicious presence. Without being successful in his mission, the large-armed prince, Angada, the foremost of the monkeys, would not have come to me.

If the monkeys had engaged in such an unfair proceeding without being successful in their mission, Angada would have looked poorly and his mind would have been overwhelmed with grief and forgetfulness.
Without beholding the daughter of the king Janaka they would not have dared to destroy Madhuvana obtained and preserved by my forefathers.

sanskrit: दृष्टा देवी न सन्देहो न चान्येन हनूमता
transliteration: dṛṣṭā devī na sandeho na cānyena hanūmatā
english: Do you console yourself, O Räma, by whom Kausalyā has become the mother of a good son. O you, rigidly observing any religious vow or obligation, forsooth has Hanumān behold the worshipful dame and none else.

sanskrit: न ह्यन्यः कर्मणो हेतुः साधने ऽस्य हनूमतः
व्यवसायश्च वीर्यं च सूर्य तेज इव ध्रुवम्
transliteration: na hyanyaḥ karmaṇo hetuḥ sādhane 'sya hanūmataḥ
vyavasāyaśca vīryaṃ ca sūrya teja iva dhruvam
english: No other wight is so qualified an instrument in encompassing this end. O you of excellent intellect, Hanumān know the art of success, is gifted with intellect, perseverance and courage and is versed in Šāstras. That work cannot fail, which is worked out by Jāmbavān and Angada and presided over by Hanumān.

Be not laden with anxiety, O you of unmitigated prowess. These monkey have come here excited with pride and drink. They would not have come with such a grandeur had they been but unsuccessful. From their breaking down the orchard and drinking honey I inferred SO.
Thereupon he heard in the sky the joyous sounds of the monkeys proud on account of Hanuman's work, proceeding towards Kişkindhā and as if announcing their success.

sanskrit: ततः श्रुत्वा निनादं तं कपीनां कपिसत्तमः
transliteration: tataḥ śrutvā ninādaṃ taṃ kapīnāṃ kapisattamaḥ
english: Thereupon hearing the noise of these monkeys Sugriva, their chief, being greatly delighted, uplifted his tail.

sanskrit: अङ्गदं पुरतः कृत्वा हनूमन्तं च वानरम्
transliteration: aṅgadaṃ purataḥ kṛtvā hanūmantaṃ ca vānaram
english: And placing Angada and Hanumān before them those monkeys proceeded to behold Rāma.

sanskrit: ते ऽङ्गदप्रमुखा वीराः प्रहृष्टाश्च मुदा ऽन्विताः
english: Those heroes headed by Angada, delighted and intoxicated, descended before Rāghava and the lord of the monkeys.
And the mighty-armed Hanumān, lowering his head, related to Rāghava, Sītā's spiritual and physical well-being.
And being confirmed thus by the Wind-god's son, Laksmana, greatly pleased, respectfully looked towards Sugriva.

sanskrit: प्रीत्या च रममाणो ऽथ राघवः परवीरहा
english: And Rāghava too, the slayer of foes, worked up with joy, cast respectful looks towards Hanuman.

sanskrit: ततः प्रस्रवणं शैलं ते गत्वा चित्रकाननम्
प्रणम्य शिरसा रामं लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्
transliteration: tataḥ prasravaṇaṃ śailaṃ te gatvā citrakānanam
praṇamya śirasā rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
english: Thereupon getting at the Mount Prasravana surrounded by a variegated forest, lowering their heads to the mighty Rāma and Lakşmaņa, placing before them their prince (Angada) and bowing to Sugrīva, the monkeys began to relate the story of Sītā.

Thereupon getting at the Mount Prasravana surrounded by a variegated forest, lowering their heads to the mighty Rāma and Lakşmaņa, placing before them their prince (Angada) and bowing to Sugrīva, the monkeys began to relate the story of Sītā.

sanskrit: रामे समनुरागं च यश्चायं समयः कृतः
transliteration: rāme samanurāgaṃ ca yaścāyaṃ samayaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: And they described to Ráma, the confinement of Sītā in Rāvana's seraglio, the remonstrances of the she-demons, her unflinching attachment in her lord and the time appointed (by the Rākṣasa for her destruction). And hearing of Vaidehi's well-being Rāma said.

And they described to Ráma, the confinement of Sītā in Rāvana's seraglio, the remonstrances of the she-demons, her unflinching attachment in her lord and the time appointed (by the Rākṣasa for her destruction). And hearing of Vaidehi's well-being Rāma said.

sanskrit: क्व सीता वर्तते देवी कथं च मयि वर्तते
transliteration: kva sītā vartate devī kathaṃ ca mayi vartate
english: O monkeys where live the worshipful Sītā? And how is her attachment to me? Do you relate everything to me.
Hearing those painful words of Răma, the monkeys desired Hanumān, conversant with the whereabouts of Sītā, to describe every thing to him.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः
प्रणम्य शिरसा देव्यै सीतायै तां दिशं प्रति
उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञः सीताया दर्शनं यथा
transliteration: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣāṃ hanumān mārutātmajaḥ
praṇamya śirasā devyai sītāyai tāṃ diśaṃ prati
uvāca vākyaṃ vākyajñaḥ sītāyā darśanaṃ yathā
english: Hearing their words, Hanuman, the Windgod's son, versed in the art of speech, lowering his head in Sītā's name and towards the southern direction (where she lives) began to relate how he succeeded in beholding Sītā.

sanskrit: तत्र दृष्टा मया सीता रावणान्तःपुरे सती
संन्यस्य त्वयि जीवन्ती रामा राम मनोरथम्
transliteration: tatra dṛṣṭā mayā sītā rāvaṇāntaḥpure satī
saṃnyasya tvayi jīvantī rāmā rāma manoratham

english: And I saw there Sītā, in the inner appartment of Ravana. Centring all her thoughts in you, breathes that damsel, O Rama. I saw her reviled by the she demons again and again. She is being guarded in that garden by the grim-visaged Raksasis.

And that worshipful came, O hero, ever used to happiness, is now stricken with grief in your absence. Confined in Ravana's inner apartment, well protected by those she-demons, wearing a single braid of hair and poorly, she is engaged only in thoughts touching you.

sanskrit: देवी कथंचित् काकुत्स्थ त्वन्मना मार्गिता मया
transliteration: devī kathaṃcit kākutstha tvanmanā mārgitā mayā
english: She in lying on earth, shorn of all grace like to a lotus on the appearance of the winter. She has not the least attachment for Rāvana and is resolved upon putting an end to her existence.

O Kākutstha, O innocent prince, after enquiring for sometime, I found that worshipful dame devoted to you, and narrating the glories of the Ikşvāku race, O foremost of men, I created her confidence by and by, and addressing her I related everything.

sanskrit: ततः सम्भाषिता देवी सर्वमर्थं च दर्शिता
transliteration: tataḥ sambhāṣitā devī sarvamarthaṃ ca darśitā

english: Hearing of the friendship between you and Sugrīva she was greatly delighted. And she has her respect for you unshaken and all her actions are for you.
O great man, O you best of men, I beheld the daughter of Janaka in this plight, engaged in hard austerities and ever devoted to you.

sanskrit: अभिज्ञानं च मे दत्तं यथा वृत्तं तवान्तिके
transliteration: abhijñānaṃ ca me dattaṃ yathā vṛttaṃ tavāntike
english: O you of great intelligence, O Raghava, offering me (this jewel) as a token, she wanted me to relate to you, the occurrence at the mount Citrakūța regarding the crow.

And Jānakī addressing me said'O Windgod's son, do you describe everything of what you have seen here, to Rāma. And relating everything before Sugrīva, do you present him with this jewel which has been preserved by me with great care.

sanskrit: त्वया प्रनष्टे तिलके तं किल स्मर्तुमर्हसि
एष निर्यातितः श्रीमान् मया ते वारिसम्भवः
transliteration: tvayā pranaṣṭe tilake taṃ kila smartumarhasi
eṣa niryātitaḥ śrīmān mayā te vārisambhavaḥ

english: Breathe shall I only for a month, beyond that I shall never live, subject as I am to the demons.'
Thus was I accosted by Sītā, reduced to a skeleton, observing pious observances, shut up in Rāvana's inner apartment and having eyes like those of a hind.

sanskrit: एतदेव मया ऽ ऽख्यातं सर्वं राघव यद्यथा
english: I have described to you everything, O Rāghava, do you make arrangements for bridging over the ocean.

sanskrit: तौ जाताश्वासौ राजपुत्रौ विदित्वा तच्चाभिज्ञानं राघवाय प्रदाय
देव्या चाख्यातं सर्वमेवानुपूर्व्याद्वाचा सम्पूर्णं वायुपुत्रः शशंस
transliteration: tau jātāśvāsau rājaputrau viditvā taccābhijñānaṃ rāghavāya pradāya
devyā cākhyātaṃ sarvamevānupūrvyādvācā sampūrṇaṃ vāyuputraḥ śaśaṃsa
english: And considering those two princes greatly consoled, the Wind-god's son handed over that token to Rāghava and described everything from the beginning to the end.

sanskrit: तं मणिं हृदये कृत्वा प्ररुरोद सलक्ष्मणः
transliteration: taṃ maṇiṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā praruroda salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Being thus accosted by Hanumān, Rāma, the son of Dasaratha, placing that jewel on his breast, wept with Laksmana.

sanskrit: तं तु दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं राघवः शोककर्शितः
transliteration: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā maṇiśreṣṭhaṃ rāghavaḥ śokakarśitaḥ
english: Beholding that excellent jewel, Rāghava, stricken with grief, with eyes full of tears, spake to Sugriva, saying.
Forsooth my heart melt on beholding this jewel as milk trickle down from the udders of a cow on beholding its calf.
This jewel was conferred on Sītā by my father-in-law at the time of our wedding, and to enhance its beauty, she wore it on her head.
And this jewel, obtained from the bed of the ocean, was conferred on him (Janaka) by the intelligent Sakra, greatly delighted for being adored in a sacrifice.

sanskrit: इमं दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं यथा तातस्य दर्शनम्
transliteration: imaṃ dṛṣṭvā maṇiśreṣṭhaṃ yathā tātasya darśanam
english: O gentle one, this bring back to my mind, the memory of my father, and father-in-law the king of Videha.

sanskrit: अयं हि शोभते तस्याः प्रियाया मूर्ध्नि मे मणिः
transliteration: ayaṃ hi śobhate tasyāḥ priyāyā mūrdhni me maṇiḥ
english: This excellent jewel appeared beautiful on the crown of my dear one, and methinks, on beholding it, I have as if got back my beloved spouse.

sanskrit: किमाह सीता वैदेही ब्रूहि सौम्य पुनः पुनः
transliteration: kimāha sītā vaidehī brūhi saumya punaḥ punaḥ
english: Do you relate to me again and again, O gentle one what Vaidehi has said, as if sprinkling me with the water of her words like to one rendered senseless.
What greater grief can there be, O Saumitri, that I behold the jewel obtained from the ocean but not Vaidehi.?

sanskrit: चिरं जीवति वैदेही यदि मासं धरिष्यति
क्षणं सौम्य न जीवेयं विना तामसितेक्षणाम्
transliteration: ciraṃ jīvati vaidehī yadi māsaṃ dhariṣyati
kṣaṇaṃ saumya na jīveyaṃ vinā tāmasitekṣaṇām
english: Truly dose Vaidehī live for a long time if she breathes for a month. But O hero, I cannot live blue eyes.

sanskrit: नय मामपि तं देशं यत्र दृष्टा मम प्रिया
transliteration: naya māmapi taṃ deśaṃ yatra dṛṣṭā mama priyā
english: Do you take me there where you had beheld iny dear spouse. I cannot live for a moment while I have received intelligence about her.

sanskrit: कथं सा मम सुश्रोणी भीरुभीरुः सती सदा
transliteration: kathaṃ sā mama suśroṇī bhīrubhīruḥ satī sadā
english: How live that timid damsel, having a beautiful waist, being terrified, amidst the terrible and grim Raksasis?

sanskrit: आवृतं वदनं तस्या न विराजति राक्षसैः
transliteration: āvṛtaṃ vadanaṃ tasyā na virājati rākṣasaiḥ
english: Truly her countenance is not appearing beautiful like to the autumnal moon, enveloped with clouds, although cleared off the darkness.
Do you relate to me in sooth, O Hanuman, what Şītā has spoken to you. I shall live by these words, as the sick are cured by medicine.
O Hanumān, what has my dear wife, sweetspeeched, and highly beautiful, spoken to you, being separated form me? How breathes she going through a series of calamities?
Being thus addressed by the high-souled Rāghava, Hanumān, related to him all of what Sita had said,
O foremost of men, the worshipful Jānaki, related as a token, all the incidents at the Mount Citrakūta from the beginning to the end.
Sleeping happily with you, Janaki one day awoke before, and in the meantime, a crow wounded her breast with its beaks.

sanskrit: पुनश्च किल पक्षी स देव्या जनयति व्यथाम्
transliteration: punaśca kila pakṣī sa devyā janayati vyathām
english: O Rāma, you wert then asleep on Sītā's lap and that crow again afflicted the worshipful dame.
And it again wounded her. And being bathed in blood and suffering terrible pangs, that worshipful dame aroused you.

sanskrit: बोधितः किल देव्या त्वं सुखसुप्तः परन्तप
transliteration: bodhitaḥ kila devyā tvaṃ sukhasuptaḥ parantapa
english: And it again wounded her. And being bathed in blood and suffering terrible pangs, that worshipful dame aroused you.

sanskrit: तां तु दृष्ट्वा महाबाहो दारितां च स्तनान्तरे
transliteration: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā mahābāho dāritāṃ ca stanāntare
english: O slayer of foes, O you of mighty-arms, seeing her breast wounded, you, wroth like a serpent, didst speak saying.

sanskrit: नखाग्रैः केन ते भीरु दारितं तु स्तनान्तरम्
transliteration: nakhāgraiḥ kena te bhīru dāritaṃ tu stanāntaram
english: O timid damsel, who, with his nails, has wounded your breast? Who has played with an angry serpent having five faces?
Casting your looks around you didst behold a crow facing the worshipful dame with sharpened nails besmeared with blood.

sanskrit: सुतः किल स शक्रस्य वायसः पततां वरः
transliteration: sutaḥ kila sa śakrasya vāyasaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ
english: That crow, the best of the birds, was Sakra's son. And it entered speedily into the earth with the velocity of the wind,

sanskrit: वायसे त्वं कृथाः क्रूरां मतिं मतिमतां वर
transliteration: vāyase tvaṃ kṛthāḥ krūrāṃ matiṃ matimatāṃ vara
english: Thereupon, your eyes rolling with ire, you, O mighty armed hero, O foremost of the intelligent, did resolve to destroy that crow.

sanskrit: स दर्भं संस्तराद् गृह्य ब्रह्मास्त्रेण ह्ययोजयः
transliteration: sa darbhaṃ saṃstarād gṛhya brahmāstreṇa hyayojayaḥ
english: Taking a kusa off your seat you did set it on Brahma weapon. And it flamed like to the fire of desolation before that crow.

sanskrit: क्षिप्तवांस्त्वं प्रदीप्तं हि दर्भं तं वायसं प्रति
ततस्तु वायसं दीप्तः स दर्भो ऽनुजगाम ह
transliteration: kṣiptavāṃstvaṃ pradīptaṃ hi darbhaṃ taṃ vāyasaṃ prati
tatastu vāyasaṃ dīptaḥ sa darbho 'nujagāma ha
english: You did let off that burning Kuśa towards that birds. And there upon that burning Kuća followed the crow.

sanskrit: स पित्रा च परित्यक्तः सुरैश्च समहर्षिभिः
transliteration: sa pitrā ca parityaktaḥ suraiśca samaharṣibhiḥ
english: And being forsaken even by the celestials, who were terrified, and ransacking the three worlds it did not get a refuge.

sanskrit: स तं निपतितं भूमौ शरण्यः शरणागतम्
transliteration: sa taṃ nipatitaṃ bhūmau śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatam
english: Thereupon it again came to you, O subduer of foes. And seeking your shelter it laid itself low on the ground. And O Kākutstha, you didst save it albeit it was worthy of being slain.

sanskrit: मोघमस्त्रं न शक्यं तु कर्तुमित्येव राघव
भवांस्तस्याक्षि काकस्य हिनस्ति स्म स दक्षिणम्
transliteration: moghamastraṃ na śakyaṃ tu kartumityeva rāghava
bhavāṃstasyākṣi kākasya hinasti sma sa dakṣiṇam
english: And thinking if improper to baffle the aim of the weapon, you didst, O Rāghava, destroy the right eye of the crow.

sanskrit: राम त्वां स नमस्कृत्य राज्ञे दशरथाय च
transliteration: rāma tvāṃ sa namaskṛtya rājñe daśarathāya ca
english: Thereupon bowing to you and the king Dasaratha, that crow, bidding adieu, went to its quarter.
O Rāghava, you are the foremost of those skilled in the use of weapons, powerful and gifted with an excellent character, why do you not discharge weapons towards the Rākşasas?

sanskrit: न नागा नापि गन्धर्वा नासुरा न मरुद्गणाः
न च सर्वे रणे शक्ता रामं प्रतिसमासितुम्
transliteration: na nāgā nāpi gandharvā nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ
na ca sarve raṇe śaktā rāmaṃ pratisamāsitum
english: The celestials, the Gandharvas, the Asuras, the Marutas-none of them is qualified, O Rāma, to equal you in conflict.
If you, gifted with great prowess, had any armed shafts, destroy Rāvana in conflict.

sanskrit: स किमर्थं नरवरो न मां रक्षति राघवः
transliteration: sa kimarthaṃ naravaro na māṃ rakṣati rāghavaḥ
english: And obtaining the behests of his brother, why dose not Lakşmaņa, the subduer of foes and best of men, protect me, O Rāghava?
Those two best of men, gifted with the effulgence of Wind and Fire, and incapable of being repressed even by the celestials, are disregarding me.
Forsooth have I perpetrated a mighty iniquity since those two slayers of foes, being capable, do not protect me.

Hearing those sweet and piteous accents of Vaidehi I again spoke to that worshipful dame, saying. 'Forsooth can I swear by you, O worshipful dame, that Rāma is sorely stricken with grief in your absence. And Lakšmaņa too relent heavily beholding him laden with sorrow.

sanskrit: त्वच्छोकविमुखो रामो देवि सत्येन ते शपे
transliteration: tvacchokavimukho rāmo devi satyena te śape
english: Hearing those sweet and piteous accents of Vaidehi I again spoke to that worshipful dame, saying. 'Forsooth can I swear by you, O worshipful dame, that Rāma is sorely stricken with grief in your absence. And Lakšmaņa too relent heavily beholding him laden with sorrow.
It dose not behove you to relent any more as I have succeeded in finding you out. You shall at this very moment behold the end of your grief.
And those two princes, the foremost of men and slayers of foes, actuated with energy on hearing that I have seen you, shall reduce Lankā to ashes.

sanskrit: हत्वा च समरे रौद्र रावण सहबान्धवम्
राघवस्त्वां वरारोहे स्वां पुरीं नयते ध्रुवम्
transliteration: hatvā ca samare raudra rāvaṇa sahabāndhavam
rāghavastvāṃ varārohe svāṃ purīṃ nayate dhruvam
english: And slaying in conflict the terrible Rāvaņa, with his kith and kin, Rāghava, in sooth, O excellent damsel, shall take you back to his own city.
O you of a blameless person, do you confer on me such a token, as might be recognized by Ráma and conduce to his pleasure.
Thereat, casting her looks around, she took out an excellent jewel from her cloth, worthy of being set on her braid and conferred it on me, O you of great strength.

sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य मणिं दिव्यं तव हेतो रघूद्वह
transliteration: pratigṛhya maṇiṃ divyaṃ tava heto raghūdvaha
english: O you, the most favourite of the Raghu race, taking for you that gem with my hands and bowing to her, I addressed myself speedily for departure.

Thereupon beholding me ready to depart and increase in bulk and about to leap up in the welkin, Sītā, the daughter of the king Janaka, poorly, bathed in tears, overwhelmed with sorrow and having her voice choked with grief, saying 'Blessed are you O great monkey, since you shall behold the large-armed and the lotuseyed Ráma and the highly famed Lakşmaņa, my lord's younger brother.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवं च सहामात्य सर्वान् ब्रूया ह्यनामयम्
transliteration: sugrīvaṃ ca sahāmātya sarvān brūyā hyanāmayam
english: Addressing me with these words she again said-O Hanuman, do you relate my well-being to Rāma and Lakshamana of leonine prowess, and Sugrīva accompanied by his followers.

sanskrit: यथा च स महाबाहुर्मां तारयति राघवः
transliteration: yathā ca sa mahābāhurmāṃ tārayati rāghavaḥ
english: Do you so describe as the large-armed Rāghava may save me from this ocean of grief.

sanskrit: इमं च तीव्रं मम शोकवेगं रक्षोभिरेभिः परिभर्त्सनं च
ब्रूयास्तु रामस्य गतः समीपं शिवश्च ते ऽध्वा ऽस्तु हरिप्रवीर
transliteration: imaṃ ca tīvraṃ mama śokavegaṃ rakṣobhirebhiḥ paribhartsanaṃ ca
brūyāstu rāmasya gataḥ samīpaṃ śivaśca te 'dhvā 'stu haripravīra
english: Do you narrate to Rāma this my terrible sorrow and the affliction by the she-demons. May good betide you, on your way, O foremost of the monkeys.'

sanskrit: एतत्तवार्या नृपराजसिंह सीता वचः प्राह विषादपूर्वम्
एतच्च बुद्ध्वा गदितं मया त्वं श्रद्धत्स्व सीतां कुशलां समग्राम्
transliteration: etattavāryā nṛparājasiṃha sītā vacaḥ prāha viṣādapūrvam
etacca buddhvā gaditaṃ mayā tvaṃ śraddhatsva sītāṃ kuśalāṃ samagrām
english: Thus the worshipful Sítă gave vent to these piteous accents. Hearing these words do you believe that it is all well with her.
Thereupon, O foremost of men, out of your love and adoring me for your friendship, that worshipful dame-addressed me again, saying.
Do you thus speak every thing to Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, so that he might soon take me hence, slaying Ravana in battle.
O hero, O slayer of foes, if it please you, you may relieve yourself of the toil by living in a secret nook and then proceed to-morrow.
O monkey, in your company, I do momentarily forget the weight of my grief, unfortunate as I am.

sanskrit: गते हि त्वयि विक्रान्ते पुनरागमनाय वै
transliteration: gate hi tvayi vikrānte punarāgamanāya vai
english: O you gifted with great prowess, yourself departing, I shall wait for your return, but doubt I very much whether I shall live till then.
Burnt I shall be with the fear of not beholding you again, wretched and stricken with grief as I am. And so I shall be, hereafter, overwhelmed with a mightier grief.
O hero, besides, I entertain a grave doubt about your assistants, the monkeys and bears. I do not know how shall the host of monkeys and bears and those two princes cross over the mighty main?

sanskrit: कथं नु खलु दुष्पारं तरिष्यन्ति महोदधिम्
transliteration: kathaṃ nu khalu duṣpāraṃ tariṣyanti mahodadhim
english: O hero, besides, I entertain a grave doubt about your assistants, the monkeys and bears. I do not know how shall the host of monkeys and bears and those two princes cross over the mighty main?

sanskrit: शक्तिः स्याद्वैनतेयस्य तव वा मारुतस्य वा
transliteration: śaktiḥ syādvainateyasya tava vā mārutasya vā
english: O innocent monkey of all the creatures three only are qualified to cross over the ocean, yourself, Garuda and the Wind.

sanskrit: किं पश्यसि समाधानं ब्रूहि कार्यविदां वर
transliteration: kiṃ paśyasi samādhānaṃ brūhi kāryavidāṃ vara
english: O you foremost of those skilled in speech, what had you settled about the accomplishment of this hard work?
True it is that you are alone qualified to accomplish this work, you the slayer of inimical heroes-but such manifestation of your prowess shall increase your glory only.

sanskrit: विजयी स्वां पुरीं रामो नयेत्तत् स्याद्यशस्करम्
transliteration: vijayī svāṃ purīṃ rāmo nayettat syādyaśaskaram
english: But if Rāma, obtaining victory, can take me hence to his own city, it shall redound to his glory.

sanskrit: यथा ऽहं तस्य वीरस्य वनादुपधिना हृता
रक्षसा तद्भया देव तथा नार्हति राघवः
transliteration: rakṣasā tadbhayā deva tathā nārhati rāghavaḥ
english: It dose not behove the heroic Rāghava, to take me away by steal, like to Rāvaņa capturing me from the forest under a disguise.
Truly it shall be his becoming work, if Kākutstha, the repressor of enemy's host, can take me away, enveloping the city Lankā with his army.
Do you therefore initiate that work as become that high-souled hero and may display his prowess.
Hearing these sound reasonable and affectionate words I gave her the last reply, saying.
O worshipful dame, Sugrīva, the foremost of the monkeys, the lord of monkey and bear hosts and gifted with manliness, has resolved upon rescuing you.
He has under his command a number of mighty and courageous monkeys gifted with great prowess and quick-coursing like imagination.

sanskrit: येषां नोपरि नाधस्तान्न तिर्यक् सज्जते गतिः
transliteration: yeṣāṃ nopari nādhastānna tiryak sajjate gatiḥ
english: Their course is never thwarted-whether going upwards or downwardsor moving tortuously. They are never exhausted in their actions—highly courageous and of measureless prowess.
And those great and powerful monkeys, coursing in the air, have again and again circumambulated the earth.
Sugriva has many monkeys-my equal-and greater than I but none of inferior strength.

sanskrit: अहं तावदिह प्राप्तः किं पुनस्ते महाबलाः
न हि प्रकृष्टाः प्रेष्यन्ते प्रेष्यन्ते हीतरे जनाः
transliteration: ahaṃ tāvadiha prāptaḥ kiṃ punaste mahābalāḥ
na hi prakṛṣṭāḥ preṣyante preṣyante hītare janāḥ
english: While I have crossed over the main-what of these mighty heroes? The leading heroes are never sent on a mission but only those of inferior merit.
No more of bewailing, O worshipful dame. Do you remove your grief. And with one leap these leaders of monkey-hosts shall reach Lankā.
O great damsel, these two princes, placing themselves on my back shall come to you like to the rising Sun and Moon.
You shall soon behold before Lanka's gate Rāghava the slayer of foes resembling a lion and Lakşmana with a bow in his hand.
You shall soon observe in a band the heroic monkeys, gifted with the strength of lions and tigers, and having nails and teeth for their weapons.
You shall soon bear the roaring of the leading monkeys on the summit of mount Malaya, resembling the muttering of the clouds.
You shall soon behold Rāghava, the slayer of foes, installed along with you on the throne of Ayodhya after returning from the forest.

sanskrit: जगाम शान्तिं मम मैथिलात्मजा तवापि शोकेन तदा ऽभिपीडिता
transliteration: jagāma śāntiṃ mama maithilātmajā tavāpi śokena tadā 'bhipīḍitā
english: That daughter of the king of Mithilā although heavily laden with sorrow in your absence was greatly comforted and pleased by my auspicious words boding the fulfilment of her desire.
Hearing the words of Hanumän rehearsed properly, Rāma, exceedingly delighted, said.
By Hanumān has been performed a very great deed, rare on earth, and one incapable of being even conceived by any other in the world.

sanskrit: न हि तम् परिपश्यामि यस्तरेत महोदधिम्
transliteration: na hi tam paripaśyāmi yastareta mahodadhim
english: Save Garuda and the Wind-god, and save also Hanumān, him find I not who cross the wide ocean.

Entering by main force the city of Larkā, incapable of being subjugated by the gods and Dänavas and Yaksas, the Gandharvas, serpents or Raksasas, and well protected by Ravana, who, living, come out (of it)?

sanskrit: एवम् विधाय स्वबलम् सदृशम् विक्रमस्य च
यो हि भृत्यो नियुक्तः सन् भर्त्रा कर्मणि दुष्करे
transliteration: evam vidhāya svabalam sadṛśam vikramasya ca
yo hi bhṛtyo niyuktaḥ san bhartrā karmaṇi duṣkare

sanskrit: यो नियुक्तः परम् कार्यम् न कुर्यान्नऋपतेः प्रियम्
transliteration: yo niyuktaḥ param kāryam na kuryānnaṛpateḥ priyam

sanskrit: नियुक्तो नृपतेः कार्यम् न कुर्याद्यः समाहितः
transliteration: niyukto nṛpateḥ kāryam na kuryādyaḥ samāhitaḥ

sanskrit: न चात्मा लघताम् नीतः सुग्रीवश्चापि तोषितः
transliteration: na cātmā laghatām nītaḥ sugrīvaścāpi toṣitaḥ

sanskrit: इदम् तु मम दीनस्य मनो भूयः प्रकर्षति
transliteration: idam tu mama dīnasya mano bhūyaḥ prakarṣati

sanskrit: सागरम् तु समासाद्य पुनर्नष्टम् मनो मम
transliteration: sāgaram tu samāsādya punarnaṣṭam mano mama

sanskrit: यद्यप्येष तु वृत्तान्तो वैदेह्या गदितो मम
transliteration: yadyapyeṣa tu vṛttānto vaidehyā gadito mama

english: Then the graceful Sugrīva spoke words capable of soothing sorrow, to Dasaratha's son, Rāma, who was wrought up with grief.

sanskrit: किम् त्वया तप्यते वीर यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा
मैवम् भूस्त्यज सतापम् कृतघ्न इव सौहृदम्
transliteration: kim tvayā tapyate vīra yathānyaḥ prākṛtastathā
maivam bhūstyaja satāpam kṛtaghna iva sauhṛdam
english: Why, O hero, does you grieve, like one that is base? Let not this be so. Chase away you grief, even as an ingrate resign amity.

sanskrit: सम्तापस्य च ते स्थानम् न हि पश्यामि राघव
transliteration: samtāpasya ca te sthānam na hi paśyāmi rāghava
english: Nor, O Rāghava, when the whereabouts of Sītă has been discovered, and when too the abode itself of the foe has been known, do I perceive the reason of your sorrow.

You, O Raghava, are intelligent, conversant with learning, wise, and judicious. Do you cast away this sorry way of thinking, even as a selfcontrolled (ascetic) caste away any course of thought interfering with the attainment of his purpose.
Crossing over the ocean swarming with gigantic alligators, we shall enter Lankā and slay the enemy.
Of a person that is dispirited and poor in pluck and that has his soul overwhelmed with grief, every interest droops, and he comes by misfortunes (one after another).
All these heroes, these leaders of monkeyhordes, who are ardent for they welfare, are competent to enter into fire itself. From their cheerful attitude I know this, and firm is my faith.

sanskrit: एषाम् हर्षेण जानामि तर्कश्चापि दृढो मम
विक्रमेण समानेष्ये सीताम् हत्वा यथा रिपुम्
transliteration: eṣām harṣeṇa jānāmi tarkaścāpi dṛḍho mama
vikrameṇa samāneṣye sītām hatvā yathā ripum

sanskrit: सेतुरत्र यथा बद्ध्येथा पश्येम ताम् पुरीम्
transliteration: seturatra yathā baddhyethā paśyema tām purīm

sanskrit: तस्य राक्षसराजस्य तथा त्वम् कुरु राघव
दृष्ट्वा ताम् हि पुरीम् लङ्काम् त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिताम्
transliteration: tasya rākṣasarājasya tathā tvam kuru rāghava
dṛṣṭvā tām hi purīm laṅkām trikūṭaśikhare sthitām

sanskrit: अबद्ध्वा सागरे सेतुम् घोरे च वरुणालये
transliteration: abaddhvā sāgare setum ghore ca varuṇālaye

sanskrit: लङ्का न मर्दितुम् शक्या सेन्द्रैरपि सुरासुरैः
transliteration: laṅkā na marditum śakyā sendrairapi surāsuraiḥ

sanskrit: सर्वम् तीर्णम् च मे सैन्यम् जितमित्युपधारय
इमे हि समरे वीरा हरयः कामरूपिणः
transliteration: sarvam tīrṇam ca me sainyam jitamityupadhāraya
ime hi samare vīrā harayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ

english: When the bridge over the ocean has been constructed up to near Laňkä, and when my forces have crossed (over the sea), consider victory as secured. As these monkeys are heroic in fight, and able to wear forms at will, O king, do not let your intellect get stupefied and thus mar all interests. In this world, sorrow berefts people of their prowess.
Do you do even what should be done by a man-summon your manliness; for what an actor does promptly, conduce to his success.

sanskrit: अस्मिन् काले महाप्राज्ञ् सत्त्वमातिष्ठ ते जसा
transliteration: asmin kāle mahāprājñ sattvamātiṣṭha te jasā
english: At this time, O eminently wise one, do you realise goodness through they energy.* Of heroic, high-souled, men like yourself, on their sustaining and entire or a partial loss, grief undo every interest. *i.e. as I understand this rather obscure passage, prove the good through your vigour-secure victory to the cause of goodness through they might.

sanskrit: न हि पश्याम्यहम् कम् चित्त्रिषु लोकेषु राघव
transliteration: na hi paśyāmyaham kam cittriṣu lokeṣu rāghava

sanskrit: वानरेषु समासक्तम् न ते कार्यम् विपत्स्यते
transliteration: vānareṣu samāsaktam na te kāryam vipatsyate

sanskrit: निश्चेष्टाह् क्षत्रिया मन्दाः सर्वे चण्डस्य् बिभ्यति
transliteration: niśceṣṭāh kṣatriyā mandāḥ sarve caṇḍasy bibhyati
english: Therefore, O king, renounce your sorrow, and call up wrath. Those Ksatriyas that conceive no anger in respect of their enemies, have their activity annulled; and all fear furious persons.

sanskrit: सर्वम् तीर्णम् च मे सैन्यम् जितमित्यवधार्यताम्
इमे हि हरयः शूराः समरे कामरूपिणः
transliteration: sarvam tīrṇam ca me sainyam jitamityavadhāryatām
ime hi harayaḥ śūrāḥ samare kāmarūpiṇaḥ

sanskrit: किमुक्त्वा बहुधा चापि सर्वथा विजया भवान्
transliteration: kimuktvā bahudhā cāpi sarvathā vijayā bhavān

sanskrit: सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हेतुमत् परम अर्थवित्
transliteration: sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā hetumat parama arthavit
english: Hearing Sugrīva's speech, reasonable and fraught with high sense, Kākutstha accorded his assent to it and spoke to Hanumān, saying.

sanskrit: तरसा सेतु बन्धेन सागर उच्चोषणेन वा
सर्वथा सुसमर्थो अस्मि सागरस्य अस्य लन्घने
transliteration: tarasā setu bandhena sāgara uccoṣaṇena vā
sarvathā susamartho asmi sāgarasya asya langhane
english: By asceticism, or constructing a bridge, or drying up the ocean, competent every way am I for crossing over this ocean.

sanskrit: कति दुर्गाणि दुर्गाया लंकायास् तद् ब्रवीहि मे
ज्ञातुम् इच्चामि तत् सर्वम् दर्शनाद् इव वानर
transliteration: kati durgāṇi durgāyā laṃkāyās tad bravīhi me
jñātum iccāmi tat sarvam darśanād iva vānara
english: Of impracticable places, tell me how many there are in (Lankā), which are incapable of being come at.

sanskrit: बलस्य परिमाणम् च द्वार दुर्ग क्रियाम् अपि
गुप्ति कर्म च लंकाया रक्षसाम् सदनानि च
transliteration: balasya parimāṇam ca dvāra durga kriyām api
gupti karma ca laṃkāyā rakṣasām sadanāni ca
english: O monkey, as you have seen personally, I wish to get acquainted with all this. And you have at your leisure duly noticed in Lankā the nur.ber of the army, the inaccessibility (or otherwise) of the gates, the defence of Lankā, and the dwellings of the Rākşasas. Do you faithfully relate this to me, for you are observant.

sanskrit: यथा सुखम् यथावच् च लंकायाम् असि दृष्टवान्
सरम् आचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन सर्वथा कुशलो हि असि
transliteration: yathā sukham yathāvac ca laṃkāyām asi dṛṣṭavān
saram ācakṣva tattvena sarvathā kuśalo hi asi
english: O monkey, as you have seen personally, I wish to get acquainted with all this. And you have at your leisure duly noticed in Lankā the nur.ber of the army, the inaccessibility (or otherwise) of the gates, the defence of Lankā, and the dwellings of the Rākşasas. Do you faithfully relate this to me, for you are observant.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा रामस्य वचनम् हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः
वाक्यम् वाक्यविदाम् श्रेष्ठो रामम् पुनर् अथ अब्रवीत्
transliteration: śrutvā rāmasya vacanam hanūmān māruta ātmajaḥ
vākyam vākyavidām śreṣṭho rāmam punar atha abravīt

sanskrit: श्रूयताम् सर्वम् आख्यास्ये दुर्ग कर्म विधानतः
गुप्ता पुरी यथा लंका रक्षिता च यथा बलैः
transliteration: śrūyatām sarvam ākhyāsye durga karma vidhānataḥ
guptā purī yathā laṃkā rakṣitā ca yathā balaiḥ

sanskrit: राक्षसाश्च यथा स्निग्धा रावणस्य च तेजसा
पराम् समृद्धिम् लंकायाः सागरस्य च भीमताम्
transliteration: rākṣasāśca yathā snigdhā rāvaṇasya ca tejasā
parām samṛddhim laṃkāyāḥ sāgarasya ca bhīmatām

sanskrit: विभागम् च बल ओघस्य निर्देशम् वाहनस्य च
transliteration: vibhāgam ca bala oghasya nirdeśam vāhanasya ca

sanskrit: प्रहृष्टा मुदिता लंका मत्त द्विप समाकुला
महती रथ सम्पूर्णा रक्षो गण समाकुला
transliteration: prahṛṣṭā muditā laṃkā matta dvipa samākulā
mahatī ratha sampūrṇā rakṣo gaṇa samākulā
english: Lankā, filled with mad elephants, ever rejoice. She is great, thronging with cars and inhabited by Raksasas.
Her doors are firmly established and furnished with massy bolts. And she has four wide and giant gates.

sanskrit: आगतम् पर सैन्यम् तैस् तत्र प्रतिनिवार्यते
transliteration: āgatam para sainyam tais tatra pratinivāryate
english: (At those gates) are powerful and large arms, stones, and engines, whereby a hostile host approaching, is opposed.

sanskrit: द्वारेषु सम्स्कृता भीमाः काल आयस मयाः शिताः
शतशो रोचिता वीरैः शतघ्न्यो रक्षसाम् गणैः
transliteration: dvāreṣu samskṛtā bhīmāḥ kāla āyasa mayāḥ śitāḥ
śataśo rocitā vīraiḥ śataghnyo rakṣasām gaṇaiḥ
english: At the entrances are arrayed and set in order by bands of heroic Rākşasas, hundreds of dreadful sharp iron sataghnis.* *A kind of fire-arms, or ancient Hindu rocket; or a stone set round with sharp iron spikes. According to Rāmānuja, a sort of mace about two yards in length, with spikes.

sanskrit: सौवर्णः च महाम्स् तस्याः प्राकारो दुष्प्रधर्षणः
मणि विद्रुम वैदूर्य मुक्ता विचरित अन्तरः
transliteration: sauvarṇaḥ ca mahāms tasyāḥ prākāro duṣpradharṣaṇaḥ
maṇi vidruma vaidūrya muktā vicarita antaraḥ
english: She has a mighty impassable golden wall, having its side emblazoned in the centre with costly stones, coral, lapises and pearls.

sanskrit: सर्वतः च महाभीमाः शीत तोया महाशुभाः
अगाधा ग्राहवत्यः च परिखा मीन सेविताः
transliteration: sarvataḥ ca mahābhīmāḥ śīta toyā mahāśubhāḥ
agādhā grāhavatyaḥ ca parikhā mīna sevitāḥ
english: Round about is a moat, exceedingly dreadful, with cool water, eminently grand, fathomless, containing ferocious aquatic animals, and inhabited by fishes.

sanskrit: द्वारेषु तासाम् चत्वारः सम्क्रमाः परम आयताः
यन्त्रैर् उपेता बहुभिर् महद्भिर् दृढ सम्धिभिः
transliteration: dvāreṣu tāsām catvāraḥ samkramāḥ parama āyatāḥ
yantrair upetā bahubhir mahadbhir dṛḍha samdhibhiḥ
english: At the gates are four broad bridges, furnished with machines and many rows of grand structures.

sanskrit: त्रायन्ते सम्क्रमास् तत्र पर सैन्य आगमे सति
transliteration: trāyante samkramās tatra para sainya āgame sati
english: On the approach of hostile forces, their attack is repulsed by these machines, and they are thrown into the ditch.

sanskrit: एकस् त्व् अकम्प्यो बलवान् सम्क्रमः सुमहादृढः
काञ्चनैर् बहुभिः स्तम्भैर् वेदिकाभिः च शोभितः
transliteration: ekas tv akampyo balavān samkramaḥ sumahādṛḍhaḥ
kāñcanair bahubhiḥ stambhair vedikābhiḥ ca śobhitaḥ
english: One among these bridges is immovable, strong and fast established; adorned with golden pillars and daises.

sanskrit: स्वयम् प्रकृति सम्पन्नो युयुत्सू राम रावणः
उत्थितः च अप्रमत्तः च बलानाम् अनुदर्शने
transliteration: svayam prakṛti sampanno yuyutsū rāma rāvaṇaḥ
utthitaḥ ca apramattaḥ ca balānām anudarśane
english: O Rāma, albeit Rāvaņa hunger for fight, yet is he calm; and he is vigilant and ever engaged in superintending his army.

sanskrit: लंका पुरी निरालम्बा देव दुर्गा भय आवहा
न अदेयम् पार्वतम् वन्यम् कृत्रिमम् च चतुर् विधम्
transliteration: laṃkā purī nirālambā deva durgā bhaya āvahā
na adeyam pārvatam vanyam kṛtrimam ca catur vidham
english: And dreadful and resembling a celestial citadel, Lankā cannot be ascended by means of any support. She has fortresses composed of streams, those of hills, and artificial ones of four kinds.

sanskrit: स्थिता पारे समुद्रस्य दूर पारस्य राघव
नौ पथः च अपि न अस्ति अत्र निरादेशः च सर्वतः
transliteration: sthitā pāre samudrasya dūra pārasya rāghava
nau pathaḥ ca api na asti atra nirādeśaḥ ca sarvataḥ
english: O Rāghava, she is situated on the other shore of the ocean having its limit far away. And way there is none even for barks, and all sides are destitute of division.

sanskrit: शैल अग्रे रचिता दुर्गा सा पूर् देव पुर उपमा
वाजि वारण सम्पूर्णा लंका परम दुर्जया
transliteration: śaila agre racitā durgā sā pūr deva pura upamā
vāji vāraṇa sampūrṇā laṃkā parama durjayā
english: That citadel is built on the mountain's brow; and, resembling the metropolis of the immortals, the exceedingly invincible Larkā is filled with horses and elephants.

sanskrit: परिघाः च शतघ्न्यः च यन्त्राणि विविधानि च
transliteration: parighāḥ ca śataghnyaḥ ca yantrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: And a moat and sataghnís and various engines adorn the city of Lankā, belonging to the wicked Rāvana.

sanskrit: अयुतम् रक्षसाम् अत्र पश्चिम द्वारम् आश्रितम्
शूल हस्ता दुराधर्षाः सर्वे खड्ग अग्र योधिनः
transliteration: ayutam rakṣasām atra paścima dvāram āśritam
śūla hastā durādharṣāḥ sarve khaḍga agra yodhinaḥ
english: And an ayuta of Raksasas, dart-handed, hard to subdue, and all fighting at the front with their swords-protect the Eastern gate.

sanskrit: नियुतम् रक्षसाम् अत्र दक्षिण द्वारम् आश्रितम्
चतुर् अन्गेण सैन्येन योधास् तत्र अपि अनुत्तमाः
transliteration: niyutam rakṣasām atra dakṣiṇa dvāram āśritam
catur angeṇa sainyena yodhās tatra api anuttamāḥ
english: And a lac of Rākşasas with a fourfold force, and with the flower of the soldiery-protect the Southern gate.

sanskrit: प्रयुतम् रक्षसाम् अत्र पूर्व द्वारम् समाश्रितम्
चर्म खड्ग धराः सर्वे तथा सर्व अस्त्र कोविदाः
transliteration: prayutam rakṣasām atra pūrva dvāram samāśritam
carma khaḍga dharāḥ sarve tathā sarva astra kovidāḥ
english: And a prayuta of Rākṣasas, bearing swords and shields, and skilled in all arms, protect the Western gate.

sanskrit: न्यर्बुदम् रक्षसाम् अत्र उत्तर द्वारम् आश्रितम्
रथिनः च अश्व वाहाः च कुल पुत्राः सुपूजिताः
transliteration: nyarbudam rakṣasām atra uttara dvāram āśritam
rathinaḥ ca aśva vāhāḥ ca kula putrāḥ supūjitāḥ
english: And an arbuda of Rākṣasas protect the Northern gate. And car-warriors and horsemenpersons honoured and sprung from noble linesby hundreds and thousands,tand irrepressible goblins and koțis of Rākşasas, protect the garrison.

sanskrit: शतम् शत सहस्राणाम् मध्यमम् गुल्मम् आश्रितम्
यातु धाना दुराधर्षाः साग्र कोटिः च रक्षसाम्
transliteration: śatam śata sahasrāṇām madhyamam gulmam āśritam
yātu dhānā durādharṣāḥ sāgra koṭiḥ ca rakṣasām

sanskrit: ते मया सम्क्रमा भग्नाः परिखाः च अवपूरिताः
दग्धा च नगरी लंका प्राकाराः च अवसादिताः
transliteration: te mayā samkramā bhagnāḥ parikhāḥ ca avapūritāḥ
dagdhā ca nagarī laṃkā prākārāḥ ca avasāditāḥ
english: I have broken down the bridges and filled up the entrenchment. I have burnt that city of Lankā and laid the wall low.

sanskrit: येन केन तु मार्गेण तराम वरुण आलयम्
transliteration: yena kena tu mārgeṇa tarāma varuṇa ālayam

sanskrit: हता इति नगरी लंकाम् वानरैर् अवधार्यताम्
अङ्गदो द्विविदो मैन्दो जाम्बवान् पनसो नलः
transliteration: hatā iti nagarī laṃkām vānarair avadhāryatām
aṅgado dvivido maindo jāmbavān panaso nalaḥ

sanskrit: नीलः सेना पतिः चैव बल शेषेण किम् तव
प्लवमाना हि गत्वा ताम् रावणस्य महापुरीम्
transliteration: nīlaḥ senā patiḥ caiva bala śeṣeṇa kim tava
plavamānā hi gatvā tām rāvaṇasya mahāpurīm

sanskrit: एवम् आज्ञापय क्षिप्रम् बलानाम् सर्व सम्ग्रहम्
transliteration: evam ājñāpaya kṣipram balānām sarva samgraham
english: If this be so,* do you order the entire body of the army to be brought; and do you set out at the proper hour. *Ebam ajnápaya: Ramanuja reads sense into this passage. If you wishes the principal monkeys to go, bring them; if you wish the whole host to march, call it hither, and march at the auspicious moment.

sanskrit: ततो अब्रवीन् महातेजा रामः सत्य पराक्रमः
transliteration: tato abravīn mahātejā rāmaḥ satya parākramaḥ
english: Hearing Hanumăn's speech duly from the beginning, the exceedingly energetic Rāma having truth for this prowess, said.

sanskrit: याम् निवेदयसे लंकाम् पुरीम् भीमस्य रक्षसः
क्षिप्रम् एनाम् वधिष्यामि सत्यम् एतद् ब्रवीमि ते
transliteration: yām nivedayase laṃkām purīm bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ
kṣipram enām vadhiṣyāmi satyam etad bravīmi te
english: What you say 'I shall speedily destroy the city of this dreadful Raksasa,' is true, I tell you.

sanskrit: युक्तो मुहूर्तो विजयः प्राप्तो मध्यम् दिवा करः
transliteration: yukto muhūrto vijayaḥ prāpto madhyam divā karaḥ
english: Therefore, at this very moment arrange for Sugrīva's march. The Sun has attained his meridian at this proper moment, capable of conferring victory.* *The moment is named abhijit.

sanskrit: सीताम् गृत्वा तु तद्यातु क्वासौ यास्यति जीवितः
transliteration: sītām gṛtvā tu tadyātu kvāsau yāsyati jīvitaḥ
english: Let Rāvana carry away Sītā (to his own country), whither shall Ravana, living, repair? Like a dying person who has taken a deathdispelling drug and drunk ambrosia, Sītā, hearing of my preparations for war, shall inspire hope of life.

sanskrit: उत्तरा फल्गुनी हि अद्य श्वस् तु हस्तेन योक्ष्यते
transliteration: uttarā phalgunī hi adya śvas tu hastena yokṣyate

sanskrit: निमित्तानि च धन्यानि यानि प्रादुर् भवन्ति मे
transliteration: nimittāni ca dhanyāni yāni prādur bhavanti me

sanskrit: उपरिष्टाद्द् हि नयनम् स्फुरमाणम् इदम् मम
transliteration: upariṣṭādd hi nayanam sphuramāṇam idam mama

sanskrit: विजयम् समनुप्राप्तम् शम्सति इव मनो रथम्
transliteration: vijayam samanuprāptam śamsati iva mano ratham

sanskrit: अग्रे यातु बलस्य अस्य नीलो मार्गम् अवेक्षितुम्
transliteration: agre yātu balasya asya nīlo mārgam avekṣitum

sanskrit: पथा मधुमता च आशु सेनाम् सेना पते नय
transliteration: pathā madhumatā ca āśu senām senā pate naya
english: O Nīla, do you, O general, expeditiously take the army by a path furnished with fruits and roots, having cool waters of the woods, and replenished with honey.

sanskrit: फल मूलवता नील शीत कानन वारिणा
दूषयेयुर् दुरात्मानः पथि मूल फल उदकम्
transliteration: phala mūlavatā nīla śīta kānana vāriṇā
dūṣayeyur durātmānaḥ pathi mūla phala udakam

sanskrit: राक्षसाः परिरक्षेथास् तेभ्यस् त्वम् नित्यम् उद्यतः
निम्नेषु वन दुर्गेषु वनेषु च वन ओकसः
transliteration: rākṣasāḥ parirakṣethās tebhyas tvam nityam udyataḥ
nimneṣu vana durgeṣu vaneṣu ca vana okasaḥ

sanskrit: एतद्धि कृत्यम् घोरम् नो विक्रमेण प्रयुज्यताम्
सागर ओघ निभम् भीमम् अग्र अनीकम् महाबलाः
transliteration: etaddhi kṛtyam ghoram no vikrameṇa prayujyatām
sāgara ogha nibham bhīmam agra anīkam mahābalāḥ

sanskrit: कपि सिम्हा प्रकर्षन्तु शतशो अथ सहस्रशः
गजः च गिरि सम्काशो गवयः च महाबलः
transliteration: kapi simhā prakarṣantu śataśo atha sahasraśaḥ
gajaḥ ca giri samkāśo gavayaḥ ca mahābalaḥ

sanskrit: गव अक्षः च अग्रतो यान्तु गवाम् दृप्ता इव ऋषभाः
यातु वानर वाहिन्या वानरः प्लवताम् पतिः
transliteration: gava akṣaḥ ca agrato yāntu gavām dṛptā iva ṛṣabhāḥ
yātu vānara vāhinyā vānaraḥ plavatām patiḥ

sanskrit: पालयन् दक्षिणम् पार्श्वम् ऋषभो वानर ऋषभः
गन्ध हस्ती इव दुर्धर्षस् तरस्वी गन्ध मादनः
transliteration: pālayan dakṣiṇam pārśvam ṛṣabho vānara ṛṣabhaḥ
gandha hastī iva durdharṣas tarasvī gandha mādanaḥ
english: And let that foremost of monkeys, Rşabha, go, protecting the right wing (of the army); and let Gandha, irresistible like an elephant with the fragrant temporal juice trickling down, and the vehement Gandhamādana, go,* protecting the left wing (of the monkey-army). *The verb is singular, instead of dual, as also the qualifying epithet, Pārsamadishthita. But the sense is clear. on

sanskrit: यातु वानर वाहिन्याः सव्यम् पार्श्वम् अधिष्ठितः
यास्यामि बल मध्ये अहम् बल ओघम् अभिहर्षयन्
transliteration: yātu vānara vāhinyāḥ savyam pārśvam adhiṣṭhitaḥ
yāsyāmi bala madhye aham bala ogham abhiharṣayan

sanskrit: अन्गदेन एष सम्यातु लक्ष्मणः च अन्तक उपमः
transliteration: angadena eṣa samyātu lakṣmaṇaḥ ca antaka upamaḥ

sanskrit: सार्वभौमेन भूत ईशो द्रविण अधिपतिस् यथा
जाम्बवामः च सुषेणः च वेग दर्शी च वानरः
transliteration: sārvabhaumena bhūta īśo draviṇa adhipatis yathā
jāmbavāmaḥ ca suṣeṇaḥ ca vega darśī ca vānaraḥ

sanskrit: ऋक्ष राजो महासत्त्वः कुक्षिम् रक्षन्तु ते त्रयः
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो वाहिनी पतिः
transliteration: ṛkṣa rājo mahāsattvaḥ kukṣim rakṣantu te trayaḥ
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo vāhinī patiḥ

sanskrit: ते वानर गणाः सर्वे समुत्पत्य युयुत्सवः
transliteration: te vānara gaṇāḥ sarve samutpatya yuyutsavaḥ

sanskrit: गुहाभ्यः शिखरेभ्यः च आशु पुप्लुविरे तदा
ततो वानर राजेन लक्ष्मणेन च पूजितः
transliteration: guhābhyaḥ śikharebhyaḥ ca āśu pupluvire tadā
tato vānara rājena lakṣmaṇena ca pūjitaḥ

sanskrit: जगाम रामो धर्म आत्मा ससैन्यो दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
शतैः शत सहस्रैः च कोटीभिर् अयुतैर् अपि
transliteration: jagāma rāmo dharma ātmā sasainyo dakṣiṇām diśam
śataiḥ śata sahasraiḥ ca koṭībhir ayutair api

sanskrit: वारणाभिः च हरिभिर् ययौ परिव्Rतस् तदा
तम् यान्तम् अनुयाति स्म महती हरि वाहिनी
transliteration: vāraṇābhiḥ ca haribhir yayau parivtas tadā
tam yāntam anuyāti sma mahatī hari vāhinī

sanskrit: आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तः च गर्जन्तः च प्लवम् गमाः
transliteration: āplavantaḥ plavantaḥ ca garjantaḥ ca plavam gamāḥ

sanskrit: क्ष्वेलन्तो निनदन्तः च जग्मुर् वै दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
भक्षयन्तः सुगन्धीनि मधूनि च फलानि च
transliteration: kṣvelanto ninadantaḥ ca jagmur vai dakṣiṇām diśam
bhakṣayantaḥ sugandhīni madhūni ca phalāni ca

sanskrit: अन्योन्यम् सहसा दृष्टा निर्वहन्ति क्षिपन्ति च
transliteration: anyonyam sahasā dṛṣṭā nirvahanti kṣipanti ca

sanskrit: पतन्तः च उत्पतन्ति अन्ये पातयन्ति अपरे परान्
रावणो नो निहन्तव्यः सर्वे च रजनी चराः
transliteration: patantaḥ ca utpatanti anye pātayanti apare parān
rāvaṇo no nihantavyaḥ sarve ca rajanī carāḥ

sanskrit: पुरस्ताद् ऋषभ्हो वीरो नीलः कुमुद एव च
transliteration: purastād ṛṣabhho vīro nīlaḥ kumuda eva ca

sanskrit: पथानम् शोधयन्ति स्म वानरैर् बहुभिः सह
मध्ये तु राजा सुग्रीवो रामो लक्ष्मण एव च
transliteration: pathānam śodhayanti sma vānarair bahubhiḥ saha
madhye tu rājā sugrīvo rāmo lakṣmaṇa eva ca

sanskrit: बहुभिर् बलिभिर् भीमैर् व्Rताः शत्रु निबर्हणः
हरिः शत बलिर् वीरः कोटीभिर् दशभिर् वृतः
transliteration: bahubhir balibhir bhīmair vtāḥ śatru nibarhaṇaḥ
hariḥ śata balir vīraḥ koṭībhir daśabhir vṛtaḥ

sanskrit: सर्वाम् एको हि अवष्टभ्य ररक्ष हरि वाहिनीम्
कोटी शत परीवारः केसरी पनसो गजः
transliteration: sarvām eko hi avaṣṭabhya rarakṣa hari vāhinīm
koṭī śata parīvāraḥ kesarī panaso gajaḥ

sanskrit: अर्कः च अतिबलः पार्श्वम् एकम् तस्य अभिरक्षति
सुषेणो जाम्बवामः चैव ऋक्षैर् बहुभिर् आवृतः
transliteration: arkaḥ ca atibalaḥ pārśvam ekam tasya abhirakṣati
suṣeṇo jāmbavāmaḥ caiva ṛkṣair bahubhir āvṛtaḥ

sanskrit: तेषाम् सेना पतिर् वीरो नीलो वानर पुम्गवः
transliteration: teṣām senā patir vīro nīlo vānara pumgavaḥ

sanskrit: सम्पतन् पतताम् श्रेष्ठस् तद् बलम् पर्यपालयत्
transliteration: sampatan patatām śreṣṭhas tad balam paryapālayat

sanskrit: सर्वतः च ययुर् वीरास् त्वरयन्तः प्लवम् गमान्
एवम् ते हरि शार्दूला गच्चन्तो बल दर्पिताः
transliteration: sarvataḥ ca yayur vīrās tvarayantaḥ plavam gamān
evam te hari śārdūlā gaccanto bala darpitāḥ

sanskrit: अपश्यम्स् ते गिरि श्रेष्ठम् सह्यम् द्रुम लता युतम्
सागर ओघ निभम् भीमम् तद् वानर बलम् महत्
transliteration: apaśyams te giri śreṣṭham sahyam druma latā yutam
sāgara ogha nibham bhīmam tad vānara balam mahat

english: Knowing the order of Rāma of dreadful wrath, that terrible and mighty host, exceedingly terrific and resembling the bosom of the deep, cowed down through fear, leaving behind cities and villages and provinces, went like the deepsounding sea.

sanskrit: निह्ससर्प महाघोषम् भीम वेग इव अर्णवः
transliteration: nihsasarpa mahāghoṣam bhīma vega iva arṇavaḥ

sanskrit: तस्य दाशरथेः पार्श्वे शूरास् ते कपि कुन्जराः
तूर्णम् आपुप्लुवुः सर्वे सद् अश्वा इव चोदिताः
transliteration: tasya dāśaratheḥ pārśve śūrās te kapi kunjarāḥ
tūrṇam āpupluvuḥ sarve sad aśvā iva coditāḥ
english: At the side of Daſaratha's son those heroic monkeys resembling elephants, proceeded by bounds, like noble horses, spurred on.

sanskrit: कपिभ्याम् उह्यमानौ तौ शुशुभते नर ऋषभौ
महद्भ्याम् इव सम्स्पृष्टौ ग्राहाभ्याम् चन्द्र भास्करौ
transliteration: kapibhyām uhyamānau tau śuśubhate nara ṛṣabhau
mahadbhyām iva samspṛṣṭau grāhābhyām candra bhāskarau
english: Those foremost of men, mounted on the monkeys, looked beautiful like this Sun and the Moon half eclipsed by the two mighty planets, viz., Rahu and Ketu.

sanskrit: जगाम रामो धर्मात्मा ससैन्यो दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
transliteration: jagāma rāmo dharmātmā sasainyo dakṣiṇām diśam

sanskrit: तम् अन्गद गतो रामम् लक्ष्मणः शुभया गिरा
transliteration: tam angada gato rāmam lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhayā girā
english: Then Lakşmaņa, furnished with consummate sense and promptitude, who was mounted on Angada spoke to Rāma, inviting words, fraught with import.

sanskrit: हृताम् अवाप्य वैदेहीम् क्षिप्रम् हत्वा च रावणम्
समृद्ध अर्थः समृद्ध अर्थाम् अयोध्याम् प्रतियास्यसि
transliteration: hṛtām avāpya vaidehīm kṣipram hatvā ca rāvaṇam
samṛddha arthaḥ samṛddha arthām ayodhyām pratiyāsyasi
english: Speedily recovering Vaidehi, who has been carried away, and slaying Rāvana, you will, your end attained, return to Ayodhyā, who shall also have her desire. O Rāghava, I see all the great auspicious omens on earth and in the sky, signifying success to you.

sanskrit: महान्ति च निमित्तानि दिवि भूमौ च राघव
शुभान्ति तव पश्यामि सर्वाणि एव अर्थ सिद्धये
transliteration: mahānti ca nimittāni divi bhūmau ca rāghava
śubhānti tava paśyāmi sarvāṇi eva artha siddhaye
english: Speedily recovering Vaidehi, who has been carried away, and slaying Rāvana, you will, your end attained, return to Ayodhyā, who shall also have her desire. O Rāghava, I see all the great auspicious omens on earth and in the sky, signifying success to you.

sanskrit: अनु वाति शुभो वायुः सेनाम् मृदु हितः सुखः
पूर्ण वल्गु स्वराः च इमे प्रवदन्ति मृग द्विजाः
transliteration: anu vāti śubho vāyuḥ senām mṛdu hitaḥ sukhaḥ
pūrṇa valgu svarāḥ ca ime pravadanti mṛga dvijāḥ

sanskrit: प्रसन्नाः च दिशः सर्वा विमलः च दिवा करः
उशना च प्रसन्न अर्चिर् अनु त्वाम् भार्गवो गतः
transliteration: prasannāḥ ca diśaḥ sarvā vimalaḥ ca divā karaḥ
uśanā ca prasanna arcir anu tvām bhārgavo gataḥ

sanskrit: ब्रह्म राशिर् विशुद्धः च शुद्धाः च परम ऋषयः
transliteration: brahma rāśir viśuddhaḥ ca śuddhāḥ ca parama ṛṣayaḥ

sanskrit: त्रिशन्कुर् विमलो भाति राज ऋषिः सपुरोहितः
transliteration: triśankur vimalo bhāti rāja ṛṣiḥ sapurohitaḥ

english: And before us shine the grandfather of the high-souled Ikşavākus; the spotless Rājarși Trisaiku, with his priest.-And stainless and free from disturbances appear Visākhā. This is the racial star of us, the high-souled Ikșwākus.

sanskrit: मूलम् मूलवता स्प्Rष्टम् धूप्यते धूम केतुना
transliteration: mūlam mūlavatā spṣṭam dhūpyate dhūma ketunā

sanskrit: काले काल गृहीतानाम् नकत्रम् ग्रह पीडितम्
सरम् च एतद् विनाशाय राक्षसानाम् उपस्थितम्
transliteration: kāle kāla gṛhītānām nakatram graha pīḍitam
saram ca etad vināśāya rākṣasānām upasthitam

sanskrit: प्रसन्नाः सुरसाः च आपो वनानि फलवन्ति च
प्रवान्ति अभ्यधिकम् गन्धा यथा ऋतु कुसुमा द्रुमाः
transliteration: prasannāḥ surasāḥ ca āpo vanāni phalavanti ca
pravānti abhyadhikam gandhā yathā ṛtu kusumā drumāḥ
english: The water is dear and tastes sweet; and the woods are stocked with fruit. And the odorous gale does not blow strongly; and the trees are furnished with all blossoms of the season.

sanskrit: व्यूढानि कपि सैन्यानि प्रकाशन्ते अधिकम् प्रभो
transliteration: vyūḍhāni kapi sainyāni prakāśante adhikam prabho
english: O lord, this host of monkeys appear splendid to the height, as did the celestial host on the occasion of the destruction of Tāraka. Seeing all this, you should, O noble one, feel delighted.

sanskrit: एवम् आर्य समीक्ष्य एतान् प्रीतो भवितुम् अर्हसि
इति भ्रातरम् आश्वास्य हृष्टः सौमित्रिर् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: evam ārya samīkṣya etān prīto bhavitum arhasi
iti bhrātaram āśvāsya hṛṣṭaḥ saumitrir abravīt

sanskrit: अथ आव्Rत्य महीम् कृत्स्नाम् जगाम महती चमूः
ऋक्ष वानर शार्दूलैर् नख दम्ष्ट्र आयुधैर् वृता
transliteration: atha āvtya mahīm kṛtsnām jagāma mahatī camūḥ
ṛkṣa vānara śārdūlair nakha damṣṭra āyudhair vṛtā

sanskrit: कर अग्रैः चरण अग्रैः च वानरैर् उद्धतम् रजः
भीमम् अन्तर् दधे लोकम् निवार्य सवितुः प्रभाम्
transliteration: kara agraiḥ caraṇa agraiḥ ca vānarair uddhatam rajaḥ
bhīmam antar dadhe lokam nivārya savituḥ prabhām
english: The mighty dust raised by bears, monkeys, and tigers, having for their weapons nails and teeth, with the foreparts of their feet and hands, enveloped the world, and the splendour of the sun was obscured.

sanskrit: सा स्म याति दिवा रात्रम् महती हरि वाहिनी
transliteration: sā sma yāti divā rātram mahatī hari vāhinī

english: As they marched covering many a yojana, the streams seemed as if they flowed in an opposite direction.* *Kataka remark-"As when clouds, drift past, the Moon it is that seems to send accross the sky, as the monkey-army marched on, the rivers seemed to flow in an opposite direction.” Rāmānuja says that the waters of the streams dashed by the monkeys, held an opposite course. The former interpretation is hardly satisfactory, and Rāmānuja seems to be right.

They while proceeding, took rest by pools of clear water, on mountains covered with trees, on plains and in forests teeming with fruits. Some moving straight, some moving askance, and some moving on the earth, that enormous monkey-host went on covering the entire earth.

sanskrit: मध्येन च समन्ताच्च वनानि फलवन्ति च
समावृत्य महीम् कृत्स्नाम् जगाम महती चमूः
transliteration: madhyena ca samantācca vanāni phalavanti ca
samāvṛtya mahīm kṛtsnām jagāma mahatī camūḥ

english: They were all of delighted countenances and gifted with the velocity of the wind. And these monkeys devoted all their energy to the accomplishment of Rāghava's work.
They were displaying to each other their joy, prowess and energy. And influenced with the vanity of youth they set up diverse cries.
Some proceeded with speed, some leaped, some set up cries expressing joy, some were uplifting their tails, and some were striking the ground with their feet.
Some began to make terrible sounds, and other made a tingling noise. And many others blasted the creepers with the velocity of their thighs.
Some were engaged in sporting with trees and rocks. And thus was the earth enveloped with millions and koțis of fearful monkeys.

sanskrit: सा स्म याति दिवारात्रम् महती हरिवाहिनी
transliteration: sā sma yāti divārātram mahatī harivāhinī

sanskrit: वनरास् त्वरितम् यान्ति सर्वे युद्ध अभिनन्दनः
मुमोक्षयिषवः सीताम् मुहूर्तम् क्व अपि न आसत
transliteration: vanarās tvaritam yānti sarve yuddha abhinandanaḥ
mumokṣayiṣavaḥ sītām muhūrtam kva api na āsata
english: Thus the enormous monkey host went on day and night. And all those monkeys, delighted, guided by Sugrīva, and taking delight in battle, went on speedily. And they did not take rest even for a moment, desirous of rescuing Sītā.

sanskrit: ततः पादप सम्बाधम् नाना मृग समाकुलम्
सह्य पर्वतम् आसेदुर् मलयम् च मही धरम्
transliteration: tataḥ pādapa sambādham nānā mṛga samākulam
sahya parvatam āsedur malayam ca mahī dharam
english: Thereupon, getting at the mount Sahya covered with various trees and forests, those monkeys ascended it.

sanskrit: पश्यन्न् अपि ययौ रामः सह्यस्य मलयस्य च
transliteration: paśyann api yayau rāmaḥ sahyasya malayasya ca
english: Rāma went on beholding the variegated forest, rivers and fountains of the mount Sahya and Malaya.

sanskrit: चम्पकाम्स् तिलकामः चूतान् अशोकान् सिन्दु वारकान्
तिनिशान् करवीरामः च तिमिशान् भन्जन्ति स्म प्लवम् गमाः
transliteration: campakāms tilakāmaḥ cūtān aśokān sindu vārakān
tiniśān karavīrāmaḥ ca timiśān bhanjanti sma plavam gamāḥ
english: Those monkeys broke down various treesCampakas, Tilakas, mangoes, Prasekas, Sinduvaras, Tinisas and Karaviras, Asokas, Karanjas, Plaksas, Nyagrodhas, Jambukas and Amalakas.
Those monkeys broke down various treesCampakas, Tilakas, mangoes, Prasekas, Sinduvaras, Tinisas and Karaviras, Asokas, Karanjas, Plaksas, Nyagrodhas, Jambukas and Amalakas.
And seated on picturesque rocks, various forest trees, shaken by the wind, showered flowers on them.
There blew in those forests filled with the smell of honey, a wind of pleasant touch, cool as the Moon, accompanied by the hummings of the bees.
That mount was richly embellished with diverse metals. And dust issuing from these metals and thickened by the air, enveloped on all sides the huge monkey-host.

There blossomed in that picturesque mountain-vale Ketakis, Sinduvāras, beautiful Vasantis, Madhavis, Gandhapurnas, Kundas, Cirivilvas, Madhūkas, Vañjulas, Bakulas, Ranjakas, Tilakas, Nagas, mangoes, Patalikas, Kovidāras, Muculindas, Arjunas, “insapas, Kutajas, Hintālas, Tinisas, Curnakas, Nipakas, Nila-asokas, Saralas, Ankolas and lotuses.

sanskrit: हिन्तालास्तिनिशाश्चैव चूर्णका नीपकास्तथा नीलाशोकाश्च सरला अङ्कोलाः पद्मकास्तथा
transliteration: hintālāstiniśāścaiva cūrṇakā nīpakāstathā nīlāśokāśca saralā aṅkolāḥ padmakāstathā

sanskrit: व्यास्तिस्मिन् गिरौ रम्याः पल्वलानि तथैव च
transliteration: vyāstismin girau ramyāḥ palvalāni tathaiva ca

sanskrit: फलानि अमृत गन्धीनि मूलानि कुसुमानि च
बुभुजुर् वानरास् तत्र पादपानाम् बल उत्कटाः
transliteration: phalāni amṛta gandhīni mūlāni kusumāni ca
bubhujur vānarās tatra pādapānām bala utkaṭāḥ

sanskrit: ययुः पिबन्तो हृष्टास् ते मधूनि मधु पिन्गलाः
transliteration: yayuḥ pibanto hṛṣṭās te madhūni madhu pingalāḥ

sanskrit: विधमन्तो गिरि वरान् प्रययुः प्लवग ऋषभाः
transliteration: vidhamanto giri varān prayayuḥ plavaga ṛṣabhāḥ

sanskrit: वृक्षेभ्यो अन्ये तु कपयो नर्दन्तो मधु दर्पिताः
अन्ये वृक्षान् प्रपद्यन्ते प्रपतन्ति अपि च अपरे
transliteration: vṛkṣebhyo anye tu kapayo nardanto madhu darpitāḥ
anye vṛkṣān prapadyante prapatanti api ca apare

sanskrit: बभूव वसुधा तैस् तु सम्पूर्णा हरि पुम्गवैः
यथा कमल केदारैः पक्वैर् इव वसुम् धरा
transliteration: babhūva vasudhā tais tu sampūrṇā hari pumgavaiḥ
yathā kamala kedāraiḥ pakvair iva vasum dharā

sanskrit: महाइन्द्रम् अथ सम्प्राप्य रामो राजीव लोचनः
transliteration: mahāindram atha samprāpya rāmo rājīva locanaḥ
english: And reaching the mount Mahendra, the largearmed Rāma, having eyes like lotuses, ascended the summit adorned with diverse trees.

sanskrit: ततः शिखरम् आरुह्य रामो दशरथ आत्मजः
कूर्म मीन समाकीर्णम् अपश्यत् सलिल आशयम्
transliteration: tataḥ śikharam āruhya rāmo daśaratha ātmajaḥ
kūrma mīna samākīrṇam apaśyat salila āśayam
english: Getting at the top, Daśaratha's son espied the vast deep filled with tortoises and fishes.

sanskrit: ते सह्यम् समतिक्रम्य मलयम् च महागिरिम्
transliteration: te sahyam samatikramya malayam ca mahāgirim
english: There upon, passing by the mounts Sahya and Malaya and arranging their enormous host, they* by and by reached the roaring deep. *The monkey leader.

sanskrit: अवरुह्य जगाम आशु वेला वनम् अनुत्तमम्
transliteration: avaruhya jagāma āśu velā vanam anuttamam
english: And descending therefore, Rāma, the foremost of those who minister happiness to all, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva, entered the forest situate on the banks of the ocean.

sanskrit: अथ धौत उपल तलाम् तोय ओघैः सहसा उत्थितैः
वेलाम् आसाद्य विपुलाम् रामो वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: atha dhauta upala talām toya oghaiḥ sahasā utthitaiḥ
velām āsādya vipulām rāmo vacanam abravīt
english: Reaching the expansive banks having rocks there on and continually washed by the rising billow, Rāma spoke these words.

sanskrit: एते वयम् अनुप्राप्ताः सुग्रीव वरुण आलयम्
इह इदानीम् विचिन्ता सा या न पूर्वम् समुत्थिता
transliteration: ete vayam anuprāptāḥ sugrīva varuṇa ālayam
iha idānīm vicintā sā yā na pūrvam samutthitā
english: O Sugrīva we have arrived at the abode of Varuņa. Now has arisen in my mind what I had not thought of before.

sanskrit: अतः परम् अतीरो अयम् सागरः सरिताम् पति
न च अयम् अनुपायेन शक्यस् तरितुम् अर्णवः
transliteration: ataḥ param atīro ayam sāgaraḥ saritām pati
na ca ayam anupāyena śakyas taritum arṇavaḥ
english: This ocean, the lord of the streams, whose other side is not seen, cannot be crossed over without some excellent measure.

sanskrit: तद् इह एव निवेशो अस्तु मन्त्रः प्रस्तूयताम् इह
यथा इदम् वानर बलम् परम् पारम् अवाप्नुयात्
transliteration: tad iha eva niveśo astu mantraḥ prastūyatām iha
yathā idam vānara balam param pāram avāpnuyāt
english: Let the monkey-host be encamped here therefore, and then concert a plan by means of which they might get at the other side.

sanskrit: इति इव स महाबाहुः सीता हरण कर्शितः
रामः सागरम् आसाद्य वासम् आज्ञापयत् तदा
transliteration: iti iva sa mahābāhuḥ sītā haraṇa karśitaḥ
rāmaḥ sāgaram āsādya vāsam ājñāpayat tadā
english: And reaching the shores of the ocean, the large-armed Rāma, stricken with grief for Sītā, ordered their encampment, saying.

sanskrit: सम्प्राप्तो मन्त्र कालो नः सागरस्य इह लन्घने
transliteration: samprāpto mantra kālo naḥ sāgarasya iha langhane
english: O foremost of monkeys, do you encamp your host on the bring of the ocean. Now has arrived the hour for counsel, when we should devise some plan for crossing over the main.

sanskrit: स्वाम् स्वाम् सेनाम् समुत्स्Rज्य मा च कश्चित् कुतो व्रजेत्
गच्चन्तु वानराः शूरा ज्ञेयम् चन्नम् भयम् च नः
transliteration: svām svām senām samutsjya mā ca kaścit kuto vrajet
gaccantu vānarāḥ śūrā jñeyam cannam bhayam ca naḥ
english: I fear the Rākşasas at every step, for they are greatly illusion creating, let the leaders therefore go to their own hosts and let them not proceed anywhere else, renouncing them.

sanskrit: रामस्य वचनम् श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवः सह लक्ष्मणः
सेनाम् न्यवेशयत् तीरे सागरस्य द्रुम आयुते
transliteration: rāmasya vacanam śrutvā sugrīvaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
senām nyaveśayat tīre sāgarasya druma āyute
english: Hearing the words of Rama, Sugrīva along with Lakşmana, encamped the army on the brink of the ocean, covered with trees.

sanskrit: विरराज समीपस्थम् सागरस्य तु तद् बलम्
मधु पाण्डु जलः श्रीमान् द्वितीय इव सागरः
transliteration: virarāja samīpastham sāgarasya tu tad balam
madhu pāṇḍu jalaḥ śrīmān dvitīya iva sāgaraḥ
english: Stationed near the main, the monkey-host in consequence of their resemblance in colour with blue contents of the deep, looked like a second ocean.

sanskrit: वेला वनम् उपागम्य ततस् ते हरि पुम्गवाः
transliteration: velā vanam upāgamya tatas te hari pumgavāḥ
english: There upon, reaching the shore, those leading monkeys engaged in concerning a plan to cross over the vastly deep.
The tumult, of that monkey-host encamped there, was heard above the roaring of the deep.

sanskrit: सा महाअर्णवम् आसाद्य ह्Rष्टा वानर वाहिनी
transliteration: sā mahāarṇavam āsādya hṣṭā vānara vāhinī

english: And reaching the shore of the vastly deep, that monkey host, delighted, beheld the ocean moved by the Wind.

sanskrit: दूर पारम् असम्बाधम् रक्षो गण निषेवितम्
पश्यन्तो वरुण आवासम् निषेदुर् हरि यूथपाः
transliteration: dūra pāram asambādham rakṣo gaṇa niṣevitam
paśyanto varuṇa āvāsam niṣedur hari yūthapāḥ

sanskrit: चण्ड नक्र ग्रहम् घोरम् क्षपा आदौ दिवस क्षये
transliteration: caṇḍa nakra graham ghoram kṣapā ādau divasa kṣaye

sanskrit: चण्ड अनिल महाग्राहैः कीर्णम् तिमि तिमिम्गिलैः
transliteration: caṇḍa anila mahāgrāhaiḥ kīrṇam timi timimgilaiḥ

sanskrit: दीप्त भोगैर् इव आक्रीर्णम् भुजम्गैर् वरुण आलयम्
transliteration: dīpta bhogair iva ākrīrṇam bhujamgair varuṇa ālayam

sanskrit: सुदुर्गम् द्रुगम् अमार्गम् तम् अगाधम् असुर आलयम्
मकरैर् नाग भोगैः च विगाढा वात लोहिताः
transliteration: sudurgam drugam amārgam tam agādham asura ālayam
makarair nāga bhogaiḥ ca vigāḍhā vāta lohitāḥ

sanskrit: उत्पेतुः च निपेतुः च प्रवृद्धा जल राशयः
अग्नि चूर्णम् इव आविद्धम् भास्कर अम्बु मनो रगम्
transliteration: utpetuḥ ca nipetuḥ ca pravṛddhā jala rāśayaḥ
agni cūrṇam iva āviddham bhāskara ambu mano ragam

sanskrit: सुर अरि विषयम् घोरम् पाताल विषमम् सदा
transliteration: sura ari viṣayam ghoram pātāla viṣamam sadā

sanskrit: सागरम् च अम्बर प्रख्यम् अम्बरम् सागर उपमम्
सागरम् च अम्बरम् च इति निर्विशेषम् अदृश्यत
transliteration: sāgaram ca ambara prakhyam ambaram sāgara upamam
sāgaram ca ambaram ca iti nirviśeṣam adṛśyata

sanskrit: ताद्Rग् रूपे स्म द्Rश्येते तारा रत्न समाकुले
सम्पृक्तम् नभसा हि अम्भः सम्प्Rक्तम् च नभो अम्भसा
transliteration: tādg rūpe sma dśyete tārā ratna samākule
sampṛktam nabhasā hi ambhaḥ sampktam ca nabho ambhasā

sanskrit: समुत्पतित मेघस्य वीच्चि माला आकुलस्य च
विशेषो न द्वयोर् आसीत् सागरस्य अम्बरस्य च
transliteration: samutpatita meghasya vīcci mālā ākulasya ca
viśeṣo na dvayor āsīt sāgarasya ambarasya ca
english: They sky enveloped with clouds and the ocean overflowing with surges presented no contrast whatsoever.

sanskrit: ऊर्मयः सिन्धु राजस्य महाभेर्य इव आहवे
रत्न ओघ जल सम्नादम् विषक्तम् इव वायुना
transliteration: ūrmayaḥ sindhu rājasya mahābherya iva āhave
ratna ogha jala samnādam viṣaktam iva vāyunā

sanskrit: उत्पतन्तम् इव क्रुद्धम् यादो गण समाकुलम्
ददृशुस् ते महात्मानो वात आहत जल आशयम्
transliteration: utpatantam iva kruddham yādo gaṇa samākulam
dadṛśus te mahātmāno vāta āhata jala āśayam

sanskrit: अनिल उद्धूतम् आकाशे प्रवल्गतम् इव ऊर्मिभिः
transliteration: anila uddhūtam ākāśe pravalgatam iva ūrmibhiḥ

sanskrit: सा तु नीलेन विधिवत् स्वारक्षा सुसमाहिता
सागरस्य उत्तरे तीरे साधु सेना विनिएशिता
transliteration: sā tu nīlena vidhivat svārakṣā susamāhitā
sāgarasya uttare tīre sādhu senā vinieśitā
