english: There on the northern shore of the ocean the army was encamped and arranged in order by Nila.

sanskrit: मैन्दः च द्विविधः च उभौ तत्र वानर पुम्गवौ
विचेरतुः च ताम् सेनाम् रक्षा अर्थम् सर्वतो दिशम्
transliteration: maindaḥ ca dvividhaḥ ca ubhau tatra vānara pumgavau
viceratuḥ ca tām senām rakṣā artham sarvato diśam
english: The two leading monkeys Mainda and Dvivida patrolled about on all sides to protect the monkey host.

sanskrit: निविष्टायाम् तु सेनायाम् तीरे नद नदी पतेः
पार्श्वस्थम् लक्ष्मणम् दृष्ट्वा रामो वचनम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: niviṣṭāyām tu senāyām tīre nada nadī pateḥ
pārśvastham lakṣmaṇam dṛṣṭvā rāmo vacanam abravīt
english: The army being encamped on the shore of the lord of streams and rivers, Rāma, beholding Laksmana by his side, spoke, saying.

sanskrit: शोकः च किल कालेन गच्चता हि अपगच्चति
मम च अपश्यतः कान्ताम् अहनि अहनि वर्धते
transliteration: śokaḥ ca kila kālena gaccatā hi apagaccati
mama ca apaśyataḥ kāntām ahani ahani vardhate
english: I know that grief abates as time passes by, but my sorrow arising from the separation of my spouse, is increasing day by day.

sanskrit: न मे दुह्खम् प्रिया दूरे न मे दुह्खम् हृता इति च
तद् एव अनुशोचामि वयो अस्या हि अतिवर्तते
transliteration: na me duhkham priyā dūre na me duhkham hṛtā iti ca
tad eva anuśocāmi vayo asyā hi ativartate
english: I am not sorry that she has been stealthily taken away by the demon-but my sorrow is that her end is drawing high.

sanskrit: वाहि वात यतः कन्या ताम् स्पृष्ट्वा माम् अपि स्पृश
त्वयि मे गात्र सम्स्पर्शः चन्द्रे दृष्टि समागमः
transliteration: vāhi vāta yataḥ kanyā tām spṛṣṭvā mām api spṛśa
tvayi me gātra samsparśaḥ candre dṛṣṭi samāgamaḥ
english: O Wind, do you go there where my dear spouse is, and touching her person, do you touch me, for I shall then be happy stationing my looks in the Moon and being touched by you.

sanskrit: तन् मे दहति गात्राणि विषम् पीतम् इव आशये
हा नाथ इति प्रिया सा माम् ह्रियमाणा यद् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: tan me dahati gātrāṇi viṣam pītam iva āśaye
hā nātha iti priyā sā mām hriyamāṇā yad abravīt
english: Alas! my dear one cried 'O lord, O lord' when she was taken away. Those words, revolving burn me like poison.

sanskrit: तद् वियोग इन्धनवता तच् चिन्ता विपुल अर्चिषा
रात्रिम् दिवम् शरीरम् मे दह्यते मदन अग्निना
transliteration: tad viyoga indhanavatā tac cintā vipula arciṣā
rātrim divam śarīram me dahyate madana agninā
english: I am now being burnt down day and night by the fire of desire, having separation from her for its fuel and her thoughts for its flame.

sanskrit: अवगाह्य अर्णवम् स्वप्स्ये सौमित्रे भवता विना
कथम्चित् प्रज्वलन् कामः समासुप्तम् जले दहेत्
transliteration: avagāhya arṇavam svapsye saumitre bhavatā vinā
kathamcit prajvalan kāmaḥ samāsuptam jale dahet
english: Leaving you, O Son of Sumitrā, I shall jump into the deep and then shall not this fire burn me any more.

sanskrit: बह्व् एतत् कामयानस्य शक्यम् एतेन जीवितुम्
यद् अहम् सा च वाम ऊरुर् एकाम् धरणिम् आश्रितौ
transliteration: bahv etat kāmayānasya śakyam etena jīvitum
yad aham sā ca vāma ūrur ekām dharaṇim āśritau
english: This is my only consolation, for which I draw my vital breath-that myself and she breathe on the same earth.

sanskrit: केदारस्य इव केदारः स उदकस्य निरूदकः
उपस्नेहेन जीवामि जीवन्तीम् यत् शृणोमि ताम्
transliteration: kedārasya iva kedāraḥ sa udakasya nirūdakaḥ
upasnehena jīvāmi jīvantīm yat śṛṇomi tām
english: Like to a dry land drawing water from a watered ground, I do live, hearing that Janaki still survives.

sanskrit: कदा तु खलु सुस्शोणीम् शत पत्र आयत ईक्षणाम्
विजित्य शत्रून् द्रक्ष्यामि सीताम् स्फीताम् इव श्रियम्
transliteration: kadā tu khalu susśoṇīm śata patra āyata īkṣaṇām
vijitya śatrūn drakṣyāmi sītām sphītām iva śriyam
english: When shall I, discomfiting my enemies, behold Sītā, having a beautiful waist and eyes resembling lotus-petals, as a victorious hero behold the royal Grace.

sanskrit: कदा नु चारु बिम्ब ओष्ठम् तस्याः पद्मम् इव आननम्
ईषद् उन्नम्य पास्यामि रसायनम् इव आतुरः
transliteration: kadā nu cāru bimba oṣṭham tasyāḥ padmam iva ānanam
īṣad unnamya pāsyāmi rasāyanam iva āturaḥ
english: Like to the sick drinking the elixir of life, when shall I, raising a little her lotus-like countenance having graceful teeth and lips, imprint kisses thereon?

sanskrit: तौ तस्याः सम्हतौ पीनौ स्तनौ ताल फल उपमौ
कदा नु खलु स उत्कम्पौ हसन्त्या माम् भजिष्यतः
transliteration: tau tasyāḥ samhatau pīnau stanau tāla phala upamau
kadā nu khalu sa utkampau hasantyā mām bhajiṣyataḥ
english: When shall she, laughing, embrace me with her rising breast resembling the palm fruit?

sanskrit: सा नूनम् असित अपान्गी रक्षो मध्य गता सती
मन् नाथा नाथ हीना इव त्रातारम् न अधिगच्चति
transliteration: sā nūnam asita apāngī rakṣo madhya gatā satī
man nāthā nātha hīnā iva trātāram na adhigaccati
english: Alas that chaste dame having scarlet corners of the eye, being encircled by the demons, is wishing for a protector like to one having no husband, albeit having a husband in me.

sanskrit: कदा विक्षोभ्य रक्षाम्सि सा विधूय उत्पतिष्यति
transliteration: kadā vikṣobhya rakṣāmsi sā vidhūya utpatiṣyati

sanskrit: विधूय जलदान् नीलान् शशि लेखा शरत्स्व् इव
transliteration: vidhūya jaladān nīlān śaśi lekhā śaratsv iva
english: And having those Rākṣasas, hard to repress, slain by me, truly shall she appear like to the rays of the Moon extricated from sable autumnal clouds.

sanskrit: स्वभाव तनुका नूनम् शोकेन अनशनेन च
भूयस् तनुतरा सीता देश काल विपर्ययात्
transliteration: svabhāva tanukā nūnam śokena anaśanena ca
bhūyas tanutarā sītā deśa kāla viparyayāt
english: Sītā is constitutionally slender, and forsooth, she has been greatly reduced by sorrow, fasting and calamities touching time and place.

sanskrit: कदा नु राक्षस इन्द्रस्य निधाय उरसि सायकान्
transliteration: kadā nu rākṣasa indrasya nidhāya urasi sāyakān
english: When shall I, piercing with my shafts the breast of the lord of Raksasas, renounce my mind's grief?

sanskrit: कदा नु खलु माम् साध्वी सीता अमर सुता उपमा
स उत्कण्ठा कण्ठम् आलम्ब्य मोक्ष्यति आनन्दजम् जलम्
transliteration: kadā nu khalu mām sādhvī sītā amara sutā upamā
sa utkaṇṭhā kaṇṭham ālambya mokṣyati ānandajam jalam
english: When shall my devoted Sītā resembling the daughter of a celestial, fling herself anxiously around my neck and shed tears of joy?

sanskrit: कदा शोकम् इमम् घोरम् मैथिली विप्रयोगजम्
सहसा विप्रमोक्ष्यामि वासः शुक्ल इतरम् यथा
transliteration: kadā śokam imam ghoram maithilī viprayogajam
sahasā vipramokṣyāmi vāsaḥ śukla itaram yathā
english: When shall I renounce this my sorrow arising out of Maithili's separation, like to one casting off his soiled clothes?

sanskrit: एवम् विलपतस् तस्य तत्र रामस्य धीमतः
दिन क्षयान् मन्द वपुर् भास्करो अस्तम् उपागमत्
transliteration: evam vilapatas tasya tatra rāmasya dhīmataḥ
dina kṣayān manda vapur bhāskaro astam upāgamat
english: The highly intelligent Rāma bewailing thus, the day passed away and the Sun, decreasing gradually, disappeared at last.

sanskrit: स्मरन् कमल पत्र अक्षीम् सीताम् शोक आकुली कृतः
transliteration: smaran kamala patra akṣīm sītām śoka ākulī kṛtaḥ
english: And consoled by Laksmana, Rama, stricken with thought touching Sītā having eyes like lotus-petals, engaged in rites relating to the worship of Eve.

sanskrit: लंकायाम् तु कृतम् कर्म घोरम् दृष्ट्वा भव आवहम्
राक्षस इन्द्रो हनुमता शक्रेण इव महात्मना
transliteration: laṃkāyām tu kṛtam karma ghoram dṛṣṭvā bhava āvaham
rākṣasa indro hanumatā śakreṇa iva mahātmanā
english: Beholding in Lankā that dreadful and aweinspiring work performed by Hanuman like to the high-souled Sakra, the lord of Raksasas, looking down with shame, addressed them all, saying.

sanskrit: अब्रवीद् राक्षसान् सर्वान् ह्रिया किम्चिद् अवान् मुखः
धर्षिता च प्रविष्टा च लंका दुष्प्रसहा पुरी
transliteration: abravīd rākṣasān sarvān hriyā kimcid avān mukhaḥ
dharṣitā ca praviṣṭā ca laṃkā duṣprasahā purī

sanskrit: तेन वानर मात्रेण दृष्टा सीता च जानकी
प्रसादो धर्षितः चैत्यः प्रवरा राक्षसा हताः
transliteration: tena vānara mātreṇa dṛṣṭā sītā ca jānakī
prasādo dharṣitaḥ caityaḥ pravarā rākṣasā hatāḥ

sanskrit: आविला च पुरी लंका सर्वा हनुमता कृता
किम् करिष्यामि भद्रम् वः किम् वा युक्तम् अनन्तरम्
transliteration: āvilā ca purī laṃkā sarvā hanumatā kṛtā
kim kariṣyāmi bhadram vaḥ kim vā yuktam anantaram

sanskrit: उच्यताम् नः समर्थम् यत् कृतम् च सुकृतम् भवेत्
मन्त्र मूलम् हि विजयम् प्राहुर् आर्या मनस्विनः
transliteration: ucyatām naḥ samartham yat kṛtam ca sukṛtam bhavet
mantra mūlam hi vijayam prāhur āryā manasvinaḥ

sanskrit: तस्माद् वै रोचये मन्त्रम् रामम् प्रति महाबलाः
त्रिविधाः पुरुषा लोके उत्तम अधम मध्यमाः
transliteration: tasmād vai rocaye mantram rāmam prati mahābalāḥ
trividhāḥ puruṣā loke uttama adhama madhyamāḥ

sanskrit: तेषाम् तु समवेतानाम् गुण दोषम् वदामि अहम्
मन्त्रिभिर् हित सम्युक्तैः समर्थैर् मन्त्र निर्णये
transliteration: teṣām tu samavetānām guṇa doṣam vadāmi aham
mantribhir hita samyuktaiḥ samarthair mantra nirṇaye

sanskrit: मित्रैर् वा अपि समान अर्थैर् बान्धवैर् अपि वा हितैः
सहितो मन्त्रयित्वा यः कर्म आरम्भान् प्रवर्तयेत्
transliteration: mitrair vā api samāna arthair bāndhavair api vā hitaiḥ
sahito mantrayitvā yaḥ karma ārambhān pravartayet
english: He is said to belong to the superior order, whose counsel contains the three signs (mentioned below), or who engages in works after consulting duly with friends capable or with persons having the same end in view, and some times with others, and who serve Providence.

sanskrit: दैवे च कुरुते यत्नम् तम् आहुः पुरुष उत्तमम्
एको अर्थम् विम्Rशेद् एको धर्मे प्रकुरुते मनः
transliteration: daive ca kurute yatnam tam āhuḥ puruṣa uttamam
eko artham vimśed eko dharme prakurute manaḥ

sanskrit: एकः कार्याणि कुरुते तम् आहुर् मध्यमम् नरम्
गुण दोषाव् अनिश्चित्य त्यक्त्वा दैव व्यपाश्रयम्
transliteration: ekaḥ kāryāṇi kurute tam āhur madhyamam naram
guṇa doṣāv aniścitya tyaktvā daiva vyapāśrayam

sanskrit: करिष्यामि इति यः कार्यम् उपेक्षेत् स नर अधमः
यथा इमे पुरुषा नित्यम् उत्तम अधम मध्यमाः
transliteration: kariṣyāmi iti yaḥ kāryam upekṣet sa nara adhamaḥ
yathā ime puruṣā nityam uttama adhama madhyamāḥ

sanskrit: एवम् मन्त्रो अपि विज्ञेय उत्तम अधम मध्यमः
transliteration: evam mantro api vijñeya uttama adhama madhyamaḥ

sanskrit: मन्त्रिणो यत्र निरस्तास् तम् आहुर् मन्त्रम् उत्तमम्
बह्व्यो अपि मतयो गत्वा मन्त्रिणो हि अर्थ निर्णये
transliteration: mantriṇo yatra nirastās tam āhur mantram uttamam
bahvyo api matayo gatvā mantriṇo hi artha nirṇaye

sanskrit: पुनर् यत्र एकताम् प्राप्तः स मन्त्रो मध्यमः स्मृतः
transliteration: punar yatra ekatām prāptaḥ sa mantro madhyamaḥ smṛtaḥ

sanskrit: न च ऐकमत्ये श्रेयो अस्ति मन्त्रः सो अधम उच्यते
तस्मात् सुमन्त्रितम् साधु भवन्तो मन्त्रि सत्तमाः
transliteration: na ca aikamatye śreyo asti mantraḥ so adhama ucyate
tasmāt sumantritam sādhu bhavanto mantri sattamāḥ

sanskrit: रामो अभ्येति पुरीम् लंकाम् अस्माकम् उपरोधकः
तरिष्यति च सुव्यक्तम् राघवः सागरम् सुखम्
transliteration: rāmo abhyeti purīm laṃkām asmākam uparodhakaḥ
tariṣyati ca suvyaktam rāghavaḥ sāgaram sukham

sanskrit: तरसा युक्त रूपेण सानुजः सबल अनुगः
transliteration: tarasā yukta rūpeṇa sānujaḥ sabala anugaḥ

sanskrit: तस्मिन्न् एवम् गते कार्ये विरुद्धे वानरैः सह
हितम् पुरे च सैन्ये च सर्वम् सम्मन्त्र्यताम् मम
transliteration: tasminn evam gate kārye viruddhe vānaraiḥ saha
hitam pure ca sainye ca sarvam sammantryatām mama
english: He can by his prowess dry up the ocean and do the other.* Rāma approaching thus with a hostile intention along with the monkeys, it behove you to devise such means as might protect my city and army. *i.e. bridge over the ocean.

sanskrit: इति उक्ता राक्षस इन्द्रेण राक्षसास्ते महाबलाः
ऊचुः प्रान्जलयः सर्वे रावणम् राक्षस ईश्वरम्
transliteration: iti uktā rākṣasa indreṇa rākṣasāste mahābalāḥ
ūcuḥ prānjalayaḥ sarve rāvaṇam rākṣasa īśvaram
english: Being thus accosted by their lord, the highly powerful Rākşasas, devoid of good sense and ignorant of sound counsel, replied with folded palms, saying.

sanskrit: राजन् परिघ शक्ति ऋष्टि शूल पट्टस सम्कुलम्
transliteration: rājan parigha śakti ṛṣṭi śūla paṭṭasa samkulam

sanskrit: सुमहन् नो बलम् कस्माद् विषादम् भजते भवान्
त्वया भोगवतीम् गत्वा निर्जताः पन्नगा युधि
transliteration: sumahan no balam kasmād viṣādam bhajate bhavān
tvayā bhogavatīm gatvā nirjatāḥ pannagā yudhi

sanskrit: कैलास शिखर आवासी यक्षैर् बहुभिर् आवृतः
सुमहत् कदनम् कृत्वा वश्यस् ते धनदः कृतः
transliteration: kailāsa śikhara āvāsī yakṣair bahubhir āvṛtaḥ
sumahat kadanam kṛtvā vaśyas te dhanadaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: Repairing to Bhagavatī, you did discomfit the serpents in battle. The God of Death, living on mount Kailasa, encircled by Yaksas, was subjugated by you in a great battle.

sanskrit: स महाईश्वर सख्येन श्लाघमानस् त्वया विभो
निर्जितः समरे रोषाल् लोक पालो महाबलः
transliteration: sa mahāīśvara sakhyena ślāghamānas tvayā vibho
nirjitaḥ samare roṣāl loka pālo mahābalaḥ
english: That mighty lord of men, proud of his friendship with Śiva, was defeated by you wrathfully in battle.

sanskrit: विनिहत्य च यक्षौघान् विक्षोभ्य च विगृह्य च
त्वया कैलास शिखराद् विमानम् इदम् आहृतम्
transliteration: vinihatya ca yakṣaughān vikṣobhya ca vigṛhya ca
tvayā kailāsa śikharād vimānam idam āhṛtam
english: Discomfiting and slaying the band of Yaksas, you did bring this flowery car from the mount Kailasa.

sanskrit: मयेन दानव इन्द्रेण त्वद् भयात् सख्यम् इच्चता
दुहिता तव भार्या अर्थे दत्ता राक्षस पुम्गव
transliteration: mayena dānava indreṇa tvad bhayāt sakhyam iccatā
duhitā tava bhāryā arthe dattā rākṣasa pumgava
english: O lord of Rākşasas, desiring your friendship out of fear, Maya, the king of Danavas, offered you his daughter for your spouse.

sanskrit: दानव इन्द्रो मधुर् नाम वीर्य उत्सिक्तो दुरासदः
विगृह्य वशम् आनीतः कुम्भीनस्याः सुख आवहः
transliteration: dānava indro madhur nāma vīrya utsikto durāsadaḥ
vigṛhya vaśam ānītaḥ kumbhīnasyāḥ sukha āvahaḥ
english: O you of mighty arms, you did bring under your subjection the powerful and irrepressible Dänava for the pleasure of Kumbhīnasī.

sanskrit: निर्जितास् ते महाबाहो नागा गत्वा रसा तलम्
वासुकिस् तक्षकः शन्खो जटी च वशम् आहृताः
transliteration: nirjitās te mahābāho nāgā gatvā rasā talam
vāsukis takṣakaḥ śankho jaṭī ca vaśam āhṛtāḥ
english: And entering the region under the earth, you did defeat the serpents-and thus bring under your subjection Väsuki, Takşaka, Sankha, and Jațī.

sanskrit: अक्षया बलवन्तः च शूरा लब्ध वराः पुनः
त्वया सम्वत्सरम् युद्ध्वा समरे दानवा विभो
transliteration: akṣayā balavantaḥ ca śūrā labdha varāḥ punaḥ
tvayā samvatsaram yuddhvā samare dānavā vibho
english: Those heroic Dänavas, the Kālakeyas, were greatly powerful, irrepressible, and proud of the boons conferred on them. And fighting with them perpetually for a year, you did bring them under your control, O lord, O slayer of foes, and learn from them the science o varied illusions, O king of the Rākşasas.

sanskrit: स्व बलम् समुपाश्रित्य नीता वशम् अरिम् दम
मायाः च अधिगतास् तत्र बहवो राक्षस अधिप
transliteration: sva balam samupāśritya nītā vaśam arim dama
māyāḥ ca adhigatās tatra bahavo rākṣasa adhipa
english: Those heroic Dänavas, the Kālakeyas, were greatly powerful, irrepressible, and proud of the boons conferred on them. And fighting with them perpetually for a year, you did bring them under your control, O lord, O slayer of foes, and learn from them the science o varied illusions, O king of the Rākşasas.

sanskrit: शूराः च बलवन्तः च वरुणस्य सुता रणे
निर्जितास् ते महाबाग चतुर् विध बल अनुगाः
transliteration: śūrāḥ ca balavantaḥ ca varuṇasya sutā raṇe
nirjitās te mahābāga catur vidha bala anugāḥ
english: O great hero, by you were defeated in battle, the heroic and powerful sons of Varuņa, followed by a fourfold division of their army.

sanskrit: मृत्यु दण्ड महाग्राहम् शाल्मलि द्वीप मण्डितम्
transliteration: mṛtyu daṇḍa mahāgrāham śālmali dvīpa maṇḍitam

sanskrit: अवगाह्य त्वया राजन् यमस्य बल सागरम्
transliteration: avagāhya tvayā rājan yamasya bala sāgaram

sanskrit: जयः च विप्लुलः प्राप्तो मृत्युः च प्रतिषेधितः
सुयुद्धेन च ते सर्वे लोकास् तत्र सुतोषिताः
transliteration: jayaḥ ca viplulaḥ prāpto mṛtyuḥ ca pratiṣedhitaḥ
suyuddhena ca te sarve lokās tatra sutoṣitāḥ

sanskrit: क्षत्रियैर् बहुभिर् वीरैः शक्र तुल्य पराक्रमैः
आसीद् वसुमती पूर्णा महद्भिर् इव पादपैः
transliteration: kṣatriyair bahubhir vīraiḥ śakra tulya parākramaiḥ
āsīd vasumatī pūrṇā mahadbhir iva pādapaiḥ
english: The Earth was filled with various heroic Kșatriyas, resembling Sakra in prowess as she is adorned now with various trees.

sanskrit: तेषाम् वीर्य गुण उत्साहैर् न समो राघवो रणे
प्रसह्य ते त्वया राजन् हताः परम दुर्जयाः
transliteration: teṣām vīrya guṇa utsāhair na samo rāghavo raṇe
prasahya te tvayā rājan hatāḥ parama durjayāḥ
english: Rāghava is not their equal either is strength or prowess. And all those heroes, hard to repress in battle, were slain by you, O king.

sanskrit: तिष्ठ वा किम् महाराज श्रमेण तव वानरान्
transliteration: tiṣṭha vā kim mahārāja śrameṇa tava vānarān
english: Do you wait here, O great king; you need not take any trouble, Indrajit alone shall slay all these monkeys.

sanskrit: इष्ट्वा यज्ञम् वरो लब्धो लोके परमदुर्लभः
transliteration: iṣṭvā yajñam varo labdho loke paramadurlabhaḥ
english: This one, O mighty monarch, having celebrated the the Māheśvara* sacrifice, has obtained a noble boon, rarely (attained by persons). *Relating to Mahasvara, the great Lord, a designation of Sivā.
Then, O king, liberated agreeably to the injunction of the Great-father, the slayer of Sambara and Vſtra, worshipped of all the celestials, went (back) to heaven.
Do you, O great king, entrust Indrajit with this business, until he bring to destruction the monkey-host along with Rāma.

sanskrit: राजन् न आपद् अयुक्ता इयम् आगता प्राकृताज् जनात्
हृदि न एव त्वया कार्या त्वम् वधिष्यसि राघवम्
transliteration: rājan na āpad ayuktā iyam āgatā prākṛtāj janāt
hṛdi na eva tvayā kāryā tvam vadhiṣyasi rāghavam
english: O king, you must not think that this calamity, coming from an ignoble person is not insignificant. You shall slay Rāghava.

sanskrit: ततो नील अम्बुद निभः प्रहस्तो नाम राक्षसः
अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर् वाक्यम् शूरः सेना पतिस्तदा
transliteration: tato nīla ambuda nibhaḥ prahasto nāma rākṣasaḥ
abravīt prāñjalir vākyam śūraḥ senā patistadā
english: Then that heroic general, the Rākşasa named Prahasta, possessing the splendour of sable clouds, submitted with joined hands.

sanskrit: न त्वाम् धर्षयितुम् शक्ताः किम् पुनर् वानरा रणे
transliteration: na tvām dharṣayitum śaktāḥ kim punar vānarā raṇe
english: I am competent to baffle in battle gods and Dänavas and Gandharvas, ghosts, birds and serpents, what then is a couple of human beings?

sanskrit: सर्वे प्रमत्ता विश्वस्ता वन्चिताः स्म हनूमता
न हि मे जीवतो गच्चेज् जीवन् स वन गोचरः
transliteration: sarve pramattā viśvastā vancitāḥ sma hanūmatā
na hi me jīvato gaccej jīvan sa vana gocaraḥ
english: Having been negligent and confident (in our power), we have all been deceived by Hanumān. But, I living, that ranger of woods shall not (again) go hence with his life.

sanskrit: सर्वाम् सागर पर्यन्ताम् सशैल वन काननाम्
करोमि अवानराम् भूमिम् आज्ञापयतु माम् भवान्
transliteration: sarvām sāgara paryantām saśaila vana kānanām
karomi avānarām bhūmim ājñāpayatu mām bhavān
english: All the earth down to the ocean, containing hills, forests and woods, shall be rendered free from monkeys. Do you command me.

sanskrit: रक्षाम् चैव विधास्यामि वानराद् रजनी चर
न आगमिष्यति ते दुह्खम् किम्चिद् आत्म अपराधजम्
transliteration: rakṣām caiva vidhāsyāmi vānarād rajanī cara
na āgamiṣyati te duhkham kimcid ātma aparādhajam
english: O ranger of the night, I shall deliver (the Rāks asas) from the monkeys; and you shall not have to suffer in the least in consequence of your transgression.* *i.e. the ravishment of Sitā

sanskrit: इदम् न क्षमणीयम् हि सर्वेषाम् नः प्रधर्षणम्
transliteration: idam na kṣamaṇīyam hi sarveṣām naḥ pradharṣaṇam
english: Then the Rāksasa named Durmukha, growing enraged, said, This overpowering of all of us must not be forgiven-this flagrant discomfiture of the metropolis of the auspicious lord of the Rākşasas as well as of his inner apartment by the foremost of monkeys.

sanskrit: अयम् परिभवो भूयः पुरस्य अन्तः पुरस्य च
श्रीमतो राक्षस इन्द्रस्य वानर इन्द्र प्रधर्षणम्
transliteration: ayam paribhavo bhūyaḥ purasya antaḥ purasya ca
śrīmato rākṣasa indrasya vānara indra pradharṣaṇam
english: Then the Rāksasa named Durmukha, growing enraged, said, This overpowering of all of us must not be forgiven-this flagrant discomfiture of the metropolis of the auspicious lord of the Rākşasas as well as of his inner apartment by the foremost of monkeys.

sanskrit: अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते हत्वा एको निवर्तिष्यामि वानरान्
प्रविष्टान् सागरम् भीमम् अम्बरम् वा रसा तलम्
transliteration: asmin muhūrte hatvā eko nivartiṣyāmi vānarān
praviṣṭān sāgaram bhīmam ambaram vā rasā talam
english: This moment marching alone (from hence) will I exterminate the monkeys, even if they shall have entered the dreadful deep, or the sky, or the subterranean regions.

sanskrit: ततो अब्रवीत् सुसम्क्रुद्धो वज्र दम्ष्ट्रो महाबलः
प्रगृह्य परिघम् घोरम् माम्स शोणित रूपितम्
transliteration: tato abravīt susamkruddho vajra damṣṭro mahābalaḥ
pragṛhya parigham ghoram māmsa śoṇita rūpitam
english: Then the exceedingly powerful Vajradańșțra, wielding up a terrific bludgeon, stained with flesh and gore, wrathfully observed.

sanskrit: किम् नो हनुमता कार्यम् कृपणेन तपस्विना
रामे तिष्ठति दुर्धर्षे सुग्रीवे सह लक्ष्मणे
transliteration: kim no hanumatā kāryam kṛpaṇena tapasvinā
rāme tiṣṭhati durdharṣe sugrīve saha lakṣmaṇe
english: Rāma the irrepressible existing, and also Sugrīva with Lakşmaņa, what have we to do with the weak and wretched Hanumăn?

sanskrit: आगमिष्यामि हत्वा एको विक्षोभ्य हरि वाहिनीम्
transliteration: āgamiṣyāmi hatvā eko vikṣobhya hari vāhinīm
english: This very day, staying single-handed Rāma with Sugrīva and with Lakşmaņa, with this bludgeon shall I return, after having sorely troubled the monkey-host.
O monarch, if you are minded, hear this other word of mine! Verily he that is fertile in resources and ever ready, compass success.

Then, equipped with darts, javelins and maces, and bearing bows, arrows and scimitars in our hands, we shall swiftly and summoning speed* set out (from hence); and stationing ourselves in the sky in bands, and slaughtering the monkey-army with mighty showers of rocks and weapons, we shall lead it to Death's door. *Tvarita-summoning speed-redundant.

sanskrit: आकाशे गणशः स्थित्वा हत्वा ताम् हरिवाहिनीम्
transliteration: ākāśe gaṇaśaḥ sthitvā hatvā tām harivāhinīm
english: Then, equipped with darts, javelins and maces, and bearing bows, arrows and scimitars in our hands, we shall swiftly and summoning speed* set out (from hence); and stationing ourselves in the sky in bands, and slaughtering the monkey-army with mighty showers of rocks and weapons, we shall lead it to Death's door. *Tvarita-summoning speed-redundant.
Let us in this wise decoy Rāma and Laks mana; and if they fall into our design, they shall, without doubt, lose their lives.

sanskrit: कौम्भकर्णिस् ततो वीरो निकुम्भो नाम वीर्यवान्
अब्रवीत् परम कुर्द्धो रावणम् लोक रावणम्
transliteration: kaumbhakarṇis tato vīro nikumbho nāma vīryavān
abravīt parama kurddho rāvaṇam loka rāvaṇam
english: Then that hero, Kumbhakarma's son, named Nikumbha, endowed with exceeding prowess, in high wrath remarked to Rāvana, destroyer of worlds.

sanskrit: अहम् एको हनिष्यामि राघवम् सह लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: aham eko haniṣyāmi rāghavam saha lakṣmaṇam
english: Do you, all of you, stay here along with the great king. I alone shall slay Rāghava together with Laksmana, and Sugrīva with Hanumān, and all the monkeys.

sanskrit: क्रुद्धः परिलिहन् वक्त्रम् जिह्वया वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
स्वैरम् कुर्वन्तु कार्याणि भवन्तो विगत ज्वराः
transliteration: kruddhaḥ parilihan vaktram jihvayā vākyam abravīt
svairam kurvantu kāryāṇi bhavanto vigata jvarāḥ

sanskrit: एको अहम् भक्षयिष्यामि तान् सर्वान् हरि यूथपान्
स्वस्थाः क्रीडन्तु निश्चिन्ताः पिबन्तु मधु वारुणीम्
transliteration: eko aham bhakṣayiṣyāmi tān sarvān hari yūthapān
svasthāḥ krīḍantu niścintāḥ pibantu madhu vāruṇīm

sanskrit: अहम् एको हनिष्यामि सुग्रीवम् सह लक्ष्मणम्
स अन्गदम् च हनूमन्तम् रामम् च रण कुन्जरम्
transliteration: aham eko haniṣyāmi sugrīvam saha lakṣmaṇam
sa angadam ca hanūmantam rāmam ca raṇa kunjaram

sanskrit: ततो निकुम्भो रभसः सूर्य शत्रुर् महाबलः
सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञ कोपः च महापार्श्वो महाउअरः
transliteration: tato nikumbho rabhasaḥ sūrya śatrur mahābalaḥ
suptaghno yajña kopaḥ ca mahāpārśvo mahāuaraḥ

sanskrit: अग्नि केतुः च दुर्धर्षो रश्मि केतुः च राक्षसः
इन्द्रजिच् च महातेजा बलवान् रावण आत्मजः
transliteration: agni ketuḥ ca durdharṣo raśmi ketuḥ ca rākṣasaḥ
indrajic ca mahātejā balavān rāvaṇa ātmajaḥ

sanskrit: प्रहस्तो अथ विरूप अक्षो वज्र दम्ष्ट्रो महाबलः
धूम्र अक्षः च अतिकायः च दुर्मुखः चैव राक्षसः
transliteration: prahasto atha virūpa akṣo vajra damṣṭro mahābalaḥ
dhūmra akṣaḥ ca atikāyaḥ ca durmukhaḥ caiva rākṣasaḥ

sanskrit: परिघान् पट्टसान् प्रासान् शक्ति शूल परश्वधान्
चापानि च सबाणानि खड्गामः च विपुलान् शितान्
transliteration: parighān paṭṭasān prāsān śakti śūla paraśvadhān
cāpāni ca sabāṇāni khaḍgāmaḥ ca vipulān śitān

sanskrit: प्रगृह्य परम क्रुद्धाः समुत्पत्य च राक्षसाः
अब्रुवन् रावणम् सर्वे प्रदीप्ता इव तेजसा
transliteration: pragṛhya parama kruddhāḥ samutpatya ca rākṣasāḥ
abruvan rāvaṇam sarve pradīptā iva tejasā

sanskrit: अद्य रामम् वधिष्यामः सुग्रीवम् च सलक्ष्मणम्
कृपणम् च हनूमन्तम् लंका येन प्रधर्षिता
transliteration: adya rāmam vadhiṣyāmaḥ sugrīvam ca salakṣmaṇam
kṛpaṇam ca hanūmantam laṃkā yena pradharṣitā

sanskrit: तान् गृहीत आयुधान् सर्वान् वारयित्वा विभीषणः
अब्रवीत् प्रान्जलिर् वाक्यम् पुनः प्रत्युपवेश्य तान्
transliteration: tān gṛhīta āyudhān sarvān vārayitvā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
abravīt prānjalir vākyam punaḥ pratyupaveśya tān
english: Then, preventing them, who had (thus) equipped themselves with all kinds of weapons, and making them sit down, Vibhisana, with joined hands, again spoke to them, saying.

sanskrit: अपि उपायैस् त्रिभिस् तात यो अर्थः प्राप्तुम् न शक्यते
तस्य विक्रम कालाम्स् तान् युक्तान् आहुर् मनीषिणः
transliteration: api upāyais tribhis tāta yo arthaḥ prāptum na śakyate
tasya vikrama kālāms tān yuktān āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: The wise have asserted that an appeal to prowess should be resorted to anent a business then only when the end sought cannot be attained through the three (other) means. Prowess produce fruit only in respect of welladvised action directed while carefully watching (enemies) that are negligent, or captive, or under Divine affliction.

sanskrit: विक्रमास् तात सिध्यन्ति परीक्ष्य विधिना कृताः
transliteration: vikramās tāta sidhyanti parīkṣya vidhinā kṛtāḥ
english: The wise have asserted that an appeal to prowess should be resorted to anent a business then only when the end sought cannot be attained through the three (other) means. Prowess produce fruit only in respect of welladvised action directed while carefully watching (enemies) that are negligent, or captive, or under Divine affliction.

sanskrit: अप्रमत्तम् कथम् तम् तु विजिगीषुम् बले स्थितम्
transliteration: apramattam katham tam tu vijigīṣum bale sthitam
english: But why do you intend to discomfit (Rāma), who is vigilant, who desire victory, who is strong in the Divine strength, who has subdued passion, and who is hard to subdue?

sanskrit: समुद्रम् लन्घयित्वा तु घोरम् नद नदी पतिम्
कृतम् हनुमता कर्म दुष्करम् तर्कयेत कः
transliteration: samudram langhayitvā tu ghoram nada nadī patim
kṛtam hanumatā karma duṣkaram tarkayeta kaḥ

sanskrit: बलानि अपरिमेयानि वीर्याणि च निशा चराः
परेषाम् सहसा अवज्ञा न कर्तव्या कथम्चन
transliteration: balāni aparimeyāni vīryāṇi ca niśā carāḥ
pareṣām sahasā avajñā na kartavyā kathamcana
english: Who had in this world ever thought of or reasoned at ɔut Hanuman's career over the dreadful deep, the lord of streams and rivers? O rangers of the night, the strength and prowess (of the foe) being immeasurable, you should by no means recklessly disregard him.

sanskrit: किम् च राक्षस राजस्य रामेण अपकृतम् पुरा
आजहार जन स्थानाद् यस्य भार्याम् यशस्विनः
transliteration: kim ca rākṣasa rājasya rāmeṇa apakṛtam purā
ājahāra jana sthānād yasya bhāryām yaśasvinaḥ
english: And what was the wrong that formerly had been done by Rāma to the king of the Rākşasas, that he has carried off from Janasthāna the spouse of that illustrious one?

sanskrit: खरो यदि अतिवृत्तस् तु रामेण निहतो रणे
अवश्यम् प्राणिनाम् प्राणा रक्षितव्या यथा बलम्
transliteration: kharo yadi ativṛttas tu rāmeṇa nihato raṇe
avaśyam prāṇinām prāṇā rakṣitavyā yathā balam
english: If Khara, who had trespassed into regions not his own, has buen slain in battle by Rāma, surely a creature should to the best of his might preserve his life.

sanskrit: एतन् निमित्तम् वैदेही भयम् नः सुमहद् भवेत्
आहृता सा परित्याज्या कलह अर्थे क्Rते न किम्
transliteration: etan nimittam vaidehī bhayam naḥ sumahad bhavet
āhṛtā sā parityājyā kalaha arthe kte na kim
english: It is for this great fear that exercise us on the score of Vaidehi owing its existence to this,* that she, having been ravished, should (now) be given up. What is the use of acting so that quarrel may be the consequence? *The feeling of revenge for the slaughter of Khara and the rest.

sanskrit: न नः क्षमम् वीर्यवता तेन धर्म अनुवर्तिना
वैरम् निरर्थकम् कर्तुम् दीयताम् अस्य मैथिली
transliteration: na naḥ kṣamam vīryavatā tena dharma anuvartinā
vairam nirarthakam kartum dīyatām asya maithilī
english: And (Rama), possessed of prowess, yet ever abiding by morality, is incapable of initiating hostilities for no purpose. Therefore, do you give him his Maithili.

sanskrit: यावन् सगजाम् साश्वाम् बहु रत्न समाकुलाम्
पुरीम् दारयते बाणैर् दीयताम् अस्य मैथिली
transliteration: yāvan sagajām sāśvām bahu ratna samākulām
purīm dārayate bāṇair dīyatām asya maithilī
english: And before, he by means of his shafts rive this city together with her elephants and steeds, overflowing with countless gems, do you give him his Maithili.

sanskrit: यावत् सुघोरा महती दुर्धर्षा हरि वाहिनी
न अवस्कन्दति नो लंकाम् तावत् सीता प्रदीयताम्
transliteration: yāvat sughorā mahatī durdharṣā hari vāhinī
na avaskandati no laṃkām tāvat sītā pradīyatām
english: And before the dreadful, irrepressible and mighty monkey-host block up this Lankā of ours, do you give (back) Sītā.

sanskrit: विनश्येद्द् हि पुरी लंका शूराः सर्वे च आक्षसाः
रामस्य दयिता पत्नी न स्वयम् यदि दीयते
transliteration: vinaśyedd hi purī laṃkā śūrāḥ sarve ca ākṣasāḥ
rāmasya dayitā patnī na svayam yadi dīyate
english: This city of Lankā shall perish as also all the heroic Rākṣasas, if you did not yourself make over Rāma's spouse to him.

sanskrit: प्रसादये त्वाम् बन्धुत्वात् कुरुष्व वचनम् मम
हितम् पथ्यम् त्व् अहम् ब्रूमि दीयताम् अस्य मैथिली
transliteration: prasādaye tvām bandhutvāt kuruṣva vacanam mama
hitam pathyam tv aham brūmi dīyatām asya maithilī
english: I exert myself to pleasure you, because of the fraternity (that subsist between us). Do what I say. I say what is truth and what also is for your good. Do you render (back) Rama's Maithili.

sanskrit: नव अग्र पुन्खान् सुदृढान् नृप आत्मजः
transliteration: nava agra punkhān sudṛḍhān nṛpa ātmajaḥ
english: Ere yet the king's son, for compassing your destruction, shower sure shafts resembling the rays of the autumnal Sun, having shining heads and feathered parts, and exceedingly hard, do you render Maithili to son of Daſaratha.

Ere yet the king's son, for compassing your destruction, shower sure shafts resembling the rays of the autumnal Sun, having shining heads and feathered parts, and exceedingly hard, do you render Maithili to son of Daſaratha.

Forsake your wrath at once, which destroy happiness and virtue; and follow righteousness, which enhance enjoyment and fame. Be you propitious, so that we may live (at ease) along with our sons and relatives. Render (back) Maithili to Dasaratha's son.

Forsake your wrath at once, which destroy happiness and virtue; and follow righteousness, which enhance enjoyment and fame. Be you propitious, so that we may live (at ease) along with our sons and relatives. Render (back) Maithili to Dasaratha's son.

sanskrit: विसर्जयित्वा तान् सर्वान् प्रैवेश स्वकम् गृहम्
transliteration: visarjayitvā tān sarvān praiveśa svakam gṛham
english: Having heard Vibhisana's speech, Ravanalord of Raksasas-leaving all of them, entered his own chamber.

Then early in the morning, like the fiery and refulgent sun entering a mighty mass of clouds, Vibhisana, fast to virtue and interest, heroic and possessed of exceeding splendour, playing a perilous part, * entered the apartment of his elder brother, resembling an assemblage of mountain summits and elevated like the peak of a mountain, orderly, divided into spacious rooms, the resort of the great-inhabited by august and intelligent persons attached (to Răvaņa); guarded around by lusty Rakşasas in limited numbers; having the air agitated by the breath of mad elephants; with loud blares of conchs, and resounding with trumpets; with loud blares of conchs, and resounding with trumpets; embosoming numbers of beautiful damsels, with its high-ways (overflowing with talk); furnished with doors of polished gold; embellished with excellent ornaments; resembling the abode of the Gandharvas, or the mansion of the Maruts; containing heaps of gems; like to the dwelling of serpents. *The project he had conceived, viz., converting Rāvana to his own polloy of pacification, was fraught with peril to himself, considering his brother's fierce temperament.

That one of exceeding energy heard sacred and holy sounds uttered by Veda-versed Brāhmaṇas celebrating the victory of his brother; and that highly powerful (hero) acquainted with Mantras and the Vedas saw Vipras worshipped with vessels of curds, clarified butter, flowers and fried paddy.

That one of exceeding energy heard sacred and holy sounds uttered by Veda-versed Brāhmaṇas celebrating the victory of his brother; and that highly powerful (hero) acquainted with Mantras and the Vedas saw Vipras worshipped with vessels of curds, clarified butter, flowers and fried paddy.
The mighty-armed (Vibhisana) saluted the younger brother of the bestower of riches, * seated there. *Kuvera-Ravana was Kuvera's younger brother.
That one acquainted with manners, after proper courtesy, sat him down on a seat decked in gold, which was pointed out (by a royal glance).

In retirement as also in presence only of his counsellors, Vibhīşaņa spoke to the high souled Rāvana words backed by reason, and greatly fraught with his welfare. And having, with soothing speech, pacified his elder brother and extended towards him the due civilities, that one, who through height of sentiment had noted excellence and the want of it, addressed (Vibhīş aņa) in words befitting the occasion and the place.

In retirement as also in presence only of his counsellors, Vibhīşaņa spoke to the high souled Rāvana words backed by reason, and greatly fraught with his welfare. And having, with soothing speech, pacified his elder brother and extended towards him the due civilities, that one, who through height of sentiment had noted excellence and the want of it, addressed (Vibhīş aņa) in words befitting the occasion and the place.
Ever since, O subduer of enemies, Vaidehi has come hither, are seen inauspicious omens.

Fire, enveloped in smoke at the time of its being ignited, and thereafter throwing out scintillation's, with its brightness obscured by vapour, does not increase adequately even n oblations being poured into it with Mantras,
Reptiles are discovered in kitchens, sacrificial fire-chambers, and the places of Vaidika recitations; and ants (are found) in clarified butter.

The milk of the kine has been dried up; and the nobler elephants are without the temporal juice. And horses, albeit they have feasted on feasted on fresh grass, neigh distressfully.* *The commentator remarks, evidently with justice, "That is, the horses, having eaten their fill, still hunger."
Asses, camels and mules, O king, with their hair standing erect, shed tears; and although they are ministered to medically, they do not return to nature.
And crows in numbers emit harsh cries on all sides, and are seen in swarms at the tops of edifices.
Vultures sit sadly and distressed upon the roofs of houses. During the two twilights, the jackals, coming in sight, utter ominous howls.
Wolves and other (ferocious) animals, as well as deer, approaching the gate of the palace in swarms, are heard to set up loud roars resembling the thunder.
Things having come to this pass, even this expiation, I fancy, is capable of removing the evil omens. Do you render back Vaidehī to Raghava.

sanskrit: इदम् च यदि वामोहाल्लोभाद्वा व्याहृतम् मया
तत्राप् च महाराज न दोषम् कर्तुमर्हसि
transliteration: idam ca yadi vāmohāllobhādvā vyāhṛtam mayā
tatrāp ca mahārāja na doṣam kartumarhasi
english: If I have said this through ignorance or covetousness, you ought not, O mighty monarch, criminate me.

sanskrit: रक्षसाम् राक्षसीनाम् च पुरस्यान्तः पुरस्य च
transliteration: rakṣasām rākṣasīnām ca purasyāntaḥ purasya ca
english: All Rākşasas and Rākşasis, as well as those belonging to palace and the inner apartmentshall have to experience the even consequence (of this act of your).

sanskrit: अवश्यम् च मया वाच्यम् यद्दृष्टमथवा श्रुतम्
transliteration: avaśyam ca mayā vācyam yaddṛṣṭamathavā śrutam
english: All the counsellors have refrained from tendering this counsel to you; but surely I must tell you what I have seen or heard; and adopting proper measures, it behove you to act so.* *In accordance with my suggestion.
(Ravana's) brother, Vibhisana, thus spoke, to his brother, the chief of Rākşasa, in the midst of counsellors, these words fraught with his good.
Having said this, that destroyer of celestial hosts, the Ten-necked one, possessed of mighty strength and of terrific prowess in battle, then dismissed his brother Vibhīşaņa, who had spoken truth.
Having said this, that destroyer of celestial hosts, the Ten-necked one, possessed of mighty strength and of terrific prowess in battle, then dismissed his brother Vibhīşaņa, who had spoken truth.
The unrighteous king, overmastered by his passion (for Sītā), in consequence of his sinful act as well as the loss of honour he sustained at the hands of his friends, became reduced.
The occasion for war was (wanting Rāvana, possessed by lust, and continually thinking of Vaidehī, conceived along with his counsellors that the time for entering into hostilities had arrived.
Sallying forth, he ascended a mighty car furnished with golden network, adorned with pearls and coral and yoked with trained steeds.

sanskrit: प्रययौ रक्षसाम् श्रेष्ठो दशग्रीवः सभाम् प्रति
transliteration: prayayau rakṣasām śreṣṭho daśagrīvaḥ sabhām prati
english: Having ascended that excellent vehicle, having sounds resembling those of mighty clouds, that foremost of Raksasa, the Tennecked one, drove towards the court.
As he coursed on, Rākşasas, bearing swords and shields, and carrying all kinds of weapons, went before the lord of the Rākşasas.
And (some of) these, wearing various frightful suits, and decked with diverse ornaments, went, surrounding his rear and flanks.
And many atiratha heroes went with cars, and superb mad elephants, and sportive steeds; and bearing in their hands maces and bludgeons; and darts and clubs.
Some of them were bearing spades and others with darts in hands. As Rāvana marched towards the court, there arose the loud blares of a thousand trumpet, and the uproarious sounds of conchs.
That redoubtable and mighty car-warrior held his course, suddenly making sides resound, and beautifying the high ways.
The spotless white umbrella of the lord of Rākşasa, being raised up, looked beautiful like the Moon at her full.
On his right and left graced two crystal white cámaras furnished with threads of gold.
All those Rākşasas standing on the ground with joined hands, bowed down their heads to the foremost of Rākşasas who was seated on his car.
Hymned by the Råkşasas with blessings of victory, that exceedingly energetic chastiser of enemies arrived at the court constructed (by Viśvakarmā).

That highly energetic one in person entered that court paved with silver and gold, having its heart decorated with crystal, and gracefully covered with silk, embroidered with gold; excellently constructed by Viśvakarma, and guarded by six hundred ghosts.

That highly energetic one in person entered that court paved with silver and gold, having its heart decorated with crystal, and gracefully covered with silk, embroidered with gold; excellently constructed by Viśvakarma, and guarded by six hundred ghosts.
Rävaņa sat down on a superb and august seat consisting of lapises, furnished with a pillow; and covered with a soft dear-skin. And lord-like he commanded the envoys possessed of fleet vigour, saying.
Hearing his words, the envoys began to range Lankā; and going to every house, they fearlessly collected the Rākṣasas from places of sport, bedrooms, and gardens.

sanskrit: ते रथान् रुचिरानेके दृप्तानेके दृढान् हयान्
transliteration: te rathān rucirāneke dṛptāneke dṛḍhān hayān
english: Then some set out, mounting cars, and some mounting proud coursers, and some on foot.
And like the welkin filled with fowls, the city thronged with approaching cars, elephants and steeds.
Leaving their various vehicles and cars behind, they entered the court on foot, like lions entering mountain caverns.

sanskrit: राज्ञः पादौ गृहीत्वा तु राज्ञा ते प्रतिपूजिताः
transliteration: rājñaḥ pādau gṛhītvā tu rājñā te pratipūjitāḥ
english: Taking the feet of the sovereign, and honoured by him (in turn), they sat them down, some-on raised seats, some on cushions of Kusa, and some on the floor.

sanskrit: ते समेत्य सभायाम् वै राक्षसा राजशासनात्
transliteration: te sametya sabhāyām vai rākṣasā rājaśāsanāt
english: Presenting themselves agreeably to the command of the monarch, they sat them down each according to his position, before the lord of Raksasas, Ravana.

There came also the learned and competent to arrive at infallible decisions, and they sat them down in order of merit. And there also came courtiers endowed with virtues, versed in every thing, and having intelligence for their eye-sight, and innumerable heroes by hundreds also (arrived) at that court for ascertaining the course the would prove beneficial.

There came also the learned and competent to arrive at infallible decisions, and they sat them down in order of merit. And there also came courtiers endowed with virtues, versed in every thing, and having intelligence for their eye-sight, and innumerable heroes by hundreds also (arrived) at that court for ascertaining the course the would prove beneficial.
Then mounting a large, noble and splendid car, having its parts decked with gold, and yoked with horses, the magnanimous and renowned Vibhīşana went to the court of his elder brother.
That younger brother (of Rāvana), announcing his name, bowed down at the feet of his elder brother. And Śuka and Prahasta were employed in giving to each a separate seat befitting his rank.
From all sides in the court there began to spread the odour of excellent agura and sandal and wreaths belonging to the Räkşasas, decked in gold and various gems, and clad in costly attires.

And no one among these present at court uttered any thing, or spoke any falsehood, or conversed in loud accents. And having completely attained their desire, all of fierce prowess, gazed at the face of their lord.
In the assembly of those intelligent, and exceedingly powerful persons, equipped with arms, the intelligent Rāvaņa appeared splendid like the vaira-handed Indra among the Vasus.

sanskrit: स ताम् परिषदम् कृत्स्नाम् समीक्ष्य समितिम्जयः
transliteration: sa tām pariṣadam kṛtsnām samīkṣya samitimjayaḥ
english: Then surveying that entire assembly, that conqueror in battle delivered himself to Prahasta, general of the forces, saying.
O general, it behove you so to order the disciplined fourfold forces that they may successfully protect the city.
Thereat, Prahasta, carefully carrying out the royal behest, stationed all the forces within and without the city.

sanskrit: प्रहस्तः प्रमुखे राज्ञो निषसाद जगाद च
transliteration: prahastaḥ pramukhe rājño niṣasāda jagāda ca
english: Having posted the army for the defence of the city, Prahasta sitting down before the king, said.

I have stationed the forces belonging to you who are possessed of strength, inside as well as outside. (Now), without suffering your mind to be agitated with anxiety, speedily, do what is in your heart.

sanskrit: सुखेप्सुः सुहृदाम् मध्ये व्याजहार स रावणः
transliteration: sukhepsuḥ suhṛdām madhye vyājahāra sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Hearing the speech of Prahasta seeking the welfare of the kingdom, Rāvaņa craving for enjoyment, spoke in the midst of his aderents.
When virtue, or happiness, or interest is in straits, it behove you to (know your course) in relation to pleasant and unpleasant, happiness and misery, profitable and unprofitable, and good and evil.
No business of mine which you have set about after taking counsel, has miscarred.
Like Väsava environed by the moon, stars and planets and the Maruts, I surrounded by you, have attained to plenitude of prosperity.
I am, for certain, going to employ you all. In consequence of Kumbhakarņa's sleep, I could not inform him of this matter.

sanskrit: अयम् हि सुप्तः ष्ण्मासान् कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः
transliteration: ayam hi suptaḥ ṣṇmāsān kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
english: After having slept for six months that one of prodigious strength, foremost of those bearing arms, has just risen.
Janaka's daughter and Rāma's beloved wife has been brought hither from the forest of Dandaka, the region ranged by Raksasa.

sanskrit: त्रिषुलोकेषु चान्या मे न सीतासदृशी मता
transliteration: triṣulokeṣu cānyā me na sītāsadṛśī matā
english: That indolent damsel wish not to ascend my bed; nor is there any in the three spheres, that to me is like to Sītā.

She is slender waisted and high-hipped and her face is as the autumnal Moon resembling a golden image. She is meek and look like the hand work of Maya himself gifted with an infinite variety of fascinations.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा ताम्रनखौ तस्या दीप्यते मे शरीरजः
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā tāmranakhau tasyā dīpyate me śarīrajaḥ
english: And beholding her dainty and tender fect with roseate soles, and having coppery nails, my mind burn (with desire).

Seeing her resembling the flame of a sacrificial fire and the splendour of the Sun himself; and her fair face furnished with a prominent nose and elegant eyes, I, having lost control over self, have come under the sway of desire.

sanskrit: सा तु सम्वत्सरम् कालम् मामयाचत भामिनी
transliteration: sā tu samvatsaram kālam māmayācata bhāminī
english: And my passion, uninfluenced by anger and joy, capable of producing pallor, and constantly causing anguish and sorrow, has rendered me pale.
Expecting her lord, Rāma, the beautiful one having expansive eyes, has solicited for a year's space; and I have pledged my fair woods to her of graceful eyes.

But tired am I on account of my passion, like a horse spent on the way. How can the rangers of the woods, or the sons of Dasaratha cross over the sea ungovernable and swarming with countless creatures and fishes?

sanskrit: अथवा कपिनैकेन कृतम् नः कदनम् महत्
transliteration: athavā kapinaikena kṛtam naḥ kadanam mahat

sanskrit: मानुषान्नो भयम् नास्ति तथापि तु विमृश्यताम्
transliteration: mānuṣānno bhayam nāsti tathāpi tu vimṛśyatām
english: On the other hand, a single monkey has troubled us grievously. Hard it is therefore to understand the course of events. Do you act, each as he thinks proper, And although no fear come from mortals, yet you should deliberate (as to what you should do).

sanskrit: ते मे भवन्तश्च तथा सुग्रीवप्रमुखान् हरीन्
transliteration: te me bhavantaśca tathā sugrīvapramukhān harīn
english: Formerly, I had gained victory with the help given by you; do you in the same way stand by me now. The king's son, having learnt that Sita can is on the other shore of the ocean, taking before them monkey headed by Sugriva, reached Varuna's abode.

Formerly, I had gained victory with the help given by you; do you in the same way stand by me now. The king's son, having learnt that Sita can is on the other shore of the ocean, taking before them monkey headed by Sugriva, reached Varuna's abode.

sanskrit: अदेया च यथा सीता वध्यौ दशरथात्मजौ
transliteration: adeyā ca yathā sītā vadhyau daśarathātmajau
english: Do you so counsel that Sītã may be withholden by me and the sons of Dasaratha may be slain; but you must prefer certain counsel. No other* person in this world has the power to cross the sea along with the monkeys, victory, therefore, is undubitably mine." *I fail to understand anyasya, "no other person" nor does the commentator helps me anyway.

sanskrit: न हि शक्तिम् प्रपश्यामि जगत्यन्यस्य कस्यचित्
transliteration: na hi śaktim prapaśyāmi jagatyanyasya kasyacit
english: Do you so counsel that Sītã may be withholden by me and the sons of Dasaratha may be slain; but you must prefer certain counsel. No other* person in this world has the power to cross the sea along with the monkeys, victory, therefore, is undubitably mine." *I fail to understand anyasya, "no other person" nor does the commentator helps me anyway.
Hearing the sorrowful speech of (Rāvana) afflicted with lust, Kumbhakarma grew enraged, . and said.

When just on seeing (Sītā) of Rāma along with Lakşmaņa, you did by main force carry away, it plainly appear that your mind, like the Yamunā filling her bed, has been possessed by her).* *This passage very obscure, and the commentator's gloss does not at all serve.
O great king! all this (that you have done) is not worthy of you. If you had at the outset consulted us in this matter, we would have done what was proper. *i.e. we would have prevented you.
O ten-faced one, the king, that arriving at certain conclusions, carry on his regal affairs agreeably to justice, has not to repent afterwards.
But those actions that are done without deliberation, like to clarified butter poured in an impure sacrifice, conducted only to harma.

sanskrit: पूर्वम् चापरकर्याणि न स वेद नयानयौ
transliteration: pūrvam cāparakaryāṇi na sa veda nayānayau
english: He does not know what is proper and what not, that performs prior actions afterwards, and posterior actions first.
Others spy holes in the actions of the volatile, the latter may be possessed of great power, like swans passing Krauñca through the hole. * *The hole made by the dart of Kumāra.
By luck it is that Rāma has not yet slain you, who has done this tremendous thing, with poison.
But as you have entered upon a course of action which is improper even in respect of foes, I will, O sinless one, perform your work by slaying your enemies.
O ranger of the night, I will exterminate your foe. Even if Sakra and the sun, even if fire and the War-god, even if Kubera and Varuna, should range themselves against me, I will fight them.
Purandara himself shall be afflicted with fright when I having my body measuring a mountain, and furnished with sharp teeth, shall, setting up roars, fight with my huge bludgeon.
Be you comforted by slaying Daſaratha's son, I will exert to secure blessed victory for you. Having killed Rāma along with Lakşmaņa, I shall devour all the principal monkeys.

Do you make merry at your will, drink the Vāruņi, and, with your mind set at rest, conduct affairs fraught with your welfare. On Rāma being despatched to the mansion of Yama, Sītā shall come under your subjection for ever and a day.
Seeing Ravana wrought up with wrath, the exceedingly strong Mahāpārsva, reflecting for a moment, observed with joined hands.

sanskrit: न पिबेन्मधु सम्प्राप्य स नरो बालिशो ध्रुवम्
transliteration: na pibenmadhu samprāpya sa naro bāliśo dhruvam
english: The man that, entering the forest, abounding with deer and ferocious animals, does not drink honey, make a fool of himself.
O destroyer of foes, who is the lord of you, that are lord yourself? Enjoy with Vaidehi, taking your enemy by the hand.

sanskrit: अक्रम्याक्रम्य सीताम् वै ताम् भुङिक्स्व च रमस्व च
transliteration: akramyākramya sītām vai tām bhuṅiksva ca ramasva ca
english: O you endowed with prodigious power, do you exerting your might lead your life, after the manner of hens, and invading Sītā again and again, do you enjoy her and derive pleasure (therefrom).
When you have attained your purpose; what fear can succeed? Alike when on your guard, and off it, you shall provide against all exigencies.
Kumbhakarņa along with us, as well the exceedingly powerful Indrajit, are competent to chastise the thunder-bearing (Deity) equipped with his thunder.

sanskrit: उपप्रदानम् सान्त्वम् वा भेदम् वा कुशलैः कृतम्
transliteration: upapradānam sāntvam vā bhedam vā kuśalaiḥ kṛtam
english: Passing by gift, conciliation, and dissension, which have been as signed by the wise as the means of success, I relish the success in business which is attained through chastisement.
O highly powerful one, we shall, without doubt, by the prowess of our arms, subdue all these enemies of your that have come hither.
Thus addressed by Mahāpārsva, king Rāvana, honouring his speech, said.

O Mahāparáva, I will relate to you, who have spoken (thus), a secret matter relating to myself, which befell me long since I saw Puñjikasthală, like a flame in the sky, coursing to the Greatfather's mansion.

sanskrit: सा प्रसह्य मया भुक्ता कृता विवसना ततः
transliteration: sā prasahya mayā bhuktā kṛtā vivasanā tataḥ
english: Her pace slackened, as soon as she saw me, (turn) I feasted on her and deprived her of her attire. Then she went to the Great-father's place, like a crumpled lotus.
That high-souled one received information of all that I had done; and thereat, waxing enraged, the Deity spoke to me.

sanskrit: तदा ते शतधा मुर्धा फलिष्यति न सम्शयः
transliteration: tadā te śatadhā murdhā phaliṣyati na samśayaḥ
english: If from this day, you ravish a female by force, your head certainly shall be riven in an hundred pieces.

sanskrit: इत्यहम् तस्य शापस्य भीतः प्रसभमेव ताम्
transliteration: ityaham tasya śāpasya bhītaḥ prasabhameva tām
english: It is for this, that with my mind afflicted with fear, I do not violently force, Videha's daughter Sītā, anent lying with her fair self.

sanskrit: सागरस्येव मे वेगो मारुतस्येव मे गतिः
transliteration: sāgarasyeva me vego mārutasyeva me gatiḥ
english: My rush is like that of the sea, and my motion that of the wind. Dasaratha's son does not know this, and therefore does he approach sea.
Who wish to address a lion that is lying asleep in a cave, resembling Death wrought up by wrath?

sanskrit: न मत्तो निर्गतान् बाणान् द्विजिह्वान् पन्न्गानिव
transliteration: na matto nirgatān bāṇān dvijihvān panngāniva
english: Răma has not seen shafts shot by me, resembling two-tongued serpents, and therefore, it is that he approach me.
Like a meteor burning an elephant, I shall, with shafts shot from bow in hundreds, resembling the thunder-bolt, consume Rāma.
As at the proper hour the risen Sun defeat the splendour of the stars, will I, surrounded by a mighty army, overpower his strength.
Neither the thousand-eyed Vasava, nor yet Varuņa, is capable of fighting me. By the might of this arm did I formerly conquer this city, governed by Vaiśravana.
Hearing the words of the lord of Rākşasas, as well as the thundering of Kumbhakarņa, Vibhīşaņa addressed the Rākşasa chief, in a pregnant speech, fraught with his welfare.
You have been bound about your neck by the mighty and huge serpent, Sītā, having her breast for its body anxiety for its venom, smile for its sharp fangs, and her five fingers for its hood.
Therefore before the monkeys, resembling mountain peaks, having teeth for their arms and nails, for their weapons, subjugate Lankā, do you render Maithili to Dasaratha's son.

Before the shafts shot by Ráma, resembling the thunder-bolt and having impetuosity of the wind, cut off the heads of the foremost of the Rākșasas, do you render Mithila's daughter to the son of Dasaratha.
Neither Kumbhakarņa nor Indrajit, neither Mahāparáva nor Mahodara, neither Nikumbha nor Kumbha nor yet Atikāya, O king, can stay in the field against Rāghava.
Living, you, whether you are protected by the Sun or the winds, or throw yourself into the lap itself of Vāsava, or enter the sky or the nether spheres, shall not escape death.

sanskrit: न नो भयम् विद्म न दैवतेभ्यो
transliteration: na no bhayam vidma na daivatebhyo
english: Hearing Vibhisana's words, Prahasta said, Fear know we none whatever from the celestials, or Danavas, or Yaksas, or Gandharvas, or huge snakes; fear know we none in battle with birds and serpents. How can fear at all afflict us proceeding from the king's son, Rāma?

Hearing Vibhisana's words, Prahasta said, Fear know we none whatever from the celestials, or Danavas, or Yaksas, or Gandharvas, or huge snakes; fear know we none in battle with birds and serpents. How can fear at all afflict us proceeding from the king's son, Rāma?
Hearing Prahasta's speech, Vibhisana, seeking the welfare of the king, and having his intellect grounded in virtue, interest and profit, said words enfolding high sense.
O Prahasta, like a sinful person being unable to ascend heaven what the king, Mahodara, you, and Kumbhakarņa, are saying with reference to Rāma, shall not prove true.
As one without a raft cannot cross over the mighty main, how can I, or you, or all the Raksasa combined, cause death to Rāma, who, O Prahasta, is versed in the sense of things.

Even the gods become stolid before the sovereign of the Ikşvāku race, having righteousness for his principle quality, and being a mighty car-warrior and of such a character, and who is competent in action.
As yet the Kaňka-feathered, terrible and sharp shafts shot by Raghava, have not pierced into your body; and therefore you did speak so.
And neither Devāntaka nor Narāntaka, neither Atikāya, nor the magnanimous Atiratha, nor the equally strong Akampana, is competent to stay Rāghava in fight.
The king, naturally of fierce temper and thoughtless, through the instrumentality of you who appearing to be his friends are in reality his foes, seek to destroy the Rākşasas.
Do you take out and deliver the monarch, who has through force become subject to a dreadful and mighty, and thousand-headed serpent bursting with immeasurable prowess.
As a person possessed by fearfully strong ghosts, is saved by his friends pulling him by his hair, attaining your desire you desire you should, assembling together, rescuer the king.
This one is sunk in the Rāghava sea having excellent waters. He (the king) has fallen into the Kākutstha neither regions. Do you speedily coming together deliver him.
I tell you my full mind, fraught with the welfare of this city together with the Rākṣasas, as well of the king with his adherents. Do you make over Maithili to the son of the king.
He is a true counsellor who advises his master, after duly ascertaining the strength, position, increase or destruction of the enemies as well as of their own party.
Hearing carefully the words of Vibhīşaņa, gifted with the intelligence of the lord of speech, the high-souled Indrajit, the leader of demons, spoke, saying.

sanskrit: किम् नाम ते तात कनिष्ठ वाक्य
transliteration: kim nāma te tāta kaniṣṭha vākya
english: Why are you, O uncle, speaking these useless words like one terrified? He even, who is not born in this race, cannot speak or act in this wise.

sanskrit: सत्त्वेन वीर्येण पराक्रमेणधैर्येण शौर्येण च तेजसा च
transliteration: sattvena vīryeṇa parākrameṇadhairyeṇa śauryeṇa ca tejasā ca
english: Only one man in this family, my uncle Vibhisana, is weak in energy, strength, prowess, patience, heroism and vigour.
Why are you O timid one, afraid of them since any one of these Rākṣasas is capable of slaying those two princes, human beings as they are?
The master of the three worlds, the lord of the celestials, has been brought down by me as captive on this earth. And all the celestials smitten with fear fled to different quarters.
I brought down on earth the loud-roaring celestial elephant Airavata and uprooted by force its tusks. And all the celestials were terrified at this.

Am I not, who have shattered the pride of the celestials, afflicted the leading Daityas, and am gifted with excellent prowess, capable of discomfiting these two princess-very ordinary mortals as they are?

Hearing the words of (Indrajit) gifted with high energy irrepressible and resembling the lord of celestials, Vibhisana, the foremost of those using weapons, addressed him with words, fraught with high import.

O my son, you are a mere child and of unripe intellect and hence you are not capable of as certaining the propriety and impropriety of counsels. You are therefore speaking thus like a maniac for your own destruction.
You are known as a son to Ravana, O Indrajit, but in sooth, you are his foe in disguise, since knowing of his destruction from Rāghava, you did not prevent him.
You are brave, childish and have been impelled by your silly understanding. You shall be slain along with him who has brought you in this counsel chamber.

You are, O Indrajit, foolish, imprudent, devoid of humility, of an irritable temper, of feeble sense, vicious-minded and of a silly understanding. And you did speak so, being impelled by childishness.
Who shall withstand in battle, the shafts, shot by Raghava, resembling the rod of Death, the stick of Brahmā, flaming like the Fire of Dissolution.

sanskrit: अब्रवीत् परुषम् वाक्यम् रावणः काल चोदितः
transliteration: abravīt paruṣam vākyam rāvaṇaḥ kāla coditaḥ
english: Vibhīşaņa addressing him with these excellent and auspicious words, fraught with high sense, Rāvaņa, impelled by Death, again spoke in harsh accents.

sanskrit: वसेत् सह सपत्नेन क्रुद्धेन आशी विषेण च
न तु मित्र प्रवादेन सम्वस्च्चत्रुणा सह
transliteration: vaset saha sapatnena kruddhena āśī viṣeṇa ca
na tu mitra pravādena samvasccatruṇā saha
english: It is better to live with open enemies or enraged serpents than with those who pass for friends but are in reality foes.

sanskrit: जानामि शीलम् ज्ञातीनाम् सर्व लोकेषु राक्षस
transliteration: jānāmi śīlam jñātīnām sarva lokeṣu rākṣasa
english: I know well the nature of kinsmen, in all the worlds, O Raksasas, one takes delight in another's misfortune.

sanskrit: प्रधानम् साधकम् वैद्यम् धर्म शीलम् च राक्षस
transliteration: pradhānam sādhakam vaidyam dharma śīlam ca rākṣasa
english: The kinsmen, O Raksasa, generally disregard him who is their king, * protects the kingdom, educated and pious-and they always try to discomfit him, if he be a heroe. *On account of the priority of his birth,

sanskrit: प्रच्चन्न हृदया घोरा ज्ञातयस् तु भय आवहाः
transliteration: praccanna hṛdayā ghorā jñātayas tu bhaya āvahāḥ
english: These terrible enemies-the kinsmen, hypocrite as they are, always take delight in one another's calamity.

sanskrit: श्रूयन्ते हस्तिभिर् गीताः श्लोकाः पद्म वने पुरा
पाश हस्तान् नरान् दृष्ट्वा शृणु तान् गदतो मम
transliteration: śrūyante hastibhir gītāḥ ślokāḥ padma vane purā
pāśa hastān narān dṛṣṭvā śṛṇu tān gadato mama
english: Hear, I shall relate what elephants, in yore, spoke beholding some persons with noose in hand-We do not fear, fire, weapons, or even the terrible noose-we fear only the dreadful kinsmen, blinded with selfishness.

sanskrit: नाग्निर्नान्यानि शस्त्राणि न नः पाशा भयावहाः
transliteration: nāgnirnānyāni śastrāṇi na naḥ pāśā bhayāvahāḥ
english: Hear, I shall relate what elephants, in yore, spoke beholding some persons with noose in hand-We do not fear, fire, weapons, or even the terrible noose-we fear only the dreadful kinsmen, blinded with selfishness.

sanskrit: कृत्स्नाद् भयाज्ज्ञातिभयम् सुकष्टम् विदितम् च नः
transliteration: kṛtsnād bhayājjñātibhayam sukaṣṭam viditam ca naḥ
english: They alone unfold the means of our detection, there is not the least doubt about it. Fear from kinsmen is therefore known as the worst of all fears.

sanskrit: विद्यते गोषु सम्पन्नम् विद्यते ज्ञातितो भयम्
विद्यते स्त्रीषु चापल्यम् विद्यते ज्ञातितो भयम्
transliteration: vidyate goṣu sampannam vidyate jñātito bhayam
vidyate strīṣu cāpalyam vidyate jñātito bhayam
english: In kine there is milk, in kinsmen, there is fear, in women there is fickleness, and in Brahmanas, there is asceticism.

sanskrit: ततो नेष्टम् इदम् सौम्य यदहम् लोक सत्कृतः
ऐश्वर्यम् अभिजातः च रिपूणाम् मूर्ध्नि च स्थितः
transliteration: tato neṣṭam idam saumya yadaham loka satkṛtaḥ
aiśvaryam abhijātaḥ ca ripūṇām mūrdhni ca sthitaḥ
english: It does not please you, I fancy, O gentle one, that I am honoured of the three worlds, the lord of riches, and the subduer of my foes.
As the drops of water do not last long on the leaves of lotuses, so is the friendship with unworthy persons.
As the autumnal clouds, albeit muttering, do not pour forth water, so is the friendship with unworthy persons.
As a bee flies away after sucking up the honey so is the friendship with unworthy persons.
As a bee, after feeding uport the Kāśa flowers, does not get honey so is (fruitless) the friendship with unworthy persons.

sanskrit: यथा पूर्वम् गजः स्नात्वा गृह्य हस्तेन वै रजः
transliteration: yathā pūrvam gajaḥ snātvā gṛhya hastena vai rajaḥ
english: As an elephant, after being bathed, covers its body again with dust, taking it with its trunk, so is the friendship with unworthy persons.* *They afterwards forsake their former friends.

sanskrit: अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते न भवेत् त्वाम् तु धिक् कुलपाम्सनम्
transliteration: asmin muhūrte na bhavet tvām tu dhik kulapāmsanam
english: Fie you, O night ranger, O you that bring disgrace on the family. Had any one else spoken thus he would have ceased to live by this time.
Being thus accosted harshly, Vibhisana, speaking truth, rose up along with four Rākṣasas having maces in their hands.
There upon, rising up in the welkin, the graceful brother Vibhisana, worked up with ire, addressed the lord of Rāshasas.

sanskrit: स त्वम् भ्राता असि मे राजन् ब्रूहि माम् यद् यद् इच्चसि
ज्येष्ठो मान्यः पितृसमो न च धर्मपथे स्थितः
transliteration: sa tvam bhrātā asi me rājan brūhi mām yad yad iccasi
jyeṣṭho mānyaḥ pitṛsamo na ca dharmapathe sthitaḥ
english: You are mistaken, O king. Do you speak what you wish, you are my elder brother, adorable like to father-you did not follow the track of virtue. I cannot tolerate the harsh accents of you, my elder brother.

sanskrit: इदम् तु परुषम् वाक्यम् न क्षमामि अनृतम् तव
सुनीतम् हित कामेन वाक्यम् उक्तम् दश आनन
transliteration: idam tu paruṣam vākyam na kṣamāmi anṛtam tava
sunītam hita kāmena vākyam uktam daśa ānana

sanskrit: न गृह्णन्ति अकृत आत्मानः कालस्य वशमागताः
सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन् सततम् प्रिय वादिनः
transliteration: na gṛhṇanti akṛta ātmānaḥ kālasya vaśamāgatāḥ
sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājan satatam priya vādinaḥ

sanskrit: अप्रियस्य तु पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः
बद्धम् कालस्य पाशेन सर्व भूत अपहारिणा
transliteration: apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ
baddham kālasya pāśena sarva bhūta apahāriṇā

sanskrit: न नश्यन्तम् उपेक्षेयम् प्रदीप्तम् शरणम् यथा
दीप्त पावक सम्काशैः शितैः कान्चन भूषणैः
transliteration: na naśyantam upekṣeyam pradīptam śaraṇam yathā
dīpta pāvaka samkāśaiḥ śitaiḥ kāncana bhūṣaṇaiḥ

sanskrit: न त्वाम् इच्चामि अहम् द्रष्टुम् रामेण निहतम् शरैः
शूराः च बलवन्तः च कृत अस्त्राः च नर आजिरे
transliteration: na tvām iccāmi aham draṣṭum rāmeṇa nihatam śaraiḥ
śūrāḥ ca balavantaḥ ca kṛta astrāḥ ca nara ājire

sanskrit: काल अभिपन्ना सीदन्ति यथा वालुक सेतवः
transliteration: kāla abhipannā sīdanti yathā vāluka setavaḥ

sanskrit: आत्मानम् सर्वथा रक्ष पुरीम् च इमाम् सराक्षसाम्
स्वस्ति ते अस्तु गमिष्यामि सुखी भव मया विना
transliteration: ātmānam sarvathā rakṣa purīm ca imām sarākṣasām
svasti te astu gamiṣyāmi sukhī bhava mayā vinā
english: You are worshipful to me, do you forgive me for what I have said for your welfare. Do you protect yourself and this city, abounding in Raksasas. May good betide you! I am going away and do you be happy without me.

sanskrit: न रोचते ते वचनम् निशा चर
परीत काला हि गत आयुषो नरा
transliteration: na rocate te vacanam niśā cara
parīta kālā hi gata āyuṣo narā
english: What, I spoke to you, O ranger of the night, to prevent you, for your welfare, did not please you. Persons, whose lease of life is well-nigh expired, do not pay heed to the well-meaning words of their friends.

sanskrit: इति उक्त्वा परुषम् वाक्यम् रावणम् रावण अनुजः
transliteration: iti uktvā paruṣam vākyam rāvaṇam rāvaṇa anujaḥ
english: Having addressed Rāvana with these harsh words, his younger brother, reached in no time, where Rāma along with Lakṣmaṇa was.

sanskrit: तम् मेरु शिखर आकारम् दीप्ताम् इव शत ह्रदाम्
गगनस्थम् महीस्थास् ते ददृशुर् वानर अधिपाः
transliteration: tam meru śikhara ākāram dīptām iva śata hradām
gaganastham mahīsthās te dadṛśur vānara adhipāḥ
english: The leading monkeys, stationed on earth, espied him on the welkin, resembling in size the summit of the mount Meru, and burning like lightning in the effulgence of his own person.
And his four attendants of terrible prowess were adorned with excellent ornaments and armed with armours and maces.
He was like to a collection of clouds, powerful as the thunder-bolt, holding an excellent mace, heroic and embellished with excellent ornaments.

sanskrit: तम् आत्म पन्चमम् दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवो वानर अधिपः
वानरैः सह दुर्धर्षः चिन्तयाम् आस बुद्धिमान्
transliteration: tam ātma pancamam dṛṣṭvā sugrīvo vānara adhipaḥ
vānaraiḥ saha durdharṣaḥ cintayām āsa buddhimān
english: Beholding him along with four counsellors, the highly intelligent Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, engaged in meditation along with them.

sanskrit: चिन्तयित्वा मुहूर्तम् तु वानराम्स् तान् उवाच ह
हनूमत् प्रमुखान् सर्वान् इदम् वचनम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: cintayitvā muhūrtam tu vānarāms tān uvāca ha
hanūmat pramukhān sarvān idam vacanam uttamam
english: And meditating for a while, he spoke to the monkeys headed by Hanuman the following excellent words.

sanskrit: एष सर्व आयुध उपेतः चतुर्भिः सह राक्षसैः
राक्षसो अभ्येति पश्यध्वम् अस्मान् हन्तुम् न सम्शयः
transliteration: eṣa sarva āyudha upetaḥ caturbhiḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ
rākṣaso abhyeti paśyadhvam asmān hantum na samśayaḥ
english: Behold, there comes a Rākşasa, armed with various weapons and followed by four demons to slay us and there is not the least doubt about it.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वे ते वानर उत्तमाः
सालान् उद्यम्य शैलामः च इदम् वचनम् अब्रुवन्
transliteration: sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve te vānara uttamāḥ
sālān udyamya śailāmaḥ ca idam vacanam abruvan
english: And hearing the words of Sugrīva, the excellent monkeys, taking up huge trees and crages, bespoke him.

sanskrit: शीघ्रम् व्यादिश नो राजन् वधाय एषाम् दुरात्मनाम्
निपतन्तु हताः च एते धरण्याम् अल्प जीविताः
transliteration: śīghram vyādiśa no rājan vadhāya eṣām durātmanām
nipatantu hatāḥ ca ete dharaṇyām alpa jīvitāḥ
english: Do you order us, O king, to destroy these vicious-souled demons. These shall crush them to death, limited as is the tenure of their life.

sanskrit: उत्तरम् तीरम् आसाद्य खस्थ एव व्यतिष्ठत
transliteration: uttaram tīram āsādya khastha eva vyatiṣṭhata
english: They addressing each other in this wise, Vibhīşaņa descended from the sky on the northern shore.

sanskrit: स उवाच च महाप्राज्ञः स्वरेण महता महान्
सुग्रीवम् तामः च सम्प्रेक्ष्य खस्थ एव विभीषणः
transliteration: sa uvāca ca mahāprājñaḥ svareṇa mahatā mahān
sugrīvam tāmaḥ ca samprekṣya khastha eva vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: And beholdings Sugrīva and all others stationed near him, the highly intelligent Vibhīşaņa accosted them, at the highest pitch of his voice, saying.

sanskrit: रावणो नाम दुर्वृत्तो राक्षसो राक्षस ईश्वरः
तस्य अहम् अनुजो भ्राता विभीषण इति श्रुतः
transliteration: rāvaṇo nāma durvṛtto rākṣaso rākṣasa īśvaraḥ
tasya aham anujo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇa iti śrutaḥ
english: There lives a Raksasa, named Ravana, the lord of demons, and perpetrator of many iniquitous deeds. I am his younger brother known as Vibhişaņa.

sanskrit: तेन सीता जन स्थानाद्द् हृता हत्वा जटायुषम्
रुद्ध्वा च विवशा दीना राक्षसीभिः सुरक्षिता
transliteration: tena sītā jana sthānādd hṛtā hatvā jaṭāyuṣam
ruddhvā ca vivaśā dīnā rākṣasībhiḥ surakṣitā
english: By him, slaying the vulture Jatayu, was carried away Sītā from Janasthana. She is imprisoned, brought under his sway, poorly, and being well guarded by the Rakşasees.

sanskrit: तम् अहम् हेतुभिर् वाक्यैर् विविधैः च न्यदर्शयम्
साधु निर्यात्यताम् सीता रामाय इति पुनः पुनः
transliteration: tam aham hetubhir vākyair vividhaiḥ ca nyadarśayam
sādhu niryātyatām sītā rāmāya iti punaḥ punaḥ
english: With various well meaning words and reasonings I pointed out to him, the necessity of rendering back Sītā to Rāma.

sanskrit: स च न प्रतिजग्राह रावणः काल चोदितः
उच्यमानो हितम् वाक्यम् विपरीत इव औषधम्
transliteration: sa ca na pratijagrāha rāvaṇaḥ kāla coditaḥ
ucyamāno hitam vākyam viparīta iva auṣadham
english: And Ravana, possessed by Death, paid no heed to my well-meaning words, like to one, lying on the brink of death, neglecting the administration of medicine.

sanskrit: सो अहम् परुषितस् तेन दासवच् च अवमानितः
त्यक्त्वा पुत्रामः च दारामः च राघवम् शरणम् गतः
transliteration: so aham paruṣitas tena dāsavac ca avamānitaḥ
tyaktvā putrāmaḥ ca dārāmaḥ ca rāghavam śaraṇam gataḥ
english: Being reviled by him and treated harshly like a menial, I have come to seek Rāghava's shelter, renouncing my children and wives.
Do you soon mention to the high-souled Rāghava, the refuge of all creatures, that Vibhīşaņa has arrived.

sanskrit: एतत्तु वचनम् श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो लघु विक्रमः
लक्ष्मणस्य अग्रतो रामम् सम्रब्धम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: etattu vacanam śrutvā sugrīvo laghu vikramaḥ
lakṣmaṇasya agrato rāmam samrabdham idam abravīt
english: Hearing those words the quick-paced Sugrīva, excited with ire, spoke to Rāma, before Laksmana, saying.

sanskrit: प्रविष्टः शत्रु सैन्यम् हि प्राप्तः शत्रुरतर्कितः
transliteration: praviṣṭaḥ śatru sainyam hi prāptaḥ śatruratarkitaḥ
english: Forsooth has an enemy entered secretly in our midst and he shall slay us getting an opportunity like to an owl killing the crows.

sanskrit: मन्त्रे व्यूहे नये चारे युक्तो भवितुमर्हसि
वानराणाम् च भद्रम् ते परेषाम् च परम्तप
transliteration: mantre vyūhe naye cāre yukto bhavitumarhasi
vānarāṇām ca bhadram te pareṣām ca paramtapa
english: O slayer of foes, it now behove you to be particularly careful about the counsels, arrangement of soldiers, polity-civil and military and spies of our own party as well as those of the enemies.

sanskrit: शूराश्च निकृतिज्ञाश्च तेषाम् जातु न विश्वसेत्
transliteration: śūrāśca nikṛtijñāśca teṣām jātu na viśvaset
english: These Rākşasas are heroic; they assume shapes at will, always lie in ambush and secretly bring about others' ruin-we should not therefore place confidence in them.

sanskrit: अनुप्रविश्य सोऽ स्मासु भेदम् कुर्यान्न सम्शयः
transliteration: anupraviśya so' smāsu bhedam kuryānna samśayaḥ
english: This must be the emissary of Rāvaņa-the lord of Raksasas. Entering in our midst, he shall, in sooth, sow dissensions in our camp, or he shall slay us when we are careless, confiding in them.
This must be the emissary of Rāvaņa-the lord of Raksasas. Entering in our midst, he shall, in sooth, sow dissensions in our camp, or he shall slay us when we are careless, confiding in them.
Avoiding the enemies, we should now collect the forest-rangers our friends and servants.

sanskrit: प्रकृत्या राक्षसो ह्येष भ्रातामित्रस्य वै प्रभो
transliteration: prakṛtyā rākṣaso hyeṣa bhrātāmitrasya vai prabho
english: O lord, this man is a Rākşasa by birth and the brother of our foe and so is he our enemy, how can we trust him?

sanskrit: रावणस्य अनुजो भ्राता विभीषण इति श्रुतः
चतुर्भिः सह रक्षोभिर् भवन्तम् शरणम् गतः
transliteration: rāvaṇasya anujo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇa iti śrutaḥ
caturbhiḥ saha rakṣobhir bhavantam śaraṇam gataḥ
english: Ravana's younger brother, known Vibilisana, uc come here with four Raksasas, to seck your shelter.

sanskrit: तस्य अहम् निग्रहम् मन्ये क्षमम् क्षमवताम् वर
transliteration: tasya aham nigraham manye kṣamam kṣamavatām vara
english: O you the foremost of forgiving persons, I consider this Vibhīşaņa, who has been despatched by Ravana, worthy of being slain. as

sanskrit: राक्षसो जिह्मया बुद्ध्या सम्दिष्टो अयम् उपस्थितः
प्रहर्तुम् मायया चन्नो विश्वस्ते त्वयि राघव
transliteration: rākṣaso jihmayā buddhyā samdiṣṭo ayam upasthitaḥ
prahartum māyayā canno viśvaste tvayi rāghava
english: Being impelled by his wicked intention and commissioned by Rävaņa, this Rākşasa has come here and secretly by virtue of his illusive powers he shall slay you, O innocent one, when you shall place confidence in him.

sanskrit: बध्यताम् एष तीव्रेण दण्डेन सचिवैः सह
रावणस्य नृशम्सस्य भ्राता हि एष विभीषणः
transliteration: badhyatām eṣa tīvreṇa daṇḍena sacivaiḥ saha
rāvaṇasya nṛśamsasya bhrātā hi eṣa vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Being impelled by his wicked intention and commissioned by Rävaņa, this Rākşasa has come here and secretly by virtue of his illusive powers he shall slay you, O innocent one, when you shall place confidence in him.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा तु तम् रामम् सम्रब्धो वाहिनी पतिः
वाक्यज्ञो वाक्य कुशलम् ततो मौनम् उपागमत्
transliteration: evam uktvā tu tam rāmam samrabdho vāhinī patiḥ
vākyajño vākya kuśalam tato maunam upāgamat
english: Having thus accosted Rāma, skilled in the are of speech, that lord of the army, Sugriva, well versed in speech, became silent.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवस्य तु तद् वाक्यम् श्रुत्वा रामो महाबलः
समीपस्थान् उवाच इदम् हनूमत् प्रमुखान् हरीन्
transliteration: sugrīvasya tu tad vākyam śrutvā rāmo mahābalaḥ
samīpasthān uvāca idam hanūmat pramukhān harīn
english: And hearing the words of Sugrīva, the mighty Rāma spoke to the monkeys, near him, headed by Hanumān, saying.

sanskrit: यद् उक्तम् कपि राजेन रावण अवरजम् प्रति
वाक्यम् हेतुमद् अत्यर्थम् भवद्भिर् अपि तत् श्रुतम्
transliteration: yad uktam kapi rājena rāvaṇa avarajam prati
vākyam hetumad atyartham bhavadbhir api tat śrutam
english: You have all heard, the words well grounded in reason, the lord of monkeys has said, regarding Rāvana's younger brother.

sanskrit: सुहृदा हि अर्थ कृच्चेषु युक्तम् बुद्धिमता सता
समर्थेन अपि सम्देष्टुम् शाश्वतीम् भूतिम् इच्चता
transliteration: suhṛdā hi artha kṛcceṣu yuktam buddhimatā satā
samarthena api samdeṣṭum śāśvatīm bhūtim iccatā
english: It behove him, who desires for perpetual wealth, and is intelligent and capable of giving sound counsels, to advise his friends in difficult matters.

sanskrit: इति एवम् परिपृष्टास् ते स्वम् स्वम् मतम् अतन्द्रिताः
स उपचारम् तदा रामम् ऊचुर् हित चिकीर्षवः
transliteration: iti evam paripṛṣṭās te svam svam matam atandritāḥ
sa upacāram tadā rāmam ūcur hita cikīrṣavaḥ
english: Being thus addressed by Rāma (to minister to him best counsels) all those monkeys, intent upon encompassing his well-being, gave out their respective opinions.

sanskrit: अज्ञातम् न अस्ति ते किम्चित् त्रिषु लोकेषु राघव
आत्मानम् पूजयन् राम पृच्चसि अस्मान् सुहृत्तया
transliteration: ajñātam na asti te kimcit triṣu lokeṣu rāghava
ātmānam pūjayan rāma pṛccasi asmān suhṛttayā
english: O Rāghava, there is nothing beyond your knowledge in the three worlds. It is only to show your respect towards us; O Răma, that you did accost us in this wise.

sanskrit: त्वम् हि सत्य व्रतः शूरो धार्मिको दृढ विक्रमः
परीक्ष्य कारा स्मृतिमान् निसृष्ट आत्मा सुहृत्सु च
transliteration: tvam hi satya vrataḥ śūro dhārmiko dṛḍha vikramaḥ
parīkṣya kārā smṛtimān nisṛṣṭa ātmā suhṛtsu ca
english: You are of truthful vows, heroic, pious, of firm prowess, discriminating, recollecting and having implicit confidence in your friends.

sanskrit: तस्माद् एक एकशस् तावद् ब्रुवन्तु सचिवास् तव
हेतुतो मति सम्पन्नाः समर्थाः च पुनः पुनः
transliteration: tasmād eka ekaśas tāvad bruvantu sacivās tava
hetuto mati sampannāḥ samarthāḥ ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Let the intelligent and capable counsellors deliver their reasonable opinions to you.

sanskrit: इति उक्ते राघवाय अथ मतिमान् अन्गदो अग्रतः
विभीषण परीक्षा अर्थम् उवाच वचनम् हरिः
transliteration: iti ukte rāghavāya atha matimān angado agrataḥ
vibhīṣaṇa parīkṣā artham uvāca vacanam hariḥ
