english: They speaking thus to Rāghava, the intelligent monkey Angada, spoke as follows for sounding the intention of Vibhīşaņa.

sanskrit: शत्रोः सकाशात् सम्प्राप्तः सर्वथा शन्क्य एव हि
विश्वास योग्यः सहसा न कर्तव्यो विभीषणः
transliteration: śatroḥ sakāśāt samprāptaḥ sarvathā śankya eva hi
viśvāsa yogyaḥ sahasā na kartavyo vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: We should always suspect him since he has come from the side of our enemies, and should not, all on a sudden, place confidence in him.

sanskrit: चादयित्वा आत्म भावम् हि चरन्ति शठ बुद्धयः
प्रहरन्ति च रन्ध्रेषु सो अनर्थः सुमहान् भवेत्
transliteration: cādayitvā ātma bhāvam hi caranti śaṭha buddhayaḥ
praharanti ca randhreṣu so anarthaḥ sumahān bhavet
english: The wicked-minded always move about hiding their real self, and bring about peoples' calamity, taking advantage of their weak points. And great is the disaster thereof.

sanskrit: अर्थ अनर्थौ विनिश्चित्य व्यवसायम् भजेत ह
गुणतः सम्ग्रहम् कुर्याद् दोषतस् तु विसर्जयेत्
transliteration: artha anarthau viniścitya vyavasāyam bhajeta ha
guṇataḥ samgraham kuryād doṣatas tu visarjayet
english: It is always proper to engage in actions, considering what is right and what is wrong. Virtues should always be gathered and vices abondoned.

sanskrit: यदि दोषो महाम्स् तस्मिम्स् त्यज्यताम् अविशन्कितम्
गुणान् वा अपि बहून् ज्ञात्वा सम्ग्रहः क्रियताम् नृप
transliteration: yadi doṣo mahāms tasmims tyajyatām aviśankitam
guṇān vā api bahūn jñātvā samgrahaḥ kriyatām nṛpa
english: Do you renounce him unhesitatingly, if did you find in him a source of a great calamity and do you embrace him if did you find him crowned with many virtues.

sanskrit: शरभस् त्व् अथ निश्चित्य सार्थम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
क्षिप्रम् अस्मिन् नर व्याघ्र चारः प्रतिविधीयताम्
transliteration: śarabhas tv atha niścitya sārtham vacanam abravīt
kṣipram asmin nara vyāghra cāraḥ pratividhīyatām
english: There upon followed Sarava with words fraught with high import, best of men, do you speedily despatch emissaries to sound Vibhis ana.

sanskrit: प्रणिधाय हि चारेण यथावत् सूक्ष्म बुद्धिना
परीक्ष्य च ततः कार्यो यथा न्यायम् परिग्रहः
transliteration: praṇidhāya hi cāreṇa yathāvat sūkṣma buddhinā
parīkṣya ca tataḥ kāryo yathā nyāyam parigrahaḥ
english: If did you, sounding him well through the instrumentality of sharp spies, find him friendly, do you win him over to your side.

sanskrit: जाम्बवाम्स् त्व् अथ सम्प्रेक्ष्य शास्त्र बुद्ध्या विचक्षणः
वाक्यम् विज्ञापयाम् आस गुणवद् दोष वर्जितम्
transliteration: jāmbavāms tv atha samprekṣya śāstra buddhyā vicakṣaṇaḥ
vākyam vijñāpayām āsa guṇavad doṣa varjitam
english: There upon the wise Jāmbavān, arriving at conclusions by virtue of his knowledge of Šāstras, began with words, void of defects.

sanskrit: बद्ध वैराच् च पापाच् च राक्षस इन्द्राद् विभीषणः
अदेश काले सम्प्राप्तः सर्वथा शन्क्यताम् अयम्
transliteration: baddha vairāc ca pāpāc ca rākṣasa indrād vibhīṣaṇaḥ
adeśa kāle samprāptaḥ sarvathā śankyatām ayam
english: Surely does Vibhīşaņa come from the vicious lord of Räkşasas, dead set against us and has arrived at such a bad piace and in such a bad hour. We should always fear him.

sanskrit: ततो मैन्दस् तु सम्प्रेक्ष्य नय अपनय कोविदः
transliteration: tato maindas tu samprekṣya naya apanaya kovidaḥ
english: There upon followed Mainda, conversant with what is right and wrong, after due deliberation, with words pregnant with words pregnant with reason.

sanskrit: अनुहो नाम तस्य एष रावणस्य विभीषणः
पृच्च्यताम् मधुरेण अयम् शनैर् नर वर ईश्वर
transliteration: anuho nāma tasya eṣa rāvaṇasya vibhīṣaṇaḥ
pṛccyatām madhureṇa ayam śanair nara vara īśvara
english: He is Rāvana's younger brother, by name Vibhīşana. Let the lord of men ask him every thing at first in sweet words.

sanskrit: भावम् अस्य तु विज्ञाय ततस् तत्त्वम् करिष्यसि
यदि दृष्टो न दुष्टो वा बुद्धि पूर्वम् नरषभ
transliteration: bhāvam asya tu vijñāya tatas tattvam kariṣyasi
yadi dṛṣṭo na duṣṭo vā buddhi pūrvam naraṣabha
english: Do you first ascertain, O foremost of men, with what intention he has come evil or good and then settle what course to adopt.

sanskrit: अथ सम्स्कार सम्पन्नो हनूमान् सचिव उत्तमः
उवाच वचनम् श्लक्ष्णम् अर्थवन् मधुरम् लघु
transliteration: atha samskāra sampanno hanūmān saciva uttamaḥ
uvāca vacanam ślakṣṇam arthavan madhuram laghu
english: There upon spoke Hanumān, the foremost of the counsellors and well versed in Šāstras, in accents sweet, glorious and fraught with a high value.

sanskrit: न भवन्तम् मति श्रेष्ठम् समर्थम् वदताम् वरम्
transliteration: na bhavantam mati śreṣṭham samartham vadatām varam
english: Even Brhaspati, (the lord of speech) cannot excel you, capaable,* gifted with the best of intellect and foremost of those skilled in the are of speech, as you are. *Capable to ascertain the truth of all Sastras.

sanskrit: न वादान् न अपि सम्घर्षान् न आधिक्यान् न च कामतः
वक्ष्यामि वचनम् राजन् यथा अर्थम् राम गौरवात्
transliteration: na vādān na api samgharṣān na ādhikyān na ca kāmataḥ
vakṣyāmi vacanam rājan yathā artham rāma gauravāt
english: And what I know I speak, o king. I do so, in the interest of Rāma's work and not impelled by my skill in the are of speech, by the pride of being a counsellor, by the vanity of being gifted with a high intellect or by the desire of speaking for its own sake.

sanskrit: अर्थ अनर्थ निमित्तम् हि यद् उक्तम् सचिवैस् तव
तत्र दोषम् प्रपश्यामि क्रिया न हि उपपद्यते
transliteration: artha anartha nimittam hi yad uktam sacivais tava
tatra doṣam prapaśyāmi kriyā na hi upapadyate
english: What your counsellors have said for ascertaining the good or evil intention of Vibhīş aņa appear to me as most defective and productive of no consequence whatever. It is impossible to sound him without any command.* *To command to relate for what he has come.

sanskrit: ऋते नियोगात् सामर्थ्यम् अवबोद्धुम् न शक्यते
सहसा विनियोगो हि दोषवान् प्रतिभाति मे
transliteration: ṛte niyogāt sāmarthyam avaboddhum na śakyate
sahasā viniyogo hi doṣavān pratibhāti me
english: And even to command him now for the same appears to me as improper.

sanskrit: चार प्रणिहितम् युक्तम् यद् उक्तम् सचिवैस् तव
अर्थस्य असम्भवात् तत्र कारणम् न उपपद्यते
transliteration: cāra praṇihitam yuktam yad uktam sacivais tava
arthasya asambhavāt tatra kāraṇam na upapadyate
english: And as regards the despatch of spies, anent what you have been advised by your ministers, I do not observe any utility.

sanskrit: अदेश काले सम्प्राप्त इति अयम् यद् विभीषणः
विवक्षा च अत्र मे अस्ति इयम् ताम् निबोध यथा मति
transliteration: adeśa kāle samprāpta iti ayam yad vibhīṣaṇaḥ
vivakṣā ca atra me asti iyam tām nibodha yathā mati
english: And what little I have thought of, I have something to say (regarding Jambaban's proposal) that Vibhīşaņa has arrived at such a bad place and in such an evil hour.

sanskrit: स एष देशः कालः च भवति इह यथा तथा
पुरुषात् पुरुषम् प्राप्य तथा दोष गुणाव् अपि
transliteration: sa eṣa deśaḥ kālaḥ ca bhavati iha yathā tathā
puruṣāt puruṣam prāpya tathā doṣa guṇāv api

sanskrit: दौरात्म्यम् रावणे दृष्ट्वा विक्रमम् च तथा त्वयि
युक्तम् आगमनम् तस्य सदृशम् तस्य बुद्धितः
transliteration: daurātmyam rāvaṇe dṛṣṭvā vikramam ca tathā tvayi
yuktam āgamanam tasya sadṛśam tasya buddhitaḥ
english: He has really come to a very good place and in a very good hour. And truly has he performed a becoming and sensille action by coming here after duly ascertaining that Rāvana is a vicious wight and you are a pious person-he is full of vices-you are gifted with many virtues-he is tyrannical and you are powerful.

sanskrit: अज्ञात रूपैः पुरुषैः स राजन् पृच्च्यताम् इति
यद् उक्तम् अत्र मे प्रेक्षा काचिद् अस्ति समीक्षिता
transliteration: ajñāta rūpaiḥ puruṣaiḥ sa rājan pṛccyatām iti
yad uktam atra me prekṣā kācid asti samīkṣitā
english: And what they have said, O king, as regards sounding him through secret spies, appear to me as one requiring great wisdom.

sanskrit: तत्र मित्रम् प्रदुष्येत मिथ्य पृष्टम् सुख आगतम्
transliteration: tatra mitram praduṣyeta mithya pṛṣṭam sukha āgatam
english: An intelligent man, when questioned by any suddenly, suspects many things. And if the newcomer be a friend and has come here for his own happiness, how greatly shall his mind be changed by such a course?

sanskrit: अशक्यः सहसा राजन् भावो वेत्तुम् परस्य वै
अन्तः स्वभावैर् गीतैस् तैर् नैपुण्यम् पश्यता भृशम्
transliteration: aśakyaḥ sahasā rājan bhāvo vettum parasya vai
antaḥ svabhāvair gītais tair naipuṇyam paśyatā bhṛśam
english: Besides by a sudden questioning it is impossible to ascertain the intention of a foreigner. Do you therefore yourself accost him and determine, by his voice, his secret motive.

sanskrit: न त्वस्य ब्रुवतो जातु लक्ष्यते दुष्ट भावता
प्रसन्नम् वदनम् च अपि तस्मान् मे न अस्ति सम्शयः
transliteration: na tvasya bruvato jātu lakṣyate duṣṭa bhāvatā
prasannam vadanam ca api tasmān me na asti samśayaḥ
english: I did not however mark anything of his wickedness while he spoke; rather I did observe signs of gladness on his countenance. So I do not suspect him.

sanskrit: अशन्कित मतिः स्वस्थो न शठः परिसर्पति
न च अस्य दुष्टा वागस्ति तस्मान् न अस्ति इह सम्शयः
transliteration: aśankita matiḥ svastho na śaṭhaḥ parisarpati
na ca asya duṣṭā vāgasti tasmān na asti iha samśayaḥ
english: The wily can never come fearless and undisturbed. Nor were his words cunning. So I do not suspect him.

sanskrit: आकारः चाद्यमानो अपि न शक्यो विनिगूहितुम्
बलाद्द् हि विवृणोति एव भावम् अन्तर् गतम् नृणाम्
transliteration: ākāraḥ cādyamāno api na śakyo vinigūhitum
balādd hi vivṛṇoti eva bhāvam antar gatam nṛṇām
english: It is not very easy to hide one's real nature. It manifests itself by force.

sanskrit: देश काल उपपन्नम् च कार्यम् कार्यविदाम् वर
transliteration: deśa kāla upapannam ca kāryam kāryavidām vara
english: So this action of Vibhīşana is not out of place or season. When accomplished it shall redound to his own interest.

sanskrit: उद्योगम् तव सम्प्रेक्ष्य मिथ्या वृत्तम् च रावणम्
वालिनः च वधम् श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवम् च अभिषेचितम्
transliteration: udyogam tava samprekṣya mithyā vṛttam ca rāvaṇam
vālinaḥ ca vadham śrutvā sugrīvam ca abhiṣecitam
english: Considering well your preparations for war and Ravana's vain conduct, hearing of Vah's destruction and Sugrīva's installation on the throne he has, impelled by his good sense, come here, desirous of gaining the kingdom. Taking these into account, it seems prudent to take him to our side.

sanskrit: राज्यम् प्रार्थयमानः च बुद्धि पूर्वम् इह आगतः
एतावत् तु पुरस् कृत्य युज्यते त्व् अस्य सम्ग्रहः
transliteration: rājyam prārthayamānaḥ ca buddhi pūrvam iha āgataḥ
etāvat tu puras kṛtya yujyate tv asya samgrahaḥ

sanskrit: यथा शक्ति मया उक्तम् तु राक्षसस्य आर्जवम् प्रति
प्रमाणम् तु शेषस्य श्रुत्वा बुद्धिमताम् वर
transliteration: yathā śakti mayā uktam tu rākṣasasya ārjavam prati
pramāṇam tu śeṣasya śrutvā buddhimatām vara
english: O you the foremost of the intelligent, I have spok thus considering him sincere. It now behove you to perform what you think proper.

sanskrit: राघवेन अभये दत्ते सम्नतो रावण अनुजः
transliteration: rāghavena abhaye datte samnato rāvaṇa anujaḥ

sanskrit: खात् पपात अवनिम् हृष्टो भक्तैर् अनुचरैः सह
स तु रामस्य धर्म आत्मा निपपात विभीषणः
transliteration: khāt papāta avanim hṛṣṭo bhaktair anucaraiḥ saha
sa tu rāmasya dharma ātmā nipapāta vibhīṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: पादयोः शरण अन्वेषी चतुर्भिः सह राक्षसैः
अब्रवीच् च तदा रामम् वाक्यम् तत्र विभीषणः
transliteration: pādayoḥ śaraṇa anveṣī caturbhiḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ
abravīc ca tadā rāmam vākyam tatra vibhīṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: धर्म युक्तम् च युक्तम् च साम्प्रतम् सम्प्रहर्षणम्
अनुजो रावणस्य अहम् तेन च अस्मि अवमानितः
transliteration: dharma yuktam ca yuktam ca sāmpratam sampraharṣaṇam
anujo rāvaṇasya aham tena ca asmi avamānitaḥ

sanskrit: भवन्तम् सर्व भूतानाम् शरण्यम् शरणम् गतः
परित्यक्ता मया लंका मित्राणि च धनानि च
transliteration: bhavantam sarva bhūtānām śaraṇyam śaraṇam gataḥ
parityaktā mayā laṃkā mitrāṇi ca dhanāni ca

sanskrit: भवद् गतम् हि मे राज्यम् च जीवितम् च सुखानि च
transliteration: bhavad gatam hi me rājyam ca jīvitam ca sukhāni ca

sanskrit: राम सेनापतिस्तस्य प्रहस्तो यदि ते श्रुतः
transliteration: rāma senāpatistasya prahasto yadi te śrutaḥ

sanskrit: सह देवैस्तु ते भग्ना रावणेन दुरात्मना
transliteration: saha devaistu te bhagnā rāvaṇena durātmanā

sanskrit: राक्षसानाम् वधे साह्यम् लंकायाः च प्रधर्षणे
करिष्यामि यथा प्राणम् प्रवेक्ष्यामि च वाहिनीम्
transliteration: rākṣasānām vadhe sāhyam laṃkāyāḥ ca pradharṣaṇe
kariṣyāmi yathā prāṇam pravekṣyāmi ca vāhinīm

sanskrit: इति ब्रुवाणम् रामस् तु परिष्वज्य विभीषणम्
अब्रवील् लक्ष्मणम् प्रीतः समुद्राज् जलम् आनय
transliteration: iti bruvāṇam rāmas tu pariṣvajya vibhīṣaṇam
abravīl lakṣmaṇam prītaḥ samudrāj jalam ānaya

sanskrit: तेन च इमम् महाप्राज्ञम् अभिषिन्च विभीषणम्
राजानम् रक्षसाम् क्षिप्रम् प्रसन्ने मयि मानद
transliteration: tena ca imam mahāprājñam abhiṣinca vibhīṣaṇam
rājānam rakṣasām kṣipram prasanne mayi mānada

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तस् तु सौमित्रिर् अभ्यषिन्चद् विभीषणम्
मध्ये वानर मुख्यानाम् राजानम् राम शासनात्
transliteration: evam uktas tu saumitrir abhyaṣincad vibhīṣaṇam
madhye vānara mukhyānām rājānam rāma śāsanāt

sanskrit: तम् प्रसादम् तु रामस्य दृष्ट्वा सद्यः प्लवम् गमाः
प्रचुक्रुशुर् महानादान् साधु साध्व् इति च अब्रुवन्
transliteration: tam prasādam tu rāmasya dṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ plavam gamāḥ
pracukruśur mahānādān sādhu sādhv iti ca abruvan

sanskrit: अब्रवीच् च हनूमामः च सुग्रीवः च विभीषणम्
कथम् सागरम् अक्षोभ्यम् तराम वरुण आलयम्
transliteration: abravīc ca hanūmāmaḥ ca sugrīvaḥ ca vibhīṣaṇam
katham sāgaram akṣobhyam tarāma varuṇa ālayam

sanskrit: उपायैर् अभिगच्चामो यथा नद नदी पतिम्
transliteration: upāyair abhigaccāmo yathā nada nadī patim

sanskrit: तराम तरसा सर्वे ससैन्या वरुण आलयम्
एवम् उक्तस् तु धर्मज्ञः प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः
transliteration: tarāma tarasā sarve sasainyā varuṇa ālayam
evam uktas tu dharmajñaḥ pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: समुद्रम् राघवो राजा शरणम् गन्तुम् अर्हति
transliteration: samudram rāghavo rājā śaraṇam gantum arhati

sanskrit: कर्तुम् अर्हति रामस्य ज्ञातेः कार्यम् महाउदधिः
transliteration: kartum arhati rāmasya jñāteḥ kāryam mahāudadhiḥ

sanskrit: प्रकृत्या धर्म शीलस्य राघवस्य अपि अरोचत
transliteration: prakṛtyā dharma śīlasya rāghavasya api arocata

sanskrit: स लक्ष्मणम् महातेजाः सुग्रीवम् च हरि ईश्वरम्
सत् क्रिया अर्थम् क्रिया दक्षः स्मित पूर्वम् उवाच ह
transliteration: sa lakṣmaṇam mahātejāḥ sugrīvam ca hari īśvaram
sat kriyā artham kriyā dakṣaḥ smita pūrvam uvāca ha

sanskrit: विभीषणस्य मन्त्रो अयम् मम लक्ष्मण रोचते
सुग्रीवः पण्डितो नित्यम् भवान् मन्त्र विचक्षणः
transliteration: vibhīṣaṇasya mantro ayam mama lakṣmaṇa rocate
sugrīvaḥ paṇḍito nityam bhavān mantra vicakṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: उभाभ्याम् सम्प्रधार्य आर्यम् रोचते यत् तद् उच्यताम्
एवम् उक्तौ तु तौ वीराव् उभौ सुग्रीव लक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: ubhābhyām sampradhārya āryam rocate yat tad ucyatām
evam uktau tu tau vīrāv ubhau sugrīva lakṣmaṇau

sanskrit: किम् अर्थम् नो नर व्याघ्र न रोचिष्यति राघव
transliteration: kim artham no nara vyāghra na rociṣyati rāghava

sanskrit: विभीषणेन यत् तु उक्तम् अस्मिन् काले सुख आवहम्
अबद्ध्वा सागरे सेतुम् घोरे अस्मिन् वरुण आलये
transliteration: vibhīṣaṇena yat tu uktam asmin kāle sukha āvaham
abaddhvā sāgare setum ghore asmin varuṇa ālaye

sanskrit: लंका न आसादितुम् शक्या स इन्द्रैर् अपि सुर असुरैः
विभीषणस्य शूरस्य यथा अर्थम् क्रियताम् वचः
transliteration: laṃkā na āsāditum śakyā sa indrair api sura asuraiḥ
vibhīṣaṇasya śūrasya yathā artham kriyatām vacaḥ

sanskrit: अलम् काल अत्ययम् कृत्वा समुद्रो अयम् नियुज्यताम्
transliteration: alam kāla atyayam kṛtvā samudro ayam niyujyatām

sanskrit: एवम् उक्तः कुश आस्तीर्णे तीरे नद नदी पतेः
सम्विवेश तदा रामो वेद्याम् इव हुत अशनः
transliteration: evam uktaḥ kuśa āstīrṇe tīre nada nadī pateḥ
samviveśa tadā rāmo vedyām iva huta aśanaḥ

english: Rāghava thus declaring to him 'no fear' Ravana's younger brother, the greatly wise Vibhișana, bending low his head, cast his looks on the earth.

sanskrit: स तु रामस्य धर्मात्मा निपपात विभीषणः
transliteration: sa tu rāmasya dharmātmā nipapāta vibhīṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: अब्रवीच्च तदा रामं वाक्यं तत्र विभीषणः
धर्मयुक्तं च युक्तं च साम्प्रतं सम्प्रहर्षणम्
transliteration: abravīcca tadā rāmaṃ vākyaṃ tatra vibhīṣaṇaḥ
dharmayuktaṃ ca yuktaṃ ca sāmprataṃ sampraharṣaṇam
english: Descending from the welkin with his devoted attendants the virtuous-souled Vibhisana, delighted, bowed to Rāma. And thereupon touching his feet along with four Rākşasas, Vibhisana addressed Rama, with words, fraught with piety, befitting the occasion and conducing to pleasure.

I am Rāvana's younger brother and have been greatly insulted by him. I have therefore come to seek your shelter, the refuge of all creatures, abandoning Lanka and renouncing my friends and riches. My kingdom, life and happiness are all at your disposal.

sanskrit: परित्यक्ता मया लङ्का मित्राणि च धनानि वै
भवद्गतं मे राज्यं च जीवितं च सुखानि च
transliteration: parityaktā mayā laṅkā mitrāṇi ca dhanāni vai
bhavadgataṃ me rājyaṃ ca jīvitaṃ ca sukhāni ca
english: I am Rāvana's younger brother and have been greatly insulted by him. I have therefore come to seek your shelter, the refuge of all creatures, abandoning Lanka and renouncing my friends and riches. My kingdom, life and happiness are all at your disposal.
Hearing his words Räma replied, comforting him with words and favouring him as if with looks.
Do you relate to me truly the strength and weakness of the enemies. Being thus accosted by Råma unwearied actions, the Raksasa, began to describe the strength of Rāvana.
Do you relate to me truly the strength and weakness of the enemies. Being thus accosted by Råma unwearied actions, the Raksasa, began to describe the strength of Rāvana.
O prince, by virtue of the bocn acquired from the Self-Create, the Ten-necked one is incapable of being slain by all creatures-Gandharvas, serpents, or birds.
My elder brother, the one next to Rāvana, is the heroic and highly effulgent Kumbhakarņa, Śakra's equal in battle.

sanskrit: राम सेनापतिस्तस्य प्रहस्तो यदि वा श्रुतः
transliteration: rāma senāpatistasya prahasto yadi vā śrutaḥ
english: You may have heard, O Rama, his commander is Prahasta, by whom was defeated Manibhadra on the mount Kailāsa.
(His son) Indrajit, equipped with invincible armour, bow and finger-protector made of the skin of iguana, becomes invisible in fight.
And, worshipping Fire and becoming invisible, Indrajit, that graceful hero, O Raghava, slays the enemies in conflict, having the contending parties vast and well arranged.
Mahodara, Mahāpārsva and the Rākşasa, Akampana, are his lieutenants, who equal the Lokapālas* in battle. *Divinities who protect regions, or the Sun, Moon, Fire, Wind, Indra, Yama, Varuna and Kabera.

His army consists of ten thousand kotis of Rākşasas, wearing shapes at will, inhabiting the city of Lankā, and living on flesh and gore. And with the Lokpalas and the celestials, they were all defeated by the vicious-souled Ravana.

His army consists of ten thousand kotis of Rākşasas, wearing shapes at will, inhabiting the city of Lankā, and living on flesh and gore. And with the Lokpalas and the celestials, they were all defeated by the vicious-souled Ravana.

sanskrit: सह देवैस्तु ते भग्ना रावणेन महात्मना
transliteration: saha devaistu te bhagnā rāvaṇena mahātmanā

english: Hearing the words of Vibhīşana and weighing them in his mind, that foremost of Raghu's race said.
I understand well the strength and prowess of Ravana, which you have depicted truly, O Vibhisana.

sanskrit: राजानं त्वां करिष्यामि सत्यमेतद् ब्रवीमि ते
transliteration: rājānaṃ tvāṃ kariṣyāmi satyametad bravīmi te
english: Do you hear truly that I shall slay the Tennecked one together with Prahasta and his sons, and I shall make you king.

sanskrit: रसातलं वा प्रविशेत् पातालं वापि रावणः
पितामहसकाशं वा न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यते
transliteration: rasātalaṃ vā praviśet pātālaṃ vāpi rāvaṇaḥ
pitāmahasakāśaṃ vā na me jīvan vimokṣyate
english: Whether he entered the Rasåtala or the regions under the earth, or seek shelter of the Grand-father of the celestials, he shall not be able to save his life from me.
I do swear by my three brethren that I shall enter the city of Ayodhyā, after slaying in battle Ravana with his sons, kinsmen and friends.
Hearing these words of Rāma of unwearied action, the virtuous-souled (Vibhisana), bowing his head to him, began.
I shall lend you my might in slaying the Raksasas and devastating the city of Larkā, and shall be in the midst of Rāvana's army.

There upon, embracing Vibhīşaņa, who spoke thus, Rama, delighted, said to Laksmana, Omy brother, do you bring water from the ocean. Sprinkling the greatly wise Vibhișana, I shall make him at once the king of the Rākşasas, o confrere of honour; for I am greatly pleased with him.

sanskrit: राजानं रक्षसां क्षिप्रं प्रसन्ने मयि मानद
transliteration: rājānaṃ rakṣasāṃ kṣipraṃ prasanne mayi mānada
english: There upon, embracing Vibhīşaņa, who spoke thus, Rama, delighted, said to Laksmana, Omy brother, do you bring water from the ocean. Sprinkling the greatly wise Vibhișana, I shall make him at once the king of the Rākşasas, o confrere of honour; for I am greatly pleased with him.
Being thus addressed, Saumitri, at the command of the king, anointed Vibhișana and made him the king of the Räkşasas in the presence of the monkey host.

sanskrit: तं प्रसादं तु रामस्य दृष्ट्वा सद्यः प्लवङ्गमाः
transliteration: taṃ prasādaṃ tu rāmasya dṛṣṭvā sadyaḥ plavaṅgamāḥ
english: Beholding Rāma's kindness (towards Vibhīş ana), the monkeys eulogized the high-souled one, exclaiming “Excellent! Excellent!”
Thereupon, Hanumān and Sugrīva addressed Vibhisana, saying, Do you tell us how we shall cross over the main-the abode of Varuņa, along with the host of the highly powerful monkeys.
Thereupon, Hanumān and Sugrīva addressed Vibhisana, saying, Do you tell us how we shall cross over the main-the abode of Varuņa, along with the host of the highly powerful monkeys.
Do you inform us of the means by which we may cross over, along with our army, the lord of rivers and streams-the abode of Varuna."
Being thus addressed, the virtuous-souled Vibhisana replied, "It behovth the king, Rāghava, to seek refuge from the Ocean.

This measureless deep was dug out by (the king) Sagara.* And the great ocean shall surely help Rāma belonging to Sagara's race. *Sagara was a sovereign of Ayodhyā, belonging to the same family with Rāma.
Being thus accosted by the wise Rākşasa, Vibhīşaņa. Sugrīva reached where Rāma with Laksmana was.
Thereupon, the broad-necked Sugrīva began to explain the well-meaning words of Vibhīşaņa, requesting Ráma to seek the shelter of the Ocean.

sanskrit: स लक्ष्मणं महातेजाः सुग्रीवं च हरीश्वरम्
transliteration: sa lakṣmaṇaṃ mahātejāḥ sugrīvaṃ ca harīśvaram
english: And those words pleased Răma, pious by nature. And the highly effulgent (hero) requested, smiling, the active Lakşmaņa and the monkey-chief Sugrīva to collect necessaries for his adoration.

sanskrit: विभीषणस्य मन्त्रो ऽयं मम लक्ष्मण रोचते
english: O Lakşmaņa, this counsel of Vibhīşaņa appear to me as most sound. Sugrīva is a ways greatly wise, and you are greatly proficient in counsel. Do you, holding a conference, intimate to me what you think becoming."

O Lakşmaņa, this counsel of Vibhīşaņa appear to me as most sound. Sugrīva is a ways greatly wise, and you are greatly proficient in counsel. Do you, holding a conference, intimate to me what you think becoming."
Thus addressed, those two heroes-Lakşmaņa and Sugriva, spoke respectfully the following words fraught with propriety.

sanskrit: किमर्थं नौ नरव्याघ्र न रोचिष्यति राघव
transliteration: kimarthaṃ nau naravyāghra na rociṣyati rāghava
english: Why shall not the well-meaning words of Vibhīşaņa expressed now, please us O Rāghava, O you best of men?

sanskrit: अबद्ध्वा सागरे सेतुं घोरे ऽस्मिन् वरुणालये
english: Without constructing a bridge over the deep, the terrible abode of Varuņa, even the celestials and their lord (India) cannot get at the city of Lanka.

sanskrit: अलं कालात्ययं कृत्वा समुद्रो ऽयं नियुज्यताम्
english: Do you act on the genuine counsel of the heroic Vibhisana, and without losing time, do you engage the Ocean for this work, so that we may with our army proceed to the city protected by Ravana.
Being thus addressed Räma reached the shore of the lord of rivers and streams, covered with Kusa, like to fire getting into the sacrificial dais.

Thereupon the greatly powerful Rākşasa, by name Śārdüla, beheld the army of Sugrīva arranged on the shore of the ocean. And, beholding the army all busy, the emissary of the vicious-souled Raksasa-Ravana, entered the city of Lanka and, approaching his lord, said.

sanskrit: ताम् दृष्ट्वा सर्वतोऽव्यग्रम् प्रतिगम्य स राक्षसः
transliteration: tām dṛṣṭvā sarvato'vyagram pratigamya sa rākṣasaḥ

sanskrit: उपप्रदानम् सान्त्वम् वा भेदो वात्र प्रयुज्यताम्
transliteration: upapradānam sāntvam vā bhedo vātra prayujyatām

english: Hearing the words of Sardāla, Ravana, the lord of Rākşasas, being anxious to ascertain his duty, addressed a Raksasa by name Suka, the most sensible of his counsellors, with the following pregnant words.

sanskrit: शुकम् नाम तदा रक्षो वाक्यमर्थविदाम् वरम्
transliteration: śukam nāma tadā rakṣo vākyamarthavidām varam

english: You are born of a great family and are the mighty son of the king of bears. I have no dissension with you. In fact I consider you as my brother, O king of monkeys.

sanskrit: किम् तत्र तव सुग्रीव किश्किन्धाम् प्रति गम्यताम्
transliteration: kim tatra tava sugrīva kiśkindhām prati gamyatām
english: Though I have stolen the spouse of the highsouled prince (Räma), yet what is that to you, Sugriva? Do you return to Kiskindhā.

sanskrit: न हीयम् हरिभिर्लङ्का प्राप्तुम् शक्या कथम् चन
transliteration: na hīyam haribhirlaṅkā prāptum śakyā katham cana
english: The monkeys shall not by any means be able to attack the city of Lankā. Even the celestials and Gandharvas could not-what of these men and monkeys?
And being thus commissioned by the lord of Rākşasas, that night-ranger assumed the shape of a bird and, bounding, speedily reached the sky.
And, proceeding far over the deep and stationing himself at the welkin, he spoke to Sugrīva all the words with which he was addressed by the vicious-souled Ravana.

sanskrit: प्रापद्यन्त तदा क्षिप्रम् लोप्तुम् हन्तुम् च मुष्टिभिः
transliteration: prāpadyanta tadā kṣipram loptum hantum ca muṣṭibhiḥ

sanskrit: न दूतान् घ्नन्ति काकुत्थ्स वार्यन्ताम् साधु वानराः
यस्तु हित्वा मतम् भर्तुः स्वमतम् सम्प्रभाषते
transliteration: na dūtān ghnanti kākutthsa vāryantām sādhu vānarāḥ
yastu hitvā matam bhartuḥ svamatam samprabhāṣate
english: And being assailed by the monkeys, suka said, O Kākutstha, it does not behove (people) to slay an emissary. Do you therefore prevent the monkeys. He who passing by his master's behest, give out his own intention, is not faithful; and he therefore deserve to be slain.

sanskrit: अनुक्तवादी दूतः सन्न् स दूतो वधमर्हति
शुकस्य वचनम् रामः श्रुत्वा तु परिदेवितम्
transliteration: anuktavādī dūtaḥ sann sa dūto vadhamarhati
śukasya vacanam rāmaḥ śrutvā tu paridevitam

sanskrit: किम् मया खलु नक्तव्यो रावणो लोकरावणः
transliteration: kim mayā khalu naktavyo rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ
english: Being thus addressed, that mighty king of monkeys the bull among them, of unwearied energy, spoke to that emissary—the nightranger, Suka, saying.

O Rāvana, you are not my friend or an object of pity. You are not my benefactor, not are liked by me. You are Rāma's enemy, and you did therefore deserve to be slain by him like Vāli along with your friends and relatives.
I shall therefore slay you, O king of nightrangers, together with your sons, friends and relatives. And I shall have the whole city of Lankă reduced to ashes by my mighty force.

You shall not be able to escape Rāghava, O Rāvana, O you who have lost your sense, even if you are protected by the celestials. And you shall with your brother be slain by Rāma, even if you did fly into the sky, enter into the regions under the earth, or seek shelter of Mahādeva.

sanskrit: तस्य ते त्रिषु लोकेषु न पिशाचम् न राक्षसम्
transliteration: tasya te triṣu lokeṣu na piśācam na rākṣasam
english: I do not behold any in these three worldsPiśāca, Rākşasa, Gandharva, or Asura, who can protect you.

sanskrit: किम् मते रामसाम्निध्ये सकाशे लक्ष्मणस्य च
transliteration: kim mate rāmasāmnidhye sakāśe lakṣmaṇasya ca

sanskrit: हृता सीता विशालाक्षि याम् त्वम् गृह्य न बुध्यसे
transliteration: hṛtā sītā viśālākṣi yām tvam gṛhya na budhyase

sanskrit: न बुध्यसे रघुश्रेष्ठम् यस्ते प्राणान् हरिष्यति
transliteration: na budhyase raghuśreṣṭham yaste prāṇān hariṣyati

sanskrit: वायम् दूतो महाप्राज्ञ चारकः प्रतिभाति मे
तुलितम् हि बलम् सर्वमनेन तव तिष्ठता
transliteration: vāyam dūto mahāprājña cārakaḥ pratibhāti me
tulitam hi balam sarvamanena tava tiṣṭhatā
english: Then spoke that best of monkeys, Angada, son of Vali, O highly wise one, this is no emissary. This one clearly appear to me as a spy. He has come to form and estimate of your entire army. Take him. Let him not go (back) to lanka. This is indeed what I would,

sanskrit: लुप्येते मे बलात्पक्षौ भिद्येते मे तथाक्षिणी
transliteration: lupyete me balātpakṣau bhidyete me tathākṣiṇī

sanskrit: याम् च रात्रिम् मरिष्यामि जाये रात्रिम् च यामहम्
transliteration: yām ca rātrim mariṣyāmi jāye rātrim ca yāmaham

english: Then on the shore of the sea, Rāghava, spreading darbha, with his hands joined towards the great deep, laid him down, with his face to the East.

That slayer of foes (lay down), making his pillow his arm resembling the shining form of a serpent; always dight with golden ornaments; full many a time pressed with the palms of beauteous damsels,* decked with jewelled golden Keyūras and superb ornaments studded with pearls; smeared from above with sandal and aguru; (his arm) which formerly had been graced in bed with the head of Sītā; like to the body of Takşaka under the waters of the Gangā; resembling a yoke; in battle increasing the sorrow of foes and enhancing for long the delight of friends; his arm having its skin destroyed by the strokes of the bow-string; which was the refuge of the entire earth; his right arm resembling a mighty bludgeon, the donor of thousands of kine, making this great arm his pillow (he laid him down). To-day either I shall die, or shall the Ocean. Having thus formed his resolution in respect of the great deep, Rama, restraining his speech, with a concentrated mind lay down there agreeably to rule. *The commentator appropriately remarks-As Rāma was wedded to a single wife, these damsels must mean nurses attending on him.

That slayer of foes (lay down), making his pillow his arm resembling the shining form of a serpent; always dight with golden ornaments; full many a time pressed with the palms of beauteous damsels,* decked with jewelled golden Keyūras and superb ornaments studded with pearls; smeared from above with sandal and aguru; (his arm) which formerly had been graced in bed with the head of Sītā; like to the body of Takşaka under the waters of the Gangā; resembling a yoke; in battle increasing the sorrow of foes and enhancing for long the delight of friends; his arm having its skin destroyed by the strokes of the bow-string; which was the refuge of the entire earth; his right arm resembling a mighty bludgeon, the donor of thousands of kine, making this great arm his pillow (he laid him down). To-day either I shall die, or shall the Ocean. Having thus formed his resolution in respect of the great deep, Rama, restraining his speech, with a concentrated mind lay down there agreeably to rule. *The commentator appropriately remarks-As Rāma was wedded to a single wife, these damsels must mean nurses attending on him.

sanskrit: अद्य मे मरणम् वाथ तरणम् सागरस्य वा
transliteration: adya me maraṇam vātha taraṇam sāgarasya vā

sanskrit: तस्य रामस्य सुप्तस्य कुश आस्तीर्णे मही तले
transliteration: tasya rāmasya suptasya kuśa āstīrṇe mahī tale
english: As Rāma slept on the earth on Kuśa spread over, without ever swerving from the rule, three nights passed away.

sanskrit: उपासत तदा रामः सागरम् सरिताम् पतिम्
transliteration: upāsata tadā rāmaḥ sāgaram saritām patim
english: me. And while spending three nights, Rāma, learned in polity and attached to virtue, prayed to that lord of streams-the Ocean. Yet the wicked Ocean, albeit adored according to his deserts by Rāma with his mind concentrated, did not show himself.

sanskrit: न च दर्शयते मन्दस् तदा रामस्य सागरः
प्रयतेन अपि रामेण यथा अर्हम् अभिपूजितः
transliteration: na ca darśayate mandas tadā rāmasya sāgaraḥ
prayatena api rāmeṇa yathā arham abhipūjitaḥ
english: me. And while spending three nights, Rāma, learned in polity and attached to virtue, prayed to that lord of streams-the Ocean. Yet the wicked Ocean, albeit adored according to his deserts by Rāma with his mind concentrated, did not show himself.

sanskrit: समुद्रस्य ततः क्रुद्धो रामो रक्त अन्त लोचनः
समीपस्थम् उवाच इदम् लक्ष्मणम् शुभ लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: samudrasya tataḥ kruddho rāmo rakta anta locanaḥ
samīpastham uvāca idam lakṣmaṇam śubha lakṣmaṇam
english: Thereat Răma grew enraged and had the corners of his eyes crimsoned; and he spank to Laksmana of auspicious marks, saying.

sanskrit: अवलेपम् समुद्रस्य न दर्शयति यत् स्वयम्
प्रशमः च क्षमा चैव आर्जवम् प्रिय वादिता
transliteration: avalepam samudrasya na darśayati yat svayam
praśamaḥ ca kṣamā caiva ārjavam priya vāditā
english: Behold the hauteur of the Ocean in not presenting himself before Calmness, forbearance, candour, and soft speech-these virtues of the good are by the insolent taken for the effects of incompetency.

sanskrit: असामर्थ्यम् फलन्ति एते निर्गुणेषु सताम् गुणाः
transliteration: asāmarthyam phalanti ete nirguṇeṣu satām guṇāḥ

sanskrit: सर्वत्र उत्सृष्ट दण्डम् च लोकः सत् कुरुते नरम्
न साम्ना शक्यते कीर्तिर् न साम्ना शक्यते यशः
transliteration: sarvatra utsṛṣṭa daṇḍam ca lokaḥ sat kurute naram
na sāmnā śakyate kīrtir na sāmnā śakyate yaśaḥ

sanskrit: प्राप्तुम् लक्ष्मण लोके अस्मिन् जयो वा रण मूधनि
अद्य मद् बाण निर्भिन्नैर् मकरैर् मकर आलयम्
निरुद्ध तोयम् सौमित्रे प्लवद्भिः पश्य सर्वतः
transliteration: prāptum lakṣmaṇa loke asmin jayo vā raṇa mūdhani
adya mad bāṇa nirbhinnair makarair makara ālayam
niruddha toyam saumitre plavadbhiḥ paśya sarvataḥ

sanskrit: भोगामः च पश्य नागानाम् मया भिन्नानि लक्ष्मण
transliteration: bhogāmaḥ ca paśya nāgānām mayā bhinnāni lakṣmaṇa

sanskrit: महाभोगानि मत्स्यानाम् करिणाम् च करान् इह
सशन्ख शुक्तिका जालम् समीन मकरम् शरैः
transliteration: mahābhogāni matsyānām kariṇām ca karān iha
saśankha śuktikā jālam samīna makaram śaraiḥ

sanskrit: क्षमया हि समायुक्तम् माम् अयम् मकर आलयः
transliteration: kṣamayā hi samāyuktam mām ayam makara ālayaḥ

sanskrit: असमर्थम् विजानाति धिक् क्षमाम् ईदृशे जने
स दर्शयति साम्ना मे सागरो रूपमात्मनः
transliteration: asamartham vijānāti dhik kṣamām īdṛśe jane
sa darśayati sāmnā me sāgaro rūpamātmanaḥ

sanskrit: चापम् आनय सौमित्रे शरामः च आशी विष उपमान्
transliteration: cāpam ānaya saumitre śarāmaḥ ca āśī viṣa upamān

sanskrit: अद्य अक्षोभ्यम् अपि क्रुद्धः क्षोभयिष्यामि सागरम्
वेलासु कृत मर्यादम् सहसा ऊर्मि समाकुलम्
transliteration: adya akṣobhyam api kruddhaḥ kṣobhayiṣyāmi sāgaram
velāsu kṛta maryādam sahasā ūrmi samākulam
english: Being angered, today, albeit incapable of being agitated, will I agitate the deep. And by means of my shafts will I make Varuna's abode, surging with a thousand billows and having his dignity maintained by his shores, overleep his continents. And I will agitate the deep harbouring numbers of mighty Dānavas.

Being angered, today, albeit incapable of being agitated, will I agitate the deep. And by means of my shafts will I make Varuna's abode, surging with a thousand billows and having his dignity maintained by his shores, overleep his continents. And I will agitate the deep harbouring numbers of mighty Dānavas.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा धनुष् पाणिः क्रोध विस्फारित ईक्षणः
बभूव रामो दुर्धर्षो युग अन्त अग्निर् इव ज्वलन्
transliteration: evam uktvā dhanuṣ pāṇiḥ krodha visphārita īkṣaṇaḥ
babhūva rāmo durdharṣo yuga anta agnir iva jvalan
english: Having spoken you, Rāma, equipped with his bow, with his eyes dilated in wrath, became exceedingly irrepressible, like to the flaming fire at the final dissolution.

sanskrit: सम्पीड्य च धनुर् घोरम् कम्पयित्वा शरैर् जगत्
मुमोच विशिखान् उग्रान् वज्राणि इव शत क्रतुः
transliteration: sampīḍya ca dhanur ghoram kampayitvā śarair jagat
mumoca viśikhān ugrān vajrāṇi iva śata kratuḥ
english: And straining his dreadful bow, making the earth shake, tremulously, he let fly fierce shafts like him of an hundred sacrifices hurling his thunder-bolt.

sanskrit: ते ज्वलन्तो महावेगास् तेजसा सायक उत्तमाः
transliteration: te jvalanto mahāvegās tejasā sāyaka uttamāḥ
english: Thereat, flaming up, those vehement choice shafts surcharged with energy, enter into the waters of the sea, with its serpents afflicted with fear.

sanskrit: ततो वेगः समुद्रस्य सनक्र मकरो महान्
स बभूव महाघोरः समारुत रवस् तदा
transliteration: tato vegaḥ samudrasya sanakra makaro mahān
sa babhūva mahāghoraḥ samāruta ravas tadā
english: Then great and exceedingly dreadful was the motion of the sea, with fishes and Makaras, and with the roar of the winds (blowing there).

sanskrit: महाऊर्मि माला विततः शन्ख शुक्ति समाकुलः
सधूम परिवृत्त ऊर्मिः सहसा अभून् महाउदधिः
transliteration: mahāūrmi mālā vitataḥ śankha śukti samākulaḥ
sadhūma parivṛtta ūrmiḥ sahasā abhūn mahāudadhiḥ
english: On a sudden the mighty deep was heaving with mighty surges, with conchs scattered about, and a smoke (enveloped) the ocean; and the billows became visible on all sides.

sanskrit: व्यथिताः पन्नगाः च आसन् दीप्त आस्या दीप्त लोचनाः
दानवाः च महावीर्याः पाताल तल वासिनः
transliteration: vyathitāḥ pannagāḥ ca āsan dīpta āsyā dīpta locanāḥ
dānavāḥ ca mahāvīryāḥ pātāla tala vāsinaḥ
english: The serpents were distressed, with their faces flaming and their eyes aglow; as well as the Dānavas of terrific energy, and the dwellers of the nether spheres.

sanskrit: ऊर्मयः सिन्धु राजस्य सनक्र मकरास् तदा
transliteration: ūrmayaḥ sindhu rājasya sanakra makarās tadā
english: Billows of the sovran Ocean, resembling Vindhya or Mandara, containing crocodiles and Makaras, sprang up by thousands.

sanskrit: आघूर्णित तरन्ग ओघः सम्ब्भ्रान्त उरग राक्षसः
transliteration: āghūrṇita taranga oghaḥ sambbhrānta uraga rākṣasaḥ
english: Varuņa's abode had its surges whirling its serpents and Räkşasas seized with affright, and its ferocious aquatic animals borne all around; and it sent forth sounds.
Then Sumitrā's son, springing up, said to Raghava of fiery vehemence, as he sighed and kept stretching his matchless bow. This must not be. And he took away his (Rāma's) bow.

Without doing this to the Ocean, you supreme of heroes, may have your work accomplished. Personages like you do not come under the influence of passion. Do you deliberately look about for some worthy means (for compassing your end.)
Then remaining invisible in the sky, Brahmarsis and Surarsis,* exclaiming, Well-aday! and Do'nt, in loud accents ajaculated, (Oh! and alas!) *Celestial saints.
Then the foremost of Raghus addressed Ocean in stern words, saying, To-day will I dry up the Ocean along with the nether regions.
O Ocean, your waters being burnt up by my shafts, and you being dried up, with your (aquatic) animals slaughtered, a mighty volume of dust shall arise (from your bed).
O Ocean, in consequence of the arrowy shower discharged from my bow, the monkeys shall go over to the further shore on foot.
Having attained dimensions in consequence of access of waters you know not my manliness or my prowess. But, o abode of Dānavas, grief shall you reap at my hands.

sanskrit: सम्योज्य धनुषि श्रे ष्ठे विचकर्ष महाबलः
transliteration: samyojya dhanuṣi śre ṣṭhe vicakarṣa mahābalaḥ
english: Then fixing an arrow resembling the rod of Brahmā with a Brahmā Mantra, on the best of bows, that exceedingly strong on drew it.
As Rāghava suddenly stretched his bow, heaven and earth seemed to be riven, and the mountains trembled.
And darkness covered the world, and the cardinal points became invisible. And at once the watery expanses and rivers were agitated.

sanskrit: तिर्यक् च सह नक्षत्रैः सम्गतौ चन्द्रभास्करौ
transliteration: tiryak ca saha nakṣatraiḥ samgatau candrabhāskarau
english: The stars appeared simultaneously with the Sun and Moon.* And the sky was illumined with the rays of the Sun, and yet it was overspread with darkness; and it burned with an hundred meteors. And thunder-bolts sending forth sounds surpassing all others, dropped from the firmament. *The phenomenon, remarks the commentator, was owing to the heavenly bodies obstructing each other's orbit.

The stars appeared simultaneously with the Sun and Moon.* And the sky was illumined with the rays of the Sun, and yet it was overspread with darkness; and it burned with an hundred meteors. And thunder-bolts sending forth sounds surpassing all others, dropped from the firmament. *The phenomenon, remarks the commentator, was owing to the heavenly bodies obstructing each other's orbit.

sanskrit: बभञ्ज च तदा वृक्षान् जलदानुद्वहन् मुहुः
transliteration: babhañja ca tadā vṛkṣān jaladānudvahan muhuḥ
english: The winds began to below violently; breaking down trees and momentarily scattering clouds; damaging mountain-tops and shattering summits.

sanskrit: दिवि च स्म महावेगाः सम्हताः समहास्वनाः
transliteration: divi ca sma mahāvegāḥ samhatāḥ samahāsvanāḥ

english: Then the dread and mighty thunders possessing impetuous speed and emitting tremendous roars, coming together, produced lightning flashes. And those creatures that could be seen, uttered sounds resembling the thunder; and those that were invisible gave forth f rightful cries.

sanskrit: सम्प्रविव्यथिरे चापि न च पस्पन्दिरे भयात्
transliteration: sampravivyathire cāpi na ca paspandire bhayāt

english: Then the mighty deep with its animals, and with its waters and waves, and with its serpents and Rākşasas, was suddenly wrought up with a violent motion. And albeit it was not the occasion of the universal dissolution, the Ocean passed beyond his shores for a full hundred yojanas.

Seeing the elated Ocean-lord of streams and rivers, thus overpass his bounds, that destroyer of enemies, Raghu's son, Rāma, was not moved.* *Naticakrāma may also mean, (Rama) did not discharge any more arrows.

sanskrit: ततो मध्यात् समुद्रस्य सागरः स्वयम् उत्थितः
उदयन् हि महाशैलान् मेरोर् इव दिवा करः
transliteration: tato madhyāt samudrasya sāgaraḥ svayam utthitaḥ
udayan hi mahāśailān meror iva divā karaḥ
english: Then from forth the mid-sea arose Ocean himself, even as the maker of day rise from the mighty ascending-hill, Meru.

sanskrit: पन्नगैः सह दीप्त आस्यैः समुद्रः प्रत्यदृश्यत
स्निग्ध वैदूर्य सम्काशो जाम्बू नद विभूषितः
transliteration: pannagaiḥ saha dīpta āsyaiḥ samudraḥ pratyadṛśyata
snigdha vaidūrya samkāśo jāmbū nada vibhūṣitaḥ

sanskrit: रत्न माल्य अम्बर धरः पद्म पत्र निभ ईक्षणः
transliteration: ratna mālya ambara dharaḥ padma patra nibha īkṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: अब्रवीत् प्रान्जलिर् वाक्यम् राघवम् शर पाणिनम्
transliteration: abravīt prānjalir vākyam rāghavam śara pāṇinam
english: And approaching the arrow-showering Rāma, and greeting him fair, Ocean spoke to him with joined hands.

sanskrit: पृथिवी वायुर् आकाशम् आपो ज्योतिः च राघवः
स्वभावे सौम्य तिष्ठन्ति शाश्वतम् मार्गम् आश्रिताः
transliteration: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiḥ ca rāghavaḥ
svabhāve saumya tiṣṭhanti śāśvatam mārgam āśritāḥ
english: O Rāghava, earth, air, sky, water and light, these, O mild one, retaining their eternal course, maintain their (respective) nature.

sanskrit: तत् स्वभावो मम अपि एष यद् अगाधो अहम् अप्लवः
विकारस् तु भवेद् राध एतत् ते प्रवदामि अहम्
transliteration: tat svabhāvo mama api eṣa yad agādho aham aplavaḥ
vikāras tu bhaved rādha etat te pravadāmi aham
english: Mine also is that nature whereby I am fathomless and incapable of being crossed. The reverse of this is the having a bottom. And for this reason I speak to you (concerning the means).

sanskrit: न कामान् न च लोभाद् वा न भयात् पार्थिव आत्मज
transliteration: na kāmān na ca lobhād vā na bhayāt pārthiva ātmaja
english: O king's son, not from desire, covetousness, or fear, or anger, can I anywise deprive my waters abounding in alligators of their (perpetual) motion.

sanskrit: विधास्ये येन गन्तासि विषहिष्ये ह्यहम् तथा
transliteration: vidhāsye yena gantāsi viṣahiṣye hyaham tathā
english: I will tell you how you will pass (over me); or and I will bear it. And no ferocious aquatic animals shall do wrong so long as your forces have not crossed. And, O Rāma, I will make as it were firm land for the crossing over of the monkeys.

sanskrit: रामस्य वचनम् श्रुत्वा तम् च दृष्ट्वा महाशरम्
transliteration: rāmasya vacanam śrutvā tam ca dṛṣṭvā mahāśaram

sanskrit: द्रुमकुल्य इति ख्यातो लोके ख्यातो यथा भवान्
transliteration: drumakulya iti khyāto loke khyāto yathā bhavān

sanskrit: अमोघः क्रियताम् राम तत्र तेषु शरोत्तमः
transliteration: amoghaḥ kriyatām rāma tatra teṣu śarottamaḥ

sanskrit: मुमोच तम् शरम् दीप्तम् परम् सागरदर्शनात्
transliteration: mumoca tam śaram dīptam param sāgaradarśanāt

sanskrit: ननाद च तदा तत्र वसुधा शल्यपीडिता
transliteration: nanāda ca tadā tatra vasudhā śalyapīḍitā

sanskrit: स बभूव तदा कूपो व्रण इत्येव विश्रुतः
transliteration: sa babhūva tadā kūpo vraṇa ityeva viśrutaḥ

sanskrit: शोषयित्वा तु तम् कुक्षिम् रामो दशरथात्मजः
transliteration: śoṣayitvā tu tam kukṣim rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
english: Having dried up Marukāntāra famous throughout the three regions, as well as the reservoirs of water Rāma the son of Dasaratha, learned and of god-like prowess, conferred a boon on the desert, saying. *i.e. the sound.

This place shall be filled with food nourishing beasts; and ailments shall be rare here. And the fruits and roots shall be replete with relish; and it shall abound in oil and overflow with milk; and it shall contain various adorous drugs.

sanskrit: रामस्य वरदानाच्च शिवः पन्था बभूव ह
transliteration: rāmasya varadānācca śivaḥ panthā babhūva ha
english: Thus did the desert come to possess these attributes; and from Rāma's bestowal of a boon, it attained a pleasant aspect.

sanskrit: तस्मिन् दग्धे तदा कुक्षौ समुद्रः सरिताम् पतिः
transliteration: tasmin dagdhe tadā kukṣau samudraḥ saritām patiḥ
english: On that place being burnt up, that lord of streams, the Ocean, thus spoke to Rāghava, versed in every branch of learning.

sanskrit: अयम् सौम्य नलो नाम तनुजो विश्व कर्मणः
पित्रा दत्त वरः श्रीमान् प्रतिमो विश्व कर्मणः
transliteration: ayam saumya nalo nāma tanujo viśva karmaṇaḥ
pitrā datta varaḥ śrīmān pratimo viśva karmaṇaḥ
english: O mild one, this one is named Nala, son to Viśvakarmā. He has received a boon from his sire. Visvakarma's son is well pleased with you. Let this monkey, surcharged with exhuberant spirits, build a bridge over me. I will hold that up. This one is as his sire.

sanskrit: एष सेतुम् महाउत्साहः करोतु मयि वानरः
तम् अहम् धारयिष्यामि तथा हि एष यथा पिता
transliteration: eṣa setum mahāutsāhaḥ karotu mayi vānaraḥ
tam aham dhārayiṣyāmi tathā hi eṣa yathā pitā

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा उदधिर् नष्टः समुत्थाय नलस् ततः
अब्रवीद् वानर श्रेष्ठो वाक्यम् रामम् महाबलः
transliteration: evam uktvā udadhir naṣṭaḥ samutthāya nalas tataḥ
abravīd vānara śreṣṭho vākyam rāmam mahābalaḥ
english: Having delivered himself thus, Ocean disappeared. Then that foremost of monkeys, Nala, arising, spoke to the mighty Rāma.

sanskrit: अहम् सेतुम् करिष्यामि विस्तीर्णे वरुण आलये
पितुः सामर्थ्यम् आस्थाय तत्त्वम् आह महाउदधिः
transliteration: aham setum kariṣyāmi vistīrṇe varuṇa ālaye
pituḥ sāmarthyam āsthāya tattvam āha mahāudadhiḥ
english: Resorting to my sire's skill, I will build a bridge over the spacious abode of Makaras. The mighty Ocean has spoken justly.
This dreadful Ocean, this mighty deep, expecting to see a bridge (thrown over him), has granted depth to Rāghava.

sanskrit: मम मातुर् वरो दत्तो मन्दरे विश्व कर्मणा
औरसस् तस्य पुत्रो अहम् सदृशो विश्व कर्मणा
transliteration: mama mātur varo datto mandare viśva karmaṇā
aurasas tasya putro aham sadṛśo viśva karmaṇā
english: (Formerly) in Mandara, Visvakarma had conferred a boon on my mother: 'O exalted one, your son shall be like me.
I am a son of his, sprung from his lions, and I am like to Viśvakarmā. Ocean reminded me all the things. Not having been asked by you, I had not unfolded my qualifications.

sanskrit: न च अपि अहम् अनुक्तो वै प्रब्रूयाम् आत्मनो गुणान्
transliteration: na ca api aham anukto vai prabrūyām ātmano guṇān

sanskrit: ततो निसृष्ट रामेण सर्वतो हरि यूथपाः
transliteration: tato nisṛṣṭa rāmeṇa sarvato hari yūthapāḥ

sanskrit: ते नगान् नग सम्काशाः शाखा मृग गण ऋषभाः
transliteration: te nagān naga samkāśāḥ śākhā mṛga gaṇa ṛṣabhāḥ

sanskrit: बभन्जुर् वानरास् तत्र प्रचकर्षुः च सागरम्
ते सालैः च अश्व कर्णैः च धवैर् वम्शैः च वानराः
transliteration: babhanjur vānarās tatra pracakarṣuḥ ca sāgaram
te sālaiḥ ca aśva karṇaiḥ ca dhavair vamśaiḥ ca vānarāḥ

sanskrit: कुटजैर् अर्जुनैस् तालैस् तिकलैस् तिमिशैर् अपि
transliteration: kuṭajair arjunais tālais tikalais timiśair api
english: The monkeys filled the Ocean with Sālas, and Ašvakarņas, dhavas, bamboo's and kutajas, arjunas, palms, tilakas, tinicas, billakas, saptaparnas, and blossoming karnikāras, mangoes, and asoka trees.

sanskrit: चूतैः च अशोक वृक्षैः च सागरम् समपूरयन्
समूलामः च विमूलामः च पादपान् हरि सत्तमाः
transliteration: cūtaiḥ ca aśoka vṛkṣaiḥ ca sāgaram samapūrayan
samūlāmaḥ ca vimūlāmaḥ ca pādapān hari sattamāḥ

sanskrit: इन्द्र केतून् इव उद्यम्य प्रजह्रुर् हरयस् तरून्
transliteration: indra ketūn iva udyamya prajahrur harayas tarūn

sanskrit: नलः चक्रे महासेतुम् मध्ये नद नदी पतेः
transliteration: nalaḥ cakre mahāsetum madhye nada nadī pateḥ
english: And (the trees) dropping (into the deep), vexed it all around. And some took lines (for insuring straightness to the bridge). And at the middle of the lord of rivers and streams, Nala made a grand bridge measuring an hundred Yojanas.

sanskrit: बभूव तुमुलः शब्दस् तदा तस्मिन् महाउदधौ
transliteration: babhūva tumulaḥ śabdas tadā tasmin mahāudadhau

sanskrit: अह्ना तृतीयेन तथा योजनानि तु सागरे
transliteration: ahnā tṛtīyena tathā yojanāni tu sāgare

english: And on fourth day the exceedingly impetuous monkeys, bestirring themselves vigorously, did two and twenty Yojanas. And on the fifth day they monkeys leaping speedily twenty three Yojanas reaching to the fair shore.

sanskrit: बबन्ध सागरे सेतुम् यथा चास्य तथा पिता
स नलेन कृतः सेतुः सागरे मकर आलये
transliteration: babandha sāgare setum yathā cāsya tathā pitā
sa nalena kṛtaḥ setuḥ sāgare makara ālaye

sanskrit: शुशुभे सुभगः श्रीमान् स्वाती पथ इव अम्बरे
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाः च परम ऋषयः
transliteration: śuśubhe subhagaḥ śrīmān svātī patha iva ambare
tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāḥ ca parama ṛṣayaḥ

sanskrit: आप्लवन्तः प्लवन्तः च गर्जन्तः च प्लवम् गमाः
transliteration: āplavantaḥ plavantaḥ ca garjantaḥ ca plavam gamāḥ

sanskrit: तम् अचिन्त्यम् असह्यम् च अद्भुतम् लोम हर्षणम्
ददृशुः सर्व भूतानि सागरे सेतु बन्धनम्
transliteration: tam acintyam asahyam ca adbhutam loma harṣaṇam
dadṛśuḥ sarva bhūtāni sāgare setu bandhanam
english: The monkeys, leaping and bounding and roaring, as well as all creatures, beheld that building of the bridge the ocean, on inconceivable, and marvellous, displaying skill past thought and capable of making one's hair stand on end.

sanskrit: बध्नन्तः सागरे सेतुम् जग्मुः पारम् महाउदधेः
transliteration: badhnantaḥ sāgare setum jagmuḥ pāram mahāudadheḥ
english: And those thousands of Koțis of exceeding vigour, having constructed the bridge over the ocean, went over to the other shore of the mighty main.
And spacious, skilfully constructed, graceful, well-paved and nicely finished, the great bridge appeared like the line where the hair has been parted on the Ocean's head.

sanskrit: ततः परे समुद्रस्य गदा पाणिर् विभीषणः
परेषाम् अभिघत अर्थम् अतिष्ठत् सचिवैः सह
transliteration: tataḥ pare samudrasya gadā pāṇir vibhīṣaṇaḥ
pareṣām abhighata artham atiṣṭhat sacivaiḥ saha
english: Then on the other shore of the ocean, Bibhisbana with the view of opposing foes (that might advance), stationed himself mace in hand, along with some councilors.

Then Sugrīva spoke to Rāma having truth for his prowess, Do you get upon Hanumān, and let Laksmana get upon Angada. O hero, vast is this Ocean-abode of Makaras. These monkeys, rangers of the sky, shall hold you up both.

sanskrit: अयम् हि विपुलो वीर सागरो मकरालयः
transliteration: ayam hi vipulo vīra sāgaro makarālayaḥ
english: Then Sugrīva spoke to Rāma having truth for his prowess, Do you get upon Hanumān, and let Laksmana get upon Angada. O hero, vast is this Ocean-abode of Makaras. These monkeys, rangers of the sky, shall hold you up both.

sanskrit: अग्रतस् तस्य सैन्यस्य श्रीमान् रामः सलक्ष्मणः
जगाम धन्वी धर्म आत्मा सुग्रीवेण समन्वितः
transliteration: agratas tasya sainyasya śrīmān rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
jagāma dhanvī dharma ātmā sugrīveṇa samanvitaḥ
english: Thereat the graceful and righteous Rāma along with Laksmana, equipped with his bow, set out in the van of the army in company with Sugriva.

sanskrit: अन्ये मध्येन गच्चन्ति पार्श्वतो अन्ये प्लवम् गमाः
सलिले प्रपतन्ति अन्ये मार्गम् अन्ये न लेभिरे
transliteration: anye madhyena gaccanti pārśvato anye plavam gamāḥ
salile prapatanti anye mārgam anye na lebhire
english: And some monkeys proceeded along the middle, and some plunged into the deep, and some went by the road. And some coursed through the air, bounding up bird-like.

sanskrit: केचिद् वैहायस गताः सुपर्णा इव पुप्लुवुः
transliteration: kecid vaihāyasa gatāḥ suparṇā iva pupluvuḥ

sanskrit: भीमम् अन्तर् दधे भीमा तरन्ती हरि वाहिनी
वानराणाम् हि सा तीर्णा वाहिनी नल सेतुना
transliteration: bhīmam antar dadhe bhīmā tarantī hari vāhinī
vānarāṇām hi sā tīrṇā vāhinī nala setunā

sanskrit: तीरे निविविशे राज्ञा बहु मूल फल उदके
transliteration: tīre niviviśe rājñā bahu mūla phala udake
english: Beholding that work of Rāghava incapable of being performed the deities together with the Siddhas and Caranas, and the Maharsis, suddenly presenting themselves before Rāma, sprinkled him one by one with sacred water, and said.

sanskrit: इति इव रामम् नर देव सत्कृतम्
transliteration: iti iva rāmam nara deva satkṛtam
english: May you be victorious, O human-divine one! Rule you the Earth eternally! Thus in various auspicious words, did they pay homage to that one honoured by the Brāhmanas, Rāma.
Having seen omens, that one, Laksmina's elder brother, conversant with them, embracing the son of Sumitrā, said these words.

sanskrit: बलौ घम् सम्विभज्येमम् व्यूह्य तिष्ठेम लक्ष्मण
transliteration: balau gham samvibhajyemam vyūhya tiṣṭhema lakṣmaṇa
english: O Laksmana, occupying (this tract) of cool waters and woods affluent with fruits, will we, dividing and arranging our forces, stay here.
Mighty is the fear that I see at hand, boding destruction to people and the slaughter of the foremost heroes of bears, monkeys and Rākşasas.

sanskrit: वाताश्च कलुषा वान्ति कम्पते च वसुन्धरा
transliteration: vātāśca kaluṣā vānti kampate ca vasundharā
english: The wind blow darkly, and the Earth shake. The tops of the mountains tremble, and trees topple down.
The clouds are ashen and roistering, and roar roughly. And lowering, they shower portentous drops of blood.
The twilight is terrible and look like the red sandal. And a fiery circle dropped from the flaming sun.
And on all sides birds and beasts, distressed, uttering woe-begone notes, and grim-visaged, set up cries against the sun, arousing great fear.
The Moon, although not appearing* in the night, burns, and with dark and red rays rises, as if it intended to exterminate people. *The moon, it seems appear, but does not look out clearly.

sanskrit: आदित्ये विमले वीलम् लक्ष्म लक्ष्मण दृश्यते
transliteration: āditye vimale vīlam lakṣma lakṣmaṇa dṛśyate
english: The aspect (of the sun) is slight, rough, and good;* and, O Lakşmaņa, a blue mark is visible on the unclouded Sun. *Prasasta-I do not see the propriety of this epithet in this connection. This may be a mistake.

sanskrit: रजसा महता चापि नक्षत्राणि हतानि च
transliteration: rajasā mahatā cāpi nakṣatrāṇi hatāni ca
english: The stars seem crased by a mighty volume of dust. O Lakşmaņa, behold this sight disastrous to people like to the universal dissolution.

sanskrit: काकाः श्येनास्तथा नीचा गृध्राः परिपतन्ति च
transliteration: kākāḥ śyenāstathā nīcā gṛdhrāḥ paripatanti ca
english: Crows, and hawks, and the inferior vultures, wheel all round. And jackals are sending inauspicious yells, exciting great fear.
The earth shall be covered with darts and javelins, and swords discharged by monkeys and Räkşasas, and be turned into mire with flesh and gore.
Surrounded by all the monkeys, will we, using speed, this very day rapidly enter into the city ruled by Ravana, incapable of being subdued.

Having said this, that subduer in conflict, that lord, that enchanter of men, Rāma,* equipped with his bow, proceeded in the direction of Lankā. *The word Räma occurs twice, one being the cognomen of the solar hero. The other means, the enchanter of men.
And all the principal monkeys-Sugrīva with Vibhisana-went on, setting up roars, for the destruction of foes, who were determined to battle with them.
And consequently Raghu's son was well pleased with the fortitude and exertions of the powerful monkeys, for bringing about what dear to Ravhava.
With the presence of the king* that assembly of heroes looked beautiful, as does the autumnal night, garnished with beauteous stars, with the Moon. *Rāma.

sanskrit: प्रचचाल च वेगेन त्रस्ता चैव वसुन्धरा
transliteration: pracacāla ca vegena trastā caiva vasundharā
english: And oppressed with the bursting energy of the host resembling the ocean, the Earth trembled.
Then the rangers of the forest heard a hubbub in Lankä, as well as the sounds of trumpets and Mşdangas, mighty and capable of making people's down stand on end.
At those sounds, the leaders of monkey-bands were delighted beyond measure, and, resenting the same, set up cries louder than those sounds.
The Rākşasas also heard the roars of the monkeys, resembling the rumbling of haughty clouds in the sky.
Beholding Lankā with variegated standards, and streamers, Dasaratha's son went* to Sītā with an aggrieved heart. *i.e. mentally.
Here that one having eyes resembling those of a young deer, is confined by Rāvana, like to Rohini overpowered by the red-bodied planet.* *Angāraka.

sanskrit: दीर्घमुष्णम् च निःश्वस्य समुद्वीक्ष्य च लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: dīrghamuṣṇam ca niḥśvasya samudvīkṣya ca lakṣmaṇam
english: Sighing hot and long, and looking at Laks maņa, that hero spoke words fraught with his good at that time.
Behold, O Laksmana, Lanka towering up as if piercing the heavens; and, built by Viśvakarmā on the brow of the mountain, she seems to have been made by the Mind.
Constructed in time past with edifices thronging her, Larkā looks the all-encasing air, covered with pale clouds.
Larikā is embellished with groves resembling Citraratha, fair, and eloquent with the notes of various birds, and fraught with fruits and flowers.
Behold the intoxicated birds, and the black bees blending (with the blossoms). And the blessed breeze sway the trees vocal with the coels.
Having divided his forces there agreeably to the directions of the scriptures, Dasaratha's son, Rāma, thus spoke to Laksmana.

sanskrit: अङ्गदः सह नीलेन तिष्ठे दुरपि दुर्जयः
transliteration: aṅgadaḥ saha nīlena tiṣṭhe durapi durjayaḥ
english: He ordered that monkey-army, saying, taking his own forces, let the puissant and invincible Angada along with Nila, station himself in the centre of the forces.
Let the monkey, named Rşabha, surrounded by numbers of monkeys, post himself at the right of the monkey-army.
Let the active and irrepressible Gandhamādana, resembling an elephant fragrant with the temporal exudation, stay, occupying the left of the forces.

I myself along with Lakşmaņa, shall heedfully stay in the fore-front. And the monkeys, Jāmvabān, Sușeņa and Vagadarci, the three high-souled, foremost bears,* shall protect the interior (of the forces). *The epithet 'bear' coming after 'monkey' may look incongruous; but, I fancy, 'monkeys' is used in the general sense of being connected with the monkeys-hest.

sanskrit: ऋक्षमुख्या महात्मानः कुक्षिम् रक्षन्तु ते त्रयः
transliteration: ṛkṣamukhyā mahātmānaḥ kukṣim rakṣantu te trayaḥ

sanskrit: इति स्म दधिरे सर्वे मानाम्सि हरिपुङ्गवाः
transliteration: iti sma dadhire sarve mānāmsi haripuṅgavāḥ

sanskrit: रामस्य तु वचः श्रुत्वा वानरेन्द्रो महाबलः
transliteration: rāmasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā vānarendro mahābalaḥ

sanskrit: मोचयामास तम् दूतम् शुकम् रामस्य शासनात्
transliteration: mocayāmāsa tam dūtam śukam rāmasya śāsanāt

sanskrit: किमिमौ ते सितौ पक्षौ लूनपक्ष्श्च दृश्यसे
transliteration: kimimau te sitau pakṣau lūnapakṣśca dṛśyase
english: There at, Ravana, laughing, said to Suka, Are your wings fettered? And you seemst as if your wings had been severed. Why? Did you come under the control of the volatile (monkeys)?
Thereat, exercised with fear, Suka, commanded by the monarch, answered the lord of Rākşasas in this excellent speech, saying.
Repairing to the northern shore of the sea, I, pacifying (the monkeys) with mild speech, communicated your tidings clearly (to Sugrīva).

sanskrit: गृहितोऽस्म्यपि चारब्धो हन्तुम् लोप्तुम् च मुष्टिभिः
transliteration: gṛhito'smyapi cārabdho hantum loptum ca muṣṭibhiḥ
english: Thereat, as soon as they saw me, the monkeys flying into a wrath, captured me, and attempted to clip my wings and slay me with their clenched fists.

sanskrit: न ते सम्भाषितुम् शक्याः सम्प्रश्नोऽत्र न विद्यते
transliteration: na te sambhāṣitum śakyāḥ sampraśno'tra na vidyate
english: They are insuseptible of being spoken, to. No doubt whatever can exist that, o lord of Rāskhasas, the monkeys are by nature wrathful and fierce.

sanskrit: स च हन्ता विराधस्य कबन्धस्य खरस्य च
transliteration: sa ca hantā virādhasya kabandhasya kharasya ca
english: The same Rāma that has slain Virādha and Kabandha and Khara, has arrived (here) along with Sugrīva, searching for the whereabouts of Sītă.

sanskrit: स कृत्वा सागरे सेतुम् तीर्त्वा च लवणोदधिम्
एष रक्षासि निर्धूय धन्वी तिष्ठति राघवः
transliteration: sa kṛtvā sāgare setum tīrtvā ca lavaṇodadhim
eṣa rakṣāsi nirdhūya dhanvī tiṣṭhati rāghavaḥ
english: Having thrown a bridge across the brine and crossed the salt sea, Rāghava, equipped with his bow, stay here, setting the Raksasa at naught.
The hosts consisting of thousands of bears and monkeys, resembling hills and clouds, envelope the Earth.
And peace there can be none between the forces of the Rákşasas and the hosts of the sovereign of monkeys, like to the deities and the Danavas.

sanskrit: सीताम् वास्मै प्रयच्चाशु युद्धम् वापि प्रदीयताम्
transliteration: sītām vāsmai prayaccāśu yuddham vāpi pradīyatām
english: They advance before the wall. Speedily do one of these things-make over Sītā without delay, or give (him) battle.

sanskrit: शुकस्य वचनम् श्रुत्वा रावणो वाक्य मब्रवीत्
transliteration: śukasya vacanam śrutvā rāvaṇo vākya mabravīt
english: Hearing Suka's speech, Ravana with his eyes reddened in wrath, spoke, as if burning (Suka) with them.
Even if gods, and Gandharvas, and Danavas should array themselves against me, I will not from fear of all creatures, render (back) Sītā.

sanskrit: वसन्ते पुष्पितम् मत्ता भ्रमरा इव पादपम्
transliteration: vasante puṣpitam mattā bhramarā iva pādapam
english: When shall my shafts pursue Raghava, like maddened Bhramaras making towards blossomy trees in spring?
When by means of flaming shafts shot from my bow shall I burn (Rāghava) with his body bathed in blood, even as a meteor (burn) an elephant?
When, surrounded by a mighty host, shall I confound his ranks, even as the Sun arising, (vanquish) the light of the stellar spheres?

sanskrit: सागरस्येव मे वेगो मारुतस्येव मे बलम्
न च दाशरथिर्वेद तेन माम् योद्धुमिच्चति
transliteration: sāgarasyeva me vego mārutasyeva me balam
na ca dāśarathirveda tena mām yoddhumiccati
english: My impetuosity like the Ocean's, my strength like the Wind's, Dācarathi does not know, and therefore it is that he desire to fight with me.

sanskrit: न मे तूणीशयान् बाणान् सनिषानिव पन्नगान्
रामः पश्यति सम्ग्रामे तेन माम् योद्धुमिच्चति
transliteration: na me tūṇīśayān bāṇān saniṣāniva pannagān
rāmaḥ paśyati samgrāme tena mām yoddhumiccati
english: Rāma has not seen my shafts resting in the quiver, resembling venomous serpents, and therefore it is that he seek to fight with me.

sanskrit: न जानाति पुरा वीर्यम् मम युद्धे स राघवः
transliteration: na jānāti purā vīryam mama yuddhe sa rāghavaḥ

english: Neither the thousand-eyed Vasava, Varuna himself, can (cope) with me in battle; nor can Yama, or Vaiśravana's self vanquish me in mighty conflict with the fire of arrows. nor
On Dasaratha's son, Rama, having crossed the Ocean with his forces, the graceful Răvaņa addressed his two counsellors, Suka and Sarana, saying.
The crossing the entire ocean incapable of being crossed, by the monkey-forces, and the building over the sea of the bridge by Rāma, all this had never happened before.
The construction of a bridge over the ocean cannot at all command credence. But (however it be), I must enumerate the monkey-hosts.
Being thus commissioned, these heroes, the Raksasas, Suka and Sarana, assuming monkeyshapes, entered into the hosts of monkeys.
But Suka and Sāraṇa could not number that army of monkeys, incomprehensible and capable of making people's hair stand on end.

The forces were on mountain-tops, by fountains and in caves. And those rangers of the night beheld those forces, some having already crossed, and some crossing, and some intent on doing so, and some having sat down and some sitting that mighty army sending terrific roars, that ocean of hosts incapable of being disturbed.
As they remained thus disguised, they were discovered by Vibhisana. Thereat, taking them captive, he unfolded (the fact) to Rama, saying.
These are the counsellors of the lord of Raksasas-Suka and Sarana. O captor of hostile capitals, they have come as spies from Lankā.
Seeing Ráma, they were greatly afflicted, and, despairing of their lives and exercised with fear, with joined hands, said.
O placid one, commanded by Ravana, we have come here, O son of Raghu, for the purpose of gathering information concerning this army.
Hearing their speech, Rāma, son to Dasaratha, ever engaged in the welfare of all beings, laughing, remarked.
If you have heedfully noted this entire array, or if you have done what you had been commanded to do, return in peace.
If aught remain unseen, do you see it anew. Or Vibhīşaņa will again fully show it to you.
Having been taken, you need not fear on the score of your lives. Even if envoys happen to be taken who are equipped with weapons, they should not be slain.
And albeit these night-rangers have come as spies in disguise, with the view of creating division among their foes, yet, O Vibhisana, let them off.
Entering the extensive Lankā, you should say to the king-younger brother to the Dispenser of riches-the words which I utter.
That force relying on which you have carried away my Sita, do you as you wish, along with your forces and friends, display the same.
On the morning of the morrow behold the city of Larikā with her wall and gates, as well as the hosts of Räkşasas, destroyed by me with my shafts.
As Väsava equipped with the thunder-bolt hurled the same amidst the Dänavas, will I, O Rāvana, on the morning of the morrow pour down my dreadful ire upon you along with your forces.
Being thus commissioned, these heroes, the Raksasas, Suka and Sarana, assuming monkeyshapes, entered into the hosts of monkeys.
Thus directed (by Rama), those Raksasas, Śuka and Säraņa, having saluted the righteous Raghava with 'Victory!,' came (back) to Lanka and spoke to the lord of Rākşasas, saying.
O lord of Rākşasas, having been taken by Vibhīşaņa for the purpose of being slain, we came to be seen by the righteous-souled Rāma of immeasurable energy, and (finally) were liberated (by him).
Such is Rāma's figure and arms that he shall alone demolish Lankā, leave the other three alone.
That host protected by Rāma, Lakşmaņa and Sugrīva, shall become exceedingly hard to combat even by the Asuras and gods.

The army of the high-souled rangers of the woods, eager for encounter, contains warriors bursting with high spirits. No use of dispute. Be you intent on pacification. Do you render back Maithili to Dasaratha's son.

sanskrit: तद् वचः पथ्यम् अक्लीबम् सारणेन अभिभाषितम्
transliteration: tad vacaḥ pathyam aklībam sāraṇena abhibhāṣitam
english: Hearing Sarana's words, pregnant and truthful, king Ravana addressed him, saying.

sanskrit: यदि माम् अभियुन्जीरन् देव गन्धर्व दानवाः
न एव सीताम् प्रदास्यामि सर्व लोक भयाद् अपि
transliteration: yadi mām abhiyunjīran deva gandharva dānavāḥ
na eva sītām pradāsyāmi sarva loka bhayād api
english: Even if the gods, Gandharvas and Dänavas should attack me, Sītā will I not part with from fear of all creatures.

sanskrit: त्वम् तु सौम्य परित्रस्तो हरिभिर् निर्जितो भृशम्
प्रतिप्रदानम् अद्य एव सीतायाः साधु मन्यसे
transliteration: tvam tu saumya paritrasto haribhir nirjito bhṛśam
pratipradānam adya eva sītāyāḥ sādhu manyase
english: O amiable one, you, having been hard handled by the monkeys and distressed in consequence, deems it fit that Sītā should be rendered back this very day. What foe of mine is there who is competent to conquer me in battle?

sanskrit: को हि नाम सपत्नो माम् समरे जेतुम् अर्हति
इति उक्त्वा परुषम् वाक्यम् रावणो राक्षस अधिपः
transliteration: ko hi nāma sapatno mām samare jetum arhati
iti uktvā paruṣam vākyam rāvaṇo rākṣasa adhipaḥ

sanskrit: आरुरोह ततः श्रीमान् प्रासादम् हिम पाण्डुरम्
बहु ताल समुत्सेधम् रावणो अथ दिदृक्षया
transliteration: āruroha tataḥ śrīmān prāsādam hima pāṇḍuram
bahu tāla samutsedham rāvaṇo atha didṛkṣayā
english: Having uttered this rough speech, the graceful Ravana-lord of the Raksasas, desirous of surveying (the monkey-hosts), ascended an edifice white like snow, and elevated like many palms (placed one upon another).

sanskrit: ताभ्याम् चराभ्याम् सहितो रावणः क्रोध मूर्चितः
पश्यमानः समुद्रम् च पर्वतामः च वनानि च
transliteration: tābhyām carābhyām sahito rāvaṇaḥ krodha mūrcitaḥ
paśyamānaḥ samudram ca parvatāmaḥ ca vanāni ca

sanskrit: ददर्श पृथिवी देशम् सुसम्पूर्णम् प्लवम् गमैः
तद् अपारम् असम्ख्येयम् वानराणाम् महद् बलम्
transliteration: dadarśa pṛthivī deśam susampūrṇam plavam gamaiḥ
tad apāram asamkhyeyam vānarāṇām mahad balam

sanskrit: एषाम् वानर मुख्यानाम् के शूराः के महाबलाः
transliteration: eṣām vānara mukhyānām ke śūrāḥ ke mahābalāḥ

sanskrit: केषाम् शृणोति सुग्रीवः के वा यूथप यूथपाः
transliteration: keṣām śṛṇoti sugrīvaḥ ke vā yūthapa yūthapāḥ
english: Who, bursting with spirits, stay all about the fore? Whom does Sugriva listen to? And who are the leaders of the monkey-leader? O Sarana, relate you all this to me. And what is the prowess of the monkeys?

sanskrit: सारण आचक्ष्व मे सर्वम् के प्रधानाः प्लवम् गमाः
transliteration: sāraṇa ācakṣva me sarvam ke pradhānāḥ plavam gamāḥ

sanskrit: आचचक्षे अथ मुख्यज्ञो मुख्याम्स् ताम्स् तु वन ओकसः
एष यो अभिमुखो लंकाम् नर्दम्स् तिष्ठति वानरः
transliteration: ācacakṣe atha mukhyajño mukhyāms tāms tu vana okasaḥ
eṣa yo abhimukho laṃkām nardams tiṣṭhati vānaraḥ

sanskrit: लंका प्रवेपते सर्वा सशैल वन कानना
सर्व शाखा मृग इन्द्रस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
transliteration: laṃkā pravepate sarvā saśaila vana kānanā
sarva śākhā mṛga indrasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ

sanskrit: बल अग्रे तिष्ठते वीरो नीलो नाम एष यूथपः
बाहू प्रगृह्य यः पद्भ्याम् महीम् गच्चति वीर्यवान्
transliteration: bala agre tiṣṭhate vīro nīlo nāma eṣa yūthapaḥ
bāhū pragṛhya yaḥ padbhyām mahīm gaccati vīryavān

sanskrit: लंकाम् अभिमुखः कोपाद् अभीक्ष्णम् च विजृम्भते
गिरि शृन्ग प्रतीकाशः पद्म किन्जल्क सम्निभः
transliteration: laṃkām abhimukhaḥ kopād abhīkṣṇam ca vijṛmbhate
giri śṛnga pratīkāśaḥ padma kinjalka samnibhaḥ

sanskrit: स्फोटयति अभिसम्रब्धो लान्गूलम् च पुनः पुनः
यस्य लान्गूल शब्देन स्वनन्ति इव दिशो दश
transliteration: sphoṭayati abhisamrabdho lāngūlam ca punaḥ punaḥ
yasya lāngūla śabdena svananti iva diśo daśa

sanskrit: यौवराज्ये अन्गदो नाम त्वाम् आह्वयति सम्युगे
transliteration: yauvarājye angado nāma tvām āhvayati samyuge

sanskrit: वालिनः सदृशः पुत्रः सुग्रीवस्य सदा प्रियः
transliteration: vālinaḥ sadṛśaḥ putraḥ sugrīvasya sadā priyaḥ
english: The worthy son of Vālī and ever dear to Sugrīva, he puts forth his prowess, as Varuņa does for Sakra. That that well-wished of Rāghava, the vehement Hanumān, has seen Janaka's daughter, was owing to the advice of this one.

sanskrit: एतस्य सा मतिः सर्वा यद्दृष्टा जनकात्मजा
transliteration: etasya sā matiḥ sarvā yaddṛṣṭā janakātmajā
english: The worthy son of Vālī and ever dear to Sugrīva, he puts forth his prowess, as Varuņa does for Sakra. That that well-wished of Rāghava, the vehement Hanumān, has seen Janaka's daughter, was owing to the advice of this one.
That powerful (hero) is proceeding, taking innumerable bands belonging to the lord of monkeys, for the purpose of beating you by means of his soldiery.
Following Väli's son, and surrounded by a mighty force, stay in the field the heroic Nala, the builder of the bridge.

sanskrit: ये तु विष्टभ्य गात्राणि क्ष्वेडयन्ति नदन्ति च
उत्थाय च विजृम्भन्ते क्रोधेन हरि पुम्गवाः
transliteration: ye tu viṣṭabhya gātrāṇi kṣveḍayanti nadanti ca
utthāya ca vijṛmbhante krodhena hari pumgavāḥ
english: Those that with their limbs lying inactive, and setting up roars and ululation's, are following this one,' are heroes dwelling in Candana.? *The reference is prospective. It means the monkeys, Sveta, in the next slok.

sanskrit: एते दुष्प्रसहा घोराः चण्डाः चण्ड पराक्रमाः
अष्टौ शत सहस्राणि दश कोटि शतानि च
transliteration: ete duṣprasahā ghorāḥ caṇḍāḥ caṇḍa parākramāḥ
aṣṭau śata sahasrāṇi daśa koṭi śatāni ca

sanskrit: य एनम् अनुगच्चन्ति वीराः चन्दन वासिनः
एष आशम्सते लंकाम् स्वेन अनीकेन मर्दितुम्
transliteration: ya enam anugaccanti vīrāḥ candana vāsinaḥ
eṣa āśamsate laṃkām svena anīkena marditum

sanskrit: श्वेतो रजत सम्काशः सबलो भीम विक्रमः
बुद्धिमान् वानरः शूरस् त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः
transliteration: śveto rajata samkāśaḥ sabalo bhīma vikramaḥ
buddhimān vānaraḥ śūras triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ

sanskrit: तूर्णम् सुग्रीवम् आगम्य पुनर् गच्चति वानरः
transliteration: tūrṇam sugrīvam āgamya punar gaccati vānaraḥ

sanskrit: यः पुरा गोमती तीरे रम्यम् पर्येति पर्वतम्
नाम्ना सम्कोचनो नाम नाना नग युतो गिरिः
transliteration: yaḥ purā gomatī tīre ramyam paryeti parvatam
nāmnā samkocano nāma nānā naga yuto giriḥ
english: From days of yore on the banks of the Gomatī there is a mountain, (named) Ramya, (otherwise) called Sanrocana. The mount abounds with various trees. There that leader of bands, named Kumuda, governs his kingdom.

sanskrit: तत्र राज्यम् प्रशास्ति एष कुमुदो नाम यूथपः
यो असौ शत सहस्राणाम् सहस्रम् परिकर्षति
transliteration: tatra rājyam praśāsti eṣa kumudo nāma yūthapaḥ
yo asau śata sahasrāṇām sahasram parikarṣati

sanskrit: यस्य वाला बहु व्यामा दीर्घ लान्गूलम् आश्रिताः
ताम्राः पीताः सिताः श्वेताः प्रकीर्णा घोर कर्मणः
transliteration: yasya vālā bahu vyāmā dīrgha lāngūlam āśritāḥ
tāmrāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ prakīrṇā ghora karmaṇaḥ
english: He that cheerfully draws after him hundreds and thousands of monkeys, and the long grim hairs of whose tail, coppery, yellow, sable and white, are cast about, is the energetic monkey, Canda, eager for encounter. And he hopes to conquer Laňkā by help of his own forces.

sanskrit: एष एव आशम्सते लंकाम् स्वेन अनीकेन मर्दितुम्
transliteration: eṣa eva āśamsate laṃkām svena anīkena marditum

sanskrit: यस् त्व् एष सिम्ह सम्काशः कपिलो दीर्घ केसरः
निभृतः प्रेक्षते लंकाम् दिधक्षन्न् इव चक्षुषा
transliteration: yas tv eṣa simha samkāśaḥ kapilo dīrgha kesaraḥ
nibhṛtaḥ prekṣate laṃkām didhakṣann iva cakṣuṣā

sanskrit: विन्ध्यम् कृष्ण गिरिम् सह्यम् पर्वतम् च सुदर्शनम्
राजन् सततम् अध्यास्ते रम्भो नाम एष यूथपः
transliteration: vindhyam kṛṣṇa girim sahyam parvatam ca sudarśanam
rājan satatam adhyāste rambho nāma eṣa yūthapaḥ

sanskrit: शतम् शत सहस्राणाम् त्रिम्शच् च हरि यूथपाः
transliteration: śatam śata sahasrāṇām trimśac ca hari yūthapāḥ

sanskrit: यस् तु कर्णौ विवृणुते जृम्भते च पुनः पुनः
transliteration: yas tu karṇau vivṛṇute jṛmbhate ca punaḥ punaḥ

sanskrit: न च सम्विजते मृत्योर् न च यूथाद् विधावति
transliteration: na ca samvijate mṛtyor na ca yūthād vidhāvati

sanskrit: महाबलो वीत भयो रम्यम् साल्वेय पर्वतम्
transliteration: mahābalo vīta bhayo ramyam sālveya parvatam

sanskrit: राजन् सततम् अध्यास्ते शरभो नाम यूथपः
एतस्य बलिनः सर्वे विहारा नाम यूथपाः
transliteration: rājan satatam adhyāste śarabho nāma yūthapaḥ
etasya balinaḥ sarve vihārā nāma yūthapāḥ

sanskrit: राजन् शत सहस्राणि चत्वारिम्शत् तथैव च
यस् तु मेघ इव आकाशम् महान् आवृत्य तिष्ठति
transliteration: rājan śata sahasrāṇi catvārimśat tathaiva ca
yas tu megha iva ākāśam mahān āvṛtya tiṣṭhati

sanskrit: मध्ये वानर वीराणाम् सुराणाम् इव वासवः
भेरीणाम् इव सम्नादो यस्य एष श्रूयते महान्
transliteration: madhye vānara vīrāṇām surāṇām iva vāsavaḥ
bherīṇām iva samnādo yasya eṣa śrūyate mahān

sanskrit: घोरः शाखा मृग इन्द्राणाम् सम्ग्रामम् अभिकान्क्षताम्
transliteration: ghoraḥ śākhā mṛga indrāṇām samgrāmam abhikānkṣatām

sanskrit: युद्धे दुष्प्रसहो नित्यम् पनसो नाम यूथपः
एनम् शत सहस्राणाम् शत अर्धम् पर्युपासते
transliteration: yuddhe duṣprasaho nityam panaso nāma yūthapaḥ
enam śata sahasrāṇām śata ardham paryupāsate

sanskrit: यूथपा यूथप श्रेष्ठम् येषाम् यूथानि भागशः
यस् तु भीमाम् प्रवल्गन्तीम् चमूम् तिष्ठति शोभयन्
transliteration: yūthapā yūthapa śreṣṭham yeṣām yūthāni bhāgaśaḥ
yas tu bhīmām pravalgantīm camūm tiṣṭhati śobhayan

sanskrit: स्थिताम् तीरे समुद्रस्य द्वितीय इव सागरः
एष दर्दर सम्काशो विनतो नाम यूथपः
transliteration: sthitām tīre samudrasya dvitīya iva sāgaraḥ
eṣa dardara samkāśo vinato nāma yūthapaḥ

sanskrit: पिबमः चरति पर्णाशाम् नदीनाम् उत्तमाम् नदीम्
षष्टिः शत सहस्राणि बलम् अस्य प्लवम् गमाः
transliteration: pibamaḥ carati parṇāśām nadīnām uttamām nadīm
ṣaṣṭiḥ śata sahasrāṇi balam asya plavam gamāḥ

sanskrit: त्वाम् आह्वयति युद्धाय क्रथनो नाम यूथपः
transliteration: tvām āhvayati yuddhāya krathano nāma yūthapaḥ
english: The monkey, named Krathana, challenges you to conflict. He has (under him) powerful and vigorous generals, and forces well divided.

sanskrit: यस् तु गैरिक वर्ण आभम् वपुः पुष्यति वानरः
transliteration: yas tu gairika varṇa ābham vapuḥ puṣyati vānaraḥ

sanskrit: गवयो नाम तेजस्वी त्वाम् क्रोधाद् अभिवर्तते
एष आशम्सते लंकाम् स्वेन अनीकेन मर्दितुम्
transliteration: gavayo nāma tejasvī tvām krodhād abhivartate
eṣa āśamsate laṃkām svena anīkena marditum
english: The monkey owning that person of the hue of red chalk, and, who, elated with strength, disregard all the monkeys, is named Gavaya, who approach you wrathfully. Seventy lacs (of troops) girt him round; and by their means he hopes to bring down Lankā.

sanskrit: एते दुष्प्रसहा घोरा बलिनः काम रूपिणः
यूथपा यूथप श्रेष्ठा येषाम् सम्ख्या न विद्यते
transliteration: ete duṣprasahā ghorā balinaḥ kāma rūpiṇaḥ
yūthapā yūthapa śreṣṭhā yeṣām samkhyā na vidyate
english: These are the heroes, incapable of being borne, whose numbers cannot be enumerated. These are the leaders and the heads thereof, as well as the forces set in order of battle.

sanskrit: राघव अर्थे पराक्रान्ता ये न रक्षन्ति जीवितम्
transliteration: rāghava arthe parākrāntā ye na rakṣanti jīvitam
english: As you look on, I shall describe to you those leaders who shall put forth their prowess for Rāghava, and lay down their lives in his behalf.)

sanskrit: स्निग्धा यस्य बहु श्यामा बाला लान्गूलम् आश्रिताः
ताम्राः पीताः सिताः श्वेताः प्रकीर्णा घोर कर्मणः
transliteration: snigdhā yasya bahu śyāmā bālā lāngūlam āśritāḥ
tāmrāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ prakīrṇā ghora karmaṇaḥ

sanskrit: पृथिव्याम् च अनुकृष्यन्ते हरो नाम एष यूथपः
transliteration: pṛthivyām ca anukṛṣyante haro nāma eṣa yūthapaḥ

sanskrit: यम् पृष्ठतो अनुगच्चन्ति शतशो अथ सहस्रशः
transliteration: yam pṛṣṭhato anugaccanti śataśo atha sahasraśaḥ

sanskrit: नीलान् इव महामेघाम्स् तिष्ठतो याम्स् तु पश्यसि
transliteration: nīlān iva mahāmeghāms tiṣṭhato yāms tu paśyasi

sanskrit: असितान् जन सम्काशान् युद्धे सत्य पराक्रमान्
असम्ख्येयान् अनिर्देश्यान् परम् पारम् इव उदधेः
transliteration: asitān jana samkāśān yuddhe satya parākramān
