asamkhyeyān anirdeśyān param pāram iva udadheḥ

sanskrit: पर्वतेषु च ये केचिद् विषमेषु नदीषु च
एते त्वाम् अभिवर्तन्ते राजन्न् ऋष्काः सुदारुणाः
transliteration: parvateṣu ca ye kecid viṣameṣu nadīṣu ca
ete tvām abhivartante rājann ṛṣkāḥ sudāruṇāḥ

sanskrit: एषाम् मध्ये स्थितो राजन् भीम अक्षो भीम दर्शनः
transliteration: eṣām madhye sthito rājan bhīma akṣo bhīma darśanaḥ

sanskrit: ऋक्षवन्तम् गिरि श्रेष्ठम् अध्यास्ते नर्मदाम् पिबन्
सर्व ऋक्षाणाम् अधिपतिर् धूम्रो नाम एष यूथपः
transliteration: ṛkṣavantam giri śreṣṭham adhyāste narmadām piban
sarva ṛkṣāṇām adhipatir dhūmro nāma eṣa yūthapaḥ

sanskrit: यवीयान् अस्य तु भ्राता पश्य एनम् पर्वत उपमम्भ्रात्रा समानो रूपेण विशिष्टस् तु पराक्रमे
transliteration: yavīyān asya tu bhrātā paśya enam parvata upamambhrātrā samāno rūpeṇa viśiṣṭas tu parākrame
english: Behold this one resembling a hill-younger brother of Dhūmra, lord of all the bears. He is equal to this brother in beauty, and of superior prowess. This leader of redoubtable leaders is named Jämbavān. He is mild, obedient to his superiors and fierce in fight.

sanskrit: स एष जाम्बवान् नाम महायूथप यूथपः
प्रशान्तो गुरु वर्ती च सम्प्रहारेष्व् अमर्षणः
transliteration: sa eṣa jāmbavān nāma mahāyūthapa yūthapaḥ
praśānto guru vartī ca samprahāreṣv amarṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: एतेन साह्यम् सुमहत् कृतम् शक्रस्य धीमता
देव असुरे जाम्बवता लब्धाः च बहवो वराः
transliteration: etena sāhyam sumahat kṛtam śakrasya dhīmatā
deva asure jāmbavatā labdhāḥ ca bahavo varāḥ
english: The intelligent Jāmbavan assisted Sakra signally in the war of the gods and Asuras, and he has won many boons (in consequence).

sanskrit: आरुह्य पर्वत अग्रेभ्यो महाअभ्र विपुलाः शिलाः
मुन्चन्ति विपुल आकारा न मृत्योर् उद्विजन्ति च
transliteration: āruhya parvata agrebhyo mahāabhra vipulāḥ śilāḥ
muncanti vipula ākārā na mṛtyor udvijanti ca
english: Ascending the tops of mountains, these hurl down gigantic crags huge as colossal clouds, for does (the fear of)-death (ever) disquiet them. And their bodies covered with hair, they resemble Raksasas and ghosts (in their conduct).

sanskrit: राक्षसानाम् च सदृशाः पिशाचानाम् च रोमशाः
एतस्य सैन्ये बहवो विचरन्ति अग्नि तेजसः
transliteration: rākṣasānām ca sadṛśāḥ piśācānām ca romaśāḥ
etasya sainye bahavo vicaranti agni tejasaḥ
english: Ascending the tops of mountains, these hurl down gigantic crags huge as colossal clouds, for does (the fear of)-death (ever) disquiet them. And their bodies covered with hair, they resemble Raksasas and ghosts (in their conduct).

sanskrit: यम् त्व् एनम् अभिसम्रब्धम् प्लवमानम् इव स्थितम्
प्रेक्षन्ते वानराः सर्वे स्थितम् यूथप यूथपम्
transliteration: yam tv enam abhisamrabdham plavamānam iva sthitam
prekṣante vānarāḥ sarve sthitam yūthapa yūthapam
english: This one one of immeasurable energy has innumerable troops going about, who behold this leader of leaders under unusual excitement leaping and resting (by turns). This lord of monkeys dwell near the thousand-eyed Deity; and this leader of hands, gifted with strength, is named Rambha.

sanskrit: एष राजन् सहस्र अक्षम् पर्युपास्ते हरि ईश्वरः
बलेन बल सम्पन्नो रम्भो नाम एष यूथपः
transliteration: eṣa rājan sahasra akṣam paryupāste hari īśvaraḥ
balena bala sampanno rambho nāma eṣa yūthapaḥ
english: This one one of immeasurable energy has innumerable troops going about, who behold this leader of leaders under unusual excitement leaping and resting (by turns). This lord of monkeys dwell near the thousand-eyed Deity; and this leader of hands, gifted with strength, is named Rambha.

sanskrit: यः स्थितम् योजने शैलम् गच्चन् पार्श्वेन सेवते
ऊर्ध्वम् तथैव कायेन गतः प्राप्नोति योजनम्
transliteration: yaḥ sthitam yojane śailam gaccan pārśvena sevate
ūrdhvam tathaiva kāyena gataḥ prāpnoti yojanam

sanskrit: यस्मान् न परमम् रूपम् चतुष्पादेषु विद्यते
transliteration: yasmān na paramam rūpam catuṣpādeṣu vidyate

sanskrit: येन युद्धम् तदा दत्तम् रणे शक्रस्य धीमता
पराजयः च न प्राप्तः सो अयम् यूथप यूथपः
transliteration: yena yuddham tadā dattam raṇe śakrasya dhīmatā
parājayaḥ ca na prāptaḥ so ayam yūthapa yūthapaḥ

sanskrit: एष गन्धर्व कन्यायाम् उत्पन्नः कृष्ण वर्त्मना
transliteration: eṣa gandharva kanyāyām utpannaḥ kṛṣṇa vartmanā

sanskrit: यो राजा पर्वत इन्द्राणाम् बहु किम्नर सेविनाम्
विहार सुखदो नित्यम् भ्रातुस् ते राक्षस अधिप
transliteration: yo rājā parvata indrāṇām bahu kimnara sevinām
vihāra sukhado nityam bhrātus te rākṣasa adhipa

sanskrit: तत्र एष वसति श्रीमान् बलवान् वानर ऋषभः
युद्धेष्व् अकत्थनो नित्यम् क्रथनो नाम यूथपः
transliteration: tatra eṣa vasati śrīmān balavān vānara ṛṣabhaḥ
yuddheṣv akatthano nityam krathano nāma yūthapaḥ

sanskrit: हरीणाम् वाहिनी मुख्यो नदीम् हैमवतीम् अनु
उशीर बीजम् आश्रित्य पर्वतम् मन्दर उपमम्
transliteration: harīṇām vāhinī mukhyo nadīm haimavatīm anu
uśīra bījam āśritya parvatam mandara upamam

sanskrit: रमते वानर श्रेष्ठो दिवि शक्र इव स्वयम्
transliteration: ramate vānara śreṣṭho divi śakra iva svayam

sanskrit: स एष नेता न्हैतेषाम् वानराणाम् महात्मनम्
transliteration: sa eṣa netā nhaiteṣām vānarāṇām mahātmanam

sanskrit: स एष दुर्मर्षणो राजन् प्रमाथी नाम यूथपः
वातेन इव उद्धतम् मेघम् यम् एनम् अनुपश्यसि
transliteration: sa eṣa durmarṣaṇo rājan pramāthī nāma yūthapaḥ
vātena iva uddhatam megham yam enam anupaśyasi

sanskrit: विवर्तमानम् बहुशो यत्र एतद् बहुलम् रजः
एते असित मुखा घोरा गो लान्गूला महाबलाः
transliteration: vivartamānam bahuśo yatra etad bahulam rajaḥ
ete asita mukhā ghorā go lāngūlā mahābalāḥ

sanskrit: शतम् शत सहस्राणि दृष्ट्वा वै सेतु बन्धनम्
गो लान्गूलम् महावेगम् गव अक्षम् नाम यूथपम्
transliteration: śatam śata sahasrāṇi dṛṣṭvā vai setu bandhanam
go lāngūlam mahāvegam gava akṣam nāma yūthapam
english: These wondrous strong and dreadful Golāngülas* numbering hundreds and hundred thousands, seeing the building of the bridge, surrounding, O mighty monarch, the leader named Gavākṣa—a Golāngūla-set up shouts, intending to demolish Lankā with their prowess. *Vide anti.

sanskrit: भ्रमर आचरिता यत्र सर्व काम फल द्रुमाः
transliteration: bhramara ācaritā yatra sarva kāma phala drumāḥ

sanskrit: यम् सूर्य तुल्य वर्ण आभम् अनुपर्येति पर्वतम्
यस्य भासा सदा भान्ति तद् वर्णा मृग पक्षिणः
transliteration: yam sūrya tulya varṇa ābham anuparyeti parvatam
yasya bhāsā sadā bhānti tad varṇā mṛga pakṣiṇaḥ

sanskrit: यस्य प्रस्थम् महात्मानो न त्यजन्ति महर्षयः
transliteration: yasya prastham mahātmāno na tyajanti maharṣayaḥ

sanskrit: तत्र एष रमते राजन् रम्ये कान्चन पर्वते
transliteration: tatra eṣa ramate rājan ramye kāncana parvate

sanskrit: मुख्यो वानर मुख्यानाम् केसरी नाम यूथपः
षष्टिर् गिरि सहस्राणाम् रम्याः कान्चन पर्वताः
transliteration: mukhyo vānara mukhyānām kesarī nāma yūthapaḥ
ṣaṣṭir giri sahasrāṇām ramyāḥ kāncana parvatāḥ

sanskrit: तेषाम् मध्ये गिरि वरस् त्वम् इव अनघ रक्षसाम्
तत्र एते कपिलाः श्वेतास् ताम्र आस्या मधु पिन्गलाः
transliteration: teṣām madhye giri varas tvam iva anagha rakṣasām
tatra ete kapilāḥ śvetās tāmra āsyā madhu pingalāḥ

sanskrit: निवसन्ति उत्तम गिरौ तीक्ष्ण दम्ष्ट्रा नख आयुधाः
सिम्ह इव चतुर् दम्ष्ट्रा व्याघ्रा इव दुरासदाः
transliteration: nivasanti uttama girau tīkṣṇa damṣṭrā nakha āyudhāḥ
simha iva catur damṣṭrā vyāghrā iva durāsadāḥ

sanskrit: सर्वे वैश्वनर समा ज्वलित आशी विष उपमाः
सुदीर्घ अन्चित लान्गूला मत्त मातम्ग सम्निभाः
transliteration: sarve vaiśvanara samā jvalita āśī viṣa upamāḥ
sudīrgha ancita lāngūlā matta mātamga samnibhāḥ

sanskrit: मर्दयन्तीव ते सर्वे तस्थुर्लङ्काम् समीक्ष्य ते
transliteration: mardayantīva te sarve tasthurlaṅkām samīkṣya te

sanskrit: नाम्ना पृथिव्याम् विख्यातो राजन् शत बली इति यः
transliteration: nāmnā pṛthivyām vikhyāto rājan śata balī iti yaḥ
english: This powerful one staying in their midst, is their leader, eager for victory; and the puissant (monkey) always look like the Sun himself; and this one, o king, is famed on earth by the name of Satabalr.

sanskrit: एष एव आशम्सते लंकाम् स्वेन अनीकेन मर्दितुम्
विक्रान्तो बलवान् शूरः पौरुषे स्वे व्यवस्थितः
transliteration: eṣa eva āśamsate laṃkām svena anīkena marditum
vikrānto balavān śūraḥ pauruṣe sve vyavasthitaḥ
english: This heroic one, powerful and mighty, established in his own prowess, hope to devastate Lankā with his own forces. And for compassing Rāma's desire, the monkeys does not cherish and kindness for his life.

sanskrit: रामप्रियार्थम् प्राणानाम् दयाम् न कुरुते हरिः
गजो गव अक्षो गवयो नलो नीलः च वानरः
एक एक एव यूथानाम् कोटिभिर् दशभिर् वृतः
transliteration: rāmapriyārtham prāṇānām dayām na kurute hariḥ
gajo gava akṣo gavayo nalo nīlaḥ ca vānaraḥ
eka eka eva yūthānām koṭibhir daśabhir vṛtaḥ
english: Gaya, Gavākşa, Nala, and the monkey Nīlaeach of these is encompassed by ten koțis of warriors.

sanskrit: तथा अन्ये वानर श्रेष्ठा विन्ध्य पर्वत वासिनः
न शक्यन्ते बहुत्वात् तु सम्ख्यातुम् लघु विक्रमाः
transliteration: tathā anye vānara śreṣṭhā vindhya parvata vāsinaḥ
na śakyante bahutvāt tu samkhyātum laghu vikramāḥ
english: (Besides these), there are other choice monkeys dwelling in the Vindhya mountain, but I cannot enumerate these (monkeys) possessed of fleet vigour, in consequence of their vast number.
All these, O mighty monarch, are of exceeding prowess, all possess persons resembling mighty mountains; and all are competent in a moment to remove and scatter the Earth with them.

sanskrit: सारणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रावणम् राक्षस अधिपम्
बलम् आलोकयन् सर्वम् शुको वाक्यम् अथ अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sāraṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā rāvaṇam rākṣasa adhipam
balam ālokayan sarvam śuko vākyam atha abravīt
english: Having heard the words of Säraņa, who had described the forces (of the monkeys), Suka, addressed Rāvana, lord of Rākşasas, saying.

sanskrit: स्थितान् पश्यसि यान् एतान् मत्तान् इव महाद्विपान्
न्यग्रोधान् इव गान्गेयान् सालान् हैमवतीन् इव
transliteration: sthitān paśyasi yān etān mattān iva mahādvipān
nyagrodhān iva gāngeyān sālān haimavatīn iva
english: Those, o king, whom you see stationed, resembling mad elephants, like to nyagrodhas* belonging to the Gangă, like to Sālas in the Himavān, are incapable of being borne, they are possessed of strength, and able to wear forms at will; resembling deities and Dänavas, and like the gods in conflict. *Banians.

sanskrit: एते दुष्प्रसहा राजन् बलिनः काम रूपिणः
दैत्य दानव सम्काशा युद्धे देव पराक्रमाः
transliteration: ete duṣprasahā rājan balinaḥ kāma rūpiṇaḥ
daitya dānava samkāśā yuddhe deva parākramāḥ
english: Those, o king, whom you see stationed, resembling mad elephants, like to nyagrodhas* belonging to the Gangă, like to Sālas in the Himavān, are incapable of being borne, they are possessed of strength, and able to wear forms at will; resembling deities and Dänavas, and like the gods in conflict. *Banians.

sanskrit: एषाम् कोटि सहस्राणि नव पन्च च सप्त च
तथा शन्ख सहस्राणि तथा वृन्द शतानि च
transliteration: eṣām koṭi sahasrāṇi nava panca ca sapta ca
tathā śankha sahasrāṇi tathā vṛnda śatāni ca
english: These, numbering nine, five, and seven thousand koțis and thousand sankus and an hundred urindas, are the ministers of Sugriva, residing in Kişkindhā-monkeys begot by gods and Gandharvas, capable of assuming shapes at will.

sanskrit: एते सुग्रीव सचिवाः किष्किन्धा निलयाः सदा
हरयो देव गन्धर्वैर् उत्पन्नाः काम रूपिणः
transliteration: ete sugrīva sacivāḥ kiṣkindhā nilayāḥ sadā
harayo deva gandharvair utpannāḥ kāma rūpiṇaḥ
english: These, numbering nine, five, and seven thousand koțis and thousand sankus and an hundred urindas, are the ministers of Sugriva, residing in Kişkindhā-monkeys begot by gods and Gandharvas, capable of assuming shapes at will.

sanskrit: यौ तौ पश्यसि तिष्ठन्तौ कुमारौ देव रूपिणौ
मैन्दः च द्विविदः च उभौ ताभ्याम् न अस्ति समो युधि
transliteration: yau tau paśyasi tiṣṭhantau kumārau deva rūpiṇau
maindaḥ ca dvividaḥ ca ubhau tābhyām na asti samo yudhi
english: Those two whom you beholdest, staying there, of equal proportions and endowed with god-like shapes, are Mainda and Dvivida, who have no equals in fight. Permitted by Brahma, they had partaken of ambrosia. They hope to humble Lanka by their prowess.

sanskrit: आशम्सेते युधा लंकाम् एतौ मर्दितुम् ओजसा
transliteration: āśamsete yudhā laṃkām etau marditum ojasā
english: Those two whom you beholdest, staying there, of equal proportions and endowed with god-like shapes, are Mainda and Dvivida, who have no equals in fight. Permitted by Brahma, they had partaken of ambrosia. They hope to humble Lanka by their prowess.

sanskrit: यम् तु पश्यसि तिष्ठन्तम् प्रभिन्नम् इव कुन्जरम्
यो बलात् क्षोभयेत् क्रुद्धः समुद्रम् अपि वानरः
transliteration: yam tu paśyasi tiṣṭhantam prabhinnam iva kunjaram
yo balāt kṣobhayet kruddhaḥ samudram api vānaraḥ

sanskrit: एषो अभिगन्ता लंकाया वैदेह्यास् तव च प्रभो
एनम् पश्य पुरा दृष्टम् वानरम् पुनर् आगतम्
transliteration: eṣo abhigantā laṃkāyā vaidehyās tava ca prabho
enam paśya purā dṛṣṭam vānaram punar āgatam

sanskrit: ज्येष्ठः केसरिणः पुत्रो वात आत्मज इति श्रुतः
हनूमान् इति विख्यातो लन्घितो येन सागरः
transliteration: jyeṣṭhaḥ kesariṇaḥ putro vāta ātmaja iti śrutaḥ
hanūmān iti vikhyāto langhito yena sāgaraḥ

sanskrit: काम रूपी हरि श्रेष्ठो बल रूप समन्वितः
अनिवार्य गतिः चैव यथा सततगः प्रभुः
transliteration: kāma rūpī hari śreṣṭho bala rūpa samanvitaḥ
anivārya gatiḥ caiva yathā satatagaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Capable of wearing forms at pleasure, that first of monkeys is endued with grace and strength, and is of irresistible impetuosity even as that lord, the Wind.

sanskrit: उद्यन्तम् भास्करम् दृष्ट्वा बालः किल पिपासितः
त्रियोजन सहस्रम् तु अध्वानम् अवतीर्य हि
transliteration: udyantam bhāskaram dṛṣṭvā bālaḥ kila pipāsitaḥ
triyojana sahasram tu adhvānam avatīrya hi
english: Seeing the Sun risen, (he) while a boy, resolving in his mind, Coursing a way measuring three thousand Yojanas, I will bring the Sun, my hunger is not appeased; and he sprang up, elated with strength.

sanskrit: आदित्यम् आहरिष्यामि न मे क्षुत् प्रतियास्यति
इति सम्चिन्त्य मनसा पुरा एष बल दर्पितः
transliteration: ādityam āhariṣyāmi na me kṣut pratiyāsyati
iti samcintya manasā purā eṣa bala darpitaḥ
english: Seeing the Sun risen, (he) while a boy, resolving in his mind, Coursing a way measuring three thousand Yojanas, I will bring the Sun, my hunger is not appeased; and he sprang up, elated with strength.

sanskrit: अनाधृष्यतमम् देवम् अपि देव ऋषि दानवैः
अनासाद्य एव पतितो भास्कर उदयने गिरौ
transliteration: anādhṛṣyatamam devam api deva ṛṣi dānavaiḥ
anāsādya eva patito bhāskara udayane girau
english: And, not getting that god, incapable of being subdued by the deities, saints and Rākṣasas, he dropped down on the Ascending-hill. And thereat a jaw of that strong jawed one was little fractured on the rock, and he is called Hanuman in consequence.

sanskrit: पतितस्य कपेर् अस्य हनुर् एका शिला तले
किम्चिद् भिन्ना दृढ हनोर् हनूमान् एष तेन वै
transliteration: patitasya kaper asya hanur ekā śilā tale
kimcid bhinnā dṛḍha hanor hanūmān eṣa tena vai
english: And, not getting that god, incapable of being subdued by the deities, saints and Rākṣasas, he dropped down on the Ascending-hill. And thereat a jaw of that strong jawed one was little fractured on the rock, and he is called Hanuman in consequence.

sanskrit: सत्यम् आगम योगेन मम एष विदितो हरिः
न अस्य शक्यम् बलम् रूपम् प्रभावो वा अनुभाषितुम्
transliteration: satyam āgama yogena mama eṣa vidito hariḥ
na asya śakyam balam rūpam prabhāvo vā anubhāṣitum

sanskrit: एष आशम्सते लंकाम् एको मर्दितुम् ओजसा
transliteration: eṣa āśamsate laṃkām eko marditum ojasā

sanskrit: यः च एषो अनन्तरः शूरः श्यामः पद्म निभ ईक्षणः
transliteration: yaḥ ca eṣo anantaraḥ śūraḥ śyāmaḥ padma nibha īkṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: यस्मिन् न चलते धर्मो यो धर्मम् न अतिवर्तते
transliteration: yasmin na calate dharmo yo dharmam na ativartate

sanskrit: यो ब्राह्मम् अस्त्रम् वेदामः च वेद वेदविदाम् वरः
यो भिन्द्याद् गगनम् बाणैः पर्वतामः च अपि दारयेत्
transliteration: yo brāhmam astram vedāmaḥ ca veda vedavidām varaḥ
yo bhindyād gaganam bāṇaiḥ parvatāmaḥ ca api dārayet

sanskrit: यस्य मृत्योर् इव क्रोधः शक्रस्य इव पराक्रमः
यस्य भार्या जन्स्थानात्सीता चापि हृता त्वया
transliteration: yasya mṛtyor iva krodhaḥ śakrasya iva parākramaḥ
yasya bhāryā jansthānātsītā cāpi hṛtā tvayā

sanskrit: स एष रामस् त्वाम् योद्धुम् राजन् समभिवर्तते
यः च एष दक्षिणे पार्श्वे शुद्ध जाम्बू नद प्रभः
transliteration: sa eṣa rāmas tvām yoddhum rājan samabhivartate
yaḥ ca eṣa dakṣiṇe pārśve śuddha jāmbū nada prabhaḥ

sanskrit: विशाल वक्षास् ताम्र अक्षो नील कुन्चित मूर्धजः
एषो अस्य लक्ष्मणो नाम भ्राता प्राण समः प्रियः
transliteration: viśāla vakṣās tāmra akṣo nīla kuncita mūrdhajaḥ
eṣo asya lakṣmaṇo nāma bhrātā prāṇa samaḥ priyaḥ

sanskrit: नये युद्धे च कुशलः सर्व शास्त्रभृताम् वरः
अमर्षी दुर्जयो जेता विक्रान्तो बुद्धिमान् बली
transliteration: naye yuddhe ca kuśalaḥ sarva śāstrabhṛtām varaḥ
amarṣī durjayo jetā vikrānto buddhimān balī

sanskrit: रामस्य दक्षिणो बाहुर् नित्यम् प्राणो बहिः चरः
न हि एष राघवस्य अर्थे जीवितम् परिरक्षति
transliteration: rāmasya dakṣiṇo bāhur nityam prāṇo bahiḥ caraḥ
na hi eṣa rāghavasya arthe jīvitam parirakṣati

sanskrit: एष एव आशम्सते युद्धे निहन्तुम् सर्व राक्षसान्
यस् तु सव्यम् असौ पक्षम् रामस्य आश्रित्य तिष्ठति
transliteration: eṣa eva āśamsate yuddhe nihantum sarva rākṣasān
yas tu savyam asau pakṣam rāmasya āśritya tiṣṭhati

sanskrit: रक्षो गण परिक्षिप्तो राजा हि एष विभीषणः
transliteration: rakṣo gaṇa parikṣipto rājā hi eṣa vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: He that stay occupying the left side of Rāma, and surrounded by Raksasas, is the king, Vibhīșana, sprinkled as the king of Lankā by the auspicious king of kings, he, filled with wrath, approach you (for battle).

sanskrit: त्वाम् एव प्रतिसम्रब्धो युद्धाय एषो अभिवर्तते
यम् तु पश्यसि तिष्ठन्तम् मध्ये गिरिम् इव अचलम्
transliteration: tvām eva pratisamrabdho yuddhāya eṣo abhivartate
yam tu paśyasi tiṣṭhantam madhye girim iva acalam

sanskrit: सर्व शाखा मृग इन्द्राणाम् भर्तारम् अपराजितम्
तेजसा यशसा बुद्ध्या ज्ञानेन अभिजनेन च
transliteration: sarva śākhā mṛga indrāṇām bhartāram aparājitam
tejasā yaśasā buddhyā jñānena abhijanena ca

sanskrit: यः कपीन् अति बभ्राज हिमवान् इव पर्वतान्
किष्किन्धाम् यः समध्यास्ते गुहाम् सगहन द्रुमाम्
transliteration: yaḥ kapīn ati babhrāja himavān iva parvatān
kiṣkindhām yaḥ samadhyāste guhām sagahana drumām

sanskrit: दुर्गाम् पर्वत दुर्गस्थाम् प्रधानैः सह यूथपैः
यस्य एषा कान्चनी माला शोभते शत पुष्करा
transliteration: durgām parvata durgasthām pradhānaiḥ saha yūthapaiḥ
yasya eṣā kāncanī mālā śobhate śata puṣkarā

sanskrit: कान्ता देव मनुष्याणाम् यस्याम् लक्ष्मीः प्रतिष्ठिता
एताम् च मालाम् ताराम् च कपि राज्यम् च शाश्वतम्
transliteration: kāntā deva manuṣyāṇām yasyām lakṣmīḥ pratiṣṭhitā
etām ca mālām tārām ca kapi rājyam ca śāśvatam

sanskrit: एवम् कोटि सहस्रेण शन्कूनाम् च शतेन च
transliteration: evam koṭi sahasreṇa śankūnām ca śatena ca

english: Thus backed by a thousand koțſ, and an hundred Sanku, and a thousand Mahāśanku, and an hundred Vrinda, and a thousand Mahāvrinda, and an an hundred Padma, and a thousand Mahāpadma and an hundred kharva, and an equal Samudra and an equal Mahaugha, by koțis of Mahaughas-resembling the sea, and surrounded by the heroic Vibhīşana as well as his counsellors, that Lord of monkeys, always engirt by a mighty force, and possessed of exceeding strength and prowess, will encounter you in battle.

sanskrit: समुद्रेण च तेनैव महुघेन तथैव च
transliteration: samudreṇa ca tenaiva mahughena tathaiva ca

english: Thus backed by a thousand koțſ, and an hundred Sanku, and a thousand Mahāśanku, and an hundred Vrinda, and a thousand Mahāvrinda, and an an hundred Padma, and a thousand Mahāpadma and an hundred kharva, and an equal Samudra and an equal Mahaugha, by koțis of Mahaughas-resembling the sea, and surrounded by the heroic Vibhīşana as well as his counsellors, that Lord of monkeys, always engirt by a mighty force, and possessed of exceeding strength and prowess, will encounter you in battle.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवो वानर इन्द्रस् त्वाम् युद्ध अर्थम् अभिवर्तते
transliteration: sugrīvo vānara indras tvām yuddha artham abhivartate

sanskrit: यथा जयः स्यान् न परैः पराजयः
transliteration: yathā jayaḥ syān na paraiḥ parājayaḥ
english: Observing this host, that has presented itself, resembling a flaming planet, do you, O might monarch, prepare yourself to the uttermost, so that victory may be your, and that you may not come by discomfiture at the hands of the foe.

sanskrit: शुकेन तु समाख्याताम्स् तान् दृष्ट्वा हरि यूथपान्
लक्ष्मणम् च महावीर्यम् भुजम् रामस्य दक्षिणम्
transliteration: śukena tu samākhyātāms tān dṛṣṭvā hari yūthapān
lakṣmaṇam ca mahāvīryam bhujam rāmasya dakṣiṇam

sanskrit: समीपस्थम् च रामस्य भ्रातरम् स्वम् विभीषणम्
सर्व वानर राजम् च सुग्रीवम् भीम विक्रमम्
transliteration: samīpastham ca rāmasya bhrātaram svam vibhīṣaṇam
sarva vānara rājam ca sugrīvam bhīma vikramam

sanskrit: हनूमन्तम् च विक्रान्तम् जाम्बवन्तम् च दुर्जयम्
transliteration: hanūmantam ca vikrāntam jāmbavantam ca durjayam

sanskrit: सुषेणम् कुमुदम् नीलम् नलम् च प्लवगर्षभम्
गजम् गवाक्षम् शरभम् वैन्दम् च द्विविदम् तथा
transliteration: suṣeṇam kumudam nīlam nalam ca plavagarṣabham
gajam gavākṣam śarabham vaindam ca dvividam tathā

sanskrit: किम्चिद् आविग्न हृदयो जात क्रोधः च रावणः
भर्त्सयाम् आस तौ वीरौ कथा अन्ते शुक सारणौ
transliteration: kimcid āvigna hṛdayo jāta krodhaḥ ca rāvaṇaḥ
bhartsayām āsa tau vīrau kathā ante śuka sāraṇau

sanskrit: अधो मुखौ तौ प्रणताव् अब्रवीत् शुक सारणौ
रोष गद्गदया वाचा सम्रब्धः परुषम् वचः
transliteration: adho mukhau tau praṇatāv abravīt śuka sāraṇau
roṣa gadgadayā vācā samrabdhaḥ paruṣam vacaḥ
english: And he wrathfully spoke to them, standing in humble guise with their heads hung down, harsh words faltering with passion.

sanskrit: न तावत् सदृशम् नाम सचिवैर् उपजीविभिः
विप्रियम् नृपतेर् वक्तुम् निग्रह प्रग्रहे विभोः
transliteration: na tāvat sadṛśam nāma sacivair upajīvibhiḥ
vipriyam nṛpater vaktum nigraha pragrahe vibhoḥ
english: That counsellors subsisting (on the wealth of their master and sovereign), should say aught disagreeable to him, whether they meet with his favour or disfavour-is not meet.

sanskrit: उभाभ्याम् सदृशम् नाम वक्तुम् अप्रस्तवे स्तवम्
transliteration: ubhābhyām sadṛśam nāma vaktum aprastave stavam
english: Without being questioned, it is (proper) for you both to hymn the praises of a foes that is opposed and that has advanced for encounter! You have in vain worshipped your preceptors, aged people, and spiritual guides, for you have failed to appropriate the cream of Political Science, which should be availed of.

sanskrit: आचार्या गुरवो वृद्धा वृथा वाम् पर्युपासिताः
सारम् यद् राज शास्त्राणाम् अनुजीव्यम् न गृह्यते
transliteration: ācāryā guravo vṛddhā vṛthā vām paryupāsitāḥ
sāram yad rāja śāstrāṇām anujīvyam na gṛhyate
english: Without being questioned, it is (proper) for you both to hymn the praises of a foes that is opposed and that has advanced for encounter! You have in vain worshipped your preceptors, aged people, and spiritual guides, for you have failed to appropriate the cream of Political Science, which should be availed of.

sanskrit: गृहीतो वा न विज्ञातो भारो ज्ञानस्य वा उच्यते
ईदृशैः सचिवैर् युक्तो मूर्खैर् दिष्ट्या धरामि अहम्
transliteration: gṛhīto vā na vijñāto bhāro jñānasya vā ucyate
īdṛśaiḥ sacivair yukto mūrkhair diṣṭyā dharāmi aham
english: Or if you had appropriated the same, you have forgotten it afterwards;;and you bear the burden of ignorance. And it is owing to my good fortune that, having such stupid counsellors, I have as yet held my kingdom.

sanskrit: किम् नु मृत्योर् भयम् न अस्ति माम् वक्तुम् परुषम् वचः
यस्य मे शासतो जिह्वा प्रयच्चति शुभ अशुभम्
transliteration: kim nu mṛtyor bhayam na asti mām vaktum paruṣam vacaḥ
yasya me śāsato jihvā prayaccati śubha aśubham
english: Have you no fear of death that you use harsh speech towards me, who am the ruler and whose tongue dispense good and evil?

sanskrit: अपि एव दहनम् स्पृष्ट्वा वने तिष्ठन्ति पादपाः
राज दोष परामृष्टास् तिष्ठन्ते न अपराधिनः
transliteration: api eva dahanam spṛṣṭvā vane tiṣṭhanti pādapāḥ
rāja doṣa parāmṛṣṭās tiṣṭhante na aparādhinaḥ
english: Even trees may exist in the forest, coming in contact with burning fire; but transgressors cannot exist, visited with the chastisement of the monarch.

sanskrit: हन्याम् अहम् इमौ पापौ शत्रु पक्ष प्रशम्सकौ
यदि पूर्व उपकारैर् मे न क्रोधो मृदुताम् व्रजेत्
transliteration: hanyām aham imau pāpau śatru pakṣa praśamsakau
yadi pūrva upakārair me na krodho mṛdutām vrajet
english: I shall slay these wicked wights, who praise the side of the enemy, if my anger be not moderated, remembering their former good offices.

sanskrit: न हि वाम् हन्तुम् इच्चामि स्मरन्न् उपकृतानि वाम्
transliteration: na hi vām hantum iccāmi smarann upakṛtāni vām
english: Avaunt! Go hence from near me! I do not wish to slay you, remembering your good acts. Slain you (already) are, who are ingrate and cherish no affection for me.

sanskrit: हताव् एव कृतघ्नौ तौ मयि स्नेह परान् मुखौ
एवम् उक्तौ तु सव्रीडौ ताव् उभौ शुक सारणौ
transliteration: hatāv eva kṛtaghnau tau mayi sneha parān mukhau
evam uktau tu savrīḍau tāv ubhau śuka sāraṇau

sanskrit: उपस्थापय शीघ्रम् मे चारान् नीति विशारदान्
transliteration: upasthāpaya śīghram me cārān nīti viśāradān
english: Then that ranger of night, the Ten-necked one, said to Mahodara, who was present, to summon some spies. Thus accosted, Mahodara speedily ordered some spies (to present themselves).
Thereat, the spies, hurriedly arriving there at the mandate of the monarch, and, presenting themselves, stood with joined hands, uttering blessing of victory.

sanskrit: तान् अब्रवीत् ततो वाक्यम् रावणो राक्षस अधिपः
transliteration: tān abravīt tato vākyam rāvaṇo rākṣasa adhipaḥ

sanskrit: चारान् प्रत्ययिकान् शूरान् भक्तान् विगत साध्वसान्
transliteration: cārān pratyayikān śūrān bhaktān vigata sādhvasān
english: Then the lord of Rākşasas, Rāvana, addressed the spies, who were heroic, faithful, calm, and courageous, Go hence, and acquaint yourselves with the exertions of Rama; as well as with those who, being the custodians of Rāma's close counsels, have gladly joined him (here).

sanskrit: मन्त्रेष्व् अभ्यन्तरा ये अस्य प्रीत्या तेन समागताः
कथम् स्वपिति जागर्ति किम् अन्यच् च करिष्यति
transliteration: mantreṣv abhyantarā ye asya prītyā tena samāgatāḥ
katham svapiti jāgarti kim anyac ca kariṣyati

sanskrit: चारेण विदितः शत्रुः पण्डितैर् वसुधा अधिपैः
transliteration: cāreṇa viditaḥ śatruḥ paṇḍitair vasudhā adhipaiḥ

sanskrit: चारास् तु ते तथा इति उक्त्वा प्रहृष्टा राक्षस ईश्वरम्
transliteration: cārās tu te tathā iti uktvā prahṛṣṭā rākṣasa īśvaram

sanskrit: कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम् जग्मुर् यत्र रामः सलक्ष्मणः
ते सुवेलस्य शैलस्य समीपे राम लक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam jagmur yatra rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
te suvelasya śailasya samīpe rāma lakṣmaṇau

sanskrit: ते तु धर्म आत्मना दृष्टा राक्षस इन्द्रेण राक्षसाः
transliteration: te tu dharma ātmanā dṛṣṭā rākṣasa indreṇa rākṣasāḥ

sanskrit: वानरैर् अर्दितास् ते तु विक्रान्तैर् लघु विक्रमैः
transliteration: vānarair arditās te tu vikrāntair laghu vikramaiḥ

sanskrit: पुनर् लंकाम् अनुप्राप्ताः श्वसन्तो नष्ट चेतसः
चारा बहिर् नित्य चरा निशा चराः
transliteration: punar laṃkām anuprāptāḥ śvasanto naṣṭa cetasaḥ
cārā bahir nitya carā niśā carāḥ
english: Then those exceedingly strong spies, always ranging outside, presenting themselves before the Ten-necked one, informed him of the forces of Rāma, stationed near mount Suvela.
Then the spies communicated to Lankā's lord news concerning Rāghava and his host stationed at the mount Suvela.

sanskrit: चाराणाम् रावणः श्रुत्वा प्राप्तम् रामम् महाबलम्
जात उद्वेगो अभवत् किम्चित् शार्दूलम् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: cārāṇām rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptam rāmam mahābalam
jāta udvego abhavat kimcit śārdūlam vākyam abravīt
english: Hearing the words of the spies, that Rama, accompanied by a mighty army, had arrived (there), Rāvana was a little agitated and spoke to Sardula.

sanskrit: अयथावच् च ते वर्णो दीनः च असि निशा चर
न असि कच्चिद् अमित्राणाम् क्रुद्धानाम् वशम् आगतः
transliteration: ayathāvac ca te varṇo dīnaḥ ca asi niśā cara
na asi kaccid amitrāṇām kruddhānām vaśam āgataḥ
english: Your colour has changed its natural aspect, and O ranger of the night, you look poorly. Did not come under the control of the wrathful foes?

sanskrit: इति तेन अनुशिष्टस् तु वाचम् मन्दम् उदीरयत्
तदा राक्षस शार्दूलम् शार्दूलो भय विह्वलः
transliteration: iti tena anuśiṣṭas tu vācam mandam udīrayat
tadā rākṣasa śārdūlam śārdūlo bhaya vihvalaḥ
english: Thus ordered by him, then (Sārdula), bewildered by fear, addressed that tiger of a Raksasa, saying.

sanskrit: न ते चारयितुम् शक्या राजन् वानर पुम्गवाः
विक्रान्ता बलवन्तः च राघवेण च रक्षिताः
transliteration: na te cārayitum śakyā rājan vānara pumgavāḥ
vikrāntā balavantaḥ ca rāghaveṇa ca rakṣitāḥ
english: Those powerful monkeys, o king, puissant, strong, and protected by Rāghava, are incapable of being ranged (by us). or

sanskrit: न अपि सम्भाषितुम् शक्याः सम्प्रश्नो अत्र न लभ्यते
सर्वतो रक्ष्यते पन्था वानरैः पर्वत उपमैः
transliteration: na api sambhāṣitum śakyāḥ sampraśno atra na labhyate
sarvato rakṣyate panthā vānaraiḥ parvata upamaiḥ
english: They cannot be conversed with interrogated. All around, the courses are kept by monkeys resembling hills.

sanskrit: प्रविष्ट मात्रे ज्ञातो अहम् बले तस्मिन्न् अचारिते
बलाद् गृहीतो बहुभिर् बहुधा अस्मि विदारितः
transliteration: praviṣṭa mātre jñāto aham bale tasminn acārite
balād gṛhīto bahubhir bahudhā asmi vidāritaḥ
english: As soon as I entered, and was scanning that host, I was discovered. And forcibly taken by the Rākşasa, I was pulled by them hither and thither.

sanskrit: जानुभिर् मुष्टिभिर् दन्तैस् तलैः च अभिहतो भृशम्
transliteration: jānubhir muṣṭibhir dantais talaiḥ ca abhihato bhṛśam
english: And furiously assailed by the monkeys with thighs, clenched fists, teeth, and palms, I was dragged in the midst of the army by the enraged monkeys.

sanskrit: परिणीय च सर्वत्र नीतो अहम् राम सम्सदम्
रुधिर आदिग्ध सर्व अन्गो विह्वलः चलित इन्द्रियः
transliteration: pariṇīya ca sarvatra nīto aham rāma samsadam
rudhira ādigdha sarva ango vihvalaḥ calita indriyaḥ
english: And, after having been taken all about, I was (at length) taken before Rāma, bleeding, with my limbs showing sorry work, and my senses swimming and paralysed.

sanskrit: हरिभिर् वध्यमानः च याचमानः कृत अन्जलिः
transliteration: haribhir vadhyamānaḥ ca yācamānaḥ kṛta anjaliḥ
english: And, having been belaboured by the monkeys, I, on craving his kindness with joined hands, was, at his pleasure, rescued by Rāghava, with, Don't, don't!

sanskrit: एष शैलैः शिलाभिः च पूरयित्वा महाअर्णवम्
द्वारम् आश्रित्य लंकाया रामस् तिष्ठति सायुधः
transliteration: eṣa śailaiḥ śilābhiḥ ca pūrayitvā mahāarṇavam
dvāram āśritya laṃkāyā rāmas tiṣṭhati sāyudhaḥ
english: Having filled up the deep with rocks and crags, Rāma equipped with weapons, stay, occupying the gate of Lanka.

sanskrit: गरुड व्यूहम् आस्थाय सर्वतो हरिभिर् वृतः
माम् विसृज्य महातेजा लंकाम् एव अभिवर्तते
transliteration: garuḍa vyūham āsthāya sarvato haribhir vṛtaḥ
mām visṛjya mahātejā laṃkām eva abhivartate
english: And, letting me off, that one of suspassing vigour, surrounded by monkeys, and, arranging his forces in the Garuda fashion, advance upon Lanka.

sanskrit: पुरा प्राकारम् आयाति क्षिप्रम् एकतरम् कुरु
सीताम् च अस्मै प्रयच्च आशु सुयुद्धम् वा प्रदीयताम्
transliteration: purā prākāram āyāti kṣipram ekataram kuru
sītām ca asmai prayacca āśu suyuddham vā pradīyatām
english: He draw nigh to the wall. Therefore, do one of these things in preference to the other, either render back Sītā, or give him battle.

sanskrit: मनसा सम्तताप अथ तत् श्रुत्वा राक्षस अधिपः
शार्दूलस्य महद् वाक्यम् अथ उवाच स रावणः
transliteration: manasā samtatāpa atha tat śrutvā rākṣasa adhipaḥ
śārdūlasya mahad vākyam atha uvāca sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Hearing this, Ravana, lord of Raksasas, then reflecting in his mind, spoke to Sārdula these pregnant words.

sanskrit: यदि माम् प्रतियुध्येरन् देव गन्धर्व दानवाः
न एव सीताम् प्रदास्यामि सर्व लोक भयाद् अपि
transliteration: yadi mām pratiyudhyeran deva gandharva dānavāḥ
na eva sītām pradāsyāmi sarva loka bhayād api
english: Even if the gods, Gandharvas, and Dānavas should array themselves against me, Sītā I shall not give, from fear of all creatures.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा महातेजा रावणः पुनर् अब्रवीत्
चारिता भवता सेना के अत्र शूराः प्लवम् गमाः
transliteration: evam uktvā mahātejā rāvaṇaḥ punar abravīt
cāritā bhavatā senā ke atra śūrāḥ plavam gamāḥ
english: Having said this, that exceedingly energetic one again said,You have ranged this army. Who here among the monkeys are heroic?

sanskrit: कीदृशाः किम् प्रभावाः च वानरा ये दुरासदाः
कस्य पुत्राः च पौत्राः च तत्त्वम् आख्याहि राक्षस
transliteration: kīdṛśāḥ kim prabhāvāḥ ca vānarā ye durāsadāḥ
kasya putrāḥ ca pautrāḥ ca tattvam ākhyāhi rākṣasa
english: O amiable one, what is their potency? And what are those monkeys that are hard to approach, like? And, O you of fair vows, whose sons and grandsons are they? Truly relate all this (to me).

sanskrit: तथात्र प्रतिपत्स्यामि ज्ञात्वा तेषाम् बल अबलम्
अवश्यम् बल सम्ख्यानम् कर्तव्यम् युद्धम् इच्चता
transliteration: tathātra pratipatsyāmi jñātvā teṣām bala abalam
avaśyam bala samkhyānam kartavyam yuddham iccatā
english: Having ascertained their strength and weakness, I shall in this matter adopt my course. Those who wish for fight, certainly take account of all this.

sanskrit: अथ एवम् उक्तः शार्दूलो रावणेन उत्तमः चरः
इदम् वचनम् आरेभे वक्तुम् रावण सम्निधौ
transliteration: atha evam uktaḥ śārdūlo rāvaṇena uttamaḥ caraḥ
idam vacanam ārebhe vaktum rāvaṇa samnidhau
english: Thus addressed by Rāvana, Sārdula—best of spies-thus began to speak in the presence of Ravana.

sanskrit: अथ ऋक्ष रजसः पुत्रो युधि राजन् सुदुर्जयः
गद्गदस्य अथ पुत्रो अत्र जाम्बवान् इति विश्रुतः
transliteration: atha ṛkṣa rajasaḥ putro yudhi rājan sudurjayaḥ
gadgadasya atha putro atra jāmbavān iti viśrutaḥ
english: O king, that unconquerable one in fight, Jāmbavān, is well known as the son Gadgada, king of bears.

sanskrit: गद्गदस्य एव पुत्रो अन्यो गुरु पुत्रः शत क्रतोः
कदनम् यस्य पुत्रेण कृतम् एकेन रक्षसाम्
transliteration: gadgadasya eva putro anyo guru putraḥ śata kratoḥ
kadanam yasya putreṇa kṛtam ekena rakṣasām
english: The other son of Gadgada is the son of Śakra's preceptor. By which son, single-handed, was done immense oppression to the Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: सुषेणः च अपि धर्म आत्मा पुत्रो धर्मस्य वीर्यवान्
सौम्यः सोम आत्मजः च अत्र राजन् दधि मुखः कपिः
transliteration: suṣeṇaḥ ca api dharma ātmā putro dharmasya vīryavān
saumyaḥ soma ātmajaḥ ca atra rājan dadhi mukhaḥ kapiḥ
english: The righteous and puissant Sușeņa is the son of Dharma. And the mild monkey, Dadhimukha, O king, is the son of Soma. 1. Righteousness. 2. Moon.

sanskrit: सुमुखो दुर्मुखः च अत्र वेग दर्शी च वानरः
मृत्युर् वानर रूपेण नूनम् सृष्टः स्वयम्भुवा
transliteration: sumukho durmukhaḥ ca atra vega darśī ca vānaraḥ
mṛtyur vānara rūpeṇa nūnam sṛṣṭaḥ svayambhuvā
english: And Sumukha, Durmukha and the monkey, vegadarcin (resembling) Death himself, were for certain begot by the Self-create in the shape of a monkey.* *Another meaning is, “The monkey, Vegadarsi who is death himself in the shape of a monkey." But I give the acceptable sense.

sanskrit: पुत्रो हुत वहस्य अथ नीलः सेना पतिः स्वयम्
अनिलस्य च पुत्रो अत्र हनूमान् इति विश्रुतः
transliteration: putro huta vahasya atha nīlaḥ senā patiḥ svayam
anilasya ca putro atra hanūmān iti viśrutaḥ
english: Nīla himself is the son of the bearer of sacrificial oblations;* and Hanumán is famed as the son of the Wind-god. * Fire.

sanskrit: नप्ता शक्रस्य दुर्धर्षो बलवान् अन्गदो युवा
मैन्दः च द्विविदः च उभौ बलिनाव् अश्वि सम्भवौ
transliteration: naptā śakrasya durdharṣo balavān angado yuvā
maindaḥ ca dvividaḥ ca ubhau balināv aśvi sambhavau
english: The irrepressible and youthful Angada is the grandson of Śakra. And the lusty Mainda and Dvivida are sprung from Aśvi.

sanskrit: पुत्रा वैवस्वतस्य अत्र पन्च काल अन्तक उपमाः
गजो गव अक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्ध मादनः
transliteration: putrā vaivasvatasya atra panca kāla antaka upamāḥ
gajo gava akṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandha mādanaḥ
english: And five are the sons of Vaivasvata, resembling the Reaper himself, Gaya, Gavāks a, gavaya, Sarabha and Gandhamādana.
But I can not enumerate the rest, ten koțis of heroic monkeys-all sons of deities—burning for battle.
And this is Dasaratha's son—this you resembling a lion, who slew Düşana and Khara and Triſiras.

sanskrit: नास्ति रामस्य सदृशो विक्रमे भुवि कश्चन
transliteration: nāsti rāmasya sadṛśo vikrame bhuvi kaścana
english: There breathes none on Earth that is like to Rāma in prowess, by whom was slain Virādha and Kabandha, resembling the Destroyer.

sanskrit: वक्तुम् न शक्तो रामस्य गुणान् कश्चिन्नरः क्षितौ
transliteration: vaktum na śakto rāmasya guṇān kaścinnaraḥ kṣitau
english: No person can on earth describe the virtues of Rāma; by whom have been slain all those Rākşasas that had gone to Janasthāna.

sanskrit: यस्य बाणपथम् प्राप्य व जीवेदपि वासवः
transliteration: yasya bāṇapatham prāpya va jīvedapi vāsavaḥ
english: Here also is the virtuous Lakşmaņa, like to the foremost of elephants, coming in the way of whose shafts, even Vasava does not live.

sanskrit: श्वेतो ज्योतिर् मुखः च अत्र भास्करस्य आत्म सम्भवौ
वरुणस्य च पुत्रो अथ हेम कूटः प्लवम् गमः
transliteration: śveto jyotir mukhaḥ ca atra bhāskarasya ātma sambhavau
varuṇasya ca putro atha hema kūṭaḥ plavam gamaḥ
english: And here are ſveta and Jyotirmukha, sprung from Vāskara's self; and the monkey Hemakūta is the son of Varuna.

sanskrit: विश्व कर्म सुतो वीरो नलः प्लवग सत्तमः
विक्रान्तो वेगवान् अत्र वसु पुत्रः सुदुर्धरः
transliteration: viśva karma suto vīro nalaḥ plavaga sattamaḥ
vikrānto vegavān atra vasu putraḥ sudurdharaḥ
english: The heroic Nalabest of monkeys, is the son of Viśvakarmă. And powerful and impetuous, Durdhara is the son of Vasu.

sanskrit: राक्षसानाम् वरिष्ठः च तव भ्राता विभीषणः
परिगृह्य पुरीम् लंकाम् राघवस्य हिते रतः
transliteration: rākṣasānām variṣṭhaḥ ca tava bhrātā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
parigṛhya purīm laṃkām rāghavasya hite rataḥ
english: That foremost of Rāksasas, Vibhisana, your brother, engaged in the welfare of Raghava, has laid seige to Lankā.

sanskrit: इति सर्वम् समाख्यातम् तव इदम् वानरम् बलम्
सुवेले अधिष्ठितम् शैले शेष कार्ये भवान् गतिः
transliteration: iti sarvam samākhyātam tava idam vānaram balam
suvele adhiṣṭhitam śaile śeṣa kārye bhavān gatiḥ
english: Thus have I described to you the entire monkey host stationed in mount Suvela. As for what remain to be done, you are the master.

Then the spies of the king informed him of the forces of Rāghava, incapable of being agitated, which had stationed themselves on Suvela. Hearing the arrival of Rāma's mighty army from the spies, Ravana was a little agitated, and he spoke to the ministers.

Then the spies of the king informed him of the forces of Rāghava, incapable of being agitated, which had stationed themselves on Suvela. Hearing the arrival of Rāma's mighty army from the spies, Ravana was a little agitated, and he spoke to the ministers.
Let the ministers speedily present themselves, having their wits about them, the time forsooth has come for counsel.
Hearing his mandate, those Raksasas, his counsellors, swiftly presented themselves. And then he consulted with his Rākşasa counsellors.
Having deliberated duly, that resistless one, dismissing his ministers, entered his own abode.
Then, taking with him the highly strong Vidyujjihva, huge bodied and gifted with the powers of illusion, he entered where Mithila's daughter was.
The lord of Rākşasas said to Vidyujjihva, skilled in illusion, Do you bring Janaka's daughter under the sway of illusion.
O ranger of the night, do you, taking an illusory head of Rāghava, as well as a mighty bow with the shaft (set), present yourself before me.
Thus accosted, the night-ranger, Vidyujjibha, saying, So be it, displayed that desired illusion to Ravana.
O gentle one, he depending on whom you, being soothed by (me), slight me-that slayer of Khara, your husband, Rāghava, has fallen in battle.

Your roots have been completely severed, and your pride has been destroyed by me. In consequence of this calamity, O Sītā, you shall become my wife. O foolish (girl), renounce this idea. What will you do with that is dead?

O meek (wench), be you the mistress of all my wives. O you of slender religious merit! O you whose object has been defeated! O you that presumes to be wise! Hearken to the destruction of your lord, like the dreadful destruction of Vrtra!
Surrounded by a vast army gathered by the sovereign of the monkeys, Raghava had presented himself on the shore of the sea, for compassing my destruction.
And on the sun have set, Rama stationed himself with his mighty army, oppressing the northern shore (of the sea).
Then at midnight (my) spies coming to that host, thus stationed, fatigued from travel, and sleeping soundly (in consequence), first ranged it.
Then my mighty forces led by Prahasta slew his host overnight, where was present Răma along with Lakşmaņa.

And repeatedly upraising pattiśas and bludgeons, swords, rods and other mighty weapons; and (discharging) showers of arrows, and darts, and daggers and maces and sticks and crows and bearded darts and discuses and clubs; the Rākşasas discharged these among the monkeys.

And repeatedly upraising pattiśas and bludgeons, swords, rods and other mighty weapons; and (discharging) showers of arrows, and darts, and daggers and maces and sticks and crows and bearded darts and discuses and clubs; the Rākşasas discharged these among the monkeys.
While Räma was sleeping, the furious Prahasta by means of a mighty falchion, with speed cut off his head clean.
Vibhīşaņa, who was flying at his will, was taken captive. And Lakşmaņa along with the monkeys army has departed somewhere.
O Sītā, Sugriva lord of monkeys-has his neck broken; and, O Sītā, with his jaw fractured, Hanuman has been slaughtered by the Rākşasas.
And Jāmbavān, endeavouring to spring up bearded darts, even as a tree cut off.
The stalwart Mainda and Dvivida-those foremost of monkeyssighing and lamenting, bathed in blood, destroyers of foes-were cut off with a sword.
Panasa is rolling on the earth like a (veritable) Panasa. And mangled by many iron arrows, Darīmukha lies in a cave. And the exceedingly energetic Kumuda, dumb, is slain by shafts.
And torn by innumerable (arrows) discharged on all sides by Raksasas. Angada, vomiting blood, Leith on the ground.
The monkeys, hard pressed by elephants, and others by networks of cars, lie low in the field, having been agitated like clouds by winds.
And others afflicted with affright, flee, attacked (by the enemy) in the rear, and followed by the Rākṣasas, like mighty elephants pursued by lions.
Some have fallen into the sea, and some have taken refuge in the sky; and the bears have mounted up trees along with the monkeys.
And on the shore of the sea, and in mountains and woods many are the tawny-hued monkeys that have been slain by Rākşasas of frightful forms.
Thus has your lord been slain by my forces, along with his army; and I have his head, washed in blood and besmeared with dust.
Thereat, the exceedingly irrepressible lord of Raksasas, Ravana, spoke to a Raksasi, in the hearing of Sītā.
Bring (hither) the Raksasa, Vidyujjibha of cruel deeds, who has personally brought Rāghava's head from the field.

Thereat, Vidyujjibha, taking the head along with the bow, bowing down the head (to Ravana), stood before him. Then spoke king Rävaņa to the Rākşasa, Vidyujjibha of the long tongue, who was staying by.

Thereat, Vidyujjibha, taking the head along with the bow, bowing down the head (to Ravana), stood before him. Then spoke king Rävaņa to the Rākşasa, Vidyujjibha of the long tongue, who was staying by.
Do you at once hold before Sītā the head of Dasaratha's son. Let her clearly behold the ultimate sad plight of her lord.
Thus addressed, that Raksasa, throwing that graceful head before Sītā, swiftly vanished,
Rāvana cast down the mighty blazing bow, famed through the three worlds, saying.
This is Rāma's. This is the bow of your Rāma with the string fixed. Slaying that man over night, Prahasta brought it hither.
When Vidyujjibha placed the head of that man, Ravana poured the bow on earth. Then he spoke to illustrious Sītā, the daughter of king Videha to submit to his desire.

sanskrit: सा सीता तच्चिरो दृष्ट्वा तच् च कार्मुकम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: sā sītā tacciro dṛṣṭvā tac ca kārmukam uttamam

sanskrit: नयने मुख वर्णम् च भर्तुस् तत् सदृशम् मुखम्
केशान् केश अन्त देशम् च तम् च चूडा मणिम् शुभम्
transliteration: nayane mukha varṇam ca bhartus tat sadṛśam mukham
keśān keśa anta deśam ca tam ca cūḍā maṇim śubham

sanskrit: विजगर्हे अथ कैकेयीम् क्रोशन्ती कुररी यथा
transliteration: vijagarhe atha kaikeyīm krośantī kurarī yathā

sanskrit: सकामा भव कैकेयि हतो अयम् कुल नन्दनः
कुलम् उत्सादितम् सर्वम् त्वया कलह शीलया
transliteration: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi hato ayam kula nandanaḥ
kulam utsāditam sarvam tvayā kalaha śīlayā
english: O Kaikeyſ, have your wishes attained. Slain has been the son of the race; and the entire race is exterminated by you, partial to dissension.

sanskrit: आर्येण किम् नु कैकेय्याः कृतम् रामेण विप्रियम्
यन्मया चीर वसनस् तया प्रस्थापितो वनम्
transliteration: āryeṇa kim nu kaikeyyāḥ kṛtam rāmeṇa vipriyam
yanmayā cīra vasanas tayā prasthāpito vanam
english: What evil had been done to Kaikeyi by the revered Rāma, that along with me, he had been banished into the woods, with rags given him (for his covering)?

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा तु वैदेही वेपमाना तपस्विनी
जगाम जगतीम् बाला चिन्ना तु कदली यथा
transliteration: evam uktvā tu vaidehī vepamānā tapasvinī
jagāma jagatīm bālā cinnā tu kadalī yathā
english: Having said this, Vaidehi, forlorm and trembling (all over), dropped to the earth, like a plantain cut off.

sanskrit: सा मुहूर्तात् समाश्वस्य प्रतिलभ्य च चेतनाम्
तत् शिरह् समुपाघ्राय विललाप आयत ईक्षणा
transliteration: sā muhūrtāt samāśvasya pratilabhya ca cetanām
tat śirah samupāghrāya vilalāpa āyata īkṣaṇā
english: Then, recovering after a while, and having regained her consciousness, the large-eyed one, placing the head in her front, gave way to grief.

sanskrit: हा हता अस्मि महा बाहो वीर व्रतम् अनुव्रता
इमाम् ते पश्चिम अवस्थाम् गता अस्मि विधवा कृता
transliteration: hā hatā asmi mahā bāho vīra vratam anuvratā
imām te paścima avasthām gatā asmi vidhavā kṛtā
english: Ah! I am undone, O mighty-armed one! ) you that did follow stern vows! From your (death), I have come by this final plight, having been rendered a widow.

sanskrit: प्रथमम् मरणम् नार्या भर्तुर् वैगुण्यम् उच्यते
सुवृत्तः साधु वृत्तायाः सम्वृत्तस् त्वम् मम अग्रतः
transliteration: prathamam maraṇam nāryā bhartur vaiguṇyam ucyate
suvṛttaḥ sādhu vṛttāyāḥ samvṛttas tvam mama agrataḥ
english: The greatest calamity (that can befall a woman), is said to be the death of her husband. And, possessor of an excellent character, you have departed before me, who have ever trod the path of the righteous; but who have come by a mighty grief and am plunged in a sea of sorrow.

sanskrit: दुह्खाद् दुह्कःअम् प्रपन्नाया मग्नायाः शोक सागरे
यो हि माम् उद्यतस् त्रातुम् सो अपि त्वम् विनिपातितः
transliteration: duhkhād duhkaḥam prapannāyā magnāyāḥ śoka sāgare
yo hi mām udyatas trātum so api tvam vinipātitaḥ

sanskrit: सा श्वश्रूर् मम कौसल्या त्वया पुत्रेण राघव
वत्सेन इव यथा धेनुर् विवत्सा वत्सला कृता
transliteration: sā śvaśrūr mama kausalyā tvayā putreṇa rāghava
vatsena iva yathā dhenur vivatsā vatsalā kṛtā
english: And you, who was engaged in delivering me, have yourself fallen! And my mother-in-law, Kausalyā, attached (to you), through the death of you, her son, at the hands of Raksasas, has been reduced to the condition of a cow that has been deprived of her calf.

sanskrit: उदिष्टम् दीर्घम् आयुस् ते यैर् अचिन्त्य पराक्रम
अनृतम् वचनम् तेषाम् अल्प आयुर् असि राघव
transliteration: udiṣṭam dīrgham āyus te yair acintya parākrama
anṛtam vacanam teṣām alpa āyur asi rāghava
english: O Rāghava, even the astrologers had predicted long life for you. But their words are false, you, O Rāghava, wast short-lived. me

sanskrit: अथ वा नश्यति प्रज्ना प्राज्नस्य अपि सतस् तव
पचत्य् एनम् तथा कालो भूतानाम् प्रभवो ह्ययम्
transliteration: atha vā naśyati prajnā prājnasya api satas tava
pacaty enam tathā kālo bhūtānām prabhavo hyayam
english: Or did your wisdom, wise and good as you were, come to naught? For God, who is the origin of all beings, make (every one) reap the fruit of his own acts.

sanskrit: अदृष्टम् मृत्युम् आपन्नः कस्मात् त्वम् नय शास्त्रवित्
transliteration: adṛṣṭam mṛtyum āpannaḥ kasmāt tvam naya śāstravit
english: And why, versed in polity as you wast, did you come by death, unforeseen? You were acquainted with the means of warding off misfortune, and skilled in doing so.

sanskrit: काल रात्र्या मया आच्चिद्य हृतः कमल लोचन
transliteration: kāla rātryā mayā āccidya hṛtaḥ kamala locana
english: Having been brought hither by representing the Fatal Night, fierce and fell, after (being) embraced, and by force, the lotus-eyed one has met with his death. Here lie you, O longarmed one, leaving me lone, and embracing the Earth like your beloved fair.

sanskrit: उपशेषे महा बाहो माम् विहाय तपस्विनीम्
प्रियाम् इव शुभाम् नारीम् पृथिवीम् पुरुष ऋषभ
transliteration: upaśeṣe mahā bāho mām vihāya tapasvinīm
priyām iva śubhām nārīm pṛthivīm puruṣa ṛṣabha
english: Having been brought hither by representing the Fatal Night, fierce and fell, after (being) embraced, and by force, the lotus-eyed one has met with his death. Here lie you, O longarmed one, leaving me lone, and embracing the Earth like your beloved fair.

sanskrit: अर्चितम् सततम् यत्नाद् गन्ध माल्यैर् मया तव
इदम् ते मत् प्रियम् वीर धनुः कान्चन भूषितम्
transliteration: arcitam satatam yatnād gandha mālyair mayā tava
idam te mat priyam vīra dhanuḥ kāncana bhūṣitam
english: Ever carefully worshipped with perfumed wreaths, this bow of your, O hero, embellished with gold, is dear to me.

sanskrit: पित्रा दशरथेन त्वम् श्वशुरेण मम अनघ
पूर्वैसः च पितृभिः सार्धम् नूनम् स्वर्गे समागतः
transliteration: pitrā daśarathena tvam śvaśureṇa mama anagha
pūrvaisaḥ ca pitṛbhiḥ sārdham nūnam svarge samāgataḥ
english: O sinless one, you have surely gone to heaven, and (are there) in the company of your sire and my father-in-law, Dasaratha, and all your ancestors.

sanskrit: दिवि नक्षत्र भूतस् त्वम् महत् कर्म कृतम् प्रियम्
पुण्यम् राज ऋषि वंशम् त्वम् आत्मनः समुपेक्षसे
transliteration: divi nakṣatra bhūtas tvam mahat karma kṛtam priyam
puṇyam rāja ṛṣi vaṃśam tvam ātmanaḥ samupekṣase
english: You have become a star of the firmament as the fruit of your great act.* You have disregarded your righteous race of Rājarşis. *The carrying out the command of your sire.

sanskrit: किम् मान् न प्रेक्षसे राजन् किम् माम् न प्रतिभाषसे
बालाम् बालेन सम्प्राप्ताम् भार्याम् माम् सह चारिणीम्
transliteration: kim mān na prekṣase rājan kim mām na pratibhāṣase
bālām bālena samprāptām bhāryām mām saha cāriṇīm
english: O king, why do you not look at me? And why is it that you do not answer me, who am a girl, hardly arrived at youth, and who am your wife and companion?

sanskrit: संश्रुतम् गृह्णता पाणिम् चरिष्यामि इति यत् त्वया
स्मर तन् मम काकुत्स्थ नय माम् अपि दुह्खिताम्
transliteration: saṃśrutam gṛhṇatā pāṇim cariṣyāmi iti yat tvayā
smara tan mama kākutstha naya mām api duhkhitām
english: That you at the time of your espousing my hand had vowed, I will practise (righteousness) with you, do you, O Kakutstha, recollect the same, and take me, who am overwhelmed with distrees.

sanskrit: कस्मान् माम् अपहाय त्वम् गतो गतिमताम् वर
अस्माल् लोकाद् अमुम् लोकम् त्यक्त्वा माम् इह दुह्खिताम्
transliteration: kasmān mām apahāya tvam gato gatimatām vara
asmāl lokād amum lokam tyaktvā mām iha duhkhitām
english: Why, O best of goers, have you gone from this world to that other, leaving behind me, overwhelmed with distress?

sanskrit: कल्याणैर् उचितम् यत् तत् परिष्वक्तम् मया एव तु
क्रव्य अदैस् तत् शरीरम् ते नूनम् विपरिकृष्यते
transliteration: kalyāṇair ucitam yat tat pariṣvaktam mayā eva tu
kravya adais tat śarīram te nūnam viparikṛṣyate
english: That person of your which, decked out with auspicious things, I used to embrace, beasts of prey will for certain tear the same.

sanskrit: अग्निष्तोम आदिभिर् यज्नैर् इष्टवान् आप्त दक्षिणैः
अग्नि होत्रेण संस्कारम् केन त्वम् तु न लप्स्यसे
transliteration: agniṣtoma ādibhir yajnair iṣṭavān āpta dakṣiṇaiḥ
agni hotreṇa saṃskāram kena tvam tu na lapsyase
english: Having performed the Agnishtoma and other sacrifices with Dakşinăs (dispensed, why had not you attained purity by means of the sacrificial fire?
Kaucalya, over-whelmed with sorrow, shall only behold one of the three that had gone away to distant lands, come (back)-Laksmana.

sanskrit: स तस्याः परिपृच्चन्त्या वधम् मित्र बलस्य ते
तव च आख्यास्यते नूनम् निशायाम् राक्षसैर् वधम्
transliteration: sa tasyāḥ paripṛccantyā vadham mitra balasya te
tava ca ākhyāsyate nūnam niśāyām rākṣasair vadham
english: On being asked by her, he shall relate your as well as the deaths of your friend's troops over night at the hands of the Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: सा त्वाम् सुप्तम् हतम् श्रुत्वा माम् च रक्षो गृहम् गताम्
transliteration: sā tvām suptam hatam śrutvā mām ca rakṣo gṛham gatām
english: O Raghava, hearing you slain while asleep, and me staying in the abode of the Rākşasa, she with her heart cleft (in twain), shall cease to exist.
And for the sake of me, abject that I am, that sinless son of the king, Rāma, possessed of prowess, having crossed the ocean, has been slain in the footprint of a cow.
I, the befouler of my line, who had been wedded by Dasaratha's son through want of discretion, becoming the wife of the revered Rāma, was (in reality) his Death.
Without doubt, in another birth I had abstained from choice gifts, and therefore it is that I sorrow today, albeit being the wife of one that (ever dear) to guests.

sanskrit: साधु पातय माम् क्षिप्रम् रामस्य उपरि रावणः
समानय पतिम् पत्न्या कुरु कल्याणम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: sādhu pātaya mām kṣipram rāmasya upari rāvaṇaḥ
samānaya patim patnyā kuru kalyāṇam uttamam
english: Do you, O Ravana, speedily slay me upon Rāma; and, bringing the wife to the husband, compass my best benefit.

sanskrit: शिरसा मे शिरसः च अस्य कायम् कायेन योजय
transliteration: śirasā me śirasaḥ ca asya kāyam kāyena yojaya
english: Do you join my head to his and my body to his body. I will, O Rāvana, follow the way of my high-souled lord.

sanskrit: इति सा दुह्ख सम्तप्ता विललाप आयत ईक्षणा
भर्तुः शिरो धनुस् तत्र समीक्ष्य जनक आत्मजा
transliteration: iti sā duhkha samtaptā vilalāpa āyata īkṣaṇā
bhartuḥ śiro dhanus tatra samīkṣya janaka ātmajā
english: Thus, burning in grief, did that large-eyed one indulge in lamentations; and Janaka's daughter kept fast gazing at the head and bow of her lord.
As the Rāksasa was by while Sītā was thus bewailing, there appeared before his lord, with joined hands, the warder, saying.

sanskrit: विजयस्व आर्य पुत्र इति सो अभिवाद्य प्रसाद्य च
transliteration: vijayasva ārya putra iti so abhivādya prasādya ca
english: May the worshipful one be victorious! And saluting and propitiating him, (Ravana), he told him that Prahasta, general of the forces, had arrived.
Prahasta has come to you, surrounded by all the courtiers. And, O lord, I was despatched by him, desirous of seeing you.

sanskrit: किंचिद् आत्ययिकम् कार्यम् तेषाम् त्वम् दर्शनम् कुरु
transliteration: kiṃcid ātyayikam kāryam teṣām tvam darśanam kuru
english: O mighty monarch, surely there is and you are forgiving from your regal sentiment some work which is momentous; and do you see them.

sanskrit: अशोक वनिकाम् त्यक्त्वा मन्त्रिणाम् दर्शनम् ययौ
transliteration: aśoka vanikām tyaktvā mantriṇām darśanam yayau
english: Hearing these words of the Rākşasa, the Tennecked one, leaving the Asoka wood, went to see the counsellors.

sanskrit: स तु सर्वम् समर्थ्य एव मन्त्रिभिः क्ऱ्त्यम् आत्मनः
सभाम् प्रविश्य विदधे विदित्वा राम विक्रमम्
transliteration: sa tu sarvam samarthya eva mantribhiḥ ktyam ātmanaḥ
sabhām praviśya vidadhe viditvā rāma vikramam
english: Having decided his entire course of action in consultation with his competent advisers, (Ravana), entering his court, well knowing Rāma's prowess, set about his work.

sanskrit: अन्तर्धानम् तु तत् शीर्षम् तच् च कार्मुकम् उत्तमम्
transliteration: antardhānam tu tat śīrṣam tac ca kārmukam uttamam
english: As soon as Rāvaņa left that place, that head and that bow vanished. And in company with the councillors of dreadful power, (Ravana) decided his course with reference to Rāma.

sanskrit: राक्षस इन्द्रस् तु तैः सार्धम् मन्त्रिभिर् भीम विक्रमैः
समर्थयाम् आस तदा राम कार्य विनिश्चयम्
transliteration: rākṣasa indras tu taiḥ sārdham mantribhir bhīma vikramaiḥ
samarthayām āsa tadā rāma kārya viniścayam
english: As soon as Rāvaņa left that place, that head and that bow vanished. And in company with the councillors of dreadful power, (Ravana) decided his course with reference to Rāma.

sanskrit: अविदूर स्थितान् सर्वान् बल अध्यक्षान् हित एषिणः
अब्रवीत् काल सद्ऱ्शो रावणो राक्षस अधिपः
transliteration: avidūra sthitān sarvān bala adhyakṣān hita eṣiṇaḥ
abravīt kāla sadśo rāvaṇo rākṣasa adhipaḥ
english: Then the lord of Raksasas, Ravana, resembling the day of doom, addressed his generals, all well-wishers-staying hard by, saying.

sanskrit: शीघ्रम् भेरी निनादेन स्फुट कोण आहतेन मे
समानयध्वम् सैन्यानि वक्तव्यम् च न कारणम्
transliteration: śīghram bherī ninādena sphuṭa koṇa āhatena me
samānayadhvam sainyāni vaktavyam ca na kāraṇam
english: Do you speedily summon my forces with the beat of drums—not do you give out the reason (of the summons).

sanskrit: ततस् तथा इति प्रतिगृह्य तद् वचो
transliteration: tatas tathā iti pratigṛhya tad vaco
english: Then assenting to his speech with So be it, the envoys immediately summoned that mighty force; and, when in had arrived, they informed their master, eager for conflict, of its arrival.

sanskrit: सीताम् तु मोहिताम् दृष्ट्वा सरमा नाम राक्षसी
आससाद आशु वैदेहीम् प्रियाम् प्रणयिनी सखी
transliteration: sītām tu mohitām dṛṣṭvā saramā nāma rākṣasī
āsasāda āśu vaidehīm priyām praṇayinī sakhī
english: Seeing Sītā overwhelmed with grief, a Rākşasi, named Saramā, who was the beloved companion (of Sītā), drew near to his dear (friend), Vaidehi.
The mild-speeched Saramă comforted the exceedingly distressed Sītā, who had been bereft of her senses by the lord of Rākşasas.

sanskrit: सा हि तत्र कृता मित्रम् सीतया रक्ष्यमाणया
रक्षन्ती रावणाद् इष्टा सानुक्रोशा दृढ व्रता
transliteration: sā hi tatra kṛtā mitram sītayā rakṣyamāṇayā
rakṣantī rāvaṇād iṣṭā sānukrośā dṛḍha vratā
english: Sītā, who was protected there (by Saramā), had been made a friend by her. And, protecting her at the command of Rāvana, that kind-hearted companion, firm in vows, saw Sītā, deprived of her consciousness. And she' comforted with a friend's affection that one of fair vows, who was rolling in the dust and rising up from it like a mare. 1. Saramă. 2. The commentator intelligently remarks. As a mare does, to remove fatigue.

sanskrit: सा ददर्श सखीम् सीताम् सरमा नष्ट चेतनाम्
उपावृत्य उत्थिताम् ध्वस्ताम् वडवाम् इव पांसुषु
transliteration: sā dadarśa sakhīm sītām saramā naṣṭa cetanām
upāvṛtya utthitām dhvastām vaḍavām iva pāṃsuṣu
english: Sītā, who was protected there (by Saramā), had been made a friend by her. And, protecting her at the command of Rāvana, that kind-hearted companion, firm in vows, saw Sītā, deprived of her consciousness. And she' comforted with a friend's affection that one of fair vows, who was rolling in the dust and rising up from it like a mare. 1. Saramă. 2. The commentator intelligently remarks. As a mare does, to remove fatigue.

sanskrit: ताम् समाश्वासयाम् आस सखी स्नेहेन सुव्रता
उक्ता यद् रावणेन त्वम् प्रत्युक्तम् च स्वयम् त्वया
transliteration: tām samāśvāsayām āsa sakhī snehena suvratā
uktā yad rāvaṇena tvam pratyuktam ca svayam tvayā
english: Having come to the solitary wood for protecting you, I, renouncing all fear of Ravana, have, remaining hid, heard everything that he addressed to you, as well as what you had replied to him. For you, O you of expansive eyes, I have no fear of Rāvana.

sanskrit: उक्ता यद्रावणेन त्वम् प्रत्युक्तश्च स्वयम् त्वया
सखी स्नेहेन तद् भीरु मया सर्वम् प्रतिश्रुतम्
transliteration: uktā yadrāvaṇena tvam pratyuktaśca svayam tvayā
sakhī snehena tad bhīru mayā sarvam pratiśrutam

sanskrit: लीनया गनहे शूह्ये भयम् उत्सृज्य रावणात्
तव हेतोर् विशाल अक्षि न हि मे जीवितम् प्रियम्
transliteration: līnayā ganahe śūhye bhayam utsṛjya rāvaṇāt
tava hetor viśāla akṣi na hi me jīvitam priyam

sanskrit: स सम्भ्रान्तश च निष्क्रान्तो यत् कृते राक्षस अधिपः
तच् च मे विदितम् सर्वम् अभिनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलि
transliteration: sa sambhrāntaśa ca niṣkrānto yat kṛte rākṣasa adhipaḥ
tac ca me viditam sarvam abhiniṣkramya maithili
english: And, O Maithili, I, coming out, have also learnt well as to why the lord of Rākṣasas has gone out hence hurriedly.

sanskrit: न शक्यम् सौप्तिकम् कर्तुम् रामस्य विदित आत्मनः
वधश्च पुरुष व्याघ्रे तस्मिन्न् एव उपपद्यते
transliteration: na śakyam sauptikam kartum rāmasya vidita ātmanaḥ
vadhaśca puruṣa vyāghre tasminn eva upapadyate
english: Rāma, acquainted with self, is incapable of being surprised in sleep; nor does the slaying of that tiger-like one commend itself to me as probable.

sanskrit: न च एव वानरा हन्तुम् शक्याः पादप योधिनः
सुरा देव ऋषभेण इव रामेण हि सुरक्षिताः
transliteration: na ca eva vānarā hantum śakyāḥ pādapa yodhinaḥ
surā deva ṛṣabheṇa iva rāmeṇa hi surakṣitāḥ
english: The monkeys fighting with trees, well protected by Rāghava, like the gods protected by the foremost of the celestials, are incapable of being slain.

sanskrit: दीर्घ वृत्त भुजह् श्रीमान् महा उरस्कह् प्रतापवान्
धन्वी सम्हनन उपेतो धर्म आत्मा भुवि विश्रुतः
transliteration: dīrgha vṛtta bhujah śrīmān mahā uraskah pratāpavān
dhanvī samhanana upeto dharma ātmā bhuvi viśrutaḥ

sanskrit: विक्रान्तो रक्षिता नित्यम् आत्मनश्च परस्य च
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा कुशली नय शास्त्रवित्
transliteration: vikrānto rakṣitā nityam ātmanaśca parasya ca
lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā kuśalī naya śāstravit

sanskrit: हन्ता पर बल ओघानाम् अचिन्त्य बल पौरुषः
न हतो राघवः श्रीमान् सीते शत्रु निबर्हणः
transliteration: hantā para bala oghānām acintya bala pauruṣaḥ
na hato rāghavaḥ śrīmān sīte śatru nibarhaṇaḥ

sanskrit: अयुक्त बुद्धि कृत्येन सर्व भूत विरोधिना
इयम् प्रयुक्ता रौद्रेण माया मायाविदा त्वयि
transliteration: ayukta buddhi kṛtyena sarva bhūta virodhinā
iyam prayuktā raudreṇa māyā māyāvidā tvayi
english: This illusion has been spread around you by that fierce, illusion-creating one, whose mind over runs upon improper acts and who oppose himself to all creatures.

sanskrit: शोकस् ते विगतः सर्वः कल्याणम् त्वाम् उपस्थितम्
ध्रुवम् त्वाम् भजते लक्ष्मीः प्रियम् प्रीति करम् शृणु
transliteration: śokas te vigataḥ sarvaḥ kalyāṇam tvām upasthitam
dhruvam tvām bhajate lakṣmīḥ priyam prīti karam śṛṇu
english: All your sorrow has departed, and your good day has dawned. Certainly Laksmi seek you. And, O lady, hearken to what is dear to you!

sanskrit: उत्तीर्य सागरम् रामः सह वानर सेनया
transliteration: uttīrya sāgaram rāmaḥ saha vānara senayā
english: Having crossed over the ocean, along with the monkey-host, Rāma has encamped himself on the southern shore of the sea.

sanskrit: दृष्टो मे परिपूर्ण अर्थः काकुत्स्थः सह लक्ष्मणः
सहितैः सागर अन्तस्थैर् बलैस् तिष्ठति रक्षितः
transliteration: dṛṣṭo me paripūrṇa arthaḥ kākutsthaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
sahitaiḥ sāgara antasthair balais tiṣṭhati rakṣitaḥ
english: By me has been seen the complete Kākutstha along with Lakşmaņa, accompanied by the forces, stationed on the marge of the main, protected (by his native might).

sanskrit: अनेन प्रेषिता ये च राक्षसा लघु विक्रमः
राघवस् तीर्णैत्य् एवम् प्रवृत्तिस् तैर् इह आहृता
transliteration: anena preṣitā ye ca rākṣasā laghu vikramaḥ
rāghavas tīrṇaity evam pravṛttis tair iha āhṛtā
english: Those Rākşasas of fleet vigour who had been despatched by this one, have brought the news that Rāghava has crossed.

sanskrit: स ताम् श्रुत्वा विशाल अक्षि प्रवृत्तिम् राक्षस अधिपः
एष मन्त्रयते सर्वैः सचिवैः सह रावणः
transliteration: sa tām śrutvā viśāla akṣi pravṛttim rākṣasa adhipaḥ
eṣa mantrayate sarvaiḥ sacivaiḥ saha rāvaṇaḥ
english: And, O large-eyed lady, having learnt this news, Rāvaņa-lord of Rākşasas, is consulting with all his counsellors.

sanskrit: इति ब्रुवाणा सरमा राक्षसी सीतया सह
सर्व उद्योगेन सैन्यानाम् शब्दम् शुश्राव भैरवम्
transliteration: iti bruvāṇā saramā rākṣasī sītayā saha
sarva udyogena sainyānām śabdam śuśrāva bhairavam
english: As the Rākşasī, Saramā, was relating this to Sita, she heard the leonine roars of the army, emitted with the greatest energy.

sanskrit: दण्ड निर्घात वादिन्याः श्रुत्वा भेर्या महा स्वनम्
उवाच सरमा सीताम् इदम् मधुर भाषिणी
transliteration: daṇḍa nirghāta vādinyāḥ śrutvā bheryā mahā svanam
uvāca saramā sītām idam madhura bhāṣiṇī
english: Hearing the mighty sounds of kettledrums produced by sticks struck (thereon), the honeytongued Saramā spoke thus to Sītā.

sanskrit: सम्नाह जननी ह्य् एषा भैरवा भीरु भेरिका
भेरी नादम् च गम्भीरम् शृणु तोयद निस्वनम्
transliteration: samnāha jananī hy eṣā bhairavā bhīru bherikā
bherī nādam ca gambhīram śṛṇu toyada nisvanam
english: These dreadful sounds of the kettledrum, O mother, call to arms. And hark to the solemn notes of the kettledrums, resembling the rumbling of clouds!

sanskrit: कल्प्यन्ते मत्त मातम्गा युज्यन्ते रथ वाजिनः
तत्र तत्र च सम्नद्धाः सम्पतन्ति पदातयः
transliteration: kalpyante matta mātamgā yujyante ratha vājinaḥ
tatra tatra ca samnaddhāḥ sampatanti padātayaḥ
english: The mad elephants are caparisoned and the car-horses are yoked; and thousands of warriors) are seen, mounted on steeds, with bearded darts in their hands.

sanskrit: तत्र तत्र च सन्नद्धाः सम्पतन्ति सहस्रशः
आपूर्यन्ते राज मार्गाः सैन्यैर् अद्भुत दर्शनैः
transliteration: tatra tatra ca sannaddhāḥ sampatanti sahasraśaḥ
āpūryante rāja mārgāḥ sainyair adbhuta darśanaiḥ
english: As waters fill up the ocean, mailed warriors of wonderful forms, vehement and roaring, by thousands rush out on all aides and fill the highways.

sanskrit: वेगवद्भिर् नदद्भिश्च तोय ओघैर् इव सागरः
शास्त्राणाम् च प्रसन्नानाम् चर्मणाम् वर्मणाम् तथा
transliteration: vegavadbhir nadadbhiśca toya oghair iva sāgaraḥ
śāstrāṇām ca prasannānām carmaṇām varmaṇām tathā

sanskrit: रथ वाजि गजानाम् च भूषितानाम् च रक्षसाम्
transliteration: ratha vāji gajānām ca bhūṣitānām ca rakṣasām

sanskrit: प्रभाम् विसृजताम् पश्य नाना वर्णाम् समुत्थिताम्
वनम् निर्दहतो धर्मे यथा रूपम् विभावसोः
transliteration: prabhām visṛjatām paśya nānā varṇām samutthitām
vanam nirdahato dharme yathā rūpam vibhāvasoḥ

sanskrit: घण्टानाम् शृणु निर्घोषम् रथानाम् शृणु निस्वनम्
हयानाम् हेषमाणानाम् शृणु तूर्य ध्वनिम् यथा
transliteration: ghaṇṭānām śṛṇu nirghoṣam rathānām śṛṇu nisvanam
hayānām heṣamāṇānām śṛṇu tūrya dhvanim yathā

sanskrit: उद्यत आयुध हस्तानाम् राक्षस इन्द्र अनुयायिनाम्
सम्भ्रमो रक्षसाम् एष तुमुलो लोम हर्षणः
transliteration: udyata āyudha hastānām rākṣasa indra anuyāyinām
sambhramo rakṣasām eṣa tumulo loma harṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: श्रीस् त्वाम् भजति शोकघ्नी रक्षसाम् भयम् आगतम्
रामात् कमल पत्र अक्षि दैत्यानाम् इव वासवात्
transliteration: śrīs tvām bhajati śokaghnī rakṣasām bhayam āgatam
rāmāt kamala patra akṣi daityānām iva vāsavāt

sanskrit: अवजित्य जित क्रोधस् तम् अचिन्त्य पराक्रमः
रावणम् समरे हत्वा भर्ता त्वा अधिगमिष्यति
transliteration: avajitya jita krodhas tam acintya parākramaḥ
rāvaṇam samare hatvā bhartā tvā adhigamiṣyati
english: As Vasava did to the Daityas, the lotus-eyed Rāma, your lord-of controlled anger, and of inconceivable prowess, slaying Rävaņa in battle and thus delivering you, shall approach you.

sanskrit: विक्रमिष्यति रक्षह्सु भर्ता ते सह लक्ष्मणः
यथा शत्रुषु शत्रुघ्नो विष्णुना सह वासवः
transliteration: vikramiṣyati rakṣahsu bhartā te saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
yathā śatruṣu śatrughno viṣṇunā saha vāsavaḥ
english: And, as Väsava put forth his prowess among his foes, in company with the foe-destroying Visnu, your lord, along with Laksmana, shall display his prowess among the Rākşasa.

sanskrit: आगतस्य हि रामस्य क्षिप्रम् अन्क गताम् सतीम्
अहम् द्रक्ष्यामि सिद्ध अर्थाम् त्वाम् शत्रौ विनिपातिते
transliteration: āgatasya hi rāmasya kṣipram anka gatām satīm
aham drakṣyāmi siddha arthām tvām śatrau vinipātite
english: On the enemy having fallen, I shall behold you, devoted to your lord, with your desire attained, soon lying on the lap of Rama.

sanskrit: समागम्य परिष्वक्ता तस्य उरसि महा उरसः
transliteration: samāgamya pariṣvaktā tasya urasi mahā urasaḥ
english: And, O Janaki, embracing (your lord) you shall shed tears of joy on his mighty breast.

sanskrit: अचिरान् मोक्ष्यते सीते देवि ते जघनम् गताम्
धृताम् एताम् बहून् मासान् वेणीम् रामो महा बलः
transliteration: acirān mokṣyate sīte devi te jaghanam gatām
dhṛtām etām bahūn māsān veṇīm rāmo mahā balaḥ
english: O Sitä, soon shall the highly powerful Răma loosen this braid of your reaching to your hips, which you have been wearing for many a month.

sanskrit: तस्य दृष्ट्वा मुखम् देवि पूर्ण चन्द्रम् इव उदितम्
मोक्ष्यसे शोकजम् वारि निर्मोकम् इव पन्नगी
transliteration: tasya dṛṣṭvā mukham devi pūrṇa candram iva uditam
mokṣyase śokajam vāri nirmokam iva pannagī
english: O exalted one, seeing his face like the full moon risen, you shall shed water begot of ruth, even as a she-serpent casts off her slough.

sanskrit: रावणम् समरे हत्वा नचिराद् एव मैथिलि
त्वया समग्रम् प्रियया सुख अर्हो लप्स्यते सुखम्
transliteration: rāvaṇam samare hatvā nacirād eva maithili
tvayā samagram priyayā sukha arho lapsyate sukham
english: O Mithila's daughter, speedily slaying Ravana in battle, that one worthy of happiness shall reap felicity in the company of you, his beloved.
And, loved by the high-souled Rama, you, shall be happy, even as the Earth furnished with crops brought forth by plenteous showers.

sanskrit: हय इव मण्डलम् आशु यः करोति
तम् इह शरणम् अभ्युपेहि देविदिवस करम् प्रभवो ह्ययम् प्रजानाम् ६-३३-३९
transliteration: haya iva maṇḍalam āśu yaḥ karoti
tam iha śaraṇam abhyupehi devidivasa karam prabhavo hyayam prajānām 6-33-39
english: Do you, O exalted one, take refuge with him, who, going round the foremost of mountains, speedily assume a steed-like circular movement; for even the maker of day is the source of people's joy and grief.

sanskrit: अथ ताम् जात सम्तापाम् तेन वाक्येन मोदिताम्
transliteration: atha tām jāta samtāpām tena vākyena moditām
english: Burning with grief on account of those words,* Sarama gladdened and cheered her, even as masses of clouds (cheer up) the burning Earth. *i.e.the words of Ravana.

sanskrit: ततस् तस्या हितम् सख्याश् चिकीर्षन्ती सखी वचः
उवाच काले कालज्ना स्मित पूर्व अभिभाषिणी
transliteration: tatas tasyā hitam sakhyāś cikīrṣantī sakhī vacaḥ
uvāca kāle kālajnā smita pūrva abhibhāṣiṇī
english: Then, desirous of doing her good, (Sita's) friend, conversant with season, and ever precluding her speech with a smile, spoke to her seasonably.

sanskrit: उत्सहेयम् अहम् गत्वा त्वद् वाक्यम् असित ईक्षणे
transliteration: utsaheyam aham gatvā tvad vākyam asita īkṣaṇe
english: O you having dark eyes, I can, secretly going to Rama and communicating to him your auspicious words, come back clandestinely.

sanskrit: न हि मे क्रममाणाया निरालम्बे विहायसि
समर्थो गतिम् अन्वेतुम् पवनो गरुडो अपि वा
transliteration: na hi me kramamāṇāyā nirālambe vihāyasi
samartho gatim anvetum pavano garuḍo api vā
english: Nor, when I course the supportless sky, can even the Wind or Garuda follow me.

sanskrit: एवम् ब्रुवाणाम् ताम् सीता सरमाम् पुनर् अब्रवीत्
मधुरम् श्लक्ष्णया वाचा पूर्व शोक अभिपन्नया
transliteration: evam bruvāṇām tām sītā saramām punar abravīt
madhuram ślakṣṇayā vācā pūrva śoka abhipannayā
english: As she said this, Sita with her grief a little lightened, said to Sarama in sweet and smooth words.

sanskrit: समर्था गगनम् गन्तुम् अपि वा त्वम् रसा तलम्
अवगच्चाम्य् अकर्तव्यम् कर्तव्यम् ते मद् अन्तरे
transliteration: samarthā gaganam gantum api vā tvam rasā talam
avagaccāmy akartavyam kartavyam te mad antare
english: You are capable of even going to the nethermost regions. But do you on my behalf that which is fit to be done by you.

sanskrit: मत् प्रियम् यदि कर्तव्यम् यदि बुद्धिः स्थिरा तव
ज्नातुम् इच्चामि तम् गत्वा किम् करोति इति रावणः
transliteration: mat priyam yadi kartavyam yadi buddhiḥ sthirā tava
jnātum iccāmi tam gatvā kim karoti iti rāvaṇaḥ
english: If you intend doing me a good turn, and if your sense be steady, I would know what Ravana is doing after having left this place.

sanskrit: स हि माया बलः क्रूरो रावणः शत्रु रावणः
माम् मोहयति दुष्ट आत्मा पीत मात्रा इव वारुणी
transliteration: sa hi māyā balaḥ krūro rāvaṇaḥ śatru rāvaṇaḥ
mām mohayati duṣṭa ātmā pīta mātrā iva vāruṇī
english: That guileful and wicked-minded one, Rāvana, destroyer of enemies, having powers of illusion, overwhelms me even as the Vāruni just drunk.

sanskrit: तर्जापयति माम् नित्यम् भर्त्सापयति च असक्र्त्
राक्षसीभिः सुघोराभिर् या माम् रक्षन्ति नित्यशः
transliteration: tarjāpayati mām nityam bhartsāpayati ca asakrt
rākṣasībhiḥ sughorābhir yā mām rakṣanti nityaśaḥ
english: Confining me here for ever and a day, (Rāvana) sets on dreadful Räksnasas to alike threaten and scold me constantly.

sanskrit: उद्विग्ना शन्किता च अस्मि न च स्वस्थम् मनो मम
तद् भयाच् च अहम् उद्विग्ना;अशोक वनिकाम् गताः
transliteration: udvignā śankitā ca asmi na ca svastham mano mama
tad bhayāc ca aham udvignā;aśoka vanikām gatāḥ
english: And I am agitated and alarmed and my mind is (always) uneasy. And I, dwelling in the Asoka wood, is ever agitated.

sanskrit: यदि नाम कथा तस्य निश्चितम् वा अपि यद् भवेत्
निवेदयेथाः सर्वम् तत् परो मे स्याद् अनुग्रहः
transliteration: yadi nāma kathā tasya niścitam vā api yad bhavet
nivedayethāḥ sarvam tat paro me syād anugrahaḥ
english: If there is any talk (of delivering me), or keeping me confined, you should communicate to me the decision arrived at.

sanskrit: साप्येवम् ब्रुवतीम् सीताम् सरमा वल्गु भाषिणी
उवाच वचनम् तस्याः स्पृशन्ती बाष्प विक्लवम्
transliteration: sāpyevam bruvatīm sītām saramā valgu bhāṣiṇī
uvāca vacanam tasyāḥ spṛśantī bāṣpa viklavam
english: This is the highest favour that I seek (at hands). Thereat, the mild-speeched Saramā, wiping (Sītā's) face washed in tears, spoke to her, as she said this.

sanskrit: एष ते यद्य् अभिप्रायस् तस्माद् गच्चामि जानकि
गृह्य शत्रोर् अभिप्रायम् उपाव्र्त्ताम् च पश्य माम्
transliteration: eṣa te yady abhiprāyas tasmād gaccāmi jānaki
gṛhya śatror abhiprāyam upāvrttām ca paśya mām
english: If this is your wish, I will go, O Jānaki. O Mithila's daughter, having possessed myself of the intent of the enemy, I shall come back.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा ततो गत्वा समीपम् तस्य रक्षसः
transliteration: evam uktvā tato gatvā samīpam tasya rakṣasaḥ
english: Having said this, (Saramā), repairing to the Raksasa, heard Raksa, heard Ravana's converse with his counsellors.

sanskrit: सा श्रुत्वा निश्चयम् तस्य निश्चयज्ना दुरात्मनः
पुनर् एव अगमत् क्षिप्रम् अशोक वनिकाम् तदा
transliteration: sā śrutvā niścayam tasya niścayajnā durātmanaḥ
punar eva agamat kṣipram aśoka vanikām tadā
english: Having heard of the decision of that wickedminded one, she, understanding decisions, swiftly retraced her steps to the fair Asoka forest.

sanskrit: सा प्रविष्टा पुनस् तत्र ददर्श जनक आत्मजाम्
प्रतीक्षमाणाम् स्वाम् एव भ्रष्ट पद्माम् इव श्रियम्
transliteration: sā praviṣṭā punas tatra dadarśa janaka ātmajām
pratīkṣamāṇām svām eva bhraṣṭa padmām iva śriyam
english: Then, entering there, she saw Janaka's daughter, expecting (her) like a very Sri,, bereft of her lotus.

sanskrit: ताम् तु सीता पुनः प्राप्ताम् सरमाम् वल्गु भाषिणीम्
परिष्वज्य च सुस्निग्धम् ददौ च स्वयम् आसनम्
transliteration: tām tu sītā punaḥ prāptām saramām valgu bhāṣiṇīm
pariṣvajya ca susnigdham dadau ca svayam āsanam
english: And, the fair-spoken Sarama, on getting back (near her), Sītā, embracing her affectionately, herself gave her a seat.

sanskrit: इह आसीना सुखम् सर्वम् आख्याहि मम तत्त्वतः
transliteration: iha āsīnā sukham sarvam ākhyāhi mama tattvataḥ
english: Sitting down here at ease, do you relate to me faithfully all about the determination of the wicked-minded and guileful Ravana.

sanskrit: एवम् उक्ता तु सरमा सीतया वेपमानया
transliteration: evam uktā tu saramā sītayā vepamānayā
english: Thus accosted by the trembling Sītä, Saramā related everything that had been said by Råvaņa and his counsellors.

sanskrit: जनन्या राक्षस इन्द्रो वै त्वन् मोक्ष अर्थम् बृहद् वचः
अविद्धेन च वैदेहि मन्त्रि वृद्धेन बोधितः
transliteration: jananyā rākṣasa indro vai tvan mokṣa artham bṛhad vacaḥ
aviddhena ca vaidehi mantri vṛddhena bodhitaḥ
english: O Vaidehi, the Rākşasa lord was advised by his mother and the aged counsellors in pregnant words informed with affection, having your deliverance for their object.

sanskrit: निदर्शनम् ते पर्याप्तम् जन स्थाने यद् अद्भुतम्
transliteration: nidarśanam te paryāptam jana sthāne yad adbhutam
english: Do you make over Maithili to the king of men, paying him homage due. You have in Janasthāna profusely witnessed wonderful instances (of his prowess).

sanskrit: लन्घनम् च समुद्रस्य दर्शनम् च हनूमतः
वधम् च रक्षसाम् युद्धे कः कुर्यान् मानुषो भुवि
transliteration: langhanam ca samudrasya darśanam ca hanūmataḥ
vadham ca rakṣasām yuddhe kaḥ kuryān mānuṣo bhuvi
english: The crossing of the ocean, Hanuman's sight (of Sītā) and the slaughter of the Rākşasa in fight, what person is capable of doing all this in battle?

sanskrit: एवम् स मन्त्रि वृद्धैश्च मात्रा च बहु भाषितः
न त्वाम् उत्सहते मोक्तुम् अर्तह्म् अर्थ परो यथा
transliteration: evam sa mantri vṛddhaiśca mātrā ca bahu bhāṣitaḥ
na tvām utsahate moktum artahm artha paro yathā
english: Thus long exhorted by his counsellors as well as his mother, Rāvaņa does not make up his mind to emancipate you, even as a covetous person is loath to pare with wealth (appropriated).

sanskrit: न उत्सहत्य् अम्र्तो मोक्तुम् युद्धे त्वाम् इति मैथिलि
सामात्यस्य नृशम्सस्य निश्चयो ह्य् एष वर्तते
transliteration: na utsahaty amrto moktum yuddhe tvām iti maithili
sāmātyasya nṛśamsasya niścayo hy eṣa vartate

sanskrit: तद् एषा सुस्थिरा बुद्धिर्मृत्यु लोभाद् उपस्थिता
भयान् न शक्तस् त्वाम् मोक्तुम् अनिरस्तस् तु सम्युगे
transliteration: tad eṣā susthirā buddhirmṛtyu lobhād upasthitā
bhayān na śaktas tvām moktum anirastas tu samyuge

sanskrit: राक्षसानाम् च सर्वेषाम् आत्मनश् च वधेन हि
निहत्य रावणम् सम्ख्ये सर्वथा निशितैः शरैः
transliteration: rākṣasānām ca sarveṣām ātmanaś ca vadhena hi
nihatya rāvaṇam samkhye sarvathā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ

sanskrit: प्रतिनेष्यति रामस् त्वाम् अयोध्याम् असित ईक्षणे
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे शब्दो भेरी शन्ख समाकुलः
transliteration: pratineṣyati rāmas tvām ayodhyām asita īkṣaṇe
etasminn antare śabdo bherī śankha samākulaḥ

sanskrit: श्रुतो वै सर्व सैन्यानाम् कम्पयन् धरणी तलम्
श्रुत्वा तु तम् वानर सैन्य शब्दम्
transliteration: śruto vai sarva sainyānām kampayan dharaṇī talam
śrutvā tu tam vānara sainya śabdam
english: Hearing that hubbub of the monkey-army, the servants of the Råkşasa monarch, ran who were in Lankā, growing dispirited, and bereft of energy, with weakness overcoming their powers, did not see any good, in consequence of the fault of the ruler.

sanskrit: तेन शन्ख विमिश्रेण भेरी शब्देन राघवः
उपयतो महा बाहू रामह् पर पुरम् जयः
transliteration: tena śankha vimiśreṇa bherī śabdena rāghavaḥ
upayato mahā bāhū rāmah para puram jayaḥ
english: That captor of hostile capitals, the mightarmed Rāma, was advancing (upon Larikā) with the sounds of drums mixed with the blares of conchs.

sanskrit: तम् निनादम् निशम्य अथ रावणो राक्षस ईश्वरः
transliteration: tam ninādam niśamya atha rāvaṇo rākṣasa īśvaraḥ
english: Hearing this noise, Ravana-lord of Raks asas-reflecting for a while, cast his eyes upon his counsellors.

sanskrit: अथ तान् सचिवाम्स् तत्र सर्वान् आभाष्य रावणः
सभाम् सम्नादयन् सर्वाम् इत्य् उवाच महा बलः
transliteration: atha tān sacivāms tatra sarvān ābhāṣya rāvaṇaḥ
sabhām samnādayan sarvām ity uvāca mahā balaḥ
english: Addressing there all those counsellors, that afflictor of the world—the crooked and highly powerful lord of the Rākşasas, Rāvaņa, making his court resound, running down (Rāma's) crossing the main, as well as his vigour, strength and manhood, said to them.

sanskrit: तरणम् सागरस्य अपि विक्रमम् बल सम्चयम्
transliteration: taraṇam sāgarasya api vikramam bala samcayam

sanskrit: यद् उक्तवन्तो रामस्य भवन्तस् तन् मया श्रुतम्
transliteration: yad uktavanto rāmasya bhavantas tan mayā śrutam
