english: What you have said touching Rama's (prowess), has been heard by me. And I also know you to be of sterling valour in the field. Yet why, knowing Rāma's prowess, do you silently look at each other?

sanskrit: ततस् तु सुमहा प्राज्नो माल्यवान् नाम राक्षसः
transliteration: tatas tu sumahā prājno mālyavān nāma rākṣasaḥ

sanskrit: रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मातुः पैतामहो अब्रवीत्
विद्यास्वभिविनीतो यो राजा राजन् नय अनुगः
transliteration: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā mātuḥ paitāmaho abravīt
vidyāsvabhivinīto yo rājā rājan naya anugaḥ

sanskrit: स शास्ति चिरम् ऐश्वर्यम् अरीम्श्च कुरुते वशे
सम्दधानो हि कालेन विगृह्णम्सः चारिभिः सह
transliteration: sa śāsti ciram aiśvaryam arīmśca kurute vaśe
samdadhāno hi kālena vigṛhṇamsaḥ cāribhiḥ saha

sanskrit: स्व पक्ष वर्धनम् कुर्वन् महद् ऐश्वर्यम् अश्नुते ॥हीयमानेन कर्तव्यो राज्ना सम्धिः समेन च
transliteration: sva pakṣa vardhanam kurvan mahad aiśvaryam aśnute hīyamānena kartavyo rājnā samdhiḥ samena ca

sanskrit: न शत्रुम् अवमन्येत ज्यायान् कुर्वीत विग्रहम्
तन्मह्यम् रोचते सम्धिः सह रामेण रावण
transliteration: na śatrum avamanyeta jyāyān kurvīta vigraham
tanmahyam rocate samdhiḥ saha rāmeṇa rāvaṇa

sanskrit: यद् अर्थम् अभियुक्ताः स्म सीता तस्मै प्रदीयताम्
तस्य देव ऋषयः सर्वे गन्धर्वासः च जय एषिणः
transliteration: yad artham abhiyuktāḥ sma sītā tasmai pradīyatām
tasya deva ṛṣayaḥ sarve gandharvāsaḥ ca jaya eṣiṇaḥ

sanskrit: विरोधम् मा गमस् तेन सम्धिस् ते तेन रोचताम्
असृजद् भगवान् पक्षौ द्वाव् एव हि पितामहः
transliteration: virodham mā gamas tena samdhis te tena rocatām
asṛjad bhagavān pakṣau dvāv eva hi pitāmahaḥ

sanskrit: सुराणाम् असुराणाम् च धर्म अधर्मौ तद् आश्रयौ
धर्मो हि श्रूयते पक्षः सुराणाम् च महात्मनाम्
transliteration: surāṇām asurāṇām ca dharma adharmau tad āśrayau
dharmo hi śrūyate pakṣaḥ surāṇām ca mahātmanām

sanskrit: अधर्मो रक्षसाम् पक्षोह्य असुराणाम् च रावण
धर्मो वै ग्रसते अधर्मम् ततः कृतम् अभूद् युगम्
transliteration: adharmo rakṣasām pakṣohya asurāṇām ca rāvaṇa
dharmo vai grasate adharmam tataḥ kṛtam abhūd yugam

sanskrit: अधर्मो ग्रसते धर्मम् ततस् तिष्यः प्रवर्तते
तत् त्वया चरता लोकान् धर्मो विनिहतो महान्
transliteration: adharmo grasate dharmam tatas tiṣyaḥ pravartate
tat tvayā caratā lokān dharmo vinihato mahān

sanskrit: अधर्मः प्रगृहीतसः च तेन अस्मद् बलिनः परे
स प्रमादाद् विवृद्धस् ते अधर्मो अहिर् ग्रसते हि नः
transliteration: adharmaḥ pragṛhītasaḥ ca tena asmad balinaḥ pare
sa pramādād vivṛddhas te adharmo ahir grasate hi naḥ

sanskrit: विवर्धयति पक्षम् च सुराणाम् सुर भावनः
विषयेषु प्रसक्तेन यत् किम्चित् कारिणा त्वया
transliteration: vivardhayati pakṣam ca surāṇām sura bhāvanaḥ
viṣayeṣu prasaktena yat kimcit kāriṇā tvayā

sanskrit: Rषीणाम् अग्नि कल्पानाम् उद्वेगो जनितो महान्
transliteration: ṣīṇām agni kalpānām udvego janito mahān

sanskrit: तपसा भावित आत्मानो धर्मस्य अनुग्रहे रताः
मुख्यैर् यज्नैर् यजन्त्य् एते नित्यम् तैस् तैर् द्विजातयः
transliteration: tapasā bhāvita ātmāno dharmasya anugrahe ratāḥ
mukhyair yajnair yajanty ete nityam tais tair dvijātayaḥ

sanskrit: जुह्वत्य् अग्नीम्सः च विधिवद् वेदाम्सः च उच्चैर् अधीयते
अभिभूय च रक्षाम्सि ब्रह्म घोषान् उदैरयन्
transliteration: juhvaty agnīmsaḥ ca vidhivad vedāmsaḥ ca uccair adhīyate
abhibhūya ca rakṣāmsi brahma ghoṣān udairayan
english: The twice-born ones engage in contemplation with intent minds, offer oblations into the fire according to the ordinance, and loudly recite the Vedas. They overpower the Rākşasa, uttering the Vedas; and thereat they fly in all directions like clouds scattered in summer.

sanskrit: दिशो विप्रद्रुताः सर्वे स्तनयित्नुर् इव उष्णगे
ऋषीणाम् अग्नि कल्पानाम् अग्नि होत्र समुत्थितः
transliteration: diśo vipradrutāḥ sarve stanayitnur iva uṣṇage
ṛṣīṇām agni kalpānām agni hotra samutthitaḥ

sanskrit: आदत्ते रक्षसाम् तेजो धूमो व्याप्य दिशो दश
तेषु तेषु च देशेषु पुण्येषु च दृढ व्रतैः
transliteration: ādatte rakṣasām tejo dhūmo vyāpya diśo daśa
teṣu teṣu ca deśeṣu puṇyeṣu ca dṛḍha vrataiḥ
english: The smoke that arise from the Agnihotra sacrifices of saints resembling fire, enveloping the energy of the Räkşasas, spreads over the ten cardinal quarters.
The fierce austerities of vow-observing saints, performed at particular sacred spots, try the Rākş asas sore.

You have obtained a boon, conferring immunity at the hands of deities, Dänavas and Yakşas. But men and monkeys, bears and Golăngülas, possessed of enormous strength and endowed with vigour, and of indomitable prowess, coming here, are setting up roars.

sanskrit: उत्पातान् विविधान् दृष्ट्वा घोरान् बहु विधाम्स् तथा
transliteration: utpātān vividhān dṛṣṭvā ghorān bahu vidhāms tathā
english: Witnessing various and many dire portents, I perceive the destruction of all the Rākşasas.

sanskrit: खराभिस् तनिता घोरा मेघाह् प्रतिभयम् करः
transliteration: kharābhis tanitā ghorā meghāh pratibhayam karaḥ
english: Dreadful and terrific clouds, uttering harsh sounds, are showering blood all around Lankā.

sanskrit: रुदताम् वाहनानाम् च प्रपतन्त्य् अस्र बिन्दवः
ध्वजा ध्वस्ता विवर्णासः च न प्रभान्ति यथा पुरम्
transliteration: rudatām vāhanānām ca prapatanty asra bindavaḥ
dhvajā dhvastā vivarṇāsaḥ ca na prabhānti yathā puram
english: And (live) vehicles are dropping profuse tears. And all sides, covered with dust, do not appear bright as formerly.

sanskrit: व्याला गोमायवो ग्R^ इध्रा वाशन्ति च सुभैरवम्
प्रविश्य लन्काम् अनिशम् समवायाम्सः च कुर्वते
transliteration: vyālā gomāyavo g idhrā vāśanti ca subhairavam
praviśya lankām aniśam samavāyāmsaḥ ca kurvate
english: And beasts of prey, jackals and vultures, are emitting frightful cries, and, entering into the garden of Lankā, form themselves into bands.

sanskrit: कालिकाः पाण्डुरैर् दन्तैः प्रहसन्त्य् अग्रतः स्थिताः
स्त्रियः स्वप्नेषु मुष्णन्त्यो गृहाणि प्रतिभाष्य च
transliteration: kālikāḥ pāṇḍurair dantaiḥ prahasanty agrataḥ sthitāḥ
striyaḥ svapneṣu muṣṇantyo gṛhāṇi pratibhāṣya ca
english: In dreams mighty dark-hued women in front of dwellings, seizing at (the furniture) thereof, and speaking inauspiciously, laugh displaying their sable teeth.

sanskrit: खरा गोषु प्रजायन्ते मूषिका नकुलैः सह
transliteration: kharā goṣu prajāyante mūṣikā nakulaiḥ saha
english: In houses dogs are feasting on the articles of worship. And cows bring forth asses, and mungooses, mice.

sanskrit: मार्जारा द्वीपिभिः सार्धम् सूकराः शुनकैः सह
किम्नरा राक्षसैसः च अपि समेयुर् मानुषैः सह
transliteration: mārjārā dvīpibhiḥ sārdham sūkarāḥ śunakaiḥ saha
kimnarā rākṣasaisaḥ ca api sameyur mānuṣaiḥ saha
english: And cats are pairing with leopards, and swine with dogs, and Kinnaras with Rākşasas and human being.

sanskrit: पाण्डुरा रक्त पादासः च विहगाः काल चोदिताः
transliteration: pāṇḍurā rakta pādāsaḥ ca vihagāḥ kāla coditāḥ
english: are And red-footed white sky-coursing pigeons, urged on by Doom, are going about for the destruction of the Raksasas.

sanskrit: पतन्ति ग्रथितासः च अपि निर्जिताः कलह एषिणः
transliteration: patanti grathitāsaḥ ca api nirjitāḥ kalaha eṣiṇaḥ
english: And female-parrots in houses, wounded and worsted by other birds delighting in discord, are dropping down, emitting indistinct notes.

sanskrit: पक्षिणश्च मृगाः सर्वे प्रत्यादित्यम् रुदन्ति ते
करालो विकटो मुण्डः पुरुषः कृष्ण पिन्गलः
transliteration: pakṣiṇaśca mṛgāḥ sarve pratyādityam rudanti te
karālo vikaṭo muṇḍaḥ puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇa pingalaḥ
english: All the birds and beasts crying (distressfully) with their faces turned towards the sun. And at dusk a frightful, withered, tawnyhued male figure, looking like Death himself, with his head shaven, peer into the houses (of people).

sanskrit: कालो गृहाणि सर्वेषाम् काले काले अन्ववेक्षते
एतान्य् अन्यानि दुष्टानि निमित्तान्य् उत्पतन्ति च
transliteration: kālo gṛhāṇi sarveṣām kāle kāle anvavekṣate
etāny anyāni duṣṭāni nimittāny utpatanti ca

sanskrit: विष्णुम् मन्यामहे रामम् मानुषम् देहम् आस्थितम्
न हि मानुष मात्रो असौ राघवो दृढ विक्रमः
transliteration: viṣṇum manyāmahe rāmam mānuṣam deham āsthitam
na hi mānuṣa mātro asau rāghavo dṛḍha vikramaḥ

sanskrit: येन बद्धः समुद्रस्य स सेतुः परम अद्भुतः
कुरुष्व नर राजेन सम्धिम् रामेण रावण
transliteration: yena baddhaḥ samudrasya sa setuḥ parama adbhutaḥ
kuruṣva nara rājena samdhim rāmeṇa rāvaṇa

english: Having said this to that vile one, and known the intention of the lord of Rākşasa, that strong Mālyavān, of exceeding prowess, became silent, eying Ravana.

sanskrit: तत्तु माल्यवतो वाक्यम् हितम् उक्तम् दzअ आननः
न मर्षयति दुष्ट अत्मा कालस्य वzअम् आगतः
transliteration: tattu mālyavato vākyam hitam uktam daa ānanaḥ
na marṣayati duṣṭa atmā kālasya vaam āgataḥ
english: The Ten-necked one, come under the control of Time, did not brook the beneficial speech, spoken by Mālyavān.

sanskrit: स बद्ध्वा भ्रु कुटिम् वक्त्रे क्रोधस्य वzअम् आगतः
अमर्षात् परिवृत्त अक्षो माल्यवन्तम् अथ अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sa baddhvā bhru kuṭim vaktre krodhasya vaam āgataḥ
amarṣāt parivṛtta akṣo mālyavantam atha abravīt
english: Contracting his face into a frown, he, coming under the masterdom of passion, with his eyes rolling in wrath, addressed Mayavān, saying.

sanskrit: हित बुद्ध्या यद् अहितम् वचह् परुषम् उच्यते
पर पक्षम् प्रविzय एव न एतत् zरोत्र गतम् मम
transliteration: hita buddhyā yad ahitam vacah paruṣam ucyate
para pakṣam praviya eva na etat rotra gatam mama
english: The words which, deeming the strength of the enemy as superior, you have harshly spoken, considering it as beneficial, had never before entered my ears.

sanskrit: मानुषम् कृपणम् रामम् एकम् zआखा मृग आzरयम्
समर्थम् मन्यसे केन त्यक्तम् पित्रा वन आलयम्
transliteration: mānuṣam kṛpaṇam rāmam ekam ākhā mṛga ārayam
samartham manyase kena tyaktam pitrā vana ālayam
english: A (mere) man, and feeble, and alone, and having monkeys for his support, why do you deem Rāma, who has (further) been cast off by his sire, and has in consequence taken refuge in the woods, as competent (to cope with me)?

sanskrit: रक्षसाम् ईzवरम् माम् च देवतानाम् भयम् करम्
हीनम् माम् मन्यसे केन;अहीनम् सर्व विक्रमैः
transliteration: rakṣasām īvaram mām ca devatānām bhayam karam
hīnam mām manyase kena;ahīnam sarva vikramaiḥ
english: Why do you consider me, who am the lord of the Räksasa, and feared even by the immortals, as weak and reft of all power?

sanskrit: वीर द्वेषेण वा zअन्के पक्ष पातेन वा रिपोः
त्वया अहम् परुषाण्य् उक्तः पर प्रोत्साहनेन वा
transliteration: vīra dveṣeṇa vā anke pakṣa pātena vā ripoḥ
tvayā aham paruṣāṇy uktaḥ para protsāhanena vā
english: You, I suspect, speak (thus) roughly either from jealousy of my heroism, or for inciting me.

sanskrit: प्रभवन्तम् पदस्थम् हि परुषम् को अह्बिधास्यति
पण्डितह् zआस्त्र तत्त्वज्नो विना प्रोत्साहनाद् रिपोः
transliteration: prabhavantam padastham hi paruṣam ko ahbidhāsyati
paṇḍitah āstra tattvajno vinā protsāhanād ripoḥ
english: Who that is wise and learned, ever address him roughly that is at once puissant and of (high) station, if not to spur him on?

sanskrit: आनीय च वनात् सीताम् पद्म हीनाम् इव zरियम्
किम् अर्थम् प्रतिदास्यामि राघवस्य भयाद् अहम्
transliteration: ānīya ca vanāt sītām padma hīnām iva riyam
kim artham pratidāsyāmi rāghavasya bhayād aham
english: Why, having brought Sītā like a Sri shorn of her lotus, shall I give her up, from fear of Rāghava?

sanskrit: पzय कैzचिद् अहोभिस् त्वम् राघवम् निहतम् मया
transliteration: paya kaicid ahobhis tvam rāghavam nihatam mayā
english: Behold Rāghava, environed by Koțis of monkeys, with Sugrīva and Lakşmaņa, slain on of these days!

sanskrit: द्वन्द्वे यस्य न तिष्ठन्ति दैवतान्य् अपि सम्युगे
स कस्माद् रावणो युद्धे भयम् आहारयिष्यति
transliteration: dvandve yasya na tiṣṭhanti daivatāny api samyuge
sa kasmād rāvaṇo yuddhe bhayam āhārayiṣyati
english: He before whom even the gods cannot stay in the battle field, how can that Råvaņa ever come by fear?

sanskrit: द्विधा भज्येयम् अप्य् एवम् न नमेयम् तु कस्यचित्
एष मे सहजो दोषह् स्वभावो दुरतिक्रमः
transliteration: dvidhā bhajyeyam apy evam na nameyam tu kasyacit
eṣa me sahajo doṣah svabhāvo duratikramaḥ
english: Better that I should be riven in twain, but bend I never will. This is my native fault; and nature is incapable of being overcome.

sanskrit: यदि तावत् समुद्रे तु सेतुर् बद्धो यदृच्चया
रामेण विस्मयः को अत्र येन ते भयम् आगतम्
transliteration: yadi tāvat samudre tu setur baddho yadṛccayā
rāmeṇa vismayaḥ ko atra yena te bhayam āgatam
english: If Rāma bath at his pleasure constructed a bridge over the ocean, what is the wonder in this that you have conceived such a fear?

sanskrit: स तु तीर्त्वा अर्णवम् रामः सह वानर सेनया
प्रतिजानामि ते सत्यम् न जीवन् प्रतियास्यति
transliteration: sa tu tīrtvā arṇavam rāmaḥ saha vānara senayā
pratijānāmi te satyam na jīvan pratiyāsyati
english: And although Rāma has crossed the ocean along with the monkey-army, yet I swear to you truly, living, he shall not back hence.

sanskrit: एवम् ब्रुवाणम् सम्रब्धम् रुष्टम् विज्नाय रावणम्
व्रीडितो माल्यवान् वाक्यम् न उत्तरम् प्रत्यपद्यत
transliteration: evam bruvāṇam samrabdham ruṣṭam vijnāya rāvaṇam
vrīḍito mālyavān vākyam na uttaram pratyapadyata
english: When Ravana, wrought up with passion, had spoken thus, Malyavan, knowing him wroth, did not return a reply.

sanskrit: जय आzइषा च राजानम् वर्धयित्वा यथा उचितम्
transliteration: jaya āiṣā ca rājānam vardhayitvā yathā ucitam
english: And, duly tendering blessings to the king, Mālyavān, taking his permission, went to his own abode.

sanskrit: रावणस् तु सह अमात्यो मन्त्रयित्वा विमृzय च
लन्कायाम् अतुलाम् गुप्तिम् कारयाम् आस राक्षसः
transliteration: rāvaṇas tu saha amātyo mantrayitvā vimṛya ca
lankāyām atulām guptim kārayām āsa rākṣasaḥ
english: The Räkşasa, Rāvaņa, along with his courtiers, having consulted together as to what was fit to be done, set about the defence of Lankā.

sanskrit: व्यादिदेzअ च पूर्वस्याम् प्रहस्तम् द्वारि राक्षसम्
दक्षिणस्याम् महा वीर्यौ महा पार्zव महा उदरौ
transliteration: vyādidea ca pūrvasyām prahastam dvāri rākṣasam
dakṣiṇasyām mahā vīryau mahā pārva mahā udarau
english: He commanded the Raksasa Prahasta (to guard) the Eastern gate; and the exceedingly powerful Mahaparsva and Mahodara (to guard) the Southern gate; and he ordered his son Indrajit, possessing mighty powers of illusion, girt by innumerable Räkșasas, to guard the Western gate.

sanskrit: पzचिमायाम् अथो द्वारि पुत्रम् इन्द्रजितम् तथा
व्यादिदेzअ महा मायम् राक्षसैर् बहुभिर् वृतम्
transliteration: pacimāyām atho dvāri putram indrajitam tathā
vyādidea mahā māyam rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtam
english: He commanded the Raksasa Prahasta (to guard) the Eastern gate; and the exceedingly powerful Mahaparsva and Mahodara (to guard) the Southern gate; and he ordered his son Indrajit, possessing mighty powers of illusion, girt by innumerable Räkșasas, to guard the Western gate.

sanskrit: उत्तरस्याम् पुर द्वारि व्यादिzय zउक सारणौ
स्वयम् च अत्र भविष्यामि मन्त्रिणस् तान् उवाच ह
transliteration: uttarasyām pura dvāri vyādiya uka sāraṇau
svayam ca atra bhaviṣyāmi mantriṇas tān uvāca ha
english: He commanded Suka and Sārana to defend the Northern gate. But he said to the counsellors, I will myself go thither.* *i.e. to defend the Northerm gate.

sanskrit: राक्षसम् तु विरूप अक्षम् महा वीर्य पराक्रमम्
मध्यमे अस्थापयद् गुल्मे बहुभिह् सह राक्षसैः
transliteration: rākṣasam tu virūpa akṣam mahā vīrya parākramam
madhyame asthāpayad gulme bahubhih saha rākṣasaiḥ
english: And he posted in the middle in the garrison the Raksasa, Virupaksa, endowed with exceeding prowess and energy, backed by countless rākşasas.

sanskrit: एवम् विधानम् लन्कायाम् कृत्वा राक्षस पुम्गवः
मेने कृत अर्थम् आत्मानम् कृत अन्त वzअम् आगतः
transliteration: evam vidhānam lankāyām kṛtvā rākṣasa pumgavaḥ
mene kṛta artham ātmānam kṛta anta vaam āgataḥ
english: Having taken these measures in Lankā, the raksasa-chief, urged by Fate, deemed himself as having achieved success.

sanskrit: विवेzअ सो अन्तह् पुरम् ऋद्धिमन् महत्
transliteration: vivea so antah puram ṛddhiman mahat
english: Having thus completely provided for the defence of the city, he dismissed the ministers; and, honoured by the counsellors with blessings of victory, (then) entered his magnificent and splendid inner apartment.

sanskrit: नर वानर राजौ तौ स च वायु सुतः कपिः
जाम्बवान् ऋक्ष राजसः च राक्षससः च विभीषणः
transliteration: nara vānara rājau tau sa ca vāyu sutaḥ kapiḥ
jāmbavān ṛkṣa rājasaḥ ca rākṣasasaḥ ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: अन्गदो वालि पुत्रसः च सौमित्रिः शरभः कपिः
सुषेणः सह दायादो मैन्दो द्विविद;एव च
transliteration: angado vāli putrasaḥ ca saumitriḥ śarabhaḥ kapiḥ
suṣeṇaḥ saha dāyādo maindo dvivida;eva ca

sanskrit: गजो गव अक्षो कुमुदो नलो अथ पनसस् तथा
transliteration: gajo gava akṣo kumudo nalo atha panasas tathā

sanskrit: इयम् सा लक्ष्यते लन्का पुरी रावण पालिता
सासुर उरग गन्धर्वैर् अमरैर् अपि दुर्जया
transliteration: iyam sā lakṣyate lankā purī rāvaṇa pālitā
sāsura uraga gandharvair amarair api durjayā
english: Yonder is that Lankā ruled by Rāvana, invincible even to the celestials, serpents and Gandharvas.

sanskrit: कार्य सिद्धिम् पुरस् क्Rत्य मन्त्रयध्वम् विनिर्णये
नित्यम् सम्निहितो ह्य् अत्र रावणो राक्षस अधिपः
transliteration: kārya siddhim puras ktya mantrayadhvam vinirṇaye
nityam samnihito hy atra rāvaṇo rākṣasa adhipaḥ
english: Let us, keeping before us success in the enterprise, consult together for the purpose of arriving at a decision.

sanskrit: तथा तेषु ब्रुवाणेषु रावण अवरजो अब्रवीत्
वाक्यम् अग्राम्य पदवत् पुष्कल अर्थम् विभीषणः
transliteration: tathā teṣu bruvāṇeṣu rāvaṇa avarajo abravīt
vākyam agrāmya padavat puṣkala artham vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: We are here daily nearing Răvaņa, lord of Raksasas. As they were speaking thus, Ravana's younger brother, Vibhīşaņa, said in a pregnant speech free from provinicialism.

sanskrit: अनलः शरभसः चैव सम्पातिः प्रघसस् तथा
गत्वा लन्काम् मम अमात्याः पुरीम् पुनर् इह आगताः
transliteration: analaḥ śarabhasaḥ caiva sampātiḥ praghasas tathā
gatvā lankām mama amātyāḥ purīm punar iha āgatāḥ
english: Anala, Panasa, Sampāti and Pramāti— all courtiers of mine-having gone up to Lanka, have come back here.

sanskrit: भूत्वा शकुनयः सर्वे प्रविष्टासः च रिपोर् बलम्
विधानम् विहितम् यच् च तद् द्Rष्ट्वा समुपस्थिताः
transliteration: bhūtvā śakunayaḥ sarve praviṣṭāsaḥ ca ripor balam
vidhānam vihitam yac ca tad dṣṭvā samupasthitāḥ
english: Wearing the forms of birds, they entered into the hostile forces; and, having seen the measures that had been adopted (by them, have come (back).

sanskrit: सम्विधानम् यथा आहुस् ते रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
राम तद् ब्रुवतः सर्वम् यथातथ्येन मे शृणु
transliteration: samvidhānam yathā āhus te rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
rāma tad bruvataḥ sarvam yathātathyena me śṛṇu
english: O Rāma, hearken to me as I tell you truly anent the provisions which they have related, made by the wicked-minded Ravana.

sanskrit: पूर्वम् प्रहस्तः सबलो द्वारम् आसाद्य तिष्ठति
दक्षिणम् च महा वीर्यौ महा पार्श्व महा उदरौ
transliteration: pūrvam prahastaḥ sabalo dvāram āsādya tiṣṭhati
dakṣiṇam ca mahā vīryau mahā pārśva mahā udarau

sanskrit: इन्द्रजित् पश्चिम द्वारम् राक्षसैर् बहुभिर् वृतः
पट्टस असि धनुष्मद्भिः शूल मुद्गर पाणिभिः
transliteration: indrajit paścima dvāram rākṣasair bahubhir vṛtaḥ
paṭṭasa asi dhanuṣmadbhiḥ śūla mudgara pāṇibhiḥ
english: In the Eastern gate stay Prahasta along with his forces; in the Southern, the exceedingly powerful Mahāpārsva and Mahodara, and in the Western. Ravana's son, Indrajit, supported by innumerable Räkşasas, equipped with pattiśas, swords and bows, and bearing darts and maces in their hands, surrounded by heroes carrying various weapons.

sanskrit: नाना प्रहरणैः शूरैर् आवृतो रावण आत्मजः
राक्षसानाम् सहस्रैस् तु बहुभिः शस्त्र पाणिभिः
transliteration: nānā praharaṇaiḥ śūrair āvṛto rāvaṇa ātmajaḥ
rākṣasānām sahasrais tu bahubhiḥ śastra pāṇibhiḥ

sanskrit: युक्तः परम सम्विग्नो राक्षसैर् बहुभिर् व्Rतः
उत्तरम् नगर द्वारम् रावणः स्वयम् आस्थितः
transliteration: yuktaḥ parama samvigno rākṣasair bahubhir vtaḥ
uttaram nagara dvāram rāvaṇaḥ svayam āsthitaḥ
english: And, backed by many thousands of Räkşasas wielding weapons, and accompanied by Rākşasas conversant with counsel, Rāvana himself, his heart agitated to the height, gaurd the Northern gate of the city.

sanskrit: विरूप अक्षस् तु महता शूल खड्ग धनुष्मता
बलेन राक्षसैः सार्धम् मध्यमम् गुल्मम् आस्थितः
transliteration: virūpa akṣas tu mahatā śūla khaḍga dhanuṣmatā
balena rākṣasaiḥ sārdham madhyamam gulmam āsthitaḥ
english: Virüpākṣa with a powerful force accoutred in javelins, clubs and bows, protects the garrison in the centre.

sanskrit: एतान् एवम् विधान् गुल्माम्ल् लन्कायाम् समुदीक्ष्य ते
मामकाः सचिवाः सर्वे शीघ्रम् पुनर् इह आगताः
transliteration: etān evam vidhān gulmāml lankāyām samudīkṣya te
māmakāḥ sacivāḥ sarve śīghram punar iha āgatāḥ
english: Having seen these hosts thus disposed in Lankä, my counsellors have speedily come back here.

sanskrit: गजानाम् च सहस्रम् च रथानाम् अयुतम् पुरे
हयानाम् अयुते द्वे च साग्र कोटी च रक्षसाम्
transliteration: gajānām ca sahasram ca rathānām ayutam pure
hayānām ayute dve ca sāgra koṭī ca rakṣasām
english: There are ten thousand elephants, an Ayuta cars, two of horses, and abouta koti of Raksasas, powerful and strong, and equipped with arms in conflict.* *These are, remarks the commentator, the leader.

sanskrit: इष्टा राक्षस राजस्य नित्यम् एते निशा चराः
transliteration: iṣṭā rākṣasa rājasya nityam ete niśā carāḥ
english: These night-rangers are ever the favourites of the Raksasa ruler. And, O kine, a koti of forces accompany each of these Rākşasas in battle.

sanskrit: एक एकस्य अत्र युद्ध अर्थे राक्षसस्य विशाम् पते
transliteration: eka ekasya atra yuddha arthe rākṣasasya viśām pate
english: These night-rangers are ever the favourites of the Raksasa ruler. And, O kine, a koti of forces accompany each of these Rākşasas in battle.

sanskrit: एताम् प्रवृत्तिम् लन्कायाम् मन्त्रि प्रोक्तम् विभीषणः
रामम् कमल पत्र अक्षम् इदम् उत्तरम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: etām pravṛttim lankāyām mantri proktam vibhīṣaṇaḥ
rāmam kamala patra akṣam idam uttaram abravīt

sanskrit: कुबेरम् तु यदा राम रावणः प्रत्ययुध्यत
transliteration: kuberam tu yadā rāma rāvaṇaḥ pratyayudhyata

sanskrit: षष्टिः शत सहस्राणि तदा निर्यान्ति राक्षसाः
transliteration: ṣaṣṭiḥ śata sahasrāṇi tadā niryānti rākṣasāḥ
english: O Răma, when Rāvana battled with Kuvera, sixty lacs of Raksasas marched forth (to meet him). In prowess, energy, vigour, exceeding fortitude, and hauteur, they resembled the wicked-minded Ravana himself.

sanskrit: सदृशा यो अत्र दर्पेण रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
अत्र मन्युर् न कर्तव्यो रोषये त्वाम् न भीषये
transliteration: sadṛśā yo atra darpeṇa rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
atra manyur na kartavyo roṣaye tvām na bhīṣaye

sanskrit: समर्थो ह्य् असि वीर्येण सुराणाम् अपि निग्रहे
तद् भवाम्सः चतुर् अन्गेण बलेन महता वृतः
transliteration: samartho hy asi vīryeṇa surāṇām api nigrahe
tad bhavāmsaḥ catur angeṇa balena mahatā vṛtaḥ

sanskrit: व्यूह्य इदम् वानर अनीकम् निर्मथिष्यसि रावणम्
रावण अवरजे वाक्यम् एवम् ब्रुवति राघवः
transliteration: vyūhya idam vānara anīkam nirmathiṣyasi rāvaṇam
rāvaṇa avaraje vākyam evam bruvati rāghavaḥ

sanskrit: शत्रूणाम् प्रतिघात अर्थम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
पूर्व द्वारे तु लन्काया नीलो वानर पुम्गवः
transliteration: śatrūṇām pratighāta artham idam vacanam abravīt
pūrva dvāre tu lankāyā nīlo vānara pumgavaḥ

sanskrit: प्रहस्तम् प्रतियोद्धा स्याद् वानरैर् बहुभिर् वृतः
अन्गदो वालि पुत्रस् तु बलेन महता वृतः
transliteration: prahastam pratiyoddhā syād vānarair bahubhir vṛtaḥ
angado vāli putras tu balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
english: Let that foremost of monkey, Nila, surrounded to by an immense number of monkeys, cope with Prahasta at the Eastern gate of Lankā.

sanskrit: दक्षिणे बाधताम् द्वारे महा पार्श्व महा उदरौ
हनूमान् पश्चिम द्वारम् निपीड्य पवन आत्मजः
transliteration: dakṣiṇe bādhatām dvāre mahā pārśva mahā udarau
hanūmān paścima dvāram nipīḍya pavana ātmajaḥ

sanskrit: प्रविशत्व् अप्रमेय आत्मा बहुभिः कपिभिर् वृतः
दैत्य दानव सम्घानाम् ऋषीणाम् च महात्मनाम्
transliteration: praviśatv aprameya ātmā bahubhiḥ kapibhir vṛtaḥ
daitya dānava samghānām ṛṣīṇām ca mahātmanām

sanskrit: विप्रकार प्रियः क्षुद्रो वर दान बल अन्वितः
परिक्रामति यः सर्वाम्ल् लोकान् सम्तापयन् प्रजाः
transliteration: viprakāra priyaḥ kṣudro vara dāna bala anvitaḥ
parikrāmati yaḥ sarvāml lokān samtāpayan prajāḥ

sanskrit: तस्य अहम् राक्षस इन्द्रस्य स्वयम् एव वधे धृतः
उत्तरम् नगर द्वारम् अहम् सौमित्रिणा सह
transliteration: tasya aham rākṣasa indrasya svayam eva vadhe dhṛtaḥ
uttaram nagara dvāram aham saumitriṇā saha

sanskrit: वानर इन्द्रसः च बलवान् ऋक्ष राजसः च जाम्बवान्
transliteration: vānara indrasaḥ ca balavān ṛkṣa rājasaḥ ca jāmbavān

sanskrit: राक्षस इन्द्र अनुजसः चैव गुल्मे भवतु मध्यमे
न च एव मानुषम् रूपम् कार्यम् हरिभिर् आहवे
transliteration: rākṣasa indra anujasaḥ caiva gulme bhavatu madhyame
na ca eva mānuṣam rūpam kāryam haribhir āhave

sanskrit: एषा भवतु नः सम्ज्ना युद्धे अस्मिन् वानरे बले
वानरा;एव निश्चिह्नम् स्व जने अस्मिन् भविष्यति
transliteration: eṣā bhavatu naḥ samjnā yuddhe asmin vānare bale
vānarā;eva niścihnam sva jane asmin bhaviṣyati
english: In this battle, the monkeys need not assume the forms of human being. And let this serve for a sign that the monkeys, in order to the recognition of our own forces, appear with their proper monkey-marks. We seven only shall battle with the foe in human shapes, viz.

sanskrit: वयम् तु मानुषेण एव सप्त योत्स्यामहे परान्
अहम् एव सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन महा ओजसा
transliteration: vayam tu mānuṣeṇa eva sapta yotsyāmahe parān
aham eva saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena mahā ojasā

sanskrit: आत्मना पन्चमसः च अयम् सखा मम विभीषणः
स रामः कार्य सिद्ध्य् अर्थम् एवम् उक्त्वा विभीषणम्
transliteration: ātmanā pancamasaḥ ca ayam sakhā mama vibhīṣaṇaḥ
sa rāmaḥ kārya siddhy artham evam uktvā vibhīṣaṇam

sanskrit: सुवेल आरोहणे बुद्धिम् चकार मतिमान् मतिम्
transliteration: suvela ārohaṇe buddhim cakāra matimān matim
english: Having said this to Vibhísaņa for attaining success in the enterprise, that lord, the intelligent Rāma, seeing the sides of Suvela more beautiful (than other places), intended to ascend it.

sanskrit: कृत्वा मतिम् सो अरि वधे महात्मा
transliteration: kṛtvā matim so ari vadhe mahātmā
english: Then, environed by a mighty host, the highsouled and magnanimous Rāma, his features mirroring forth high exultation, overshadowing the entire Earth (with his forces), set out for Lankā, determined upon destroying the enemy.

sanskrit: स तु कृत्वा सुवेलस्य मतिम् आरोहणम् प्रति
लक्ष्मण अनुगतो रामह् सुग्रीवम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
transliteration: sa tu kṛtvā suvelasya matim ārohaṇam prati
lakṣmaṇa anugato rāmah sugrīvam idam abravīt
english: Having been bent upon mounting Suvela, Rāma, followed by Lakşmaņa, addressed in sweet and excellent words, Sugriva, and that righteous night-ranger, Vibhisana, versed in। counsel and conversant with precepts, who was devoted to him, saying.

sanskrit: विभीषणम् च धर्मज्नम् अनुरक्तम् निज़ा चरम्
मन्त्रज्नम् च विधिज्नम् च ज़्लक्ष्णया परया गिरा
transliteration: vibhīṣaṇam ca dharmajnam anuraktam nijā caram
mantrajnam ca vidhijnam ca jlakṣṇayā parayā girā
english: Having been bent upon mounting Suvela, Rāma, followed by Lakşmaņa, addressed in sweet and excellent words, Sugriva, and that righteous night-ranger, Vibhisana, versed in। counsel and conversant with precepts, who was devoted to him, saying.

sanskrit: सुवेलम् साधु ज़ैल इन्द्रम् इमम् धातु ज़तैज़् चितम्
अध्यारोहामहे सर्वे वत्स्यामो अत्र निज़ाम् इमाम्
transliteration: suvelam sādhu jaila indram imam dhātu jataij citam
adhyārohāmahe sarve vatsyāmo atra nijām imām
english: We shall all ascend this mount Suvela, be dight with metals; and pass this night even here.

sanskrit: लन्काम् च आलोकयिष्यामो निलयम् तस्य रक्षसह्
येन मे मरण अन्ताय हृता भार्या दुरात्मना
transliteration: lankām ca ālokayiṣyāmo nilayam tasya rakṣasah
yena me maraṇa antāya hṛtā bhāryā durātmanā

sanskrit: येन धर्मो न विज्नातो न वृत्तम् न कुलम् तथा
राक्षस्या नीचया बुद्ध्या येन तद् गर्हितम् कृतम्
transliteration: yena dharmo na vijnāto na vṛttam na kulam tathā
rākṣasyā nīcayā buddhyā yena tad garhitam kṛtam

sanskrit: यस्मिन् मे वर्धते रोषह् कीर्तिते राक्षस अधमे
यस्य अपराधान् नीचस्य वधम् द्रक्ष्यामि रक्षसाम्
transliteration: yasmin me vardhate roṣah kīrtite rākṣasa adhame
yasya aparādhān nīcasya vadham drakṣyāmi rakṣasām

sanskrit: एको हि कुरुते पापम् काल पाज़ वज़म् गतः
नीचेन आत्म अपचारेण कुलम् तेन विनज़्यति
transliteration: eko hi kurute pāpam kāla pāja vajam gataḥ
nīcena ātma apacāreṇa kulam tena vinajyati

sanskrit: एवम् सम्मन्त्रयन्न् एव सक्रोधो रावणम् प्रति
रामह् सुवेलम् वासाय चित्र सानुम् उपारुहत्
transliteration: evam sammantrayann eva sakrodho rāvaṇam prati
rāmah suvelam vāsāya citra sānum upāruhat
english: Having decided thus, Rāma, filled with wrath at Ravana, coming to Suvela, ascended its variegated plateau.

sanskrit: पृष्ठतो लक्ष्मण च एनम् अन्वगच्चत् समाहितः
सज़रम् चापम् उद्यम्य सुमहद् विक्रमे रतः
transliteration: pṛṣṭhato lakṣmaṇa ca enam anvagaccat samāhitaḥ
sajaram cāpam udyamya sumahad vikrame rataḥ
english: And Laksmana, collected, went in his wake. And, upraising bow and arrow, Sugriva, (ever) engaged in valorous acts, accompanied with Vibhişaņa as well as his counsellors, following him, also ascended (the mountain).

sanskrit: हनूमान् अन्गदो नीलो मैन्दो द्विविद;एव च
transliteration: hanūmān angado nīlo maindo dvivida;eva ca

sanskrit: गजो गव अक्षो गवयह् ज़रभो गन्ध मादनह्
पनसह् कुमुदज़् चैव हरो रम्भज़् च यूथपह्
transliteration: gajo gava akṣo gavayah jarabho gandha mādanah
panasah kumudaj caiva haro rambhaj ca yūthapah

sanskrit: एते च अन्ये च बहवो वानराह् ज़ीघ्र गामिनह्
ते वायु वेग प्रवणास् तम् गिरिम् गिरि चारिणह्
transliteration: ete ca anye ca bahavo vānarāh jīghra gāminah
te vāyu vega pravaṇās tam girim giri cāriṇah

sanskrit: ते त्व् अदीर्घेण कालेन गिरिम् आरुह्य सर्वतह्
transliteration: te tv adīrgheṇa kālena girim āruhya sarvatah
english: And all those rangers of mountains, gifted with the vehemence of the Wind in hundreds ascended mount Suvela, where Rāghava was stationed.

sanskrit: ददृज़ुह् ज़िखरे तस्य विषक्ताम् इव खे पुरीम्
ताम् ज़ुभाम् प्रवत द्वाराम् प्राकार वर ज़ोभिताम्
transliteration: dadṛjuh jikhare tasya viṣaktām iva khe purīm
tām jubhām pravata dvārām prākāra vara jobhitām
english: Ascending the mountain in a short time, they all beheld from its summit the city, appearing to be built on the air. And the monkey-leaders beheld Lankā, exceedingly splendid with noble gateways; gracefully enclosed with a wall; thronging with Rakşasas; and defended by sable Raksasas.

sanskrit: लन्काम् राक्षस सम्पूर्णाम् ददृज़ुर् हरि यूथपाह्
प्राकार चय संस्थैज़् च तथा नीलैर् निज़ा चरैह्
transliteration: lankām rākṣasa sampūrṇām dadṛjur hari yūthapāh
prākāra caya saṃsthaij ca tathā nīlair nijā caraih

sanskrit: ददृज़ुस् ते हरि ज़्रेष्ठाह् प्राकारम् अपरम् कृतम्
ते दृष्ट्वा वानराह् सर्वे राक्षसान् युद्ध कान्क्षिणह्
transliteration: dadṛjus te hari jreṣṭhāh prākāram aparam kṛtam
te dṛṣṭvā vānarāh sarve rākṣasān yuddha kānkṣiṇah

sanskrit: मुमुचुर् विपुलान् नादांस् तत्र रामस्य पज़्यतह्
ततो अस्तम् अगमत् सूर्यह् संध्यया प्रतिरन्जितह्
transliteration: mumucur vipulān nādāṃs tatra rāmasya pajyatah
tato astam agamat sūryah saṃdhyayā pratiranjitah

sanskrit: पूर्ण चन्द्र प्रदीपा च क्षपा समभिवर्तते
ततः स रामो हरि वाहिनी पतिर्
transliteration: pūrṇa candra pradīpā ca kṣapā samabhivartate
tataḥ sa rāmo hari vāhinī patir
english: Then the master of the monkey-army, Rāma, saluted and honoured by Vibhisana, accompanied by Lakşmaņa as well as the leaders of the monkeys, sojourned happily on the beast of Suvela.

sanskrit: ताम् रात्रिम् उषितास् तत्र सुवेले हरि पुम्गवाः
लन्कायाम् ददृशुर् वीरा वनान्य् उपवनानि च
transliteration: tām rātrim uṣitās tatra suvele hari pumgavāḥ
lankāyām dadṛśur vīrā vanāny upavanāni ca
english: Having passed the night in Suvela, the heroic monkey-leaders surveyed woods and forests in Lankā.

sanskrit: सम सौम्यानि रम्याणि विशालान्य् आयतानि च
दृष्टि रम्याणि ते दृष्ट्वा बभूवुर् जात विस्मयाः
transliteration: sama saumyāni ramyāṇi viśālāny āyatāni ca
dṛṣṭi ramyāṇi te dṛṣṭvā babhūvur jāta vismayāḥ
english: Seeing those extensive (woods and forests), mild, and charming, and beautiful to behold, they were seized with wonderment.

sanskrit: चम्पक अशोक पुम्नाग साल ताल समाकुला
तमाल वन संचन्ना नाग माला समावृता
transliteration: campaka aśoka pumnāga sāla tāla samākulā
tamāla vana saṃcannā nāga mālā samāvṛtā

sanskrit: हिन्तालैर् अर्जुनैर् नीपैः सप्त पर्णैश् च पुष्पितैः
तिलकैः कर्णिकारैश् च पटालैश् च समन्ततः
transliteration: hintālair arjunair nīpaiḥ sapta parṇaiś ca puṣpitaiḥ
tilakaiḥ karṇikāraiś ca paṭālaiś ca samantataḥ

sanskrit: शुशुभे पुष्पित अग्रैश् च लता परिगतैर् द्रुमैः
लन्का बहु विधैर् दिव्यैर् यथा इन्द्रस्य अमरावती
transliteration: śuśubhe puṣpita agraiś ca latā parigatair drumaiḥ
lankā bahu vidhair divyair yathā indrasya amarāvatī

शाद्वलैश् च तथा नीलैश् चित्राभिर् वन राजिभिः
transliteration: vicitra kusuma upetai rakta komala pallavaiḥ
śādvalaiś ca tathā nīlaiś citrābhir vana rājibhiḥ
english: And trees there, furnished with variegated flowers having tender rosy leaves, and blue lawns, and rows of woods; and bearing odorous and charming blossoms and fruits, looked like men adorned with ornaments.

धारयन्त्य् अगमास् तत्र भूषणानि इव मानवाः
transliteration: gandha āḍhyāny abhiramyāṇi puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca

english: And trees there, furnished with variegated flowers having tender rosy leaves, and blue lawns, and rows of woods; and bearing odorous and charming blossoms and fruits, looked like men adorned with ornaments.

sanskrit: तच् चैत्र रथ सम्काशम् मनोज्नम् नन्दन उपमम्
वनम् सर्व ऋतुकम् रम्यम् शुशुभे षट्पद आयुतम्

vanam sarva ṛtukam ramyam śuśubhe ṣaṭpada āyutam
english: There a delightful and pleasant wood resembling Caitraratha, and like to Nandana itself, having all the seasons present, appeared beauteous to the view, with black bees all around.

sanskrit: नत्यूह कोयष्टि भकैर् नृत्यमानैश् च बर्हिभिः
रुतम् पर भृतानाम् च शुश्रुवे वन निर्झरे
transliteration: natyūha koyaṣṭi bhakair nṛtyamānaiś ca barhibhiḥ

english: And it had Dātyühas, and Koyașthivas, and peacocks dancing; and the strains of the coels were heard at the woodland rills.

कोकिल आकुल षण्डानि विहग अभिरुतानि च

english: The heroic and exhilarated monkeys, capable of wearing forms at pleasure, entered those woods and groves frequented by maddened birds and ranged by Bhramaras, tracts overflowing with the lays of coels, and ringing with the voices of songsters, resonant with the notes of Bhramaras, sovereigns of their species and eloquent with the cries of ospreys.

sanskrit: भृन्ग राज अभिगीतानि भ्रमरैः सेवितानि च
transliteration: bhṛnga rāja abhigītāni bhramaraiḥ sevitāni ca

transliteration: teṣām praviśatām tatra vānarāṇām mahā ojasām
puṣpa saṃsarga surabhir vavau ghrāṇa sukho anilaḥ

sanskrit: अन्ये तु हरि वीराणाम् यूथान् निष्क्रम्य यूथपाः
transliteration: anye tu hari vīrāṇām yūthān niṣkramya yūthapāḥ
english: As the exceedingly energetic monkeys entered, there blew upon them the breeze-like to life-redolent of perfume obtained from contact with the blossoms. And others of the leaders among the heroic monkeys, coming out from the bands, ordered by Sugriva, made in the direction of Lankā crowned with ensigns.

sanskrit: कम्पयन्तश् च ताम् लन्काम् नादैः स्वैर् नदताम् वराः
transliteration: kampayantaś ca tām lankām nādaiḥ svair nadatām varāḥ
english: And, terrifying the fowls and dispiriting beasts and birds and shaking Lankā with their roars, those foremost monkeys set up shouts.

sanskrit: कुर्वन्तस् ते महा वेगा महीम् चारण पीडिताम्
अजश् च सहसा एव ऊर्ध्वम् जगाम चरण उद्धतम्
transliteration: kurvantas te mahā vegā mahīm cāraṇa pīḍitām
ajaś ca sahasā eva ūrdhvam jagāma caraṇa uddhatam
english: They, endowed with great impetuosity, went on, oppressing the earth with their battle-array; and clouds of dust suddenly arose from the march of the soldiery.

sanskrit: ऋक्षाः सिम्हा वराहाश् च महिषा वारणा मृगाः
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ता जग्मुर् भीता दिशो दश
transliteration: ṛkṣāḥ simhā varāhāś ca mahiṣā vāraṇā mṛgāḥ
tena śabdena vitrastā jagmur bhītā diśo daśa
english: And bears, and lions, and buffaloes, and elephants, and deer, and birds, overwhelmed with affright, made for the t en cardinal points.

sanskrit: शिखरम् तु त्रिकूटस्य प्रांशु च एकम् दिवि स्पृशम्
समन्तात् पुष्प संचन्नम् महा रजत सम्निभम्
transliteration: śikharam tu trikūṭasya prāṃśu ca ekam divi spṛśam
samantāt puṣpa saṃcannam mahā rajata samnibham

transliteration: śata yojana vistīrṇam vimalam cāru darśanam
ślakṣṇam śrīman mahac caiva duṣprāpam śakunair api

निविष्टा तत्र शिखरे लन्का रावण पालिता
transliteration: manasā api durāroham kim punaḥ karmaṇā janaiḥ
niviṣṭā tatra śikhare lankā rāvaṇa pālitā

transliteration: sā purī gopurair uccaiḥ pāṇḍura ambuda samnibhaiḥ

transliteration: prāsādaiś ca vimānaiś ca lankā parama bhūṣitā
ghanair iva ātapa apāye madhyamam vaiṣṇavam padam

transliteration: kailāsa śikhara ākāro dṛśyate kham iva ullikhan
english: That palace, which was adorned with thousands of pillars, and which, as if piercing the heavens, looked like a peak of Kailasa—was the residence of the Sovereign of the Rākşasas—the ornament of the city, (ever guarded by full hundreds of Raksasas.

sanskrit: चैत्यः स राक्षस इन्द्रस्य बभूव पुर भूषणम्
शतेन रक्षसाम् नित्यम् यः समग्रेण रक्ष्यते
transliteration: caityaḥ sa rākṣasa indrasya babhūva pura bhūṣaṇam
śatena rakṣasām nityam yaḥ samagreṇa rakṣyate
english: That palace, which was adorned with thousands of pillars, and which, as if piercing the heavens, looked like a peak of Kailasa—was the residence of the Sovereign of the Rākşasas—the ornament of the city, (ever guarded by full hundreds of Raksasas.

sanskrit: ताम् समृद्धाम् समृद्ध अर्थो लक्ष्मीवाम्ल् लक्ष्मण अग्रजः
रावणस्य पुरीम् रामो ददर्श सह वानरैः
transliteration: tām samṛddhām samṛddha artho lakṣmīvāml lakṣmaṇa agrajaḥ
rāvaṇasya purīm rāmo dadarśa saha vānaraiḥ

english: Rāma, surrounded by his mighty forces, saw that palace, filled with diverse kinds of gems, adorned with rows of edifices, and having huge engines and gateways.
Then Rāma, accompanied by the monkeyleaders, along with Sugrīva, ascended the top of Suvela, measuring a circumference of two Yojanas.

sanskrit: स्थित्वा मुहूर्तं तत्रैव दिशो दश विलोकयन्
transliteration: sthitvā muhūrtaṃ tatraiva diśo daśa vilokayan

english: On seeing the Raksasa-chief, Sugriva suddenly rose up in the sight of the lords of monkeys as well as Rāghava.

sanskrit: क्रोधवेगेन सं युक्तः सत्त्वेन च बलेन च
transliteration: krodhavegena saṃ yuktaḥ sattvena ca balena ca
english: And influenced by wrath, he, mustering strength and vigour, rising from the brow of the mountain, bounded to the gateway.
And pausing for a while and eyeing the Rāks asa intrepidly, he, slighting the Raksasa, addressed him in harsh speech, saying.

sanskrit: न मया मोक्यसे.द्य त्वं पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य तेजसा
transliteration: na mayā mokyase.dya tvaṃ pārthivendrasya tejasā
english: O Rākşasa, I am the friend as well as the slave of Rāma-lord of men. Me, backed by the energy of that king of the Earth, shall you not escape today.
Saying this, he, suddenly springing up, descended on him; and snatching away his variegated crown, let it fa}l on the earth.
Seeing his come abruptly, the night-ranger spoke to him thus, Thus that were Sugrīva beyond my ken, shall be neckless near me.
Having said this, be rose up swiftly and dragged him down to the earth. Thereat springing like pith, the monkey pushed down his antagonist with his arms.

Each having his body bathed in sweat and his person covered with blood each choking and annulling the efforts of the other, and resembling a Sālmali or a Kinsuka, and dealing blows and slaps, and hitting with his arms and hands, those exceedingly strong ones, the lord of the Rākşasas and that of the monkeys, fought wonderfully.

Each having his body bathed in sweat and his person covered with blood each choking and annulling the efforts of the other, and resembling a Sālmali or a Kinsuka, and dealing blows and slaps, and hitting with his arms and hands, those exceedingly strong ones, the lord of the Rākşasas and that of the monkeys, fought wonderfully.

And having for a long time encountered each other in combat on the dais belonging to the gate, they, now lifting up their persons and now lowering them, went down, each felling the other with his legs.
Smiting each other, they, their bodies fastened together, went down between the wall and the moat, and again stood upon the ground.

Having breath, they, resting for a space, grappled with each other; and they fast bound each other with their arms serving for ropes. And each fired with wrath, and each having both strength and skill, they now bore themselves in the lists like a tiger and a lion, furnished with teeth; or like the young of the foremost elephants engaged in encounter, and restraining and pushing each other with their arms, they simultaneously both came down to the ground, Then starting again to their feet, they, vituperating each other, ranged the lists, displaying feats expressive of skill and strength. Nor did those heroes speedily come by fatigue.
And resembling mighty elephants, they, resisting each other by means of their powerful arms like to the trunks of elephants, fought for a long while, swiftly wheeling about the arena.
Approaching each other, they strove to slay each other, like to two cats seated, momentarily encountering each other over some food.

The lord of monkeys and Ravana, accomplished in fight, coursed the arena, displaying wonderful Mandalas, various sthānas, (a) curious gomutrakas, (b) gatapratyagatas, tirascinagatas, Vakragatas, parimoksas, varjanas, paridhāvanas, abhidravaņas, (c) aplavanas (d) savigrahāvasthānas, (e) paravrttas, (1) apavrttas, (g) apadrutas, (h) avaplutas, (i) apanyastas, (j) and upanyastas (k).

In the meanwhile the Rākşasa attempted to put forth his power of illusion. Knowing this, the king of monkeys shot into the sky. And Rāvana, overpowered by fatigue and out of breath, thus baffled by the monkey-king, stood where he was.

In the meanwhile the Rākşasa attempted to put forth his power of illusion. Knowing this, the king of monkeys shot into the sky. And Rāvana, overpowered by fatigue and out of breath, thus baffled by the monkey-king, stood where he was.

Thus the master of the foremost monkeys, securing fame in fight, beat the night-ranger, causing him to experience fatigue. And bounding beyond the spacious sky, the offspring of the Sun came to the side of Rāma in the midst of the monkey-forces.

Having done that deed, the son of the Sun, lord of monkeys-with his heart surcharged with rejoicing, entered that host having the speed of the wind; enhancing the martial ardour of the son of the foremost of the Raghus, and honoured by the monkeys.
Seeing those ominous signs, Lakşmaņa's elder brother, Ramā, embracing Sugrīva, said.

sanskrit: असम्मन्त्र्य मया सार्द्धं तदिदं साहसं कृतम्
transliteration: asammantrya mayā sārddhaṃ tadidaṃ sāhasaṃ kṛtam
english: Without consulting with me, you have acted thus rashly. But kings should not act in such a rash way.

sanskrit: संशये स्थाप्य मां चेदं बलं च सविभीषणम्
transliteration: saṃśaye sthāpya māṃ cedaṃ balaṃ ca savibhīṣaṇam
english: Placing in suspense, me, this army and Vibhīş aņa, you, O hero, enamoured of daring deeds, have put yourself to all this trouble.

sanskrit: त्वयि किञ्चित् समापन्ने किं कार्यं सीतया मम
transliteration: tvayi kiñcit samāpanne kiṃ kāryaṃ sītayā mama
english: But, O hero, henceforth, do not act so. O subduer of enemies, if you come by any mischance, what shall Sita avail me; or Bharata; my younger brother-Lakşmaņa; or Satrughna, O slayer of enemies; or, again, my own person?

sanskrit: शत्रुघ्नेन च शत्रुघ्न स्वशरीरेण वा पुनः
transliteration: śatrughnena ca śatrughna svaśarīreṇa vā punaḥ
english: But, O hero, henceforth, do not act so. O subduer of enemies, if you come by any mischance, what shall Sita avail me; or Bharata; my younger brother-Lakşmaņa; or Satrughna, O slayer of enemies; or, again, my own person?

sanskrit: त्वयि चानागते पूर्वमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः
transliteration: tvayi cānāgate pūrvamiti me niścitā matiḥ
english: Ere you had come, I had arrived at this determination; albeit, O you that are equal to the mighty Indra or Varuna, I knew your prowess full well. Slaying Rāvana in battle along with his sons, forces and vehicles, and installing Vibhīşaņa in Lankā, and placing the kingdom in the hands of Bharata, I shall renounce my body, O exceedingly powerful one!

Ere you had come, I had arrived at this determination; albeit, O you that are equal to the mighty Indra or Varuna, I knew your prowess full well. Slaying Rāvana in battle along with his sons, forces and vehicles, and installing Vibhīşaņa in Lankā, and placing the kingdom in the hands of Bharata, I shall renounce my body, O exceedingly powerful one!
When Rāma had said this, Sugrīva answered, Knowing my own strength, how, O Rāghava, viewing Rāvana, who had ravished away your wife, could I forbear, O hero?
When Rāma had said this, Sugrīva answered, Knowing my own strength, how, O Rāghava, viewing Rāvana, who had ravished away your wife, could I forbear, O hero?
As that hero was speaking thus Raghava addressed Lakṣmaṇa having auspiciousness, thus.
O Lakşmaņa, occupying some tract furnished with cool water and woods bearing fruits, we shall sojourn, dividing and marshalling our forces.
I see a mighty fear present, destructive of people, and boding destruction to the foremost heroes among the bears, monkeys and Rākşasas.

sanskrit: वाताश्च परुषा वान्ति कम्पते च वसुन्धरा
transliteration: vātāśca paruṣā vānti kampate ca vasundharā
english: The winds ruffle; and the earth is tremulous. And the tops of mountains tremble, and the mountains themselves send up loud sounds.
The clouds are goblinish; and fierce; and harsh-sounding. And wearing terrific looks, they fiercely pour down showers mixed with drops of blood.
The Evening resembles the red sandal, and is fearful. And a flaming circle dropped from the Sun.
And exciting great fear, inauspicious birds and beasts, wearing cruel looks, and in distressful guise, cry in piteous accents, facing the Sun.
At night, the ominous Moon with a black-red brim as at the time of universal wreck, burn.
O Laksmana, there is a crimson, rough, slight, and graceful rim round the Sun; and a blue mark is visible on his disc.
The stars do not course as formerly. Behold, O Laksmana, all these, prefiguring the Doom.

sanskrit: काकाः श्येनास्तथा गृध्रा नीचैः परिपतन्ति च
transliteration: kākāḥ śyenāstathā gṛdhrā nīcaiḥ paripatanti ca
english: And crows and hawks and vultures drop down. And jackals yell loud inauspicious notes.
This very day with all expedition shall we surrounded on all sides by the monkeys, march towards the city governed by Rāvaņa.
Having said this to Laksmana, Laksmana's elder brother possessed of exceeding strength, hastily descended from the top of the mountain.

sanskrit: अवतीर्यं च धर्मात्मा तस्माच्छैलात् स राघवः
transliteration: avatīryaṃ ca dharmātmā tasmācchailāt sa rāghavaḥ
english: And descending from the mountain, the righteous Rāghava surveyed his troops, incapable of being beaten by enemies.
After making the mighty host of the monkeysking equip itself, Raghava versed in season, along with Sugrīva, at the proper hour, issued orders for battle.
Then in due time that one, accoutred with his bow, surrounded by a mighty army, set out, with the intention of entering the city of Lanka.
Those two-Vibhisana and Sugriva-~-and Hanumān, and jāmbavăn, and Nala, and the bear-king Nila, and Laksmana, followed (Rama).
Behind them, the mighty array of bears and monkeys followed Rāghava, severing a wide surface of land.
The monkeys, resembling elephants, capable of resisting foes, took mountain-peaks and tall trees by hundreds.

sanskrit: तौ तु दीर्घेण कालेन भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: tau tu dīrgheṇa kālena bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: In a short time those repressors of foes— two brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa-arrived at the city of Răvaņa; with pennons streaming over her; charming; garnished with groves and woods, having variegated gateways; inaccessible; and having walls and gates.

In a short time those repressors of foes— two brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa-arrived at the city of Răvaņa; with pennons streaming over her; charming; garnished with groves and woods, having variegated gateways; inaccessible; and having walls and gates.
And urged on by Rāma's command, the wood-raingers,* as commanded, blocking up (Lankā) incapable of being subdued even by the gods, stationed themselves. *Monkeys.

sanskrit: रामः सहानुजो धन्वी जुगोप च रुरोध च
transliteration: rāmaḥ sahānujo dhanvī jugopa ca rurodha ca

sanskrit: विन्यस्तानि च योधानां बहूनि विविधानि च
transliteration: vinyastāni ca yodhānāṃ bahūni vividhāni ca

sanskrit: अतिष्ठत् सह मैन्देन द्विविदेन च वीर्यवान्
transliteration: atiṣṭhat saha maindena dvividena ca vīryavān
english: And coming to the Eastern gate, that leader of the monkeys-army, the powerful Nila, along with Mainda and Dvivida, took up his post there.
The exceedingly strong Angada, accompanied by Risabha, Gavaksa, Gaya, and Gavaya, occupied the Southern gate. And the mighty monkey Hanumān protected the Western entrance.

sanskrit: मध्यमे च स्वयं गुल्मे सुग्रीवः समतिष्ठत
transliteration: madhyame ca svayaṃ gulme sugrīvaḥ samatiṣṭhata

english: And accompanied by all the foremost monkeys resembling Suparņa or the Wind, twenty kotis of renowned monkey-leaders, blocking up all sides, stationed themselves near the monkeys, Sugriva.

sanskrit: द्वारे द्वारे हरीणां तु कोटिं कोटिं न्यवेशयत्
transliteration: dvāre dvāre harīṇāṃ tu koṭiṃ koṭiṃ nyaveśayat
english: At Rama's command, Laksmana along with Vibhisana, went from door to door, issuing instructions to kotis of monkeys.
On the west of Rāma, Jāmbavän along with Susena, followed by innumerable troops, remained hard by at the garrison in the minddle.

sanskrit: ते तु वानरशार्दूलाः शार्दूला इव दंष्ट्रिणः
transliteration: te tu vānaraśārdūlāḥ śārdūlā iva daṃṣṭriṇaḥ
english: And those tiger-like monkeys, furnished with teeth like to tigers, wielding trees and mountaintops, stood ready for fight.
All had their tails curled up, and all were armed with teeth and nails, and all had chequered bodies, and all had frightful faces.
Some had the strength of ten elephants; and some had strength ten times as much; and some of the monkeys-leaders there had the strength of a thousand elephants.
Some had the strength of numbers (of elephants); and some had strength hundred times as much. And others had immeasurable might.
And wonderful and astonishing was their meeting. And the concourse at that place of the monkey-forces was like the concourse of locusts.
The air was filled up, and the earth was covered quite with the monkeys coursing towards Lankā and dropping down into it.
And hundreds and thousands making up the army of monkeys, arrived at the gate of Lanka; while others were pouring in from all sides for encounter.

sanskrit: आवृतः स गिरिः सर्वैस्तैः समन्तात् प्लवङ्गमैः
transliteration: āvṛtaḥ sa giriḥ sarvaistaiḥ samantāt plavaṅgamaiḥ
english: That mount was covered with monkeys by all sides and a thousand ayutas were going round the city.
That mount was covered with monkeys by all sides and a thousand ayutas were going round the city.
And Larkā, blocked up everywhere with powerful monkeys bearing trees in their hands, was incapable of being entered even by the Wind.
The Rākşasas, sore pressed by thousands of monkeys resembling masses of clouds, and like to Śakra himself in battle, were seized with amazement.
Like to the roar of water on the ocean being riven, there arose a mighty tumult in consequence of the forces surging hither and thither.
With that sound the entire Lankā, with her wall and gateways, her mountains, woods, and forests, began to shake.
That army, protected by Rāma and Lakşmaņa as well as Sugrīva, became and the more invincible even by the Asuras and celestials.

sanskrit: राघवः सन्निवेश्यैव सैन्यं स्वं रक्षसां वधे
सम्मन्त्र्य मन्त्रिभिः सार्धं निश्चित्य च पुनःपुनः
transliteration: rāghavaḥ sanniveśyaiva sainyaṃ svaṃ rakṣasāṃ vadhe
sammantrya mantribhiḥ sārdhaṃ niścitya ca punaḥpunaḥ
english: Having arraigned his forces with the view of destroying the Räkşasa, Rāghava, versed in the resources of war, taking counsel of the counsellors, and deciding again and again his course of action, intending to adopt further measures, resolved to abide by the advice of Vibhīşaņa, remembering the morality regulating monarchs. And then, calling Vāli's son, Angada, (Rāma) said.

sanskrit: गत्वा सोम्य दशग्रीवं ब्रुहि मद्वचनात् कपे
लङ्घयित्वा पुरीं लङ्कां भयं त्यक्त्वा गतव्यथः
transliteration: gatvā somya daśagrīvaṃ bruhi madvacanāt kape
laṅghayitvā purīṃ laṅkāṃ bhayaṃ tyaktvā gatavyathaḥ
english: O mild one, going to the Ten-necked one, tell him in my words, Bounding over the deep and casting off fear and dejection, I have laid siege to the city of Lankā; and have reft you of your prosperity and your wealth; and rendered you moribund and senseless.

You have, O night-ranger, through delusion and pride injured saints and celestials, and Gandharvas and Apsaras, and Serpents, and Yaksas, and crowned heads. But, O Raksasa, your pride begot of the boon received from the Self-create has gone from you, whose destroyer I, afflicted in consequence of my wife having been carried off, wielding the rod, have sat down at the door of Lankā.

sanskrit: पदवीं देवतानां च महर्षीणां च राक्षस
राजर्षीणां च सर्वेषां गमिष्यसि मया हतः
transliteration: padavīṃ devatānāṃ ca maharṣīṇāṃ ca rākṣasa
rājarṣīṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ gamiṣyasi mayā hataḥ
english: O Rākşasa, you shall, remaining steady in fight, attain the state of celestials and Maharsis and Rājarşis.

sanskrit: बलेन येन वै सीतां मायया राक्षसाधम
transliteration: balena yena vai sītāṃ māyayā rākṣasādhama
english: O worst of Rākşasas, do you display that prowess of your by which, aided by your power of illusion, you have forcible carried off Sītā, disregarding me.
I shall with my sharpened shafts render this world free from Rākşasas, unless rendering back Mitbila's daughter, you throw yourself on my mercy.

sanskrit: धर्मात्मा रक्षसां श्रेष्ठः सम्प्राप्तो ऽयं विभीषणः
english: And, for certain, that foremost of Rākşasas, the righteous and graceful Vibhīşaņa, who has joined us, shall obtain, without having a thorn in his side, all this wealth of Lankā.

sanskrit: न हि राज्यमधर्मेण भोक्तुं क्षणमपि त्वया
transliteration: na hi rājyamadharmeṇa bhoktuṃ kṣaṇamapi tvayā
english: For you, foolish, wicked, ignorant of selfknowledge, and having dolts for councillors, are not competent to unrighteously exercise kingship for a moment.

sanskrit: युद्ध्यस्व वा धृतिं कृत्वा शौर्यमालम्ब्य राक्षस
transliteration: yuddhyasva vā dhṛtiṃ kṛtvā śauryamālambya rākṣasa
english: Fight you, O Rāksasa, summoning fortitude and heroism. On being slain with my shafts, you shall attain peace.

sanskrit: मम चक्षुष्पथं प्राप्य न जीवन् प्रतियास्यसि
transliteration: mama cakṣuṣpathaṃ prāpya na jīvan pratiyāsyasi
english: O night-ranger, if you should range the three worlds in the shape of a bird, you, coming in my ken, shall not be able to preserve your life.

sanskrit: सुदृष्टा क्रियतां लङ्का जीवितं ते मयि स्थितम्
transliteration: sudṛṣṭā kriyatāṃ laṅkā jīvitaṃ te mayi sthitam
english: It is all this for your good; do you perform acts for the good of your body surviving death; and do you see Lankā well; for your life is in my keeping.
Thus addressed by Rāma of untiring deeds, Tara's son went through the welkin like the embodied bearer of sacrificial offerings.
Arriving near that subduer of enemies, Rāvana, in a moment, that graceful one saw Rāvana, sitting calmly in the midst of his ministers.
And dropping down in his vicinity like a flaming fire, that best of monkeys, Augada, resembling a golden bracelet, stood there.
Then introducing himself, Angada delivered to Rāvana along with his ministers all that Rama had excellently spoken to him, neither extenuating nor setting down aught of himself.

sanskrit: वालिपुत्रो ऽङ्गदो नाम यदि ते श्रोत्रमागतः
english: I am the envoy of the king of Kosala, Rāma of untiring deeds; and I am the son of Vāli I do not know whether you have heard of me.
Raghu's son, Rāma-enhancer of Kausaiya's joy-has said to you, 'Do you, O fell one, coming out, give me battle and prove your prowess.
I shall slay you together with your ministers, and with your sons and relations and friends. And you being slain, the three worlds shall attain peace.
Today shall I destroy the enemy of the gods and Dänavas, and Yakşas, of the Gandharvas serpents and Rākṣasas, and the thorn (in the side of the Saints).

sanskrit: न चेत् सत्कृत्य वैदेहीं प्रणिपत्य प्रदास्यसि
transliteration: na cet satkṛtya vaidehīṃ praṇipatya pradāsyasi
english: On you being slain, all the wealth shall be Vibhisana's; unless, bowing down (to me) and paying me homage, you render back Maithilī.
When that monkey-chief had spoken thus, the lord of the night-rangers was wrought up with wrath.
And coming under the sway of passion, he commanded his counsellors, saying, "Take this one of perverse understanding, and slay him at once.”
Hearing Råvaņa's speech, four grim-visaged night rangers seized (Angada) flaming in energy like fire itself,
Tara's son suffered himself to be taken, in order that the hero might then display his prowess before the Yātudhānas.
Then Angada, taking them up, who were pressed against his arms, like insects, leapt up on a palace resembling a hill.
Thereat, in consequence of the impetuosity of his bound, the Raksasas, slipping off, fell on to the ground in the very sight of the Rākṣasa king.
Then the powerful son of Vāli with his legs attacked the top of that palace, elevated like a hill, of the lord of Rākşasas.
Thereat, as formerly the summit of the Himavān had been cleft by the thunder bold, the palace, thus assailed, was split in the very presence of the Ten-necked one.
Having reft the top of the edifice, and proclaimed his name, Angada, setting up a mighty roar, sprang into the sky.
Aggrieving the Rākşasas and rejoicing all the monkeys, he came back to the side of Rāma in the midst of the monkeys.
Rāvana was transported with wrath in consequence of the breaking down of the palace. And, finding his destruction (at hand), he began to heave sighs.
Rāma, surrounded by innumerable delighted monkeys setting up shouts, anxious for slaying his foe, prepared for battle.

At the command of Sugrīva, the exceedingly powerful monkey-Susena, resembling a mountain-summit, surrounded by a large number of monkeys capable of assuming shapes at pleasure, began to range from door to door; like the Moon ranging the stars.

At the command of Sugrīva, the exceedingly powerful monkey-Susena, resembling a mountain-summit, surrounded by a large number of monkeys capable of assuming shapes at pleasure, began to range from door to door; like the Moon ranging the stars.

Seeing the hundred Akşauhinis of the woodrangers, stationed in Lankā, extending down to the sea, some of the Rākşasas were struck with astonishment, while some came under the influence of fear; and some experienced delight from the (anticipated) delight of battle.

The space between the well and the moat all was flooded with monkeys.
