english: Go you. I know that you are worn out with fight. Therefore, O king of night-rangers, enter Lankā. Havirg a little respite, do you depart on your car along with your bowmen. Afterwards, mounted on your car, shall you behold my power.

sanskrit: स एवमुक्तो हतदर्पहर्षो निकृत्तचापः स हताश्वसूतः
शरार्दितः कृत्तमहाकिरीटो विवेश लङ्कां सहसा स राजा
transliteration: sa evamukto hatadarpaharṣo nikṛttacāpaḥ sa hatāśvasūtaḥ
śarārditaḥ kṛttamahākirīṭo viveśa laṅkāṃ sahasā sa rājā
english: Thus addressed, the king, with his pride and joy defeated, with his bow severed, and his steeds and charioteer killed himself smarting under. shafts, and having his crown splintered, speedily entered Lankā.

sanskrit: हरीन् विशल्यान् सह लक्ष्मणेन चकार रामः परमाहवाग्रे
transliteration: harīn viśalyān saha lakṣmaṇena cakāra rāmaḥ paramāhavāgre
english: On that foe of the deities and the Dănavas-the puissant lord of the night-rangers-entering (into Lankā), Rāma rendered the monkeys along with Lakşmaņa hale in that fierce conflict.

sanskrit: तस्मिन् प्रभिन्ने त्रिदशेन्द्रशत्रौ सुरासुरा भूतगणा दिशश्च
transliteration: tasmin prabhinne tridaśendraśatrau surāsurā bhūtagaṇā diśaśca
english: At the break-down of that foe of the immortals, the celestials and the Asuras, the ghosts and the Cardinal points, and all the mighty serpents together with the oceans and the creatures inhabiting earth and water, felt exceedingly delighted.
Entering the city of Larkā, the king afflicted with the fear of Rāma's arrows, with his pride humbled, was undergoing great torments:
Overpowered by the high souled Rāghava, the king resembled an elephant defeated by a lion or a serpent defeated by Garuda.
Remembering Råghava's arrows resembling a comet risen at the universal wreck, and of the splendour of live lightning, the Raksasa chief was aggrieved.
Rāma, seated on a superb golden seat and eyeing the Raksasas, spoke this word.

sanskrit: सर्वं तत् खलु मे मोघं यत्तप्तं परमं तपः
transliteration: sarvaṃ tat khalu me moghaṃ yattaptaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ
english: Forsooth all the austere asceticism I have performed go go for nothing, for although resembling the redoubtable Indra, I have been overcome by a mortal.
This dire speech of Brahmā also reverts to my remembrance, Know you that the fear come from a human being.

sanskrit: अवध्यत्वं मया प्राप्तं मानुषेभ्यो न याचितम्
transliteration: avadhyatvaṃ mayā prāptaṃ mānuṣebhyo na yācitam
english: You are incapable of being slain by deities and Danavas, Gandharvas, Yaksas, Raksasas and serpents. But you have not asked for immunity from men.

I deem even this son of Dasaratha as the occasion of my fear. I was formerly cursed by that lord of the Ikşawaku line-Anaranya-saying, 'O worst of Rākşasas, a person shall spring in my race, who, O wicked-minded one, shall you in battle along with your sons and courtiers and forces and horses and charioteers.

sanskrit: शप्तो ऽहं वेदवत्या च यदा सा धर्षिता पुरा
transliteration: śapto 'haṃ vedavatyā ca yadā sā dharṣitā purā
english: I was also cursed by Vedavatī, who was formerly outraged by me. And she is (perchance) born as the exalted daughter of Janaka.
What had also been uttered by Umā and Nandisvara and Rambhā and Varuna's daughter, has come to pass.
Taking note of this, you should strive (to the uttermost.) And let the Räkşasas be posted at the gateways, highways, and the walls.
Do you wake up that destroyer of the pride of the deities and then Danavas-Kumbhakarma, endowed with unparalleled gravity, overwhelmed with the curse of Brahmā.

Seeing himself worsted and Prahasta also slain, that Rākşasa endowed with dreadful power issued his orders to the fearful force. “Do you vigilantly guard the gates and mount the wall. And do you wake up Kumbhakarņa come under the sway of slumber.

Seeing himself worsted and Prahasta also slain, that Rākşasa endowed with dreadful power issued his orders to the fearful force. “Do you vigilantly guard the gates and mount the wall. And do you wake up Kumbhakarņa come under the sway of slumber.

sanskrit: नव षट् सप्त चाष्टौ च मासान् स्वपिति राक्षसः
transliteration: nava ṣaṭ sapta cāṣṭau ca māsān svapiti rākṣasaḥ
english: And deprived of his senses through lust, he sleep secure. And the Rākşasa sometimes sleep nine, seven, ten, or eight months away. Of measureless might he has slept for nine months.

sanskrit: तं तु बोधयत क्षिप्रं कुम्भकर्णं महाबलम्
transliteration: taṃ tu bodhayata kṣipraṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam

sanskrit: स तु सङ्ख्ये महाबाहुः ककुदः सर्वरक्षसाम्
transliteration: sa tu saṅkhye mahābāhuḥ kakudaḥ sarvarakṣasām
english: Therefore, speedily rouse very powerful Kumbhakarņa. Foremost of all the Rākşasas in fight, that long armed one shall speedily slay the monkeys as well as the princes.

sanskrit: एष केतुः परः सङ्ख्ये मुख्यो वै सर्वरक्षसाम्
कुम्भकर्णः सदा शेते मूढो ग्राम्यसुखे रतः
transliteration: eṣa ketuḥ paraḥ saṅkhye mukhyo vai sarvarakṣasām
kumbhakarṇaḥ sadā śete mūḍho grāmyasukhe rataḥ
english: He is a very banner in battle, and the crown of all the Raksasa. But intent on common pleasure, Kumbhakarna, with his senses stupefied, sleep ever.

sanskrit: रामेण हि निरस्तस्य सङ्ग्रामे ऽस्मिन् सुदारुणे
भविष्यति न मे शोकः कुम्भकर्णे विबोधिते
transliteration: bhaviṣyati na me śokaḥ kumbhakarṇe vibodhite
english: I have been worsted in fierce fight by Rāma; but on Kumbhakarņa being awakened, my grief shall go.

sanskrit: ईद्दशे व्यसने प्राप्ते यो न साह्याय कल्पते
transliteration: īddaśe vyasane prāpte yo na sāhyāya kalpate
english: If he does not help me in such high peril, what shall I do with his strength resembling the strength of Sakra himself?

sanskrit: ते तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य राक्षसाः
transliteration: te tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasendrasya rākṣasāḥ
english: Hearing the words of the lord of the Rākşasas, the Rākşasas, bestirring themselves, went to the abode of Kumbhakarņa.
And desired by Rāvana, those feeding on flesh and blood went off hurriedly taking perfumes and wreaths and a mass of food.

And entering Kumbhakarņa's charming cave having a wide gateway, measuring a yojana breathing around perfumes of flowers, those highly powerful ones, pushed off by Kumbhakarna's breath, with the utmost energy they could summon up stood their ground and entered the cave.

And entering Kumbhakarņa's charming cave having a wide gateway, measuring a yojana breathing around perfumes of flowers, those highly powerful ones, pushed off by Kumbhakarna's breath, with the utmost energy they could summon up stood their ground and entered the cave.

sanskrit: तां प्रविश्य गुहां रम्यां शुभां काञ्चनकुट्टिमाम्
transliteration: tāṃ praviśya guhāṃ ramyāṃ śubhāṃ kāñcanakuṭṭimām
english: Then entering that charming cave having floors paved with gold and gems. those Naiſtas endowed with great strength, saw that one of dreadful prowess, lying down.

sanskrit: ते तु तं विकृतं सुप्तं विकीर्णमिव पर्वतम्
transliteration: te tu taṃ vikṛtaṃ suptaṃ vikīrṇamiva parvatam

english: Then they huge bodied Rākșasas piled up before Kumbhakarma, Meru-like animals for conferring rare gratification and heaps of deer and buffaloes and boars. And the Rākşasas made an astounding heap of rice.

sanskrit: मृगाणां महिषाणां च वराहाणां च सञ्चयान्
transliteration: mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca varāhāṇāṃ ca sañcayān
english: Then they huge bodied Rākșasas piled up before Kumbhakarma, Meru-like animals for conferring rare gratification and heaps of deer and buffaloes and boars. And the Rākşasas made an astounding heap of rice.
They winded conchs beaming moon-like. And they incapable of being beaten shouted in full chorus.
The night-rangers shouted and struck at their arms with their hands and began to pull him. And for rousing Kumbhakarņa, mighty was the din that they raised.

sanskrit: दिशो द्रवन्तस्त्रिदिवं किरन्तः श्रुत्वा विहङ्गाः सहसा निपेतुः
transliteration: diśo dravantastridivaṃ kirantaḥ śrutvā vihaṅgāḥ sahasā nipetuḥ
english: Hearing those loud sounds of conchs and drums and Papavas; and those proceeding from persons striking at their arms with their hands; and leonine roars, rushing on all sides and riving the very heavens, birds suddenly dropped down.

sanskrit: यदा भृशार्तैर्निनदैर्महात्मा न कुम्भकर्णो बुबुधे प्रसुप्तः
transliteration: yadā bhṛśārtairninadairmahātmā na kumbhakarṇo bubudhe prasuptaḥ
english: When the high-souled Kumbhakarņa sleeping soundly did not awake at that terrific tumult, the Raksasas took up Bhusundis and maces.

sanskrit: सुखप्रसुप्तं भुवि कुम्भकर्णं रक्षांस्युदग्राणि तदा निजघ्नुः
transliteration: sukhaprasuptaṃ bhuvi kumbhakarṇaṃ rakṣāṃsyudagrāṇi tadā nijaghnuḥ
english: Then the Raksasas, drawing near, smote Kumbhakarņa sleeping sweetly in the chest with mountain-peaks, maces and clubs.

sanskrit: राक्षसा बलवन्तो ऽपि स्थातुं नाशक्नुवन् पुरः
english: But the Rākşasas could not stay before Kumbhakarņa owing to the hurricane heaving at his breath.

Then tightening their cloth (about their waist), those Rākşasas of dreadful prowess sounded Mşdangas and Paņavas, conchs and kumbhas. And ten thousand Rākṣasas together surrounded that one resembling a heap of darkblue collyrium and fell to rousing him.

Then tightening their cloth (about their waist), those Rākşasas of dreadful prowess sounded Mşdangas and Paņavas, conchs and kumbhas. And ten thousand Rākṣasas together surrounded that one resembling a heap of darkblue collyrium and fell to rousing him.

sanskrit: अभिघ्नन्तो नदन्तश्च नैव संविविदे तु सः
transliteration: abhighnanto nadantaśca naiva saṃvivide tu saḥ

sanskrit: यदा चैनं न शेकुस्ते प्रतिबोधयितुं तदा
transliteration: yadā cainaṃ na śekuste pratibodhayituṃ tadā
english: But albeit assailed with shouts and smite with weapons, he did not wake up. And when they succeeded not in rousing him, they more than ever exerted themselves.

sanskrit: सपर्वतवना सर्वा सो ऽपि नैव प्रबुध्यते

english: Then they simultaneously sounded a thousand kettle-drums beaten with sticks of polished gold.
And coming under the sway of the curse, when that one sunk in slumber did not wake up, the night-rangers were wrought up with wrath.
And overcome with choler, they endowed with dreadful prowess addressed themselves vigorously to awakening him; and others put forth their energy.
Others smote the kettle-drums, and others set up loud cries. And others cut off his hair, and others bit his ears.
Others poured into his ears a thousand vessels of water. But Kumbhakarņa come under the spell of a mighty slumber did not wink.
Others-strong ones-armed with poniards (kūt as) and maces, made their poniards and maces alight on his person.
And struck with sataghnis bound with cords, that huge-bodied one did not wake up.

sanskrit: वारणानां सहस्रं तु शरीरे ऽस्य प्रधावितम्
english: Then when a thousand elephants rushed against his body, recovering his consciousness, he awoke.
Assailed with mountain-peaks and trees descending on his body, he without minding those tremendous blows, on sleep having been dispelled. Suddenly got up yawning, suffering the pangs of hunger.

sanskrit: विवृत्य वक्त्रं वडवामुखाभं निशाचरो ऽसौ विकृतं जजृम्भे
transliteration: vivṛtya vaktraṃ vaḍavāmukhābhaṃ niśācaro 'sau vikṛtaṃ jajṛmbhe
english: Then that night-ranger resembling an elephant or a serpent or a mountain-peak, casting about his arms superior in force to the thunder-bolt itself, and opening his deformed mouth like to that of a mule, yawned (again and again).
As he yawned, his mouth resembling the subterraneous regions, looked like the Sun stationed at the summit of Meru.
That night ranger possessed of unwieldly strength woke up, yawning. And the breath that he breathed resembled a storm raging in a mountain.
Then as he sat up, Kumbhakarņa's form appeared like that of the Destroyer himself at the universal wreck, intent upon consuming all creatures.
The large eyes of that one, resembling a life flame and endowed with the splendour of lighting, appeared like a pair of glowing planets.
Then they pointed to him all those heaps of edibles, various and profuse, bears and buffaloes, and that powerful (Raksasa) fell to.

sanskrit: अदन् बुभुक्षितो मांसं शोणितं तृषितः पिबन्
transliteration: adan bubhukṣito māṃsaṃ śoṇitaṃ tṛṣitaḥ piban
english: And hungering, he fed on flesh and athirst, drank blood. And then that enemy of Sakra drank vesselfuls of fat and blood.
And concluding that he was replete, the nightrangers came up; and bowing down their heads stood circling him on all sides.

sanskrit: चारयन् सर्वतो दृष्टिं तान् ददर्श निशाचरान्
transliteration: cārayan sarvato dṛṣṭiṃ tān dadarśa niśācarān
english: Then with his eyes discoloured and drooping from drowsiness, he casting his eyes around addressed those night-rangers.
That foremost of Naiſtas cheered all those Naiſtas: and surprised at his having been roused, spoke to the Rākşasas.

sanskrit: कच्चित् सुकुशलं राज्ञो भयवानेष वा न किम्
transliteration: kaccit sukuśalaṃ rājño bhayavāneṣa vā na kim
english: Why, being honoured, have I been awakened by you? Is it well with the king? Or has any fear : sprung up here?
Or has a mighty fear presented itself forsooth from among others; for which I have bee speedily awakened by you?

sanskrit: पातयिष्ये महेन्द्रं वा शातयिष्ये तथा ऽनलम्
english: This very day will I uproot quite the fear of the sovereign of the Rākşasas. I will split up the great Indra himself, or make Fire himself give up his heat.

sanskrit: न ह्यल्पकारणे सुप्तं बोधयिष्यति मां गुरुः
transliteration: na hyalpakāraṇe suptaṃ bodhayiṣyati māṃ guruḥ
english: One does not awaken my like for a light cause. therefore do you give the real truth of the cause of your awakening me.
Thereat a minister of the king, named Yupakş a, with joined hands said to that humbler of foesKumbhakarna-wrought up with wrath, who was thus speaking.
No fear anywise springs to us fro the Deities. But, О king, a great fear does cross us, coming from a mortal.

sanskrit: न दैत्यदानवेभ्यो वा भयमस्ति हि तादृशम्
transliteration: na daityadānavebhyo vā bhayamasti hi tādṛśam
english: And never fear so come to us anywise from Daityas or Dānavas, as it has arrived from a man, O king.
This Lanka has been hemmed in by monkeys resembling mountains. And terrific is the terror that come even from Rāma scorched with fire springing from the ravishment of Sītă.
Ere this by a single monkey was this splendid city burnt down. And the prince Akşa has been slain along with his following and elephants.
That thorn in the sides of deities, that lord of the Raksasas-Pulastya's son himself-has been set free in conflict by Rāghava endowed with the splendour of the Sun, Saying, “Go you.

sanskrit: यन्न दैवैः कृतो राजा नापि दैत्यैर्न दानवैः
कृतः स इह रामेण विमुक्तः प्राणसंशयात्
transliteration: yanna daivaiḥ kṛto rājā nāpi daityairna dānavaiḥ
kṛtaḥ sa iha rāmeṇa vimuktaḥ prāṇasaṃśayāt
english: What had been done to the king by neither the gods nor Daityas nor yet the Dănavas, has been done by Rāma; and he has been set free, having come to a pass imperilling his life.
Hearing Yüpākşa's speech and hearing of the defeat of his brother, Kumbhakarņa, with his eyes whirling, spoke to him, saying..

sanskrit: राघवं च रणे हत्वा पश्चाद्द्रक्ष्यामि रावणम्
transliteration: rāghavaṃ ca raṇe hatvā paścāddrakṣyāmi rāvaṇam
english: Today, O Yüpākṣa, after vanquishing in battle the monkey-army together with Laksmana and Raghava, shall I see Ravana.
I shall regale the Rākṣasas with the flesh and blood of the monkeys, and myself drink the blood of Rāma and Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: तत्तस्य वाक्यं ब्रुवतो निशम्य सगर्वितं रोषविवृद्धदोषम्
transliteration: tattasya vākyaṃ bruvato niśamya sagarvitaṃ roṣavivṛddhadoṣam
english: Hearing his words as he haughtily spoke thus with his spirit of insolence magnified by much, that foremost of the Nairta soldiers, Mahodara, with joined hands observed.

sanskrit: रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा गुणदोषौ विमृश्य च
transliteration: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā guṇadoṣau vimṛśya ca
english: O long-armed one, having at first heard Rāvana's words and considered their justice or otherwise, you will afterwards defeat the foe in fight.
Hearing Mahodara's words, the exceedingly energetic and mighty (Kumbhakarma) surrounded by the Rākşasas, prepared to depart.
Having roused from his slumbers that one of terrific prowess having dreadful eyes the Rāks asas speedily arrived at the residence of the Tennecked one.
And presenting themselves before the Tennecked on seated on a superb seat, all the nightrangers spoke with joined hands.

sanskrit: प्रबुद्धः कुम्भकर्णो ऽयं भ्राता ते राक्षसर्षभ
english: O lord of the Rākṣasas, your brother, Kumbhakarņa, has been roused. Shall he march from there; or will you see him come here?
Thereat, Ravana, pleased, spoke to those Raks asas who had presented themselves, “I wish to see him here, and do you honour him fittingly."

sanskrit: तथेत्युक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे पुनरागम्य राक्षसाः
transliteration: tathetyuktvā tu te sarve punarāgamya rākṣasāḥ
english: Thereat, saying 'So be it', the Rākşasas, directed by Ravana, going back, spoke to Kumbhakarna.
That foremost of all the Rākşasas-the kingwish to see you. So mind you going, and gladden your brother.
The irrepressible Kumbhakarna possessed of prodigious prowess, learning the mandate of his brother, sa', ing, 'So be it', rose up from his bed.
Washing his face, and having bathed, that one, feeling refreshed and enjoying exceeding exhilaration of spirit, wishing to drink, urged (the Rākşasas) to bring the nerve-conferring draught.
Then the Rākşasas at the command of Rāvana speedily procured wine and various kinds of viands.

Having drunk two thousand vessels (of wine) he prepared to go. And slightly swollen and flushed, Kumbhakarma, attaining access of strength and fire, waxed wroth and resembled the Doom and Destroyer-Yama himself. And striding to the residence of his brother backed by the Raksasa force, Kumbhakarņa shook the earth with his tread.

Having drunk two thousand vessels (of wine) he prepared to go. And slightly swollen and flushed, Kumbhakarma, attaining access of strength and fire, waxed wroth and resembled the Doom and Destroyer-Yama himself. And striding to the residence of his brother backed by the Raksasa force, Kumbhakarņa shook the earth with his tread.

Illuming the highway with the splendour of his person, like the thousand-rayed (Sun) discovering the earth with his rays, (Kumbhakarna) went on, engirt around by joined hands resembling wreaths, like Śatakratu* going to the abode of the Self-sprung. *Lit. him of an hundred sacrifices-an appellation of Indra.

sanskrit: तं राजमार्गस्थममित्रघातिनं वनौकसस्ते सहसा बहिः स्थिताः
transliteration: taṃ rājamārgasthamamitraghātinaṃ vanaukasaste sahasā bahiḥ sthitāḥ
english: Suddenly seeing that slayer of foes of immeasurable prowess, resembling a mountainsummit, walking along the highways, the woodrangers stationed outside (the monkey-camp), along with the leaders of bands, were seized with affright.

sanskrit: केचिच्छरण्यं शरणं स्म रामं व्रजन्ति केचिद्व्यथिताः पतन्ति
केचिद्दिशः स्म व्यथिताः प्रयान्ति केचिद्भयार्ता भुवि शेरते स्म
transliteration: keciccharaṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ sma rāmaṃ vrajanti kecidvyathitāḥ patanti
keciddiśaḥ sma vyathitāḥ prayānti kecidbhayārtā bhuvi śerate sma
english: Then some sought the shelter of Răma, worthy of being so sought; and some, stricken (with panic), dropped to the earth; and some, suffering (from fear), fled to the carindal points; and some through stress (of apprehension) lay down on the ground.

sanskrit: वनौकसः प्रेक्ष्य विवृद्धमद्भुतं भयार्दिता दुद्रुविरे ततस्ततः
transliteration: vanaukasaḥ prekṣya vivṛddhamadbhutaṃ bhayārditā dudruvire tatastataḥ
english: Seeing that one resembling a very mountainpeak, decked with a diadem, seeming to touch the Sun himself with his energy, of colossal altitude, and wonderful to behold, the woodrangers, tormented with fright, began to scamper on all sides.
Then the exceedingly energetic Rāma possessed of prowess, taking his bow, saw Kumbhakarņa, having a huge body and decked with a diadem.

Seeing that foremost of Rākşasas looking like a mountain; filling all the heavens as formerly Nārāyaṇa had done; resembling clouds charged with rain; and adorned with golden Angadas, the mighty army of monkeys began to run away at the top of its speed.

Seeing that foremost of Rākşasas looking like a mountain; filling all the heavens as formerly Nārāyaṇa had done; resembling clouds charged with rain; and adorned with golden Angadas, the mighty army of monkeys began to run away at the top of its speed.

sanskrit: विद्रुतां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा वर्धमानं च राक्षसम्
transliteration: vidrutāṃ vāhinīṃ dṛṣṭvā vardhamānaṃ ca rākṣasam
english: Seeing the army scamper and the Rākşasa swelling, Rāma struck with surprise, said to Vibhisana. mass
Who is that tawny-eyed one, decked with a diadem, and looking like a hill? And in Lankā the hero appear like a of clouds embosoming lightning.

sanskrit: पृथिव्याः केतुभूतो ऽसौ महानेको ऽत्र दृश्यते
यं दृष्ट्वा वानराः सर्वे विद्रवन्ति ततस्ततः
transliteration: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve vidravanti tatastataḥ
english: And alone he seem like an ensign of the Earth; and seeing him the monkeys dart away hither and thither.

sanskrit: आचक्ष्व मे महान् को ऽसौ रक्षो वा यदि वा ऽसुरः
transliteration: ācakṣva me mahān ko 'sau rakṣo vā yadi vā 'suraḥ
english: Tell me who he is, whether a Rākṣasa or an Asura. The like of him mine eyes had never before lighted on.
Accosted by the king's son-Rāma of untiring deeds-the exceedingly wise Vibhīşaņa said to Kakutstha.

sanskrit: अस्य प्रमाणात् सदृशो राक्षसो ऽन्यो न विद्यते
transliteration: asya pramāṇāt sadṛśo rākṣaso 'nyo na vidyate
english: By whom in battle Vivasvata's offspring* and Vasava himself had been vanquished this is hethe wondrous powerful Kumbhakarņa, son to Visravā. No Rākṣasa is there that equals this one in size. *Yama-son of Vivasvata or the Sun.

sanskrit: एतेन देवा युधि दानवाश्च यक्षा भुजङ्गाः पिशिताशनाश्च
transliteration: etena devā yudhi dānavāśca yakṣā bhujaṅgāḥ piśitāśanāśca
english: O Rāghava, this one in battle has brought down Dānavas and Yakşas and Serpents' and flesh-feeders and Gandharvas and Vidyādharas and Pannagas by thousands. 1. Bhujanga:-semi-divine serpents. 2. Semi-divine serpents.

sanskrit: हन्तुं न शेकुस्त्रिदशाः कालो ऽयमिति मोहिताः
english: The immortals themselves thinking the darthanded and fierce-eyed Kumbhakarņa possessed of great strength, as the Destroyer himself, were overwhelmed with stupor and were foiled in their exertions to slay him.
The exceedingly powerful Kumbhakarņa is mighty by nature: the strength of other redoubtable Rākşasas is owing to boons obtained by them.
As soon as this high-souled one was born and was a babe, he began to devour up countless creatures by the thousand.

sanskrit: यान्ति स्म शरणं शक्रं तमप्यर्थं न्यवेदयन्
transliteration: yānti sma śaraṇaṃ śakraṃ tamapyarthaṃ nyavedayan
english: On these having been devoured, creatures, afflicted with affright consequent on those having been eaten up, sought the shelter of Sakra and told him what had happened.

sanskrit: स कुम्भकर्णं कुपितो महेन्द्रो जघान वज्रेण शितेन वज्री
स शक्रवज्राभिहतो महात्मा चचाल कोपाच्च भृशं ननाद
transliteration: sa kumbhakarṇaṃ kupito mahendro jaghāna vajreṇa śitena vajrī
sa śakravajrābhihato mahātmā cacāla kopācca bhṛśaṃ nanāda
english: Thereat the great Indra, waxing wroth, smote Kumbhakarna with the whetted levin. And hit at with Sakra's thunder bolt, that high-souled (hero) shook, and in wrath set up roars.
Hearing the roars of the Raksasa-Kumbhakarna, as he kept crying, creatures, seized with fear, were greatly agitated.
Thereat, enraged with the great Indra, the mighty Kumbhakarņa plucking a tusk of Airāvata, hurled it at Vāsava's chest.

With blood overflowing his person, Vāsava looked as if aflame. Thereat, all of a sudden the gods and the Brahmarşis and the Dānavas were dispirited. Then ſakra Then Śakra alongwith alongwith others proceeded to the abode of Brahma.

sanskrit: प्रजाभिः सह शक्रश्च ययौ स्थानं स्वयम्भुवः
transliteration: prajābhiḥ saha śakraśca yayau sthānaṃ svayambhuvaḥ

sanskrit: प्रजानां भक्षणं चापि देवानां चापि धर्षणम्
transliteration: prajānāṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ cāpi devānāṃ cāpi dharṣaṇam

sanskrit: एवं प्रजा यदि त्वेष भक्षयिष्यति नित्यशः
transliteration: evaṃ prajā yadi tveṣa bhakṣayiṣyati nityaśaḥ
english: Then they informed the lord of creatures touching the ravages of Kumbhakarna, and informed the gods about Kumbhakarna's devouring up, destroying asylums and outraging others, wives. If this one devour creatures constantly, in a short space the world would be empty of any.
Hearing Vasava's speech, the Great-father of all creatures called up* the Rākṣasas and saw Kumbhakarņa (before him). *By reciting a certain scriptural formula.
Seeing Kumbhkarņa, Prajāpati* was seized with exceeding great fear. And then pacifying Kumbhakarma, the Self-sprung addressed him, saying. *Lit. lord of creatures.
Forsooth for compassing the destruction of creatures, have you been begot by Paulasta* Therefore from this day forth, you shall lie down as one dead. *ViSravana.
Stricken with the of Brahma, Kumbhakarma fell down before the Lord. Then, "extremely agitated, Ravana said. curse

sanskrit: न नप्तारं स्वकं न्याय्यं शप्तुमेवं प्रजापते
transliteration: na naptāraṃ svakaṃ nyāyyaṃ śaptumevaṃ prajāpate
english: You hew down a golden tree when about to bear fruit. O lord of creatures, you ought not to curse thus your own grandson.

sanskrit: न मिथ्यावचनश्च त्वं स्वप्स्यत्येष न संशयः
transliteration: na mithyāvacanaśca tvaṃ svapsyatyeṣa na saṃśayaḥ
english: Your words will never go for naught; sleep he will, without doubt. But do you appoint a time for his sleeping and one for his awaking,
Hearing Rāvana's speech, the Self-sprung said, "having slept for six months, he shall wake for one day.
And for a single day, that hero, coming under the influence of hunger, shall range the earth, opening his mouth wide open, and devouring people like a fire that has spread far and wide.
Now king Rāvaņa struck with terror at your prowess, encompassed with peril, has waked up Kumbhakarņa.
That hero possessed of dreadful prowess, wrought up with high wrath, sallying forth from his camp, rush about, eating up monkeys.
Soon as the monkeys see Kumbhakarna, they fly away. And How can they resist in battle the enraged Kumbhakarna?
Do you tell the monkeys this is an uplifted engine. Thus assured, the monkeys shall take heart.

sanskrit: उवाच राघवो वाक्यं नीलं सेनापतिं तदा
transliteration: uvāca rāghavo vākyaṃ nīlaṃ senāpatiṃ tadā
english: Hearing Vibhīşaņa's words informed with reason and tending to the good (of the monkeys), Rāghava then addressed general Nila, saying.

sanskrit: गच्छ सैन्यानि सर्वाणि व्यूह्य तिष्ठस्व पावके
transliteration: gaccha sainyāni sarvāṇi vyūhya tiṣṭhasva pāvake
english: Let you, monkeys, equipped with weapons and holding hill tops in your hands, and furnished with mountain-summits and trees and rocks, stay, occupying the highways and the bridges.
Thus instructed by Rāghava, that powerful monkey, Nila-general of the forces-accordingly issue I his orders to the monkey-hosts.
Then Gavākṣa and Sarabha and Hanumān and Angada, themselves endowed with the splendour of mountain-summits, taking up mountain-tops, drew towards the gateway.
Hearing Rāma's words,* the heroic monkeys inspired with intrepidity, fiercely fell on the foe with trees. *Namely, "that is an uplifted engine.”

Then that dreadful army of monkeys, upraising crags and holding trees in their hands, appeared like mighty masses of scowling clouds bordering a mountain.* *This is apt, seeing that Larika was situated on a hill.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe ekaṣaṣṭitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: That tiger-like Rakşasa possessed of prowess, (still) under the influence of slumber, strode along the picturesque highway.
That exceedingly unconquerable one, surrounded by thousands of Raksasas, went on, showered with blossoms from the houses (standing by).
Then he saw the grand and graceful residence of the lord of the Räkşasas, having golden networks and sun-bright to behold.

sanskrit: स तत्तदा सूर्य इवाभ्रजालं प्रविश्य रक्षोधिपतेर्निवेशम्
ददर्श दूरे ऽग्रजमासनस्थं स्वयम्भुवं शक्र इवासनस्थम्
transliteration: sa tattadā sūrya ivābhrajālaṃ praviśya rakṣodhipaterniveśam
english: Entering the mansion of the Raksasa sovereign, like the sun entering into a mass of clouds, he saw his elder brother seated at a distance; even as Sakra sees the Self-sprung seated.
Kumbhakarņa surrounded by numbers of Rākşasas, entered his brother's abode, making the very earth tremble with his tread.

sanskrit: सो ऽभिगम्य गृहं भ्रातुः कक्ष्यामभिविगाह्य च
english: Arriving at the abode and passing the entrance, he saw his superior anxiously seated on the car, Pusphaka.
Seeing Kumbhakarņa come, the Ten necked one, exceedingly rejoiced, raised him up and drew him near himself.
Then the exceedingly mighty Kumbhakarņa saluted the feet of his brother and said, "What did you say ?"
Thereat, delighted, Ravana, springing up, again embraced (his brother). And embraced (by his brother), and duly greeted by him, that brother (of Ravana).
Kumbhakarņa seated himself on a shining and superb seat. And seating himself on that seat, the wondrous powerful Kumbhakarna, with his eyes reddened in wrath, addressed Ravana, saying.

sanskrit: शंस कस्माद्भयं ते ऽस्ति को ऽद्य प्रेतो भविष्यति
transliteration: śaṃsa kasmādbhayaṃ te 'sti ko 'dya preto bhaviṣyati
english: O king, why honouring me, has you awaked me? Tell me whence springs your fear? And who shall be a ghost?* Thereat Ravana, waxing wroth, and with his eyes rolling in rage, said to Kumbhakarma, seated. *Having been slain by me.

O king, why honouring me, has you awaked me? Tell me whence springs your fear? And who shall be a ghost?* Thereat Ravana, waxing wroth, and with his eyes rolling in rage, said to Kumbhakarma, seated. *Having been slain by me.

sanskrit: अद्य ते सुमहान् कालः शयानस्य महाबल
सुखितस्त्वं न जानीषे मम रामकृतं भयम्
transliteration: adya te sumahān kālaḥ śayānasya mahābala
sukhitastvaṃ na jānīṣe mama rāmakṛtaṃ bhayam
english: O highly powerful one, you have slept away a long space of time. And having been asleep, you did not know the great fear of mine springing from Rama.
This graceful son to Daśaratha possessed of strength, along with Sugriva, having crossed the ocean, is destroying our race.
Alack! see in own Lanka, woods and forests have been flooded with an ocean of monkeys never even coming without any ado by the bridge (which they have constructed).

sanskrit: वानराणां क्षयं युद्धे न पश्यामि कदाचन
transliteration: vānarāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ yuddhe na paśyāmi kadācana
english: Those Rākşasas that were prime have been slain in battle by the monkeys; but I find no destruction of the monkeys in fight. Nay, the monkeys have been before vanquished (by the Raksasas) in battle.

sanskrit: न चापि वानरा युद्धे जितपूर्वाः कदाचन
transliteration: na cāpi vānarā yuddhe jitapūrvāḥ kadācana
english: Those Rākşasas that were prime have been slain in battle by the monkeys; but I find no destruction of the monkeys in fight. Nay, the monkeys have been before vanquished (by the Raksasas) in battle.
Therefore has this fear sprung up in my heart). Save me from this, O exceedingly powerful one. Do you now destroy these. It is for this that I have roused you.
Do you, favouring me, whose exchequer is empty, save this city of Lanka, having only young folks and the aged left.

sanskrit: मयैवं नोक्तपूर्वो हि कच्चिद् भ्रातः परन्तप
transliteration: mayaivaṃ noktapūrvo hi kaccid bhrātaḥ parantapa
english: O long-armed one, do you perform your dearest acts in behalf of your brother. O subduer of enemies, I had never before said so to my brother.

sanskrit: त्वय्यस्ति तु मम स्नेहः परा सम्भावना च मे
transliteration: tvayyasti tu mama snehaḥ parā sambhāvanā ca me
english: In you is my affection and great is the probability of your succeeding. In the wars of the celestials and Asuras, O foremost of Rāks asas, countless were the celestials that you as an antagonist had beaten.

sanskrit: न हि ते सर्वभूतेषु दृश्यते सदृशो बली
transliteration: na hi te sarvabhūteṣu dṛśyate sadṛśo balī
english: Therefore, o you of dreadful strength! summon your entire energy. Him find I not among all beings, who is your peer in prowess.

sanskrit: स्वतेजसा विधम सपत्नवाहिनीं शरद्घनं पवन इवोद्यतो महान्
transliteration: svatejasā vidhama sapatnavāhinīṃ śaradghanaṃ pavana ivodyato mahān
english: O lover of battle! O dear to friends, as you like, do this beloved good office, this prime benefit, to me. By your own energy, smite the hostile hosts, even as a mighty and strong wind (scattered away) autumnal clouds.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe dviṣaṣṭitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Hearing the lament of the king of Rākşasas, Kumbhakarma, laughing said.

sanskrit: दृष्टो दोषो हि यो ऽस्माभिः पुरा मन्त्रविनिर्णये
transliteration: dṛṣṭo doṣo hi yo 'smābhiḥ purā mantravinirṇaye
english: That evil which on the occasion of the conclave we had seen, has befallen you, who have passed by what was fraught with your good.

sanskrit: शीघ्रं खल्वभ्युपेतं त्वां फलं पापस्य कर्मणः
transliteration: śīghraṃ khalvabhyupetaṃ tvāṃ phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ
english: Even as a sinner reaps perdition, verily has the fruit of your unrighteous act found you.
At first, O mighty king, you did not ponder over this course of conduct; nor, from pride of prowess, did you at all take note of the evil thereof.

sanskrit: पूर्वं चापरकार्याणि न स वेद नयानयौ
transliteration: pūrvaṃ cāparakāryāṇi na sa veda nayānayau
english: He that dose last what should be done first, and what should be done last, is ignorant of what is prudence and what not.

Acts not performed in harmony with season and place, like to acts performed counter to season and place, are the occasions of misery, and resemble clarified butter poured into fire that has not been sanctified.

sanskrit: त्रयाणां पञ्चधा योगं कर्मणां यः प्रपश्यति
सचिवैः समयं कृत्वा स सभ्ये वर्तते पथि
transliteration: trayāṇāṃ pañcadhā yogaṃ karmaṇāṃ yaḥ prapaśyati
sacivaiḥ samayaṃ kṛtvā sa sabhye vartate pathi
english: He stay well in the path that, in consultation with his counsellors, ascertain the five way touching the three kinds of action* *The five ways are (1) the mans of commencing an act (2) person, thing and wealth, (3) division of season and place, (4) providing agains mischance (5) success. The three kinds of action are treaty, war, etc. All this is nebulous; And the commentator is sadly reticent over this extremely important passage.

sanskrit: यथागमं च यो राजा समयं विचिकीर्षति
transliteration: yathāgamaṃ ca yo rājā samayaṃ vicikīrṣati
english: The king that aided by his own intelligence as well as his counsellors act after reflection in consonance with the science of polity, that distinguish his friends from his foes), and, O lord of the Raksasas, that seasonably' pursue righteousness, or profit, or desire, or any two, or all these combined-truly has understanding.? 1. Religion is to be sought in the morning, profit in the afternoon, and desire at nigh, so the commentator. 2. One is at sea in the midst of these formless generalities. The tantalized intellect makes a desperate attempt to grasp the body of the shadow seeming substance, but the empty air mocks his pains. A translator, however, is fast bound to the oar and must pull on, will be, nil he.

sanskrit: धर्ममर्थं च कामं च सर्वान् वा रक्षसां पते
भजेत पुरुषः काले त्रीणि द्वन्द्वानि वा पुनः
transliteration: dharmamarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca sarvān vā rakṣasāṃ pate
bhajeta puruṣaḥ kāle trīṇi dvandvāni vā punaḥ
english: The king that aided by his own intelligence as well as his counsellors act after reflection in consonance with the science of polity, that distinguish his friends from his foes), and, O lord of the Raksasas, that seasonably' pursue righteousness, or profit, or desire, or any two, or all these combined-truly has understanding.? 1. Religion is to be sought in the morning, profit in the afternoon, and desire at nigh, so the commentator. 2. One is at sea in the midst of these formless generalities. The tantalized intellect makes a desperate attempt to grasp the body of the shadow seeming substance, but the empty air mocks his pains. A translator, however, is fast bound to the oar and must pull on, will be, nil he.

sanskrit: राजा वा राजमात्रो वा व्यर्थं तस्य बहुश्रुतम्
transliteration: rājā vā rājamātro vā vyarthaṃ tasya bahuśrutam
english: But the king or the heir apparent, that, having heard what is prime among the three, does not understand, has his time in vain on his erudition.

sanskrit: उपप्रदानं सान्त्वं वा भेदं काले च विक्रमम्
योगं च रक्षसां श्रेष्ठ तावुभौ च नयानयौ
transliteration: upapradānaṃ sāntvaṃ vā bhedaṃ kāle ca vikramam
yogaṃ ca rakṣasāṃ śreṣṭha tāvubhau ca nayānayau
english: He that controlling his own self, consult with his counsellors seasonably touching gift, forbearance, difference and prowess, as well as virtue, profit and desire-does not in this world come by calamity.

sanskrit: काले धर्मार्थकामान् यः सम्मन्त्र्य सचिवैः सह
transliteration: kāle dharmārthakāmān yaḥ sammantrya sacivaiḥ saha
english: He that controlling his own self, consult with his counsellors seasonably touching gift, forbearance, difference and prowess, as well as virtue, profit and desire-does not in this world come by calamity.

sanskrit: राजा सहार्थतत्त्वज्ञैः सचिवैः स हि जीवति
transliteration: rājā sahārthatattvajñaiḥ sacivaiḥ sa hi jīvati
english: Perceiving the fair fruit (of a line of action) accruing to him here, a king should act in consultation with counsellors endowed with intelligence and versed in the import of things.
Not understanding the sense of the scriptures, persons possessed of beastly intelligence, entering into the heart of their counsellors, are inspired with a desire of speaking out of sheer volubility.
Albeit uttered heedfully, the speech of those that are ignorant of learning and the knowledge of the sense of things, and who are intent upon attaining abounding affluence, should not be acted upon.

sanskrit: अहितं च हिताकारं धार्ष्ट्याज्जल्पन्ति ये नराः
transliteration: ahitaṃ ca hitākāraṃ dhārṣṭyājjalpanti ye narāḥ
english: Those-spoilers of business-who from recklessness talk of pernicious as if profitableshould certainly be rejected as counsellors.
Some counsellors-destroyers of their mastersjoining intelligent enemies (of their lords), act in a way opposed to their interests in this world.
Their lords, at the hour of consultation, by their behaviour should know these counsellorsenemies in the guise of friends-who have been won over (by the opposite party).
Even as the fowls of the air enter the hole in the Krauñca, enemies find and easy entrance into the short comings of him that is fickle and that rush into act without heed.

sanskrit: अवाप्नोति हि सो ऽनर्थान् स्थानाच्च व्यवरोप्यते
english: He that disregarding his foe, omits to guard himself, come by disasters and lose his place.

sanskrit: तदेव नो हितं कार्यं यदिच्छसि च तत् कुरु
transliteration: tadeva no hitaṃ kāryaṃ yadicchasi ca tat kuru
english: Even what had been advanced by the beloved and my younger brother is fraught with our welfare. Do you now what you-wish.
Hearing Kumbhakarma's words, the Tennecked one knit up his brows, and, wrought up with wrath, said to him.
I am worthy of being honoured by you, like your superior. What needs this verbal travail? Do you what is fit.
Vain is the mention now of what I did either through stupor or delusion or pride of prowess. Now bethink you of what is proper.

sanskrit: अस्मिन् काले तु यद्युक्तं तदिदानीं विधीयताम्
गतं तु नानुशोचन्ति गतं तु गतमेव हि
transliteration: asmin kāle tu yadyuktaṃ tadidānīṃ vidhīyatām
gataṃ tu nānuśocanti gataṃ tu gatameva hi

sanskrit: यदि खल्वस्ति मे स्नेहो विक्रमं वा ऽवगच्छसि
यदि वा कार्यमेतत्ते हृदि कार्यतमं मतम्
transliteration: yadi khalvasti me sneho vikramaṃ vā 'vagacchasi
yadi vā kāryametatte hṛdi kāryatamaṃ matam
english: Do you through your prowess assuage the sorrow of mine springing from my impolitic conduct, if you cherish any feeling for me, if your strength stay and if you deem this business of mine as by far more momentous to you.
He is a friend that succour one fallen in distress and is undergoing affliction; and he acts friendly that helped a person lapsing from the path of morality.

sanskrit: रुष्टो ऽयमिति विज्ञाय शनैः श्लक्ष्णमुवाच ह
english: As he was speaking thus in words sedate yet severe, Kumbhakarma, concluding that Ravana was undelighted, makes his remarks mildly. And seeing his brother extremely sorry, Kumbhakarņa, pacifying him, gently said.

As he was speaking thus in words sedate yet severe, Kumbhakarma, concluding that Ravana was undelighted, makes his remarks mildly. And seeing his brother extremely sorry, Kumbhakarņa, pacifying him, gently said.
O king, intently hear my words. O repressor of foes! O lord of Raksasas, banish this sorrow, and casting away your wrath, return you to nature.
O king, so long as I live, you must not suffer your heart to fare thus. Him will I slay for whom you grieve.

sanskrit: अवश्यं तु हितं वाच्यं सर्वावस्थं मया तव
transliteration: avaśyaṃ tu hitaṃ vācyaṃ sarvāvasthaṃ mayā tava
english: But whatever condition you may be in, I must tell what is for your welfare; and therefore from sentiment of friendship as well as from fraternal affection I have spoken thus to you o King.

sanskrit: सदृशं यत्तु काले ऽस्मिन् कर्तुं स्निग्धेन बन्धुना
शत्रूणां कदनं पश्य क्रियमाणं मया रणे
transliteration: sadṛśaṃ yattu kāle 'smin kartuṃ snigdhena bandhunā
śatrūṇāṃ kadanaṃ paśya kriyamāṇaṃ mayā raṇe
english: What a friend from affection should do at a time like this, I shall do the same. See the havoc I spread among the foes in fight.

sanskrit: हते रामे सह भ्रात्रा द्रवन्तीं परवाहिनीम्
transliteration: hate rāme saha bhrātrā dravantīṃ paravāhinīm
english: O long-armed one, behold, on Rāma having been slain by me on the edge of battle along with his brother, the monkey-army in headlong flight.

sanskrit: अद्य रामस्य तद् दृष्ट्वा मया ऽ ऽनीतं रणाच्छिरः
सुखी भव महाबाहो सीता भवतु दुःखिता
transliteration: adya rāmasya tad dṛṣṭvā mayā ' 'nītaṃ raṇācchiraḥ
sukhī bhava mahābāho sītā bhavatu duḥkhitā
english: And today seeing Rāma's head brought by me from the field, be you, O long-armed one, happy; and let Sitā be overwhelmed with woe.

sanskrit: अद्य रामस्य पश्यन्तु निधनं सुमहत् प्रियम्
लङ्कायां राक्षसाः सर्वे ये ते निहतबान्धवाः
transliteration: adya rāmasya paśyantu nidhanaṃ sumahat priyam
laṅkāyāṃ rākṣasāḥ sarve ye te nihatabāndhavāḥ
english: And let those Raksasas in Lankā who have had their kindred slain (in battle), see that dear sight-Rāma slain (in fight).
Today shall I slaying the enemies in battle, wipe the tears of those who mourn their friend slain and are overwhelmed with grief.
To-day behold the lord of monkeys-Sugrivaresembling a mountain or a mass of clouds lighted up by (the living) sun, lying stretched on the field.
But why, O sinless one, albeit comforted by these Rākşasas eager for saying Dasaratha's son, as well as by me, did your persist in your sorrow?

sanskrit: अथ पूर्वं हते तेन मयि त्वां हन्ति राघवः
transliteration: atha pūrvaṃ hate tena mayi tvāṃ hanti rāghavaḥ
english: Rāghava forsooth shall slay you after slaying me But, O lord of Raksasas, I cannot come by grief (at Rāghava's hands).

sanskrit: कामं त्विदानीमपि मां व्यादिश त्वं परन्तप
transliteration: kāmaṃ tvidānīmapi māṃ vyādiśa tvaṃ parantapa
english: O repressor of foes, do you now command me O you of unparalleled prowess, you need not yourself face the foe in fight.

sanskrit: यदि शक्रो यदि यमो यदि पावकमारुतौ
transliteration: yadi śakro yadi yamo yadi pāvakamārutau
english: I shall abolish your foes endowed with redoubted might. If even Śakra himself, and Yama, and the god of Fire, and the god of Wind, and Kubera, and Varuņa-shall range themselves against me, them shall I encounter in fight.
Purandara himself is seized with fright at sight of me, having a body measuring a mountain, equipped with sharpened spears, furnished with sharp teeth, and setting up shouts.

sanskrit: न मे प्रतिमुखे स्थातुं कश्चिच्छक्तो जिजीविषुः
transliteration: na me pratimukhe sthātuṃ kaścicchakto jijīviṣuḥ
english: And who wishing to save himself shall be able to stay before me as I casting away my weapons keep pounding my enemies with celerity?

sanskrit: नैव शक्त्या न गदया नासिना निशितैः शरैः
transliteration: naiva śaktyā na gadayā nāsinā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: No need of the dart, or the mace, or the sword, or whetted arrows. I shall with my bare arms alone slay (Rāma) along with the thunderer himself.

sanskrit: यदि मे मुष्टिवेगं स राघवो ऽद्य सहिष्यते
ततः पास्यन्ति बाणौघा रुधिरं राघवस्य तु
transliteration: yadi me muṣṭivegaṃ sa rāghavo 'dya sahiṣyate
tataḥ pāsyanti bāṇaughā rudhiraṃ rāghavasya tu
english: If Raghava bear the impetus of my blows, the shall the vollies of my shafts drink his life blood.

sanskrit: चिन्तया बाध्यसे राजन् किमर्थं मयि तिष्ठति
transliteration: cintayā bādhyase rājan kimarthaṃ mayi tiṣṭhati
english: Why, O king, while I remain, did you burn in anxiety. And I am ready to sally out for compassing the destruction of your enemies.

sanskrit: राघवं लक्ष्मणं चैव सुग्रीवं च महाबलम्
हनुमन्तं च रक्षोघ्नं लङ्का येन प्रदीपिता
transliteration: rāghavaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva sugrīvaṃ ca mahābalam
hanumantaṃ ca rakṣoghnaṃ laṅkā yena pradīpitā
english: Cast off all terror of Rāma. I shall slay in battle Rāghava and Lakşmaņa and the exceedingly powerful Sugrīva and the Räksasadestroying Hanumān, who made Lankā blaze. I shall cat up the monkeys present in the encounter. And signal is the celebrity that I shall confer on you.

sanskrit: यदि चेन्द्राद्भयं राजन् यदि वापि स्वयम्भुवः
transliteration: yadi cendrādbhayaṃ rājan yadi vāpi svayambhuvaḥ

sanskrit: अपि देवाः शयिष्यन्ते क्रुद्धे मयि महीतले
transliteration: api devāḥ śayiṣyante kruddhe mayi mahītale
english: O king, if your fear springs from Indra or the Self-create, even the immortals shall measure their lengths on the earth when I am wrought with rage. And I shall subdue Yama himself and devour the God of Fire.

I shall crush the mountains and rive the earth. And today let all creatures as they are being eaten up, witness the prowess of Kumbhakarņa, after he has slept for a long time. Even the celestial regions do not suffice for me as my fare.

sanskrit: वधेन ते दाशरथेः सुखार्हं सुखं समाहर्तुमहं व्रजामि
निहत्य रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन खादामि सर्वान् हरियूथमुख्यान्
transliteration: vadhena te dāśaratheḥ sukhārhaṃ sukhaṃ samāhartumahaṃ vrajāmi
nihatya rāmaṃ saha lakṣmaṇena khādāmi sarvān hariyūthamukhyān
english: I go for securing felicity us huring in pleasures plenteous flowing from the destruction of Dasaratha's son. And slaying Rāma along with Lakşmaņa, I shall eat up all the foremost of monkey-bands.

sanskrit: रमस्व कामं पिब चाग्र्यवारुणीं कुरुष्व कृत्यानि विनीयतां ज्वरः
मया ऽद्य रामे गमिते यमक्षयं चिराय सीता वशगा भविष्यति
transliteration: ramasva kāmaṃ piba cāgryavāruṇīṃ kuruṣva kṛtyāni vinīyatāṃ jvaraḥ
mayā 'dya rāme gamite yamakṣayaṃ cirāya sītā vaśagā bhaviṣyati
english: Make merry, my king; today drink Varuni. Enjoy pleasures, banishing sorrow. And today on my having despatched Rāma to the mansion of Yama, Sītā shall come under your control for good.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe triṣaṣṭitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Hearing the speech of the huge-bodied, longarmed and mighty Kumbhkarma, Mahodara said.

sanskrit: अवलिप्तो न शक्नोषि कृत्यं सर्वत्र वेदितुम्
transliteration: avalipto na śaknoṣi kṛtyaṃ sarvatra veditum
english: O Kumbhakarņa, although sprung in a noble line, you are wondrous haughty and of a vulgar form; and you are not everywhere competent to discern your course.

sanskrit: न हि राजा न जानीते कुम्भकर्ण नयानयौ
transliteration: na hi rājā na jānīte kumbhakarṇa nayānayau
english: It certainly cannot well be that the king cannot distinguish between proper and improper; but you has from your youth upwards been insolent; and your joy is in talking perenially.

sanskrit: स्थानं वृद्धिं च हानिं च देशकालविभागवित्
transliteration: sthānaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca hāniṃ ca deśakālavibhāgavit
english: But the foremost of the Raksasa is versed in place and increase and injury, and know the duties touching season and place, and how to advance his own party and lower that of the foe.
But what person ever act according to what is proposed feebly by one having strength, yet of inferior intelligence, and who has never respected the aged.
You are not naturally competent to understand what you yourself says touching the opposed virtue, profit and desire.

sanskrit: कर्म चैव हि सर्वेषां कारणानां प्रयोजकम्
श्रेयः पापीयसां चात्र फलं भवति कर्मणाम्
transliteration: karma caiva hi sarveṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ prayojakam
śreyaḥ pāpīyasāṃ cātra phalaṃ bhavati karmaṇām

sanskrit: तत्र क्लृप्तमिदं राज्ञा हृदि कार्यं मतं च नः
शत्रौ हि साहसं यत् स्यात् किमिवात्रापनीयताम्
transliteration: tatra klṛptamidaṃ rājñā hṛdi kāryaṃ mataṃ ca naḥ
śatrau hi sāhasaṃ yat syāt kimivātrāpanīyatām

english: Did you show the reasons for your taking the field alone? But I shall point you out what is improper and unreasonable in this (proposed) course.

sanskrit: येन पूर्वं जनस्थाने बहवो ऽतिबला हताः
राक्षसा राघवं तं त्वं कथमेको जयिष्यसि
transliteration: rākṣasā rāghavaṃ taṃ tvaṃ kathameko jayiṣyasi
english: How shall you alone vanquish that Rāghava who formerly routed in Jansthāna innumerable Rākşasas possessed of exceeding strength?
Did you not today in the palace behold those powerful Rākşasas that had been beaten in Janasthana-cowed down in fear?
Alas! you wished to awake Rima, son to Daśaratha-knowing full well that le resembles an enraged lion or a sleeping serpeni.

sanskrit: ज्वलन्तं तेजसा नित्यं क्रोधेन च दुरासदम्
transliteration: jvalantaṃ tejasā nityaṃ krodhena ca durāsadam
english: But whom does it behove to confront him ever flaming in energy, difficult of being approached when enraged, and unbearable even like Death himself?

sanskrit: एकस्य गमनं तत्र नहि मे रोचते भृशम्
transliteration: ekasya gamanaṃ tatra nahi me rocate bhṛśam
english: On approaching the foe, this whole host itself shall be imperilled: and therefore, my child, your marching alone does nowise recommend itself to me.

sanskrit: हीनार्थः सुसमृद्धार्थं को रिपुं प्राकृतं यथा
transliteration: hīnārthaḥ susamṛddhārthaṃ ko ripuṃ prākṛtaṃ yathā
english: Who is there that, albeit weak bent on renouncing his life, wish to bring under subjection a foe that is powerful, as if he would act with reference to one that is inferior?
O foremost of Rākasas, why did you wish to fight with him whose peer there is none among men, and who is equal to Indra and Vavasvata himself?
Having said this to Kumbhakarņa wrought up with wrath, Mahodara addressed that destroyer of creature-Ravana-in the midst of the Raksasas.

sanskrit: यदीच्छसि तदा सीता वशगा ते भविष्यति
transliteration: yadīcchasi tadā sītā vaśagā te bhaviṣyati
english: Having already obtained Vaidehi, why did you delay ? If you wish it, Sītā shall come under your control.

sanskrit: रुचिरश्चेत् स्वया बुद्ध्या राक्षसेश्वर तं शृणु
transliteration: ruciraścet svayā buddhyā rākṣaseśvara taṃ śṛṇu
english: I have perceived a way as to how Sītā may smile upon you. Do you listen: and should it please you; act you accordingly.
Do you proclaim it about that I and Dvijihva and Samhrādī, and Kumbhakarņa and Vitardanathese five-are marching for compassing the destruction of Rāma.

sanskrit: ततो गत्वा वयं युद्धं दास्यामस्तस्य यत्नतः
जेष्यामो यदि ते शत्रून्नोपायैः कृत्यमस्ति नः
transliteration: tato gatvā vayaṃ yuddhaṃ dāsyāmastasya yatnataḥ
jeṣyāmo yadi te śatrūnnopāyaiḥ kṛtyamasti naḥ
english: We, marching out, shall battle with Rāma, putting forth our uttermost. And if we succeed in securing victory, no expedient need we resort to (or bringing Sītā round).

sanskrit: अथ जीवति नः शत्रुर्वयं च कृतसंयुगाः
transliteration: atha jīvati naḥ śatrurvayaṃ ca kṛtasaṃyugāḥ
english: But if our foe live after fight and we also having faught the fight, then shall we do what I conceive in my mind.

We shall come hither from the field, bathed in blood, and having our bodies cleft with arrows marked with the name of Rama. And we shall give out that both Ráma and Lakşmaņa have been eaten up by us And then we Shall hold your feet, saying, 'Do you gratify us'.

sanskrit: तव पादौ ग्रहीष्यामस्त्वं नः कामं प्रपूरय
transliteration: tava pādau grahīṣyāmastvaṃ naḥ kāmaṃ prapūraya
english: We shall come hither from the field, bathed in blood, and having our bodies cleft with arrows marked with the name of Rama. And we shall give out that both Ráma and Lakşmaņa have been eaten up by us And then we Shall hold your feet, saying, 'Do you gratify us'.

sanskrit: हतो रामः सह भ्रात्रा ससैन्य इति सर्वतः
transliteration: hato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā sasainya iti sarvataḥ
english: Then, O king, do you through Gajaskandha publish it all round that Ráma has been slain along with his brother and the army.

sanskrit: प्रीतो नाम ततो भूत्वा भृत्यानां त्वमरिन्दम
transliteration: prīto nāma tato bhūtvā bhṛtyānāṃ tvamarindama
english: O repressor of foes, (pretending to be) well pleased, do you dispense-viands, and servants, and objects of enjoyments, and wealth to your retainers; and to the many heroes and warriors distribute wreaths and attires and unguents. And do you (Simulating) delight drink.

sanskrit: पेयं च बहु योधेभ्यः स्वयं च मुदितः पिब
transliteration: peyaṃ ca bahu yodhebhyaḥ svayaṃ ca muditaḥ piba
english: O repressor of foes, (pretending to be) well pleased, do you dispense-viands, and servants, and objects of enjoyments, and wealth to your retainers; and to the many heroes and warriors distribute wreaths and attires and unguents. And do you (Simulating) delight drink.

sanskrit: ततो ऽस्मिन् बहुलीभूते कौलीने सर्वतो गते
english: On this report-name that Rāma has been eaten up by the Rākşasas along with his friends, having spread round and round entering (the Asoka wood), and soothing and pacifying Sītā in solitude, Allure her with corn and riches and gems.

sanskrit: प्रविश्याश्वास्य चापि त्वं सीतां रहसि सान्त्वय
transliteration: praviśyāśvāsya cāpi tvaṃ sītāṃ rahasi sāntvaya
english: On this report-name that Rāma has been eaten up by the Rākşasas along with his friends, having spread round and round entering (the Asoka wood), and soothing and pacifying Sītā in solitude, Allure her with corn and riches and gems.
By this deceit, О king, working powerfully through Sītā's sorrow, she albeit unwilling, shall, having lost her lord, come under your control.
Losing her charming husband, she from despair and female railty, shall come under your away.

Having formerly been brought up in happiness, she, although worthy of felicity, (ultimately) had come by misfortune. And now finding happiness to be in your custody, she shall unreservedly come over to you.

sanskrit: एतत् सुनीतं मम दर्शनेन रामं हि दृष्ट्वैव भवेदनर्थः
इहैव ते सेत्स्यति मोत्सुको भूर्महानयुद्धेन सुखस्य लाभः
transliteration: etat sunītaṃ mama darśanena rāmaṃ hi dṛṣṭvaiva bhavedanarthaḥ
ihaiva te setsyati motsuko bhūrmahānayuddhena sukhasya lābhaḥ
english: In my opinion this is the proper course to follow. As soon as you see Rāma, evil shall befall you. Remain here. Do not wish (to go to the field). By refraining from fight, you shall acquire great good.

sanskrit: यशश्च पुण्यं च महन्महीपते श्रियं च कीर्तिं च चिरं समश्नुते
transliteration: yaśaśca puṇyaṃ ca mahanmahīpate śriyaṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca ciraṃ samaśnute
english: O lord of people, by conquering the foe without battle, you without losing your forces and putting yourself to peril, you, O lord of earth, shall attain fame and high religious merit, and prosperity and renown for ever and for ever.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे चतुष्षष्ठितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe catuṣṣaṣṭhitamaḥ sargaḥ

transliteration: atha pūrvaṃ hate tena mayi tvāṃ hanti rāghavaḥ

transliteration: kāmaṃ tvidānīmapi māṃ vyādiśa tvaṃ parantapa

transliteration: yadi śakro yadi yamo yadi pāvakamārutau

transliteration: na me pratimukhe sthātuṃ kaścicchakto jijīviṣuḥ

transliteration: api devāḥ śayiṣyante kruddhe mayi mahītale

निहत्य रामं सह लक्ष्मणेन खादामि सर्वान् हरियूथमुख्यान्
transliteration: vadhena te dāśaratheḥ sukhārhaṃ sukhaṃ samāhartumahaṃ vrajāmi
nihatya rāmaṃ saha lakṣmaṇena khādāmi sarvān hariyūthamukhyān

sanskrit: रमस्व कामं पिब चाग्र्यवारुणीं कुरुष्व कृत्यानि विनीयतां ज्वरः
मया ऽद्य रामे गमिते यमक्षयं चिराय सीता वशगा भविष्यति
transliteration: ramasva kāmaṃ piba cāgryavāruṇīṃ kuruṣva kṛtyāni vinīyatāṃ jvaraḥ
mayā 'dya rāme gamite yamakṣayaṃ cirāya sītā vaśagā bhaviṣyati

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe triṣaṣṭitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Thus addressed, Kumbhakarņa rebuking Mahodara, said to that foremost of Rākşasa-his brother-Ravana.

sanskrit: सो ऽहं तव भयं घोरं वधात्तस्य दुरात्मनः
रामस्याद्य प्रमार्जामि निर्वैरो हि सुखी भव
transliteration: so 'haṃ tava bhayaṃ ghoraṃ vadhāttasya durātmanaḥ
rāmasyādya pramārjāmi nirvairo hi sukhī bhava
english: Even I shall remove your great fear by slaying the wicked minded Råma. On your foe having been slain, attain you ease.

sanskrit: गर्जन्ति न वृथा शूरा निर्जला इव तोयदाः
पश्य सम्पाद्यमानं तु गर्जितं युधि कर्मणा
transliteration: garjanti na vṛthā śūrā nirjalā iva toyadāḥ
paśya sampādyamānaṃ tu garjitaṃ yudhi karmaṇā
english: It is not for naught that the heroes roar, like to clouds containing no rain. Behold you their, like roaring resulting in action in the field!
Heroes do not vaunt: but without boasting of their prowess in speech, they perform feats difficult of being achieved.
O Mahodara, what you say is ever acceptable only to kings that are incompetent, and foolish, pluming themselves on their knowledge.

All the affairs of the monarch have been wrecked by you-cravens in fight, sleek-tongued, following the king (fawning) you have made Lankā contain only the king, the treasury is lean; and the forces have been slain. By the king you have done like foes in the guise of friends.

sanskrit: राजशेषा कृता लङ्का क्षीणः कोशो बलं हतम्
transliteration: rājaśeṣā kṛtā laṅkā kṣīṇaḥ kośo balaṃ hatam
english: All the affairs of the monarch have been wrecked by you-cravens in fight, sleek-tongued, following the king (fawning) you have made Lankā contain only the king, the treasury is lean; and the forces have been slain. By the king you have done like foes in the guise of friends.
For repairing in mighty conflict the wrong that you have perpetrated, I am about to set out for battle for routing the enemy.
Thus addressed by the intelligent Kumbhakarna, the lord of Raksasas, laughing answered.

sanskrit: महोदरो ऽयं रामात्तु परित्रस्तो न संशयः
न हि रोचयते तात युद्धं युद्धविशारद
transliteration: na hi rocayate tāta yuddhaṃ yuddhaviśārada
english: Sure this Mahodara is affrighted at Rāma. Therefore, my child, O you versed in warfare, he does not relish battle.

sanskrit: कश्चिन्मे त्वत्समो नास्ति सौहृदेन बलेन च
गच्छ शत्रुवधाय त्वं कुम्भकर्ण जयाय च
transliteration: kaścinme tvatsamo nāsti sauhṛdena balena ca
gaccha śatruvadhāya tvaṃ kumbhakarṇa jayāya ca
english: Like you have I none either in friendship or strength. Therefore, O Kumbhakama, go for destroying the foe and securing celebrity.
I have waked you up that wast lying down, in order that you mightst destroy the enemy. O subduer of foes, perilous is the time for the Rāks asas.
Go forth, grasping your spear, like the noosehanded Destroyer himself. Do you devour up the monkeys as well as the princes possessed of the energy of the Sun himself.

sanskrit: समालोक्य तु ते रूपं विद्रविष्यन्ति वानराः
transliteration: samālokya tu te rūpaṃ vidraviṣyanti vānarāḥ
english: On seeing your form the monkeys shall flee away; and the breasts of Rāma and Lakşmaņa shall be riven.
Having spoken thus to Kumbhakarna endowed with prodigious might, that foremost of Rakşasas-the exceedingly energetic Rāvaņa-felt as if he had received life over again.

sanskrit: बभूव मुदितो राजा शशाङ्क इव निर्मलः
transliteration: babhūva mudito rājā śaśāṅka iva nirmalaḥ
english: And well acquainted with Kumbhakarņa's might, and knowing his prowess, the king felt delighted, like the cloudless Moon.
Having been thus accosted, that highly powerful one, went out cheerfully. And hearing the king's speech, he made ready for fight.
Today hungry and enraged, I shall devour up the monkeys. Hearing Kumbhakarma's words. Rāvana said.

sanskrit: अद्य तान् क्षुभितान् क्रुद्धो भक्षयिष्यामि वानरान्
transliteration: adya tān kṣubhitān kruddho bhakṣayiṣyāmi vānarān
english: Today hungry and enraged, I shall devour up the monkeys. Hearing Kumbhakarma's words. Rāvana said.

Go you surrounded by the forces bearing darts and maces in their hands. The monkeys are highsouled, heroic and well-skilled in battle; and if they find you alone or unwary, they may slay you with their teeth, Therefore do you exceedingly irresistible, go, environed by the forces; and destroy the entire party of the foes, who are bent upon doing harm to the Rākşasa.

Go you surrounded by the forces bearing darts and maces in their hands. The monkeys are highsouled, heroic and well-skilled in battle; and if they find you alone or unwary, they may slay you with their teeth, Therefore do you exceedingly irresistible, go, environed by the forces; and destroy the entire party of the foes, who are bent upon doing harm to the Rākşasa.
Then starting up form his seat, the exceedingly energetic Rāvana hung on Kumbhakarņa's neck a wreath stringed with gems in the centre.
Rāvaņa also decked that high-souled one with Angadas, and finger fences and noble ornaments, and a chain resembling the Moon.

Rāvaņa adorned his person with garlands gorgeous and fragrant, and set ear-rings to his ears. And adorned with golden Angadas and Keyūras and other ornaments of gold, the largeeared Kumbhakarņa appeared like a fire fed full of sacrificial libations.

Rāvaņa adorned his person with garlands gorgeous and fragrant, and set ear-rings to his ears. And adorned with golden Angadas and Keyūras and other ornaments of gold, the largeeared Kumbhakarņa appeared like a fire fed full of sacrificial libations.
With his great dark girdle he seemed like the Mandara fastened by the serpent on the occasion of the churning of the sea.

sanskrit: स काञ्चनं भारसहं निवातं विद्युत्प्रभं दीप्तमिवात्मभासा
transliteration: sa kāñcanaṃ bhārasahaṃ nivātaṃ vidyutprabhaṃ dīptamivātmabhāsā
english: Donning on his impenetrable golden mail, splendid like lightning, and shining in its own brilliance, Kumbhakarņa appeared like the monarch of mountains enveloped with evening clouds.

Having all his limbs adorned with ornaments and bearing a dart in his hand, the Rakşasas resembled Nārāyaṇa in elation of spirits, when he covered heaven and earth and the nether regions with three paces.
Then embracing his brother and going round him and bowing down the head to him, that exceedingly powerful one went out.
And high-souled mighty warriors followed that foremost of heroes with elephant and steeds and chariots sending out rattle resembling the rumbling of thunder.
And mounting serpents and camels and asses and lions and leopards and deer and birds, (Rāks asas) followed the grim Kumbhakarņa endowed with tremendous strength.
And strewn with blossoms, and, with an umbrella held over him, that exceedingly terrible enemy of the Deities and the Dănvas, wielding a dz.: in his hand-went out maddened with the smell of blood.
Countless footmen wondrous powerful and mighty and dreadful and fierce-sighted Räksasas, carrying weapons in their hands, went in his wake.

The Räkşasa measuring each many a vyama and red, eyed, and resembling masses of darkblue collyrium, went out upraising darts and swords and sharpened axes and bhindipälas and parighas and maces and huge talaskandhas and irrisistible Kșepaņis.

The Räkşasa measuring each many a vyama and red, eyed, and resembling masses of darkblue collyrium, went out upraising darts and swords and sharpened axes and bhindipälas and parighas and maces and huge talaskandhas and irrisistible Kșepaņis.
The exceedingly energetic Kumbhakarna endowed with prodigious strength sallied forth, assuming another form terrific and dreadful to behold.
But the wood-ranging monkeys have not transgressed anywise to the like of us. That species is the ornament of the gardens attached to our residences.

sanskrit: हते तस्मिन् हतं सर्वं तं वधिष्यामि संयुगे
transliteration: hate tasmin hataṃ sarvaṃ taṃ vadhiṣyāmi saṃyuge
english: The cause of the siege of the city is Rāghava along with Laksmana. He being slain, all are slain. Therefore shall I slay him in battle.
As the Rākşa—Kumbhakarņa—was speaking thus, the Rākşasas sent up terrific shouts, as if making the very sea shake.
As the intelligent Kumbhakarņa sallied out speedily, dreadful were the omens that presented themselves on all sides.
Clouds containing meteors and lightning looked dark like asses. And the earth shook with her oceans and woods.
And fierce jackals began to cry, opening their fiaming mouths. And birds began to wheel at the left.

sanskrit: निष्पपात च मालेव गृध्रो ऽस्य पथि गच्छतः
transliteration: niṣpapāta ca māleva gṛdhro 'sya pathi gacchataḥ
english: As he marched a vulture alighted on his dart. And his left eye throbbed and his left arm shook.
A meteor dropped down with a tremendous crash. And the sun was bedimmed, and the air did not blow, enhancing pleasure.
But without heeding these mighty omens that took place, capable of making people's down stand on end, Kumbhakarna went out, urged on by the force of the Finisher.
And leaping over the wall with his legs, that one resembling a mountain saw the wonderful array of the monkeys, resembling clouds.

sanskrit: वायुनुन्ना इव घना ययुः सर्वा दिशस्तदा
transliteration: vāyununnā iva ghanā yayuḥ sarvā diśastadā
english: Seeing that foremost of Rākşasas resembling a hill, the monkeys began to disperse in all the ten cardinal directions like clouds driven by the wind.

sanskrit: स कुम्भकर्णः समवेक्ष्य हर्षान्ननाद भूयो घनवद् घनाभः
transliteration: sa kumbhakarṇaḥ samavekṣya harṣānnanāda bhūyo ghanavad ghanābhaḥ
english: Seeing that terrific host of monkeys scattering in all directions, like clouds broken through (by winds), Kumbhakarņa possessed the splendour of clouds, from joy, emitted roars like clouds.

sanskrit: ते तस्य घोरं निनदं निशम्य यथा निनादं दिवि वारिदस्य
पेतुर्धरण्यां बहवः प्लवङ्गा निकृत्तमूला इव सालवृक्षाः
transliteration: te tasya ghoraṃ ninadaṃ niśamya yathā ninādaṃ divi vāridasya
peturdharaṇyāṃ bahavaḥ plavaṅgā nikṛttamūlā iva sālavṛkṣāḥ
english: Hearing those terrible shouts like to the roaring of clouds in the welkin, innumerable monkeys dropped to the earth even as sāla trees that have their roots severed.

sanskrit: विपुलपरिघवान् स कुम्भकर्णो रिपुनिधनाय विनिस्सृतो महात्मा
transliteration: vipulaparighavān sa kumbhakarṇo ripunidhanāya vinissṛto mahātmā
english: And issuing forth for destroying the foe, the high-souled Kumbhakarņa, equipped with a tremendous bludgeon, struck extreme terror into the monkey-ranks, like to the Lord armed with the Fatal rod at the Universal wreck.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe pañcaṣaṣṭitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Having leapt over the wall, the exceedingly powerful and gigantic Kumbhakarņa resembling a mountain-summit, speedily went out of the city.
Then he sent up a mighty shout making the sea resound, and as if drowning the roar of the thunder and riving mountains.
Seeing that fierce-eyed one, incapable of being vanquished by Maghavān or Varuņa or Yama, the monkeys began to fly away.

sanskrit: तांस्तु विप्रद्रुतान् दृष्ट्वा वालिपुत्रो ऽङ्गदो ऽब्रवीत्
नलं नीलं गवाक्षं च कुमुदं च महाबलम्
transliteration: nalaṃ nīlaṃ gavākṣaṃ ca kumudaṃ ca mahābalam
english: Seeing them scamper, the king's son-Angada said to Nala and Nīla and Gavākșa and the mighty Kumuda.

sanskrit: क्व गच्छत भयत्रस्ताः प्राकृता हरयो यथा
transliteration: kva gacchata bhayatrastāḥ prākṛtā harayo yathā
english: Forgetting your lineage and prowess, whither do you, exercised with fear, fly-like inferior monkeys?

sanskrit: साधु सौम्या निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान् परिरक्षथ
नालं युद्धाय वै रक्षो महतीयं बिभीषिका
transliteration: sādhu saumyā nivartadhvaṃ kiṃ prāṇān parirakṣatha
nālaṃ yuddhāya vai rakṣo mahatīyaṃ bibhīṣikā
english: You amiable ones, desist. Why should you save yourselves? This Rākşasa does not come to fight, this is only a great phenomenon to affright.
We shall by our vigour destroy this featful phenomenon of the Rākşasas that has presented itself. Therefore, let the monkeys desist.

sanskrit: कृच्छ्रेण तु समाश्वस्य सङ्गम्य च ततस्ततः
transliteration: kṛcchreṇa tu samāśvasya saṅgamya ca tatastataḥ
english: Cheered with much ado, the monkeys rallying, took up trees and advanced to the field of fight.

sanskrit: ते निवृत्य तु सङ्क्रुद्धाः कुम्भकर्णं वनौकसः
transliteration: te nivṛtya tu saṅkruddhāḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ vanaukasaḥ
english: Ceasing from flight, the wood-rangers waxing, enraged, began to assail Kumbhakarņa, like to elephants in rut. And the exceedingly strong Kumbhakarna, attacked with towering mountain peaks and crags and trees with flowering top, did not shake.

Ceasing from flight, the wood-rangers waxing, enraged, began to assail Kumbhakarņa, like to elephants in rut. And the exceedingly strong Kumbhakarna, attacked with towering mountain peaks and crags and trees with flowering top, did not shake.

sanskrit: तस्य गात्रेषु पतिता भिद्यन्ते शतशः शिलाः
transliteration: tasya gātreṣu patitā bhidyante śataśaḥ śilāḥ
english: And countless crags descending on his person, were shattered; and trees with flowering tops, being broken, fell down to the earth.

sanskrit: सो ऽपि सैन्यानि सङ्क्रुद्धो वानराणां महौजसाम्
english: Incapable of containing himself (through rage), Kumbhakarņa on his part fell to agitating the ranks of the powerful monkeys, even as a fire breaking out burn dowit a forest.

sanskrit: निरस्ताः पतिता भूमौ ताम्रपुष्पा इव द्रुमाः
transliteration: nirastāḥ patitā bhūmau tāmrapuṣpā iva drumāḥ
english: Many a prime monkey, crimsoned and drenched (with blood) lay down (on the ground); and many, resisted dropped to the earth, like trees bearing coppery flowers.
Without looking before or after, the monkeys bounded and rushed. And on being attacked by the Rāksasa with ease some of those heroes dropped into the deep and some entered the wilderness.

sanskrit: सागरं येन ते तीर्णाः पथा तेन प्रदुद्रुवुः
transliteration: sāgaraṃ yena te tīrṇāḥ pathā tena pradudruvuḥ

sanskrit: ते स्थलानि तथा निम्नं विषण्णवदना भयात्
transliteration: te sthalāni tathā nimnaṃ viṣaṇṇavadanā bhayāt
english: Some ran by the same way by which they had crossed the ocean; and some with pale faces darted into downs. And some of the bears ascended up trees, and some took shelter in mountains.

sanskrit: भग्नानां वो न पश्यामि परिगम्य महीमिमाम्
स्थानं सर्वे निवर्तध्वं किं प्राणान् परिरक्षथ
transliteration: bhagnānāṃ vo na paśyāmi parigamya mahīmimām
sthānaṃ sarve nivartadhvaṃ kiṃ prāṇān parirakṣatha
english: Desist, you monkeys. Going round this Earth place find I none where you may rest. Stop you all. What is the need of preserving your lives.

sanskrit: दारा ह्यपहसिष्यन्ति स वै घातस्तु जीविनाम्
transliteration: dārā hyapahasiṣyanti sa vai ghātastu jīvinām
english: You poltroons, if you fly away leaving your arms behind, your wives shall deride you; and that is more painful to honourable persons than death itself.

sanskrit: कुलेषु जाताः सर्वे स्म विस्तीर्णेषु महत्सु च
क्व गच्छथ भयत्रस्ता हरयः प्राकृता यथा
transliteration: kuleṣu jātāḥ sarve sma vistīrṇeṣu mahatsu ca
kva gacchatha bhayatrastā harayaḥ prākṛtā yathā
english: Born in long and noble lines, whither go you, suffering from fear, like abject monkeys? When renouncing your prowess, you fly away in fear, forsooth you are base.
Born in long and noble lines, whither go you, suffering from fear, like abject monkeys? When renouncing your prowess, you fly away in fear, forsooth you are base.

sanskrit: विकत्थनानि वो यानि तदा वै जनसंसदि
तानि वः क्व नु यातानि सोदग्राणि महान्ति च
transliteration: vikatthanāni vo yāni tadā vai janasaṃsadi
tāni vaḥ kva nu yātāni sodagrāṇi mahānti ca
english: Where now is gone that talk of your anent your nobility and the welfare (of your king) which you had held in society.
He that live, despised (of all), hear the reproach of being a craven. Therefore do you follow the way frequented by the worthy, and cast off fear.

sanskrit: दुष्प्रापं ब्रह्मलोकं वा प्राप्नुमो युधि सूदिताः
transliteration: duṣprāpaṃ brahmalokaṃ vā prāpnumo yudhi sūditāḥ

english: We will either lie down on the earth, being slain in consequence of our shortness of days, and thus attain the region of Brahmä incapable of being attained by dastards; or achieve renown by slaying the foe in fight and slain in battle, we shall enjoy the wealth of the region of heroes.

sanskrit: न कुम्भकर्णः काकुत्स्थं दृष्ट्वा जीवन् गमिष्यति
transliteration: na kumbhakarṇaḥ kākutsthaṃ dṛṣṭvā jīvan gamiṣyati
english: Like an insect coming to a glowing and flaming fire, Kumbhakarna, seeing Kākutstha, shall not away.hence living.

sanskrit: एकेन बहवो भग्ना यशो नाशं गमिष्यति
transliteration: ekena bahavo bhagnā yaśo nāśaṃ gamiṣyati
english: If we save our lives by flight, and if the many are brought down by one, we shall lose our fame utterly.
As Angada decked in golden angadas was saying this, the monkeys, flying away spoke to that hero words not worthy of being spoken to an hero.

sanskrit: कृतं नः कदनं घोरं कुम्भकर्णेन रक्षसा
न स्थानकालो गच्छामो दयितं जीवितं हि नः
transliteration: kṛtaṃ naḥ kadanaṃ ghoraṃ kumbhakarṇena rakṣasā
na sthānakālo gacchāmo dayitaṃ jīvitaṃ hi naḥ
english: Great is the havoc that the Rākşasa-Kumbhakarma-has spread among us. “This not the time to stay: life is dear to us."

sanskrit: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं सर्वे ते भेजिरे दिशः
transliteration: etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ sarve te bhejire diśaḥ
english: Having said this the monkey bands darted to the ten cardinal points, as they saw that dreadful and grim-eyed one approach.
As those flower of the forces were on the flight, those heroes were made to desist by Angada with words of comfort and hope pointing to the future.
On being cheered by the intelligent son of Vāli, all the monkey-bands stood expecting his commands.
Rşabha, Sarabha, Mainda, Dhūmra, Nila, Kumuda, Susena, Gavaksa, Rambha, Dvivida, Panasa, and son of wind Hanuman and other powerf:! leaders speedily proceeded to the battle field.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe ṣaṭṣaṣṭitamaḥ sargaḥ

sanskrit: हते तस्मिन् हतं सर्वं तं वधिष्यामि संयुगे
transliteration: hate tasmin hataṃ sarvaṃ taṃ vadhiṣyāmi saṃyuge

sanskrit: निष्पपात च मालेव गृध्रो ऽस्य पथि गच्छतः
transliteration: niṣpapāta ca māleva gṛdhro 'sya pathi gacchataḥ

sanskrit: वायुनुन्ना इव घना ययुः सर्वा दिशस्तदा
transliteration: vāyununnā iva ghanā yayuḥ sarvā diśastadā

sanskrit: स कुम्भकर्णः समवेक्ष्य हर्षान्ननाद भूयो घनवद् घनाभः

peturdharaṇyāṃ bahavaḥ plavaṅgā nikṛttamūlā iva sālavṛkṣāḥ

transliteration: vipulaparighavān sa kumbhakarṇo ripunidhanāya vinissṛto mahātmā

english: Having desisted on hearing the words of Angada those huge-bodied ones, regaining calmness, became (again) intent on fight.
Inspired with spirits, the monkeys, determined to face their fate, rushed into the conflict, and, casting away all care for their lives, entered into a furious fight (with the foe)

sanskrit: अथ वृक्षान् महाकायाः सानूनि सुमहान्ति च
transliteration: atha vṛkṣān mahākāyāḥ sānūni sumahānti ca
english: And speedily upraising trees and gigantic crags, the huge-bodied monkeys charged Kumbhakarņa.
Thereat the mighty Kumbhakarņa possessed of a prodigious person waxing wroth taking up his mace let the same alight on the enemies.

sanskrit: शतानि सप्त चाष्टौ च सहस्राणि च वानराः
transliteration: śatāni sapta cāṣṭau ca sahasrāṇi ca vānarāḥ
english: Attacked by Kumbhakarma, seven, eight hundreds and thousands of monkeys measure their lengths on the earth.

sanskrit: षोडशाष्टौ च दश च विंशत्ऺित्रंशत्तथैव च
transliteration: ṣoḍaśāṣṭau ca daśa ca viṃśattraṃśattathaiva ca
english: Casting about his arms, he rush on, devouring sixteen, eight, ten, twenty or thirty. And he devoured (the monkeys) like Garuda swallowing up serpents.

sanskrit: कृच्छ्रेण च समाश्वस्ताः सङ्गम्य च ततस्ततः
transliteration: kṛcchreṇa ca samāśvastāḥ saṅgamya ca tatastataḥ
english: Then cheered up with much ado, the monkeys meeting together, and taking trees and rocks in their hands, stood their ground in the van of battle.
Then uprooting a crag, Dvivide-foremost of monkeys-resembling an extended mass of clouds rushed against (Kumbhakarņa) having the aspect of a mountain-summit.
And uprooting it, the monkey hurled it at Kumbhakarņa. And without descending on him, the crag fell down amidst the army, and smashed steeds and elephants and cans and choice chargers.
And uprooting it, the monkey hurled it at Kumbhakarņa. And without descending on him, the crag fell down amidst the army, and smashed steeds and elephants and cans and choice chargers.
The high-souled monkeys also, uprooting gaints trees, destroyed cars and horses and elephants and camels and Raksasas
And remaining in the sky, Hanumān discharged at Kumbhakarņa's head mountainpeaks and rocks and various trees.

sanskrit: तानि पर्वतशृङ्गाणि शूलेन स बिभेद ह
transliteration: tāni parvataśṛṅgāṇi śūlena sa bibheda ha
english: And all those mountain-tops he cut off with his dart; and the mighty Kumbhakarņa also baffled the shower of trees.

sanskrit: ततो हरीणां तदनीकमुग्रं दुद्राव शूलं निशितं प्रगृह्य
तस्थौ ततो ऽस्यापततः पुरस्तान्महीधराग्रं हनुमान् प्रगृह्य
transliteration: tato harīṇāṃ tadanīkamugraṃ dudrāva śūlaṃ niśitaṃ pragṛhya
english: Then grasping his sharpened spear, Kumbhakarņa darted against that terrific array of monkeys. And as he charged them, Hanuman armed with a mountain-peak, stood before him.

sanskrit: स कुम्भकर्णं कुपितो जघान वेगेन शैलोत्तमभीमकायम्
स चुक्षुभे तेन तदा ऽभिभूतो मेदार्द्रगात्रो रुधिरावसिक्तः
transliteration: sa kumbhakarṇaṃ kupito jaghāna vegena śailottamabhīmakāyam
sa cukṣubhe tena tadā 'bhibhūto medārdragātro rudhirāvasiktaḥ
english: Waxing enraged (Hanuman) vehemently smote Kumbhakarņa with a gigantic crag. And overpowered by that, Kumbhakarna experienced great torments, and his body was covered with fat and blood.

sanskrit: स शूलमाविध्य तडित्प्रकाशं गिरिं यथा प्रज्वलिताग्रशृङ्गम्
transliteration: sa śūlamāvidhya taḍitprakāśaṃ giriṃ yathā prajvalitāgraśṛṅgam
english: Then as Guha had pierced Krauñca with his fierce dart, Kumbhakarna the mountain-like smote the Wind-god's son in the chest with his dart resembling lightning or like a glowing mountain-summit.

And having his mighty chest pierced in the mighty encounter, Hanumān, overwhelmed, and vomiting blood-transported with wrath, set up roars resembling the roaring of the clouds at the universal disruption.

sanskrit: ततो विनेदुः सहसा प्रहृष्टा रक्षोगणास्तं व्यथितं समीक्ष्य
प्लवङ्गमास्तु व्यथिता भयार्ताः प्रदुद्रुवुः संयति कुम्भकर्णात्
transliteration: tato vineduḥ sahasā prahṛṣṭā rakṣogaṇāstaṃ vyathitaṃ samīkṣya
plavaṅgamāstu vyathitā bhayārtāḥ pradudruvuḥ saṃyati kumbhakarṇāt
