sanskrit: पपात सहसा चैव ध्वजस्तस्य च रक्षसः
transliteration: papāta sahasā caiva dhvajastasya ca rakṣasaḥ
english: And all on a sudden the reins slipped off (the hands of) the charioteer and the flag of the Råkşasas dropped down.
The course of the steeds was thus slackened and they began to move slowly and poorly with their heads drooping down.
There blew a terribly rough wind mixed with dust when the fearfully wicked-minded Makaraksa's issued out for battle.

sanskrit: अचिन्त्य निर्गताः सर्वे यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: acintya nirgatāḥ sarve yatra tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Those powerful Rākşasas neglecting those bad omens proceeded towards where Rāma and Laksmana were.

They were all black like to clouds, elephants and buffaloes, and had marks of swords and maces on their persons. And all those nightrangers were skilled in the art of warfare and began to range to and fro (in the battle field) saying, “I shall to first.”

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे अष्टसप्ततितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe aṣṭasaptatitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Beholding Makarākṣa out for battle, those foremost monkeys leaping on a sudden, addressed themselves for fight.
Thereupon ensued a terrible conflict, capable of making one's down stand on end, between the right-rangers and the monkeys like to one between the celestials and Dänavas.
Those monkeys and night-rangers crushed each other down with trees, darts, maces and parighas.

Those night-rangers began to assail those foremost of monkeys with sakti.' swords, maces, kuntas, tomaras, pattisas, Bhindipālas, arrows, nooses and clubs. 1. A short arrow thrown from the hand or shot through a tube. 2. An Iron spear or dart.

Those night-rangers began to assail those foremost of monkeys with sakti.' swords, maces, kuntas, tomaras, pattisas, Bhindipālas, arrows, nooses and clubs. 1. A short arrow thrown from the hand or shot through a tube. 2. An Iron spear or dart.
Being thus assailed with fearful arrows by Khara's son, those monkeys, stricken with fear, fled away.

sanskrit: तान् दृष्ट्वा राक्षसाः सर्वे द्रवमाणान् वलीमुखान्
transliteration: tān dṛṣṭvā rākṣasāḥ sarve dravamāṇān valīmukhān
english: Beholding those monkeys fly away, all the victorious Rakşasas began to roar like excited lions.
The monkeys thus flying away to all quarters, Rāma with a downpour of shafts assailed the Räkşasas.
Beholding the Rākşasas thus overpowered, the night-ranger Makarākşa, excited with the flame of ire, said.

sanskrit: तिष्ठ राम मया सार्धं द्वन्द्वयुद्धं ददामि ते
त्याजयिष्यामि ते प्राणान् धनुर्मुक्तैः शितैः शरैः
transliteration: tiṣṭha rāma mayā sārdhaṃ dvandvayuddhaṃ dadāmi te
tyājayiṣyāmi te prāṇān dhanurmuktaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Stay, O Rama, let us both fight with each other; I shall take your life with sharp arrows discharged off my bow.
You did slay my father in the forest of Dandaka. Remembering your action and finding you before, my ire is excited.

sanskrit: यन्मया ऽसि न दृष्टस्त्वं तस्मिन् काले महावने
transliteration: yanmayā 'si na dṛṣṭastvaṃ tasmin kāle mahāvane
english: O Raghava! O Vicious souled one! My limbs are being burnt (with wrath) for I did not see you then in that mighty forest.

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या ऽसि दर्शनं राम मम त्वं प्राप्तवानिह
transliteration: diṣṭyā 'si darśanaṃ rāma mama tvaṃ prāptavāniha
english: O Rāma, by my good luck, I have got you today, like to a hungry lion desiring to have other animals.

sanskrit: ये त्वया निहता वीराः सह तैश्च समेष्यसि
transliteration: ye tvayā nihatā vīrāḥ saha taiśca sameṣyasi
english: Being despatched by my arrows to the world of devils, you shall live with those heroes, who had been killed by you before.

sanskrit: बहुना ऽत्र किमुक्तेन शृणु राम वचो मम
पश्यन्तु सकला लोकास्त्वां मां चैव रणाजिरे
transliteration: bahunā 'tra kimuktena śṛṇu rāma vaco mama
paśyantu sakalā lokāstvāṃ māṃ caiva raṇājire
english: What is the use of speaking more, O Rāma, do you hear my words. Let all the people behold your as well as my prowess in the battle-field.

sanskrit: अस्त्रैर्वा गदया वापि बाहुभ्यां वा महाहवे
अभ्यस्तं येन वा राम तेनैव युधि वर्तताम्
transliteration: astrairvā gadayā vāpi bāhubhyāṃ vā mahāhave
abhyastaṃ yena vā rāma tenaiva yudhi vartatām
english: Either with weapon or with clubs, in whatever you are expert, do you fight .with me in the battle-field, O Rāma.
Hearing the words of Makarākşa, Rāma, Dasaratha's son, smiling, replied to the words of the babbler.

sanskrit: कत्थसे किं वृथा रक्षो बहून्यसदृशानि तु
न रणे शक्यते जेतुं विना युद्धेन वाग्बलात्
transliteration: katthase kiṃ vṛthā rakṣo bahūnyasadṛśāni tu
na raṇe śakyate jetuṃ vinā yuddhena vāgbalāt
english: O Rākşasa, what is the use of idle prating? None can achieve success in a battle with idle words—but with fighting.

I slew in the forest of Dandaka your father with fourteen thousand Räksasas, Trisira and Duşana. O vile one, you being slain to day, with your flesh, vultures and crows, having sharp beaks and nails, and jackals shall be satisfied.* [*Here is another śloka, which is to be found in all N.W.P. texts and in one or two texts published in Bengal-but it has been omitted by many for it conveys the same meaning as the previous ſloka; the meaning is-And the birds drinking your blood shall fly away to various quarters.]
Being thus addressed by Rāghava, the mighty Makarākşa, began to dart sharp arrows towards him in the battle-field.
And Rāma, with his shafts, sundered into several pieces, those arrows. And being thus rendered useless those arrows, feathered in gold, fell down on the earth.
Then there arose a terrible conflict between the Raksasa Khara's son and Dasaratha's son.
There were audible in that battle-field, the outcry of the heroes and the twang of the bows stretched by their hands, like to the muttering of the clouds in the sky.
To see that wondrous conflict, the celestials, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras and the mighty serpents stationed themselves in the sky.

They were wounded with the discharged by each other and their strength was doubled. And they began to fight in that battlefield one attacking and the other withstanding the attack. And in that conflict the Rākşasa artOWS sundered the shafts discharged by Räma. And likewise Rāma severed into several pieces the arrows shot by the Räksasa.

They were wounded with the discharged by each other and their strength was doubled. And they began to fight in that battlefield one attacking and the other withstanding the attack. And in that conflict the Rākşasa artOWS sundered the shafts discharged by Räma. And likewise Rāma severed into several pieces the arrows shot by the Räksasa.
All the quarters were covered with arrows and nothing on earth or in the sky was visible.
Thereupon being excited with ire, Rāghava of long arms sundered his (Raksasa's) bow in conflict and with eight Näräcas pierced the charioteer.

sanskrit: भित्त्वा शरै रथं रामो रथाश्वान् समपातयत्
transliteration: bhittvā śarai rathaṃ rāmo rathāśvān samapātayat
english: And with arrows Rāma sundered the chariot and killing the horses brought them down. And the night-ranger Makarākṣa was brought down on the earth from the chariot.

He then again rose up with a dart in his hand creating terror to all creatures and resembling the Fire of Dissolution in resplendence. It was a terribly huge dart conferred on him by Śiva, shining in the sky in its native brilliance and like to another weapon of destruction.* *This refers to the weapon used by Śiva for destruction-for Siva, according to the Hindu Mythology is the God of destruction.
Beholding which dart even the celestials fly away in fear to different quarters. And taking up that huge flaming dart, the night-ranger, being excited with ire, hurled it at the high-souled Rāghava.
Rāghava, with four shafts, sundered that dart, in the sky, flaming and hurled at him by the son of Khara.
That flaming dart, feathered in gold, being splintered into several pieces by Rāma's arrows fell down on earth like a huge fire-brand.
Beholding that dart beffled thus by Rāma of unwearied actions all those, stationed in the welkin began to shout, “Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं शूलं मकाराक्षो निशाचरः
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ śūlaṃ makārākṣo niśācaraḥ
english: Beholding his dart thus sundered, the nightranger Makarākșa clenching his fist spoke to Kakutstha, saying, "Stay! Stay!"

sanskrit: स तं दृष्ट्वा पतन्तं वै प्रहस्य रघुनन्दनः
पावकास्त्रं ततो रामः सन्दधे तु शरासने
transliteration: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā patantaṃ vai prahasya raghunandanaḥ
pāvakāstraṃ tato rāmaḥ sandadhe tu śarāsane
english: Seeing him advance thus, the descendant of Raghu, smiling, fixed a fiery arrow on his bow.

sanskrit: तेनास्त्रेण हतं रक्षः काकुत्स्थेन तदा रणे
सञ्छिन्नहृदयं तत्र पपात च ममार च
transliteration: tenāstreṇa hataṃ rakṣaḥ kākutsthena tadā raṇe
sañchinnahṛdayaṃ tatra papāta ca mamāra ca
english: With that arrow the Räksa was slain by Kākutstha in battle. And having his heart pierced he fell down and died.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे मकराक्षस्य पातनम्
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā te rākṣasāḥ sarve makarākṣasya pātanam
english: Beholding Makarākṣa thus slain all the Rāks asas, being afraid of Rama's arrows, proceeded towards Lankā.

sanskrit: ददृशुरथ सुरा भृशं प्रहृष्टा गिरिमिव वज्रहतं यथा विकीर्णम्
transliteration: dadṛśuratha surā bhṛśaṃ prahṛṣṭā girimiva vajrahataṃ yathā vikīrṇam
english: Seeing that night-ranger, the son of Khara, slain by Rāma's arrows, like to a mountain clept by a thunder-bolt, the celestials were greatly delighted.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे एकोनाशीतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe ekonāśītitamaḥ sargaḥ

sanskrit: क्रोधेन महता ऽ ऽविष्टो दन्तान् कटकटापयन्
english: Hearing of the destruction of Makarākşa, the heroic Răvaņa, being excited with ire, began to grind his teeth.

sanskrit: कुपितश्च तदा तत्र किं कार्यमिति चिन्तयन्
transliteration: kupitaśca tadā tatra kiṃ kāryamiti cintayan
english: Being thus angered, and thinking within himself what steps to take, he ordered his son Indrajit to proceed to the battle-field.

sanskrit: अदृश्यो दृश्यमानो वा सर्वथा त्वं बलाधिकः
transliteration: adṛśyo dṛśyamāno vā sarvathā tvaṃ balādhikaḥ
english: O hero, gifted with great prowess as you are, do you, hidden (in clouds) or appearing before them, slay the two heroic brothers Rāma and Laksmana.

sanskrit: किं पुनर्मानुषौ दृष्ट्वा न वधिष्यसि संयुगे
transliteration: kiṃ punarmānuṣau dṛṣṭvā na vadhiṣyasi saṃyuge
english: You did defeat in conflict Indra of unequalled prowess. Shall you then neglect to slay men as they are?
Being thus addressed by the lord of the Raks asas and obeying his father's command, Indrajit proceeded towards the sacrificial ground to satisfy Fire (with oblations).
There came some she-demons with crimson turbans and waited respectfully where Rävaņa's son was offering oblations to Fire.

sanskrit: लोहितानि च वासांसि स्रुवं कार्ष्णायसं तथा
transliteration: lohitāni ca vāsāṃsi sruvaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ tathā
english: In that sacrifice the weapons were the leaves of sara,' bibhitakas? were fuels, and there were brought crimson clothes and sruvas made of black iron. 1. Saccharum-a reed or grass. 2. Beleric myrobalan. 3. A ladle with a double extremity or two oval collateral excavations made of wood to pour ghee
Spreading fire on all sides with śare leaves and Tomaras, (Indrajit) caught a living goat, all black, by the neck.
The fire, with oblations of sara, became greatly blazed and devoid of smoke. There were visible many good omens indicating victory.
The flame of the fire was like to gold, and moving Southwards began to receive offerings of clarified butter.
Thus offering oblations to fire and to celestials, Dänavas and Raksasas, he ascended in excellent car and soon disappeared.
It was drawn by four horses and a huge bow, set with sharp arrows, appeared beautiful on that excellent car.
The chariot was brilliant with its own native resplendence, adorned with gold and painted with the figures of deer and a cresent.
It was encircled on all sides with golden bracelets, adorned with flags made of viadurja and was like to the flaming fire.
Being thus well protected with Brahma weapons resembling the Sun in brilliance, the mighty son of Rāvana became invincible.
Offering oblations to Fire in accordance with demoniac incantations and thus obtaining the power of hiding himself, that hero, ever victorious in battle, issued out of the city and said.

sanskrit: अद्य हत्वा रणे यौ तौ मिथ्या प्रव्राजितौ वने
transliteration: adya hatvā raṇe yau tau mithyā pravrājitau vane
english: Slaying these two brothers in battle, who have uselessly wandered away into the forest, shall I crown my father Răvana with victory.
Destroying Rāma and Lakşmaņa, and clearing the monkeys off the earth, shall I satisfy my sire greatly. Saying this, he disappeared from their view.
Thereupon that fearful foe of the lord of celestials appeared in the battle-field, excited with wrath, armed with bow and sharp Nārācas and commissioned thus by the Ten-necked one.
He beheld there those two heroes discharging flaming arrows and surrounded by the monkeys like to the fearful three-hooded serpent in the midst of other serpents.

sanskrit: इमौ ताविति सञ्चिन्त्य सज्यं कृत्वा च कार्मुकम्
transliteration: imau tāviti sañcintya sajyaṃ kṛtvā ca kārmukam
english: Thinking "these must be both brothers, Rāma and Lakşmaņa," and stretching his bow he began showering arrows like to clouds.

sanskrit: स तु वैहायसं प्राप्य सरथो रामलक्ष्मणौ
transliteration: sa tu vaihāyasaṃ prāpya saratho rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: He was seated in a car in the welkin and hidden from the human gaze and began to assail! Ráma and Lakşmaņa with sharp shafts.
Being hurt with the arrows, Rāma and Lakş mana, fixing arrows on their bows, began to discharge celestial shafts.
Those two highly powerful heroes could not even touch his person with their arrows resembling the Sun albeit they covered the whole welkin therewith.

sanskrit: स हि धूमान्धकारं च चक्रे प्रच्छादयन्नभः
transliteration: sa hi dhūmāndhakāraṃ ca cakre pracchādayannabhaḥ
english: And clouding the whole sky with smoke that effulgent one, enveloped in frost, his himself from their gaze.

sanskrit: शश्रुवे चरतस्तस्य न च रूपं प्रकाशते
transliteration: śaśruve caratastasya na ca rūpaṃ prakāśate
english: There was not audible the twang of kis bow, the sound of the wheels, or the noise of the steeds. Nor was he seen by any.
In that terrible darkness of clouds that one of mighty arms began to make a downpour of Nāracas and arrows like hail storms.
In that encounter, Rāvana's son, inflamed with ire, wounded Rāma, with shafts, resembling the Sun and obtained by him as a boon.
Being hurt with Nārāchas, like to mountains wet with rain, those two foremost of men, began to discharge shafts feathered in gold.
Reaching the son of Rāvana in the sky and soaked in blood those golden arrows, fell down on earth.
Those two best of men, hurt with his arrows, became more effulgent and beffled the shafts discharged by the Räkşasa.

sanskrit: यतो हि ददृशाते तौ शरान्निपततः शितान्
transliteration: yato hi dadṛśāte tau śarānnipatataḥ śitān
english: Thereupon Rama and Lakşmaņa began to aim their sharp shafts to the direction whence the arrows came down.

sanskrit: विव्याध तौ दाशरथी लध्वस्त्रो निशितैः शरैः
transliteration: vivyādha tau dāśarathī ladhvastro niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And stationed in his chariot that mighty carwarrior disturbed all quarters with his arrows and pierced Dasaratha's sons with sharp shafts won by him.
Being greatly hurt with those sharp-pointed and terrible arrows Rāma and Lakşmaņa appeared like blossoming kingsukas.

sanskrit: नास्य वेद गतिं कश्चिन्न च रूपं धनुः शरान्
transliteration: nāsya veda gatiṃ kaścinna ca rūpaṃ dhanuḥ śarān
english: Like to the sun hidden in clouds they could see neither his countenance and motion, nor his bow and arrows.
Being wounded with those arrows hundreds of monkeys died and fell down on the earth.
Thereupon Lakşmaņa, being excited with wrath, spoke to his brother, saying-"To slay all the Rākṣasas shall I discharge today Brahma weapon.'
Thereupon Rāma spoke to Lakşmaņa, gifted with auspicious . marks, saying.-"It does not behove you to clear all the Rākşasas off the earth for the folly of one individual.

sanskrit: नैकस्य हेतो रक्षांसि पृथिव्यां हन्तु मर्हसि
पलायन्तं प्रमत्तं वा न त्वं हन्तुमिहार्हसि
transliteration: naikasya heto rakṣāṃsi pṛthivyāṃ hantu marhasi
palāyantaṃ pramattaṃ vā na tvaṃ hantumihārhasi

sanskrit: अस्यैव तु वधे यत्नं करिष्यावो महाबल
transliteration: asyaiva tu vadhe yatnaṃ kariṣyāvo mahābala
english: You should not slay him, who has retired from battle, has hidden himself, has sought your shelter, has stood before you with joined palms, has fled away or who is bewildered. O you of mighty-arms, let us try to slay him (Indrajit). And to accomplish it I shall use the weapons gifted with great impetuosity and resembling the serpents.
He is hidden from the public gaze so we must slay him, had he been fighting openly the leaders of the monkey hosts could have slain that Räks asas.

sanskrit: यद्येष भूमिं विशते दिवं वा रसातलं वापि नभस्स्थलं वा
एवं निगूढो ऽपि ममास्त्रदग्धः पतिष्यते भूमितले गतासुः
transliteration: yadyeṣa bhūmiṃ viśate divaṃ vā rasātalaṃ vāpi nabhassthalaṃ vā
evaṃ nigūḍho 'pi mamāstradagdhaḥ patiṣyate bhūmitale gatāsuḥ
english: Truly he shall be burnt to death with my shafts and fall down on the earth albeit he entered the regions under the earth of the abode of the celestials.

sanskrit: वधाय रौद्रस्य नृशंसकर्मणस्तदा महात्मा त्वरितं निरीक्षते
transliteration: vadhāya raudrasya nṛśaṃsakarmaṇastadā mahātmā tvaritaṃ nirīkṣate
english: Having said these words pregnant with a high significance, the high-souled and heroic descendant of Raghu, being surrounded by monkeys, began to concert various plans for the destruction of that terrible Raksasa of wicked deeds.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे अशीतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe aśītitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Having read the intention of that high-souled Raghava, he retired from the battle-field and entered into the city of Lankā.

sanskrit: सो ऽनुस्मृत्य वधं तेषां राक्षसानां तरस्विनाम्
english: And remembering the destruction of many a। quick-paced Raksasa, his eyes were rendered coppery with ire; and that hero, the son of Ravana, issued out of the city again.
That highly powerful, Indrajit, a descendant of Pulasta and an enemy of the celestials, issued out, encircled by the Rākşasas, by the western gate.
Then beholding the heroic brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa prepared for fight, Indrajit spread illusions.

sanskrit: इन्द्रजित्तु रथे स्थाप्य सीतां मायामयीं ततः
बलेन महता ऽ ऽवृत्य तस्या वधमरोचयत्
transliteration: indrajittu rathe sthāpya sītāṃ māyāmayīṃ tataḥ
english: Placing an illusory figure of Sītā on the car, encircled by a huge army he began to make arrangements for her destruction.

sanskrit: मोहनार्थं तु सर्वेषां बुद्धिं कृत्वा सुदुर्मतिः
transliteration: mohanārthaṃ tu sarveṣāṃ buddhiṃ kṛtvā sudurmatiḥ
english: Desiring to charm all with his illusions, that one of wicked intent, preparing himself to slay Sītā, proceeded towards the monkeys.
Beholding him thus proceed, the monkeys, inflamed with ire, desirous of fighting and with crags in their hands, moved on.
And preceded them all, Hanuman, the foremost of the monkeys, with a huge mountaintop in his hand.
He beheld there, on Indrajit's car, Sita, deprived of all joy, poorly, greatly reduced with fasts and wearing a single braid.
Rāghava's beloved spouse wore a piece of soiled cloth, and though highly beautiful, the grace of her person was greatly spoiled with dirt.

sanskrit: तां निरीक्ष्य मुहूर्तं तु मैथिलीत्यध्यवस्य तु
transliteration: tāṃ nirīkṣya muhūrtaṃ tu maithilītyadhyavasya tu
english: That daughter of Janaka, was not seen by him for a long time. And beholding her and deciding instantly that she is the daughter of Mithilā, (he became greatly sorry).

sanskrit: तां दीनां मलदिग्धाङ्गीं रथस्थां दृश्य मैथिलीम्
transliteration: tāṃ dīnāṃ maladigdhāṅgīṃ rathasthāṃ dṛśya maithilīm

english: Seeing her on the car, innocent, poor, deprived of joy and brought under the influence of the son of the lord Rākşasas that great monkey thought within himself— 'What must be the intention of Indrajit?' and accompanied by heroic monkeys advanced towards the son of Ravana.

Seeing her on the car, innocent, poor, deprived of joy and brought under the influence of the son of the lord Rākşasas that great monkey thought within himself— 'What must be the intention of Indrajit?' and accompanied by heroic monkeys advanced towards the son of Ravana.

sanskrit: कृत्वा विकोशं निस्त्रिंशं मूर्ध्नि सीतां परामृशत्
transliteration: kṛtvā vikośaṃ nistriṃśaṃ mūrdhni sītāṃ parāmṛśat
english: Beholding that monkey host, Ravana's son became beside himself with ire and unsheathing his weapon Nistrinsha, caught her by the hair.

sanskrit: तां स्त्रियं पश्यतां तेषां ताडयामास रावणिः
क्रोशन्तीं राम रामेति मायया योजितां रथे
transliteration: tāṃ striyaṃ paśyatāṃ teṣāṃ tāḍayāmāsa rāvaṇiḥ
krośantīṃ rāma rāmeti māyayā yojitāṃ rathe
english: The Räkşasa addressed himself to strike her in the presence of all those monkeys and that illusory figure of Sītā began to bewail saying, “O Rāma! O Rāma!”
Seeing her thus caught by the head, Hanumān, the son of Maruta, greatly sorry, began to shed tears.

sanskrit: तां दृष्ट्वा चारुसर्वाङ्गीं रामस्य महिषीं प्रियाम्
transliteration: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā cārusarvāṅgīṃ rāmasya mahiṣīṃ priyām
english: Beholding that beloved spouse of Räma, having a tender and beautiful person, he addressed angrily the son of the lord of Rākşasas with harsh words.
It is for your destruction, O Vicious-souled one! that you have touched her hair. Being descended from that great Brahmă ascetic you are born as a Rākşasa.

sanskrit: धिक् त्वां पापसमाचारं यस्य ते मतिरीदृशी
transliteration: dhik tvāṃ pāpasamācāraṃ yasya te matirīdṛśī
english: O! cursed are you, since you have cherished such a desire and engaged in such a vicious deed. O vile! O wicked! O! cruel and dishonourable wight! O you having vice for your prowess!

sanskrit: अनार्यस्येदृशं कर्म घृणा ते नास्ति निर्घृण
transliteration: anāryasyedṛśaṃ karma ghṛṇā te nāsti nirghṛṇa
english: O! cursed are you, since you have cherished such a desire and engaged in such a vicious deed. O vile! O wicked! O! cruel and dishonourable wight! O you having vice for your prowess!

sanskrit: किं तवैषा ऽपराद्धा हि यदेनां हन्तुमिच्छसि
english: O shameless! Are you not ashamed of perpetrating such an inhuman deed. What has Maithili done by you, O cruel one! that you are ready to slay her—She has been banished from her home, territory and has been separated from her lord.

sanskrit: सीतां च हत्वा न चिरं जीविष्यसि कथञ्चन
वधार्ह कर्मणा ऽनेन मम हस्तगतो ह्यसि
transliteration: sītāṃ ca hatvā na ciraṃ jīviṣyasi kathañcana
english: O you worthy of being slain, destroying Sītā, you shall not live long as you have been brought under me.

sanskrit: ये च स्त्रीघातिनां लोका लोकवध्येषु कुत्सिताः
transliteration: ye ca strīghātināṃ lokā lokavadhyeṣu kutsitāḥ
english: You shall after the death reach the place which is occupied by those who murder women, a place which is avoided even by those who commit every sort of crime punishable by law.
Saying this Hanuman, accompanied by monkeys armed with weapons, and excited with ire, proceeded towards the son of the lord or Raksasas.
Beholding the highly powerful monkeys advance thus the Rākṣasas, inflamed with wrath, obstructed them.
Assailing the monkey-hosts with thousands of arrows, Indrajit spoke to that foremost of monkeys, Hanumān, saying.
Today I shall slay before you all Vaidehī, for whom you, Sugriva and Rama have come. Slaying her, O monkey, I shall afterwards kill you, Rama, Laksmana and Sugriva and the dishonourable Vibhişaņa.

sanskrit: इमां हत्वा ततो रामं लक्ष्मणं त्वां च वानर
सुग्रीवं च वधिष्यामि तं चानार्यं विभीषणम्
transliteration: imāṃ hatvā tato rāmaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tvāṃ ca vānara
sugrīvaṃ ca vadhiṣyāmi taṃ cānāryaṃ vibhīṣaṇam
english: Today I shall slay before you all Vaidehī, for whom you, Sugriva and Rama have come. Slaying her, O monkey, I shall afterwards kill you, Rama, Laksmana and Sugriva and the dishonourable Vibhişaņa.

O monkey, about not destroying women, of which you were speaking (I might say) that we must always do what pains our enemies."* *There is one śloka intervening according to some texts, but it has been omitted by many. The reasons for this omission are best known to them. The purport is:-"Why did Rama slay Taraka before? And I shall therefore slay his spouse the daughter of king Janaka.” Hear in Indrajit attempts to justify himself and wants to prove that Räma is equally blameable for this.)
Saying this, Indrajit with a sharp sword, himself killed the illusory Sitā thus bewailing.
Being sundered by him obliquely in a way in which a sacred thread lies on one's own person, the innocent (Sitā) having beautiful countenance fell down on the earth.

sanskrit: मया रामस्य पश्येमां कोपेन च निषूदिताम्
एषा विशस्ता वैदेही विफलो वः परिश्रमः
transliteration: mayā rāmasya paśyemāṃ kopena ca niṣūditām
eṣā viśastā vaidehī viphalo vaḥ pariśramaḥ
english: Slaying her Indrajit spoke to Hanumān,“Behold I have slain (before you) with my sword Rāma's beloved. And Vaidehi being thus slain, all your labours have been rendered useless."

sanskrit: ततः खड्गेन महता हत्वा तामिन्द्रिजित् स्वयम्
transliteration: tataḥ khaḍgena mahatā hatvā tāmindrijit svayam
english: a Destroying her with his own hand by means of a huge sword, Indrajit, greatly pleased ascended his car and began to emit dreadful roars.
The monkeys stationed near heard that terrible roar and saw him enter the castel.* *The castle built by Indrajit by means of his illusory power in the air.

sanskrit: तथा तु सीतां विनिहत्य दुर्मतिः प्रहृष्टचेताः स बभूव रावणिः
तं हृष्टरूपं समुदीक्ष्य वानरा विषण्णरूपाः सहसा प्रदुद्रुवुः
transliteration: tathā tu sītāṃ vinihatya durmatiḥ prahṛṣṭacetāḥ sa babhūva rāvaṇiḥ
taṃ hṛṣṭarūpaṃ samudīkṣya vānarā viṣaṇṇarūpāḥ sahasā pradudruvuḥ
english: And slaying Sītā that wicked-minded son of Rāvana became greatly pleased. And beholding him thus delighted the monkeys being greatly sorry fled away.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे एकाशीतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe ekāśītitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Hearing that dreadful uproar resembling the sound of Indra's thunder-bolt, the monkeys, casting their looks on all sides fled away.
Thereupon Hanumān, the son of Maruta, spoke to them, poorly, terrified and of a sorrowful countenance, saying.
O monkeys, why do you look so melancholy and why are you flying away? Why have you renounced your earnest desire for fight? And where is your heroism gone?
Do you remain behind me, I shall go first in the battle. It is improper for heroes of noble descent to escape from battle field.
Being thus addressed by that highly intelligent son of the Wind-god, they were greatly excited with wrath and being pleased took up trees and। crags in their hands.
Roaring thus the leading monkeys advanced towards the Rākşasas and stood encircling Hanumān in the battle-field.
Being surrounded on all sides by leading monkeys, Hanuman began to burn down enemy's host like to fire spreading its flames.
Being encircled by monkey-hosts that mighty monkey resembling death himself began to grind the Rākşasas.

sanskrit: स तु कोपेन चाविष्टः शोकेन च महाकपिः
transliteration: sa tu kopena cāviṣṭaḥ śokena ca mahākapiḥ
english: Being overwhelmed with grief and wrought up with ire, that monkey Hanumān, threw a huge crag on the car of that son of Rāvana.
Beholding that crag about to fall down on the car, the charioteer moved his horses and it was speedily brought at some distance.
And not reaching Indrajit stationed on the car and the charioteer, that crag, uselessly hurled, fell down on the earth.

sanskrit: पातितायां शिलायां तु रक्षसां व्यथिता चमूः
निपतन्त्या च शिलया राक्षसा मथिता भृशम्
transliteration: pātitāyāṃ śilāyāṃ tu rakṣasāṃ vyathitā camūḥ
nipatantyā ca śilayā rākṣasā mathitā bhṛśam
english: As the crag falling down the army of the Rakşasas were violently crushed.
Thereupon hundreds of huge-bodied monkeys, emitting cries and taking up crags and trees proceeded towards him (Indrajit) and hurled them at him.
The monkeys gifted with dreadful prowess began to make a down-pour of crags and trees. They thus assailed the enemies and frequently emitted cries.
The grim-visaged night-rangers were assailed with trees in that field by the terrible monkeys.
The highly powerful monkeys destroyed his retinue, with crags, stones and trees having strong trunks. And Hanumān thus crushed many a Rākşasa of terrible deeds.

sanskrit: हनुमान् सन्निवर्तध्वं न नः साध्यमिदं बलम्
transliteration: hanumān sannivartadhvaṃ na naḥ sādhyamidaṃ balam
english: Obstructing the Rākṣasas (for some time) Hanumān spoke to monkeys, saying, “Stay, we should not fight now.

sanskrit: यन्निमित्तं हि युद्ध्यामो हता सा जनकात्मजा
transliteration: yannimittaṃ hi yuddhyāmo hatā sā janakātmajā
english: That daughter of Janaka has been slain, for whom we have engaged in fight, renouncing all hope of life and desiring to accomplish Rāma's satisfaction.

sanskrit: इममर्थं हि विज्ञाप्य रामं सुग्रीवमेव च
तौ यत् प्रतिविधास्येते तत् करिष्यामहे वयम्
transliteration: imamarthaṃ hi vijñāpya rāmaṃ sugrīvameva ca
tau yat pratividhāsyete tat kariṣyāmahe vayam
english: Let us now go and inform Rāma and Sugrīva of it. And we shall do as we shall be commanded by them.
Saying this and desisting all the monkeys from encounter that foremost of monkeys proceeded undaunted and heroically.

sanskrit: ततः प्रेक्ष्य हनूमन्तं व्रजन्तं यत्र राघवः
transliteration: tataḥ prekṣya hanūmantaṃ vrajantaṃ yatra rāghavaḥ
english: Beholding Hanumăn proceed thus where Rāghava was that wicked-minded one (Indrajit) with a view to offer oblations to fire entered the sacrificial altar Nikumbhila.
Beholding Hanumăn proceed thus where Rāghava was that wicked-minded one (Indrajit) with a view to offer oblations to fire entered the sacrificial altar Nikumbhila.
Reaching there Indrajit lighted up fire and began to pour oblations therein. And the fire blazed up receiving oblations of blood, and being satisfied assumed the appearance of the setting sun.
Reaching there Indrajit lighted up fire and began to pour oblations therein. And the fire blazed up receiving oblations of blood, and being satisfied assumed the appearance of the setting sun.

sanskrit: अथेन्द्रजिद्राक्षसभूतये तु जुहाव हव्यं विधिना विधानवित्
दृष्ट्वा व्यतिष्ठन्त च राक्षसास्ते महासमूहेषु नयानयज्ञाः
transliteration: athendrajidrākṣasabhūtaye tu juhāva havyaṃ vidhinā vidhānavit
dṛṣṭvā vyatiṣṭhanta ca rākṣasāste mahāsamūheṣu nayānayajñāḥ
english: Indrajit conversant with all ceremonials, offered oblations in due form for the welfare of the Rākşasas. And they all stood there watching the result and desirous of ascertaining the success of the battle.* *This Sloka has been left off in some editions.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे द्व्यशीततमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe dvyaśītatamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Hearing the terrible war-cry of the Rākşasas and monkeys Rāghava spoke to Jämbavän, saying.

sanskrit: सौम्य नूनं हनुमता क्रियते कर्म दुष्करम्
transliteration: saumya nūnaṃ hanumatā kriyate karma duṣkaram
english: O gentle one, forsooth has Hanumān performed some mighty act for I hear the dreadful sound of the weapons.
Do you therefore proceed speedily, O lord of bears, with all your soldiers to assist that foremost of monkeys.

sanskrit: आगच्छत् पश्चिमं द्वारं हनुमान् यत्र वानरः
transliteration: āgacchat paścimaṃ dvāraṃ hanumān yatra vānaraḥ
english: Thereupon, saying, 'So be it,' that king of bears, surrounded by his forces, approached the Western gate, where the monkey, Hanumān, was stationed.
Then the lord of bears saw Hanumān approach, surrounded by monkeys sighing hard, who had faught the fight.
Seeing on the way that host of bears dreadful and resembling dark clouds, on the march, Hanumān made them desist.
That illustrious one along with that force, speedily presented himself (before Rāma), and with a heavy heart addressed him, saying.
As we were fighting the field, Ravana's son, Indrajit in our very sight slew Sītā, crying (in distress).
O subduer of enemies, seeing her (in this plight) I, with my senses bewildered, have been overwhelmed with grief. Therefore I have come to you to inform you of what has befallen.

sanskrit: निपपात तदा भूमौ छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः
transliteration: nipapāta tadā bhūmau chinnamūla iva drumaḥ
english: Hearing these words of his, Raghava, overwhelmed with grief, dropped down to the earth, like a tree whose roots have been severed.

sanskrit: तं भूमौ देवसङ्काशं पतितं प्रेक्ष्य राघवम्
transliteration: taṃ bhūmau devasaṅkāśaṃ patitaṃ prekṣya rāghavam
english: Seeing the god-like Råghava down on the earth, the foremost monkeys from all sides rushed forward and came to where (he was).

With water scented with lotuses, they fell to sprinkling that one resembling a furious fire that has suddenly arisen. 1. Padmotpalasugadhibhiḥ-water scented with padmas-lotuses proper, and utpalas-blue lotuses (Nymphea cerulea). 2. 'Rama,' remarks the commentator, 'was a fire lighted by his grief for Sītā.'

sanskrit: तं लक्ष्मणो ऽथ बाहुभ्यां परिष्वज्य सुदुःखितः
english: Thereat Laksmana, over-come with sorrow, embracing Rāma, spoke to his words fraught with reason and import, “Profitless* virtue is incapable, O noble one, of delivering from calamities you, who have subdued your senses, and who ever abidst in the good path. * 'Profitless, although apparently an epither of virtue, is really the predicate of the sentence. 'Virtue, incapable of delivering you is profitless.

sanskrit: अनर्थेभ्यो न शक्नोति त्रातुं धर्मो निरर्थकः
transliteration: anarthebhyo na śaknoti trātuṃ dharmo nirarthakaḥ
english: Thereat Laksmana, over-come with sorrow, embracing Rāma, spoke to his words fraught with reason and import, “Profitless* virtue is incapable, O noble one, of delivering from calamities you, who have subdued your senses, and who ever abidst in the good path. * 'Profitless, although apparently an epither of virtue, is really the predicate of the sentence. 'Virtue, incapable of delivering you is profitless.

sanskrit: भूतानां स्थावराणां च जङ्गमानां च दर्शनम्
यथा ऽस्ति न तथा धर्मस्तेन नास्तीति मे मतिः
transliteration: bhūtānāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca jaṅgamānāṃ ca darśanam
yathā 'sti na tathā dharmastena nāstīti me matiḥ
english: Beings and the mobile as well as the immobile cannot have that direct perception of virtue which they have of happiness. Therefore, I ween, virtue is a non-entity.

sanskrit: यथैव स्थावरं व्यक्तं जङ्गमं च तथाविधम्
transliteration: yathaiva sthāvaraṃ vyaktaṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca tathāvidham
english: Inasmuch as the immobile (albeit devoid of any regard for virtue) are nevertheless happy and as the mobile also are so, this virtue cannot lead to happiness. (If it were so), one like you would have not been placed in peril.
If unrighteousness would bring unhappiness on creatures, Ravana should hence to hell, and you possessed of virtue, should not come by misfortune.

sanskrit: तस्य च व्यसनाभावाद् व्यसनं च गते त्वयि
transliteration: tasya ca vyasanābhāvād vyasanaṃ ca gate tvayi
english: Seeing that he is free from danger, and you are in itrighteousness and its opposite are found to have tendencles the very reverse of those assigned to them respectively (by the Vedas).

If by means of virtue, one attain the felicity attached to it, and by means of unrighteouness, one reap its proper fruit, then let those that are unrighteous reap the fruit of their impiety nor let those that set their face against sin, be deprived of the fruit of their righteousness, and let those that walk in the way of virtue reap the fruit of their piety.

sanskrit: धर्मेण चरतां धर्मस्तथा चैषां फलं भवेत्
transliteration: dharmeṇa caratāṃ dharmastathā caiṣāṃ phalaṃ bhavet

english: But as prosperity attend those that are established in unrighteousness, and as those regardful of righteousness fare lamentably, these*have not the senses assigned to them (by the scriptures). *Virtue and vice.

sanskrit: वधकर्म हतो ऽधर्मः स हतः कं वधिष्यति
transliteration: vadhakarma hato 'dharmaḥ sa hataḥ kaṃ vadhiṣyati
english: If, O Rāghava, Rāghava, (it is contended that) unrighteousness cut off the wicked, then whom shall Unrighteousness, himself slain by the act of slaughter of the destroyer, slay in his turn?

sanskrit: अथवा विहितेनायं हन्यते हन्ति वा परम्
विधिरालिप्यते तेन न स पापेन कर्मणा
transliteration: athavā vihitenāyaṃ hanyate hanti vā param
vidhirālipyate tena na sa pāpena karmaṇā
english: Or if it is said that one is slain or slay another by ordinance, then it is destiny, which is touched by the sinful act and not he.

O chastiser of foes, incapable of meting out retribution,* unmanifest itself, and non-existent, how can virtue, even if we grant its existence, find out the person that should be slain? *"In consequence,' remarks Ramanuja, 'of their being devoid of consciousness.

sanskrit: यदि सत् स्यात् सतां मुख्य नासत् स्यात्तव किञ्चन
transliteration: yadi sat syāt satāṃ mukhya nāsat syāttava kiñcana
english: If, O foremost of the good, it had existed, you wouldst not have come by any misfortune. But inasmuch as you have fallen into this plight, there is no such thing as virtue.

sanskrit: अथवा दुर्बलः क्लीबो बलं धर्मो ऽनुवर्तते
दुर्बलो हृतमर्यादो न सेव्य इति मे मतिः
transliteration: durbalo hṛtamaryādo na sevya iti me matiḥ
english: Or itself feeble and impotent, it take refuge in manliness. And being powerless and bereft of dignity, it should, I deem, by no means be followed.

sanskrit: धर्ममुत्सृज्य वर्तस्व यथा धर्मे तथा बले
transliteration: dharmamutsṛjya vartasva yathā dharme tathā bale
english: If virtue is a property of manliness, then carefully forsaking virtue, do you follow strength as you have hitherto followed virtue.

sanskrit: अथ चेत् सत्यवचनं धर्मः किल परन्तप
transliteration: atha cet satyavacanaṃ dharmaḥ kila parantapa
english: But, O subduer of enemies, if truthfulness be virtue, are you not bound by that departing from which the king lost his life?* *Explains the commentator, 'King Dasaratha lost his life, because he did not observe his word of installing you in the kingdom. Are you not bound by his word as well?'

sanskrit: यदि धर्मो भवेद्भूतो अधर्मो वा परन्तप
न स्म हत्वा मुनिं वज्री कुर्यादिज्यां शतक्रतुः
transliteration: yadi dharmo bhavedbhūto adharmo vā parantapa
na sma hatvā muniṃ vajrī kuryādijyāṃ śatakratuḥ
english: O chastiser of foes, if virtue must be practised above all, or if prowess must have precedence, then the thunder-handed Satakratu would not have celebrated his sacrifice, slaying the ascetic.* *The Logic is all in a jumble; but such is the text. The ascetic was Visvarūpa. The meaning, according to the commentator, is that, prowess is first and virtue next. Indra first used force, and then acquired merit.)
O Rāghava, virtue aided by prowess, destroy enemies. Therefore, O Kakutstha, people, for compassing their ends, resort to both virtue and prowess.

sanskrit: मम चेदं मतं तात धर्मो ऽयमिति राघव
transliteration: mama cedaṃ mataṃ tāta dharmo 'yamiti rāghava
english: This, sire, is my opinion, this, O Raghava, is virtue. But you, having then renounced the kingdom, have laid the axe at the root* of righteousness. **Root, remarks, Rāmānuja, 'which is interest!'
Like streams issuing out mountains, all acts spring from wealth flowing from various regions and attaining magnitude.

sanskrit: व्युच्छिद्यन्ते क्रियाः सर्वा ग्रीष्मे कुसरितो यथा
transliteration: vyucchidyante kriyāḥ sarvā grīṣme kusarito yathā
english: Like a shrunken stream in summer, all the acts of that foolish person who has been devorced by wealth, are annihilated.

He that renouncing riches, within his reach,* hankers after enjoyment, being carried away by his overmastering desire, take to getting at wealth by sinful acts; and then he incur guilt. *The commentator would have gotten riches.'

sanskrit: यस्यार्थाः स पुमान् लोके यस्यार्थाः स च पण्डितः
transliteration: yasyārthāḥ sa pumān loke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ
english: To him that has wealth are friends, to him that has wealth are acquaintances, he that has wealth is an individuality in this world, and he that has wealth is a learned person.

sanskrit: यस्यार्थाः स च विक्रान्तो यस्यार्थाः स च बुद्धिमान्
यस्यार्थाः स महाभागो यस्यार्थाः स महागुणः
transliteration: yasyārthāḥ sa ca vikrānto yasyārthāḥ sa ca buddhimān
yasyārthāḥ sa mahābhāgo yasyārthāḥ sa mahāguṇaḥ
english: He that has wealth is powerful; he that has wealth is intelligent; he that has wealth is mighty-armed; and he that has wealth is full of all graces.
All these that I have en-numerated are the evils of forsaking fortune. (I cannot divine) what made you, renouncing the monarchy, to adopt such a course.
He that has riches, has virtue and desire attending on him, and has everything auspicious. That one without wealth, that seek it, cannot secure the wealth of prowess, without riches and desire.

sanskrit: हर्षः कामश्च दर्पश्च धर्मः क्रोधः शमो दमः
transliteration: harṣaḥ kāmaśca darpaśca dharmaḥ krodhaḥ śamo damaḥ
english: O lord of men, cheerfulness, and desire, and pride, and piety, and anger, and self-restraint, and self-control, all these come from wealth.

sanskrit: ते ऽर्थास्त्वयि न दृश्यन्ते दुर्दिनेषु यथा ग्रहाः
transliteration: te 'rthāstvayi na dṛśyante durdineṣu yathā grahāḥ
english: As the planets are not discovered on a stormy day, that wealth, the want of which renders this world naught even to the ascetics practising righteousness, is not visible in you.

sanskrit: त्वयि प्रव्रजिते वीर गुरोश्च वचने स्थिते
रक्षसा ऽपहृता भार्या प्राणैः प्रियतरा तव
transliteration: tvayi pravrajite vīra gurośca vacane sthite
english: O hero, you having abode by the words of your superior and having come (to the forest), your wife dearer then life itself has been ravished by Rākṣasas.
But, O hero, today, O Raghava, by my acts will I remove this huge sorrow that has been heaped upon us by Indrajit. Therefore, rise you up.
Rise up, O foremost of men, O long-armed one, O you who observe vows. Why did you not understand yourself as the supreme soul?* *Räma is conceived as an incarnation of Vişnu.

sanskrit: अयमनघ तवोदितः प्रियार्थं जनकसुतानिधनं निरीक्ष्य रुष्टः
transliteration: ayamanagha tavoditaḥ priyārthaṃ janakasutānidhanaṃ nirīkṣya ruṣṭaḥ
english: Osinless one, urged on behalf of your welfare, I, waxing wroth on hearing of the slaughter of Janaka's daughter, shall with my shafts entirely raze to the ground Larkā with cars and elephants and steeds and the foremost Rākşasas.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे त्र्यशीतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe tryaśītitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: As Lakşmaņa devoted to his brother was comforting Rāma, Vibhīşaņa, posting his forces at their proper quarters, came there, surrounded by four heroes accoutred in various arms, resembling masses of collyrium or leaders of elephant-herds.
And approaching the high-souled Rāghava, overwhelmed with grief, he saw the monkeys with tears in their eyes.
He saw that joy of the Ikşvāku race the high-souled Raghava-stupefied with grief, lying on the lap of Lakşmaņa.
son Seeing Rāma cast down and inflamed with grief, Vibhisana, inlay pained, said, "What is this?
Thereat, gazing at Vibhisana's countenance as well as all those monkeys, Laksmana, with his eyes flooded with tears, said these words pregnant with dire import.
O placid one, hearing from Hanumān's lips that Sītā has been slain by Indrajit. Rāghava has been overcome with stupor.
As Sumitra's was speaking thus, Vibhisana,. preventing him, addressed the stupefied Rāma in these pregnant words.
O king, all that Hanumān in distressful guise had communicated to you I deem as improbable, like to the drying of the deep.

sanskrit: सीतां प्रति महाबाहो न च घातं करिष्यति
transliteration: sītāṃ prati mahābāho na ca ghātaṃ kariṣyati
english: I know the intent of the impious Rāvana with reference to Sita, O mighty-armed one. Her he will not slay.

sanskrit: वैदेहीमुत्सृजस्वेति न च तत् कृतवान् वचः
transliteration: vaidehīmutsṛjasveti na ca tat kṛtavān vacaḥ
english: I, seeking his welfare, had besought him much, saying, 'Let go Vaidehi', but he did not act up to my speech.

sanskrit: नैव साम्ना न दानेन न भेदेन कुतो युधा
सा द्रुष्टुमपि शक्येत नैव चान्येन केनचित्
transliteration: naiva sāmnā na dānena na bhedena kuto yudhā
sā druṣṭumapi śakyeta naiva cānyena kenacit
english: Neither by conciliation, nor by gift, nor by dissension, and where is war? nor by any other means is one capable of obtaining the very sight of Sītā.

sanskrit: वानरान् मोहयित्वा तु प्रतियातः स राक्षसः
चैत्यं निकुम्भिलां नाम यत्र होमं करिष्यति
transliteration: vānarān mohayitvā tu pratiyātaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ
caityaṃ nikumbhilāṃ nāma yatra homaṃ kariṣyati
english: Having bewildered the monkeys, the Raksasa has gone back; and, O mighty-armed one, know her to be the illusory daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: सीदते हि बलं सर्वं दृष्ट्वा त्वां शोककर्शितम्
transliteration: sīdate hi balaṃ sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ śokakarśitam

english: Seeing you smitten with grief, this entire host is dispirited. Here, with your heart composed, do your stay, summoning your strength. Send Lakşmañana along with us and the flower of the forces.

sanskrit: एष तं नरशार्दूलो रावणिं निशितैः शरैः
त्याजयिष्यति तत् कर्म ततो वध्यो भविष्यति
transliteration: eṣa taṃ naraśārdūlo rāvaṇiṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
tyājayiṣyati tat karma tato vadhyo bhaviṣyati
english: This foremost of men by means of sharpened shafts will make Rāvana's son give up his rites; and then shall he be capable of being slain by us.
These keen and sharpened shafts of his, attaining access of velocity through the feathers of birds, and themselves resembling fierce fowls, will drink his* blood. *Indrajit's.
Therefore, O mighty-armed one, do you in order to the destruction of the Rākşasa, commission Lakşmana, even as the wielder of the thunder-bolt command the same.

sanskrit: मनुजवर न कालविप्रकर्षो रिपुनिधनं प्रति यत् क्षमो ऽद्य कर्तुम्
त्वमति सृज रिपोर्वधाय वाणीममररिपोर्मथने यथा महेन्द्रः
transliteration: manujavara na kālaviprakarṣo ripunidhanaṃ prati yat kṣamo 'dya kartum
tvamati sṛja riporvadhāya vāṇīmamararipormathane yathā mahendraḥ
english: As today no time should be lost, therefore do you send Lakşmaņa for campassing the destruction of the foe, even as Mahendra send the thunder-bolt for bringing about the destruction of the enemies of the immortals.

sanskrit: समाप्तकर्मा हि स राक्षसाधिपो भवत्यदृस्यः समरे सुरासुरैः
युयुत्सता तेन समाप्तकर्मणा भवेत् सुराणामपि संशयो महान्
transliteration: samāptakarmā hi sa rākṣasādhipo bhavatyadṛsyaḥ samare surāsuraiḥ
yuyutsatā tena samāptakarmaṇā bhavet surāṇāmapi saṃśayo mahān
english: If that foremost of Räkşasas can finish his rites, he shall be invisible to both celestials and Asuras; and, he fighting after finishing his sacrifice, the celestials themselves shall be placed in great jeopardy.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे चतुरशीतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe caturaśītitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Hearing his speech, Rāghava, overwhelmed with grief, could not perfectly comprehend what was said by the Rākşasa.
Then, summoning up patience, Rāma-captor of hostile capitals, spoke to Vibhisana, seated near the monkeys.
O lord of Naiſtas, I once more wish to hear what, O Vibhisana, you have said.
Hearing Raghava's words, Vibhisana, skilled in speech, again spoke these words, saying.
O mighty-armed one, I have stationed the forces, O hero, agreeably to your directions.
The entire force has been divided around; and the leaders have also been placed properly.
Further, O mighty master, listen to what I have to say. On your having been causelessly aggrieve, we all of us were seized with grief.

sanskrit: प्राप्तव्या वदि ते सीता हन्तव्याश्च निशाचराः
रघुनन्दन वक्ष्यामि श्रूयतां मे हितं वचः
transliteration: prāptavyā vadi te sītā hantavyāśca niśācarāḥ
raghunandana vakṣyāmi śrūyatāṃ me hitaṃ vacaḥ

english: Let Sumitra's son go forth, environed by a mighty force, for slaying in battle the son of Ravana, who has gone to Nikumbhila; with shafts resembling Venomous serpents, discharged from the round* of his bow. *The bow drawn to its full stretch, becomes circular.
By virtue of his austerities, that hero, from a boon conferred by the self-sprung, has obtained the Brahmasira weapon, together with steeds coursing at their will.

sanskrit: स एष सह सैन्येन प्राप्तः किल निकुम्भिलाम्
यद्युत्तिष्ठेत् कृतं कर्म हतान् सर्वांश्च विद्धि नः
transliteration: sa eṣa saha sainyena prāptaḥ kila nikumbhilām
yadyuttiṣṭhet kṛtaṃ karma hatān sarvāṃśca viddhi naḥ
english: Now he with his army has gone to Nikumbhilā; and when, having finished his rites, he gets up, know that all of us are slain.

When not reaching Nikumbhilā, and not having finished your offerings to fire, you, equipped with arms, are slain by a foe, O enemy of Indra, that is your death. Thus, O mightyarmed one, did the lord of all creatures confer a boon (on Indrajit), and, o king, thus was the death of this intelligent one ordained.

sanskrit: हते तस्मिन् हतं विद्धि रावणं ससुहृज्जनम्
transliteration: hate tasmin hataṃ viddhi rāvaṇaṃ sasuhṛjjanam
english: O Rāma, for compassing the destruction of Indrajit, do you commission a mighty force. On his being slain, know that Rāvana along with his retainers are slain.
Hearing Vibhīşana's words, Rāma said, “O you having truth for prowess, I know the illusion of that fierce one.

sanskrit: स हि ब्रह्मास्त्रवित् प्राज्ञो महामायो महाबलः
transliteration: sa hi brahmāstravit prājño mahāmāyo mahābalaḥ
english: Without doubt, the is skilled in the Brahma weapon, is potent in illusion and, is possessed of exceeding strength. In conflict, he deprive of consciousness even the celestials with Varuņa (at their head).

As that illustrious (one) go about in the welkin on his chariot, none, can perceive his course, like the course of the sun when the sky is covered with clouds.” And Raghava, being well acquainted with the illusive energy of his wicked-minded foe, addressed the renowned Laksmana, saying.

Environed by the entire host of the lord of monkeys, accompanied by the leaders, O Laksmana, headed by Hanuman, with Jambavan, king of bears-and girt round by the forces, do you slay this son of the Raksasa, possessed of the strength of illusion.

Environed by the entire host of the lord of monkeys, accompanied by the leaders, O Laksmana, headed by Hanuman, with Jambavan, king of bears-and girt round by the forces, do you slay this son of the Raksasa, possessed of the strength of illusion.

sanskrit: अयं त्वां सचिवैः सार्द्धं महात्मा रजनीचरः
transliteration: ayaṃ tvāṃ sacivaiḥ sārddhaṃ mahātmā rajanīcaraḥ
english: And accompanied by his counsellors, this high-souled night-ranger shall follow at you back, in this engagement with that one skilled in illusion.
Then hearing Rāghava's words, Lakşmaņa endowed with dreadful prowess, with Vibhīşaņa, took up another excellent bow.
And donning on his mail, and putting on his armour and his sword, and furnished with arrows, and a bow in his left hand, Sumitrā's son, touching Rāma's feet, feeling elated, addressed Rāma, saying.
Today the shafts discharged from my bow, piercing Ravana's son, shall fall into Lanka, even as swans drop into a tank.

sanskrit: अद्यैव तस्य रौद्रस्य शरीरं मामकाः शराः
transliteration: adyaiva tasya raudrasya śarīraṃ māmakāḥ śarāḥ
english: This very day shall my arrows, shot from my redoubtable bow-string, rive the body of that terrific one.
Having spoken thus, the effulgent Lakşmana, eager to slay Rāvana's son, went before his brother.

sanskrit: सो ऽभिवाद्य गुरोः पादौ कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्
transliteration: so 'bhivādya guroḥ pādau kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam
english: Having saluted at the feet of his superior and went round him, Lakşmaņa set out for the sacrificial ground (named) Nikumbhila, protected by the son of Rāvana.
Accompanied by Vibhīşaņa, that powerful son of the king-Lakşmaņa-after his brother had offered up prayers in his behalf, set off with all speed.
Surrounded by thousands of monkeys, Hanumān as well as Vibhīşaņa together with his counsellors speedily went in the wake of Lakş mana.
And strongly encompassed by that mighty monkey-host, (Laksmana) saw the forces of the bear-king stationed on the way.
Having proceeded far, Sumitra's Sumitra's son-enhancer of the delight of friends, from a distance discovered the forces of the Rākşasmonarch, drawn up in battle-array.

That subduer of enemies-Raghu's sonbearing his bow in his hand, coming upon him whose martial might lay in illusion, stopped (there) for conquering his foe agreeably to the ordinance * of Brahma. *The ordinance was that Indrajit should be slain while remaining outside Nikumbhilā, his rites not yet finished.

sanskrit: अङ्गदेन च वीरेण तथा ऽनिलसुतेन च

english: Accompanied by Vibhīşaņa, the heroic Angada, and the Wind-god's offspring, the powerful son of the king dived into the forces of the foe, various, blazing with burnished arms, dense with standards, and thronging with mighty cars,* capable of striking terror (into the hearts of the spectators), instinct with immeasurable energy, and resembling darkness. *Maharathai (ab.) may also mean with mighty carwarriors.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चाशीतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe pañcāśītitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: When things were in this condition, Rāvana's younger brother addressed Lakşmaņa in words fraught with evil to foes and conducing to the welfare (of his own party), saying.

Do you without delay bring on an engagement between this cloud-black Räksasa army, which you behold, and the monkeys having rocks for their arms. O Lakşmaņa, do you exert yourself to break through his* mighty-army; and when the ranks are broken, the son of the Rákşasa-lord shall be visible. * Indrajit's, that is.

Do you without delay bring on an engagement between this cloud-black Räksasa army, which you behold, and the monkeys having rocks for their arms. O Lakşmaņa, do you exert yourself to break through his* mighty-army; and when the ranks are broken, the son of the Rákşasa-lord shall be visible. * Indrajit's, that is.
Scattering among the foes shafts resembling Indra's thunder-bolt, charge him while he has not yet finished this ceremony.
Slay, O hero, this wicked one, this son of Ravana, given to illusion, and of terrific feats, the fear of all the worlds.
Hearing Vibhisana's.words, Laksmana graced with auspicious marks began to shower arrows on the son of the Raksasa-chief.
And bears and monkeys, given to fighting excellently with trees, in a body rushed towards that army (of Rākşasa) drawn up there.
The Rākşasas (on their part) burning to slaughter the monkey-forces, rushed in the encounter with sharpened shafts and darts and tomaras.

sanskrit: शब्देन महता लङ्कां नादयन् वै समन्ततः
transliteration: śabdena mahatā laṅkāṃ nādayan vai samantataḥ
english: There took place a tremendous onslaught of the monkeys and the Raksasas. And Lankā resounded all around with that mighty tumult; and the sky was covered with weapons of various shapes, and whetted arrows and trees and dreadful upraised mountain-tops.

There took place a tremendous onslaught of the monkeys and the Raksasas. And Lankā resounded all around with that mighty tumult; and the sky was covered with weapons of various shapes, and whetted arrows and trees and dreadful upraised mountain-tops.
Rākşasas having frightful faces and arms, playing their arms among the foremost monkeys, began to spread terror (there).
In the same way the monkeys in the conflict fell to slaying and wounding the Rākşasas with trees and hill-tops.
And great was the terror that was spread among the warring Räkşasas by the flower of the bears and monkeys, possessed of gigantic persons and endowed with prodigious strength.
Hearing his own army hard beset by the enemies, and dropping, the unconquerable one, ere yet he had finished his rites, rose up.
Issuing from the gloom of the trees, Ravana's son, fired with wrath, ascended his car, which had already been well yoked (with steeds).
Accoutred in a dreadful bow and arrows, that one, resembling a mass of collyrium, having a red face and eyes, looked dreadful like the reaper-death.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वैव तु रथस्थं तं पर्यवर्तत तद्बलम्
transliteration: dṛṣṭvaiva tu rathasthaṃ taṃ paryavartata tadbalam
english: As soon as they saw him mounted on his car, that host of Rākşas possessed of dreadful impetuosity, eager to engage with Lakşmaņa, stood on their ground.
At this time that subduer of enemies, Hanumăn-resembling a mountain, uprooted a giant tree incapable of being handled.
In that encounter, the monkey, consuming (the forces) like the fire risen at Doomsday, made that army of Rākşasas insensible with innumerable trees.
Finding the Wind-god's son, Hanumān, suddenly spreading devastation among the Rāks asas by thousands, (they) showered (shafts) on him.
Indrajit saw that foremost of monkeys resembling a hill, the offspring of the Windgod possessing himself if calmness, while destroying his foes.
Thereat, be* addressed his charioteer, saying, "Go where the monkeys is. Being disregarded by the Raksasas, he makes havoc among us." *Indrajit.

sanskrit: इत्युक्तः सारथिस्तेन ययौ यत्र स मारुतिः
transliteration: ityuktaḥ sārathistena yayau yatra sa mārutiḥ
english: Thus accosted by him, the charioteer went where the Wind-god's offspring was, carrying the exceedingly invincible Indrajit seated on the car.

sanskrit: सो ऽभ्युपेत्य शरान् खड्गान् पट्टिशांश्च परश्वधान्
english: And rushing forward, that irrepressible one the Rākşasas-began to shower on the monkey's head arrows and swords and pațțišas and scimitars and axes.

sanskrit: तानि शस्त्राणि घोराणि प्रतिगृह्य स मारुतिः
रोषेण महता ऽ ऽविष्टो वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह
transliteration: tāni śastrāṇi ghorāṇi pratigṛhya sa mārutiḥ
english: And bearing all those dreadful arms, the Wind-god's offspring, overcome with a mighty rage said.

sanskrit: युद्ध्यस्व यदि शूरो ऽसि रावणात्मज दुर्मते
english: O wicked-minded son of Rävaņa, if you are a hero, fight on. Combat with me with your arms.

sanskrit: वेगं सहस्व दुर्बुद्धे ततस्त्वं रक्षसां वरः
transliteration: vegaṃ sahasva durbuddhe tatastvaṃ rakṣasāṃ varaḥ
english: If in the encounter, you bear my impetus, then, O you of perverse sense, you indeed are the foremost of Rākşasas.
Then Vibhīşana pointed out to Lakşmaņa the son of Ravana, who with his bow upraised, was eager to slay Hanumān.

This one that, mounted on his car, is eager to slay Hanumăn, is the son of Rāvaņa that has vanquished Vasava himself (in battle). Do you, O son of Sumitrā, with peerless shafts capable of resisting enemies, dreadful, and competent to finish the lives (of foes), slay the son of Ravana.

This one that, mounted on his car, is eager to slay Hanumăn, is the son of Rāvaņa that has vanquished Vasava himself (in battle). Do you, O son of Sumitrā, with peerless shafts capable of resisting enemies, dreadful, and competent to finish the lives (of foes), slay the son of Ravana.

sanskrit: ददर्श तं पर्वतसन्निकाशं रणे स्थितं भीमबलं नदन्तम्
transliteration: dadarśa taṃ parvatasannikāśaṃ raṇe sthitaṃ bhīmabalaṃ nadantam
english: Thus accosted by Vibhīşaņa terrific to foes, that high-souled one saw (Indrajit) of dreadful prowess, difficult to gut at, and resembling a hill, stationed on his car.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे षडशीतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe ṣaḍaśītitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Having spoken thus to Sumitra's son, Vibhișaņa experienced delight, and taking (Laksmana) bearing a bow in his hand, hurriedly went off.

sanskrit: अविदूरं ततो गत्वा प्रविश्य च महद्वनम्
transliteration: avidūraṃ tato gatvā praviśya ca mahadvanam
english: Proceeding some way and entering the mighty wood, Vibhīşaņa pointed out to Lakşmaņa the place (of sacrifice).
The energetic brother of Rāvana showed to Lakşmaņa the Nyagrodha, dreadful to behold and resembling a mass of sable clouds.
Here offering presents to the ghosts, the powerful son of Răvaņa afterwards engages in conflict.

sanskrit: निहन्ति समरे शत्रून् बध्नाति च शरोत्तमैः
transliteration: nihanti samare śatrūn badhnāti ca śarottamaiḥ
english: Then the Rākşasas becomes invisible to all beings; and he slay his enemies in battle and fastens them with excellent shafts.
Do you, ere he has passed beyond the Nyagrodha, with flaming arrows destroy the powerful son of Rävaņa along with his car and steeds and charioteer.
Thereupon saying, 'So be it,' the exceedingly energetic son of Sumitrā-that delight of his friends, took up his post there stretching his variegated bow.
Ravana's son Indrajit, endowed with strength, mailed, and armed with a sword, and furnished with a banner, was seen mounted on a fire-hued chariot.

sanskrit: समाह्वये त्वां समरे सम्यग्युद्धं प्रयच्छ मे
transliteration: samāhvaye tvāṃ samare samyagyuddhaṃ prayaccha me
english: The highly powerful Lakşmaņa addressed Pulastya's son never knowing defeat, saying, I challenge you to the encounter. Do you give me battle, exerting your utmost.

sanskrit: अब्रवीत् परुषं वाक्यं तत्र दृष्ट्वा विभीषणम्
transliteration: abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇam
english: Thus addressed, the exceedingly energetic and intelligent son of Rāvana, seeing Vibhīşaņa there, spoke to him harshly, thus.

sanskrit: कथं द्रुह्यसि पुत्रस्य पितृव्यो मम राक्षस
transliteration: kathaṃ druhyasi putrasya pitṛvyo mama rākṣasa
english: Born and bred in this Rākşasa race, you are the very brother of my father Why, O Rākşasa being my uncle, did you range yourself against your son?

sanskrit: न ज्ञातित्वं न सौहार्दं न जातिस्तव दुर्मते
प्रमाणं न च सौदर्यं न धर्मो धर्मदूषण
transliteration: na jñātitvaṃ na sauhārdaṃ na jātistava durmate
pramāṇaṃ na ca saudaryaṃ na dharmo dharmadūṣaṇa
english: But neither kinship, nor emity, nor race, O wicked-minded one, nor co-birth, can, destroyer of righteousness, avail to make you discern your duty.
O you of perverse understanding you are indeed to be pitied; as you are worthy of being reproached by the virtuous; since, renouncing your own, you have espoused servitude under another.
Neither by your character nor yet your understanding did you perceive the mighty difference that Leith between living with one's own kindred, and taking refuge with the base.

sanskrit: गुणवान् वा परजनः स्वजनो निर्गुणो ऽपि वा
निर्गुणः स्वजनः श्रेयान् यः परः पर एव सः
transliteration: guṇavān vā parajanaḥ svajano nirguṇo 'pi vā
nirguṇaḥ svajanaḥ śreyān yaḥ paraḥ para eva saḥ
english: If one that is not our own, be furnished with every grace, and if one's own be void of all merit, one's kindred, albeit unworthy, is preferable; and he that is not ours, is even always such.

sanskrit: स स्वपक्षे क्षयं प्राप्ते पश्चात्तैरेव हन्यते
transliteration: sa svapakṣe kṣayaṃ prāpte paścāttaireva hanyate
english: He that, forsaking his own party, serve that of another, is destroyed even by the latter, when his own party is destroyed.
O night-ranger, such is this your relentlessness, that, O Ravana's younger brother, you being a kindred, are capable of displaying your manliness (as no other person can do so).

Thus addressed by his brother's son, Vibhis ana answered, “O Raksasa, why did you speak as if in ignorance of my character? O impious son of the Rākşasa chief, do you for ego the roughness which you assume on behalf of my dignity.* *Or, on account of your heroism.

sanskrit: गुणो ऽयं प्रथमो नृणां तन्मे शीलमराक्षसम्
english: Albeit born in the race of Rākşas of cruel deeds, yet having regard to the first of principles pertaining to men, my character is not that of a Rākşasa. I do not take pleasure in the terrible; not do I revel in unrighteousness.” But how can a brother, although differing from his brother in character, be renounced by the latter?* *Some read Vişamasilena. Then the sense would be: 'How else could a brother bearing a difference in character, renounce his brother' meaning Ravana.

sanskrit: न रमे दारुणेनाहं न चाधर्मेण वै रमे
transliteration: na rame dāruṇenāhaṃ na cādharmeṇa vai rame

english: One renouncing a person, lapsing from virtue and bent on sinful acts, attain happiness, even as one does by shaking off a venomous snake from his hand.
The wise have called that impious cne given to stealing others goods and violating others wives, as worthy of being forsaken, even like a house that is aflame.
Robbing others property, outraging the wives of others, and inspiring fear among friends, these three vices lead to destruction.

The dreadful slaughter of sages, rebellion against all the gods, overweening conceit, anger long-continued enmity, and running amuck of counsel, these sins are sapping the life and fortune of my brother; and they have hidden his virtues even as clouds cover a mountain.

sanskrit: दोषैरेतैः परित्यक्तो मया भ्राता पिता तव
transliteration: doṣairetaiḥ parityakto mayā bhrātā pitā tava
english: The dreadful slaughter of sages, rebellion against all the gods, overweening conceit, anger long-continued enmity, and running amuck of counsel, these sins are sapping the life and fortune of my brother; and they have hidden his virtues even as clouds cover a mountain.

sanskrit: नेयमस्ति पुरी लङ्का न च त्वं न च ते पिता
transliteration: neyamasti purī laṅkā na ca tvaṃ na ca te pitā
english: You are proud, and haughty, and a boy, O Raksasa. You are fettered by the noose of Fate. Do you say to me whatever you like.

sanskrit: अद्य ते व्यसनं प्राप्तं किं मां त्वमिह वक्ष्यसि
प्रवेष्टुं न त्वया शक्यो न्यग्रोधो राक्षसाधम
transliteration: adya te vyasanaṃ prāptaṃ kiṃ māṃ tvamiha vakṣyasi
praveṣṭuṃ na tvayā śakyo nyagrodho rākṣasādhama
english: To-day you have addressed harshly me, who have fallen on evil days; but, O worst of Raks asas, you cannot pass this Nyagrodha.

sanskrit: धर्षयित्वा च काकुत्स्थौ न शक्यं जीवितुं त्वया
transliteration: dharṣayitvā ca kākutsthau na śakyaṃ jīvituṃ tvayā
english: Having smitten the Kākutstha, you cannot live. Fight with that man-god, Laksmana, in encounter. Being slain, you shall serve the deities in the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: न लक्ष्मणस्यैत्य हि बाणगोचरं त्वमद्य जीवन् सबलो गमिष्यसि
transliteration: na lakṣmaṇasyaitya hi bāṇagocaraṃ tvamadya jīvan sabalo gamiṣyasi
english: Displaying you own prowess, do you spend all your weapons and all your shafts. But coming within the ken of Laksmana's arrows, your will not today go hence, living with your forces.

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे सप्ताशतीतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe saptāśatītitamaḥ sargaḥ

english: Hearing Vibhisana's words, the son of Ravana, deprived of his senses by passion, spoke harshly, and rushed forward in wrath.
With upraised weapons and scimitars, he, resembling the Destroyer himself, was mounted on a mighty car yoked with black steeds, and ornamented (on all sides).
That one endowed with terrific strength upraised a huge, gigantic, strong and powerful bow, and shafts capable of destroying foes.
fo-day my shafts discharged from my mighty bow shall mangle your limbs, even as fire burn up a heap of cotton.
To-day with your persons pierced with sharp shafts, with darts, and javelins, and Rstis and arrows, Shall I despatch you all to the abode of Yama.
Who shall stay before me, fleet-handed, creating an arrows shower in the field, and roaring like to clouds?

sanskrit: शायितौ स्थो मया भूमौ विसञ्ज्ञौ सपुरस्सरौ
transliteration: śāyitau stho mayā bhūmau visañjñau sapurassarau

sanskrit: स्मृतिर्न ते ऽस्ति वा मन्ये व्यक्तं वा यमसादनम्
transliteration: smṛtirna te 'sti vā manye vyaktaṃ vā yamasādanam

english: Hearing the vaunt of the Rākşasa-chief, Rahgu's son, inflamed with rage, with an undaunted countenance, spoke to Ravana's son.

sanskrit: उक्तश्च दुर्गमः पारः कार्याणां राक्षस त्वया
कार्याणां कर्मणा पारं यो गच्छति स बुद्धिमान्
transliteration: uktaśca durgamaḥ pāraḥ kāryāṇāṃ rākṣasa tvayā
kāryāṇāṃ karmaṇā pāraṃ yo gacchati sa buddhimān
english: O Rākşasa, hard is the achievement of the task that you have mentioned. He that compass business by act is alone intelligent. He that compass business by act is alone intelligent. But you, O wicked-minded one, incompetent as you are to bring about your end, attaining your arduous aim by words only, deem yourself as crowned with success.

sanskrit: वचो व्याहृत्य जानीषे कृतार्थो ऽस्मीति दुर्मते
english: O Rākşasa, hard is the achievement of the task that you have mentioned. He that compass business by act is alone intelligent. He that compass business by act is alone intelligent. But you, O wicked-minded one, incompetent as you are to bring about your end, attaining your arduous aim by words only, deem yourself as crowned with success.
That your had rendered yourself invisible in the field of conflict, was the work of a thief, and not the way of a hero.

sanskrit: यथा बाणपथं प्राप्य स्थितो ऽहं तव राक्षस
दर्शयस्वाद्य तत्तेजो वाचा त्वं किं विकत्थसे
transliteration: yathā bāṇapathaṃ prāpya sthito 'haṃ tava rākṣasa
darśayasvādya tattejo vācā tvaṃ kiṃ vikatthase
english: Coming within the range of your shafts, I stay here, do you display your prowess. What did you say in words.?
Thus addressed, the mighty IndrajitConqueror of enemies-stretching his dreadful bow, showered sharpened shafts.

sanskrit: सम्प्राप्य लक्ष्मणं पेतुः श्वसन्त इव पन्नगाः
transliteration: samprāpya lakṣmaṇaṃ petuḥ śvasanta iva pannagāḥ
english: And discharged by him, those exceedingly impetuous arrows, resembling the venom of serpents, hitting Laksmana, fell down like to hissing snakes.
In that encounter, Rāvana's son-Indrajit, possessed of eminent impetuosity, pierced Laksmana, graced with auspicious marks, with vehement shafts.

sanskrit: शुशुभे लक्ष्मणः श्रीमान् विधूम इव पावकः
transliteration: śuśubhe lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmān vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: And pierced with those arrows and bathed in blood, the graceful Lakşmaņa appeared like a smokeless fire.
Seeing his own feat, Indrajit, coming forward, and setting up a tremendous cry, said.
O son of Sumitrā, my feathered and sharpedged shafts shot from my bow, capable of destroying life, will today finish you up.

sanskrit: गृध्राश्च निपतन्तु त्वां गतासुं निहतं मया
transliteration: gṛdhrāśca nipatantu tvāṃ gatāsuṃ nihataṃ mayā
english: To-day, O Laksmana, swarms of jackals and hosts of hawks and vultures shall alight on you lying lifeless, having been slain by me.

sanskrit: भक्तं भ्रातरमद्यैव त्वां द्रक्ष्यति मया हतम्
transliteration: bhaktaṃ bhrātaramadyaiva tvāṃ drakṣyati mayā hatam
english: This very day shall the exceedingly wicked Råma behold you, who are the friend of Kș atriyas and devoted to your brother, and who ėver bear yourself ignobly, slain by me; today see you, O Sumitra's son, slain by me, with your armour fallen off your person, your bow broken, and your head severed.

This very day shall the exceedingly wicked Råma behold you, who are the friend of Kș atriyas and devoted to your brother, and who ėver bear yourself ignobly, slain by me; today see you, O Sumitra's son, slain by me, with your armour fallen off your person, your bow broken, and your head severed.
As Ravana's son was speaking thus harshly, Lakşmaņa conversant with the import of words, replied in a reasonable speech, saying.

sanskrit: वाग्बलं त्यज दुर्बुद्धे क्रूरकर्मा ऽसि राक्षस
english: Leave off your strength of tongue, O you of perverse sense, O Räkşasa, O you of crooked ways! Wherefore did you speak thus? Bring all this to pass in worthy deed.

sanskrit: कुरु तत्कर्म येनाहं श्रद्दध्यां तव कत्थनम्
transliteration: kuru tatkarma yenāhaṃ śraddadhyāṃ tava katthanam
english: Why, O Raksasa, without doing (what you say), did you simply say it? Do the deed, so that I may have regard for your utterances.
Mark! without speaking anything harsh, without censuring you in the least, without venting any brag, shall, I, O cannibal, slay you.
Saying this, Lakşmaņa drawing his bow to its full bent, hit at the Raksasas chest five nārācas, wondrous impetuous arrows.
Those arrows resembling flaming serpents, with their velocity accelerated by the feathers (with which they were furnished), blazed on the Nairta's breast like the rays of the sun.
And wounded with those shafts, Ravana's son, fired with wrath, pierced Lakşmaņa with arrows discharged (from his bow).
And exceedingly dreadful was the encounter that took place between those leonine man and Rākşasa, each eager to conquer the other.

Both powerful, and both endowed with strength and possessed of prowess, and both exceedingly invincible; and both having unparalleled might and energy, those heroes faught like two planets in the welkin; or like Bala and Vộtra, irresistible in conflict; and those high-souled ones faught like two lions. And showering countless shafts and displaying many manoeuvres, that foremost of men and that Rāks asas, faught on cheerfully,

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे अष्टाशीतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe aṣṭāśītitamaḥ sargaḥ

sanskrit: ससर्ज राक्षसेन्द्राय क्रुद्धः सर्प इव श्वसन्
transliteration: sasarja rākṣasendrāya kruddhaḥ sarpa iva śvasan

sanskrit: त्वर तेन महाबोहो भग्न एष न संशयः
transliteration: tvara tena mahāboho bhagna eṣa na saṃśayaḥ

sanskrit: किं न स्मरसि तद्युद्धे प्रथमे मत्पराक्रमम्
निबद्धस्त्वं सह भ्रात्रा यदा भुवि विवेष्टसे
transliteration: kiṃ na smarasi tadyuddhe prathame matparākramam
nibaddhastvaṃ saha bhrātrā yadā bhuvi viveṣṭase

sanskrit: स्मृतिर्वा नास्ति ते मन्ये व्यक्तं वा यमसादनम्
transliteration: smṛtirvā nāsti te manye vyaktaṃ vā yamasādanam

sanskrit: यदि ते प्रथमे युद्धे न दृष्टो मत्पराक्रमः
transliteration: yadi te prathame yuddhe na dṛṣṭo matparākramaḥ

sanskrit: मुमोच स शरान् घोरान् सङ्गृह्य नरपुङ्गवः
transliteration: mumoca sa śarān ghorān saṅgṛhya narapuṅgavaḥ

sanskrit: इन्द्रजित् समरे वीरः प्ररूढ इव सानुमान्
transliteration: indrajit samare vīraḥ prarūḍha iva sānumān

sanskrit: अभीक्ष्णं निश्वसन्तौ तौ युद्ध्येतां तुमुलं युधि
transliteration: abhīkṣṇaṃ niśvasantau tau yuddhyetāṃ tumulaṃ yudhi

sanskrit: न च तौ युद्धवैमुख्यं श्रमं वाप्युपजग्मतुः
transliteration: na ca tau yuddhavaimukhyaṃ śramaṃ vāpyupajagmatuḥ

sanskrit: व्यपेतदोषमस्यन्तौ लघु चित्रं च सुष्ठु च
transliteration: vyapetadoṣamasyantau laghu citraṃ ca suṣṭhu ca

sanskrit: प्रकम्पयन् जनं घोरो निर्घात इव दारुणः
transliteration: prakampayan janaṃ ghoro nirghāta iva dāruṇaḥ

english: Laksmana having at Ravana's son, and Rāvana's son having at Lakşmana, critical was the huggermugger that ensued* in the encounter between each other. *i.e. in consequence of all sides being covered with arrows, neither the Rākşas nor the monkeys could distinguish their several parties in the encounter, and the blows that each dealt were misdirected in consequence.

sanskrit: न च तौ युद्धवैमुख्यं श्रमं वाप्युपजग्मतुः
transliteration: na ca tau yuddhavaimukhyaṃ śramaṃ vāpyupajagmatuḥ

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे एकोननवतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe ekonanavatitamaḥ sargaḥ

sanskrit: युध्यमानौ तु तौ दृष्ट्वा प्रसक्तौ नराक्षसौ
transliteration: yudhyamānau tu tau dṛṣṭvā prasaktau narākṣasau

sanskrit: राक्षसैस्तैः परिवृतः स तदा तु विभीषणः
transliteration: rākṣasaistaiḥ parivṛtaḥ sa tadā tu vibhīṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: ततः सञ्चोदयानो वै हरीन् रक्षो रणप्रियान्
उवाच वचनं काले कालज्ञो रक्षसां वरः
transliteration: tataḥ sañcodayāno vai harīn rakṣo raṇapriyān
uvāca vacanaṃ kāle kālajño rakṣasāṃ varaḥ

sanskrit: एतच्छेषं बलं तस्य किं तिष्ठत हरीश्वराः
transliteration: etaccheṣaṃ balaṃ tasya kiṃ tiṣṭhata harīśvarāḥ

sanskrit: रावणं वर्जयित्वा तु शेषमस्य हतं बलम्
transliteration: rāvaṇaṃ varjayitvā tu śeṣamasya hataṃ balam

sanskrit: संह्रादी विकटो निघ्नस्तपनो दम एव च

transliteration: saṃhrādī vikaṭo nighnastapano dama eva ca
praghāsaḥ praghasaścaiva prajaṅgho jaṅgha eva ca

sanskrit: बाहुभ्यां सागरं तीर्त्वा लङ्घ्यतां गोष्पदं लघु
transliteration: bāhubhyāṃ sāgaraṃ tīrtvā laṅghyatāṃ goṣpadaṃ laghu

sanskrit: तौ प्रयुद्धौ तदा वीरौ मृधे लक्ष्मणराक्षसौ
transliteration: tau prayuddhau tadā vīrau mṛdhe lakṣmaṇarākṣasau

sanskrit: न ह्यादानं न सन्धानं धनुषो वा परिग्रहः
न विप्रमोक्षो बाणानां न विकर्षो न विग्रहः
transliteration: na hyādānaṃ na sandhānaṃ dhanuṣo vā parigrahaḥ
na vipramokṣo bāṇānāṃ na vikarṣo na vigrahaḥ

sanskrit: अन्तरिक्षे हि सञ्छन्ने न रूपाणि चकाशिरे
transliteration: antarikṣe hi sañchanne na rūpāṇi cakāśire

sanskrit: अस्तं गते सहस्रांशौ संवृतं तमसेव हि
transliteration: astaṃ gate sahasrāṃśau saṃvṛtaṃ tamaseva hi

sanskrit: न तदानीं ववौ वायुर्न च जज्वाल पावकः
transliteration: na tadānīṃ vavau vāyurna ca jajvāla pāvakaḥ

sanskrit: ततो ऽपरेण भल्लेन शितेन निशितेन च
हयेषु व्यग्रहस्तं तं विव्याध निशितैः शरैः
transliteration: hayeṣu vyagrahastaṃ taṃ vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ

sanskrit: प्रजहौ समरोद्धर्षं विषण्णः स बभूव ह
transliteration: prajahau samaroddharṣaṃ viṣaṇṇaḥ sa babhūva ha

sanskrit: ते हया मथिता भग्ना व्यसवो धरणीं गताः
ते निहत्य हयांस्तस्य प्रमथ्य च महारथम्
transliteration: te hayā mathitā bhagnā vyasavo dharaṇīṃ gatāḥ
te nihatya hayāṃstasya pramathya ca mahāratham

sanskrit: ततो महेन्द्रप्रतिमः स लक्ष्मणः पदातिनं तं निशितैः शरोत्तमैः
सृजन्तमाजौ निशितान् शरोत्तमान् भृशं तदा बाणगणैर्न्यवारयत्
transliteration: tato mahendrapratimaḥ sa lakṣmaṇaḥ padātinaṃ taṃ niśitaiḥ śarottamaiḥ
sṛjantamājau niśitān śarottamān bhṛśaṃ tadā bāṇagaṇairnyavārayat

sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे नवतितमः सर्गः
transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmadyuddhakāṇḍe navatitamaḥ sargaḥ

sanskrit: नेह विज्ञायते स्वो वा परो वा राक्षसोत्तमाः
transliteration: neha vijñāyate svo vā paro vā rākṣasottamāḥ

sanskrit: धृष्टं भवन्तो युध्यन्तु हरीणां मोहनाय वै
transliteration: dhṛṣṭaṃ bhavanto yudhyantu harīṇāṃ mohanāya vai

sanskrit: स रथं भूषयित्वा तु रुचिरं हेमभूषितम्
transliteration: sa rathaṃ bhūṣayitvā tu ruciraṃ hemabhūṣitam

sanskrit: सो ऽन्यत् कार्मुकमादय सज्यं चक्रे त्वरन्निव
स भिन्नवर्मा रुधिरं वमन् वक्त्रेण रावणिः
transliteration: sa bhinnavarmā rudhiraṃ vaman vaktreṇa rāvaṇiḥ

sanskrit: स तथा ह्यर्दितो बाणै राक्षसेन महामृधे
transliteration: sa tathā hyardito bāṇai rākṣasena mahāmṛdhe

sanskrit: तस्मै दृढतरं क्रुद्धो जघान गदया हयान्
transliteration: tasmai dṛḍhataraṃ kruddho jaghāna gadayā hayān

sanskrit: ते तस्य कायं निर्भिद्य रुक्मपुङ्खा निमित्तगाः
transliteration: te tasya kāyaṃ nirbhidya rukmapuṅkhā nimittagāḥ

sanskrit: तं समीक्ष्य महातेजा महेषुं तेन संहितम्
transliteration: taṃ samīkṣya mahātejā maheṣuṃ tena saṃhitam

sanskrit: कुबेरेण स्वयं स्वप्ने स्वस्मै दत्तं महात्मना
