transliteration: ājagmuste sahāgastyā ye śritā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Kausika, and Yavakrīta, and Gārgya, and Gālava and Kaņva, son of Medhātithi,who dwelt in the east, (came thither); and the reverend Svastyāstreya, and Namuci, and Pramuci, and Agastya, and the worshipful Atri, and Sumukha, and Vimukha, who dwelt in the south, came in company with Agastya.* *The name of Agastya had before been just specified among the incomes; but so it is in the text.

sanskrit: ते ऽप्याजग्मुः सशिष्या वै ये श्रिताः पश्चिमां दिशम्
transliteration: te 'pyājagmuḥ saśiṣyā vai ye śritāḥ paścimāṃ diśam
english: Nrisadgu, and Kavasi, and Dhaumya, and that mighty sage-Kauseya-who abode in th quarter, came there accompanied by their disciples.

Vasiştha and Kasyapa and Atri and Viśvāmitra with Gautama and Jamadagni and Bharadvāja and also the seven sages*, who for aye resided in the northern quarter, (came there). *Ursa Major, or the great bear, the seven stars of which are the souls of as many saints, Marici, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasistha.

Vasiştha and Kasyapa and Atri and Viśvāmitra with Gautama and Jamadagni and Bharadvāja and also the seven sages*, who for aye resided in the northern quarter, (came there). *Ursa Major, or the great bear, the seven stars of which are the souls of as many saints, Marici, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu and Vasistha.
On arriving at the residence of Rāghava, those high-souled ones, resembling the fire in radiance, stopped at the gate, with the intention of communicating their arrival (to Rama) through the warder.
Hearing of the arrival of the anchorets, possessed of the effulgence of the sun new-risen, he answered the warder, saying, "Do you usher them in, having regard to their comfort."

sanskrit: तान् सम्प्राप्तान् मुनीन् दृष्ट्वा प्रत्युत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः
transliteration: tān samprāptān munīn dṛṣṭvā pratyutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Seeing the ascetics him, Rāma with joined hands worshipped their feet with arghyas, and with regard consecrated a cow to each, and saluting them with the collecting mind, he ordered seats (for the saints).

sanskrit: तेषु काञ्चनचित्रेषु महत्सु च वरेषु च
transliteration: teṣu kāñcanacitreṣu mahatsu ca vareṣu ca

english: And having, according to their rank, seated themselves on gorgeous and superb seats of kuća or deerskins embroidered with gold, those foremost of sages-those mighty saints, versed in the Vedas, along with their disciples and leaders, having (previously) been asked as to their welfare, addressed Rāma, saying.

And having, according to their rank, seated themselves on gorgeous and superb seats of kuća or deerskins embroidered with gold, those foremost of sages-those mighty saints, versed in the Vedas, along with their disciples and leaders, having (previously) been asked as to their welfare, addressed Rāma, saying.

sanskrit: त्वां तु दिष्ट्या कुशलिनं पश्यामो हतशात्रवम्
transliteration: tvāṃ tu diṣṭyā kuśalinaṃ paśyāmo hataśātravam
english: O son of Raghu. O mighty-armed one, complete welfare is ours. By good luck it is that we see you fortunate, with all your foes finished. Bygood luck it is that, Oking, Ravana-destroyer of creatures, has been slain byyou.

sanskrit: न हि भारः स ते राम रावणः पुत्रपौत्रवान्
transliteration: na hi bhāraḥ sa te rāma rāvaṇaḥ putrapautravān

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या त्वया हतो राम रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
transliteration: diṣṭyā tvayā hato rāma rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या विजयिनं त्वाद्य पश्यामः सह सीतया
transliteration: diṣṭyā vijayinaṃ tvādya paśyāmaḥ saha sītayā
english: By good fortune it is, O Rama, that Ravana along with his sons and grandsons has been slain by you. By good fortune it is that today we see you victorious along with $ītā, and, O righteoussouled one, with your brother, Lakşmaņa, (ever) compassing your profit. (By good fortune it is) that, Oking, today we behold (you) in company with your mothers and your brothers.
By good fortune it is that those night-rangers, Prahasta, and Vikata; and Virupāksa, and Mahodara, and the unconquerable Akampana, have all been slain (by you).

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या ते समरे राम कुम्भकर्णो निपातितः
transliteration: diṣṭyā te samare rāma kumbhakarṇo nipātitaḥ
english: By good fortune it is, O Rama, that he than whose proportions there are no other's greater on earth, even Kumbhakarņa, was brought downy (by you).

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या ते निहता राम महावीर्या निशाचराः
transliteration: diṣṭyā te nihatā rāma mahāvīryā niśācarāḥ
english: By good luck it is, O Rama, that these highly powerful night-rangers. Trisiras and Atikāya and Devāntaka and Narāntaka, have been slain by you.

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या तौ निहतौ राम कुम्भकर्णसुतौ मृधे
transliteration: diṣṭyā tau nihatau rāma kumbhakarṇasutau mṛdhe

english: By good luck it is that you had been encountered in a hand-to-hand combat with that foremost of Rākşasas, incapable of being slain by the celestials themselves; and achieved victory (ultimately).

sanskrit: सङ्ख्ये तस्य न किञ्चित्तु रावणस्य पराभवः
transliteration: saṅkhye tasya na kiñcittu rāvaṇasya parābhavaḥ
english: To defeat Ravana in battle was (for you) in small matter; but it is a piece of good fortune that Ravana's son, who had confronted you for combat, has been slain (by you) in battle.

By good fortune it is that you, O mightyarmed one, had been liberated from the bonds of) that foe of the celestials whose course resembled that of Time;*-and that you also had secured victory. *i.e. surpassing perception.
Hearing of the destruction of Indrajit, we congratulate you (on your success). He was in capable of being slain by all creatures, and in battle possessed mighty powers of illusion.

sanskrit: एते चान्ये च बहवो राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः
दिष्ट्या त्वया हता वीरा रघूणां कुलवर्द्धन
transliteration: ete cānye ca bahavo rākṣasāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
diṣṭyā tvayā hatā vīrā raghūṇāṃ kulavarddhana

english: Hearing that Indrajit slain, amazement have seized us all. Having conferred on us this holy freedom from fear, O Kākutstha, O repressor of enemies. you through good fortune, will grow in victory.
Hearing that Indrajit slain, amazement have seized us all. Having conferred on us this holy freedom from fear, O Kākutstha, O repressor of enemies. you through good fortune, will grow in victory.
Hearing the speech of the ascetics of sacred souls, Rāma, coming under the influence of a mighty wonder, said with joined hands.
You worshipful ones, wherefore, passing by those exceedingly powerful ones-Kumbhakarna and the night-ranger, Ravana, do you praise Ravana's son?

sanskrit: महोदरं प्रहस्तं च विरूपाक्षं च राक्षसम्
transliteration: mahodaraṃ prahastaṃ ca virūpākṣaṃ ca rākṣasam
english: Wherefore, passing by Mahodara, and Prahasta, and the Rākşasa-Virüpākşa-and Matta, and Unmatta, and the irrepressible Devāntaka and Narāntaka-redoubtable heroes all-do you extol Ravana's son?
And wherefore, passing by Atikāya and Trisiras and Dhumraksa, that night-ranger-all endowed with exceeding powers, do you extol Ravana's son?

sanskrit: कीदृशो वै प्रभावो ऽस्य किं बलं कः पराक्रमः
transliteration: kīdṛśo vai prabhāvo 'sya kiṃ balaṃ kaḥ parākramaḥ
english: What was his prowess? And what his strength? And what his might? And by virtue of what cause did he surpass Rāvana?

sanskrit: शक्यं यदि मया श्रोतुं न खल्वाज्ञापयामि वः
यदि गुह्यं न चेद्वक्तुं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथ्यताम्
transliteration: śakyaṃ yadi mayā śrotuṃ na khalvājñāpayāmi vaḥ
yadi guhyaṃ na cedvaktuṃ śrotumicchāmi kathyatām
english: If I can well hear the same (do you tell it me). I by no means command you. If the thing can bear disclosure, I would hear it. Pray, speak out.

sanskrit: शक्रो ऽपि विजितस्तेन कथं लब्धवरश्च सः
कथं च बलवानन्पुत्रो न पिता तस्य रावणः
transliteration: kathaṃ ca balavānanputro na pitā tasya rāvaṇaḥ
english: How was Śakra vanquished by him, and how also did he obtain the boon? And how was the son powerful and not his sire Rāvaņa.

sanskrit: कथं पितुश्चाभ्यधिको महाहवे शक्रस्य जेता हि कथं स राक्षसः
वराश्च लब्धाः कथयस्व मे ऽद्य तत्पृच्छतश्चास्य मुनीन्द्र सर्वम्
transliteration: kathaṃ pituścābhyadhiko mahāhave śakrasya jetā hi kathaṃ sa rākṣasaḥ
varāśca labdhāḥ kathayasva me 'dya tatpṛcchataścāsya munīndra sarvam
english: How could that Raksasa, surpassing his sire, conquer Sakra in mighty encounter, and how did he obtain the boon? O foremost of anchorets, do you today unfold all this to me, who ask (for the same).
Hearing those words of Rāghva, the exceedingly energetic Kumbhayoni spoke as follows.

sanskrit: शृणु राम कथावृत्तं तस्य तेजोबलं महत्
जघान शत्रून्येनासौ न च वध्यः स शत्रुभिः
transliteration: śṛṇu rāma kathāvṛttaṃ tasya tejobalaṃ mahat
jaghāna śatrūnyenāsau na ca vadhyaḥ sa śatrubhiḥ
english: Having regard to his (Indrajit's) energy and might, I shall relate to you the history of his race, in the light of which you will perceive why Rāvana's son had been capable of slaying his enemies, but could not himself be slain by them.

sanskrit: तावत्ते रावणस्येदं कुलं जन्म च राघव
वरप्रदानं च तथा तस्मै दत्तं ब्रवीमि ते
transliteration: tāvatte rāvaṇasyedaṃ kulaṃ janma ca rāghava
varapradānaṃ ca tathā tasmai dattaṃ bravīmi te
english: I shall, O Rāghava, describe to you Răvaņa's race and birth, as well as the boon that had been conferred on him.
Formerly in the Krita age, O Rama, there was a Brahmarsi-lord (of creatures), son to Prajapati, and like to the very self of the great-father.

sanskrit: प्रजापतेः पुत्र इति वक्तुं शक्यं हि नामतः
transliteration: prajāpateḥ putra iti vaktuṃ śakyaṃ hi nāmataḥ
english: His virtues, springing from righteousness and excellency of character, are past all delineation; I can only say that, forsooth, he went by the name of Prajāpati's son.
Verily on account of his being the son of Prajāpati, he was the darling of the deities; as by virtue of his spotless perfections, that magnanimous one was loved of all creatures.

sanskrit: स तु धर्मप्रसङ्गेन मेरोः पार्श्वे महागिरेः
transliteration: sa tu dharmaprasaṅgena meroḥ pārśve mahāgireḥ
english: And on a religious mission that foremost of ascetics, repairing to the asylum of Triņabindu at the side of the mighty mountain, Meru, took up his abode there.

And with his senses centred on the study of the Vedas, that righteous-souled one, going to the hermitage, carried on austerities; but his religious rites were disturbed by certain girls. And daughters of sages and Pannagas and those of Rājarşis, as well as those of Apsarās, sporting, arrived at that quarter.

And with his senses centred on the study of the Vedas, that righteous-souled one, going to the hermitage, carried on austerities; but his religious rites were disturbed by certain girls. And daughters of sages and Pannagas and those of Rājarşis, as well as those of Apsarās, sporting, arrived at that quarter.

sanskrit: नित्यशस्तास्तु तं देशं गत्वा क्रीडन्ति कन्यकाः
transliteration: nityaśastāstu taṃ deśaṃ gatvā krīḍanti kanyakāḥ
english: And an account of every season being genial at that spot and also of the loveliness of the wood, the damsels, repairing to this place. ever disport there.

And on account of the beauty of that region, those wenches, coming to where that twice-born one, Pulastya was, used to sing, to play on instruments, and to dance; and thus those blameless beauties disturbed the rites of that anchoret practising austerities. Thereat, the mighty ascetic, waxing wroth, said,

sanskrit: तास्तु सर्वाः प्रतिश्रुत्य तस्य वाक्यं महात्मनः
transliteration: tāstu sarvāḥ pratiśrutya tasya vākyaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: ‘She that comes within my kin, shall conceive.' Hearing the words of the high-souled one, (the damsels), afraid of a Brāhamana's curse, ceased to to haunt that place. But Triņabindu's daughter had not heard anything of all this, and going to the asylum, she ranged it fearlessly.

‘She that comes within my kin, shall conceive.' Hearing the words of the high-souled one, (the damsels), afraid of a Brāhamana's curse, ceased to to haunt that place. But Triņabindu's daughter had not heard anything of all this, and going to the asylum, she ranged it fearlessly.

She did not see there any of her associates come to that spot. And at that time that exceedingly energetic and mighty sage, Prajāpati's son, with his soul sanctified through eticism, was engaged in the study of the Veda.

sanskrit: सा तु वेदश्रुतिं श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा वै तपसो निधिम्
transliteration: sā tu vedaśrutiṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā vai tapaso nidhim
english: Hearing the sounds of Vedic recitation, and seeing that storehouse of asceticism, she had her body turned pale, and signs of pregnancy displayed themselves.

sanskrit: इदं मे किन्त्विति ज्ञात्वा पितुर्गत्वा ऽ ऽश्रमे स्थिता
transliteration: idaṃ me kintviti jñātvā piturgatvā ' 'śrame sthitā
english: Seeing that evil befall her, she was wrought up with anxiety; and, understanding matters, she said, "What is this?' And, going to her father's hermitage, stayed there.
Seeing her in this condition, Triņabindu said, "Wherefore is the person that you bear unlike what it used to be?'

sanskrit: सा तु कृत्वाञ्जलिं दीना कन्योवाच तपोधनम्
न जाने कारणं तात येन मे रूपमीदृशम्
transliteration: sā tu kṛtvāñjaliṃ dīnā kanyovāca tapodhanam
na jāne kāraṇaṃ tāta yena me rūpamīdṛśam
english: Thereat, in .woe-begone guise, with joined hands, his daughter replied to that one having asceticism for the riches, 'O father, cause know I none whereby I have come by this appearance.
But searching for my associates, I had ere this alone repaired to the noble asylum of the Maharși Pulastya of a purified spirit.

sanskrit: न च पश्याम्यहं तत्र काञ्चिदभ्यागतां सखीम्
transliteration: na ca paśyāmyahaṃ tatra kāñcidabhyāgatāṃ sakhīm
english: But associate found there I none, that had come thither. And seeing this change for the worse of my form, I from fear have come hither.
Thereat the Rajarsi, Trinabindu, having a live effulgence through asceticism, entered into contemplation, and saw the consequence of the sage's act.

sanskrit: स तु विज्ञाय तं शापं महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः
transliteration: sa tu vijñāya taṃ śāpaṃ maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ
english: And coming to know that curse of the Maharși of a purified spirit, he, taking his daughter, went to Pulastya and said.

sanskrit: भगवंस्तनयां मे त्वं गुणैः स्वैरेव भूषिताम्
transliteration: bhagavaṃstanayāṃ me tvaṃ guṇaiḥ svaireva bhūṣitām
english: O worshipful one, O mighty sage, do you accept this daughter of mine, adorned with her native perfections, who of herself has come to you as alms.
She will, without doubt, constantly tend you, practising asceticism, and having your senses fatigued.

sanskrit: तं ब्रुवाणं तु तद्वाक्यं राजर्षिं धार्मिकं तदा
transliteration: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ rājarṣiṃ dhārmikaṃ tadā
english: When that virtuous (sage) had said this, the twice-born Räjarși, desirous of accepting the girl (after due nuptial rights), said to the former, 'Well !'

sanskrit: दत्त्वा स तु यथान्यायं स्वमाश्रमपदं गतः
transliteration: dattvā sa tu yathānyāyaṃ svamāśramapadaṃ gataḥ
english: Having given away his daughter, the king went (back) to his asylum; and the girl stayed there, gratifying her husband with her virtues.

sanskrit: प्रीतः स तु महातेजा वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
transliteration: prītaḥ sa tu mahātejā vākyametaduvāca ha
english: And that best of ascetics was gratified with her character and behaviour. And well pleased (with her), that highly energetic one said.

sanskrit: परितुष्टो ऽस्मि सुश्रोणि गुणानां सम्पदा भृशम्
english: 'O you of shapely hips, well-pleased am I with you with your wealth of worth, and therefore, O exalted one, I will today confer on you a son like to yourself, who will perpetuate both the lines*-being celebrated as Paulastya. *(i.e. maternal and paternal lines.)

sanskrit: तस्मात्स विश्रवा नाम भविष्यति न संशयः
transliteration: tasmātsa viśravā nāma bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ

english: Thus addressed, that noble damsel with her soul wrought with delight, in a short time brought forth her son Visravā, famed over the three worlds and furnished with virtue and fame: versed in the Vedas, of an impartial spirit, and ever engaged in observing vows. And the ascetic, Viśravă, was furnished with asceticism even like his sire. ever
Pulastya's son-that prime of ascetics-Visravāin a short time was engaged in asceticism like his father.

And he was truthful, and of excellent character and controlled senses; was engaged in the study of the Vedas; and was of the sanctified spirit; and he was not addicted to any of the pleasures of life, and was always studious of religion.

sanskrit: ज्ञात्वा तस्य तु तद्वृत्तं भरद्वाजो महामुनिः
transliteration: jñātvā tasya tu tadvṛttaṃ bharadvājo mahāmuniḥ
english: Learning of his ways, that mighty ascetic, Bharadvāja, gave to Visravā for his wife, his daughter, Devavarņinſ. And having religiously wed Bhāradvāja's daughter, that foremost of ascetics, Visravā, conceiving the highest delight, began to reflect on the welfare of his offspring with an intelligence concentrated on them. And on her that one cognisant of righteousness begot child, exceedingly wonderful, endowed with energy, and adorned with all Brahma* qualities. On his having been born, his grand-father was rejoiced, and, marking the profitable intelligence (of the boy, he thought that) he would be the lord of riches. And well-pleased, (Pulastya) in company with the Devarsis (thought), Inasmuch as this is Viśravá's offspring, and as he resembles Viśravā himself, so he should be known by the name of Vaisravana. own a *Such as self-control, asceticism, purity, etc.
Then the exceedingly energetic Vaiśravana, repairing to the wood of asceticism, increased in power) like to a fire fed by sacrificial oblations.

sanskrit: चरिष्ये परमं धर्मं धर्मो हि परमा गतिः
transliteration: cariṣye paramaṃ dharmaṃ dharmo hi paramā gatiḥ
english: And as he was staying in the hermitage, that high-souled one thought, 'I shall practice prime righteousness: verily virtue is the supreme way.'
For a thousand years, he, having his senses controlled, practised rigid austerities in that mighty forest, observing (all the while) the most rigorous restrictions.

And on a thousand years having been numbered, he by turns observed the rules relative to each term; (at first) living on water, (then) on air, and (last) going absolutely without any food. Thus passed away a thousand years like one.

sanskrit: अथ प्रीतो महातेजाः सेन्द्रैः सुरगणैः सह
transliteration: atha prīto mahātejāḥ sendraiḥ suragaṇaiḥ saha

sanskrit: परितुष्टो ऽस्मि ते वत्स कर्मणानेन सुव्रत
वरं वृणीष्व भद्रं ते वरार्हस्त्वं महामते
transliteration: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te varārhastvaṃ mahāmate
english: Then the highly energetic Brahmā along with the Indra and the celestials, coming to that asylum, addressed (Vaisravana), saying, '0 child, I am well-pleased with you for this act of your, O you of excellent vows. Do you, good betide you, ask for the 'boon (that you would have), for, O magnanimous one, you are worthy of a boon.'
Then Vaisravaņa said to the Pitāmaha, who was present, 'O reverend one, I crave for the power of maintaining and protecting people.'
Thereat, Brahmä along with the deities gladly said to Vaiśravana in a gratified spirit, Very well!
I am about to create the fourth of the Protectors of the creatures-Yama, Indra and Varuna, the position which is sought for by you.
Do you, O you cognisant of righteousness, attain the same; do you receive the position of the lord of riches. You shall be the fourth among the Sakra, the lord of waters, etc.
Do you take for your vehicle this car, named Puşpaka, resembling the Sun himself, and thus raise yourself to an equality with the celestials.

sanskrit: स्वस्ति ते ऽस्तु गमिष्यामः सर्व एव यथागतम्
कृतकृत्या वयं तात दत्त्वा तव वरद्वयम्
transliteration: svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmaḥ sarva eva yathāgatam
kṛtakṛtyā vayaṃ tāta dattvā tava varadvayam
english: Good betide you! We shall (now) go whither we had come, having, my child, done my duty and bestowed on you the couple of boons.

sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा स गतो ब्रह्मा स्वस्थानं त्रिदशैः सह
transliteration: ityuktvā sa gato brahmā svasthānaṃ tridaśaiḥ saha
english: Having said this, Brahmă along with the celestials went to his own quarters. On the deities with Brahmã at their head, having departed foe the heavenly regions, the selfpossessed lord of wealth of subdued senses with joined hands spoke to his sire, saying, 'o reverend one, I have received the wished-for boon from the great-father, but the exalted lord of creatures has not fixed any abode for me. Therefore, O lord, do you seek out some dwelling for me, where no creature whatever can come by misfortune. Thus accosted by his son, that best of ascetics, Viśravä, spoke, O righteous one,' Listen! O excellent one.

sanskrit: वने स पितरं प्राह प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतात्मवान्
निवासनं न मे देवो विदधे स प्रजापतिः
transliteration: vane sa pitaraṃ prāha prāñjaliḥ prayatātmavān
nivāsanaṃ na me devo vidadhe sa prajāpatiḥ

sanskrit: तं पश्य भगवन्कञ्चिन्निवासं साधु मे प्रभो
transliteration: taṃ paśya bhagavankañcinnivāsaṃ sādhu me prabho

sanskrit: न च पीडा भवेद्यत्र प्राणिनो यस्य कस्यचित्
transliteration: na ca pīḍā bhavedyatra prāṇino yasya kasyacit
english: Having said this, Brahmă along with the celestials went to his own quarters. On the deities with Brahmã at their head, having departed foe the heavenly regions, the selfpossessed lord of wealth of subdued senses with joined hands spoke to his sire, saying, 'o reverend one, I have received the wished-for boon from the great-father, but the exalted lord of creatures has not fixed any abode for me. Therefore, O lord, do you seek out some dwelling for me, where no creature whatever can come by misfortune. Thus accosted by his son, that best of ascetics, Viśravä, spoke, O righteous one,' Listen! O excellent one.

sanskrit: तस्याग्रे तु विशाला सा महेन्द्रस्य पुरी यथा
लङ्का नाम पुरी रम्या निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा
transliteration: tasyāgre tu viśālā sā mahendrasya purī yathā
laṅkā nāma purī ramyā nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā

sanskrit: तत्र त्वं वस भद्रं ते लङ्कायां नात्र संशयः
transliteration: tatra tvaṃ vasa bhadraṃ te laṅkāyāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ

english: Formerly she was renounced by the Raksasas afflicted with the fear of Vişnu; and was empty of swarms of Rākşasa, who had gone to the nethermost regions. Now Lanka is vacant, and there is no one that lords it over her. Do you, my child, for abode, at your ease repair thither. Your stay there shall meet with no rub, and no manner of disturbance shall occur there.

sanskrit: शून्या सम्प्रति लङ्का सा प्रभुस्तस्या न विद्यते
स त्वं तत्र निवासाय गच्छ पुत्र यथासुखम्
transliteration: śūnyā samprati laṅkā sā prabhustasyā na vidyate
sa tvaṃ tatra nivāsāya gaccha putra yathāsukham
english: Formerly she was renounced by the Raksasas afflicted with the fear of Vişnu; and was empty of swarms of Rākşasa, who had gone to the nethermost regions. Now Lanka is vacant, and there is no one that lords it over her. Do you, my child, for abode, at your ease repair thither. Your stay there shall meet with no rub, and no manner of disturbance shall occur there.

sanskrit: निर्दोषस्तत्र ते वासो न बाधास्तत्र कस्यचित्
एतच्छुत्वा स धर्मात्मा धर्मिष्ठं वचनं पितुः
transliteration: nirdoṣastatra te vāso na bādhāstatra kasyacit
etacchutvā sa dharmātmā dharmiṣṭhaṃ vacanaṃ pituḥ

english: In a short time (Lankā), through his sway, abounded (in wealth). And that foremost of Nairtas, the righteous-son of Visrava, wellpleased, abode in Lankā having the Ocean for her entrenchment.

sanskrit: काले काले तु धर्मात्मा पुष्पकेण धनेश्वरः
transliteration: kāle kāle tu dharmātmā puṣpakeṇa dhaneśvaraḥ
english: At times the righteous-souled lord of riches, mounted on Pușpaka, in humble guise visited his father and mother.

sanskrit: गभस्तिभिः सूर्य इवावभासयन्पितुः समीपं प्रययौ स वित्तपः
transliteration: gabhastibhiḥ sūrya ivāvabhāsayanpituḥ samīpaṃ prayayau sa vittapaḥ
english: And hymned by hosts of deities and Gandharvas, having his mansion graced with the dancing of Apsarās, and floating on rays like the sun himself, that ruler of riches went to his sire.
Hearing the words uttered by Agastya, Răma wondered as to how formerly Rākşasas were generated in Lanka.
Then shaking his head, he, struck with wonder, momentarily eyeing Agastya, addressed Agastya resembling fire, saying.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वेदं भगवद्वाक्यं जातो मे विस्मयः परः
transliteration: śrutvedaṃ bhagavadvākyaṃ jāto me vismayaḥ paraḥ
english: O worshipful one, hearing your words that formerly Lankā had been in the possession of the flesh-eaters, I have been seized with great amazement.
We had heard that the Rākṣasas had sprung in the race of Pulastya. But now you have said that they owe their origin to a different source.

sanskrit: रावणस्य च पुत्रेभ्यः किं नु ते बलवत्तराः
transliteration: rāvaṇasya ca putrebhyaḥ kiṃ nu te balavattarāḥ
english: But were they more powerful than Rāvana, Kumbhakarma and Prahasta and Vikața and the sons of Rāvana?

sanskrit: क एषां पूर्वको ब्रह्मन्किन्नामा च बलोत्कटः
अपराधं च कं प्राप्य विष्णुना द्राविताः कथम्
transliteration: ka eṣāṃ pūrvako brahmankinnāmā ca balotkaṭaḥ
aparādhaṃ ca kaṃ prāpya viṣṇunā drāvitāḥ katham
english: Who was their progenitor? And what was the name of that terrific strength? And through what transgression were they driven out by Vişnu?
All this, O sinless one, do you tell me in detail, and do you dispel my curiosity even as the sun dispels darkness.
Hearing Rāghava's words, fair and fraught with polished phrase and period, Agastya, struck with surprise, said to Rāghava.
The lord of creatures sprang from water, first created water. And the lotus-born one generated creatures for protecting that element.
Thereupon those creatures humbly presented themselves before the creator, saying, What shall we do? We are sore tried by hunger and thirst.
The lord of creatures, laughing, addressed them, saying, “You men, do you carefully guard this (water).”

sanskrit: रक्षामेति च तत्रान्ये जक्षाम इति चापरे
transliteration: rakṣāmeti ca tatrānye jakṣāma iti cāpare
english: Thereat some said 'Raksama,' (i.e. we shall protect.) and others 'Yaksāma.' (We shall worship.) Thus accosted by those afflicted with hunger and thirst, the creator said.

sanskrit: रक्षामेति च यैरुक्तं राक्षसास्ते भवन्तु वः
जक्षाम इति यैरुक्तं यक्षा एव भवन्तु वः
transliteration: rakṣāmeti ca yairuktaṃ rākṣasāste bhavantu vaḥ
jakṣāma iti yairuktaṃ yakṣā eva bhavantu vaḥ
english: Those among you who have said 'Raksama,' shall be Raksasas; and those among you, who have said 'Yaksama' shall be Yaksas.
And there sprang the brothers-repressors of foes-Heti and Praheti lords of Raksasas, resembling Madhu Kaitabha himself.
Praheti, who was righteous, went to the wood of asceticism. And Heti exerted himself to the utmost to get himself wived.

sanskrit: स कालभगिनीं कन्यां भयां नाम भयावहाम्
transliteration: sa kālabhaginīṃ kanyāṃ bhayāṃ nāma bhayāvahām
english: And that magnanimous one of immeasurable soul married the exceedingly terrific sister of Kala, named Bhayā (Fear.)

sanskrit: पुत्रं पुत्रवतां श्रेष्ठो विद्युत्केश इति श्रुतम्
transliteration: putraṃ putravatāṃ śreṣṭho vidyutkeśa iti śrutam
english: And on her Heti-foremost of Rākşasas and best of those having sons-beget a son, known as Vidyutkeśa.
Heti's son, the exceedingly energetic Vidyutkeśa, possessed of the splendour of the sun, grew up even like a lotus in water.

sanskrit: ततो दारक्रियां तस्य कर्तुं व्यवसितः पिता
transliteration: tato dārakriyāṃ tasya kartuṃ vyavasitaḥ pitā
english: And when that night-ranger arrived at proper youth, his sire turned his attention towards his marriage.
And that best of Rākṣasas-heti-in the interests of his son asked for the hand of Sandhya's daughter; like to Sandhyā* herself in the potency. * The evening Twilight-spouse of the Sun.

Sandhya, reflecting that she needs must have to be given away by her, bestowed her on Vidyutkesa, O Raghava. Having obtained Sandhya's daughter, the night-ranger Vidyutkeśa, sports with her even as Maghavan does with the daughter of Puloma.

sanskrit: रमते स्म तया सार्धं पौलोम्या मघवानिव
transliteration: ramate sma tayā sārdhaṃ paulomyā maghavāniva
english: Sandhya, reflecting that she needs must have to be given away by her, bestowed her on Vidyutkesa, O Raghava. Having obtained Sandhya's daughter, the night-ranger Vidyutkeśa, sports with her even as Maghavan does with the daughter of Puloma.
It came to pass that after a length of time, O Răma, Sälakatankata was filled with child by Vidyutkeśa, as the clouds are furnished with water by the Ocean,

Then repairing to Mandara, the Rākşasi brought forth her child, having the splendour of rain-charged clouds; even as Gangā had delivered herself of the child begotten by fire.* And having delivered herself of her offspring, she again became bent on disporting with Vidyutkeśa. *Mahesvara.

sanskrit: रेमे तु सार्धं पतिना विस्मृत्य सुतमात्मजम्
transliteration: reme tu sārdhaṃ patinā vismṛtya sutamātmajam

english: And forsaken by them both, the infant furnished with the brightness of the autumnal sun, entering his clenched fist into his mouth, began to cry slowly.
It so fell that, journeying with Parvati, Siva, riding his bull through the serial regions, heard the sounds of weeping, on

Along with Uma, he saw the Raksasas's son, as he was crying. And sent by Pārvatī, whose heart was moved by by compassion, Bhava destroyer of Tripura-made that Raksasa's offspring attain the age of his mother, and conferred him immortality. And for compassing Parvati's pleasure, Mahadeva, indestructible and undeteriorating granted (the Raksasa) the power of ranging the air.

sanskrit: अमरं चैव तं कृत्वा महादेवो ऽक्षरो ऽव्ययः
english: Along with Uma, he saw the Raksasas's son, as he was crying. And sent by Pārvatī, whose heart was moved by by compassion, Bhava destroyer of Tripura-made that Raksasa's offspring attain the age of his mother, and conferred him immortality. And for compassing Parvati's pleasure, Mahadeva, indestructible and undeteriorating granted (the Raksasa) the power of ranging the air.
O son of the king, Umă also bestowed a boon: “Henceforth the Rāksasis shall conceive in a day, bring forth (child) in a day, and the child shall in a day be furnished with the age of its mother.'

sanskrit: ततः सुकेशो वरदानगर्वितः श्रियं प्रभोः प्राप्य हरस्य पार्श्वतः
चचार सर्वत्र महान्महामतिः खगं पुरं प्राप्य पुरन्दरो यथा
transliteration: tataḥ sukeśo varadānagarvitaḥ śriyaṃ prabhoḥ prāpya harasya pārśvataḥ
cacāra sarvatra mahānmahāmatiḥ khagaṃ puraṃ prāpya purandaro yathā
english: Then the great and magnanimous Sukeśa, puffed up with the receipt of boons, having obtained auspiciousness at the hands of the lord, Hara, began to range everywhere, even as Purandara did on having obtained heaven.

sanskrit: सुकेशं धार्मिकं दृष्ट्वा वरलब्धं च राक्षसम्
transliteration: sukeśaṃ dhārmikaṃ dṛṣṭvā varalabdhaṃ ca rākṣasam
english: Cveing Sukeśa righteous and furnished with the boon, a virtuous Gandharva, named Grāmani, of the effulgence of fire, who had a daughter, called Devavati, like to a second Sri herself, famed over the three worlds, and endowed with beauty and youth, bestowed her on Sukeśa as if he had bestowed the goddess of fortune of the Rākşasa.

sanskrit: तां सुकेशाय धर्मेण ददौ रक्षःश्रियं यथा
transliteration: tāṃ sukeśāya dharmeṇa dadau rakṣaḥśriyaṃ yathā
english: Cveing Sukeśa righteous and furnished with the boon, a virtuous Gandharva, named Grāmani, of the effulgence of fire, who had a daughter, called Devavati, like to a second Sri herself, famed over the three worlds, and endowed with beauty and youth, bestowed her on Sukeśa as if he had bestowed the goddess of fortune of the Rākşasa.

sanskrit: वरदानकृतैश्वर्यं सा तं प्राप्य पतिं प्रियम्
transliteration: varadānakṛtaiśvaryaṃ sā taṃ prāpya patiṃ priyam
english: And like an indigent person on obtaining wealth, Devavati, on obtaining her beloved husband, affluent in consequence of having received the boon, was (greatly) delighted. And in her company, that night-ranger appeared graceful, even as a mighty elephant sprung from Añjanā* does in the company of a she-elephant. *The designation of an elephant.

sanskrit: स तया सह संयुक्तो रराज रजनीचरः
transliteration: sa tayā saha saṃyukto rarāja rajanīcaraḥ
english: And like an indigent person on obtaining wealth, Devavati, on obtaining her beloved husband, affluent in consequence of having received the boon, was (greatly) delighted. And in her company, that night-ranger appeared graceful, even as a mighty elephant sprung from Añjanā* does in the company of a she-elephant. *The designation of an elephant.

sanskrit: माल्यवन्तं सुमालिं च मालिं च बलिनां वरम्
transliteration: mālyavantaṃ sumāliṃ ca māliṃ ca balināṃ varam

english: That lord of Rākşasas begot (on her) three sons, resembling his three eyes the Raksasas, Mālyavän, Sumāli and that foremost of the strong-Māli; all resembling the three worlds possessing themselves in calmness; like to the three Fires established; fierce like to the three mantras, dreadful like three diseases springing respectively from morbid Air, Bile and Phlegm.* *The entire edifice of Hindu Pathology is based on the three-fold division of the morbid humours into Air, Bile and Phlegm. This division, albeit it may appear crude and unscientific to Europeans, taken all, in all, wonderfully answers its purpose. The tact displayed by Hindu physicians in diagnosing diseases on this method is wonderful. From feeling the Pulse alone, a Hindu physician, getting at the predominance of one or more morbid humours of the system, can accurately ascertain a patient's health. The infallibility with which predictions of death are generally made, attests the scientific soundness of the division in question, and renders superfluous any elaborate argument in its defence.
The three sons of Sukeśa, having the energy of the three fires, grew up like a disease which has been disregarded.
And learning that their father had received a boon by virtue of his power proceeding from asceticism, the brothers, firmly resolved, went to Meru for practising penances.
And adopting rigid restrictions, the Rākṣasas, O best of kings, entered upon austerities, terrible, and capable of arousing the fear of all beings.
Practising penances rare on the earth with truth and candour and self-control, they afflicted the three worlds with gods, Asuras and human beings.
Then that lord-the four-faced one-stationed on a superb car, addressed Sukeśa's sons, saying, “I am for conferring boons (on you).'

sanskrit: ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे वेपमाना इव द्रुमाः
transliteration: ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve vepamānā iva drumāḥ
english: Knowing that Brahmā surrounded by Indra and the other celestials was ready to bestow boons, they, with joined hands, said, trembling like trees.

sanskrit: तपसाराधितो देव यदि नो दिशसे वरम्
transliteration: tapasārādhito deva yadi no diśase varam
english: O god! that have been adored through asceticism, if you do intend to confer on us a boon, let us be invincible, capable of slaying foes, immortal, lordly, and ever devoted to each other.'
O god! that have been adored through asceticism, if you do intend to confer on us a boon, let us be invincible, capable of slaying foes, immortal, lordly, and ever devoted to each other.'

Thereat saying 'So be it,' to the sons of Sukeśa, the lord Brahmā, (ever) cherishing Brāhmaṇas with affection, went to the Brahmā regions. O Rāma, having obtained the boons, those night-rangers, rendered intrepid in consequences of having the boon conferred on them, began to disturb celestials and Asuras.

sanskrit: वरं लब्ध्वा तु ते सर्वे राम रात्रिञ्चरास्तदा
transliteration: varaṃ labdhvā tu te sarve rāma rātriñcarāstadā
english: Thereat saying 'So be it,' to the sons of Sukeśa, the lord Brahmā, (ever) cherishing Brāhmaṇas with affection, went to the Brahmā regions. O Rāma, having obtained the boons, those night-rangers, rendered intrepid in consequences of having the boon conferred on them, began to disturb celestials and Asuras.

And like to men abiding in hell, the celestials, chāraṇas and hosts of sages, being harassed (by Raksasas), did not find any deliverer. And then, O foremost of the Raghus, the Raksasas, assembled together, joyfully said to the undeteriorating Viśvakarmá—prince of artist.

And like to men abiding in hell, the celestials, chāraṇas and hosts of sages, being harassed (by Raksasas), did not find any deliverer. And then, O foremost of the Raghus, the Raksasas, assembled together, joyfully said to the undeteriorating Viśvakarmá—prince of artist.

'You by your own energy are the architect of the great gods, endowed with energy and prowess and strength. Do you, O magnanimous one, construct a fabric for us after our heart hard by Himavān, or Meru, or Mandara. And do you erect a magnificent mansion for us resembling the mansion itself of Maheśvara.' Thereat Viśvakarmā the mighty-arm of the Rākṣasas spoke of a building like the Amarāvati of Sakra.

Thereat Viśvakarmā the mighty-arm of the Rākṣasas spoke of a building like the Amarāvati of Sakra.

'On the shore of the Southern sea is a mountain named Trikūța. A second also is there called Suvela, you lords of Raksasas.

On the midmost peak of that mountain resembling clouds, inaccessible even to the fowls of the air, all the four quarters have been hewn with bones.* If I am desired by you, I can construct the city of Lanka (there), having an area of thirty Yojanas, and measuring an hundred in length; surrounded with a golden wall and furnished with golden gateways. *Tanka-may also mean a hatchet or a sword.
And occupying the citadel of Lankā, backed by innumerable Rākṣasas, you will be invincible to foes and capable of destroying them.'

Hearing Viśvakarmā's speech, those foremost of Rākṣasas, accompanied by thousands of followers, went to the palace and set-up in the same, having a strong wall and a moat, abounding in hundreds of golden edifices. And obtaining Lanka, the night-rangers, exceedingly delighted, began to dwell therein.

sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु यथाकामं च राघव
transliteration: etasminneva kāle tu yathākāmaṃ ca rāghava
english: At this time, O Rāghava, there lived at her pleasure a Gandharvi, named Narmadā. O son of Raghu, She hai three daughters, resembling Sri, Hri, and kirti in splendour. And albeit no Rāks asi herself, she, beginning with the eldest, gladly married to the Räkşasas her daughter having faces resembling the full moon.

sanskrit: ततो माल्यवतो भार्या सुन्दरी नाम सुन्दरी
transliteration: tato mālyavato bhāryā sundarī nāma sundarī

sanskrit: स तस्यां जनयामास यदपत्यं निबोध तत्
transliteration: sa tasyāṃ janayāmāsa yadapatyaṃ nibodha tat

sanskrit: नाम्ना केतुमती राम प्राणेभ्यो ऽपि गरीयसी
english: Vajramuşti, and Virūpākşa, and the Räksasa Durmukha, and Suptaghna, and Yajñakopa, and Matta and Unmatta; and, O Rāma, there was also born a lovely daughter of Sundari, Anala. And Sumāli's wife of face like the full Moon, named Ketumati, was dearer to him than his life itself.

O mighty king, do you, gradually, know the offspring that were begot by Sumāli on Ketumatī-Prahasta and Akampana, and Vikata, and Kālikāmukha, and DhumrāKșa, and Danda, and the redoubtable Supārsva, and Sañhrãi, and Praghasa, and the Rākşasa, Bhāsakarņa, and Rākā, and Pushpotkată, and Kaikasi of luminous smiles, and Kumbhinasi these are known as the offspring of Sumali. Māli had for wife a graceful Gandharvi, named Vasudă having having eyes resembling lotus-petals, of a lovely look and like to the most magnificent Yakși of them all.

sanskrit: राका पुष्पोत्कटा चैव कैकसी च शुचिस्मिता ॥
transliteration: rākā puṣpotkaṭā caiva kaikasī ca śucismitā

sanskrit: कुम्भीनसी च इत्येते सुमालेः प्रसवाः स्मृताः
transliteration: kumbhīnasī ca ityete sumāleḥ prasavāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: O mighty king, do you, gradually, know the offspring that were begot by Sumāli on Ketumatī-Prahasta and Akampana, and Vikata, and Kālikāmukha, and DhumrāKșa, and Danda, and the redoubtable Supārsva, and Sañhrãi, and Praghasa, and the Rākşasa, Bhāsakarņa, and Rākā, and Pushpotkată, and Kaikasi of luminous smiles, and Kumbhinasi these are known as the offspring of Sumali. Māli had for wife a graceful Gandharvi, named Vasudă having having eyes resembling lotus-petals, of a lovely look and like to the most magnificent Yakși of them all.

sanskrit: अपत्यं कथ्यमानं तु मया त्वं शृणु राघव
transliteration: apatyaṃ kathyamānaṃ tu mayā tvaṃ śṛṇu rāghava
english: Do you, O master, listen to me as I mention to you, O Raghava the offspring that Sumali's younger brother beget on her, Anala, and Nila, and Sampāti. These night-rangers sons to Mali were the courtiers of Vibhișana.

sanskrit: ततस्तु ते राक्षसपुङ्गवास्त्रयो निशाचरैः पुत्रशतैश्च संवृताः
transliteration: tatastu te rākṣasapuṅgavāstrayo niśācaraiḥ putraśataiśca saṃvṛtāḥ
english: And those three foremost of Rākṣasa, accompanied by hundreds of sons night rangers all-elated on account of their measureless prowess, began to worry the sages and serpents and Yakşas, and celestials with Indra (at their head).

Incapable of being confronted (in battle), these resembling Death himself in energy, wondrous elated in consequences of the boon having been conferred on them, ranging the world like to the Wind, were ever engaged in disturbing the sacrifices (of the sages).

Thus afflicted, the deities, sages, and ascetics, wrought up with fear, sought the protection of that god of gods Maheswara creator and destroyer of the cosmos, unborn, of an unmanifest form, the stay of all creatures, worthy of being adored, and the . supreme preceptors (of all). And coming to that enemy of Kama* and foc of Tripura the three-eyed (Deity), the gods with their voices faltering through fear, represented with joined hands. *The Hindu Cupid. Mahadeva had burnt to ashes Kama, when he had the fool-hardiness to disturb the contemplation of the former. By the way, Kalidasa has cared his faery fabric, entitled Kumāra Sambhava, on the basis of this legend.

sanskrit: ते समेत्य तु कामारिं त्रिपुरारिं त्रिलोचनम्
transliteration: te sametya tu kāmāriṃ tripurāriṃ trilocanam

english: O reverend one, the creatures of the lord of creatures are being (sorely) troubled by the sons of Sukesa, given to harassing their foes,-swolen with insolence on account of the benn conferred on them by the great-father, asylums, constituting our refuges,-have been divested of their power of granting shelter, and driving off the deities from the etherial regions, they are sporting there like the immortals.

'I am Vişnu,' 'I am Rudra,' 'I am the king of the celestials,' 'I am Yama,' 'I an Varuna,' 'I am the moon,' 'I am the Sun,' flattering themselves in this fashion, Māli and Sumāli and the Rākşasa Malyavān as well as those going before them, are annoying (the gods), breathing exhilaration of martial spirits.

sanskrit: इति माली सुमाली च माल्यवांश्चैव राक्षसाः
बाधन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः
transliteration: iti mālī sumālī ca mālyavāṃścaiva rākṣasāḥ
bādhante samaroddharṣā ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ
english: 'I am Vişnu,' 'I am Rudra,' 'I am the king of the celestials,' 'I am Yama,' 'I an Varuna,' 'I am the moon,' 'I am the Sun,' flattering themselves in this fashion, Māli and Sumāli and the Rākşasa Malyavān as well as those going before them, are annoying (the gods), breathing exhilaration of martial spirits.

sanskrit: धन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः
transliteration: dhante samaroddharṣā ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ
english: Thus addressed by the immortals in a body, that lord, Kaparddi of red-blue hue, reflecting that it would be wrong for him to destroy Sukesa (with his own hands), spoke to the gods.

sanskrit: अहं तान्न हनिष्यामि मयावध्या हि ते सुराः
किं तु मन्त्रं प्रदास्यामि यो वै तान्निहनिष्यति
transliteration: ahaṃ tānna haniṣyāmi mayāvadhyā hi te surāḥ
kiṃ tu mantraṃ pradāsyāmi yo vai tānnihaniṣyati
english: I shall not slay them, you gods; they are incapable of being slain by me. But I shall unfold to you the way in which they will be destroyed.

sanskrit: गच्छध्वं शरणं विष्णुं हनिष्यति स तान्प्रभुः
transliteration: gacchadhvaṃ śaraṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ haniṣyati sa tānprabhuḥ
english: Do you, you Maharsis, in the heat of this affairs, seck the shelter of Visnu. That lord will slay them.
Thereat, saluting Maheśvara with the sounds of Jaya, (the celestial) afflicted with the fear of the night-rangers, presented themselves before Visnu.
And bowing down to the god holding the conch, discus and mace, and paying him high homage, they, greatly flurried, addressed him about the sons of Sukeśa, saying.
O god, by virtue of the boon (that has been bestowed on them), resembling the three fires, Sukesa's three sons, assailing us, have deprived us of our abode.

sanskrit: लङ्का नाम पुरी दुर्गा त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिता
transliteration: laṅkā nāma purī durgā trikūṭaśikhare sthitā
english: There is a city named Lankā, stationed on the top of Trikuta, (extremely) difficult of entrance. Taking up their station at that place, the nightrangers in a body pursue us.

sanskrit: शरणं त्वां वयं प्राप्ता गतिर्भव सुरेश्वर
transliteration: śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ vayaṃ prāptā gatirbhava sureśvara
english: Do you, O slayer of Madhu, destroy them for our welfare. We have sought your shelter. Become our refuge, O foremost of celestials.

sanskrit: भयेष्वभयदो ऽस्माकं नान्यो ऽस्ति भवता विना
english: Do you dedicate to Yama the lotuses of their faces, severed (in pieces) with your discus. Save you, we have none who can, while tormented with fright, inspire us with courage.

sanskrit: नुदं त्वं नो भयं देव नीहारमिव भास्करः
transliteration: nudaṃ tvaṃ no bhayaṃ deva nīhāramiva bhāskaraḥ
english: Slay in encounter the elated Rākşasas along with their adherents; and even as the sun dried up dew, do you dispel this fear of ours.

sanskrit: अभयं भयदो ऽरीणां दत्त्वा देवानुवाच ह
english: Thus accosted by the deities, that god of gods Janārdana who brings fear to foes cheering up the celestial up the celestials, said to them.

sanskrit: तांश्चास्य तनयाञ्जाने येषां ज्येष्ठः स माल्यवान्
transliteration: tāṃścāsya tanayāñjāne yeṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ sa mālyavān
english: 'I know the Raksasa, Sukesa, as flushed with the boon bestowed by Iśāna. And I also know his sons, of whom Mālyavān is the eldest. Those worst if Rākṣasas that have over-riden your dignity will I, wrought up with wrath, slay (in battle); therefore, you gods, be of good cheer.

'I know the Raksasa, Sukesa, as flushed with the boon bestowed by Iśāna. And I also know his sons, of whom Mālyavān is the eldest. Those worst if Rākṣasas that have over-riden your dignity will I, wrought up with wrath, slay (in battle); therefore, you gods, be of good cheer.
Thus addressed by the mighty Vişņu, the gods, highly rejoiced, went to their respective quarters, extolling Janārdana.
And hearing of the activity of the celestials; the night-rangers Mālyavân addressed his heroic brothers, saying.

The immortals and sages, going to Sankara, spoke these words, desirous of our destruction, The terrific sons of Sukeśa, puffed up, and swollen on account of their strength flowing from the boon, are crossing us at every step.

The immortals and sages, going to Sankara, spoke these words, desirous of our destruction, The terrific sons of Sukeśa, puffed up, and swollen on account of their strength flowing from the boon, are crossing us at every step.

sanskrit: राक्षसैरभिभूताः स्म न शक्ताः स्म प्रजापते
transliteration: rākṣasairabhibhūtāḥ sma na śaktāḥ sma prajāpate
english: We have been overpowered by the Rākṣasas. And, o lord of creatures, from fear of those wicked-minded ones, we cannot remain in our own homes.
Therefore, to do us good, do you, O threeeyed one, destroy them; and, O best of consuming ones, do you with your roars, burn them up.

sanskrit: शिरः करं च धुन्वान इदं वचनमब्रवीत्
transliteration: śiraḥ karaṃ ca dhunvāna idaṃ vacanamabravīt
english: Thus addressed by the deities, the slayer of Andhaka, hearing their speech, said, shaking his head and hands.

sanskrit: अवध्या मम ते देवाः सुकेशतनया रणे
मन्त्रं तु वः प्रदास्यामि यस्तान्वै निहनिष्यति
transliteration: avadhyā mama te devāḥ sukeśatanayā raṇe
mantraṃ tu vaḥ pradāsyāmi yastānvai nihaniṣyati
english: You gods, Sukesa's sons are incapable of being slain by me in battle. But I shall tell you the means whereby they may be slain.
Do you seek the shelter of him who hold the discus and mace in his hands, and who is clad in a yellow attire, of Janardana, Hari, even of the auspicious Nārāyaṇa.
Having received this counsel of Hara, they, rendering reverence to that enemy of Kāma, came the abode of Nārāyana and communicated everything to him.
Then Nārāyana spoke to the celestials with Indra at their head, I will slay those foes of the celestials. You gods, cast off all fear!

sanskrit: प्रतिज्ञातो वधो ऽस्माकं चिन्त्यतां यदिह क्षमम्
english: to O foremost of Rākşasas, Hari promised to the frightened celestials that he would slay us. Therefore do you think as to what is fit.

sanskrit: राधेयो बहुमायी च लोकपालो ऽथ धार्मिकः
english: Hiranyakaśipu has met with death (at the hands of Hari), as also other enemies of the immortals. And Namuci and Kālanemi, and that foremost of heroes, Sanhrada and Rādheya, and Bahumāyī, and the virtuous Lokapāla, and Yamala, and Arjuna, and Hardikya, and Sumbha and Niśumbhaka, Asuras and Dānavas endowed with strength and possessed of terrific prowess all these, who having come to the field, had never been heard of as worsted, who had performed hundreds of sacrifices, who had been well skilled in illusion, who had been versed in every branch of knowledge, and who were the terrors of their foes have by hundreds and by thousands been destroyed by Narayana. Learning this, it behove you to do what would conduce to the behoof of all. It is a sore task to defeat Narayana, who wish to slay us.

Hiranyakaśipu has met with death (at the hands of Hari), as also other enemies of the immortals. And Namuci and Kālanemi, and that foremost of heroes, Sanhrada and Rādheya, and Bahumāyī, and the virtuous Lokapāla, and Yamala, and Arjuna, and Hardikya, and Sumbha and Niśumbhaka, Asuras and Dānavas endowed with strength and possessed of terrific prowess all these, who having come to the field, had never been heard of as worsted, who had performed hundreds of sacrifices, who had been well skilled in illusion, who had been versed in every branch of knowledge, and who were the terrors of their foes have by hundreds and by thousands been destroyed by Narayana. Learning this, it behove you to do what would conduce to the behoof of all. It is a sore task to defeat Narayana, who wish to slay us.

Hiranyakaśipu has met with death (at the hands of Hari), as also other enemies of the immortals. And Namuci and Kālanemi, and that foremost of heroes, Sanhrada and Rādheya, and Bahumāyī, and the virtuous Lokapāla, and Yamala, and Arjuna, and Hardikya, and Sumbha and Niśumbhaka, Asuras and Dānavas endowed with strength and possessed of terrific prowess all these, who having come to the field, had never been heard of as worsted, who had performed hundreds of sacrifices, who had been well skilled in illusion, who had been versed in every branch of knowledge, and who were the terrors of their foes have by hundreds and by thousands been destroyed by Narayana. Learning this, it behove you to do what would conduce to the behoof of all. It is a sore task to defeat Narayana, who wish to slay us.

sanskrit: ततः सुमाली माली च श्रुत्वा माल्यवतो वचः
transliteration: tataḥ sumālī mālī ca śrutvā mālyavato vacaḥ
english: Thereat Sumāli and Māli, hearing the words of Malyavān, said to their eldest brother, like the Asvins addressing Vāsava.
We have studied, performed sacrifices, practised charity, and obtained riches; and attaining long health and long life, we have established sterling righteousness in our path.
With arms plunging into the sea of celestials, we have conquered our unrivalled enemies. Therefore, we have no fear touching death.

sanskrit: अस्माकं प्रमुखे स्थातुं सर्वे बिभ्यति सर्वदा
transliteration: asmākaṃ pramukhe sthātuṃ sarve bibhyati sarvadā
english: Even Narayana and Rudra, Sakra and Yama, ever fear to stay before us (in the field).
O lord of Raksasas. There is no occasion for Visnu's displeasure of us. The mind of Visnu has wavered in consequence of the evil caused by the celestials.
Therefore, will we even avenge ourselves on the gods, from whom has sprung this wrong.

Having taken counsel together, those powerful ones conciliated their forces. And proclaiming (their order) that preparations were to be made, all the foremost Nairtas sallied forth for battle, like to those led by Jambha and Vſtra.

sanskrit: इति ते राम सम्मन्त्र्य सर्वोद्योगेन राक्षसाः
transliteration: iti te rāma sammantrya sarvodyogena rākṣasāḥ

sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गताः सर्वे राक्षसा बलगर्विताः
transliteration: tyaktvā laṅkāṃ gatāḥ sarve rākṣasā balagarvitāḥ

english: Perceiving the destruction of Lanka hand, those deities that had taken up their quarters there, everywhere were struck with fear and felt their spirits depressed.

Mounting the best of the cars, the Rakşasas by hundreds and thousands with intent mind swiftly sallied forth for the celestial regions. And the deities (aforementioned) followed the tract of the Raksasas.

Mounting the best of the cars, the Rakşasas by hundreds and thousands with intent mind swiftly sallied forth for the celestial regions. And the deities (aforementioned) followed the tract of the Raksasas.
At the command of Kala, terrible evil omens foreshadowing the destruction of the Raksasachief began to arise on the earth well as in the sky.
The clouds showered down bones and hot blood. The oceans overleapt their continents and the mountains shook.
And jackals of terrific forms, having voices resembling the roaring of clouds, bursting out into a horse-laugh, began to emit cries frightfully.
Creatures were one after another seen to drop down; and mighty swarms of vultures, with mouths belching forth flames, began to wheel over the Raksasa, like to Kala himself.

sanskrit: काका वाश्यन्ति तत्रैव बिडाला वै द्विपादयः
transliteration: kākā vāśyanti tatraiva biḍālā vai dvipādayaḥ
english: And blood-footed pigeons and Sarikas* darted off (around). And crows and two-legged cats began to cry in loud accents. *A species of harlot.

But fast bound with the noose of Death, the Raksasas, proud of their strength, disregarding these omens, march on, and do not stay their course, Mälyavān and Sumāli possessed of prodigious strength, going before the Raksasas, like flaming fires.

sanskrit: माल्यवांश्च सुमाली च माली च सुमहाबलाः
transliteration: mālyavāṃśca sumālī ca mālī ca sumahābalāḥ

english: Even as the gods take refuge under Dhātā, the night-rangers take refuge under Mālyavân resembling the mountain, Mälyavān.
Under the command of Māli that host of Raksasas, roaring like mighty clouds, inspired with the desire of victory, went to the celestial regions.

sanskrit: राक्षसानां समुद्योगं तं तु नारायणः प्रभुः
transliteration: rākṣasānāṃ samudyogaṃ taṃ tu nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
english: The lord Nārāyana, hearing of the preparations of the Rākşasas from a celestial messenger, set his heart on fight. And equipped with weapons and quivers, he mounted on Vinata's offspring.* *Garuda, Narayana's vehicle.

sanskrit: श्रोणिसूत्रं च खड्गं च विमलं कमलेक्षणः ॥
transliteration: śroṇisūtraṃ ca khaḍgaṃ ca vimalaṃ kamalekṣaṇaḥ

sanskrit: सुपर्णपृष्ठे स बभौ श्यामः पीताम्बरो हरिः
transliteration: suparṇapṛṣṭhe sa babhau śyāmaḥ pītāmbaro hariḥ
english: Seated on Suparma's* back, the blue-brown Hari clad in yellow attire resembled a mass of clouds on the crest of the golden mountain, with lightning playing through it. *Lit. fair-feathered-a name of Garua.

And hymned by Siddhas and celestials and sages and mighty (semi-divine) serpents and Gandharvas and Yakşas, the enemy of the Asura hosts presented himself, bearing in his hands the discus, sword, that weapon Śärnga and the conch.

The Raksasa-hosts, struck by the wind produced by the wings of Suparņa, with their pennons swinging to and fro and their weapons scattered about, quaked like the blue summit of a mountain with its crags tossed about.

Then the night-rangers, hemming in Madhava,* began to pierce him with thousands of excellent sharpened weapons dyed in flesh and blood, and resembling the fire of Doomsday. *One of the many designations of Visnu.
As clouds assail a mountain with showers, then the Raksasas, representing clouds, setting up shouts, began to assail Nārāyaṇa representing a mountain.
Visnu of a bright brown-blue hue, being surrounded by the flower of the night-rangers with dark visages, resembled the Añjana mountain, on which the clouds pour down.

sanskrit: शलभा इव केदारं मशका इव पर्वतम्
transliteration: śalabhā iva kedāraṃ maśakā iva parvatam
english: As locusts (flood) a field, knots (throng) about a flame, gad-flies (cluster) around a pot of honey, or makaras (range) in the sea, so the shafts shot by the bows of the Rākṣasa, having (the energy of) the thunder-bolt and endowed with (the velocity of) the wind or thought, pierce Hari as if at the universal dissolution.

sanskrit: हरिं विशन्ति स्म शरा लोका इव विपर्यये
transliteration: hariṃ viśanti sma śarā lokā iva viparyaye
english: As locusts (flood) a field, knots (throng) about a flame, gad-flies (cluster) around a pot of honey, or makaras (range) in the sea, so the shafts shot by the bows of the Rākṣasa, having (the energy of) the thunder-bolt and endowed with (the velocity of) the wind or thought, pierce Hari as if at the universal dissolution.

Those mounted on cars (assailed him) with their cars, and those mounted on the backs of elephants (assailed him) with their elephants, and those riding horses (assailed him) with their horses, and the foot-soldiers attacked him, stationed in the sky; and the foremost of Rākşasas resembling mountains, by means of darts, rstis and tomaras, suspended the respiration of Hari even as the prāņāyāma* does that of a twice-born one. *The practice of regulation respiration and finally suspending the same. This is practised by the Yogis of India, who attribute wonderful virtues to it.

sanskrit: निरुछ्वासं हरिं चक्रुः प्राणायामा इव द्विजम्
transliteration: niruchvāsaṃ hariṃ cakruḥ prāṇāyāmā iva dvijam
english: Those mounted on cars (assailed him) with their cars, and those mounted on the backs of elephants (assailed him) with their elephants, and those riding horses (assailed him) with their horses, and the foot-soldiers attacked him, stationed in the sky; and the foremost of Rākşasas resembling mountains, by means of darts, rstis and tomaras, suspended the respiration of Hari even as the prāņāyāma* does that of a twice-born one. *The practice of regulation respiration and finally suspending the same. This is practised by the Yogis of India, who attribute wonderful virtues to it.
On being sore tried by the night-rangers, like the great Ocean by the fishes (residing in it), that invincible one, taking his ſārņga, showered shafts among the Rākşasas.
With sharpened arrows resembling the thunder, and endowed with the velocity of the wind, shot from his bow drawn to its fullest stretch, Visnu cut off (Raksasas) by hundreds and by thousands.
And dashing away (the Rākṣasa ranks) with his arrowy shower, even as the wind aroused dashes away a downpour, that best of male beings blew his mighty conch Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: सो ऽम्बुजो हरिणा ध्मातः सर्वप्राणेन शङ्खराट्
english: Winded by Hari with his utmost might, that water-sprung king of conchs, endowed with terrific blares, roared, as if afflicting the three worlds.
The sounds of that king of conchs struck terror into the Rākşasas, even as in a mighty forest a lion (strikes terror into the hearts of) elephants in rut.
Thereat the horses could not keep their ground, and the elephants were reſt of their temporal flow, and shorn of their virtue at the roars of the conch, heroes began to topple down from their cars.

sanskrit: विदार्य तानि रक्षांसि सुपुङ्खा विविशुः क्षितिम्
transliteration: vidārya tāni rakṣāṃsi supuṅkhā viviśuḥ kṣitim
english: And dight with dainty feathered parts having heads, the shafts discharged from the śārnga, resembling thunder-bolts, riving those Rākşása, entered the earth.

sanskrit: निपेतू राक्षसा भूमौ शैला वज्रहता इव
transliteration: nipetū rākṣasā bhūmau śailā vajrahatā iva
english: In that conflict, pierced by the arrows discharged from Nārāyana's arm, the Rākşasa began to drop to the ground like mountains struck with the thunder-bolt.
The wounds on the persons of the foes inflicted by the discus of Vişnu discharge blood in streams, like mountains discharging streams of red chalk.
The sound of that king of conchs, as well as those of the Sārnga, combined with the roars emitted by Vişņu himself, swallowed up the roars of the Rākşasas.
Hari by means of his shafts cut off their necks, and arrows, and standards, and bows, and cars, and ensigns and quivers.

Like fierce rays streaming about from sun, like torrents dashing from the ocean, like elephants coming adown a mountain, or like showers descending from clouds, the shafts shot by Nārāyaṇa pursue (the foes) by hundreds and by thousands.

Like fierce rays streaming about from sun, like torrents dashing from the ocean, like elephants coming adown a mountain, or like showers descending from clouds, the shafts shot by Nārāyaṇa pursue (the foes) by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: शरभेण यथा सिंहाः सिंहेन द्विरदा यथा
द्विरदेन यथा व्याघ्रा व्याघ्रेण द्वीपिनो यथा
transliteration: śarabheṇa yathā siṃhāḥ siṃhena dviradā yathā
dviradena yathā vyāghrā vyāghreṇa dvīpino yathā

sanskrit: द्वीपिनेव यथा श्वानः शुना मार्जारका यथा
मार्जारेण यथा सर्पाः सर्पेण च यथा ऽ ऽखवः
transliteration: dvīpineva yathā śvānaḥ śunā mārjārakā yathā
mārjāreṇa yathā sarpāḥ sarpeṇa ca yathā ' 'khavaḥ

sanskrit: तथा ते राक्षसाः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना
transliteration: tathā te rākṣasāḥ sarve viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā

english: Then, having despatched thousands of Rākşasas, the destroyer of Madhu blew his water-sprung (conch), even as the sovereign of the celestials filleth clouds (with rain).
Agitated by the arrows of Nārāyaṇa, with their senses bewildered by the blares of the conch, the broken Raksasa forces made for Lankā.
On the Rākşasa army having been broken in consequence of the beating it got at the hands of Nārāyaṇa, Sumāli with showers of shafts resisted Hari in the encounter.

sanskrit: स तु तं छादयामास नीहार इव भास्करम्
transliteration: sa tu taṃ chādayāmāsa nīhāra iva bhāskaram
english: As a mist envelops the Sun, he enveloped him (with his arrows). Thereat, the Rākşasas again summoned up their fortitude.

And fired with range, that Rākşasa, inflated with insolence on account of his strength, setting up a tremendous roar, darted at his antagonist in the conflict, thereby seeming to receive the Råkş asas.
As an elephant flourishes its trunk, that Rāks asa, lifting up his arm adorned with ornaments, began to roar from rapture, like a mass of clouds, lighted up with lightening.
And (Visņu) cut off the head flaming with ear rings of the charioteer of the shouting Sumáli; and thereat the horses of that Raksasa aimlessly strayed hither and thither.
And with his bewildered steeds Sumali wanders like a person deprived of patience, whose senses are under hallucination.

And on Sumali's car being drawn at random by his steeds, Mali, taking his bow and equipped therewith, darted at Vişnu's car and assailed that mighty-armed one as he was descending on the field of fight.
Like birds entering the Krauñca mountain, the arrows discharged from Mali's bow, graced with gold, hit Hari and entered (into his body).

sanskrit: अर्द्यमानः शरैः सो ऽथ मालिमुक्तैः सहस्रशः
english: Thereat, as a person holding his senses under subjection is not thrown out of his mental balance, Vişnu, assailed in that encounter with thousands of arrows shot by Māli, was not disturbed ever so little.
Then that creator of all beings, the reverend Gadādhara,* twanging his bow-string, showered volleys of shafts on Máli. *Lit. the holder of the mace, a name of Visnu.

sanskrit: पिबन्ति रुधिरं तस्य नागा इव सुधारसम्
transliteration: pibanti rudhiraṃ tasya nāgā iva sudhārasam
english: And getting at Mali's body, the arrows furnished with the luminousness of lightening drink his blood, like to serpents drinking nectar.
And baffling Māli, the holder of the conch, discus, and mace, brought down Māli's crown, standard, bow and steeds.
Then that foremost of night-rangers, on being deprived of his car, sprang forward, mace in hand, even as lion bounds up from the brow of a hillock.

He with his mace smote at the forehead of that lord of birds, even as the Destroyer had smitten Isana,* or as Indra smites a mountain with his thunder-bolt. *There took place an encounter betwcen Radra and Yama in the Sveta forest, for the protection of Märkandeya and a certain king. In this battle, Yama had smitten Rudra. This is narrated in the Puranas.
On being severely struck by Mali with his mace, Garuda, writhing in torments, moved the god away from the field of battle.

sanskrit: पराङ्मुखे कृते देवे मालिना गरुडेन वै
transliteration: parāṅmukhe kṛte deve mālinā garuḍena vai
english: On the god having been removed from the field by Mäli as well as Garuda, there arose a mighty din of Raksasa roaring (in chorus).

Hearing the cheers of the Raksasa, Indra's younger brother, the reverend Hari, sitting on that lord of birds, albeit moved off from the scene of conflict, waxing enraged, from a desire of slaying (Mali) hurled his disc at him.
Thereat the disc, possessed of the splendour of the solar disc, and resembling the wheel itself of Kāla, flooding all the heavens with radiance, brought down Māli's head to the ground.
That head of lord of Rākşasas, terrific to behold, on being cut off (by Visnu), vomiting blood, fell down before (the Rākşasas), as formerly Rahu's head had fallen.

Then the deities experiencing excess of joy set up leonine cheers with might and main, crying,' Excellent, O god.' Seeing Mali slain, Sumali and Mālyavån, burning in grief, fled precipitately towards Lankä along with their forces.

Then the deities experiencing excess of joy set up leonine cheers with might and main, crying,' Excellent, O god.' Seeing Mali slain, Sumali and Mālyavån, burning in grief, fled precipitately towards Lankä along with their forces.
Garuda, being cheered, turned round, and growing enraged, as before drove the Rākşasas with the wind of his wings.

And (some) with their lotus-faces cut by the discus, (some) with their chests crushed with the mace, (some) with their necks torn off by the plough, (some) with their heads riven by the club, and some hewn by the sword, and others pierced by arrows, the Rākṣasas began to drop fast from the sky into the waters of the ocean.

And (some) with their lotus-faces cut by the discus, (some) with their chests crushed with the mace, (some) with their necks torn off by the plough, (some) with their heads riven by the club, and some hewn by the sword, and others pierced by arrows, the Rākṣasas began to drop fast from the sky into the waters of the ocean.

And as the thunder-bolt with lightening (riveth) a mighty mass of clouds, Narayana by means of the thunder-bolts of his arrows discharged from his bow, rived the night-rangers with their hair dishevelled and streaming (in the wind).

The forces having their umbrellas rent, their arms falling off, their goodly garments scattered, their entrails coming out and their eyes rolling, became incapable of distinguishing their own party from that of the foe.

sanskrit: रवाश्च वेगाश्च समं बभूवुः पुराणसिंहेन विमर्दितानाम्
transliteration: ravāśca vegāśca samaṃ babhūvuḥ purāṇasiṃhena vimarditānām
english: Even like (the roars and the vehemence) displayed by elephants on being attacked by lions, the roars, and the vehemence of the nightrangers and their elephants, sore assailed by the Primaeval Lion,* were equal. *Vişnu as a man-lion had formerly taken the conceit out of Hiranyakasipu the Asura king-and slain him, to rid his devotee Prahlada of his mortal foc in the from of a father.

And driven by Hari's networks of arrows, and discharging (all the while) their own showers of shafts, those night-rangers resembling the clouds of doom, are driven like the veritable clouds of the universal dissolution drifted by the wind.

sanskrit: अभिप्रहारैर्द्विविधा विभिन्नाः पतन्ति शैला इव राक्षसेन्द्राः
transliteration: abhiprahārairdvividhā vibhinnāḥ patanti śailā iva rākṣasendrāḥ
english: Their heads cut by discus, their parts of bodies crushed with the mace, and hewn in twain with swords, thus they foremost of Rākşasas fell like to hills (toppling headlong).
The Earth was seen to be (covered) with night-rangers resembling dark clouds, adorned with jewelled necklaces and ear rings, falling down, as if covered with dark mountains dropping down.
On that host being sore pressed at its back by Padmanabha,* Mālyavăn turned back even as the ocean does on meeting with its shore. *Lit. the lotus-naveled-a name of Visnu.
And with his eyes reddened, that night-ranger waxing wroth, shaking his head, addressed that prime of male persons Padmanabha, saying.
O Nārāyaṇa, you are ignorant of the timehonoured morality of Kşatriyas; and therefore like a base wight you slay us, desisting from fight and exercised with fear.

sanskrit: स हन्ता न गतः स्वर्गं लभते पुण्यकर्मणाम्
transliteration: sa hantā na gataḥ svargaṃ labhate puṇyakarmaṇām
english: O lord of the celestials, he that commits the crime of slaying one that desists from fight cannot go to the celestial regions as the fruit of meritorious acts.

sanskrit: ४अहं स्थितो ऽस्मि पश्यामि बलं दर्शय यत्तव
english: If you are bent upon battle, a holder of the conch, the discus and the mace, taking up my post (here), I shall see (your strength). Do you show (me) the same.
Seeing Mālyavān resembling the mountain, Mālyavān, stay, the powerful younger brother of the sovereign of the celestials spoke to him.

sanskrit: युष्मत्तो भयभीतानां देवानां वै मया ऽभयम्
english: I have removed the fear of the deities, affrighted at you, by promising that I will make root and branch work with the Räkşasas; and that same promise I am now fulfilling.

sanskrit: प्राणैरपि प्रियं कार्यं देवानां हि सदा मया
transliteration: prāṇairapi priyaṃ kāryaṃ devānāṃ hi sadā mayā
english: I should always lay down my life for serving the celestials and you I will slay even if you should go to the nethermost regions.
As that god of gods having eyes resembling the red lotuses was speaking thus, the lord of Rākşasas in high wrath pierced his breast with a dart.
And hurled by the hand of Mālyavān, the dart resonant with bells, appeared graceful on Hari's breast like lightening embosomed in clouds.

Thereat drawing out the same dart, that one dear to the Wielder of the Dart,* having eyes resembling red lotuses, aiming at Mālyāvan, hurled it at him. *A name of Kārtikeya, the celestial generallissimo.

Thereat the dart discharged by the hand of Govinda like to the Dart discharged by the hand of Skanda, rushing towards the Rākṣasa like a meteor coursing towards the Anjana mountain, descended on the spacious chest of the lord of the Rākşasas decked with the weight of a chain, even as the thunder clap bursts at the summit of the mountain.

Thereat the dart discharged by the hand of Govinda like to the Dart discharged by the hand of Skanda, rushing towards the Rākṣasa like a meteor coursing towards the Anjana mountain, descended on the spacious chest of the lord of the Rākşasas decked with the weight of a chain, even as the thunder clap bursts at the summit of the mountain.
On having his mail rent, Mālyāvan was utterly deprived of his senses; but (anon) reposing for a while, he again stood like a moveless hill.
Then taking up a javelin made of black iror girt with many a thorn, he furiously smote that deity on the chest.
And that night-ranger delighting in battle, dealing a box at Vāsavā's younger brother, moved away a distance measuring a bow's length.
And now there arose a mighty tumult in the sky of 'Excellent!' 'Excellent!' and having struck Visnu, the Raksasa also hit Garuda.
Thereat Vinata's son, growing engaged, drove the Rākşasas away with the wind of his wings, even as the lusty wind bloweth about sere leaves.
Seeing his elder brother driven by the wind produced by the wings of that bird, Sumali along with his forces, made for Lankā.

sanskrit: स्वबलेन समागम्य ययौ लङ्कां ह्रिया वृतः
transliteration: svabalena samāgamya yayau laṅkāṃ hriyā vṛtaḥ
english: And pushed off by the violence of the wind of (Garuda's) wings, the Rākṣasa Mālyavān also, joined by his own forces, departed for Lankā, covered with shame.

sanskrit: एवं ते राक्षसा तेन हरिणा कमलेक्षण
transliteration: evaṃ te rākṣasā tena hariṇā kamalekṣaṇa
english: Thus, O Rama, O lotus-eyed one, (the Rākşasas) had innumerable warriors beaten down and their foremost leaders slain.

sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गता वस्तुं पातालं सहपत्नयः
transliteration: tyaktvā laṅkāṃ gatā vastuṃ pātālaṃ sahapatnayaḥ
english: And albeit inflated with pride, they, incapable of coping with Vişnu, leaving Lankā, went to the nether regions with their wives dwelling there.
O best of the Raghus, these Rākşasa of celebrated prowess, related to the race of Sälakatankața, remained under the leadership of the Rākṣasa Sumāli.

sanskrit: ये त्वया निहतास्ते तु पौलस्त्या नाम राक्षसाः सुमाली माल्यवान्माली ये च तेषां पुरःसराः
transliteration: ye tvayā nihatāste tu paulastyā nāma rākṣasāḥ sumālī mālyavānmālī ye ca teṣāṃ puraḥsarāḥ
english: All those exalted Rākşasas going under the name of Pulastya that had been headed by Sumāli, Mālyavān and Māli, were stronger than Ravana.
No other than the god Nārāyaṇa, holding the conch, the discus and the mace, could slay those Råkşasa-foes to the celestials and thorns in the side of the deties.
And you are that eternal god the four armed Narayana, the lord, undeteriorating and unconquerable, sprung to exterminate Rāksasas.

The creator of beings that one ever cherishing those seeking his refuge appeares at times to compass the destruction of marauders, bringing the religion of the people to rack and ruin.* *This tallies wonderfully with the corresponding view given in the Bible. Great men appear in the fullness of time to bring about reforms in religion, when, as was the case before the birth of Christ, men have wandered farthest from the true path.

sanskrit: एषा मया तव नराधिप राक्षसानामुत्पत्तिरद्य कथिता सकला यथावत्
भूयो निबोध रघुसत्तम रावणस्य जन्मप्रभावमतुलं ससुतस्य सर्वम्
transliteration: eṣā mayā tava narādhipa rākṣasānāmutpattiradya kathitā sakalā yathāvat
bhūyo nibodha raghusattama rāvaṇasya janmaprabhāvamatulaṃ sasutasya sarvam
english: Thus, O lord of men, to-day I have truely related to you at length the origin of the Raksasas. Again, O foremost of the Raghus, do you understand the matchless birth and potency of Rāvana and his sons related in detail.

sanskrit: पुत्रैश्च पौत्रैश्च समन्वितो बली ततस्तु लङ्कामवसद्धनेश्वरः
transliteration: putraiśca pautraiśca samanvito balī tatastu laṅkāmavasaddhaneśvaraḥ
english: And that powerful Rākṣasa, Sumāli, afflicted with the fear of Vişnu, along with his sons and grand-sons for a long time ranged the nether regions, and the lord of riches resided in Lankā.

sanskrit: कन्यां दुहितरं गृह्य विना पद्ममिव श्रियम्
transliteration: kanyāṃ duhitaraṃ gṛhya vinā padmamiva śriyam

sanskrit: राक्षसेन्द्रः स तु तदा विचरन्वै महीतलम्
transliteration: rākṣasendraḥ sa tu tadā vicaranvai mahītalam

sanskrit: किं कृतं श्रेय इत्येवं वर्धेमहि कथं वयम्
transliteration: kiṃ kṛtaṃ śreya ityevaṃ vardhemahi kathaṃ vayam

english: O daughter, the time has come when I should give you away. Your youth is about to be passed. (Kept back) by the fear of refusal, no suiter has sought you (up to his time).

sanskrit: त्वत्कृते च वयं सर्वे यन्त्रिता धर्मबुद्धयः
त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः साक्षादिव पुत्रिके
transliteration: tvatkṛte ca vayaṃ sarve yantritā dharmabuddhayaḥ
tvaṃ hi sarvaguṇopetā śrīḥ sākṣādiva putrike
english: But desirous of acquiring religious merit, we are striving our best in your interests. My daughter, you are finished with every perfection like to Śrī herself.

sanskrit: न ज्ञायते च कः कन्यां वरयेदिति कन्यके
transliteration: na jñāyate ca kaḥ kanyāṃ varayediti kanyake
english: The being father to a daughter is misery to every one that seekes honour. O daughter, one does not know who shall ask for one's daughter.

sanskrit: त्वं हि सर्वगुणोपेता श्रीः साक्षादिव पुत्रिके
मातुः कुलं पितृकुलं यत्र चैव प्रदीयते
कुलत्रयं सदा कन्या संशये स्थाप्य तिष्ठति
transliteration: tvaṃ hi sarvaguṇopetā śrīḥ sākṣādiva putrike
mātuḥ kulaṃ pitṛkulaṃ yatra caiva pradīyate
kulatrayaṃ sadā kanyā saṃśaye sthāpya tiṣṭhati
english: Whenever may a daughter be conferred, a daughter stayes, placing in uncertainly the three races* to which she is related. *The races respectively of her father, mother and husband.

sanskrit: भज विश्रवसं पुत्रि पौलस्त्यं वरय स्वयम्
transliteration: bhaja viśravasaṃ putri paulastyaṃ varaya svayam
english: Do you, my daughter, seek for your husband that best and foremost of ascetics sprung in the line of Prajăpati Pulastya's son, Viśravā, and of yourself accept him (for your lord).

sanskrit: ईदृशास्ते भविष्यन्ति पुत्राः पुत्रि न संशयः
transliteration: īdṛśāste bhaviṣyanti putrāḥ putri na saṃśayaḥ
english: Then, O daughter, even as this lord of riches, so you will, without doubt, have sons resembling the Sun himself in energy.

sanskrit: सा तु तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कन्यका पितृगौरवात्
तत्रोपागम्य सा तस्थौ विश्रवा यत्र तप्यते
transliteration: sā tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kanyakā pitṛgauravāt
tatropāgamya sā tasthau viśravā yatra tapyate
english: Hearing that speech of his, the daughter for the sake of dignity of her sire, going to where Viśravā was practising penances, stood there.
In the meanwhile, O Rama, that twice-born one-Pulastya's was performing the Agnihotra, like the fourth Fire itself.

sanskrit: अविचिन्त्य तु तां वेलां दारुणां पितृगौरवात्
transliteration: avicintya tu tāṃ velāṃ dāruṇāṃ pitṛgauravāt
english: And without minding that terrific time, (Kaikasi), having regard to the dignity of her sire, coming up before him, stood (there) son hanging her head down towards his feet and throwing up the earth with her great foe.

sanskrit: स तु तां वीक्ष्य सुश्रोणीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्
transliteration: sa tu tāṃ vīkṣya suśroṇīṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām
english: Seeing that one of the shapely hips, having a face fair as the full Moon, (that exceedingly high-minded ascetic) flaming in energy accosted her thus. O gentle one, whose daughter are you? And when do you come hither? And what is your errand? And for whom (do you come)? O beauteous (damsel), truly tell me this.

sanskrit: भद्रे कस्यासि दुहिता कुतो वा त्वमिहागता
किं कार्यं कस्य वा हेतोस्तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि शोभने
transliteration: bhadre kasyāsi duhitā kuto vā tvamihāgatā
kiṃ kāryaṃ kasya vā hetostattvato brūhi śobhane
english: Seeing that one of the shapely hips, having a face fair as the full Moon, (that exceedingly high-minded ascetic) flaming in energy accosted her thus. O gentle one, whose daughter are you? And when do you come hither? And what is your errand? And for whom (do you come)? O beauteous (damsel), truly tell me this.

Thus addressed, the girl, with joined hands, said, 'O ascetic, you are competent to get at my intent by virtue of your own power. Yet, O Brahmarși, know me as having come here at the mandate of my sire. My name is Kaikasī. The rest do you read yourself.

sanskrit: किं तु मां विद्धि ब्रह्मर्षे शासनात्पितुरागताम्
कैकसी नाम नाम्नाहं शेषं त्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि
transliteration: kiṃ tu māṃ viddhi brahmarṣe śāsanātpiturāgatām
kaikasī nāma nāmnāhaṃ śeṣaṃ tvaṃ jñātumarhasi
english: Thus addressed, the girl, with joined hands, said, 'O ascetic, you are competent to get at my intent by virtue of your own power. Yet, O Brahmarși, know me as having come here at the mandate of my sire. My name is Kaikasī. The rest do you read yourself.

sanskrit: स तु गत्वा मुनिर्ध्यानं वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह
