english: When the gods and the Gandharvas and the Yaksas, Raksasas, and Pannagas, coming to my sire asked for me, O foremost of Rākşasas, my father did not bestow me on any one of them. And I shall you the reason thereof; listen, O long-armed one.

sanskrit: पितुस्तु मम जामाता विष्णुः किल सुरेश्वरः
transliteration: pitustu mama jāmātā viṣṇuḥ kila sureśvaraḥ

sanskrit: दम्भुर्नाम ततो राजा दैत्यानां कुपितो ऽभवत्
तेन रात्रौ शयानो मे पिता पापेन हिंसितः
transliteration: tena rātrau śayāno me pitā pāpena hiṃsitaḥ
english: My father's intended son-in-law was even Vişņu sovereign of the celestials, and the lord of the triune world; and my father would not bestow me on any other. And hearing this, a certain king of the Daityas, named Sambhu proud, of his prowess was wrought up with wrath, and one night as my sire was on bed, that wicked one slew him. Thereat my forlorn mother, of exalted righteousness embracing my father's body entered into fire.

sanskrit: ततो मे जननी दीना तच्छरीरं पितुर्मम
transliteration: tato me jananī dīnā taccharīraṃ piturmama
english: My father's intended son-in-law was even Vişņu sovereign of the celestials, and the lord of the triune world; and my father would not bestow me on any other. And hearing this, a certain king of the Daityas, named Sambhu proud, of his prowess was wrought up with wrath, and one night as my sire was on bed, that wicked one slew him. Thereat my forlorn mother, of exalted righteousness embracing my father's body entered into fire.
Then wishing to realise my father's wish touching Närāyana, I have fixed my heart even upon him.
Having made this promise, I have been carrying on rigid austerities. Thus, o foremost of Raksasas. I have related to you everything.
Nārāyaṇa is my husband, and not any one else than that best of male beings; and desirous of having Nārāyaṇa I have adopted severe restraints.

sanskrit: जानामि तपसा सर्वं त्रैलोक्ये यद्धि वर्तते
transliteration: jānāmi tapasā sarvaṃ trailokye yaddhi vartate
english: I know you, O king. Go you, O son of Paulastya. By virtue of my asceticism I know all that takes place in these three regions.
Thereat descending from the front of his car, Ravana, affected with the shafts of Kandarpa, again addressed that girl, observant of a mighty VOW. a
O you of sharply hips, in as much as such is your intent, you must be very proud. O you having the eyes of young antelope, accumulation of religious merit suits old people.
You, furnished with every perfection, should not talk thus. You are the paragon in these three worlds,. Your youth wax away.

sanskrit: तस्य मे भव भार्या त्वं भुङ्क्ष्व भोगान्यथासुखम्
transliteration: tasya me bhava bhāryā tvaṃ bhuṅkṣva bhogānyathāsukham
english: I am the lord of Lărkā., O gentle lady. known as Dasagriva. Be you my wife, and enjoy pleasures according to your desire.

sanskrit: वीर्येण तपसा चैव भोगेन च बलेन च ॥
transliteration: vīryeṇa tapasā caiva bhogena ca balena ca
english: Who is he whom you call Vişņu O mild one, neither in prowess, nor in asceticism, nor in enjoyment, nor in strength, is he my equal, whom, O damsel, you seek.

sanskrit: न मया स समो भद्रे यं त्वं कामयसे ऽङ्गने
transliteration: na mayā sa samo bhadre yaṃ tvaṃ kāmayase 'ṅgane

sanskrit: मा मैवमिति सा कन्या तमुवाच निशाचरम्
transliteration: mā maivamiti sā kanyā tamuvāca niśācaram
english: Thus accosted, Vedavati said to the nightranger 'Do not say so' in respect of Visnu, lord of this triune sphere, bowed down to by all creatures. Save and except you alone, O King of Raksasa, who, that is intelligent, cried down (Narayana).
Thus addressed there by Vedavatī, the nightranger seized the girl by the hair.

sanskrit: ततो वेदवती क्रुद्धा केशान्हस्तेन सा ऽच्छिनत्
english: Thereat Vedavati, wroth, cut off her hair with her hand transformed into a sword.
Then, flaming up in ire and as if consuming the night-ranger, she, preparing a funeral pyre, hastened to make away with herself.
You object, having been outraged by you I wish not to live. Therefore, O Raksasa, I will enter into fire in your very presence.

sanskrit: यस्मात्तु धर्षिता चाहं त्वया पापात्मना वने
तस्मात्तव वधार्थं हि समुत्पत्स्ये ह्यहं पुनः
transliteration: yasmāttu dharṣitā cāhaṃ tvayā pāpātmanā vane
tasmāttava vadhārthaṃ hi samutpatsye hyahaṃ punaḥ
english: As I have in this world been dishonoured by you you are nefarious. I shall again be born to compass your destruction.

sanskrit: न हि शक्यं स्त्रिया हन्तुं पुरुषः पापनिश्चः
शापे त्वयि मयोत्सृष्टे तपसश्च व्ययो भवेत्
transliteration: na hi śakyaṃ striyā hantuṃ puruṣaḥ pāpaniścaḥ
śāpe tvayi mayotsṛṣṭe tapasaśca vyayo bhavet
english: It lie not in a female to slay a male intent on sin; and if I utter a curse, it shall cost my asceticism.

sanskrit: यदि त्वस्ति मया किञ्चित्कृतं दत्तं हुतं तथा
transliteration: yadi tvasti mayā kiñcitkṛtaṃ dattaṃ hutaṃ tathā
english: But if I have done anything, given away any thing, offered oblations to the fire, then I shall be the chaste daughter of some virtuous person, albeit unborn of any female vessel.

sanskrit: पपात च दिवो दिव्या पुष्पवृष्टिः समन्ततः
transliteration: papāta ca divo divyā puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ samantataḥ
english: Having delivered herself thus, she entered into the flaming fire; and thereat a celestial shower of blossoms rained all around from heaven.

sanskrit: एतच्छ्रुत्वा ऽर्णवे राम तां प्रचिक्षेप रावणः
तव भार्या महाबाहो विष्णुस्त्वं हि सनातनः
transliteration: tava bhāryā mahābāho viṣṇustvaṃ hi sanātanaḥ
english: O Lord, this is she that has been born as the daughter of king Janaka, your wife, O mightyarmed one. You are the eternal Visnu.
The enemy, endowed with the splendour of a hill, formerly that been slain by her, by help of your superhuman prowess.
This one of eminent righteousness would again spring up on earth like a flame from a field furrowed by the plough.
This one named Vedavatſ was born in the Kệta age; and in the Tretā age, for compassing the destruction of that Rākşasa, she was born in the Maithila line of the high-souled Janaka.
This one named Vedavatſ was born in the Kệta age; and in the Tretā age, for compassing the destruction of that Rākşasa, she was born in the Maithila line of the high-souled Janaka.

sanskrit: प्रविष्टायां हुताशं तु वेदवत्यां स रावणः
transliteration: praviṣṭāyāṃ hutāśaṃ tu vedavatyāṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: When Vedavati had entered into the fire, Rāvana, ascending Puşpaka, began to range the earth.

sanskrit: ततो मरुत्तं नृपतिं यजन्तं सह दैवतैः
transliteration: tato maruttaṃ nṛpatiṃ yajantaṃ saha daivataiḥ
english: And coming to Uśirabīja, Rāvaņa saw a king (named) Marutta, sacrificing along with the deities.
And a righteous Brahmarşi named Samvarta, the very brother of Bphaspati, officiated at the sacrifice accompanied by the deities.
Seeing that Rākşasa invincible by reason of the boon he had received, the deities, apprehensive of being worsted by him, assumed the forms of beasts.

Indra became a peacock and the king of righteousness, a crow and the bestower of riches a lizard, and Varuna a swan; and, O slayer of foes, others also became other beasts. And then Rāvana entered into that sacrifice like an unclean dog.

Indra became a peacock and the king of righteousness, a crow and the bestower of riches a lizard, and Varuna a swan; and, O slayer of foes, others also became other beasts. And then Rāvana entered into that sacrifice like an unclean dog.

sanskrit: प्राह युद्धं प्रयच्छेति निर्जितो ऽस्मीति वा वद
transliteration: prāha yuddhaṃ prayaccheti nirjito 'smīti vā vada
english: Then coming up to the king, Răvaņa lord of Raksāsas said: 'Give me battle, or say, I am defeated.

sanskrit: ततो मरुत्तो नृपतिः को भवानित्युवाच तम्
transliteration: tato marutto nṛpatiḥ ko bhavānityuvāca tam
english: Whereat king Marutta asked, him 'Who are you'? And Ravana laughing in contempt said. "O king, I am delighted, that lacking curiosity, you do not dishonour Rävaņa, younger brother to the bestower of riches.

Whereat king Marutta asked, him 'Who are you'? And Ravana laughing in contempt said. "O king, I am delighted, that lacking curiosity, you do not dishonour Rävaņa, younger brother to the bestower of riches.

sanskrit: त्रिषु लोकेषु को ऽन्यो ऽस्ति यो न जानाति मे बलम्
transliteration: triṣu lokeṣu ko 'nyo 'sti yo na jānāti me balam
english: What other man is there in these three regions that know not the might of me, who, conquering my brother, has got possession of this car.

sanskrit: धन्यः खलु भवान्येन ज्येष्ठो भ्राता रणे जितः
न त्वया सदृशः श्लाध्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते
transliteration: dhanyaḥ khalu bhavānyena jyeṣṭho bhrātā raṇe jitaḥ
na tvayā sadṛśaḥ ślādhyastriṣu lokeṣu vidyate

sanskrit: क त्वं प्राक्केवलं धर्मं चरित्वा लब्धवान्वरम्
श्रूतपूर्वं हि न मया भाषसे यादृशं स्वयम्
transliteration: ka tvaṃ prākkevalaṃ dharmaṃ caritvā labdhavānvaram
śrūtapūrvaṃ hi na mayā bhāṣase yādṛśaṃ svayam

english: But O perverse one, stay now. Living you shall not back. To-day with my sharpened shafts shall I despatch you to the abode of Yama.
Then taking up his bow and arrows, that king of men went out for encounter; but Samavartta stood in the way.

sanskrit: श्रोतव्यं यदि मद्वाक्यं सम्प्रहारो न ते क्षमः
transliteration: śrotavyaṃ yadi madvākyaṃ samprahāro na te kṣamaḥ
english: And that great sage said to Marutta words informed with affection 'If you hear my speech, you should not fight.

If this Maheśvara-sacrifice should remain incomplete, it will burn up your dynasty. Where is the fight of one initiated in a sacrifice? And where is the passion of one initiated in a sacrifice? And victory is ever uncertain; and the Rākşasa is difficult to vanquish. And thereupon, the lord of Earth Marutta desisted in consonance with the instructions of his spiritual preceptor; and composed addressed himself to completing the sacrifice, giving up his bow with the arrow set. And thereat considering him as defeated, Suka proclaimed this all round, and from delight cried aloud, 'Victory to Rāvana!

sanskrit: दीक्षितस्य कुतो युद्धं क्रोधित्वं दीक्षिते कुतः
transliteration: dīkṣitasya kuto yuddhaṃ krodhitvaṃ dīkṣite kutaḥ
english: If this Maheśvara-sacrifice should remain incomplete, it will burn up your dynasty. Where is the fight of one initiated in a sacrifice? And where is the passion of one initiated in a sacrifice? And victory is ever uncertain; and the Rākşasa is difficult to vanquish. And thereupon, the lord of Earth Marutta desisted in consonance with the instructions of his spiritual preceptor; and composed addressed himself to completing the sacrifice, giving up his bow with the arrow set. And thereat considering him as defeated, Suka proclaimed this all round, and from delight cried aloud, 'Victory to Rāvana!

sanskrit: विसृज्य सशरं चापं स्वस्थो मखमुखो ऽभवत्
english: If this Maheśvara-sacrifice should remain incomplete, it will burn up your dynasty. Where is the fight of one initiated in a sacrifice? And where is the passion of one initiated in a sacrifice? And victory is ever uncertain; and the Rākşasa is difficult to vanquish. And thereupon, the lord of Earth Marutta desisted in consonance with the instructions of his spiritual preceptor; and composed addressed himself to completing the sacrifice, giving up his bow with the arrow set. And thereat considering him as defeated, Suka proclaimed this all round, and from delight cried aloud, 'Victory to Rāvana!

sanskrit: ततस्तं निर्जितं मत्वा घोषयामास वै शुकः
transliteration: tatastaṃ nirjitaṃ matvā ghoṣayāmāsa vai śukaḥ

english: Then devouring the Maharsis that were present at the place of sacrifice, Rāvana, satiated with their blood, again went to the earth.

sanskrit: रावणे तु गते देवाः सेन्द्राश्चैव दिवौकसः
ततः स्वां योनिमासाद्य तानि सत्त्वानि चाब्रुवन्
transliteration: rāvaṇe tu gate devāḥ sendrāścaiva divaukasaḥ
tataḥ svāṃ yonimāsādya tāni sattvāni cābruvan
english: On Ravana having departed, the deities, inhabiting the etherial regions Indra etc. assuming their proper forms, addressed those creatures.

sanskrit: प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ भुजङ्गाद्धि न ते भयम्
transliteration: prīto 'smi tava dharmajña bhujaṅgāddhi na te bhayam
english: And from joy Indra spoke to the purpleplumed peacock, 'Pleased am I with you righteous one. No fear shall spring to you from serpents; and your plumage shall be furnished with an hundred eyes. And when I shall shower, you shall be filled with glee as a token of my satisfaction with you.' Thus did Indra chief of celestials, confer a boon on the peacock.

And from joy Indra spoke to the purpleplumed peacock, 'Pleased am I with you righteous one. No fear shall spring to you from serpents; and your plumage shall be furnished with an hundred eyes. And when I shall shower, you shall be filled with glee as a token of my satisfaction with you.' Thus did Indra chief of celestials, confer a boon on the peacock.

sanskrit: नीलाः किल पुरा बर्हा मयूराणां नराधिप
सुराधिपाद्वरं प्राप्य गताः सर्वे ऽपि बर्हिणः
transliteration: nīlāḥ kila purā barhā mayūrāṇāṃ narādhipa
english: Formerly, O King, the peacock's wings had one unvaried blue. Having received the boon, the peacock departed.
O Rāma, then the king of righteousness said to the crow, seated in front of the sacrificial apartment 'O bird, I am well pleased with you. Listen to my words as I utter them.

sanskrit: यथान्ये विविधै रोगै; पीड्यन्ते प्राणिनो मया
ते न ते प्रभविष्यन्ति मयि प्रीते न संशयः
transliteration: yathānye vividhai rogai; pīḍyante prāṇino mayā
te na te prabhaviṣyanti mayi prīte na saṃśayaḥ
english: As I have been pleased with you, you shall without doubt, enjoy immunity from the various ailments to which the birds are subject.
O bird, from my curse fear of death shall not approach you; and you shall exist so long as people do not slay you.

sanskrit: त्वयि भुक्ते तु तृप्तास्ते भविष्यन्ति सबान्धवाः
transliteration: tvayi bhukte tu tṛptāste bhaviṣyanti sabāndhavāḥ
english: Those men residing in my dominion, being smitten with hunger, shall be refreshed along with your relations, when you have eaten and been refreshed.

Then Varuņa addressed that lord of birds the swan ranging the waters of the Gangā, 'Listen to my words fraught with joy, your hue shall be charming, mild, and like to the lunar disc; and it shall be beautiful, resembling the sheen of spotless foam.

Then Varuņa addressed that lord of birds the swan ranging the waters of the Gangā, 'Listen to my words fraught with joy, your hue shall be charming, mild, and like to the lunar disc; and it shall be beautiful, resembling the sheen of spotless foam.
And approaching my person you shall ever be beautiful to behold; and you shall, as a sign of my gratification, attain unparalleled complacence.

sanskrit: हंसानां हि पुरा राम नीलवर्णः सपाण्डुरः
transliteration: haṃsānāṃ hi purā rāma nīlavarṇaḥ sapāṇḍuraḥ
english: Formerly, O Rama, swans had not a hue of one unvaried whiteness. Their wings ended in, blue, and their breasts wore the spotless hue of tender grass. Then Vaiśravana addressed the chameleon as it was stationed at the mountain.

sanskrit: सद्रव्यं च शिरो नित्यं भविष्यति तवाक्षयम्
एष काञ्चनको वर्णो मत्प्रीत्या ते भविष्यति
transliteration: sadravyaṃ ca śiro nityaṃ bhaviṣyati tavākṣayam
eṣa kāñcanako varṇo matprītyā te bhaviṣyati
english: Your hue shall be gold-gleaming. Pleased am I with you. Your undeteriorating head shall be ever gold-hued. And this golden hue of your shall proceed from my gratification?

sanskrit: निवृत्ताः सह राज्ञा ते पुनः स्वभवनं गताः
transliteration: nivṛttāḥ saha rājñā te punaḥ svabhavanaṃ gatāḥ
english: Having thus conferred boons on them at that festal place, the celestials, along with the king, (on the sacrifice) having ended, went to their abode.

sanskrit: अथ जित्वा मरुत्तं स प्रययौ राक्षसाधिपः
transliteration: atha jitvā maruttaṃ sa prayayau rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Having vanquished Marutta, that lord of Rākşasas the Ten-faced Răvaņa, eager for encounter, began to range the capitals of the foremost monarchs (of the earth).

And coming to the most powerful crowned heads (in the world) resembling Mahendra and Varuna, the Raksasa king said: 'Give me battle; or declare we have been defeated. This I am resolved upon. Otherwise there is no escape for you?'

sanskrit: निर्जिताः स्मेति वा ब्रूत एष मे हि सुनिश्चयः
transliteration: nirjitāḥ smeti vā brūta eṣa me hi suniścayaḥ
english: Thereat those wise kings, possessed of great strength, and ever abiding by righteousness, being frightened (at Ravana's intimidation), took counsel of each other. And knowing the superior strength of the foe, they said, “We have been defeated.

sanskrit: एते सर्वे ऽब्रुवंस्तात निर्जिताः स्मेति पार्थिवाः

english: O child, Dusyanta, Suratha, Gadhi, and Gaya and king Pururavă all these kings said: 'We have been defeated.' And then Rāvaņa sovereign of the Rākşasas presented himself before Ayodhyā, governed by Anaranya, like Amarāvati ruled by. Sakra. And coming to that foremost of men king like to Purandara himself in prowess, Rāvana said, 'Give me battle; or say I have been defeated. This is my mandate.'

sanskrit: निर्जितो ऽस्मीति वा ब्रूहि त्वमेवं मम शासनम्
transliteration: nirjito 'smīti vā brūhi tvamevaṃ mama śāsanam
english: O child, Dusyanta, Suratha, Gadhi, and Gaya and king Pururavă all these kings said: 'We have been defeated.' And then Rāvaņa sovereign of the Rākşasas presented himself before Ayodhyā, governed by Anaranya, like Amarāvati ruled by. Sakra. And coming to that foremost of men king like to Purandara himself in prowess, Rāvana said, 'Give me battle; or say I have been defeated. This is my mandate.'

The lord of Ayodhyā, on hearing the words of that wicked-minded one, Anaranya, enraged, addressed the Raksasa-chief, saying, 'O king of Raksasas, I will give you combat, stay you. At once prepare for fight, and I also shall go and prepare myself.'

The lord of Ayodhyā, on hearing the words of that wicked-minded one, Anaranya, enraged, addressed the Raksasa-chief, saying, 'O king of Raksasas, I will give you combat, stay you. At once prepare for fight, and I also shall go and prepare myself.'

When he had heard everything (regarding Răvaņa), the forces of that foremost of kings that had been intended for conquering (Ravana), sallied forth ready for bringing about the destruction of the of the Raksasa, ten-thousand elephants, a niyuta horse, and many thousands of cars and infantry, O best of men; and, that host consisting of infantry and cars, marched for encounter, covering up the earth.

When he had heard everything (regarding Răvaņa), the forces of that foremost of kings that had been intended for conquering (Ravana), sallied forth ready for bringing about the destruction of the of the Raksasa, ten-thousand elephants, a niyuta horse, and many thousands of cars and infantry, O best of men; and, that host consisting of infantry and cars, marched for encounter, covering up the earth.

sanskrit: युद्ध्वा च सुचिरं कालं कृत्वा विक्रममुत्तमम्
transliteration: yuddhvā ca suciraṃ kālaṃ kṛtvā vikramamuttamam
english: That host, of the king encountering the forces of Rāvana, were extinguished like to clarified butter thrown into the (sacrificial) fire. And having fought valorously for a long time, the remnant of the royal forces, suddenly coming in contact with the flaming Räkşasas ranks, were destroyed like to swarms of locusts entering into fire.

sanskrit: नश्यति स्म बलं तत्र हव्यं हुतमिवानले
transliteration: naśyati sma balaṃ tatra havyaṃ hutamivānale

english: He saw the mighty army of that powerful monarch destroyed by the (adversary), like to a hundred streams absorbed by an approaching ocean.
And then himself drawing his bow resembling the bow itself of Sakra, that foremost of sovereigns, beside himself with wrath, approached Rāvana.
Brought down by Anaranya, his (Ravana's) councillors Mārica, Suka, and Sarana with Prahasta, took to their heels like to dear.
Then that son of the Ikşvāku race discharged eight hundred arrows at Rāvana's head.

sanskrit: तस्य बाणाः पतन्तस्ते चक्रिरे न क्षतं क्वचित्
transliteration: tasya bāṇāḥ patantaste cakrire na kṣataṃ kvacit
english: And like to showers pouring down on the top of a mountain, his shafts did not inflict any wound (on Ravana).
Then the king, smitten on the head with a slap by the enraged king of Rākşasas, dropped down from his car.

sanskrit: स राजा पतितो भूमौ विह्वलाङ्गः प्रवेपितः
transliteration: sa rājā patito bhūmau vihvalāṅgaḥ pravepitaḥ
english: The king, deprived of his senses, fell down on the earth, with his body trembling all over; as falls in a forest a sāla scathed with heaven's fire.

sanskrit: किमिदानीं फलं प्राप्तं त्वया मां प्रति युद्ध्यता
transliteration: kimidānīṃ phalaṃ prāptaṃ tvayā māṃ prati yuddhyatā
english: Thereat the Raksasa, laughing, spoke to that Iksvāku, lord of the earth, 'What is this that you have gathered as the fruit of your encounter with me.

sanskrit: त्रैलोक्ये नास्ति यो द्वन्द्वं मम दद्यान्नराधिप
शङ्के प्रसक्तो भोगेषु न शृणोषि बलं मम
transliteration: trailokye nāsti yo dvandvaṃ mama dadyānnarādhipa
śaṅke prasakto bhogeṣu na śṛṇoṣi balaṃ mama
english: O king, there is none in this triune sphere that can combat with me. Having hitherto been sunk in lunacy, you have not heard of my strength.

sanskrit: किं शक्यमिह कर्तुं वै कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः
transliteration: kiṃ śakyamiha kartuṃ vai kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: As he was speaking thus, the king, whose sounds were fast running out said: 'What can I do in this matter. Verily time is incapable of being controlled.

sanskrit: कालेनैव विपन्नो ऽहं हेतुभूतस्तु मे भवान्
english: I have been overcome by Time; you are merely an instrument. What can I do now, when I am going to-lose my life? I never turned away from fight; I have been slain fighting.

sanskrit: किं त्विदानीं मया शक्यं कर्तुं प्राणपरिक्षये
transliteration: kiṃ tvidānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ kartuṃ prāṇaparikṣaye
english: I have been overcome by Time; you are merely an instrument. What can I do now, when I am going to-lose my life? I never turned away from fight; I have been slain fighting.

sanskrit: यदि दत्तं यदि हुतं यदि मे सुकृतं तपः ॥
transliteration: yadi dattaṃ yadi hutaṃ yadi me sukṛtaṃ tapaḥ
english: But, O Raksasas, I shall tell you something in consequence of the disgrace that the Ikşvāku race has met with (today). If I have practised charity, if I have offered oblations into fire, if I have carried on pious penances, if i have governed my people well, then be my words verified!

sanskrit: यदि गुप्ताः प्रजाः सम्यक्तदा सत्यं वचो ऽस्तु मे
transliteration: yadi guptāḥ prajāḥ samyaktadā satyaṃ vaco 'stu me
english: But, O Raksasas, I shall tell you something in consequence of the disgrace that the Ikşvāku race has met with (today). If I have practised charity, if I have offered oblations into fire, if I have carried on pious penances, if i have governed my people well, then be my words verified!
There shall spring in the line of the highsouled Ikşvāku, one named Rāma son to Dasaratha who shall deprive your life.
As he uttered this imprecation, the celestial kettle-drums sounded like the roaring of clouds; and blossoms showered down from the sky.

sanskrit: ततः स राजा राजेन्द्र गतः स्थानं त्रिविष्टपम्
स्वर्गते च नृपे तस्मिन्राक्षसः सो ऽपसर्पत
transliteration: tataḥ sa rājā rājendra gataḥ sthānaṃ triviṣṭapam
english: Then, that best of kings, went to heaven; and when that king had gone to the celestial regions, the Raksasa (also) went away.
As the lord of Rākşasas was ranging the earth frightening everyone, Nārada foremost of ascetics, came to that wood mounted on a cloud,
Thereupon saluting him, the night-ranger Tennecked one enquired after his welfare as well as the occasion of his visit.

That Devarsi the exceedingly energetic Nārada of immeasurable splendour, seated on the back of the cloud, addressed Ravana, who was stationed in Puspaka, saying, O lord of Raks asas, o placid one, O son of Viśravā, stay. I am well pleased with your prowess and fame.

That Devarsi the exceedingly energetic Nārada of immeasurable splendour, seated on the back of the cloud, addressed Ravana, who was stationed in Puspaka, saying, O lord of Raks asas, o placid one, O son of Viśravā, stay. I am well pleased with your prowess and fame.

sanskrit: त्वया समं विमर्दैश्च भृशं हि परितोषितः
transliteration: tvayā samaṃ vimardaiśca bhṛśaṃ hi paritoṣitaḥ
english: And even as Vişnu had pleased me by destroying the Daityas, you pleased me by harassing the Gandharvas and serpents.
I will tell you something. If you would hear what I have to say then, O child, listen heedfully as I unfold it.

sanskrit: किमयं वध्यते तात त्वया ऽवध्येन दैवतैः
हत एव ह्ययं लोको यदा मृत्युवशं गतः
अवध्येन त्वया लोकः क्लेष्टुं युक्तो न मानुषः
transliteration: hata eva hyayaṃ loko yadā mṛtyuvaśaṃ gataḥ
avadhyena tvayā lokaḥ kleṣṭuṃ yukto na mānuṣaḥ

english: Who should slay creatures, who are ever stupid in respect of their welfare, environed by mighty dangers, and encompassed by hundreds of decrepitude and decease?
What sensible person can set his heart on slaying human beings, who are everywhere beset with a perennial stream of evils.
Do not you enfeeble those beings who are already enfeebled and smitten by Divinity with hunger, thirst, old age etc. and who are overwhelmed with sorrow, and grief.

sanskrit: मूढमेवं विचित्रार्थं यस्य न ज्ञायते गतिः
transliteration: mūḍhamevaṃ vicitrārthaṃ yasya na jñāyate gatiḥ
english: O mighty-armed one, o lord of Rākşasas, behold man, albeit having their sense stupified, engaged in the pursuit of various interests, and themselves not understanding their own ways;* some pass their time merrily with dancing and playing on musical instruments while others weep distressfully with tears streaming from their eyes down their cheeks. *Gati, according to the commentator, means the time of employment and suffering. I think the ordinary meaning answers, and give it accordingly.

O mighty-armed one, o lord of Rākşasas, behold man, albeit having their sense stupified, engaged in the pursuit of various interests, and themselves not understanding their own ways;* some pass their time merrily with dancing and playing on musical instruments while others weep distressfully with tears streaming from their eyes down their cheeks. *Gati, according to the commentator, means the time of employment and suffering. I think the ordinary meaning answers, and give it accordingly.

sanskrit: मोहितो ऽयं जनो ध्वस्तः क्लेशं स्वं नावबुध्यते
transliteration: mohito 'yaṃ jano dhvastaḥ kleśaṃ svaṃ nāvabudhyate
english: Down fallen on account of their attachment for their mothers and fathers and sons, and of their desires touching their wives and friends they set small store by labours having the hereafter as their object.

sanskrit: जित एव त्वया सौम्य मर्त्यलोको न संशयः
transliteration: jita eva tvayā saumya martyaloko na saṃśayaḥ
english: What then is the use of affecting a race that is brought down ever by its own infatuation. O placid one, this world is verily conquered by you, there is no doubt.
These for certain will have to repair to the abode of Yama. Therefore, O Paulastya, O captor of hostile capitals, do you put down Yama. On him being conquered, all will doubtless be conquered by you.

sanskrit: तस्मिञ्जिते जितं सर्वं भवत्येव न संशयः
transliteration: tasmiñjite jitaṃ sarvaṃ bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ
english: Thus addressed Lankā's lord, flaming in native energy, addressed Narada, laughing and saluting him. 'O you that delightest in the sport of gods and Gandharvas, and that take pleasure in warfare, I am ready to go to the nethermost regions for the purpose of conquest.

Thus addressed Lankā's lord, flaming in native energy, addressed Narada, laughing and saluting him. 'O you that delightest in the sport of gods and Gandharvas, and that take pleasure in warfare, I am ready to go to the nethermost regions for the purpose of conquest.
And conquering the three worlds, and bringing under subjection serpents and celestials I shall for ambrosia churn the nether regions.

sanskrit: क्व खल्विदानीं मार्गेण त्वया ह्यन्येन गम्यते
transliteration: kva khalvidānīṃ mārgeṇa tvayā hyanyena gamyate
english: Then the reverend sage Närada spoke to the Ten-necked Ravana, Who save you can on forsooth go that journey? Verily, o irrepressible one, O destroyer of foes, the way leading to the city of the lord of the dead is difficult of access.

Then the reverend sage Närada spoke to the Ten-necked Ravana, Who save you can on forsooth go that journey? Verily, o irrepressible one, O destroyer of foes, the way leading to the city of the lord of the dead is difficult of access.

sanskrit: स तु शारदमेघाभं हासं मुक्त्वा दशाननः
transliteration: sa tu śāradameghābhaṃ hāsaṃ muktvā daśānanaḥ
english: Thereat laughing, the Ten-faced one said to the saint resembling a mass of white clouds, "This is done.
Therefore,* O great Brahmana, intent upon slaying the Vaivasvata's son, I will go by this way which lead to the king-the offspring of the sun. *As you has commanded me.
O master, from wrath I have vowed that I will, eager for encounter, O reverend one, conquer the four Lokapālas.

sanskrit: तदिह प्रस्थितो ऽहं वै प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति
english: Then here go I to the city of the lord of the Pitſs; and I am determined to compass the death of him that visit creatures with smart.
Having delivered himself thus and saluted the sage, he, entering the southern way with his councillors, proceeded along.
The exceedingly energetic Nārada best of Brāhmaṇas resembling a smokeless fire, remaining rapt for a while, began to reflect.

sanskrit: क्षीणे चायुषि धर्मेण स कालो जेष्यते कथम्
transliteration: kṣīṇe cāyuṣi dharmeṇa sa kālo jeṣyate katham
english: How can (Ravana) conquer Time who, when its life wane, righteously visit with affection the time, sphere with Indra, fraught with mobile and immobile.

How can this lord of Raksasas, of himself, go to him who, resembling another fire, bear to the gifts and acts (of persons), that high-souled one of whom attaining consciousness, people put forth their activity; and; afflicted with the fear of whom these three worlds fall away?

sanskrit: यस्य नित्यं त्रयो लोका विद्रवन्ति भयार्दिताः
तं कथं राक्षसेन्द्रो ऽसौ स्वयमेव गमिष्यति
transliteration: yasya nityaṃ trayo lokā vidravanti bhayārditāḥ
english: How can this lord of Raksasas, of himself, go to him who, resembling another fire, bear to the gifts and acts (of persons), that high-souled one of whom attaining consciousness, people put forth their activity; and; afflicted with the fear of whom these three worlds fall away?

sanskrit: यो विधाता च धाता च सुकृतं दुष्कृतं तथा
त्रैलोक्यं विजितं येन तं कथं विजयिष्यते
transliteration: yo vidhātā ca dhātā ca sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ tathā
trailokyaṃ vijitaṃ yena taṃ kathaṃ vijayiṣyate
english: How can (Rāvana) subdue him who ordain things both great and small, who met rewards and punishments for good and bad acts, and who himself has conquered the three worlds? Resorting* to what other means shall Rāvana secure (victory)? *Explains the commentator: "Time has every thing under its control. Like the all-enclosing space, time pervades all that is. This being so, resorting what transcending Time, shall Rāvana obtain victory over it."
I am curious about it. To Yama's abode shall I go for witnessing the encounter between Yama and the Raksasa.
Having reflected thus, that foremost of Vipras endowed with fleet vigour, bent his steps towards the abode of Yama, for the purpose of relating to him all that had taken place.
There he saw that god Yama sitting in front of fire and offering into it the good and evil fruits of their actions. * *Ordaining happiness and misery to the lives of people according to their acts.'

sanskrit: स तु दृष्ट्वा यमः प्राप्तं महर्षिं तत्र नारदम्
transliteration: sa tu dṛṣṭvā yamaḥ prāptaṃ maharṣiṃ tatra nāradam
english: Seeing the Maharși Nārada arrive there, Yama offering him arghya according to the ordinance, addressed him saying, when he was seated at his case:

sanskrit: कच्चित्क्षेमं तु देवर्षे कच्चिद्धर्मो न नश्यति
transliteration: kaccitkṣemaṃ tu devarṣe kacciddharmo na naśyati
english: 'O Devarsi, is it well with you? And does virtue deteriorate.'* And, why, O you honoured of deities, and Gandharvas, do you come?' *The Original has: "Do not virtue wane." This in English would imply the very reverse what Nārada intends to say. He says: 'Do religion deteriorate?' i.e. 'I hope, religion does not deteriorate.' This is an idiom and natural usage accounts for it, although that usage must in the nature of things be based on a subtle ground of season.

Thereat the reverend sage, Narada, said; Hearken. I shall tell (you); and (after hearing me out) do you what is fit. o king of the Pitrs, here come the night-ranger named ten-necked, for bringing you under his sway you who are incapable of being conquered.

Thereat the reverend sage, Narada, said; Hearken. I shall tell (you); and (after hearing me out) do you what is fit. o king of the Pitrs, here come the night-ranger named ten-necked, for bringing you under his sway you who are incapable of being conquered.
O master, for this reason it is that I have come hither hastily, doubtful what shall befall you who have the rod for your weapon.
In the meanwhile they saw the Rākṣasa's car approach from afar, flaming and like to the rayfurnished (one) risen.

sanskrit: तं देशं प्रभया तस्य पुष्पकस्य महाबलः
कृत्वा वितिमिरं सर्वं समीपं सो ऽभ्यवर्तत
transliteration: taṃ deśaṃ prabhayā tasya puṣpakasya mahābalaḥ
english: And dispelling the gloom of that region with the effulgence of Pușpaka; that exceedingly powerful (Raksasa) came forward.
The mighty-armed ten-necked one all around saw creatures reaping the consequences of their fair and foul acts.

There he saw Yama's soldiery along with Yama's followers, fierce-forms, grim-visaged and terrific. And he saw corporeal beings undergoing torments and pain, and emitting loud cries and sharp shrieks; preyed on by worms and fell dogs: and uttering words capable of striking pain and terror into the heart (of the hearer): and people swimming in the Vaitarani profusely running blood; and momentarily burning with hot sands; unrighteous wights pierced in a wood of asipatra, (plunged) in Raurava, in the river of borate of soda; and (cut) with razor-edges; asking for drinks; and afflicted with hunger and thirst; converted into corpses, lean, woe-begone, and pallid with hair flowing loosely; having dust and filth (on their bodies), and running about distressfully with dry forms; on the way saw Rāvana by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: रौरवे क्षारनद्यां च क्षुरधारासु चैव हि
transliteration: raurave kṣāranadyāṃ ca kṣuradhārāsu caiva hi
english: There he saw Yama's soldiery along with Yama's followers, fierce-forms, grim-visaged and terrific. And he saw corporeal beings undergoing torments and pain, and emitting loud cries and sharp shrieks; preyed on by worms and fell dogs: and uttering words capable of striking pain and terror into the heart (of the hearer): and people swimming in the Vaitarani profusely running blood; and momentarily burning with hot sands; unrighteous wights pierced in a wood of asipatra, (plunged) in Raurava, in the river of borate of soda; and (cut) with razor-edges; asking for drinks; and afflicted with hunger and thirst; converted into corpses, lean, woe-begone, and pallid with hair flowing loosely; having dust and filth (on their bodies), and running about distressfully with dry forms; on the way saw Rāvana by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: ददर्श रावणो मार्गे शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः

english: On being liberated by that Rākṣasa the tennecked one, those creatures in a moment began to enjoy their release, that had come to them without thought or suspense. And on the dead being delivered by the magnanimous Rākşasa, the guards of the dead, getting enraged, rushed at the Rākşasa sovereign.

On being liberated by that Rākṣasa the tennecked one, those creatures in a moment began to enjoy their release, that had come to them without thought or suspense. And on the dead being delivered by the magnanimous Rākşasa, the guards of the dead, getting enraged, rushed at the Rākşasa sovereign.
There arose a mighty clamour from all sides; from the heroic warriors of the king of righteousness rushing (all around.)

And those heroes by hundreds and by thousands assailed (Puspaka) with prāsas, and bludgeons, and darts and maces, and spears and tomaras. And swiftly swarming like bees, they began to break the seats, blocks, daises and gateways (of the car.)

And those heroes by hundreds and by thousands assailed (Puspaka) with prāsas, and bludgeons, and darts and maces, and spears and tomaras. And swiftly swarming like bees, they began to break the seats, blocks, daises and gateways (of the car.)
In that conflict Pușpaka presided over by divine energy, incapable of being destroyed by virtue of Brahma power, being broken, resumed its former shape.
Countless were the soldiers of that highsouled one consisting hundreds and thousands of heroic warriors, (ever) forward for fight.

sanskrit: अयुध्यन्त महावीराः स च राजा दशाननः
transliteration: ayudhyanta mahāvīrāḥ sa ca rājā daśānanaḥ
english: According to the measure of their might his (Rāvana's) councillors great heroes all, as well as the ten-faced one himself with might and main, fought with trees and crags and hundreds of blocks of buildings.

sanskrit: यमस्य च महाबाहो रावणस्य च मन्त्रिणः
transliteration: yamasya ca mahābāho rāvaṇasya ca mantriṇaḥ

english: And then pierced through and through by those weapons, with his person covered with blood, the Rākṣasa king appeared like a flowering Kinśuka in Pușpaka. * *This simile is peculiarly appropriate and beautiful. Puspaka, the name of Ravana's car, means composed of flowers; and this signification shining one arms. a askance, as it were, over the direct sense of the sentence, heightens the delight the reader feels on imagining the principal figure. "Rāvana seated in Puspaka, covered with blood, looked likeblossoming Kinsuka.'
Thereat that powerful one, by virtue of his mastery over weapons, began to hurl darts and maces, prāsas and spears and tomaras and crags and trees.

sanskrit: तरूणां च शिलानां च शस्त्राणां चातिदारुणम्
transliteration: tarūṇāṃ ca śilānāṃ ca śastrāṇāṃ cātidāruṇam
english: That terrific shower of trees, rocks and arms, alighted on the army of Yama (fighting) on the earth.
And snapping those weapons and resisting (those volleys of) arms, they smote at the Räkșasa fighting alone by hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: परिवार्य च तं सर्वे शैलं मोघोत्करा इव
transliteration: parivārya ca taṃ sarve śailaṃ moghotkarā iva
english: And encompassing him even as clouds encompass mountain, they rendered (Ravana) inert by means of Bhindipālas and darts. And with his mail torn open, his anger raging fiercely, and covered with blood streaming over his person, he, forsaking, his car, stood upon the ground.

And encompassing him even as clouds encompass mountain, they rendered (Ravana) inert by means of Bhindipālas and darts. And with his mail torn open, his anger raging fiercely, and covered with blood streaming over his person, he, forsaking, his car, stood upon the ground.

sanskrit: ततः स कार्मुकी वाणी समरे चाभिवर्तत
transliteration: tataḥ sa kārmukī vāṇī samare cābhivartata
english: Then furnished with his bow and holding his shafts, (Ravana) regaining his senses in a short time, increased in energy and stood in the field like the finisher.

sanskrit: तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तानुक्त्वा तच्चापं विचकर्ष स
transliteration: tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti tānuktvā taccāpaṃ vicakarṣa sa
english: Now fixing the divine Pāśupata on his bow, and saying to them, 'stay! stay!' he drew that bow.

sanskrit: मुमोच तं शरं क्रुद्धस्त्रिपुरे शङ्करो यथा
transliteration: mumoca taṃ śaraṃ kruddhastripure śaṅkaro yathā
english: And enraged, (Ravana) resembling Rudra himself, in fight drawing his bow to his car, discharged that shaft even as Sankara had discharged at Tripura.
And the appearance of the shaft was like an extinguishing fire in summer with smoke with flames, burning up a forest.

sanskrit: ज्वालामाली स तु शरः क्रव्यादानुगतो रणे
transliteration: jvālāmālī sa tu śaraḥ kravyādānugato raṇe
english: And garlanded with glory that shaft followed byghosts,* in that encounter; rushed on, burning to ashes the loose bushes and trees lying in its way. *The instrument being Siva's, it naturally was followed by ghosts as his attendants.

sanskrit: ते तस्य तेजसा दग्धाः सैन्या वैवस्वतस्य तु
transliteration: te tasya tejasā dagdhāḥ sainyā vaivasvatasya tu
english: And burnt up by its energy, the most of Vaivasvata fell down in the field like to banners of Mahendra.
Thereat the Räksasa of terrific prowess along with his councillors began to set up tremendous shouts; as if making the earth tremble.

sanskrit: स तस्य तु महानादं श्रुत्वा वैवस्वतः प्रभुः
शत्रुं विजयिनं मेने स्वबलस्य च सङ्क्षयम्
transliteration: sa tasya tu mahānādaṃ śrutvā vaivasvataḥ prabhuḥ
śatruṃ vijayinaṃ mene svabalasya ca saṅkṣayam
english: Hearing his mighty-shouts, that lord Vaivasvata knew that his adversary had gained the day and that his own host had been destroyed.
Knowing that his forces had been slain, he, with his eyes crimsoned with passion hastily spoke to his charioteer, ‘Bring you my car.'

sanskrit: स्थितः स च महातेजा ह्यध्यारोहत तं रथम्
transliteration: sthitaḥ sa ca mahātejā hyadhyārohata taṃ ratham
english: Thereat the charioteer brought the noble and mighty car and stood (there) and then that exceeding energetic one mounted the car.
And beside (him) was the rod of Kāla in its native from the divine instrument of Yama like to a flaming fire on account of its own energy.

Then on beholding Kāla, infuriated, tending to strike terror into all creatures, was agitated the triune universe, and trembling over took the denizens of heaven. The charioteer urged on the steeds possessed of graceful splendour; and arrived where the lord of Rākşasas was posted.

Then on beholding Kāla, infuriated, tending to strike terror into all creatures, was agitated the triune universe, and trembling over took the denizens of heaven. The charioteer urged on the steeds possessed of graceful splendour; and arrived where the lord of Rākşasas was posted.

sanskrit: मुहूर्तेन यमं ते तु हया हरिहयोपमाः
transliteration: muhūrtena yamaṃ te tu hayā harihayopamāḥ
english: In a moment those horses like to thought (in celerity,) and resembling the steeds themselves of Hari, took Yama where the warfare had already begun. Seeing the frightful car in that aspect with Death present in it, the ministers of the Rākşasa monarch at once took to their heels.

In a moment those horses like to thought (in celerity,) and resembling the steeds themselves of Hari, took Yama where the warfare had already begun. Seeing the frightful car in that aspect with Death present in it, the ministers of the Rākşasa monarch at once took to their heels.

sanskrit: नेह योद्धुं समर्थाः स्म इत्युक्त्वा प्रययुर्दिशः
transliteration: neha yoddhuṃ samarthāḥ sma ityuktvā prayayurdiśaḥ
english: In vonsequence of their being comparatively inferior in point of strength they were deprived of their senses, and afficted with fear; and saying, 'Here we are not equal to fighting' they went their way.

sanskrit: स तु तं तादृशं दृष्ट्वा रथं लोकभयावहम्
transliteration: sa tu taṃ tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathaṃ lokabhayāvaham
english: But seeing that car capable of striking terror into folks, the Ten-necked did not experience any agitation, nor did fear enter his heart. And approaching Ravana, Yama, enraged, discharged spears and tomaras, and began to pierce Rāvana's marrow.

But seeing that car capable of striking terror into folks, the Ten-necked did not experience any agitation, nor did fear enter his heart. And approaching Ravana, Yama, enraged, discharged spears and tomaras, and began to pierce Rāvana's marrow.

sanskrit: रावणस्तु ततः स्वस्थः शरवर्षं मुमोच ह
transliteration: rāvaṇastu tataḥ svasthaḥ śaravarṣaṃ mumoca ha
english: But Rāvana, without at all feeling any smart, began to shower arrows on Vaivasvata's vehicle, resembling a downpour caused by clouds.
Again at his spacious breast, that Raksasa who had undergone slender injury, could not resist, (Yama's arms) with hundreds of mighty darts hurled.

sanskrit: सप्तरात्रं कृतः सङ्ख्ये विसञ्ज्ञो विमुखो रिपुः
transliteration: saptarātraṃ kṛtaḥ saṅkhye visañjño vimukho ripuḥ
english: And in this way that destroyer of foes Yama fought for seven nights with various arms; until at length his enemy was driven back and deprived of his senses.
Then, O hero, there took place nighty onset between Yama and the Rākşasas both eager for victory and both never tiring of fight.
And celestials and Gandharvas and Siddhas, and the supreme saints, placing Prajāpati at their head, presented themselves at the fight.
The encounter that then took place between that foremost of Rākşasas and the lord of the Dead was like the universal upheaval.
And stretching his bow resembling in splendour the thunderbolt of Indra, he discharged arrows covering up the sky.
And he smote Death with four, the (Yama's), charioteer with seven, and swiftly struck Yama in the marrow with hundreds and thousands of shafts. :
Then from forth Yama's mouth there issued darted flames with his teeth mixed with smoke, the fire of his fury.
Witnessing this wonder in the presence of the deities and Dānavas, both Death and Time were fixed with wrath and were filled with delight.

sanskrit: नैषा रक्षो भवेदद्य मर्यादा हि निसर्गतः
transliteration: naiṣā rakṣo bhavedadya maryādā hi nisargataḥ
english: Then Death, growing still more wroth, addressed Vaivasvata saying; “Let me go. I shall slay this sinful Rākşasa.”

sanskrit: एते चान्ये च बहवो बलवन्तो दुरासदाः
transliteration: ete cānye ca bahavo balavanto durāsadāḥ

english: Even this is my native might this Räksasa will be no more. Hiranyakasipu, the graceful Namuci, and Sambara, Nişandi and Dhūmaketu and Virocana's offspring Bali, and the Daitya Śambhu that mighty monarchs, Vſtra and Bāņa; and Rājarșis versed in all branches of learnings and Gandharvas, and mighty serpents, and sages, and Pannagas and Yaksas, and swarms of Apsarās and the Earth herself containing vastly oceans and mountains and rivers and trees, at the unrolling of a Yuga all these, O mighty monarch have I brought to dissolution. All these and many more endowed with strength and incapable of being overcome, were at the very sight of me compassed with peril, and what is this ranger of the night?

sanskrit: मुञ्चं मां साधु धर्मज्ञ यावदेनं निहन्म्यहम्
transliteration: muñcaṃ māṃ sādhu dharmajña yāvadenaṃ nihanmyaham
english: Let me go. O you cognisant of righteousness, I shall slay this one. There is none that, albeit strong, can survive after having been seen by me.

sanskrit: स दृष्टो न मया कालं मुहुर्तमापि जीवति
transliteration: sa dṛṣṭo na mayā kālaṃ muhurtamāpi jīvati
english: Verily this is not mine strength, this might pertain to me by nature. O Time, if seen by me, he won't live for a moment.

sanskrit: अब्रवीत्तत्र तं मुत्युं त्वं तिष्ठैनं निहन्म्यहम्
transliteration: abravīttatra taṃ mutyuṃ tvaṃ tiṣṭhainaṃ nihanmyaham

english: Hearing these words of his, the puissant king of righteousness spoke there to death, 'Do you stay. I myself shall slay him.' Then with his eyes reddened that lord, Vaivasvata, wielded with his hand the infallible dart of time; while by him lay the redoubtable noose of time and the mace in its native shape resembling fire and the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: किं पुनः स्पृश्यमानस्य पात्यमानस्य वा पुनः
transliteration: kiṃ punaḥ spṛśyamānasya pātyamānasya vā punaḥ
english: He, who by his very sight draw away the lives of creatures, what should be said of its touching and being hurled at people?
And touched by that powerful one, that mighty weapon, engist with flames, attained access of energy, and seemed to consume the Raksasa.

sanskrit: सुराश्च क्षुभिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा दण्डोद्यतं यमम्
transliteration: surāśca kṣubhitāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā daṇḍodyataṃ yamam
english: In the field of battle, everyone afficted with fear, ran away from it. And beholding Yama with his rod uplifted, the celestials were agitated.
On Yama being desirous of slaying Rāvana, by his rod, the great-father manifesting himself spoke to Yama.
O Vaivasvata, O mighty-armed one, O you of immeasurable prowess, this certainly must not be. You should not with your rod slay the nightranger.

sanskrit: स त्वया नानृतः कार्यो यन्मया व्याहृतं वचः
transliteration: sa tvayā nānṛtaḥ kāryo yanmayā vyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ
english: For, O foremost of celestials, I have conferred a boon on him; and you should not render false the words that I have uttered.

sanskrit: यो हि मामनृतं कुर्याद्देवो वा मानुषो ऽपि वा
transliteration: yo hi māmanṛtaṃ kuryāddevo vā mānuṣo 'pi vā
english: Verily he, that, whether a god or a human being, shall falsify my words, shall render the triune universe false. There is no doubt about this. If this terrific weapon, capable of affrighting the three spheres, be discharged alike at friends and foes, it will destroy creatures.

Verily he, that, whether a god or a human being, shall falsify my words, shall render the triune universe false. There is no doubt about this. If this terrific weapon, capable of affrighting the three spheres, be discharged alike at friends and foes, it will destroy creatures.
This rod of Kāla, of immeasurable might and incapable of being resisted by creatures, was created by me as having the power of compassing th : death of all beings.

sanskrit: तन्न खल्वेष ते सौम्य पात्यो रावणमूर्धनि
transliteration: tanna khalveṣa te saumya pātyo rāvaṇamūrdhani
english: Therefore, O mild one, you forsooth should not bring it down on Rāvana's head. If this alights on any one, he does not live for a moment.
Whether on this weapon alighting, the tennecked does not die, or if he does do either way falsehood is the consequence.

sanskrit: सत्यं च मां कुरुष्वाद्य लोकांस्त्वं यद्यवेक्षसे
transliteration: satyaṃ ca māṃ kuruṣvādya lokāṃstvaṃ yadyavekṣase
english: Therefore do you keep your uplifted weapon off Larkā's lord. If you have any care for these worlds do you establish my truth.

sanskrit: एष व्यावर्तितो दण्डः प्रभविष्णुर्हि नो भवान्
transliteration: eṣa vyāvartito daṇḍaḥ prabhaviṣṇurhi no bhavān
english: Thus addressed, Yama then answered, I restrain this rod. You are our lord.

sanskrit: किं न्विदानीं मया शक्यं कर्तुं रणगतेन हि
न मया यद्ययं शक्यो हन्तुं वरपुरस्कृतः
transliteration: kiṃ nvidānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ kartuṃ raṇagatena hi
na mayā yadyayaṃ śakyo hantuṃ varapuraskṛtaḥ
english: But as I can not slay this one, who has obtained a boon, what then shall I do now in the field?
Therefore shall I disappear from the sight of this Rākşasa.' Having said this, even there did he vanish with his car and horses.

sanskrit: दशग्रीवस्तु तं जित्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः
transliteration: daśagrīvastu taṃ jitvā nāma viśrāvya cātmanaḥ
english: Having vanquished him and distinguished his name, Rāvaņa again ascended his Puşpaka and went out of the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: स तु वैवस्वतो देवैः सह ब्रह्मपुरोगमैः
transliteration: sa tu vaivasvato devaiḥ saha brahmapurogamaiḥ
english: With a delighted heart Vaivasvata along with the deities headed by Brahmā as well as that mighty ascetic-Narada, went to the celestial regions.
Having vanquished Yama, the foremost of celestials, Rāvana delighting in warfare, saw his adherents.
Then seeing Rāvaņa, with his person bathed in blood, bettered by the weapon discharged at him, they were seized with surprise.

sanskrit: पुष्पकं भेजिरे सर्वे सान्त्विता रावणेन तु
transliteration: puṣpakaṃ bhejire sarve sāntvitā rāvaṇena tu
english: And hailing him with victory, the councillors headed by Mārīca, having been encouraged by Ravana, ascended Puspaka.

sanskrit: ततो रसातलं गच्छन् प्रविष्टः पयसां निधिम्
transliteration: tato rasātalaṃ gacchan praviṣṭaḥ payasāṃ nidhim
english: Then the Rākṣasa entered the region of waters the abode of Daityas and serpents, well protected by Varuna.

sanskrit: स तु भोगवतीं गत्वा पुरीं वासुकिपालिताम्
कृत्वा नागान्वशे हृष्टो ययौ मणिमयीं पुरीम्
transliteration: sa tu bhogavatīṃ gatvā purīṃ vāsukipālitām
kṛtvā nāgānvaśe hṛṣṭo yayau maṇimayīṃ purīm
english: Arriving at Bhogavati the city governed by Vāsuki, he brought the serpents under subjection and then, delighted, bent his course to the palace Manimayi.

sanskrit: ते तु सर्वे सुविक्रान्ता दैतेया बलशालिनः
transliteration: te tu sarve suvikrāntā daiteyā balaśālinaḥ
english: There dwelt the Nivātakavacas, who had obtained boons. Those Daityas were possessed of prowess and endowed with strength, carrying various weapons, breathing high spirits and invincible in battle. And the Dānavas and Rāks asas growing enraged fell to raving each other with darts and tridents, Kuliśas and axes and pațțiśas. And as they fought one entire year passed away and neither side obtained victory or was worsted.

sanskrit: तेषां तु युध्यमानानां साग्रः संवत्सरो गतः
न चान्यतरयोस्तत्र विजयो वा क्षयो ऽपि वा
transliteration: teṣāṃ tu yudhyamānānāṃ sāgraḥ saṃvatsaro gataḥ
na cānyatarayostatra vijayo vā kṣayo 'pi vā

english: Then that way of the triune sphere, that God, the undeteriorating Great-father, swiftly presented himself on the scene mounted on his excellent car.
Making the Nivātakavacas desist from battle the ancient great-father spoke in clear words.

sanskrit: नह्ययं रावणो युद्धे शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः
transliteration: nahyayaṃ rāvaṇo yuddhe śakyo jetuṃ surāsuraiḥ
english: Even the celestials and the Asuras are not able to vanquish this Rāvaņa in battle; nor can the Dänavas backed by the gods can destroy you.

sanskrit: राक्षसस्य सखित्वं च भवद्भिः सह रोचते
transliteration: rākṣasasya sakhitvaṃ ca bhavadbhiḥ saha rocate
english: Do you therefore turn your minds to making friendship with the Rākşasas. All interests are forsooth the common possession of friends.
Thereat Rāvaņa made friendship with the Nivātakavacas in the presence of Fire; and then rejoiced greatly.
And duly honoured (by then) Daśānana passed there a year, without any feeling of that place being different from his own home: and spent his time agreeably.
Having learnt there a hundred sorts of illusion, he directed his course to Rasātala, searching for the city of the lord of waters.

sanskrit: गत्वा तु कालकेयांश्च हत्वा तत्र बलोत्कटान्
transliteration: gatvā tu kālakeyāṃśca hatvā tatra balotkaṭān
english: And then going to the city named Asma ruled by the Kālakāyas, (Rāvana) slew the Kālakāyas endowed with terrific strength; and then with his sword cut off his brother-in-law,' the husband of Śūrpanakhā, he mighty Vidyutjibha possessed of terrific strength; as the Rākşasa in the encounter was licking (the limbs of Ravana's followers).

sanskrit: श्यालं च बलवन्तं च विद्युज्जिह्वं बलोत्कटम्
जिह्वया संलिहन्तं च राक्षसं समरे तथा
transliteration: śyālaṃ ca balavantaṃ ca vidyujjihvaṃ balotkaṭam
jihvayā saṃlihantaṃ ca rākṣasaṃ samare tathā
english: And then going to the city named Asma ruled by the Kālakāyas, (Rāvana) slew the Kālakāyas endowed with terrific strength; and then with his sword cut off his brother-in-law,' the husband of Śūrpanakhā, he mighty Vidyutjibha possessed of terrific strength; as the Rākşasa in the encounter was licking (the limbs of Ravana's followers).

Having vanquished him, he, in a moment, destroyed four hundred Daityas. And then the lord of Rākṣasas saw the grand abode of Varuņa resembling a mass of white clouds, and effulgent like to Kailāśa itself;—and also saw the milkconserving Surabhi stationed there; from the streams of whose milk was produced the ocean named Ksiroda.

Having vanquished him, he, in a moment, destroyed four hundred Daityas. And then the lord of Rākṣasas saw the grand abode of Varuņa resembling a mass of white clouds, and effulgent like to Kailāśa itself;—and also saw the milkconserving Surabhi stationed there; from the streams of whose milk was produced the ocean named Ksiroda.

Having vanquished him, he, in a moment, destroyed four hundred Daityas. And then the lord of Rākṣasas saw the grand abode of Varuņa resembling a mass of white clouds, and effulgent like to Kailāśa itself;—and also saw the milkconserving Surabhi stationed there; from the streams of whose milk was produced the ocean named Ksiroda.

There Ravana saw the mother of kine and the foremost of bulls; from whom spring that maker of night the mild-beaming-moon; taking refuge under whom subsist the prime saints and those living on froth, the froth' (of milk): and wherefrom sprang ambrosia as well as the Svadha of Svădhă-subsisting ones,' even her that go with human beings under the name of Surabhi. 1. A typical instance of the lengths which the selfdenial of the Hindu sages went is furnished by the case of a certain class of ascetics, who, abstaining from every other kind of food, lived solely on the froth of milk, falling off from the udders after the calf had drunk it. This froth-drinking, in preference to drinking the milk itself was dictated by a motive of charity viz., not to deprive the calf of her legitimate fare. 2. The ancestral manes.

sanskrit: अमृतं यत्र चोत्पन्नं स्वधा च स्वधभोजिनाम्
transliteration: amṛtaṃ yatra cotpannaṃ svadhā ca svadhabhojinām
english: There Ravana saw the mother of kine and the foremost of bulls; from whom spring that maker of night the mild-beaming-moon; taking refuge under whom subsist the prime saints and those living on froth, the froth' (of milk): and wherefrom sprang ambrosia as well as the Svadha of Svădhă-subsisting ones,' even her that go with human beings under the name of Surabhi. 1. A typical instance of the lengths which the selfdenial of the Hindu sages went is furnished by the case of a certain class of ascetics, who, abstaining from every other kind of food, lived solely on the froth of milk, falling off from the udders after the calf had drunk it. This froth-drinking, in preference to drinking the milk itself was dictated by a motive of charity viz., not to deprive the calf of her legitimate fare. 2. The ancestral manes.

sanskrit: यां ब्रुवन्ति नरा लोके सुरभिं नाम नामतः
प्रदक्षिणं तु तां कृत्वा रावणः परमाद्भुताम्
transliteration: yāṃ bruvanti narā loke surabhiṃ nāma nāmataḥ
pradakṣiṇaṃ tu tāṃ kṛtvā rāvaṇaḥ paramādbhutām

english: Then he beheld Varuna's splendid mansion, streaming with hundreds of torrents, resembling a mass of autumnal clouds, and always wearing a delightful aspect.

And killing the generals of the forces, after having been resisted by them, he addressed the warriors, saying, 'Do you speedily acquaint your king with this "Rāvana has come here seeking battle." Do you give him fight, or say with joined hands. 'I have been defeated by you, and then you have no fear whatever?'

sanskrit: वद वा न भयं ते ऽस्ति निर्जितो ऽस्मीति साञ्जलिः
transliteration: vada vā na bhayaṃ te 'sti nirjito 'smīti sāñjaliḥ
english: And killing the generals of the forces, after having been resisted by them, he addressed the warriors, saying, 'Do you speedily acquaint your king with this "Rāvana has come here seeking battle." Do you give him fight, or say with joined hands. 'I have been defeated by you, and then you have no fear whatever?'

sanskrit: पुत्राः पौत्राश्च निष्क्रामन्गौश्च पुष्कर एव च
transliteration: putrāḥ pautrāśca niṣkrāmangauśca puṣkara eva ca
english: In the meantime the sons and grandsons of the high-souled Varuņa, as well as those of Puskara issued forth.

sanskrit: ते तु वीर्यगुणोपेता बलैः परिवृताः स्वकैः
transliteration: te tu vīryaguṇopetā balaiḥ parivṛtāḥ svakaiḥ
english: They, endowed with every virtue, accompanied by their own forces, yoked cars furnished with the effulgence of the rising Sun, and coursing at the desire of their riders.
Then there took place a mighty encounter capable of making people's down stand on end, between the sons of the lord of waters, and those of the intelligent Rāvana.
And in a short while that entire host of Varuņa was brought down by the highly powerful councillor of that Raksasa Daśagrīva.

Seeing their own forces brought to straits in the conflict and driven back in the fight with networks of shafts, and down on the ground and seeing Rävaņa in Puspaka, Varuņa's sons swiftly shot into the welkin with their fleet-footing cars.

Seeing their own forces brought to straits in the conflict and driven back in the fight with networks of shafts, and down on the ground and seeing Rävaņa in Puspaka, Varuņa's sons swiftly shot into the welkin with their fleet-footing cars.

After they had attained a station of equal vantage (with Ravana) in the sky,* great was the encounter that then took place in the sky, resembling the encounter of the deities and the Dānavas. *Ere the Rāvana was fighting on Puspaka, while Varuna's sons fought on the earth.
And turning away Rāvana in the conflict by means of shafts resembling fire, they, exceedingly rejoiced, emitted various shouts.

sanskrit: ततो महोदरः क्रुद्धो राजानं दृश्य धर्षितम्
transliteration: tato mahodaraḥ kruddho rājānaṃ dṛśya dharṣitam
english: Then Mahodara, enraged on seeing the king sore pressed, casting off fear, and wrought up with rage, began to go around, eager for fight.

sanskrit: तेन ते दारुणा युद्धे कामगाः पवनोपमाः
महोदरेण गदया हता वै प्रययुः क्षितिम्
transliteration: tena te dāruṇā yuddhe kāmagāḥ pavanopamāḥ
mahodareṇa gadayā hatā vai prayayuḥ kṣitim
english: And smit with his mace by Mahodara, Varuna's sons coursing at will and resembling the wind in velocity) dropped down to the ground.
Having slain those warriors and also those horses of Varuna's sons (Mahodara) seeing them lying down deprived of their cars swiftly sent up a tremendous cheer.

sanskrit: ते तु तेषां रथाः साश्वाः सह सारथिभिर्हतैः
transliteration: te tu teṣāṃ rathāḥ sāśvāḥ saha sārathibhirhataiḥ
english: And destroyed by Mahodara, their cars and horses together with their foremost charioteers, lay down on the earth.

sanskrit: ते तु त्यक्त्वा रथान्पुत्रा वरुणस्य महात्मनः
transliteration: te tu tyaktvā rathānputrā varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then forsaking their cars, the sons of highsouled Varuna, stationed in the sky, did not experience any pain* by virtue of their native power. *By virtue of their immortal origin.
Having stretched their bows they pierced Mahodara, and then, all together they greatly angered prevented Rāvana.

sanskrit: दारयन्ति स्म सङ्क्रुद्धा मेघा इव महागिरिम्
transliteration: dārayanti sma saṅkruddhā meghā iva mahāgirim
english: As the clouds, with a thousand torrents cleave a mountain, so they, with dreadful shafts, resembling thunderbolts and discharged off the bows, pierced him.
Thereupon the Ten-necked (demon), excited with wrath like the fire of dissolution, pierced them to their very vitals with highly dreadful arrows.
Thereupon with the arrows the infantry were greatly exhausted like to young elephants six years old, fallen in mire.

And stationed above, he showered on them variegated maces, Bhallas* Pattisas, Saktis and huge ſataghnis. Though pierced through and through these valiant foot-soldiers rushed forth. *An arrow with a crescent-shaped head.
Thereupon with the arrows the infantry were greatly exhausted like to young elephants six years old, fallen in mire.
Beholding Varuņa's sors thus worn out and over-whelmed the highly powerful Rāvana roared in delight like to clouds.

sanskrit: ततो रक्षो महानादान्मुक्त्वा हन्ति स्म वारुणान्
transliteration: tato rakṣo mahānādānmuktvā hanti sma vāruṇān
english: Thereupon emitting loud cries the Rākşasa, like to a cloud, with a downpour of diverse shafts, destroyed the offspring of Varuna.
There upon they were all defeated and fell dead on the ground and all their followers fled away from the field of battle to their homes.
Răvaņa spoke to them. “Do you communicate this to Varuņa.” Whereto his minister Prahasta replied to Rävana.

sanskrit: गान्धर्वं वरुणः श्रोतुं यं त्वमाह्वयसे युधि
तत्किं तव वृथा वीर परिश्रम्य गते नृपे
ये तु सन्निहिता वीराः कुमारास्ते पराजिताः
transliteration: gāndharvaṃ varuṇaḥ śrotuṃ yaṃ tvamāhvayase yudhi
tatkiṃ tava vṛthā vīra pariśramya gate nṛpe
ye tu sannihitā vīrāḥ kumārāste parājitāḥ
english: While the king is away, what is the use of taking trouble, O hero? And all these heroic sons (of Varuna) have been vanquished.
Hearing these words and spreading his own name the lord of Rākṣasas expressing sign of joy, issued out of Varuna's abode.

sanskrit: आगतस्तु पथा येन तेनैव विनिवृत्य सः
transliteration: āgatastu pathā yena tenaiva vinivṛtya saḥ
english: And returning by the way by which he had come the Raksasa, stationed in the welkin, proceeded towards Lankā.
While thus returning the vicious-souled Rāvana, with delight, carried away stealthily, on his way, the daughters of the royal saints, celestials and Dänavas.

sanskrit: दर्शनीयां हि रक्षः स कन्यां स्त्रीं वापि पश्यति
हत्वा बन्धुजनं तस्या विमाने तां रुरोध ह
transliteration: darśanīyāṃ hi rakṣaḥ sa kanyāṃ strīṃ vāpi paśyati
hatvā bandhujanaṃ tasyā vimāne tāṃ rurodha ha
english: And whatever beautiful damsel he saw, married or unmarried, that demon held them captive in his car, having slain all their friends and relatives.
In this wise he got on his chariot many a female of the Nagas, Raksasa, Asuras, Yaksas, Dänavas and of men.

They, all afflicted, shed tears, hot as fiery flames, caused by fear and fire of grief. As the ocean is filled with the currents of the rivers so that car was flooded with their tears originating from fear and sorrow.

They, all afflicted, shed tears, hot as fiery flames, caused by fear and fire of grief. As the ocean is filled with the currents of the rivers so that car was flooded with their tears originating from fear and sorrow.
And wept there in the chariot, hundreds of the females of Nagas, Gandharvas, of great ascetics, Daityas and of Dänavas.

sanskrit: काचिच्चिन्तयती तत्र किं नु मां भक्षयिष्यति
transliteration: kāciccintayatī tatra kiṃ nu māṃ bhakṣayiṣyati
english: The countenance and eyes, of those beautiful damsels, brought under the subjection of the tennecked demon, and afflicted with sorrow, looked poorly like a hind attacked by a lion. Some thought, “Will he eat me up" and another, stricken with sorrow, thought, “Will he destroy me?"

sanskrit: कथं नु खलु मे पुत्रो भविष्यति मया विना
कथं माता कथं भ्राता निमग्नाः शोकसागरे
transliteration: kathaṃ nu khalu me putro bhaviṣyati mayā vinā
kathaṃ mātā kathaṃ bhrātā nimagnāḥ śokasāgare
english: Thus remembering their mothers, fathers, husbands and brothers, all those females, overwhelmed with grief and sorrow, bewailed, some exclaiming. “What shall befall my son in my absence? Alas! into what ocean of grief my mother or brother is sunk? Alas! what shall my husband do in my absence? Therefore, O death, I propitiate you, do you take me, who am subject to miseries. Alas! what an iniquity did I perpetrate in my former birth in another body? Therefore, we all, overwhelmed with grief, are sunk in the ocean of sorrow, and I do not behold the end of my miseries.

sanskrit: हा कथं नु करिष्यामि भर्तुस्तस्मादहं विना
मृत्यो प्रसादयामि त्वां नय मां दुःखभागिनीम्
transliteration: hā kathaṃ nu kariṣyāmi bhartustasmādahaṃ vinā
mṛtyo prasādayāmi tvāṃ naya māṃ duḥkhabhāginīm
english: Thus remembering their mothers, fathers, husbands and brothers, all those females, overwhelmed with grief and sorrow, bewailed, some exclaiming. “What shall befall my son in my absence? Alas! into what ocean of grief my mother or brother is sunk? Alas! what shall my husband do in my absence? Therefore, O death, I propitiate you, do you take me, who am subject to miseries. Alas! what an iniquity did I perpetrate in my former birth in another body? Therefore, we all, overwhelmed with grief, are sunk in the ocean of sorrow, and I do not behold the end of my miseries.

sanskrit: किन्नु तद्दुष्कृतं कर्म पुरा देहान्तरे कृतम्
transliteration: kinnu tadduṣkṛtaṃ karma purā dehāntare kṛtam

sanskrit: एवं स्म दुःखिताः सर्वाः पतिताः शोकसागरे
transliteration: evaṃ sma duḥkhitāḥ sarvāḥ patitāḥ śokasāgare

sanskrit: अहो धिङ्मानुषं लोकं नास्ति खल्वधमः परः
transliteration: aho dhiṅmānuṣaṃ lokaṃ nāsti khalvadhamaḥ paraḥ
english: Oh! fie upon humanity: there is none more vile than a man for they are weak. As the stars disappear with the rising of the sun in time, so our husbands have been destroyed by the powerful Ravana.

Oh! highly powerful is this Rākşasa and he is mad after devising the means of destruction. Alas! being engaged in such vile actions, he does not consider himself cursed; he is as powerful as he is vicious. And though the ravishment of another's wife is a greets in, still that vile Rākşasa is enjoying us who belong to others. Therefore this vicious-minded one shall meet with death, by his own actions.

Oh! highly powerful is this Rākşasa and he is mad after devising the means of destruction. Alas! being engaged in such vile actions, he does not consider himself cursed; he is as powerful as he is vicious. And though the ravishment of another's wife is a greets in, still that vile Rākşasa is enjoying us who belong to others. Therefore this vicious-minded one shall meet with death, by his own actions.

sanskrit: शप्तः स्त्रीभिः स तु समं हतौजा इव निष्प्रभः
transliteration: śaptaḥ strībhiḥ sa tu samaṃ hataujā iva niṣprabhaḥ

english: Hearing their lamentations thus and being honoured by the night-rangers that foremost of Raksasas entered his city Lankā.

sanskrit: सहसा पतिता भूमौ भगिनी रावणस्य सा
transliteration: sahasā patitā bhūmau bhaginī rāvaṇasya sā
english: In the interval, Ravana sister, a dreadful and grim visaged she-demon suddenly fell down on the ground.

sanskrit: अब्रवीत्किमिदं भद्रे वक्तुकामा ऽसि मे द्रुतम्
english: Having raised up his sister and consoled her Rāvana said, “Tell me speedily, O good sister, what you wish to say.” Thereat that she-demon, having blood-red eyes, closed with tears, said.

sanskrit: कृता ऽस्मि विधवा राजंस्त्वया बलवता बलात्
एते राजंस्त्वया वीरा दैत्या विनिहता रणे
transliteration: ete rājaṃstvayā vīrā daityā vinihatā raṇe

sanskrit: प्राणेभ्यो ऽपि गरीयान्मे तत्र भर्ता महाबलः
english: “O king, by you, powerful as you are, I have forcibly been made widow." Fourteen a thousand demons, under the name of Kälakeyas, have been destroyed by you, O King, in the battle and among them was my highly powerful husband, dearer than my life. He has been slain by you, O dear one, an enemy, a brother only in name. I have been killed by you, O king, who are my brother.

sanskrit: सो ऽपि त्वया हतस्तात रिपुणा भ्रातृगृध्नुना
त्वया ऽस्मि निहता राजन्स्वयमेव हि बन्धुना
ननु नाम त्वया रक्ष्यो जामाता समरेष्वपि
स त्वया निहतो युद्धे स्वयमेव न लज्जसे
transliteration: nanu nāma tvayā rakṣyo jāmātā samareṣvapi
sa tvayā nihato yuddhe svayameva na lajjase
english: For you, O king, I shall enjoy the word 'widow!' My husband? should have been saved by you in the battle. But he was slain by your ownself in the battle; are you not ashamed of this?" 1. This is the literal translation of the passage-i.e. for you, I shall for ever be known as widow. 2. The word in the text is Tāmata, which literally means son-in-law-but here perhaps it must mean husband for she was his sister.)
Being thus addressed by his bewailing sister, the Ten-necked demon, consoling her in sweet words, said.

sanskrit: अलं वत्से रुदित्वा ते न भेतव्यं च सर्वशः
transliteration: alaṃ vatse ruditvā te na bhetavyaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Of no avail is your lamentation, dear sister; you need not be afraid of any of your of relatives. I shall please you studiously by gifts, honours and favours.

Being mad after war-fare and desirous of acquiring victory, I was continually making a downpour of shafts, so I could not distinguish in the conflict between my own men and enemies, and thus unwittingly I did hurt your husband.

sanskrit: तेनासौ निहतः सङ्ख्ये मया भर्ता तव स्वसः
transliteration: tenāsau nihataḥ saṅkhye mayā bhartā tava svasaḥ

sanskrit: अस्मिन्काले तु यत्प्राप्तं तत्करिष्यामि ते हितम्
transliteration: asminkāle tu yatprāptaṃ tatkariṣyāmi te hitam
english: And thus, sister, your husband was slain by me in the conflict; I shall now do whatever shall conduce to your well-being.

sanskrit: प्रभुः प्रयाणे दाने च राक्षसानां महाबलः
transliteration: prabhuḥ prayāṇe dāne ca rākṣasānāṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Do you ever reside by the side of your rich brother Khara he shall be the lord of fourteen thousand Räkşasas. That highly powerful one shall give food and clothes to all those Rākşasas. He is your cousin and that night-ranger shall always carry out your orders.

sanskrit: तत्र मातृष्वसेयस्ते भ्राता ऽयं वै खरः प्रभुः
transliteration: tatra mātṛṣvaseyaste bhrātā 'yaṃ vai kharaḥ prabhuḥ

english: Let that hero now speedily go to protect the Dandaka forest and the highly powerful Duşana shall be the commander of his forces.

sanskrit: तत्र ते वचनं शूरः करिष्यति सदा खरः
transliteration: tatra te vacanaṃ śūraḥ kariṣyati sadā kharaḥ
english: There the heroic Khara shall obey your words and be the lord of Raksasas assuming shapes at will.

sanskrit: स तु दत्त्वा दशग्रीवो वनं घोरं स्वरस्य तत्
भगिनीं च समाश्वास्य हृष्टः स्वस्थतरो ऽभवत्
transliteration: sa tu dattvā daśagrīvo vanaṃ ghoraṃ svarasya tat
english: Having thus given the command of a huge and dreadful army to Khara and consoled his sister the Ten-necked demon was satisfied and freed from anxiety.
Thereupon that highly powerful lord of Rāksasas with his followers entered an excellent garden in Larkā named Nikumbhilā.
There, he saw, filled with hundreds of sacrificial posts and altars, a sacrifice being celebrated, as if burning in its lustre.
He beheld his fearful son Meghanāda too, clad in an antelope skin and holding Sikhă and Kamandalu.
Having seen him (there) and embraced him by his arms the lord of Lankā said: “What are you after, O my child? Tell me the truth."

Thereupon that foremost of twice-born ones Usanas* of austere penances, wishing the prosperity of the sacrifice, said to Rāvana, the Raksasa chief. *Another name of Sukra. Indrajit took the vow of silence so he thought it improper to disturb him.

sanskrit: माहेश्वरे प्रवृत्ते तु यज्ञे पुम्भिः सुदुर्लभे
transliteration: māheśvare pravṛtte tu yajñe pumbhiḥ sudurlabhe

sanskrit: मायां च तामसीं नाम यया सम्पद्यते तमः
transliteration: māyāṃ ca tāmasīṃ nāma yayā sampadyate tamaḥ
english: He has also obtained illusory powers, which create darkness or ignorance, namely of ranging in the sky, of being eternal, of ascending a celestial car which curses at will and of creating darkness.

sanskrit: प्रयुक्तया गतिः शक्या नहि ज्ञातुं सुरासुरैः
transliteration: prayuktayā gatiḥ śakyā nahi jñātuṃ surāsuraiḥ
english: O lord of Rākşasas, these illusory powers being used in a conflict, even the celestials and Asuras shall not be able to perceive his course.
Besides he has obtained a quiver, the arrows whereof shall never be exhausted, a bow, which is hard of being got by and a dreadful weapon which destroys enemies in a conflict.

sanskrit: अद्य यज्ञसमाप्तौ च त्वां दिदृक्षुस्स्थितो ह्यहम्
transliteration: adya yajñasamāptau ca tvāṃ didṛkṣussthito hyaham
english: Having obtained these boons your son, O you having ten faces, and myself, the sacrifice being finished, have been waiting to behold you.
Whereto the Ten-necked demon replied, You have not done well as you have worshipped, with diverse articles my enemies, Indra and others.

sanskrit: एहीदानीं कृतं विद्धि सुकृतं तन्न संशयः
आगच्छ सौम्य गच्छामः स्वमेव भवनं प्रति
transliteration: ehīdānīṃ kṛtaṃ viddhi sukṛtaṃ tanna saṃśayaḥ
āgaccha saumya gacchāmaḥ svameva bhavanaṃ prati
english: However, what is done is done, there is virtue in this, no doubt; come, o gentle one, we shall go to our house.

Thereupon going there with his son and Vibhișana, the Ten-necked demon got down all those damsels, speechless with tears, gifted with auspicious marks, the precious females of the celestials, Dānavas and Räkşasas. Perceiving his vicious desire for those damsels, the virtuoussouled (Vibhisana) said.

sanskrit: तस्य तासु मतिं ज्ञात्वा धर्मत्मा वाक्यमब्रवीत्
transliteration: tasya tāsu matiṃ jñātvā dharmatmā vākyamabravīt
english: Thereupon going there with his son and Vibhișana, the Ten-necked demon got down all those damsels, speechless with tears, gifted with auspicious marks, the precious females of the celestials, Dānavas and Räkşasas. Perceiving his vicious desire for those damsels, the virtuoussouled (Vibhisana) said.
You do (still) follow your own whims, knowing that people are injured by these actions which destroy piety, wealth and fame.
Having slain their kinsmen you past brought these beautiful damsels hither, but disregarding you, O King, Madhu has carried away Kumbhīnasī.

sanskrit: को ऽयं यस्तु त्वया ऽ ऽख्यातो मधुरित्येव नामतः
english: Ravana said:-“I do not understand all this. Who is that Madhu, who has been named by you?"
Worked up with ire Vibhîşana said to his brother: "Hear, the fruit of your vicious actions has arrived.

sanskrit: मातामहस्य यो भ्राता ज्येष्ठो भ्राता सुमालिनः
transliteration: mātāmahasya yo bhrātā jyeṣṭho bhrātā sumālinaḥ

sanskrit: पिता ज्येष्ठो जनन्या नो ह्यस्माकं चार्यको ऽभवत्
transliteration: pitā jyeṣṭho jananyā no hyasmākaṃ cāryako 'bhavat

english: Your son being engaged in the sacrifice and myself being under waters she was stolen away, Oking, by the powerful Rākşasa Madhu. Kumbhakarma, ogreat king, was then asleep. Having slain all the powerful Rākşasas and your councillors, he had stolen her away, O king, who was in your inner apartments.

sanskrit: धर्षयित्वा हृता सा तु सुप्ताप्यन्तःपुरे तव
श्रुत्वा ऽपि तन्महाराज क्षान्तमेव हतो न सः
transliteration: dharṣayitvā hṛtā sā tu suptāpyantaḥpure tava
śrutvā 'pi tanmahārāja kṣāntameva hato na saḥ

sanskrit: यस्मादवश्यं दातव्या कन्या भर्त्रे हि भ्रातृभिः
transliteration: yasmādavaśyaṃ dātavyā kanyā bhartre hi bhrātṛbhiḥ
english: Hearing this even, O great king, we have pardoned and not slain him; an unmarried girl should be given away to her husband by her brothers, but that has not been the case, this is merely the result of your vicious actions, wicked-minded as you are. And this you have met with instantly, so the people say.
Hearing the words of Vibhīşaņa, Råvana, the lord of Rākşasas, became agitated like an ocean, by the recollection of his vicious deeds. And engaged, with blood-red eyes the ten-necked demon said.

sanskrit: कल्प्यतां मे रथः शीघ्रं शूराः सज्जीभवन्तु नः
transliteration: kalpyatāṃ me rathaḥ śīghraṃ śūrāḥ sajjībhavantu naḥ

sanskrit: भ्राता मे कुम्भकर्णश्च ये च मुख्या निशाचराः
transliteration: bhrātā me kumbhakarṇaśca ye ca mukhyā niśācarāḥ
english: Get my chariot ready soon and let all the heroes of our party be prepared. Let my brother Kumbhakarņa and other leading night-rangers, armed with various weapons, ascend their conveyances. Having slain today in the encounter that Madhu, who is not afraid of Ravana, I shall, encircled by my friends, and desirous of battle, proceed to the region of the celestials.

sanskrit: अद्य तं समरे हत्वा मधुं रावणनिर्भयम्
transliteration: adya taṃ samare hatvā madhuṃ rāvaṇanirbhayam
english: Get my chariot ready soon and let all the heroes of our party be prepared. Let my brother Kumbhakarņa and other leading night-rangers, armed with various weapons, ascend their conveyances. Having slain today in the encounter that Madhu, who is not afraid of Ravana, I shall, encircled by my friends, and desirous of battle, proceed to the region of the celestials.

sanskrit: राक्षसाः प्रययुः सर्वे कृत्वा ऽ ऽकाशं निरन्तरम्
english: All the Rākşasas went covering the sky, some on asses, some on camels, some on horses, some on quick-coursing porpoises and some on huge serpents.

And beholding Rävaņa proceed, hundreds of Daityas, inimical to the celestials, followed him. Having arrived at the city of Madhu and entered there the ten-necked demon did not behold Madhu but espied his sister.

sanskrit: स तु गत्वा मधुपुरं प्रविश्य च दशाननः
न ददर्श मधुं तत्र भगिनीं तत्र दृष्टवान्
transliteration: sa tu gatvā madhupuraṃ praviśya ca daśānanaḥ
na dadarśa madhuṃ tatra bhaginīṃ tatra dṛṣṭavān
