english: And beholding Rävaņa proceed, hundreds of Daityas, inimical to the celestials, followed him. Having arrived at the city of Madhu and entered there the ten-necked demon did not behold Madhu but espied his sister.

sanskrit: सा च प्रह्वाञ्जलिर्भूत्वा शिरसा चरणौ गता
transliteration: sā ca prahvāñjalirbhūtvā śirasā caraṇau gatā
english: Thereupon being afraid of the king of Raksasas, Kumbhinasi, with folded palms, touched his feet with her crown.

sanskrit: रावणो राक्षसश्रेष्ठः किं चापि करवाणि ते
transliteration: rāvaṇo rākṣasaśreṣṭhaḥ kiṃ cāpi karavāṇi te
english: Where to she replied “O King, O you having long arms, if you are pleased with me, do not slay my husband today, Oconfrere of honours. It is said there is no other fear like this for damsels of high pedigree. The greatest of fears is that of being a widow.

Where to she replied “O King, O you having long arms, if you are pleased with me, do not slay my husband today, Oconfrere of honours. It is said there is no other fear like this for damsels of high pedigree. The greatest of fears is that of being a widow.
Be you truthful, O king of Kings, do you look towards me, who am thus begging. You have yourself said, O king, "no fear.”

sanskrit: क्व चासौ तव भर्ता वै मम शीघ्रं निवेद्यताम्
transliteration: kva cāsau tava bhartā vai mama śīghraṃ nivedyatām
english: Being thus addressed Råvana said to his sister there: "Do you tell me speedily where is your husband. I shall go with him for conquests to the region of the celestials."

sanskrit: इत्युक्ता सा समुत्थाप्य प्रसुप्तं तं निशाचरम्
transliteration: ityuktā sā samutthāpya prasuptaṃ taṃ niśācaram
english: Out of pity and love for you I refrain from slaying Madhu. Being thus accosted, that Raksasi, being pleased, got her sleeping husband, the night-ranger, up and said.

sanskrit: एष प्राप्तो दशग्रीवो मम भ्राता महाबलः
transliteration: eṣa prāpto daśagrīvo mama bhrātā mahābalaḥ
english: Here is my brother, the highly power Dasagrīva. Being desirous of conquering the region of the celestials he prays for your help. Do you therefore proceed to his help, O Raksasa, with all they friends.
It behoves you to help him, who out of affection for me, has prayed for your help.” Hearing those words Madhu said:-"So be it."
Approaching a little he beheld that foremost of Rākşasas and duly welcomed Rāvana.
Being thus honoured the highly power Dasagrīva spent one night in Madhu's house and then, addressed himself for departure.
Thereupon reaching the hill Kailāsa, the abode of Vaisravana, the lord of Raksasas, resembling Mahendra, encamped his army.

sanskrit: स तु तत्र दशग्रीवः सह सैन्येन वीर्यवान्
transliteration: sa tu tatra daśagrīvaḥ saha sainyena vīryavān
english: After sunset the highly power Rāvaņa encamped his army there. And the clear moon, brilliant as the mountain, having risen, that huge army, armed with diverse weapons, became asleep.
After sunset the highly power Rāvaņa encamped his army there. And the clear moon, brilliant as the mountain, having risen, that huge army, armed with diverse weapons, became asleep.
And lying down on the summit of the mountain, the highly powerful Rāvaņa espied the caves beautified with the rays of the moon and the trees.

The interior of the forest was beautified with the brilliant groves of Karņikār, with Kadamba and Vakula trees, groves of full blown lotuses, the waters of Mandākini, with Campaka, Asoka, Punnaga, Mandāra, mangoe, Pātala, Lodhra, Priyangu, Arjuna, Ketka, Tagara, Coconut, Pyāla, Panasa and various other trees.
There sang the Kinnaras, possessed by desire, and having sweet voice, enhancing the delight of the mind.
There danced mirthfully, with their damsels, the Vidyādharas, inebriate and having their eyes reddened with drink.
There was audible in the house of the lord of riches, the sweet music of the assembled Apsarās like to the sound of the bell.
Being shaken by the wind the nectar-smelling trees made the hill fragrant with the shower of flowers.
And carrying the fragrance rendered salutary with honey and filaments of flowers, the excellent wind blew enhancing Ravana's desire.

Being possessed by desire through songs, richness of flowers, coldness of air, beauty of the hills, and the rising of the moon is night, the highly powerful Rāvana espied again and again the moon with heavy sighs.

Being possessed by desire through songs, richness of flowers, coldness of air, beauty of the hills, and the rising of the moon is night, the highly powerful Rāvana espied again and again the moon with heavy sighs.
At this time passed by that way the foremost of Apsarās, Rambhā, adorned with excellent ornaments and having a countenance like the full moon.
Her person was sprinkled with excellent sandal paste, her hairs were decked with Mandāra flowers, her body was beautified with other flowers and her movements tended to increase desire.
Her eyes were beautiful and her waist was high, adorned with Mekhala' and was as if the refuge of Rati.? 1. A kind of ornament used on the waist.) 2. Wife of Kama-the god of love in Hindu mythology.
Her forehead and other parts of the countenance were painted with the marks of red sandal and adorned with ornaments of flowers growing in six seasons.

sanskrit: यस्या वक्त्रं शशिनिभं भ्रुवौ चापनिभे शुभे
transliteration: yasyā vaktraṃ śaśinibhaṃ bhruvau cāpanibhe śubhe
english: Rambhā appeared like the second tree, in grace and beauty, natural and artificial. She wore green clothes resembling the clouds; her face was like the moon, eye brows like the excellent bows, thighs like the trunks of elephants and palms soft as leaves. She was seen by Rāvana as proceeding in the midst of soldiers.
Having got up and been influenced by lust he took her, shameful as she was, by the hand and smiling said.

sanskrit: क्व गच्छसि वरारोहे कां सिद्धिं भजसे स्वयम्
transliteration: kva gacchasi varārohe kāṃ siddhiṃ bhajase svayam
english: Where are you going, O beautiful damsel? Whom are you going of your own accord to satisfy? Whose prosperous time has appeared, with whom you shall enjoy?
Who shall be satisfied with drinking the nectar of your mouth smelling like lotus?
Whose breast, O fare damsel, your rising breast beautiful like two golden pots closely placed, shall touch?
Who will go to bestride today your large thigh resembling a disc of gold, encircled by a golden chain and which was like the form of a heaven.

sanskrit: मामतीत्य हि यं च त्वं यासि भीरु न शोभनम्
transliteration: māmatītya hi yaṃ ca tvaṃ yāsi bhīru na śobhanam
english: Who is there so beautiful as I-Indra, Visnu, or two Asvins that you are passing by me?
Do you take rest upon this excellent rock, O you having charming waist. There is no other lord, save me, in the three worlds.

sanskrit: त्रैलोक्ये यः प्रभुश्चैव मदन्यो नैव विद्यते
transliteration: trailokye yaḥ prabhuścaiva madanyo naiva vidyate
english: Do you take rest upon this excellent rock, O you having charming waist. There is no other lord, save me, in the three worlds.

sanskrit: तदेवं प्राञ्जलिः प्रह्वो याचते त्वां दशाननः
भर्तुर्भर्ता विधाता च त्रैलोक्यस्य भजस्व माम्
transliteration: tadevaṃ prāñjaliḥ prahvo yācate tvāṃ daśānanaḥ
bharturbhartā vidhātā ca trailokyasya bhajasva mām
english: And Daśānana, the lord of the lords of the three worlds, thus begs you, with folded palms. Do you therefore seek me.

sanskrit: प्रसीद नार्हसे वक्तुमीदृशं त्वं हि मे गुरुः
transliteration: prasīda nārhase vaktumīdṛśaṃ tvaṃ hi me guruḥ
english: Being thus addressed, Rambhā, trembling, with folded palms, said:-Be you propitiated; it does not behave you to speak thus, who are my superior.

sanskrit: अन्येभ्यो हि त्वया रक्ष्या प्राप्नुयां धर्षणं यदि
तद्धर्मतः स्नुषा ते ऽहं तत्त्वमेव ब्रवीमि ते
transliteration: anyebhyo hi tvayā rakṣyā prāpnuyāṃ dharṣaṇaṃ yadi
taddharmataḥ snuṣā te 'haṃ tattvameva bravīmi te
english: Rather should you protect me if any body else try to oppress me. Virtually I am your daughterin-law. I speak to you the truth.
Thereupon the Ten-necked demon said to her, standing with her face downwards, and her down standing erect at his very sight,

sanskrit: सुतस्य यदि मे भार्या ततस्त्वं हि स्नुषा भवेः
transliteration: sutasya yadi me bhāryā tatastvaṃ hi snuṣā bhaveḥ

sanskrit: धर्मतो यो भवेद्विप्रः क्षत्रियो वीर्यतो भवेत्
transliteration: dharmato yo bhavedvipraḥ kṣatriyo vīryato bhavet
english: “Had you been the wife of my son, you would have been my daughter-in-law.” Whereto Rambha replied. “Truly it is; I am, by virtue, the wife of your son, O foremost of Raksasas. Your brother Vaiśravana has a son, dearer than his life, celebrated in the three worlds under the name of Nalkūbara. In virtue he is like to a Brahmin, in prowess he equals a Kşatriya, in anger he is very fire and in patience he is like the earth. I have been thus directed by that Lokapāla's son.

sanskrit: तमुद्दिश्य तु मे सर्वं विभूषणमिदं कृतम्
transliteration: tamuddiśya tu me sarvaṃ vibhūṣaṇamidaṃ kṛtam

sanskrit: तथा तस्य हि नान्यस्य भावो मां प्रति तिष्ठति
transliteration: tathā tasya hi nānyasya bhāvo māṃ prati tiṣṭhati

sanskrit: स हि तिष्ठति धर्मात्मा मां प्रतीक्ष्य समुत्सुकः
तत्र विघ्नं सुतस्येह कर्तुं नार्हसि मुञ्च माम्
transliteration: sa hi tiṣṭhati dharmātmā māṃ pratīkṣya samutsukaḥ
tatra vighnaṃ sutasyeha kartuṃ nārhasi muñca mām

sanskrit: माननीयो मम त्वं हि पालनीया तथा ऽस्मि ते
transliteration: mānanīyo mama tvaṃ hi pālanīyā tathā 'smi te

english: "I am daughter-in-law,” as you have said, is worthy of being said by one who is the only wife. This is the everlasting law of the celestials that the Apsarās have no husband; they cannot be the wife of one husband.

"I am daughter-in-law,” as you have said, is worthy of being said by one who is the only wife. This is the everlasting law of the celestials that the Apsarās have no husband; they cannot be the wife of one husband.

sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा स तां रक्षो निवेश्य च शिलातले
transliteration: evamuktvā sa tāṃ rakṣo niveśya ca śilātale
english: Having said this, the Raksasa ravished her. Being released from his grasp Rambhā became divested of her ornaments and garland and became like the river agitated by the elephants.

Her hairs were dishevelled and her hands were trembling. Like to a blossoming creeper shaken by the wind, she, trembling and bashful and with folded hands, went to Nalakubara and fell down at his feet.

sanskrit: तदवस्थां च तां दृष्ट्वा महात्मा नलकूबरः
अब्रवीत्किमिदं भद्रे पादयोः पतिता ऽसि मे
transliteration: tadavasthāṃ ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmā nalakūbaraḥ
english: Having seen her in that plight the high-souled Nalakubara said-"O fair one, what is this? Why have you placed yourself at my feet?”

sanskrit: सा वै निःश्वसमाना तु वेपमाना कृताञ्जलिः
transliteration: sā vai niḥśvasamānā tu vepamānā kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Sighing heavily and trembling she with folded palms, related to him everything from the beginning to the end.

sanskrit: एष देव दशग्रीवः प्राप्तो गन्तुं त्रिविष्टपम्
transliteration: eṣa deva daśagrīvaḥ prāpto gantuṃ triviṣṭapam
english: O lord, on his way to heaven, Dasagrīva has arrived here and has spent the night with his army. While I was coming to you, O slayer of foes, I was seen by him. Then holding me he said-“Where are you going?"

sanskrit: गृहीता तेन पृष्टा ऽस्मि कस्य त्वमिति रक्षसा
transliteration: gṛhītā tena pṛṣṭā 'smi kasya tvamiti rakṣasā
english: O lord, on his way to heaven, Dasagrīva has arrived here and has spent the night with his army. While I was coming to you, O slayer of foes, I was seen by him. Then holding me he said-“Where are you going?"

sanskrit: मया तु सर्वं यत्सत्यं तस्मै सर्वं निवेदितम्
transliteration: mayā tu sarvaṃ yatsatyaṃ tasmai sarvaṃ niveditam
english: I related to him everything truly. But being possessed by lust he did not pay heed to my, words.

sanskrit: याच्यमानो मया देव स्नुषा ते ऽहमिति प्रभो
transliteration: yācyamāno mayā deva snuṣā te 'hamiti prabho
english: He was again prayed by me, O lord, saying “I am your daughter-in-law." But neglecting that he ravished me.

sanskrit: न हि तुल्यं बलं सौम्य स्त्रियाश्च पुरुषस्य च
transliteration: na hi tulyaṃ balaṃ saumya striyāśca puruṣasya ca
english: O you of firm vows, it behove you to forgive me for this folly. O gentle one, a woman's strength can never equal that of a man.

sanskrit: धर्षणां तां परां श्रुत्वा ध्यानं सम्प्रविवेश ह
transliteration: dharṣaṇāṃ tāṃ parāṃ śrutvā dhyānaṃ sampraviveśa ha
english: Hearing of this ravishment Vaisravana's son was greatly enraged and entered into meditation.
Having ascertained the truth within a moment Vaisravana's son, with eyes reddened with ire, took water in his palms.
Having taken this and rinsed his mouth duly, he imprecated a dreadful curse upon that lord of Raksasas.
O fair one, since you have been ravished by him despite your unwillingness he shall never be able to get by an unwilling damsel.

sanskrit: मूर्धा तु सप्तधा तस्य शकलीभविता तदा
transliteration: mūrdhā tu saptadhā tasya śakalībhavitā tadā
english: Whenever he shall, stricken by lust, ravish a reluctant damsel, his head shall be sundered into seven pieces. As soon as this curse, like to a burning flame, was uttered, the celestials bugles were sounded and a shower of flowers fell from heavens.

sanskrit: ज्ञात्वा लोकगतिं सर्वां तस्य मृत्युं च रक्षसः
transliteration: jñātvā lokagatiṃ sarvāṃ tasya mṛtyuṃ ca rakṣasaḥ

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु स दशग्रीवस्तं शापं रोमहर्षणम्
transliteration: śrutvā tu sa daśagrīvastaṃ śāpaṃ romaharṣaṇam
english: Hearing of that curse capable of making the down erect, Daśagrīva abstained from entertaining lust for unwilling females. And hearing of the curse imprecated by Nalakübara all the chaste damsels, that were kept captive, attained to great delight.

sanskrit: तेन नीताः स्त्रियः प्रीतिमापुः सर्वाः पतिव्रताः
transliteration: tena nītāḥ striyaḥ prītimāpuḥ sarvāḥ pativratāḥ
english: Hearing of that curse capable of making the down erect, Daśagrīva abstained from entertaining lust for unwilling females. And hearing of the curse imprecated by Nalakübara all the chaste damsels, that were kept captive, attained to great delight.
Having crossed the mount Kailāsa, the highiy powerful Ten-necked demon, with his army, reached the region of Indra.
There arose in the region of celestials an uproar from the Rākṣasa army, like to the sound of the agitated deep.

Hearing of the arrival of Rāvana, Indra shook on his throne and said to the assembled gods, Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sadhyas and Maruts"Prepare yourselves, for fighting with the vicious-souled Ravana."

Being thus addressed by Sakra, the celestials, his equals in the encounter and gifted with great prowess, armed themselves for fight. some

sanskrit: स तु दीनः परित्रस्तो महेन्द्रो रावणं प्रति
transliteration: sa tu dīnaḥ paritrasto mahendro rāvaṇaṃ prati
english: Mahendra, afraid of Ravana, poorly went to: Vişnu and gave vent to the following accents.

“How shall I, O Vişņu, withstand, the Rákş asa Rāvaņa? The highly powerful Rākṣasa has come here for battle. It is by virtue of the boon that he is powerful, not for any thing else. It is proper to make the words uttered by Brahmă, truthful.

“How shall I, O Vişņu, withstand, the Rákş asa Rāvaņa? The highly powerful Rākṣasa has come here for battle. It is by virtue of the boon that he is powerful, not for any thing else. It is proper to make the words uttered by Brahmă, truthful.
As resorting to your prowess I destroyed Namuci, Vrtra, Bali, Naraka and Sambara, so do you make arrangements (for his destruction).

There is no other excellent refuge but you in the three worlds, mobile and immobile, O lord, O gods of gods, O slayer of Madhu. You are the graceful, ever-existing Nārāyaṇa, having a lotus naval. By you the worlds have been settled and myself and Sakra, the lord of the celestials.

There is no other excellent refuge but you in the three worlds, mobile and immobile, O lord, O gods of gods, O slayer of Madhu. You are the graceful, ever-existing Nārāyaṇa, having a lotus naval. By you the worlds have been settled and myself and Sakra, the lord of the celestials.
You have created the three worlds, the mobile and immobile, and in you all these shall, O glorious deity, end at the time of dissolution.

sanskrit: तदाचक्ष्व यथा तत्त्वं देवदेव मम स्वयम्
transliteration: tadācakṣva yathā tattvaṃ devadeva mama svayam
english: Do you tell me, the truth, O god of gods, that I may myself fight; or do you, with your sword and discus, vanquish Ravana.

sanskrit: एवमुक्तः स शक्रेण देवो नारायणः प्रभुः
अब्रवीन्न परित्रासः कर्तव्यः श्रूयतां च मे
transliteration: evamuktaḥ sa śakreṇa devo nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
abravīnna paritrāsaḥ kartavyaḥ śrūyatāṃ ca me
english: Being thus addressed by Śakra the lord Narayana; said, "Do not fear, hear what I say. He is invincible by virtue of the boon, and that vicious-souled one is incapable of being vanquished even by the celestials and Asuras.

sanskrit: न तावदेष दुष्टात्मा शक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः
transliteration: na tāvadeṣa duṣṭātmā śakyo jetuṃ surāsuraiḥ
english: Being thus addressed by Śakra the lord Narayana; said, "Do not fear, hear what I say. He is invincible by virtue of the boon, and that vicious-souled one is incapable of being vanquished even by the celestials and Asuras.
Irrepressible by virtue of his prowess, that Raksasa, with his son, shall accomplish a mighty object. It seems to be real.

sanskrit: नाहं तं प्रतियोत्स्यामि रावणं राक्षसं युधि
transliteration: nāhaṃ taṃ pratiyotsyāmi rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasaṃ yudhi
english: O lord of celestials, even if I am requested by you. I shall not withstand the Rākşasa, Rāvana in the conflict.
Without slaying the enemies in the encounter, Vişņu does never go black, but it is hard to fulfil my desire from Rāvaņa, well protected by the boon.

sanskrit: भविता ऽस्मि यथा ऽस्याहं रक्षसो मृत्युकारणम्
english: However I do promise before you, O lord of the celestials, O performer of hundred sacrifices, I shall, soon become the cause of this Räkşasa's death.
I shall soon destroy Rāvana with his family in due time and afford delight to the celestials, O lords of ſacī; do you divested of fear, O you gifted with great strength, along with the celestials.

sanskrit: ततो रुद्राः सहादित्या वसवो मरुतो ऽश्वनौ
english: Thereupon having issued out of the city, Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Maruts and Asvins well armed with mails, appeared before the Raksasas.
Meanwhile at the latter part of the night there was audible the uproar of Rāvana's army fighting on all sides.
Having got up and cast their looks upon one another the highly powerful Rākşasas waited there for the battle, delighted.
Thereupon beholding that inexhaustible huge army at the commencement of the battle the celestial host lost heart.
Thereupon there ensued a conflict, setting up a terrible sound, with various weapons between the Räksasas and gods.
In the interval issued out for another encounter the heroic and grim-visaged Räksasas, Rāvana's councillors.

sanskrit: अकम्पनो निकुम्भश्च शुकः सारण एव च
transliteration: akampano nikumbhaśca śukaḥ sāraṇa eva ca
english: And encircled by Mārīca, Prahasta, Mahāparśva, Mahodara, Akampana, Nikumbha, Suka, Sarana, Sanghrāda, Dhumaketu, Mahadanstra, Gatodara, Jambumali, Mahahrada, Virūpākșa, Şuptaghna, Yajñakopa, Durmukha, Khara, Trisira, Karaviraksa, Süryasatru Mahakāya, Atikāya, Devāntaka, Narāntaka, all those of gifted with great prowess, there entered the battle-field, the highly powerful Sumālin, Rāvana's maternal grandfather.

And encircled by Mārīca, Prahasta, Mahāparśva, Mahodara, Akampana, Nikumbha, Suka, Sarana, Sanghrāda, Dhumaketu, Mahadanstra, Gatodara, Jambumali, Mahahrada, Virūpākșa, Şuptaghna, Yajñakopa, Durmukha, Khara, Trisira, Karaviraksa, Süryasatru Mahakāya, Atikāya, Devāntaka, Narāntaka, all those of gifted with great prowess, there entered the battle-field, the highly powerful Sumālin, Rāvana's maternal grandfather.

In the interim, O Rāma, a Rākşasa, Sumāli, by name, getting enraged, and with diverse weapons, ran amok of the soldiery. As the winds scatter clouds, so he, under the influence of rage, with various sharpened weapons, committed a havoc among the celestial soldiers.

sanskrit: प्रणुन्नं सर्वतो दिग्भ्यः सिंहनुन्ना मृगा इव
transliteration: praṇunnaṃ sarvato digbhyaḥ siṃhanunnā mṛgā iva

english: Being thus distressed by the night-rangers the hoist of the gods fled away into diverse directions like a herd of deer attacked by a lion. In the meantime, entered the battle-field, the heroic and brave Såvitra, the eight Vasu, encircled by soldiers and striking terror into the hearts of the enemies.

sanskrit: तथा ऽ ऽदित्यौ महावीर्यौ त्वष्टा पूषा च दंशितौ
निंर्भयौ सह सैन्येन तदा प्राविशतां रणे
transliteration: tathā ' 'dityau mahāvīryau tvaṣṭā pūṣā ca daṃśitau
niṃrbhayau saha sainyena tadā prāviśatāṃ raṇe
english: Then the two Ādityas, the highly powerful Tvaştă, and Puşă undaunted and united with the forces entered the arena.
Thereupon there arose with Rākşasas a terrible encounter of the celestials unable to bear their fame in battle.
Then the Rākşasas, with thousands of terrible weapons, began to belabour the deities in the encounter.
The celestials, as well, began to send the redoubtable, powerful and terrific Räkşasas, with the stroke of blameless weapons, to the abode of Death.

In the interim, O Rāma, a Rākşasa, Sumāli, by name, getting enraged, and with diverse weapons, ran amok of the soldiery. As the winds scatter clouds, so he, under the influence of rage, with various sharpened weapons, committed a havoc among the celestial soldiers.

In the interim, O Rāma, a Rākşasa, Sumāli, by name, getting enraged, and with diverse weapons, ran amok of the soldiery. As the winds scatter clouds, so he, under the influence of rage, with various sharpened weapons, committed a havoc among the celestial soldiers.

sanskrit: हन्यमानाः सुराः सर्वे न व्यतिष्ठन्त संहताः
transliteration: hanyamānāḥ surāḥ sarve na vyatiṣṭhanta saṃhatāḥ
english: Thereupon being assailed by a downpour of huge shafts, maces, Prāsas and diverse dreadful weapons, the celestials could not keep their ground upon the field of warfare.

The celestials being thus distressed by Sumāli the eighth of Vasu, Savitra stood there enraged. And encircled by his own car-warriors that highly powerful one, with his prowess, repulsed the striking night-rangers.

The celestials being thus distressed by Sumāli the eighth of Vasu, Savitra stood there enraged. And encircled by his own car-warriors that highly powerful one, with his prowess, repulsed the striking night-rangers.
Thereupon there arose a terrible encounter, capable of making down erect, between Sumālin and the Vasu, who did not retire from the field of battle.
His chariot drawn by serpents was pulled down and destroyed by the high-souled Vasu by means of his huge shafts.

sanskrit: हत्वा तु संयुगे तस्य रथं बाणशतैश्चितम्
transliteration: hatvā tu saṃyuge tasya rathaṃ bāṇaśataiścitam
english: Having destroyed his car in the warfare with hundreds of arrows Vasu took up mace in his hands for his destruction. Having taken up that mace having a burning head and resembling the rod of Death Sāvitra struck Sumálin on his head there with.

sanskrit: तां मूर्ध्नि पातयामास सावित्रो वै सुमालिनः
transliteration: tāṃ mūrdhni pātayāmāsa sāvitro vai sumālinaḥ
english: Having destroyed his car in the warfare with hundreds of arrows Vasu took up mace in his hands for his destruction. Having taken up that mace having a burning head and resembling the rod of Death Sāvitra struck Sumálin on his head there with.

sanskrit: सा तस्योपरि चोल्काभा पतन्तीव बभौ गदा
transliteration: sā tasyopari colkābhā patantīva babhau gadā
english: Having fallen on his head that mace shone like a fire-brand as the thunderbolt discharged by Indra, falls roaring on the summit of a mountain.

sanskrit: तस्य नैवास्थि न शिरो न मांसं ददृशे तदा
transliteration: tasya naivāsthi na śiro na māṃsaṃ dadṛśe tadā
english: By the stroke of that mace his person was reduced to ashes and therefore, there was not seen in the battle field either his bone, head or flesh.

sanskrit: तं दृष्ट्वा निहतं सङ्ख्ये राक्षसास्ते समन्ततः
transliteration: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ saṅkhye rākṣasāste samantataḥ
english: Having beheld him slain in the warfare the Räkşasas bewailing ran about on all sides and being distressed by Vasu they could not stay in the battle field.

sanskrit: स्वसैन्यं विद्रुतं चापि लक्षयित्वा ऽर्दितं सुरैः
english: Beholding Sumali slain and reduced to ashes by Vasu and being assailed by the deities the Räksasa host fled into diverse directions. And collecting all the Rākşasas stood there the highly powerful Meghanāda, enraged, the son of Ravana.

Beholding Sumali slain and reduced to ashes by Vasu and being assailed by the deities the Räksasa host fled into diverse directions. And collecting all the Rākşasas stood there the highly powerful Meghanāda, enraged, the son of Ravana.
Like to flaming fire approaching towards forest that great car-warrior encountered the enemies in a precious car coursing at will.
As soon as he, armed with various weapons, entered the field the celestials, at his very sight. And away to all directions.
None could stand before him, well-versed in war-fare. Thereupon beholding the deities terrified and pierced with shafts, Indra, the king of gods, said.

sanskrit: न भेतव्यं न गन्तव्यं निवर्तध्वं रणे सुराः
transliteration: na bhetavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ nivartadhvaṃ raṇe surāḥ
english: Be not afraid, O you celestials; do not fly away; come back to the battle; this my son, who has never been vanquished, goes to battle.

sanskrit: ततः शक्रसुतो देवो जयन्त इति विश्रुतः
transliteration: tataḥ śakrasuto devo jayanta iti viśrutaḥ
english: Thereupon Sakra's son, known as divine Jayanta, proceeded towards the field of action by a wondrous car.
Having encircled Saci's son and encountered Rāvana's son, the deities began to assail him.
The encounter between Mahendra's son Jayanta and Rāvana's son Meghanāda was like one between gods and demons.
Thereupon Rāvana's son began to assail, with shafts feathered in gold, his (Jayanta's) charioteer Gomukha, Mātali's son.
Sacīs son too, enraged, assailed on all sides, Rāvana's son and his charioteer. And the powerful Rāvani, stricken with ire and with eyes expanded, covered Sakra's son with arrows.
Sacīs son too, enraged, assailed on all sides, Rāvana's son and his charioteer. And the powerful Rāvani, stricken with ire and with eyes expanded, covered Sakra's son with arrows.
Thereupon Rāvana's son struck the celestial host with thousands of huge mountain summits, Śataghnīs, maces, Prāsas, Prāsas, clubs, daggers, Paraśus and various other sharp pointed weapons.
Thereupon Rāvana's son struck the celestial host with thousands of huge mountain summits, Śataghnīs, maces, Prāsas, Prāsas, clubs, daggers, Paraśus and various other sharp pointed weapons.

sanskrit: ततः प्रव्यथिता लोकाः सञ्जज्ञे च तमो ऽभवत्
transliteration: tataḥ pravyathitā lokāḥ sañjajñe ca tamo 'bhavat
english: Rāvana's son thus striking Indra's army the quarters were enshrouded with darkness by his illusory power.
Being overpowered with arrows on all sides the celestial army, leaving aside Jayanta, became restless.

sanskrit: नाभ्यजानन्त चान्योन्यं रक्षो वा देवता ऽथवा
english: The deities or the Rākşasas, they could not recognise one another. And being distressed they ran about on all sides.
Being enveloped with darkness and having their senses bewildered the celestials killed their own kith and the Rākṣasas their own men, and others fled away.
In the interim a heroic and powerful Daityachief, Pulomā, be name, taking ſacī's son disappeared.

sanskrit: सङ्गृह्य तं तु दौहित्रं प्रविष्टः सागरं तदा
आर्यकः स हि तस्यासीत्पुलोमा येन सा शची
transliteration: saṅgṛhya taṃ tu dauhitraṃ praviṣṭaḥ sāgaraṃ tadā
āryakaḥ sa hi tasyāsītpulomā yena sā śacī
english: Taking his own grand-son he entered into the ocean, Puloma was his grand-father for by him Śaci was begotten.

sanskrit: ज्ञात्वा प्रणाशं तु तदा जयन्तस्याथ देवताः
transliteration: jñātvā praṇāśaṃ tu tadā jayantasyātha devatāḥ
english: Thinking that Jayanta was slain all the deities greatly sorry and distressed fled away on all sides.
Thereupon Rāvana's son, enraged and encircled by his own powerful followers, pursued the celestials emitting loud cries.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा प्रणाशं पुत्रस्य दैवतेषु च विद्रुतम्
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā praṇāśaṃ putrasya daivateṣu ca vidrutam
english: Not beholding his son and observing the flight of the deities the king of the celestials said to Mātali, “Bring the car."

sanskrit: स तु दिव्यो महाभीमः सज्ज एव महारथः
transliteration: sa tu divyo mahābhīmaḥ sajja eva mahārathaḥ
english: By Mātali was brought, the celestial, highly dreadful, huge and quick-coursing chariot, that was ready.
(And he having) ascended the car, the huge clouds, with lightening, being driven by winds, began to emit forth loud mutterings before the chariot.
The Gandharvas began to play on various instruments and the Apsarās began to dance.
Taking up various weapons, Indra, the king of divinities, set out for the field of action, in the company of Rudras, Vasus, Adityas, the two Asvins and Maruts.
He, having set out for battle, the winds began to blow high, the sun was divested of its brilliance and the huge fire-brands began to send out flames.

In the interval the heroic and the highly powerful Daśagrīva ascended the celestial car, constructed by the Architect of the deities, encircled by the huge-bodied serpents capable of making down erect and by whose breath the battle-field was ablaze.

In the interval the heroic and the highly powerful Daśagrīva ascended the celestial car, constructed by the Architect of the deities, encircled by the huge-bodied serpents capable of making down erect and by whose breath the battle-field was ablaze.
Surrounded by demons and night-rangers and with the celestial car he encountered Mahendra in the battle-field.

sanskrit: पुत्रं तं वारयित्वा तु स्वयमेव व्यवस्थितः
transliteration: putraṃ taṃ vārayitvā tu svayameva vyavasthitaḥ
english: Having desisted his son he himself stood there. And having coming out from the field of action Ravana's son too stood silent.

sanskrit: ततो युद्धं प्रवृत्तं तु सुराणां राक्षसैः सह
transliteration: tato yuddhaṃ pravṛttaṃ tu surāṇāṃ rākṣasaiḥ saha
english: Thereupon there arose an encounter between the Räkşasas and the deities and there began a downpour of weapons in the conflict like clouds.

The vicious-souled Kumbhakarņa armed with various weapons came you, but he did not know,* O king, with whom the conflict was going on. *For he was asleep till then so he was not acquainted with the particulars war-fare. He used to sleep for six months at a time.
And by him enraged, the celestials were assailed with his teeth, feet, arms, hands, Saktis, Tomaras and clubs or any weapon whatsoever.
Thereupon the night-ranger engaged with the highly powerful Rudra and was wounded, in the conflict, with incessant strokes of weapons.
Thereupon the Rākşasas army began to fight with Maruts and they were overwhelmed in the encounter with the stroke of various weapons.
There issued out in the battle-field a river from weapons, having blood for its silent waters and infested with crows and vultures.

Having beheld his own army slain by the deities the highly powerful Daśänana, enraged beholding the army slain by gods, entered the ocean of celestial army and slaying the deities in the conflict confronted Sakra.

sanskrit: स तं प्रति विगाह्याशु प्रवृद्धं सैन्यसागरम्
transliteration: sa taṃ prati vigāhyāśu pravṛddhaṃ sainyasāgaram
english: Having beheld his own army slain by the deities the highly powerful Daśänana, enraged beholding the army slain by gods, entered the ocean of celestial army and slaying the deities in the conflict confronted Sakra.

sanskrit: यस्य विस्फारघोषेण स्तनन्ति स्म दिशो दश
transliteration: yasya visphāraghoṣeṇa stananti sma diśo daśa
english: Thereupon Śakra took up his huge bow by the twang where-of the ten quarters were filled.
Having unstrung his huge bow Indra struck Răvaņa, on his head, with arrows resembling the flame of fire and the rays of the sun.
And the Rākşasa-chief Daśānana, having long arms, also assailed Indra with hundreds of shafts discharged off his bow.

sanskrit: न ज्ञायते तदा किञ्चित्सर्वं हि तमसा वृतम्
transliteration: na jñāyate tadā kiñcitsarvaṃ hi tamasā vṛtam
english: They having been thus engaged with each other with the downpour of dreadful shafts, all the quarters were filled with darkness and in consequence thereof nothing was visible.
Thereupon darkness having set in all the celestials and Rākşasas, maddened with their strength, began to fight rushing one another.

sanskrit: दशांशं स्थापितं युद्धे शेषं नीतं यमक्षयम्
transliteration: daśāṃśaṃ sthāpitaṃ yuddhe śeṣaṃ nītaṃ yamakṣayam

sanskrit: तस्मिंस्तु तामसे युद्धे सर्वे ते देवराक्षसाः
transliteration: tasmiṃstu tāmase yuddhe sarve te devarākṣasāḥ
english: Thereupon darkness having set in all the celestials and Rākşasas, maddened with their strength, began to fight rushing one another.

And in that darkness-Indra, Ravana and Meghanāda— these three were not possessed by the influence of illusion. Beholding his whole army slain in a moment, Ravana, worked up with dreadful ire, sent out terrible roars.

sanskrit: स तु दृष्ट्वा बलं सर्वं रावणो निहतं क्षणात्
transliteration: sa tu dṛṣṭvā balaṃ sarvaṃ rāvaṇo nihataṃ kṣaṇāt
english: And in that darkness-Indra, Ravana and Meghanāda— these three were not possessed by the influence of illusion. Beholding his whole army slain in a moment, Ravana, worked up with dreadful ire, sent out terrible roars.
And in anger, that irrepressible one said to the charioteer, stationed on the car, “Do you take me to the other end of the enemies' host."
I shall soon in the field of battle, with the stroke of various weapons despatch all the deities to the abode of Death,

sanskrit: विषादो न च कर्तव्यः शीघ्रं वाहय मे रथम्
transliteration: viṣādo na ca kartavyaḥ śīghraṃ vāhaya me ratham
english: I shall slay Indra, Kubera, Varuna and Yama, what to speak of more, I shall soon destroy all the deities and place myself above them.

sanskrit: द्विः खलु त्वां ब्रवीम्यद्य यावदन्तो नयस्व माम्
transliteration: dviḥ khalu tvāṃ bravīmyadya yāvadanto nayasva mām
english: Be not sorry; do you soon drive my chariot. To-day I have told you twice to take me to the end of the enemy's army.

sanskrit: अयं स नन्दनोद्देशो यत्र वर्तामहे वयम्
नय मामद्य तत्र त्वमुदयो यत्र पर्वतः
transliteration: ayaṃ sa nandanoddeśo yatra vartāmahe vayam
naya māmadya tatra tvamudayo yatra parvataḥ
english: We are now waiting near the Nandana grove, do you take me to the hill when the sun rises.
Hearing his words the charioteer drove the steeds, coursing at will through the enemies' host.

sanskrit: तस्य तं निश्चयं ज्ञात्वा शक्रो देवेश्वरस्तदा
transliteration: tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā śakro deveśvarastadā
english: Thereupon being apprised of his intention, Śakra, the king of the celestials, stationed on car, said to the deities, in the field of battle.
O you deities-bear my words, what appear to me best. This Ten-necked demon must be vanquished by us while alive.
Ascending his car, gifted with the velocity of the wind, the highly powerful one is proceeding among the army like to the deep with waves rising during Parva.
It is not possible to slay him now, for he shall not meet with death in consequence of the boon. So let us make him captive-and we should all exert to that end.

sanskrit: यथा बलौ निरुद्धे च त्रैलोक्यं भुज्यते मया
transliteration: yathā balau niruddhe ca trailokyaṃ bhujyate mayā
english: Bali being held captive, I am enjoying the three worlds-and I think proper to obstruct the course of this vicious-souled one.

sanskrit: ततो ऽन्यं देशमास्थाय शक्रः सन्त्यज्य रावणम्
english: Having said this and left aside Råvaņa, Sakra went to another side, O King, and fought terrifying the Rākşasas in the conflict.
Dasagriva, incapable of being thwarted, entered by the northern route and the performer of hundred sacrifices by the southern.
Thereupon having entered into the army up to a hundred leagues the lord of Rākşasas overpowered the celestial host with a downpour of shafts.

sanskrit: ततः शक्रो निरीक्ष्याथ प्रनष्टं तु स्वकं बलम्
transliteration: tataḥ śakro nirīkṣyātha pranaṣṭaṃ tu svakaṃ balam
english: Thereupon beholding his own army slain Sakra, returned fearlessly and obstructed the Ten-necked demon.

sanskrit: हा हताः स्म इति ग्रस्तं दृष्ट्वा शक्रेण रावणम्
transliteration: hā hatāḥ sma iti grastaṃ dṛṣṭvā śakreṇa rāvaṇam
english: In the interim beholding Rāvaņa brought under his grasp by Śakra the demons and Raksasas cried aloud, “Alas we are slain."
Thereupon ascending his car Ravana's son, became senseless by his wrath and beside himself with rage, entered the dreadful flank.

sanskrit: तां प्रविश्य महामायां प्राप्तां गोपतिना पुरा
transliteration: tāṃ praviśya mahāmāyāṃ prāptāṃ gopatinā purā
english: Having resorted to the illusory powers, conferred upon him yore by Pasupati he entered into the enemies' camp and belaboured them.
Having left behind all other deities he pursued Indra and the highly effulgent Mahendra too espied his enemy's son.
And albeit assailed by the highly powerful deities, Ravanas son, divested of mail, entertained no fear.
Having overpowered the approaching charioteer Måtalt, with many excellent arrows he covered Mahendra with a downpour of shafts.

sanskrit: ततस्त्यक्त्वा रथं शक्रो विससर्ज च सारथिम्
transliteration: tatastyaktvā rathaṃ śakro visasarja ca sārathim
english: Thereat having left his car and charioteer Indra mounted his elephant Airāvata and ran about in search of Ravana's son.
Being invisible in the welkin by virtue of his illusory powers and having brought Indra under the influence thereof he struck him with hundreds of arrows.

sanskrit: स तं यदा परिश्रान्तमिन्द्रं जज्ञे ऽथ रावणिः
transliteration: sa taṃ yadā pariśrāntamindraṃ jajñe 'tha rāvaṇiḥ
english: When Råvaņa's son came to know that Indra was exhausted he, having bound him up by virtue of illusion, proceeded towards his army.

sanskrit: तं तु दृष्ट्वा बलात्तेन नीयमानं महारणात्
transliteration: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā balāttena nīyamānaṃ mahāraṇāt
english: Having seen Mahendra carried away by force from the battle field the deities thought“What is this?”
That conqueror of Śakra and subduer of enemies, conversant with illusory powers, was not visible, by whom, Indra, although master of many illusions, was carried away by force.
In the meantime, the celestials, all enraged, covered Rāvana with a downpour of shafts and belaboured him.

sanskrit: न शशाक स सङ्ग्रामे योद्धुं शत्रुभिरर्दितः
transliteration: na śaśāka sa saṅgrāme yoddhuṃ śatrubhirarditaḥ
english: And being worn out in the encounter with the Ādityas and Vasus he was not capable of fighting any more.
Beholding his father thus distressed and assailed in warfare with strokes, Ravana's son, although invisible, said.

sanskrit: जितं नो विदितं ते ऽस्तु स्वस्थो भव गतज्वरः
transliteration: jitaṃ no viditaṃ te 'stu svastho bhava gatajvaraḥ
english: Do you come, O father, our work in the battle field is finished; know, we have achieved victory; be you consoled and divested of agonies.

sanskrit: अयं हि सुरसैन्यस्य त्रैलोक्यस्य च यः प्रभुः
transliteration: ayaṃ hi surasainyasya trailokyasya ca yaḥ prabhuḥ
english: By virtue of my illusory powers I have made Mahendra captive the lord of the three worlds and of the celestial host and have crushed down the pride of the deities.

sanskrit: वृथा किं ते श्रमेणेह युद्धमद्य तु निष्फलम्
transliteration: vṛthā kiṃ te śrameṇeha yuddhamadya tu niṣphalam
english: Having subdued your enemy by virtue of your prowess do you enjoy the three worlds at your pleasure. What is the use of labouring again? And useless it is to fight again.
Hearing the words of Rāvana's son the deities retired from the battle field, and went away without Sakra.

sanskrit: स्वभवनमभितो जगाम हृष्टः स्वसुतमवाप्य च वाक्यमब्रवीत्
transliteration: svabhavanamabhito jagāma hṛṣṭaḥ svasutamavāpya ca vākyamabravīt

english: You have enhanced the glory of our race displaying the prowess like a highly powerful man. You have vanquished the celestials and their king of unequalled might.

sanskrit: नय रथमधिरोप्य वासवं नगरमितो व्रज सेनया वृतस्त्वम्
अहमपि तव गच्छतो द्रुतं सह सचिवैरनुयामि पृष्ठतः
transliteration: naya rathamadhiropya vāsavaṃ nagaramito vraja senayā vṛtastvam
ahamapi tava gacchato drutaṃ saha sacivairanuyāmi pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Do you set out hence for the city, taking Indra on your chariot and surrounded by soldiers. I shall, soon, delighted, follow you with my councillors.

sanskrit: अथ स बलवृतः सवाहनस्त्रिदशपतिं परिगृह्य रावणिः
transliteration: atha sa balavṛtaḥ savāhanastridaśapatiṃ parigṛhya rāvaṇiḥ
english: Thereupon having returned home with his army and chariots and taking the king of the celestials, the powerful son of Rāvana dismissed the victorious warriors.

sanskrit: जिते महेन्द्रे ऽतिबले रावणस्य सुतेन वै
english: The highly powerful Mahendra being thus defeated by Ravana's son, all the celestials, taking the patriarch Brahmä before them, went to Lanka.
Having obtained Rāvana encircled by his sons and brothers the Patriarch, stationed in the welkin, calmly said.

sanskrit: वत्स रावण तुष्टो ऽस्मि पुत्रस्य तव संयुगे
अहो ऽस्य विक्रमौदार्यं तव तुल्यो ऽधिको ऽपि वा
transliteration: vatsa rāvaṇa tuṣṭo 'smi putrasya tava saṃyuge
english: My son, Ravana, I have been pleased with your son in the conflict. Oh! what wonderful prowess, what strength-equal or greater than your.

sanskrit: जितं हि भवता सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं स्वेन तेजसा
कृता प्रतिज्ञा सफला प्रीतो ऽस्मि स्वसुतेन वै
transliteration: jitaṃ hi bhavatā sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ svena tejasā
kṛtā pratijñā saphalā prīto 'smi svasutena vai
english: You have, by your own prowess, conquered the three worlds — your promise has borne fruits-I have been pleased with you-both the father and son.

sanskrit: अयं च पुत्रो ऽतिबलस्तव रावण वीर्यवान्
english: O Rāvana, this your son is highly powerful and gifted with great strength and he shall be celebrated in the world under the appellation of 'Indrajit' or the conqueror of Indra.
The Raksasa shall be powerful and irrepressible, by those help, O King, the celestials have been brought under your subjection.
Do you therefore, O you having long arms, release Mahendra, she chastiser of Pāka and for setting him free what do you want from the celestials?
Thereupon the highly powerful Indrajit-the subduer of enemies, said: "If do you say so, O god, I pray for immortality."

sanskrit: सर्वे ऽपि जन्तवो ऽन्योन्यं भेतव्ये सति बिभ्यति
अतो ऽत्र लोके सर्वेषां सर्वस्माच्च भवेद्भयम्

english: Thereat the highly powerful patriarch said to Meghanāda, “There is none perfectly immortal on earth among created beings, birds, quadrupeds and other highly powerful beings.”
Hearing the words uttered by the grandfather, the highly powerful Meghanāda said to the eternal lord.

Hear, then, what I want in exchange for releasing Sakra. May a chariot with horses rise up from fire when I shall offer sacrifices to it, being desirous of vanquishing my enemies in the conflict. And may I be immortal as long as I shall remain on that car. This is the boon I have resolved upon praying for.

sanskrit: तत्स्थस्यामरता स्यान्मे एष मे निश्चयो वरः
transliteration: tatsthasyāmaratā syānme eṣa me niścayo varaḥ

sanskrit: युध्येयं देव सङ्ग्रामे तदा मे स्याद्विनाशनम्
transliteration: yudhyeyaṃ deva saṅgrāme tadā me syādvināśanam
english: May I meet with destruction, O deity, whenever I shall engage in fight without finishing my offerings to fire.

sanskrit: सर्वो हि तपसा देव वृणोत्यमरतां पुमान्
transliteration: sarvo hi tapasā deva vṛṇotyamaratāṃ pumān
english: All others, O god, attain to immortality by virtue of devout penances but I shall acquire that by dint of my own prowess.

sanskrit: एवमस्त्विति तं चाह वाक्यं देवः पितामहः
transliteration: evamastviti taṃ cāha vākyaṃ devaḥ pitāmahaḥ
english: Where to the grand-father replied saying "so be it." Thereupon Meghanäda released Indra and the celestials returned to their own abode.
In the interval, O Rāma, Indra became poorly, divested of his immortal brilliance, stricken with anxiety and pensive.

sanskrit: तं तु दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतं प्राह देवः प्रजापतिः
शतक्रतो किमु पुरा करोति स्म सुदुष्कृतम्
transliteration: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathābhūtaṃ prāha devaḥ prajāpatiḥ
śatakrato kimu purā karoti sma suduṣkṛtam
english: Beholding him in that plight the grand-father of the deities said:-O performer of hundred sacrifices, why did you formerly perpetrate that mighty iniquity?

sanskrit: अमरेन्द्र मया बह्व्यः प्रजाः सृष्टास्तथा प्रभो
transliteration: amarendra mayā bahvyaḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭāstathā prabho
english: O Chief of the immortals! O lord!, some creatures were all of the same colour, same speech, and same appearance.

sanskrit: तासां नास्ति विशेषो हि दर्शने लक्षणे ऽपि वा
transliteration: tāsāṃ nāsti viśeṣo hi darśane lakṣaṇe 'pi vā
english: There was no difference visible in their appearance or marks. Thereupon, with wholeminded-ness, I began to think of these created beings.

sanskrit: सो ऽहं तासां विशेषार्थं स्त्रियमेकां विनिर्ममे
english: And I created a female distinct from them. Collecting all those limbs that were most excellent among the created, I made a female under the name of Ahalyä. Hal means uglinessone born from Hal is called Halya. That female was known as Ahalyā because she had nothing blameable in her, I gave her that name.

sanskrit: हलं नामेह वैरूपं हल्यं तत्प्रभवं भवेत्
transliteration: halaṃ nāmeha vairūpaṃ halyaṃ tatprabhavaṃ bhavet

sanskrit: अहल्येति मया शक्र तस्या नाम प्रवर्तितम्
transliteration: ahalyeti mayā śakra tasyā nāma pravartitam

sanskrit: निर्मितायां च देवेन्द्र तस्यां नार्यां सुरर्षभ
भविष्यतीति कस्यैषा मम चिन्ता ततो ऽभवत्
transliteration: nirmitāyāṃ ca devendra tasyāṃ nāryāṃ surarṣabha
english: Having created that female I was thinking, O king of the celestials! O foremost of the deities!, on whom I should confer her.

sanskrit: त्वं तु शक्र तदा नारीं जानीषे मनसा प्रभो
transliteration: tvaṃ tu śakra tadā nārīṃ jānīṣe manasā prabho
english: Being proud of dignity, O Sakra, O lord, O Purandara you did regard her in your mind as your spouse.

sanskrit: सा मया न्यासभूता तु गौतमस्य महात्मनः
न्यस्ता बहूनि वर्षाणि तेन निर्यातिता च ह
transliteration: sā mayā nyāsabhūtā tu gautamasya mahātmanaḥ
nyastā bahūni varṣāṇi tena niryātitā ca ha
english: I placed her under the care of the high-souled Gautama and he rendered her back after many long years.

sanskrit: ज्ञात्वा तपसि सिद्धिं च पत्न्यर्थं स्पर्शिता तदा
transliteration: jñātvā tapasi siddhiṃ ca patnyarthaṃ sparśitā tadā
english: Thereupon considering the patience and accomplished asceticism of Gautama I married her with him.

sanskrit: सङ्क्रुद्धस्त्वं हि धर्मात्मन् गत्वा तस्याश्रमं मुनेः
transliteration: saṅkruddhastvaṃ hi dharmātman gatvā tasyāśramaṃ muneḥ
english: But being enraged and possessed by lust you did repair to the hermitage of the ascetic and see her resplendent like the flaming fire.

sanskrit: सा त्वया धर्षिता शक्र कामार्तेन समन्युना
दृष्टस्त्वं च तदा तेन ह्याश्रमे परमर्षिणा
transliteration: sā tvayā dharṣitā śakra kāmārtena samanyunā
dṛṣṭastvaṃ ca tadā tena hyāśrame paramarṣiṇā
english: Maddened with lust and ire you did ravish her and you was seen in that hermitage by the great ascetic. were

sanskrit: ततः क्रुद्धेन तेना ऽसि शप्तः परमतेजसा
english: You were then imprecated by him, enraged and gifted with great effulgence saying, 'O lord of the celestials, you have attained to a change of circumstances-for which, O Vásava, you have fearlessly ravished my spouse. You shall, therefore, O Sakra, go under the arms of the enemies, in conflict.

sanskrit: यस्मान्मे धर्षिता पत्नी त्वया वासव निर्भयम्
transliteration: yasmānme dharṣitā patnī tvayā vāsava nirbhayam
english: You were then imprecated by him, enraged and gifted with great effulgence saying, 'O lord of the celestials, you have attained to a change of circumstances-for which, O Vásava, you have fearlessly ravished my spouse. You shall, therefore, O Sakra, go under the arms of the enemies, in conflict.

sanskrit: अयं तु भावो दुर्बुद्धे यस्त्वयेह प्रवर्तितः
transliteration: ayaṃ tu bhāvo durbuddhe yastvayeha pravartitaḥ
english: And this vile desire, O you having a vicious intellect, which you have first created, shall undoubtedly spread in the world of mortals.

sanskrit: तत्रार्धं तस्य यः कर्ता त्वय्यर्धं निपतिष्यति
न च ते स्थावरं स्थानं भविष्यति न संशयः
transliteration: tatrārdhaṃ tasya yaḥ kartā tvayyardhaṃ nipatiṣyati
na ca te sthāvaraṃ sthānaṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Whoever shall commit this crime, shall be half responsible for it and the other half shall descend upon you; and forsooth your position shall not be permanent.

sanskrit: यश्च यश्च सुरेन्द्रः स्याद्ध्रुवः स न भविष्यति
एष शापो मया मुक्त इत्यसौ त्वां तदा ऽब्रवीत्
transliteration: yaśca yaśca surendraḥ syāddhruvaḥ sa na bhaviṣyati
eṣa śāpo mayā mukta ityasau tvāṃ tadā 'bravīt
english: Whoever shall be the lord of the celestials, shall not have his position secure. This is the curse I give, which I have communicated to you.

sanskrit: तां तु भार्यां स निर्भर्त्स्य सो ऽब्रवीत्सुमहातपाः
transliteration: tāṃ tu bhāryāṃ sa nirbhartsya so 'bravītsumahātapāḥ
english: Having remonstrated with his wife that one of devout penances said to her-'O vicious one, let your beauty be spoiled in the vicinity of the hermitage. You are gifted with beauty and youth but your mind is fickle; so you shall not continue as the single beautiful damsel in the world.

Having remonstrated with his wife that one of devout penances said to her-'O vicious one, let your beauty be spoiled in the vicinity of the hermitage. You are gifted with beauty and youth but your mind is fickle; so you shall not continue as the single beautiful damsel in the world.

sanskrit: रूपं च ते प्रजाः सर्वा गमिष्यन्ति न संशयः
transliteration: rūpaṃ ca te prajāḥ sarvā gamiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: All created beings shall participate your beauty; your matchless beauty has brought about this mischief.' Thenceforward all created beings were gifted with beauty.

sanskrit: सा तं प्रसादयामास महर्षिं गौतमं तदा
transliteration: sā taṃ prasādayāmāsa maharṣiṃ gautamaṃ tadā
english: Thereupon she propitiated the ascetic Gautama saying, “O twice-born one, I was unwittingly ravished by Indra, assuming your form. I have not committed this willingly, O ascetic-so do you be propitiated with me.”

Thereupon she propitiated the ascetic Gautama saying, “O twice-born one, I was unwittingly ravished by Indra, assuming your form. I have not committed this willingly, O ascetic-so do you be propitiated with me.”

Ahalyā having said this, Gautama replied:In the race of Ikşvākus, there shall be born a highly effulgent and mighty car-warrior, known in the world as Răma; for performing the rites of a Brahmana, the mighty-armed Visnu, assuming a human form, shall repair to the forest. You shall be purified when you shall behold him, O fair damsel. He shall be able to purify you from the iniquity perpetrated.

sanskrit: रामो नाम श्रुतो लोके वनं चाप्युपयास्यति
तं द्रक्ष्यसि यदा भद्रे ततः पूता भविष्यसि
transliteration: rāmo nāma śruto loke vanaṃ cāpyupayāsyati
taṃ drakṣyasi yadā bhadre tataḥ pūtā bhaviṣyasi
english: Ahalyā having said this, Gautama replied:In the race of Ikşvākus, there shall be born a highly effulgent and mighty car-warrior, known in the world as Răma; for performing the rites of a Brahmana, the mighty-armed Visnu, assuming a human form, shall repair to the forest. You shall be purified when you shall behold him, O fair damsel. He shall be able to purify you from the iniquity perpetrated.

sanskrit: स हि पावयितुं शक्तस्त्वया यद्दुष्कृतं कृतम्
तस्यातिथ्यं च कृत्वा वै मत्समीपं गमिष्यसि
transliteration: sa hi pāvayituṃ śaktastvayā yadduṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam
tasyātithyaṃ ca kṛtvā vai matsamīpaṃ gamiṣyasi

sanskrit: वत्स्यसि त्वं मया सार्धं तदा हि वरवर्णिनि
transliteration: vatsyasi tvaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ tadā hi varavarṇini

sanskrit: तत्स्मर त्वं महाबाहो दुष्कृतं यत्त्वया कृतम्
तेन त्वं ग्रहणं शत्रोर्यातो नान्येन वासव
transliteration: tatsmara tvaṃ mahābāho duṣkṛtaṃ yattvayā kṛtam
tena tvaṃ grahaṇaṃ śatroryāto nānyena vāsava

sanskrit: शीघ्रं वै यज यज्ञं त्वं वैष्णवं सुसमाहितः
transliteration: śīghraṃ vai yaja yajñaṃ tvaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ susamāhitaḥ

sanskrit: पुत्रश्च तव देवेन्द्र न विनष्टो महारणे
transliteration: putraśca tava devendra na vinaṣṭo mahāraṇe
english: You shall be purified by that sacrifice and go to heaven; and your son, O lord of celestials, has not been destroyed in the conflict. He has been taken into the ocean by his grand father.
Hearing this and having celebrated the sacrifice in honour of Vişnu he again went to the region of celestials and reigned there as their king.

sanskrit: निर्जितस्तेन देवेन्द्रः प्राणिनो ऽन्ये तु किं पुनः
transliteration: nirjitastena devendraḥ prāṇino 'nye tu kiṃ punaḥ
english: I have thus described to you the strength of Indrajit-what to speak of others he vanquished even Indra-the king of the celestials.

Hearing the words of Agastya, Rāma, Lakşmaņa, Vānaras and Rākşasas all said wonderful it is; and Vibhīşaņa, who was by the side of Rama, said:-After a long time, the old recollections have come to my mind.

Hearing the words of Agastya, Rāma, Lakşmaņa, Vānaras and Rākşasas all said wonderful it is; and Vibhīşaņa, who was by the side of Rama, said:-After a long time, the old recollections have come to my mind.

sanskrit: सपुत्रो येन सङ्ग्रामे जितः शक्रः सुरेश्वरः
transliteration: saputro yena saṅgrāme jitaḥ śakraḥ sureśvaraḥ
english: Thereupon Rāma said to Agastya-All, you have said, is true. And Agastya said Rāma, Rāvaņa, the thorn of people, then grew in power, by whom, in the company of his son, Indra, the lord of the celestials, was defeated.
Thereupon having bowed to Agastya the foremost of ascetics, the highly effulgent Rāma again surprisingly said.
"O Brāhmaṇa, O foremost of twice-born ones, when that cruel Rāvana journeyed over the earth, was it void of people? Was there no king, or prince on earth to administer punishment to him?

sanskrit: राजा वा राजमात्रो वा किं तदा नात्र कश्चन
धर्षणं यत्र न प्राप्तो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
transliteration: rājā vā rājamātro vā kiṃ tadā nātra kaścana
dharṣaṇaṃ yatra na prāpto rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
english: "O Brāhmaṇa, O foremost of twice-born ones, when that cruel Rāvana journeyed over the earth, was it void of people? Was there no king, or prince on earth to administer punishment to him?
Were all the kings then shorn of their strength and prowess? And many kings I (hear) were vanquished an driven out by him with various excellent weapons.
Hearing the words of Rāghava, the ascetic Agastya, having six sorts of wealth, laughing said, like to Brahmā, speaking to Rudra

O Rāma, O lord of earth, traversing the earth, Rāvana arrived at the city of Māhismatī, resembling the city of the celestials, where lived perpetually the deity of fire. There reigned a king named Arjuna, effulgent like fire which was kept perpetually in a well covered with Sara.

O Rāma, O lord of earth, traversing the earth, Rāvana arrived at the city of Māhismatī, resembling the city of the celestials, where lived perpetually the deity of fire. There reigned a king named Arjuna, effulgent like fire which was kept perpetually in a well covered with Sara.

sanskrit: अर्जुनो नर्मदां रन्तुं गतः स्त्रीभिः सहेश्वरः
transliteration: arjuno narmadāṃ rantuṃ gataḥ strībhiḥ saheśvaraḥ
english: One day the highly powerful Arjuna, the king of Haihayas, repaired to the river Narmadā, with his wives to sport.

sanskrit: तमेव दिवसं सो ऽथ रावणस्तत्र आगतः
english: At the very same day, Ravana, the lord of Rākṣasas, arrived there and asked his councillors saying.
Where is the king Arjuna? Do you speedily tell me; I am Rāvana, I have come to fight with your king.
Do you, at first, communicate to him the news of my arrival. Being thus addressed by Ravana, the learned ministers informed the lord of Raksasas, of the absence of the king.
Hearing of the absence of the king from the citizens Viśravasa's son came out of the city and reached the Vindhya mountain resembling the Himalayas.

He espied the mountain extending over the welkin like to clouds and rising up as if riving the earth and obstructing the sky. The mountain had a thousand summits and the lions were residing in the caves and hundreds of fountain were falling from it; the mountain was as if laughing aloud and the celestials, Gandharvas, Apsarās and Kinsaras were sporting there with their females, and it appeared in consequence thereof) like the region of celestials; and rivers, with waters transparent like crystal, were flowing. And it therefore appeared like a thousand serpents having trembling tongues. And casting his looks upon Vindhya mountain, resembling the Himalayas and having huge caves, Ravana, the king of Raksasas, reached the river Narmadā, of holy waters and going rapidly to the western ocean. Her waters were being agitated by buffaloes, deer, tigers, lions, bears and elephants distressed by heat.
Having covered her, Cakravakas, Karandavas, swans, water-cocks and Sārasas, maddened, were emitting notes.

The charming Narmadā appeared like a beautiful damsel-having blossoming trees for her waist, the row of swans for Mekhala, filaments of flowers for paste, watery foams for white silken cloth, the pleasure of descending into water for the pleasure of touch and fullblown lotuses for white eyes. Having descended from his car and bathed in the waters of Narmadā, the foremost of streams, resembling a fair one, Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, with his councillors, sat on her coast resided by many an ascetic.

sanskrit: प्रख्याय नर्मदां सो ऽथ गङ्गेयमिति रावणः

english: But seeing me here seated, his rays have become cool like those of the moon. At my fear, even the wind is blowing carefully, being cold and fragrant by the touch of the waters of the Narmadā and removing our toil.
This charming Narmadā, abounding in crocodiles, fishes and birds, though a natural stream, is standing still like a terrified damsel.
Being wounded in conflicts with many a king your persons have been pasted with blood.
Therefore like to Särvabhauma and other infuriated elephants going down into the water of the Ganges, do you descend into the water of Narmadā conferring auspiciousness and health.

Bathing in this stream you shall be cleansed from sins. I shall, also on the coast of this river, like the rays of the autumnal moon, reverentially worship with flowers Mahādeva, holding Pināka in his hands.
Hearing the words of Ravana, Prahasta, Suka, Sarana, Mahodara, Dhumraksa and other councillors descended into the waters of Narmada.
She was agitated by those elephant like leading Rākşasas like to the Gargā by Vămana, Anjana, Padma and other elephants.
Thereupon having got up from the waters the highly powerful Rākşasas culled flowers for Ravana's offerings.
In a moment the Rākṣasas collected heaps of flowers on the picturesque banks of Narmadā, resembling the white clouds.
Flowers being thus collected, Rāvana, the king of Rākşasas descended into the Narmadā for bathing like a huge elephant into the Gangā. And having bathed he got up, reciting excellent incantations.
Flowers being thus collected, Rāvana, the king of Rākşasas descended into the Narmadā for bathing like a huge elephant into the Gangā. And having bathed he got up, reciting excellent incantations.

Thereupon having left off his wet cloth he put on a white one. And to find out place for worshipping, he, with folded hands, proceeded towards the banks. And the Răkşasas too, like to so many moving mountains, followed him.

sanskrit: यत्र यत्र च याति स्म रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
जाम्बूनदमयं लिङ्गं तत्र तत्र स्म नीयते
transliteration: yatra yatra ca yāti sma rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ
jāmbūnadamayaṃ liṅgaṃ tatra tatra sma nīyate
english: Wherever Rāvana went the golden Siva Linga was brought.
Thereupon Rāvaņa placed that upon a heap of sands and began to worship it with various nectar-smelling flowers and sandal.

sanskrit: ततः सतामार्तिहरं परं वरं वरप्रदं चन्द्रमयूखभूषणम्
समर्चयित्वा स निशाचरो जगौ प्रसार्य हस्तान्प्रणनर्त चाग्रतः
transliteration: tataḥ satāmārtiharaṃ paraṃ varaṃ varapradaṃ candramayūkhabhūṣaṇam
samarcayitvā sa niśācaro jagau prasārya hastānpraṇanarta cāgrataḥ
english: Having finished the worship of Siva, the foremost of deities, having ww moon on his crown, the conferrer of boons and the remover of miseries, the night-ranger danced with uplifted hands and sang before it.

At no distance from where on the banks of the river Narmadā, that dreadful lord of Rākşasas collected the flowers, Arjuna, the King of Māhismatī, and the foremost of the victorious, was sporting with his wives in the water.

sanskrit: अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठो माहिष्मत्याः पतिः प्रभुः
transliteration: arjuno jayatāṃ śreṣṭho māhiṣmatyāḥ patiḥ prabhuḥ
english: At no distance from where on the banks of the river Narmadā, that dreadful lord of Rākşasas collected the flowers, Arjuna, the King of Māhismatī, and the foremost of the victorious, was sporting with his wives in the water.

sanskrit: तासां मध्यगतो राजा रराज च तदार्जुनः
transliteration: tāsāṃ madhyagato rājā rarāja ca tadārjunaḥ
english: And being encircled by them the king Arjuna appeared like a leading elephant surrounded by a thousands of she elephants.

sanskrit: जिज्ञासुः स तु बाहूनां सहस्रस्योत्तमं बलम्
transliteration: jijñāsuḥ sa tu bāhūnāṃ sahasrasyottamaṃ balam
english: In order to measure the strength of his thousand arms the King of Haihayas obstructed the course of Narmadă.
Being obstructed by the arms of Kārtavīryarjuna and having flooded the banks with her pure waters, Narmadā flowed in an opposite direction.
The currents of Narmadā, rising high as during the rainy season flowed with fishes, and crocodiles.
That stream, as if driven against Rävaņa by Kārtavīryarjuna, carried away his collection of flowers.

sanskrit: नर्मदां पश्यते कान्तां प्रतिकूलां यथा प्रियाम्
transliteration: narmadāṃ paśyate kāntāṃ pratikūlāṃ yathā priyām

english: Thereupon being anxious to learn the cause of the rise of the river, the Ten-necked demon, with his right finger, hinted Suka and Sarana.
Being commanded by Rāvana, the two brothers, the heroic Suka and Sāraņa proceeded towards the west by the aerial way.
And going half a league, the two night-rangers espied a man sporting in the waters with some females.
He was huge as a Sāla tree, his hairs were floating on the water, he was inebriate and his eyes were reddened in consequence thereof.
Like to Sumeru holding the earth with his thousand feet he obstructed the current of the river with his thousand arms.
He was surrounded by a thousands of beautiful damsels like an elephant by a thousands of she-elephants.
Beholding that dreadful spectacle, the Rākṣasas-Śuka and Sāraṇa came back and approaching Rāvaņa communicated (all) to him.
O lord of Rākşasas, an unknown person, huge as a Sāla tree, is sporting with females obstructing the course of Narmadā like to a dam.
Being withheld by the thousand arms of that man the waters of Narmadā were continually throwing up high waves.
Hearing the words of śuka and Sarana, Ravana exclaimed “This is Arjuna' and proceeded to fight with him.
Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, having set out with a hostile intention against Kārtavīryarjuna, the wind mixed with dust began to blow high with tumultuous sound.

sanskrit: सकृदेव कृतो रावः सरक्तः प्रेषितो घनैः
transliteration: sakṛdeva kṛto rāvaḥ saraktaḥ preṣito ghanaiḥ
english: The clouds began to mutter with a downpour of rain. And the lord of Räkşasas proceeded against Arjuna with Mahodara. Mahāparáva, Dhumraksa, Suka and Sarana.

sanskrit: अदीर्घेणैव कालेन स तदा राक्षसो बली
transliteration: adīrgheṇaiva kālena sa tadā rākṣaso balī

english: Within a short time the dreadful Raksasa, powerful as the elephant Arjuna, reached the banks of Narmada and espied there Arjuna encircled by females as an elephant surrounded by she-elephants.
At the very sight the eyes of the lord of Raksasas, proud of his prowess, grew red and addressing the councillors of the king Arjuna he said.

sanskrit: रावणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणो ऽथार्जुनस्य ते
english: Hearing the words of Rāvana, the ministers of Arjuna stood up with arms and said.

sanskrit: युद्धस्य कालो विज्ञेयः साधु भोः साधु रावण
transliteration: yuddhasya kālo vijñeyaḥ sādhu bhoḥ sādhu rāvaṇa

sanskrit: यः क्षीबं स्त्रीवृतं चैव योद्धुमुत्सहते नृपम्
transliteration: yaḥ kṣībaṃ strīvṛtaṃ caiva yoddhumutsahate nṛpam

sanskrit: युद्धे श्रद्धा च यद्यस्ति श्वस्तात समरे ऽर्जुनम्
transliteration: yuddhe śraddhā ca yadyasti śvastāta samare 'rjunam

english: Thereupon the hungry councillors of Rāvana, slew some of the ministers of the king and devoured some.
There arose a dreadful uproar on the banks of Narmada, of the councillors of Răvana and Arjuna.
The warriors of Arjuna assailed Rāvana and his ministers with hundreds of arrows, Prāsas, darts, Tomaras, thunder-bolts and Karsanas.
The warriors of Arjuna became dreadfully furious and emitted cries like the roaring of the deep infested with crocodiles, fishes and other marine monsters.
Thereupon being enraged and displaying their own prowess Suka, Sāraṇa and other ministers of Ravana began to destroy Arjuna's soldiers.
Thereupon the emissaries, stricken with fear, went to the sporting king and communicated to him the proceedings of Rāvana and his iministers.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा न भेतव्यमिति स्त्रीजनं तं ततो ऽर्जुनः
transliteration: śrutvā na bhetavyamiti strījanaṃ taṃ tato 'rjunaḥ
english: Hearing those words and saying to the females-"Do not fear” he rose up from the waters like an elephante
The eyes of that fire-like Arjuna were reddened with ire and he shone dreadfully like the fire of dissolution.
And taking up speedily his club, that one, always using golden clubs, pursued the Rakşasas like to darkness following the sun.
Holding up the huge club and hurling it with his arms, Arjuna, resorting to the velocity of Garuda, went on

sanskrit: तस्य मार्गं समारुद्ध्य विन्ध्यो ऽर्कस्येव पर्वतः
english: Thereupon stood there obstructing his course Raksasa, worked up with anger and with a mace in his hand, like to the Vindhya range standing in the way of the sun.

sanskrit: ततो ऽस्य मुसलं घोरं लोहबद्धं महोद्धतः
english: And throwing down off his hand the iron mace, he, in anger, began to roar, like Yama.
And the top of the mace freed from the hand of Prahasta, was ablaze like the tips of Asoka flowers.
Not the least agitated on beholding that mace, the king Arjuna, by his club, baffled its action.
Thereupon uplifting the huge club, five hundred hands long, the king of Haihayas pursued Prahasta.

sanskrit: तथा हतो ऽतिवेगेन प्रहस्तो गदया तदा
english: And within a short time being struck down by that club gifted with great velocity Prahasta fell down on earth like to the summit of a mountain clapped down by the thunder-bolt of Indra.
Beholding Prahasta fallen, Marica, Suka, Säraņa, Mahodara and Dhumrākṣa fled away from the battle-field.
All the councillors having thus fled away and Prahasta being slain, Rāvaņa speedily proceeded towards Arjuna, the foremost of kings.
Thereupon there ensued a terrible encounter capable of making down erect between the thousand-armed Arjuna, the king of men, and the twenty-armed Ravana, the king of Raksasas.

sanskrit: बलोद्धतौ यथा नागौ वाशितार्थे यथा वृषौ
transliteration: baloddhatau yathā nāgau vāśitārthe yathā vṛṣau

english: As the mountains suffer many clappings of thunder-bolts so did they bear many strokes.

sanskrit: यथा ऽ शनिरवेभ्यस्तु जायते ऽथ प्रतिश्रुतिः
english: And all the quarters were resounded with the sound proceeding from the stroke of their clubs like to the sound of thunder-bolts.

sanskrit: अर्जुनस्य गदा सा तु पात्यमाना ऽहितोरसि
english: Being placed against the breast of Rāvaņa Arjuna's club rendered, for a moment, the welkin look like the burning gold as does the lightning.
And striking again and again against Arjuna's breast Ravana's club looked like a huge firebrand.
Neither Arjuna was worn out nor was Rāvaņa. And the conflict went on between them like the encounter between Bali and Våsava in the days of yore.
The King of men and the King of Rākşasas assailed and wounded one another with their clubs like to two bulls striking one another with their horns and two elephants with their tusks.

sanskrit: ततो ऽर्जुनेन क्रुद्धेन सर्वप्राणेन सा गदा
english: Thereupon worked up with rage, Arjuna, with his full might, smote Răvaņa on his breast, with his club.
But Rāvana was well protected by the boon of the celestial, so the club fell on earth sundered into two pieces like one hurled by a weak wight.
Still wounded by the mace of Arjuna, Rāvana, shedding tears, ran away at a distance of four feet and sat there.

sanskrit: स विह्वलं तदालक्ष्य दशग्रीवं ततो ऽर्जुनः
english: Beholding Răvaņa thus over-whelmed Arjuna sprang up and caught him like Garuda holding a serpent and Vişņu binding Bali. Daśagrīva being thus bound, the Siddhas, Caranas and the celestials exclaiming "Well done! Well done!!” showered flowers upon Arjuna.

Beholding Răvaņa thus over-whelmed Arjuna sprang up and caught him like Garuda holding a serpent and Vişņu binding Bali. Daśagrīva being thus bound, the Siddhas, Caranas and the celestials exclaiming "Well done! Well done!!” showered flowers upon Arjuna.
And the king emitted leonine roars again and again as a tiger joyous roars like a cloud, holding a deer under his grasp.
Regaining his sense and beholding Rāvana bound, Prahasta, in great anger, pursued, the King of Haihaya.
And the Rākşasa force grew tempestuous like to the rising of the ocean during rains.
Thereupon exclaiming repeatedly “Leave him off! Leave him off Wait! Wait!!" The Raksasa host hurled hundreds of Musalas and darts in the battle-field.
Not the least moved thereby the king Arjuna, the slayer of enemies, bore those weapons of the enemies of the celestials.
Thereupon baffling the weapons of the Räkşasas by means of many a dreadful and excellent one, Arjuna, the king of Haihayas, drove them away · like winds scattering the clouds.

Having thus struck terror to the night-rangers, he, encircled by his own kinsmen, repaired to his own city with Ravana, carrying him bound like to Indra carrying Bali bound. Thereupon flowers and fried paddy were showered upon him by the Brāhmaṇas and citizens.

sanskrit: तदा ऽर्जुनः सम्प्रविवेश तां पुरीं बलिं निगृह्येव सहस्रलोचनः
transliteration: tadā 'rjunaḥ sampraviveśa tāṃ purīṃ baliṃ nigṛhyeva sahasralocanaḥ
english: Having thus struck terror to the night-rangers, he, encircled by his own kinsmen, repaired to his own city with Ravana, carrying him bound like to Indra carrying Bali bound. Thereupon flowers and fried paddy were showered upon him by the Brāhmaṇas and citizens.

sanskrit: ततः पुलस्त्यः शुश्राव कथितं दिवि दैवतैः
transliteration: tataḥ pulastyaḥ śuśrāva kathitaṃ divi daivataiḥ
english: Thereupor Pulastya heard from the celestials ot the capture of Råvana like to the holding of the.wind.
Having seen moved by the love for his son, the highly effulgent, great ascetic, proceeded to see the king of Māhismati.
Proceeding by the aerial way, that twice-born one, gifted with the velocity of wind and the flight of wind, reached the city of Māhismati.
Like to Brahma entering Indra's Amaravati, he entered the city resembling the capital of Indr and filled with delighted and plump citizens.
Beholding that dreadful Rșis approach like to Āditya walking on foot, the warders communicated the intelligence to the king Arjuna.
Understanding from their words that Pulastya was coming, the king of Haihayas, placing his folded palms on his crown, proceeded to welcome him.

sanskrit: पुरोहितो ऽस्य गृह्यार्घ्यं मधुपर्कं तथैव च
english: Like, to Brhaspati preceding Purandara, the royal priests went before him carrying, Madhuparka and water to wash feet.
And beholding the ascetic resembling the rising sun arrived, the King Arjuna bowed to him reverentially like Indra saluting Mahadeva.

sanskrit: स तस्य मधुपर्कं गां पाद्यमर्घ्यं निवेद्य च
transliteration: sa tasya madhuparkaṃ gāṃ pādyamarghyaṃ nivedya ca
english: Thereupon offering him Madhuparka, cow and water to wash feet, the king of Haihayas, in accents obstructed with delight, addressed the ascetic saying

sanskrit: अद्याहं तु द्विजेन्द्र त्वां यस्मात्पश्यामि दुर्दशम्
transliteration: adyāhaṃ tu dvijendra tvāṃ yasmātpaśyāmi durdaśam
english: Reverend Sir, your visit, it is hard to obtain. On beholding you my city Mahişmati has been turned into Amaravati.

sanskrit: अद्य मे कुशलं देव अद्य मे कुशलं व्रतम्
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे सफलं तपः
transliteration: adya me kuśalaṃ deva adya me kuśalaṃ vratam
adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me saphalaṃ tapaḥ
english: Today have I obtained all auspiciousness, O lord; today has my religious observance been fruitful; today has my birth proved blessed and today has my devout penance been crowned with success, for I bow to your feet, which have been worshipped by the celestials. This my kingdom, these my sons, this my wife and myself are all at your disposal do you order me, O Brahmaņa, what I may do for you.

sanskrit: इदं राज्यमिमे पुत्रा इमे दारा इमे वयम्
ब्रह्मन्किं कुर्मि किं कार्यमाज्ञापयतु नो भवान्
transliteration: idaṃ rājyamime putrā ime dārā ime vayam
brahmankiṃ kurmi kiṃ kāryamājñāpayatu no bhavān
english: Today have I obtained all auspiciousness, O lord; today has my religious observance been fruitful; today has my birth proved blessed and today has my devout penance been crowned with success, for I bow to your feet, which have been worshipped by the celestials. This my kingdom, these my sons, this my wife and myself are all at your disposal do you order me, O Brahmaņa, what I may do for you.

sanskrit: तं धर्मे ऽग्निषु पुत्रेषु शिवं पृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम्
transliteration: taṃ dharme 'gniṣu putreṣu śivaṃ pṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam
english: Thereupon having enquired of the king about his piety, offerings and the well-being of his sons, Pulastya said to Arjuna, the king of Haihayas.

sanskrit: अतुलं ते बलं येन दशग्रीवस्त्वया जितः
transliteration: atulaṃ te balaṃ yena daśagrīvastvayā jitaḥ
english: O foremost of kings, O you having eyes like lotus-petals! O you having a countenance like the full moon! When you have vanquished Ravaņa, your prowess is matchless in the triple world.

sanskrit: सो ऽयं मृधे त्वया बद्धः पौत्रो मे रणदुर्जयः
transliteration: so 'yaṃ mṛdhe tvayā baddhaḥ pautro me raṇadurjayaḥ
english: You have bound up my invincible son in the conflict at whose fear the wind and the ocean stand still.

sanskrit: पुत्रकस्य यशः पीतं नाम विश्रावितं त्वया
transliteration: putrakasya yaśaḥ pītaṃ nāma viśrāvitaṃ tvayā
english: Having drunk up the glories of my son you have announced your own; so I do say, O my son, do you release Dasanana.

sanskrit: पुलस्त्याज्ञां प्रगृह्योचे न किञ्चन वचो ऽर्जुनः
english: Hearing this command of Pulastya, the king Arjuna did not utter a single world and set, most delightedly the king of Räkşasas, free.

sanskrit: स तं प्रमुच्य त्रिदशारिमर्जुनः प्रपूज्य दिव्याभरणस्रगम्बरैः
अहिंसकं सख्यमुपेत्य साग्निकं प्रणम्य तं ब्रह्मसुतं गृहं ययौ
transliteration: sa taṃ pramucya tridaśārimarjunaḥ prapūjya divyābharaṇasragambaraiḥ
ahiṃsakaṃ sakhyamupetya sāgnikaṃ praṇamya taṃ brahmasutaṃ gṛhaṃ yayau
english: Having released that foe of the celestials, worshipped him with celestials ornaments and garlands and established friendship removing all enmities with Ravana before fire, and bowed to Pulastya, the son of Brahmā, he repaired to his own house.
And being released by the influence of Pulastya, the highly powerful Daśānana, the king of Raksasas, accepted his hospitality and being embraced by him, returned home ashamed.
And having set Daśagriva at liberty Pulastya, the son of Brahma and the foremost of Munis repaired to the celestial region.
O Rāma, in this wise, the highly powerful Ravana was defeated by Arjuna and released by Pulastya.

sanskrit: नावज्ञा हि परे कार्या य इच्छेत् प्रियमात्मनः
transliteration: nāvajñā hi pare kāryā ya icchet priyamātmanaḥ
english: Observe therefore, O descendant of Raghu, there is a mightier man than the mighty; therefore, one, desirous of his own well-being, should not disregard another.

sanskrit: ततः स राजा पिशिताशनानां सहस्रबाहोरुपलभ्य मैत्रीम्
पुनर्नृपाणां कदनं चकार चचार सर्वां पृथिवीं च दर्पात्
transliteration: tataḥ sa rājā piśitāśanānāṃ sahasrabāhorupalabhya maitrīm
punarnṛpāṇāṃ kadanaṃ cakāra cacāra sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ ca darpāt
english: Having acquired friendship with thousandarmed Arjuna, Daśānana, the king of Rākşasas, the world began again to journey over distressing the kings.
Released by Arjuna, and yet not conceiving any shame, Rāvana, the king of Räkşasas again began to transverse the earth.

sanskrit: राक्षसं वा मनुष्यं वा शृणुते ऽयं बलाधिकम्
transliteration: rākṣasaṃ vā manuṣyaṃ vā śṛṇute 'yaṃ balādhikam
english: Rākşasas or men, of whom the proud Rävaņa heard to be powerful he used to approach and summon them for fight.
After some time he arrived at the city of Kişkindhā reared by Vāli and invited him, wearing golden garland, to fight.
Thereat, Tara, her father Susena and the Prince Sugrīva said to the king of Rākşasas.

sanskrit: राक्षसेन्द गतो वाली यस्ते प्रतिबलो भवेत्
को ऽन्यः प्रमुखतः स्थातुं तव शक्तः प्लवङ्गमः
transliteration: rākṣasenda gato vālī yaste pratibalo bhavet
ko 'nyaḥ pramukhataḥ sthātuṃ tava śaktaḥ plavaṅgamaḥ
english: O lord of Rākşasas, he is not present here, who shall be able to withstand you. What monkey else is capable of standing before you?
However, O Ravana, Vali shall soon return after performing the Sandhya rites at the confluence of the four oceans; therefore wait here for a moment.
Behold, O Dasanana, there lie the bones of all those, like conch, who came ere this to fight with the powerful king of monkeys.
O Ravana, O Raksasa, ever if you have drunk nectar, you shall at this very moment loose your life, when the encounter with Vāli shall take place.

sanskrit: इदं मुहूर्तं तिष्ठस्व दुर्लभं ते भविष्यति
transliteration: idaṃ muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭhasva durlabhaṃ te bhaviṣyati
english: O Vaiśravaņa, do you observe the variegated universe now wait for a moment after which it will be hard for you to keep your life.
Or if you do wish to meet with death do you speedily repair to the southern ocean and you shall behold there Vali like to fire placed on earth.

sanskrit: स तु तारं विनिर्भर्त्स्य रावणो लोकरावणः
transliteration: sa tu tāraṃ vinirbhartsya rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ
english: Hearing those words, Rāvana, the aggrandiser of the triple world, remonstrated with Tāra and ascending his flowery car went to the southern ocean and espied Vali, having red countenance like the rising sun, engaged in Sandhyā rites with whole-mindedness.

Hearing those words, Rāvana, the aggrandiser of the triple world, remonstrated with Tāra and ascending his flowery car went to the southern ocean and espied Vali, having red countenance like the rising sun, engaged in Sandhyā rites with whole-mindedness.
Thereupon having descended from his Puşpaka car he with silent approached Vāli to bring him under his grasp.

sanskrit: यदृच्छया तदा दृष्टो वालिनापि स रावणः
पापाभिप्रायवान् दृष्ट्वा चकार न तु सम्भ्रमम्
transliteration: yadṛcchayā tadā dṛṣṭo vālināpi sa rāvaṇaḥ
pāpābhiprāyavān dṛṣṭvā cakāra na tu sambhramam
english: Casting his looks at pleasure, Vali saw him. Albeit apprised of his evil intention, he was not the least moved. And he did not care for him as a lion is not moved on beholding a hare and Garuda on beholding a serpent.

sanskrit: शशमालक्ष्य सिंहो वा पन्नगं गरुडो यथा
न चिन्तयति तं वाली रावणं पापनिश्चयम्
transliteration: śaśamālakṣya siṃho vā pannagaṃ garuḍo yathā
na cintayati taṃ vālī rāvaṇaṃ pāpaniścayam
english: Casting his looks at pleasure, Vali saw him. Albeit apprised of his evil intention, he was not the least moved. And he did not care for him as a lion is not moved on beholding a hare and Garuda on beholding a serpent.
