english: And in rio time the servants brought for him well-cooked meat and various fruits.
Being inebriate the beautiful Apsarās, wellskilled in the art of singing and dancing, began to dance before Rāma in the company of Kinnaris.

The intelligent and beautiful females being intoxicated after taking wine, and well-skilled in the art of singing and dancing, began to dance before Råma. The virtuous-souled Rāma, the foremost of those who know how to please, satisfied those beautiful damsels adorned with various ornaments.

sanskrit: स तया सीतया सार्धमासीनो विरराज ह
transliteration: sa tayā sītayā sārdhamāsīno virarāja ha
english: And Sītā sitting by him, he appeared like the effulgent Vaşistha in the company of Arundhatī.

sanskrit: एवं रामो मुदा युक्तः सीतां सुरसुतोपमाम्
transliteration: evaṃ rāmo mudā yuktaḥ sītāṃ surasutopamām
english: Being greatly delighted the celestial-like Rama pleased everyday Sītā resembling a celestial damsel.
Sītā and Rāghava thus spent their days happily. And thus was spent the delightful winter giving all enjoyments. Enjoying various things the high-souled Rāma and Sītā spent ten thousand years.
Once on a morning time, having performed all the religious ceremonies, in the fore part of the day, Rāma, to spend the evening, entered the inner apartment.
Sītā, too, having performed all religious ceremonies of morning, first in all, attended to the service of her mother-in-law.
Thereupon wearing a beautifully coloured cloth and being adorned with various ornaments Sītā appeared before Rāma like to ſací approaching the king of celestials in heaven.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा तु राघवः पत्नीं कल्याणेन समन्विताम्
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā tu rāghavaḥ patnīṃ kalyāṇena samanvitām
english: And beholding the auspicious signs of pregnancy in his souse Rāma attained to excessive delight.
Thereupon he said to the beautiful Sītā resembling a celestial damsel:-"0 Vaidehi, signs of pregnancy are manifest in you. What desires of your can we satisfy?"

sanskrit: किमिच्छसि वरारोहे कामः किं क्रियतां तव
transliteration: kimicchasi varārohe kāmaḥ kiṃ kriyatāṃ tava
english: Smiling a little the daughter of Janaka said:"O Rāghava, I wish to behold the holy hermitages. I wish to salute the greatly effulgent Rșis living on fruits and roots and residing on the banks of the Gangā. I greatly desire, O Rāma, that I may spend even one night in the hermitage of the Rșis living on fruits and roots.”

sanskrit: स्मितं कृत्वा तु वैदेही रामं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्
transliteration: smitaṃ kṛtvā tu vaidehī rāmaṃ vākyamathābravīt
english: Smiling a little the daughter of Janaka said:"O Rāghava, I wish to behold the holy hermitages. I wish to salute the greatly effulgent Rșis living on fruits and roots and residing on the banks of the Gangā. I greatly desire, O Rāma, that I may spend even one night in the hermitage of the Rșis living on fruits and roots.”
Whereto replied Rāma of unwearied actions, saying 'so be it.' Believe me, O Vaidehi, that you shall undoubtedly go there to-morrow.
Having thus addressed Maithili, the daughter of Janaka, Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, then issued out of the inner apartment and entered the middle one filled with his friends.
Rāma having taken his seat there, the experienced councillors encircling him began to dwell upon many amusing stories.
Vijaya, Madhumatta, Kasyapa, Mangala, Kula, Surajin, Kaliya, Bhadra Dantavaktra, Sumāgadha-all delightedly began to introduce many amusing talks before the high-souled Rāma.
Vijaya, Madhumatta, Kasyapa, Mangala, Kula, Surajin, Kaliya, Bhadra Dantavaktra, Sumāgadha-all delightedly began to introduce many amusing talks before the high-souled Rāma.

sanskrit: काः कथा नगरे भद्र वर्तन्ते विषयेषु च
transliteration: kāḥ kathā nagare bhadra vartante viṣayeṣu ca

sanskrit: किं च सीतां समाश्रित्य भरतं किं च लक्ष्मणम्
transliteration: kiṃ ca sītāṃ samāśritya bharataṃ kiṃ ca lakṣmaṇam
english: Thereupon Räma incidentally addressed them saying, “O Bhadra, how do the inhabitants of the city and provinces talk about Sītā, Bharata, Laksmana, Satrughna and the mother Kaikeyi? The kings, when they deviate from the paths of justice, become objects of censure in the houses of men and even in the forests as well.”

sanskrit: किं नु शत्रुघ्नमुद्दिश्य कैकयीं किं नु मातरम्
वक्तव्यतां च राजानो वरे राज्ये व्रजन्ति च
transliteration: kiṃ nu śatrughnamuddiśya kaikayīṃ kiṃ nu mātaram
vaktavyatāṃ ca rājāno vare rājye vrajanti ca

english: Rāma having said this, Bhadra with folded hands replied: "O king, the citizens speak many good things about you; besides they dilate upon many things in their own houses regarding your conquest acquired by the destruction of the Ten-necked demon."

Rāma having said this, Bhadra with folded hands replied: "O king, the citizens speak many good things about you; besides they dilate upon many things in their own houses regarding your conquest acquired by the destruction of the Ten-necked demon."

Hearing the words of Bhadra, Rama said:“Without hiding anything, do you relate every thing from the beginning vent to by the citizens. Hearing the good and bad opinions of the citizens I shall desist from bad actions and engage in good ones.

Hearing the words of Bhadra, Rama said:“Without hiding anything, do you relate every thing from the beginning vent to by the citizens. Hearing the good and bad opinions of the citizens I shall desist from bad actions and engage in good ones.

sanskrit: कथयन्ति यथा पौराः पापा जनपदेषु च
transliteration: kathayanti yathā paurāḥ pāpā janapadeṣu ca
english: Whatever citizens say the vicious actions of mine in the city, relate to me confidently and fearlessly.
Hearing the sweet accents of Rama, Bhadra, with a quiescent mind and folded palms, said.
Hear, o king, I shall relate to you all those unpleasant things frequently dwelt upon by people in court-yards, markets, public roads, forests and gardens.
Indeed Rāma has accomplished a wonderfully hard work; our ancestors, the celestials, the Dānavas none heard of constructing a bridge over the ocean?

sanskrit: वानराश्च वशं नीता ऋक्षाश्च सह राक्षसैः
transliteration: vānarāśca vaśaṃ nītā ṛkṣāśca saha rākṣasaiḥ
english: Rāma has slain the irrepressible Rāvana with his army and brought over the monkeys, bears and Rākşasas to his own side.

sanskrit: हत्वा च रावणं सङ्ख्ये सीतामाहृत्य राघवः
transliteration: hatvā ca rāvaṇaṃ saṅkhye sītāmāhṛtya rāghavaḥ
english: Having discomfitted Rāvana, in the encounter Rāma has released Şītā, but not being the least enraged on account of her being touched by Rāvaņa he has brought to her his own city.

sanskrit: रक्षसां वशमापन्नां कथं रामो न कुत्सते
transliteration: rakṣasāṃ vaśamāpannāṃ kathaṃ rāmo na kutsate

sanskrit: यथा हि कुरुते राजा प्रजा तमनुवर्तते
transliteration: yathā hi kurute rājā prajā tamanuvartate

english: O King, the citizens thus talk of many types in every corner of cities and provinces.
Hearings those words of Bhadra, Raghava was greatly sorry and asked his friends “Do the subjects thus talk about me?”

sanskrit: सर्वे तु शिरसा भूमावभिवाद्य प्रणम्य च
transliteration: sarve tu śirasā bhūmāvabhivādya praṇamya ca
english: Thereupon lowering their heads and saluting him they all said to Rāghava, of a depressed mind-“For sooth, the subjects thus talk about.” Thereupon Kakutstha, the slayer of enemies, bearing all those words, dismissed his friends.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु वाक्यं काकुत्स्थः सर्वेषां समुदीरितम्
transliteration: śrutvā tu vākyaṃ kākutsthaḥ sarveṣāṃ samudīritam
english: Thereupon lowering their heads and saluting him they all said to Rāghava, of a depressed mind-“For sooth, the subjects thus talk about.” Thereupon Kakutstha, the slayer of enemies, bearing all those words, dismissed his friends.

sanskrit: विसृज्य तु सुहृद्वर्गं बुद्ध्या निश्चित्य राघवः
transliteration: visṛjya tu suhṛdvargaṃ buddhyā niścitya rāghavaḥ
english: Having sent away his friends and determined what to do, Rāma, the delight of the Råghus, commanded the warder, who was seated hard by, saying.
Do you bring in no time, Lakşmaņa, a son of Sumitrā, gifted with auspicious marks, alongwith great Bharata and the irrepressible Šatrughna.

sanskrit: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः
transliteration: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dvāḥstho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Hearing the words of Rāma and placing his folded palms on his head the warder reached house of Lakşmaņa and unobstructed entered therein.

sanskrit: द्रष्टुमिच्छति राजा त्वां गम्यतां तत्र मा चिरम्
transliteration: draṣṭumicchati rājā tvāṃ gamyatāṃ tatra mā ciram
english: And having saluted him, with folded palms he said to the high-souled Laksmana and:-"The King wishes to behold you-do you soon go there.
Thereupon being apprised of Rāghava's command and saying 'so be it.' Saumitri ascended his car and went speedily towards Rāma's abode.
Having beheld Lakşmana's departure the warder humbly went to Bharata and having blessed him with folded hands said: “The King wishes to see you."
"Do you come, O foremost Raghus, the King wish to behold you.” Lakşmaņa and Bharata are also there.

sanskrit: गतो हि लक्ष्मणः पूर्वं भरतश्च महायशाः
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य शत्रुघ्नः परमासनात्
transliteration: gato hi lakṣmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ bharataśca mahāyaśāḥ
śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya śatrughnaḥ paramāsanāt

sanskrit: शिरसा धरणीं प्राप्य प्रययौ यत्र राघवः
transliteration: śirasā dharaṇīṃ prāpya prayayau yatra rāghavaḥ
english: Thereupon returning, the warder, with folded। hands, communicated to Rama, the arrivals of his brothers.

So long Rāma was engaged poorly in anxious meditation with his crown bent downwards. Informed of the princes' arrival he commanded the warder, “Do you soon bring the princes here. My life depends upon them. They are my dearest life.

sanskrit: एतेषु जीवितं मह्यमेते प्राणाः प्रिया मम
transliteration: eteṣu jīvitaṃ mahyamete prāṇāḥ priyā mama
english: So long Rāma was engaged poorly in anxious meditation with his crown bent downwards. Informed of the princes' arrival he commanded the warder, “Do you soon bring the princes here. My life depends upon them. They are my dearest life.
Having obtained Rāma's command, the princes, clothed in white raiment, entered there, with folded palms and quiescent mind.

sanskrit: ते तु दृष्ट्वा मुखं तस्य सग्रहं शशिनं यथा
transliteration: te tu dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ tasya sagrahaṃ śaśinaṃ yathā
english: Having entered there they saw that Rāma's countenance was shorn of beauty like to the moon possessed by Rāhu, the setting sun and the withered lotus and his eyes were full of tears.

sanskrit: बाष्पपूर्णे च नयने दृष्ट्वा रामस्य धीमतः
हतशोभं यथा पद्मं मुखं वीक्ष्य च तस्य ते
transliteration: bāṣpapūrṇe ca nayane dṛṣṭvā rāmasya dhīmataḥ
hataśobhaṃ yathā padmaṃ mukhaṃ vīkṣya ca tasya te
english: Having entered there they saw that Rāma's countenance was shorn of beauty like to the moon possessed by Rāhu, the setting sun and the withered lotus and his eyes were full of tears.

sanskrit: ततो ऽभिवाद्य त्वरिताः पादौ रामस्य मूर्धभिः
english: Then having approached him quickly, and saluted his feet they all anxiously sat there. Rāma also wiped off his tears.
Thereupon having embraced them with his arms he raised up the princes and pressed them to take their seats. Then he said.

sanskrit: भवन्तो मम सर्वस्वं भवन्तो जीवितं मम
transliteration: bhavanto mama sarvasvaṃ bhavanto jīvitaṃ mama
english: "You are mine all; you constitute my life; O princes, I am governing the kingdom gained by you; you are all learned, pious and intelligent. Do you follow the duties I point out."
"You are mine all; you constitute my life; O princes, I am governing the kingdom gained by you; you are all learned, pious and intelligent. Do you follow the duties I point out."
Rāma, the descendant of Kakutstha having said this, they, with anxiety and attention, awaited the orders of the king.
The princes were all waiting with a poorly heart when Rama, with a dried countenance, addressed them, saying.

sanskrit: सर्वे शृणुत भद्रं वो मा कुरुध्वं मनो ऽन्यथा
पौराणां मम सीतायां यादृशी वर्तते कथा
transliteration: sarve śṛṇuta bhadraṃ vo mā kurudhvaṃ mano 'nyathā
paurāṇāṃ mama sītāyāṃ yādṛśī vartate kathā
english: May good betide you-do not act against my desire. Hear, what the citizens have been talking about me and Sītā.

sanskrit: वर्तते मयि बीभत्सा सा मे मर्माणि कृन्तति
transliteration: vartate mayi bībhatsā sā me marmāṇi kṛntati
english: The citizens as well as the inhabitants of provinces have been showering censures upon me. I have been pierced to the very vitals by those accusations.

sanskrit: अहं किल कुले जात इक्ष्वाकूणां महात्मनाम्
सीता ऽपि सत्कुले जाता जनकानां महात्मनाम्
transliteration: ahaṃ kila kule jāta ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām
english: I have been born in the illustrious family by the high-souled Ikşvākus. Sītā has been born also in the holy family of the great Janaka; gentle Lakṣmaṇa, you know how in the solitary forest of Dandaka, Sītā was stolen away by Rāvana and how have I slain him.

sanskrit: जानासि त्वं यथा सौम्य दण्डके विजने वने
रावणेन हृता सीता स च विध्वंसितो मया
transliteration: jānāsi tvaṃ yathā saumya daṇḍake vijane vane
rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā sa ca vidhvaṃsito mayā
english: I have been born in the illustrious family by the high-souled Ikşvākus. Sītā has been born also in the holy family of the great Janaka; gentle Lakṣmaṇa, you know how in the solitary forest of Dandaka, Sītā was stolen away by Rāvana and how have I slain him.

sanskrit: तत्र मे बुद्धिरुत्पन्ना जनकस्य सुतां प्रति
transliteration: tatra me buddhirutpannā janakasya sutāṃ prati
english: At that time even I was stricken with anxiety regarding Sītā that how I could take her home since she had resided in the house of the Raksasas.

sanskrit: प्रत्ययार्थं ततः सीता विवेश ज्वलनं तदा
transliteration: pratyayārthaṃ tataḥ sītā viveśa jvalanaṃ tadā
english: To secure my confidence, Sītā, in your very presence, entered fire. At that time, O Saumitri, fire, carrying sacrificial oblations and the wind of the sky declared Sītā's innocence before the celestials. in the presence of all the Rşis and gods, the Sun and Moon announced the innocence of the daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: चन्द्रादित्यौ च शंसेते सुराणां सन्निधौ पुरा
transliteration: candrādityau ca śaṃsete surāṇāṃ sannidhau purā

english: Indra, the king of the celestials, himself handed over the chaste Sītā to me in the island of Lanka.

sanskrit: अन्तरात्मा च मे वेत्ति सीतां शुद्धां यशस्विनीम्
transliteration: antarātmā ca me vetti sītāṃ śuddhāṃ yaśasvinīm
english: My mind know Sītā as chaste for ever. So, at that time, I came back to Ayodhya with Sita.

sanskrit: अयं तु मे महान्वादः शोकश्च हृदि वर्तते
transliteration: ayaṃ tu me mahānvādaḥ śokaśca hṛdi vartate
english: But now a great sorrow consequent upon the censure of the citizens and villagers has pierced my heart.
He, who is notorious on this earth and as long as that notoriety remains current, is classed among the vile.
Even the celestials speak ill of bad name whereas fame is adored in all the regions. Therefore the high-souled exert their best to acquire reputations.
O foremost of men, what to speak of the daughter of Janaka-I can even renounce my life and yourselves in fear of a bad name.
Do you therefore perceive into what great abyss of sorrow and ill-fame I have fallen. Up to this time I have never experienced such a mighty grief.
Do you, O Laksmana, next morning, ascending the car driven by Sumantra, take away Sītā to another country.
There is a picturesque hermitage of the highsouled Vālmīki situate on the Tamasā on the other side of the river Gangā.

sanskrit: शीघ्रमागच्छ भद्रं ते कुरुष्व वचनं मम
transliteration: śīghramāgaccha bhadraṃ te kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama
english: Do you, O delight of Raghus, soon come back, leaving behind Sitā in that lonely place. Do you carry out my words. Do you not speak anything regarding Sīta's banishment.

sanskrit: न चास्मिन् प्रतिवक्तव्यः सीतां प्रति कथञ्चन
तस्मात्त्वं गच्छ सौमित्रे नात्र कार्या विचारणा
transliteration: na cāsmin prativaktavyaḥ sītāṃ prati kathañcana
tasmāttvaṃ gaccha saumitre nātra kāryā vicāraṇā

sanskrit: शापिता हि मया यूयं भुजाभ्यां जीवितेन च
transliteration: śāpitā hi mayā yūyaṃ bhujābhyāṃ jīvitena ca

english: For my life and arms, do you not proffer any request to me regarding this. If so, you shall only endanger my well-being and I shall ever regard you as my enemies. If you obey my behest's, do you honour my words now. Do you take away Sītă from here.

sanskrit: मानयन्तु भवन्तो मां यदि मच्छासने स्थिताः
इतो ऽद्य नीयतां सीता कुरुष्व वचनं मम
transliteration: mānayantu bhavanto māṃ yadi macchāsane sthitāḥ
ito 'dya nīyatāṃ sītā kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama
english: For my life and arms, do you not proffer any request to me regarding this. If so, you shall only endanger my well-being and I shall ever regard you as my enemies. If you obey my behest's, do you honour my words now. Do you take away Sītă from here.
Ere this Sītā had communicated her intention of beholding the hermitages of ascetics on the banks of the Gangā. Let that desire of hers be now satisfied.

While saying this, the eyes of the virtuoussouled Rāma were covered with tears. Sighing hard like to an elephant, he, with a heart stricken with grief, departed to his own quarter in the company of his brothers.
The night being over, Lakṣmaṇa, with a poor heart and dried countenance, addressed Sumantra, saying.

O charioteer, do you soon yoke quick coursing steeds to an excellent chariot, and for Sītā place an excellent seat on the car. At the command of the King, I shall take Sītā to the hermitage of the ascetics ever engaged in pious actions. Do you soon bring the chariot here.

O charioteer, do you soon yoke quick coursing steeds to an excellent chariot, and for Sītā place an excellent seat on the car. At the command of the King, I shall take Sītā to the hermitage of the ascetics ever engaged in pious actions. Do you soon bring the chariot here.

Obeying the mandate, and bringing a beautiful and holy car drawn by first-rate steeds and having excellent seats, he said to Saumitri, the enhancer of friends' honour “O lord, here is the chariot ready-do you now satisfy your desire.

sanskrit: रथो ऽयं समनुप्राप्तो यत्कार्यं क्रियतां प्रभो
english: Obeying the mandate, and bringing a beautiful and holy car drawn by first-rate steeds and having excellent seats, he said to Saumitri, the enhancer of friends' honour “O lord, here is the chariot ready-do you now satisfy your desire.
Hearing the words of Sumantra, Laksmana, the foremost of men, approached Sītā in the inner apartment and said.

sanskrit: त्वया किलैष नृपतिर्वरं वै याचितः प्रभुः
transliteration: tvayā kilaiṣa nṛpatirvaraṃ vai yācitaḥ prabhuḥ
english: O queen, you did request the king to show he has now commanded me to take you there. Do you therefore follow me, at the command of the king. I shall, at his behest, take you to the forest where dwell many an ascetic.

sanskrit: शीघ्रं गत्वा तु वैदेहि शासनात्पार्थिवस्य नः
transliteration: śīghraṃ gatvā tu vaidehi śāsanātpārthivasya naḥ
english: O queen, you did request the king to show he has now commanded me to take you there. Do you therefore follow me, at the command of the king. I shall, at his behest, take you to the forest where dwell many an ascetic.
Hearing the words of the high-souled Lakşmaņa, Janaki attained to excessive delight and became anxious to go.

sanskrit: वासांसि च महार्हाणि रत्नानि विविधानि च
transliteration: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: Taking various jewels and costly clothes she said to Lakşmaņa, on the eve of her departure “I shall confer these ornaments, these costly clothes and riches on the female ascetics."

sanskrit: वस्त्राणि च महार्हाणि धनानि विविधानि च
transliteration: vastrāṇi ca mahārhāṇi dhanāni vividhāni ca
english: Taking various jewels and costly clothes she said to Lakşmaņa, on the eve of her departure “I shall confer these ornaments, these costly clothes and riches on the female ascetics."
Saying 'we shall do the same' he made Sītā ascend the car and remembering Rāma's command proceeded, being carried by quickcoursing steeds.
Thereupon Sītā said to Lakşmaņa, the enhancer of prosperity:-:0 descendant of Raghu, I behold many inauspicious omens. My right eye and body are trembling.

sanskrit: औत्सुक्यं परमं चापि अधृतिश्च परा मम
transliteration: autsukyaṃ paramaṃ cāpi adhṛtiśca parā mama

sanskrit: लक्ष्मणो ऽर्थं ततः श्रुत्वा शिरसा वन्द्य मैथिलीम्
transliteration: lakṣmaṇo 'rthaṃ tataḥ śrutvā śirasā vandya maithilīm
english: Saying this Sītā, with folded hands, began to pray to gods. Hearing this Lakşmaņa bowed to her touching the ground with his crown, and though greatly sorry, said as if delighted "All well."

Thereupon having arrived at the hermitage situate on the banks of Gomati Lakşmaņa spent the night there. Thereupon at dawn he rose up and asked the charioteer to get the chariot ready, saying, “Like to the powerful Mahādeva we shall hold the waters of the Bhāgirathi on our head.”

sanskrit: सो ऽश्वान् रज्वाथ चतुरो रथे युङ्क्त्वा मनोजवान्
transliteration: so 'śvān rajvātha caturo rathe yuṅktvā manojavān
english: Thereupon Sumantra yoked the horses, gifted with the fleet course of the mind, to the chariot and with folded hands said to Sītā “Do you ascend the car."

sanskrit: सीता सौमित्रिणा सार्धं सुमन्त्रेण च धीमता
transliteration: sītā saumitriṇā sārdhaṃ sumantreṇa ca dhīmatā
english: According to the request of the intelligent charioteer, Sītā, with Lakşmaņa, ascended that excellent conveyance. In no time the daughter of Janaka, having expansive eyes, arrived at the banks of the Gangā removing all sins.
Reaching the currents of Bhāgirathi before noon Laksmana, on beholding her, cried aloud.

sanskrit: उवाच वाक्यं धर्मज्ञा किमिदं रुद्यते त्वया
transliteration: uvāca vākyaṃ dharmajñā kimidaṃ rudyate tvayā
english: Thereupon beholding Lakşmaņa thus distressed, Sītā, conversant with piety, waxing are anxious said. “Why you weeping, Lakşmaņa? I have reached the banks of Jāhnavī, for which I have so long desired. So this is the time for rejoicing and do not give me pain at this time.

Thereupon beholding Lakşmaņa thus distressed, Sītā, conversant with piety, waxing are anxious said. “Why you weeping, Lakşmaņa? I have reached the banks of Jāhnavī, for which I have so long desired. So this is the time for rejoicing and do not give me pain at this time.
O foremost of men, you do spend your days and nights in the company of Rama. You have left him for two days only, are you sorry for this?

sanskrit: न चाहमेवं शोचामि मैवं त्वं बालिशो भव
transliteration: na cāhamevaṃ śocāmi maivaṃ tvaṃ bāliśo bhava
english: O Lakşmaņa! Rāma is also dearer than my life, but I am not so sorry— do you not be therefore overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: तारयस्व च मां गङ्गां दर्शयस्व च तापसान्
transliteration: tārayasva ca māṃ gaṅgāṃ darśayasva ca tāpasān
english: Do you take me to the other side of the Gangā so that I may behold the ascetics and other confer upon them clothes and ornaments.

sanskrit: तत्र चैकां निशामुष्य यास्यामस्तां पुरीं पुनः
transliteration: tatra caikāṃ niśāmuṣya yāsyāmastāṃ purīṃ punaḥ
english: Having paid them due salutation to the ascetics, and spending a night we shall return to the capital.

sanskrit: त्वरते हि मनो द्रष्टुं रामं रमयतां वरम्
transliteration: tvarate hi mano draṣṭuṃ rāmaṃ ramayatāṃ varam
english: I am also anxious to see Rāma, having eyes like lotus petals, breast like that of a lion and foremost of men.
Hearing the words of Sītā and wiping his beautiful eyes, Laksmana, the slayer of enemies, sent for boatmen. As soon as they were called, with folded hands they said. “The boat is ready."

sanskrit: इयं च सज्जा नौश्चेति दाशाः प्राञ्जलयो ऽब्रुवन्
transliteration: iyaṃ ca sajjā nauśceti dāśāḥ prāñjalayo 'bruvan
english: Hearing the words of Sītā and wiping his beautiful eyes, Laksmana, the slayer of enemies, sent for boatmen. As soon as they were called, with folded hands they said. “The boat is ready."
Having them brought about to cross the holy Ganga Laksmana, with a quiescent mind, took her to the other side.
Having at first conducted Sītā to the spacious and well decorated boat plied by fishermen Laksmana himself got up.
Thereupon he ordered Sumantra to wait there with the chariot, and being beside himself with sorrow ordered the sailors to move on.
Thereupon having reached the other side of Bhāgirathi, Lakşmaņa, with subdued voice and folded palms, said to Sītā.
O daughter of the king of Videha, this has pierced my heart like a dart, that my brother, by making me the instrumental of this action has made me the object of censure in the world.

sanskrit: श्रेयो हि मरणं मे ऽद्य मृत्युर्वा यत्परं भवेत्
transliteration: śreyo hi maraṇaṃ me 'dya mṛtyurvā yatparaṃ bhavet
english: The death and the pain consequent upon it are better than the action I am engaged in.

sanskrit: प्रसीद च न मे पापं कर्तुमर्हसि शोभने
transliteration: prasīda ca na me pāpaṃ kartumarhasi śobhane
english: "Be you propitiated, O beautiful damsel, do not hold me responsible for this.” Saying this, the humble Lakşmaņa began to weep and pray for death. Beholding him thus overwhelmed, Sītā said "What is the matter, Lakşmaņa? I do not understand anything. Do you speak out everything plainly to me. I find you beside yourself (with grief); is it all well with the kingdom? In the name of the king, do you give out to me, the cause of your sorrow."

"Be you propitiated, O beautiful damsel, do not hold me responsible for this.” Saying this, the humble Lakşmaņa began to weep and pray for death. Beholding him thus overwhelmed, Sītā said "What is the matter, Lakşmaņa? I do not understand anything. Do you speak out everything plainly to me. I find you beside yourself (with grief); is it all well with the kingdom? In the name of the king, do you give out to me, the cause of your sorrow."

sanskrit: पश्यामि त्वां न च स्वस्थमपि क्षेमं महीपतेः
transliteration: paśyāmi tvāṃ na ca svasthamapi kṣemaṃ mahīpateḥ
english: "Be you propitiated, O beautiful damsel, do not hold me responsible for this.” Saying this, the humble Lakşmaņa began to weep and pray for death. Beholding him thus overwhelmed, Sītā said "What is the matter, Lakşmaņa? I do not understand anything. Do you speak out everything plainly to me. I find you beside yourself (with grief); is it all well with the kingdom? In the name of the king, do you give out to me, the cause of your sorrow."
Sītā having addressed him thus, Lakşmaņa with a poorly heart and suppressed tone, said thus.

sanskrit: रामः सन्तप्तहृदयो मा निवेद्य गृहं गतः
transliteration: rāmaḥ santaptahṛdayo mā nivedya gṛhaṃ gataḥ
english: O worshipful queen! I have kept within my heart all those words, which the king said, before he entered his palace, rendered sorry and impatient on hearing in the assembly the report of censure regarding you, O daughter of king Janaka. All those words are indeed above description and so I desist.

sanskrit: न तानि वचनीयानि मया देवि तवाग्रतः
transliteration: na tāni vacanīyāni mayā devi tavāgrataḥ

sanskrit: सा त्वं त्यक्ता नृपतिना निर्दोषा मम सन्निधौ
पौरापवादभीतेन ग्राह्यं देवि न ते ऽन्यथा
transliteration: sā tvaṃ tyaktā nṛpatinā nirdoṣā mama sannidhau

sanskrit: आश्रमान्तेषु च मया त्यक्तव्या त्वं भविष्यसि
transliteration: āśramānteṣu ca mayā tyaktavyā tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi

sanskrit: पुण्यं च रमणीयं च मा विषादं कृथाः शुभे
transliteration: puṇyaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ ca mā viṣādaṃ kṛthāḥ śubhe
english: Do not uselessly give vent to sorrow any more. There is the holy and beautiful hermitage of the saints on the banks of Jähnavī. There lives Vālmīki, the foremost of saints, a great friend of our sire Dasaratha. O daughter of Janaka, approaching that high-souled saint, do you spend your days happily keeping Rāma always in your mind.

Do not uselessly give vent to sorrow any more. There is the holy and beautiful hermitage of the saints on the banks of Jähnavī. There lives Vālmīki, the foremost of saints, a great friend of our sire Dasaratha. O daughter of Janaka, approaching that high-souled saint, do you spend your days happily keeping Rāma always in your mind.

sanskrit: श्रेयस्ते परमं देवि तथा कृत्वा भविष्यति
transliteration: śreyaste paramaṃ devi tathā kṛtvā bhaviṣyati
english: Do you satisfy the deities, O chaste damsel. This shall crown you with auspiciousness.
Hearing the ruthless words of Laksmana, the daughter of Janaka, greatly sorry, fell down on earth.
And remaining senseless for some time, Sītā, with her eyes full of tears said to Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: धात्रा यस्यास्तथा मे ऽद्य दुःखमूर्तिः प्रदृश्यते
english: Forsooth, O Laksmana, the great Dispenser has created this body to suffer miseries, and all my affections are manifest in form today.

sanskrit: किं नु पापं कृतं पूर्वं को वा दारैर्वियोजितः
या ऽहं शुद्धसमाचारा त्यक्ता नृपतिना सती
transliteration: kiṃ nu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ ko vā dārairviyojitaḥ
english: Methinks, I committed a mighty iniquity in my pristine existence or brought about me albeit I am pure and chaste.
O son of Sumitrā, the affliction of residing in the forest appeared to me as pleasure ere this for I knew that I would be able to serve Rāma's feet.

sanskrit: सा कथं ह्याश्रमे सौम्य वत्स्यामि विजनीकृता
transliteration: sā kathaṃ hyāśrame saumya vatsyāmi vijanīkṛtā
english: But how shall I, O gentle one, live in the hermitage being divorced from all my kith and kin? and being afflicted to whom shall I express my sorrow?

sanskrit: किं नु वक्ष्यामि मुनिषु कर्म वा सत्कृतं च किम्
transliteration: kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi muniṣu karma vā satkṛtaṃ ca kim
english: What reply shall I offer to the ascetics when they shall ask me "Child, why has the highsouled Rāghava renounced you? What sin have you committed?"
O Saumitri, I shall just renounce my life in the waters of Jāhnavi? But I desist from this for it shall bring about the termination O my husband's race.

sanskrit: यथाज्ञं कुरु सोमित्रे त्यज मां दुःखभागिनीम्
निदेशे स्थीयतां राज्ञः शृणु चेदं वचो मम
transliteration: yathājñaṃ kuru somitre tyaja māṃ duḥkhabhāginīm
nideśe sthīyatāṃ rājñaḥ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: O Saumitri, do you carry out the orders you have received. By renouncing this wretched wight do you satisfy the King's orders. But hear, what I say.

sanskrit: शिरसा ऽ ऽवन्द्य चरणौ कुशलं ब्रूहि पार्थिवम्
english: Without making any distinction, do you, in my name, with folded hands, bow to my mothers-in-law and then ask the well-being of the kingdom.
Thereupon saluting the pious King do you address him, in my name, saying:-You know, O Råghava, that Sitā is pure, ever devoted to you and engaged in your well-being.

sanskrit: जानासि च यथा शुद्धा सीता तत्त्वेन राघव
भक्त्या च परया युक्ता हिता च तव नित्यशः
transliteration: jānāsi ca yathā śuddhā sītā tattvena rāghava
bhaktyā ca parayā yuktā hitā ca tava nityaśaḥ
english: Thereupon saluting the pious King do you address him, in my name, saying:-You know, O Råghava, that Sitā is pure, ever devoted to you and engaged in your well-being.

sanskrit: अहं त्यक्ता त्वया वीर अयशोभीरुणा जने
मया च परिहर्तव्यं त्वं हि मे परमा गतिः
transliteration: ahaṃ tyaktā tvayā vīra ayaśobhīruṇā jane
mayā ca parihartavyaṃ tvaṃ hi me paramā gatiḥ
english: She knows it full well, that afraid of a bad name you have renounced her. It is her duty to put a stop to your ill-name and censure; for you are her excellent refuge.

Do you tell further-more that king established in righteousness to treat the citizens as his brothers, to acquire piety by protecting his subjects duly for this is the greatest mortality and by this may be acquired excellent fame,
Do you, O Lakşmaņa, communicate it in short to Rāma, in my name. Do you go now and behold the signs of pregnancy are manifest in me.

sanskrit: शिरसा ऽ ऽवन्द्य धरणीं व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह
transliteration: śirasā ' 'vandya dharaṇīṃ vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha
english: Sita having said this, Laksmana, with a bewildered heart, saluted her touching the ground which his head. He could not speak more.

sanskrit: प्रदक्षिणं च तां कृत्वा रुदन्नेव महास्वनः
ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं तामाह किं मां वक्ष्यसि शोभने
transliteration: pradakṣiṇaṃ ca tāṃ kṛtvā rudanneva mahāsvanaḥ
dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ tāmāha kiṃ māṃ vakṣyasi śobhane
english: Thereupon bewailing aloud and circumbulating her, he, meditating a little, said. "What are you speaking to me, O worshipful dame?

sanskrit: दृष्टपूर्वं न ते रूपं पादौ दृष्टौ तवानघे
कथमत्र हि पश्यामि रामेण रहितां वने
transliteration: dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ na te rūpaṃ pādau dṛṣṭau tavānaghe
kathamatra hi paśyāmi rāmeṇa rahitāṃ vane
english: O you having no sin, upto this time I have seen any portion of your beautiful person but feet. This is a solitary forest and besides the worshipful Räma, is not present here-under these circumstances how can I cast looks upon you?
Having addressed Sītā in this wise Lakşmaņa again sent for a boat and ascending it ordered the boatman to go.
Thereupon having reached the other side and being beside himself with sorrow and grief he speedily ascended the car.

And casting his looks behind behind while proceeding he espied that Sītā, on the other side of the Gangă, was rowing wildly like one having none to look after her. Looking again and again when Sītā saw that Lakşmaņa and the chariot have gone beyond the range of her vision, she became overwhelmed with anxiety and grief.

And casting his looks behind behind while proceeding he espied that Sītā, on the other side of the Gangă, was rowing wildly like one having none to look after her. Looking again and again when Sītā saw that Lakşmaņa and the chariot have gone beyond the range of her vision, she became overwhelmed with anxiety and grief.

sanskrit: सा दुःखभारावनता यशस्विनी यशोधना नाथमपश्यती सती
रुरोद सा बर्हिणनादिते वने महास्वनं दुःखपरायणा सती
transliteration: sā duḥkhabhārāvanatā yaśasvinī yaśodhanā nāthamapaśyatī satī
ruroda sā barhiṇanādite vane mahāsvanaṃ duḥkhaparāyaṇā satī
english: Being sunk in grief and pressed down with the weight of sorrow on not beholding Rāma, the foremost of the illustrious, the chaste Şītā began to cry aloud in the forest resounded with the notes of peacocks.

sanskrit: सीतां तु रुदतीं दृष्ट्वा ते तत्र मुनिदारकाः
transliteration: sītāṃ tu rudatīṃ dṛṣṭvā te tatra munidārakāḥ
english: Beholding Sītā thus wailing, the sons of the Rşis there speedily approached the great Vālmīki, well-established in asceticism. And saluting him they all communicated to him Sītā's bewailing and said.
Beholding Sītā thus wailing, the sons of the Rşis there speedily approached the great Vālmīki, well-established in asceticism. And saluting him they all communicated to him Sītā's bewailing and said.
O great Rşi, we do not know the wife of what great man, beautiful like the very Lakşmī, and not seen before, is crying aloud very poorly?
It is better that you should see her once. That beautiful damsel, like a goddess failing from heaven being bewildered, is waiting on the banks of the river.
We saw her alone crying aloud being overwhelmed with sorrow and grief as if she had none to look after her. A damsel like her should not be subject to such a condition.

sanskrit: न ह्येनां मानुषीं विद्मः सत्क्रिया ऽस्याः प्रयुज्यताम्
transliteration: na hyenāṃ mānuṣīṃ vidmaḥ satkriyā 'syāḥ prayujyatām

sanskrit: तेषां तु वचनं श्रुत्वा बुद्ध्या निश्चित्य धर्मवित्
transliteration: teṣāṃ tu vacanaṃ śrutvā buddhyā niścitya dharmavit

sanskrit: तं तु देशमभि प्रेत्य किञ्चित्पद्भ्यां महामतिः
transliteration: taṃ tu deśamabhi pretya kiñcitpadbhyāṃ mahāmatiḥ

english: Having gladdened a little the aggrieved Sītā by virtue of his own effulgence of the great ascetic Vālmīki addressed her in following sweet ascents. She did not appear to us to be a woman. Do you receive her duly. She is near the hermitage and so has come to seek your shelter.

sanskrit: स्नुषा दशरथस्य त्वं रामस्य महिषी प्रिया
जनकस्य सुता राज्ञः स्वागतं ते पतिव्रते
transliteration: snuṣā daśarathasya tvaṃ rāmasya mahiṣī priyā
janakasya sutā rājñaḥ svāgataṃ te pativrate
english: O chaste damsel, you at the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha, the beloved wife of Rāma and the daughter of Janaka; your coming here is auspicious. O illustrious Sir, she is on the look out for a protector-do you protect her.” The pious Vālmīki could perceive everything by virtue of his asceticism: and ascertaining the truth of the words of the Rși boys by the power of his understanding, he, with quick steps, approached Sita.

I am apprised, by virtue of asceticism and meditation, of the object of your coming here. O great lady, I am also fully aware that you are by all means chaste. In fact I am conscious of all the incidents in the three worlds. And the disciple followed that high-minded ascetic. Thereupon proceeding a little on foot with Arghya in his hands, the wise Vālmiki reached the banks of the river and saw that Rāghava's spouse was bewailing like a helpless woman.

sanskrit: तव चैव महाभागे विदितं मम तत्त्वतः
सर्वं च विदितं मह्यं त्रैलोक्ये यद्धि वर्तते
transliteration: tava caiva mahābhāge viditaṃ mama tattvataḥ
sarvaṃ ca viditaṃ mahyaṃ trailokye yaddhi vartate
english: I am apprised, by virtue of asceticism and meditation, of the object of your coming here. O great lady, I am also fully aware that you are by all means chaste. In fact I am conscious of all the incidents in the three worlds. And the disciple followed that high-minded ascetic. Thereupon proceeding a little on foot with Arghya in his hands, the wise Vālmiki reached the banks of the river and saw that Rāghava's spouse was bewailing like a helpless woman.

sanskrit: अपापां वेद्मि सीते त्वां तपोलब्धेन चक्षुषा
विस्रब्धा भव वैदेहि साम्प्रतं मयि वर्तसे
transliteration: apāpāṃ vedmi sīte tvāṃ tapolabdhena cakṣuṣā
visrabdhā bhava vaidehi sāmprataṃ mayi vartase
english: By the eyes of asceticism, I perceive, O daughter of Janaka, that you are innocent. You have come under my shelter, O Vaidehi-to be you consoled.

sanskrit: तास्त्वां वत्से यथा वत्सं पालयिष्यन्ति नित्यशः
transliteration: tāstvāṃ vatse yathā vatsaṃ pālayiṣyanti nityaśaḥ
english: O child, the pious ascetics live around my hermitage. They shall daily take care of you as their daughter.

sanskrit: यथा स्वगृहमभ्येत्य विषादं चैव मा कृथाः
transliteration: yathā svagṛhamabhyetya viṣādaṃ caiva mā kṛthāḥ
english: Do you accept this Arghya now, and confiding in me do you remove your grief. Be not sorry for anything; consider that you have come to your own home. Hearing the wonderful words of the great ascetic, Sītā humbly touched his feet and said Your desire shall be fulfilled.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु भाषितं सीता मुनेः परममद्भुतम्
शिरसा ऽ ऽवन्द्य चरणौ तथेत्याह कृताञ्जलिः
transliteration: śrutvā tu bhāṣitaṃ sītā muneḥ paramamadbhutam
english: Do you accept this Arghya now, and confiding in me do you remove your grief. Be not sorry for anything; consider that you have come to your own home. Hearing the wonderful words of the great ascetic, Sītā humbly touched his feet and said Your desire shall be fulfilled.

sanskrit: तं प्रयान्तं मुनिं सीता प्राञ्जलिः पृष्ठतो ऽन्वगात्
transliteration: taṃ prayāntaṃ muniṃ sītā prāñjaliḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt
english: Saying this, She with folded hands, followed the ascetic. Beholding the great ascetic and Sītā approach, the wives, of the Rsis, delighted neared them and said. “Do you come, O foremost of Rșis, you have arrived here after a long time. We all bow to you-do you order what we shall do."

Saying this, She with folded hands, followed the ascetic. Beholding the great ascetic and Sītā approach, the wives, of the Rsis, delighted neared them and said. “Do you come, O foremost of Rșis, you have arrived here after a long time. We all bow to you-do you order what we shall do."

sanskrit: स्वागतं ते मुनिश्रेष्ठ चिरस्यागमनं च ते
अभिवादयामस्त्वां सर्वा उच्यतां कि च कुर्महे
transliteration: svāgataṃ te muniśreṣṭha cirasyāgamanaṃ ca te
abhivādayāmastvāṃ sarvā ucyatāṃ ki ca kurmahe

english: Hearing their words the great Vālmīki replied in worthy accents-"This Sītā is the wife of the intelligent Rāma, the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha and the daughter of Janaka. She has now come to our hermitage. She is chaste and innocent, still her husband has renounced her. So we should all protect her.

sanskrit: अपापा पतिना त्यक्ता परिपाल्या मया सदा
transliteration: apāpā patinā tyaktā paripālyā mayā sadā
english: Hearing their words the great Vālmīki replied in worthy accents-"This Sītā is the wife of the intelligent Rāma, the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha and the daughter of Janaka. She has now come to our hermitage. She is chaste and innocent, still her husband has renounced her. So we should all protect her.

sanskrit: इमां भवन्त्यः(?) पश्यन्तु स्नेहेन परमेण हि
गौरवान्मम वाक्याच्च पूज्या वो ऽस्तु विशेषतः
transliteration: imāṃ bhavantyaḥ(?) paśyantu snehena parameṇa hi
english: She is worthy of your reverence specially while such is order of mine-your preceptor. So. do you all, take care of her with great affection.
Having consigned the charge of Sītā to the hands of the female ascetics, the great and illustrious ascetic Vālmīki, followed by his disciples, speedily proceeded towards his holy hermitage.
Beholding the great ascetic Vālmīki thus conducting Sītā into his own hermitage Lakş mana's heart was bewildered with grief.
Thereupon he said to the expert charioteer Sumantra. Do you perceive Rāma's grief consequent upon the separation from Sītā.

sanskrit: ततो दुःखतरं किं नु राघवस्य भविष्यति
transliteration: tato duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ nu rāghavasya bhaviṣyati
english: His spouse-the daughter of Janaka, is perfectly pure; what can be more painful than that Rāma is living alone having renounced her?

sanskrit: व्यक्तं दैवादहं मन्ये राघवस्य विना भवम्
वैदेह्या सारथे नित्यं दैवं हि दुरतिक्रमम्
transliteration: vyaktaṃ daivādahaṃ manye rāghavasya vinā bhavam
vaidehyā sārathe nityaṃ daivaṃ hi duratikramam
english: It is clear to me, O Sumantra, that this separation of Rāma, has been brought about by the influence of destiny-for it is hard to get over accident.
Even that Rāma, who, when enraged, is capable of slaying the celestials, Gandharvas, Asuras and Rākşasas, has been engaged in the worship of destiny.

sanskrit: उषित्वा नव वर्षाणि पञ्च चैव महावने
transliteration: uṣitvā nava varṣāṇi pañca caiva mahāvane
english: Formerly did Rāma go through miserics, residing in the forest of Dandaka, at the command of his sire for fourteen years.

sanskrit: पौराणां वचनं श्रुत्वा नृशंसं प्रतिभाति मे
transliteration: paurāṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā nṛśaṃsaṃ pratibhāti me
english: But this banishment of Sītā appears to me as exceedingly painful and most ruthless. O charioteer, the opinion of the citizens is by no means just; consequently what shall we gain by performing such a bad action for fame as the exile of Sita?

But this banishment of Sītā appears to me as exceedingly painful and most ruthless. O charioteer, the opinion of the citizens is by no means just; consequently what shall we gain by performing such a bad action for fame as the exile of Sita?
Hearing those words of Lakşmaņa of various types, the wise Sumantra reverentially replied.

sanskrit: न सन्तापस्त्वया कार्यः सौमित्रे मैथिलीं प्रति
transliteration: na santāpastvayā kāryaḥ saumitre maithilīṃ prati
english: Be not aggrieved for Sītā, O Saumitri Formerly in the presence of your sire the Brāhmaṇas related this account of Sītā's exile.

sanskrit: भविष्यति दृढं रामो दुःखप्रायो ऽपि सौख्यभाक्
english: Rāma shall be deprived of all happiness and be separated from his dear wife; what more, the virtuous-souled Rāma, having long arms, shall, under the influence of time, renounce you, Sītā, Śatrughna and Bharata.

Rāma shall be deprived of all happiness and be separated from his dear wife; what more, the virtuous-souled Rāma, having long arms, shall, under the influence of time, renounce you, Sītā, Śatrughna and Bharata.

sanskrit: इदं त्वयि न वक्तव्यं सौमित्रे भरते ऽपि वा
राज्ञा वो व्याहृतं वाक्यं दुर्वासा यदुवाच ह
transliteration: idaṃ tvayi na vaktavyaṃ saumitre bharate 'pi vā
rājñā vo vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ durvāsā yaduvāca ha
english: O Lakṣmaṇa, when Durvāsa was addressed by the king Dasaratha as to your future he replied in the above way. I have told you the same. Do you not communicate this to Śatrughna Bharata or any body. O foremost of men, Durbasa said this to Daſaratha before me, Vaşistha and other great men.

sanskrit: ऋषिणा व्याहृतं वाक्यं वसिष्ठस्य च सन्निधौ
transliteration: ṛṣiṇā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ vasiṣṭhasya ca sannidhau
english: O Lakṣmaṇa, when Durvāsa was addressed by the king Dasaratha as to your future he replied in the above way. I have told you the same. Do you not communicate this to Śatrughna Bharata or any body. O foremost of men, Durbasa said this to Daſaratha before me, Vaşistha and other great men.

sanskrit: सूत न क्वचिदेवं ते वक्तव्यं जनसन्निधौ
transliteration: sūta na kvacidevaṃ te vaktavyaṃ janasannidhau
english: Hearing the words of Rsi, Dasaratha, the foremost of men, said to me, "O charioteer, do not reveal this secret to any body.

sanskrit: नैव जात्वनृतं कार्यमिति मे सौम्य दर्शनम्
transliteration: naiva jātvanṛtaṃ kāryamiti me saumya darśanam
english: O gentle one, it is not proper by any means to falsify the words of the king Dasaratha. I shall always, very carefully, carry out his orders. It is not proper to reveal this mystery before you. Still I do so for your curiosity has been greatly excited.

sanskrit: सर्वथैव न वक्तव्यं मया सौम्य तवाग्रतः
यदि ते श्रवणे श्रद्धा श्रूयतां रघुनन्दन
transliteration: sarvathaiva na vaktavyaṃ mayā saumya tavāgrataḥ
yadi te śravaṇe śraddhā śrūyatāṃ raghunandana
english: O gentle one, it is not proper by any means to falsify the words of the king Dasaratha. I shall always, very carefully, carry out his orders. It is not proper to reveal this mystery before you. Still I do so for your curiosity has been greatly excited.

Tough this mystery was communicated formerly by the king Dasaratha and though it is not proper to reveal it to any body, still I express it before you that you may not, on hearing it, be worked up with sorrow; for destiny is hard to be got over. And it is by the influence of that destiny that you have met with such a sorrow and grief. However, do you not reveal this secret to Satrughna and Bharata.

sanskrit: न त्वया भरते वाच्यं शत्रुघ्नस्यापि सन्निधौ
transliteration: na tvayā bharate vācyaṃ śatrughnasyāpi sannidhau
english: Tough this mystery was communicated formerly by the king Dasaratha and though it is not proper to reveal it to any body, still I express it before you that you may not, on hearing it, be worked up with sorrow; for destiny is hard to be got over. And it is by the influence of that destiny that you have met with such a sorrow and grief. However, do you not reveal this secret to Satrughna and Bharata.
Hearing these grave and important words of Sumantra, Laksmana ordered him to relate.
Being thus requested by the high-souled Laks maņa, Sumantra began to reveal the mystery of Durbasa's account.

sanskrit: पुरा नाम्ना हि दुर्वासा अत्रेः पुत्रो महामुनिः
transliteration: purā nāmnā hi durvāsā atreḥ putro mahāmuniḥ
english: In the days of yore the great ascetic Durbāsā, the son of Atri, resided for a year in the holy hermitage of Vasiştha.
At that time your sire, the highly effulgent and illustrious Dasaratha, with a view to see his high-souled priest Vasistha, repaired there.
He saw the great ascetic Durbásā, burning like the sun in his effulgence, seated on the right hand side of Vasiștha. Thereupon he humbly saluted those two leading ascetics.

sanskrit: स ताभ्यां पूजितो राजा स्वागतेनासनेन च ॥
transliteration: sa tābhyāṃ pūjito rājā svāgatenāsanena ca
english: And they too, welcoming him, received him duly with seat, water to wash feet, Arghya, fruits and roots, Then he lived there in the company of the ascetics.
And they too, welcoming him, received him duly with seat, water to wash feet, Arghya, fruits and roots, Then he lived there in the company of the ascetics.
Thereupon during the noon, all those ascetics, seated there, began to dwell upon various pleasant topics.
During an interval Dasaratha, with folded hands and uplifted arms, said to the high-souled son of Atri-Durbāsā, having asceticism for his wealth.

sanskrit: किमायुश्च हि मे रामः पुत्राश्चान्ये किमायुषः
transliteration: kimāyuśca hi me rāmaḥ putrāścānye kimāyuṣaḥ
english: O illustrious Sir, how long shall my family remain in existence? What is the extent of the lease of life granted to Rāma and my other sons?

sanskrit: रामस्य च सुता ये स्युस्तेषामायुः कियद्भवेत्
transliteration: rāmasya ca sutā ye syusteṣāmāyuḥ kiyadbhavet
english: How long shall the descendants of Rāma live? And what shall be the end of my race? Do you relate all this to me.

sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा व्याहृतं वाक्यं राज्ञो दशरथस्य च
transliteration: tacchrutvā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ rājño daśarathasya ca
english: Hearing the words of the king Dasaratha the highly effulgent Durbāsā replied.

Hear, the early history, O king. During the encounter between the celestials and Asuras, the demons, ,, being remonstrated with by the celestials sought shelter of the wife of Bhrguyour priest. Bhrgu's wife having promised them help they lived there fearlessly.

Hear, the early history, O king. During the encounter between the celestials and Asuras, the demons, ,, being remonstrated with by the celestials sought shelter of the wife of Bhrguyour priest. Bhrgu's wife having promised them help they lived there fearlessly.
Having beheld the demons thus helped by Bhrgu's wife, Hari, the king of celestials, enraged, chopped off her head with his sharp discuss.
And angry on beholding his wife slain, Bhrgu, imprecated a curse on Vişņu, the slayer of enemies' race, saying.

Being beside yourself with anger you have slain my wife, not worthy of being killed; therefore, O Janārddana, you shall be born in the region of mortals. And there you shall remain separated from your spouse for many long years.

Being beside yourself with anger you have slain my wife, not worthy of being killed; therefore, O Janārddana, you shall be born in the region of mortals. And there you shall remain separated from your spouse for many long years.

sanskrit: अर्चयामास तं देवं भृगुः शापेन पीडितः
लोकानां संहितार्थं तु तं शापं ग्राह्यमुक्तवान्
transliteration: arcayāmāsa taṃ devaṃ bhṛguḥ śāpena pīḍitaḥ
lokānāṃ saṃhitārthaṃ tu taṃ śāpaṃ grāhyamuktavān
english: Having imprecated this curse, Bhțgu was greatly pained and being propitiated by his adoration, Visnu, fond of disciples, said. “Having slain Rāvaņa and others, I shall be, for the behoof of . mankind, subject to this imprecation."
O bestower of kings, the highly effulgent Vişnu, thus imprecated by Bhrgu in the days of yore, has been born as your son in this birth and has been celebrated under the appellation of Rama.
All his followers shall be happy and prosperous. Having reigned for eleven thousand years Rāma shall repair to the region of Brahmă.
None shall be able to vanquish him. He shall celebrate many a horse-sacrifice with profuse gifts and shall establish many royal families.

sanskrit: द्वौ पुत्रौ तु भविष्येते सीतायां राघवस्य तु
transliteration: dvau putrau tu bhaviṣyete sītāyāṃ rāghavasya tu
english: He shall beget on Sită two sorts. Having thus related to Dasaratha the past and future of his family the highly effulgent great ascetic Durbāsā became silent.
According to the words of Rși Rāma shall install two sons of Sītā in Ayodhyā, not anywhere else.
He shall beget on Sită two sorts. Having thus related to Dasaratha the past and future of his family the highly effulgent great ascetic Durbāsā became silent.
He being silent-the great king Dasaratha, having bowed to the two high-souled ascetics, again returned to his city Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: एतद्वचो मया तत्र मुनिना व्याहृतं पुरा
श्रुतं हृदि च निक्षिप्तं नान्यथा तद्भविष्यति
transliteration: etadvaco mayā tatra muninā vyāhṛtaṃ purā
śrutaṃ hṛdi ca nikṣiptaṃ nānyathā tadbhaviṣyati
english: I had heard there all there words of the great ascetic Durbāså. Up to this time they are lying in my heart. Rsis' words shall never prove fruitless.

sanskrit: एवं गते न सन्तापं कर्तुमर्हसि राघव
सीतार्थे राघवार्थे वा दृढो भव नरोत्तम
transliteration: evaṃ gate na santāpaṃ kartumarhasi rāghava
sītārthe rāghavārthe vā dṛḍho bhava narottama
english: Under these circumstances, O Laksmana, you should not grieve for Sītā or Rāma; in their interest do you become patient.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु व्याहृतं वाक्यं सूतस्य परमाद्भुतम्
transliteration: śrutvā tu vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ sūtasya paramādbhutam
english: Hearing those wondrous words of the charioteer Sumantra, Lakşmaņa became greatly happy and eulogised him again and again?
They thus conversing with one another on their way back, the sun set. They accordingly spent that night on the banks of Kesini.

Having spent the night on the banks of Kesini, the mighty car-warrior Lakşmaņa, got up early in the morning and again proceeded on his journey (home) and reached in the noon the city of Ayodhyā filled with various jewels and delighted and plump citizens.

Having spent the night on the banks of Kesini, the mighty car-warrior Lakşmaņa, got up early in the morning and again proceeded on his journey (home) and reached in the noon the city of Ayodhyā filled with various jewels and delighted and plump citizens.
But the high-souled Lakşmaņa became greatly sorry stricken with the thought as to what he should relate on approaching the feet of Rāma.
While proceeding with this thought he saw the highly picturesque palace of Rāma resembling the rays of the moon.
Having descended from his car at the palacegate, Laksmana, the foremost of men, with his face down wards and a distressed heart, unobstructed, entered the palace.

Having entered there he saw his elder brother Rāma seated poorly on an excellent seat with his eyes full of tears. Being greatly pained at the sight, Saumitri touched his feet and with folded palms said.

Having entered there he saw his elder brother Rāma seated poorly on an excellent seat with his eyes full of tears. Being greatly pained at the sight, Saumitri touched his feet and with folded palms said.

O worshipful sir, having obeyed your behest's I have left the daughter of Janaka at the holy hermitage of Vālmiki near the banks of the Gangā. Having left that illustrious pure lady at the skirt of the hermitage. I have again come to serve your feet

O worshipful sir, having obeyed your behest's I have left the daughter of Janaka at the holy hermitage of Vālmiki near the banks of the Gangā. Having left that illustrious pure lady at the skirt of the hermitage. I have again come to serve your feet

sanskrit: त्वद्विधा न हि शोचन्ति बुद्धिमन्तो मनस्विनः
transliteration: tvadvidhā na hi śocanti buddhimanto manasvinaḥ
english: Do you not grieve, O foremost of men, for such is the cause of time. The intelligent people like you do not grieve.
When there is grow there is decay, where there is prosperity there is ruin, and where there is birth there is death.

sanskrit: तस्मात्पुत्रेषु दारेषु मित्रेषु च धनेषु च
transliteration: tasmātputreṣu dāreṣu mitreṣu ca dhaneṣu ca
english: Therefore attachment to wife, sons, friends and riches is not proper, for surely shall be brought about separation with them.

sanskrit: शक्तस्त्वमात्मना ऽ ऽत्मानं विनेतुं मनसैव हि
english: O Kakutstha, While you can control yourself and your mind, should you not be able to bear this trifling pain of separation? Leading men like yourself are never overwhelmed by all these things.

sanskrit: अपवादः स किल ते पुनरेष्यति राघव
transliteration: apavādaḥ sa kila te punareṣyati rāghava

sanskrit: सो ऽपवादः पुरे राजन्भविष्यति न संशयः
english: O Rāghava, you shall again be blamed by the people. In fear of this calumny, O king, that you have renounced Maithili. And if do you grieve for that spouse your calumny shall undoubtedly be deep-routed in the kingdom.

sanskrit: त्यजैनां दुर्बलां बुद्धिं सन्तापं मा कुरुष्व ह
transliteration: tyajaināṃ durbalāṃ buddhiṃ santāpaṃ mā kuruṣva ha
english: Therefore do you restore yourself patiently, O foremost of men. Do you give up this weakness and or not sorry.
The intelligent Lakşmaņa, the son of Sumitrā, having said this, Rāma, the descendant of Käkutstha and fond of friends, with great delight said.
You have spoken the truth, O Laksmana, O foremost of men. I have been greatly delighted, O hero for your carrying out my orders.
O gentle Saumitrī, my grief and sorrow have been removed for those pleasant words of yours.
Hearing those wondrous words of Lakşmaņa Rāma was greatly delighted and said.
O you having an auspicious look, you are gifted with great intellect and after my heart; a friend like you is rare at such a time.

sanskrit: तन्निशामय च श्रुत्वा कुरुष्व वचनं मम
transliteration: tanniśāmaya ca śrutvā kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama
english: But O beautiful Saumitrī, do you, apprised of my intention, carry out my words.

sanskrit: चत्वारो दिवसाः सौम्य कार्यं पौरजनस्य वै
transliteration: catvāro divasāḥ saumya kāryaṃ paurajanasya vai
english: O gentle son of Sumitrā, for not looking to state business for these days I have been pierced to the very vitals.
Do you therefore call here men, or women, priests or councillors who have come for business.

sanskrit: पौरकार्याणि यो राजा न करोति दिने दिने
संवृते नरके घोरे पतितो नात्र संशयः
transliteration: paurakāryāṇi yo rājā na karoti dine dine
saṃvṛte narake ghore patito nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: For sooth do a king falls into the dreadful bell where the wind does not blow, who does not daily look into his state affairs.

sanskrit: श्रूयते हि पुरा राजा नृगो नाम महायशाः
transliteration: śrūyate hi purā rājā nṛgo nāma mahāyaśāḥ
english: I have heard, O foremost of men, that there lived in the days of yore a highly illustrious, truthful and pure-minded king, ever devoted to the Brahmanas, by the name Nrga.
Once on a time at the sacred pilgrimage of Puşpaka that king conferred upon the Brāhmaṇas one Koți of kine with calves adorned with golden ornaments.

sanskrit: ततः सङ्गाद्गता धेनुः सवत्सा स्पर्शिता ऽनघ
english: Accidentally on that occasion, a cow with calf belonging to a poor Brāhmaṇa, living upon law means, was given away along with other kine.

sanskrit: स नष्टां गां क्षुधार्तो वै अन्विषंस्तत्र तत्र च
transliteration: sa naṣṭāṃ gāṃ kṣudhārto vai anviṣaṃstatra tatra ca
english: Undergoing hunger and thirst, the master of that cow travelled for a long time in many places in search of it.

sanskrit: ददर्श गां स्वकां धेनुं ब्राह्मणस्य निवेशने
transliteration: dadarśa gāṃ svakāṃ dhenuṃ brāhmaṇasya niveśane
english: Thereupon having reached the province of Kanakhala he espied his own cow in the house of a Brāhmaṇa. The cow was well kept and the young one was grown up.

sanskrit: अथ तां नामधेयेन स्वकेनोवाच स द्विजः
आगच्छ शबलेत्येवं सा तु शुश्राव गौः स्वरम्
transliteration: atha tāṃ nāmadheyena svakenovāca sa dvijaḥ
āgaccha śabaletyevaṃ sā tu śuśrāva gauḥ svaram
english: Thereupon the Brāhmaṇa called the cow by the name given by him saying “Sabalā, come."

sanskrit: तस्य तं स्वरमाज्ञाय क्षुधार्तस्य द्विजस्य वै
transliteration: tasya taṃ svaramājñāya kṣudhārtasya dvijasya vai
english: The cow heard that and recognising the voice of the Brāhmaṇa followed him. And he preceded her burning like fire.

sanskrit: यो ऽपि पालयते विप्रः सो ऽपि गामन्वगाद्द्रुतम्
english: And the Brāhmaṇa, in whose house the cow so long remained, speedily pursued her and approaching the ascetic said. “This cow is mine. The king Nrga conferred this upon me.”

sanskrit: स्पर्शिता राजसिंहेन मम दत्ता नृगेण ह
transliteration: sparśitā rājasiṃhena mama dattā nṛgeṇa ha

sanskrit: ऊचतुश्च महात्मानौ तावुभौ द्विजसत्तमौ ॥क्रुद्धौ परमसम्प्राप्तौ वाक्यं घोराभिसंहितम्
transliteration: ūcatuśca mahātmānau tāvubhau dvijasattamau kruddhau paramasamprāptau vākyaṃ ghorābhisaṃhitam

english: And though they waited for a long time at the gate they did not obtain permission to enter the palace. Thereat both of them were greatly enraged and imprecated dreadful curses, saying Since you have not granted us an interview though we have been waiting here for a long time, you shall, by our curse, remain invisible, being a lizard. You shall in this state live in a den for many hundred and thousand years.

sanskrit: श्वभ्रे ऽस्मिन् कृकलासो वै दीर्घकालं वसिष्यसि

english: When Vişņu assuming a human person shall be born in the Vasudeva family of Yādavas and enhance their glory he shall liberate you from the curse. Immediately before the advent of the Kali Yuga the Rși Nara Nārāyaṇa gifted with great prowess shall descend upon earth to relieve her of the burden.

sanskrit: कृता च तेन कालेन निष्कृतिस्ते भविष्यति
transliteration: kṛtā ca tena kālena niṣkṛtiste bhaviṣyati

sanskrit: तां गां हि दुर्बलां वृद्धां ददतुर्ब्राह्मणाय वै
transliteration: tāṃ gāṃ hi durbalāṃ vṛddhāṃ dadaturbrāhmaṇāya vai
english: Having thus imprecated the curse upon the king the Rșis became silent. The cow was old and weak so they both, with mutual consent, conferred that upon another Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: एवं स राजा तं शापमुपभुङ्क्ते सुदारुणम्
transliteration: evaṃ sa rājā taṃ śāpamupabhuṅkte sudāruṇam
english: O Lakşmaņa, the king Nțga is still suffering from that dreadful curse. It is the king's folly that is manifest from the mutual disagreement of the workers. Do you bring them all speedily to me who have come for business. For, sooth shall the kings profit by the just administration. Do you therefore go in person, O Lakşmaņa and see who has come for business.

sanskrit: कार्यार्थिनां विमर्दो हि राज्ञां दोषाय कल्पते
transliteration: kāryārthināṃ vimardo hi rājñāṃ doṣāya kalpate
english: O Lakşmaņa, the king Nțga is still suffering from that dreadful curse. It is the king's folly that is manifest from the mutual disagreement of the workers. Do you bring them all speedily to me who have come for business. For, sooth shall the kings profit by the just administration. Do you therefore go in person, O Lakşmaņa and see who has come for business.

sanskrit: सुकृतस्य हि कार्यस्य फलं नापैति पार्थिवः
transliteration: sukṛtasya hi kāryasya phalaṃ nāpaiti pārthivaḥ
english: O Lakşmaņa, the king Nțga is still suffering from that dreadful curse. It is the king's folly that is manifest from the mutual disagreement of the workers. Do you bring them all speedily to me who have come for business. For, sooth shall the kings profit by the just administration. Do you therefore go in person, O Lakşmaņa and see who has come for business.
Hearing the words of the highly effulgent Rama, Laksmana, conversant with discriminative knowledge, replied with folded hands, saying.
"O Kakutstha, it is for a very simple folly that the two Brāhmaṇas imprecated that curse upon the king Nrga, dreadful as the rod of Yama.
May I ask you, O foremost of men, what did that king say to the Brāhmaṇas when he saw thus imprecated?

sanskrit: शृणु सौम्य यथा पूर्वं स राजा शापविक्षतः
transliteration: śṛṇu saumya yathā pūrvaṃ sa rājā śāpavikṣataḥ
english: Where to Rāma replied saying:-O gentle one, hear, what the king Nrga said when imprecated.

sanskrit: अथाध्वनि गतौ विप्रौ विज्ञाय स नृगस्तदा
transliteration: athādhvani gatau viprau vijñāya sa nṛgastadā
english: Hearing of the departure of the Brāhmaṇas he sent for his priest, minister, the citizens and subjects and filled with sorrow said: "Do you all hear attentively my words.

Having imprecated a dreadful curse upon me the jolly saint Nārada and the ascetic Parvata have speedily, like the wind, repaired to the region of Brahmă.

sanskrit: कुमारो ऽयं वसुर्नाम स देवो ऽद्याभिषिच्यताम्
english: Do you therefore even today, place the prince Vasu on the throne, and let the architects prepare ap leasant den for me.

Living therein I shall waste the curse of the Brāhmaṇas. Let the architects dog one den to protect me against the rains, one against the affliction of the winter and one against the distresses of summer.

sanskrit: फलवन्तश्च ये वृक्षाः पुष्पवत्यश्च या लताः
transliteration: phalavantaśca ye vṛkṣāḥ puṣpavatyaśca yā latāḥ
english: Let them enhance the picturesqueness of those dens by planting many trees having profuse branches and fruits and flowers. As long as time shall not change so long I shall spend my days happily in the den. For a half league on all sides around me let flower trees be planted.

parivārya yathā me syuradhyardhaṃ yojanaṃ tathā

transliteration: evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānaṃ sa sandideśa vasaṃ tadā
english: Having made those arrangements and placed Vasu on the throne the king Nļga said:-“Do not leave the path of morality, O my son, and do you duly govern the subjects according to the custom of the Ksatriyas.

sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षं ते यथा शापो द्विजाभ्यां मयि पातितः
transliteration: pratyakṣaṃ te yathā śāpo dvijābhyāṃ mayi pātitaḥ
english: You have seen, with your own eyes, the curse that the Brāhmaṇas have given me being enraged for a very trifling folly of mine.
Do you not repent for me. My son, time is the lord of happiness and sorrow; it is by the influence of time that I have fallen into such a disaster.

sanskrit: लब्धव्यान्येव लभते दुःखानि च सुखानि च
transliteration: labdhavyānyeva labhate duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca
english: Creatures must meet with what is kept in store by destiny; they must go where they are bound for and they must acquire what is set apart for them. Pristine actions are the root of all these; so, be not sorry, O my son.

sanskrit: पूर्वे जात्यन्तरे वत्स मा विषादं कुरुष्व ह
transliteration: pūrve jātyantare vatsa mā viṣādaṃ kuruṣva ha
english: Creatures must meet with what is kept in store by destiny; they must go where they are bound for and they must acquire what is set apart for them. Pristine actions are the root of all these; so, be not sorry, O my son.
O foremost of men, having given this advice to his son, the highly illustrious king Nțga proceeded to live in the sweet fragrant den.

sanskrit: एवं प्रविश्यैव नृपस्तदानीं श्वभ्रं महारत्नविभूषितं तत्
सम्पादयामास तदा महात्मा शापं द्विजाभ्यां हि रुषा विमुक्तम्

sampādayāmāsa tadā mahātmā śāpaṃ dvijābhyāṃ hi ruṣā vimuktam
english: Having entered the den filled with many jewels the high-souled king began to spend his days in the satisfaction of the curse imprecated by the two Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: एष ते नृगशापस्य विस्तरो ऽभिहितो मया
english: I Have thus given to you an account of the curse imprecated on Nțga. Listen, if do you wish to hear of any other theme.
Råma having said this Lakşmaņa replied: “I am not satiated with the account of those wonderful stories, oking."
Hearing the reply of Laksmana, Rama, the descendant of Ikşvāku, began again with themes instinct with morality.

sanskrit: पुत्रो द्वादशमो वीर्ये धर्मे च परिनिष्ठितः
transliteration: putro dvādaśamo vīrye dharme ca pariniṣṭhitaḥ
english: There lived a highly pious and powerful king by the name of Nimi. He was twelfth of Ikş vāku's sons.
That powerful king made a picturesque city like that of the celestials near the hermitage of Gautama.
The name of that beautiful city was Vaijayanta and the highly illustrious royal saint used to live there.
Having thus reared a highly picturesque city he thought of worshipping the deity by celebrating a sacrifice for the satisfaction of his sire.

sanskrit: ततः पितरमामन्त्र्य इक्ष्वाकुं हि मनोः सुतम्
transliteration: tataḥ pitaramāmantrya ikṣvākuṃ hi manoḥ sutam
english: Having thus resolved and invited his sire Ikşvāku the son of Manu, he first welcomed the celestial saint. Nimi, the descendant of Ikşvāku, then welcomed the saints Atri, Angiras and Bhrgu having asceticism for their wealth.

Thereupon Vasiştha said to Nimi, the foremost of royal_saints-"I have already been engaged by Indra. Do you therefore wait as long as his sacrifice is not finished there."
After the departure of Vasiştha the great Gautama engaged in the satisfaction of Vasist ha's duties. And the high-souled Vasistha too engaged in Indra's sacrifice.
On the other hand having united all the Brāhmaṇas the great king began to celebrate the sacrifice extending over five thousand years near his city by the side of the Himālaya.
Finding Gautama engaged in his room he was exceedingly enraged. Thereupon he waited there for some time to see the King. On that day the royal saint Nimi was deeply asleep.
Finding Gautama engaged in his room he was exceedingly enraged. Thereupon he waited there for some time to see the King. On that day the royal saint Nimi was deeply asleep.
And not beholding the King the high-souled Vasiştha was greatly angry and said.
Since you have, O king, engaged another neglecting me, your body shall remain senseless.
Thereupon hearing the curse of Vasiştha, the king got up. There beside himself with ire he said.
I was unconscious in sleep-— still soiled with anger you have hurled the fiery curse against me like the second rod of Yama.
Therefore, O ascetic, your person shall remain senseless for a long time.
That king and the ascetic having thus imprecated one another under the influence of anger, they immediately were deprived of their bodies.
Hearing the words of the effulgent Rāma, Lakşmaņa, the slayer of enemies, said with folded hands.
Having thus cast off their bodies how did that Brāhmaṇa worshipped of the celestial and the king regain them?
Having been thus accosted by Lakşmaņa, Rāma, the descendant of Ikşvākus and the foremost of men, replied.
Having renounced their persons both Nimi and the pious Vasiştha, having asceticism for their wealth, were metamorphosed into air.
Thereupon being thus deprived of his body like the highly effulgent and great ascetic Vasiştha went to the Patriarch Brahmā with the object of acquiring from his another.

sanskrit: सो ऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ देवदेवस्य धर्मवित्
english: Being merged in the air, he, conversant with religion, bowed to his father and said.
O illustrious god of gods! O you lotus-sprung! by the imprecation of Nimi I have been now deprived of my body and been converted into air.
O lord, the state of being bodiless is highly painful to all. The bodiless cannot perform any work; do you, therefore, by the favour, grant me another body.

sanskrit: धर्मेण महता युक्तः पुनरेष्यसि मे वशम्
transliteration: dharmeṇa mahatā yuktaḥ punareṣyasi me vaśam
english: Whereto the self-sprung Brahma, of unmitigated prowess, replied. O great one, do you enter into the vital energy of Mitra and Varuņa; and even then, O foremost of twiceborn ones, you shall not be born of a woman and being greatly pious shall attain to the rank of a patriarch.
The Patriarch Brahma having said this, Vasishtha, saluting and circumbulating him, repaired to the region of Varuņa.
At that time Mitra in conjunction with Varuņa was reigning in Varuna's kingdom being worshipped by all celestials.
Meanwhile encircled by her mates the leading Apsarā Urvasi by name arrived there at her pleasure.
Beholding the frolicsome and beautiful Urvasi, Varuna attained to an excess of delight.
Thereupon he expressed his intention of living with that queen of Apsarās, having a moon-like countenance and lotus-eyes.

sanskrit: प्रत्युवाच ततः सा तु वरुणं प्राञ्जलिः स्थिता
transliteration: pratyuvāca tataḥ sā tu varuṇaṃ prāñjaliḥ sthitā
english: Thereat Urvasi, with folded hands, said-0 lord of celestials, Mitra himself has already invited me for the same.
Being stricken by the bow of Kupid, Varuņa said to Urvasī I shall discharge my vital energy into this pot if you do not wish to live with me.
Being stricken by the bow of Kupid, Varuņa said to Urvasī I shall discharge my vital energy into this pot if you do not wish to live with me.
Hearing those sweet words of the Patriarch Varuna, Urvasi was highly pleased and said.
Do what you have said. Now my body is under the possession of Mitra but my mind is attached to your and you are equally attached to me.
Urvaśī having said this, Varuņa discharged his vital energy into the pot.

sanskrit: उर्वशी त्वगमत्तत्र मित्रो वै यत्र देवता
transliteration: urvaśī tvagamattatra mitro vai yatra devatā
english: Thereupon Urvasi approached Mitra. And thereat highly enraged he said to her.
I invited you first; O you of vicious actions, why have, you, renouncing me, secured another. for this vile action, you shall, by my curse live in the land of mortals for some time.

sanskrit: तमद्य गच्छ दुर्बुद्धे स ते भर्ता भविष्यति
transliteration: tamadya gaccha durbuddhe sa te bhartā bhaviṣyati
english: The royal saint Pururava, the king of kasi, is the son of Budha. Do you go to him, O you of a vicious intellect; he shall be your husband.
Thereupon being thus placed under the influence of curse Urvasi went to Pururavă.

sanskrit: तस्य जज्ञे ततः श्रीमानायुः पुत्रो महाबलः
transliteration: tasya jajñe tataḥ śrīmānāyuḥ putro mahābalaḥ
english: The king Paruravă was the begotten son of Budha. He reigned in the foremost of cities Pratişțaro. He begot on Urvaší a highly powerful and beautiful son by the name of Āyu. Nahuşa, powerful as Indra, was the son of
When Indra, the king of the celestials, was assailed with thunderbolt by the Asura Větra, Nahuşa governed his kingdom for a hundred thousand years.

sanskrit: सा तेन शापेन जगाम भूमिं तदोर्वशी चारुदती सुनेत्रा
बहूनि वर्षाण्यवसच्च सुभ्रूः शापक्षयादिन्द्रसदो ययौ च

english: In this wise Urvasi, having beautiful teeth, eyes and brow, remained on earth for many years and then returned to the region of Indra after the period of curse had been over.
Hearing this wonderful and heavenly theme Lakşmaņa was highly gratified and said to Rāma.
O Kakuthstha, how did that twice-born one worshipped by the celestials and the king regain their bodies, after being bodiless.
Hearing the words of Laksmana, Rama, having truth for his prowess, began to relate the story of Vasiştha.
O foremost of Raghus, there sprang up two foremost Brahmin saints from the vital energy discharged by the high-souled Mitra and Varuņa into the pot.
At first therefrom rose up the illustrious Rși Agastya and saying 'I am not your son' Varuņa was thrown into the pot Mitra.

Before the vital energy of Varuna was thrown into the pot Mitra discharged his own on Urvasi's account which was the source of Agastya's birth. (Into the pot in which Mitra's energy was discharged Varuņa also put his own and both the energies were mixed up).
There upon after some time from the energies of both Mitra and Varuņa sprang up the effulgent Vasistha-the priest of Iksvākus.

sanskrit: वव्रे पुरोधसं सौम्य वंशस्यास्य भवाय नः
transliteration: vavre purodhasaṃ saumya vaṃśasyāsya bhavāya naḥ
english: O gentle one, the highly effulgent Iksavāku appointed that blameless Rși as the priest of our family as soon as he was born.

sanskrit: कथितो निर्गमः सौम्य निमेः शृणु यथा ऽभवत्
transliteration: kathito nirgamaḥ saumya nimeḥ śṛṇu yathā 'bhavat
english: I have thus described to you the story of Vasistha's birth possessing a wonderful body. Hear now what befell the king Nimi.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा विदेहं राजानमृषयः सर्व एव ते
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā videhaṃ rājānamṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te
english: And beholding the king Nimi bodiless the intelligent Rșis initiated him into the rites of sacrifice.

sanskrit: तं च देहं नरेन्द्रस्य रक्षन्ति स्म द्विजोत्तमाः
transliteration: taṃ ca dehaṃ narendrasya rakṣanti sma dvijottamāḥ
english: And those leading twice-born ones, with assembled citizens and servants, began to protect that body with unguents, garlands and clothes.

english: There upon at the end of the sacrifice Bhrgu said O king, I am propitiated with you; I shall restore you to senses.

transliteration: varaṃ varaya rājarṣe kva te ceto nirūpyatām
english: There upon the celestials, highly pleased, addressed the consciousness of Nimi saying O royal saint, do you accept boons; where shall we place your consciousness?

The exhaustion, that their their eyes shall experience on account of your moving about as the air, shall be removed within this moment.

He was called Mithi for he originated from Manthana; he was called Janaka for his having sprung up from Janana and Vaideha from having been born from Videha. english: Rama having said this, Laksmana, the slayer of enemies, burning in his native effulgence, said.
O foremost of kings, this ancient account of the ascetic Vasiştha and the king Nimi is highly surprising and wonderful.

sanskrit: निमिस्तु क्षत्रियः शूरो विशेषेण च दीक्षितः

english: But Nimi is a Ksatriya king and a hero besides although initiated he did not forgive the highsouled Vasiştha.
Being thus accosted Rāma, the Kșatriya-chief, said to the effulgent Lakşmaņa conversant with all Sastras.

sanskrit: न सर्वत्र क्षमा वीर पुरुषेषु प्रदृश्यते

english: O hero, forgiveness is not to be seen in all men. O Saumitri, do you hear attentively, the unbearable anger which was you hear attentively, the unbearable anger which was forgiven by the king Yayāti resorting to the quality of goodness.

sanskrit: सौमित्रे दुःसहो रोषो यथा क्षान्तो ययातिना
transliteration: saumitre duḥsaho roṣo yathā kṣānto yayātinā

english: She was the more beloved of the two; his other spouse was Devayāni, grand daughter of Ušanas. She was not liked by her husband. Both of them gave birth to a son each and both the sons were beautiful and attentive. Puru was born of Śarmisthā and Yadu of Devayāni.

Puru was the favourite son of the king, both on account of his mother and of his personal graces, Thereat Yadu, greatly sorry, said to his mother.

sanskrit: क्षम त्वं न क्षमिष्ये ऽहं मरिष्यामि न संशयः

english: You may withstand the insults but I shall never broke them. Permit me, I shall, in sooth, renounce my life.

transliteration: devayānī tu saṅkruddhā sasmāra pitaraṃ tadā
english: The son having, weepingly and distressingly, said this, Devayāni was greatly engaged and thought of her father.
