transliteration: āgatastvaritaṃ tatra devayānī tu yatra sā
english: As soon as he was thought of by his daughter Bhargava speedily came there and beholding her senseless and deprived from joy said "Daughter, what is the matter?
As soon as he was thought of by his daughter Bhargava speedily came there and beholding her senseless and deprived from joy said "Daughter, what is the matter?

The effulgent father having addressed his daughter repeatedly in this wise, Devayāni, enraged, replied, O foremost of ascetics, I shall either enter into fire water or drink poison, by no means I shall preserve this life of mine.

sanskrit: भक्षयिष्ये प्रवेक्ष्यामि न तु शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम्
transliteration: bhakṣayiṣye pravekṣyāmi na tu śakṣyāmi jīvitum
english: The effulgent father having addressed his daughter repeatedly in this wise, Devayāni, enraged, replied, O foremost of ascetics, I shall either enter into fire water or drink poison, by no means I shall preserve this life of mine.

You do not know of the miseries and insults I have been subject to. O Brāhmaṇa, when a tree is neglected, those who live thereon are also distressed. The king having disregarded me, forsooth you have also been neglected.

sanskrit: अवज्ञया च राजर्षिः परिभूय च भार्गव
मय्यवज्ञां प्रयुङ्क्ते हि न च मां बहु मन्यते
transliteration: avajñayā ca rājarṣiḥ paribhūya ca bhārgava
mayyavajñāṃ prayuṅkte hi na ca māṃ bahu manyate
english: You do not know of the miseries and insults I have been subject to. O Brāhmaṇa, when a tree is neglected, those who live thereon are also distressed. The king having disregarded me, forsooth you have also been neglected.
Hearing the words of his daughter, Bhārgava, being enraged said to the king Yayāti.
You are vicious-minded, O son of Nahusa; you have dishonoured me and therefore in your youth shall be subject to decrepitude and infirmities of age.
Having thus imprecated the curse and consoled his sorrowful daughter the highly illustrious Rși Bhārgava repaired to his own habitation.

sanskrit: स एवमुक्त्वा द्विजपुङ्गवाग्र्यः सुतां समाश्वास्य च देवयानीम्
पुनर्ययौ सूर्यसमानतेजा दत्त्वा च शापं नहुषात्मजाय
transliteration: sa evamuktvā dvijapuṅgavāgryaḥ sutāṃ samāśvāsya ca devayānīm
punaryayau sūryasamānatejā dattvā ca śāpaṃ nahuṣātmajāya
english: Having thus conferred solace to his daughter that leading Brahmana, effulgent as the son, returned therefrom.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तूशनसं क्रुद्धं तदा ऽ ऽर्तो नहुषात्मजः
english: Yayāti the son of Nahușa, was greatly distressed on hearing of the ire of the preceptor Sukra. Thereupon meeting with the infirmities of age by the imprecation of the saint he said to his son Yadu.

sanskrit: जरां परमिकां पुत्र भोगै रंस्ये महायशः
transliteration: jarāṃ paramikāṃ putra bhogai raṃsye mahāyaśaḥ
english: O Yadu you are cognisant of religion; do you therefore take this decrepitude for me; I shall satisfy myself with various enjoyments. O foremost of men, I have not yet been satisfied with worldly enjoyments, I shall therefore again take upon myself this decrepitude after having enjoyed all objects of sense.

sanskrit: अनुभूय तदा कामं ततः प्राप्स्याम्यहं जराम्
transliteration: anubhūya tadā kāmaṃ tataḥ prāpsyāmyahaṃ jarām
english: O Yadu you are cognisant of religion; do you therefore take this decrepitude for me; I shall satisfy myself with various enjoyments. O foremost of men, I have not yet been satisfied with worldly enjoyments, I shall therefore again take upon myself this decrepitude after having enjoyed all objects of sense.

sanskrit: पुत्रस्ते दयितः पूरुः प्रतिगृह्णातु वै जराम्
transliteration: putraste dayitaḥ pūruḥ pratigṛhṇātu vai jarām
english: Hearing those words of Yayāti, the foremost of men, Yadu replied: "Let your most favourite son Puru take upon himself this decrepitude.
O king, you have deprived me from all things, what more, you do not allow me to come near you. Let that Puru take this, with whom you do eat and live.
Hearing the words of Yadu, Yayāti said to Puru: “O you having large arms, do you take the decrepitude for me."

sanskrit: धन्यो ऽस्म्यनुगृहीतो ऽस्मि शासने ऽस्मि तव स्थितः
english: Hearing the words of Yayāti, Puru, with folded hands, said: “I am always ready to satisfy your commands; and I have been favoured and honoured by this command of your."
Hearing those words of Puru Yayāti was highly pleased and attained to an excess of delight and then transferred his won decrepitude to him.

sanskrit: ततः स राजा तरुणः प्राप्य यज्ञान्सहस्रशः
transliteration: tataḥ sa rājā taruṇaḥ prāpya yajñānsahasraśaḥ
english: Thereupon regaining his youth the king reigned in earth for many thousand years celebrating thousands of sacrifices.

sanskrit: आनयस्व जरां पुत्र न्यासं निर्यातयस्व मे
transliteration: ānayasva jarāṃ putra nyāsaṃ niryātayasva me
english: Thereupon after a long time Yayāti said to Puru O my son, do you bring the decrepitude I have kept as deposit with you, let it now assail me.

sanskrit: न्यासभूता मया पुत्र त्वयि सङ्क्रामिता जरा
तस्मात्प्रतिग्रहीष्यामि तां जरां मा व्यथां कृथाः
transliteration: nyāsabhūtā mayā putra tvayi saṅkrāmitā jarā
tasmātpratigrahīṣyāmi tāṃ jarāṃ mā vyathāṃ kṛthāḥ
english: I transferred it to you as a deposit. For this I shall take it back; be not sorry for this.
I have been greatly pleased that you have satisfied my behests. I shall, now pleased, install you on the royal throne.
Having thus addressed his son Puru, the king Yayāti angrily said to Yadu, the son of Devayāni.

sanskrit: प्रतिहंसि ममाज्ञां यत् प्रजार्थे विफलो भव
transliteration: pratihaṃsi mamājñāṃ yat prajārthe viphalo bhava
english: You, vicious Rākhasa, are born of me in the shape of a Kşatriya, or else why should you disobey my orders? For this you shall never be a king.
I am your father and preceptor and still you have disregarded me. You shall be the father of dreadful Räksasas.

sanskrit: न तु सोमकुलोत्पन्ने वंशे स्थास्यति दुर्मतेः
transliteration: na tu somakulotpanne vaṃśe sthāsyati durmateḥ
english: O vicious minded; your descendants shall be degraded from the lunar race and your children shall be equally vicious-minded like you.
Having thus imprecated Yadu, the royal saint Yayāti honoured Puru, Puru, the enhancer of prosperity of the kingdom, with installation and then retired to woods.
Thereupon after a long time he breathed his last and went to the abode of the celestials.
The highly illustrious Puru reigned piously in the foremost of cities Pratisthan.
Yadu begot thousands and thousands of Räkşasas and being degraded from the royal family reigned in a city named Krauñcavana, hard to be got at.
In this wise, according to the custom of the Kșatriya the king Yayāti took upon himself the imprecation of the preceptor śukra, but he did not forgive him.

sanskrit: अनुवर्तामहे सौम्य दोषो न स्याद्यथा नृगे
transliteration: anuvartāmahe saumya doṣo na syādyathā nṛge
english: I have thus related to you everything. O gentle one, we shall follow the examples of these illustrious men. And in that case we shall not be degraded like the king Nļga.

sanskrit: इति कथयति रामे चन्द्रतुल्यानने च प्रविरलतरतारं व्योम जज्ञे तदानीम्
अरुणकिरणरक्ता दिग्बभौ चैव पूर्वा कुसुमरसविमुक्तं वस्त्रमाकुण्ठितेव
transliteration: iti kathayati rāme candratulyānane ca praviralataratāraṃ vyoma jajñe tadānīm
aruṇakiraṇaraktā digbabhau caiva pūrvā kusumarasavimuktaṃ vastramākuṇṭhiteva
english: While Rāma, having moon-like countenance, was speaking thus, the stars became fewer in the welkin, and east, stricken with the early rays of the sun, appeared like a damsel, clothed in a raiment coloured with the dye of flowers.

sanskrit: वासन्तिकी निशा प्राप्ता न शीता न च घर्मदा
transliteration: vāsantikī niśā prāptā na śītā na ca gharmadā
english: As Rama and Laksmana were (daily) engaged. in conversing thus, the vernal night; neither hot nor cold, came on.

And it came to pass that one bright morning, after having performed his first diurnal rites, Käkutstha, understanding the ways of the citizens, became anxious to present himself at a spot when he could observe the citizens.

At this time Sumantra, entering, addressed him, saying, “O king, stopped at the gate, some ascetic stay there, Maharsis, led by Bhargava and Cyavana. And, O mighty monarch, eager for a sight of you, those dwellers on the banks of the Yamunā, well pleased, have despatched me (hither), O tiger among men.” Hearing his words, the righteous Rāma answered: “Let the exalted Brāhmaṇas leaded by Bhārgava, enter."

sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामः प्रोवाच धर्मवित्
transliteration: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāmaḥ provāca dharmavit
english: At this time Sumantra, entering, addressed him, saying, “O king, stopped at the gate, some ascetic stay there, Maharsis, led by Bhargava and Cyavana. And, O mighty monarch, eager for a sight of you, those dwellers on the banks of the Yamunā, well pleased, have despatched me (hither), O tiger among men.” Hearing his words, the righteous Rāma answered: “Let the exalted Brāhmaṇas leaded by Bhārgava, enter."
Thereat, honouring the royal mandate, the warder with joined hands brought those ascetics difficult of being approached.

And numbering over an hundred, flaming up in their native effulgence, those high-souled anchorites entered the royal residence. And they presented Rāma with various fruits in profusion and vessels filled with sanctified waters of all holy spots. Thereupon, accepting the waters of the holy places as well as the various kinds of fruit, that mighty-armed one spoke to the mighty ascetics.

And numbering over an hundred, flaming up in their native effulgence, those high-souled anchorites entered the royal residence. And they presented Rāma with various fruits in profusion and vessels filled with sanctified waters of all holy spots. Thereupon, accepting the waters of the holy places as well as the various kinds of fruit, that mighty-armed one spoke to the mighty ascetics.

sanskrit: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा सर्व एव महर्षयः
transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā sarva eva maharṣayaḥ

english: And seeing the saints seated there, that captor of hostile capitals Rāghava, restraining himself, with joined hands, observed.
What is the reason of your visit? What shall I heedfully perform for you? I am worthy of being commanded by the Maharşis; and I must without demur compass every pleasure of theirs.

sanskrit: इदं राज्यं च सकलं जीवितं च हृदि स्थितम्
transliteration: idaṃ rājyaṃ ca sakalaṃ jīvitaṃ ca hṛdi sthitam
english: And this entire monarchy, and the life that is resident in my heart, all these are for the regenerate ones. This I tell you in the name of truth.
Hearing his words, the sages of fierce austerities inhabiting the banks of the Yamunā, broke out into a peal of plandits.

sanskrit: ऊचुश्च ते महात्मानो हर्षेण महता वृताः
transliteration: ūcuśca te mahātmāno harṣeṇa mahatā vṛtāḥ
english: And those high-souled ones, exceedingly rejoiced, said: On earth, O crown of men, this can only be expected from you and nobody else.
Many kings wielding great power have passed away who, having regard to the (possible) gravity of the undertaking, could not bring themselves to promise anything before hand.

sanskrit: त्वया पुनर्ब्राह्मणगौरवादियं कृता प्रतिज्ञा ह्यनवेक्ष्य कारणम्
ततश्च कर्ता ह्यसि नात्र संशयो महाभयात्ऺत्रातुमृषींस्त्वमर्हसि
transliteration: tvayā punarbrāhmaṇagauravādiyaṃ kṛtā pratijñā hyanavekṣya kāraṇam
tataśca kartā hyasi nātra saṃśayo mahābhayāttrātumṛṣīṃstvamarhasi
english: But, without knowing the task, you have bound yourself by a promise for the glory of the Brahmanas. And you, without doubt, will succeed in effecting the work; and it behove you to deliver the sages from a mighty fright.

sanskrit: किं कार्यं ब्रूत मुनयो भयं तावदपैतु वः
transliteration: kiṃ kāryaṃ brūta munayo bhayaṃ tāvadapaitu vaḥ
english: When the sages had spoken thus, Käkutstha said: "O ascetics, tell me what is the work which I shall have to accomplish in your behalf. Your fear shall be removed."

sanskrit: भयानां शृणु यन्मूलं देशस्य च नरेश्वर
transliteration: bhayānāṃ śṛṇu yanmūlaṃ deśasya ca nareśvara
english: As Käkutstha was speaking thus, Bhārgava remarked! O lord of men, do you hear of the origin of the fear that threatens our country.
O king, formerly in the Kita age, there was a magnanimous offspring of Diti, the mighty Asura, Madhu, eldest son of Lotā.
He was well disposed towards Brāhmaṇas, kind to those seeking his refuge, and gifted with high intelligence. The exceedingly generous deities delighted in him greatly.
And by way of honouring him, Rudra conferred a wonderful boon upon Madhu endowed with prowess and ever intent on religion.

sanskrit: रुद्रः प्रीतो ऽभवत्तस्मै वरं दातुं ययौ च सः
transliteration: rudraḥ prīto 'bhavattasmai varaṃ dātuṃ yayau ca saḥ
english: And by way of honouring him, Rudra conferred a wonderful boon upon Madhu endowed with prowess and ever intent on religion.

sanskrit: ददौ महात्मा सुप्रीतो वाक्यं चैतदुवाच ह
transliteration: dadau mahātmā suprīto vākyaṃ caitaduvāca ha
english: And extracting a dart from his own, possessed of terrific energy, endowed with great force; and furnished with exceeding splendour that highsouled one, well pleased, made it over (to Madhu) and spoke to him.
You have practised excellent and unrivalled righteousness, which has won my good graces, and (therefore), I highly gratified, bestow on you this choice weapon.
So long as you, O mighty Asura, do not assail celestials and Vipras, so long shall this be your, otherwise it shall come to naught.

sanskrit: तं शूलो भस्मसात्कृत्वा पुनरेष्यति ते करम्
transliteration: taṃ śūlo bhasmasātkṛtvā punareṣyati te karam
english: Reducing to cinders the person that shall rashly enter upon conflict with you, this dart shall return to your hand.

sanskrit: एवं रुद्राद्वरं लब्ध्वा भूय एव महासुरः
transliteration: evaṃ rudrādvaraṃ labdhvā bhūya eva mahāsuraḥ
english: Having thus obtained the boon from Rudra, the mighty Asura, again bowing to Mahādeva, addressed him, saying.
O reverend one, may this excellent dart be the possession of my family O god, you are the lord of the immortals.

sanskrit: तं ब्रुवाणं मधुं देवः सर्वभूतपतिः शिवः
transliteration: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ madhuṃ devaḥ sarvabhūtapatiḥ śivaḥ
english: Thereat the lord of all beings, the mighty deity Śiva, answered Madhu, when he had spoken thus: This will not be.

sanskrit: मा भूत्ते विफला वाणी मत्प्रसादकृता शुभा
transliteration: mā bhūtte viphalā vāṇī matprasādakṛtā śubhā
english: But in order that your prayer may not go for nothing. I graciously say in your behalf that one of your sons shall sway this dart.

sanskrit: यावत्करस्थः शूलो ऽयं भविष्यति सुतस्य ते
english: So long that dart-handed one shall be incapable of being destroyed be any creature.
Having obtained this wonderful boon from the god, Madhu, foremost of Asuras, caused a splendid city to be constructed.

sanskrit: तस्य पत्नी महाभागा प्रिया कुम्भीनसीति या
transliteration: tasya patnī mahābhāgā priyā kumbhīnasīti yā
english: His beloved wife the exalted and majestic Kumbhīnasſ is the offspring of Viśvāvasu by Anala.

sanskrit: तस्याः पुत्रो महावीर्यो लवणो नाम दारुणः
transliteration: tasyāḥ putro mahāvīryo lavaṇo nāma dāruṇaḥ
english: Her son, the highly powerful wicked, and fierce Lavana, ever since his boyhood, gave himself up to a sinful course of life.

sanskrit: तं पुत्रं दुर्विनीतं तु दृष्ट्वा क्रोधसमन्वितः
मधुः स शोकमापेदे न चैनं किञ्चिदब्रवीत्
transliteration: taṃ putraṃ durvinītaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā krodhasamanvitaḥ
madhuḥ sa śokamāpede na cainaṃ kiñcidabravīt
english: Seeing his son, committed to an impious course Madhu was overcome with grief, but he did not say anything to him.

sanskrit: स विहाय त्विमं लोकं प्रविष्टो वरुणालयम्
शूलं निवेश्य लवणे वरं तस्मै न्यवेदयत्
transliteration: sa vihāya tvimaṃ lokaṃ praviṣṭo varuṇālayam
śūlaṃ niveśya lavaṇe varaṃ tasmai nyavedayat
english: And forsaking this world, he entered the region of Varuņa; and making over the dart to Lavana, communicated to him all about the boon he had obtained.

And by virtue of the power of the dart, he oppress the three worlds in especial the ascetics; such is the power of Lavaņa, and such is his dart. Hearing all this O Kākutstha, you are capable (of righting our wrong.) You are our chief resource.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा प्रमाणं काकुत्स्थ त्वं हि नः परमा गतिः
transliteration: śrutvā pramāṇaṃ kākutstha tvaṃ hi naḥ paramā gatiḥ
english: And by virtue of the power of the dart, he oppress the three worlds in especial the ascetics; such is the power of Lavaņa, and such is his dart. Hearing all this O Kākutstha, you are capable (of righting our wrong.) You are our chief resource.

sanskrit: अभयं याचिता वीर त्रातारं न च विद्महे
transliteration: abhayaṃ yācitā vīra trātāraṃ na ca vidmahe
english: O Rāma, many a monarch has been already sued by the sages, O hero, to deliver them from this fear, but we have not yet found a deliverer.

sanskrit: ते वयं रावणं श्रुत्वा हतं सबलवाहनम्
त्रातारं विद्महे तात नान्यं भुवि नराधिपम्
transliteration: te vayaṃ rāvaṇaṃ śrutvā hataṃ sabalavāhanam
trātāraṃ vidmahe tāta nānyaṃ bhuvi narādhipam
english: Hearing, O child, that Ravana together with all his forces and vehicles has been destroyed (by you), we know that there breathes not another king on earth capable of delivering us. Therefore our prayer is that you may deliver us afflicted with the fear of Lavana.

sanskrit: इति राम निवेदितं तु ते भयजं कारणमुत्थितं च यत्
transliteration: iti rāma niveditaṃ tu te bhayajaṃ kāraṇamutthitaṃ ca yat
english: Thus, O Rāma, have we acquainted you with the occasion of fear that has arisen. You are capable of coping with the same. Do you of undeteriorated prowess, do the needful.

sanskrit: किमाहारः किमाचारो लवणः क्व च वर्तते
transliteration: kimāhāraḥ kimācāro lavaṇaḥ kva ca vartate
english: Thus accosted (by the sages), Rāma answered them with joined hands: "What does he live on? What are his ways? And where does Lavana live?"

sanskrit: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषयः सर्व एव ते
transliteration: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te
english: Hearing Räghava's words, the sages informed him of the way in which Lavana increased in power.

sanskrit: आचारो रौद्रता नित्यं वासो मधुवने तथा
transliteration: ācāro raudratā nityaṃ vāso madhuvane tathā
english: His food is every creature specially ascetics; his manner of life is regulated by ferocity and his constant home is Madhuvana.
Slaying constantly thousands on thousands of lions and tigers and deer, and birds and human beings, he provides his daily food (with their flesh.)

sanskrit: ततो ऽन्तराणि सत्त्वानि खादते स महाबलः
english: And like the Destroyer on the occasion of the universal dissolution, that one possessed of gigantic strength feeds on other creatures as well.
Hearing this, Rāghava spoke to the mighty ascetics: "I will slay that Raksasa. Let your depart."
Having thus bound himself with that promise to the ascetics of fierce energy, Raghu's son along with his brothers spoke.

sanskrit: को हन्ता लवणं वीरः कस्यांशः स विधीयताम्
transliteration: ko hantā lavaṇaṃ vīraḥ kasyāṃśaḥ sa vidhīyatām
english: What hero shall slay Lavana? Do you decide this. On whom shall devolve this duty? Whether the mighty armed Bharata or the intelligent Śatrughna shall (do this work?).
Thus addressed by Raghava Bharata remarked: "I will slay this. Let this task be entrusted to me."

Hearing Bharata's speech instinct with fortitude and valour, the younger brother of Lakş maņa stood up, leaving his golden seat. And Śatrughna, saluting the king represented: “The mighty-armed second son of Raghu has already achieved a grand work: he formerly governed Ayodhyā empty of the noble one,* bearing in his heart the grief connected with his return. *Rama.

sanskrit: आर्येण हि पुरा शून्या त्वयोध्या परिपालिता
transliteration: āryeṇa hi purā śūnyā tvayodhyā paripālitā

english: Undergoing many a hardship, o king, that illustrious one passed his days, lying down on a bed of sorrow, and living on fruits and roots, and wearing rags.

sanskrit: प्रेष्ये मयि स्थिते राजन्न भूयः क्लेशमाप्नुयात्
transliteration: preṣye mayi sthite rājanna bhūyaḥ kleśamāpnuyāt
english: Having suffered such misery, Raghu's son should not be suffered to undergo trouble, while, O king I his servant is by.

sanskrit: एवं भवतु काकुत्स्थ क्रियतां मम शासनम्
transliteration: evaṃ bhavatu kākutstha kriyatāṃ mama śāsanam
english: On Satrughna saying this, Raghava again said: Let this be so. Do you do my bidding. I shall install you on the graceful city of Madhu; or if you wish without and entrust Bharata with this task, O long-armed Heroic, and accomplished, you are combatant to found a city on the Yamună as well as flourishing provinces. He that, having people's dominion, does not flourish it with a king. Go to hell. one.

On Satrughna saying this, Raghava again said: Let this be so. Do you do my bidding. I shall install you on the graceful city of Madhu; or if you wish without and entrust Bharata with this task, O long-armed Heroic, and accomplished, you are combatant to found a city on the Yamună as well as flourishing provinces. He that, having people's dominion, does not flourish it with a king. Go to hell. one.

I shall install you on the graceful city of Madhu; or if you wish without and entrust Bharata with this task, O long-armed Heroic, and accomplished, you are combatant to found a city on the Yamună as well as flourishing provinces. He that, having people's dominion, does not flourish it with a king. Go to hell. one.

sanskrit: यो हि शत्रुं समुत्पाट्य पार्थिवस्य पुनः क्षये
न विधत्ते नृपं तत्र नरकं स हि गच्छति
transliteration: yo hi śatruṃ samutpāṭya pārthivasya punaḥ kṣaye
na vidhatte nṛpaṃ tatra narakaṃ sa hi gacchati

sanskrit: स त्वं हत्वा मधुसुतं लवणं पापनिश्चयम्
राज्यं प्रशाधि धर्मेण वाक्यं मे यद्यवेक्षसे
transliteration: sa tvaṃ hatvā madhusutaṃ lavaṇaṃ pāpaniścayam
rājyaṃ praśādhi dharmeṇa vākyaṃ me yadyavekṣase
english: So if you accept my words, then slaying Madhu's son, the sinful Lavana, rule the kingdom righteously. O hero, you must say anything after what I have spoken. Without doubt, a youthful younger brother must obey the injunctions of his elder brother. Do you, o Kākutstha, accept the installation which I confer on the, precluded by the prescribed religious formulae uttered by Vipras headed by Vasiştha."

sanskrit: उत्तरं च न वक्तव्यं शूर वाक्यान्तरे मम
transliteration: uttaraṃ ca na vaktavyaṃ śūra vākyāntare mama
english: So if you accept my words, then slaying Madhu's son, the sinful Lavana, rule the kingdom righteously. O hero, you must say anything after what I have spoken. Without doubt, a youthful younger brother must obey the injunctions of his elder brother. Do you, o Kākutstha, accept the installation which I confer on the, precluded by the prescribed religious formulae uttered by Vipras headed by Vasiştha."
Thus accosted by Rāma, the exceedingly energetic Satrughna was powerfully wrought up with bashfulness, and replied slowly.
O lord of men, this does not appear to be in consonance with morality. Wherefore, an elder brother existing, would you install a younger one?
I must, O best of men, do your behest: for, O exalted one, your mandate can never be passed by me.

sanskrit: त्वत्तो मया श्रुतं वीर श्रुतिभ्यश्च मया श्रुतम्
नोत्तरं हि मया वाच्यं मध्यमे प्रतिजानति
transliteration: tvatto mayā śrutaṃ vīra śrutibhyaśca mayā śrutam
nottaraṃ hi mayā vācyaṃ madhyame pratijānati
english: O hero, I have heard from you as well as from the Śruti (touching the morality concerned).* i.e. of being installed as a king during the life of my elder brother. When my second brother had already vowed (that he would slay Lavana), I ought not to have returned the answer I actually have. I saying, 'I will in battle slay the dreadful Lavaņa.' I have been guilty of an unrighteous speech. And it is for this transgression that, O powerful one, I shall have to undergo this improper process. *(i.e. of being installed as a king during the life of my elder brother.)

sanskrit: व्याहृतं दुर्वचो घोरं हन्तास्मि लवणं मृधे
transliteration: vyāhṛtaṃ durvaco ghoraṃ hantāsmi lavaṇaṃ mṛdhe
english: O hero, I have heard from you as well as from the Śruti (touching the morality concerned).* i.e. of being installed as a king during the life of my elder brother. When my second brother had already vowed (that he would slay Lavana), I ought not to have returned the answer I actually have. I saying, 'I will in battle slay the dreadful Lavaņa.' I have been guilty of an unrighteous speech. And it is for this transgression that, O powerful one, I shall have to undergo this improper process. *(i.e. of being installed as a king during the life of my elder brother.)
But, albeit this course is unrighteous and entails perdition, yet desired by an eldest brother, I certainly ought not to make any answer.

sanskrit: सो ऽहं द्वितीयं काकुत्स्थ न वक्ष्यामि तवोत्तरम्
मा द्वितीयेन दण्डो वै निपतेन्मयि मानद
transliteration: so 'haṃ dvitīyaṃ kākutstha na vakṣyāmi tavottaram
mā dvitīyena daṇḍo vai nipatenmayi mānada
english: And, O Kākutstha, a second answer I would not return; so that, О bestower of honour, I may not, by a second reply, render myself liable to a fresh punishment.
In this matter, O chief of men, I will even do your desire. Do you, O descendant of Ragu, so order that sin may not be mine (in having obeyed your mandate.)

sanskrit: उवाच रामः संहृष्टो भरतं लक्ष्मणं तथा
transliteration: uvāca rāmaḥ saṃhṛṣṭo bharataṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tathā
english: Thus addressed by the heroic and high-souled Śatrughna, Rāma, delighted, spoke to Bharata and Laksmana.
Do you carefully provide the things necessary for the coronation: this very day shall I install that foremost of men, the descendant of Raghu.
And by my order do you summon the Purodhasas, O Kākutstha, and the citizens and the Rtvijas, and the councillors.

Having received the royal behest, the mighty car-warriors did accordingly. And the Kșatriyas and the Brāhmaṇas entered the royal mansion with the priest as well as the requisite things for the installation.
And then commenced the auspicious sprinkling of the high-souled Satrughna, gladdening (the hearts of all in) the palace of Rāghava.
And on being installed Käkutstha resembled the sun; and he like Skanda formerly installed by the celestials led by Indra.
And when Šatrughna had been installed by Rāma of untiring deeds, the citizens as well as the Brāhmaṇas of vast Vedic, attainments experienced excess of joy.

sanskrit: कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च मङ्गलं केकयी तथा
transliteration: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca maṅgalaṃ kekayī tathā
english: And Kausaly, and Sumitrā and Kaikeyi and the other wives of the king set up festal salutation in the palace. And on Satrughna having been installed the high-souled sages dwelling on the banks of the Jamunā, thought that Lavaņa had been slain.
Then placing the installed Satrughna on his lap Rāghava, extolling his prowess, addressed him sweet words.

sanskrit: अनेन लवणं सौम्य हन्ता ऽसि रघुनन्दन
english: O captor of hostile capitals, this divine arrow never missing is your. With this, O son of Raghu, you, O spliced one, with slay Lavana.

sanskrit: सृष्टः शरो ऽयं काकुत्स्थ यदा शेते महार्णवे
transliteration: sṛṣṭaḥ śaro 'yaṃ kākutstha yadā śete mahārṇave
english: O Kākutstha, this shaft was forged when invisible by celestials and Asuras the divine selfsprung and invincible (deity) reposed on the mighty main, and when creation was oppressed by Madhu and Kaitabha as well as other Räks asas. He, overwhelmed with rage desirous of creating the three worlds, created the best of arrows invincible to all beings, for the extraction of the wicked ones; and destroyed them in battle by means of this very arrow. And having with this foremost of shafts finished Madhu and Kait abha, they set about creating the worlds.

sanskrit: तौ हत्वा जनभोगार्थं कैटभं तु मधुं तथा
transliteration: tau hatvā janabhogārthaṃ kaiṭabhaṃ tu madhuṃ tathā

sanskrit: नायं मया शरः पूर्वं रावणस्य वधार्थिना
transliteration: nāyaṃ mayā śaraḥ pūrvaṃ rāvaṇasya vadhārthinā
english: When, O Satrughna, formerly I sought to slay Råvaņa, I did not discharge this arrow, thinking that if discharged, it would inflict great havoc on creatures.

Keeping in his abode that great and redoubled which had been bestowed on Madhu by the high-souled Tryambaka, for the destruction of foes, and worshipping the same ever, Lavaņa go about and secure excellent fare( for himself) when one challenge him, desirous of reducing him (his antagonist) to ashes.

sanskrit: स तं निक्षिप्य भवने पूज्यमान पुनः पुनः
transliteration: sa taṃ nikṣipya bhavane pūjyamāna punaḥ punaḥ

sanskrit: तदा शूलं गहीत्वा तं भस्म रक्षः करोति हि
transliteration: tadā śūlaṃ gahītvā taṃ bhasma rakṣaḥ karoti hi

sanskrit: अप्रविष्टं पुरं पूर्वं द्वारि तिष्ठ धृतायुधः
transliteration: apraviṣṭaṃ puraṃ pūrvaṃ dvāri tiṣṭha dhṛtāyudhaḥ
english: Therefore, O foremost of men, you should, before entering the city, stand at the gate obstructing his course. O you having long arms, you should invite him for battle when he shall be weaponless and in that way would be able to destroy him.

Therefore, O foremost of men, you should, before entering the city, stand at the gate obstructing his course. O you having long arms, you should invite him for battle when he shall be weaponless and in that way would be able to destroy him.

sanskrit: अन्यथा क्रियमाणे तु अवध्यः स भविष्यति
transliteration: anyathā kriyamāṇe tu avadhyaḥ sa bhaviṣyati
english: And by no other means he is to be slain. If you can encompass this, he shall forsooth be slain.
O my son, I have thus told you the way in which the dare should be thwarted. It is impossible to surpass the prowess of the graceful Nilkantha.

sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा च काकुत्स्थं प्रशस्य च पुनः पुनः
transliteration: evamuktvā ca kākutsthaṃ praśasya ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Having thus addressed Satrughna, Rāma again and again praised him and said.

sanskrit: रथानां द्वे सहस्रे च गजानां शतमुत्तमम्
transliteration: rathānāṃ dve sahasre ca gajānāṃ śatamuttamam
english: O foremost of men, let four thousand horses, two thousand chariots, one hundred excellent elephants, shops with various articles and songsters follow you.
O foremost of men, let four thousand horses, two thousand chariots, one hundred excellent elephants, shops with various articles and songsters follow you.
O foremost of men, O Śatrughna, do you proceed with Niyuta gold and silver coins and necessary riches and conveyances.

Do you so act, O hero, that soldiers might be well-fed and delighted and be not annoyed with you. Do you please them with sweet words, for the servants, when they face enemies, have not with them friends or wives—and so they are pleased, O Rāghava when they receive sufficient food and presents.

sanskrit: न ह्यर्थास्तत्र तिष्ठन्ति न दारा न च बान्धवाः
transliteration: na hyarthāstatra tiṣṭhanti na dārā na ca bāndhavāḥ
english: Do you so act, O hero, that soldiers might be well-fed and delighted and be not annoyed with you. Do you please them with sweet words, for the servants, when they face enemies, have not with them friends or wives—and so they are pleased, O Rāghava when they receive sufficient food and presents.

sanskrit: एक एव धनुष्पाणिर्गच्छ त्वं मधुनो वनम्
transliteration: eka eva dhanuṣpāṇirgaccha tvaṃ madhuno vanam
english: O Śatrughna, having sent before a huge and well contended army do you proceed afterwards to Madhuvana. You should proceed so fearlessly that Madhu's son Lavaņa might not know that you were going for encounter.

sanskrit: यथा त्वां न प्रजानाति गच्छन्तं युद्धकाङ्क्षिणम्
transliteration: yathā tvāṃ na prajānāti gacchantaṃ yuddhakāṅkṣiṇam
english: O Śatrughna, having sent before a huge and well contended army do you proceed afterwards to Madhuvana. You should proceed so fearlessly that Madhu's son Lavaņa might not know that you were going for encounter.

sanskrit: न तस्य मूत्युरन्यो ऽस्ति कश्चिद्धि पुरुषर्षभ
दर्शनं यो ऽभिगच्छेत स वध्यो लवणेन हि
transliteration: darśanaṃ yo 'bhigaccheta sa vadhyo lavaṇena hi
english: O foremost of men, he shall not be slain by any other expedient than that I have acquainted yourself with. If he can perceive before, whoever that enemy might be, Lavana shall forsooth destroy him.

sanskrit: स हि ग्रीष्मो ऽपयाते तु वर्षारात्र उपागते
हन्यास्त्वं लवणं सौम्य सहि कालो ऽस्य दुर्मतेः
transliteration: sa hi grīṣmo 'payāte tu varṣārātra upāgate
hanyāstvaṃ lavaṇaṃ saumya sahi kālo 'sya durmateḥ
english: When rains shall set in after the expiration of the present summer you should slay him for that is the proper time for destroying that viciousminded one.

Let the soldiers only now proceed with ascetics before them; the summer has not as yet fully expired and this is the time, when they shall, without any trouble, be able to cross the Gangā. Afterwards having encamped your army on the other side of the Gangā you should alone proceed speedily with your bow.

sanskrit: तत्र स्थाप्य बलं सर्वं नदीतीरे समाहितः
अग्रतो धनुषा सार्धं गच्छ त्वं लघुविक्रमः
transliteration: tatra sthāpya balaṃ sarvaṃ nadītīre samāhitaḥ
agrato dhanuṣā sārdhaṃ gaccha tvaṃ laghuvikramaḥ
english: Let the soldiers only now proceed with ascetics before them; the summer has not as yet fully expired and this is the time, when they shall, without any trouble, be able to cross the Gangā. Afterwards having encamped your army on the other side of the Gangā you should alone proceed speedily with your bow.

Hearing those words of Rāma and summoning all his highly powerful and leading warriors Satrughna said "Do you all proceed and halt at those places which are well known to you. Do not oppress any body."

sanskrit: एते वो गणिता वासा यत्र तत्र निवत्स्यथ
स्थातव्यं चाविरोधेन यथा बाधा न कस्यचित्
transliteration: ete vo gaṇitā vāsā yatra tatra nivatsyatha
sthātavyaṃ cāvirodhena yathā bādhā na kasyacit
english: Hearing those words of Rāma and summoning all his highly powerful and leading warriors Satrughna said "Do you all proceed and halt at those places which are well known to you. Do not oppress any body."

sanskrit: तथा तांस्तु समाज्ञाप्य प्रस्थाप्य च महद्बलम्
कौसल्यां च सुमित्रां च कैकेयीं चाभ्यवादयत्
transliteration: tathā tāṃstu samājñāpya prasthāpya ca mahadbalam
kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ cābhyavādayat
english: Having thus ordered the powerful warriors the highly powerful Śatrughna bowed to Kausalyā, Sumitrā and Kaikeyi.

Thereupon having circumambulated with folded hands Rāma, Lakşmaņa and Bharata he reverentially saluted the feet of the priests. And then with Rāma's permission and having gone round him the highly powerful Śatrughna issued out.

Thereupon having circumambulated with folded hands Rāma, Lakşmaņa and Bharata he reverentially saluted the feet of the priests. And then with Rāma's permission and having gone round him the highly powerful Śatrughna issued out.

sanskrit: उपास मासं तु नरेन्द्रपार्श्वतस्त्वथ प्रयातो रघुवंशवर्धनः
transliteration: upāsa māsaṃ tu narendrapārśvatastvatha prayāto raghuvaṃśavardhanaḥ
english: Having thus despatched before a huge army consisting of selected elephants and horses, Śatrughna, the enhancer of the glory of Raghu's race, took farewell from Rāma. And all showed him proper respect.

sanskrit: प्रस्थाप्य च बलं सर्वं मासमात्रोषितः पथि
एक एवाशु शत्रुघ्नो जगाम त्वरितं तदा
transliteration: prasthāpya ca balaṃ sarvaṃ māsamātroṣitaḥ pathi
eka evāśu śatrughno jagāma tvaritaṃ tadā
english: Having thus despatched his army and waited at Ayodhya for a month Śatrughna, the slayer of enemies, proceeded alone.
Having spent two nights on his way he arrived at the holy and picturesque hermitage of the great ascetic Vālmīki.
And having bowed to that high-souled Muni Vālmīki, he with folded palms, said thus.

sanskrit: श्वः प्रभाते गमिष्यामि प्रतीचीं वारुणीं दिशम्
transliteration: śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmi pratīcīṃ vāruṇīṃ diśam
english: "O illustrious Sir, I wish to wait here this day; I have come here for some business of our master Rāma. To-morrow morning I shall proceed to the dreadful West.”

Hearing the words of the high-souled Śatrughna, Vālmīki, the foremost of ascetics, replied saying: “O you of great renown, do you wait here without any hesitation. O gentle one, this hermitage belongs to the descendants of the Raghu face. Do you fearlessly take your seat and water to wash your feet.”

sanskrit: आसनं पाद्यमर्ध्यं च निर्विशङ्कः प्रतीच्छ मे
transliteration: āsanaṃ pādyamardhyaṃ ca nirviśaṅkaḥ pratīccha me
english: Hearing the words of the high-souled Śatrughna, Vālmīki, the foremost of ascetics, replied saying: “O you of great renown, do you wait here without any hesitation. O gentle one, this hermitage belongs to the descendants of the Raghu face. Do you fearlessly take your seat and water to wash your feet.”

sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य तदा पूजां फलमूलं च भोजनम्
transliteration: pratigṛhya tadā pūjāṃ phalamūlaṃ ca bhojanam
english: Thereupon taking water to wash his feet and feeding upon fruits and roots Satrughna attained to great delight.

sanskrit: स भुक्त्वा फलमूलं च महर्षिं तमुवाच ह
transliteration: sa bhuktvā phalamūlaṃ ca maharṣiṃ tamuvāca ha
english: After eating the fruits and roots he asked the great ascetic Vālmīki saying: “O great ascetic, to whom belong the articles of sacrifice in the east near this hermitage?”
Whereto Vālmīki replied “Satrughna, hear I shall tell you, whose sacrificial ground was this in the days of yore.
There was a king by the name of Saudāsa, one of your ancestors. His son Vīryasaha was a highly powerful and pious king.

The heroic Saudāsa was fond of hunting from his boyhood. Once on a time while a hunting, he espied two Rākṣasas in the forest. He had heard about them many times before: they were in the shape of tigers and of a dreadful figure and were not satisfied with devouring many thousand deer.

The heroic Saudāsa was fond of hunting from his boyhood. Once on a time while a hunting, he espied two Rākṣasas in the forest. He had heard about them many times before: they were in the shape of tigers and of a dreadful figure and were not satisfied with devouring many thousand deer.

sanskrit: स तु तौ राक्षसौ दृष्ट्वा निर्मृगं च वनं कृतम्
क्रोधेन महता ऽ ऽविष्टो जघानैकं महेषुणा
transliteration: sa tu tau rākṣasau dṛṣṭvā nirmṛgaṃ ca vanaṃ kṛtam
english: King Saudāsa saw those two Rākşasas and found the forest divested of all creatures. And enraged in consequence thereof he slew one of them.

sanskrit: निरीक्षमाणं तं दृष्ट्वा सहायं तस्य रक्षसः
transliteration: nirīkṣamāṇaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahāyaṃ tasya rakṣasaḥ

english: Having said this the Rākşasa vanished therefrom. Thereupon in time the prince Mitrasaha became king.
Saudása engaged in celebrating a mighty horse-sacrifice in the vicinity of this hermitage. Vasiștha officiated as a priest at that sacrifice.
It continued for many Ayuta years. For immense riches the sacrifice appeared like one performed by the celestials.
Thereupon when the sacrifice was about to be finished the aforesaid Rākşasa, remembering his former enmity, assumed the shape of Vasiştha and said to the king Saudāsa.

sanskrit: अस्य यज्ञस्य जातो ऽन्तः सामिषं भोजनं मम
दीयतामिह शीघ्रं वै नात्र कार्या विचारणा
transliteration: asya yajñasya jāto 'ntaḥ sāmiṣaṃ bhojanaṃ mama
dīyatāmiha śīghraṃ vai nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: O king, today the sacrifice shall end; do therefore, without any delay, feed me with meat.
Hearing the words of the Rākşasa in the guise of a Brāhmaṇa, the king ordered his expert cooks, saying.

sanskrit: हविष्यं सामिषं स्वादु यथा भवति भोजनम्
तथा कुरुष्व शीघ्रं वै परितुष्येद्यथा गुरुः
transliteration: haviṣyaṃ sāmiṣaṃ svādu yathā bhavati bhojanam
tathā kuruṣva śīghraṃ vai parituṣyedyathā guruḥ
english: "Do you soon prepare such dishes of meat as may satisfy my preceptor Vasiştha."

sanskrit: इदं स्वादु हविष्यं च सामिषं चान्नमाहृतम्
transliteration: idaṃ svādu haviṣyaṃ ca sāmiṣaṃ cānnamāhṛtam

sanskrit: ज्ञात्वा तदामिषं विप्रो मानुषं भाजनं गतम्
transliteration: jñātvā tadāmiṣaṃ vipro mānuṣaṃ bhājanaṃ gatam

english: "O king, let this be your food which you have offered me; this shall not prove otherwise."

Being enraged on hearing it the king Saudāsa took water in his palms and was about to imprecate Vasiștha, when his queen, preventing him said. “O king, the illustrious great ascetic Vasiştha is our preceptor and priest and so you should not imprecate him."

Being enraged on hearing it the king Saudāsa took water in his palms and was about to imprecate Vasiștha, when his queen, preventing him said. “O king, the illustrious great ascetic Vasiştha is our preceptor and priest and so you should not imprecate him."

sanskrit: व्यसर्जयत धर्मात्मा ततः पादौ सिषेच च
transliteration: vyasarjayata dharmātmā tataḥ pādau siṣeca ca
english: Hearing those words of his queen, the king Saudāsa, threw off that powerful water on his own feet which at once became dark. From that time the illustrious king Saudása became also known by the name of Kalmāşapāda.

sanskrit: तेनास्य राज्ञस्तौ पादौ तदा कल्माषतां गतौ
transliteration: tenāsya rājñastau pādau tadā kalmāṣatāṃ gatau
english: Hearing those words of his queen, the king Saudāsa, threw off that powerful water on his own feet which at once became dark. From that time the illustrious king Saudása became also known by the name of Kalmāşapāda.

sanskrit: स राजा सह पत्न्या वै प्रणिपत्य मुहुर्मुहुः
transliteration: sa rājā saha patnyā vai praṇipatya muhurmuhuḥ
english: Thereupon the king with his spouse again and again bowed to Vasistha's feet and informed him of what the Rākşasa had done under the guise of a Brāhmana.

sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य रक्षसा विकृतं च तत्
transliteration: tacchrutvā pārthivendrasya rakṣasā vikṛtaṃ ca tat
english: Hearing the words of the king and being apprised that this wife vile act had been done by the Rākşasa, Vasiștha said, “O king, even what I have said angrily shall not prove futile. However I confer upon you this boon that after twelve years you shall be freed from this curse, and by my favour you shall cherish no recollection of your condition extending ever those twelve years."

sanskrit: नैतच्छक्यं वृथा कर्तुं प्रदास्यामि च ते वरम्
transliteration: naitacchakyaṃ vṛthā kartuṃ pradāsyāmi ca te varam
english: Hearing the words of the king and being apprised that this wife vile act had been done by the Rākşasa, Vasiștha said, “O king, even what I have said angrily shall not prove futile. However I confer upon you this boon that after twelve years you shall be freed from this curse, and by my favour you shall cherish no recollection of your condition extending ever those twelve years."
Having thus suffered the consequences of the curse, Saudasa, the slayer of enemies, again obtained his kingdom an governed his subjects.

sanskrit: आश्रमस्य समीपे ऽस्य यन्मां पृच्छसि राघव
english: O descendant of Raghu, the sacrificial ground of which you have asked me, belongs to the king Saudasa.

sanskrit: तस्य तां पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य कथां श्रुत्वा सुदारुणाम्
transliteration: tasya tāṃ pārthivendrasya kathāṃ śrutvā sudāruṇām
english: Having thus heard the dreadful; story of the king Saudāsa and saluted the ascetic Vālmīki, Śatrughna entered a thatched cottage.
On the same night ſatrughna housed himself in a thatched cottage Sitā gave birth to twin sons.

In the midnight the Muni boys came to Vālmīki and communicated to him this auspicious intelligence, saying. “O illustrious Sir, the beloved spouse of Rāma has given birth to two sons; do you so protect them that evil spirits not injure them."

In the midnight the Muni boys came to Vālmīki and communicated to him this auspicious intelligence, saying. “O illustrious Sir, the beloved spouse of Rāma has given birth to two sons; do you so protect them that evil spirits not injure them."

Hearing those words the highly effulgent Vālmīki went there and attained to great on beholding those two highly effulgent sons, resembling the newly risen sun and the celestials. Thereupon he made arrangements against the oppression of ghosts and goblins.

sanskrit: जगाम तत्र हृष्टात्मा ददर्श च कुमारकौ
transliteration: jagāma tatra hṛṣṭātmā dadarśa ca kumārakau
english: Hearing those words the highly effulgent Vālmīki went there and attained to great on beholding those two highly effulgent sons, resembling the newly risen sun and the celestials. Thereupon he made arrangements against the oppression of ghosts and goblins.

sanskrit: कुशमुष्टिमुपादाय लवं चैव तु स द्विजः
transliteration: kuśamuṣṭimupādāya lavaṃ caiva tu sa dvijaḥ
english: Thereupon taking Kuśa (the upper part of the grass) and Lava (the lower part) the great ascetic Vālmīki made those arrangements.

sanskrit: निर्मार्जनीयस्तु तदा कुश इत्यस्य नाम तत्
transliteration: nirmārjanīyastu tadā kuśa ityasya nāma tat
english: And giving Kuśa sanctified by Mantras to the hands of elderly women he said, “do you rub the person of the elder boy with these”; and giving them Lava he said “do you rub the person of the younger brother with this. And according to this I shall name the first Son Kuśa and the second Lava; and by those names they shall be celebrated on earth.”
Thereupon reverentially taking from the hands of Vālmīki and Kuśa Lava, the means of protection, the elderly ladies engaged in guarding them.

sanskrit: तथा तां क्रियमाणां च वृद्धाभिर्जन्म नाम च
सङ्कीर्तनं च रामस्य सीतायाः प्रसवौ शुभौ
transliteration: tathā tāṃ kriyamāṇāṃ ca vṛddhābhirjanma nāma ca
saṅkīrtanaṃ ca rāmasya sītāyāḥ prasavau śubhau

english: Hearing the Sītā without any trouble had given birth to two sons and elderly female ascetics had been engaged in protecting them and bearing the chanting of Råma's glories in the midnight, Satrughna thought within himself.
"Blessed it is that Sītā has given birth to two sons.” And with this joy the live long night of Śrāvaņa passed away in no time.
Having performed the morning rites after the expiration of the night and taken farewell from the ascetic Vālmīki, Lakşmaņa proceeded towards the west.
And having spent seven nights he at last arrived at the hermitage of the pious Rși living on the banks of the Yamuna.

Taking shelter there be engaged in pleasant conversation with Cyavana (son of Bhrgu), and other ascetics. Having remained there for the night and talked with those ascetics the highsouled, heroic Raghu prince Śatrughna was greatly delighted.

sanskrit: स काञ्चनाद्यैर्मुनिभिः समेतो रघुप्रवीरो रजनीं तदानीम्
transliteration: sa kāñcanādyairmunibhiḥ sameto raghupravīro rajanīṃ tadānīm
english: Taking shelter there be engaged in pleasant conversation with Cyavana (son of Bhrgu), and other ascetics. Having remained there for the night and talked with those ascetics the highsouled, heroic Raghu prince Śatrughna was greatly delighted.

sanskrit: पप्रच्छ च्यवनं विप्रं लवणस्य यथा बलम्
transliteration: papraccha cyavanaṃ vipraṃ lavaṇasya yathā balam
english: Thereupon when the night set in Śatrughna accosted Bhrgu's son Cyavana saying, “O Brāhmaṇa how powerful is Lavaņa? And what is the strength of his dart? What persons before had been destroyed by this dart in conflict?”

sanskrit: शूलस्य च बलं ब्रह्मन्के च पूर्वं विनाशिताः
transliteration: śūlasya ca balaṃ brahmanke ca pūrvaṃ vināśitāḥ
english: Thereupon when the night set in Śatrughna accosted Bhrgu's son Cyavana saying, “O Brāhmaṇa how powerful is Lavaņa? And what is the strength of his dart? What persons before had been destroyed by this dart in conflict?”
Hearing the words of the high-souled descendant of Raghu, Satrughna, the highly effulgent Cyavana replied saying.
O descendant of Raghu, Lavaņa has accomplished many works by this dart; among them, hear, what Māndhāta, born in the race of Iksawaku, did.
The early king of Ayodhyā was known over the three worlds under the name of Māndhātā. He was the son of Yuvanāśva, highly powerful and strong.

sanskrit: स कृत्वा पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां शासने पृथिवीपतिः
transliteration: sa kṛtvā pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ śāsane pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: Having brought the whole world under his subjection the king Māndhātā engaged in the conquest of the celestial region.

sanskrit: इन्द्रस्य च भयं तीव्रं सुराणां च महात्मनाम्
transliteration: indrasya ca bhayaṃ tīvraṃ surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
english: He having been engaged in making preparations to conquer the world of gods—the celestial chief Indra with other immortals was greatly terrified.

With this promise, the king Mândhāta went into the celestial region that he would occupy the half of Indra's throne and kingdom and the celestials would adore him. Being apprised of this vicious intention of his, Indra, the slayer of Pāka, consoled him in sweet words, saying.

With this promise, the king Mândhāta went into the celestial region that he would occupy the half of Indra's throne and kingdom and the celestials would adore him. Being apprised of this vicious intention of his, Indra, the slayer of Pāka, consoled him in sweet words, saying.

sanskrit: राजा त्वं मानुषे लोके न तावत्पुरुषर्षभ
transliteration: rājā tvaṃ mānuṣe loke na tāvatpuruṣarṣabha
english: O foremost of men, even in the land of men, you have not been able to become the real king. Without perfectly subjugating the earth how do you wish to lord over the celestial kingdom?

sanskrit: यदि वीर समग्रा ते मेदिनी निखिला वशे
transliteration: yadi vīra samagrā te medinī nikhilā vaśe
english: If the whole world is under your subjection, O hero, be you, with the whole host of your servants and soldiers, installed on the celestial throne.

sanskrit: क्व मे शक्र प्रतिहतं शासनं पृथिवीतले
transliteration: kva me śakra pratihataṃ śāsanaṃ pṛthivītale
english: Indra having said this, the high-souled Māndhātā replies: O Sakra, who on this earth, has disobeyed my commands.?

sanskrit: मधुपुत्रो मधुवने न ते ऽ ऽज्ञां कुरुते ऽनघ
english: Whereto Indra replied o sinless one, the night-ranger, Lavana, Madhu's son, living in Madhuvana, is not under your control.

sanskrit: व्रीडितो ऽवाङ्मुखो राजा व्याहर्तुं न शशाक ह
transliteration: vrīḍito 'vāṅmukho rājā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha
english: Hearing those dreadful and unpleasant words from Indra, the king lowered his head in shame and became silent.

Thereupon, having welcomed Indra in that way, he left there and returned earth. O slayer of enemies, with an angry heart, army and conveyance he went to subjugate Madhu's son Lavaņa and sent an emissary inviting him to battle.

Thereupon, having welcomed Indra in that way, he left there and returned earth. O slayer of enemies, with an angry heart, army and conveyance he went to subjugate Madhu's son Lavaņa and sent an emissary inviting him to battle.
The ambassador, having gone there, addressed many unpleasant words to Lavaņa and the nightranger devoured him.

sanskrit: स गत्वा विप्रियाण्याह बहूनि मधुनः सुतम्
transliteration: sa gatvā vipriyāṇyāha bahūni madhunaḥ sutam
english: The ambassador, having gone there, addressed many unpleasant words to Lavaņa and the nightranger devoured him.
On the other hand finding the delay of his return the king Māndhāta, enraged, began to assail the Raksasa Lavaņa with arrows from all sides.

sanskrit: ततः प्रहस्य तद्रक्षः शूलं जग्राह पाणिना
transliteration: tataḥ prahasya tadrakṣaḥ śūlaṃ jagrāha pāṇinā
english: Laughing wild Lavaņa took up the dart in his hand and discharged it to destroy the king with his followers.
Thereupon growing powerful the dart reduced the king with his servants and army into ashes and returned to Lavaņa.
In this wise the high-souled king Māndhāta, with his huge army, was slain. O gentle hero, incomparable and great is the strength of the dart..

sanskrit: श्वः प्रभाते तु लवणं वधिष्यसि न संशयः
transliteration: śvaḥ prabhāte tu lavaṇaṃ vadhiṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ
english: Forsooth you shall slay Lavaņa next morning. Certain is your victory if Lavana cannot take up his dart.

sanskrit: लोकानां स्वस्ति चैव स्यात्कृते कर्मणि च त्वया
transliteration: lokānāṃ svasti caiva syātkṛte karmaṇi ca tvayā
english: People shall be at ease if you can bring about the destruction of Lavaņa. O foremost of men, I shall then describe to you the incomparable and dreadful prowess of the vicious-souled Lavaņa and his dart. O king, with great exertions did Lavaņa slay Māndhāta and not easily.

People shall be at ease if you can bring about the destruction of Lavaņa. O foremost of men, I shall then describe to you the incomparable and dreadful prowess of the vicious-souled Lavaņa and his dart. O king, with great exertions did Lavaņa slay Māndhāta and not easily.

sanskrit: त्वं श्वः प्रभाते लवणं महात्मन्वधिष्यसे नात्र तु संशयो मे
शूलं विना निर्गतमामिषार्थे ध्रुवो जयस्ते भविता नरेन्द्र
transliteration: tvaṃ śvaḥ prabhāte lavaṇaṃ mahātmanvadhiṣyase nātra tu saṃśayo me
śūlaṃ vinā nirgatamāmiṣārthe dhruvo jayaste bhavitā narendra
english: O high-minded one, next morning you shall surely destroy Lavaņa. He shall issue our for flesh without taking his dart. And at that time, O lord of man, you shall, forsooth, be crowned with victory.

sanskrit: कथां कथयतां तेषां जयं चाकाङ्क्षतां शुभम्
transliteration: kathāṃ kathayatāṃ teṣāṃ jayaṃ cākāṅkṣatāṃ śubham
english: They being thus engaged in conversation regarding his achieving victory without any danger Satrughna in no time passed the night.

sanskrit: ततः प्रभाते विमले तस्मिन्काले स राक्षसः
transliteration: tataḥ prabhāte vimale tasminkāle sa rākṣasaḥ
english: The clear morning having arrived, that time the heroic Lavana issued out of his city to collect food.
In the meantime having crossed the river Yamunā, the heroic Satrughna, with bow in his hands, stood at the gate of Madhu's city.

sanskrit: ततो ऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते क्रूरकर्मा स राक्षसः
english: There upon returning in the noon with many thousand animals, the night-ranger Lavana, of dreadful actions, espied Satrughna standing at the gate with a weapon in his hand. Thereupon he said: What shall you do with this weapon? O vile wight, enraged I have devoured many thousand persons holding weapons like you. I now perceive you have also been possessed by Kala.

sanskrit: ततो ददर्श शत्रुघ्नं स्थितं द्वारि धृतायुधम्
transliteration: tato dadarśa śatrughnaṃ sthitaṃ dvāri dhṛtāyudham

sanskrit: स्वयं प्रविष्टो ऽद्य मुखं कथमासाद्य दुर्मते
english: O vile man, I am fully fed. How shall you, of your own accord, enter into my mouth?
Lavaņa having said this again and again laughing the great hero Satrughna shed tears in anger.
The high-minded Śatrughna being beside himself with rage, from all his person issued burning lustre.
Greatly enraged he said to the night-ranger O you of a vicious intellect, I wish to enter into a dual encounter with you.
I am the son of the great king Dasaratha, brother of the intelligent Rāma and my name is Satrughna. I slay all my enemies and have come here to destroy you.
I wish now to fight with you-do you enter into a dual conflict. You are the enemy of all animals. You shall not be able to survive at my hands.

sanskrit: प्रत्युवाच नरश्रेष्ठं दिष्ट्या प्राप्तो ऽसि दुर्मते
english: He having said this, the Rākṣasa, laughing aloud, replied to that foremost of men:-Your understanding is bewildered. By the influence of destiny you have come under my control.
The Räksasa Rāvana was the brother of my aunts. O you of vicious understanding, O vile wight, it is for his wife that Rāma did slay him.

sanskrit: तच्च सर्वं मया क्षान्तं रावणस्य कुलक्षयम्
अवज्ञां पुरतः कृत्वा मया यूयं विशेषतः
transliteration: tacca sarvaṃ mayā kṣāntaṃ rāvaṇasya kulakṣayam
avajñāṃ purataḥ kṛtvā mayā yūyaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: It is out of hatred that I have tolerated the destruction of Rāvana's family and have pardoned you all.

sanskrit: निहताश्च हि मे सर्वे परिभूतास्तृणं यथा
transliteration: nihatāśca hi me sarve paribhūtāstṛṇaṃ yathā
english: You are all vile men; I have slain and defeated all of your family that have passed away and shall destroy all that are living and shall come into existence.

sanskrit: तस्य ते युद्धकामस्य युद्धं दास्यामि दुर्मते
तिष्ठं त्वं च मुहूर्तं तु यावदायुधमानये
transliteration: tasya te yuddhakāmasya yuddhaṃ dāsyāmi durmate
tiṣṭhaṃ tvaṃ ca muhūrtaṃ tu yāvadāyudhamānaye
english: O you of vicious intellect, if you wish I shall fight with you. Do you wait here so long I do not bring my weapon.

sanskrit: यो हि विक्लवया बुद्ध्या प्रसरं शत्रवे ददौ
transliteration: yo hi viklavayā buddhyā prasaraṃ śatrave dadau
english: The practical men should never let off the enemies who come out of their own accord. He, who invite an enemy into battle under the influence of perverted understanding, is slain like a coward.

sanskrit: तस्मात्सुदृष्टं कुरु जीवलोकं शरैः शितैस्त्वां विविधैर्नयामि
यमस्य गेहाभिमुखं हि पापं रिपुं त्रिलोकस्य च राघवस्य
transliteration: tasmātsudṛṣṭaṃ kuru jīvalokaṃ śaraiḥ śitaistvāṃ vividhairnayāmi
yamasya gehābhimukhaṃ hi pāpaṃ ripuṃ trilokasya ca rāghavasya
english: Do you behold this world of creatures to your hearts' content for I shall by various sharp weapons despatch you to Yama's abode who is the enemy of the three worlds and Rāghava.
Hearing the words of the high-souled Śatrughna Lavaņa was greatly enraged and again and again asked him to wait.
Clashing his hands and grinding his teeth he invited that foremost of Raghus to fight.

sanskrit: तं ब्रुवाणं तथा वाक्यं लवणं घोरदर्शनम्
transliteration: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tathā vākyaṃ lavaṇaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: And Satrughna, the slayer of celestial's enemies, said to the dreadful Lavaņa, giving vent to those words.

sanskrit: न शत्रुघ्नस्तथा जातो यथा ऽन्ये निर्जितास्त्वया
english: Śatrughna was not born when you did defeat other kings; do you therefore proceed to Death's abode being assailed by shafts.

sanskrit: ऋषयो ऽप्यद्य पापात्मन्मया त्वां निहतं रणे
english: O you of a vicious soul, as did the celestials behold Rāvana slain so shall the Rșis and learned Brāhmaṇas behold you, destroyed by me.
O Rākşasa, forsooth shall good crown cities and villages when you shall fall down brunt by my arrow.
As the rays of the sun enter into lotus so shall arrows, hard as lightning, discharged by my hands, shall enter into your heart.

sanskrit: शत्रुघ्नोरसि चिक्षेप स च तं शतधाच्छिनत्
transliteration: śatrughnorasi cikṣepa sa ca taṃ śatadhācchinat
english: Being beside himself with ire on hearing those words of Śatrughna, Lavaņa threw a huge tree against his breast. And ſatrughna too sundered it into a hundred pieces.

sanskrit: तद्दृष्ट्वा विफलं कर्म राक्षसः पुनरेव तु
transliteration: taddṛṣṭvā viphalaṃ karma rākṣasaḥ punareva tu
english: Beholding his own action baffled the Rākşasa again took up many trees and hurled them at Śatrughna, who, with three or four hundred bent arrow, cut them all, one by one, into pieces.
Beholding his own action baffled the Rākşasa again took up many trees and hurled them at Śatrughna, who, with three or four hundred bent arrow, cut them all, one by one, into pieces.

sanskrit: शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो विव्यथे न स राक्षसः
transliteration: śatrughno vīryasampanno vivyathe na sa rākṣasaḥ
english: Thereupon when the powerful Satrughna assailed him with arrows the Rākşasa was not the least pained.
Rather laughing aloud the valiant Räksasa uprooted a tree and struck him with that on the head. With that stroke he was wounded and slain.
And that hero falling there arose a terrible uproar among the Rșis, celestials, Gandharvas and Apsarās.

sanskrit: तमवज्ञाय तु हतं शत्रुघ्नं भुवि पातितम्
transliteration: tamavajñāya tu hataṃ śatrughnaṃ bhuvi pātitam
english: There upon considering Śatrughna slain the night-ranger did not enter his house albeit he got the opportunity; and moreover beholding him fallen and destroyed he did not take up his dart. He then began to carry his collected food.

sanskrit: नापि शूलं प्रजग्राह तं दृष्ट्वा भुवि पातितम्
transliteration: nāpi śūlaṃ prajagrāha taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhuvi pātitam
english: There upon considering Śatrughna slain the night-ranger did not enter his house albeit he got the opportunity; and moreover beholding him fallen and destroyed he did not take up his dart. He then began to carry his collected food.
Regaining his sense within a moment, Śatrughna, with a weapon in his hand, stood at the city gate and the Rșis began to praise him.

sanskrit: ज्वलन्तं तेजसा घोरं पूरयन्तं दिशो दश
transliteration: jvalantaṃ tejasā ghoraṃ pūrayantaṃ diśo daśa
english: There upon, he having taken up an excellent arrow of unfailing aim the ten quarters were filled with its native brilliance.
Its face was like lightning and its velocity the same and it looked like Meru and Mandāra; its joints were all bent. None could defeat it in battle.

It was pasted with red sandal resembling blood and its feathers were beautiful. Beholding that dart like to the fire of dissolution, and dreadful to lords of Dānavas, mountains and Asuras, the creatures were greatly terrified.

It was pasted with red sandal resembling blood and its feathers were beautiful. Beholding that dart like to the fire of dissolution, and dreadful to lords of Dānavas, mountains and Asuras, the creatures were greatly terrified.

What more, being disturbed, the celestials, Asuras, Gandharvas, saints and Apsarās and all other creatures of the world approached the Great Patriarch, the conferrer of boons and said. The fear of the celestials and the destruction of the creatures has arrived.

What more, being disturbed, the celestials, Asuras, Gandharvas, saints and Apsarās and all other creatures of the world approached the Great Patriarch, the conferrer of boons and said. The fear of the celestials and the destruction of the creatures has arrived.

sanskrit: नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं च न श्रुतं प्रपितामह
transliteration: nedṛśaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ ca na śrutaṃ prapitāmaha

english: Hearing those words the Patriarch Brahmă replied Although it is a source of great fear still it is not dreadful to the celestials. There upon with sweet accents he said:-Hear, O you celestials, ſatrughna has taken up this arrow for the destruction of Pavana.

sanskrit: तेजसा तस्य सम्मूढाः सर्वे स्मः सुरसत्तमाः
transliteration: tejasā tasya sammūḍhāḥ sarve smaḥ surasattamāḥ

english: By the energy thereof we have all been overwhelmed. This effulgent, ever existing arrow was made by the Primeval, Deity, Vis nu-the lord of creatures. My children, the burning arrow, of which you are afraid, was made by the high-minded Vişņu for slaying the demons Madhu and Kaitabha.

sanskrit: एषा एव तनुः पूर्वा विष्णोस्तस्य महात्मनः
transliteration: eṣā eva tanuḥ pūrvā viṣṇostasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Vişņu alone is cognisant of its energy. This Śatrughna is the first portion of Vişnu's person; do you all go hence and behold the destruction of the foremost Raksasa, Lavana, by the highsouled, heroic Satrughna, the younger brother of Rama.

Vişņu alone is cognisant of its energy. This Śatrughna is the first portion of Vişnu's person; do you all go hence and behold the destruction of the foremost Raksasa, Lavana, by the highsouled, heroic Satrughna, the younger brother of Rama.

sanskrit: तस्य ते देवदेवस्य निशम्य वचनं सुराः
transliteration: tasya te devadevasya niśamya vacanaṃ surāḥ
english: Hearing the words of the Patriarch Brahmă, the celestials arrived at the battle-field of Šatrughna and Lavana and saw that the arrow, held by Satrughna's hands, was burning like the fire of dissolution.

Hearing the words of the Patriarch Brahmă, the celestials arrived at the battle-field of Šatrughna and Lavana and saw that the arrow, held by Satrughna's hands, was burning like the fire of dissolution.

sanskrit: सिंहनादं भृशं कृत्वा ददर्श लक्षणं पुनः
transliteration: siṃhanādaṃ bhṛśaṃ kṛtvā dadarśa lakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ
english: Beholding the welkin covered by the celestials, Satrughna, the descendant of Raghu, emitting leonine roars, again and again looked towards Lavaņa. And being again excited by the high-souled Śatrughna and enraged Lavaņa arrived for encounter.

Beholding the welkin covered by the celestials, Satrughna, the descendant of Raghu, emitting leonine roars, again and again looked towards Lavaņa. And being again excited by the high-souled Śatrughna and enraged Lavaņa arrived for encounter.

There upon expanding his bow up to ears, Satrughna, the the most accomplished archer, discharged his arrow against the spacious breast of Lavaņa. And piercing his heart that arrow entered speedily into Rasātala and having entered Rasātala that arrow, honoured by the celestials, again came to the descendant of Raghu.
And being pierced by that shaft the nightranger Lavaņa fell down on earth like a mountain clapped by a thunder-bolt.
The Rākşasa being slain that celestial, huge arrow came into the possession of Rudra before the gods.

Having removed the fear of the three worlds with one shaft, that heroic Raghu, Satrughnayounger brother of Lakşmaņa, holding excellent bow and arrow, appeared like the Sun of thousand rays removing darkness.

sanskrit: ततो हि देवा ऋषिपन्नगाश्च प्रपूजिरे ह्यप्सरसश्च सर्वाः
दिष्ट्या जयो दाशरथेरवाप्तस्त्यक्त्वा भयं सर्प इव प्रशान्तः
transliteration: tato hi devā ṛṣipannagāśca prapūjire hyapsarasaśca sarvāḥ
diṣṭyā jayo dāśaratheravāptastyaktvā bhayaṃ sarpa iva praśāntaḥ
english: There upon chanting the glories of Satrughna, the celestials, Rşis, Pannagas, Apsarās, said “O son of Dasaratha, it is really fortunate, that you, renouncing fear, have acquired victory, and that the Rākṣasa Lavaņa has been vanquished like a serpent."

sanskrit: हते तु लवणे देवाः सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः
transliteration: hate tu lavaṇe devāḥ sendrāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ
english: Lavana being slain the celestials headed by Agni and Indra said in sweet accents to Śatrughna the represser of enemies.

sanskrit: दिष्ट्या ते विजयो वत्स दिष्ट्या लवणराक्षसः
transliteration: diṣṭyā te vijayo vatsa diṣṭyā lavaṇarākṣasaḥ
english: O child, fortunate it is that you have been crowned with success after slaying the Rākṣasa Lavaņa. Do you, therefore, O foremost of men, O you of firm vows, accept boons.
O you having long arms, all those who can confer boons have arrived here; they all wish for your victory; seeing us does not go without fruits.

sanskrit: देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा शूरो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः
transliteration: devānāṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā śūro mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Hearing the words of the celestials the largearmed and self-controlled Satrughna placed his hands on his head and said.

sanskrit: निवेशं प्राप्नुयाच्छीघ्रमेष मे ऽस्तु वरः परः
english: Let this picturesque and charming city of Madhu, built by the celestials, by my capital; this is the only excellent boon I can beg.

sanskrit: भविष्यति पुरी रम्या शूरसेना न संशयः
transliteration: bhaviṣyati purī ramyā śūrasenā na saṃśayaḥ
english: The celestials, with a delighted heart, said to the descendant of Raghu.-Your desire shall be fulfilled and forsooth shall your city be turned into a picturesque capital under the name of Surasena.
The high-souled celestials having ascended the welkin saying this, the highly effulgent Śatrughna brought the soldiers there, that were encamped on the banks of the Gangā.
When the soldiers arrived there on hearing the commands of Satrughna he engaged in making encampments in the month of Śrāvan.

sanskrit: सा पुरा दिव्यसङ्काशा वर्षे द्वादशमे शुभे
transliteration: sā purā divyasaṅkāśā varṣe dvādaśame śubhe
english: In this wise the fearlessness of the celestial host, taking the shape of a country, that beautiful and picturesque city was reared in the course of twelve years. All the fields there were filled with crops and Indra began to pour showers in due seasons. And being protected by the strength of Śatrughna's arms all men there became valiant and were freed from deseases.

In this wise the fearlessness of the celestial host, taking the shape of a country, that beautiful and picturesque city was reared in the course of twelve years. All the fields there were filled with crops and Indra began to pour showers in due seasons. And being protected by the strength of Śatrughna's arms all men there became valiant and were freed from deseases.
That city on the banks of Yamună appeared beautiful like the half moon and was filled with yards, shops, streets beautiful houses, men of four orders and various articles of trade.

sanskrit: यच्च तेन पुरा शुभ्रं लवणेन कृतं महत्
transliteration: yacca tena purā śubhraṃ lavaṇena kṛtaṃ mahat
english: Śatrughna now engaged in beautifying the spacious, white houses that were made by Lavana before, with various ornamental works.

Beholding the city interspersed with various excellent gardens, pleasure grounds and prosperously filled with celestials and men and diverse articles of trade and merchants hailing from various countries, Satrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, attained to the satisfaction of desire and excess of delight.

sanskrit: तस्य बुद्धिः समुत्पन्ना निवेश्य मधुरां पुरीम्
रामपादौ निरीक्षे ऽहं वर्षे द्वादश आगते
transliteration: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā niveśya madhurāṃ purīm
english: Having thus reared the beautiful city he resolved within himself The twelfth year has come. I shall now behold the feet of Rāma.

sanskrit: ततः स ताममरपुरोपमां पुरीं निवेश्य वै विविधजनाभिसंवृताम्
transliteration: tataḥ sa tāmamarapuropamāṃ purīṃ niveśya vai vividhajanābhisaṃvṛtām
english: There upon having set up the city resembling the region of the celestials and filled with various men, the king Satrughna, the enhancer of Raghu's race, determined on beholding Rāma's feet.
There upon on the completion of the twelfth year, Satrughna, with few servants, soldiers and followers, desired to proceed to Ayodhyā protected by Rama.

sanskrit: जगाम हयमुख्यैश्च रथानां च शतेन सः
transliteration: jagāma hayamukhyaiśca rathānāṃ ca śatena saḥ
english: Having prevented his minister and leading generals he proceeded with one hundred chariots and cavalry.
And having counted seven halting stations on his way, the highly illustrious descendant of Raghu, Satrughna, arrived at the hermitage of Valmiki.

sanskrit: सो ऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ वाल्मीकेः पुरुषर्षभः
english: And having bowed to the feet of the leading Muni, that foremost of men took from his hands water to wash feet and Arghya and accepted his hospitality.
The great ascetic Valmiki addressed to the high-souled Śatrughna many sweet word.

sanskrit: सुदुष्करं कृतं कर्म लवणं निघ्नता त्वया
transliteration: suduṣkaraṃ kṛtaṃ karma lavaṇaṃ nighnatā tvayā
english: Having referred first Lavana's destruction, he said: Having slain Lavana you have performed a very hard work.
O gentle one, O foremost of men, Lavana had slain in conflict many hundred highly powerful kings with their army and conveyances. at to

sanskrit: स त्वया निहतः पापो लीलया पुरुषर्षभ
जगतश्च भयं तत्र प्रशान्तं तव तेजसा
transliteration: sa tvayā nihataḥ pāpo līlayā puruṣarṣabha
jagataśca bhayaṃ tatra praśāntaṃ tava tejasā
english: And you have easily slain that vicious-souled Rākşasa, Lavaņa. By your prowess the whole world has been divested of fear.

sanskrit: रावणस्य वधो घोरो यत्नेन महता कृतः
transliteration: rāvaṇasya vadho ghoro yatnena mahatā kṛtaḥ
english: With great difficulty Rāma had slain Rāvana but without any trouble whatsoever you have accomplished this mighty work,

sanskrit: भूतानां चैव सर्वेषां जगतश्च प्रियं कृतम्
transliteration: bhūtānāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ jagataśca priyaṃ kṛtam
english: Lavaņa being slain, the celestials have been greatly delighted-what more the well-being of the whole universe and all creatures has been brought about.
O Rāghava, O foremost of men, being present in the assemblage of Vāsava I duly witnessed your combat.

sanskrit: उपाघ्रास्यामि ते मूर्ध्नि स्नेहस्यैषा परा गतिः
transliteration: upāghrāsyāmi te mūrdhni snehasyaiṣā parā gatiḥ
english: O Śatrughna, I too have been greatly delighted I therefore smell your crown for this is the best expression of love.
Saying this the high-minded Vālmīki smelled his crown and made arrangements for his reception as well as that of his followers.

After meals, Satrughna, the foremost of men, listened to themes relating to Rāma and set musical notes. Those themes were composed describing the early actions of Rāma. They were composed in Sanskrit, set to the tune of a musical instrument, adorned with all the marks of vocal music and arranged in accompaniment with notes.

After meals, Satrughna, the foremost of men, listened to themes relating to Rāma and set musical notes. Those themes were composed describing the early actions of Rāma. They were composed in Sanskrit, set to the tune of a musical instrument, adorned with all the marks of vocal music and arranged in accompaniment with notes.

sanskrit: परस्परं च ये तत्र सैनिकाः सम्बभाषिरे
transliteration: parasparaṃ ca ye tatra sainikāḥ sambabhāṣire

sanskrit: अर्थो यो नः पुरा दृष्टस्तमाश्रमपदे पुनः
शृणुमः किमिदं स्वप्नो गीतबन्धं श्रियो भवेत्
transliteration: artho yo naḥ purā dṛṣṭastamāśramapade punaḥ
śṛṇumaḥ kimidaṃ svapno gītabandhaṃ śriyo bhavet

english: O foremost of men, do you ask particularly, about this, Vālmīki, the foremost of ascetics. They being all thus struck with curiosity, Satrughna said: It is not proper for us, O You soldiers, to question him in this way. There are many such wonders in the hermitage of this ascetic.

sanskrit: अभिवाद्य महर्षिं तं स्वं निवेशं ययौ तदा
transliteration: abhivādya maharṣiṃ taṃ svaṃ niveśaṃ yayau tadā
english: It is not therefore becoming to ask him about this our of curiosity. Having thus addressed the soldiers and bowed to the ascetic, Satrughna, the descendant of Raghu, entered his own quarter.
There upon going to bed, ſatrughna began to meditate upon that excellent theme relating to Rāma and treating of diverse subjects and did not enter into sleep.
In sooth the high-minded Śatrughna spent the night in no time listening to that charming song set unmusical notes.

sanskrit: तस्यां निशायां व्युष्टायां कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकं क्रमम्
transliteration: tasyāṃ niśāyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ kṛtvā paurvāhṇikaṃ kramam
english: The night being over, he first went through the morning sites and then with folded hands addressed the foremost of ascetics, Valmiki, saying.
O illustrious Sir, I am anxious to see Rāma, the enhancer of the delight of the Raghu race, And my desire is that you may with other illustrious Rsis, grant me permission on this.
Satrughna, the slayer of enemies, having said this, the great ascetic Vālmīki embraced and bacle him farewell.
He was greatly anxious to behold Rāma and saluting the foremost of Munis he speedily preceded to Ayodhyā.
There upon having entered the highly picturesque city Ayodhyā, city Ayodhyā, the graceful descendant of Ikşvākus, ſatrughna, reached where the long-armed and the highly effulgent Råma was waiting.

He espied there Rāma in the midst of the councillors like Indra among the immortals burning in his own effulgence. And having bowed with folded hands to Răma, having truth for his prowess, Śatrughna, said.

He espied there Rāma in the midst of the councillors like Indra among the immortals burning in his own effulgence. And having bowed with folded hands to Răma, having truth for his prowess, Śatrughna, said.

sanskrit: हतः स लवणः पापः पुरी चास्य निवेशिता
transliteration: hataḥ sa lavaṇaḥ pāpaḥ purī cāsya niveśitā
english: O great king, I have carried out all your behests; I have slain the vicious Lavaņa and filled his city with subjects. O descendant of Raghu, twelve years have passed away without you, I do not wish to live any longer separated from you.

O great king, I have carried out all your behests; I have slain the vicious Lavaņa and filled his city with subjects. O descendant of Raghu, twelve years have passed away without you, I do not wish to live any longer separated from you.

sanskrit: मातृहीनो यथा वत्सो न चिरं प्रवसाम्यहम्
transliteration: mātṛhīno yathā vatso na ciraṃ pravasāmyaham
english: Do you therefore, O Kākutstha of unmitigated prowess, have compassion on me. Without you, I cannot live for ever in a foreign province like a motherless child.
He having said this, Rāma embraced him and said: Be not sorry O hero. This is not a becoming action for Kşatriyas.

sanskrit: प्रजा नः परिपाल्या हि क्षत्रधर्मेण राघव
transliteration: prajā naḥ paripālyā hi kṣatradharmeṇa rāghava
english: The kings, O Raghava, are never tired of living in a foreign land. According to the morality of the Kșatriyas, their greatest duty consists in governing the subjects.

sanskrit: काले काले तु मां वीर अयोध्यामवलोकितुम्
आगच्छ त्वं नरश्रेष्ठ गन्तासि च पुरं तव
transliteration: kāle kāle tu māṃ vīra ayodhyāmavalokitum
āgaccha tvaṃ naraśreṣṭha gantāsi ca puraṃ tava
english: O heroic and foremost of men, do you, at intervals, come to Ayodhyå to see me and return to your own city.

sanskrit: ममापि त्वं सुदयितः प्राणैरपि न संशयः
transliteration: mamāpi tvaṃ sudayitaḥ prāṇairapi na saṃśayaḥ
english: Forsooth you are dearer than my life. But it is an incumbent duty to govern the kingdom. Do you therefore, O Kakutstha, live with me for seven nights, and afterwards return to your city with your servants, army and conveyances.

Forsooth you are dearer than my life. But it is an incumbent duty to govern the kingdom. Do you therefore, O Kakutstha, live with me for seven nights, and afterwards return to your city with your servants, army and conveyances.
Hearing those moral and charming words of Rama, Satrughna poorly replied, saying: Your command shall be carried out.
Thereupon Satrughna, well-skilled in the use of bows, remained with Rāma for seven nights and then addressed himself for departure.
Thereupon having invited Bharata and Laksmana, the high-souled Rama, having truth for his prowess, speedily went for his city in a huge chariot.

sanskrit: भरतेन च शत्रुघ्नो जगामाशु पुरं ततः
transliteration: bharatena ca śatrughno jagāmāśu puraṃ tataḥ
english: The high-souled Lakşmaņa and slayer of enemies Bharata followed him on foot for some distance.

sanskrit: प्रस्थाप्य तु स शत्रुघ्नं भ्रातृभ्यां सह राघवः
transliteration: prasthāpya tu sa śatrughnaṃ bhrātṛbhyāṃ saha rāghavaḥ
english: Having bade adieu to Satrughna, Rama, the descendant of Raghu, was greatly delighted by governing his subjects piously in the company of Bharata and Laksmana.
Some days having passed in this wise-a villager, an old Brālimaņa, arrived at the palace gate with a dead boy.

That Brāhmaṇa, stricken with affection, again and again bewailed in various piteous accents exclaiming What heinous crime had I committed in my pristine birth that I have been constrained to witness the death of my son.

sanskrit: किं नु मे दुष्कृतं कर्म पुरा देहान्तरे कृतम्
यदहं पुत्रमेकं त्वां पश्यामि निधनं गतम्
transliteration: kiṃ nu me duṣkṛtaṃ karma purā dehāntare kṛtam
yadahaṃ putramekaṃ tvāṃ paśyāmi nidhanaṃ gatam
english: That Brāhmaṇa, stricken with affection, again and again bewailed in various piteous accents exclaiming What heinous crime had I committed in my pristine birth that I have been constrained to witness the death of my son.
My son, you have not as yet completed fourteen years. To my misery you have met with untimely death. Forsooth, for your grief, O my son, myself and your mother shall soon be snatched away by death.

sanskrit: अहं च जननी चैव तव शोकेन पुत्रक
transliteration: ahaṃ ca jananī caiva tava śokena putraka
english: My son, you have not as yet completed fourteen years. To my misery you have met with untimely death. Forsooth, for your grief, O my son, myself and your mother shall soon be snatched away by death.

sanskrit: न स्मराम्यनृतं ह्युक्तं न च हिंसां स्मराम्यहम्
सर्वेषां प्राणिनां पापं कृतं नैव स्मराम्यहम्
transliteration: na smarāmyanṛtaṃ hyuktaṃ na ca hiṃsāṃ smarāmyaham
sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ naiva smarāmyaham
english: I do not remember to have ever uttered a falsehood, or injured an animal or perpetrated any other crime. Therefore for some other sinful action, this boy, without performing the son's duties towards his parents, has gone to the abode of death.

I do not remember to have ever uttered a falsehood, or injured an animal or perpetrated any other crime. Therefore for some other sinful action, this boy, without performing the son's duties towards his parents, has gone to the abode of death.

sanskrit: नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं मे श्रुतं वा घोरदर्शनम्
transliteration: nedṛśaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ me śrutaṃ vā ghoradarśanam
english: Save under the regime of Rama, I have never seen or heard of the dreadful death of such a boy who has not attained the age.
